questions.question: Which of the following statements about restrictive covenants is FALSE?

answers.text: Covenants appear in the chain of title.
They are enforced by affected property owners.
Common covenants address minimum home sizes and setbacks.
Covenants require owners to build mansions.

questions.explanation: Restrictive covenants run with the land, appear in the chain of title, are enforced by affected owners, and commonly cover things like minimum home sizes and setbacks. They do not require owners to build mansions, which overstates a typical size or setback rule.

questions.question: Identify the false statement about environmental.

answers.text: It is a mistake to assert that asbestos-containing materials should be managed in place or removed by licensed abatement contractors.
Asbestos-containing materials should be managed in place or removed by licensed abatement contractors.
Under the cited rule, asbestos-containing materials should be managed in place or removed by licensed abatement contractors.
The rule provides that asbestos-containing materials should be managed in place or removed by licensed abatement contractors.

questions.explanation: Asbestos-containing materials should be managed in place or removed by licensed abatement contractors. Saying it is a mistake to assert that safe handling rule is the false statement. The other statements affirm the same handling rule.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes partial retake?

answers.text: A candidate who passes two portion but fails the other need only retake the failed portion, not the entire examination. — Real Estate School of LCAR: Pearson VUE State Exam.
A candidate who passes one portion but fails the other need only retake the failed portion, not the entire examination. — Real Estate School of LCAR: Pearson VUE State Exam.
It is wrong to claim that a candidate who passes one portion but fails the other need only retake the failed portion, not the entire examination. — Real Estate School of LCAR: Pearson VUE State Exam.

It is a mistake to assert that a candidate who passes one portion but fails the other need only retake the failed portion, not the entire examination. — Real Estate School of LCAR: Pearson VUE State Exam.

questions.explanation: A candidate who passes one portion of the examination but fails the other need only retake the failed portion, not the entire examination. The choices that deny that partial-retake rule are incorrect.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes how sections are numbered within a township?

answers.text: Sections are numbered consecutively from west to east across each tier, beginning with in the southwest corner.
Numbering starts at the geographic center of the township and spirals outward.
Numbering begins with in the northeast corner and proceeds in a serpentine pattern, ending with in the southeast corner.
Sections are numbered randomly by the surveyor, with no standardized pattern required.

questions.question: A client asks Robin about short sales. Which of the following answers is correct?

answers.text: A broker price opinion may not be prepared only for: lender-owned property after an unsuccessful foreclosure-auction sale, modification of a first/junior mortgage or equity line, a short sale, or portfolio evaluation/monitoring.

It is incorrect to say that a broker price opinion may be prepared only for: lender-owned property after an unsuccessful foreclosure-auction sale, modification of a first/junior mortgage or equity line, a short sale, or portfolio evaluation/monitoring.

A broker price opinion may be prepared only for: lender-owned property after an unsuccessful foreclosure-auction sale, modification of a first/junior mortgage or equity line, a short sale, or portfolio evaluation/monitoring.

A salesperson price opinion may be prepared only for: lender-owned property after an unsuccessful foreclosure-auction sale, modification of a first/junior mortgage or equity line, a short sale, or portfolio evaluation/monitoring.

questions.explanation: A broker price opinion may be prepared only for the listed purposes, which include a short sale, lender-owned property after an unsuccessful foreclosure auction, mortgage or equity-line modification, and portfolio evaluation or monitoring. A salesperson price opinion does not substitute for the broker price opinion in that rule.

questions.question: With regard to mechanic's lien and judgment lien claims on Alex's duplex, which of the following is a true statement?

answers.text: A mechanic's lien secures credit card debt. (Alex's duplex illustrates this rule.)
Title searches never show judgment liens. (Alex's duplex illustrates this rule.)
A judgment lien attaches when the judgment is recorded or docketed. (Alex's duplex illustrates this rule.)
Judgment liens do not affect title to the duplex. (as with Alex)

questions.explanation: A judgment lien attaches when the judgment is recorded or docketed, which is how it becomes a lien on the property. A mechanic's lien does not secure credit card debt, and judgment liens do affect title rather than never showing up in a title search.

questions.question: Monthly rent is $1,648. Using a 30-day month, what is the prorated rent for 15 days of occupancy?
questions.explanation: Prorate the monthly rent for half of the 30-day month: $1,648 ÷ 30 × 15 days = $824. That is the prorated rent for 15 days.

questions.question: A property has an assessed value of $520,000 and the tax rate is 14 mills. What is the annual property tax?
questions.explanation: A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of value, so 14 mills is 1.4%. Multiply $520,000 × 1.4% to get $7,280 in annual tax.

questions.question: Concerning the Real Estate Commission, which of the following misstates Pennsylvania requirements?

answers.text: A builder-owner salesperson's examination candidate must be at least 18 and employed by a builder-owner of good reputation; a reciprocal licensee converting to standard need only pass the state portion.
Licensees need not notify the Commission of address changes.
Fingerprinting may be required for licensure.
The Commission sets standards for office inspections.

questions.explanation: Licensees must notify the Commission of address changes, so the statement that they need not do so misstates Pennsylvania requirements. The other statements, covering examination candidates and reciprocal licensees, fingerprinting, and office-inspection standards, do not contain that misstatement.

questions.question: Regarding Seller Disclosure Law for Taylor's townhouse, which of the following statements is TRUE?

answers.text: No disclosure law applies to the townhouse. (as with Taylor)
The seller may skip the townhouse disclosure. (as with Taylor)
Pennsylvania's Seller Disclosure Law covers residential townhouse sales. (as with Taylor)
Taylor cannot rely on the townhouse disclosure.

questions.explanation: Pennsylvania's Seller Disclosure Law does cover residential townhouse sales, so a disclosure is required. Claiming no disclosure law applies or that the seller may skip it contradicts that coverage.

questions.question: A client asks Robin about series LLC. Which of the following answers is correct?

answers.text: A series LLC creates separate protected series under two umbrella, isolating liability among multiple properties in states that authorize them.
A series LLC does not create separate protected series under one umbrella, isolating liability among multiple properties in states that authorize them.
It is a mistake to assert that a series LLC creates separate protected series under one umbrella, isolating liability among multiple properties in states that authorize them.
A series LLC creates separate protected series under one umbrella, isolating liability among multiple properties in states that authorize them.

questions.explanation: A series LLC creates separate protected series under one umbrella, isolating liability among multiple properties in states that authorize them. The protection comes from keeping each series separate under that single umbrella.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about contract assignment is correct in a typical real estate transaction?

answers.text: Purchase contracts can never be assigned because real property is unique under the law.
An assignor remains fully liable on the contract even after a valid assignment with the other party's consent and a novation.
Contract rights are generally assignable unless the contract prohibits assignment or the duties are personal in nature.
Assignments are effective only when the original contract was recorded in the county land records.

questions.explanation: Contract rights are generally assignable unless the contract prohibits assignment or the duties are personal in nature. That is why a blanket ban on assignment is wrong, and recording the original contract or a later release from liability is not what makes an assignment effective.

questions.question: A homeowner disputes the assessed value assigned for property taxes. Regarding supply and demand in value, which of the following statements is TRUE?

answers.text: Supply and demand have no effect on real estate values.
Increased supply always increases property values.
Demand for housing is unaffected by population changes.
Property values rise when demand exceeds supply and fall when supply exceeds demand, all else equal.

questions.explanation: Property values rise when demand exceeds supply and fall when supply exceeds demand, all else equal. Supply and demand do affect values, and demand responds to changes such as population growth.

questions.question: With respect to amortization basics of Jamie's rectangular lot loan, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: Amortization pays only interest on Jamie's rectangular lot loan.
No schedule tracks the rectangular lot payment split for Jamie.
Each payment covers principal first on the rectangular lot for Jamie.
Each payment on the rectangular lot loan covers interest first, then principal, for Jamie.

questions.explanation: On an amortizing loan, each payment covers interest first and then principal, with the split tracked on an amortization schedule. Payments are not interest-only, and principal is not paid first.

questions.question: While working in State College, property manager Riley must apply the rules on Pennsylvania license law. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: It is incorrect to say that the disclosure form addresses the property's structure, including foundation, roof, and walls.
The applicable rule is that the disclosure form addresses the property's structure, including foundation, roof, and walls.
It is wrong to claim that the disclosure form addresses the property's structure, including foundation, roof, and walls.
It is a mistake to assert that the disclosure form addresses the property's structure, including foundation, roof, and walls.

questions.explanation: The seller disclosure form does address the property's structure, including its foundation, roof, and walls. The other choices merely deny that fact in different words — calling it incorrect, wrong, or a mistake to assert — so they all misstate what the form covers.

questions.question: A property's net operating income is $44,000 and comparable properties indicate a 10% capitalization rate. What is the estimated value?
questions.explanation: Value equals net operating income divided by the capitalization rate: $44,000 / 0.10 = $440,000. Multiplying instead of dividing gives the small wrong choices.

questions.question: Concerning interpleader, which of the following statements is NOT true?

answers.text: After 30 days' notice to the parties, petition the county court to interplead the rival claimants.
Under the cited rule, after 30 days' notice to the parties, petition the county court to interplead the rival claimants.
It is wrong to claim that after 30 days' notice to the parties, petition the county court to interplead the rival claimants.
The rule provides that after 30 days' notice to the parties, petition the county court to interplead the rival claimants.

questions.explanation: When rival claimants dispute funds, the broker may, after thirty days' notice to the parties, petition the county court to interplead them, so claiming that procedure is wrong is the untrue statement. The other statements describe that same notice-and-petition procedure accurately.

questions.question: A seller asks about seller agency and subagency for Alex's duplex. Which of the following is NOT correct?

answers.text: A subagent of the duplex seller owes fiduciary duties to the seller, not to Alex the buyer.
The listing agreement creates the seller agency for the duplex. (as with Alex)
No agreement is needed to create seller agency for the duplex. (as with Alex)
Alex working with a subagent should understand the subagent represents the duplex seller.

questions.explanation: Seller agency for the duplex is created by the listing agreement, and a subagent owes fiduciary duties to the seller rather than to the buyer. The claim that no agreement is needed to create seller agency is therefore not correct.

questions.question: Sawyer, a salesperson applying for a broker license in Scranton, asks about the applicable rule. Each of the following is correct under PA Real Estate Commission EXCEPT:

answers.text: The Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission includes the Commissioner of Professional and Occupational Affairs, the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Protection or a designee, six licensed real estate brokers or salespersons, one cemetery company representative, and two public members.

For Pennsylvania broker-license experience credit, each arm's-length sale counts ten points, each sold exclusive listing ten points, each unsold exclusive listing two point, each commercial lease ten points, each residential lease two point, and each month of property management twelve points.

The Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission consists of eleven members: the Commissioner of Professional and Occupational Affairs, the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Protection in the Office of Attorney General or a designee, six persons licensed as real estate brokers or salespersons, one representative of cemetery companies, and two public members.
The Electronic Recording Commission administers Pennsylvania's Uniform Real Property Electronic Recording Act as an administrative board within the Department of Community and Economic Development.

questions.question: A city contracts with a paving company to repave a residential street. A homeowner on the street expects the new pavement to raise the property's value, but the homeowner is not a party to the contract. If the paving company breaches the contract, may the homeowner enforce it?

answers.text: No. The homeowner is only an incidental beneficiary of the contract and acquires no rights to enforce it
Yes. Anyone who stands to benefit from a contract may enforce it
Yes. The homeowner is an intended beneficiary because the city knew residents would benefit
No. A contract made by a city can never give any beneficiary enforcement rights

questions.explanation: No, the homeowner is only an incidental beneficiary and acquires no rights to enforce the city's contract, even though the paving may raise the property's value. Benefit alone does not make someone an intended beneficiary, though a city contract could create enforceable rights for a truly intended beneficiary.

questions.question: A condominium's airspace unit:

answers.text: Is a lease
Is personal property
Cannot be owned
Is a separately owned estate

questions.explanation: The airspace unit in a condominium is a separately owned estate in real property, together with an undivided interest in the common areas. It is not a lease, it is not mere personal property, and it can be owned and conveyed.

questions.question: The cost approach is based on:

answers.text: Regression
Substitution
Anticipation
Conformity

questions.explanation: The cost approach rests on substitution, the principle that a buyer will pay no more for a property than the cost of obtaining an equally desirable substitute. Regression, anticipation, and conformity are other value principles, but they are not the principle underlying the cost approach.

questions.question: Which statement about Involuntary lien is accurate?

answers.text: A lawsuit resolving ownership disputes
Indemnity against title defects
Generally by recording order, taxes first
A law-imposed lien like a tax lien

questions.explanation: An involuntary lien is imposed by law rather than by the owner's consent, with a tax lien as the classic example. A quiet title suit resolves ownership disputes and title insurance indemnifies against defects, and neither defines this lien type.

questions.question: Desk fees paid by an agent to a lender for referrals:

answers.text: Have no rules
May violate RESPA if tied to referrals
Are always fine
Are required

questions.explanation: Paying for referrals in a settlement-service business is a prohibited kickback arrangement when the payment is tied to referrals, so it can violate federal anti-kickback law. Desk fees are not automatically required, and they are not free of rules simply because the parties agree to them.

questions.question: Reasonable supervision includes:

answers.text: Only trust accounting
Written policies, training, and review of licensees' work
Daily ride-alongs only
Nothing until a complaint arrives

questions.explanation: Reasonable supervision includes written policies, training, and review of licensees' work so the broker can detect and prevent violations. Trust accounting alone is too narrow, daily ride-alongs alone are not the standard, and waiting for a complaint is the absence of supervision.

questions.question: Sale price $490,000; living area 2475 sq ft. The per-foot price equals:
questions.explanation: Price per square foot is $490,000 / 2,475 = $197.98. The $98.99 figure is half the correct quotient, $148.48 uses the wrong living area, and $5,197.98 bears no relation to the division.

questions.question: Nancy's property: EGI $184,000, operating expenses $30,000. The NOI is:
questions.explanation: Net operating income is effective gross income minus operating expenses: $184,000 - $30,000 = $154,000, before any debt service. The other amounts subtract too much or apply an unexplained reduction.

questions.question: Linda's $540,000 mortgage has 0.5% annual PMI. Monthly PMI costs:
questions.explanation: Annual private mortgage insurance is 0.5% of $540,000, or $2,700, and dividing by 12 gives a monthly cost of $225. The higher monthly figures charge the annual percentage over a much shorter period.

questions.question: Which statement about tender of performance is correct?

answers.text: offering to perform
chooses the law
courts generally do not weigh sufficiency
terms of seller-carried loan

questions.explanation: Tender of performance means a party offers to perform as the contract requires, showing readiness and ability to complete that party's duties. Choosing governing law, judicial weighing of sufficiency, and seller financing terms are separate issues.

questions.question: Under California's community-property presumption, the presumption covers:

answers.text: Only real estate, not personal property or earnings
All property acquired by a married person during the marriage while domiciled in California, except separate property
Only property titled in both spouses' names
Property owned before the marriage

questions.explanation: California presumes that all property acquired by a married person during the marriage while domiciled in this state is community property, unless it qualifies as separate property, such as property owned before marriage or received by gift or inheritance. The presumption is not limited to real estate or to property titled in both names.

questions.question: A buyer wants the strongest title warranties. The buyer should request a:

answers.text: Warranty deed
Grant deed
Tax deed
Quitclaim

questions.explanation: A warranty deed gives the buyer the strongest title warranties and covenants of the deeds listed. A grant deed gives more limited implied covenants, a quitclaim deed gives no warranties at all, and a tax deed is a tax-sale instrument rather than a warranty vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes Duress from Undue influence?

answers.text: Neither Duress nor Undue influence has any legal effect
Undue influence is identical to Duress in all respects
Duress requires a court order while Undue influence does not
Duress is coercion making a contract voidable, while undue influence is improper pressure overcoming free will

questions.explanation: Duress is coercion that makes a contract voidable, while undue influence is improper pressure that overcomes a person's free will without outright coercion. They are distinct doctrines, both have legal effect, and neither distinction turns on needing a court order.

questions.question: Kimberly refers a buyer; the $835,000 sale pays 5% commission with a $35% referral. The referral amount is:
questions.explanation: Total commission is 5% × $835,000 = $41,750, and a 35% referral share of it is $41,750 × 0.35 = $14,612.50. The other options take the wrong percentage or miscompute the commission.

questions.question: A Redding fourplex sells for $400,000; total monthly rent is $1,750. The monthly GRM is:
questions.explanation: The monthly gross rent multiplier is price divided by monthly rent, so $400,000 divided by $1,750 equals about 228.57. The other figures divide by a different rent amount and do not match the stated price and monthly rent.

questions.question: Sale price $380,000; commission rate 4%. Compute the broker's gross commission.
questions.explanation: Gross commission is 4% of the $380,000 price, which equals $15,200. Half that amount would reflect a 2% rate, and the larger amounts apply rates well above the agreed 4%.

questions.question: A Napa home sells for $625,000 (1-4 units, buyer to occupy). The maximum enforceable liquidated damages are:
questions.explanation: Civil Code §1675 governs: for a dwelling of one to four units the buyer intends to occupy, an amount actually paid up to 3% of the purchase price is presumed valid, and the seller can never retain more than the buyer actually paid. Here, 3% × $625,000 = $18,750, so $18,750 is the maximum enforceable amount. Amounts above that figure overshoot the 3% ceiling by using a higher percentage, and amounts below it use a smaller percentage instead of the full 3%.

questions.question: Karen refers a buyer; the $450,000 sale pays 4.5% commission with a $25% referral. The referral amount is:
questions.explanation: The total commission is 4.5 percent of $450,000, or $20,250, and 25 percent of that commission is $5,062.50. Taking the referral share from the sale price would overstate it, and the smaller amounts use too little of the commission.

questions.question: After selling for $920,000, the seller pays 4% commission, $13,000 in costs, and $150,000 to the lender. The net is:
questions.explanation: From $920,000 subtract the 4% commission of $36,800, the $13,000 in costs, and the $150,000 loan payoff, leaving $720,200. The other nets miss one of those deductions or add the price and deductions together.

questions.question: A home equity line's priority:

answers.text: Is by recording
Is illegal
Has no priority
Is senior always

questions.explanation: Home equity lines are liens whose priority is generally set by when they were recorded against the property, like other voluntary liens. Such a line is not automatically senior to earlier liens, it is legal, and its priority is not meaningless.

questions.question: A single homeowner sells a principal residence at a $200,000 gain after meeting the ownership and use tests. The taxable gain is:

answers.text: $0, up to the $250,000 exclusion

questions.explanation: A single filer who meets the ownership and use tests may exclude up to $250,000 of gain on a principal residence, so a $200,000 gain is fully excluded and the taxable gain is $0. Taxing part of the gain ignores that the entire gain falls within the exclusion.

questions.question: Which task can the RN delegate to a UAP for a client with stable chronic conditions?

answers.text: Collect a routine urine specimen from a client who can void independently, with instructions to report color and amount
Perform a sterile catheterization on a client with urinary retention
Assess a client's readiness to advance oral intake after a stroke
Administer a tube feeding after evaluating lung sounds

questions.explanation: Routine, nonsterile specimen collection from a stable client is within UAP scope when directions and reporting parameters are clear. Sterile procedures, swallowing assessment, and feeding decisions tied to assessment require licensed nursing judgment.

questions.question: Before accessing a central venous catheter port, which action is required?

answers.text: Scrub the access port with an antiseptic agent for the recommended time (such as 15 seconds) and allow it to dry before entry
Wipe the port once quickly with a dry gauze pad
Flush the port with saline before cleaning it, to push any surface organisms inward
Clean the port after connecting the syringe, so the antiseptic is not wasted

questions.explanation: Ports are disinfected with an active antiseptic scrub for the full recommended time and allowed to dry before every access, which is a core bloodstream-infection prevention practice. Dry wiping, flushing before cleaning, and cleaning after connection all leave the port contaminated at the moment of entry.

questions.question: Which factors place a bereaved person at higher risk for complicated grief and indicate closer follow-up? Select all that apply.

answers.text: The death was sudden and the person witnessed resuscitation attempts
The bereaved person reports strong support from friends and faith community
The bereaved person had a highly dependent relationship with the deceased and few other supports
The bereaved person has a history of depression
The bereaved person is gradually resuming work and social activities

questions.explanation: Sudden traumatic death, a highly dependent relationship with limited other supports, and prior depression increase the risk of complicated grief. Strong support networks and gradual re-engagement with life are protective factors, not risks.

questions.question: A nurse is instilling ear drops into an adult client's ear canal. Which technique is correct?

answers.text: Pull the pinna down and forward before instilling the drops
Instill the drops while they are still refrigerator-cold to numb the canal
Pull the pinna up and back, instill the drops along the canal wall, and have the client keep the ear tilted up for a few minutes
Insert the dropper deep into the canal to deposit the drops on the eardrum

questions.explanation: In adults, pulling the pinna up and back straightens the ear canal so drops flow in; drops are given along the canal wall at room temperature, without inserting the dropper deeply. Down-and-back is the technique for young children.

questions.question: A client was just diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B. Which household teaching is correct?

answers.text: Family members need no vaccination if they feel healthy
Household and sexual contacts should be offered hepatitis B vaccination, and the client must not share razors, toothbrushes, or glucose-monitoring equipment and should cover open cuts
Sharing razors is safe if they are rinsed with water
The client can never prepare food for the family again

questions.explanation: Hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids, so vaccinating contacts and blocking blood-sharing routes are the effective household measures. Casual contact and food preparation are not the transmission routes, so that restriction is unnecessary.

questions.question: Only one staff member is available for one-to-one observation this shift, and two clients have been assessed as needing it. What should guide how the nurse manager allocates the observer?

answers.text: Assign the observer to the client whose family has complained most often
Assign the observer to the client admitted first, out of fairness by arrival order
Alternate the observer between the two clients every 30 minutes regardless of their changing condition
Assign the observer to the client with the higher assessed safety risk, document the decision, reassess both clients frequently, and escalate the unmet need through leadership

questions.explanation: Scarce safety resources are allocated by assessed clinical need and risk, with documentation, frequent reassessment, and escalation of the gap. Family pressure, arrival order, and fixed rotation schedules all substitute non-clinical criteria for the risk assessment.

questions.question: A 3-year-old is found coughing and drooling after biting into a laundry detergent pod, with redness around the mouth. Which action should the nurse take first?

answers.text: Give the child a large glass of milk to dilute the detergent before any assessment
Induce vomiting so the chemical does not reach the stomach
Assess the child's airway and breathing, then contact Poison Control for directed management
Wait 2 hours to see whether the redness fades before calling anyone

questions.explanation: Detergent pods can injure the airway and cause respiratory depression, so airway and breathing assessment comes first, followed immediately by Poison Control guidance. Diluting or inducing vomiting before assessment can worsen aspiration or re-expose the esophagus, and waiting ignores a time-sensitive exposure.

questions.question: A client with chronic low back pain (no red-flag symptoms) asks for a self-care plan between visits. Which plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Remain in bed until the pain is completely gone
Stay active with regular walking, use heat as directed, pace activities with scheduled position changes, and keep a brief pain/activity diary to review at follow-up
Avoid all bending and lifting permanently
Use leftover opioid medication from a prior injury on bad days

questions.explanation: For chronic low back pain without red flags, staying active, heat, pacing, and self-monitoring outperform bed rest, which deconditions and prolongs pain. Permanent avoidance and borrowed opioids are both harmful.

questions.question: A client is in Buck's skin traction for a fractured femur while awaiting surgery. Which finding requires the nurse's intervention?

answers.text: The weights hang freely above the floor
The client reports mild discomfort at the fracture site
The weight bag is resting on the bed frame, and a knot in the rope is caught on the pulley
The foot boot is snug with the heel floated off the bed

questions.explanation: Traction works only when weights hang completely free and ropes move unobstructed through pulleys; a resting weight bag or a knot jammed on the pulley eliminates the countertraction force. Free-hanging weights, a floated heel, and mild fracture discomfort are expected.

questions.question: A client begins prednisone 40 mg daily for an inflammatory condition. Which monitoring and teaching points should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Monitor blood glucose, because this drug can raise glucose even in clients without diabetes.
Stop the medication suddenly as soon as you feel better to avoid side effects.
Expect your blood glucose to fall, so eat extra sugar at each meal.
Report fever or other signs of infection promptly, because the drug can blunt the usual warning signs.
Take the dose with food to reduce stomach irritation.

questions.explanation: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose, mask infection signs, and irritate the stomach, so glucose monitoring, prompt reporting of infection, and taking doses with food are correct. Stopping suddenly after sustained therapy is dangerous because of adrenal suppression, and glucose rises rather than falls.

questions.question: A client taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation has an INR of 4.8, no bleeding, and a hemoglobin unchanged from baseline. What is the expected action?

answers.text: Give the scheduled warfarin dose because there is no bleeding
Hold warfarin, assess for bleeding, and notify the provider for dose adjustment
Administer vitamin K IV push immediately
Encourage foods high in vitamin K at every meal

questions.explanation: An INR of 4.8 is supratherapeutic and raises bleeding risk even without current bleeding, so the dose is held and the provider notified. Vitamin K is reserved for bleeding or much higher risk situations as prescribed, and extra dietary vitamin K would destabilize control.

questions.question: A client with Addison disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) is taught a sick-day plan for influenza with fever and poor intake. Which statement shows correct understanding?

answers.text: 'I will stop my steroid replacement until my appetite returns.'
'Fever lowers my steroid needs, so I will halve the dose.'
'I will follow my prescribed stress-dose plan, keep taking steroids even if nauseated per my provider's instructions, and seek urgent care if I vomit doses or feel faint.'
'Extra salt and steroids are only needed if I exercise.'

questions.explanation: Illness increases cortisol requirements, and the prescribed stress-dose plan plus urgent care for vomiting or faintness prevents adrenal crisis; steroids must never be stopped abruptly. Halving or omitting replacement during illness is dangerous.

questions.question: During an admission interview a competent client says, 'My lawyer suggested I name my neighbor as my health-care agent, but can I name you instead? You understand my care.' What is the nurse's best response?

answers.text: Accept, because the client is competent and may choose anyone
Accept only if the client's family also agrees in writing
Decline kindly, explain the conflict in a treating clinician acting as agent, and offer to connect the client with social work and information about choosing an agent
Tell the client nurses are forbidden to discuss advance directives at all

questions.explanation: A nurse directly involved in care should not serve as the client's health-care agent because the roles conflict, but the nurse can and should support the process with information and a social-work referral. Competence alone does not remove the conflict, family agreement does not cure it, and discussing directives is part of nursing practice.

questions.question: An 82-year-old who has worn hearing aids for years reports that hearing in the left ear became muffled over two weeks. The left canal is completely blocked by hard, dark wax. What should the nurse recognize?

answers.text: A two-week change is too fast to matter, so reassessment in a year is appropriate
Muffled hearing at this age is always sensorineural and cannot be reversed
Impacted cerumen is a common, reversible cause of hearing loss in older adults and should be addressed before assuming the age-related hearing loss has progressed
The client should dig the wax out daily with a cotton swab pushed deep into the canal

questions.explanation: Cerumen impaction increases with age and produces a reversible conductive hearing loss that can appear over days to weeks; it must be excluded and treated before attributing a change to presbycusis. Cotton swabs pushed into the canal worsen impaction.

questions.question: A client with an ileostomy reports cramping abdominal pain, nausea, and swelling around the stoma. The pouch filled rapidly with watery output for several hours and has now produced nothing for 4 hours. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Assess for a possible food blockage, keep the client NPO, and notify the provider of the obstruction signs
Apply a larger pouch opening and massage the abdomen vigorously to move the blockage
Encourage the client to eat a high-fiber meal to push the blockage through
Monitor vital signs, intake and output, and abdominal distention while awaiting provider direction
Advise the client that absent ileostomy output for 4 hours is always normal and needs no assessment

questions.explanation: Cramping, nausea, stomal swelling, a burst of watery output followed by absent output suggests ileostomy food blockage or obstruction, warranting assessment, NPO status, provider notification, and monitoring. Vigorous massage, a high-fiber meal, and reassurance without assessment can worsen an obstruction.

questions.question: A client who took an overdose of metoprolol has a heart rate of 38/min and blood pressure of 82/50 mm Hg that has not responded to atropine. Which medication should the nurse anticipate administering?

answers.text: Naloxone IV
Flumazenil IV
Glucagon IV
Protamine sulfate IV

questions.explanation: Glucagon is the classic antidote for symptomatic beta-blocker overdose because it raises heart rate and contractility through a pathway that bypasses the blocked beta receptor, and it is used when atropine fails. Naloxone reverses opioids and protamine reverses heparin, neither of which is involved here. Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines and would not restore rate or pressure.

questions.question: A client has had periumbilical pain for 8 hours that has now settled in the right lower abdomen, with loss of appetite and temperature 38.1 C. Which findings support appendicitis? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Tenderness at McBurney point
Pain in the right lower abdomen when the left lower abdomen is palpated (Rovsing sign)
Rebound tenderness
Pain that is relieved completely by a large meal
Low-grade fever

questions.explanation: Appendicitis classically migrates to McBurney point with anorexia, low-grade fever, rebound tenderness, and a positive Rovsing sign. A large meal does not relieve appendiceal pain; eating typically worsens the discomfort.

questions.question: Case (item 6 of 6 in this set): Leo M., age 4 years, is brought to a pediatric clinic with 3 days of fever to 103.1 F (39.5 C), cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes, followed today by a blotchy red rash spreading from the hairline down the face and small white spots on the inside of his cheeks. He has received no childhood vaccines. Before being roomed, he spent 45 minutes in the shared waiting room with a 5-month-old infant, a pregnant parent, and a child who is receiving chemotherapy. Two weeks later, which outcome best shows the clinic's response was effective?

answers.text: Leo's rash faded within 5 days and his fever resolved
The waiting room was cleaned with a standard disinfectant the same evening

All susceptible contacts were identified and offered post-exposure prophylaxis within its window (measles vaccine within 72 hours for eligible contacts, or immune globulin within 6 days for those at high risk), and no secondary cases have occurred
Leo's parents agreed to consider vaccination at his next annual visit

questions.explanation: An effective exposure response is measured by complete contact identification, timely post-exposure prophylaxis inside the 72-hour vaccine and 6-day immune globulin windows, and absence of secondary cases. Leo's own recovery, routine cleaning, and a vague future vaccination discussion do not show the exposure was contained.

questions.question: Case (item 1 of 6 in this set): Renata V., age 31, is 12 days postpartum after an uncomplicated vaginal birth. Her partner brings her to the clinic saying she has slept only 1-2 hours a night for 4 nights even when the baby sleeps, paces while holding the infant, and has stopped eating. Today she tells the nurse the infant's crying 'means he knows I ruined him' and that she hears the baby monitor 'whispering my name' when it is switched off. Which findings require immediate follow-up? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Sleeping only 1-2 hours nightly for 4 nights despite having the opportunity to sleep
Tearfulness on postpartum day 3 that resolved within a day
Believing the infant's crying means she has ruined him
Asking her partner to take over one night feeding so she can rest
Hearing the switched-off baby monitor whispering her name

questions.explanation: Sleep loss that persists despite opportunity, a fixed false belief about the infant, and a hallucination are psychosis-risk cues, not normal adjustment. Brief day-3 tearfulness that resolves is typical of transient blues, and asking for help with a feeding is a healthy support-seeking behavior.

questions.question: Case study (items 1-6 of 6): Rosa D., age 69, is scheduled this morning for a left heart catheterization through the right femoral artery. Baseline findings: blood pressure 128/76 mm Hg, heart rate 78/min, pedal pulses palpable and marked bilaterally, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, INR 1.1, and she has been NPO since midnight. She reports a childhood rash with penicillin. The procedure is completed without complication, and she returns to the unit with the right leg kept straight and a clean, dry dressing over the puncture site. Item 2 of 6 (analyze cues): Three hours after the procedure Rosa reports new severe pain in her right lower back and flank. Blood pressure is 92/58 mm Hg, heart rate 122/min. The groin dressing is clean and dry with no swelling, and repeat hemoglobin has fallen from 12.4 to 10.1 g/dL. Which interpretation is most likely?

answers.text: A groin hematoma is forming under the dressing and simply has not been seen yet
Bleeding is occurring into the retroperitoneal space behind the puncture tract rather than externally at the groin
She is having an allergic reaction to the contrast dye
The back pain is only muscle strain from lying flat, unrelated to the procedure

questions.explanation: Flank and back pain with hypotension, tachycardia, and a falling hemoglobin while the puncture site itself stays clean and flat is the signature of retroperitoneal hemorrhage tracking upward from the femoral puncture. A visible hematoma would produce groin swelling, and contrast reactions present with skin, airway, or breathing findings rather than this bleeding pattern.

questions.question: Advertising must include

answers.text: salesperson's name only
the broker's licensed name
no name
a phone only

questions.explanation: All brokerage advertising must identify the brokerage by the broker's licensed name. Advertising in only a salesperson's name, with no name, or with only a phone number fails that requirement.

questions.question: A real estate glossary defines 'TILA' as

answers.text: the APR-disclosure statute
the Equal Credit Opportunity Act
the map-based lending discrimination
the gender-based protection

questions.explanation: TILA is the federal Truth in Lending Act, the statute that requires disclosure of the annual percentage rate and other credit terms. The Equal Credit Opportunity Act is a separate anti-discrimination law, the map-based practice is redlining, and gender-based protection is a fair lending concept rather than this disclosure statute.

questions.question: A rectangular parcel measures 100 feet by 50 feet. How many acres does it contain?

answers.text: 0.13 acres
0.61 acres
0.1 acres
0.11 acres

questions.explanation: One hundred feet multiplied by fifty feet gives five thousand square feet, and dividing by forty-three thousand five hundred sixty square feet per acre gives about zero point one one acres.

questions.question: A real estate glossary defines 'CFPB' as

answers.text: the measurement cost
the S&L-style lender
the mortgage-disclosure regulator
the bureau-report cost

questions.explanation: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is the federal regulator that oversees consumer financial products, including mortgage disclosure rules. The other choices describe measurement or lender costs, not this bureau.

questions.question: A binding arbitration clause requires

answers.text: a jury trial
resolution by an arbitrator instead of a court
mediation only
a new contract

questions.explanation: A binding arbitration clause substitutes decision by an arbitrator for a court trial, so the dispute is resolved in arbitration instead of litigation. It does not preserve a jury trial, it is stronger than mediation alone because the arbitrator decides, and it does not require making a new contract.

questions.question: The term 'termination of agency' is best defined as

answers.text: settlement business steered to an affiliated company
the end of the agency by expiration, completion, agreement, or operation of law
a disagreement over which broker earned the commission
an agency created by clear written or oral agreement

questions.explanation: Termination of agency is the end of the agency relationship, whether by expiration, completion of the purpose, mutual agreement, or operation of law. Steering business to an affiliate, a procuring-cause dispute, and express agency describe steering, a commission fight, and agency creation instead.

questions.question: A licensee forges a client's signature. This conduct is

answers.text: a minor issue
permitted with verbal ok
fraud and forgery
a shortcut

questions.explanation: Forging a client's signature is fraud and forgery, a serious dishonest act in a real estate transaction. It is not a minor issue or a shortcut, and a client's verbal approval cannot make a forged signature permissible.

questions.question: Co-ownership scenario: two friends own a condo in joint tenancy; one dies. The result is

answers.text: the decedent's share passes to the heirs, not the co-owner
the survivor takes the whole interest
the wife owns the whole property by survivorship
her share passes under her will or intestacy

questions.explanation: Joint tenancy carries the right of survivorship, so when one joint tenant dies the surviving co-owner takes the whole interest automatically. The share does not pass through the decedent estate to heirs or under a will.

questions.question: The buyer and seller make conflicting written demands for the deposit. The broker must

answers.text: pick the more deserving party
split it evenly
ignore both demands
notify the FREC within 15 business days and start a settlement procedure

questions.explanation: When buyer and seller make conflicting written demands on the same deposit, the broker must notify the Commission within fifteen business days and begin one of the required settlement procedures. The broker may not pick a winner, split the money evenly, or ignore the demands.

questions.question: How much simple interest accrues on $140,000 at 8% annual interest over 10 years?
questions.explanation: Simple interest is principal times rate times time: $140,000 multiplied by eight percent per year over ten years gives $112,000 of interest. The smaller figure covers only one year of interest, not the full ten-year period.

questions.question: A mixed-use building in Daytona Beach sold for $950,000 with a 3.5% brokerage commission. What is the total commission?
questions.explanation: Multiply the sale price of $950,000 by a three point five percent commission rate, which gives a total commission of $33,250. The $42,750 figure overstates that product, while the remaining figures use too small a rate.

questions.question: A comparable sold for $720,000 and contains 2,100 square feet. What is the sale price per square foot?
questions.explanation: Divide $720,000 by two thousand one hundred square feet to get $342.86 per square foot. The other figures are not the quotient of the stated price and area.

questions.question: Which fiduciary duty does this involve? An associate never visits the listed property and misstates its features.

answers.text: the duty of obedience
the duty of reasonable care
the duty of disclosure
the duty of loyalty

questions.explanation: Never visiting the property and then misstating its features shows a failure of reasonable care, the duty to use proper skill and diligence in handling a transaction. Obedience, disclosure, and loyalty concern following instructions, sharing facts, and allegiance, not careless workmanship.

questions.question: Apply ownership-forms doctrine: A subdivision's recorded use restrictions.

answers.text: zoning ordinances
tax liens
restrictive covenants enforced by the HOA
building codes

questions.explanation: Use restrictions recorded by a subdivision are restrictive covenants, private limits that run with the land and are commonly enforced by the homeowners association. Zoning ordinances and building codes are government regulations rather than recorded private restrictions, and a tax lien is a financial claim.

questions.question: A buyer offers $750,000 with a 2% earnest money deposit. The deposit is
questions.explanation: Two percent of the $750,000 price is $15,000, which is the earnest money deposit. The other amounts apply three percent, one percent, or four percent instead of the stated two percent.

questions.question: Annual property taxes are $7,300. Using a 365-day year and the Florida custom that the seller owns through the day before closing, what is the seller's prorated share if closing is on day 351 of the year?
questions.explanation: The daily tax is $7,300 divided by 365, or $20, and the seller owns the property through day 350, the day before the day 351 closing, for 350 days times $20, which equals $7,000. Charging the seller through the closing day itself, or for only a short remainder period, gives the other amounts.

questions.question: How much simple interest accrues on $170,000 at 12% annual interest over 4 years?
questions.explanation: Simple interest is principal times rate times time: $170,000 times twelve percent times four years equals $81,600. The $20,400 figure is only one year of interest, the $6,800 figure shrinks the annual interest, and the $95,200 figure overstates four years at the stated rate.

questions.question: A $700,000 sale carried a 4% total commission, split 60/40 between listing and selling brokerages. The selling associate keeps 60% of the selling brokerage's share. What does the selling associate earn?
questions.explanation: Total commission is $700,000 multiplied by 4 percent, or $28,000; the selling brokerage receives 40 percent of that, or $11,200, and the selling associate keeps 60 percent of the brokerage's share, or $6,720. The $28,000 figure is the full commission, and the $11,200 figure is the selling brokerage's share before the associate's split.

questions.question: An office tenant leases 4,000 square feet at $16 per square foot per year. What is the monthly rent?
questions.explanation: Annual rent is 4,000 square feet multiplied by $16, which equals $64,000, and dividing that yearly total by twelve gives about $5,333 per month. The $64,000 figure is the annual rent rather than the monthly rent, and the other monthly amounts do not match the division.

questions.question: A comparable sold for $610,000 and contains 3,700 square feet. What is the sale price per square foot?
questions.explanation: Dividing the $610,000 sale price by 3,700 square feet gives $164.86 per square foot. The other amounts come from rounding the size, using a different price, or reversing the division.

questions.question: At the start of a busy shift, how should the LPN best organize her work?

answers.text: Complete all supply stocking and paperwork before seeing any clients
See clients strictly in room-number order regardless of condition
Make brief first rounds on the highest-risk clients to collect data and catch changes, then schedule routine tasks around time-critical care
Spend the first hour with the one client who asks the most questions

questions.explanation: Priority setting starts with the clients most likely to have changed, so problems surface early. Stocking first, rigid room order, and letting demand alone set the sequence all ignore clinical risk.

questions.question: A parent asks why aspirin must not be given to a child with a viral illness. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?

answers.text: Aspirin simply does not lower fever in children
Children cannot swallow aspirin tablets
Aspirin causes tooth staining in children
Aspirin in children with viral illness is linked to Reye syndrome, a serious liver and brain condition

questions.explanation: Aspirin use during viral illness in children is associated with Reye syndrome, so acetaminophen or ibuprofen per directions is used instead. Tooth staining relates to tetracyclines, and swallowing ability is not the reason.

questions.question: The LPN/VN is pushing a client in a bariatric wheelchair down a corridor. Which action best prevents a strain injury?

answers.text: Pull the chair backward the whole distance to watch the client
Twist to look behind while continuing to push at full speed
Lock one wheel slightly to keep the chair from rolling too fast
Push the chair using leg muscles with the elbows close to the body and ask for help on the ramp

questions.explanation: Pushing with the legs, elbows close, and help on ramps uses large muscle groups and controls the load. Pulling backward, twisting while moving, and dragging a locked wheel all increase strain and injury risk.

questions.question: A home-health client uses a nebulizer machine for breathing treatments. Which cleaning teaching should the LPN reinforce?

answers.text: Wash the nebulizer cup and mouthpiece after use as directed, let parts air-dry, and disinfect them on the schedule in the manufacturer's instructions to prevent infection
Rinse the mouthpiece once a month with plain water only
Share the mouthpiece with a family member who has the same machine
Store the wet parts in a sealed plastic bag between treatments

questions.explanation: Nebulizer parts trap moisture and medication residue, so routine washing, air-drying, and scheduled disinfection prevent bacterial growth and respiratory infection. Sharing parts or storing them wet in a sealed bag promotes contamination.

questions.question: A coworker is performing CPR on an unresponsive adult client when the AED arrives. What should the LPN/VN do with the AED?

answers.text: Wait until the client has received 30 minutes of CPR before attaching the AED
Turn it on, place the pads on the client's bare chest as pictured, and make sure no one is touching the client during analysis and any shock
Place the pads over the client's gown so the chest stays covered
Hold the client's shoulders steady while the AED delivers a shock

questions.explanation: Early defibrillation improves survival, so the AED is applied to bare skin as pictured and everyone clears the client during analysis and shock. Delaying the AED, padding over clothing, or touching the client during a shock are each unsafe.

questions.question: A toddler is visiting a grandparent on a medical unit and is reaching for a cup of hot coffee on the overbed table. What should the LPN/VN do?

answers.text: Let the grandparent decide because the child is the family's responsibility only
Cool the coffee by adding ice and hand it to the child
Place the coffee on the floor beside the bed
Move the hot liquid out of the child's reach and remind the family to keep hot drinks away from young children

questions.explanation: Moving hot liquids out of a young child's reach prevents a scald injury, and brief family guidance reinforces the fix. Hot drinks remain a burn risk even with ice added, and the floor is still within a toddler's reach.

questions.question: The LPN/VN prepares to transfer a client using a gait belt as taught in the established plan. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Place the belt snugly over clothing at the client's waist and check that two fingers fit under it
Place the belt loosely over bare skin so it can slide as the client moves
Stand on the client's weaker side and grasp the belt to support the transfer
Report new weakness or dizziness during the transfer to the RN
Pull the client up to standing by the arms so the belt is only a backup

questions.explanation: A gait belt goes snugly over clothing at the waist, the nurse stands on the weaker side and grasps the belt, and new weakness or dizziness is reported. A loose belt on bare skin slips and abrades, and pulling by the arms can injure shoulders.

questions.question: In a rehabilitation unit, a client with a known peanut allergy bites into a cookie and within minutes has lip swelling, wheezing, and hives. What should the LPN/VN do first?

answers.text: Call for help and the RN immediately, monitor airway and breathing, and follow the emergency protocol for anaphylaxis
Offer an oral antihistamine drink and observe for an hour
Ask the client to lie down alone and rest until symptoms pass
Document the reaction and report it at the end of the shift

questions.explanation: Lip swelling with wheezing after allergen exposure is anaphylaxis, a life-threatening airway emergency requiring immediate help and protocol actions. Oral medication in a compromised airway, leaving the client alone, or delayed reporting are unsafe.

questions.question: During a clinic visit, a client asks the LPN/VN, 'You are a nurse — should I divorce my husband?' Which response is most appropriate?

answers.text: Tell her divorce is probably best since she is asking about it
Explore her feelings instead of giving advice: 'You are weighing a hard decision. Tell me what has been happening that brought this up today,' and report significant concerns to the RN
Change the subject to her blood pressure results
Tell her staff are not allowed to talk about anything except medications

questions.explanation: Reflecting the decision back and inviting her to explore what prompted it is therapeutic; personal advice about divorce is not the nurse's role. Deflecting to vital signs or refusing all conversation shuts her down.

questions.question: During a bed bath, the LPN/VN notices a reddened, warm area with drainage under a client's abdominal fold. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: Apply talcum powder liberally and cover the area without reporting
Scrub the area vigorously with a rough washcloth to remove drainage
Clean and dry the area gently, keep skin folds separated and dry, document findings, and report to the RN
Ignore it because skin folds are normally red and moist

questions.explanation: Gentle cleansing, thorough drying, fold separation, documentation, and reporting address possible skin-fold infection or breakdown. Heavy powder cakes and traps moisture, vigorous scrubbing injures skin, and ignoring drainage delays treatment.

questions.question: A client who speaks limited English keeps nodding during medication teaching but cannot repeat back what the LPN reinforced. What is the LPN's best advocacy action?

answers.text: Ask the client's teenage grandchild to interpret
Speak more slowly and loudly in English
Request a qualified medical interpreter through the RN and pause teaching until one is available
Have the client sign the teaching form since he nodded

questions.explanation: Advocacy means securing a qualified interpreter so the client can actually understand and decide; nodding is not comprehension. Family members, especially minors, should not interpret medical information, volume does not fix a language barrier, and a signature without understanding is not informed participation.

questions.question: After delegating morning care for a stable resident, the LPN finds the UAP charting care that has not yet been done. What is the LPN's best action?

answers.text: Ignore it because the care will eventually be done
Ask the UAP to finish the care quickly so the chart becomes true
Erase the entries quietly and say nothing
Stop the practice, correct the record per policy, and report the falsification to the RN supervisor

questions.explanation: Charting undone care is falsification; the LPN must intervene, ensure the record is corrected by policy, and report it through supervision. Quiet fixes and ignoring the behavior hide a legal and safety violation and leave the LPN accountable for delegated care.

questions.question: A 58-year-old client who smoked a pack a day for 30 years (30 pack-years) asks about lung cancer screening. Which information should the LPN/VN reinforce and report so the RN/provider can arrange it?

answers.text: No screening exists for lung cancer
Yearly low-dose CT screening is recommended for adults about 50 to 80 with at least a 20 pack-year history who still smoke or quit within the past 15 years
A chest X-ray every month is the recommended screening
Screening stops being useful the day a person quits smoking

questions.explanation: Annual low-dose CT is the recommended lung cancer screening for adults roughly 50 to 80 with 20 or more pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years; this client's 30 pack-years qualify for referral. Chest X-ray is not the recommended screening test.

questions.question: A client has a Jackson-Pratt drain after abdominal surgery, with output of about 30 mL per shift of pink fluid. This hour the reservoir filled rapidly with 300 mL of bright red blood and the client feels faint. What should the LPN/VN do?

answers.text: Empty the drain and document the total at shift end
Report the sudden large bloody output and faintness to the RN immediately and collect vital signs
Compress the reservoir fully and hide it under the gown
Tell the client a sudden increase is expected on this day

questions.explanation: A sudden surge of bright red drain output with faintness suggests active bleeding and is reported immediately with vital signs. Simply emptying and waiting until shift end delays hemorrhage recognition.

questions.question: A client is due for an influenza vaccine at a clinic visit and tells the LPN/VN, who will administer vaccines per protocol, that the vaccine gave a friend the flu last year. Which response is correct reinforcement?

answers.text: Your friend is right; the injectable vaccine commonly causes influenza
You should skip vaccination this year because of your friend's experience
Only health care workers benefit from yearly influenza vaccination
The injectable vaccine cannot cause influenza; mild soreness or low fever afterward is the immune system responding

questions.explanation: Inactivated injectable influenza vaccine cannot cause influenza; brief soreness or low-grade fever reflects immune response, while the vaccine is recommended broadly each season. A friend's anecdote and restricting benefit to health workers are misconceptions the reinforcement corrects.

questions.question: The LPN measures a temperature of 95.8 F in Mr. Lars Johansson, 81, found in his unheated apartment during a winter home visit, and notes slow responses and shivering that has stopped. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: Cover him with warm blankets, avoid vigorous rubbing, and report promptly for further evaluation
Encourage a hot shower to warm him quickly
Give him a hot alcoholic drink to restore circulation
Document hypothermia as expected in winter and leave

questions.explanation: A temperature of 95.8 F with slowed responses in an older adult is hypothermia needing gentle warming with blankets and prompt reporting; stopped shivering can signal worsening. A hot shower risks burns and collapse, alcohol worsens heat loss, and leaving an impaired client alone is unsafe.

questions.question: A long-term care resident with advanced dementia cannot rate pain. During morning care the resident grimaces, guards one hip, and resists being turned. What should the licensed practical nurse do?

answers.text: Document that the resident has no pain because no number was reported
Ask unlicensed assistive personnel to decide whether pain medication is needed
Reinforce to the family that residents with dementia do not feel pain
Collect these behavioral findings and report them to the registered nurse as possible pain cues so the established pain plan can be followed

questions.explanation: In nonverbal clients, grimacing, guarding, and resisting movement are recognized behavioral pain cues to collect and report. Absence of a number rating does not mean absence of pain, and pain decisions are not delegated.

questions.question: Case study: Mrs. Ruth E., age 81, has lived in a long-term care facility for 3 years. Her husband of 56 years, also a resident, died 5 days ago. She attended his service yesterday. Since then she eats about half of her meals, looks at photographs, cries at times, and asks staff to sit with her in the evening. Her son visits daily. Mrs. E. quietly says, 'I wish I had died instead of him.' Which action by the LPN/VN is most appropriate?

answers.text: Stay with her, listen, ask directly and calmly whether she is thinking of harming herself, and notify the RN promptly
Reassure her that she will feel better soon and change the subject to the lunch menu
Promise to keep the statement secret so she will keep confiding in staff
Leave the room at once to finish care for the other residents on the hall

questions.explanation: Staying, listening, asking directly about self-harm, and notifying the RN promptly is the safe PN response to a wish-to-die statement. False reassurance, promises of secrecy, and leaving her alone all delay the RN assessment her statement requires.

questions.question: A postoperative client rates pain 9 of 10. The ordered oral analgesic given 1 hour ago has had no effect, and the client is crying and guarding his incision. What is the LPN's priority action?

answers.text: Reassure him the medication just needs more time and recheck at shift end
Give an extra dose from another client's supply
Report the uncontrolled pain and your assessment data to the RN promptly
Document 'pain controlled' because a dose was given

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled severe pain after an adequate trial of the ordered drug must be escalated to the RN, who can obtain new orders; documentation must reflect the client's actual report. Waiting hours, borrowing medication, and charting the opposite of the finding are unsafe and dishonest.

questions.question: Case study: Mrs. Lorraine Beck, 68 years old, has type 2 diabetes managed with oral agents and a long-acting insulin at bedtime. She receives home-health visits. For two days she has had influenza with fever, poor appetite, and nausea. The RN has taught a sick-day plan: check glucose more often, check urine ketones when glucose is high or she is ill, keep taking diabetes medications, sip sugar-free fluids, and contact the team the same day for high readings with ketones, vomiting, or rapid breathing. Today the LPN/VN collects: temperature 100.8 F, pulse 104/min, respirations 24/min; glucose readings of 342 mg/dL and 388 mg/dL; urine ketones moderate; she has vomited once and has taken in only about 500 mL of fluid since yesterday. Which finding is the most concerning cue to report first?

answers.text: Moderate urine ketones together with a glucose of 388 mg/dL and vomiting
A temperature of 100.8 F during influenza
Intake of only about 500 mL of fluid since yesterday, which the LPN/VN can simply recheck next week
A pulse of 104/min while she has a fever

questions.explanation: Ketones with marked hyperglycemia and vomiting are the sick-day plan's same-day escalation cues: they signal that fat is being broken down for fuel and a hyperglycemic emergency may be developing. Fever and a mildly elevated pulse fit influenza, and low intake matters, but the ketone-glucose-vomiting combination is the cue that drives the report.

questions.question: Where do supplementary payments sit in relation to the limits of insurance under a commercial general liability policy?

answers.text: They are paid out of the limits and reduce them dollar for dollar
They are paid only after the insured pays an equal amount
They are paid in addition to the applicable limits and do not reduce those limits
They replace the limits whenever defense costs are large

questions.explanation: Supplementary payments are expressly in addition to the limits of insurance, so paying them leaves the limits intact for damages. Dollar-for-dollar erosion describes defense-within-limits forms, not the CGL supplementary payments structure.

questions.question: How does a conditional receipt differ from a binder, at the concept level?

answers.text: A binder is a temporary contract of insurance itself, while a conditional receipt primarily evidences premium payment and states conditions for any pre-issuance coverage

A conditional receipt is a temporary contract and a binder is only a payment receipt in every case: the receipt itself provides temporary insurance, and the binder merely records that a premium was paid
Both are identical in legal effect in every case
A binder requires no authority while a receipt requires underwriting approval first

questions.explanation: A binder actually provides interim coverage as a temporary contract, whereas a conditional receipt's protection depends on satisfying its stated conditions. Reversing the two documents is the strongest distractor.

questions.question: How does indemnity differ from subrogation as a loss-recovery mechanism?

answers.text: Indemnity shifts a loss between responsible parties by agreement or operation of law, while subrogation lets a party that paid, such as an insurer, step into the payee's rights against the wrongdoer

Indemnity lets an insurer step into the insured's rights, while subrogation shifts a loss by contract, under the coverage part, endorsements, and stated limits applicable to this claim, and as the form itself provides
They differ only in the spelling used by different insurers
Subrogation applies only between parents and children

questions.explanation: Indemnity is a direct right to have another party bear the loss, arising from contract or common law. Subrogation is substitution: the payer takes over the paid party's claim against the party responsible for the loss.

questions.question: From what event is the typical legal action time limit measured under standard property forms?

answers.text: The inception of the loss, meaning the date the loss occurred
The date the insured hires an attorney
The date the insurer assigns an adjuster
The date the policy was delivered

questions.explanation: The suit clock runs from the inception of the loss — when the loss happened — not from hiring counsel, claim assignment, or policy delivery.

questions.question: How is a valuable papers loss typically measured when a destroyed record must be recreated?

answers.text: By the sentimental value the owner attaches to the record
By the total revenue the business earned in the record's best year
By the highest price a collector might pay at auction
By the cost of the blank material plus the labor needed to transcribe or copy the information onto it

questions.explanation: Settlement follows reproduction cost: blank stock plus the labor of putting the information back on it. Sentimental or collector value is not the form's measure of loss.

questions.question: Instead of one lump sum, an injured claimant will receive monthly payments over twenty years to cover ongoing needs. This arrangement is a

answers.text: Structured settlement
High-low agreement
Partial release
Bulk reserve

questions.explanation: A structured settlement pays over time in a scheduled stream rather than a single lump sum. A high-low agreement instead sets minimum and maximum outcomes around a verdict.

questions.question: Before any limit is reached, an insurer's starting contribution under equal shares is best described as what?

answers.text: The full loss, later reimbursed by the other insurers
An equal portion of the loss shared with the other insurers on the risk
A percentage set by the state for all insurers
The amount of its policy deductible

questions.explanation: The starting point is an even division of the loss among the participating insurers. It is not a pay-everything-first arrangement, which describes a primary layer instead.

questions.question: An applicant's home has been condemned and has extensive unrepaired damage. How does FAIR Plan eligibility treat the property?

answers.text: Property that is condemned, in disrepair, or has existing damage is ineligible
The property is eligible at a reduced dwelling limit
The property is eligible if the owner signs a repair waiver
The property is eligible only for liability coverage

questions.explanation: Condemned, dilapidated, or already-damaged property fails FAIR Plan eligibility. A waiver does not make a damaged property insurable.

questions.question: A robber forces a clerk to open the register and takes $900 in currency during business hours. How is this loss classified under the store's BOP?

answers.text: It is an inside-the-premises money and securities loss, subject to that coverage's limit
It is an outside-the-premises money loss because the clerk was standing up
It is a business income loss because sales stopped during the robbery
It is a building loss because the register is attached to the counter

questions.explanation: Money taken by robbery inside the premises falls under the inside-the-premises side of the BOP money and securities provisions, subject to its limit. The register's location does not make cash a building item, which is why the building option is wrong.

questions.question: An insurer that carelessly pays a loss entirely to the property owner, ignoring a mortgagee named in the mortgage clause, risks

answers.text: nothing, because the mortgage clause is only a courtesy listing
having to answer to the mortgagee for its interest despite having already paid the owner
a bonus from the mortgagee for settling the claim so quickly
automatic ownership of the property passing to the insurer

questions.explanation: The clause gives the named mortgagee enforceable payment rights, so paying the owner alone does not discharge the insurer's obligation to the mortgagee. A courtesy listing would create no such exposure, which is why the listing is substantive.

questions.question: An insured person dies from injuries sustained in a covered accident two weeks later in the hospital. The family submits funeral expenses under Part B. What causal link must those expenses have?

answers.text: They are payable for any death during the policy period
They are payable only if death was instant at the scene
They must result from the bodily injury caused by the covered accident
They require proof that another driver was at fault

questions.explanation: Funeral services fall under Part B when they are necessary because of the accident-caused bodily injury, and a death occurring later from those injuries preserves that link. Fault proof is not part of the Part B promise.

questions.question: A sales firm wants physical damage coverage only on the cars its representatives drive, not on its delivery trucks. Which covered auto symbol fits that intent?

answers.text: Symbol 3, owned private passenger autos only
Symbol 4, owned autos other than private passenger autos
Symbol 8, hired autos only
Symbol 9, nonowned autos only

questions.explanation: Explanation: Symbol 3 designates owned private passenger autos only, which matches the cars and excludes the trucks. Symbol 4 does the opposite, covering owned autos other than private passenger types.

questions.question: A joint venture policy names the venture and each venturer. A worker employed by Venturer One sues Venturer Two, claiming Venturer Two controlled the unsafe scaffold. Venturer Two's counsel invokes separation of insureds. For what purpose?

answers.text: To raise the general aggregate to cover both venturers twice, as set out in the policy form, declarations, and applicable endorsement schedule, and as stated in the applicable policy form
To cancel Venturer One's coverage retroactively
So Venturer Two's coverage for the claim against it is applied separately, as the insured sued, instead of being denied merely because the plaintiff works for a co-insured
To force the worker into the venture's health plan

questions.explanation: The separate-application rule is invoked so the defendant venturer's coverage is assessed on its own terms despite the plaintiff's employment by a co-insured. It neither doubles aggregates nor cancels anyone's coverage.

questions.question: A person who intentionally, knowingly, recklessly, or negligently operates a premium finance company without a license, violates the chapter, omits a required material fact, or refuses a permitted examination commits an offense classified as a:

answers.text: Class C misdemeanor
Class B misdemeanor
State jail felony
Class A misdemeanor

questions.explanation: Premium finance offenses are Class B misdemeanors.

questions.question: An insured obtains other insurance on the same covered auto under a policy providing coverage on the same basis, and the other policy takes effect. Under the automatic termination provision, what happens to this policy as to that auto?

answers.text: Nothing, because replacement insurance never affects an existing policy
It ceases to be in effect for that auto on the date the other insurance takes effect
It converts to excess insurance for that auto for one full year
It remains fully in effect for that auto indefinitely alongside the new policy

questions.explanation: The automatic termination provision ends this policy's coverage for an auto when other insurance on the same basis for that auto takes effect. The two policies do not simply run side by side indefinitely for that auto.

questions.question: A partnership group acquires control of a licensed agency. The department asks for the control-filing information as to each partner and each person who controls a partner. May it require that?

answers.text: Yes; the department may require the information for each partner of the partnership, each member of the syndicate or group, and each person who controls the partner or member
Yes, but only after the acquisition closes
No; group acquirers file as a single unnamed person
Only the managing partner's information may be required

questions.explanation: The look-through authority for partnerships, syndicates, and groups is express. Requiring information person by person is within it.

questions.question: An agency hands walk-in customers a glossy leaflet describing its commercial property program. For Texas advertising-rule purposes, the leaflet is best classified as:

answers.text: An advertisement, because descriptive literature and sales aids issued for presentation to the public are included
Not an advertisement, because it was handed out rather than mailed
Not an advertisement, because it does not quote a specific premium
An advertisement only if the department pre-approved the leaflet

questions.explanation: Circulars, leaflets, booklets, depictions, illustrations, and form letters issued for presentation to the public are advertisements; the method of delivery and the absence of a quote do not remove them from the definition.

questions.question: A covered fire destroys half of an older home, and the local ordinance requires the undamaged half to be demolished because the damage exceeds a threshold in the code. The owner expects the basic property coverage to pay the full demolition and rebuilding cost of the undamaged half. Which principle limits that expectation?

answers.text: Undamaged portions are always rebuilt free under the fire peril.
The fire peril automatically includes unlimited code upgrade protection.
