The ordinance or law exclusion means costs imposed by code enforcement, including required demolition of undamaged portions, are payable only within the form's additional ordinance or law coverage, not as ordinary fire damage.

Governmental action pays for any demolition a city requires, with no limit, based on the facts presented and recorded when the claim was submitted for review, and as shown by the documentation maintained with the policy and claim records.

questions.explanation: The undamaged half was not damaged by fire, so its demolition cost arises from the ordinance, and that category is excluded except for the stated additional coverage. Governmental action does not create a payment for code-required demolition after a covered loss.

questions.question: An employee sues an employer solely for discriminatory termination and seeks lost wages and emotional distress damages, alleging no bodily injury caused by an accident. Why is the employer's commercial general liability policy generally the wrong place to look?

answers.text: General liability policies never exist for employers with more than ten employees, because an employer with eleven or more employees must buy its general liability protection under a commercial farm program
The employee seeks money damages, and general liability never pays money
The claim alleges an intentional employment practice rather than bodily injury or property damage from an occurrence, so it belongs under employment practices liability
The termination happened indoors rather than outdoors

questions.explanation: Discrimination claims are employment practices claims; general liability is triggered by bodily injury or property damage from an occurrence, or a listed personal and advertising injury. Seeking money damages is common to all liability claims and is not the reason for the mismatch.

questions.question: A Texas homeowner wants to voluntarily cover a domestic worker who is exempt from the workers' compensation subtitle. May the employer elect coverage, and what does electing it do?

answers.text: No, exempt employees can never be covered voluntarily
Yes, and the election is permanent even after the coverage ends

Yes, the employer may elect coverage for an exempt domestic or casual worker or a farm or ranch employee, and obtaining it is acceptance of the rights and responsibilities of the subtitle for as long as the coverage remains in effect
Yes, but the employer accepts none of the subtitle's responsibilities by electing it

questions.explanation: An employer may elect coverage for the listed exempt classes, and obtaining coverage accepts the subtitle's rights and responsibilities while the coverage remains in effect. The acceptance is real but tied to the coverage period.

new-york-real-estate.quiz_title: New York Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Broker qualifying experience is documented by

answers.text: The broker application must include the sponsoring broker's certification of the applicant's experience, which the Department may verify
The applicant's promise
A client's letter
Nothing at all

questions.explanation: Broker qualifying experience is documented by the sponsoring broker's certification of the applicant's experience on the application, which the Department may verify. The applicant's own promise alone is not the required documentation, a client's letter does not certify qualifying experience, and claiming nothing at all is needed ignores the certification requirement.

questions.question: The Property Condition Disclosure Statement is based on.

answers.text: a mandatory professional inspection
the seller's actual knowledge of the property's condition
the listing agent's opinion
the buyer's inspection

questions.explanation: The Property Condition Disclosure Statement rests on the seller's actual knowledge of the property's condition, which is why it is not a warranty. It does not require a mandatory professional inspection, it is not the listing agent's opinion, and it is not based on the buyer's inspection, since the seller completes and signs the statement.

questions.question: Which statement about brownfield completion is TRUE?

answers.text: No relief follows cleanup
Completing a brownfield cleanup under the state program earns the participant a certificate of completion that provides liability limitations and tax credits
Credits are federal only
Volunteers stay fully liable

questions.explanation: Completing a brownfield cleanup under the state program earns the participant a certificate of completion that provides liability limitations and tax credits, rewarding remediation of a contaminated site. Saying no relief follows cleanup denies the certificate's benefits, saying credits are federal only misplaces a state program's incentives, and saying volunteers stay fully liable contradicts the liability limitations the certificate provides.

questions.question: Amending a condo declaration often requires

answers.text: no vote
a court order
only board approval
a super-majority vote

questions.explanation: Amending a condominium declaration often requires a super-majority vote of the unit owners because the declaration is the project's governing document. It cannot be done with no vote at all, a court order is not the routine requirement, and board approval alone is generally insufficient for so fundamental a change.

questions.question: True or false: Surface and mineral owners can differ.

answers.text: False
Cannot be determined
True
True only in part

questions.explanation: The statement is true because surface rights and mineral rights are severable estates, so one owner can hold the surface while another holds the minerals beneath it. Calling it false denies that severance, the ownership split is a settled property concept so it is determinable, and it is fully true rather than only partly true.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines "grievance committee"?

answers.text: a court order prohibiting specified acts pending further proceedings
the broker responsible for a brokerage office and its associated licensees
the association body that reviews ethics complaints
the segregated bank account for escrow funds required by the escrow regulations

questions.explanation: The grievance committee is the association body that reviews ethics complaints against members before any hearing. The court order prohibiting specified acts pending further proceedings is an injunction rather than a committee, the broker responsible for a brokerage office and its associated licensees is the broker of record rather than a grievance body, and the segregated bank account for escrow funds is an escrow account rather than a committee.

questions.question: True or false: A gift deed recites love and affection rather than monetary consideration.

answers.text: True
Cannot be determined
False
True only in part

questions.explanation: It is true that a gift deed recites love and affection rather than monetary consideration. Saying it cannot be determined avoids a standard deed feature, saying it is false denies the customary recital in a gift deed, and saying it is true only in part understates a correct statement.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines "underwriting"?

answers.text: the total obligations ratio
the evaluation of the risk of a loan application
a loan exceeding the conforming loan limit
the limit on how much disclosed costs may increase at closing

questions.explanation: Underwriting is the evaluation of the risk of a loan application, weighing the borrower's credit and capacity and the property's value before the lender commits. A total obligations ratio is one underwriting measure, a loan above the conforming limit is a jumbo loan, and limits on cost increases at closing are a disclosure tolerance rule.

questions.question: True or false: Familial status covers households with minors.

answers.text: Cannot be determined
False
True
True only in part

questions.explanation: The statement is true: familial status protects households with children under eighteen, including families with minors. It is not indeterminate, because the federal definition is settled; it is not false, since households with minors are the core of the class; and it is not only partly true, because the protection applies fully to such households.

questions.question: Concerning assessment challenge evidence, which statement is true?

answers.text: Comparable sales and income data support assessment challenges.
An assessor's valuation can never be challenged.
The assessor personally collects the property taxes.
The redemption period is the same in every jurisdiction.

questions.explanation: Comparable sales and income data support an assessment challenge by showing the property is overvalued relative to similar properties or its earnings. An assessor's valuation can be challenged through grievance procedures, the assessor values property rather than personally collecting taxes, and redemption periods vary by jurisdiction rather than being the same everywhere.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines "buyer agency agreement"?

answers.text: an agency imposed by law when a principal's conduct causes a third party to reasonably believe an agency exists
a buyer's deposit delivered with an offer to evidence good-faith intent to purchase
a contract establishing the broker as the agent of the buyer
a false statement of material fact made carelessly and without reasonable care for its truth

questions.explanation: A buyer agency agreement is a contract establishing the broker as the agent of the buyer. Agency by estoppel from a principal's conduct, an earnest money deposit, and negligent misrepresentation are different agency and contract concepts.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the rule of a waterfall distribution?

answers.text: the sponsor returns excess promote if the deal underperforms
it tests how returns change with rent, vacancy, and exit assumptions
first-year NOI divided by purchase price
it splits cash flow by tiers: return of capital, preferred return, then promote

questions.explanation: A waterfall distribution splits cash flow in tiers, paying return of capital first, then a preferred return, and then the sponsor's promote share. A sponsor giving back excess promote describes a clawback, testing returns under changed rent and vacancy assumptions describes sensitivity analysis, and first-year net operating income divided by price describes a capitalization rate, not a waterfall.

questions.question: Which term is described as follows: the individual licensee a broker designates to represent one party when the broker acts as a dual agent

answers.text: disclosed principal
tie-in agreement
general agent
designated sales agent

questions.explanation: A designated sales agent is the individual licensee a broker designates to represent one party when the brokerage is acting as a dual agent with informed consent. A general agent has broad authority for a principal, and the other choices are unrelated agency and antitrust terms.

questions.question: A lease runs 3 years at $10,900 per month. The leasing commission is 5% of the total rent over the full lease term. What is the commission?
questions.explanation: Total rent over the lease is $10,900 per month for thirty-six months, which is $392,400, and five percent of that total is $19,620. The other commissions are five percent of a larger or smaller rent total than the full three-year term produces.

questions.question: A commercial lot with 35 feet of frontage sells for $141,750. What is the price per front foot?

answers.text: $3,645.00 per front foot
$4,455.00 per front foot
$3,240.00 per front foot
$4,050.00 per front foot

questions.explanation: Dividing $141,750 by thirty-five feet of frontage gives $4,050.00 per front foot. The other per-front-foot figures do not result from that division.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the practical note of a discounted payoff (DPO)?

answers.text: it is not forgiveness; arrears still accrue
it requires the plan to be fair and equitable
it is common when the borrower finds new capital
it gives the lender control of cash flow

questions.explanation: A discounted payoff commonly becomes practical when the borrower brings in new capital, such as a new investor's money, that lets the lender accept a reduced amount and close out the loan. Describing it as mere non-forgiveness with arrears still accruing misses that an accepted payoff settles the debt, the fair-and-equitable standard belongs to bankruptcy plan confirmation, and lender control of cash flow describes a lockbox or cash-collateral arrangement rather than a payoff.

questions.question: Federal law adds its own shield for the military class: the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act gives deployed servicemembers rights such as

answers.text: free housing
exemption from all contracts
permanent rent control
terminating a residential lease after deployment orders and stays of eviction and foreclosure proceedings during service

questions.explanation: The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act gives deployed servicemembers rights such as terminating a residential lease after deployment orders and stays of eviction and foreclosure proceedings during service, so military duty does not cost them their housing protections. It does not provide free housing because the law shields existing rights rather than supplying homes, it does not exempt servicemembers from all contracts because its relief is targeted and conditional, and it does not impose permanent rent control because its protections are tied to the period of service.

questions.question: A broker may assign ministerial, administrative tasks to an unlicensed assistant, but the unlicensed assistant may NOT

answers.text: answer phones and schedule appointments
prepare advertising copy for the broker's approval
file documents and maintain the office calendar
show properties to buyers, discuss price or terms, or perform any other act that requires a real estate license

questions.explanation: An unlicensed assistant may not show properties to buyers, discuss price or terms, or perform any other act that requires a real estate license. Taking phone calls and scheduling appointments, preparing advertising copy for the broker's approval, and filing documents and maintaining the office calendar are ministerial tasks that may be assigned.

questions.question: A seller closes at $850,000, pays a commission of 6.0% of the price, and pays $8,000 in other seller closing costs. What are the seller's net proceeds before paying off any mortgage?
questions.explanation: Net proceeds are eight hundred fifty thousand dollars minus a six percent commission of fifty-one thousand dollars, minus eight thousand dollars of other costs, which equals seven hundred ninety-one thousand dollars. The seven hundred eleven thousand nine hundred dollar figure understates the proceeds by deducting too much. The eight hundred seventy thousand one hundred dollar figure overstates them because it exceeds the sale price despite the stated costs, and six hundred thirty-two thousand eight hundred dollars understates them severely.

questions.question: A property's net operating income is $188,000, its annual debt service is $83,000, and the investor's cash invested is $630,000. What is the cash-on-cash return?
questions.explanation: Cash flow after debt service is $188,000 minus $83,000, or $105,000, and dividing that by the $630,000 cash invested gives a cash-on-cash return of sixteen and sixty-seven hundredths percent. A return of fifteen percent understates the result, eighteen and thirty-four hundredths percent overstates it, and thirteen and thirty-four hundredths percent understates it by the widest margin.

georgia-real-estate.quiz_title: Georgia Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A conservation easement restricts

answers.text: Development to preserve land, often held by a land trust
Parking
Pet ownership
Interior paint colors

questions.explanation: The conservation easement restricts development to preserve the land, and it is often held by a land trust. Parking regulation is not the preservation restriction that defines the easement; pet ownership is an unrelated private matter the easement does not govern; interior paint colors concern the inside of a home, not the development rights surrendered to protect the land.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of disclosed dual agency?

answers.text: An example is a buyer's agent is a fiduciary of the buyer.
An example is buyer and seller sign the dual-agency consent.
An example is the listing agreement granting authority to market the home.
An example is a property manager is the owner's general agent.

questions.explanation: Buyer and seller signing the dual-agency consent is the example of disclosed dual agency because both parties knowingly consent in writing to the same brokerage representing both sides. The fiduciary-of-the-buyer example defines buyer agency, in which the agent represents only the buyer; the listing-authority example defines seller agency created by a listing agreement to market the home; the property-manager example defines general agency, in which the manager handles a continuing range of matters for the owner.

questions.question: A borrower pays 2.25% in discount points on a $250,000 loan. The points cost
questions.explanation: Taking 2.25% of the $250,000 loan gives a points cost of $5,625. $469 is $5,156 under the exact $5,625; $562 is $5,063 under the exact $5,625; $8,125 is $2,500 over the exact $5,625.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of lapse of time?

answers.text: An example is a purchase agreement signed by buyer and seller before closing.
An example is an offer good for 48 hours receives no response for a week.
An example is seller, buyer, and a new buyer agree the new buyer replaces the old one.
An example is a developer pays $1,000 for a 60-day right to buy a lot at $200,000.

questions.explanation: An offer good for 48 hours that receives no response for a week has ended by lapse of time. A purchase agreement signed before closing is an accepted contract, not an expired offer; an agreement substituting a new buyer for the old one is a novation, not expiration; paying $1,000 for a 60-day right to buy is an option contract, which holds the offer open rather than letting it lapse.

questions.question: A dispute over Georgia earnest money

answers.text: Is decided by the agent
Goes to the broker automatically
Is ignored
May require interpleader or written release per contract terms

questions.explanation: A dispute over earnest money may require interpleader or a written release under the contract terms, because the holder cannot simply pick a winner. The agent does not decide the dispute, the broker does not receive the funds automatically, and the dispute cannot be ignored.

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: a use allowed with conditions

answers.text: The term described is the HOA.
The term described is a conditional use.
The term described is the coastal zone regulations.
The term described is the HOA lien.

questions.explanation: Term for a use allowed with conditions is a conditional use, permitted only after review with conditions ensuring compatibility. Homeowners association is the community organization enforcing private rules rather than a conditional permission; coastal zone regulations are shoreline development limits rather than a use allowed with conditions; homeowners association lien is a claim for unpaid assessments rather than a conditional use.

questions.question: An option agreement sets a 3% option fee on a $388,000 price. The fee is
questions.explanation: The option fee at 3 percent of a $388,000 price equals $11,640. $5,820 is one-half of the correct fee, priced at one and one-half percent, and understates it by $5,820; $15,520 prices 4 percent and overstates the fee by $3,880; $3,880 prices only 1 percent and understates the fee by $7,760.

questions.question: A personal representative's deed is used by

answers.text: An executor or administrator conveying estate property
The lender
A tenant
The buyer

questions.explanation: A personal representative's deed is used by an executor or administrator to convey property belonging to an estate. A lender conveys through its own deed or foreclosure process, not as the estate's representative; a tenant holds only a leasehold and cannot convey estate title; a buyer receives a conveyance rather than issuing a personal representative's deed.

questions.question: Before acting as a Georgia dual agent, the broker discloses

answers.text: Only to the seller
Only the commission
The dual role and its limits to all parties and gets written consent
Nothing

questions.explanation: Before acting as a dual agent, the broker must disclose the dual role and its limits to all parties and obtain their informed written consent, because Georgia permits dual agency only on that basis. Disclosure to the seller alone, disclosure limited to commission, or no disclosure at all does not satisfy that requirement.

questions.question: Which term does this example illustrate: a 3% seller concession toward closing costs

answers.text: The example illustrates the PT-61 at closing.
The example illustrates Georgia seller-concession limits.
The example illustrates the mail-away closing.
The example illustrates the Georgia closing disclosure.

questions.explanation: A 3 percent seller concession toward closing costs illustrates Georgia seller-concession limits, because the seller is paying part of the buyer's costs within an allowed cap. The transfer-tax form, a mail-away closing by remote signing, and the closing disclosure with final figures are unrelated to a seller contribution.

questions.question: Which of the following about Georgia real estate license law is correct?

answers.text: The written deposit notice is the foreclosure sale must be advertised four consecutive weeks in the county paper
The written deposit notice is permanently changing loan terms to avoid default
Constructive notice is notice imputed from properly recorded instruments
A security deed is qualifying charitable property is exempt from Georgia ad valorem tax

questions.explanation: Constructive notice is notice imputed from properly recorded instruments, which is the correct statement. Calling the written deposit notice the foreclosure advertising rule splices the deposit location notice to the weekly advertising requirement; calling the written deposit notice a permanent change of loan terms splices it to a loan modification; calling a security deed exempt charitable property splices the security instrument to an ad valorem exemption.

questions.question: Pick the FALSE statement concerning Georgia real estate practice.

answers.text: Advertising under a broker's supervision is the 25-hour Georgia course required for the community association manager license
A Georgia broker who learns the buyer's identity is confidential must not reveal it to the seller.
Conversion in georgia is misappropriating client trust funds for the broker's own use
Inspections are for the buyer's information and negotiation.

questions.explanation: The advertising pairing is false because it attaches advertising under broker supervision to the separate twenty-five hour course required for the community association manager license. Keeping a buyer identity confidential from the seller, treating conversion as misappropriation of trust funds for personal use, and using inspections for buyer information and negotiation are all true statements.

questions.question: Using the cost approach on a Smyrna property: land $70,000, cost new $260,000, accrued depreciation $166,400. The indicated value is closest to
questions.explanation: Indicated value is $70,000 plus $260,000 minus $166,400 in depreciation, which equals exactly $163,600. The $93,600 figure is $70,000 too low because it omits the land value; the $496,400 figure is $332,800 too high because it adds depreciation instead of subtracting it; the $330,000 figure is $166,400 too high because it ignores depreciation entirely.

questions.question: Which term does this example illustrate: a 10-day inspection contingency

answers.text: The example illustrates the Superfund site.
The example illustrates the buyer's inspection right.
The example illustrates CERCLA.
The example illustrates asbestos.

questions.explanation: A 10-day inspection contingency illustrates the buyer's inspection right, because the contingency reserves time for the buyer's professional inspections. The Superfund site instead is a federally listed hazardous waste site and has nothing to do with an inspection contingency; the federal Superfund statute instead is the hazardous-waste cleanup law rather than an inspection right; asbestos instead is a fibrous mineral in older building materials rather than an inspection right.

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: abolished in Georgia; replaced by year's support

answers.text: The term described is the branch office license.
The term described is the 90-day lien filing.
The term described is dower and curtesy.
The term described is the familial-status protection.

questions.explanation: Abolished in Georgia and replaced by year's support describes dower and curtesy, the former spousal rights Georgia replaced with the surviving spouse's year's support claim; a branch office license concerns an additional licensed office. The ninety-day lien filing concerns a lien filing period; the familial-status protection concerns families with children in housing.

questions.question: In Andre’s $400,000 transaction at 6%, the total commission is $24,000. If split evenly, each side receives
questions.explanation: Six percent of $400,000 is a $24,000 total commission, and splitting that total evenly gives each side $12,000. The $18,000 figure is $6,000 over the exact $12,000 result; the $6,000 figure is $6,000 under the exact $12,000 result; the $24,000 figure is $12,000 over the exact $12,000 result and is the unsplit total.

questions.question: Annual property taxes of $6,000 on Deshawn’s Brunswick home are prorated with 250 days charged to the seller (365-day year). The seller’s share is
questions.explanation: The seller's share is $6,000 multiplied by 250 and divided by 365, which equals $4,109.59. The $2,054.79 figure is $2,054.80 below that exact value; the $8,219.18 figure is $4,109.59 above it; the $1,890.41 figure is $2,219.18 below it.

questions.question: Which statement about acceleration clause is NOT correct?

answers.text: Lien priority generally follows first in time, first in right, with property tax liens typically superior.
An acceleration clause prevents the lender from ever demanding early repayment.
An acceleration clause lets the lender demand the full balance upon the borrower's default.
An alienation (due-on-sale) clause lets the lender accelerate when the borrower transfers the property.

questions.explanation: The statement that an acceleration clause prevents the lender from ever demanding early repayment is not correct, because acceleration does the opposite and lets the lender demand the full balance on default. The lien priority statement is a true rule about priority, following first in time, first in right with tax liens typically superior; the statement that acceleration lets the lender demand the full balance on default correctly describes the clause; the alienation clause statement correctly describes acceleration triggered by a transfer.

questions.question: A $45,000 commission is split 60% to Jordan, the salesperson, and the rest to the broker. Jordan's share is
questions.explanation: Jordan's 60 percent share of $45,000 is exactly $27,000. The $18,000 figure is $9,000 under that exact amount and equals the broker's 40 percent share; the $22,500 figure is $4,500 under it and equals 50 percent; the $30,000 figure is $3,000 over it.

questions.question: All of the following are incorrect EXCEPT:

answers.text: State law makes an exception for licensees.
Oral leases over a year are enforceable.
Zoning affects rental use.
A related principle applies in every transaction.

questions.explanation: Zoning affects rental use by controlling what uses are permitted on a property, which is the one correct statement among the choices. The statement that state law makes an exception for licensees states no specific rule and so cannot be the correct statement; oral leases over a year are not enforceable because of the writing requirement for longer leases; the statement that a related principle applies in every transaction likewise states no specific rule.

new-jersey-real-estate.quiz_title: New Jersey Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Fee simple subject to condition subsequent?

answers.text: A New Jersey grantor exercising a right of reentry after the condition fails
New Jersey's ownership of submerged lands under navigable waters
A New Jersey homeowner claiming homestead protections
A historical New Jersey grant creating a qualified fee

questions.explanation: A grantor exercising a retained right of reentry after the stated condition fails is this estate in action, because retaking requires that affirmative election. Ownership of submerged lands, a homeowner's homestead claim, and a historical qualified fee in general do not specifically show the reentry step that defines the condition-subsequent form.

questions.question: Consent to dual agency may be revoked:

answers.text: Never
Per the agreement’s terms and applicable law
Only by the broker
Only after closing

questions.explanation: Consent to dual agency may be revoked as the agreement's terms and applicable law allow; because agency consent is governed by the parties' written agreement and governing law. It is not irrevocable; the broker alone cannot control revocation; and revocation is not limited to after closing.

questions.question: The commission on a Milltown transaction is $12,025 at a 6.5% rate. What did the property sell for?
questions.explanation: Divide the commission by the rate to recover the price: $12,025 ÷ 6.5% = $185,000. Checking the alternatives, 6.5% of $190,000, $183,000, or $180,000 would be $12,350, $11,895, or $11,700, so none matches the stated commission.

questions.question: A 17-year-old is generally liable for contracts for:

answers.text: Luxuries
Brokerage services
Real estate purchases
Necessaries like food and shelter

questions.explanation: Minors are generally liable for necessaries, essentials such as food and shelter suited to their station in life, because providers must be able to supply them. Contracts for luxuries, brokerage services, and real estate purchases are not necessaries and remain voidable at the minor's election.

questions.question: What happens if the requirements of Express contract are not met?

answers.text: The cancellation is effective
The seller must honor the highest bid
A court enforces the stated terms
The contract is discharged by impossibility

questions.question: Which statement about Overlay zones is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: Overlays replace base zoning entirely
The primary purpose of zoning is to raise property tax revenue
Overlays add special requirements to base zoning
A permit moratorium is an exercise of eminent domain

questions.explanation: Overlay zones add special requirements on top of the base zoning for an area, supplementing rather than replacing the underlying district rules. Zoning's primary purpose is protecting health, safety, and welfare rather than raising tax revenue, and a permit moratorium is a temporary exercise of the police power rather than a taking by eminent domain.

questions.question: A buyer and seller are reviewing offer basics. Which statement is FALSE?

answers.text: If the subject matter is destroyed before acceptance, the offer ends
Illegality of the proposed performance terminates the offer
Adjudicated insanity of the offeror terminates the offer
Secret unexpressed intent controls whether an offer was made

questions.explanation: The false statement is that secret unexpressed intent controls whether an offer was made; because offer and acceptance are judged by outward objective manifestations. Destruction of the subject matter before acceptance does end the offer; illegality of the proposed performance does terminate it; and adjudicated insanity of the offeror does terminate it.

questions.question: Which statement about Adverse possession is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: Squatters never gain rights
Hostile possession for the statutory period can ripen
A living trust eliminates estate taxes
A general warranty deed warrants only against taxes

questions.explanation: Adverse possession can ripen into title when possession is hostile and meets the other legal requirements for the full statutory period. It is not true that squatters can never gain rights, and the deed and trust statements describe different doctrines incorrectly.

questions.question: Which statement about Interest-bearing escrow is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: Interest belongs to the broker
Orders to show cause issue from the Executive Director on the Commission's behalf
Paraphrasing the no-obligation statement does not satisfy the rule
Interest handling follows written agreement

questions.explanation: Interest handling on interest-bearing escrow follows the parties' written agreement, which determines who receives the interest. The broker may not simply claim the interest as the broker's own, and statements about orders to show cause and paraphrasing a no-obligation statement concern enforcement and disclosure wording, not escrow interest.

questions.question: Which statement about Seller's residency certification is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: Residency certification is never required
The Guaranty Fund pays brokers' lost commissions
Sellers certify residency to avoid withholding
Brokers may lawfully agree to boycott discount competitors

questions.explanation: Sellers certify residency to avoid withholding, because a seller who certifies New Jersey residency is not treated as a nonresident whose gain must be withheld against state tax at closing. Residency certification therefore does have a required use, the fund does not pay brokers' lost commissions, and boycotting competitors is not lawful.

questions.question: Which statement about Real Estate Commission is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: The Commission licenses mortgage bankers
The NJ Real Estate Commission licenses brokers and salespersons
Deemed consent also requires the listing agreement to authorize posting on the broker's site, an MLS site, or a designated third-party site
The duty flows to all licensees once the broker is affiliated

questions.explanation: The New Jersey Real Estate Commission is the licensing authority for real estate brokers and salespersons. It does not license mortgage bankers, whose licensing sits elsewhere, so the licensing statement is the accurate description of the Commission's role.

questions.question: Which statement about Experience for broker is true under New Jersey law?

answers.text: Broker applicants need no experience
The fee line is May 1, not the renewal deadline
Broker applicants need 3 years licensed experience
Ethics credits are mandatory within the 12-credit total

questions.explanation: Broker applicants need three years of licensed experience, on top of the broker education requirements, so the claim that no experience is needed is false. The other statements recite genuine continuing education rules (the May fee line and mandatory ethics credit within the 12-credit total), but they do not describe the experience requirement this item targets.

questions.question: Regarding this situation — Jessica Yates describes positive and negative leverage. — all of the following are correct about Leverage EXCEPT:

answers.text: Negative leverage occurs when borrowing costs exceed returns
Leverage is positive when the property's return exceeds the borrowing cost
The spread between return and cost determines the effect
Leverage is irrelevant to real estate investors

questions.explanation: The exception is the claim that leverage is irrelevant to real estate investors; leverage is central to how financed purchases perform. Negative leverage occurs when borrowing costs exceed returns, leverage is positive when the property's return exceeds the borrowing cost, and the spread between return and cost determines which effect occurs.

questions.question: A seller fills out the property condition disclosure statement marking 'unknown' for every item despite living there 20 years. What risk does this create?

answers.text: No risk; 'unknown' is always safe
Automatic contract termination
A fine from the Real Estate Commission
Liability for misrepresentation if the seller actually knew of defects

questions.explanation: Answering unknown to every item does not shield a seller who actually knew of defects after living in the home for many years; claiming ignorance of known conditions can create liability for misrepresentation. There is no automatic termination or automatic Commission fine, but the answers are not risk-free.

questions.question: Regarding this situation — Dorothy Lombardi counsels a Marlboro agent whose license lapsed. — all of the following correctly describe Failure to renew EXCEPT:

answers.text: Deadlines make the renewal system enforceable
A lapsed license renews automatically with no action
The public must be able to rely on license status
Renewal requires timely CE, fees, and application

questions.explanation: The exception is automatic renewal of a lapsed license: renewal requires timely continuing education, fees, and application, and deadlines make the system enforceable. A lapsed license does not simply renew with no action.

questions.question: A Brick broker asks which provision governs the rule that the client receives fiduciary duties; the customer receives fairness. Which is correct?

answers.text: PSI NJ salesperson exam content outline — Agency (national portion) — Abandonment
PSI NJ salesperson exam content outline — Agency (national portion) — Death of agent
PSI NJ salesperson exam content outline — Agency (national portion) — Client versus customer
PSI NJ salesperson exam content outline — Agency (national portion) — Principal

questions.explanation: The client-versus-customer provision governs because it states the exact split: the client receives fiduciary duties and the customer receives fairness. Abandonment, death of an agent, and the definition of a principal are separate agency subjects that do not state this two-level duty structure.

questions.question: A salesperson in Cherry Hill collects a $2,000 deposit directly from a buyer and holds it for three weeks without telling the broker. What rules are implicated?

answers.text: No rules, because small deposits are exempt
Only the federal tax code
The five-business-day deposit rule and the broker-supervision requirement, since all funds flow through the broker
Only the local zoning ordinance

questions.question: Scenario: A Georgetown buyer asks Dorothy Iversen about contracts for deed. Regarding Land contract, the legal result is: In a land contract, the seller keeps legal title while the buyer gains equitable title and possession Why does this result follow?

answers.text: Because last-minute cost changes need review time
Because no lawsuit is needed
Because standardized disclosure aids comparison
Because possession plus payments create equity

questions.explanation: The land contract result follows because possession plus payments create equity: the buyer lives in and pays on the property while the seller holds legal title. Review time for cost changes, avoiding a lawsuit, and standardized disclosure for comparison concern other consumer-protection rules.

questions.question: Regarding this situation — A Cedar Falls buyer asks Jerry Holloway about use legality. — all of the following are correct about Zoning compliance at closing EXCEPT:

answers.text: Lenders may require zoning compliance
Zoning violations never affect value
Lenders require compliance
Illegal use threatens value

questions.explanation: Zoning violations do affect value, so the claim that they never do is incorrect. Lenders may require zoning compliance, and an illegal use threatens value because it may have to stop or be brought into compliance.

questions.question: Regarding this situation — Raymond Ellison sues to force a Westfield Junction sale. — all of the following are correct about Specific performance EXCEPT:

answers.text: Courts order conveyance when land is unique
Each parcel is unique
Specific performance applies to car sales
Land has no substitute

questions.explanation: Specific performance compels conveyance when land is unique, each parcel has no substitute, and equity orders the transfer rather than leaving the buyer to damages. It does not apply to ordinary car sales as a comparable routine remedy, making that the incorrect statement about the doctrine.

texas-real-estate.quiz_title: Texas Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A lot with 189 front feet at $359 per front foot is priced at:
questions.explanation: One hundred eighty-nine front feet at $359 per front foot price the lot at $67,851, computed as one hundred eighty-nine multiplied by $359. The $57,900 price understates that product; the $72,000 price overstates it; and the $60,500 price also understates it.

questions.question: Mold remediation for a 5,425-square-foot area is bid at $12 per square foot. The total is:
questions.explanation: Multiplying 5,425 square feet by $12 per square foot gives $65,100. The choice stating $71,610 is $6,510 too high; the choice stating $58,590 is $6,510 too low; the choice stating $68,355 is $3,255 too high.

questions.question: An agent does 12 BPOs at $294 each. Total earned is:
questions.explanation: Twelve broker price opinions at $294 each total $3,528, computed as twelve multiplied by $294. The $3,400 total understates that product by $128; the $3,300 total understates it by $228; and the $3,200 total understates it by $328.

questions.question: The key characteristic of a trustee's deed is:

answers.text: it warranty deeds
it tax deeds
it requires no signature
conveys after a foreclosure by the trustee

questions.explanation: A trustee's deed conveys property after a foreclosure sale conducted by the trustee under a deed of trust. It is not a warranty deed given in an ordinary sale, not a tax deed from a tax sale, and it does require proper execution rather than no signature.

questions.question: Mold remediation for a 6,500-square-foot area is bid at $18 per square foot. The total is:
questions.explanation: The total bid is the area times the rate, and 6,500 square feet times $18 per square foot equals $117,000. The $128,700 figure is $11,700 too high; the $105,300 figure is $11,700 too low; the $122,850 figure is $5,850 too high.

questions.question: A $658,826 property is held in joint tenancy by 4 owners. Each equal share is:
questions.explanation: Each equal share is $658,826 divided by 4, which is $164,706.50, and the $164,700 figure is the uniquely closest listed amount. The $181,900 figure is $17,193.50 too high, the $143,500 figure is $21,206.50 too low, and the $147,900 figure is $16,806.50 too low.

questions.question: A $267,941 home sells with a 6.5% commission. The total commission is:
questions.explanation: Six and one-half percent of $267,941 is about $17,416 in commission. The $15,400 figure is $2,016 less than the correct commission; the $15,260 figure is $2,156 less than the correct commission; and the $19,350 figure is $1,934 more than the correct commission.

questions.question: Regarding commission split, a $35,000 total commission is split with 40% going to the selling side. How much does the selling side receive?
questions.explanation: Forty percent of a $35,000 total commission is $14,000 to the selling side. The $16,100 figure exceeds 40 percent, $21,000 is 60 percent, and $11,900 falls short of 40 percent.

questions.question: Monthly rent $2,460, management fee 12%. Fee is:
questions.explanation: Twelve percent of the $2,460 monthly rent is $295.20, so the $295 figure is the closest management fee listed. The $305 figure is $9.80 too high, the $258 figure is $37.20 too low, and the $326 figure is $30.80 too high.

questions.question: A 120-foot wide lot has 14-foot side setbacks. The buildable width is:

answers.text: 92 feet
87 feet
97 feet
88 feet

questions.explanation: Subtracting two fourteen-foot side setbacks, totaling twenty-eight feet, from the one hundred twenty-foot width leaves ninety-two feet of buildable width. Eighty-seven feet subtracts too much, ninety-seven feet subtracts too little, and eighty-eight feet also subtracts too much.

questions.question: A $461,239 home sells with a 6.5% commission. The total commission is:
questions.explanation: $461,239 multiplied by 6.5% equals about $29,981 in total commission. The $26,290 figure understates that product, $34,050 overstates it, and $32,620 also overstates it.

questions.question: A $369,939 contract requires 1% earnest money. The amount is:
questions.explanation: One percent of $369,939 is $3,699.39, so the keyed $3,699 is the exact amount truncated to whole dollars. The $3,500 and $3,300 figures understate one percent, while $4,100 overstates it.

questions.question: Priya is studying comparable analysis and asks about transactional. Which statement is true?

answers.text: Adjustments are unnecessary.
Comps must be identical.
Transactional adjustments come first.
Older sales are better.

questions.explanation: Transactional adjustments, covering matters such as financing, conditions of sale, and market timing, are made first in comparable analysis before property adjustments. Adjustments are unnecessary denies that comparable sales must be adjusted for differences; comps must be identical sets an impossible standard instead of requiring the most similar available sales; older sales are better reverses the preference for the most recent comparable sales.

questions.question: A $512,848 sale has a $229,382 loan payoff and $17,312 closing costs. Seller proceeds are:
questions.explanation: Seller proceeds are the $512,848 sale price minus the $229,382 loan payoff and minus the $17,312 in closing costs, which leaves $266,154. The $242,400 figure deducts too much, the $286,700 figure deducts too little, and the $254,700 figure also deducts too much, so none matches the subtraction.

questions.question: Regarding earnest money and escrow, Noor in Amarillo asks about additional earnest money. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: No receipt is needed.
The broker may use the funds.
Additional earnest money follows the same rules.
Commingling is acceptable.

questions.explanation: Additional earnest money follows the same escrow rules as the original earnest money, so it is handled and disbursed under the same contract terms. The choice that no receipt is needed is wrong because escrow funds must be documented; the choice allowing the broker to use the funds describes conversion of client money; the choice accepting commingling contradicts the requirement to keep trust funds separate.

questions.question: A comparable is 359 sqft larger than the subject at $158/sqft. The adjustment is:
questions.explanation: The size adjustment is 359 square feet times $158 per square foot, which equals $56,722. The $61,000 figure is $4,278 too high; the $54,100 figure is $2,622 too low; the $58,900 figure is $2,178 too high.

questions.question: A sales agent on a 82/18 agent-broker split closes a deal generating a $9,500 commission to the brokerage. The agent's share is:
questions.explanation: The agent's share is 82 percent of the $9,500 commission, which equals $7,790. The choice stating $8,569 is $779 too high; the choice stating $7,011 is $779 too low; the choice stating $8,180 is $390 too high.

questions.question: On the national exam topic of contract law, Linda asks about offer. Which statement accurately reflects the rule?

answers.text: An offer is a promise to act.
Minors can contract freely.
Acceptance can differ from the offer.
Oral contracts are always enforceable.

questions.explanation: An offer is a promise or commitment to act on stated terms, made so that acceptance can form a contract. Minors cannot contract freely because their contracts are generally voidable, an acceptance that differs from the offer operates as a counteroffer rather than acceptance, and oral contracts are not always enforceable because many agreements must be in writing.

questions.question: A broker's trust account holds earnest-money deposits of $17,265, $19,645, and $27,891 for three pending transactions. The total held in trust is:
questions.explanation: Adding the three deposits gives $17,265 plus $19,645 plus $27,891, which totals $64,801 held in trust. The $71,281 figure overstates the sum by $6,480; the $58,321 figure understates it by $6,480; the $68,041 figure overstates it by $3,240.

questions.question: On the national exam topic of brokerage practice, Chris asks about the independent contractor. Which statement accurately reflects the rule?

answers.text: Brokers need no supervision.
Listings belong to agents.
Agents can work alone.
Agents are often contractors.

questions.explanation: Sales agents commonly work as independent contractors of their sponsoring broker rather than as employees, which governs their tax and control status. Saying brokers need no supervision inverts the broker's own supervisory role over the brokerage; saying listings belong to agents is wrong because listings are held by the broker; saying agents can work alone contradicts the rule that a salesperson must act under a sponsoring broker.

utah-real-estate.quiz_title: Utah Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes right of exclusion?

answers.text: The owner's right to sell, gift, lease, or otherwise transfer interests in the property
The owner's right to use the property in any lawful manner
The owner's right to decide how the property is used, within the law
The owner's right to keep others off the property

questions.explanation: The right of exclusion is the owner's right to keep others off the property. Selling or leasing is the right of disposition, and using the property or deciding its lawful use describes enjoyment and control, not excluding others.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes mistake?

answers.text: Revocation is the offeror's withdrawal of the offer before it has been accepted.
New construction is property sold by the builder before or just after completion.
Video marketing uses recorded property walkthroughs to promote listings online.
A mistake is an erroneous belief about a fact that is material to the contract.

questions.explanation: A mistake in contract law is an erroneous belief about a fact material to the deal, which can affect whether the contract is enforceable. Revocation, new construction, and video marketing define unrelated terms.

questions.question: Which of the following facts about steering is accurate?

answers.text: Prices soften
Broker supervision is a core broker responsibility
Backup offer provides security
Includes selective showing of listings

questions.explanation: Steering includes selectively showing listings — channeling buyers toward or away from neighborhoods based on protected characteristics — which fair housing law forbids. Market softness, broker supervision, and backup offers are legitimate or unrelated practice points.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST illustrates cooperation?

answers.text: The closing attorney
The commission check
The approved school
The referral

questions.explanation: Cooperation is best illustrated by the referral, in which one licensee works with another to serve a client rather than keeping the business entirely in-house. A closing attorney, a commission check, and an approved school are transaction or licensing items, not acts of cooperation between licensees.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about podcast?

answers.text: Seeking the Fund does not bar the underlying lawsuit
Podcast is niche
Audio marketing
Podcast builds authority

questions.explanation: The statement about seeking the Fund is not a statement about podcasts at all, while the other choices do describe podcasts: a niche medium, an audio form of marketing, and a way to build authority with an audience. A claim must actually concern the named subject to be true about it.

questions.question: Which of the following facts about historic district is accurate?

answers.text: Wetlands provide flood control and wildlife habitat
A general tax lien need not be recorded to be effective
Special assessments fund improvements like sidewalks benefiting nearby parcels
Tearing down buildings is restricted in heritage districts

questions.explanation: Historic districts impose preservation controls, so tearing down buildings in a heritage district is restricted. Flood control by wetlands, general tax liens, and special assessments for sidewalks are separate topics that say nothing about historic districts.

questions.question: What NOI is indicated for a $400,000 property at a 7% cap rate?
questions.explanation: Net operating income equals value times the capitalization rate, so $400,000 times 7 percent gives $28,000. Dividing value by the rate instead would produce a multimillion-dollar figure that cannot be one year's income on this property.

questions.question: The term 'minor breach' is BEST defined as which of the following?

answers.text: A small violation
The bargained exchange
When the buyer gets it
The deposit

questions.explanation: A minor breach is a small violation of a contract, a partial failure that does not defeat the contract's purpose, unlike a material breach. The bargained exchange defines consideration, and the deposit is earnest money, neither of which measures how serious a breach is.

questions.question: A $320,000 purchase is financed at 75% loan-to-value. What is the loan amount?
questions.explanation: Loan amount is price times loan-to-value: $320,000 times 75% equals $240,000. The $80,000 figure is the down payment portion, and the other amounts use the wrong percentage.

questions.question: A 5% commission produced $2,500 for the brokerage. What did the property sell for?
questions.explanation: If 5 percent of the price produced $2,500, divide $2,500 by 0.05 to get a $50,000 sale price. A $100,000 price would have produced double that commission.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST illustrates Utah agency disclosure?

answers.text: A 10-day due diligence period with a 500 dollar non-refundable fee
The for-sale sign
Giving the buyer a written explanation of brokerage relationships at the first serious meeting
The divorce attorney

questions.explanation: Utah agency disclosure means giving the buyer a written explanation of the brokerage relationships available and which one the brokerage will have with them, early in the relationship. A yard sign, a due-diligence fee term, and an unrelated attorney do not disclose agency.

questions.question: Which term is defined as follows? "Buyers typically pay 2-5 percent of price"

answers.text: Utah trust closing
Utah closing costs
Utah FSBO closing
good funds

questions.explanation: The charges a buyer pays to complete a purchase — lender, title, and related fees, typically a few percent of the price as the stem notes — are closing costs. A trust closing describes how funds are handled, an FSBO closing describes a sale without an agent, and good funds describes money in collectible form, not the charges themselves.

questions.question: A client asks their sales agent to explain 'conventional life estate.' Which explanation is CORRECT?

answers.text: A remainder waits until the prior estate terminates, then becomes possessory
A fee simple absolute estate can last forever and may be sold, devised, or inherited without restriction
A conventional life estate is created by the intentional act of the owner
An estate for years terminates automatically with no notice required

questions.explanation: A conventional life estate is created by the intentional act of the owner, typically by deed or will granting property for someone's lifetime. A remainder interest, a fee simple absolute, and an estate for years are different estates with different creation and duration.

questions.question: Which term BEST fits the following situation? A judge ordering the seller to convey the contracted property

answers.text: mutual assent
express contract
lawful purpose
specific performance

questions.explanation: Specific performance is the court remedy in which a judge orders the seller to convey the property as the contract requires, used because real estate is unique. Mutual assent, an express contract, and lawful purpose are contract elements, not a court-ordered remedy.

questions.question: "Preparing for chemical releases" is the definition of which of the following terms?

answers.text: emergency planning
exposure pathway
bona fide purchaser
stigma

questions.explanation: Preparing for chemical releases, with plans for responding to spills and emergencies, is emergency planning under the federal hazardous materials framework. An exposure pathway is the route a contaminant takes to reach people, a bona fide purchaser is a liability defense status, and stigma is a property's damaged reputation.

questions.question: "A group marketing name under the brokerage" is the definition of which of the following terms?

answers.text: phone protocol
team name
employee
closure procedures

questions.explanation: A group marketing name used by agents under one brokerage is a team name, identifying the team while it operates under the brokerage's license. Phone protocols, employee status, and closure procedures are office operations, not a marketing identity.

questions.question: An exam candidate is asked to identify a true fact about national database. Which choice is CORRECT?

answers.text: Administrative law judges may preside
The nationwide registry follows the practitioner
Bias requires it
Conclusions of law justify sanctions

questions.question: Which of the following terms BEST describes the cost to construct an exact duplicate of the improvements at current prices?

answers.text: net operating income
income approach
sales comparison approach
reproduction cost

questions.explanation: Reproduction cost is the cost to construct an exact duplicate of the improvements at current prices, using the same materials and design. The other choices name an income figure and two appraisal approaches, none of which is a construction cost measure.

questions.question: For a six-month period, a brokerage holds written authorization to advertise a residence at 425,000 dollars and to present all offers to the owners for a negotiated fee. Which of the following BEST identifies this arrangement?

answers.text: listing agreement
auction
security deposit
reasonable accommodation

questions.explanation: Written authorization to advertise a home and present all offers to the owners for a negotiated fee is a listing agreement between the owners and the brokerage. An auction sells to the highest bidder, and a security deposit and a reasonable accommodation are unrelated.

questions.question: After showings, a Utah listing agent collects buyer agents' comments about the property. Which of the following terms describes these buyer reactions?

answers.text: REO
possession
feedback
Utah earnest money disputes

questions.explanation: Comments that buyer agents pass back to the listing agent after showings are feedback, meaning the buyers' reactions to the property. Foreclosure-owned property, possession, and earnest money disputes are unrelated concepts.

arizona-real-estate.quiz_title: Arizona Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Immobility and indestructibility are both

answers.text: market traits
legal characteristics
economic characteristics
physical characteristics

questions.explanation: Immobility, the inability to move land, and indestructibility, the permanence of land, are both physical characteristics describing the land itself. They are not market traits, not legal characteristics created by law, and not economic characteristics, which concern value influences such as scarcity and situs.

questions.question: Agents owe clients

answers.text: minimal effort
duties to others
only speed
loyalty

questions.explanation: Agents owe their clients loyalty, putting the client's interests ahead of the agent's own and those of others in the transaction. Minimal effort falls short of the duty of reasonable care, duties to others do not replace duties to the client, and speed alone is not a fiduciary duty.

questions.question: A lot 165 feet by 264 feet contains about

answers.text: 2 acres
0.5 acre
1.5 acres
1 acre

questions.explanation: The lot contains 165 times 264, which is 43,560 square feet, and one acre is exactly 43,560 square feet, so the lot is about one acre. Two acres and one and one-half acres are both above the true size, while one-half acre is below it.

questions.question: Regarding presenting offers, the duty is

answers.text: prompt presentation of all
when the broker chooses
delayed
selective

questions.explanation: Offers must be presented promptly and all of them must reach the seller, because selective or delayed presentation deprives the principal of choices the agent is bound to deliver. Presenting only when the broker chooses subordinates the principal's decision to the brokerage's timing, delay contradicts promptness, and presenting selectively hides offers the seller is entitled to consider.

questions.question: Regarding appraisal waivers, risks are

answers.text: handled informally
skipped
denied
explained

questions.explanation: Risks of an appraisal waiver must be explained so the buyer understands that waiving protection can require extra cash if value is low. Handling the risk informally, skipping the explanation, or denying the risk fails the duty of reasonable skill and care.

questions.question: A variance from a zoning ordinance is typically granted when

answers.text: the owner wants a more profitable use
the property has been vacant one year
neighbors all agree verbally
strict enforcement would cause undue hardship due to unique lot conditions

questions.explanation: A variance is relief from strict zoning enforcement granted when unique conditions of the lot itself cause undue hardship. Wanting a more profitable use alone does not meet that standard, a year of vacancy does not create the hardship, and informal verbal agreement by neighbors cannot substitute for the required showing and approval.

questions.question: "non-agency disclosure" is best defined as

answers.text: a consensual relationship where the agent acts for the principal
telling a party the licensee does not represent them
one authorized to act for the principal
the party the agent represents

questions.explanation: Non-agency disclosure means telling a party that the licensee does not represent them, so the party does not mistakenly rely on fiduciary protection. A consensual relationship where the agent acts for the principal defines agency, one authorized to act for the principal is an agent, and the party represented is the principal.

questions.question: A property is near a former gas station. Prudent buyers

answers.text: investigate potential underground tank contamination
skip all inspections
rely on the seller's word only
a selling point

questions.explanation: A former gas station site raises the risk of leaking underground storage tanks, so prudent buyers investigate potential soil and groundwater contamination before buying. Skipping inspections or relying only on the seller's word leaves that risk unexamined, and a possible contamination source is a concern rather than a selling point.

questions.question: "civil penalty (ACFA)" is best defined as

answers.text: up to $10,000 per violation for willful violations
deception or unfair acts in selling or advertising merchandise
a misleading act or representation
Arizona's 1967 law against deceptive trade practices

questions.explanation: For a willful violation of the Consumer Fraud Act, the civil penalty can reach up to $10,000 per violation. Deception or unfair acts in selling or advertising merchandise describes the prohibited conduct, a misleading act or representation describes deception, and Arizona's 1967 law against deceptive trade practices describes the Act itself rather than the penalty amount.

questions.question: The real estate term for "stating prices" is

answers.text: price advertising
broker identification
blind ads
advertising (Arizona)

questions.explanation: Stating prices in advertising is price advertising, because the content being published is the price term. Broker identification concerns displaying the brokerage name, blind ads conceal the brokerage, and advertising generally is the broader category rather than this specific practice.

questions.question: Regarding post-closing occupancy, agreements

answers.text: ban it
cover it
hide it
when the lender feels like it

questions.explanation: Post-closing occupancy must be covered by the parties' agreement, because a seller remaining in the home after closing needs written terms for rent, duration, and responsibility. It is not banned outright, it must not be hidden from lenders or insurers, and its terms are set by the agreement rather than whenever a lender happens to allow it.

questions.question: "document fees" is best defined as

answers.text: HOA resale charges
condominium ownership
planned community associations
resale package charges

questions.question: A life tenant who cannot sell the full fee. This best describes

answers.text: fee simple absolute
fee simple determinable
life estate
fee simple subject to condition subsequent

questions.explanation: A life tenant holds only a life estate and therefore cannot sell the full fee, only an interest lasting for the measuring life. Fee simple absolute carries full ownership, and the determinable and condition-subsequent fees are fee estates rather than interests limited to a person's lifetime.

questions.question: A distinguishing characteristic of Jones v. Mayer (1968) is that

answers.text: it is the main law
it was based on 1866 law
it has no exemptions
it is historic

questions.explanation: The decision rested on the post-Civil War civil rights law from 1866, which the Court held bars racial discrimination in buying and selling property. It is not the main modern fair housing statute, its significance is that statutory basis rather than a statement about exemptions, and calling it merely historic understates the specific legal ground of the ruling.

questions.question: A distinguishing characteristic of Real Estate Commissioner is that

answers.text: it covers duties as counsel
they enforce Title 32, Chapter 20
it covers owners acting for themselves
it covers court appointees

questions.explanation: The Real Estate Commissioner is Arizona's real estate regulator, charged with enforcing the state's license law and disciplining licensees under it. Serving as counsel to the parties is a lawyer's role, owners acting for themselves are an exempt category rather than the Commissioner, and court appointees are another exempt category rather than the regulator.

questions.question: An Arizona licensee with a personal interest in a transaction must

answers.text: disclose only to the broker
hide it to avoid bias claims
withdraw from the transaction
disclose that interest in writing to all parties

questions.explanation: A licensee with a personal interest in a transaction must disclose that interest in writing to all parties, so everyone can weigh the bias for themselves. Disclosing only to the broker leaves the parties uninformed, hiding the interest breaches the duty, and withdrawal is not required when the interest is properly disclosed.

questions.question: The real estate term for "the records examination" is

answers.text: title search
escrow (Arizona)
escrow agent
escrow instructions

questions.explanation: Examining the public records for a property's title history is a title search. Escrow is the neutral closing arrangement, an escrow agent is the neutral third party who runs it, and escrow instructions are the parties' written directions for closing, none of which names the records examination.

questions.question: A comparable duplex rents for $900 per month and similar properties sell at a gross rent multiplier of 105. Its indicated value is
questions.explanation: $900 times a gross rent multiplier of 105 equals $94,500. The $103,500 and $103,950 figures overstate the product and sit above it, while $85,500 understates the monthly rent or multiplier and sits below it.

questions.question: A purchase contract states that "time is of the essence" for closing. The buyer arrives three days late with the funds. The seller may generally:

answers.text: Extend the closing by 30 days automatically
Sue the buyer's lender
Treat the delay as a breach and cancel the contract
Do nothing; late closing is always permitted

questions.explanation: When a contract makes time of the essence, the stated closing date is a material term, so an unjustified three-day delay can be treated as a breach allowing the seller to cancel as the contract and law permit. There is no automatic thirty-day extension, suing the buyer's lender is not the seller's remedy for the buyer's delay, and late performance is not always permitted.

questions.question: In an Arizona limited-representation transaction, one party's confidential information

answers.text: may be disclosed to the other side without permission
is shared automatically with both parties
may be disclosed to the other party only with that party's written authorization
loses all protection once dual agency begins

questions.explanation: A dual agent must not disclose one party's confidential information, such as price flexibility or motivation, to the other party without that party's written authorization. Disclosure without permission, automatic sharing with both sides, and the idea that protection disappears once dual agency begins all violate that confidentiality duty.

illinois-real-estate.quiz_title: Illinois Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of fee simple defeasible?

answers.text: To confuse parties
To increase costs
Can be lost
To maximize profit

questions.explanation: A fee simple defeasible estate is one that can be lost — it may terminate if a stated condition occurs or a limitation is breached, unlike a fee simple absolute. Its defining feature is that potential loss, not cost or profit.

questions.question: About mutual agreement, which statement is FALSE?

answers.text: Death is irrelevant.
A holdover clause must be conspicuous and reasonable.
Destruction of the property can terminate a listing.
Files and records must be retained after termination.

questions.explanation: Death is not irrelevant, so that claim is false; death can terminate an agency and a listing. A holdover clause must be conspicuous and reasonable, destruction of the property can terminate a listing, and files must be retained after termination.

questions.question: At a 90% loan-to-value ratio, what is the maximum loan on a $500,000 property?
questions.explanation: Maximum loan equals property value times the loan-to-value ratio: $500,000 times 90 percent equals $450,000. The $50,000 figure is the down payment, not the loan.

questions.question: An Illinois buyer who waives the home-inspection contingency

answers.text: still retains the right to sue for the seller's fraud or concealment
waives all rights against the seller forever
must close even if the home burns down
cannot obtain title insurance

questions.explanation: Waiving an inspection contingency gives up the inspection-based right to object, but it does not waive claims for the seller's fraud or concealment, which cannot be signed away by that waiver. The buyer does not lose all rights forever, is not forced to close on a destroyed home by the waiver alone, and can still obtain title insurance.

questions.question: How is Drone photography best described?

answers.text: the contract specifying how the brokerage is compensated
aerial property images captured by unmanned aircraft
marketing a listing or services, subject to fair housing and license laws
the symbol indicating compliance with fair housing laws in advertising

questions.explanation: Drone photography means aerial property images captured by an unmanned aircraft. It is not the agreement that sets brokerage compensation, not a description of advertising generally, and not the symbol used to show fair-housing compliance in ads.

questions.question: A buyer asks if the subdivision allows chickens. The broker checks

answers.text: the CC&Rs and HOA rules
the plat's scale
the tax rate
the flood map

questions.explanation: Whether a subdivision allows chickens is governed by its covenants, conditions, and restrictions and any association rules, so the broker checks those documents. The plat's scale, the tax rate, and the flood map do not state the use restrictions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about option rights is FALSE?

answers.text: An option must be exercised within its term.
Accord doubles the obligation.
Severability saves the rest if one clause fails.
Termination can occur by performance, agreement, or breach.

questions.explanation: An accord is an agreement to accept a different performance in satisfaction of an obligation; it does not double the obligation, so that statement is false. An option must be used within its term, severability can save the rest of a contract, and termination by performance, agreement, or breach are all correctly described.

questions.question: In a real estate closing, the escrow (settlement) agent acts as

answers.text: a neutral third party carrying out the parties' written instructions
an advocate for the seller's interests
an advocate for the buyer's interests
a guarantor of the property's condition

questions.explanation: At closing, the escrow or settlement agent is a neutral third party who carries out the parties' written instructions and disburses funds as directed. The agent does not advocate for either side or guarantee the property's condition.

questions.question: Laura Davis lists a property Laura Davis has no authority to sell. The advertising

answers.text: authority is implied
advertising requires authority
only sales need authority
anyone may advertise

questions.explanation: A licensee may advertise a property only with the owner's authority to sell it; listing or marketing property the licensee has no authority to sell is improper advertising. Authority is never implied merely because the property exists, and the rule covers advertising as well as the sale itself.

questions.question: What is the county transfer tax on a $195,000 sale at $0.50 per $1,000?
questions.explanation: At $0.50 for each $1,000 of price, a $195,000 sale has 195 taxable units, and 195 times $0.50 equals $97.50. The larger amounts charge a higher per-thousand rate and the smaller amount charges only half the stated rate.

questions.question: Material facts should be disclosed at which of the following times?

answers.text: At closing
As soon as practicable
After closing
Never

questions.explanation: Material facts must be disclosed as soon as practicable once the licensee knows them, so the other party can rely on them while decisions are still being made. Waiting until closing, disclosing after closing, or never disclosing defeats the purpose of disclosure.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes seller disclosure?

answers.text: occupying beyond the agreed date
a junior loan encompassing the existing mortgage
the direct relationship between contracting parties
the statutory property condition statement

questions.explanation: Seller disclosure means the statutory property condition statement in which a seller reports known conditions of the property to a buyer. Holding over after a lease, a wraparound junior loan, and privity of contract are unrelated concepts that merely sound technical.

questions.question: A property sells for $581,000 with monthly rent of $4,004. What is the gross rent multiplier (monthly)?
questions.explanation: The monthly gross rent multiplier is sale price divided by monthly rent: $581,000 divided by $4,004 is about 145.1. Dividing by twelve months of rent instead gives the much smaller annual figure, which is a different measure, and the remaining figures scale this result up or down.

questions.question: The buyer's agent duty regarding a seller's disclosure statement is to

answers.text: deliver it to the buyer and note that it is the seller's statement, not the agent's verification
certify that every answer is accurate
rewrite answers the agent doubts
discard statements that look incomplete

questions.explanation: The buyer's agent must deliver the seller's disclosure statement to the buyer while making clear it is the seller's statement, which the agent has not verified. The agent may not certify its accuracy, rewrite answers the agent doubts, or throw away a statement that looks incomplete.

questions.question: An Illinois licensee changes their email address on March 1. Under the License Act, the licensee must inform the Department of the change by

answers.text: March 31
March 8
March 2
September 1

questions.explanation: Illinois requires a licensee to report a change of address, email, phone, or office within 24 hours, so a March 1 change must be reported by March 2. Waiting until March 8 or March 31 — or months later — violates the current 24-hour rule.

questions.question: A commercial lot has 109 front feet valued at $1,990 per front foot. What is the lot's front-footage value?
questions.explanation: Front-footage value is front feet times value per front foot: 109 times $1,990 equals $216,910.

questions.question: A licensee is caught cheating on the Real Estate License Exam. Under the License Act, exam cheating is

answers.text: cheating on or attempting to subvert the Real Estate License Exam or a continuing education examination
failing the exam on the first attempt
studying with a partner
taking notes during the exam

questions.explanation: Cheating under the License Act means cheating on, or attempting to subvert, the licensing or continuing education examination itself. Simply failing an attempt is not cheating, and studying with a partner is legitimate preparation.

questions.question: Which term is defined as follows: a refinance that replaces the existing loan without the borrower receiving cash at closing?

answers.text: recast
atr
forbearance agreement
no-cash-out refinance

questions.explanation: A no-cash-out refinance replaces the existing loan with a new one without the borrower receiving cash at closing, apart from closing costs.
