questions.question: Mr. Almeida, 83, is NPO after midnight for a morning procedure, and the nurse aide finds a full water pitcher and cup that were left at his bedside overnight. The aide's FIRST action is to:

answers.text: Pour him half a cup now and remove the pitcher afterward so he is not too thirsty
Leave the pitcher but turn the cup upside down as a reminder not to drink from it
Remove the pitcher and cup from his reach, offer mouth care for comfort, and tell the nurse they were at the bedside
Cover the pitcher with a towel so he cannot see it but staff can still use it later

questions.explanation: Correct action: Remove the pitcher and cup from his reach, offer mouth care for comfort, and tell the nurse they were at the bedside. Removing water from reach protects the NPO order, mouth care relieves dryness, and the nurse is told so the team knows access occurred. Hidden or half-served water still breaks the restriction and risks the procedure.

questions.question: Mrs. Haddad, 84, has dementia and often does not ask for the toilet, but her care plan lists toileting after meals and every two hours while awake. The nurse aide supports her continence best by:

answers.text: Waiting for her to ask for the toilet so her independence is fully respected
Reminding her once each morning that the bathroom is down the hall from her room
Giving her fluids only at meals so she needs the toilet less often between them
Taking her to the toilet at the planned times, using simple cues and the same routine each time

questions.explanation: Correct action: Taking her to the toilet at the planned times, using simple cues and the same routine each time. Scheduled toileting with simple cues and a consistent routine is how a care plan supports continence for a resident who does not ask. Waiting for a request she cannot make, or restricting fluids, leads to incontinence and dehydration.

ptcb.quiz_title: PTCB PTCE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A prescription specifies Cipro tablets. What is the generic name?

answers.text: Ciprofloxacin
Ofloxacin
Moxifloxacin
Levofloxacin

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Ciprofloxacin. Cipro is the brand name for ciprofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone; the other options are different fluoroquinolones.

questions.question: What is the purpose of viable surface sampling in a sterile compounding area?

answers.text: Culturing surface samples to detect living microorganisms on work surfaces
Testing surface samples for leftover chemotherapy drug residue
Measuring surface temperature where compounded products are stored
Weighing dust collected on surfaces to set the cleaning budget

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Culturing surface samples to detect living microorganisms on work surfaces — Viable sampling swabs or plates surfaces and incubates them; colonies that grow reveal where living microbes persist despite cleaning, so corrective action can target the right spots.

questions.question: A near-miss caught before it reaches the patient should be reported internally because it:

answers.text: Satisfies a billing requirement for the claim
Exposes a weakness while no harm has occurred
Documents that a staff member was at fault
Raises the pharmacy's public quality rating

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Exposes a weakness while no harm has occurred. Near misses reveal the same system weaknesses as harmful errors, without a harmed patient. Reporting them lets the pharmacy fix the weakness before the next attempt succeeds in causing harm.

questions.question: USP  was written mainly to address which workplace concern?

answers.text: Protecting temperature-sensitive products during shipment to patients only
Protecting compounded sterile products from microbial contamination only
Protecting pharmacy records from unauthorized access by outside hackers
Protecting workers, patients, and the environment from hazardous drugs

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Protecting workers, patients, and the environment from hazardous drugs. USP  sets handling standards for hazardous drugs in health care settings, covering receiving, storage, compounding, dispensing, administration support, and waste, to limit occupational exposure.

questions.question: In USP  surface cleaning, the decontamination step has which purpose?

answers.text: To sterilize every surface in the entire building
To inactivate or remove hazardous drug residue from surfaces
To polish metal surfaces until they shine brightly
To add a protective fragrance layer to surfaces

questions.explanation: Correct answer: To inactivate or remove hazardous drug residue from surfaces — Decontamination works to inactivate or remove hazardous drug residue from surfaces, as part of the deactivation, decontamination, cleaning, and disinfection sequence for containment equipment.

questions.question: When compounding or handling hazardous drugs that require glove protection, USP  calls for:

answers.text: No gloves at all when the drug is supplied in a sealed unit package
Two pairs of chemotherapy-tested gloves for many handling activities
One pair of heavy utility gloves washed and reused between activities
One pair of ordinary examination gloves for all handling activities

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Two pairs of chemotherapy-tested gloves for many handling activities. Double gloving with ASTM-tested chemotherapy gloves (changed at least every 30 minutes and whenever torn or punctured) is a core USP  control for compounding and other higher-risk handling.

questions.question: Calcium carbonate gives fast relief of occasional heartburn mainly by what action?

answers.text: It neutralizes stomach acid on contact in the stomach
It coats the esophagus with a thick protective foam
It blocks the stomach pumps that produce new acid
It speeds the emptying of the stomach into the bowel

questions.explanation: Correct answer: It neutralizes stomach acid on contact in the stomach — Calcium carbonate is an antacid: it chemically neutralizes acid already in the stomach, giving quick but relatively short relief compared with acid-suppressing drugs.

questions.question: Under the CMEA, what is the maximum amount of pseudoephedrine base one person may purchase within a 30-day period from a retailer?

answers.text: 30 grams in 30 days
3.6 grams in 30 days
9 grams in 30 days
15 grams in 30 days

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 9 grams in 30 days — The CMEA sets a 30-day purchase limit of 9 grams in 30 days of pseudoephedrine base for sales by a regulated seller to an individual purchaser.

questions.question: Which routine must a wholesale distributor maintain to keep illegitimate product out of distribution?

answers.text: A practice of discounting suspect returns to other sellers
A policy of restocking all returns the same day they arrive
A rule that drivers decide which returns look acceptable
Written procedures to quarantine suspect returns and inspect them before any restocking

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Written procedures to quarantine suspect returns and inspect them before any restocking — Distributors must run formal suspect-product systems, including holding and examining returned product for signs of tampering, diversion, or counterfeiting before it can re-enter saleable stock.

questions.question: What do artificial tears (ocular lubricant drops) actually do for dry eyes?

answers.text: Artificial tears lubricate dry eyes but do not treat infection
Artificial tears kill the bacteria that cause pink eye
Artificial tears are a mild antibiotic for daily eye use
Artificial tears change the shape of the eye over time

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Artificial tears lubricate dry eyes but do not treat infection — Lubricant drops add moisture and comfort for dryness and irritation; they contain no anti-infective drug, so spreading redness, pain, or discharge needs pharmacist and medical assessment instead.

questions.question: Nitroglycerin for chest pain is supplied as a small tablet placed under the tongue. This is the:

answers.text: Sublingual route, giving rapid absorption into the bloodstream
Buccal route, giving slow absorption through the cheek lining
Topical route, giving absorption through intact skin surfaces
Oral route, giving absorption after passage through the liver

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Sublingual route, giving rapid absorption into the bloodstream. Sublingual tablets dissolve under the tongue, where a rich blood supply absorbs the drug quickly and largely bypasses first-pass liver metabolism, suiting nitroglycerin for acute chest pain.

questions.question: Which accompanying feature makes a new drug rash especially concerning for Stevens-Johnson syndrome?

answers.text: Dry flaking on the scalp occurring together with the rash
A faint pink color that fades within an hour of the dose
Mild itching on one elbow occurring together with the rash
Sores in the mouth and eyes occurring together with the rash

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Sores in the mouth and eyes occurring together with the rash — Involvement of mucous membranes — painful mouth sores, eye redness or sores, or genital sores — alongside a spreading rash points toward Stevens-Johnson syndrome rather than a simple rash and needs urgent referral.

questions.question: Under Medicare, blood glucose monitors and test strips a patient uses at home are generally covered under which part?

answers.text: No part; Medicare never covers testing supplies
Part B, as durable medical equipment and related supplies
Part D, as ordinary retail prescription drug items
Part A, as inpatient hospital supplies only items

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Part B, as durable medical equipment and related supplies — Medicare treats home blood glucose monitors, strips, and lancets as durable medical equipment and supplies under Part B, subject to its quantity limits and documentation rules, rather than as Part D drugs.

questions.question: A claim rejects with a drug utilization review (DUR) conflict code for duplicate therapy. What is the pharmacist's usual path?

answers.text: Ignore the code and promise the patient it is only a computer error
Review the conflict and, when appropriate, override it with the plan's documented codes
Delete one of the patient's active prescriptions from the profile silently
Refuse every future prescription written for that patient by anyone

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Review the conflict and, when appropriate, override it with the plan's documented codes — DUR rejections are clinical checkpoints: the pharmacist evaluates the duplication and either resolves it with the prescriber or documents a permitted override for the plan.

questions.question: A prescriber orders a compound with a flavoring the patient's profile lists as an allergy. What is the correct entry action?

answers.text: Substitute a different flavor personally without telling the pharmacist
Enter the order and let the compounder notice the flavoring conflict
Stop and bring the flavoring conflict to the pharmacist before entry ends
Delete the allergy from the profile so the compound can be prepared

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Stop and bring the flavoring conflict to the pharmacist before entry ends — Excipients and flavors in compounds can carry allergens just as active drugs do; the conflict must be resolved by the pharmacist with the prescriber before the preparation is made.

questions.question: A patient uses 2 puffs twice daily and needs a 30-day supply. How many actuations must the dispensed inhaler provide?

answers.text: 60 actuations
120 actuations
90 actuations
240 actuations

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 120 actuations — Work: 2 puffs x 2 doses per day = 4 puffs per day. 4 puffs per day x 30 days = 120 actuations.

questions.question: Nasacort nasal spray is recommended for a patient's seasonal allergies. What is the generic name of Nasacort?

answers.text: Chlorpheniramine
Fexofenadine
Oxymetazoline
Triamcinolone acetonide

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Triamcinolone acetonide — Triamcinolone acetonide is the generic name of Nasacort, an intranasal corticosteroid spray for allergic rhinitis.

questions.question: A prescriber has raised a patient's opioid dose sharply three months in a row with no documented change in condition. What resolution record fits corresponding responsibility?

answers.text: Require the patient to change to a different prescriber
Cut the dispensed dose in half without contacting anyone
Fill it because dose changes are never the pharmacy's concern
Document the prescriber's clinical rationale in the patient profile

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Document the prescriber's clinical rationale in the patient profile — Steady unexplained escalation is a red flag; obtaining the prescriber's clinical reason and documenting it in the profile lets this fill, and every later fill, be judged against a recorded rationale.

questions.question: A patient taking an SGLT2 inhibitor becomes ill, stops eating, and has nausea with rapid breathing but a near-normal glucose reading. Why is this still an emergency pattern?

answers.text: SGLT2 drugs can cause ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose
Ketoacidosis cannot occur unless glucose is very high
Nausea during illness is always simple food poisoning
Near-normal glucose rules out any metabolic emergency

questions.explanation: Correct answer: SGLT2 drugs can cause ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose — SGLT2 therapy is linked to euglycemic ketoacidosis: dangerous ketone buildup during illness, fasting, or surgery even when glucose looks deceptively normal, so symptoms matter more than the meter reading.

questions.question: A wholesaler successfully verifies a returned unit's identifier, confirms the unit is otherwise saleable and in date, and documents the return. What may the wholesaler then do with that unit?

answers.text: Place the verified unit back into saleable inventory
Place the unit into the hazardous waste container
Give the unit free to any requesting pharmacy
Remove the unit's identifier and repackage it

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Place the verified unit back into saleable inventory — Verification is the gate for returns: after the identifier verifies and the unit is otherwise saleable, the wholesaler may place the verified unit back into saleable inventory for redistribution.

teas.quiz_title: TEAS Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question:
Unlike drip irrigation, which delivers water slowly at a plant's roots, overhead sprinklers spray water over a whole bed at once. Sprinklers are cheaper to install, but more of their water evaporates before reaching the soil.
The passage is organized primarily by

answers.text: contrasting two watering methods
listing events in the order they occurred
narrating a gardener's personal experience
defining a single scientific term

questions.explanation: Correct answer: contrasting two watering methods. The passage sets drip irrigation against overhead sprinklers on delivery, cost, and evaporation. That point-by-point contrast is its organizing method.

questions.question: What is 0.85 expressed as a fraction in lowest terms?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: 17/20. 0.85 = 85/100, and dividing the numerator and denominator by 5 gives 17/20.

questions.question: What is (−4) + 9?
questions.explanation: 5. Start at −4 and move 9 units in the positive direction. That lands at 5.

questions.question: What is 15% of 240?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: 36. Change 15% to 0.15 and multiply by 240. The product is 36.

questions.question: What is the value of x in the equation 3(x + 4) = 27?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: 5. Dividing both sides by 3 gives x plus 4 equals 9, and subtracting 4 gives x equals 5.

questions.question: How many quarts are in 3.5 gallons?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: 14. Multiply by 4 because each gallon is 4 quarts: 3.5 × 4 = 14. There are 14 quarts in 3.5 gallons.

questions.question:
Source 1: The minute book kept by the founders of the Riverton Farmers Cooperative records that the cooperative held its first meeting and elected officers in March 1911.
Source 2: A magazine article published in 2011 for the cooperative's centennial celebration states that the cooperative was founded in 1912, the year its first warehouse opened.
Which statement best evaluates these two sources on the founding date?

answers.text: The magazine is more reliable because it was written for a celebration
Both sources are equally reliable because both discuss the cooperative
The sources agree on the founding date, so there is nothing to resolve
The founders' own minute book is the stronger source for the founding date

questions.explanation: Correct answer: The founders' own minute book is the stronger source for the founding date. The founders' own minute book is the stronger source for the founding date. A record written by the participants at the time is generally more reliable for the date than an article written a century later, and the sources disagree, so the difference does need resolving.

questions.question: Which word correctly completes the sentence? After weeks of illness, he still felt too ___ to climb the stairs.

answers.text: weak
week
weeks
weakest

questions.explanation: Correct answer: weak. Weak means lacking strength; week is a period of seven days, and the other forms do not fit.

questions.question: Which word is an antonym, or opposite in meaning, of expand as it is used in the phrase expand the garden?

answers.text: enlarge
stretch
widen
contract

questions.explanation: Correct answer: contract. Contract means to make smaller, the opposite of expand; the other words are synonyms.

questions.question:
Instructional signs at the recycling center remind visitors to empty and rinse food containers before dropping them off. Workers explain that leftover food can spoil an entire bin of otherwise recyclable material. The center provides a rinse station near the entrance for this purpose. Since the signs went up, the number of rejected bins has fallen by half.
Which of the following statements best captures the author's message?

answers.text: Rinsing containers before recycling keeps more material usable
Recycling centers should reject every bin that contains food containers
Visitors dislike using the rinse station at the recycling center
Food containers can never be recycled, even when clean

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Rinsing containers before recycling keeps more material usable. The message is that rinsing prevents contamination, supported by rejected bins falling by half after the signs. The passage never calls for rejecting all bins or claims clean containers are unrecyclable.

questions.question: Passage: When the town library moved its children's section to a larger room, librarians expected noise complaints from the reading room next door. Instead, visits by families doubled within three months, and the library responded by adding Saturday story hours and a second row of low shelves for picture books. Which sentence best states the main idea of the passage?

answers.text: The library's move caused noise complaints from the reading room next door.
Families in the town doubled in size within three months of the move.
Picture books must be kept on low shelves so children can reach them.
The library's move led to more family visits and expanded children's services.

questions.explanation: Correct answer: The library's move led to more family visits and expanded children's services.. The passage centers on the unexpected rise in family visits and the services added in response; the complaints were expected but never reported as happening.

questions.question: Which membrane covers the outer surface of a long bone and contains blood vessels and cells important for bone growth and repair?

answers.text: The periosteum covering the bone
The endosteum lining the marrow cavity
The perichondrium covering the cartilage
The periosteal sheath is not a real structure

questions.explanation: Correct answer: The periosteum covering the bone. The periosteum is a fibrous, vascular membrane whose inner layer supplies osteoblasts for appositional growth and fracture healing.

questions.question: Researchers randomly assign volunteers to a treatment group or a control group rather than letting them choose. Random assignment mainly helps by doing what?

answers.text: Making the groups similar in ways that could matter
Guaranteeing that the treatment will work as hoped
Removing the need for a control group entirely
Allowing each volunteer to pick a preferred group

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Making the groups similar in ways that could matter. Random assignment balances known and unknown differences between groups, so outcomes can be compared fairly.

questions.question: The unbalanced equation for burning magnesium in oxygen is Mg + O2 -> MgO. When the equation is balanced, what coefficient appears in front of MgO?

answers.text: 1, giving the balanced equation Mg + O2 -> MgO
3, giving the balanced equation 3Mg + O2 -> 3MgO
4, giving the balanced equation 4Mg + O2 -> 4MgO
2, giving the balanced equation 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 2, giving the balanced equation 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO. Balancing requires two magnesium atoms and two oxygen atoms on each side: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO places the coefficient 2 in front of MgO.

questions.question: A nurse prepares a saline mixture by dissolving 10 grams of salt in water to make 50 grams of total solution. The mass percent of salt in the solution is

answers.text: 10 percent, from 10 divided by 100
20 percent, from 10 divided by 50
5 percent, from 10 divided by 200
50 percent, from 50 divided by 100

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 20 percent, from 10 divided by 50. Mass percent equals the solute mass divided by the total solution mass, times 100: 10/50 x 100 = 20 percent.

questions.question: In some ecosystems, removing a single predator species causes the whole community to change drastically, even though the predator was never very numerous. Such a species is called what?

answers.text: A keystone species with an outsized effect on its community
A pioneer species that first colonizes a disturbed area
An invasive species that spreads rapidly in a new habitat
A producer species that forms the base of the food web

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A keystone species with an outsized effect on its community. Keystone species hold community structure together, often by keeping prey populations in check, so their loss triggers cascading changes.

questions.question: During a lesson on atomic structure, a student lists the charges of the three main particles. Which pairing is correct for the proton?

answers.text: The proton carries no electrical charge at all
The proton carries a positive electrical charge
The proton carries a negative electrical charge
The proton carries whichever charge balances the atom

questions.explanation: Correct answer: The proton carries a positive electrical charge. Protons carry a positive charge, electrons carry a negative charge, and neutrons carry none. A proton's charge is a fixed property and does not change to balance the atom.

questions.question: Read the paragraph. (1) Regular stretching improves flexibility over time. (2) It can also ease muscle tension after exercise. (3) Many athletes stretch before competitions. (4) My brother bought new running shoes last week. Which sentence does not belong in the paragraph?

answers.text: Regular stretching improves flexibility over time.
It can also ease muscle tension after exercise.
My brother bought new running shoes last week.
Many athletes stretch before competitions.

questions.explanation: Correct answer: My brother bought new running shoes last week. Sentences 1-3 all concern stretching, while sentence 4 about buying shoes is unrelated to the topic.

questions.question:
The City History Museum will open a special exhibit about river trade next month. The exhibit will run from March 4 through May 19 in the west gallery on the second floor. Admission to the exhibit is included with a regular museum ticket, which costs twelve dollars for adults and six dollars for children. On the first Sunday of each month, however, admission to the whole museum is free for city residents who show proof of address. School groups may book guided tours of the exhibit on weekday mornings by calling the education office at least two weeks ahead.

According to the passage, how much does a regular adult ticket cost?

answers.text: Twelve dollars for an adult regular museum ticket
Six dollars for an adult regular museum ticket
Ten dollars for an adult regular museum ticket
Eight dollars for an adult regular museum ticket

questions.explanation: Twelve dollars for an adult regular museum ticket. The passage gives the adult price as twelve dollars and the child price as six dollars. Exhibit admission is included with that regular ticket.

questions.question: A writer has finished a first draft and is now checking sentence structure, word choice, and punctuation before submitting the essay. Which stage of the writing process is the writer in?

answers.text: The editing stage of writing
The brainstorming stage of writing
The prewriting stage of writing
The publishing stage of writing

questions.explanation: The editing stage of writing. Editing focuses on correctness and polish at the sentence level near the end of the process. Prewriting and brainstorming happen before drafting begins.

hesi-a2.quiz_title: HESI A2 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is 1 1/4 x 2?
At standard pressure, pure water freezes and melts at the same temperature. That temperature is

answers.text: 0 degrees Celsius
100 degrees Celsius
32 degrees Celsius
212 degrees Celsius

questions.explanation: 0 degrees Celsius -- Pure water freezes and melts at 0 degrees Celsius at standard pressure; 100 degrees Celsius is its boiling point, and 32 and 212 are the Fahrenheit freezing and boiling points.

questions.question: The suffix '-osis' in 'cirrhosis' and 'neurosis' means

answers.text: a surgical removal
an inflammation
an abnormal condition
a written recording

questions.explanation: an abnormal condition — -osis means an abnormal condition: cirrhosis is an abnormal condition of the liver, and neurosis of the mind.

questions.question: A patient touches a hot pan and pulls the hand away before consciously feeling pain. This rapid response is an example of what?

answers.text: A reflex arc through the spinal cord
A reflex arc through the cerebrum
A reflex arc through the cerebellum
A reflex arc through the thalamus

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A reflex arc through the spinal cord. Reflex arcs route through the spinal cord, producing a fast involuntary response.

questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?

answers.text: neccessary
necesary
necessery
necessary

questions.explanation: Correct answer: necessary. Necessary is the correct spelling, with one c and double s.

questions.question: Passage: 'At the Redwood Wildlife Center, the busiest season is spring, when hikers and gardeners bring in baby owls that have fallen from their nests. Licensed rehabilitators examine each bird, feed it a diet close to what its parents would catch, and house it with other young owls so it learns to be an owl, not a pet. As the birds grow, they move to a large flight cage, where they must catch live prey and fly strongly before staff will consider release. In late summer, the center returns the young owls to the woods near where they were found. Most patients, staff say, survive because finders brought them in quickly instead of trying to raise them at home.' What is the main idea of the passage?

answers.text: Baby owls at the center are housed with other young owls so they learn to be owls, not pets
Young owls must catch live prey and fly strongly in a flight cage before staff release them
A wildlife center cares for young owls found out of their nests until they can be released into the woods
Most young owls survive because finders bring them to the center quickly in the spring

questions.explanation: A wildlife center cares for young owls found out of their nests until they can be released into the woods — the passage follows the whole process, from the owls' arrival through their care to their release in late summer.

questions.question: A bacterium's single circular DNA molecule is concentrated in one irregular region of the cell that is not enclosed by any membrane. This region is called the

answers.text: Nucleolus
Chromatin mass
Nuclear envelope
Nucleoid region

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Nucleoid region. Prokaryotic DNA sits in a nucleoid region with no surrounding membrane. A nucleolus is a dense body inside a eukaryotic nucleus, and a nuclear envelope is the membrane bacteria do not have.

questions.question: Solve for x: 2x + 6 = 26.
questions.explanation: 10 — Subtract 6 to get 2x = 20, then divide by 2: x = 10.

questions.question: An amoeba takes in tiny droplets of surrounding fluid, pinching them off in small vesicles rather than engulfing a solid particle. This form of bulk intake is called

answers.text: Phagocytosis
Pinocytosis
Exocytosis
Osmosis

questions.explanation: Pinocytosis — it is 'cell drinking' of fluid droplets; phagocytosis engulfs solids, and osmosis is water movement across a membrane.

questions.question: A weather report and a recipe both use the Fahrenheit scale. At standard pressure, pure water freezes at which temperature on that scale?

answers.text: 0 degrees Fahrenheit
50 degrees Fahrenheit
100 degrees Fahrenheit
32 degrees Fahrenheit

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 32 degrees Fahrenheit. Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit, which equals 0 degrees Celsius. Zero on the Fahrenheit scale is well below freezing, and 100 degrees Fahrenheit is hot weather, not a phase-change point.

questions.question: The root 'rhin-' in 'rhinitis' and 'rhinoplasty' refers to the

answers.text: ear
eye
nose
mouth

questions.explanation: nose — rhin- refers to the nose: rhinitis affects the nose, and rhinoplasty reshapes it.

questions.question: Near the ends of a long bone, bone tissue forms a lattice of thin plates with red marrow in the spaces, rather than a solid shell. This lattice tissue is

answers.text: Spongy bone forming an inner lattice
Compact bone forming an outer shell
Hyaline cartilage forming a joint cap
Fibrous tissue forming a bone covering

questions.explanation: Spongy bone forming an inner lattice — spongy (cancellous) bone is a lattice of trabeculae that keeps bone light while resisting stress, with marrow in its spaces.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Before the operation, anesthesia kept the patient from feeling any pain during surgery,' the word 'anesthesia' most nearly means

answers.text: a drug given to lower a patient's body temperature
a test used to measure a patient's lung capacity
a loss of feeling or sensation, often produced by drugs
a bandage applied to a wound after an operation

questions.explanation: Correct answer: a loss of feeling or sensation, often produced by drugs. Anesthesia is the drug-produced loss of sensation that allows surgery without pain.

questions.question: Each lung is wrapped in a double membrane whose slippery fluid lets the lung slide smoothly against the chest wall during breathing. What is this membrane called?

answers.text: The pericardium surrounding each lung
The peritoneum surrounding each lung
The meninges surrounding each lung
The pleura surrounding each lung

questions.explanation: The pleura surrounding each lung — the pleura is the serous membrane enclosing each lung within the thoracic cavity.

questions.question: In the sentence "He taught himself to juggle," what kind of pronoun is the word "himself"?

answers.text: Intensive pronoun
Possessive pronoun
Demonstrative pronoun
Reflexive pronoun

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Reflexive pronoun. Himself is a reflexive pronoun because it reflects the action of the verb back onto the subject, he.

questions.question: A patient had 62.40 mL of fluid and 28.75 mL was removed. How many milliliters remain?
A single base in a gene is substituted, and the codon still specifies the same amino acid as before, so the finished protein is completely unchanged. This kind of change is called a

answers.text: Silent mutation
Missense mutation
Nonsense mutation
Frameshift mutation

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Silent mutation. A silent mutation alters a codon without altering the amino acid. A missense mutation swaps one amino acid for another, a nonsense mutation creates an early stop, and a frameshift shifts the reading frame.

questions.question: In the sentence "Maria and Tomas volunteered, but the rain delayed the fair," what part of speech is the word "but"?

answers.text: conjunction
preposition
adverb
pronoun

questions.explanation: Correct answer: conjunction. But joins two complete clauses, so it is a conjunction.

questions.question: Passage: 'The Riverbend Community Choir accepts singers without auditions, a policy its director adopted so that anyone who enjoys singing can join. The choir's 80 members range from teenagers to an 87-year-old bass. Because members have widely different levels of experience, rehearsals spend extra time on difficult passages, and section leaders run optional practice sessions for newcomers. The choir performs three concerts a year, including a December concert where the audience is invited to sing along on familiar carols. Its director says the no-audition policy sometimes means the music must be chosen carefully, but she believes a choir that welcomes everyone serves the community better than a smaller, more selective one.' Which statement best summarizes the passage?

answers.text: The choir's director plans to begin holding auditions next year to raise the quality of its concerts.
Only singers with years of formal training are allowed to join the Riverbend Community Choir.
An unauditioned community choir welcomes singers of all ages and abilities and adapts its rehearsals and music choices to include them.
The choir performs a single concert each December for families of its eighty members.

questions.explanation: Correct answer: An unauditioned community choir welcomes singers of all ages and abilities and adapts its rehearsals and music choices to include them.. The summary joins the no-audition policy, the wide range of members, and the rehearsal and music adjustments that policy requires.

questions.question: Passage: 'The trail association installed a public bike repair station - an air pump, wrenches, and other basic tools secured to a post - at the busiest trailhead of the Cedar Creek Trail. In the first month, rangers noticed the station in use nearly every time they passed, often by riders fixing flat tires. A survey of trail users found that a quarter of riders had started carrying fewer tools of their own since the station appeared, trusting it would be there if needed. The association, encouraged by the response, plans two more stations but says each will need a volunteer assigned to check the tools weekly, because a station with missing or broken tools could leave a rider worse off than one who had brought their own.' Why does the association most likely want volunteers to check the new stations weekly?

answers.text: The station's tools are frequently stolen by visitors to the trail.
Riders have begun relying on the station instead of carrying their own tools.
Rangers on the trail have refused to maintain the repair stations.
The association plans to remove the first station at the trailhead.

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Riders have begun relying on the station instead of carrying their own tools.. Because a quarter of riders now carry fewer tools of their own, a broken or incomplete station would leave them worse off, so the tools must be checked.

nremt-emt.quiz_title: NREMT EMT Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A wheezing infant with heavy nasal secretions is suspected of having RSV, and you will suction the nose. Which protection fits best?

answers.text: Mask and gloves, adding a gown because secretions are copious
No protection, because infants cannot transmit respiratory viruses
A gown alone, because RSV spreads only through the skin surface
A fit-tested respirator alone, with bare hands for the suctioning

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Mask and gloves, adding a gown because secretions are copious — RSV spreads through droplets and contact with secretions, so mask and gloves — plus a gown when secretions are heavy — cover both routes.

questions.question: Your patient is on the far side of a divided highway and traffic between you is heavy and fast. How should you reach that patient?

answers.text: Have law enforcement walk you across one lane at a time while traffic continues in the others
Cross the lanes on foot during a gap in traffic, carrying the minimum of monitoring equipment
Cross in the ambulance slowly with lights on, expecting drivers to yield across all the lanes
Drive to the next interchange or authorized crossover and approach from the patient's own side

questions.explanation: Drive to the next interchange or authorized crossover and approach from the patient's own side — Crossing live high-speed lanes on foot or against flow is one of the deadliest acts at a highway scene; the longer driven route is the safe one.

questions.question: A nursing-home patient has scabies, with intense itching and burrow marks in the finger webs. Which protection fits this infestation?

answers.text: Gloves and a gown, avoiding prolonged skin-to-skin contact
A fit-tested respirator, because the mites travel through the air
A surgical mask only, because the mites spread in large droplets
No special protection, because scabies cannot pass between people

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Gloves and a gown, avoiding prolonged skin-to-skin contact — Scabies mites pass by direct skin contact and shared bedding, so contact precautions with gloves and a gown — not airborne or droplet protection — fit.

questions.question: While scanning the neck of a trauma patient, which set of findings are you specifically looking for?

answers.text: Carotid pulse equality, thyroid size, and swallowing ability now
Range of motion, muscle strength, and sensation in both arms
Pupil size, ear drainage, and bruising behind both of the ears
Jugular vein distension, tracheal position, and air under the skin

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Jugular vein distension, tracheal position, and air under the skin. The neck portion of the scan checks the neck veins, the trachea's midline position, and crepitus from subcutaneous air. Pupils and ears belong to the head check, and neck range of motion is not tested in trauma.

questions.question: An ALS-placed airway was working well, but you have just log-rolled and reloaded the patient onto the cot. What device check is required now?

answers.text: Skip rechecking because the device was confirmed before the move began
Confirm the device is secured and recheck after every patient move
Remove and refit the securing device only if the patient complains
Check the device again only when you arrive at the hospital bay

questions.explanation: Confirm the device is secured and recheck after every patient move. Movement can displace an airway; security and placement are rechecked after every move.

questions.question: A 10-month-old is checked while asleep: heart rate 132, refill under 2 seconds, warm pink skin, and he wakes alert and playful. How should this set be judged?

answers.text: Bradycardia, because infants must stay above 150 even in sleep
Adequate perfusion, with a sleeping rate expected for an infant
Poor perfusion, because a sleeping rate below 140 means weak flow
A concerning set, because playful waking follows poor perfusion

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Adequate perfusion, with a sleeping rate expected for an infant — Infant heart rates fall in sleep; 132 asleep with brisk refill, warm skin, and a playful waking state is an adequate-perfusion set.

questions.question: Responding with lights and siren, you approach a red light with crossing traffic that may not see you. What does the due-regard standard require?

answers.text: Slow or stop as needed at the red light despite lights and siren privileges
Proceed at speed because emergency privileges transfer right-of-way to you
Accelerate through quickly so your time in the intersection is shortest
Close your eyes to cross traffic and rely on the siren to warn them

questions.explanation: Slow or stop as needed at the red light despite lights and siren privileges. Emergency privileges are conditional; due regard requires slowing or stopping when traffic has not yielded.

questions.question: You applied a tourniquet to a thigh wound, but blood continues to pump from the wound at nearly the same rate. What is your NEXT action?

answers.text: Remove it and rely on direct pressure alone instead
Tighten the tourniquet until the bleeding stops completely
Wait five minutes to see whether bleeding slows itself
Loosen it briefly to let the trapped blood drain out

questions.explanation: Tighten the tourniquet until the bleeding stops completely. A tourniquet that is not tight enough can block veins while letting arterial blood in, worsening bleeding. It must be tightened until hemorrhage actually stops, and a second device placed above it if needed.

questions.question: A 50-year-old woman who takes insulin is sweaty, shaky, and confused but awake and able to swallow. Her glucose is low. What treatment is appropriate?

answers.text: Give oral glucose only if she falls asleep
Place glucose gel inside her cheek while lying flat
Give her insulin from her own pen injector
Give oral glucose by mouth as directed

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Give oral glucose by mouth as directed. Oral glucose is given to a conscious diabetic patient with low blood sugar who can swallow and protect her airway.

questions.question: A ventilator-dependent patient's tubing keeps catching on the stretcher rail during loading. What is the safest handling?

answers.text: Assign a crew member to manage the tubing and ventilations continuously during loading
Let the tubing drag, because ventilator tubing is designed to stretch without harm
Disconnect the tubing at the door and reconnect it once the patient is inside
Ask the patient to hold his own tubing so the crew can focus on the lift itself

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Assign a crew member to manage the tubing and ventilations continuously during loading — During loading, one person's job is the airway circuit — managing tubing and breaths while others move the stretcher.

questions.question: Minutes after delivery, a smooth round mass protrudes from the vagina, the fundus cannot be felt, and the mother shows signs of shock. What should you do?

answers.text: Do not push the mass back; cover it and transport rapidly
Push the uterus back inside firmly before it swells any further
Pull on the cord to draw the uterus back into its normal place
Massage the fundus hard through the abdomen until it returns

questions.explanation: Do not push the mass back; cover it and transport rapidly — This is a uterine inversion; replacing it is hospital care. Cover it with a moist sterile dressing, treat for shock, and transport immediately.

questions.question: A newborn's heart rate is 118 beats per minute after drying and stimulation, but she remains apneic with no respiratory effort. What should you do?

answers.text: A heart rate above 100 means no breathing help is needed at all
Flick the feet repeatedly for two minutes before trying ventilation
Begin ventilations, because apnea alone requires them despite the rate
Start compressions, because apnea in a newborn is treated as arrest

questions.explanation: Begin ventilations, because apnea alone requires them despite the rate — Apnea or gasping after the initial steps requires positive-pressure ventilation even when the heart rate is still above 100.

questions.question: A bleeding patient's first vitals are pulse 96, BP 118/76. Fifteen minutes later they are pulse 124, BP 96/70, with increasing anxiety. What does this trend MOST strongly indicate?

answers.text: His shock is progressing despite a still-measurable pressure
His condition is improving because his heart rate rose
His anxiety alone fully explains both sets of vitals
His bleeding has stopped because his pressure fell

questions.explanation: His shock is progressing despite a still-measurable pressure. A rising heart rate with a falling, narrowing blood pressure is the classic worsening-shock trend. A single normal-looking first reading should never override a deteriorating trend.

questions.question: A 6-year-old with a severe asthma history is found unresponsive, barely breathing, and then pulseless as you assess. What does pediatric arrest physiology demand in your sequence?

answers.text: Make effective ventilations a priority, because pediatric arrest is usually respiratory in cause
Use a compressions-only approach, because children's arrests are usually primary cardiac events
Delay ventilations until the AED has analyzed, because rhythm decides everything here
Give abdominal thrusts first, because a foreign body is the usual cause at this age

questions.explanation: Make effective ventilations a priority, because pediatric arrest is usually respiratory in cause. Most pediatric arrests follow respiratory failure, so restoring oxygenation with effective ventilations is central to the sequence rather than an afterthought.

questions.question: In the doorway you see a 2-year-old sitting silently in her mother's arms, staring ahead, not reaching for a toy or pushing you away as you approach. This appearance in a young child is:

answers.text: Reassuring, because quiet children are usually well children
Concerning, because a listless, uninterested child may be very ill
Normal, because toddlers rarely react to unfamiliar adults
A sign the child mainly needs a nap and fluids at home

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Concerning, because a listless, uninterested child may be very ill. In children, appearance is a key general impression element: a listless child who does not interact, reach, or resist examination may be seriously ill, whereas a crying, consolable, active child is usually less concerning.

questions.question: A 73-year-old woman in severe respiratory distress is placed on a nonrebreather mask. Which THREE actions are correct for this device? Select the three correct answers.

answers.text: Fill the reservoir bag before placing the mask
Set the flow rate at 10 to 15 liters per minute
Leave large gaps at the sides for fresh air
Make sure the reservoir bag stays partly inflated
Set the flow rate at 2 to 4 liters per minute

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Fill the reservoir bag before placing the mask; Set the flow rate at 10 to 15 liters per minute; Make sure the reservoir bag stays partly inflated. A nonrebreather runs at 10 to 15 liters per minute with the reservoir prefilled, and flow is adjusted so the bag does not fully collapse.

questions.question: An elderly patient with known poor leg circulation has slow refill in both feet but brisk refill at the fingertip, normal mentation, and warm hands. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: Slow foot refill alone proves he is in decompensated shock
Foot refill is the preferred shock test in vascular disease
His fingertip refill must be a false reading
It likely reflects his chronic leg circulation, not necessarily acute shock

questions.explanation: It likely reflects his chronic leg circulation, not necessarily acute shock — Chronic peripheral vascular disease delays foot refill at baseline; acute perfusion is judged from central signs, mentation, and unaffected sites.

questions.question: A patient with a fractured pelvis from a crush injury has a falling blood pressure and a rising heart rate but no external bleeding. Which shock type and priority BEST fit this picture?

answers.text: Neurogenic shock from spinal injury; no transport urgency
Cardiogenic shock from a heart attack; slow routine transport
Hypovolemic shock from hidden bleeding; rapid trauma-center transport
Anaphylactic shock from the crush injury; give oral fluids

questions.explanation: Hypovolemic shock from hidden bleeding; rapid trauma-center transport. The pelvis can hold a large volume of blood with no external sign, and the vital-sign trend shows decompensating blood loss. Warmth, oxygen, and minimal scene time are the EMT priorities.

questions.question: A patient consents to vital signs and an examination but clearly refuses a finger-stick glucose test. The EMT holds her hand still and performs the test anyway because it seems important. What legal problem does this create?

answers.text: Touching beyond the consent given can be battery, even in care
Consent to any one procedure covers every other procedure that day
Battery requires that the patient be physically injured by the touch
Refusal ends only when the crew judges the test important enough

questions.explanation: Touching beyond the consent given can be battery, even in care — Consent is specific; performing a refused procedure is an intentional unconsented touching, which is battery even when the intent was to help.

questions.question: From the doorway you see a 78-year-old man slumped sideways in a recliner. His skin looks gray, his mouth hangs open, and he does not look up when you call his name. Your initial general impression is that he is:

answers.text: Sick — this overall look demands immediate hands-on assessment
Apparently well and probably asleep after lunch
Stable, because no injury is visible from the door
Behavioral, because he is ignoring the crew's arrival

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Sick — this overall look demands immediate hands-on assessment. Posture, color, and lack of response combine into one impression: this patient looks seriously ill before any vital sign exists.

nremt-paramedic.quiz_title: NREMT Paramedic Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A 70 kg adult requires rocuronium for rapid sequence intubation at 1.2 mg per kilogram. What dose should be prepared?

answers.text: About 35 mg, from 70 kilograms multiplied by 0.5 milligrams
About 84 mg, from 70 kilograms multiplied by 1.2 milligrams
About 70 mg, from 70 kilograms multiplied by 1.0 milligrams
About 140 mg, from 70 kilograms multiplied by 2.0 milligrams

questions.explanation: Correct answer: About 84 mg, from 70 kilograms multiplied by 1.2 milligrams. Worked calculation: 70 kg x 1.2 mg/kg = 84 mg. The check is 70 x 1.2 = 70 + 14 = 84. Rocuronium needs the higher 1.2 mg/kg dose to approach succinylcholine's onset speed for a true rapid sequence technique.

questions.question: A deceased patient's 8-year-old child asks whether her father is dead. With the mother's agreement, what is the appropriate approach?

answers.text: Tell the child her father is sleeping and will wake up later
Refuse to answer and change the subject to something cheerful
Answer honestly in simple, age-appropriate words she understands
Give the child the full clinical details of the resuscitation

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Answer honestly in simple, age-appropriate words she understands. With a parent's agreement, answer honestly in simple, age-appropriate words she understands, such as that his body stopped working and he died. Euphemisms like 'sleeping' can frighten or mislead a young child.

questions.question: Which finding set best supports oliguric acute kidney injury in a transported adult?

answers.text: A single large urine void immediately after a fluid bolus
Scant urine output over many hours with rising waste products
Frequent urination of large volumes throughout the night
Clear pale urine produced at a normal hourly rate

questions.explanation: Scant urine output over many hours with rising waste products. Oliguria sustained over hours, paired with accumulating urea and creatinine and often potassium and acidosis, defines the oliguric pattern the crew should report and monitor.

questions.question: Which findings in a patient with low back pain form the cauda equina pattern that demands an emergent pathway? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Pain that is worse after a long day of standing
New urinary retention or overflow incontinence
Bilateral leg weakness or numbness
Saddle anaesthesia in the perineal region
A single episode of pain on bending to lift

questions.explanation: Correct answer: New urinary retention or overflow incontinence; Bilateral leg weakness or numbness; Saddle anaesthesia in the perineal region. Cauda equina compression announces itself below the lesion: saddle anaesthesia, bladder dysfunction, and bilateral leg signs. Those three together convert back pain from a common complaint into a surgical clock. Unilateral, posture-related pain without neurologic or bladder findings is the far commoner, far less urgent pattern.

questions.question: A team leader opens a goals-of-care conversation with a seriously ill patient. Which opening best serves the conversation?

answers.text: Ask only yes-or-no questions so the conversation finishes as quickly as possible
Announce the crew's recommended treatment ceiling before the patient says anything at all
Ask what the patient understands about their illness and what matters most to them now
Direct every question to the family, because the patient is too ill to have views

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Ask what the patient understands about their illness and what matters most to them now. Effective goals-of-care conversations begin with the patient's own understanding and values, because acceptable treatment can only be defined against what the patient is hoping for and what they fear. Leading with the clinician's ceiling turns a dialogue about the person's priorities into a negotiation about the service's plan.

questions.question: Pacing spikes appear without capture. Output has been increased and fresh pads are firmly applied, yet capture is still absent, and another monitor with pacing capability is available. What is the next troubleshooting step?

answers.text: Assume the patient cannot be paced by any device
Sedate the patient more deeply and reassess later
Check and replace the pacing cable and device connections
Turn the pacing rate down to the lowest setting

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Check and replace the pacing cable and device connections. When output and pads have been addressed, the remaining link in the chain is hardware: check and replace the pacing cable and device connections, or swap to the other monitor. A fractured cable or loose connector produces exactly this picture of spikes that never reach the patient.

questions.question: A worker is down inside a permit-required confined space, and coworkers want the paramedic crew to climb in immediately. What must happen before any entry?

answers.text: One crew member enters alone quickly while the other watches
The space is tested for atmosphere and a trained rescue plan is in place
The space is assumed safe because the worker entered it earlier
Entry is safe whenever the patient can still be heard calling out

questions.explanation: The space is tested for atmosphere and a trained rescue plan is in place. Confined-space entry requires atmospheric testing, ventilation as needed, trained and equipped rescuers, and an attendant and retrieval plan; an unprotected entry is how rescuers become second victims.

questions.question: A post-ROSC patient is comatose with an oxygen saturation of 100 percent on a nonrebreather. What oxygenation target should guide titration?

answers.text: Keep saturation at 100 percent for at least the first full hour
Reduce oxygen until saturation falls below 88 percent consistently
Titrate oxygen down to keep saturation about 92 to 98 percent
Remove oxygen entirely once a pulse has returned after arrest

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Titrate oxygen down to keep saturation about 92 to 98 percent. After ROSC, avoid both hypoxia and prolonged hyperoxia, which is associated with worse outcomes. Titrate inspired oxygen to maintain saturation roughly 92 to 98 percent.

questions.question: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis is tachycardic, hypotensive, and breathing deeply and rapidly. What is the FIRST treatment priority?

answers.text: An insulin infusion started before any fluids are given
IV fluid resuscitation to restore perfusion
Sodium bicarbonate to correct the acidemia directly
A benzodiazepine to slow the respiratory rate

questions.explanation: Correct answer: IV fluid resuscitation to restore perfusion. IV fluid resuscitation to restore perfusion. In DKA, volume depletion drives the shock state, so isotonic fluids come first; insulin follows per protocol/medical direction, and bicarbonate is not a field treatment for the acidosis.

questions.question: A patient with hemophilia who has just been injured keeps his own factor concentrate at home and asks whether to bring it. What is the best guidance?

answers.text: Bring the factor supply and its dosing information along
Take a double dose at home and then decline transport
Leave the factor at home; hospitals refuse outside supplies
Discard expired-looking boxes before the crew documents them

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Bring the factor supply and its dosing information along. Patients are commonly prescribed home factor for exactly these events, and bringing the supply with its concentration and dosing card can save critical time if the receiving facility's stock differs. The crew documents what the patient has and contacts the receiving team or hematology service early.

questions.question: A toddler is brought in four hours after swallowing iron tablets: she vomited twice with streaks of blood, but for the last hour she has seemed settled and playful. Why should the crew resist reassurance?

answers.text: The vomiting phase is the final stage, after which recovery is guaranteed and complete
Iron poisoning classically has a deceptive quiet latent phase before systemic toxicity declares itself
A settled period after iron ingestion proves the tablets have passed harmlessly through
Iron tablets only ever cause local stomach irritation and never systemic harm at all

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Iron poisoning classically has a deceptive quiet latent phase before systemic toxicity declares itself. After the initial corrosive gastrointestinal phase, iron poisoning often enters a latent interval of apparent recovery while absorbed iron is injuring the liver, heart, and vasculature; shock and metabolic acidosis can follow. Apparent wellness a few hours after a significant ingestion is a documented trap, not a discharge criterion.

questions.question: A patient's EtCO2 during CPR has been 12 mmHg and abruptly rises to 38 mmHg while compressions continue. This change most likely indicates what?

answers.text: Return of spontaneous circulation has occurred just now
The endotracheal tube has become dislodged from the trachea
The compressor is pressing too deeply on the chest wall
The capnography sensor has failed and should be removed

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Return of spontaneous circulation has occurred just now. An abrupt sustained rise in EtCO2 during CPR reflects restored pulmonary blood flow and is a recognized early sign of return of spontaneous circulation, prompting a rhythm and pulse check.

questions.question: A patient has a segment of chest wall that moves inward on inspiration and outward on expiration, with severe pain and hypoxia. Which care is most appropriate?

answers.text: Bind the whole chest tightly with a wide elastic wrap
Splint the segment by pressing a heavy sandbag onto it
Delay ventilation until the patient reaches the trauma center
Provide positive-pressure ventilation and adequate analgesia

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Provide positive-pressure ventilation and adequate analgesia. Provide positive-pressure ventilation and adequate analgesia. Paradoxical motion defines flail chest, and the underlying pulmonary contusion plus pain drive hypoxia; positive-pressure ventilation acts as an internal splint, while circumferential binding and sandbags worsen ventilation.

questions.question: A ventilated patient with obstructive disease has breath stacking from incomplete exhalation. The inspiratory flow rate is currently slow, prolonging each inspiration. Adjusting flow in which direction best lengthens exhalation time?

answers.text: Decrease flow so inspiration lasts longer
Leave flow unchanged and raise the rate
Match flow exactly to the respiratory rate
Increase flow so inspiration ends sooner

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Increase flow so inspiration ends sooner — A faster inspiratory flow delivers the tidal volume in less time, leaving a larger share of each cycle for exhalation. Slowing flow or raising the rate does the opposite and worsens stacking in obstructive disease.

questions.question: At a bus crash, a patient with a minor hand laceration walks to the treatment area on request and is alert with normal breathing and perfusion. Which START category applies?

answers.text: Immediate (red), because every patient from a bus crash is tagged red
Delayed (yellow), because any bleeding at all requires a yellow tag
Minimal (green), because the patient can walk and has no RPM abnormality
Expectant (black), because walking patients are assumed to be uninjured

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Minimal (green), because the patient can walk and has no RPM abnormality. START begins by directing everyone who can walk to a designated area, and those patients are categorized minimal (green) pending later re-triage. Walking wounded are not automatically red for mechanism, nor assumed uninjured; they are rechecked after the RPM-based triage of non-walking patients.

questions.question: A 9-month-old with bronchiolitis has repeated apneic pauses of about fifteen seconds with desaturation. What is the priority action?

answers.text: Give nebulized albuterol and reassess in thirty minutes
Support ventilation with a bag-mask device as needed
Give a fluid bolus and observe for spontaneous recovery
Place the infant prone and stimulate the feet repeatedly

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Support ventilation with a bag-mask device as needed. Apnea in a young infant with bronchiolitis requires the crew to support ventilation with a bag-mask device as needed, with preparation for an advanced airway if pauses persist. Bronchodilators do not treat bronchiolitis apnea.

questions.question: An LVAD patient's wife, who manages his driveline dressings and batteries daily, offers detailed information about his device and baseline. How should the crew leader use her?

answers.text: Hand her the monitor and ask her to run the resuscitation
Ask her to leave the room so the crew can work undisturbed
Ignore her input because family observations are never reliable
Treat her as an expert resource and include her in the plan

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Treat her as an expert resource and include her in the plan. LVAD caregivers are formally trained on the device and often know its normal sounds, alarm history, and the patient's baseline better than any responder; including them improves assessment and continuity. She remains a resource and historian, while clinical tasks stay with the crew.

questions.question: A patient's limb strength paradoxically improves after brief repeated activity, and he also reports a very dry mouth and constipation. Which neuromuscular disorder does this pattern favour over myasthenia gravis?

answers.text: Lambert-Eaton syndrome, where activity briefly boosts strength
Myasthenia gravis, where activity briefly boosts strength
Botulism, where activity briefly boosts strength by toxin
Tick paralysis, where activity removes the attached tick

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Lambert-Eaton syndrome, where activity briefly boosts strength. In Lambert-Eaton syndrome, brief exercise transiently increases acetylcholine release at the presynaptic terminal, so strength improves with activity, the mirror image of myasthenic fatigability. Autonomic features such as dry mouth are common, and the syndrome is often associated with small-cell lung cancer.

questions.question: A 25-kilogram child with a displaced forearm fracture has no IV access, and ketamine is ordered intramuscularly at 4 milligrams per kilogram. What dose should be drawn up? Show the calculation in your reasoning.

answers.text: 100 milligrams, from 4 times 25 kilograms
250 milligrams, from 10 times 25 kilograms
40 milligrams, from 4 times 10 kilograms
10 milligrams, from 4 divided by 25 kilograms

questions.explanation: Correct answer: 100 milligrams, from 4 times 25 kilograms. The calculation is 4 mg/kg x 25 kg = 100 mg IM. Intramuscular dissociative dosing is higher per kilogram than intravenous dosing, which is why the per-kilogram figure looks large; dividing by the weight or borrowing an adult weight produces the dangerous distractors.

questions.question: A nursing facility sends a patient out for 'weakness', but on arrival the crew finds a stage-deep sacral wound, fever, and confusion. The facility resists the crew's suggestion of the hospital's sepsis pathway. What is the crew's correct position?

answers.text: The sending facility's preference legally overrides the crew's assessment in all transfer disputes
Confusion and fever in a facility patient are always baseline and need no escalation at all
The crew must return the patient to her room if the facility objects to the sepsis pathway
The patient's clinical cues, not the sending facility's preference, drive destination and notification decisions

questions.explanation: Correct answer: The patient's clinical cues, not the sending facility's preference, drive destination and notification decisions. Interfacility loyalty never outranks the patient in front of the crew: fever, confusion, and an infected deep wound are sepsis cues that demand the sepsis destination and notification. The disagreement is documented factually and escalated through medical control if it persists.

aswb-masters.quiz_title: ASWB Masters Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Field instructors preparing interns for a trauma-clinic placement BEST reduce secondary-trauma risk by:

answers.text: Assigning a full trauma caseload immediately so interns adapt quickly
Educating interns about secondary stress before exposure, staging caseload intensity, and scheduling reflective supervision from the start
Advising interns to keep reactions to themselves to appear professional
Waiting until an intern shows symptoms before mentioning the risk

questions.explanation: Prevention for trainees mirrors prevention for staff: anticipatory education, graded exposure, and structured reflection, arranged before harm rather than after. Immersion without preparation maximizes dose at minimum experience, silence norms suppress help-seeking, and symptom-triggered education arrives too late for the first affected intern.

questions.question: Arriving unannounced for an investigation, a worker sees a father stiffen and block the doorway. The worker can BEST use authority responsibly by:

answers.text: Telling the father that blocking the door will count against him
Entering quickly while he is deciding how to respond
Stating the purpose of the visit, the family's rights, and what will happen next before asking to enter
Leaving without explanation so the family calms down

questions.explanation: Explaining purpose, rights, and next steps makes state authority transparent and lowers the coercion the family reasonably feels. Threatening consequences for hesitation abuses the power gap, entering without clear consent escalates risk for everyone, and unexplained departure leaves the family in fearful uncertainty.

questions.question: A practitioner completing a biopsychosocial assessment of a client with chronic pain and depression should gather information that includes:

answers.text: Only the client's medical diagnoses and current medications
Only the client's childhood history and family relationships
Biological factors such as health and sleep, psychological factors such as coping and beliefs, and social factors such as work, relationships, and resources
Only standardized test scores, which summarize the other domains

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial model is defined by its three interacting domains: bodily health, inner experience and coping, and the social environment of relationships, work, and resources. Any single-domain version — medical facts alone, history alone, or test scores alone — abandons the model, because each domain can drive or relieve problems in the others.

questions.question: A client taking a prescribed SSRI mentions starting St. John's wort from a health store. The worker should:

answers.text: Encourage it as a natural complement
Advise stopping the SSRI since the supplement is safer
Document it without mentioning it to anyone
Explain the risk of excessive serotonin effects from combining them and urge prompt discussion with the prescriber and pharmacist

questions.explanation: St. John's wort has serotonergic activity, and combining it with an SSRI can produce serotonin toxicity, so prompt prescriber and pharmacist involvement is the safe response. Encouraging the combination invites the interaction, advising discontinuation of the prescribed drug exceeds scope, and silent documentation leaves the risk unaddressed.

questions.question: Invited to testify on a proposed cut to a state respite program, a worker prepares testimony. The MOST effective advocacy content combines:

answers.text: Aggregated service data showing impact with a brief account from an affected caregiver illustrating the numbers
Only the worker's personal opinion that the cut feels wrong
A detailed clinical history of one client, shared without that client's consent
Threats that agency staff will refuse to implement any cut

questions.explanation: Effective legislative advocacy pairs population-level evidence with a representative human story, offered with consent. Personal opinion alone lacks weight, disclosing a client's history without consent violates confidentiality, and threats of non-implementation exceed the worker's role and credibility.

questions.question: Turnover spikes on a unit where caseloads doubled and supervision was cut. Leadership asks what would MOST address the burnout pattern. The worker should recommend:

answers.text: Structural changes such as manageable caseloads, restored supervision, and recovery time
Telling staff to become more resilient without changing conditions
Replacing burned-out staff with new graduates
Adding a pizza lunch each month

questions.explanation: Burnout research reflected in NASW self-care guidance treats workload, control, and support as organizational drivers; structural fixes target causes. Resilience messaging alone shifts system problems onto individuals. Replacing staff repeats the cycle. Occasional perks do not alter the conditions producing exhaustion.

questions.question: Parents in a mixed-status family avoid applying for nutrition benefits their citizen children qualify for, fearing consequences for themselves. The worker should:

answers.text: Apply on the family's behalf without their knowledge to secure the benefit
Confirm that applying will definitely harm the parents' prospects
Give accurate information distinguishing the children's eligibility from the parents' status, explain what information the application actually requires, and respect the family's decision
Report the family's status to the benefits office to clarify eligibility

questions.explanation: Policy practice here is precision: eligible children are not barred by their parents' status, applications require defined information, and the family decides with facts rather than rumor. Applying secretly violates consent, blanket warnings may be inaccurate and deterrent, and reporting the family destroys trust and exceeds any duty.

questions.question: Mr. Osei, 79, lives amid spoiled food and unpaid bills, has lost weight, and refuses home help, saying he manages fine. His adult son lives nearby and visits weekly. Assessment should distinguish:

answers.text: Elder abuse by the son, proven by the home's condition
Normal aging, since most older adults live this way
Financial exploitation, since bills are unpaid
Self-neglect by the older adult himself from neglect by a caregiver responsible for his care

questions.explanation: Self-neglect and caregiver neglect carry different interventions and legal framings, so assessment starts by identifying whose behavior is producing the risk. The son's visits alone do not prove abusive conduct, most older adults do not live in hazardous decline, and unpaid bills signal capacity and resource questions rather than theft.

questions.question: A clinician routinely asks clients to rate progress and the working relationship, then changes course when ratings stall. This practice primarily serves to:

answers.text: Involve the client as an active monitor whose feedback reshapes the plan
Prove the chosen model is being delivered correctly
Satisfy documentation requirements for the chart
Replace the need for a formal treatment plan

questions.explanation: Routine outcome and alliance feedback makes the client a co-monitor of the work, and acting on stalled ratings is a concrete form of client involvement in planning. The ratings are not merely paperwork, they do not by themselves establish model fidelity, and they supplement rather than replace a formal plan.

questions.question: During a joint interview, one partner answers every question, including those directed at the other, who sits silently. To assess both perspectives, the worker should FIRST:

answers.text: Continue with the talkative partner, since the quiet partner can speak at the next session
Ask the talkative partner to leave the room for the remainder of the interview
Name the pattern kindly and invite the quieter partner to respond to the next question before discussion opens up
Ask the talkative partner why they feel the need to control the conversation

questions.explanation: Gently structuring turn-taking lets each partner's perspective enter the assessment while keeping both engaged. Deferring the quieter partner loses present data, removing a partner and interpreting motives both escalate defensiveness before basic information is gathered.

questions.question: Everything feels like one huge problem to a client facing debt, eviction risk, and a child's truancy. Which contracting technique should the worker use FIRST?

answers.text: Write one contract covering all three problems with a single thirty-day deadline
Partialize the concerns into separate, ranked problems and contract around one manageable piece at a time
Ask the client to choose which problem the worker will solve entirely for her
Postpone contracting until the client feels calmer about the overall situation

questions.explanation: Partializing breaks an overwhelming whole into workable parts, making contracting and early success possible. A single all-problem contract with one deadline recreates the overwhelm, solving a problem entirely for her removes her participation, and waiting for calm delays the structure that itself reduces distress.

questions.question: Two clinicians independently rating the same recorded intake interviews assign very different severity scores. Supervisor Elena concludes the rating procedure most needs attention to which property?

answers.text: Test-retest stability over a two-week interval
Agreement among different raters using the same procedure
Ability to predict future hospitalization
Coverage of all relevant symptom domains in the items

questions.explanation: When independent raters scoring identical material disagree, the concern is interrater reliability, meaning consistency across observers. Stability over time, prediction of a future criterion, and breadth of item coverage address different measurement properties that would not explain simultaneous rater disagreement.

questions.question: Both a client's health plan and a grant program could pay for the same session, and a biller suggests submitting to both to 'use up the grant.' The worker should:

answers.text: Agree, because total payment still feels modest
Submit to the grant only and hide the health plan claim
Alternate payers by month without telling either
Refuse duplicate payment for a single service and coordinate benefits so each payer is billed appropriately and transparently

questions.explanation: Duplicate billing for one service is double payment for a single unit of care, prohibited by billing integrity standards regardless of the amounts involved. Coordination of benefits exists precisely to allocate payment openly. Concealment from either payer is the feature that makes each variant improper.

questions.question: A teenager damaged a neighbor's fence during a dispute; the neighbor is angry, the teenager's parent wants consequences, and both households agree to try a community conference. What is essential for the process to be restorative?

answers.text: The neighbor agrees in advance to drop all anger as a condition of attending
The teenager's parent delivers the apology on the teenager's behalf to save time
The conference focuses on setting a punishment the neighbor finds satisfying
The teenager hears the damage's impact, takes responsibility, and agrees to specific amends such as repair work or restitution, with follow-up

questions.explanation: Restorative practice centers the harmed person's experience, the responsible person's own acknowledgment, and agreed amends that are actually completed. Pre-scripted forgiveness, a proxy apology, or punishment selection each remove one of those elements and turn the conference into either pressure or sentencing.

questions.question: Jamal, 16, gives one-word answers and stares at the floor during a school meeting. Which approach is MOST likely to engage him?

answers.text: Ask his mother to answer on his behalf
Fill silences quickly with the worker's own examples
Confront the silence as resistance that must be addressed
Use open-ended prompts paired with supportive silence

questions.explanation: Open prompts with tolerant silence reduce pressure and signal respect for an adolescent's pace, supporting engagement. Labeling silence as resistance risks shaming, having a parent answer undermines the youth's voice, and filling silence centers the worker rather than the client.

questions.question: Since reaching her goals, a client has weathered a job loss using her coping plan, kept her routines, and sought support early rather than decompensating. For termination readiness, this is significant because:

answers.text: It proves she will not need help in any future crisis
It shows the worker can stop documenting her progress
Job loss automatically qualifies a client for discharge
Her gains have been tested under genuine stress and held, with help-seeking used appropriately
