e / 2 and e / 3, from using the power instead of its factorial
1 / 2 and 1 / 6, from evaluating the derivatives at zero instead

questions.explanation: Every derivative of e^x at the center a = 1 equals e, and the Taylor coefficient of (x - 1)^k is that derivative divided by k factorial. This gives e/2! = e/2 and e/3! = e/6.

questions.question: For which exponent does the p-series sum 1/n^p diverge in the case p = 1/2?

answers.text: It diverges since p <= 1
It converges since p > 0, and any positive exponent is enough for convergence of a p-series
It converges to 2, since the exponent 1/2 is applied in reverse to produce the sum
It diverges only at p = 1, so every other positive exponent gives a convergent series

questions.explanation: A p-series converges exactly when p > 1; with p = 1/2 <= 1 the series diverges.

questions.question: A spherical balloon's radius is increasing at (1/2) cm/s. How fast is its volume increasing when the radius is 3 cm?

answers.text: 6pi cm^3/s
18pi cm^3/s
36pi cm^3/s
18pi cm^3/s plus 4pi cm^3/s

questions.explanation: V = (4/3)pi r^3, so dV/dt = 4pi r^2 (dr/dt) = 4pi(9)(1/2) = 18pi cm^3/s.

questions.question: A tank 2 feet tall has horizontal slices of volume 4 dy cubic feet at height y, the water weighs 50 pounds per cubic foot, and each slice must be lifted (2 - y) feet to the top. Find the work to empty the tank.
questions.explanation: Each slice weighs 50 * 4 dy = 200 dy pounds and is lifted (2 - y) feet, so work is integral from 0 to 2 of 200(2 - y) dy. Evaluating gives 200(4 - 2) = 400.

questions.question: Let C be given by r(t) =  for 0 <= t <= 1. What is the line integral of f(x, y) = x + y along C with respect to arc length?

answers.text: sqrt(2)
2 sqrt(2)

questions.explanation: Here ds = sqrt(2) dt and x + y = 2t, so the integral is sqrt(2) times the integral of 2t from 0 to 1, which is sqrt(2) * 1 = sqrt(2).

intro-psychology.quiz_title: Introductory Psychology Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: If adopted children resemble their biological parents more than their adoptive parents on a trait, that pattern most directly suggests:

answers.text: A genetic influence on the trait
That the trait is entirely determined at birth
That adoptive homes were unusually uniform
That adoption has no environmental effect

questions.explanation: Adoption studies separate heredity from shared home environment; resemblance to biological parents points toward genetic influence.

questions.question: To untangle genetic and environmental influences, behavior geneticists rely most heavily on studies of:

answers.text: Single case studies
Opinion surveys
Brain imaging alone
Twins and adopted individuals

questions.explanation: Twin and adoption studies are the core methods of behavior genetics because they allow comparisons that separate shared genes from shared environments.

questions.question: Staring at a green flag for a minute and then looking at white paper produces a reddish afterimage. This phenomenon is best explained by:

answers.text: trichromatic theory alone
place theory
opponent-process theory
frequency theory

questions.explanation: Opponent-process theory proposes opposing red-green, blue-yellow, and black-white processes; fatiguing one side of a pair produces an afterimage in the opponent color.

questions.question: In Freud's theory, the remembered storyline of a dream is its manifest content, while the hidden, disguised wishes it expresses are its:

answers.text: activation pattern
information-processing record
latent content
consolidated memory trace

questions.explanation: Freud viewed dreams as a royal road to the unconscious: the manifest storyline disguises latent content, often driven by unacceptable wishes.

questions.question: According to activation-synthesis theory, dreams arise when the sleeping brain tries to make a story out of:

answers.text: random neural activation originating in the brainstem
accurately replayed video-like memories
signals sent by other sleeping people
suppressed wishes decoded by symbols

questions.explanation: Activation-synthesis theory says REM sleep triggers neural activity that the cortex synthesizes into dreams, giving them a makeshift, bizarre character.

questions.question: When stimulation reaches a minimum threshold, a neuron fires at full strength; stronger stimulation does not make that single impulse stronger. This describes the action potential's:

answers.text: graded response that grows with input
partial firing proportional to stimulus size
continuous leak of charge
all-or-none response

questions.explanation: An action potential is all-or-none: once threshold is reached the neuron fires fully, and intensity is instead coded by firing rate and number of neurons.

questions.question: A drug eases pain because its molecules closely resemble endorphins and activate the same receptors, increasing their activity. In pharmacology terms, this drug is an:

answers.text: agonist
antagonist
reuptake pump
enzyme that destroys receptors

questions.explanation: Agonists increase a neurotransmitter's action by mimicking it or by blocking its reuptake so it stays active longer.

questions.question: A poison causes paralysis because its molecules occupy acetylcholine receptors and prevent the real messenger from acting, without activating the receptors themselves. This poison acts as an:

answers.text: agonist
antagonist
second messenger
growth hormone

questions.explanation: Antagonists block or decrease a neurotransmitter's action by occupying receptors or preventing its release, without mimicking it.

questions.question: Much of the cortex does not receive sensory input or trigger movement directly, yet damage there can disrupt thinking, remembering, and speaking. These regions are the:

answers.text: primary sensory areas
association areas
brainstem relay areas
reflex arcs

questions.explanation: Association areas integrate information from different senses and link it with memories and actions, supporting higher mental functions.

questions.question: In a dark, silent room, a researcher finds the faintest tone that Nadia can detect on exactly half the trials. That minimum stimulation is her:

answers.text: difference threshold
terminal threshold
absolute threshold
subliminal prime

questions.explanation: The absolute threshold is the minimum stimulation needed to detect a stimulus 50 percent of the time.

questions.question: Young-Helmholtz theory proposes that color vision arises from three types of cones, each sensitive mainly to one range of wavelengths. Those three ranges correspond to:

answers.text: red-green, blue-yellow, and black-white pairs
red, green, and blue light
hue, saturation, and brightness
rods, cones, and ganglion cells

questions.explanation: Trichromatic theory holds that the retina contains three types of color receptors sensitive to red, green, and blue, whose combined activity produces all hues.

questions.question: Even in a windowless lab, volunteers' body temperature and alertness rise and fall on a roughly 24-hour cycle, reset each day by light. This internal clock is the:

answers.text: sleep cycle of 90 minutes
circadian rhythm
REM rebound cycle
ultradian rhythm of dreaming

questions.explanation: The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour biological clock, regulating temperature, alertness, and sleepiness, and it is tuned by light exposure.

questions.question: A lab studies only how often a rat presses a lever after different reward schedules, deliberately avoiding any claims about the rat's thoughts. This restriction to observable events defines:

answers.text: Cognitive psychology
Psychoanalytic theory
Humanistic psychology
Behaviorism

questions.explanation: Behaviorism redefined psychology as the scientific study of observable behavior and rejected reliance on unobservable mental processes.

questions.question: A clinician explains a patient's depression by considering brain chemistry, negative thought patterns, and a recent loss of social support together. The clinician is using:

answers.text: The behaviorist approach alone
The structuralist approach
The biopsychosocial approach
A single-level explanation

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial approach integrates biological, psychological, and social-cultural levels of analysis instead of relying on one factor alone.

questions.question: Regular brisk walking and cycling are associated with lower depression and anxiety, better stress management, and increased longevity. Such sustained activity that raises heart rate is called:

answers.text: Aerobic exercise
Anaerobic resistance only
Biofeedback training
The general adaptation syndrome

questions.explanation: Aerobic exercise — sustained activity that increases heart and lung fitness — is linked to reduced stress, depression, and anxiety and to longer life.

questions.question: A treatment pairs drinking alcohol with a drug that produces nausea, so that alcohol itself begins to trigger an unpleasant reaction. Substituting a negative reaction for a previously attractive one is:

answers.text: aversive conditioning
systematic desensitization
unconditional positive regard
cognitive restructuring

questions.explanation: Aversive conditioning uses classical conditioning to create an unpleasant response to a harmful stimulus or habit.

questions.question: To decide quickly whether a robin, a penguin, and an ostrich all belong in the same group despite looking very different, a person relies on a mental grouping of similar objects or events called a:

answers.text: heuristic that guarantees a correct answer
phoneme
concept
standard deviation

questions.explanation: Concepts are mental groupings of similar objects, events, ideas, or people that simplify thinking. Category membership lets us generalize knowledge to new instances.

questions.question: To treat a fear of flying, a therapist has a client repeatedly confront flight-related experiences, first in imagination and later on an actual short flight, until the fear response weakens. The core method here is:

answers.text: free association
rational-emotive disputing
transference interpretation
exposure therapy

questions.explanation: Exposure therapies treat anxiety by having clients confront feared objects or situations so the conditioned fear response can diminish.

questions.question: A hired driver deliberately blocks a rival company's truck solely to make its driver furious and frightened, gaining nothing material from the act. Aggression whose primary aim is to inflict harm or pain, rather than to obtain something, is classified as:

answers.text: instrumental aggression
hostile aggression
assertive behavior
altruistic aggression

questions.explanation: Hostile aggression springs from anger and aims at harm itself; instrumental aggression aims at a further goal, such as money or status, with harm as a means.

questions.question: A therapist first teaches a client deep muscle relaxation, builds a ranked list of feared situations from least to most frightening, and then pairs relaxation with each step in turn. This procedure is:

answers.text: aversive conditioning
a token economy
systematic desensitization
electroconvulsive therapy

questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization is a type of exposure in which a pleasant, relaxed state is gradually associated with increasing levels of a feared stimulus.

questions.question: What is betterment in the context of a Part D repair?

answers.text: A penalty the insurer charges for filing a second claim, even if the result in a neighboring line of coverage, such as a related endorsement, might differ
A discount the repair shop gives the insurer
The increase in premium after an accident
An improvement in the auto's condition or value because new parts replace older worn parts during a covered repair

questions.explanation: Betterment describes the windfall avoided when new parts replace worn ones, leaving the auto better than it was before the loss. It is a settlement concept, not a premium or penalty term.

questions.question: Under model unfair claims concepts, after an insurer receives notice of a claim, its first communications duty is to do what?

answers.text: Admit that the loss is covered in full
Wait until the insured hires an attorney before responding
Close the claim if no lawsuit has been filed
Acknowledge receipt of the claim promptly

questions.explanation: Prompt acknowledgment tells the claimant the claim was received and is being handled. Acknowledgment is not an admission of coverage, which is why the promise-to-pay distractor is wrong.

questions.question: How does contributory negligence differ from comparative negligence at the most basic level?

answers.text: Contributory negligence reduces the award, while comparative negligence bars it entirely
Contributory negligence either allows full recovery or bars it entirely, while comparative negligence reduces the award by the claimant's share of fault
Contributory negligence applies only to property damage, while comparative negligence applies only to injury
The two rules are identical and differ only in name

questions.explanation: The two systems answer the same question in opposite ways: contributory is all-or-nothing, comparative apportions. Reversing those descriptions is the classic confusion this item tests.

questions.question: An insured pays the first premium for a new policy. In unilateral-contract terms, what has the insured done?

answers.text: Made a counteroffer to the insurer
Accepted the insurer's promise by performance, completing the exchange without making a return promise to pay all future premiums
Drafted a contract of adhesion
Promised to insure with the same insurer for life with that insurer, renewing automatically for life and binding the insured's heirs to keep the same coverage in force

questions.explanation: Paying the premium is performance that accepts the insurer's standing promise; it is not a counteroffer because the terms are taken as offered. The insured does not thereby promise lifetime renewals.

questions.question: When can a mobile or manufactured home fit the dwelling program?

answers.text: Never, under any placement or condition
Whenever it still has wheels and a trailer hitch attached and can be towed away from the site where it is currently parked
When it is permanently attached to a foundation, where that placement makes it eligible under the program
Only while it is being transported on a highway

questions.explanation: Foundation placement is the key eligibility fact for a mobile or manufactured home in the dwelling program. A unit in transit or still set up as a vehicle does not present the same fixed-location dwelling risk.

questions.question: Under the traditional collateral source rule, how are benefits a plaintiff receives from an independent source treated?

answers.text: They convert the claim into a nominal damages case
They are paid over to the defendant as a credit
They do not reduce the damages the defendant must pay for the harm caused
They are subtracted dollar for dollar from the defendant's liability

questions.explanation: The traditional rule keeps the defendant's liability measured by the harm, without discount for independent benefits such as the plaintiff's own insurance. Whether and how the rule has been modified is a separate, jurisdiction-specific question.

questions.question: A laundry holds a customer's garments worth far more than the laundry's service charge. The laundry's insurable interest is best described as what?

answers.text: An interest limited in all cases to the cleaning fee alone, even when the garments are worth many times that service charge
No interest because customers retain ownership
Full ownership of every garment left for cleaning
An interest arising from its responsibility for garments in its custody, not ownership of the garments

questions.explanation: Custody plus responsibility creates a bailee interest even though ownership stays with the customer. The fee alone does not define the responsibility exposure.

questions.question: A surplus lines agent's underlying general lines appointment is revoked for misconduct. The effect on the agent's surplus lines appointment is that:

answers.text: Revocation, suspension, or nonrenewal of the agent's qualification or appointment under the general-agent provisions automatically cascades to the surplus lines appointment
Nothing happens; the licenses are independent, with no exception for the situation described, under any reading of the facts presented
The surplus lines appointment continues until its biennial renewal, in each instance of the conduct described, without regard to the surrounding circumstances
Only a fine may be imposed, in every case, with no qualification of any kind

questions.explanation: Loss of the underlying general lines qualification or appointment automatically grounds discipline of the surplus lines appointment, because the surplus lines license rests on that foundation. The appointments are not independent.

questions.question: A retailer finishes a storage addition that is attached to its insured store and fully completed. Under the Building and Personal Property Coverage Form, how is that completed addition classified?

answers.text: It is part of the covered Building, because completed additions are included in the Building definition.
It is Your Business Personal Property, because anything added after construction is contents.
It is covered only under the newly acquired property extension for 30 days.
It is not covered property until a separate building policy is issued.

questions.explanation: Completed additions are expressly part of Building coverage, not contents. Treating the addition as business personal property is wrong because that category covers movable business property, not structural additions.

questions.question: A representation is generally judged by whether it was substantially true and made in good faith, rather than by what stricter standard?

answers.text: Whether the applicant chose a low deductible
Whether the insurer liked the applicant
Whether a loss later occurred
The literal, guaranteed accuracy required of a warranty

questions.explanation: Substantial truth in good faith fits representations. Literal guaranteed accuracy is the warranty standard, which is the precise contrast tested.

questions.question: A worker dies from injuries received in a covered workplace accident, leaving a dependent spouse. Which two benefits are potentially payable?

answers.text: Temporary total disability to the spouse and a burial allowance
Death benefits to the dependent spouse and a burial allowance
Rehabilitation services to the spouse and death benefits
Medical benefits only, with no income benefit of any kind

questions.explanation: A fatal covered injury can produce both dependent death benefits and a burial allowance. Disability income categories apply to a living disabled worker, not to the surviving spouse.

questions.question: A homeowner signs the surplus lines disclosure acknowledgment before placement. The legal effect of the signature is that the insured is:

answers.text: Presumed to have been informed and to know that other coverage may be available
Barred from ever buying admitted coverage for the property, with no exception for the situation described
Deemed to have waived all claim rights against the insurer, under any reading of the facts presented
Required to keep the surplus lines policy for its full term, in each instance of the conduct described

questions.explanation: A signed acknowledgment creates the presumption that the insured was informed and knows other coverage may be available. It does not waive claim rights, compel keeping the policy, or bar future admitted coverage.

questions.question: A project owner believes it is protected by a waiver of subrogation, but its name never appears in the endorsement's schedule and no blanket wording covers it. What is its position after the insurer pays a loss the owner caused?

answers.text: It is protected anyway, because it believed a waiver existed
It is not protected by the waiver, so the insurer may pursue recovery against it
It is protected if it holds a certificate mentioning the project
It is protected because waivers automatically cover all project owners

questions.explanation: Protection depends on being the scheduled, or otherwise covered, person or organization under the endorsement. Belief or a certificate mention does not substitute for being within the waiver's terms.

questions.question: An insurer has withdrawn from Florida and writes no new business here, but life policies it issued earlier remain in force for Florida residents. Continuing to service those policies:

answers.text: Does not require a certificate of authority under the withdrawal servicing exception
Is permitted only for 90 days, whether the matter arises at application, at issuance, or at renewal
Requires the policies to be cancelled, with no exception for the situation described
Requires a new certificate in all cases, under any reading of the facts presented, in each instance of the conduct described

questions.explanation: Continuation and servicing of life, health, or annuity contracts remaining in force for Florida residents after withdrawal, without transacting new insurance, is excepted.

questions.question: A rideshare driver is logged into the app, available for requests, but has not yet accepted a trip and has no passenger, when the driver causes an accident. At concept level, how is this period treated differently from offline driving?

answers.text: It is identical to offline driving in every coverage respect
It is the period after drop-off, when no coverage questions ever arise, under the conditions stated in the policy, and as set out in the policy form, declarations, and applicable endorsement schedule
It is an intermediate app-on, available-for-hire period, where personal auto exclusions for livery or rideshare use commonly apply and platform contingent coverage is designed to be considered
It is automatically a racing period

questions.explanation: Explanation: The app-on and available period is the middle rideshare period, distinct from both offline personal use and an accepted trip with a passenger, and it is where personal policy livery exclusions and platform contingent arrangements intersect. Treating it as identical to offline driving misses the availability-for-hire fact.

questions.question: An agency first ceases transacting insurance on May 1 and does not resume. The agent in charge must complete all of the required closure steps no later than:

answers.text: July 30, within 90 days after cessation
June 5, within 35 days after the agency first ceased transacting insurance
May 31, within 30 days after cessation
June 15, within 45 days after cessation

questions.explanation: The closure steps are due within 35 days after the agency first ceases transacting insurance. May 1 plus 35 days is June 5.

questions.question: Which arrangement is expressly NOT treated as discrimination or an unlawful rebate for life insurance or a life annuity?

answers.text: Abating premiums for new buyers only, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind

Paying bonuses to all policyholders, or abating premiums in whole or in part out of surplus from nonparticipating insurance, when fair and equitable to all policyholders and in the best interests of the company and its policyholders
Using surplus to pay one agent's top clients, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Paying a bonus only to the largest policyholder, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind

questions.explanation: The life bonus/abatement exception requires surplus accumulated from nonparticipating insurance and treatment that is fair and equitable to all policyholders and in the best interests of the company and policyholders. Selective favors to a few fail those conditions.

questions.question: The weight of accumulated snow causes a freestanding fence and an outdoor antenna at a business insured under the Broad form to fail, while the building itself is unharmed and does not collapse. How does the weight of snow, ice, or sleet peril treat the fence and antenna?

answers.text: It covers the antenna only if it is used for business communications.
It covers all outdoor property damaged by snow weight.
It covers the fence but never an antenna.
It does not cover that outdoor property under this peril, except as a result of the collapse of the building.

questions.explanation: The weight peril carves out outdoor items such as antennas, gutters, fences, and outdoor fixtures, except as a result of the building's collapse, which did not happen here. Business use of the antenna does not change the carve-out.

questions.question: A trucking firm schedules its commercial umbrella over its business auto and employers liability policies, both expiring on the same date as the umbrella. At renewal it switches auto insurers but lets the new auto policy start ten days after the old one ends. Which duty and structure are implicated?

answers.text: The follow-form definition only, for the insured, premises, and policy period identified in the declarations, and as the form itself provides
The premium audit only
The aircraft exclusion only
The maintenance of underlying coverage and concurrent periods, because a ten-day underlying gap breaks the aligned program

questions.explanation: Letting the underlying auto layer lapse for ten days breaks both the duty to keep scheduled underlying coverage in force and the concurrent alignment of the program. The problem is timing and upkeep of the underlying layer, not the form's aircraft exclusion.

questions.question: A Florida worker is disabled for 17 days by a work injury, then fully recovers. For how many days is disability compensation payable?

answers.text: 7 days, because the waiting period is added at the end, under any reading of the facts presented
0 days, because the disability lasted under thirty days, in each instance of the conduct described
10 days — compensation runs from the eighth day of disability through the seventeenth
17 days, because any disability over a week is paid in full, without regard to the surrounding circumstances

questions.explanation: The first seven days are unpaid unless disability exceeds twenty-one days; at seventeen days the worker is paid for days eight through seventeen. Full retroactive payment of the first week requires more than twenty-one days of disability.

questions.question: Under a 50 percent bar system, a claimant 20 percent at fault proves $95,000 in damages. What is the award?
questions.explanation: The defendant's 80 percent share of $95,000 is $76,000. The claimant's own 20 percent share of $19,000 is the deduction, a frequent trap answer.

questions.question: What does actual cash value mean for a damaged auto at the concept level?

answers.text: The value of the auto immediately before the loss, reflecting its age, condition, and depreciation
The price the insured originally paid for the auto, without depreciation
The highest advertised price for a similar auto anywhere in the country
The cost to buy the newest model year of the same auto

questions.explanation: Actual cash value reflects what the auto was worth just before the loss, accounting for depreciation and condition. Original price and new-model cost ignore depreciation.

questions.question: An insurer declines an application and returns the unearned premium. In formation terms, what has occurred?

answers.text: The insurer accepted and then breached the contract
The insurer rejected the applicant's offer, so no insurance contract was formed
The applicant made a counteroffer
The contract became executory

questions.explanation: Declining the application is a rejection of the offer, leaving no contract to breach. A counteroffer would propose different terms rather than simply refusing, and executory status applies only to a formed contract.

questions.question: What does Refrigerated Property coverage in a homeowners policy pay for?

answers.text: The full cost of a new freezer plus a year of groceries
Replacement of the refrigerator itself whenever it stops working for any reason, regardless of which party first raises the point or how the claim is characterized when presented
Food spoiled because the insured left it unrefrigerated on a counter
Spoilage of perishable contents of a refrigerator or freezer caused by a covered power interruption or mechanical breakdown, up to its limit

questions.explanation: The coverage is for the perishable contents lost to a covered failure or outage. It is not a warranty for the appliance itself or for food spoiled by neglect.

questions.question: On which documents must the principal office address appear?

answers.text: Only the office lease
Only the first policy sold each year
Only fictitious name filings
All applications for a license and renewal applications

questions.explanation: The office address must be specified on license applications and renewal applications.

questions.question: A fellow producer says an occurrence must always be a sudden, split-second event. Why is that statement incomplete?

answers.text: The definition also covers any event that occurs after the policy expires
The definition also covers losses the insured intended to cause
The definition also covers purely economic loss with no accident at all
The definition also covers continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions

questions.explanation: The exposure language broadens occurrence beyond split-second events. It does not broaden it to intended harm, which the accident element still excludes.

questions.question: A switchyard employee of an interstate carrier is injured after the carrier ignores repeated reports of a broken walkway. Which framework should the adjuster identify?

answers.text: The federal railroad liability act, because the claim turns on the carrier’s negligence toward its employee
The longshore program, because the yard handles freight containers
The black lung program, because rail yards are dusty workplaces
The defense contractor program, because the freight includes government cargo

questions.explanation: Ignored safety reports supply the negligence core of the federal railroad remedy for a carrier’s own employee. Freight type and cargo ownership do not change the worker’s railroad identity.

questions.question: A person who regularly resides in an apartment above the insured's store slips on the store's stairs and files a Coverage C claim. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Coverage C covers residents on the same terms as any casual visitor
Coverage C covers residents only when the stairs are part of the store
Coverage C excludes residents only if they are related to the named insured
Coverage C excludes a person who regularly resides on premises the insured owns or rents

questions.explanation: Coverage C excludes persons who regularly reside on the insured premises, distinguishing them from members of the public passing through. Casual visitors are the intended beneficiaries, so the same-terms distractor is wrong.

questions.question: A covered fire loss of $120,000 hits a bakery building valued at $480,000. The policy has 75% coinsurance, a limit of $240,000, and a $2,000 deductible. How much does the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Should = $480,000 x 75% = $360,000. Payment = ($240,000/$360,000) x $120,000 - $2,000 = $80,000 - $2,000 = $78,000. The $118,000 option ignores the coinsurance penalty and pays the loss as if the requirement had been met.

questions.question: While traveling abroad, a thief steals the insured's camera and suitcase from a locked hotel room. Which statement best describes Coverage C?

answers.text: It applies only up to $500 for property in a hotel
It applies only if the property was scheduled in advance
It does not apply once property leaves the country
It applies, because Coverage C covers the insured's personal property anywhere in the world

questions.explanation: Coverage C follows the insured's personal property worldwide, including property temporarily in a hotel abroad. It is not confined to the residence premises.

questions.question: A lender conditions a loan renewal, rather than the original loan, on using its chosen broker. Is that covered by the prohibition?

answers.text: Yes. The bar applies to renewals and extensions and other acts in connection with the loan, not just the original financing
No, only original loans are covered, as the complete answer for the situation described, applying to the facts stated without any added condition
No, renewals are exempt, so that no different result, separate requirement, or added condition would arise on the facts given in the question
Yes, but only for commercial property, and that treatment is presented as the complete answer on the facts stated, with no further step or condition applying

questions.explanation: The prohibition expressly reaches conditions for renewal, extension, or any other act connected with the loan.

questions.question: Absent an endorsement or provision specifically covering earthquake, a California policy that by its terms does not cover earthquake:

answers.text: Covers the loss unless the insurer proves intent to harm, and that treatment applies in the same way at renewal, regardless of where in California the property is located
Provides no coverage for loss or damage when earthquake is a proximate cause, even if another covered cause contributes concurrently or in sequence
Covers the loss if any covered cause contributed at all, and the rule cannot be changed by a side agreement
Covers half the loss under a statutory sharing rule, and it applies to every policyholder in the same position

questions.explanation: California's anti-concurrent-cause rule for earthquake provides that a policy not covering earthquake provides no coverage when earthquake is a proximate cause, regardless of other contributing causes, unless earthquake was specifically endorsed or provided. There is no half-sharing rule.

questions.question: An applicant for commercial liability coverage knows its premises had two prior slip-and-fall claims, is asked about prior claims, and deliberately withholds that information. This conduct is best described as which of the following?

answers.text: Concealment
Estoppel
Waiver
Subrogation

questions.explanation: Concealment is the intentional withholding of a material fact the applicant knows should be communicated. Waiver and estoppel concern giving up or being barred from asserting a right, not hiding a fact on an application.

questions.question: One partner in the insured firm secretly sets out to damage a rival's sign, while another partner knows nothing of the plan and is later sued only for negligent supervision. Which standpoint point is central to the expected or intended analysis?

answers.text: One partner's intent automatically proves every partner expected the damage
Intent is judged from the rival's standpoint once a lawsuit is filed
The exclusion never applies to partnerships because partners act separately
The exclusion is judged from the standpoint of the insured whose conduct and expectation are at issue

questions.explanation: The phrase from the standpoint of the insured focuses the inquiry on the insured whose expectation is being judged, rather than automatically treating a rival's or a stranger's view as controlling. Partnership status alone neither triggers nor defeats the exclusion.

questions.question: An insurer's representative, not its own employee, handles claims and engages in unfair delay. Can the insurer avoid responsibility by pointing to the representative?

answers.text: No, an insurer remains responsible for fair claims conduct by those acting on its behalf
Yes, if the representative works from a different office
Yes, delegation transfers all claims duties to the representative
Only if the claimant signed a waiver of prompt handling

questions.explanation: Claims duties are not delegated away; conduct by representatives acting for the insurer is the insurer's conduct for fair-claims purposes. Office location and claimant waivers do not change that.

questions.question: Two unrelated roommates share a rented house. One buys a tenants form in her own name and assumes her roommate's belongings are automatically protected too. What should the roommate understand?

answers.text: Any person sleeping in the home is a named insured on a tenants form
The landlord's policy automatically covers both roommates' belongings, and no other fact about the loss or the insured changes that stated treatment
An unrelated roommate is not automatically an insured under the other's tenants form and generally needs a policy of her own
Roommates are treated as spouses under every homeowners form

questions.explanation: Tenants coverage follows the named insured and household members as the policy defines them; an unrelated roommate is a separate household member in name only to herself. She is not swept in as a spouse or automatic insured.

questions.question: A shipping clerk whose employer has an insurable interest in the cargo completes and delivers a certificate of coverage under a running inland marine contract, negotiating only as needed to complete the delivery. Is a license required?

answers.text: Yes, because delivering a certificate of coverage is always transacting insurance, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
No, but only when the certificate covers exported goods rather than domestic shipments, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Yes, unless the clerk also holds a cargo shipper's agent license for the same shipment, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
No, because completing or delivering such a certificate, with only the negotiations necessary to that task, is exempt when the person or the employer has an insurable interest in the risk

questions.explanation: The running inland marine certificate exemption turns on the limited completion-and-delivery role and on the person or employer having an insurable interest in the covered risk.

questions.question: A general contractor and a subcontractor are both insureds under one CGL policy and are both named in a single lawsuit over a visitor's injury. The insurer evaluates the defense for each defendant. What does separation of insureds require in that evaluation?

answers.text: The policy must be applied separately to each insured against whom the suit is brought
Only the defendant with the larger contract gets a defense analysis
The two defendants must be treated as one person for every policy purpose
The suit must be split into two lawsuits before coverage is read

questions.explanation: Even within one lawsuit, the condition directs that the insurance apply separately to each insured sued. It does not require separate lawsuits, and it does not merge the defendants into a single insured.

questions.question: An owner and a lender hold separate property interests in the same building under different policies. Why does pro rata apportionment between those two policies generally NOT apply?

answers.text: The building has more than one person interested in it
One of the policies was issued in a different month
The policies insure different interests rather than the same interest in the property
The lender's interest is smaller than the owner's interest

questions.explanation: Pro rata sharing requires the same interest to be insured more than once. Different interests, such as an owner's and a lender's, are not duplicate coverage of one interest.

questions.question: Within the past three years, how much minor adverse history can a low cost applicant have and still have a good driving record?

answers.text: Up to two at-fault accidents involving bodily injury and up to two points for moving violations during the same three-year period
An unlimited number of at-fault property-damage-only accidents, as long as none of them involved any bodily injury to any person
No more than three points for moving violations of any kind, with no restriction at all on at-fault property damage accidents
No more than one at-fault property-damage-only accident, or no more than one point for a moving violation

questions.explanation: The program allows no more than one at-fault property-damage-only accident or one moving-violation point in three years. Injury accidents and multiple points fall outside the good-record definition.

new-york-insurance.quiz_title: New York Insurance FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why do assigned risk policies usually cost more than voluntary market policies?

answers.text: The state adds a luxury tax available only through the plan
Assigned insurers are allowed to charge any amount with no regulation
The pool concentrates higher-risk drivers whose expected losses are greater
Drivers in the plan receive unlimited coverage limits automatically

questions.explanation: Residual market premiums reflect the poorer loss experience of the high-risk pool. Rates remain regulated, and assigned policies carry set limits rather than unlimited coverage.

questions.question: Which set lists only categories that count as a serious injury under the verbal threshold?

answers.text: Death, dismemberment, significant disfigurement, fracture, and loss of a fetus
Any injury needing an emergency visit
Only death and fracture
Whiplash and bruising

questions.explanation: Those five listed outcomes are all statutory serious-injury categories; minor sprains and bruising are not.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding association notice of market assistance eligibility in New York?

answers.text: Notice is required only when a policyholder files a complaint
The association must keep market assistance programs confidential from its policyholders
The notice need only name the program, with no application information
Association policyholders in market assistance areas must be told of possible program eligibility and how to apply

questions.explanation: The association must notify its policyholders in market assistance areas of possible eligibility and include how to apply. Silence until a complaint is filed does not satisfy the duty.

questions.question: A hire stretch limousine seating ten is insured. What supplementary combined limit is required?

answers.text: One million dollars per person
Five hundred thousand dollars combined single limit
One million five hundred thousand dollars combined single limit
Two hundred fifty thousand dollars per person

questions.explanation: The stretch limousine supplementary requirement is a one million five hundred thousand dollar combined single limit. Five hundred thousand is wrong because that is the ordinary combined ceiling, not the limousine figure.

questions.question: How does the policy period condition interact with an occurrence liability form?

answers.text: The bodily injury or property damage must occur during the policy period for that policy to respond
Occurrences at any time in the insured's history are covered
The period applies to premiums but not to losses
Only the claim date matters and the occurrence date is irrelevant

questions.explanation: Occurrence forms key response to when injury or damage occurs within the period. Treating only the claim date as relevant describes a different trigger and is wrong.

questions.question: An insured has an Outside the Premises limit of $15,000 and a deductible of $250. A messenger robbery causes a covered loss of $9,250. Ignoring any other provision, what is payable?
questions.explanation: Explanation: The $9,250 loss is within the $15,000 limit, and subtracting the $250 deductible leaves $9,000: 9,250 minus 250 equals 9,000. Paying the limit would exceed the actual loss.

questions.question: A small group's premiums are cancelled after two employees file large claims. Is claims experience a lawful ground?

answers.text: Coverage ends after the first large claim
Claims experience alone can never end coverage
High claims are a valid termination ground
Termination is allowed whenever losses exceed premiums

questions.explanation: No — once accepted, an individual or small group cannot be terminated due to claims experience.

questions.question: A disapproved homeowners reduction plan is returned to the insurer on March 2, 2026. By what date must the amended plan be filed?

answers.text: April 16, 2026
March 17, 2026
April 1, 2026
March 12, 2026

questions.explanation: The amended plan is due within fifteen days from the date of return. Thirty days and six months are not the statutory periods.

questions.question: The named insured's spouse lives in the same household and is injured while occupying the covered auto. Under Part B, the spouse's status rests on what relationship?

answers.text: A spouse is never an insured person under Part B
A spouse is covered only when separately named as an additional insured by endorsement for Part B
A spouse residing in the same household is treated within the family member framework
A spouse is covered only while driving, never as a passenger

questions.explanation: The family member concept in the personal auto form includes the resident spouse within the household framework, and passengers as well as drivers can be insured persons. A special endorsement is not the source of the spouse's basic Part B status.

questions.question: A homeowner's pipe bursts on the same night that floodwater surrounds the house, causing two distinct kinds of water damage. How should the provisions be applied?

answers.text: All water damage is denied if any flood is present

The homeowners policy pays for both because the pipe loss happened first, including the flood damage surrounding the house, because the order in which the two water losses happened controls both policies
The flood policy pays for the burst pipe because both involve water
The plumbing discharge loss is analyzed under the homeowners policy while the flood loss is analyzed under flood coverage, keeping the distinct causes separate

questions.explanation: Distinct causes are evaluated under their own provisions: accidental plumbing discharge under the property policy and flood under flood coverage. The presence of flood does not automatically erase a separate covered plumbing loss.

questions.question: A nonresident worker's dependent sibling abroad claims death benefits. Which dependents abroad are permitted?

answers.text: All relatives abroad qualify equally
Foreign dependents limited to spouse and children or a supported parent
Only siblings abroad qualify
Foreign dependents receive half the resident amount

questions.explanation: Only spouse and children, or a supported parent if none, qualify abroad. Siblings are wrong because they are outside the limited classes.

questions.question: An applicant asks a producer about homeowners insurance definition. Which response states the New York rule correctly?

answers.text: Homeowners coverage applies even when the person has no interest in any residence
A dwelling fire policy with no liability or personal property coverage of any kind
Any policy with homeowners in its title, including commercial package policies
A personal lines covered policy for property and liability, with the property and liability parts requiring an insurable interest in the home or residential unit

questions.explanation: Homeowners insurance is the personal lines covered policy combining the listed real property, personal property, and liability contingencies, with an insurable-interest condition on the personal property and liability parts. The policy's title alone is not the test.

questions.question: A new building ordinance will require a damaged commercial building to be rebuilt to costlier standards, increasing the amount an insurer may have to pay after a fire. What type of hazard does the ordinance create?

answers.text: A physical hazard
A moral hazard
A legal hazard
A morale hazard

questions.explanation: A legal hazard arises when laws, regulations, or court decisions increase the chance or size of a loss. A physical hazard, a close distractor, is a tangible property condition, not a legal requirement.

questions.question: A described dwelling sits vacant for seventy-five straight days with no added written provision, and then burns. How does the standard form treat the loss?

answers.text: The suspension period is thirty consecutive days
Vacancy never suspends fire coverage under the standard form
No liability only after the building is vacant for a full year
No liability for loss while the building has been vacant or unoccupied beyond 60 consecutive days, unless written policy terms provide otherwise

questions.explanation: Coverage is suspended for loss occurring while the building is vacant or unoccupied beyond sixty consecutive days, absent a written provision added to the policy. Seventy-five days exceeds the period.

questions.question: A claimant condition materially worsens two years after an award, and the wage rate used was also wrong. What review is available?

answers.text: Awards can never be modified once made
Only an increase, never a decrease, is permitted on review
Wage rate errors are uncorrectable
Changed conditions or an erroneous wage rate support board review that may end, decrease, or increase an award

questions.explanation: Changed conditions or proof of an erroneous wage rate let the board review and end, diminish, or increase compensation within the stated limits. Awards are not frozen forever.

questions.question: An insurer proposes overlapping subjective homeowners tiers with no coastal availability purpose. Why does it fail the statutory conditions?

answers.text: Coastal availability is irrelevant
Tiers may overlap at insurer discretion
Multi-tier needs availability purpose, objective tiers and approved credits
Credits need no approved plan

questions.explanation: Tiers must be mutually exclusive and objective where feasible with an availability-encouraging plan. Subjective overlap fails both.

questions.question: Sprinkler leakage at a store insured under the Basic form wets the ceiling and stock. The leakage was caused by a damaged sprinkler pipe. Which related cost does the peril also address when the building is covered property?

answers.text: The cost of lost profits while the store is dried out
The cost to replace the entire sprinkler system with an upgraded model
The cost to refill the municipal water supply
The cost to repair or replace the damaged parts of the sprinkler system that resulted in the leakage

questions.explanation: If the building containing the system is covered property, the form also pays to repair or replace damaged parts of the system when the damage results in sprinkler leakage or is directly caused by freezing. It pays for the damaged parts, not a full system upgrade.

questions.question: A breakdown of a hotel boiler forces the hotel to close during the period of restoration. The hotel loses net income it would have earned of $8,200 and continues to incur $4,700 of normal operating expenses during the closure. Ignoring any deductible and limits, what is the hotel's business income loss from these two components?
questions.explanation: Business income loss from a breakdown is the lost net income plus continuing normal operating expenses, so $8,200 plus $4,700 equals $12,900. Counting only the lost income or only the continuing expenses understates the loss, and subtracting one from the other is the wrong operation.

questions.question: A regulator reviews conduct involving specific approval option for workers compensation filings. Which of the following actions would violate New York law?

answers.text: Using a filing after the ordinary waiting period runs with no disapproval and no specific-approval regulation
Using a workers compensation rate that a regulation requires to be specifically approved, before that approval is given
Waiting for the specific approval a regulation requires before using the rate
Furnishing added supporting information the superintendent requests

questions.explanation: The superintendent may by regulation require workers compensation filings to be specifically approved before effectiveness, in lieu of the waiting period. Insurers do not choose the standard.

questions.question: An applicant meets the paper qualifications but the superintendent finds licensing it would not serve the public. May the license be refused?

answers.text: Refuse based solely on the insurer state of origin
Refuse only after the insurer becomes insolvent
Never refuse a renewal for any reason
Refuse issuance or renewal to protect the public interest

questions.explanation: Refusal discretion exists to protect the public interest. It is not limited to applicants already insolvent.

questions.question: Why does the accrual date matter for a liability claim?

answers.text: It sets the amount of damages the jury may award
It sets the policy limit available for the claim
It is the starting point from which the filing period specified by law is measured
It identifies the claimant's attorney of record

questions.explanation: The filing deadline is measured from accrual, so identifying when the cause of action arose determines whether a later suit is timely. The accrual date does not set damages amounts or policy limits.

questions.question: Which of the following best states the Pennsylvania rule on basic property insurance definition for continuation?

answers.text: Only fire and lightning coverage on dwellings
Liability insurance on residential premises

Standard fire and extended coverage perils plus vandalism, malicious mischief, burglary, theft and other Commissioner-determined classes, excluding motor vehicle, farm and excluded manufacturing risks
All property insurance including motor vehicle and farm risks

questions.explanation: Basic property insurance spans standard fire and extended coverage perils plus vandalism, malicious mischief, burglary, theft and other Commissioner-determined classes. Motor vehicle, farm and excluded manufacturing risks are outside the definition.

questions.question: Which of the following best states the Pennsylvania rule on commercial nonrenewal sixty-day notice?

answers.text: At least fifteen days advance written notice of nonrenewal
No advance notice is required for a commercial nonrenewal
At least thirty days advance written notice of nonrenewal
At least sixty days advance written notice of nonrenewal, forwarded directly to the named insured

questions.explanation: Commercial nonrenewal requires written notice forwarded directly to the named insured at least sixty days before termination takes effect. Thirty days is the period for a renewal premium increase notice, not for nonrenewal.

questions.question: Regarding application contents for individuals, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Only proof of an office lease
Only a resume and a business plan
Lines sought, required fees, and proof of passing or exemption from the exam
Lines sought with no fee and no exam proof

questions.explanation: The correct answer states the verified Pennsylvania rule on application contents for individuals. The strongest wrong choice, 'Only a resume and a business plan', contradicts that rule's amount, timing, condition or scope.

questions.question: A Coverage B payment for a destroyed detached garage has what effect on the Coverage A limit?

answers.text: It reduces Coverage A dollar for dollar
None; the Coverage B amount is additional insurance and does not reduce Coverage A
It reduces Coverage A by one half of the payment
It suspends Coverage A until the garage is rebuilt

questions.explanation: The Coverage B limit is an additional amount of insurance. Using it for an other structure does not eat into the dwelling limit, unlike coverages that are paid within another limit.

questions.question: A claim otherwise fits Coverage A, but the injury happened before the policy took effect. Why does the insuring agreement not respond?

answers.text: The bodily injury or property damage must occur during the policy period
Coverage A only applies to injuries that happen after a lawsuit is filed
Coverage A pays only when the insured reports the event before it happens
Coverage A excludes every injury that is not discovered on the day it occurs

questions.explanation: Two threshold conditions in the insuring agreement are that the injury or damage occurs in the coverage territory and during the policy period. An injury predating the policy fails the period condition, even though discovery or suit may come later.

questions.question: A regulator reviews conduct involving dwelling insurer duty to assure notice given. Which of the following actions would violate Pennsylvania law?

answers.text: An insurer mails the notice itself when its agent cannot
An insurer verifies that its agent mailed the required notice to the policyholder
An insurer takes no steps to assure that a nonrenewal notice its agent was supposed to mail ever reached the policyholder
An insurer keeps records of the notices given to affected policyholders

questions.explanation: The regulation places the duty on the insurer to assure the notice is given to each affected policyholder.

questions.question: A regulator reviews conduct involving MCARE fund excess role. Which of the following actions would violate Pennsylvania law?

answers.text: Notifying the fund promptly of a claim likely to exceed primary limits
Carrying the higher limits required of a nonparticipating provider
Keeping the primary policy in force beneath the fund layer
Telling a participating provider to drop primary coverage because the fund will pay from the first dollar

questions.explanation: The fund pays claims in excess of the participating provider's primary coverage up to its limit. Primary coverage must still be carried and exhausted first.

questions.question: An accountant switches claims-made insurers and the new insurer agrees in writing to full prior acts coverage back to the original retroactive date. What does that agreement commonly let the accountant avoid?

answers.text: Keeping any records of prior engagements
Reporting future claims to the new insurer, since the new insurer has agreed to cover the accountant's earlier professional work
Buying a tail, or extended reporting period, from the old insurer for the same prior work
Paying any premium to the new insurer

questions.explanation: When the incoming policy picks up the prior acts, the same acts do not also need a purchased reporting extension from the old insurer. The accountant must still report claims under the new policy as required.

questions.question: A tenant wants to insure only personal belongings inside a rented house. What does that need show about dwelling-policy eligibility?

answers.text: A tenant automatically owns an insurable interest in the whole building, as set out in the policy form, declarations, and applicable endorsement schedule, and as shown by the documentation maintained with the policy and claim records
Contents-only renters never need a separate renters-type solution

Insuring the building for its owner and insuring a tenant's contents are different needs, and the dwelling form is aimed at the described dwelling interest rather than automatically solving a tenant's contents-only need
Every tenant must buy a dwelling policy on the landlord's building

questions.explanation: A dwelling policy is placed on an eligible dwelling interest, commonly the owner's. A tenant seeking only belongings is the classic renters-form need, not a reason to insure the landlord's building to the tenant.

questions.question: Two liability policies cover the same loss. Policy X has a limit of $100,000 and Policy Y has a limit of $300,000. The covered loss is $80,000 and contribution is by limits. How much does Policy X pay?
questions.explanation: By limits, Policy X bears 100,000 divided by 400,000, or 25 percent, of the $80,000 loss, which is $20,000. An equal $40,000 split would be contribution by equal shares, not by limits.

questions.question: An insurer's capital report is 40 days late and the maximum daily forfeit is imposed. What is the total forfeit?

answers.text: $2,000, which is 40 days at $50 per day
$200, because the forfeit is a single flat amount
$40,000, which is 40 days at $1,000 per day
$8,000, which is 40 days at $200 per day

questions.explanation: The forfeit runs up to $200 for each day of failure — up to $5,000 for 25 days — and it is in addition to other penalties, not a substitute for them.

questions.question: A broker is counseling a client who proposes carrying the lowest limit the lender will accept on a valuable commercial building. Which point about coinsurance should the broker emphasize?

answers.text: If a partial loss occurs, the lender will pay the difference between the limit and the loss
A low limit affects only total losses, because coinsurance does not apply to partial losses
If a partial loss occurs, the claim payment will be cut in the same proportion that the limit falls short of the required amount
A low limit is safe because the deductible will absorb any coinsurance reduction

questions.explanation: The broker should stress that the shortfall penalty falls mainly on partial losses, reducing payment by the did/should proportion. The statement that coinsurance does not apply to partial losses reverses the clause's main effect.

questions.question: A managing general agent that sets loss reserves demands its interim profit share on casualty business six months after the profits were earned. When may it be paid?

answers.text: Interim profits are payable quarterly as estimated
Interim profits wait one year after earning for property business and five years for casualty business
Both lines wait a flat three years
Profit sharing may be paid before reserves are verified if the contract allows

questions.explanation: Casualty interim profits cannot be paid until five years after they are earned, and only after the insurer's verification. Six months is far too early; property business carries the shorter one-year wait.

questions.question: An applicant asks a producer about state workers insurance fund false statement penalty. Which response states the Pennsylvania rule correctly?

answers.text: Automatic loss of coverage retroactive to the first policy year
A fine of ten thousand dollars per false statement, with no daily penalty
Only a warning letter, because fund statements carry no penalties
A misdemeanor for a knowingly false statement, and ten dollars per day for a subscriber who ignores the ten-day deadline for the annual statement after notice

questions.explanation: The subscriber owes ten dollars for each day the neglect or refusal continued after the ten-day post-notice deadline, recoverable by the fund; knowingly false fund statements are separately a misdemeanor.

questions.question: A producer violates the Pennsylvania rule on patient safety reporting failure penalty per day. Which of the following is a possible consequence?

answers.text: A penalty paid to the injured patient as automatic damages
Suspension of the facility's operating license with no monetary penalty
A single penalty of one thousand dollars for the entire episode
An administrative penalty of one thousand dollars per day imposed by the Department of Health

questions.explanation: The failure is a health care facilities law violation punishable by an administrative penalty of one thousand dollars per day.

questions.question: If a licensee fails to comply with the Pennsylvania requirements on prohibited managing general agent acts, which of the following may result?

answers.text: Loss of the agent's right to hold a producer license in any state permanently
License suspension or revocation and a civil penalty of up to $5,000 for each separate violation
A fine of $100,000 per prohibited act
A verbal warning from the insurer's president

questions.explanation: Both acts are on the prohibited list: appointing a sub-managing general agent and committing the insurer to syndicate participations. The narrow reinsurance exception covers only qualifying facultative obligations.

questions.question: A warehouse owner has a covered fire claim caused by a negligent electrical contractor, but the insurer has not yet paid anything. At what point does the insurer's subrogation right against the contractor normally arise?

answers.text: After the insurer pays the loss to the insured
When the fire occurs, regardless of payment
Only after the insured wins a lawsuit against the contractor
When the policy is first issued

questions.explanation: Subrogation is triggered by payment: once the insurer pays the insured, it steps into the insured's rights against the responsible party. Mere occurrence of the loss, without payment, does not yet give the insurer that right.

questions.question: An injured insured receives remedial care through a recognized religious method of healing and submits the cost under first-party medical benefits. Is that kind of care within the benefit?

answers.text: Religious healing care is excluded because it is not medical treatment
Nonmedical remedial care under a recognized religious method of healing is included in the medical benefit
Any alternative therapy the insured prefers is included without qualification
Only care delivered inside a hospital counts toward the medical benefit

questions.explanation: Yes; the medical benefit expressly includes nonmedical remedial care rendered under a recognized religious method of healing.

questions.question: An insured loses $2,500 of gross income from a crash injury. Applying the income loss percentage, how much does the benefit address?

answers.text: $2,500, which is 100 percent of $2,500
$1,667, which is two-thirds of $2,500
$2,000, which is 80 percent of $2,500
$1,250, which is 50 percent of $2,500

questions.explanation: Pennsylvania first-party income loss benefits pay 80 percent of actual gross income loss: 80 percent of the $2,500 loss is $2,000. The benefit does not replace the full amount.

us-history-survey.quiz_title: US History Survey Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: The Battle of the Thames in Upper Canada in October 1813 had consequences beyond a single American victory because

answers.text: the battle forced Britain to evacuate all of Canada east of the Great Lakes
American forces captured Montreal and held it until the peace treaty
the British commander signed an armistice ending naval operations on Lake Erie
Tecumseh was killed in the fighting and the Native confederacy he had built in the Old Northwest collapsed

questions.explanation: Harrison's army defeated the British and their Native allies near Moraviantown, and Tecumseh's death removed the leader holding the northwestern confederacy together; it disintegrated afterward. Britain did not evacuate Canada, Montreal was never captured in this campaign, and the Lake Erie naval contest had already been decided the previous month.

questions.question: Before steamboats, western river commerce relied heavily on flatboats whose economic limitation was that they

answers.text: required more fuel per ton than any steamboat of the 1830s
could float downstream with a cargo but could not return upstream, so they were broken up and sold for lumber at destination while crews walked or rode home
were legally barred from carrying cotton by the Louisiana purchase treaty
could carry goods upstream faster than downstream because of their flat hulls

questions.explanation: A flatboat was essentially a one-way raft: it drifted and was poled downstream, then was worth more as lumber in New Orleans than as a vessel to fight the current home, so return cargo capacity upriver stayed tiny until steam. Flatboats burned no fuel, faced no treaty ban on cotton, and their hulls made upstream travel slower, not faster.

questions.question: The Rhode Island system of early textile production, descended from Slater's mills, differed from the Lowell pattern chiefly in that it

answers.text: recruited only single adult men on short seasonal contracts
employed whole families, including young children, in mill villages and often paid workers partly in credit at the company store
forbade child labor by charter and paid wages exclusively in gold coin
housed workers in supervised boardinghouses with curfews and mandatory church attendance

questions.explanation: Rhode Island mills hired family units, put children to work alongside parents, and anchored paternalistic mill villages with company housing and store credit. Supervised boardinghouses for young single women describe Lowell, not Rhode Island; neither child labor bans nor gold-only wages nor all-male seasonal hiring characterized the system.

questions.question: When President William Henry Harrison died in 1841, Vice President John Tyler established a precedent with long constitutional significance by

answers.text: agreeing to serve only until a special election could be held that autumn
insisting he was fully president in his own right, not a caretaker, a reading of succession later written into the Twenty-fifth Amendment
sharing executive power with the cabinet in a formal council of regency
resigning the office to the secretary of state as next in the constitutional line

questions.explanation: Despite opponents calling him His Accidency, Tyler took the presidential oath, title, salary, and full powers, and Congress acquiesced; every later vice-presidential succession followed the Tyler precedent. No special election was held, no regency council existed, and Tyler did not yield to the secretary of state.

questions.question: Use the stated census summary for 1860: the total population of the United States was about 31.4 million, of whom about 3.95 million were enslaved. Enslaved people therefore made up approximately

answers.text: 3 percent of the national population
13 percent of the national population, roughly one person in eight
26 percent of the national population
40 percent of the national population

questions.explanation: Dividing 3.95 million by 31.4 million gives about 0.126, or roughly 13 percent, close to one in eight. Three percent would imply fewer than a million enslaved people, 26 percent would require over eight million, and 40 percent would require more than twelve million, none consistent with the stated figures.

questions.question: In several Eastern Woodlands societies, dreams were treated as communications carrying obligations: a dream of receiving a gift or of a feast could require the dreamer to hold that feast or give that gift publicly. This practice indicates that in these societies dreams functioned as

answers.text: private entertainment with no social consequences
a socially binding source of guidance that could obligate public generosity and ritual action
evidence used in courts to convict people of witchcraft
a skill restricted to a hereditary priestly caste

questions.explanation: Dreams carried duties enforceable by community expectation, channeling generosity and ceremony rather than remaining private experience. They were not courtroom evidence in this setting, and dreaming and interpretation were broadly shared, not caste monopolies.

questions.question: After the Stuart restoration, Charles II rewarded a group of courtiers with a vast proprietary grant for Carolina, whose Fundamental Constitutions envisioned hereditary nobility with titled ranks and large seigniories. In practice the colony developed instead around

answers.text: exact implementation of the titled-nobility plan for two centuries
a single royal governor ruling without any assembly
small farms in the north and Barbadian-style plantations in the south, while the elaborate constitution failed to take root
the immediate abolition of proprietary government in 1670

questions.explanation: The paper constitution's hereditary lords and leet-men never materialized; actual settlement followed the Albemarle small-farm pattern and the lowcountry plantation pattern. An assembly existed from early on, and proprietary rule lasted until 1719-1729.

questions.question: The Articles of Confederation required nine of thirteen states to approve major measures such as war, treaties, and appropriations, and all thirteen to amend the Articles. In practice this supermajority structure meant that

answers.text: small minorities of states — sometimes a handful of delegates — could block national action even when most states favored it
a single populous state could impose policy on all others
amendments were enacted frequently and quickly
Congress could tax imports whenever a simple majority agreed

questions.explanation: Nine-state and unanimity thresholds convert abstentions and small-state vetoes into systemic gridlock, which is why impost amendments failed by one state. No state could impose policy alone, amendments essentially never passed, and no taxing power existed at any threshold.

questions.question: Congress funded the new government predominantly through customs duties, which supplied the overwhelming share of federal revenue in the 1790s, supplemented by excises and land sales. This revenue structure had the political consequence that federal finance depended on

answers.text: continued imports — especially from Britain — so that the government's solvency was tied to the very trade its foreign policy had to manage
direct taxes levied annually on every household's income
state legislatures voting annual grants to the treasury
a permanent federal property tax on land in all states

questions.explanation: Tariffs on a booming, Britain-centered import trade paid the government's bills, which constrained policy toward Britain and made customs houses the fiscal state's front line. Income and general property taxes were not the 1790s base, and state grants were the discarded Confederation model.

questions.question: The Judiciary Act of 1789 created a Supreme Court of six justices, district and circuit courts, and required the justices themselves to ride circuit, traveling to hear cases in regional courts. One reason the system mattered beyond its court structure is that circuit riding

answers.text: removed federal judges entirely from contact with local communities
made state courts subordinate appellate bodies of the federal system
carried federal authority physically into the states and exposed national judges to local conditions, while burdening the justices with exhausting travel that they repeatedly protested
was required of judges by the Constitution's text verbatim

questions.explanation: Riding circuit put the national judiciary visibly on the road in every region, legitimating federal law locally at real personal cost the justices complained about to Congress. State courts were not made appellate subordinates, and the Constitution left court organization to statute.

questions.question: In November 1811 Governor William Henry Harrison marched on Prophetstown, the Shawnee settlement on the Wabash, while Tecumseh was away in the South recruiting allies. The resulting Battle of Tippecanoe mattered most because

answers.text: American forces burned Prophetstown in Tecumseh's absence, weakening his pan-Indian confederacy before it could fully form
Tecumseh was killed in the battle, ending organized Native resistance in the Old Northwest at once
the battle persuaded Britain to sign a formal alliance with the Shawnee the following month
Harrison captured the settlement's British-supplied artillery park and its Canadian advisers

questions.explanation: Tenskwatawa's followers attacked Harrison's camp, and after repelling them Harrison's men destroyed Prophetstown, the confederacy's base, while its principal organizer was absent. Tecumseh survived and died two years later at the Thames; no British alliance signing or captured Canadian advisers followed, and Native resistance in the region continued into the War of 1812.

questions.question: The Amistad case, decided by the Supreme Court in 1841 with former president John Quincy Adams arguing for the defense, freed a group of Africans who had seized the ship carrying them because the Court found that

answers.text: all slavery everywhere in Spanish territory had been abolished by the United States Constitution
ships carrying enslaved people automatically forfeited them upon entering any Atlantic port
they had been kidnapped and illegally enslaved in violation of Spanish law and treaties banning the African trade, and so were free persons entitled to resist
the president had ordered their release as part of a treaty with Britain

questions.explanation: The Mende captives had been taken from Sierra Leone and sold in Cuba in defiance of Spain's treaty obligations and its ban on the trade; as free people wrongfully confined, their revolt was self-defense. The ruling rested on their illegal enslavement, not on any universal constitutional abolition, automatic forfeiture rule, or presidential treaty order.

questions.question: In 1692-1693, courts in and around Salem, Massachusetts, admitted testimony about spectral appearances — harm allegedly done by an accused person's spirit, visible only to the afflicted — and hanged nineteen people before the governor halted the proceedings. The episode's collapse came largely when

answers.text: spectral testimony was discredited after accusations reached prominent families and ministers pressed evidentiary objections
all accused persons confessed and were pardoned
Parliament passed a law abolishing all colonial courts
the accused were rescued by an armed uprising of their neighbors

questions.explanation: Once accusations touched the governor's own household and leading clergy questioned evidence no bystander could verify, the proceedings lost legitimacy and were shut down. Most of the condemned had maintained innocence, and neither Parliament nor an uprising ended the trials.

questions.question: Under the task system used on many lowcountry rice estates, an enslaved worker who completed an assigned daily task — a measured portion of field or dike work — could use remaining daylight for provision grounds and family plots, whereas Chesapeake field hands typically worked gang labor from sunup to sundown under direct supervision. The contrast shows that

answers.text: labor organization within slavery varied by crop and ecology, with consequences for enslaved families' time and informal economies
all enslaved work regimes in British America were identical
task workers were legally free once their task was done
gang labor was used only on small farms with few workers

questions.explanation: Crop requirements shaped supervision: measurable rice tasks could be assigned individually, while tobacco's continuous care favored gangs — and the difference governed enslaved people's discretionary time and garden production. Task completion conferred no legal freedom, and gangs were the large plantations' norm.
