answers.text: Cap the well immediately and wait, leaving the chlorine sitting only in the top few feet of the water column above the screen and gravel pack zone below
Pump and surge the well to move the chlorinated water throughout the well so it reaches the casing, screen, and surrounding zone
Drain the well completely so the chlorine coats the dry casing
Add the chlorine only to the discharge line leaving the well

questions.explanation: The disinfectant must be distributed through the entire well — pumping and surging move chlorinated water through the casing, screen, and gravel zone instead of leaving it pooled at the top.

questions.question: A storage tank gains 45,000 gal while it is being filled over 2.5 hours. What was the average fill rate?

answers.text: 300 gpm
750 gpm
150 gpm

questions.explanation: Flow rate = Volume / Time = 45,000 gal / (2.5 hr x 60 min/hr) = 45,000 / 150 = 300 gpm (18,000 forgets to convert hours to minutes).

questions.question: A chemical feed pump that traps and delivers a set volume of liquid on each stroke is what type of pump?

answers.text: A centrifugal pump with a spinning impeller
A booster pump
A turbine pump
A positive-displacement pump

questions.explanation: Delivering a fixed volume on each cycle is the defining action of a positive-displacement pump, the type used for chemical feed.

questions.question: A two-person crew must enter a below-ground pump vault to inspect a valve. Which sequence follows confined space practice?

answers.text: Enter first and test the air only if someone feels dizzy
Send the smaller worker in without testing to save time
Test the atmosphere and follow confined-space entry procedures before anyone enters the vault
Prop the cover open for an hour, which replaces all entry procedures, no matter what the atmosphere inside the vault actually contains that day

questions.explanation: Confined-space practice requires atmosphere testing and entry procedures before entry. Ventilation, body size, and symptoms are not substitutes for testing and procedure.

questions.question: Which regulations set the trenching and shoring requirements that distribution excavation work must follow?

answers.text: OSHA and Cal-OSHA safety regulations
The system's internal payroll rules
Equipment manufacturers' sales warranties
Local parking and traffic ordinances

questions.explanation: Administering compliance includes knowledge of OSHA and Cal-OSHA safety regulations, and excavation work follows the Cal-OSHA trenching and shoring discipline. Warranties and ordinances do not set those worker-protection requirements.

questions.question: A service trench is 36 ft long, 2.5 ft wide, and 4.5 ft deep. What is the volume of the trench in cubic feet?

answers.text: 202 cubic feet
810 cubic feet
15 cubic feet
405 cubic feet

questions.explanation: Trench volume = length x width x depth = 36 ft x 2.5 ft x 4.5 ft = 405 cu ft. No conversion is made, because the question asks for cubic feet.

questions.question: For a monitoring report, a distribution system flow of 0.72 MGD must be expressed in gallons per minute. What is the flow in gpm?
questions.explanation: Convert: 0.72 MGD x 1,000,000 = 720,000 gal per day, divided by 1,440 minutes per day = 500.00 gpm. Multiplying by 1,440 instead of dividing gives the larger distractor.

questions.question: After heavy runoff, a system feeding its usual chlorine dose finds the residual at a reservoir outlet much lower than normal. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: The test kit has certainly failed, because a fixed dose must always produce exactly the same residual regardless of the quality of the water being treated
The water's chlorine demand has increased, so more of the dose is being consumed before a residual can remain
The residual fell because chlorine works better in dirty water
The dose should be cut until the residual returns on its own

questions.explanation: Dosage = demand + residual. Runoff raises the load of chlorine-consuming material, demand rises, and the same dose leaves a lower residual.

questions.question: An elevated tank holds its water surface 87 ft above a service connection. Using that elevation difference, what static pressure is expected at the connection?
questions.explanation: Pressure = head x 0.433, so 87 ft x 0.433 = 37.67 psi. The 200.97 psi distractor wrongly multiplies by 2.31, which is the factor for converting psi to feet of head.

questions.question: A crew needs a valve on a distribution main that will normally sit fully open and be closed only to shut off a section for repair work. Which valve type fits that on/off isolation service?

answers.text: A globe valve, which is intended for daily throttling of the flow
A gate valve, which is intended for on/off isolation of a section
A check valve, which opens and closes itself with the flow
An air valve, which releases air collected at a high point

questions.explanation: Gate valves isolate sections of main in on/off service and are not intended for throttling. Globe valves throttle, check valves prevent reverse flow, and air valves release trapped air.

questions.question: An inspector finds a length of new pipe resting on a few hard high spots in the trench bottom, with gaps under much of its barrel. What should happen before the pipe zone is covered?

answers.text: The gaps are left as they are, because backfill placed later will settle in and support the barrel on its own
The bedding is reworked so the pipe barrel is supported evenly along its length on suitable material
The pipe is rolled a quarter turn so a stronger side of the wall faces downward onto the high spots
Extra water is ponded in the trench to soften the high spots until the pipe settles onto them

questions.explanation: Pipe supported only at points is point-loaded, which bedding exists to prevent. The bedding is corrected to give even barrel support before the pipe zone is covered.

questions.question: A pump station's daily total is logged as 1.08 MGD, and the log's second column is kept in gallons per minute. What value goes in that column?

answers.text: 694 gpm
750 gpm
540 gpm

questions.question: One gallon of water is equal to how many liters?
questions.explanation: The Equivalents sheet gives 1 gal = 3.785 L. The 7.48 figure is the number of gallons in one cubic foot, and 2.31 and 0.433 are the pressure-to-head conversion factors.

questions.question: A well's resting water level is measured at 62 ft below the surface. Once pumping is under way and steady, the level measures 104 ft below the surface. By how much has the water level been drawn down?

answers.text: 166 ft
38 ft
42 ft
52 ft

questions.explanation: Drawdown = pumping level − static level = 104 ft − 62 ft = 42 ft. The 166 ft figure adds the two levels instead of subtracting.

questions.question: A home adds a second kitchen and bathroom, and afterward its water flow is weak whenever several fixtures run at once. The service's tap in the main was sized for the original small demand. What does differentiating tap size point to?

answers.text: The tap is oversized, and a smaller tap would raise the flow by speeding the water up
Tap size has no relation to demand, so the weak flow must be accepted as permanent
The meter has grown, because meters enlarge themselves as demand rises over the years, and the enlarged meter is now taking room in the line that the added fixtures' water used to pass through freely
The tap is now undersized for the service's demand, so the service is starved; the tap must be sized for the demand it feeds

questions.explanation: Tap size is differentiated — matched to the service's demand. An undersized tap starves the service, which is the symptom described after the home's demand outgrew its original tap.

california-water-distribution-d2.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D2 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which pair of conditions both increase disinfection by-product formation?

answers.text: Shorter contact time and colder water
Lower dose and shorter contact time
Longer contact time and warmer water
Colder water and lower precursor levels

questions.explanation: DBPs keep forming while chlorine and precursors remain in contact, so longer contact time and warmer water both increase formation.

questions.question: In distribution hydraulics, the velocity of water in a pipe is best defined as what?

answers.text: The distance the water travels per unit of time
The volume of water passing a point per day
The pressure the water exerts on the pipe wall
The weight of water contained in one foot of pipe

questions.explanation: Velocity is how fast the water moves — distance traveled per unit time, expressed in feet per second. Volume per time is flow rate, and pressure and weight describe different properties.

questions.question: In a centrifugal pump, what does the spinning impeller do to the water?

answers.text: It squeezes a fixed volume of water out on each revolution of its rotating piston
It adds velocity to the water as it throws the water outward
It lowers the water's velocity so pressure can fall
It filters solids from the water before discharge

questions.explanation: The impeller of a centrifugal pump adds velocity to the water, throwing it outward; squeezing fixed volumes describes positive-displacement action, and an impeller neither slows water to drop its pressure nor filters it.

questions.question: In emergency response planning, what role do the AWWA disinfection standards play?

answers.text: They set the prices a system may charge after an emergency
They replace the system's own emergency response plan as the governing document followed during every emergency
They govern how facilities are disinfected when emergency work is done
They apply only to routine work and never to emergencies

questions.explanation: Emergency response planning includes knowledge of the AWWA disinfection standards because emergency repairs still require proper disinfection of mains, wells, and storage before return to service. The standards guide that work; they do not replace the plan itself.

questions.question: How does a concrete thrust block actually resist the thrust at a fitting?

answers.text: It absorbs the force by compressing like a spring and then releasing it slowly, in every part of the distribution system and under all operating conditions
It transfers the force to the soil over the block's bearing area, spreading the load so the soil can carry it
It redirects the water around the fitting so no force develops
It glues the fitting to the pipe so the joint cannot move

questions.explanation: A thrust block bears against the soil and transfers the thrust to it over the block's bearing area; spreading the force over enough area keeps the soil from failing and the fitting from moving.

questions.question: A reservoir is refilled with noticeably turbid water and disinfection results disappoint despite an adequate measured residual. Why?

answers.text: Turbidity converts free chlorine to chloramine
Turbidity makes the DPD test read high
Turbidity raises the pH above the workable range
Suspended matter shields microorganisms from the chlorine

questions.explanation: Turbidity and suspended matter shield microorganisms from contact with the disinfectant, so organisms survive even where a residual is measured in the bulk water.

questions.question: To compare a service elevation with the system map, an operator converts a gauge reading of 25 psi to feet of head. What is the equivalent head?

answers.text: 50 ft
75 ft

questions.explanation: Head = psi x 2.31 = 25 x 2.31 = 57.75 ft. Dividing by 2.31 gives 10.82 ft, and using a factor of 2.0 or 3.0 gives the other incorrect figures.

questions.question: One system map is drawn at 1 inch = 100 ft and another at 1 inch = 500 ft. Compared with the first map, the second map shows what?

answers.text: A smaller ground area on the page, with more detail for each feature shown
A larger ground area on the page, with less detail for each feature shown
Exactly the same ground area, because both maps use inches the same way
Only underground features, because large scales are reserved for buried pipe

questions.explanation: At 1 inch = 500 ft, each inch covers five times the ground distance of the 1 inch = 100 ft map, so more area fits on the page but individual features are shown with less detail.

questions.question: After the impeller of a centrifugal pump has added velocity to the water, what does the volute (casing) do?

answers.text: Its widening passage slows the water and converts that velocity into pressure
It speeds the water up further so pressure keeps falling
It returns the water to the suction side of the pump so it can pass through the impeller again
It measures the flow and sends it to the register

questions.explanation: The volute's expanding passage converts the velocity the impeller added into pressure, which is the operating principle of a centrifugal pump. It does not return water to suction or meter the flow.

questions.question: Why does disinfection by-product sampling focus on locations where water has spent the most time in the distribution system?

answers.text: By-products form fastest in brand-new pipe near the entry point
By-products keep forming as water ages in the system, so their levels are highest where residence time is longest
Water at those locations is the easiest for samplers to reach
Formation stops once water leaves the treatment plant, so any site gives the same result, no matter how long the water has been sitting in the mains

questions.explanation: Disinfection by-products form as chlorine reacts with organic matter over time, so formation is greatest in the oldest water. Sampling at maximum-residence-time sites captures that worst case instead of the low formation seen near the entry point.

questions.question: At which of these fittings does the branch outlet create unbalanced thrust that calls for a thrust block or restrained joints?

answers.text: A straight coupling joining two aligned pipe ends in a continuous run, with no change of direction or branch at all
A short repair sleeve slipped over a break in a straight section
A tapping saddle strapped onto a straight barrel for a small service
A tee, where the branch leaves the run of the main

questions.explanation: A tee is a thrust point: pressure acting at the branch outlet creates unbalanced thrust, so the fitting is blocked against undisturbed soil or held with restrained joints.

questions.question: Water entering a chloraminated zone carries free ammonia. In what sequence do nitrifying bacteria transform that ammonia within the system?

answers.text: Ammonia is oxidized first to nitrite and then to nitrate
Ammonia is converted directly into nitrogen gas at once
Nitrate forms first and is then reduced to ammonia
Ammonia becomes chloramine and then inert solids

questions.explanation: Nitrification proceeds in steps: ammonia is oxidized to nitrite, and nitrite is then oxidized to nitrate. That sequence, driven by nitrifying bacteria, is how nitrate forms inside a distribution system.

questions.question: A system needs a strong, fast-acting disinfectant to carry the primary disinfection duty before water enters distribution. Why would chloramine be the wrong choice for that duty?

answers.text: Chloramine cannot be measured in the field, so the operator would have no way to confirm that any disinfectant was present in the water leaving the treatment plant
Chloramine is much weaker and slower than free chlorine and needs far more contact for the same kill
Chloramine forms trihalomethanes faster than free chlorine does, so using it for primary disinfection would raise by-product levels above those from free chlorination
Chloramine reacts instantly and is consumed within seconds, so none of it would survive long enough to provide even the first minutes of contact in the clear well

questions.explanation: Chloramines are much weaker disinfectants than free chlorine and require far higher contact for the same effect; that is why a stronger disinfectant carries the primary duty and chloramine serves as the persistent secondary residual.

questions.question: A repair replaces a section of main with a smaller-diameter section, and the same flow is pushed through it. Downstream pressure while flowing drops more than before. Why?

answers.text: The smaller section slows the water and saves head
The tank level must have fallen by the same amount at the same moment
Velocity rises in the smaller section, so friction head loss rises
Smaller pipe always raises pressure while flowing

questions.explanation: The same flow through a smaller area must move faster, and higher velocity means more friction, so head loss through the section increases and flowing pressure downstream drops further.

questions.question: A station has a duty pump and an identical standby pump, and the standby unit has not run in months. What maintenance practice should the operator follow?

answers.text: Leave the standby unit untouched until the duty pump fails, however many months that takes to happen
Rotate the pumps on schedule so the standby unit is exercised and wear is shared
Run both pumps together at all times to halve the load
Drain the standby pump and remove its coupling for storage

questions.explanation: Rotating duty and standby pumps exercises the standby unit, proves it will run, and shares wear between them. Leaving it idle for months risks finding it failed on the day it is needed.

questions.question: An alignment must bend gradually through unstable, shifting ground where a rigid line would be stressed at its joints. Which material's flexibility best fits the condition?

answers.text: Rigid steel pipe with welded joints throughout
Older cast iron with rigid leaded joints
Any material, because flexibility has no bearing on shifting ground
HDPE, which flexes with ground movement and is joined by fusion

questions.explanation: HDPE's flexibility lets it tolerate gradual curvature and ground movement, and its fused joints move with it; rigid materials and rigid joints concentrate that stress at the joints.

questions.question: In a chloraminated zone, nitrate measured at far-end taps is clearly higher than in water entering the zone, while no new source has been added. What is forming the nitrate?

answers.text: Scale sloughing off the inside of old heaters in the homes along the affected streets after many years of service
Backflow from a single customer's boiler
The gravel pack releasing stored nitrate
Nitrification within the distribution system, as bacteria oxidize ammonia first to nitrite and then to nitrate

questions.explanation: Nitrate can be formed inside the system itself: where free ammonia is present, nitrifying bacteria oxidize it to nitrite and on to nitrate, so levels grow with distance and time in a chloraminated zone.

questions.question: A round tank measures 40 ft across, and water stands 15 ft deep against its side wall. For the disinfection work plan, how much interior side-wall surface, in square feet, is wetted by the stored water?

answers.text: 125.66 sq ft

questions.explanation: Wall area = circumference x depth = 3.1416 x diameter x depth = 3.1416 x 40 x 15 = 1,884.96 sq ft. The 1,256.64 sq ft figure is the circular floor area, not the wall area.

questions.question: During inspection of a repair, an operator finds a joint that weeps steadily even though the bolts are evenly tightened, and removing the fitting shows its gasket torn and pinched. What is the correct finding and action?

answers.text: The weeping is normal and the repair should be backfilled as-is before the end of the working day
The bolts should be tightened further until the gasket crushes flat
The joint should be sealed from outside with tape and buried
The gasket is damaged; replace it and remake the joint before the repair is accepted

questions.explanation: A torn, pinched gasket cannot seal, so the gasket is replaced and the joint remade before acceptance. Overtightening, taping, or burying a weeping joint leaves a defective repair in the ground.

questions.question: A new bend is pressurized for the first time and is found pushed slightly out of line with a leaking joint, in a spot where no blocking or restraint was installed. What most likely caused the movement?

answers.text: Unbalanced thrust at the bend acted on the fitting with nothing to resist it
The water in the main became too warm and expanded the pipe
The gasket dissolved in the chlorinated water during the test, at every location in the system and at all times of the year
The pipe shrank in length as the trench cooled overnight

questions.explanation: At a bend, pressure produces unbalanced thrust that pushes the fitting; with no thrust block or restrained joint to resist it, the fitting moves and the joint leaks when the line is pressurized.

california-water-distribution-d3.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D3 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Chloroform belongs to which family of chlorination by-products?

answers.text: The haloacetic acids
The trihalomethanes
The inorganic disinfectants
The chloramines

questions.explanation: Chloroform is one of the trihalomethane compounds, the by-product family tracked together as total trihalomethanes.

questions.question: Which function belongs to a trunk main rather than to a transmission main?

answers.text: Moving raw water from a distant source directly into a treatment plant
Connecting one customer's meter directly to the main in the street out front
Carrying treated water between two storage facilities in different towns
Feeding the smaller distribution mains within a service area

questions.explanation: Inside a service area, the large feeder that supplies the smaller distribution mains is the trunk main. Source-to-plant and facility-to-facility bulk transfer is transmission work, and a meter connection is a service line.

questions.question: In corrosion work on coated pipe and tanks, what is a holiday?

answers.text: A scheduled shutdown day when coating crews are not allowed to work on the structure
A thickened ridge of coating left where two sprayed passes overlap on a tank wall
A pinhole or break in the coating that exposes bare metal
A test in which coating thickness is measured at random points along the pipeline

questions.explanation: A holiday is a pinhole or discontinuity in the coating that leaves bare metal exposed. Cathodic protection matters largely because it protects the metal at those holidays.

questions.question: Under a maintenance plan, what do maintenance records document?

answers.text: The parts a crew expects to order during the next budget cycle
What work was done, when it was done, and what was found
Complaints customers have phoned in about water quality
The training certificates held by each crew member

questions.explanation: Maintenance records document what work was done, when it was done, and what was found, so the history of each asset is available for planning and troubleshooting. Parts forecasts, customer complaints, and training certificates are kept in other records.

questions.question: Why is a thrust block placed behind the cap at the dead end of a pressurized main?

answers.text: To resist the thrust pushing on the cap
To hold the cap up off the trench bottom so groundwater cannot collect underneath the end of the main
To mark the end of the line for future locating crews, since a buried block of concrete is easy to find
To add weight to the end of the pipe run so the whole line settles evenly into its bedding over time

questions.explanation: Pressure acting on a cap creates unbalanced thrust that would push the fitting apart, and a thrust block resists that thrust by bearing against the soil. The block is not a support pad, a locating marker, or ballast.

questions.question: A tank operates with a disinfectant level of only 0.65 mg/L, so the water is held for 92 minutes of contact. Compute the CT obtained under those conditions.

answers.text: 59.80 mg-min/L
91.35 mg-min/L
119.60 mg-min/L
0.01 mg-min/L

questions.explanation: CT = residual x contact time = 0.65 mg/L x 92 min = 59.80 mg-min/L. The low level is compensated by the long interval in the product, not by adding the two numbers together.

questions.question: Tuberculation harms a main hydraulically in part because the corrosion deposits do what to the pipe interior?

answers.text: They polish the wall smoother, widening the effective bore the water passes through
They coat the wall with a thin even lining that leaves the bore exactly as built
They build inward, shrinking the effective bore the water must pass through
They dissolve the wall evenly, enlarging the bore beyond its original diameter

questions.explanation: Tubercles grow inward from the wall, so the opening left for water is smaller than the pipe's nominal bore. A smaller bore at the same flow means higher velocity through the opening and higher friction loss.

questions.question: A booster pump delivers 910 gpm against a total head of 98 ft while its driver supplies 36 brake horsepower. Calculate the pump efficiency.
questions.explanation: Water hp = 910 x 98 / 3960 = 22.52 hp; efficiency = 22.52 / 36 x 100 = 62.56%. Reporting 22.52% mistakes the water horsepower itself for the efficiency.

questions.question: A steel pipe carries a zinc coating. In galvanic terms, why does the zinc coating protect the steel beneath it?

answers.text: Zinc is more noble than steel, so the steel corrodes first and the coating is left untouched by the reaction
Zinc is more active than steel, so the zinc corrodes preferentially and sacrifices itself
Zinc and steel sit at the same point in the galvanic series, so neither metal ever corrodes
Zinc protects only by changing the taste of the water so corrosion products are not noticed

questions.explanation: Zinc sits above steel in the galvanic series as the more active, anodic metal. Joined to steel in water, the zinc corrodes preferentially, sacrificing itself while the steel is protected.

questions.question: How are Lead and Copper Rule tap samples collected differently from most other distribution samples?

answers.text: They are collected only after an extended high-velocity flush that scours the service line completely
They are taken from fire hydrants rather than from taps inside the homes selected for the sampling pool
They are first-draw samples taken after water stood in the plumbing
They are composited from several taps drawn at different times spread across an entire sampling day

questions.explanation: Lead and Copper Rule samples are first-draw samples drawn after the water has stood in the plumbing, which is the exception to the usual flush-before-sampling practice. That standing water is what contacts lead-bearing materials.

questions.question: Which observation is direct physical evidence of tuberculation, rather than an indirect sign of it?

answers.text: A cluster of discolored-water complaints logged from one neighborhood over the course of a single month
Rust tubercles visible on the inside surface of a fitting or section removed from the line
A hydrant flow test result that has fallen compared with tests from earlier years
A pumping record showing the station working harder to move the same flow

questions.explanation: Rust tubercles seen on the inside of a removed fitting or section are direct physical evidence of tuberculation. Complaints, falling flow tests, and rising pumping effort are indirect signs that point to the same condition.

questions.question: A routine water-quality report lists a supply's Langelier Index as approximately zero. How is that water classified?

answers.text: Strongly scale-forming, certain to plug household plumbing and water heaters with heavy calcium deposits
Strongly corrosive, certain to attack every metal surface it touches in the system
Approximately stable, tending neither to deposit scale nor to dissolve protective film
Completely free of dissolved minerals, hardness, and alkalinity of any kind at all

questions.explanation: An index near zero means the water is approximately stable, tending neither to deposit scale nor to dissolve protective film, because it sits close to calcium carbonate saturation.

questions.question: A cylindrical standpipe is being prepared for a disinfection job. Its diameter is 11 ft and it has been filled to a depth of 8 ft. How many gallons of water in the standpipe must be dosed?
questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x diameter squared x depth x 7.48 = 0.785 x 11 x 11 x 8 x 7.48 = 5,683.90 gal. The 759.88 figure is the volume in cubic feet, before the 7.48 conversion to gallons.

questions.question: An engineer sizing a new iron main expects its interior to roughen gradually in service. To be sure the main still meets its duty years later, how should the engineer treat friction in the design?

answers.text: Base the head-loss allowance on the highest C-factor the pipe will ever have, since friction only falls with age
Base the head-loss allowance on a lowered, aged-pipe C-factor rather than the new-pipe value, so capacity remains as the interior roughens
Leave friction out of the sizing entirely, because a new main's smoothness can be restored by flushing alone
Assume the C-factor will rise as deposits build, and count on the deposits to carry part of the flow and add their thickness to what the main is credited with carrying

questions.explanation: The design should base its head-loss allowance on a lowered, aged-pipe C-factor rather than the new-pipe value, so capacity remains as the interior roughens. Friction rises with age, deposits never carry flow, and flushing does not restore a design allowance that was never made.

questions.question: A single buried steel valve assembly at a remote site needs cathodic protection, and there is no electrical service anywhere near the site. Which protection approach fits this situation?

answers.text: Attach sacrificial anodes, which supply protective current with no external power source
Install an impressed-current system and run its rectifier from the nearest building regardless of distance
Leave the assembly unprotected, since cathodic protection is only ever applied to long pipelines
Apply a thicker coat of paint, which provides the same electrochemical protection as an anode system

questions.explanation: Sacrificial (galvanic) anodes supply protective current by corroding themselves and need no external power, so they fit an isolated structure with no electrical service. Impressed-current systems require a rectifier and a power source.

questions.question: After an earthquake, crews survey the damage across the system, rank repairs so water service can be restored to the most customers first, and lay out the steps to full recovery. Which emergency response activity is this?

answers.text: The vulnerability assessment, which is a pre-event review of assets, threats, and weak points only
Routine preventive maintenance scheduling, which plans ordinary work for the coming budget year
Public notification drafting, which only concerns the wording of messages sent during an emergency
Damage assessment and recovery planning

questions.explanation: After an event, assessing the damage, prioritizing restoration of service, and planning the recovery is damage assessment and recovery planning. The vulnerability assessment is the pre-event counterpart.

questions.question: Following heavy rain, nitrate levels rise in a shallow source surrounded by fertilized fields, and the increase is traced to water washing across the land surface. How is this source pathway classed?

answers.text: An inorganic contaminant reaching the water through surface runoff
An organic contaminant manufactured inside the distribution system by the disinfectant residual itself
A metal dissolved out of household plumbing by corrosive water standing in the pipes overnight
A mineral the groundwater dissolved directly out of solid bedrock deep below the fields

questions.explanation: This is an inorganic contaminant reaching the water through surface runoff: runoff is a recognized source of inorganic contaminants, and nitrate is one of the common inorganic compounds named for drinking water.

questions.question: A well job treats 0.05 MG at 30 mg/L using a liquid product of 12.5 percent strength weighing 10.0 lb per gallon. Determine how many gallons of liquid product the job requires.

answers.text: 1.25 gal

questions.explanation: Liquid (gal) = volume (MG) x dose x 8.34 / [(strength/100) x solution weight] = 0.05 x 30 x 8.34 / (0.125 x 10.0) = 10.01 gal. The 12.51 figure is pounds of available chlorine, before conversion into gallons of product.

questions.question: An operator partly closes a discharge valve at a booster station, making the system head curve steeper. The pump keeps running steadily. What happens to its operating point?

answers.text: It moves to a higher flow at a lower head along the same system curve
It moves to a lower flow at a higher head
It stays exactly where it was, because throttling a valve cannot change where the two curves cross in service
It jumps to the shutoff point and the pump stops delivering water altogether while still turning

questions.explanation: Throttling steepens the system curve, so it crosses the pump curve at a lower flow and a higher head. The duty point always sits where the pump curve and the system curve cross.

questions.question: A growing neighborhood is comfortable on an average day, but pressures collapse whenever peak customer use coincides with hydrant use during an incident. What does this pattern say about the main serving the area?

answers.text: It is oversized, and the excess diameter is letting the water slow down and lose its pressure at peak times
It is correctly sized, and the pressure loss proves the customers are simply using more water than expected
It is leaking at every joint, which is the only possible explanation whenever pressures fall during heavy use
It is undersized for the required demand

questions.explanation: A main that performs on an average day but fails when peak demand and fire flow coincide is undersized for its demand requirements. Demand requirements drive diameter selection precisely so the main holds adequate pressure at those moments.

california-water-distribution-d4.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D4 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly characterizes ultraviolet disinfection in a comparison of disinfectant options?

answers.text: It inactivates microorganisms, including Cryptosporidium, but provides no residual
It leaves a combined residual that can be measured at the far ends of the system
It works by forming hypochlorous acid when the lamps are switched on in the water
It removes the need for any disinfectant residual anywhere in the distribution system

questions.explanation: Ultraviolet light inactivates microorganisms, including Cryptosporidium, but it provides no residual at all. Because nothing persists after treatment, a residual disinfectant is still required to protect the distribution system.

questions.question: Why are station pressure gauges and test gauges placed on a calibration schedule?

answers.text: So gauges can be used as the shutoff devices for the pumps they monitor
So every gauge in the station displays exactly the same age and purchase date, and that single step by itself is sufficient for the whole system
So readings used for pump tests, pressure decisions, and records can be trusted to match actual pressure
So the station can stop recording pressures once gauges are certified

questions.explanation: Pump acceptance tests, efficiency calculations, and pressure management all rest on gauge readings. Scheduled calibration against a known standard keeps those readings, and the decisions built on them, trustworthy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a capital improvement and capital replacement plan for a distribution system?

answers.text: It lists office supplies and minor tools to be purchased during the year, so storeroom shelves can be restocked without special approval
It schedules employee vacations around construction season, so the maximum number of staff are away during the busiest work months
It identifies needed projects, their timing, and their funding, so aging infrastructure is replaced before it fails
It sets the price of water sold to neighboring systems, so wholesale deliveries can be billed at a uniform rate across the region

questions.explanation: Capital planning looks ahead: which assets will need replacement, when, and with what funding. Its point is planned replacement before failure, not supplies, scheduling, or wholesale pricing.

questions.question: In the primary drinking water standards, a maximum contaminant level is best defined as what?

answers.text: The highest level of a contaminant allowed in drinking water under the enforceable health-based standards
The level of a contaminant a laboratory hopes to achieve in a blank sample
The average concentration found across all systems in a national survey
A target that systems may exceed whenever treatment becomes expensive, or whenever meeting it would require capital spending the board would rather postpone to some later year instead

questions.explanation: The highest level of a contaminant allowed in drinking water under the enforceable health-based standards — An MCL is the enforceable ceiling for a contaminant in drinking water under the primary standards; a confirmed exceedance is a violation, not a missed target.

questions.question: Which description fits a confined aquifer?

answers.text: It lies open to the ground surface along its whole length, so rain anywhere above it enters the formation immediately
It is a layer of clay at the surface that stores water tightly and is pumped directly as the producing formation
It is sandwiched between low-permeability layers, and its water is under pressure within the formation
It has no confining beds and no pressure, so a well in it can never rise above the top of the formation

questions.explanation: A confined aquifer is sandwiched between low-permeability layers (aquitards or confining beds), and its water is under pressure.

questions.question: When a chloraminated system receives chlorine-like taste and odor complaints tied to speciation, which compounds are responsible?

answers.text: Monochloramine and free chlorine in equal parts
Dichloramine and trichloramine
Chloroform and the haloacetic acids
Nitrite and nitrate from the source water

questions.explanation: Dichloramine and trichloramine cause the chlorine-like taste and odor complaints in a chloraminated supply. Their appearance signals that feed ratio or mixing control has drifted away from favoring monochloramine.

questions.question: For a demand review, a service meter is read at 128,400 gallons and read again 15 days later at 173,100 gallons. What was the average use in gallons per day?

answers.text: 2980 gallons per day
3725 gallons per day
2235 gallons per day
2580 gallons per day

questions.explanation: Use = 173,100 - 128,400 = 44,700 gallons over 15 days. Average = 44,700 / 15 = 2980 gallons per day.

questions.question: Why does slowing a pump with a variable-frequency drive to match demand generally use less energy than throttling a discharge valve at full speed?

answers.text: Because a throttled valve converts the surplus head into wasted energy, while slowing the pump reduces the head and flow the pump actually produces
Because a drive eliminates the need for any discharge piping at the station, whatever the actual conditions found at the site turn out to be
Because a slowed pump produces more head than a full-speed pump does
Because throttling a valve increases the electrical efficiency of the motor

questions.explanation: Throttling burns the surplus head across the valve while the pump still produces it. Reducing speed lowers the pump's own output to what the system needs, so less energy is produced only to be wasted.

questions.question: A confirmed result establishes a maximum contaminant level violation. A sample taken weeks later is below the level. What is the status of the violation?

answers.text: It stands — the violation must still be addressed through the required notification and correction, despite the later lower result
It is cancelled automatically, because any later passing result erases an earlier violation
It never existed, because the later result is the most recent information about the system

It converts into a secondary-standard issue, because time has passed since the confirmed result, because the newest laboratory report is always the one that decides whether a violation ever existed in the first place

questions.explanation: A later lower sample does not erase a confirmed violation; the violation stands and the required notification and correction still apply. The later result is useful operating information, not a cancellation.

questions.question: During a distribution emergency, the public-notification element of response planning exists to give the people served what?

answers.text: Timely information about what happened, what protective actions to take, and where to get updates
A technical engineering report on the failed asset once repairs are finished
Reassurance that no information will be released until every fact is final
Instructions to direct all questions to neighboring water systems instead

questions.explanation: Timely information about what happened, what protective actions to take, and where to get updates — Emergency public notification tells affected people what happened, the potential effects and protective actions, and where to get more information, through paths that actually reach them.

questions.question: A crew preparing a trench places a layer of selected granular material along the bottom before the pipe is lowered in. What job does that layer do for the pipe once the line is in service?

answers.text: It raises the pipe above the trench floor so groundwater can flow freely underneath the line, whether or not anyone outside the system ever learns of it
It colors the trench bottom so inspectors can tell at a glance where the pipe was laid
It replaces the need for compaction of the backfill placed over the pipe later in the job
It supports the pipe evenly along its barrel on suitable material, so loads do not point-load the pipe

questions.explanation: Bedding supports the pipe evenly along its barrel on suitable material, so loads do not point-load the pipe. Point loading on an unsupported section can crack or deflect the pipe; even support along the barrel is what the bedding is placed to provide.

questions.question: Which set of compounds belongs to the common organic contaminants a distribution chief operator should recognize by name?

answers.text: Volatile organic solvents, pesticides, and the trihalomethanes
Calcium, magnesium, and dissolved solids, because conditions at one location on one day are assumed to describe every part of the system at all times
Lead, copper, arsenic, and nitrate, and the item is simply carried forward unchanged from one operating period to the next without review
Chloride, sulfate, and bicarbonate only, which rests on treating a single favorable result as proof that the underlying condition cannot change

questions.explanation: The common organic contaminant compounds recognized at name level are the volatile organic solvents, pesticides, and trihalomethanes. Lead, copper, arsenic, and nitrate are inorganic contaminants, and the remaining sets are ordinary dissolved minerals rather than the named organic compounds.

questions.question: Auditing the reference shelf before a season of disinfection work, the chief operator confirms how the industry disinfection standards are organized. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Separate disinfection standards govern water mains, wells, and storage facilities respectively
One single standard covers mains, wells, and storage facilities with identical steps
Disinfection standards exist only for storage facilities, not for mains or wells
Disinfection of mains and wells is unstandardized and left entirely to each crew

questions.explanation: The disinfection standards are organized by facility type, with a standard governing water mains, a standard governing wells, and a standard governing storage facilities. The applicable standard's procedure governs the disinfection work for that facility.

questions.question: Build-out of a subdivision doubles the peak flow carried by the same feeder main, and no change is made to the pipe itself. What should the chief operator expect to happen to that feeder's hydraulic gradient at peak hour?

answers.text: It will steepen, because the higher flow consumes more head to friction in each unit of length
It will flatten, because a greater volume of moving water carries its own head with it as it travels
It will stay exactly the same, because gradient is a property of the pipe and never of the flow in it
It will disappear at peak hour, because the pumps supplying the feeder raise their discharge head then

questions.explanation: Correct: It will steepen, because the higher flow consumes more head to friction in each unit of length. Pushing more water through the same passage raises friction loss per foot, so the grade line falls faster along the feeder.

questions.question: At the same flow, one reach of a system shows a much steeper hydraulic gradient than the reaches on either side of it. What should the chief operator conclude about that reach?

answers.text: It is consuming more head per unit length, pointing to a smaller, rougher, or more restricted passage than its neighbors
It is gaining energy from the surrounding reaches and should be left alone until the gradient reverses itself, which may take several full seasons of normal operation to occur
It proves the reach is oversized for its flow and is the best candidate for immediate downsizing in place
It has no operational meaning, because gradients can only be compared between different systems, never within one

questions.explanation: A steeper gradient means more head is being consumed per unit length in that reach. At a common flow, that points to a smaller, rougher, or restricted passage compared with the flatter neighboring reaches.

questions.question: For one quarter, a utility's ledgers put all of its source, treatment, and pumping expense at $244,800, while its source meters delivered 120 MG into distribution over those same three months. On a per-million-gallons basis, what did production cost?
questions.explanation: $2,040.00/MG — Production cost = total cost / volume = $244,800 / 120 MG = $2,040.00/MG.

questions.question: At the same pumping rate used in past seasons, a well's water level now drops considerably farther during each run and takes longer to come back afterward. What should the chief operator schedule?

answers.text: Nothing, because a well's drawdown and recovery pattern never changes over the life of a properly built well
A permanent increase in pumping rate, because producing more water is the standard cure for a falling pumping level
An inspection of the well and its pumping condition, because worsening drawdown and recovery signal the well or its producing zone is deteriorating
A reduction in monitoring, because level records that show a worsening trend are usually discarded as unreliable data

questions.explanation: Drawdown that grows at the same pumping rate, with slower recovery, is a deteriorating-well signal. The chief-operator response is to schedule inspection of the well rather than ignore or out-pump the trend.

questions.question: A contractor is mobilized, grout is on site, and the crew is ready to seal a retired well this morning, but the overseeing agency's required authorization for the work has not yet been obtained. What should the chief operator do?

answers.text: Fill only the screen interval and postpone the paperwork indefinitely
Tell the crew to seal the well quickly before the agency learns of the job
Cap the well at the surface and record the abandonment as complete
Hold the sealing work until the required authorization and notification are in place, then proceed

questions.explanation: Well abandonment is done under the required authorization and notification of the overseeing agency, which must be covered before the work proceeds. The correct answer is: Hold the sealing work until the required authorization and notification are in place, then proceed.

questions.question: A major break has pulled pressure to near zero across a district and muddy water has entered the broken main. Laboratory confirmation will take time, and customers are already asking whether the water is safe. What chief-operator decision fits the emergency and notification framework?

answers.text: Issue prompt public notification with the required protective guidance while pressure is restored, the area is flushed and disinfected, and sampling proceeds
Say nothing publicly until laboratory results return, even though customers are drinking the water in the meantime and asking the system directly whether it is safe to use today
Announce that the water is definitely safe, since no laboratory has yet confirmed any contamination in the district
Notify only the customers who happen to telephone the office, one call at a time

questions.explanation: Issue prompt public notification with the required protective guidance while pressure is restored, the area is flushed and disinfected, and sampling proceeds — Acute contamination risk is not held for laboratory certainty: the response plan and notification framework require prompt notice with protective guidance alongside isolation, restoration, disinfection, and sampling.

questions.question: A developer asks the system to commit service to a large new subdivision at the edge of the service area. Current customers are fully supplied, and the added demand has not yet been compared with anything. What must the chief operator do before supporting the commitment?

answers.text: Approve the commitment because current customers are supplied today and new connections can be sorted out as they are built over the coming years
Approve it on the strength of wet-year production records alone, since those are the most recent complete figures the system holds
Compare the projected added demand with the dependable long-term supply, including source rights and dry-year capacity
Decline to evaluate supply at all and leave the question entirely to the developer's engineer

questions.explanation: Compare the projected added demand with the dependable long-term supply, including source rights and dry-year capacity — Service commitments add permanent demand; the chief operator tests projected demand against dependable long-term supply, source capacity and rights, and dry-year performance before the system promises water it may not dependably have.

california-water-distribution-d5.quiz_title: California Water Distribution D5 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: On the chlorine curve used to oversee a chlorination program, what does the sharp dip in residual mark?

answers.text: The point where combined residual first begins to form as chlorine meets ammonia in the water
The point where all chlorine demand has returned and the residual climbs back to its peak value
The point where chloramine formation stops permanently and only combined residual can exist
The breakpoint, after which added chlorine produces a proportional free residual

questions.explanation: As chlorine is added it first satisfies demand, then forms chloramines, then destroys them, and the residual falls to the breakpoint dip; beyond that point additional chlorine appears as free residual in proportion to the dose. The earlier rise is chloramine formation, and past the dip the residual is predominantly free, not combined.

questions.question: A well has a static water level of 132 feet and a pumping water level of 185 feet. What is the drawdown?

answers.text: 53 feet
36 feet
71 feet
44 feet

questions.explanation: Drawdown = pumping level - static level. Substituting: 185 - 132 = 53 feet. The other figures come from adding the levels, reversing parts of the subtraction, or using an incorrect difference.

questions.question: The reporting and recordkeeping duties a system carries are best stated as which practice?

answers.text: Results are reported when the system's annual report is convenient to prepare, and records are kept at crew discretion
Monitoring results are reported to the state primacy agency on the required schedule, and records are retained and available
Only results that exceed a limit are reported, and records of routine results may be discarded once billed
Records are retained by the contract laboratory, relieving the system of any recordkeeping duty of its own

questions.explanation: The system reports its monitoring results to the primacy agency on schedule and retains its records so they are available. Convenience timing, exceedance-only reporting, and shifting retention to a laboratory each break duties the system itself carries.

questions.question: Which statement states the operator-manager's duty for stationary-source air authorizations?

answers.text: Keep required permits current and operate the equipment within the conditions of those permits
Keep permits only for sources that run every day, and let standby equipment paperwork lapse
Keep a single permit for the whole utility regardless of how many sources or sites it operates
Keep permits current only until the equipment passes its first successful operating season

questions.explanation: The duty has two halves: authorizations stay current, and operation stays within their conditions, for the sources the utility runs. Standby use, multiple sites, and time in service do not shrink that duty.

questions.question: A laboratory reports a presumptive result on a sample. That term means the result is:

answers.text: A preliminary positive indication from an initial test that further specific testing must verify
A final verified finding ready to report as a confirmed contamination event
Proof that no contamination is present and the sample can be discarded
A result obtained only after a second laboratory repeats the full analysis

questions.explanation: Presumptive means the initial test suggests a positive that confirmation testing has not yet verified. It is not the final finding, it does not clear the sample, and confirmation — not mere repetition by another laboratory — is what converts it.

questions.question: A chloramine booster review records 4.37 mg/L of chlorine and 0.92 mg/L of ammonia, both expressed by weight. What is the chlorine-to-ammonia ratio?
questions.explanation: Ratio = chlorine ÷ ammonia = 4.37 mg/L ÷ 0.92 mg/L = 4.75, expressed as 4.75 to 1. The other values come from dividing by a different ammonia figure.

questions.question: A cold-climate system where the barrel must not hold water that can freeze specifies hydrants for a new development. Which choice matches that need?

answers.text: Wet-barrel hydrants with water standing in the barrel at all times
Dry-barrel hydrants, whose barrel drains after use with the main valve below the frost line
Either type, because climate has no bearing on hydrant selection
Hydrants with no main valve so the barrel stays full

questions.explanation: A dry-barrel hydrant keeps its main valve below the frost line and drains the barrel after use, preventing freeze damage in cold climates. A wet barrel holds water up to the outlets, which is suited to warm climates, and climate is a deciding factor rather than an irrelevance.

questions.question: A chief operator drafts the revenue side of next year's budget. Which source should the forecast treat as the principal revenue the system depends on?

answers.text: Depreciation recovered from the system's own asset accounts
Insurance proceeds expected from losses that have not occurred
Rate revenue collected from the customers the system serves
Reserve balances accumulated in earlier years, counted again as new revenue

questions.explanation: Rate revenue from customers is the principal money coming into a water system and the foundation of its revenue forecast. Depreciation is a cost allocation rather than income, hypothetical insurance proceeds are not a revenue plan, and counting old reserves again as new revenue double-counts the same money.

questions.question: A chief operator conducts water audits on a regular cycle and compares the loss results from one audit to the next. What does that comparison allow management to do?

answers.text: Retire the system's production meters once two audits agree
Treat a single favorable audit as having fixed the system's loss rate permanently, with no need to audit again in future years
Show whether loss-control efforts are reducing losses over time, and support continued funding for the programs that work
Set the chlorine residual targets for the distribution system

questions.explanation: One audit is a snapshot; a series of audits is a trend, and the trend is what tells management whether leak-control and metering programs are working and deserve their funding. Audits depend on accurate production metering rather than replacing it, loss rates change as the system changes, and audit results do not set disinfection targets.

questions.question: To close a one-year budget gap, a proposal deletes the system's insurance line entirely. What is the chief operator's sound objection?

answers.text: Insurance premiums are the system's largest single source of revenue
System assets cannot be damaged in any year the system carries no insurance
The deletion is sound because risk management and insurance are administrative extras rather than real components of the system's budget, and several systems operate without them
A single uninsured loss or liability claim could cost far more than the premiums saved, because insurance is how the budget absorbs that risk

questions.explanation: Insurance and risk management are named budget components because they protect the system against loss and liability. Removing them saves a predictable premium while exposing the system to an unpredictable loss that could dwarf the saving. Premiums are an expenditure, not revenue, and going uninsured changes who bears a loss, not whether losses occur.

questions.question: During a capacity study, water moves at 2.6 ft/s through a main whose inside diameter is 1.5 ft. Express that main's carrying capacity in gallons per minute.
questions.explanation: Pipe capacity = 0.785 x diameter squared x velocity x 448.8. Substituting: 0.785 x 1.5 x 1.5 = 1.77 sq ft; 1.77 x 2.6 = 4.59 cu ft/s; 4.59 x 448.8 = 2,061.01 gpm. The other values result from using a smaller diameter, a higher velocity, or skipping the gallons-per-minute conversion.

questions.question: A proposed well site sits in dense fractured bedrock rather than alluvial deposits. Which yield expectation should guide the program decision?

answers.text: Expect the highest and steadiest yields in the system from the solid rock itself
Expect the rock to behave like clean sand and gravel for storage
Expect yield to depend only on the pump size selected
Expect yield only where fractures are intersected, with output that is typically modest and variable compared with good alluvial aquifers

questions.explanation: Fractured bedrock holds and transmits water in its fractures, so wells produce only where fractures are hit and yields are typically modest and variable beside productive alluvium. The solid rock matrix is not a high-yield or sand-like storage medium, and pump size cannot create aquifer yield.

questions.question: A developer proposes extending an already long dead-end main to serve many more homes at its far end. What concern should weigh most in the chief operator's response?

answers.text: The extension is ideal, because dead ends improve as more homes are added to them and a single feed becomes more dependable the more homes depend on it
The added homes would all depend on one path with aging water at the end, so looping or another feed should be part of the proposal
The only concern is paint color for the new hydrants along the extension
More homes on a dead end remove any need to think about water age there

questions.explanation: Every added home on a single dead-end path deepens dependence on that one feed and lengthens the water's travel to the far end, so a looped or second feed belongs in the proposal. A longer dead end does not improve with crowding, hydrant appearance is trivial beside supply and quality, and added homes make water age more important to address, not less.

questions.question: A gate valve that is fully opened still passes almost no flow, and the stem turns without the usual resistance change. What does this most likely indicate?

answers.text: The valve is throttling correctly as gate valves are designed to do, which is the normal way a gate valve is meant to control flow
The downstream meter is reading too slowly
The main needs a higher chlorine dose
The gate has separated from the stem or the valve is otherwise internally failed

questions.explanation: Loss of stem-to-gate connection or internal failure explains a valve that operates at the stem but does not open the passage. Gate valves are isolation valves rather than throttling devices, and meter accuracy or chlorine dose cannot block flow at an open valve.

questions.question: Per-capita use in a system has fallen steadily for years as efficient fixtures spread. What error results from applying the oldest, highest per-capita figure to the future population?

answers.text: Future needs are understated, because efficient fixtures raise daily use per person
There is no error, because per-capita use never changes over time
The projection becomes a rate schedule instead of a demand estimate
Future needs are overstated, because the figure assumes each person will use more than current behavior shows

questions.explanation: Applying an outdated high per-capita figure to future population overstates need when actual per-person use has been falling. Efficient fixtures lower rather than raise per-person use, per-capita use does change over time, and the result is still a demand estimate, just an inflated one.

questions.question: A rate study shows a large increase is needed to reach the revenue requirement, and the board wants to avoid imposing it all in one year. What is the sound rate-setting approach?

answers.text: Postpone all increases indefinitely and let reserves absorb the gap with no schedule
Adopt a schedule of planned step increases that reaches the requirement over a defined period, checking revenue against expenditures at each step
Raise only the rates of the newest customers until the gap closes
Set rates once and bar any future review of the schedule

questions.explanation: A phased schedule of step increases reaches the revenue requirement over a set period while each step is tested against expenditures. Indefinite postponement depletes reserves with no path to balance, singling out new customers is not cost-of-service allocation, and the schedule must remain open to review as conditions change.

questions.question: A wellfield's combined pumping has deepened the overlapping drawdown between two wells so much that one pump is breaking suction. What is the soundest operating response?

answers.text: Run both wells at maximum rate continuously to outpace the drawdown
Seal the lower-yielding well the same day without evaluating the field, as the routine first step to take in every case of this kind
Coordinate the wells' pumping, such as staggering or reducing rates, so their cones of depression interfere less
Raise the breaking-suction pump higher above the water level

questions.explanation: Overlapping cones of depression add drawdown at each well; coordinating schedules and rates reduces that interference. Pumping harder deepens the cones, sealing a well is a drastic step before evaluation, and raising a pump worsens suction conditions rather than fixing them.

questions.question: As part of a capacity project, a chief operator needs the total force acting on a closed gate valve that is 1.5 ft in diameter with 70 psi held against it. What total force should be used?
questions.explanation: Total force = 0.785 x diameter^2 x 144 x pressure = 0.785 x 1.5^2 x 144 x 70 = 0.785 x 2.25 x 144 x 70 = 17,803.80 lb. Using the diameter without squaring it understates the area and the force, while the smallest figure omits the pressure conversion across the valve area.

questions.question: During budget preparation, a utility lists four annual amounts: $1,125,000 for operations and maintenance, $475,000 for capital work, $298,000 for debt service, and $142,000 for reserve contributions. What total must the budget carry as the system's annual expenditures?
questions.explanation: Annual expenditures = operations and maintenance + capital + debt service + reserves = $1,125,000 + $475,000 + $298,000 + $142,000 = $2,040,000. Leaving out the reserve contributions gives $1,898,000, leaving out debt service gives $1,742,000, and counting the reserves twice gives $2,182,000.

questions.question: A chief operator judges the health of the maintenance program by tracking the share of work orders that are planned preventive work versus emergency repairs. A steadily rising emergency share indicates that:

answers.text: The maintenance program is improving, because crews are responding to emergencies faster and closing them out sooner
The system has too many preventive tasks and should schedule fewer of them
Emergency repairs are cheaper in the long run than planned maintenance
The preventive program is failing, because work is increasingly being done only after equipment breaks down

questions.explanation: A maintenance program exists to do work on schedule, before failure. When the balance shifts toward emergency work, assets are running to failure and the system is paying breakdown prices in money and service interruptions. Fast emergency response does not repair a failed preventive program, and cutting preventive tasks accelerates the trend.

california-water-treatment-t1.quiz_title: California Water Treatment T1 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the main purpose of screens at a surface-water intake?

answers.text: To disinfect the raw water as it enters the plant.
To keep fish, leaves, sticks, and other large debris out of the intake and pumps.
To remove dissolved minerals and soften the water before it reaches the treatment processes inside the plant building.
To measure the flow entering the plant.

questions.explanation: Screens at a surface-water intake block large debris such as leaves, sticks, and trash from entering the intake structure. This protects pumps and downstream equipment from clogging and damage.

questions.question: Which pairing of taste-and-odor causes is correct?

answers.text: Geosmin and MIB from algae and actinomycetes - earthy or musty; Phenols reacting with chlorine - medicinal
Geosmin and MIB - rotten egg; Phenols - earthy or musty only
Geosmin and MIB - metallic; Phenols - no odor after chlorination
Geosmin and MIB - caused by lime feed at the treatment plant during softening; Phenols - caused by aeration in an open finished-water basin

questions.explanation: Geosmin and MIB, produced by algae and actinomycetes, cause earthy and musty tastes and odors, while phenols react with chlorine to form compounds with a medicinal taste and odor. Each cause has a distinct odor character.

questions.question: How does activated carbon remove taste- and odor-causing compounds from water?

answers.text: By adsorption, in which the compounds stick to the carbon's very large surface area as water passes, instead of being strained out like particles in a filter.
By chlorination, in which the carbon slowly releases chlorine that burns up the odor compounds dissolved in the water.
By dissolving into the water and neutralizing the odor compounds chemically, the way an acid neutralizes a base.
By settling, in which the carbon grains sink and drag the lighter odor compounds down to the bottom of the contactor with them.

questions.explanation: Activated carbon works by adsorption: taste- and odor-causing molecules adhere to the enormous internal surface area of the carbon as water contacts it. It does not disinfect the water or strain particles the way a filter bed does.

questions.question: Why do plants rotate duty and standby pumps on a regular schedule?

answers.text: So the duty pump can be worn out completely before the standby is ever used
Because a pump that rests rusts solid within a few days
To keep the standby pump's warranty paperwork current
Rotation evens out wear and proves the standby unit still starts and runs when it is needed

questions.explanation: Rotating service shares run time between units and regularly proves the standby will start and perform, instead of discovering a dead standby during an emergency. It also evens wear across the set.

questions.question: Which pair of limits applies to disinfection byproducts in drinking water?

answers.text: Total trihalomethanes at 0.60 mg/L and haloacetic acids at 0.80 mg/L in drinking water
Total trihalomethanes at 0.080 mg/L and haloacetic acids at 0.060 mg/L
Total trihalomethanes at 0.015 mg/L and haloacetic acids at 1.3 mg/L
Total trihalomethanes at 4.0 mg/L and haloacetic acids at 4.0 mg/L

questions.explanation: The limits are 0.080 mg/L for total trihalomethanes and 0.060 mg/L for haloacetic acids, the two regulated groups of disinfection byproducts. Monitoring is done at locations including maximum-residence-time sites, where byproducts have the most time to form.

questions.question: Which statement best describes surface water from a river or reservoir used as a drinking water source?

answers.text: Its temperature and turbidity stay nearly the same all year, even during storms, heavy runoff, and hot summer weather.
Its turbidity, temperature, and algae levels can change with the seasons, so it needs full treatment.
It normally contains more dissolved minerals than groundwater.
It rarely contains microorganisms of any kind.

questions.explanation: Surface water is exposed to weather, runoff, and sunlight, so its turbidity, temperature, and algae content vary seasonally. Because of that variability and its microbial load, surface water requires full treatment.

questions.question: Which description best fits typical groundwater compared with surface water from a river?

answers.text: Its temperature swings widely from week to week with the weather, and it changes even faster than the river water it is compared with here.
Its temperature and quality stay fairly steady, it often carries more dissolved minerals, and it usually has low turbidity.
It always needs no disinfection under any condition.
It carries more algae than a reservoir in summer.

questions.explanation: Water moving slowly through soil and rock is shielded from weather, so groundwater temperature and quality are comparatively constant and turbidity is low. Contact with rock also dissolves more minerals, so hardness and iron or manganese are common.

questions.question: The free chlorine residual in treated water is best described as the chlorine that does what?

answers.text: Was consumed destroying reducing compounds present in the raw water
Remains after the demand is met, available for disinfection
Was lost to the atmosphere during feeding
Exists only in combined chloramine form

questions.explanation: Residual is what is left of the applied dose after the chlorine demand has been satisfied, and it remains available to disinfect and protect the water.

questions.question: Why is prompt cleanup of chemical spills and drips in a feed area part of equipment maintenance, not just tidiness?

answers.text: Spilled chemical left in place corrodes pumps, piping, and concrete and creates a slipping and exposure hazard
Inspectors grade the plant mainly on how shiny the floors are
Dried chemical residue improves the grip of pump seals
Leftover chemical on the floor can be swept back into the day tank later

questions.explanation: Many feed chemicals attack metal and concrete, so residue left standing quietly corrodes the equipment it sits on while also endangering staff. Prompt cleanup, with floors kept clear and dry, protects both equipment and operators.

questions.question: Why are chemical feed lines flushed with clean water after maintenance work on the line is finished?

answers.text: To raise the chemical concentration in the line before it returns to service
To warm the line so the feed pump primes faster
To wash out leftover chemical and loosened debris so the line returns to service clean and clear
To fill the line completely with water for a full week so operators can postpone restarting the feeder and still record the system as ready for service without checking it

questions.explanation: Maintenance can leave residual chemical, scale, and debris inside a feed line. Flushing with clean water clears those materials out before the feeder restarts, so they are not pushed into the process or left to plug the line and injection point.

questions.question: Besides the DPD colorimetric method, another approved procedure for measuring chlorine is:

answers.text: Amperometric titration
Estimating from the water temperature
Comparing odor strength between samples
Reading the sample in a turbidity tube

questions.explanation: Amperometric titration is another approved method for chlorine analysis. Approved chlorine procedures come from Standard Methods and other approved method sources, not from estimates based on temperature or odor.

questions.question: In a lockout/tagout program, who is the authorized employee for a piece of equipment?

answers.text: The newest employee on the crew, who is assigned lockout duties as part of learning the plant during the first months of employment
Any employee who happens to be working in the same building, whether or not that person will touch or service the equipment
The trained employee who applies the lock and tag and performs the servicing or maintenance on that equipment
The office staff member who keeps the inventory of locks, tags, and hasps and issues them to maintenance crews on request

questions.explanation: The authorized employee is the trained person who locks out, tags out, and services the equipment. Other employees who use or work around the equipment have a different role and different duties under the program.

questions.question: Besides the well's own construction details, what does the driller's log record about what was found underground during drilling?

answers.text: Only the final depth reached on the last day of drilling, with no note of anything that was passed through on the way down to that depth at any point in the work.
The chlorine dose used on the first day of operation.
The kinds and thicknesses of the formations passed through and the depths where water-bearing zones were met.
The names of every customer the well will serve.

questions.explanation: The driller's log records the sequence of materials drilled through, their depths and thicknesses, and where water-bearing zones were encountered, alongside the casing and screen details. Those formation notes are what let later operators understand the aquifer the well draws from and plan work on the well.

questions.question: A customer's water heater pops and rumbles, heats slowly, and is found coated inside with a white, chalky mineral layer. What kind of water produces this?

answers.text: Scale-forming hard water, which deposits calcium carbonate scale on hot surfaces as the water is heated.
Very soft, corrosive water, which eats away the tank lining and leaves the metal bare, thin, and pitted throughout the heater.
Highly chlorinated water, which bleaches the inside of the tank and leaves a pale chemical residue on the heating elements.
Turbid water, whose suspended silt settles out in the tank and bakes into a hard gray layer on the bottom.

questions.explanation: Hard, scale-forming water deposits calcium carbonate as a white, chalky scale, especially on hot surfaces like water-heater elements and tank walls. The insulating scale makes the heater work harder, heat slowly, and wear out sooner.

questions.question: An impeller removed from a pump that ran for months with low suction pressure shows metal that looks eaten away and spongy, worst near the eye of the impeller. What caused this damage?

answers.text: Cavitation — vapor bubbles formed in the low-pressure zone and collapsed on the metal, pitting it away over time
Normal polishing from clean water flowing over the metal
Paint failure on the outside of the pump casing
Sand blasting done intentionally during manufacturing

questions.explanation: Cavitation damage has a distinctive pitted, spongy look where collapsing vapor bubbles hammer the metal surface, typically near the impeller eye. It is damage from operation with inadequate suction pressure, not normal wear.

questions.question: A routine quality control check run with a batch of samples comes back outside its acceptable range. What should the operator do with the sample results from that batch?

answers.text: Report them as usual, since one failed check rarely matters for a routine batch of samples
Adjust each sample result by the amount the check was off and then report the corrected values
Set the results aside, flag them as questionable, re-run the check, and notify a supervisor
Discard the sample results without recording that the quality control check ever failed

questions.explanation: When a quality control check fails, the associated results cannot be trusted until the problem is found. The results are flagged rather than reported, the check is re-run, and a supervisor is notified so the cause can be corrected.

questions.question: A plant's monthly operating record shows iron entering a treatment step at 1.80 mg/L and leaving at 0.30 mg/L. What is the percent reduction in iron across the step?
questions.explanation: Percent removal = (in - out) / in x 100 = (1.80 - 0.30) / 1.80 x 100 = 83.3%. The iron concentration fell by 83.3% across the step.

questions.question: Two neighboring wells tap different aquifers. In the shallow well, the level marks the top of the saturated zone; in the deep confined well, the level stands far above the top of its aquifer. What is the level in the deep well called?

answers.text: The water table, exactly the same surface as in the shallow well.
The potentiometric surface, the level to which water rises in wells tapping the confined aquifer under its pressure.
The cone of depression, which forms only while a well is actively pumping at a steady rate and disappears completely as soon as the pump is switched off and the level recovers.
The static level of the shallow aquifer only.

questions.explanation: The water table is the actual top of saturation in an unconfined aquifer, while the potentiometric surface is the imaginary surface defined by the levels water reaches in wells in a pressurized, confined aquifer. Recognizing which surface a well shows tells the operator which kind of aquifer it taps.
