questions.explanation: Within the distribution system, Texas caps free chlorine or chloramine at a maximum residual disinfectant level of 4.0 mg/L on a running annual average, so a 4.6 average exceeds the limit. Staying above the minimum residual does not excuse exceeding that cap.

questions.question: A new water main must pass beneath a state highway that cannot be open-cut. The crew bores under the road, installs a large steel pipe through the bore, and then runs the water main inside it. What is the large outer pipe's job?

answers.text: It is a casing shielding the inner carrier main from road loads, so the main can be replaced without excavating the highway
It is a second water main running in parallel that doubles the flow capacity of the crossing during hours of peak demand each day
It is a spare empty main that stays dry and is connected only if the inner main ever fails in service
It is a drain sleeve that carries groundwater seepage from one side of the roadbed to the other side

questions.explanation: The outer pipe is a casing: it carries the traffic loads and protects the carrier main inside it, and the carrier can later be withdrawn and replaced through the casing without disturbing the road. It conveys no water itself, so it adds no parallel capacity to the crossing.

questions.question: On a routine visit, a new operator finds drums of diesel fuel and herbicide stored against the wellhouse wall, a few feet from the wellhead of a small groundwater system. What is the best response?

answers.text: Cover the drums with a heavy tarp so rain cannot reach them, and leave them stored where they are.
Move the drums inside the wellhouse so they are stored out of the weather next to the wellhead.
Report the storage to the supervisor and have the fuel and chemicals moved to a storage area well away from the wellhead.
Take no action at all, because the drums are not a problem as long as every lid is closed tightly and the drums look sound.

questions.explanation: Fuel and chemicals stored beside a wellhead can spill or leak and migrate to the groundwater the well draws from, so they belong in storage away from the well. A tarp or a closed lid does not remove the spill risk, and moving them indoors puts them even closer to the well.

questions.question: The chief operator of a small groundwater system is away for two weeks, and a licensed operator steps in with overall responsibility for the system during that absence. What is that operator's role called?

answers.text: Chief operator pro tem, a separate license class
Operator-in-training
Contract operator, regardless of the employment relationship, whenever the operator works for an operations company rather than the system itself
Operator-in-charge, the individual with overall responsibility for the system in the chief operator's absence

questions.explanation: The operator-in-charge is defined as the individual who has overall responsibility for the operation of a public water system in the absence of the chief operator. An operator-in-training is by definition unlicensed and in training, so that title cannot fit a licensed operator carrying full responsibility.

questions.question: A plant treats 0.38 MGD and needs a dose of 3.4 mg/L. The chemical product is 85 percent pure. How many pounds of product must be fed per day?

answers.text: 10.78 lb/day
12.68 lb/day
9.16 lb/day
20.29 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds of pure chemical = 0.38 x 3.4 x 8.34 = 10.78 lb/day, and dividing by the purity fraction 0.85 gives 12.68 lb/day of product. Feeding only 10.78 lb/day ignores the purity adjustment and underfeeds.

questions.question: How do the mini and midi parts of a basic extended reporting period differ?

answers.text: The mini part covers new acts and the midi part covers old acts, in accordance with the policy conditions, under the policy form in effect, and consistent with the wording of the form edition in effect during the policy period

The mini part is the short 60-day window for reporting claims from unreported occurrences, while the midi part is the five-year window for claims arising from an occurrence that was reported within that 60-day window
The mini part lasts five years and the midi part lasts 60 days
Both parts require an additional premium

questions.explanation: The labels track the two lengths in the basic period: 60 days and five years, with the longer one conditioned on reporting the occurrence in the shorter one. Neither part is a purchased feature.

questions.question: A loss occurs two days before the stated effective date of a proper cancellation. How does the cancellation affect that loss?

answers.text: It does not affect it, because coverage was still in force when the loss occurred
The loss is denied because cancellation was already in process
The loss is paid only if the insured withdraws the cancellation
The loss is treated as occurring under the next policy term

questions.explanation: Cancellation operates prospectively from its effective date; losses occurring while coverage was in force remain subject to the policy. A pending cancellation does not erase an earlier covered loss.

questions.question: How is contractual liability protection typically structured in a general liability policy?

answers.text: The policy excludes all liability whenever a written contract exists
The policy covers every promise in every contract without any exclusion
An exclusion removes liability assumed by contract, and the policy then gives coverage back for liability under an insured contract and for liability the insured would have had anyway
Coverage exists only if a certificate of insurance was issued before the loss, under the schedule of forms and endorsements attached to the policy at inception, and as the form itself provides

questions.explanation: The standard structure is an exclusion with a give-back for insured contracts and for liability that would exist absent the contract. A certificate plays no role in creating this coverage.

questions.question: Under the standard mortgage clause, what must a mortgagee tell the insurer when it learns of one?

answers.text: A change in ownership or occupancy of the property, or a substantial increase in the hazard, that the mortgagee knows about
The mortgagor's credit score each quarter
Nothing at all, under any circumstances
Every payment the mortgagor makes on the loan, on the day it is made, in the claim situation presented, under the terms of the policy then in effect

questions.explanation: The mortgagee's protection comes with its own duties, including notifying the insurer of known changes in ownership, occupancy, or hazard. Routine loan bookkeeping is not the clause's concern.

questions.question: What financial reporting does a Georgia liquidation order require of the liquidator?

answers.text: A single final accounting at discharge only, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Reports showing at least the insurer's assets and liabilities and all funds received and disbursed, filed within one year of the order and at least annually thereafter
Quarterly reports to the NAIC only, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Reports only if a creditor requests one, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind

questions.explanation: The order must require financial reports at least covering assets, liabilities, and all funds received and disbursed in the reporting period, filed within one year of the order and at least annually after that. A discharge-only accounting does not satisfy the rule.

questions.question: A claimant with a weak case argues that because the jurisdiction's cap on noneconomic damages is generous, some noneconomic award is assured. What is the flaw in that argument?

answers.text: Caps apply only when the plaintiff loses at trial
Caps are paid by the court rather than the defendant
A cap is only a ceiling; it creates no entitlement, and a plaintiff who proves no compensable harm recovers nothing
Caps guarantee a minimum payment equal to half the ceiling, in the situation described, as the governing provision of the form provides

questions.explanation: A generous ceiling does not supply proof of liability or loss. Caps matter only after a plaintiff has established a recoverable award that reaches the ceiling.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the mortgagee's protection under a standard mortgage clause when the mortgagor neglects to pay the renewal premium?

answers.text: The mortgagee loses its protection automatically and without any opportunity to cure
The mortgagee's interest remains protected if the mortgagee pays the premium on demand
The mortgagee is protected only when the premium was escrowed by the loan servicer
The insurer must keep the owner's coverage in force free of charge until the loan matures

questions.explanation: The standard mortgage clause protects the mortgagee against the mortgagor's neglect to pay premiums, provided the mortgagee pays on demand when asked. Protection is not automatic without that payment, and escrow arrangements are not what creates the right.

questions.question: A licensee receives a Certificate of Licensure and wants to add a line of authority to the document by hand. What does the rule say?

answers.text: Once issued, the form and content of the Certificate of Licensure shall not be altered in any way; the certificate states the licensee's name, license number, kinds of insurance covered, and other conditions of licensing
The certificate may be altered by the licensee's agency, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Alterations are allowed for a small fee, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Handwritten additions are allowed if initialed, whether the matter arises at application, at issuance, or at renewal

questions.explanation: An issued Certificate of Licensure may not be altered in any way. Any change in authority requires a properly issued document, not a handwritten edit.

questions.question: An insured acquires a building, and on Day 10 reports its full values to the insurer for endorsement. A loss occurs on Day 20. The newly acquired extension itself:

answers.text: Has already ended on Day 10, when the values were reported, so the loss is handled under the endorsed coverage terms instead
Runs until Day 30 no matter what the insured reported
Restarts for another 30 days when values are reported
Never applied, because reporting values voids all coverage, regardless of the deductible amount or the limit that would otherwise apply to the loss in question

questions.explanation: Reporting values is one of the three events that end the extension, because the property is then placed on the policy properly. Reporting does not void coverage; it moves the property from the temporary extension to the regular policy terms.

questions.question: When other insurance covers the same loss, what does the other insurance condition generally allow an insurer to do?

answers.text: Refuse to pay anything whenever another policy exists
Pay the loss and then cancel the other insurer's policy
Charge the insured a second premium for the claim
Pay only its share of the loss rather than the entire loss

questions.explanation: The condition limits each insurer to its apportioned share of the one loss. It does not permit an insurer on the risk to walk away from its share entirely.

questions.question: After a covered fire, an insured who elected Replacement Cost decides not to repair or replace the damaged business personal property at all. How will the claim generally be settled?

answers.text: On an actual cash value basis, because full replacement cost depends on actually repairing or replacing the property
At full replacement cost anyway, because the election alone guarantees it
At the agreed value, because the two options pay the same way
For no amount, because declining to replace voids the entire claim

questions.explanation: The insured can collect the actual cash value without replacing, but the extra amount up to replacement cost is earned by actually repairing or replacing. The claim is not void merely because the insured chooses the lesser settlement.

questions.question: Part of the insured farmhouse is lawfully rented to another person, and a covered loss prevents that part from being occupied. Which Coverage D concept addresses the lost rent?

answers.text: Scheduled farm personal property value
Blanket herd value
Fair rental value
Actual cash value of the dwelling

questions.explanation: Fair rental value addresses rent the insured loses for the rented portion after a covered loss. It is distinct from the value of the building itself under Coverage A.

questions.question: An insurer pays the full value of stolen securities, and a month later police recover the intact certificates and return them to the insured. Under the transfer of rights and recovery principles, what is the problem with the insured keeping both?

answers.text: The insured cannot retain both the full payment and the recovered property for the same loss; the recovery belongs to the insurer to the extent of its payment
There is no problem, because found property is a windfall the insured may always keep, as reflected in the certificate of insurance issued to the interested party for that project
The insured must destroy the certificates to avoid a conflict
The insurer must pay a second time for the recovered certificates

questions.explanation: Recovery after payment inures to the insurer up to what it paid, preventing the insured from being paid twice for one loss. Keeping both the money and the intact certificates would be a double recovery.

questions.question: A covered operator was convicted, within 36 months before the notice, of homicide arising out of the operation of a motor vehicle. Which cancellation ground covers this?

answers.text: No ground covers crimes involving a vehicle, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
The speeding-violations ground, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind
Criminal negligence resulting in death, homicide, or assault arising out of the operation of a motor vehicle is a listed conviction ground
The fraudulent claim ground, in accordance with the process the statute establishes for determinations of this kind

questions.explanation: Conviction or bail forfeiture for criminal negligence resulting in death, homicide, or assault arising out of operating a motor vehicle is expressly listed among the conviction grounds for cancellation. It is not handled under the speeding ground.

questions.question: A discovery form policy runs through calendar year 2026 with a retroactive date of January 1, 2024. The insured discovers a loss on June 10, 2026, and establishes the theft occurred on March 15, 2023. Applying the two dates, what is the outcome?

answers.text: Coverage applies, because June 10, 2026 is after January 1, 2024
Coverage applies, because any theft within three years of discovery qualifies
No coverage, because March 15, 2023 falls before the January 1, 2024 retroactive date
No coverage, because the theft was not discovered in the month it occurred

questions.explanation: The comparison that matters for the backward boundary is occurrence date against retroactive date, and March 2023 precedes January 2024. Comparing the discovery date to the retroactive date, as the strongest distractor does, tests the wrong pair of dates.

questions.question: Workload in examinations and consumer services outgrows the Georgia department's structure. Who may set up divisions or sections within the department as needed?

answers.text: The Commissioner
The Governor, by executive order only
The House Insurance Committee
Each insurer, for its own filings

questions.explanation: The Commissioner organizes the department into the divisions or sections the Commissioner deems necessary. Insurers cannot structure the regulator.

questions.question: A manager, wanting to drive a tenant out, knowingly cuts the tenant's power to force a wrongful eviction and expects the tenant to suffer. Which Coverage B exclusion is most directly triggered?

answers.text: Knowing violation of another's rights
Prior publication
Wrong description of prices
Quality or performance failure

questions.explanation: Intentionally violating the tenant's occupancy rights to inflict injury triggers the exclusion for personal injury caused with knowledge that the act would violate another's rights. Price, timing, and product-quality exclusions do not fit.

questions.question: A tenant paid $5,000 for covered improvements to the rented unit. The tenants policy has a $40,000 Coverage C limit with the standard improvements percentage and no increased limit, and no deductible applies to this calculation. What is the most the improvements coverage can pay?
questions.explanation: The loss is $5,000, but the improvements additional coverage is capped at ten percent of $40,000, which is $4,000, so $4,000 is the maximum payable. The tenant would need a higher purchased limit to insure the full $5,000 exposure.

questions.question: A client files a lawsuit alleging that an accountant's negligent work caused a financial loss, and the accountant believes the work was careful. What is an important function of the accountant's errors and omissions policy at this early stage?

answers.text: It guarantees in advance that the accountant will win the lawsuit
It pays the client's loss automatically without any claim investigation
It replaces the accountant's license while the lawsuit is pending
It provides a defense against the covered negligence claim while liability is being determined

questions.explanation: Professional liability coverage defends covered claims alleging negligent professional work, even when the insured disputes the allegation. It does not guarantee the outcome or pay automatically without investigation.

questions.question: Angered by a trespasser, the insured fires a warning shot deliberately aimed to wound the man's leg, and the man is hit as planned. The man sues for his wound. What is the Coverage A result under the expected or intended exclusion?

answers.text: Coverage applies, because the insured called the shot a warning
Coverage applies whenever the injured person was trespassing
No coverage, but only because a firearm rather than a hand was used
No coverage for that injury, because wounding the man was the insured's intended result

questions.explanation: Aiming to wound and hitting as planned is injury intended from the insured's standpoint, regardless of the label the insured later gives the shot. Trespass by the victim and the type of weapon do not change that intended-result analysis.

massachusetts-real-estate.quiz_title: Massachusetts Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best describes race-notice act?

answers.text: A wild deed gives perfect constructive notice because it appears in the grantor index.
Title by will passes automatically without any probate court involvement.
Under a race-notice statute, the first conveyance always wins even if never recorded.
Under a race-notice statute, a later bona fide purchaser without notice must also record first to prevail.

questions.explanation: Under a race-notice recording rule, a later purchaser who buys in good faith and without notice must also win the race to record in order to prevail. Simply being first to receive a conveyance, recorded or not, is not enough, and a wild deed outside the chain gives no such perfect notice.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about accounting and one about escrow funds — contains two true statements?

answers.text: The agent may commingle the principal's funds with personal funds. A broker may mix client funds with personal money.
Accounting requires safeguarding and reporting all money and documents belonging to the principal. A broker must deposit trust funds promptly into a separate escrow account and never commingle.
The agent may commingle the principal's funds with personal funds. A broker must deposit trust funds promptly into a separate escrow account and never commingle.
Accounting requires safeguarding and reporting all money and documents belonging to the principal. A broker may mix client funds with personal money.

questions.explanation: Accounting means safeguarding and reporting money and documents that belong to the principal. Client funds belong promptly in the broker separate escrow account and may never be mixed with personal money, which rules out every pairing built on commingling.

questions.question: A lender charges a 1% origination fee on a $582,000.00 loan. Regarding loan fees, what is the dollar amount of the origination fee?
questions.explanation: One percent of $582,000.00 is $5,820.00, found by multiplying the loan amount by 0.01. The larger and smaller figures result from applying a different percentage to the loan.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about inquiries and one about harassment — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Housing providers may not ask about the nature or severity of a disability; limited verification is permitted. Harassing tenants based on protected characteristics is permissible.
A landlord may demand full medical records from every applicant. Harassing tenants based on protected characteristics is permissible.
Housing providers may not ask about the nature or severity of a disability; limited verification is permitted. Sexual and other discriminatory harassment of tenants or buyers is prohibited.
A landlord may demand full medical records from every applicant. Sexual and other discriminatory harassment of tenants or buyers is prohibited.

questions.explanation: A housing provider may not probe the nature or severity of an applicant's disability, though limited verification of disability status is permitted when it is genuinely needed. Harassment is equally barred: sexual or other discriminatory harassment of tenants and buyers based on protected characteristics violates fair housing law, so calling it permissible is false.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about steering and one about escrow — contains two false statements?

answers.text: Steering is good customer service. Escrow lets the broker use client funds freely.
Steering is good customer service. Escrow is the neutral holding of funds and documents until transaction conditions are met.
Steering buyers toward or away from neighborhoods based on protected class is illegal. Escrow is the neutral holding of funds and documents until transaction conditions are met.
Steering buyers toward or away from neighborhoods based on protected class is illegal. Escrow lets the broker use client funds freely.

questions.explanation: Steering buyers by protected characteristic is illegal discrimination, not good customer service. Escrow funds likewise are held neutrally until the transaction's conditions are met; the broker may not treat client money as freely usable.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about density and one about subdivision — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Density controls set the minimum sale price of homes. An owner may subdivide and sell lots with no approvals.
Density controls set the minimum sale price of homes. Subdividing land into lots for sale generally requires plat approval under local regulations.
Density controls limit how many dwelling units may occupy an acre of land. Subdividing land into lots for sale generally requires plat approval under local regulations.
Density controls limit how many dwelling units may occupy an acre of land. An owner may subdivide and sell lots with no approvals.

questions.explanation: Density rules count dwelling units per acre of land; they do not set minimum sale prices for homes. Subdividing land into lots for sale likewise is not approval-free, since it generally requires plat approval under local regulations — the pairing that gets both land-use points right is the sound one.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about commission and one about amendments — contains two false statements?

answers.text: The commission rate is negotiable between seller and broker; no fixed or standard rate exists. Contract changes should be in signed written amendments.
A legally fixed commission rate applies to all listings. Oral changes are always effective.
A legally fixed commission rate applies to all listings. Contract changes should be in signed written amendments.
The commission rate is negotiable between seller and broker; no fixed or standard rate exists. Oral changes are always effective.

questions.explanation: No legally fixed commission rate applies to all listings, because rates are negotiable between seller and broker. Oral changes are not always effective either, since contract changes should be made in signed written amendments.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about bargain and sale and one about funding — contains two true statements?

answers.text: A bargain and sale deed implies the grantor holds title, without full warranties. Funding disburses loan proceeds and purchase funds per the settlement statement.
A bargain and sale deed implies the grantor holds title, without full warranties. Funding occurs before any documents are signed.
A bargain and sale deed offers full warranties. Funding disburses loan proceeds and purchase funds per the settlement statement.
A bargain and sale deed offers full warranties. Funding occurs before any documents are signed.

questions.explanation: A bargain and sale deed carries an implication that the grantor holds the title being conveyed, but it stops short of full warranties. Funding then disburses the loan proceeds and purchase money according to the settlement statement once documents are in place.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about zoning and use and one about branch offices — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Known zoning or use restrictions affecting the buyer's intended use must be disclosed. Branch offices must be properly licensed and supervised under Board rules.
Known zoning or use restrictions affecting the buyer's intended use must be disclosed. A brokerage may open unsupervised branch offices anywhere without approval.
A licensee may assure a buyer that any business use is allowed without checking. A brokerage may open unsupervised branch offices anywhere without approval.
A licensee may assure a buyer that any business use is allowed without checking. Branch offices must be properly licensed and supervised under Board rules.

questions.explanation: Restrictions in zoning or permitted use that affect what a buyer plans to do with a property must be disclosed, and no licensee should assure a buyer that any business use is allowed without checking. Branch offices likewise need proper licensing and supervision rather than opening unsupervised anywhere.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about knowing violation and one about honest dealing — contains two true statements?

answers.text: A defendant's knowledge of the deception is irrelevant under c. 93A. Licensees may mislead consumers whenever it helps close a deal.
A defendant's knowledge of the deception is irrelevant under c. 93A. Brokers and salespersons must deal honestly with consumers at all times.
A willful or knowing violation exposes the defendant to multiple damages under c. 93A. Licensees may mislead consumers whenever it helps close a deal.
A willful or knowing violation exposes the defendant to multiple damages under c. 93A. Brokers and salespersons must deal honestly with consumers at all times.

questions.explanation: Under the state consumer-protection law, a willful or knowing violation exposes the defendant to multiple damages, so the defendant's knowledge matters a great deal, and brokers and salespersons must deal honestly with consumers at all times rather than misleading them to close a deal — that pairing joins both truths.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about disclosure and one about designated agency — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Disclosure requires telling the principal all material facts affecting their decisions. Designated agency appoints different licensees within one brokerage to represent each party.
The agent may hide material facts from the principal. Designated agency appoints different licensees within one brokerage to represent each party.
The agent may hide material facts from the principal. Designated agency is the same as dual agency.
Disclosure requires telling the principal all material facts affecting their decisions. Designated agency is the same as dual agency.

questions.explanation: A principal is entitled to disclosure of all material facts bearing on the principal's decisions; hiding them breaches the agent's duty. Designated agency appoints different licensees within one brokerage for each party, which is different from dual agency, where one licensee serves both sides.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about competent parties and one about option — contains two false statements?

answers.text: Parties must have legal capacity; minors and the mentally incapacitated generally lack full capacity. An option is a free promise with no consideration.
Parties must have legal capacity; minors and the mentally incapacitated generally lack full capacity. An option is a separate contract keeping an offer open for a period, supported by consideration.
Anyone, including young children, has full contracting capacity. An option is a separate contract keeping an offer open for a period, supported by consideration.
Anyone, including young children, has full contracting capacity. An option is a free promise with no consideration.

questions.explanation: Contracting parties must have legal capacity, which minors and the mentally incapacitated generally lack in full, and an option is a separate contract supported by consideration that keeps an offer open for a period rather than a free promise. Granting young children full capacity makes the pairing doubly false.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about adjustment direction and one about cap rate — contains two false statements?

answers.text: When the comparable is superior to the subject on a feature, the comparable's price is adjusted downward. The capitalization rate expresses the ratio of NOI to value; value equals NOI divided by the cap rate.
Superior comparables are adjusted upward. The cap rate is added to NOI to find value.
Superior comparables are adjusted upward. The capitalization rate expresses the ratio of NOI to value; value equals NOI divided by the cap rate.
When the comparable is superior to the subject on a feature, the comparable's price is adjusted downward. The cap rate is added to NOI to find value.

questions.explanation: A comparable that is superior to the subject gets adjusted downward, because its price reflects the better feature, so adjusting upward reverses the method. Value comes from dividing net operating income by the capitalization rate, not from adding the rate to that income.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about death on property and one about lead paint — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Every death must always be disclosed everywhere. Pre-1978 housing triggers federal lead-paint disclosure, pamphlet delivery, and a 10-day inspection opportunity.
Many states limit or exclude required disclosure of deaths or illness; licensees follow state law. Lead paint need never be disclosed.
Every death must always be disclosed everywhere. Lead paint need never be disclosed.

Many states limit or exclude required disclosure of deaths or illness; licensees follow state law. Pre-1978 housing triggers federal lead-paint disclosure, pamphlet delivery, and a 10-day inspection opportunity.

questions.explanation: Many states, Massachusetts included, limit or exclude any duty to disclose deaths or illness on a property, and licensees follow that state law rather than disclosing every death everywhere. Pre-1978 housing does trigger lead-paint disclosure, pamphlet delivery, and a ten-day inspection opportunity.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about termination notice and one about reciprocity conditions — contains two false statements?

answers.text: A broker and salesperson may end affiliation with no notice to anyone. Any out-of-state licensee automatically receives a Massachusetts license on request.
A broker and salesperson may end affiliation with no notice to anyone. Reciprocal licensure is available only to applicants meeting the Board's conditions.
When affiliation ends, proper notice procedures keep the license record accurate. Any out-of-state licensee automatically receives a Massachusetts license on request.
When affiliation ends, proper notice procedures keep the license record accurate. Reciprocal licensure is available only to applicants meeting the Board's conditions.

questions.question: All of the following are eviction procedure EXCEPT:

answers.text: expiration of the notice period
filing summary process in court
a proper notice to quit
the master deed

questions.explanation: Expiration of the notice period, filing summary process in court, and a proper notice to quit are all parts of eviction procedure. A master deed belongs to condominium creation and ownership, not to the court process for removing a tenant.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about no price fixing and one about seller's statements — contains two true statements?

answers.text: Brokers in the same market may agree on a uniform commission rate. A licensee may repeat known-false seller claims because the seller said them.
Brokers in the same market may agree on a uniform commission rate. A licensee must not repeat a seller's statement they know to be false.
Brokers must not fix or agree on commission rates with competitors. A licensee may repeat known-false seller claims because the seller said them.
Brokers must not fix or agree on commission rates with competitors. A licensee must not repeat a seller's statement they know to be false.

questions.explanation: Competing brokers may not agree among themselves on a uniform commission rate; rates stay negotiable, and fixing them violates antitrust principles. A licensee also cannot hide behind the seller's words — repeating a seller's statement the licensee knows is false is still a misrepresentation, so both halves of the keyed pairing hold.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about conventional and one about secondary market — contains two true statements?

answers.text: A conventional loan is not insured or guaranteed by a government agency. The secondary market originates loans directly to borrowers.
Conventional loans are insured by the federal government. The secondary market originates loans directly to borrowers.
Conventional loans are insured by the federal government. The secondary market buys existing mortgages, giving lenders funds to make new loans.
A conventional loan is not insured or guaranteed by a government agency. The secondary market buys existing mortgages, giving lenders funds to make new loans.

questions.explanation: A conventional loan stands on the borrower's credit without government insurance or a government guarantee, unlike the federal programs. The secondary market buys existing mortgages so lenders regain funds for new lending, rather than originating loans directly to borrowers.

questions.question: A salesperson cold-calls homeowners from a purchased list to solicit listings, ignoring numbers registered on the National Do Not Call Registry. What is the risk?

answers.text: There is no risk if the calls are made on weekdays
There is no risk because real estate calls are always exempt
The risk falls only on the company that sold the list
The salesperson risks federal Do Not Call violations and significant penalties

questions.explanation: Calling numbers on the National Do Not Call Registry to solicit listings exposes the salesperson to federal Do Not Call violations and significant penalties. Real estate calls enjoy no blanket exemption, weekday timing does not cure the violation, and the list seller does not absorb the risk.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of statements — one about time is of the essence and one about listing term — contains two true statements?

answers.text: 'Time is of the essence' makes deadlines flexible. Listings should have no expiration date.
'Time is of the essence' makes deadlines flexible. A listing agreement should state its definite term; open-ended listings are problematic.
'Time is of the essence' makes deadlines strictly enforceable. A listing agreement should state its definite term; open-ended listings are problematic.
'Time is of the essence' makes deadlines strictly enforceable. Listings should have no expiration date.

questions.explanation: When time is of the essence, contract deadlines bind strictly rather than flexibly, so the flexible reading reverses the clause. A listing also needs a definite stated term, because an open-ended listing leaves the seller tied to the brokerage indefinitely.

virginia-real-estate.quiz_title: Virginia Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A 116-front-foot lot in an area of $146 per front foot sales is worth
questions.explanation: Front-foot value is frontage times the rate per front foot, so 116 feet times $146 equals $16,936. The $17,082 figure charges for an extra foot of frontage, $8,468 is half the correct value, and $2,620 matches neither the frontage nor the rate.

questions.question: The timing of agency disclosure

answers.text: is at first substantive contact, per state law
is at closing
is optional
is never

questions.explanation: Agency disclosure is due at first substantive contact under state law, when the relationship discussion first matters to the consumer. Waiting until closing is far too late, and the disclosure is neither optional nor never required.

questions.question: On a $745,000.00 purchase, the buyer deposits 5.5% as earnest money. How much is the deposit?
questions.explanation: Earnest money is the price times the stated percentage, so $745,000 times 5.5 percent equals $40,975. The $81,950 figure doubles the percentage, $20,487.50 is half the correct deposit, and $14,900 applies only 2 percent.

questions.question: Under Sec. 43-4.01 F, a mechanics' lien agent may charge for the agent's services a

answers.text: fee fixed at one percent of the contract price
reasonable fee for administering the notice process and disbursing funds for labor and materials
flat statutory fee of $250
fee set by the building permit office

questions.question: An agent who receives a W-2

answers.text: is treated as an employee for tax
violates RESPA
is exempt
is an IC

questions.explanation: An agent who receives the employee tax form is treated as an employee for tax purposes, because that form reports wages paid to employees rather than payments to independent contractors. Receiving it does not make the agent an independent contractor, does not exempt the agent, and does not violate the federal settlement-services law.

questions.question: A property is assessed at $930,000.00 and the local real estate tax rate is $1.12 per $100 of assessed value. What is the annual tax?
questions.explanation: The tax is $930,000 divided by 100, times $1.12, which equals $10,416. The $5,208 figure is half the annual tax, the $15,624 figure is one and a half times it, and the $20,832 figure doubles it.

questions.question: A $664,750 contract includes a 6% seller concession toward the buyer's closing costs. The concession totals
questions.explanation: A seller concession toward closing costs equals the contract price times the concession percentage, and 6 percent of the price given yields 39885 dollars. The smallest figure is one tenth of that amount, the next figure is half of it at 3 percent, and the largest figure applies 7 percent and overstates the concession.

questions.question: An interest-only loan of $735,000.00 has an annual rate of 5.4%. What is the monthly interest payment?
questions.explanation: Monthly interest on an interest-only loan is the balance multiplied by the annual rate and divided by twelve, so $735,000 at 5.4 percent gives $3,307.50 per month. The $1,653.75 figure is half the correct payment, the $4,961.25 figure is one and a half times it, and the $6,615 figure is double it.

questions.question: A buyer skips the home inspection, claiming the disclosure statement protects them. Which is correct?

answers.text: Correct; the statement replaces inspections
Correct for newer homes
Correct when the seller is honest
Wrong; the statement expressly advises buyers to obtain inspections and exercise their own diligence

questions.explanation: The disclosure statement is a buyer-beware notice that expressly advises buyers to get inspections and do their own diligence, so skipping an inspection leaves the buyer unprotected. It never replaces inspections, for newer homes or otherwise, and seller honesty does not convert it into a warranty.

questions.question: Regarding adjacent-property issues, a listing agent asked about highway noise. Which statement is true?

answers.text: The agent must disclose everything about adjacent parcels
The agent must research neighboring land uses
Matters outside the boundaries of the land or relating to adjacent or nearby properties are outside the statutory meaning of physical condition
The agent must disclose pending zoning cases nearby

questions.explanation: Virginia's physical-condition disclosure duty concerns the property itself, so matters outside the boundaries of the land or relating to adjacent or nearby properties fall outside the statutory meaning of physical condition. The agent need not disclose everything about adjacent parcels, research neighboring land uses, or disclose pending nearby zoning cases under that duty.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes advance consent to dual agency in a listing agreement

answers.text: valid only for commercial deals
unenforceable without a seal
valid as advance informed consent, which the client can withdraw before dual service commences
binding on future buyers

questions.explanation: A client may give advance informed consent to dual agency in a listing agreement, and that consent can be withdrawn before dual service actually commences. It is not valid only for commercial deals, it does not require a seal to be enforceable, and it cannot bind future buyers, who must consent for themselves.

questions.question: Knowledge of one Virginia licensee in a brokerage relationship is generally treated under § 54.1-2142 as

answers.text: always imputed to every client of the firm
not imputed to the client merely because of the relationship, in the circumstances the section specifies
imputed only to the principal broker
imputed to the other party

questions.explanation: Virginia law does not impute knowledge to a client merely because of the brokerage relationship, in the circumstances the governing rule specifies, and knowledge is not imputed between licensees. Treating knowledge as always imputed to every client, imputed only to the principal broker, or imputed to the other party each contradicts that non-imputation rule.

questions.question: A $1725000 Virginia property’s building earns $51658 NOI capitalized at 10.75%. By the building residual technique, the land is worth
questions.explanation: By the building residual technique, the building value is its income divided by the cap rate: $51,658 divided by 10.75 percent is about $480,540, and subtracting that from the $1,725,000 total leaves land worth about $1,244,460. The $480,540 figure is the building component itself rather than the land, while $622,230 and $1,673,342 do not follow from removing the building value from the total.

questions.question: The HUD lead rule differs from the disclosure rule by requiring

answers.text: federal ownership
visual assessments, risk assessments or inspections, hazard reduction, and ongoing maintenance
annual XRF testing
demolition

questions.explanation: The federal housing lead rule goes beyond disclosure by requiring visual assessments, risk assessments or inspections, hazard reduction, and ongoing maintenance in covered housing. It does not require federal ownership of the housing, annual X-ray fluorescence testing, or demolition.

questions.question: Under 18VAC135-20-335(A)(5), which of the following statements about negotiating/agreeing to any commission split management fee or is correct?

answers.text: Unlicensed assistants may negotiate referral fees
Commission splits are clerical matters open to staff
Only management fees require a license to negotiate
Negotiating or agreeing to any commission, commission split, management fee, or referral fee may only be performed by a licensee

questions.explanation: Negotiating or agreeing to any commission, commission split, management fee, or referral fee is licensed brokerage activity in Virginia and may be performed only by a licensee. Unlicensed assistants therefore cannot negotiate referral fees, these negotiations are not open clerical work for staff, and the license requirement is not limited to management fees.

questions.question: Under Sec. 6.2-1701(B)(1), although an individual engaged solely as a loan processor or underwriter is generally exempt from mortgage loan originator licensing, an individual acting as an independent contractor

answers.text: may not engage in residential mortgage loan origination activities as a loan processor or underwriter unless the individual first obtains and maintains a mortgage loan originator license
is exempt from licensing in all residential mortgage origination activities
must register with the Commission as an independent lending business
may act as a processor only for loans of immediate family members

questions.question: A listing agent with waterfront property is listing waterfront property that may lie in a Chesapeake Bay resource protection area. Which is correct?

answers.text: The owner must certify the property is outside the RPA
The buyer-beware statement addresses whether the property is protected under the Chesapeake Bay Preservation Act, with the owner making no representation and the buyer advised to investigate
The seller guarantees no Bay Act restrictions
The Bay Act never affects residential lots

questions.explanation: Virginia's buyer-beware disclosure statement addresses whether the property is protected under the Chesapeake Bay Preservation Act, with the owner making no representation and the buyer advised to investigate for themselves. The owner does not certify the property is outside a resource protection area, the seller guarantees nothing about Bay Act restrictions, and the Act can affect residential waterfront lots.

questions.question: Servicer personnel who offer or negotiate terms to renegotiate, modify, replace, or subordinate principal on existing mortgages for consumers who are behind or in default are excluded from 'loan originator,' but the exclusion does not apply when

answers.text: the consumer is only one payment behind
the modification lowers the interest rate
the transaction they offer or negotiate is a refinancing or obligates a different consumer on the existing debt
the servicer charges no fee for the modification

questions.explanation: Servicer staff who work on modifying an existing borrower's own troubled loan are excluded from loan originator status only while they are renegotiating that same debt for that same consumer. Offering a refinancing, or obligating a different consumer on the debt, is new origination activity outside the exclusion, while being one payment behind, lowering the rate, or charging no fee does not change the character of a genuine modification.

questions.question: A property has effective gross income of $68,920 and total operating expenses of $21,375. What is its net operating income?
questions.explanation: Net operating income is effective gross income minus operating expenses, and $68,920 minus $21,375 equals $47,545. The $42,315 figure deducts too much, $52,300 deducts too little, and $68,920 is the income before any expenses are deducted.

questions.question: The settlement statement on a $511,000 sale shows a 5.5% commission, a $416,500 existing lien payoff, and $7,000 in seller costs. The seller receives
questions.explanation: The seller receives the price minus commission, the existing lien payoff, and seller costs: 511,000 dollars minus 28,105 dollars, minus 416,500 dollars, minus 7,000 dollars equals 59,395 dollars. The 60,395-dollar figure is 1,000 dollars too high, the 31,290-dollar figure subtracts far too much, and the 87,500-dollar figure ignores the commission.

part-107.quiz_title: Part 107 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A pilot inspects a 340-foot radio tower, flying 320 feet laterally from it at 640 feet above the ground. No airspace authorization issue applies. The altitude is

answers.text: Illegal, because no part 107 flight may ever exceed 400 feet above ground level
Illegal, because the structure exception allows only 100 feet above the structure
Legal only if the pilot holds a waiver of the altitude limitation
Legal, because the aircraft is within 400 feet of a structure and is no higher than 400 feet above the structure's uppermost point, the part 107 structure exception to the 400-foot AGL limit

questions.explanation: The general limit is 400 feet above ground level, but part 107 permits flight above that height when the aircraft remains within 400 feet horizontally of a structure and does not fly higher than 400 feet above the structure's immediate uppermost point; a 340-foot tower supports flight up to 740 feet within that radius, so 640 feet at 320 feet away fits. The blanket statement that 400 feet AGL can never be exceeded ignores the exception, the exception is 400 feet above the structure rather than 100, and no waiver is needed when the exception's terms are met.

questions.question: For a night operation, the aircraft's anti-collision lighting must be

answers.text: switched on only for takeoff and landing to conserve the battery
replaced by the remote pilot's ground flashlight once the aircraft is airborne
operating for the entire flight, with a flash rate sufficient to avoid a collision
set to a slow flash rate so it does not distract other pilots

questions.explanation: Part 107 night operations require anti-collision lighting for the duration of the flight, and the lighting standard calls for a flash rate sufficient to support collision avoidance, not a token blink at the ends of the flight. Conserving battery by darkening the aircraft in flight defeats the requirement's purpose. A light on the ground cannot mark the aircraft's position in the air. Slowing the flash to avoid distracting others contradicts the requirement that the rate be sufficient for avoidance.

questions.question: (Scenario) A night crew must read checklists and a site map during setup without destroying the dark adaptation they have built. What lighting practice serves both needs?

answers.text: Use the brightest white light available so the documents can be read quickly
Read under vehicle headlights and launch immediately afterward
Use dim red lighting for the close work, because the rod cells responsible for night vision are relatively insensitive to red light, then allow adaptation to continue before launch
Rely on phone flashlights held close to the eyes between tasks

questions.explanation: Rod vision, which carries night perception, responds weakly to red wavelengths, so dim red light lets a crew read while largely preserving adaptation that bright white light would reset. Bright white light is the fastest way to lose adaptation, however quickly documents get read. Headlights followed by an immediate launch combine maximum exposure with minimum recovery. A flashlight held near the eyes delivers intense white light at the worst distance for adaptation.

questions.question: Which set of features identifies a Category 4 operation over people?

answers.text: An aircraft weighing 0.55 pounds or less with no declaration
An aircraft with an airworthiness certificate issued under part 21, operated within its approved flight manual limitations and maintained and inspected under the Category 4 program
Any aircraft whose manufacturer filed a declaration of compliance
An aircraft that simply avoids sustained flight over people

questions.explanation: Category 4 is the certification-based category: the aircraft must have been issued an airworthiness certificate under part 21, must be operated in accordance with the operating limitations in its approved flight manual or as the Administrator specifies, and must be maintained and inspected under the program those documents establish. The 0.55-pound description belongs to Category 1. A declaration of compliance is the Category 2 and 3 mechanism, not Category 4. Avoiding sustained flight is a general operating technique, not the defining feature of a category.

questions.question: A remote pilot plans a civil twilight operation in Alaska and asks where that period is defined. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: In Alaska, the period of civil twilight is defined in the Air Almanac
In Alaska, civil twilight is defined by the airport manager
In Alaska, civil twilight lasts two hours by regulation
Alaska has no civil twilight period under the rule

questions.explanation: The daylight rule gives Alaska a specific reference: the period of civil twilight there is the period defined in the Air Almanac, reflecting the extended twilight at high latitudes. The definition comes from that publication, not from a local airport manager. The rule does not assign Alaska a fixed two-hour twilight period. Civil twilight operations are recognized in Alaska under the almanac definition rather than excluded.

questions.question: (Chart reading) A sectional chart shows a magenta parachute symbol near an airport along a planned drone route, and the Chart Supplement lists jump times and altitudes for that airport. What is the correct response?

answers.text: Assume the symbol is decorative, because jump operations are never charted
Obtain restricted-area permission from a using agency before crossing the area
Treat the area as an active jump site during its listed times, exercise extra vigilance for descending parachutists and jump aircraft, and plan the route or timing to avoid the jump activity
Close the airport to other traffic by notifying the airport manager

questions.explanation: A charted parachute symbol plus Chart Supplement data identify where and when jumps occur, and the safe response is heightened vigilance and deconfliction in time or space, since parachutists descend quickly and are hard to see. The symbol carries real operational meaning, a jump area is not a restricted area requiring agency permission, and a remote pilot has no authority to close the airport.

questions.question: Two pilots compare aircraft: one flies a 0.5-pound Category 1 aircraft, the other a Category 3 aircraft. Which statement about Declarations of Compliance is correct?

answers.text: Both aircraft require an FAA-accepted Declaration of Compliance

The Category 3 aircraft must be covered by an FAA-accepted Declaration of Compliance, while Category 1 eligibility rests on weight and the absence of exposed rotating parts that could cause severe laceration rather than on a declaration
Neither aircraft ever needs any FAA documentation of any kind
The Category 1 aircraft needs a declaration, but Category 3 does not

questions.explanation: Category 2 and Category 3 eligibility is declaration-based, so the Category 3 aircraft must be covered by an FAA-accepted Declaration of Compliance supported by an accepted Means of Compliance, while Category 1 eligibility is established by the aircraft weighing 0.55 pound or less and having no exposed rotating parts that could cause severe laceration. It is therefore wrong that both need declarations, wrong that documentation never matters for the declaration categories, and backwards to require one for Category 1 but not Category 3.

questions.question: After a hard landing, a pilot finds a visibly bent motor mount. The aircraft still starts and hovers, so the pilot plans to finish the afternoon's jobs and repair it over the weekend. This plan is

answers.text: Acceptable because the aircraft can still fly
Acceptable if a visual observer watches the flights
Prohibited, because no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system unless it is in a condition for safe operation, and the remote pilot must check that condition before flight
Prohibited only for flights over people, since the condition rule applies nowhere else

questions.explanation: Part 107 prohibits operating a small unmanned aircraft system that is not in a condition for safe operation, and the remote pilot in command must ensure the system is in a condition for safe operation before flight; a bent motor mount is exactly the kind of damage that must be corrected first. The ability to still hover does not cure an unsafe condition, adding a visual observer does not repair the aircraft, and the condition-for-safe-operation rule applies to part 107 operations generally, not only to flights over people.

questions.question: (Scenario) A job site sits downwind of a power plant whose cooling towers release a tall, visible plume of warm, moist air. The plume leans over the planned operating area. What hazard should the remote pilot plan around?

answers.text: A layer of smooth, stable air that improves the drone's climb performance inside the plume
No hazard at all, because a visible plume is only water vapor and cannot move air
A permanent flight restriction, because every industrial plume is charted as prohibited airspace
Rising, turbulent air in and around the plume, with possible downdrafts at its edges and reduced visibility inside it, so the flight should be routed clear of the plume rather than through it

questions.explanation: Strong heat sources drive thermal plumes: air rises vigorously and turbulently inside them, sinks around their margins, and the condensed moisture cuts visibility, all of which can upset a light unmanned aircraft. The air in a plume is convective and rough, not smooth and stable. The plume is visible precisely because air is moving and condensing within it. Industrial plumes are a hazard to avoid tactically, not charted prohibited airspace.

questions.question: (Scenario) Replacing a damaged clockwise propeller in the field, a crew member finds the spare bag holds a propeller of the same size and pitch but the opposite rotation, and proposes flying carefully with it. Why is that a grounding decision instead?

answers.text: Opposite rotation is fine at low throttle settings
The flight controller will reverse the motor to compensate automatically in all cases
Any propeller of the same diameter is interchangeable on a multirotor

A multirotor's propellers are rotation-specific and often paired by position; an opposite-rotation propeller produces wrong or unbalanced thrust at that corner, so the aircraft does not fly until the correct propeller is fitted

questions.explanation: Thrust direction and balance depend on the correct rotation propeller at each motor, and fitting the wrong one compromises the aircraft from the first takeoff attempt, making it a no-fly item. Low throttle does not change the direction the wrong propeller pushes air. Compensation cannot be assumed for a mismatched propeller. Diameter alone has never made propellers interchangeable.

questions.question: A person who designs, but does not produce, a small unmanned aircraft submits a declaration of compliance for it. How long must that person retain the information supporting the declaration?

answers.text: For two years after the cessation of production of the aircraft
For two years after the person submitted the declaration of compliance, and make it available to the Administrator on request
For one year after the person submitted the declaration of compliance
Only until the first aircraft built to the design is sold

questions.explanation: Record retention for declarations has two triggers: a producer retains the supporting information for two years after cessation of production, while a person who designs or modifies the aircraft retains it for two years after submitting the declaration; the designer in this scenario is governed by the submission-based period. The production-based period is the producer's trigger, not the designer's. One year is shorter than either prescribed period. A first sale is not a retention milestone in the rule.

questions.question: On a long mapping leg, the remote pilot in command can track the aircraft only through binoculars for an extended stretch, and without them cannot determine its attitude or altitude. What is the problem?

answers.text: There is no problem, because binoculars are an approved substitute for unaided vision

Visual line of sight must be maintained with vision unaided by any device other than corrective lenses, and the remote pilot must be able to know the aircraft's location, determine its attitude, altitude, and direction, and scan for hazards
The only problem is that binoculars must be at least 10-power to be used at all
The flight is legal if the visual observer also uses binoculars

questions.explanation: Visual line of sight means the remote pilot in command, the person manipulating the controls, and any visual observer must be able to see the aircraft throughout the flight with vision unaided by devices other than corrective lenses, well enough to know its location and determine its attitude, altitude, and direction of flight and to observe the airspace for other traffic and hazards. Binoculars are not an approved substitute for that unaided sight, no minimum binocular power creates an exception, and the observer using binoculars does not fix the remote pilot's loss of unaided visual contact.

questions.question: (Scenario) A remote pilot calls an airport's ASOS phone line twice, twenty minutes apart, and hears slightly different wind and altimeter values, each announced with a new time. What explains the updates, and how should the pilot treat the broadcast?

answers.text: The station is malfunctioning, because automated reports are issued only once a day
Each call reaches a different airport, so the values should be averaged before use

ASOS observes and updates its report minute by minute, so each call gives the current official observation for that airport, and the pilot should use the latest one together with forecasts and a briefing
The broadcast is a forecast, so its changing values show tomorrow's trend

questions.explanation: Automated surface observing systems sample the weather continuously and issue updated observations minute by minute, which is why successive calls differ; the newest report is the current official observation for that station. Frequent updates are normal operation, not a malfunction. The phone line reaches the one station dialed, and observations are used as reported, not averaged. ASOS reports present conditions, not a forecast trend.

questions.question: (Scenario) A crew working near a runway at dusk can see the airport's precision approach path indicator showing two white lights and two red lights to an arriving pilot. What does that indication mean for the arriving aircraft, and why does it matter to the crew?

answers.text: The aircraft is on the proper glidepath, so the crew can predict it will keep descending steadily along that path toward the runway
The aircraft is dangerously low and about to climb away
The aircraft is far above the glidepath and will dive steeply
The lights are a drone signal authorizing the crew to cross the final

questions.explanation: Two white and two red PAPI lights mean on glidepath, so the airplane will continue a steady descent to the runway and the crew can predict its path precisely. All red would mean low and all white high; the mixed display is neither. Approach lights give the drone crew no crossing authorization of any kind.

questions.question: An applicant can read, write, and understand English but, for a documented medical reason, cannot speak it clearly. How does part 107 treat this applicant's eligibility for a Remote Pilot Certificate with an sUAS rating?

answers.text: The applicant is permanently ineligible in all circumstances

The FAA may issue the certificate with such operating limitations as are necessary for the safe operation of small unmanned aircraft, because the English requirement may be accommodated when a medical reason prevents meeting one of its elements
The applicant must obtain a certificate of waiver under subpart D
The English-language requirement does not apply to remote pilots

questions.explanation: Eligibility normally requires the applicant to read, speak, write, and understand English, but the rule provides that if an applicant is unable to meet one of those requirements due to medical reasons, the FAA may place operating limitations on the certificate as are necessary for safe operation. The applicant is therefore not permanently barred. A subpart D waiver addresses deviations from operating rules, not certificate eligibility limitations, and the English requirement itself is a stated element of eligibility.

questions.question: (Scenario) Midway through a survey, the wind at altitude strengthens enough that the aircraft's groundspeed home is half its outbound speed and the battery gauge is falling faster than planned. A remote pilot using a structured decision process first does what with this development?

answers.text: Ignore it until the low-battery warning, which is the official decision point
Photograph faster to compress the remaining survey into the original timing
Decide the flight was a mistake and shut the motors down
Detect and name the change explicitly - the return leg now costs far more energy than planned - so the remaining steps of estimating, choosing, and acting rest on the real situation

questions.explanation: Structured decision-making begins with detecting that the situation has changed; only then can the pilot estimate its significance and choose a response such as an early return. Waiting for a warning outsources detection to the last alarm. Working faster raises energy use against a shrinking reserve. Shutting down in flight converts a manageable change into a crash.

questions.question: A broken cloud deck has a base at 1,200 feet above ground level. A remote pilot plans a flight at 350 feet above ground level, with the route passing no closer than 2,500 feet horizontally to any cloud. Does this plan meet the cloud clearance requirements?

answers.text: No, because the aircraft would be only 850 feet below the clouds
No, because horizontal distance to clouds must be at least 5,000 feet
No, because flights are prohibited whenever a cloud deck exists
Yes, because the aircraft would be 850 feet below the clouds, more than the required 500 feet, and 2,500 feet horizontally from them, more than the required 2,000 feet

questions.explanation: The cloud clearance minimums are 500 feet below the cloud and 2,000 feet horizontally from the cloud; flying 850 feet below the deck clears the vertical minimum, and a 2,500-foot horizontal distance clears the horizontal minimum, so the plan complies. The 850-foot figure is larger than the required separation, not smaller. The horizontal requirement is 2,000 feet, not 5,000 feet. The presence of clouds alone does not prohibit flight when the clearances are kept.

questions.question: (Scenario) A company flight risk assessment tool scores a proposed flight in the red band because a first-time site combines gusty winds, a new aircraft type, and a crowd nearby. Company policy for a red score is to mitigate or not fly. The client offers a bonus for flying anyway. What does sound risk management require?

answers.text: Reduce the risk first, for example by moving the date, changing the site layout, or using a proven aircraft, and do not fly the job as scored
Fly, because the bonus offsets the risk
Average the red score with earlier green scores to reach yellow
Let the visual observer make the final call instead

questions.explanation: A structured risk tool only helps if its result governs the decision: a red-band score means mitigating the hazards, such as changing timing, layout, or aircraft, or not flying, and a client bonus does not change likelihood or severity. Averaging scores away or handing the decision to the observer defeats the assessment.

questions.question: (Chart reading) A sectional chart excerpt described in this stem shows the dashed blue Class D boundary around a towered airport with a narrow dashed blue protrusion extending several miles to one side, aligned with an instrument approach course. How should a remote pilot treat the protrusion?

answers.text: As uncontrolled airspace drawn only to warn of arriving traffic
As part of the Class D surface area, so an ATC authorization is required to operate a small unmanned aircraft inside the protrusion as well as inside the main boundary
As Class E airspace beginning at 700 feet above the surface
As airspace reserved for instrument departures that unmanned aircraft may use freely below 400 feet

questions.explanation: Charted extensions are part of the surface area they extend: the dashed blue protrusion is Class D airspace arranged for instrument approaches, and part 107 operations inside it require the same prior ATC authorization as operations inside the main Class D boundary. It is controlled airspace rather than a warning-only drawing, it begins at the surface rather than at 700 feet, and an approach alignment does not make it free for unmanned use at low altitude.

questions.question: While keeping a required record, a remote pilot inadvertently transposes two digits in an entry, realizes the mistake the next day, and corrects it. The error was an honest mistake, with no purpose to mislead anyone. How is this conduct treated under the falsification prohibition?

answers.text: It is falsification, because any incorrect entry in a required record is treated the same as a deliberate falsehood
It is falsification, because intent to deceive is presumed whenever a required record turns out to be wrong

It is not falsification, because the prohibition is written in terms of a fraudulent or intentionally false statement, a reproduction or alteration made for a fraudulent purpose, or a knowing omission of a material fact, and an honest inadvertent error lacks that intent
It is falsification only if the FAA discovers the error before the pilot corrects it

questions.explanation: The falsification prohibition is scienter-based: it reaches fraudulent or intentionally false statements, reproductions or alterations made for a fraudulent purpose, and knowing omissions of material fact, a framing the FAA's small UAS guidance likewise describes in terms of fraudulently or knowingly providing false records, and the federal false-statements statute similarly requires knowing and willful conduct. An honestly made transposition error therefore is not the same as a deliberate falsehood, because the prohibition does not impose falsification liability for every incorrect entry regardless of intent. Intent is an element to be established, not a presumption that attaches whenever a record is wrong. The timing of discovery does not supply the missing intent, since whether the FAA or the pilot notices the mistake first does not change an inadvertent error into a knowingly false statement.

cmaa.quiz_title: CMAA Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding the prefix in the term bradypnea, what does brady- indicate about the patient's breathing rate?

answers.text: It is slower than normal
It is faster than normal
It has stopped entirely for a prolonged period
It is painful with each breath

questions.explanation: A is correct: brady- means slow, so bradypnea is an abnormally slow breathing rate. B is wrong because fast is expressed by tachy-, the opposite prefix. C is wrong because brady- describes a slow rate, not a complete stop. D is wrong because pain is expressed by a different word part, such as -algia, not by brady-.

questions.question: Regarding the role of an answering service for a medical practice, which statement describes how it handles calls received after hours?

answers.text: It schedules all after-hours callers for the next open appointment slot
It relays urgent messages to the on-call provider and holds routine messages for the next business day
It gives callers general medical advice from a prepared script
It discards messages from callers who are not established patients

questions.explanation: An answering service extends the practice's reach after hours by taking messages, forwarding urgent ones to the on-call provider, and holding routine matters for staff on the next business day. A is wrong because after-hours services take messages; they do not manage the practice's appointment schedule. C is wrong because giving medical advice is a clinical act outside an answering service's role. D is wrong because messages are recorded and passed to the practice regardless of whether the caller is established.

questions.question: Among commercial plan types, employer-sponsored group coverage is best described as coverage obtained in which of the following ways?

answers.text: Coverage is offered through a workplace to eligible employees, with the premium typically shared between the employer and the employee
Coverage is purchased only by individuals directly from a government agency based on income
Coverage is limited to active-duty service members and their dependents
Coverage is a supplement sold to Medicare beneficiaries to fill cost-sharing gaps

questions.explanation: A is correct because employer-sponsored coverage is a commercial group plan obtained through employment, with premium cost commonly split between employer and employee. B is wrong because income-based government coverage describes a public program such as Medicaid, not an employer group plan. C is wrong because coverage for service members and dependents describes TRICARE, a government military program. D is wrong because a supplement to Medicare describes Medigap, not employer-sponsored group coverage.

questions.question: Regarding telephone confidentiality, before discussing a patient's appointment details with a caller, the assistant should first:

answers.text: Verify the caller's identity using the practice's identifiers before sharing any appointment information
Confirm that the caller knows the patient's first name
Share the details if the caller says they are a relative
Read the full schedule for the day so the caller can pick out the right entry

questions.explanation: A is correct: the assistant verifies the caller's identity with the practice's standard identifiers before discussing any appointment information, which prevents disclosures to impersonators. B is wrong because knowing a first name proves nothing about identity or authorization. C is wrong because a claimed family relationship is unverified and does not by itself authorize disclosure. D is wrong because reading the whole day's schedule would expose many other patients' information, compounding the confidentiality problem.

questions.question: Regarding audit controls as a HIPAA Security safeguard, what does the record system's audit log allow the practice to do?

answers.text: Track which workforce accounts viewed or changed electronic PHI, so unusual access can be reviewed
Automatically correct errors that providers make in clinical documentation
Replace the need for individual passwords, since activity is recorded
Prevent patients from requesting copies of their own records

questions.explanation: A is correct: audit controls record activity in systems holding electronic PHI so the practice can review who accessed or altered records and spot improper use. B is wrong because an audit log records activity; it does not edit or correct clinical content. C is wrong because audit trails work alongside unique logins and passwords, not instead of them. D is wrong because audit controls concern workforce system activity and have nothing to do with limiting a patient's right of access.

questions.question: Regarding patient educational materials, which source of educational information is appropriate for the assistant to give a patient who wants to learn more about a condition discussed at their visit?

answers.text: A printed article the assistant found on a general internet forum
Notes the assistant wrote summarizing what the provider usually tells patients
A photocopy of another patient's education handout that has notes written on it
Provider-approved educational material the practice stocks for patient distribution

questions.explanation: D is correct because provider-approved materials stocked for distribution are accurate, current, and intended for patients. A is wrong because forum content is unverified and may be inaccurate or unsafe. B is wrong because the assistant's own summary is unreviewed and can distort the provider's guidance. C is wrong because another patient's annotated handout may contain that patient's private information and personal notes.

questions.question: An encounter form reaches the front desk with charges marked, but the provider's sign-off is missing, so the visit documentation is not yet complete. Before entering the charges, what should the assistant do?

answers.text: Enter the charges anyway and add the sign-off themselves later
Enter only the most expensive charge and discard the rest of the form
Ask the patient to confirm the charges and sign in place of the provider
Hold the charge entry and route the form back to the provider for review and sign-off

questions.explanation: D is correct because charges should be entered from completed, provider-signed encounter documentation; routing the form back gets the required sign-off before posting. A is wrong because the assistant cannot supply a provider's sign-off, and posting from unsigned documentation risks charging for an unverified visit. B is wrong because dropping charges from the form corrupts both the account and the record of the visit. C is wrong because a patient cannot provide the provider's professional sign-off on encounter documentation.

questions.question: A patient who is deaf arrives for a visit and communicates using sign language. A qualified sign language interpreter is joining by video screen at the front desk. How should the assistant conduct the check-in conversation?

answers.text: Look at the interpreter on the screen throughout and speak as if the interpreter is the patient
