questions.explanation: Exclusions mark the boundary of assumed risk; conditions impose requirements attached to the contract's operation. Reversing those roles misreads both provisions.

questions.question: What does the coverage territory condition do in a property policy?

answers.text: It sets the time zone used to date claim payments
It lists the countries where the insurer is licensed to sell policies
It identifies the geographic area within which a loss must occur for the policy to respond
It determines which state's courts hear coverage disputes

questions.explanation: Territory is a geographic test for the loss itself. Licensing footprints and court rules are separate matters that do not define where a covered loss may happen.

questions.question: Who develops the experience modification factor for an eligible employer?

answers.text: The injured employees, by voting on the employer's safety record
The employer's own accountant, using figures the employer chooses
A rating organization (or the insurer where permitted), using the employer's reported loss and payroll data
The employer's general liability insurer, using liability loss data

questions.explanation: Mods are developed by a rating organization, or the insurer where permitted, from uniformly reported payroll and loss data. The employer cannot set its own mod from figures it selects.

questions.question: A dealer's inventory swells before a holiday sales event and shrinks afterward. Which open lot arrangement is designed for this pattern?

answers.text: A fixed limit that can never change during the policy term once the policy is issued, and the dealer may not report higher or lower inventory values at any point during the term
A reporting form arrangement, under which the dealer reports inventory values periodically and premium and coverage track the reported values
A garagekeepers direct primary endorsement
A liability-only policy with a seasonal endorsement

questions.explanation: Explanation: Reporting forms exist for fluctuating values: the dealer reports the values on hand and the coverage follows those reports. A dealer that underreports values risks a reduced recovery, which is why accurate reporting matters.

questions.question: Under Ohio law, which statement about minor drivers under financial responsibility law is accurate?

answers.text: A parent's proof automatically covers a minor with no filing
Minors are treated the same as adults
Minors are exempt until age eighteen
Minors need only half the required limits

questions.explanation: They apply in the same manner to minor and adult drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following best states the Ohio rule on failure to file payroll report brings penalties?

answers.text: Only self-insuring employers file reports
There is no consequence for skipping the report
The report is excused if no claims occurred
Penalties may include exclusion from rating plans and discount programs

questions.explanation: Penalties for the missing report, including exclusion from alternative rating plans and discount programs.

questions.question: An authorized insurer prepares its year-end filings. By when must the annual statement copy reach the national association?

answers.text: On or before the first day of March each year
Only in years when it is examined
Within ninety days after its fiscal year ends
On or before the first day of January each year

questions.explanation: The March first deadline, convention blank format, jurat page, and actuarial certification are all required elements.

questions.question: A sole proprietor named insured dies, and a claim arises from the business the proprietor owned. Who may qualify as an insured to protect the estate's interest in that business?

answers.text: The proprietor's legal representative, with respect to the conduct of the business the proprietor owned
Any creditor of the proprietor, for any debt owed
Any former employee, for any later business the employee starts
The proprietor's customers, with respect to their own businesses

questions.explanation: A legal representative steps into insured status only with respect to the deceased insured's business. A creditor gains no insured status merely by being owed money.

questions.question: A basic dwelling policyholder wants protection against windstorm and hail. How is that protection normally obtained on the basic form?

answers.text: It is already included as a core basic-form peril
By adding extended coverage to the basic form
By adding liability coverage to the policy
By converting personal property to open perils

questions.explanation: Windstorm and hail are not core perils of the basic form; extended coverage is the mechanism that adds them. Adding liability would not add a property peril at all.

questions.question: An owner switching from the comprehensive form to the broad form asks what changes for personal property. What is the honest answer?

answers.text: Nothing changes for contents; only the dwelling basis changes
Contents move from named perils to open perils, which is why the broad form costs less
Contents move from an open-perils basis to a named-perils basis, so a cause of loss must be listed to be covered
Contents are no longer covered at all under the broad form

questions.explanation: The comprehensive form's signature advantage is open-perils contents, and the broad form gives that up for contents as well as for the dwelling. Contents are still covered under the broad form — but only for listed perils.

questions.question: A building valued at $900,000 has a 90% coinsurance clause. The owner carries $540,000, a covered partial loss is $120,000, and the deductible is $3,000. What does the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Should = $900,000 x 90% = $810,000. Payment = ($540,000/$810,000) x $120,000 - $3,000 = $80,000 - $3,000 = $77,000. The $78,000 option proportions the deductible as well, instead of subtracting the full $3,000 after the factor.

questions.question: An applicant asks a producer about association may not insure automobiles or manufacturing risks. Which response states the Ohio rule correctly?

answers.text: Manufacturing risks are the association's main line
The association may insure a factory if it also insures the owner's home
Automobiles and manufacturing risks are outside the association's authority
The association insures automobiles but not dwellings

questions.explanation: The association is not authorized to provide coverage for automobiles or manufacturing risks.

questions.question: Which of the following best states the Ohio rule on betterment deductions are capped by the part's replacement cost?

answers.text: Betterment must reflect real condition loss and cannot exceed the part's replacement cost
Condition before the loss is irrelevant
Betterment may exceed the cost of the new part
Any new part automatically justifies a fifty per cent cut

questions.explanation: Betterment deductions must track a measurable condition-based loss and are limited to no more than the replacement cost of the parts involved.

questions.question: A claimant buys a replacement car three weeks after a cash total-loss settlement and documents the sales tax promptly. What is owed?

answers.text: Documentation deadlines do not exist
No sales tax is ever owed on a total loss
Reimbursement is available for a purchase two years later
Reimbursement for a documented replacement bought within thirty days, claimed within thirty-three days

questions.explanation: Reimbursement of the applicable sales tax — up to the tax on the settlement value, or the actual tax if the replacement cost less — because the purchase and documentation fell inside the thirty and thirty-three day windows.

questions.question: A newspaper’s plant is damaged by a covered peril, so it pays a rival plant to print its editions for three weeks and earns its usual subscription and advertising income. With only the Extra Expense Coverage Form in force, what is payable?

answers.text: The newspaper’s full projected net income for three weeks
Both the added printing costs and three weeks of net income
Nothing, because the newspaper kept publishing
The necessary added printing costs during the period of restoration

questions.explanation: This is the classic extra-expense-only pattern: income continued, so there is no income loss to pay, but the necessary added cost of operating elsewhere is exactly what the form covers.

questions.question: A producer tells a client that because the client's flood policy came from a familiar national insurer's Write Your Own operation, disputes over the policy's meaning will be decided under that insurer's private homeowners wording. Why is that statement wrong?

answers.text: The flood policy has no written terms
Private wording controls whenever a brand name is printed on the declarations, as described in the endorsement request the agent submitted during the policy term
Write Your Own flood coverage remains the federal standard policy, so its federal terms control rather than the company's private homeowners wording
Disputes are decided by the mortgage lender's loan documents

questions.explanation: The Write Your Own arrangement does not turn the federal standard policy into the company's private product. Loan documents govern the loan, not the meaning of the flood policy's coverage terms.

questions.question: A customer walking through a repair shop's service area slips on an oil patch and is injured, with no auto involved in the accident. Under the shop's garage coverage form, this claim falls within which part of garage operations?

answers.text: Garage operations other than covered autos, covering the premises and operations exposure
Covered autos, because the accident happened near a vehicle
Garagekeepers, because the customer was on the premises
Products coverage for the oil the shop sells

questions.explanation: Explanation: Premises injuries with no auto involvement belong to the garage operations other-than-covered-autos side of the form. Garagekeepers addresses damage to customers' autos, not bodily injury to customers on the premises.

questions.question: A bid package requires a waiver of subrogation in favor of the owner. The contractor provides only a certificate describing a waiver, but no endorsement is ever issued before a loss occurs. What is the weakness in the contractor's position?

answers.text: There is no weakness, because certificates amend policies automatically
The weakness is only that the certificate lists the wrong project address
A certificate does not create the waiver; without a pre-loss endorsement, the standard waiver protection is not in place
The waiver exists but cannot be read by the owner, which is the only problem

questions.explanation: Only the endorsement changes the policy; a certificate is evidence and does not amend coverage or rights. Without the endorsement issued before the loss, the waiver is not effective on standard forms.

questions.question: What losses does a wrongful death claim primarily compensate?

answers.text: The deceased person's medical bills incurred before death
The punishment the defendant deserves for the conduct
The pain the deceased person felt between the injury and death, and that is so under the form regardless of how the loss itself developed
The losses the surviving family members themselves suffer because of the death, such as lost support and companionship

questions.explanation: Wrongful death compensates the survivors for what the death took from them, including financial support and companionship. The deceased's own pre-death pain and bills belong to a survival action instead.

questions.question: What does the noncontributory part of a primary and noncontributory endorsement promise?

answers.text: The named insured will not have to contribute any premium toward the policy
The insurer will not contribute to a defense if the claim is large
The additional insured's own insurance will not be required to contribute to the covered loss alongside this policy
The additional insured never has to contribute a deductible on any claim

questions.explanation: Noncontributory means the insurer will not seek contribution from the additional insured's own insurance for the covered loss. It concerns sharing between insurers, not premiums or deductibles.

questions.question: Which statement about a unilateral contract is correct?

answers.text: The promisor may revoke at any time even after full performance
The promisee can accept only by performing the requested act, rather than by making a return promise
No consideration is needed because only one promise exists
Both parties are bound to future performance from the start

questions.explanation: Acceptance by performance is the hallmark of a unilateral contract; the premium payment is consideration even though there is only one promise. Once performance is rendered as required, the promisor cannot revoke to escape the promise.

questions.question: Why is a dwelling form often the practical choice for a house the owner rents to someone else?

answers.text: Standard homeowners forms are designed for owner-occupied residences, while dwelling forms accept tenant-occupied houses
Homeowners forms are only for houses worth more than a set amount
Homeowners forms pay no claims at rental houses because rent is illegal to insure
Dwelling forms include unlimited liability for rental activity

questions.explanation: Owner occupancy is built into the main homeowners forms, so a rented house usually points to a dwelling form. The reason is occupancy design, not the house's value or the legality of rent.

questions.question: Which reason for a civil authority order fits the coverage conditions?

answers.text: The action is taken to promote a new shopping district
The action closes the street for a scheduled parade
The action enforces a zoning rule unrelated to any property damage, such as a routine setback or signage violation that officials happened to discover during an ordinary inspection of the area
The action responds to dangerous physical conditions resulting from the damage, or is taken so authorities can have unimpeded access to the damaged property

questions.explanation: The order must grow out of the covered damage: dangerous conditions from that damage or the need for unimpeded access to the damaged property. A parade closure has no such connection.

questions.question: An unknown driver sideswipes the covered auto, injuring the named insured, and flees without being identified. Under Part C, how is that vehicle classified?

answers.text: A hit-and-run vehicle whose owner or operator cannot be identified is treated as an uninsured motor vehicle
It is excluded because an unidentified vehicle can never be uninsured
It is treated as an underinsured vehicle with known limits
It becomes the insured's covered auto by operation of the form

questions.explanation: The form expressly includes within the uninsured definition a hit-and-run vehicle whose owner or operator cannot be identified. Unknown limits are not underinsurance; the vehicle is handled on the uninsured side of Part C.

questions.question: A Virginia public adjuster wants to use a particular engineer's bid in estimating a loss. What must happen first, and what right does the policyholder have?

answers.text: The adjuster must obtain the insurer's written approval of the engineer; the policyholder has no say

The adjuster must notify the policyholder or claimant in writing, in advance, of the proposed professional's name and location before the bid is used in estimating; the policyholder or claimant may veto that person, who then may not be used in estimating costs
The adjuster need only disclose the engineer's name after the estimate is finalized
The policyholder may veto the engineer only if the engineer is unlicensed

questions.explanation: Before any bid or proposal of a proposed contractor, architect, engineer, or similar professional may be used in estimating the loss, the public adjuster must give the policyholder or claimant advance written notice of the person's name and location. The policyholder or claimant holds a veto: a vetoed person may not be used in estimating costs.

questions.question: A contract between a Virginia controlling producer and its controlled insurer fixes the dates for remitting collected premiums. What outside limit does the law set?

answers.text: By the end of the calendar year in which they are collected
No later than 30 days after the policy effective date
Premiums and installments collected must be remitted no later than 90 days after the effective date of any policy placed under the contract, with remittance of all funds due at least monthly
No later than 180 days after the policy effective date

questions.explanation: The controlling producer remits all funds due at least monthly, and the due date must be set so that collected premiums reach the controlled insurer within 90 days of the policy's effective date. The monthly rhythm does not extend the 90-day outside limit.

questions.question: Under a standard property form that requires payment within 30 days after the insurer receives proof of loss and the amount is determined, when does that payment duty mature?

answers.text: Immediately when the loss occurs, before any proof is submitted, including when the underlying event involves more than one location, vehicle, or injured person
After proof of loss is received and the amount of loss has been agreed, appraised, or otherwise determined as the form provides
Only after the insured files suit
Only at the next policy renewal

questions.explanation: The timing clock depends on proof of loss plus a mechanism for fixing the amount, such as agreement or appraisal. Payment is not due at the moment of loss before proof, and suit is not a prerequisite.

questions.question: A clothing retailer asks to buy the standard financial institution bond form that banks use, for its store. What is the correct identity-level response?

answers.text: That form is a financial institution bond for banks and similar institutions; a retailer uses commercial crime coverage instead
The form covers only shoplifting by customers
Retailers are required to buy it instead of crime coverage
Any business may buy it and it is always the cheapest option, as noted in the file memorandum prepared by the adjuster assigned to the claim

questions.explanation: Standard Form 24 is built for financial institutions, not ordinary mercantile risks. The retailer's parallel protection is the commercial crime policy, not the bank bond form.

questions.question: A seaman is injured after following an unsafe work method directed by a supervising crew officer. Which fact is most important to the Jones Act analysis?

answers.text: Whether the employer, through its supervisors and methods, was negligent in a way that contributed to the injury
Whether the vessel was insured under a state compensation policy
Whether the seaman had worked for the employer for more than a year
Whether the injury happened during daylight hours

questions.explanation: Jones Act liability focuses on employer negligence, including unsafe methods directed by supervisors, that contributed to the injury. Length of service and daylight are irrelevant details, not elements of the claim.

questions.question: A basic dwelling policyholder wants protection against windstorm and hail. How is that protection normally obtained on the basic form?

answers.text: It is already included as a core basic-form peril
By adding extended coverage to the basic form
By adding liability coverage to the policy
By converting personal property to open perils

questions.explanation: Windstorm and hail are not core perils of the basic form; extended coverage is the mechanism that adds them. Adding liability would not add a property peril at all.

questions.question: A buyer is told a property needs flood insurance only if a human-made water source fails, such as a dam or levee, because natural overflow is not flood. Why is that explanation wrong?

answers.text: Flood is limited to ocean storm surge in all definitions
Natural rain can never contribute to a flood event
Flood includes overflow of inland or tidal waters and rapid accumulation of surface waters, not only structure failures
Levee failure is the sole cause recognized by the program, regardless of any contrary statement in a certificate of insurance or other summary of coverage

questions.explanation: The flood definition includes overflow of inland or tidal waters and unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of surface waters, in addition to certain shoreline collapse and mudflow events. Limiting flood to dam or levee failure omits the central natural causes.

questions.question: A condominium owner replaced builder-grade counters and flooring inside the unit with much more expensive materials. Where should the added value of those upgrades be reflected?

answers.text: In the owner's Coverage A limit, because improvements inside the unit are the owner's to insure
In the association's master policy limit, which the owner can raise directly
In Coverage B, other structures
Nowhere, because upgrades inside a unit cannot be insured

questions.explanation: Improvements and betterments inside a unit belong to the unit owner's Coverage A exposure, especially where the master policy covers only original construction. The owner cannot change the association's limit, and detached-structure coverage is not where interior upgrades belong.

questions.question: A company occupies a warehouse under a long-term lease. Its forklift crew negligently gouges deep cuts into the warehouse's own concrete floor, and the company must pay to restore the floor it occupies. Which exclusion most directly applies?

answers.text: Damage to your product, because concrete is a product, as recorded in the premium audit worksheet prepared at the end of the policy period
Recall, because the floor must be withdrawn
Damage to your property, because the floor is part of real property the insured rents or occupies, including costs to restore it
War, because heavy equipment was involved

questions.explanation: Real property the insured rents or occupies, and the costs required to repair or restore it, sit squarely in the damage to your property exclusion. The short-rental and fire carve-backs do not fit a long-term occupied warehouse floor damaged by operations.

questions.question: A deli sells a prepared tray, and a guest at the buyer's office becomes ill from the food hours later at another location. Which part of the deli's business liability coverage addresses this kind of claim?

answers.text: The medical expenses coverage, because the guest was never on the deli's premises by choice
The premises hazard only, because food was prepared in the deli kitchen
The products and completed operations hazard, because the injury arose from the insured's product after it left the insured's premises
The damage to premises rented coverage, because the food was eaten elsewhere

questions.explanation: Harm caused by the insured's products or finished work after the product has left the insured's control is a products and completed operations exposure. Premises coverage alone is the strongest distractor, but the injury came from the product itself after the sale, not from a condition of the deli.

questions.question: A business owner worries that paying a visitor's bill under Coverage C will be treated in court as the business admitting it caused the accident. What is the correct response?

answers.text: Payment under Coverage C is not an admission of liability by the insured
Payment under Coverage C admits liability for the full amount of any later verdict
Payment under Coverage C admits liability only if it exceeds half the limit
Payment under Coverage C bars the visitor from ever bringing a claim

questions.explanation: Medical payments are made without regard to fault and are not an admission of liability. Paying a bill also does not, by itself, bar the injured person from pursuing a separate liability claim.

questions.question: Two weeks after a policy's inception, the insurer and the insured agree to cancel it flat, effective at inception, and the paperwork is completed that day. The next day the insured reports a fire at the premises and asks for payment under that policy. What is the correct analysis?

answers.text: The policy is treated as never having been in force, so it provides no coverage for the fire
The policy covers the fire because it was physically in the insured's hands for two weeks
The policy covers half the loss because the cancellation came midway through the month
The insurer must pay because the fire happened after inception on the calendar

questions.explanation: Because the completed flat cancellation made the termination effective at inception, the contract is treated as never in force. Calendar time before the paperwork was finished does not create coverage once the flat date applies.

questions.question: A named insured's teenager is licensed on Monday and has an at-fault accident on Wednesday while driving a listed auto. The parents first try to add the teenager on Thursday, asking that the addition be backdated to Monday. What should the agent explain?

answers.text: An operator addition takes effect when it is made and agreed to, and it cannot be backdated after a loss to manufacture coverage or rating the insurer never accepted

Backdating an operator addition after a known accident is routine and always allowed by every insurer, and the parents may obtain coverage for the Wednesday accident by adding the teenager the following day
The addition can be backdated if the parents pay the premium in cash
The teenager's accident is automatically rated as the parents' accident instead

questions.explanation: Policy changes operate from when they are requested and accepted, not retroactively after a known loss. The Thursday request cannot rewrite the operator and rating facts that existed for the Wednesday accident.

questions.question: A building owner and a tenant each insure their own separate interests in the same building under their own policies, and a fire damages both interests. How does the other insurance condition ordinarily treat these policies?

answers.text: The tenant's policy pays the owner's entire loss first
The owner's policy is void because another policy exists
They are not prorated against each other, because each covers a different insurable interest
They are always prorated by limits, because the same building is involved

questions.explanation: Other insurance sharing applies to concurrent coverage of the same interest, and the owner and tenant hold different interests. The shared building alone does not make the policies concurrent.

north-carolina-real-estate.quiz_title: North Carolina Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Severance:

answers.text: converts real to personal property
converts personal to real
is the same
has no severance

questions.explanation: Severance converts real property to personal property, as when timber or crops are cut and detached from the land. It does not convert personal property to real property, which is the opposite process, it is not the same as that opposite process, and the claim that there is no severance denies the conversion the term names.

questions.question: Which statement best describes airport and flight-path noise?

answers.text: maps are secret
noise disclosure may be required in some areas
brokers may mislead
airport noise never matters

questions.explanation: Airport and flight-path noise can be a material condition, and in some areas disclosure of that noise to buyers may be required. Brokers may not mislead buyers about it, and it cannot be dismissed as never mattering.

questions.question: A BIC's email review:

answers.text: is part of supervision
has no email
is the client's
has no review

questions.explanation: Reviewing affiliated brokers' email is part of the broker-in-charge's supervision, because the broker-in-charge must assure that affiliated brokers comply with the license law and rules. The claims that there is no email, that the review is the client's, and that there is no review each deny a supervisory activity the broker-in-charge is charged with performing.

questions.question: Concerning buyer confirm zoning, which of the following is true?

answers.text: rules are uniform statewide
coordination is unnecessary
the buyer should confirm the zoning supports their plans
recording is pointless

questions.explanation: Zoning is set by local ordinances, so the rules are not uniform statewide, and a buyer should confirm that the property's zoning actually supports their intended use before buying. Recording documents is far from pointless, since recording is what protects priority in North Carolina.

questions.question: Oral consent from both parties to dual agency:

answers.text: is sufficient if confirmed by email
satisfies the requirement if witnessed
is sufficient for transactions under $500,000
does not satisfy North Carolina's written-authority requirement

questions.explanation: North Carolina dual agency requires the written authority of each party, so oral consent — even if confirmed by email afterward, witnessed, or for a smaller transaction — does not satisfy the requirement. Without that written authority, the broker may not act as a dual agent.

questions.question: A Sanford designated agent explains notice to a client. Which statement is true?

answers.text: interest transfers equal property deeds
an estate for years has no end
recording gives constructive notice
annexation does not exist

questions.explanation: Recording a deed gives constructive notice to the world of the transfer, which is why North Carolina's pure race system ties protection to registration. The recorded instrument, not the transfer of an interest alone, is what charges later parties with notice.

questions.question: Lisa Whitaker asks a Boone instructor about disclosure. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: brokers need not understand
full disclosure prevents disputes
data need not be shown
preparation is unnecessary

questions.explanation: Full disclosure is a core risk-management practice because it prevents the misunderstandings and surprises that turn into disputes and claims. Brokers are expected to understand the matters they disclose and to support them with data when needed.

questions.question: A buyer in Hendersonville borrows $400,000 at 6% annual interest (interest-only). How much interest is owed for the first full year?
questions.explanation: Interest-only interest for one year is the principal times the rate: $400,000 times 6 percent equals $24,000. Because the loan is interest-only, no principal is repaid during that year.

questions.question: A Monroe mentor quizzes a new agent on cap affects high. Which statement is true?

answers.text: title searches never show taxes
brokers prepare the figures
lenders do not require it
the cap affects high-tax areas

questions.explanation: The cap on the state and local tax deduction affects taxpayers most in high-tax areas, because more of their state and local taxes exceed the cap and go undeducted. Title searches do show tax information, brokers do not prepare lenders' figures, and lenders do require tax-related documentation.

questions.question: A broker studying manufactured-home closings asks which statement is true. Which is it?

answers.text: brokers need not understand
the broker should understand the basics
installation does not matter
the broker guides the legal process

questions.explanation: A broker handling a manufactured-home closing should understand the basics of that transaction type well enough to serve the client competently. The broker still must not guide the legal process itself, which belongs to legal professionals.

questions.question: Regarding specifics govern, a Sanford exam asks which statement is correct?

answers.text: explanations are unnecessary
full responsibility should be immediate
state law specifics govern
new supply never affects prices

questions.explanation: General national principles yield to the specific law of the state where the property and transaction sit, so state law specifics govern practice in that state. Explanations still matter, responsibility is not transferred instantly, and new supply does affect prices.

questions.question: A Greensboro agent tests a trainee on sets tax rates. Which statement is wrong?

answers.text: the Commission holds disciplinary hearings
the License Law sets property tax rates
unnecessary hardship must generally be shown
HOAs commonly enforce covenants

questions.explanation: The License Law does not set property tax rates; tax rates are set by the taxing units, not by the real estate licensing statute, so that statement is wrong. Commission disciplinary hearings, hardship showings for variances, and associations enforcing covenants are correct.

questions.question: An appraiser in Cary estimates site value at $75,000 and replacement cost of the improvements at $275,000. Accrued depreciation is 15%. What is the indicated value by the cost approach?
questions.explanation: The $275,000 cost reduced by 15 percent depreciation leaves $233,750, and adding the $75,000 site value gives $308,750. Ignoring depreciation would produce the higher figure and overvalue the improvements.

questions.question: A Thomasville buyer borrows $240,000 at 6.0% interest for 30 years, fully amortized. What is the monthly principal and interest payment?
questions.explanation: For a $240,000 loan at 6 percent over 30 years, the standard amortization payment is $1,438.92 per month for principal and interest. The $1,200 figure is interest-only for the first month, and the other amounts do not match the amortizing payment at these terms.

questions.question: Three of these statements about no training are true. Which one is NOT?

answers.text: training is pointless
the stakeholder deposits the funds with the court
provide requested records
electronic advertising follows the same rules

questions.explanation: Training is not pointless; it is a core risk-management tool for a brokerage. A stakeholder in a fund dispute deposits the funds with the court through interpleader, requested records must be provided, and electronic advertising follows the same rules as other advertising.

questions.question: A Statesville broker's policy manual addresses reconciliation weighs strengths. Which statement is true?

answers.text: reconciliation weighs the strengths of each approach applied
direct capitalization uses ten years
prior services need not be disclosed
extraction is impossible

questions.explanation: Reconciliation is the appraiser's weighing of the strengths and weaknesses of each approach applied before reaching a final value opinion. It does not use a ten-year direct-capitalization stream, prior services are not hidden by reconciliation, and extraction is a recognized technique rather than an impossibility.

questions.question: A North Carolina broker who performs an act that constitutes the unauthorized practice of law is subject to:

answers.text: disciplinary action for the unauthorized practice of law
no discipline if the client consented
only a bar complaint with no Commission action
a bonus for helpfulness

questions.explanation: Performing acts that constitute the unauthorized practice of law is a ground for Commission disciplinary action against the broker. Client consent does not excuse it, and the consequence is not limited to a bar complaint.

questions.question: In North Carolina, which statement about transaction brokerage is NOT correct?

answers.text: transaction brokers owe full fiduciary duties
the broker cannot advocate for either side
the broker assists without representing either party
honesty and fairness are owed to both sides

questions.explanation: A transaction broker assists the parties without representing either one and owes both sides honesty and fairness, but cannot advocate for either side and does not owe the full fiduciary duties an agent owes a client. The claim of full fiduciary duties is therefore the incorrect statement.

questions.question: A Greensboro exam prep session covers open ended listing. Which statement does NOT belong?

answers.text: the buyer must understand the agent represents the seller
withholding the listing limits the seller's market exposure
the exemption covers only the WWREA form, not agency disclosure itself
an open-ended listing fully complies with Commission rules

questions.explanation: An open-ended listing does not fully comply with the rules, because agency agreements must be in writing for a definite period of time. The buyer must understand when the agent represents the seller, withholding a listing limits the seller's market exposure, and a form exemption does not erase agency disclosure itself.

questions.question: A Raleigh brokerage discusses ambiguities never explained. Which statement is NOT true?

answers.text: escalation clauses typically require proof of the competing offer
discriminatory advertising violates fair housing law
the listing is the most common residential form
ambiguities may never be explained

questions.explanation: Ambiguities may be explained; evidence outside the contract can be used to clarify an ambiguous term even though it cannot contradict clear terms. Escalation clauses typically requiring proof of the competing offer, discriminatory advertising violating fair housing law, and the listing being the most common residential form are all true.

montana-real-estate.quiz_title: Montana Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Noah in Livingston notes an iron pin at the corner. What is a meander line?

answers.text: a fence
a road
the boundary
a survey line along water, not the exact boundary

questions.explanation: A meander line is a survey line run along water to approximate its course; it is not the exact boundary itself, since the actual boundary follows the water. Noah's iron pin marks a corner, but a meander line's special point is that the line on the plat only approximates the shifting water boundary it traces.

questions.question: A Havre agent states the roof is new. Is it allowed?

answers.text: never
nothing
generally
only the agent

questions.question: Omar in Bozeman explains the Montana act. What about the exam?

answers.text: nothing
only federal
ignore it
know the state law

questions.explanation: For the Montana fair-housing exam content, the point is to know the state law. Montana's Human Rights Act governs alongside federal law and adds its own protected classes, so ignoring the state act or treating the topic as federal-only leaves the agent unprepared.

questions.question: In Helena, the broker approves. Must the broker approve?

answers.text: nothing
never
generally
only the agent

questions.question: The relationship is preserved. What is the standard?

answers.text: a tax
professionalism
a gift
a guess

questions.question: A Livingston buyer is offered only a quitclaim. What warranties does it give?

answers.text: limited
none
only the price
full

questions.explanation: A quitclaim deed gives no warranties at all; it conveys only whatever interest the grantor happens to have. A buyer offered only a quitclaim gets no promise about title, unlike the full or limited warranties of other deeds.

questions.question: In Bozeman, the marketing plan is presented. What about the plan?

answers.text: it should be in writing
verbal
never
only the agent

questions.explanation: When the marketing plan is presented in Bozeman, it should be in writing, giving the seller a concrete record of the services and steps being committed to. A verbal presentation cannot be checked later against what was actually promised.

questions.question: A building valued at $250,000 depreciates at 4% per year for 6 years (straight-line). What is the depreciated value?
questions.explanation: Straight-line depreciation takes 4% of $250,000, or $10,000, per year for 6 years — $60,000 total. Subtracting from $250,000 leaves a depreciated value of $190,000.

questions.question: A deed conveying whatever interest the grantor has, with no warranties, is a

answers.text: trustee's deed
warranty deed with full covenants
general warranty deed
quitclaim deed

questions.explanation: A quitclaim deed transfers only whatever interest, if any, the grantor actually has and gives the grantee no warranty promises. Warranty deeds are the opposite family because they carry covenants backing the title conveyed.

questions.question: The appraiser keeps the workfile for the required period. Why keep it?

answers.text: for fun
it is optional
for taxes
to document compliance if reviewed

questions.explanation: An appraiser keeps the workfile because it documents the data and analysis behind the opinion, allowing the appraiser to demonstrate compliance if the assignment is later reviewed or questioned. Retention is a professional obligation, not an optional or recreational practice.

questions.question: A Bozeman buyer sues for specific performance. When is it available?

answers.text: only the agent
never
for unique property like real estate
always

questions.explanation: Specific performance is available when money damages are inadequate because the property is unique, as real estate is, so a buyer can ask a court to force the sale. It is not available for ordinary, interchangeable goods or as an automatic remedy in every case.

questions.question: Alex in Great Falls collects buyer feedback after each showing. What if feedback cites price?

answers.text: ignore it
blame the buyers
discuss a price adjustment with the seller
hide it

questions.explanation: Feedback that zeroes in on price calls for a conversation with the seller about adjusting it, using buyer evidence rather than blame or concealment. Alex serves the listing by surfacing the concern and discussing the change.

questions.question: In Livingston, Carl calculates replacement cost, subtracts depreciation, and adds land value early in the transaction. Why?

answers.text: the cause is outside the property boundaries
value equals depreciated cost plus land value
the cost to cure is less than the value added
the deficiency is in the property's design or layout

questions.explanation: Carl's steps are the cost approach: replacement cost, minus depreciation, plus land value equals the indicated value. The other choices describe causes of depreciation, not this computation.

questions.question: A senior homeowner borrows against equity with no monthly payments required. What is this loan?

answers.text: a reverse mortgage (HECM)
a standard mortgage
a tax lien
a personal loan

questions.explanation: A loan for a senior homeowner that taps equity with no required monthly payments is a reverse mortgage, commonly the federally insured home equity conversion type. A standard mortgage requires regular payments, the opposite structure.

questions.question: A subdivision's recorded declaration requires wood-shake roofs and bans backyard fences over four feet. What are these private land-use controls?

answers.text: deed restrictions (CC&Rs)
zoning ordinances
building codes
subdivision exactions

questions.explanation: Recorded declarations like the roof and fence limits here are private controls the buyers accept with the land, known as deed restrictions. Zoning and building codes come from government, so they describe public regulation rather than these subdivision covenants.

questions.question: A new agent meets a stranger at a vacant listing. What is the protocol?

answers.text: nothing
a gift
a tax
as the brokerage's policy provides

questions.question: Maya in Livingston presents the seller's counter without adding personal pressure. What is the agent's negotiation role?

answers.text: facilitate agreement within the client's lawful instructions
decide the outcome
pressure both sides
delay

questions.explanation: A negotiator's role is to facilitate agreement while staying inside the client's lawful instructions, carrying offers and counters faithfully between the sides. Deciding the outcome for the client, pressuring both parties, or stalling all abandon that facilitator role.

questions.question: In Livingston, Alex signs a buyer agreement limited to homes in one school district early in the transaction. What is the practical result?

answers.text: purchases outside the area are not covered
the buyer keeps flexibility
buying through another broker may still trigger the fee
disputes are resolved under the contract

questions.explanation: Alex's buyer agreement reaches only homes inside the named school district, so a purchase outside that territory simply falls outside the agreement's coverage; the geographic limit the parties signed defines where the agreement operates.

questions.question: Lily, a Havre seller's agent, negotiates with an unrepresented buyer who thinks Lily is helping both sides. Why is the clarification required?

answers.text: to generate dual agency
to prevent misunderstanding about loyalty and duties
to increase paperwork
to slow the deal

questions.explanation: Clarifying the relationship is required to prevent misunderstanding about loyalty and duties, so an unrepresented buyer does not wrongly believe the seller's agent also serves the buyer. The clarification does not create dual agency, which arises only with both parties' consent.

questions.question: Chris in Helena meets a buyer at a showing and discusses representation without ever stating licensee status. Why is first-contact identification required?

answers.text: to satisfy the MLS
to start the commission clock
so parties know they are dealing with a licensee from the start
to generate referrals

maryland-real-estate.quiz_title: Maryland Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Encroachments discovered by a survey

answers.text: should be disclosed and may require resolution before closing
automatically transfer title
are always ignored
void the listing

questions.explanation: An encroachment found on a survey means one party's structure crosses onto another's land, a defect the parties need disclosed and typically resolved before closing because it clouds what the buyer is actually getting. Encroachments do not transfer title by themselves, are not safely ignored, and do not automatically void a listing.

questions.question: Nancy Allen of Westminster lies to an unrepresented buyer. What is the correct agency practice?

answers.text: A licensee who lies to an unrepresented buyer has satisfied every agency duty.
A licensee who lies to an unrepresented buyer only needs to apologize after closing.
Agency duties do not apply when a licensee lies to an unrepresented buyer.
The correct agency practice is to disclose, obey lawful instructions, and protect confidences — a licensee who lies to an unrepresented buyer must correct course and do all three.

questions.explanation: Lying to an unrepresented buyer is never proper agency practice; the licensee must correct course by disclosing whom the licensee represents, following the principal's lawful instructions, and protecting confidences while dealing honestly with the buyer. Agency duties do not disappear merely because the person deceived is not a client.

questions.question: A rectangular lot measures 132 feet by 330 feet. Its area in acres is:

answers.text: 0.5 acre
Exactly 1 acre
2 acres
1.5 acres

questions.explanation: A lot 132 feet by 330 feet contains 43,560 square feet, and since one acre is exactly 43,560 square feet, the lot is exactly one acre. It is neither half an acre nor one and one-half or two acres.

questions.question: Jessica Baker of Cumberland commingles personal funds with trust funds; the broker must

answers.text: intervene immediately and stop the violation.
wait a month.
blame the client.
do nothing.

questions.explanation: Commingling personal money with client trust funds is a violation the broker must halt the moment it surfaces, intervening immediately rather than waiting. Trust accounts stay separate from the broker's own funds, and supervision means acting on a breach at once.

questions.question: Deborah Lee of Waldorf confuses customers about their role. What happens if this is mishandled?

answers.text: A licensee who confuses customers about their role has satisfied every agency duty.
A licensee who confuses customers about their role only needs to apologize after closing.
If mishandled, the customer is harmed and the licensee faces liability — a licensee who confuses customers about their role harms the customer and risks a claim.
Agency duties do not apply when a licensee confuses customers about their role.

questions.explanation: Clients and customers hold different places in a transaction, and confusing a customer about that role can cause real harm — the customer may share information believing representation exists when it does not. Mishandling that confusion exposes the licensee to liability; agency duties are not switched off by the mix-up.

questions.question: HOA records show a lien on a Easton unit for unpaid assessments. It is classified as

answers.text: a judgment.
a general voluntary lien.
a mortgage.
an involuntary lien specific to the unit.

questions.explanation: A lien for unpaid association assessments arises by operation of law against the particular unit rather than from a voluntary borrowing, so it is an involuntary lien specific to that property. It is not a court judgment, a mortgage the owner signed, or a general voluntary lien.

questions.question: Deborah Lopez of Westminster fails to explain why consideration matters; the governing principle provides

answers.text: that consideration is the same as the down payment.
that consideration is unnecessary.
that consideration is the legal value each party gives to make the contract binding.
that consideration means the deed.

questions.explanation: Consideration is the legal value each side gives up or promises in exchange, and that mutual exchange is what makes the bargain enforceable. It is not limited to a down payment, and it refers to the parties' exchange rather than the deed that later transfers title.

questions.question: Paul Wright of Columbia tells a buyer the search is a formality; the correct result is

answers.text: that title searches are a mere formality
that skipping the title search saves money safely
that the seller's word on title is sufficient
that title must be verified by a proper search before closing — the seller's word is not title evidence and skipping the search is negligent

questions.explanation: Title must be verified by a proper search before closing, because the seller's word is not evidence of title and skipping the search can miss liens and defects. A search is not a mere formality, and skipping it does not save money safely.

questions.question: Matthew Garcia's Frederick broker retires and closes the office. Matthew Garcia's license becomes

answers.text: a broker license.
valid independently.
permanently revoked.
inactive until Matthew Garcia affiliates with another broker.

questions.explanation: Salespersons and associate brokers may act only while affiliated with a licensed broker, so when the broker retires and closes the office the licensee's license becomes inactive until affiliation with another broker. It does not become a broker license, is not valid independently, and is not permanently revoked.

questions.question: An Ellicott City broker agrees to pay a 30% referral fee on a $424,000 sale. The referral fee is

answers.text: $0 — referrals are illegal.

questions.question: Nancy Turner of Salisbury fails to explain performance as acceptance; the correct legal result is

answers.text: Unilateral offers require written acceptances.
Only promises can accept offers.
In a unilateral contract, the offeree accepts by performing the requested act; no return promise is needed.
Performance can never accept an offer.

questions.explanation: In a unilateral contract the offeror asks for an act rather than a promise, so performing that act is itself the acceptance and forms the contract. Requiring a separate written acceptance or a return promise would convert it into a different, bilateral arrangement.

questions.question: Stephanie Jones of Ellicott City fails to explain the option period; the governing principle provides

answers.text: that the option must be exercised exactly as the contract requires, within the option period.
that oral exercise is always sufficient.
that an option may be exercised any time after it expires.
that the seller may ignore a proper exercise.

questions.explanation: An option is a contract right that must be exercised exactly as its terms require and within its stated period; a late or nonconforming exercise does not bind the seller. Oral exercise is not automatically sufficient, and a proper exercise cannot simply be ignored.

questions.question: An Annapolis home's replacement cost new is $380,000, depreciation is 5%, and the site is worth $65,000. The cost-approach value is

answers.text: the land alone.

questions.explanation: Depreciated cost is $380,000 multiplied by ninety-five percent, or $361,000, and adding the $65,000 site value yields $426,000. The $411,000 figure understates that sum, so it cannot be the cost-approach result.

questions.question: David Davis of Frederick sells a pre-1978 home with no lead disclosure; the governing rule provides

answers.text: optional tips.
vague hints.
clear disclosure obligations.
no duties.

questions.explanation: Selling a pre-1978 home triggers clear lead-based paint disclosure obligations, not optional tips or vague hints. The seller and licensee must give the required disclosures and information about known lead hazards before the buyer is bound.

questions.question: A person who violates a listed provision of the title, such as providing real estate brokerage services without a license, is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction for a first offense faces:

answers.text: Only a written warning
A mandatory five-year prison term
A $100 maximum fine
A fine of up to $5,000 or imprisonment of up to one year, or both

questions.question: Andrew Scott of Bowie deposits $6,000 of trust funds 12 business days after both parties accepted the contract. The broker has

answers.text: complied, because 12 days is reasonable.
promptly after acceptance — Maryland allows no more than 7 business days from acceptance by both parties.
no duty as long as the funds are safe.
complied if the client agreed orally.

questions.question: Robert Adams of Ellicott City skips the buyer agreement discussion. What do professional standards require?

answers.text: A licensee who skips the buyer agreement discussion is meeting the professional standard.
Professional standards require knowledge, skill, and integrity — a licensee who skips the buyer agreement discussion is missing at least one of the three.
A licensee who skips the buyer agreement discussion only needs to try harder next time.
Professional standards excuse a licensee who skips the buyer agreement discussion.

questions.explanation: Skipping the buyer agreement discussion leaves the buyer unclear about representation, duties, and compensation, falling short of the knowledge, skill, and integrity professional practice requires. The conversation is part of competent service, not an optional courtesy that standards excuse omitting.

questions.question: Thomas Martinez of Hagerstown misstates the difference between conventional and government loans; the correct course is to

answers.text: FHA/VA/USDA programs impose property and borrower rules that conventional loans do not.
All mortgage loans are government-insured.
Conventional and FHA loans have identical requirements.
Government loans require no underwriting.

questions.explanation: Government programs such as the federal housing, veterans, and rural housing loans impose their own property and borrower requirements that conventional loans do not carry. Conventional loans are not government-insured, the two categories do not share identical requirements, and government loans still go through underwriting.

questions.question: When Jennifer Mitchell's Ellicott City listing sells through the MLS, the cooperating broker's compensation comes from

answers.text: the state fund.
the buyer's pocket directly.
the listing broker's offered compensation.
the MLS.

questions.explanation: When a listing sells through the multiple listing service, the cooperating broker is paid from the compensation the listing broker offered in that listing. The money does not come from a state fund, the service itself, or directly out of the buyer's pocket.

questions.question: David Taylor of Frederick lets a personal deal take priority over a client's. What is the ethical course?

answers.text: The ethical course is to act honestly and put the client's lawful interests first — a licensee who lets a personal deal take priority over a client's must stop and do exactly that.
A licensee who lets a personal deal take priority over a client's is acting ethically.
A licensee who lets a personal deal take priority over a client's only needs to keep it quiet.
The Code of Ethics excuses a licensee who lets a personal deal take priority over a client's.

questions.explanation: A client's lawful interests come before the licensee's own deals, so letting a personal transaction take priority inverts the ethical order and the licensee must put the client first and act honestly. Elevating the personal deal is not ethical, and hiding the conflict does not make it so.

washington-real-estate.quiz_title: Washington Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding legal descriptions and land characteristics, which of the following situations illustrates homestead designation?

answers.text: Wind rights are leased to an energy company.
A married couple designates their home as homestead.
A deed gives both a distance and a conflicting bearing.
An owner controls who enters the property.

questions.explanation: Homestead designation is the act of claiming the family home as the protected homestead, which is what the married couple does here. Leasing wind rights, resolving a conflicting legal description, and controlling entry describe other property rights, not a homestead claim.

questions.question: Regarding brokerage practice and agency operations, Carol Garcia is in a situation where a broker blogs. Which rule applies?

answers.text: Implied agency can never arise from the parties' conduct.
A broker may collect a commission without any written or oral agreement.
The content is accurate.
Fiduciary duties end the moment an offer is signed.

questions.question: Regarding special assessment per unit, a $325,000 special assessment is spread equally over 100 condo units. What is each unit's share?
questions.explanation: Spread equally, $325,000 ÷ 100 units = $3,250 per unit. The full assessment amount is the whole project's cost, not any single unit's share.

questions.question: Regarding agency duties, which of the following situations illustrates SB 6091 exception?

answers.text: A broker withholds a listing from the public for health and safety reasons.
A private listing without public marketing is challenged as discrimination.
A limited dual agent pushes the seller's price on the buyer.
A broker's buyer agreement auto-renews without notice.

questions.explanation: Washington's private-marketing rule carries a health-and-safety exception, so withholding a listing from the public for genuine health or safety reasons fits that carve-out. A private listing challenged as discrimination, a limited dual agent favoring one side, and an auto-renewing buyer agreement illustrate violations or unrelated problems, not the exception.

questions.question: Regarding professional standards, which of the following situations illustrates suspension?

answers.text: A broker ties listings to mortgage referrals.
A broker's license is suspended.
Continuing education is incomplete at renewal.
A former client asks for their file.

questions.explanation: Suspension is the temporary withdrawal of a license, so a broker whose license is suspended is the direct example of that sanction. Tying listings to referrals, incomplete education, and a file request describe other conduct or events, not a suspension itself.

questions.question: Regarding land-use controls and zoning, which of the following situations illustrates abandonment of nonconforming use?

answers.text: The factory closes for two years.
A short-term rental ban is proposed.
An HOA lien is foreclosed.
A developer seeks a density bonus for affordable units.

questions.explanation: Abandonment of a nonconforming use is shown by discontinuing it, and a factory that closes and stays closed for two years demonstrates that abandonment. A proposed rental ban, an association lien foreclosure, and a density-bonus request do not involve giving up an existing nonconforming use.

questions.question: Regarding listing and buyer agreements, where a contract includes a seller financing addendum, which statement describes an exception or limit to the rule?

answers.text: Oral agreements for the sale of land are fully enforceable.
The addendum's terms govern.
An expired protection clause still guarantees the commission.
The breaching party automatically keeps the earnest money.

questions.explanation: Once the parties sign it, a seller financing addendum becomes part of their contract, and its financing terms control that subject instead of any conflicting general assumption. It does not make oral land contracts enforceable, revive an expired protection period, or hand earnest money to whoever breaches.

questions.question: Where a foreclosure sale brings surplus funds, regarding settlement and foreclosure, which statement of the consequence is correct?

answers.text: The deed is effective before delivery.
Ownership reverts after ten years.
Junior liens gain priority automatically.
Priority determines distribution.

questions.explanation: When a foreclosure sale leaves money beyond what the foreclosed lien is owed, the leftover is handed out according to the priority of the remaining claims. Junior liens do not leap ahead automatically, and ownership questions do not control the distribution.

questions.question: Where a broker's license is suspended for misconduct, regarding Washington license administration, which statement of the rule is correct?

answers.text: A revoked license reactivates automatically after one year.
Suspension prohibits practice during its term.
The department cannot subpoena records.
The testing vendor sets Washington license law.

questions.explanation: A suspended licensee is barred from practicing while the suspension runs, because suspension withdraws the authority to act during its term. It is not an automatic one-year path back from revocation, and neither a testing vendor nor a subpoena limit changes that consequence.

questions.question: Regarding condominium act provisions, Chris Mitchell is in a situation where a manager wants to use reserves for a lobby remodel. Which rule applies?

answers.text: Assessment liens have no legal priority.
Association books are secret from unit owners.
Conversion tenants receive no notice at all.
Reserve account withdrawals are restricted to repair and replacement purposes.

questions.question: Where a seller asks the broker to list at an inflated price, regarding agency creation and representation, which statement of the rule is correct?

answers.text: Compensation terms may stay secret from the parties to the transaction.
Dual agency is permitted without disclosure when it speeds the closing.
The broker should provide honest pricing data.
A licensee may act as an undisclosed dual agent to keep a deal together.

questions.explanation: Faced with a seller's inflated asking price, the broker should supply honest market pricing data so the seller can judge realistically. Hiding compensation terms or acting as an undisclosed dual agent would violate disclosure duties instead of solving the pricing problem.

questions.question: Regarding contract formation and breach, Elena Parker is in a situation where a buyer refuses to close without any contingency. Which rule applies?

answers.text: An expired protection clause still guarantees the commission.
Unexcused nonperformance is a breach.
Only the seller's breach has legal consequences.
An offer remains open forever until the offeree responds.

questions.explanation: Refusing to close with no contingency excusing performance is unexcused nonperformance, which is a breach of the purchase contract. Only excused failures, like an unmet contingency, avoid breach; the seller's breaches count too, and an expired protection clause does not manufacture a commission.

questions.question: Comparable rentals in Bothell show a gross rent multiplier of 8.0 (based on monthly rent). Deborah Bell's subject rents for $4,900/month. Regarding the GRM-indicated value, what is it?
questions.explanation: The stem states the multiplier is 8.0 based on monthly rent, so the indicated value is the $4,900 monthly rent multiplied by 8. That stem-supplied computation gives $39,200, using the monthly figure exactly as the stem frames it.

questions.question: Regarding broker disclosure duties, in a situation where a tsunami zone includes the property, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

answers.text: Tsunami zone designation is material
Designation is disclosable
Safety and insurance are affected
Tsunamis are too rare to matter

questions.explanation: A tsunami-zone designation affects safety, insurability, and value, so it is a material, disclosable fact about the property. Claiming tsunamis are too rare to matter is the false statement, because rarity does not erase a known hazard's materiality.

questions.question: Regarding commission, administration, and general provisions, Sandra Singh is in a situation where a consumer checks a license online. What is the legal consequence?

answers.text: The exam fee is returned with interest.
The license issues without an application.
The public confirms status.
The credential never requires renewal.

questions.explanation: An online license lookup lets a consumer verify whether a credential is current and in good standing, so the public-confirmation result is the real consequence. Checking a database does not issue a license, refund an exam fee, or abolish renewal.

questions.question: Regarding ownership interests, in a situation where air rights above a downtown lot are sold, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

answers.text: The sale conveys the defined airspace
Airspace cannot be owned
Severance creates the interest
Air rights are severable property interests

questions.explanation: Air rights are severable property interests, and selling them conveys the defined airspace above the lot, so declaring that airspace cannot be owned is the incorrect statement. Severance is precisely how a separate air-rights interest is created and transferred.

questions.question: Where a broker fails to disclose a known sex-offender group home next door when asked directly, regarding prohibited conduct, which statement of the consequence is correct?

answers.text: The unlicensed person keeps the commission.
Lying in response to a direct question is misrepresentation.
The advertising rules expire yearly.
The WAC is repealed by inaction.

questions.explanation: Whatever may or may not have to be volunteered about a neighboring group home, lying when asked directly is misrepresentation, because the broker must deal honestly and in good faith with every party. A false direct response is not excused by an unlicensed person keeping a commission, by advertising rules, or by any repeal of the administrative rules.

questions.question: Regarding qualifying ratios, betty Collins earns $10,750 monthly; the lender applies a 31% front-end ratio. Regarding the maximum monthly housing payment, what amount qualifies?
questions.explanation: Apply the 31 percent front-end ratio to the $10,750 monthly income by multiplying them together. The maximum qualifying monthly housing payment is $3,332.50, listed as $3,333.

questions.question: Regarding gross commission, a vacant residential lot in Auburn closes at $525,000. The listing agreement calls for a 6% commission. Regarding the total commission, how much is due?
questions.explanation: Multiply the $525,000 sale price by the 6 percent commission rate and the gross commission is $31,500. Halving that figure or inflating it misapplies a straightforward percentage-of-price calculation.

questions.question: Regarding general contract law, in a situation where a buyer recovers the difference between contract price and market value, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

answers.text: Compensatory damages punish the breaching party
Compensatory damages put the injured party in the position expected had the contract been performed
The award covers foreseeable losses from the breach
Punitive damages are rarely available in contract cases

questions.explanation: Compensatory damages are meant to make the injured party whole by covering foreseeable losses from the breach, not to punish the breaching party. Punishment is the role of punitive damages, which contract law rarely awards, so the punishment statement is the incorrect one.

michigan-real-estate.quiz_title: Michigan Real Estate FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A lot measuring 120 feet by 100 feet has a total square footage of

answers.text: 440 sq ft
12,000 sq ft
6,000 sq ft
13,000 sq ft

questions.explanation: Area is length times width, so a lot measuring 120 feet by 100 feet contains 12,000 square feet. Adding the side lengths gives the 440-foot perimeter figure, not the area.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of duty to obey lawful instructions?

answers.text: a friend marketing a home for free who must still act honestly and carefully.
a listing agent asking another broker to negotiate terms without the seller's approval.
an agent ordered to disgorge an undisclosed markup on repairs.
an agent refusing to discriminate as instructed by the seller.

questions.explanation: The duty of obedience runs only to lawful instructions, so an agent who refuses a seller's instruction to discriminate is honoring that duty rather than breaking it. Negotiating without the seller's approval exceeds authority, and the disgorgement and honesty examples describe other duties.

questions.question: Annual rent for a 1,200-square-foot shop at $16 per square foot per year comes to
questions.explanation: Rent quoted per square foot per year multiplies across the whole space: 1,200 square feet at $16 gives $19,200 in annual rent. The $1,600 figure is the monthly amount, not the yearly total the stem asks for.

questions.question: A pollutant regulated under Michigan's Part 201 is a

answers.text: asbestos
lead paint
hazardous substance
radon

questions.question: Under Michigan law, a landlord must not:

answers.text: coercing, intimidating, threatening, or interfering with a person in the exercise or enjoyment of rights protected by the source-of-income subsection
evicting for documented lease violations unrelated to income source
sending a late-rent reminder permitted by the lease
inspecting the unit on 24 hours' notice

questions.explanation: Since April 2025 Michigan landlords may not discriminate based on source of income, and the law also forbids coercing, intimidating, threatening, or interfering with someone exercising those source-of-income rights. Ordinary reminders, noticed inspections, and evictions for unrelated documented violations remain lawful.

questions.question: A developer dividing acreage into 40 lots in Portage must generally

answers.text: obtain plat approval from the local governing body and comply with subdivision regulations
only record a deed for each lot
get federal approval for every subdivision
nothing until the first home is built

questions.explanation: Dividing acreage into many lots is a subdivision, which generally requires plat approval from the local governing body and compliance with subdivision regulations. Recording deeds alone or waiting until construction starts does not substitute for that approval.

questions.question: Which term is characterized by the following statement? buyers still inspect and can walk away per contingencies.

answers.text: appraisal gap clause
as-is clause
severability clause
home solicitation sales

questions.explanation: An as-is clause tells the buyer the property is accepted in its present condition with no promise of repairs, yet inspection contingencies can still let the buyer walk away. That present-condition bargain differs from a clause about covering an appraisal shortfall or from severability, which concerns salvaging the rest of a contract.

questions.question: Annual property taxes are $6,681. Using a 365-day year, the tax proration for 157 days is:
questions.explanation: With a 365-day year, each day carries about $18.30 of the $6,681 annual tax, and 157 days at that daily rate comes to $2,873.75. Using a larger day count or a different divisor drifts away from the stated period.

questions.question: Under R 125.102(g), "family" under the MSHDA general rules means:

answers.text: Any single person or group of persons sharing a unit
Two or more persons living together not contrary to law
Persons related by blood or marriage living together
A household head and spouse with their dependents

questions.question: Under Michigan law, co-owners must be notified of a proposed amendment to the condominium documents:

answers.text: only after the amendment is recorded
only if the amendment changes their percentage of value
not less than 60 days before the amendment is recorded
not less than 10 days before the amendment is recorded

questions.question: An exam question asks for an illustration of divorce leads. The best answer is:

answers.text: calling expired-listing owners.
a discreet attorney referral network.
past clients and friends.
a FSBO outreach campaign.

questions.explanation: Divorce leads typically come through a discreet referral network of divorce attorneys, whose clients often must sell a home as part of a settlement. Expired listings, past clients, and for-sale-by-owner outreach generate other kinds of leads, not divorce-driven ones.

questions.question: Annual property taxes are $6,254. Using a 365-day year, the tax proration for 251 days is:
questions.explanation: Divide the annual tax by 365 to get the daily amount, then multiply by 251 days: $6,254 over 365, times 251, equals $4,300.70. The $1,953.30 figure is the remaining part of the year rather than the 251-day share.

questions.question: Monthly scheduled rents are $1,600 per unit for 1 units, and similar buildings recently sold for about 110 times their monthly gross rents. What value is indicated?
questions.explanation: The gross rent multiplier approach multiplies monthly rent by the market multiplier: $1,600 times 110 equals an indicated value of $176,000 for the one unit. Dividing rent by the multiplier produces the smallest figure, and doubling the product invents a second unit the stem does not include.

questions.question: A principal of $286,079 earns simple interest at 5.4% per year for 7 years. The total interest earned is:
questions.explanation: Total simple interest is principal times rate times years: $286,079 times 5.4 percent times 7 equals about $108,137.86. The figure near fifteen thousand dollars is only one year's interest, not the accumulation over the full term.

questions.question: For a summary proceeding under section 5726, MCL 600.5735(2)(a) sets the appearance for trial within 30 days of the summons' issuance, with service required:

answers.text: at least 45 days before the trial date
any time before judgment is entered
not less than 10 days before the date set for trial
not less than 3 days before the trial date

questions.question: Two parties make an illegal agreement to fix prices. When one sues to enforce it, the court will refuse under the doctrine of

answers.text: in pari delicto (courts will not aid wrongdoers)
quantum meruit
unjust enrichment
promissory estoppel

questions.explanation: Parties to an illegal price-fixing bargain stand in equal fault, so under the in pari delicto doctrine a court leaves them where it finds them and refuses to enforce the deal. Restitution-style doctrines do not rescue a claimant who must rely on the illegal agreement itself.

questions.question: A Michigan apartment rents for $2,180 per month. What is the maximum security deposit the landlord may require under Michigan law (1.5 months' rent)?
questions.explanation: At one and one-half months' rent, the ceiling on a $2,180 monthly rent is $3,270. Collecting two months' rent would exceed the Michigan cap, and one month's rent understates the maximum the landlord may require.

questions.question: All of the following are true of land contract EXCEPT:

answers.text: the buyer receives a deed at signing.
a buyer making monthly payments to the seller for five years before receiving the deed.
seller financing where the seller keeps title until the buyer pays in full.
the buyer gets equitable title and possession, the seller keeps legal title.

questions.explanation: Under a land contract the buyer does not get a deed at signing — the seller keeps legal title until the price is paid in full, while the buyer holds equitable title and possession and pays over time. Every other statement matches how the arrangement actually works, so the deed-at-signing claim is the false one.

questions.question: A home sells for $298,300 with a total commission of 5%, split equally between the listing and selling brokers. The selling agent receives 60% of the selling broker's share. The agent receives:
questions.explanation: Total commission is $298,300 × 5% = $14,915; the selling broker's equal half is $7,457.50, and the agent takes 60% of that half, which is $4,474.50. Paying 60% of the full commission would give the $8,949 distractor.

questions.question: A homeowner's principal residence exemption eliminates the 18-mill school operating tax on a home with a taxable value of $189,250. How much does the exemption save the homeowner per year?
questions.explanation: The exemption removes 18 mills of school operating tax, so savings are $189,250 times 18 divided by 1,000. That computation gives $3,406.50 per year on the stated taxable value.

texas-water-operator-class-c.quiz_title: Texas Water Operator Class C Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: After passing the Class C computer-based exam, within what time is the license issued?

answers.text: Within one month of the exam date
Within one week of the exam date
Within three months of the exam date
Only at the start of the next renewal cycle

questions.explanation: An applicant who passes the computer-based exam is issued the license within one week of the exam date. The longer periods would leave a passing applicant unlicensed well past the published issuance time.

questions.question: You assign a crew the routine hydrant maintenance round. Which direction makes the round complete?

answers.text: Operate each hydrant, check caps and gaskets, confirm the barrel drains after closing, and log every deficiency for repair
