Flow each hydrant at full pressure until the water runs clear, record the date, and treat the round as complete with no other checks
Paint each hydrant and record only the ones that could not be opened
Check only the hydrants customers have complained about during the year

questions.explanation: A complete maintenance round exercises the hydrant, checks its caps, gaskets, and drainage, and turns findings into logged repair work. Painting alone, flowing alone, or visiting only complained-about hydrants leaves inoperable hydrants undiscovered.

questions.question: A worker takes a chemical splash to the eyes while handling treatment chemicals. What do you direct first?

answers.text: Immediate, continuous flushing at the eyewash station, followed by medical evaluation, with the work held until the worker is cared for
Direct the worker to drive themselves to the nearest clinic before any flushing is done, in order to save time and keep the job on schedule
Have the worker blink rapidly for a minute and return to the task if vision clears
Apply a dry bandage over both eyes and schedule an evaluation the next day

questions.explanation: Chemical eye exposure is treated on the spot: prolonged eyewash flushing starts at once and medical evaluation follows, because delay costs vision. Blinking is not decontamination, driving delays flushing when minutes matter, and bandaging over unflushed chemical traps it against the eye.

questions.question: Why does storage turnover deserve extra attention during hot Texas weather?

answers.text: Stored water loses its disinfectant residual faster as temperatures rise, so aged water must be turned over
Hot weather makes tank coatings cure faster, so interior work can be scheduled and tanks returned to service sooner
Warm stored water gains residual from the tank walls as it sits
Turnover matters only in cold weather, when water can freeze in the tank

questions.explanation: Warmth speeds the loss of disinfectant residual in stored water, so summer storage that sits too long can reach customers weakly protected unless it is turned over. Residual is consumed as water ages; it is never gained from sitting against a tank wall.

questions.question: After a plant outage, you are bringing a groundwater plant back online. Which order do you direct?

answers.text: Push water to distribution first and start disinfection once pressure recovers before the monthly operating report is prepared and signed
Fill every storage tank first and disinfect the tanks at the next cleaning
Start production and confirm treatment and disinfection are operating before water is released to distribution
Release water to the nearest customers while the far side of the system waits

questions.explanation: Restart protects the public-health barrier first: treatment and disinfection are confirmed running before produced water goes out to customers. Sending water first and disinfecting later exposes the distribution system to untreated well water.

questions.question: A coworker suffers a deep cut from a broken fitting and is bleeding heavily. What is the correct first response?

answers.text: Apply firm direct pressure to the wound and get emergency help
Have the coworker walk to the office and rest until the bleeding slows down on its own
Wash the wound thoroughly before applying any pressure
Apply a tourniquet above every bleeding wound first

questions.explanation: Severe bleeding is controlled first with firm direct pressure on the wound while emergency help is obtained. Delaying pressure to wash the wound first allows continued blood loss.

questions.question: Your basins hold sludge between cleanings. Rather than reacting to solids at the outlet, how should sludge withdrawal be scheduled?

answers.text: Measure the blanket depth on a routine schedule and withdraw sludge based on the measured depth, before it nears the outlet zone
Withdraw sludge only on the days when the wash-water tank is full
Withdraw a fixed amount every Friday regardless of how much has collected, whether the problem shows up on a weekday round or a weekend round
Wait until the blanket is visible at the surface, which shows it is ready

questions.explanation: Blanket depth is measurable, so withdrawal can be planned on the measurement and stay ahead of carryover instead of chasing it. A fixed weekday amount ignores how much solids the raw water actually delivered, and a surface-visible blanket is already too deep.

questions.question: A contact basin holds 97,500 gallons and water flows through it at 250 gallons per minute. What is the detention time in hours?

answers.text: 390 hours
6.50 hours
5.42 hours
7.80 hours

questions.explanation: Detention time = volume / flow, so 97,500 / 250 = 390 minutes, and 390 / 60 = 6.50 hours. Reporting 390 as hours skips the minutes-to-hours conversion the problem requires.

questions.question: A chlorinator at a well plant is being returned to service after maintenance. What do you direct the crew to do before the unit is left running unattended?

answers.text: Open the gas supply fully and check for leaks the following morning
Rely on the room's odor alone, since a small leak is not worth a formal check and file the paperwork with the system's routine records
Paint the fittings so any future leak will stain the paint visibly
Start the unit, then check every fitting and connection for leaks while it operates under its normal vacuum

questions.explanation: A chlorinator goes back into unattended service only after its fittings and connections are checked for leaks while it is operating, so a maintenance error is caught with the crew present. Deferring the check leaves a possible gas leak undiscovered overnight.

questions.question: Customers are reporting earthy taste and odor, and the reservoir is in an algal bloom. What is the directing operator's best plant response?

answers.text: Add extra disinfectant to the clearwell until the odor is masked
Tell customers the water is safe and take no plant action during the bloom, even on shifts when everything else at the plant is running normally
Bypass sedimentation so algae reach the filters faster for removal
Address the load at pretreatment and aeration and check coagulation, rather than trying to fix taste in finished water

questions.explanation: Taste-and-odor material from an algal bloom is handled at pretreatment and aeration, with coagulation checked, not masked in finished water. Bypassing sedimentation loads the filters with the very material causing the complaints.

questions.question: You are verifying the system's record files after a survey cycle. Sanitary survey reports belong in which retention class?

answers.text: Records retained for at least ten years
Records retained for at least three years
Records retained for at least five years
Records retained for at least two years

questions.explanation: Sanitary survey reports sit in the class retained for at least ten years, with operating reports and chemical analyses, so they remain available across survey cycles. The two-year class holds items such as flushing dates, the three-year class holds items such as public notices, and the five-year class holds microbiological results.

questions.question: A plant treats 0.47 MGD and applies a chlorine dose of 2.35 mg/L. How many pounds of chlorine per day are required?

answers.text: 1.10 lb/day
92.12 lb/day
9.21 lb/day
4.61 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow in MGD x dose in mg/L x 8.34, so 0.47 x 2.35 x 8.34 = 9.21 lb/day. The 1.10 lb/day figure stops after multiplying flow by dose and never applies the 8.34 conversion.

questions.question: Complaint entries show a cluster of discolored-water calls from one part of town over two days, all logged but never acted on. As the directing operator, what do you order?

answers.text: Close the complaints, since logging them completes the system's duty
Flush the affected area, check residuals there, and review the log for a cause
Advise each caller to run a tap for an hour and record no further action
Wait for the cluster to appear in a second month before treating it as real

questions.explanation: A complaint log is a monitoring tool: a geographic cluster points to a localized cause, answered by flushing, residual checks, and a review of what changed in that area. Merely logging complaints without acting on the pattern leaves the cause in place.

questions.question: A new chlorine container is delivered and a crew member removes its valve protection cap at the loading dock, before the container is moved into place. What do you direct?

answers.text: Leave the cap off, because it is only a shipping cover and serves no purpose once the container is on site
Remove the valve outlet plug as well, so the container can be connected faster when it reaches the feeder
Set the cap aside in the office, where it will be available when the empty container is shipped back
Refit the cap; it stays on until the container is placed and ready to be connected

questions.explanation: The valve protection cap protects the container valve from damage during handling and stays in place until the container is positioned and ready for connection. Removing it, or the outlet plug, early exposes the valve for the whole move into place.

questions.question: A ground storage tank has been repaired and repainted inside, and the contractor wants it refilled and returned to service the same afternoon. What do you require first?

answers.text: Refill it immediately, because the repair crew's schedule and remaining daylight set the return date
Disinfection of the facility, satisfactory bacteriological clearance, and the licensed operator's approval before it enters service
A single visual check of the paint finish by the newest crew member
One flush of the tank's inlet line, with sampling deferred to the next routine round

questions.explanation: Repaired facilities are disinfected and shown free of microbiological contamination by accredited-lab results, and a licensed operator's guidance and approval precede placing them into service. A visual paint check and a line flush do not establish that the tank is safe to serve.

questions.question: Reviewing records for a system that distributes chloraminated water, you find the operator has been judging the residual from free chlorine readings. What do you direct?

answers.text: Judge and record the chloramine residual as total chlorine, the measure that applies to chloraminated water
Keep judging by the free chlorine readings, because free chlorine is the fraction that does the disinfecting
Average the free and total readings together, because the true chloramine residual falls between the two
Double the free chlorine reading, because total chlorine in chloraminated water runs about twice the free reading

questions.explanation: The residual of a chloraminated system is measured as total chlorine, which captures the combined chlorine actually carrying the disinfection through the system. Judging it by free chlorine readings alone understates the disinfectant present and misstates the records the directing operator signs.

questions.question: Staff find the elevated tank's ladder access damaged in an apparent climbing attempt, though the hatch stayed locked. What do you direct first?

answers.text: Post a warning sign at the fence and consider the response complete
Leave the ladder exactly as found until the next scheduled site visit, so nothing at the site is disturbed for the rest of the month
Direct the crew to remove the tank from service permanently because its security was challenged
Secure the ladder access against climbing, inspect the hatch and vents for tampering, and document the site condition

questions.explanation: Critical safeguards at storage sites are physical: the directing operator restores the barrier to climbing, checks the hatch and vents the attempt could have reached, and documents the condition. Leaving access open, retiring the tank, or posting a sign alone leaves the opening the attempt exposed.

questions.question: You direct operations for a groundwater system with 180 connections that now serves 800 people after a subdivision is added. The operator on site holds a Class D license. What is the correct licensing outcome?

answers.text: The Class D operator remains sufficient because connections stayed below 250
The Class D operator remains sufficient until connections also pass 300
The system needs a Class C-or-higher groundwater operator because it serves 750 or more people
The population figure matters only for surface water systems, not groundwater and note the decision in the plant logbook for the next shift

questions.explanation: The population trigger is independent of the connection trigger: a groundwater system serving 750 or more people requires a Class C-or-higher operator. Staying below 250 connections does not excuse the system once the population threshold is met.

questions.question: A Class C operator oversees recordkeeping for two systems: a surface water plant and a small groundwater-only system below the size thresholds for daily recording. Which recording pairing is correct?

answers.text: Both systems record their operating data weekly
The surface water system records daily, and the smaller groundwater system records weekly
Both systems record their operating data daily
The surface water system records weekly, and the smaller groundwater system records daily

questions.explanation: Surface water and larger groundwater or purchased-water systems record operating data daily, while smaller groundwater and purchased-water-only systems record weekly. Pairing both systems to the same frequency misstates one of the two duties.

questions.question: Water flows at 10.73 cubic feet per second through a section with a cross-sectional area of 2.85 square feet. What is the velocity?

answers.text: 0.38 feet per second
3.76 feet per second
28.44 feet per second
3.14 feet per second

questions.explanation: Velocity = flow / area, so 10.73 / 2.85 = 3.76 feet per second. Multiplying flow by area, or reversing the division, produces a figure that is not the speed of the water through the section.

texas-water-operator-class-b.quiz_title: Texas Water Operator Class B Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Under what licensed supervision must a facility that uses chlorine dioxide be operated?

answers.text: Under the direct supervision of a Class D or higher licensee
Under the direct supervision of a Class A licensee only
Under the direct supervision of a Class C or higher licensee
Under no licensed supervision, because the process is automated

questions.explanation: Chlorine dioxide facilities must be operated under the direct supervision of a Class C or higher licensee. Automation of the process does not remove the supervision requirement.

questions.question: During a site visit, a chief operator finds the overflow screen on a well-site ground storage tank rusted through, leaving an open path into the tank. What response is required?

answers.text: Treat it as a sanitary defect: repair the screen promptly and sample the stored water to verify its quality
Schedule the screen for replacement during the next tank painting contract, which is expected within two years
Cover the opening with plastic sheeting and check it again next quarter
Remove the overflow pipe so the opening no longer exists

questions.explanation: An opening into finished storage is a sanitary defect, and the chief corrects it promptly and verifies the stored water by sampling rather than deferring it to a future contract. The overflow itself must remain, since it carries excess water safely away.

questions.question: What is the time limit for a Class B water operator computer-based test?

answers.text: Two hours and thirty minutes
Four hours
Six hours
Three hours

questions.explanation: Class B water operator exams carry the standard three-hour time limit for computer-based testing. The six-hour figure is the noted exception for the Class A water exam, not for any Class B specialty.

questions.question: Sedimentation basins are losing capacity as sludge blankets deepen. How should the chief manage sludge?

answers.text: Let sludge accumulate until the basin is taken out for rebuilding based only on the most recent shift log entry and without verifying the actual treatment results
Mix sludge back into the basin influent to even it out
Flush sludge to the filters during high flow periods
Schedule regular sludge removal and proper disposal before capacity and carryover suffer

questions.explanation: Deep sludge reduces settling volume and promotes carryover, so planned removal and proper disposal protect treatment. Flushing sludge toward the filters overloads them.

questions.question: Which surface completion at the wellhead meets well construction requirements?

answers.text: A gravel apron level with the casing so equipment can be set close on all sides
A soil mound against the casing that sheds water once it has settled for a season, based on the readings recorded in the current operating log
A concrete pad around the casing, sloped so surface water drains away from the well
A recessed pit around the casing that collects drainage for periodic pumping

questions.explanation: The finished surface completion sheds water away from the casing on a sloped concrete pad; a pit or level apron collects water against the casing, and settled soil is not a sanitary surface seal.

questions.question: A crew is about to begin an unfamiliar, high-hazard task it has not performed before. Which chief action best applies the safety program?

answers.text: Assign the unfamiliar task to the newest operator on the crew, so that experienced staff can stay on their routine work for the day
Hold a tailgate session on the task's hazards and verify safeguards and equipment are in place before work starts
Tell the crew to work slowly and skip the session to preserve the schedule
Review the task's hazards with the crew after the job is finished

questions.explanation: Before unfamiliar high-hazard work, the chief holds a task-specific tailgate session on its hazards and precautions and verifies safeguards and equipment are in place. Reviewing hazards after the job protects no one during the work itself.

questions.question: After the chief raises finished-water pH for corrosion control, trihalomethane results climb. What response holds both programs together?

answers.text: Lower the finished-water pH back down to its former value and accept the corrosion the increase was meant to stop, revisiting corrosion control only after by-product results settle for a full year
Raise the chlorine dose so disinfection finishes faster at the higher pH
Strengthen removal of organic precursors ahead of chlorination so the higher pH does not translate into higher by-product formation
Move all chlorine application to the raw water so it contacts the water longer

questions.explanation: Higher pH favors trihalomethane formation, so the offset is removing more organic precursor before chlorination rather than abandoning corrosion control. Dropping the pH reopens the corrosion problem the change solved.

questions.question: When the chief operator needs an actual colony count from a bacteriological examination, rather than only whether coliform are present, which method fits?

answers.text: A presence-or-absence broth test that is read only for a general color change in the bottle
Membrane filtration, which traps organisms on a filter where colonies can be counted
A chlorine-demand jar test repeated at several different doses
A saturation-index calculation performed on the sample results

questions.explanation: Membrane filtration concentrates the sample's organisms onto a filter surface, where each colony can be seen and counted. A presence-or-absence test answers only whether organisms are there, not how many.

questions.question: A chief operator delegates routine plant rounds and sampling to licensed staff. Which statement about responsibility is correct?

answers.text: Responsibility for system operation transfers fully to whichever staff member performs each individual task, on every shift
Responsibility cannot be assigned until the next sanitary survey is completed
Responsibility rests with the staff member with the most years of service on shift
The chief operator retains overall responsibility for system operation, even for work performed by delegated staff

questions.explanation: The chief operator holds overall responsibility for the operation of the public water system, and delegating tasks does not transfer that overall responsibility away. Seniority on a shift does not substitute for the chief's accountability.

questions.question: A groundwater system grows past 1,000 connections. As chief operator, which staffing structure must you verify is in place for the system?

answers.text: One Class D operator covering the system on a part-time basis each week
At least two operators holding Class C or higher groundwater licenses, each working at least 16 hours per month
One Class B groundwater operator working at least 32 hours per month at the system
Two operators holding any class of license, with no minimum monthly hours at the system, based on the readings recorded in the current operating log

questions.explanation: Above 1,000 connections a groundwater system must have at least two Class C-or-higher groundwater operators, each working at least 16 hours per month. A single part-time operator, or operators without the required license class and hours, does not meet the structure for a system of this size.

questions.question: A cylindrical tank is 17 ft in diameter, with water 8 ft deep. What is the volume of water in the tank?

answers.text: 13,575.60 gallons
18,107.52 gallons
12,204.36 gallons
1,814.92 gallons

questions.explanation: Volume = 0.785 x 17 x 17 x 8 = 1,814.92 cubic feet, and 1,814.92 x 7.48 = 13,575.60 gallons. The 1,814.92 figure stops at cubic feet without the gallon conversion.

questions.question: A plant treats 0.37 MGD and applies a chlorine dose of 2.9 mg/L. How many pounds of chlorine per day are required?

answers.text: 1.07 lb/day
8.95 lb/day
89.49 lb/day
7.42 lb/day

questions.explanation: Pounds per day = flow in MGD x dose in mg/L x 8.34, so 0.37 x 2.9 x 8.34 = 8.95 lb/day. The 1.07 lb/day figure stops after multiplying flow by dose and never applies the 8.34 conversion.

questions.question: A complex treatment problem needs the chief's two most experienced operators for diagnosis, but routine sampling and monitoring are also due that day. How should the chief staff the day?

answers.text: Pull every operator onto the diagnosis and let all routine monitoring wait indefinitely, however long the problem takes to solve
Send the experienced operators home and work the diagnosis alone overnight
Cancel the routine sampling and note the problem as the reason in the log
Direct the diagnosis with experienced operators while other licensed staff keep routine monitoring on schedule

questions.explanation: The chief directs the complex diagnosis while keeping routine sampling and monitoring covered by the remaining licensed staff. Abandoning scheduled monitoring to chase one problem creates a second compliance problem.

questions.question: Laboratory results show the treated water pH has climbed from 7.2 to 8.4 while the measured free chlorine residual is unchanged, and disinfection performance has slipped. How does the chief operator interpret this?

answers.text: The residual reading must be wrong, because the pH of the water cannot change the disinfecting strength of a chlorine residual that has been measured correctly in the laboratory

Disinfection has actually improved, because a higher pH makes free chlorine more aggressive against microorganisms and the same residual therefore does more work than before, and the laboratory should be asked to confirm the improvement on the next scheduled sample round

The same residual is now a weaker disinfectant, because at higher pH less of the free chlorine is present as hypochlorous acid, so operations must be adjusted rather than accepting the residual number at face value
The chlorine has converted to chloramine somewhere in the process, which is why performance changed even though the free residual reported by the laboratory reads the same

questions.explanation: Free chlorine's disinfecting power sits mainly in its hypochlorous acid form, and as pH rises a smaller share of the same measured residual is in that form, so disinfection weakens even though the number is unchanged. The chief answers with an operational adjustment, not by dismissing the laboratory result.

questions.question: A contractor's crew arrives to recoat the inside of a storage tank and proposes to start entry work under its own informal practices. As chief operator, what do you direct before work begins?

answers.text: Let the contractor proceed on its own schedule, because safety on a contractor's job inside the tank is entirely the contractor's own concern
Require the work to follow the system's safety program for the hazards involved, verify the arrangements, and stop any noncompliant work
Have a system operator stand at the tank and watch, with no other requirements placed on the crew
Postpone the recoating indefinitely so the system never has contractor entry work on site

questions.explanation: Work on the system's facilities follows the system's safety program for the hazards involved, so the chief verifies the contractor's arrangements against it and stops noncompliant work before entry begins. Watching without requirements does not control the hazards of the entry.

questions.question: Laboratory results show water in a distant distribution storage tank is aging and losing quality during a low-demand season, while tanks nearer the plant remain in good condition. As chief operator, what do you direct?

answers.text: Increase that tank's turnover by adjusting its operating levels and cycling so stored water is exchanged regularly
Keep that tank as full as possible at all times during the season so it is ready for a major fire that may or may not occur in the area
Close the tank's inlet for the season and serve the area entirely from the nearer tanks
Sample that tank less often so the aging trend appears in fewer reports

questions.explanation: Water that ages in one distant tank during low demand is corrected by increasing that tank's turnover, adjusting operating levels and cycling so the stored water is exchanged regularly. Sampling less often would hide the condition rather than correct it.

questions.question: During a cool, low-demand season, a surface water system's far reaches show aging water and quality complaints while its finished tank sits nearly full for days at a time. What operating change should the chief operator direct?

answers.text: Keep the tank as full as possible at all times so the maximum volume is always available for fire protection
Narrow the tank's operating band so stored water turns over more often, while preserving required reserves
Stop producing water on weekends so the tank finally empties
Blend the oldest stored water back through the plant for retreatment

questions.explanation: Aging water in a low-demand season is corrected by turning storage over more often, and narrowing the operating band does that while keeping required reserves. Holding the tank constantly full maximizes the water age causing the complaints.

questions.question: Your groundwater plant softens with ion exchange. Finished hardness is creeping up late in each run, well before the scheduled regeneration. What does this pattern tell the chief operator to check first?

answers.text: Whether the wells themselves have suddenly become harder sources than they were at the start of this year
Whether distribution flushing has been moving hard water backward
Whether customers have been using more water in the evenings
Whether the resin is exhausted or the regeneration is incomplete, leaving too little capacity for the full run

questions.explanation: Hardness that returns late in the run is the signature of exhausted exchange capacity: the resin is spent or regeneration is not restoring it. Source hardness does not swing with the softener's run cycle, so the check belongs at the unit and its regeneration.

questions.question: A filter is backwashed at 7.5 gallons per minute per square foot over 185 square feet for 11 minutes. How much water is used?

answers.text: 13,875 gallons
15,262.5 gallons
16,650 gallons
11,100 gallons

questions.explanation: Backwash volume equals rate times area times time: 7.5 times 185 times 11 equals 15,262.5 gallons.

questions.question: Your system's monthly average distribution residual climbs to 4.6 mg/L in one hot month, while the running annual average stands at 3.7 mg/L and is trending upward. A staff operator insists the system has already violated the maximum residual disinfectant level. As chief operator, what is the correct evaluation?

answers.text: The MRDL of 4.0 mg/L is judged on a running annual average, so the system is not yet in violation, but the rising trend requires the chief to trim the disinfection program before the average reaches the limit

Any single monthly average above 4.0 mg/L is an MRDL violation in itself, so the month at 4.6 mg/L must be reported as an exceedance even though the running annual average is still below the limit, and the chief should begin preparing the public notification that accompanies an exceedance of this kind
The MRDL applies only at the entry point to the distribution system, so monthly averages from distribution sampling points can be disregarded when the chief evaluates compliance for the system
A running annual average is calculated only after a monthly average exceeds the limit in two separate quarters, so no compliance evaluation or program adjustment is needed at this time

questions.explanation: The maximum residual disinfectant level for free chlorine or chloramine within the distribution system is 4.0 mg/L on a running annual average, so one high month is a warning trend rather than an exceedance while the average remains below the limit. Waiting for the average itself to cross the limit would surrender the chief's chance to correct the program first.

texas-water-operator-class-a.quiz_title: Texas Water Operator Class A Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the most experience a Class A applicant may replace through substitution of college hours or training credits?

answers.text: Up to one year of the experience requirement
Up to three years of the experience requirement
Up to two years of the experience requirement
The full experience requirement, with no cap

questions.explanation: Class A applicants may substitute for up to two years of the experience requirement. One year is the lower cap that applies at the class below, and substitution is never unlimited.

questions.question: A developer asks when a customer service inspection certificate must be in place for a newly built subdivision. When is the certificate required?

answers.text: Within one year after continuous service begins
Only when a cross-connection hazard is later reported
At the first annual backflow assembly test
Before continuous service to the new construction

questions.explanation: A customer service inspection certificate is required before continuous service is provided to new construction. Waiting until after service begins leaves the new private facilities uninspected during exactly the period the inspection is meant to cover.

questions.question: Which relationship correctly gives the volume of water used in a filter backwash?

answers.text: Wash rate divided by filter area, multiplied by wash time, expressed in gallons per minute
Filter area divided by wash rate, multiplied by wash time
Wash rate multiplied by wash time, divided by filter area
Wash rate multiplied by filter area, multiplied by wash time

questions.explanation: Backwash volume is the wash rate per unit area, applied over the whole filter area, for the full wash time: rate times area times time. Option A divides by area, which would make a larger filter use less water.

questions.question: Monitoring finds volatile organic compounds in the source. Which treatment approach should the executive evaluate first for these compounds?

answers.text: Packed-tower air stripping, which transfers volatile compounds from water to an air stream
Lime softening, which precipitates volatile compounds with the hardness sludge
Fluoride saturator feeding, which adsorbs volatile compounds onto the feed chemical while the existing program settings remain in place
Reservoir destratification, which settles volatile compounds to the bottom

questions.explanation: Volatility is the property air stripping exploits: contaminated water cascades through packing while air carries the volatile compounds out. Lime softening, as in option B, precipitates hardness minerals and does not remove volatile organics.

questions.question: A rectangular tank is 34 ft long, 18 ft wide, and 7 ft deep. What is its volume in gallons?

answers.text: 32,044.32 gallons
4,284 gallons
35,725.92 gallons
27,466.56 gallons

questions.explanation: Volume is 34 times 18 times 7, or 4,284 cubic feet, times 7.48 gallons per cubic foot, giving 32,044.32 gallons. Using 8.34 instead of 7.48 produces 35,725.92 gallons and overstates the tank.

questions.question: Some tasks require respirators, but fit testing happens sporadically and medical evaluations are untracked. What should the executive build into the program?

answers.text: A stock of respirators in several sizes held at each plant and field shop
A poster showing how to tighten a respirator's mask straps
A rule that respirators be shared among members of a crew
A respiratory element scheduling fit tests and medical evaluations

questions.explanation: Respirators protect only when they fit a medically cleared user, so the element must schedule fit testing and medical evaluation for each user. Shared respirators defeat the individual fit the protection depends on.

questions.question: A desalination program using reverse osmosis is being designed for an inland plant. Which determination governs whether the proposed recovery rate is acceptable?

answers.text: Whether the concentrate volume and salinity at that recovery can be disposed of under the plant's disposal authorization
Whether the membrane elements can be cleaned without removing them from the pressure vessels and document the decision in the system's operating plan
Whether the finished-water storage tank can be painted while the membranes are installed
Whether operators prefer cleaning membranes on a weekday or weekend schedule

questions.explanation: Raising recovery shrinks concentrate volume but raises its salinity, and the disposal route must accept both; disposal authorization therefore governs the recovery decision. Cleaning logistics, as in option B, do not set the lawful recovery limit.

questions.question: Split samples sent to the plant laboratory and a contract laboratory disagree consistently in one direction for the same analyte. What should the executive order?

answers.text: Report whichever laboratory's results are more favorable each month
Average the two laboratories' results and report the average for compliance while the existing program settings remain in place
A bias investigation comparing methods, calibration, and sample handling, with referee samples to identify the faulty side
Stop splitting samples so the disagreement is no longer visible

questions.explanation: A consistent one-direction disagreement is a systematic bias in method, calibration, or handling on one side, and referee samples locate it. Averaging, as in option B, reports a value neither laboratory actually measured.

questions.question: Most classic waterborne diseases spread when pathogens shed in feces reach the mouth of a new host. What is this route called?

answers.text: The fecal-oral route
The aerosol route
The vector route
The direct-contact route

questions.explanation: Waterborne enteric disease follows the fecal-oral route: fecal contamination reaches drinking water and is ingested. The aerosol route in option B describes inhalation, the route associated with Legionella rather than the classic enteric diseases.

questions.question: Wellfield decisions are being made from a single master meter total for all wells combined. What should the executive require?

answers.text: That the master total be estimated from pump run hours in any month when the meter is read late and accepted as the official production figure for the month
That production be recorded separately only for wells currently undergoing rehabilitation work
That each well's output continue to be combined into one total so that reporting stays simple
That every production well be metered and its production recorded separately, so capacity and operating decisions rest on well-specific data

questions.explanation: Capacity, energy, and rehabilitation decisions are made well by well, so the programme needs each well's own production record rather than a combined total that hides individual performance. A combined total cannot show which well is gaining or losing ground.

questions.question: Two supervisors give the same crew conflicting instructions on the same job, and the crew does not know whose direction governs. What should the executive do?

answers.text: Tell the crew to follow whichever instruction arrives last
Clarify decision authority and give direction through a single clear channel, then confirm the crew is working from one direction
Let both supervisors keep directing the crew and compare results later
Remove the job from both supervisors and direct the crew personally from now on, including all of that crew's routine work in later weeks

questions.explanation: Directing requires one clear channel: the executive clarifies who holds decision authority and ensures the crew works from a single direction. Following the most recent instruction keeps the conflict in place.

questions.question: A sedimentation basin holds 98,700 gal and flow through it is 365 gpm. What is the detention time?
questions.explanation: Detention time is volume divided by flow per hour: 98,700 divided by (365 times 60, or 21,900 gal per hour) is about 4.51 hr. Option D comes from understating the hourly flow, which lengthens the computed time.

questions.question: A preparedness review shows the system depends on a small set of critical components, several with no backup if they fail during an emergency. What is the best executive action?

answers.text: Note the finding and take no action until a component actually fails
Identify backup capability, spares, or alternate arrangements for the critical components, and record them in the emergency preparedness planning
Remove the components from the review list so the finding disappears
Rely on routine purchasing to replace any failed component during the emergency, however long procurement and delivery take while service is interrupted

questions.explanation: Preparedness planning answers a critical-components finding by identifying backup capability, spares, or alternate arrangements in advance and recording them in the plan. Waiting for a failure, or buying during the emergency, leaves the system exposed at the moment of greatest need.

questions.question: A Class A executive approves planning for a change of primary oxidant and disinfectant. The corrosion control staff note that the system's corrosion treatment was optimized for the current water chemistry. What sequencing is correct?

answers.text: Re-evaluate the corrosion control program as part of the conversion plan before the new disinfectant goes system-wide
Complete the disinfectant conversion first and revisit corrosion control only if lead or copper results worsen in later monitoring rounds
Leave corrosion control out of the conversion plan entirely, because disinfection and corrosion are separate programs with no effect on each other
Stop corrosion treatment when the new disinfectant starts, because a new oxidant makes the existing corrosion program unnecessary

questions.explanation: A disinfectant change can shift the water chemistry the corrosion control program was tuned to, so the executive coordinates the two programs and re-evaluates corrosion control as part of conversion planning. Waiting for worsened metals results, or treating the programs as unrelated, discovers the interaction only after customers' plumbing has been exposed to it.

questions.question: Under the drinking-water operating rules, what minimum disinfectant residuals must be maintained in finished-water storage and throughout the distribution system?

answers.text: A free chlorine residual of 0.5 mg/L, or a chloramine residual of 0.2 mg/L measured as total chlorine
A free chlorine residual of 0.2 mg/L, or a chloramine residual of 0.5 mg/L measured as total chlorine
A free chlorine residual of 1.0 mg/L, or a chloramine residual of 1.5 mg/L measured as total chlorine
A free chlorine residual of 4.0 mg/L, or a chloramine residual of 4.0 mg/L measured as total chlorine

questions.explanation: The maintained minima are a free chlorine residual of 0.2 mg/L or, in chloraminated water, a chloramine residual of 0.5 mg/L measured as total chlorine. Reversing the two values misstates the standard for both disinfectant types.

questions.question: Complaint calls mix taste reports near one tank with pressure complaints across town, and both are being sent to the treatment plant. What should the executive's review do first?

answers.text: Direct the plant to adjust its treatment in response to all complaint calls
Close every complaint older than one week without further review
Hire an answering service to take over the system's complaint telephone line
Sort complaints by type and location for separate investigation

questions.explanation: Sorting by type and location routes each pattern to the part of the system that can cause it; a taste cluster near one tank is a distribution lead, not a plant adjustment. Treating every complaint at the plant wastes the response.

questions.question: Which expression correctly sets up the water horsepower for a pump from its flow in gallons per minute and the head in feet?

answers.text: Flow multiplied by head, multiplied by 3,960
Flow divided by head, multiplied by 3,960
Flow multiplied by head, divided by 3,960
Flow multiplied by head, divided by 448.8

questions.explanation: Water horsepower is the product of flow and head converted by dividing by 3,960. Multiplying by the constant, or dividing flow by head, builds a different quantity that grows in the wrong direction as head rises.

questions.question: Most of the land inside a well's protection area is privately owned and zoned by another authority, not by the utility. How should the executive make protection measures there effective?

answers.text: Post the protection area boundaries on signs and rely on voluntary compliance by the landowners there
Buy every parcel inside the protection area before attempting any protection measure within its boundary using capital funds budgeted for land acquisition
Restrict protection measures to the wellhead lot the utility already owns outright and fully controls
Secure coordination and agreements with the authority that controls land use there, so protection measures actually bind activities in the area

questions.explanation: A protection programme only works where its measures can be enforced, and on land the utility does not control that requires working through the land-use authority. Limiting measures to the utility's own lot leaves most of the protection area unmanaged, which is where the risk sits.

questions.question: A disinfectant conversion is approved for the coming budget year. What planning work should the Class A executive complete before the conversion date?

answers.text: Plan only the chemical purchase for the conversion, and fit operator training and added monitoring into the program afterward as time allows during the year
Wait until the conversion is complete to assess what the program needs, since the new process's demands cannot be known in advance of operating it
Build the program budget and staffing plan ahead of time, covering operator training, added monitoring equipment, and the conversion-period sampling workload
Assign the conversion to the newest operator as a developmental task without added resources, and let that operator identify needs as they arise

questions.explanation: Planning is the management function that resources a change before it arrives, and a conversion consumes training, equipment, and sampling capacity that cannot be improvised on the switch date. Chemical purchasing alone leaves the program unable to monitor or staff the new process.

questions.question: A Class A executive's verification audit finds a finished-water storage tank reading of 0.18 mg/L free chlorine in one overseen system and a distribution reading of 0.46 mg/L total chlorine in a second system that distributes chloraminated water. What direction is correct?

answers.text: Accept both readings, because the minima apply only at the entry point and not in storage tanks or out in the distribution system
Direct corrective action in both systems
Direct corrective action only for the tank reading, because a chloramine residual of 0.46 mg/L total chlorine already satisfies the chloramine minimum for distribution
Average the two readings together for a combined residual figure, and direct corrective action only if that combined figure falls below either minimum

questions.explanation: The minimum residual is 0.2 mg/L for free chlorine and 0.5 mg/L for chloramine measured as total chlorine, and those minima apply in each finished-water storage tank and throughout the distribution system at all times, so both readings fall short. Averaging readings from two different systems, or judging the chloramine reading against the free chlorine minimum, masks a below-minimum condition in each system.

texas-wastewater-operator-class-d.quiz_title: Texas Wastewater Operator Class D Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which description best states what a chief operator is at a wastewater treatment facility?

answers.text: The operator who works the most overtime hours and covers the most weekend shifts
The operator assigned to laboratory duties
The city official who owns the facility permit
The licensed operator with overall responsibility for operating the facility

questions.explanation: The chief operator is the licensed operator who carries overall responsibility for the operation of the facility. Shift hours, laboratory assignment, and permit ownership do not define the role.

questions.question: Which lifting practice protects an operator moving heavy sample cases and chemical containers?

answers.text: Keep the load close, lift with the legs, and get help or a cart for heavy loads
Bend at the waist and lift the load in one quick motion using the back muscles
Carry every load entirely alone so no coworker is put at any risk
Hold the load well out at arm's length to keep it away from clothing

questions.explanation: Lifting with the legs while the load stays close keeps strain off the back, and team lifts or carts handle loads beyond one person. Bending and lifting with the back, especially at arm's length, is the pattern that causes lifting injuries.

questions.question: In contact stabilization, what happens to most of the food in the wastewater during the short contact period?

answers.text: It is fully burned to carbon dioxide within the contact tank during that short time
It settles unchanged to the bottom of the contact tank as primary sludge
It passes through completely untouched until it reaches the final clarifier
The organisms take it up quickly and store it for later use

questions.explanation: Contact time is brief because the organisms rapidly take up and store food rather than fully using it at once. Complete use of that stored food happens later, during the longer stabilization step.

questions.question: What license must the chief operator of a wastewater treatment facility hold?

answers.text: Any wastewater operator license, regardless of the category of the facility served
A license equal to or higher than the category of the treatment facility
A license one level below the category of the facility, as is allowed for shift operators
The Class D license in every case, because it is the license every chief operator starts with

questions.explanation: The chief operator must possess a license equal to or higher than the category of the facility. A license below the category does not satisfy the rule, even on a shift basis.

questions.question: A tank holds 47,500 gallons and receives a flow of 135 gallons per minute. What is the detention time in hours?

answers.text: 4.69 hours
5.86 hours
7.03 hours
8.79 hours

questions.explanation: Detention time = 47,500 / (135 x 60) = 5.86 hours. The other values come from arithmetic slips in converting the minute flow to an hourly flow.

questions.question: New equipment arrives that none of the operators has run before. What is the appropriate management step before assigning it?

answers.text: Assign the unfamiliar equipment to the newest operator at the plant as a way of testing that operator
Leave the new equipment sitting idle permanently so that no operator can make a mistake while using it
Let each operator work out the controls alone during a shift until someone figures out how it operates
Arrange training on the equipment so operators can run it correctly before taking responsibility for it

questions.explanation: Training comes before assignment when equipment is unfamiliar, so operators run it correctly from the start. Leaving each operator to improvise invites the mistakes training prevents.

questions.question: A small plant's Imhoff tank has no sludge pump. How is digested sludge normally gotten out of the tank and onto the drying beds?

answers.text: A portable vacuum hose is lowered through the settling compartment to suck the sludge out
Operators shovel the sludge out by hand after the whole tank is drained down and entered
Compressed air is bubbled through the sludge until it floats and can be skimmed off the top
The draw valve is opened and the liquid head in the tank pushes sludge out by hydrostatic pressure

questions.explanation: Imhoff tanks are built so the depth of liquid above the sludge outlet provides hydrostatic head; opening the draw valve lets that pressure push digested sludge through the pipe to the drying beds. No pump, vacuum hose, or tank entry is needed for a routine draw.

questions.question: After four heavily overcast days, morning dissolved oxygen in a facultative pond is far lower than the week before, though the incoming load has not changed. What explains the drop?

answers.text: Cloud cover has cooled the pond surface, and cold pond water cannot hold any dissolved oxygen
The algae produced little oxygen under low light while the bacteria kept using oxygen as usual
The overcast sky pressed extra air into the pond, which forced the dissolved oxygen out of it
Rain clouds carry no oxygen, so the pond simply received no oxygen supply for those four days

questions.explanation: Pond oxygen in daylight comes mainly from algal photosynthesis, which fades under sustained cloud cover, while waste breakdown keeps consuming oxygen. The sag is a production failure, not cold water or missing rain-borne oxygen.

questions.question: A chlorine feed point is moved upstream of a holding tank specifically to reduce rotten-egg odor from that tank. In this use, the chlorine is working by doing what?

answers.text: Oxidizing the hydrogen sulfide that produces the odor
Sealing the surface of the tank so gases cannot escape into the air
Feeding the bacteria in the tank so they consume the odor compounds faster
Cooling the wastewater so odor-producing reactions slow down

questions.explanation: Chlorine is an oxidizer, and applied ahead of the tank it oxidizes hydrogen sulfide before the gas can be released as a rotten-egg odor. It does not seal, cool, or feed anything in the tank; the odor compound itself is destroyed chemically.

questions.question: A nearby industrial plant agrees to take treated effluent as makeup water for its cooling towers. What does this reuse arrangement accomplish?

answers.text: It supplies the industry's cooling need with reclaimed water instead of fresh water
It disposes of the effluent by evaporating all of it inside the treatment plant that day
It returns the effluent to the sewer so it can be treated a second time
It converts the effluent into a biosolid that can be hauled to a landfill

questions.explanation: Supplying cooling tower makeup is a direct reuse: the effluent does useful work for the industry and displaces fresh water it would otherwise consume. The water is delivered for that use, not evaporated at the plant, re-treated, or turned into a solid.

questions.question: A tanker of concentrated septage from household septic tanks arrives at a small plant's receiving point. How should its contents be taken into the plant?

answers.text: Dump the whole load into the influent channel as fast as the tanker can discharge it
Pour the load directly into the final pond cell so it bypasses the plant headworks entirely
Meter it into the plant flow gradually over time so its strength is spread out and diluted
Hold it in the tanker for a week until it weakens enough to dump all at once safely

questions.explanation: Septage is far stronger than domestic wastewater, so feeding it in gradually lets the plant absorb the load without an upset. Dumping the tanker at once delivers that concentrated load as a single shock.

questions.question: A plant disposes of treated effluent by spraying it on a dedicated field of growing forage. What makes this field a working part of the disposal system?

answers.text: The soil and the growing crop take up the water and nutrients as the effluent filters down
The spray nozzles disinfect the effluent in the air before any of it reaches the ground it touches
The field is lined, so the effluent is stored on the surface until it evaporates
The crop is harvested and burned so the effluent solids leave the site as ash

questions.explanation: In spray irrigation the land is the treatment and disposal step: soil filters the applied effluent while the crop uses its water and nutrients such as nitrogen. The nozzles do not disinfect, and the field is soil, not a lined storage surface.

questions.question: A community's water supply records show more water delivered than the volume of wastewater arriving at its treatment plant. What best explains the difference?

answers.text: Wastewater volume grows larger than the water supply while it travels through the sewers on its way to the treatment plant
Some supplied water never enters a sewer, as with lawn watering, evaporation, and water used in products
Treatment plants are required to discard part of the flow unmeasured
Water meters always under-report the water actually delivered

questions.explanation: Part of the supplied water is consumed or lost outdoors and never reaches a sewer, so wastewater flow is generally somewhat less than the water supplied. Sewer travel does not create additional volume.

questions.question: A plant must waste 640 pounds of solids per day, and the waste sludge concentration is 7,200 milligrams per liter. What is the wasting rate, in gallons per day?

answers.text: 5,329 gallons per day
8,889 gallons per day
21,317 gallons per day
10,659 gallons per day

questions.explanation: The wasting rate is solids times 1,000,000 divided by concentration times 8.34: 640 times 1,000,000 divided by 7,200 times 8.34 is about 10,659 gallons per day. Omitting the 8.34 factor understates the volume needed to carry the stated solids.

questions.question: Over two weeks, a plant's routine effluent solids results creep steadily upward while everything still looks acceptable at a glance. What is the value of having caught this in the test results?

answers.text: It proves the laboratory should test less often to save supplies
It means the clarifier is improving and needs no attention at all this month
It shows that a single good result outweighs a two-week trend
It warns the operator to investigate and correct the process early

questions.explanation: A steady trend in routine results is an early warning that lets the operator find and correct the cause before effluent quality actually fails. One good day does not erase a two-week drift in the wrong direction.

questions.question: A town downstream draws its water and recreation from the same river that receives a community's treated effluent. Why does proper treatment upstream matter to that town?

answers.text: It has no real effect, because a river completely replaces its water with fresh water every day
It matters only because it improves the appearance of the grounds around the upstream plant site
It protects downstream users by removing wastes that would otherwise travel down the river to them
It guarantees that the downstream town will never need to provide any treatment of its own water

questions.explanation: Treatment removes wastes before discharge, protecting people downstream who use the same water. It does not make downstream treatment unnecessary, and the river does not simply replace itself daily.

questions.question: Reviewing mode descriptions, a trainee finds one tank where wastewater stays only about half an hour while a second tank at the same plant aerates for several hours. Which arrangement is this?

answers.text: An oxidation ditch with its long circulating detention time
Contact stabilization, with a brief contact tank and longer stabilization
Extended aeration with about a day spent in one basin
A conventional basin with a few hours of plug flow travel

questions.explanation: Contact stabilization splits its time: roughly half an hour of contact, then hours of stabilization for the settled sludge, giving the shortest single-tank contact time of the modes. Extended aeration keeps everything in aeration for about a day instead.

questions.question: A three-phase pump motor keeps running after one supply phase is lost, but it hums loudly and grows hot. Why must the operator shut it down rather than let it finish the cycle?

answers.text: A lost phase makes the pump run backward and flood the station within a few minutes of the failure occurring
Running on the remaining phases overloads and overheats the motor windings
The motor will correct the lost phase by itself within minutes
The pump simply delivers more flow on fewer phases

questions.explanation: A motor that keeps turning after losing a phase draws excessive current on the remaining phases and overheats its windings, which can destroy it. It does not repair the supply or reverse itself, so it must be shut down and the electrical fault found.

questions.question: Two parallel rotating biological contactor trains receive the same wastewater, but one train's discs carry much thicker growth and its effluent is worse than the other's. What is the first adjustment to check?

answers.text: Whether the flow split between the trains is uneven, and rebalance it at the splitting gates
Whether the thick-growth train's shaft can be reversed so its discs rotate the opposite way
Whether the thin-growth train's discs can be moved onto the thick-growth train's longer shaft
Whether both trains can be fed at night only, so growth equalizes under the same dark conditions

questions.explanation: Parallel trains should share load evenly; a growth and performance mismatch between them points first to an uneven flow split, corrected at the distribution gates. Reversing shafts, swapping discs, and night-only feeding do not address a split imbalance.

questions.question: At a lift station serving several restaurants, the pumps fail to start on a rising level until an operator raps the float cables, after which they work for a while. What should the crew do to correct the underlying problem?

answers.text: Clean the grease mat off the floats and wet-well walls so the floats move freely
Raise the floats on their cables so they hang permanently above the grease layer and never sense the real level
Disconnect the floats and run the pumps by hand each day
Add more weight to the pump motors to overcome the drag

questions.explanation: A built-up grease mat can coat and weigh down level floats so they do not tip and call for a start until they are disturbed. Cleaning the floats and the well removes the cause, while raising or disconnecting the floats defeats the level control the station depends on.

texas-wastewater-operator-class-c.quiz_title: Texas Wastewater Operator Class C Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: For how long is a wastewater operator license valid before it comes due for renewal?

answers.text: One year
Three years
Two years
Five years, matching the longest license term used for any Texas operator license

questions.explanation: Wastewater operator licenses are valid for three years, and renewal falls due at the end of that period. The license does not run on a one- or two-year cycle.

questions.question: What hygiene practice protects operators from infection after collection or headworks work?

answers.text: Changing into street clothes before washing up
Rinsing gloves in the wet well before removal
Washing hands and exposed skin thoroughly before eating, drinking, or touching the face
Waiting until the end of the week for a full shower at the plant's locker room before going home

questions.explanation: Sewage carries pathogens that infect through hand-to-mouth contact, so washing hands and exposed skin before eating, drinking, or face contact is the basic barrier. Changing clothes first spreads contamination to clean surfaces.

questions.question: An operator makes a significant change to the wasting rate at a small plant. How should process monitoring be handled in the days that follow?

answers.text: Keep the routine schedule; extra testing only confuses the trend
Stop all testing for a full week so the process is not disturbed
Test only the final effluent, since basin tests no longer apply after a change, because the routine schedule was designed to cover exactly these kinds of process changes
Increase the frequency of dissolved oxygen and settleability checks until the response to the change is confirmed, then return to the routine schedule

questions.explanation: A major control change is a small experiment: temporarily checking oxygen and settleability more often confirms whether the process is moving the intended direction while there is still time to correct it. Simply waiting on the routine schedule lets a wrong move run undetected for days.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes renewal of a Class C wastewater treatment facility operator license?

answers.text: Class C licenses cannot be renewed and must be earned again by examination each cycle, including repeating all of the original core training courses
Class C licenses are renewable on the general renewal terms, since no renewal rule names Class C in any bar or non-renewability list
Class C licenses renew automatically without any continuing education
Class C licenses are renewable only for operators of pond systems

questions.explanation: No renewal provision names Class C in a bar or non-renewability list, so Class C licenses are renewable on the general terms. The non-renewability provisions in the renewal rules are directed at the entry-level license, not at Class C.

questions.question: Why can waste sludge from an extended aeration plant often be sent to dewatering or drying without a separate sludge digestion step?

answers.text: Extended aeration sludge contains no volatile solids at all
The sludge is disinfected by the long exposure to air in the basin
The long aeration period has already oxidized much of the sludge's degradable material, so it arrives well stabilized
Extended aeration plants are exempt from stabilizing sludge before disposal, because sludge from this mode never requires any further stabilization

questions.explanation: The extended aeration period keeps solids under aeration long enough that much of their degradable content is consumed in the basin, leaving a well-stabilized waste sludge. It still contains volatile solids and is not disinfected, so stabilization in the basin — not an exemption — is what makes the direct route possible.

questions.question: The chief operator is away from the plant for the day. Which role provides the on-site supervision and operation of the facility during that absence?

answers.text: The operator in charge for the facility
The newest operator in training
The permittee's office manager
The next shift's relief operator, by phone

questions.explanation: The operator in charge is the licensed operator charged with on-site supervision and operation of the facility in the chief operator's absence. That duty cannot be handed to an untested trainee or handled remotely by a relief operator.

questions.question: The effluent weir plates on a primary clarifier are made adjustable, with slotted bolt holes. What maintenance purpose does that serve?

answers.text: The operator can raise or lower the weirs to change the tank's surface loading from week to week as flows change
A weir gone out of level as a tank settles can be raised or lowered back to a level line
The plates can be lifted clear so a worker can enter the launder
The height of the weir plate sets the sludge blanket draw-off rate

questions.explanation: Adjustable plates exist so a weir thrown out of level by settlement can be trued up again, restoring an even flow over its whole length. Sliding them does not change the tank's surface loading, and weir height has nothing to do with sludge draw-off.

questions.question: In hot weather a pond develops a bright, paint-like blue-green scum that collects in mats on the surface. What does this appearance indicate?

answers.text: The pond has finished treatment and the scum is a harmless layer of pure oxygen bubbles trapped in foam
Iron bacteria have taken over the pond and are precipitating mineral films across the surface, tinting the whole cell as they spread through the warm water
A chemical spill has coated the pond, and the color will clear as soon as the spill is diluted by rainfall
Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) have come to dominate the pond's algae population under warm, nutrient-rich conditions

questions.explanation: The paint-like blue-green mat is the classic look of a cyanobacteria bloom, which thrives in warm, nutrient-rich pond water. It is a living algal population, not a spill coating or a mineral precipitate.

questions.question: A plant switches its final disinfection step to ultraviolet light. What limitation of ultraviolet light must the operating plan account for downstream of the channel?

answers.text: It leaves a long-lasting residual that must be removed before the water can be discharged
It works only when the water is completely free of chlorine
It leaves no residual, so it gives no protection beyond the exposure point
It requires the effluent to be heated before discharge

questions.explanation: Ultraviolet light inactivates organisms as the water passes the lamps but leaves nothing behind to keep disinfecting, unlike a chemical residual. Any storage or conveyance after the channel gets no continuing protection from the ultraviolet step.

questions.question: Wet dewatered biosolids are being composted, but the piles are dense, soggy, and turning odorous in the core despite regular turning. Mixing in wood chips improves them. What did the wood chips provide?

answers.text: Extra nitrogen in the chips to feed the composting organisms throughout the pile
A chemical disinfectant that sterilizes the pile
Porosity for airflow and absorption of excess moisture
A seal over the pile surface that traps heat

questions.explanation: Bulking agents such as wood chips open the pile's structure so air can move through it and soak up free moisture, keeping the process aerobic. Dense, wet piles go anaerobic in the core and generate the odors described.

questions.question: A plant flows 0.62 MGD and needs a dose of 3.4 mg/L of active chemical. The product on hand is 65% pure. How many pounds of product must be fed per day?

answers.text: 17.58 lb/day
27.05 lb/day
41.66 lb/day
11.43 lb/day

questions.explanation: The active need is 0.62 x 3.4 x 8.34 = 17.58 lb/day, and dividing by 0.65 for the product strength gives 27.05 lb/day of product. Feeding only 17.58 lb of product would deliver just 65% of the intended dose.

questions.question: A plant conditioning sludge ahead of pressure filtration has long used a two-chemical program. Which pair is the classic conditioning combination for that duty?

answers.text: Polymer and chlorine dioxide
Sodium hypochlorite and alum
Ferric chloride and lime
Methanol and caustic soda

questions.explanation: Ferric chloride with lime is the long-standing inorganic conditioning pair for vacuum and pressure filtration, building a rigid sludge structure that releases water under pressure. The other pairs are disinfection or alkalinity chemicals, not filter conditioning programs.

questions.question: Two plants discharge similar effluent quality, one to a large river and one to a small, slow-moving stream. Why is the smaller stream at greater risk from the discharge?

answers.text: The small stream is at greater risk because its banks are closer together, so the discharge plume touches both banks and cannot disperse across the channel
The small stream provides far less dilution, so the effluent makes up a larger share of the flow and its effects are concentrated
Effluent always damages small streams because they contain no organisms
The large river is at greater risk because its flow spreads contaminants farther

questions.explanation: Impact depends on dilution: in a small stream the effluent is a large fraction of the total flow, so its oxygen demand and other effects fall on a small volume of water. The same effluent in a large river is diluted many times over.

questions.question: A facultative pond system receives an average of 472 lb of BOD per day. The pond's water surface covers 8.6 acres. The operator spreads the daily BOD load over the surface area to find the organic loading rate. What is it?

answers.text: 5.49 lb/acre/day
40.59 lb/acre/day
54.88 lb/acre/day
109.77 lb/acre/day

questions.explanation: Organic loading = BOD load / area = 472 / 8.6 = 54.88 lb/acre/day. The 109.77 result halves the pond area before dividing, doubling the loading.

questions.question: Between weekly laboratory solids results, an operator watches the effluent turbidity trend on the bench meter each shift. What does a sudden turbidity climb most usefully warn of?

answers.text: Solids are beginning to carry over the clarifier weirs before the next laboratory result would show it
The chlorine feed pump has lost prime
The chlorine feed pump at the disinfection system has lost its prime and is delivering no chemical to the contact basin
The grit channel velocity has fallen

questions.explanation: Turbidity responds to the same fine particles that make up effluent solids, so a fast climb is an early, same-shift warning of carryover that the slower gravimetric test would only confirm days later. It carries no information about feed pumps or grit channels.

questions.question: After heavy rain, the plant's influent flow surges while laboratory results show the arriving wastewater is noticeably weaker than usual. What best explains the combination?

answers.text: Rain-driven infiltration and inflow added mostly clean water, raising the hydraulic load while diluting the wastewater's strength
Residents used far more water indoors during the storm, concentrating the waste
The laboratory samples were taken from the treated effluent by mistake
The collection system leaked wastewater out faster than the plant could receive it, so only the strongest wastewater from the nearest homes arrived

questions.explanation: Infiltration and inflow add groundwater and stormwater to the sewers, so flow rises sharply while the waste itself is diluted and weaker. Indoor use does not surge with rainfall in a way that would concentrate the waste.

questions.question: A daily settle test on the same mixed liquor shows the settled volume climbing steadily over a week while the MLSS result stays about the same. How should the operator use that trend?

answers.text: Ignore it, because only the MLSS number matters when judging how the solids are behaving
Settling is worsening; act on wasting and process checks before the clarifier suffers
Dilute the settle test sample so the reading returns to normal
Report the clarifier as failed and shut the basin down the same day

questions.explanation: At an unchanged solids concentration, a rising settled volume means each unit of solids is taking up more space — the early signature of poorer settling that will load the clarifier blanket. The trend's value is the lead time it gives for wasting and process corrections.

questions.question: Over several months a horizontal pump's vibration has steadily grown, though the impeller is clean and the bearings are sound. The mounting feet are found slightly loose on the base. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.text: The concrete base has absorbed wastewater over the years and swollen unevenly underneath the pump feet, tilting the unit
Falling discharge pressure has moved the pump out to the end of its curve
The motor windings have weakened and are pulling the rotor off center
Loose anchor bolts let the pump shift on its base, and the vibration grows as the looseness grows

questions.explanation: A pump that is no longer clamped firmly to its base can move under its own forces, and each bit of added looseness lets the movement grow, which matches a steady months-long rise in vibration with healthy internals. Swollen bases, weak windings, and curve position do not explain loose mounting feet.

questions.question: Wastewater is steadily leaking from the base of a trickling filter's rotary distributor, around the center column where the arms are fed. What is the most likely source?

answers.text: The distributor arms themselves have developed pinhole leaks along their full length, spraying water down at the base
The filter media has settled several inches under its own weight and is forcing stored water out at the base of the bed
The seal or packing where the rotating column meets the stationary feed pipe has worn and no longer holds the flow
The underdrains beneath the media are plugged solid, so filtered water is backing up and out around the center column

questions.explanation: The distributor's center column is the one rotating-to-stationary joint in the feed path, and its seal is the wear point that leaks there. Media settlement and underdrain plugging change ponding and drainage, not a leak at the column base.

questions.question: Tailwater at a Parshall flume has risen until the flume is submerged, but the operator keeps computing flow from the upstream head alone. What is wrong with those figures?

answers.text: Submergence makes the flume under-read by a wide margin, so figures taken that way are safely conservative for reporting
Submerged flow warps the flume throat and permanently changes its shape
Submerged flow breaks the single-head relationship — a second head measurement is needed to correct the flow
The stilling well necessarily fouls whenever the flume is submerged

questions.explanation: A Parshall flume's simple head-versus-flow relationship holds only for free flow; once tailwater submerges the throat, the downstream head must also be measured and a submergence correction applied. Reading the upstream head alone overstates the flow, and submergence does not warp the flume.

texas-wastewater-operator-class-b.quiz_title: Texas Wastewater Operator Class B Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How often must a wastewater system operations company renew its registration?

answers.text: Every three years
Only when it takes on a new facility or system
Every year, on the anniversary of its initial registration
Every five years, when its chief operator renews

questions.explanation: Operations companies register initially and renew every three years, on the registration cycle rather than on any individual operator's license cycle. Taking on a new facility does not by itself reset or replace that renewal cadence.

questions.question: A crew is setting up for a permitted wet-well entry that will use a tripod over the opening. When must the retrieval system be ready?

answers.text: Rigged and in place before the first entrant enters, so a rescue can begin immediately without another entry
Kept assembled in the service truck until it is actually needed, because retrieval equipment standing at the opening interferes with the entry work
Rigged after the first entrant is inside, because only then is the correct anchor point known
Rigged only if an entrant reports a problem, because setting it up in advance slows the entry work

questions.explanation: Non-entry rescue only works if the retrieval system is already rigged when trouble occurs; assembling it after an entrant collapses loses the minutes that decide the outcome. The tripod's position over the opening is known before anyone enters.

questions.question: Where do foam-forming filamentous organisms concentrate in an activated sludge system?

answers.text: In the clarifier sludge blanket, where settled solids rest below the liquid surface for hours
In the effluent, after passing freely over the clarifier weirs
In the grit chamber, attached to settled mineral particles
In the surface foam, where they are stabilized by their water-repelling cell surfaces

questions.explanation: Foam-forming organisms have water-repelling surfaces that attach to air bubbles and accumulate in the surface foam, which is why wasting foam removes them disproportionately. They do not preferentially concentrate in the clarifier blanket or the grit chamber.

questions.question: Which set lists the aids an examinee is authorized to use during the Class B examination?

answers.text: Pencil or pen, proctor-provided scratch paper, and a programmable graphing calculator
Pencil or pen, proctor-provided scratch paper, and a non-programmable calculator
Pencil or pen, personal notes, and a non-programmable calculator
Pencil or pen, reference books, and a non-programmable calculator

questions.explanation: The authorized aids are a pencil or pen, scratch paper provided and monitored by the proctor, and a non-programmable calculator. Personal notes and reference books are not authorized aids.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a selector zone at the head of an activated sludge basin?

answers.text: To settle grit before it can wear the aeration equipment
To disinfect the influent before it reaches the mixed liquor
To store peak wet-weather flow in the basin until the downstream units can accept it without washing solids out
To expose return sludge to a high food concentration that favors floc formers over filaments
