questions.explanation: A selector gives floc-forming organisms first access to a high concentration of food, so they outcompete filamentous organisms that thrive when food is dilute throughout the basin. A selector does not settle grit, disinfect, or store peak flow.

questions.question: How should a senior operator best develop a shift operator in charge who has never led the response to a process upset?

answers.text: Keep the operator away from upset situations until a promotion requires leading one, to avoid mistakes during real events
Let the operator lead the next upset response entirely alone, with no senior operator present to advise or intervene if the response goes wrong
Assign the operator only routine rounds and readings for the foreseeable future, postponing any upset experience indefinitely
Delegate the lead role on an upset response while supervising and coaching through it

questions.explanation: Delegating the lead role under supervision builds the operator's judgment on a real event while the senior operator remains available to intervene. Withholding all upset experience leaves the operator unprepared for the first solo event.

questions.question: A new operator assumes the headworks grinder removes the solids it shreds, the way the bar screen removes its screenings. What is the correct understanding of the grinder's action?

answers.text: It removes the shredded solids through its discharge chute, which must be emptied and hauled away with the plant screenings
It dissolves organic solids on contact, so only grit and plastics remain in the flow after it
It removes exactly the same material as a screen, and the two units are interchangeable in duty
It cuts solids into small pieces that stay in the wastewater and pass on downstream; it removes no material from the flow

questions.explanation: A grinder's cutters only subdivide solids; everything it shreds stays in the flow and travels downstream, which is why it protects pumps without producing a removed-solids stream. It neither hauls material out like a screen nor dissolves what passes through it.

questions.question: As sustained cold weather arrives, a pond system's effluent quality slips even though loads are unchanged and oxygen stays adequate. A parallel cell stands empty after summer maintenance. What is the sound seasonal response?

answers.text: Rest the working cell and run the whole flow through the empty cell so it warms up first
Accept the slippage, because temperature has no effect on pond treatment rates at any load, so no change in operation is needed until the warm season returns on its own
Double the recirculation rate so the same water passes the algae twice as often each day
Put the standby cell into service alongside the working cell so total detention lengthens while bacterial rates are slowed by the cold

questions.explanation: Pond bacteria work more slowly in cold water, so the system compensates with more time: adding the standby cell lengthens detention at the same load. Recirculating faster does not add detention volume, and simply accepting the slippage ignores an available cell.

questions.question: A delivered load of sodium hypochlorite assays noticeably weaker than the strength the feed pump settings assumed, and the effluent residual has sagged since the delivery. What adjustment keeps the applied dose on target?

answers.text: Hold the feed settings unchanged, because strength differences average out over a full tank and the residual will return to normal on its own once this load has been in service for a week or two
Dilute the new load further so it matches the pump's original calibration curve
Reset the feed rate using the measured strength of the delivered chemical so the same mass of chlorine is applied
Sample the residual less often until the next delivery, so the sag does not trigger false alarms

questions.explanation: Dose is a mass of chlorine per volume of wastewater, so when the product carries less chlorine per gallon, more product must be fed to deliver the same mass. Feeding by the label strength after an assay shows otherwise guarantees an underdose.

questions.question: Solids in a gravity thickener keep rising to the surface trailing fine bubbles even though the blanket is being kept shallow, and the feed is well-nitrified return sludge. What is carrying the solids up?

answers.text: Grease worked into the sludge at the head of the plant, lightening every particle it coats
Air entrained by the thickener's rotating rake as it stirs the blanket on each pass
Oxygen released by algae growing on the thickener's sunlit surface during the day
Denitrification in the blanket, whose nitrogen gas attaches to the solids and floats them

questions.explanation: Nitrified sludge held in an oxygen-free blanket denitrifies, and the nitrogen gas bubbles that form buoy the solids to the surface regardless of blanket depth. The remedy targets detention and nitrate in the blanket, not grease removal at the headworks.

questions.question: During an upset the operator reconstructs the chlorine balance in steps: the feed was raised to a dosage of 9.47 mg/L, the outlet residual held at 2.13 mg/L, and the difference between the chlorine applied and the chlorine remaining is the demand the upset imposed. What was the demand, in mg/L?
questions.explanation: Demand = 9.47 - 2.13 = 7.34 mg/L. The upset consumed most of a much larger dose, which is why the feed had to be raised so far to hold the 2.13 mg/L residual.

questions.question: A digester's volatile acids have risen sharply over three days after a period of heavy sludge pumping into it, gas quality is deteriorating, and pH has begun to edge down. What is the correct first response?

answers.text: Increase the feed rate with the strongest sludge available, so the acid formers are diluted by fresh material entering the tank
Raise the digester temperature quickly by several degrees, because hotter conditions force the methane formers to consume acids faster
Cut back or pause the feed and protect the digester's alkalinity, giving the methane formers time to consume the accumulated acids
Drain and reseed the digester at once, because a rising volatile acid level always means the existing biology is already lost

questions.explanation: An overload means acids are being made faster than the slower methane formers can use them; reducing the load and preserving buffer lets them catch up while the population is still viable. Adding feed or swinging temperature adds stress to the very organisms that must recover.

questions.question: A food-processing discharge with very high salt content reaches the plant and biological performance drops, with no toxic chemical identified. What is the likely mechanism?

answers.text: The high dissolved salt stresses the treatment organisms osmotically, inhibiting their activity
The salt raises the wastewater temperature beyond the range the treatment organisms can tolerate for very long
Salt discharges always improve settling and cannot inhibit treatment, so the cause must be something else entirely
The salt consumed the wastewater's dissolved oxygen directly, leaving too little for the treatment organisms

questions.explanation: A large dissolved-salt load changes the osmotic environment the treatment organisms live in and can inhibit their activity even when no conventional toxicant is present. The effect is on the organisms themselves, not a direct consumption of oxygen by the salt.

questions.question: Reviewing basin loading in steps: the applied load has been worked out at 2,014 pounds of biochemical oxygen demand per day. The solids inventory is the sum of two basins holding 2,150 pounds and 1,650 pounds of mixed liquor solids. The loading carried by each pound of solids is the ratio of the two totals. What is the food-to-microorganism ratio?
questions.explanation: Inventory is 2,150 + 1,650 = 3,800 pounds, so the ratio is 2,014 / 3,800 = 0.53. The 1.89 option inverts the ratio, dividing the solids by the food instead of the food by the solids.

questions.question: An operator needs to judge whether the morning load surge is overwhelming the aeration basin and must choose sampling to support an aeration change within the same shift. Which approach fits that decision?

answers.text: Collect a single composite and wait for the five-day demand result before changing anything
Rely on last week's permit samples, which describe the same influent stream
Grab samples with fast plant-run tests taken through the surge
Send samples to an outside laboratory and hold the process unchanged for a week

questions.explanation: Same-shift process decisions need data on the same timescale: grab samples with rapid measurements taken through the event show what the basin is experiencing while it can still be corrected. Composite and five-day analyses describe the event only after it has passed.

questions.question: At the start of a storm, the headworks sees a sudden surge of grit and debris heavier than the flow increase alone would explain. What accounts for it?

answers.text: Material deposited in the collection lines during dry weather is flushed out by the first storm flows
Rainwater generates grit as it falls through the air and runs across the ground on its way into the system
The preliminary treatment equipment manufactures debris whenever the flow through it rises suddenly at the headworks
Operators upstream are dumping grit they have stored at lift stations into the lines during the storm to clear their sumps

questions.explanation: Solids and grit settle in collection lines during low dry-weather flows and are scoured out when storm flows arrive, so the first flush delivers an accumulated load to preliminary treatment. The material was already in the system, waiting to be mobilized.

questions.question: A colorimetric nutrient test on a strongly colored effluent sample reads implausibly high, and a sample blank prepared without the color-forming reagent shows substantial absorbance of its own. What is the correct analytical response?

answers.text: Report the high reading, because color always means more nutrient
Account for the sample's own color with the blank so only the reagent-produced color is measured
Dilute the sample until its natural color disappears completely
Switch the sample over to a suspended solids test, where its natural color can simply be ignored entirely

questions.explanation: A sample blank reveals how much absorbance comes from the sample's own color rather than the analytical reaction, and correcting for it isolates the color the reagent actually produced. Diluting until the color vanishes also dilutes the analyte and still leaves the interference unmeasured.

questions.question: A lift station pump overheats and delivers almost nothing. Its discharge gate valve handle turns freely and the stem rises to the full-open position, yet a gauge just past the valve shows almost no pressure while the pump strains. What has most likely happened inside the valve?

answers.text: The valve packing has failed, letting the discharge escape around the stem and starve the line
The gate has separated from its stem, so the stem travels as if opening while the gate stays seated across the flow path
The valve was installed backward, so its gate lifts against the flow and seals tighter as it opens
The stem threads are stripped at the top, so the valve is actually open and the pump itself has failed

questions.explanation: A stem that rises and turns normally while the gate it left behind stays across the port explains full-open indications with almost no flow and a straining pump. A packing leak would show as external leakage and would not block the line.

questions.question: A two-stage trickling filter plant assigns nearly all of its carbonaceous removal to the first filter and expects ammonia conversion mainly in the second. What is the first stage's role called and why does the arrangement work?

answers.text: It is a contact filter; holding the flow first equalizes temperature so the second stage's film never experiences a change
It is a polishing filter; straining solids first raises the ammonia concentration the second stage needs to begin nitrifying
It is a humus filter; settling sloughed film first prevents the second stage from receiving any oxygen demand at all
It is a roughing filter; removing the carbon load first leaves the second stage's film free of fast-growing competitors so nitrifiers can establish

questions.explanation: A roughing first stage strips most of the carbonaceous load, and only with that competition removed can the slow-growing nitrifiers hold film space and oxygen in the second stage. The first stage does not raise ammonia or remove all oxygen demand; it changes who can grow downstream.

questions.question: A mechanical bar screen that raked reliably now blinds during wet-weather flows, and the upstream channel level surges before the rake finally starts by hand. The rake motor and chain test fine, but the stilling well for the differential-level sensor is packed with grit and rags. What is the corrective action?

answers.text: Shorten the timer interval so the rake runs constantly and ignore the level signal until the wet season ends whenever the upstream level begins to climb during a storm event of any size
Open the bypass gate a fixed amount during every storm so part of the flow never reaches the screen
Raise the rake start setpoint so the mechanism runs less often and wears more slowly through the storm
Clean the stilling well and verify the sensor reads the true level difference so rake starts again track actual screen blinding

questions.explanation: The rake responds to the level difference across the screen; with the sensing well fouled, the control never sees the blinding that is actually occurring, so restoring clean, accurate sensing restores automatic starts. Constant timer running masks the fault while wearing the mechanism and bypassing sends unscreened flow forward.

texas-wastewater-operator-class-a.quiz_title: Texas Wastewater Operator Class A Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: When does a Class A candidate who tests by computer learn the examination result?

answers.text: When the license itself is issued, about a week later
Immediately, at the testing center
Only after requesting the score in writing
By mail, after the results are reviewed centrally

questions.explanation: Computer-based testing provides the score immediately at the center. The candidate does not wait for mailed results or for the license to be issued to learn the outcome.

questions.question: A station tour finds a wet-well hatch propped open with no barrier while a lone operator works nearby on another task. What must the chief require?

answers.text: Guarding, a cover, or an attendant at the opening whenever it is open and not actively in use
A sign on the hatch warning visitors to watch their step while work is underway at the station
A rope laid on the floor around the opening to mark where the safe walking zone ends
Nothing further, because the operator on site is experienced and knows the hatch is open

questions.explanation: An open well is both a fall opening and a source of hazardous atmosphere, and familiarity is the classic setup for a fall. Physical guarding or a cover, not signage or memory, is what protects the next person through the room.

questions.question: What does a state point analysis tell the chief operator of a large activated sludge plant?

answers.text: The exact filament species responsible for a bulking episode, read from the shape of the flux curve
Whether the clarifier's operating point sits within its thickening capacity or has passed beyond it
The oxygen transfer efficiency of the aeration grid serving the basin ahead of the clarifier
The alkalinity that will remain in the effluent once nitrification there is fully complete

questions.explanation: State point analysis plots the clarifier's operating point against its limiting solids flux curve, showing whether the unit is underloaded, critically loaded, or overloaded in thickening. It is a clarifier solids-flux tool; it identifies neither filaments nor aeration efficiency.

questions.question: What coverage must a Category A facility have?

answers.text: Round-the-clock on-site staffing every day, with no telephone or pager provision in the rule
Operated at least five days a week by the chief or a required-level operator, available by telephone or pager seven days a week
Operation seven days a week by the chief personally, with no separate availability requirement on any other day of the week at all
Operation three days a week by any licensed operator, with telephone availability on operating days only

questions.explanation: The facility must be operated at least five days per week by the licensed chief operator or an operator at the required level or higher, who must be available by telephone or pager seven days per week. The chief need not personally work every operating day.

questions.question: An effluent BOD result returns implausibly low from a sample drawn downstream of chlorination, and the bench sheet shows the sample was neither neutralized nor seeded. What went wrong?

answers.text: The sample was simply too warm on arrival, and warmth always lowers a BOD result to nearly zero regardless of the waste's strength
The chlorine in the sample raised its oxygen level, which the test then reads as negative demand
Nothing went wrong with the test, because chlorine has no effect inside a sealed BOD bottle
Chlorine kept disinfecting inside the bottle, suppressing the test organisms, so the sample must be dechlorinated and seeded

questions.explanation: Residual chlorine carried into the bottle continues to act on the test organisms, so the measured demand reflects disinfection rather than the wastewater's content; neutralizing the chlorine at collection and seeding the sample restores a valid test. Warmth does not erase demand, and chlorine exerts no such oxygen effect.

questions.question: An investigation confirms an operator falsified entries in an operating log. What is the upper-management response?

answers.text: Quietly correct the log entries and say nothing about it, so the operator is not discouraged from reporting in future
Transfer the operator to the laboratory, where entries matter less
Address it through the documented disciplinary process, applied consistently and with the facts recorded
Dismiss every operator on that shift, whether involved or not

questions.explanation: Falsified records are a serious integrity matter handled through the documented disciplinary process, with the facts recorded and the process applied consistently. Quiet correction hides the problem, and punishing uninvolved staff is not a defensible process.

questions.question: A large plant in a dense neighborhood draws repeated odor complaints traced to its open headworks and primary tanks, even though the processes run well. What facility modification addresses the complaints at their source?

answers.text: Plant a row of tall trees along the fence line so the odors leaving the plant are hidden from the neighbors who complain
Pump sludge out of the primary tanks far more often so nothing rests in them long enough to turn septic and release odor at the surface
Enclose the headworks and primary surfaces and collect the captured air for treatment before it is released to the neighborhood
Add fragrance masking at the fence line so the air leaving the plant smells acceptable even though the odor sources stay open

questions.explanation: Covering the sources and treating the collected air removes the odor load itself; trees hide nothing from the nose, withdrawal changes do not stop surface emissions from open tanks, and masking perfumes a problem instead of capturing it.

questions.question: A soil-bottom pond cell loses water through a permeable native bottom, and the rehabilitation plan for its outage calls for rebuilding the bottom as a soil liner. What work does that rehabilitation consist of?

answers.text: Amend the bottom soil with fine clay material and compact it in controlled layers, building a low-permeability soil liner across the cell floor
Pave the cell floor with concrete panels, because a rigid slab is the only bottom treatment that can reduce water loss from a pond of this size
Spread the sludge already in the cell evenly over the floor, because a layer of pond sludge seals a permeable bottom by itself
Line the cell with the geotextile fabric used for road work, because any manufactured sheet placed on the floor stops the water loss

questions.explanation: A soil liner works by mixing clay-rich material into the bottom and compacting it so the pores that carried water are closed; it is a recognized repair where a soil liner fits the plan. Sludge layers wash and crack, road fabric is not a barrier, and concrete is not the only way to cut a bottom's permeability.

questions.question: At night a large plant's flow falls to a small fraction of its daytime peak, and the effluent chlorine residual repeatedly overshoots, overloading dechlorination, while daytime control is good. What facility-level change best corrects this?

answers.text: Add a smaller trim feed pump or staged feed capacity so chlorine feed can turn down at low flows
Raise the daytime dose so the night overshoot looks smaller by comparison
Take the residual analyzer offline at night so the overshoot stops being recorded
Hold night flow in the influent wet well and release it in one large morning surge through the contact basin

questions.explanation: A feed system that cannot turn down below the night requirement will overshoot whenever flow collapses; adding trim capacity matched to low flow fixes control at both ends of the range. Recording less or surging flow hides or worsens the problem.

questions.question: A large plant's dewatering results stay poor even as the polymer dose is raised, and the chief suspects the polymer itself is wrong for the sludge. Which evaluation should guide the change?

answers.text: Run the current polymer at double dose for a full week and judge the cake, and keep doubling the dose each week until the cake finally firms up
Test candidate polymers of different charge and molecular weight with bench drainage tests, and select by how the sludge actually releases water
Switch to whichever polymer the neighboring plant uses, at the same dose
Judge polymers by the clarity of the mixing-tank solution alone

questions.explanation: Bench drainage testing of polymers with different charge and weight characteristics shows which product fits this sludge's surface chemistry, which dose alone cannot fix. Doubling a mismatched polymer wastes chemical, another plant's sludge differs from this one, and solution clarity says nothing about drainage performance.

questions.question: A state point plot for one of a large plant's clarifiers puts the operating point above the limiting flux curve during the afternoon peak, and the blanket is rising toward the weirs. What is the chief's best move?

answers.text: Increase the return sludge rate sharply, since a higher underflow always relieves an overloaded state point
Raise the mixed liquor concentration further, so the floc becomes heavier and settles through the overload
Wait for the overnight low flow to arrive, since an overloaded state point corrects itself without action
Bring the standby clarifier into service and trim the solids loading on the overloaded unit

questions.explanation: An operating point above the limiting flux means the clarifier cannot pass the applied solids downward, so solids accumulate and the blanket climbs; adding area and cutting the unit's solids loading restores a workable point. Raising return rate or mixed liquor concentration adds to the flux the unit already cannot pass.

questions.question: A vendor offers a large plant a continuing program of cultured organisms, promising to dose its way out of recurring nitrification losses that follow cold snaps and load swings. How should the chief evaluate the offer?

answers.text: Reject outside sludge under all circumstances, including emergency reseeding after a genuine kill
Buy a double quantity of the culture, so half can be stored in the equalization basin as a reserve for the next cold snap
Accept it at once, because dosed cultures permanently replace a plant's own nitrifying population
Judge it against the governing facts: dosed organisms persist only if the plant's conditions suit them

questions.explanation: Any introduced organism survives only where temperature, solids age, and food suit it, which are the same conditions governing the plant's own nitrifiers; the recurring losses trace to those conditions, not to a shortage of purchased culture. Emergency reseeding after a genuine kill is a different, legitimate case.

questions.question: A chief must decide whether a system's wet-weather surges come mainly from rainfall entering through defects or from direct storm connections. What analysis separates the two?

answers.text: Measuring chlorine demand on wet and dry days, since stormwater raises demand more than groundwater does, and repeating the comparison each season so the pattern can be tracked across wet and dry years of record
Comparing flow response timing and size against rainfall records: rapid, storm-tracking rises point to direct inflow, while slower, season-long elevation points to groundwater infiltration
Counting the manholes in each sub-basin, because more structures always means more rainfall entry
Reviewing pump run times alone, which show the total extra flow but not its entry pathway

questions.explanation: Rainfall-dependent entry tracks storms closely and recedes quickly, while groundwater infiltration follows the water table and lingers. Matching the flow record against rainfall timing is how the chief apportions the problem before choosing rehabilitation or disconnection work.

questions.question: During an upset a large plant treats 13.5 MGD at a chlorine dose of 3.3 mg/L using a hypochlorite product that is 72 percent of full strength. The effluent turbidity is 3.1 units, the contact basin holds 0.9 million gallons, and two of three basins are in service. How many pounds of product per day must be fed?

answers.text: 267.51 pounds per day
371.55 pounds per day
5,160.38 pounds per day
516.04 pounds per day

questions.explanation: Product feed = 13.5 x 3.3 x 8.34 / 0.72 = 516.04 pounds per day. Turbidity, basin volume, and basins in service do not enter it; 371.55 ignores the purity correction and 267.51 multiplies by the purity instead of dividing.

questions.question: A large plant's effluent BOD results run unexpectedly high for a well-nitrified effluent, while its carbonaceous results from an outside laboratory come back much lower. What distortion should the chief operator suspect in the plant's own test?

answers.text: The effluent's remaining solids are consuming oxygen on the filter paper, and filtering the sample a second time would have removed the problem entirely
Nitrogenous oxygen demand is being exerted in the bottle by nitrifying organisms, inflating the result unless a nitrification inhibitor is used
The dilution water is too pure for any oxygen demand to register
The incubator is holding the bottles slightly below the set temperature

questions.explanation: A nitrified effluent carries nitrifying organisms that exert nitrogenous demand in the BOD bottle, so an uninhibited test reports carbonaceous plus nitrogenous demand and reads high. Solids are removed from the measured portion by the test setup, pure dilution water is the intent, and a small temperature offset would lower, not raise, the result.

questions.question: A large new industrial customer proposes discharging to the utility's system. What should the chief operator do before the utility accepts the discharge?

answers.text: Accept the discharge as soon as the customer agrees to pay its sewer charges in full, without evaluating the volume or character of the waste against the plant's capacity or its permit
Refuse the discharge outright, together with every other new industrial discharge, on the ground that a treatment plant should serve homes and small businesses only
Accept the discharge to begin on the customer's proposed start date, and evaluate its effects on the plant afterward, once the discharge has been running for a trial period
Evaluate the proposed volume and character of the discharge against the plant's capacity and permit limits, and set the acceptance conditions the discharge will have to meet

questions.explanation: Acceptance of a major discharge is a utility-level decision made before the flow arrives: capacity, permit limits, and stated conditions first. Evaluating after the discharge begins puts the plant and its permit at risk.

questions.question: An anaerobic digester at a large plant shows a steadily rising volatile-acid-to-alkalinity ratio over two weeks while pH still reads normal and gas production has begun to slip. What should the chief operator do?

answers.text: Wait for the pH to confirm the trend, because the ratio cannot move before the pH does
Increase the raw sludge feed rate to give the acid-forming organisms more material to work on
Draw down the digester level quickly, because a high ratio means the vessel is simply too full
Cut or pause feeding and hold the digester on its buffered reserves, because a rising ratio is the early warning that acid production is outrunning methane formation

questions.explanation: Volatile acids accumulate before the buffer is exhausted and pH falls, so a rising acid-to-alkalinity ratio is the earliest reliable souring warning; easing feed lets methane formers catch up. Feeding harder or waiting for the pH drop lets the digester go fully sour.

questions.question: A lift station's delivered flow and discharge pressure have both fallen gradually over two years. The force main, discharge elevation, and valve positions are unchanged, suction supply is ample, and the motor draws normal current. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Wear-ring clearances have opened, letting discharge water recirculate internally to suction instead of leaving the pump
The force main has silently grown longer, raising friction head until the pump can no longer reach its former duty point
The wastewater has become less dense, so the same impeller speed can no longer develop the pressure it once produced
The check valve has begun opening too fully, allowing discharge flow to escape back into the wet well during operation

questions.explanation: Gradual loss of both head and delivered flow on an unchanged system is the signature of internal wear: enlarged wear-ring clearances short-circuit flow from discharge back to suction inside the casing. A piping change would be needed to move the system curve, and none occurred here.

questions.question: Maintenance valving left a two-stage trickling filter plant running with its finishing filter first and its high-rate roughing filter second. Since the swap, the lead filter ponds under the raw load and the trailing filter's effluent has worsened. What should the chief operator order?

answers.text: Leave the order exactly as maintenance left it, since two filters in series treat the same in either sequence
Raise recirculation on the lead filter indefinitely until it learns to tolerate the raw load as a roughing unit and give it a full season to prove the conversion works
Convert the trailing filter into a clarifier so the lead filter's ponding solids are captured after they form
Restore the designed order with the roughing filter first to absorb the strong load and the finishing filter second to polish what remains

questions.explanation: Series stages are specialized: the roughing stage is built to absorb strong load and shed heavy film, and the finishing stage to polish weak flow, so reversing them overloads the polisher and starves the rougher of its role. Recirculation cannot turn a finishing bed into a roughing bed.

questions.question: A primary clarifier receives 1,840,000 gallons per day over a surface area of 2,150 square feet. The clarifier is 11 ft deep, its sludge blanket measures 0.8 ft, and its effluent suspended solids that day are 118 mg/L. What is the surface loading in gallons per day per square foot?

answers.text: 742.55 gpd/sq ft
855.81 gpd/sq ft
968.42 gpd/sq ft
1,070.00 gpd/sq ft

questions.explanation: Surface loading is flow divided by surface area: 1,840,000 divided by 2,150 gives 855.81 gallons per day per square foot. Tank depth, blanket depth, and effluent quality do not enter a surface loading rate.

intro-statistics.quiz_title: Introductory Statistics Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which description matches cluster sampling?

answers.text: The population is split into groups, some groups are chosen at random, and everyone in the chosen groups is studied
A random sample is taken separately from every group
Every kth person on a list is selected
People nearby are asked to participate

questions.explanation: Cluster sampling selects whole groups (clusters) at random and studies all members of the selected clusters. Stratified sampling samples from every group instead.

questions.question: What is the defining feature of an experiment?

answers.text: Researchers only watch what happens naturally
Researchers ask people to recall the past
Researchers use the largest possible sample
Researchers deliberately impose a treatment and observe the response

questions.explanation: An experiment actively applies a treatment to subjects and measures the effect. Imposition of treatment separates it from observation.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of the coefficient of variation over the standard deviation when comparing two data sets?

answers.text: It is always smaller than the standard deviation
It never changes when data are rescaled
It works even when the mean is exactly zero
It is unitless (SD divided by the mean), so it fairly compares variability for variables measured in different units or at very different scales

questions.explanation: Because CV expresses spread as a proportion of the mean, dollars can be compared with kilograms, or thousands with millions, on equal footing.

questions.question: In a box plot, the vertical line drawn inside the box marks which value?

answers.text: The mean
The maximum
The minimum
The median

questions.explanation: The line inside the box is the median of the data set. The box edges mark the quartiles.

questions.question: A temperature during an experiment is uniform between 4 and 20 degrees. What is its mean?

answers.text: 8 degrees
16 degrees
24 degrees
12 degrees

questions.explanation: The mean of a uniform distribution is the midpoint: (4 + 20) / 2 = 12 degrees.

questions.question: A survey records each participant's blood type as A, B, AB, or O. What is the level of measurement?

answers.text: Ordinal
Interval
Nominal
Ratio

questions.explanation: Blood type puts people into named categories with no natural ordering, which is the nominal level. There is no ranking or meaningful zero.

questions.question: A student is given only a data set's five-number summary and asked for its mean. What is the correct response?

answers.text: The mean equals the median entry in the summary
The mean is the average of the minimum and maximum
The mean is Q1 plus Q3 divided by 2
The mean cannot be recovered from the five-number summary; it depends on every individual value, not just the five landmarks

questions.explanation: Five landmarks do not determine how values are distributed within each quarter, so the mean (which uses all values) cannot be reconstructed.

questions.question: Data: 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 30. Using the 1.5 x IQR rule (with Q1 = 6.5 and Q3 = 13), which values, if any, are outliers?

answers.text: Only 4: it is far below the median
Both 4 and 30, because they are the minimum and maximum
Only 30: the IQR is 6.5, so the upper fence is 13 + 9.75 = 22.75, and 30 exceeds it
None: outliers require values more than 3 IQRs away

questions.explanation: IQR = 13 - 6.5 = 6.5. Upper fence = 13 + 1.5(6.5) = 22.75; lower fence = 6.5 - 9.75 = -3.25. Only 30 falls outside the fences.

questions.question: Sets P and Q both have mean 14. P = {10, 12, 14, 16, 18} and Q = {2, 8, 14, 20, 26}. Which set has the larger standard deviation, and why?

answers.text: P: its values are evenly spaced, which maximizes spread
They are equal: same mean and same count force equal SDs
Q: its values lie much farther from 14 on average (deviations up to 12) than P's (up to 4)
Neither has an SD, because both contain the mean itself

questions.explanation: P's deviations are -4, -2, 0, 2, 4, while Q's are -12, -6, 0, 6, 12. Larger typical deviations give Q a standard deviation three times P's.

questions.question: A pie chart of 'students' favorite campus activities' has slices summing to 130%. What went wrong?

answers.text: Pie charts are allowed to sum to any total under 200%
Respondents could choose more than one activity, so the categories are not mutually exclusive parts of a whole and a pie chart is inappropriate
The chart is fine: rounding explains the extra 30%
One slice must have been drawn in 3D

questions.explanation: A pie chart requires categories that partition a whole into shares summing to 100%. Multiple-response data violate that, so a bar graph should be used instead.

questions.question: Scores are bell-shaped with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. By the empirical rule, about 95% of scores lie between which values?
questions.explanation: Two standard deviations is 2 x 15 = 30, so the interval is 100 - 30 = 70 to 100 + 30 = 130. About 95% fall within 2 standard deviations.

questions.question: A student computes P(A or B) as P(A)+P(B) even though the events overlap. What error did the student make?

answers.text: Double-counting the overlap; P(A and B) must be subtracted
Forgetting to multiply the probabilities
Treating disjoint events as independent
Using the complement rule incorrectly

questions.explanation: Adding counts the overlap twice. The general addition rule subtracts P(A and B) once to correct this.

questions.question: Surveyors knock on doors only between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. on weekdays to estimate a town's unemployment rate. The estimate comes out far too high. The best explanation is:

answers.text: People who are home during work hours are disproportionately those without jobs, so the sampling procedure overrepresents the unemployed
Daytime interviewing doubles the margin of error
Unemployed people always exaggerate their status
The surveyors should have worked on Sundays only

questions.explanation: The timing of the visits selects a sample enriched with people not at work, inflating the measured unemployment rate. This is selection bias from the data-collection procedure.

questions.question: A dotplot of ages at a community center shows two clear clusters, one near age 10 and one near age 35, with almost nobody near the overall mean of about 22. The best interpretation is:

answers.text: The data are bimodal, probably mixing two subgroups (such as children in classes and their parents), so the single mean of 22 describes almost no one
The mean of 22 must be a calculation error, since nobody is 22
The distribution is symmetric because the clusters balance out
Ages near 22 are the most common at the center

questions.explanation: Two separated clusters indicate bimodality, often a sign of two distinct groups combined. The overall mean falls in the empty gap between the clusters.

questions.question: Heights of the 25 students in a class form a roughly symmetric distribution with no outliers, and the mean and median are nearly equal. A coach needs one summary of typical height. What is the best guidance?

answers.text: Either works well here; with symmetric, outlier-free data the mean is a fine (and standard) choice
Only the median may be used, because means require skewed data
Neither: symmetric data cannot be summarized
Use the maximum, since symmetry makes it typical

questions.explanation: The mean's weakness is distortion by skew and outliers. When neither is present, mean and median nearly coincide and both describe the center well.

questions.question: A real-estate report wants one number for a 'typical' sale price in a neighborhood where most homes sell near $300,000 but a few sell above $2 million. Which choice is most defensible?

answers.text: The mean, because it is the largest summary
The maximum, because it shows potential
The range, because it covers all prices
The median, because the few very large prices would distort the mean

questions.explanation: The median is resistant to the few extreme prices and reflects the typical home near $300,000. The mean would be pulled upward by the million-dollar sales.

questions.question: A survey of landline owners is used to estimate opinions of all adults, but many younger adults have only cell phones and are missed. This is mainly an example of:

answers.text: Response bias from wording
A placebo effect
Random sampling error
Undercoverage, because part of the population is missing from the frame

questions.explanation: The landline frame leaves out cell-only adults, so part of the population had no chance of selection. That is undercoverage.

questions.question: A town of 800 households wants its average monthly water use. The utility already has exact billing records for every household. A researcher instead mails a questionnaire to 100 randomly chosen households asking them to estimate their use. Which approach is stronger, and why?

answers.text: The questionnaire: any survey is automatically more accurate than records
Both are equally strong, because 100 households is a large fraction of 800
Neither: water use cannot be studied statistically
Using the billing records: they cover the entire population (a census) with measured values, while the questionnaire gives estimates from a sample with recall error

questions.explanation: Billing records provide exact measurements for all 800 households, eliminating both sampling and recall error. The questionnaire adds sampling variation and estimation error on top.

questions.question: Thirty schools are randomly assigned either a new math curriculum or the current one, and each school's average test score is later compared. A district official counts '3,900 students' as the number of experimental units. What is wrong with that count?

answers.text: Students can never be part of an experiment
The count should be 2, the number of curricula
The curriculum was assigned to schools, so there are 30 experimental units (the schools), not 3,900
Nothing is wrong: every student tested is always an experimental unit

questions.explanation: The unit of random assignment determines the experimental unit. Treatments were assigned at the school level, so the study has 30 units.

questions.question: If P(at least one defect in a batch)=0.30, what is P(no defects in the batch)?

answers.text: Impossible to tell without the batch size

questions.explanation: 'At least one' and 'none' are complements. Their probabilities sum to 1, so P(none)=1-0.30=0.70.

anatomy-physiology.quiz_title: Anatomy & Physiology Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Skin lies ___ to the underlying skeletal muscles covering most of the body.

answers.text: Deep
Superficial
Proximal
Medial

questions.explanation: Superficial means closer to the body surface, as skin is relative to muscle.

questions.question: The specific region of an enzyme where the substrate binds is called the:

answers.text: Active site
Allosteric membrane
Ribosome
Antigen-binding region of DNA

questions.explanation: Substrate binding and catalysis occur at the enzyme's active site.

questions.question: Why does injured cartilage generally heal much more slowly than injured skin?

answers.text: Cartilage contains no living cells
Cartilage is made entirely of dead collagen
Cartilage is avascular, so nutrients and repair cells reach it slowly by diffusion
Skin has no blood supply, so it heals faster

questions.explanation: Cartilage lacks blood vessels, so repair depends on slow diffusion, making cartilage healing slow.

questions.question: Which feature best distinguishes a simple epithelium from a stratified epithelium?

answers.text: A simple epithelium always has cilia
A stratified epithelium has exactly one layer of flat cells
A simple epithelium is always found in the bladder
A simple epithelium is one cell layer thick, with every cell touching the basement membrane

questions.explanation: Simple epithelia consist of a single cell layer in which all cells contact the basement membrane, whereas stratified epithelia have multiple layers.

questions.question: If the hydrogen ion concentration of a fluid increases, its pH will:

answers.text: Increase (become more alkaline)
Stay the same
Decrease (become more acidic)
Become exactly neutral

questions.explanation: pH is inversely related to H+ concentration: more H+ means a lower pH.

questions.question: A patient has pain described as deep to the ribs on the posterior body wall, medial to the scapula. Where should the examiner palpate?

answers.text: On the front of the chest below the collarbone
On the lateral abdomen near the hip
On the anterior thigh
On the back, between the spine and the shoulder blade, beneath the ribs

questions.explanation: Posterior means the back, medial to the scapula means between spine and shoulder blade, and deep to the ribs means beneath them, matching the described back location.

questions.question: Two atoms of the same element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. They are:

answers.text: Different elements
Isotopes of that element
Ions of each other
Compounds

questions.explanation: Isotopes vary in neutron number (and mass) while retaining the same atomic number.

questions.question: Fluid in joints, and mucus along airways, reduces friction and allows smooth movement. This illustrates water's role as a:

answers.text: Solvent only
Lubricant
Reactant in hydrolysis only
Structural protein

questions.explanation: Water-based fluids lubricate joints, organs, and passageways.

questions.question: Why does the plasma membrane allow lipid-soluble substances to pass through its core more readily than charged ions?

answers.text: Its cholesterol molecules actively pump ions outward
Its interior is formed by hydrophobic fatty acid tails that repel charged ions
Its outer surface is coated with a thick layer of collagen
Its proteins permanently close all pathways through the membrane

questions.explanation: The hydrophobic interior of the bilayer permits nonpolar, lipid-soluble substances to dissolve through it while presenting a barrier to charged ions.

questions.question: Why would infusing pure distilled water intravenously be dangerous for red blood cells?

answers.text: Distilled water is hypertonic and would crenate the cells
Distilled water is hypotonic, so water would rush into the cells and cause hemolysis
Distilled water contains no oxygen for the cells to use
Distilled water would trigger immediate blood clotting in veins

questions.explanation: Distilled water has essentially no solutes, making it strongly hypotonic; water enters red blood cells and can cause hemolysis.

questions.question: A biopsy from a kidney tubule shows a single layer of cube-shaped cells surrounding a small lumen. Which tissue is this?

answers.text: Stratified squamous epithelium
Simple cuboidal epithelium
Cardiac muscle tissue
Dense regular connective tissue

questions.explanation: Simple cuboidal epithelium lines kidney tubules and ducts and functions in secretion and absorption.

questions.question: An adult has burns covering the entire trunk (36%) and the entire head and neck (9%). Using the rule of nines, the estimated total is:
questions.explanation: Entire trunk 36% plus head and neck 9% equals 45% of total body surface area.

questions.question: A meal is broken down mechanically and chemically, nutrients are absorbed, and solid waste is eliminated. The system performing all three steps is the:

answers.text: Urinary system
Digestive system
Cardiovascular system
Respiratory system

questions.explanation: Ingestion, digestion, absorption, and elimination of solid wastes are the linked functions of the digestive system.

questions.question: A patient cannot empty the bladder fully, has a rising blood urea level, and ultrasound shows a normal heart and lungs. Which system is the primary source of the problem?

answers.text: The urinary system
The respiratory system
The nervous system only
The digestive system

questions.explanation: Failure to empty the bladder with rising urea (a waste normally excreted in urine) points to the urinary system as the primary source.

questions.question: Inside a cell, worn-out organelles are broken down and their components recycled after fusion with enzyme-filled sacs. Which organelle performs this digestion?

answers.text: The ribosome
The mitochondrion
The nucleolus
The lysosome

questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that break down worn organelles, ingested material, and macromolecules for recycling.

questions.question: A membrane lining a digestive tract cavity open to the exterior, containing epithelium over connective tissue and producing mucus, is which type?

answers.text: Serous membrane
Cutaneous membrane
Mucous membrane
Synovial membrane

questions.explanation: Mucous membranes line cavities open to the outside, such as the digestive tract, and secrete mucus.

questions.question: A patient with liver disease develops yellow whites of the eyes and yellow skin, with dark urine. Which pigment accumulation explains the yellow color?

answers.text: Bilirubin
Melanin
Carotene in the kidneys
Hemoglobin in the nails

questions.explanation: Liver failure impairs bilirubin clearance, and bilirubin accumulation yellows skin and sclera, which is jaundice.

questions.question: On standing quickly, a patient's blood pressure briefly dips, baroreceptors detect it, and heart rate rises within seconds to restore pressure. Which description best fits this event?

answers.text: Positive feedback amplifying a change
Negative feedback restoring a variable toward its set point
Feedforward control with no sensor
A reflex with no control center

questions.explanation: The dip was detected and counteracted to return pressure toward normal, which is negative feedback restoring a variable toward its set point.

questions.question: A patient develops watery leakage between intestinal lining cells, with contents seeping between cells rather than through them, after damage to the seals at the tops of the cells. Which junction is damaged?

answers.text: Desmosomes
Gap junctions
Hemidesmosomes only
Tight junctions

questions.explanation: Tight junctions seal the space between cells, so damaging them allows contents to leak between intestinal cells.

questions.question: The pancreas contains both ducted clusters that secrete digestive enzymes into the intestine and ductless clusters that secrete insulin into the blood. How is the pancreas best described?

answers.text: A purely endocrine gland
A mixed gland with both exocrine and endocrine portions
A purely exocrine gland
A holocrine gland only

questions.explanation: The pancreas is a mixed gland: its acinar portion is exocrine and its islets are endocrine.

introductory-physics.quiz_title: Introductory Physics I-II Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Convert 450 cm to m.

answers.text: 9 m

questions.explanation: Multiply by the conversion factor: 450 x 0.01 = 4.5 m.

questions.question: A 10 kg object moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A motor does 1500 J of work in 30 s. What is its average power?
The work-energy theorem states that net work equals

answers.text: the change in potential energy in all cases
the total mechanical energy created
force multiplied by time of contact
the change in kinetic energy

questions.explanation: W_net = KE_final - KE_initial.

questions.question: A 7 kg object moves at 6 m/s. What is its momentum?

answers.text: 84 kg m/s
21 kg m/s
52 kg m/s
42 kg m/s

questions.explanation: p = m v = 7 x 6 = 42 kg m/s.

questions.question: If velocity and acceleration point in opposite directions, the object

answers.text: must be moving backwards at all times
speeds up in the direction of motion
slows down
has zero velocity at that instant

questions.explanation: Acceleration opposing the velocity reduces the speed.

questions.question: A projectile has horizontal velocity 6 m/s and vertical velocity 8 m/s at one instant. What is its total speed then?

answers.text: 10 m/s
20 m/s
5 m/s
0 m/s

questions.explanation: Speed = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 m/s.

questions.question: A net force of 90 N acts on a 15 kg object. What is its acceleration?
A 12 kg box is pushed with 90 N while friction opposes it with 30 N. What is its acceleration?
On a level road, what provides the centripetal force for a turning car?

answers.text: The car's engine pushing it forward
The normal force from the road surface
Friction between the tires and the road
The weight of the car acting downward

questions.explanation: The center-directed force on a level turn comes from tire-road friction.

questions.question: A 5 kg object's velocity changes by 7 m/s. What is the magnitude of the impulse on it?

answers.text: 35 N s
70 N s
45 N s

questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum = m x delta-v = 5 x 7 = 35 N s.

questions.question: Compared with a single hard impact, an airbag protects a passenger by

answers.text: stretching the stopping time, which reduces the needed force for the same impulse
reducing the passenger's momentum to zero before impact
increasing the impulse so the force feels smaller
removing the passenger's kinetic energy instantly

questions.explanation: Impulse is fixed by the momentum change; a longer time means a smaller average force.

questions.question: A surface has friction coefficient 0.2 and the normal force on a sliding block is 200 N. What is the kinetic friction force?
A 4 kg object falls from rest through a height of 5 m with no air resistance. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, what is its speed at the bottom?

answers.text: 10 m/s
20 m/s
5 m/s
0 m/s

questions.explanation: m g h = (1/2) m v^2, so v = sqrt(2 g h) = sqrt(100) = 10 m/s; the mass cancels.

questions.question: Before a collision, a 2 kg object moves at 14 m/s and a 5 kg object is at rest. What is the total momentum of the system?

answers.text: 56 kg m/s
14 kg m/s
28 kg m/s
38 kg m/s

questions.explanation: Total momentum = 2 x 14 + 5 x 0 = 28 kg m/s, and it stays the same through the collision.

questions.question: A transformer (120 primary turns, 60 secondary turns) is fed 18 V. The secondary drives a 3 ohm load. What current flows in the load?

answers.text: 6 A
3 A

questions.explanation: Secondary voltage = 18 x 60/120 = 9 V; current = 9 / 3 = 3 A.

questions.question: Heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold. A refrigerator appears to reverse this, but does not violate the second law because

answers.text: refrigerators are exempt from thermodynamics
the inside of a refrigerator is not a real system
cold is a substance that flows outward
work input pays for the transfer, and total entropy still increases

questions.explanation: Driven heat transfer with work input increases total entropy overall.

questions.question: A force of 17 N acts along the hypotenuse of a 8-15-17 right triangle, with the horizontal leg 8. What is the horizontal component of the force?

answers.text: 8 N
4 N

questions.explanation: The horizontal component scales with the leg ratio: (8/17) x 17 = 8 N.

questions.question: A 50 kg passenger stands on a scale in an elevator accelerating upward at 2 m/s^2 (g = 10 m/s^2). What does the scale read (the normal force)?
questions.explanation: The floor must supply m g plus m a: 50 x (10 + 2) = 600 N.

questions.question: Light passes from a medium with n = 2 (sine of incidence = 0.5) into a medium with n = 1.25. Using n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2), what is the sine of the refraction angle?

financial-accounting.quiz_title: Financial Accounting Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A company pays $2,500 to a supplier on an account payable. What is the effect?

answers.text: Assets increase and liabilities increase
Assets decrease and equity decreases
Assets decrease and liabilities decrease
Assets increase and liabilities decrease

questions.explanation: Cash falls by $2,500 and the payable falls by $2,500, keeping the equation in balance. The payment settles a debt rather than recording an expense, so equity does not change, and neither balance rises.

questions.question: A debit to a liability account has what effect?

answers.text: It decreases the liability
It increases the liability
It converts the liability to equity
It has no effect until year end

questions.explanation: Liabilities carry credit normal balances, so debits reduce them. Debits cannot increase a liability, do not reclassify it as equity, and take effect when posted, not at year end.

questions.question: What makes a liability current rather than long-term?

answers.text: It was incurred during the current year, regardless of when it is due
It is owed to a supplier rather than to a bank
It is expected to be paid within one year or the operating cycle, whichever is longer, using current assets or by creating another current liability
It exceeds $10,000 in amount

questions.explanation: Classification turns on when the obligation comes due, not when it arose, who the creditor is, or its size. A liability due within one year or the operating cycle, whichever is longer, is current; obligations due beyond that horizon are long-term.

questions.question: Goods are shipped FOB destination. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Title passes to the buyer when the goods reach the buyer's location, and the seller normally pays the freight
Title passes when the goods leave the seller's dock
The buyer records the purchase while the goods are in transit
The seller removes the goods from inventory at shipment

questions.explanation: FOB destination keeps title with the seller until delivery, so the seller normally pays the freight and keeps the goods in its own inventory while they travel. Title at the dock and buyer recording in transit describe FOB shipping point instead.

questions.question: A company pays $200,000 cash to redeem its bonds at maturity. How is this payment classified?

answers.text: An outflow from operating activities
An outflow from investing activities
An outflow from financing activities
A noncash financing activity

questions.explanation: Redeeming bonds repays capital raised from creditors, a financing outflow. Any interest paid up to maturity would be operating under US GAAP, but the $200,000 principal redemption is financing. No asset is acquired, and cash was paid.

questions.question: Which financial statement reports revenues and expenses for a period of time?

answers.text: The balance sheet
The retained earnings statement
The statement of cash flows
The income statement

questions.explanation: The income statement summarizes revenues and expenses over a period to yield net income or loss. The balance sheet is dated at a point in time, and the other two statements track equity changes and cash movements rather than performance.

questions.question: What is the normal balance of stockholders' equity accounts such as common stock?

answers.text: Debit
Credit
Zero
Debit when profitable, credit when not

questions.explanation: Equity accounts normally carry credit balances because owner investments and earnings are recorded as credits. Profitability changes retained earnings amounts but never flips the normal side of equity accounts.

questions.question: A company's accounting year runs from July 1 to the following June 30. Which statement is true?

answers.text: The company uses a calendar year
The company has no fiscal year
June 30 is the end of its fiscal year
Its annual statements cover six months

questions.explanation: A July-to-June twelve-month period is a fiscal year ending June 30. A calendar year ends December 31, every business adopts some accounting year, and the period described spans twelve months, not six.

questions.question: How is a net loss shown in the worksheet's statement columns?

answers.text: It is entered in the balance sheet credit column only
It is entered in the income statement credit column and the balance sheet debit column
It is omitted until the loss is confirmed by an auditor
It is entered as a negative revenue in the adjusted trial balance

questions.explanation: A net loss means income statement debits exceed credits, so the loss figure goes in the income statement credit column to balance that pair, and in the balance sheet debit column because a loss decreases equity. It is a normal worksheet result that is neither omitted nor recorded as negative revenue.

questions.question: Cost of goods available for sale is $105,000 and cost of goods sold is $80,000. What is ending inventory under the periodic system?

answers.text: It cannot be determined without a perpetual record

questions.explanation: Ending inventory is the residual: $105,000 available minus $80,000 sold equals $25,000, which a physical count would confirm. Adding the two amounts gives $185,000, and restating cost of goods sold ignores that the periodic computation itself yields ending inventory.

questions.question: Ending inventory is understated by $7,000 at year-end. What is the effect on the current year's cost of goods sold and net income?

answers.text: Cost of goods sold is understated by $7,000 and net income is overstated by $7,000
Net income is correctly stated because the error reverses in the next year
There is no effect on cost of goods sold
Cost of goods sold is overstated by $7,000 and net income is understated by $7,000

questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold equals goods available minus ending inventory, so subtracting an ending inventory that is $7,000 too small overstates cost of goods sold by $7,000 and understates net income by $7,000. The reversal next year does not make the current year correct, the computation is directly affected rather than untouched, and understating the subtraction cannot lower cost of goods sold.

questions.question: A company borrowed $50,000 on a note payable and recorded the receipt by debiting Cash and crediting Service Revenue. What is the effect of this single error?

answers.text: Revenue and net income are overstated by $50,000 and notes payable is understated by $50,000, while cash is correct
Cash is overstated by $50,000
Liabilities are overstated by $50,000
Total stockholders' equity is understated by $50,000

questions.explanation: The cash is real, but its source is a lender, not a customer: crediting revenue fabricates $50,000 of income, and the obligation to repay never reaches the balance sheet. Equity is overstated, not understated, because the false income flows into it.

questions.question: Total assets are $120,000 and stockholders' equity is $45,000. What are total liabilities?
questions.explanation: Liabilities equal assets minus equity: $120,000 minus $45,000 is $75,000. Adding gives $165,000 and double-counts claims, while repeating either given figure ignores the residual relationship.

questions.question: A machine costing $12,000 with no salvage value has a five-year useful life. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the monthly depreciation expense?
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation is $12,000 divided by five years, which is $2,400, and one month is $2,400 divided by twelve, which is $200. The $2,400 figure is a full year, $240 misplaces a decimal in the monthly step, and $1,200 is half a year.

questions.question: A company owes interest on a $10,000 note at 6 percent annual interest, and three months have passed since the last interest payment. What interest has accrued?
questions.explanation: Interest equals principal times rate times time: $10,000 times 6 percent times three-twelfths of a year is $150. The $600 figure is a full year of interest, $50 is one month, and $1,800 applies the rate for three full years.

questions.question: Which amount is NOT part of operating expenses on a merchandiser's multi-step income statement?

answers.text: Sales salaries
Advertising expense
Office rent for administrative staff
Cost of goods sold

questions.explanation: Operating expenses consist of selling and administrative expenses such as sales salaries, advertising, and administrative rent. Cost of goods sold is deducted earlier to compute gross profit and is never classified as an operating expense.

questions.question: Preferred shares require the issuing company to buy them back for $500,000 cash on a fixed date five years from now, under an enforceable right held by the investors. For classification purposes, these shares are:

answers.text: Equity in all cases, because they are legally called stock
In substance a liability, because the issuer has an unavoidable obligation to transfer cash on a set date
A contra asset
Revenue when issued

questions.explanation: Substance governs: an instrument the issuer must redeem for cash at a fixed date embodies exactly what defines a liability — a present obligation to transfer assets — regardless of the stock label on the certificate. It is presented as debt, not ownership.

questions.question: Equipment is bought for $12,000, paying $4,000 cash and signing a note for the rest. What are the total debits in the entry?
questions.explanation: The single debit is to equipment for its full $12,000 cost; the credits split between cash of $4,000 and notes payable of $8,000. The $4,000 and $8,000 figures are individual credits, and $16,000 double-counts the asset.

questions.question: After revenues of $48,000 and expenses of $31,000 have been closed, Income Summary has a credit balance of $17,000. Which entry closes Income Summary, and what does the balance represent?

answers.text: Debit Retained Earnings $17,000 and credit Income Summary $17,000, representing a net loss
Debit Income Summary $17,000 and credit Dividends $17,000, representing a distribution
Debit Income Summary $17,000 and credit Retained Earnings $17,000, representing net income
No entry is needed because Income Summary carries its balance into the next year

questions.explanation: A credit balance in Income Summary means revenues exceeded expenses by $48,000 minus $31,000, which is $17,000 of net income. Income Summary is debited to clear it and Retained Earnings is credited because net income increases equity. The loss treatment would apply to a debit balance, dividends are closed separately, and Income Summary is a temporary account that must end at zero.

questions.question: A grocery store selling perishable goods most likely finds that its actual physical flow of goods corresponds to which cost flow assumption?

answers.text: FIFO, because the oldest goods are sold first
LIFO, because the newest goods are sold first
Specific identification of every low-cost item
No assumption is permitted for perishables

questions.explanation: Perishables are stocked and sold oldest-first to avoid spoilage, which is exactly the flow FIFO assumes. LIFO assumes the newest goods leave first, specific identification is impractical for masses of small items, and perishable inventory uses the standard methods like any other goods.

cet.quiz_title: CET Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Before an EKG in an inpatient room, which health-status history is most relevant for the technician to obtain and pass on?

answers.text: Favorite foods and television programs
Recent chest pain, breathlessness on exertion, fainting episodes, and ankle swelling
Names of all childhood illnesses with no current symptoms
Preferred appointment times for future visits

questions.explanation: B is correct: recent chest pain, exertional dyspnea, syncope, and edema are directly relevant to current cardiopulmonary status and testing safety. A is wrong because food and entertainment preferences do not assess cardiopulmonary health status. C is wrong because remote childhood history without current symptoms is far less relevant than present cardiac symptoms. D is wrong because scheduling preference is administrative, not a health-status assessment.

questions.question: Successive R-R intervals on an inpatient strip measure 13, 19, 25, 16, and 22 small boxes with no repeating sequence, and no distinct P waves can be identified before the narrow QRS complexes. What is the best description of the rhythm's regularity?

answers.text: Regular, because all the QRS complexes look alike
Regularly irregular, because the intervals cycle in a set pattern
Regular with a single premature beat
Irregular, with no repeating pattern

questions.explanation: D is correct: R-R intervals that vary beat to beat with no repeating sequence, together with absent identifiable P waves, describe an irregular rhythm with no pattern. A is wrong because regularity is judged by interval spacing, not by whether QRS shapes match. B is wrong because the listed intervals do not repeat in any cycle. C is wrong because a single premature beat would leave the rest of the intervals equal, whereas every interval here differs.

questions.question: A technician will walk a patient with a weak left side from the waiting area to the EKG room using a gait belt. Which use of the belt is correct?

answers.text: Fasten the belt loosely over the chest and walk on the patient's stronger right side
Fasten the belt snugly around the waist over clothing, stand on the patient's weaker left side, and grasp the belt at the back while walking
Fasten the belt around the patient's weak arm and use it to pull the patient forward
Hold the belt in one hand without fastening it, so it can be dropped quickly if the patient stumbles

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: a gait belt is fastened snugly at the waist over clothing, and the assistant walks on the patient's weaker side grasping the belt at the back, which gives support exactly where the patient is most likely to falter. A is wrong because a chest-level, loosely fastened belt can ride up and does not stabilize the waist, and the stronger side is not where support is needed. C is wrong because pulling on a weak arm can injure the shoulder and does not support the trunk. D is wrong because an unfastened belt provides no support at all if the patient begins to fall.

questions.question: Lead aVF is one of the augmented limb leads on a standard 12-lead tracing. Which electrode serves as the positive (exploring) electrode for aVF?

answers.text: The right arm electrode
The left arm electrode
The left leg electrode
The right leg electrode

questions.explanation: C is correct: aVF records the signal at the left leg (foot) electrode against a reference formed from the other limb electrodes. A is wrong because the right arm electrode is the exploring electrode for aVR. B is wrong because the left arm electrode is the exploring electrode for aVL. D is wrong because the right leg electrode is the ground/reference electrode and is not the exploring electrode for any lead.

questions.question: In the SBAR format for escalating a finding, which information belongs in the Background element?

answers.text: Relevant context such as the reason for the test, recent symptoms, and pertinent history or medications
The technician's own diagnosis of what is causing the finding
A request for the clinician to come and assess the patient now
The patient's current vital signs and the new finding itself

questions.explanation: A is correct: Background supplies the context behind the current situation — why the patient is being tested, recent symptoms, and relevant history or medications — so the clinician can judge the finding in context. B is wrong because offering a diagnosis is outside the technician's scope and is not part of any SBAR element. C is wrong because the request for action belongs to the Recommendation element, not Background. D is wrong because current vital signs and the new finding itself make up the Situation and Assessment elements, not the Background.

questions.question: On a tracing recorded at 50 mm/s, an R-R interval spans 20 small boxes. A trainee calculates a heart rate of 75 bpm. What is the correct rate, and why did the trainee err?

answers.text: The rate is 75 bpm; the trainee was correct because box counts do not depend on speed
The rate is 150 bpm; at 50 mm/s each small box is 0.02 seconds, so the interval is 0.40 seconds, not 0.80 seconds
The rate is 100 bpm; at 50 mm/s each small box is 0.03 seconds
The rate is 300 bpm; at 50 mm/s each small box is 0.01 seconds

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: at 50 mm/s one small box equals 1 divided by 50, or 0.02 seconds, so 20 boxes equal 0.40 seconds and the rate is 60 divided by 0.40, or 150 bpm; the trainee used the 0.04-second value that applies only at 25 mm/s. A is wrong because the time value of a box changes with paper speed. C is wrong because a small box at 50 mm/s is 0.02 seconds, not 0.03 seconds. D is wrong because 0.01 seconds per millimeter would require a speed of 100 mm/s.

questions.question: Resting tracings on Mr. Alvarez keep showing muscle tremor from his wrists and ankles despite repositioning and a warm blanket. Which limb-electrode adjustment best reduces the tremor while keeping the leads comparable?

answers.text: Move only the two arm electrodes higher and leave the leg electrodes at the ankles
Move the right-side electrodes proximally and leave the left-side electrodes distal
Tape each wrist and ankle electrode down harder at its original site
Move all four limb electrodes to more proximal, fleshy sites at matching levels on both sides and note the modified placement on the tracing

questions.explanation: D is correct: moving all limb electrodes proximally to fleshy, less tremor-prone sites at symmetric levels reduces somatic tremor while preserving left-right comparability, and the change must be noted because it is nonstandard. A is wrong because moving only the arms creates an asymmetric, nonstandard set and leaves leg tremor unaddressed. B is wrong because one-sided proximal placement makes the two sides non-comparable. C is wrong because firmer taping at a trembling distal site does not remove the muscle-motion source.

questions.question: At several electrode sites, a patient's skin is dry and flaky, and a trial electrode rocks on loose surface cells instead of seating flat against the skin. Which prep step best addresses this problem?

answers.text: Apply body lotion to soften the flakes so the electrode slides into place
Wet the sites with water and apply the electrodes while the skin is dripping
Gently use an abrasive prep pad to clear the loose dead skin, then apply the electrode to clean, dry skin
Shave a wide area at each site with a razor even though there is no hair present

questions.explanation: C is correct: gentle abrasion is the prep step designed to remove loose, dead surface cells so the electrode seats flat with low-resistance contact, followed by application to dry skin. A is wrong because lotion adds an oily barrier that prevents adhesion. B is wrong because electrodes applied to wet skin adhere poorly and slip. D is wrong because razoring hairless skin only risks cuts and irritation without addressing the flaky surface.

questions.question: Using the 6-second method on a rhythm strip recorded at 25 mm/s, the technician counts 8 QRS complexes within a segment spanning 30 large boxes (6 seconds). What is the heart rate?

answers.text: 48 bpm, found by dividing 300 by the number of large boxes
133 bpm, found by dividing 1500 by the number of QRS complexes
80 bpm, found by multiplying the 8 QRS complexes in 6 seconds by 10
8 bpm, because only 8 beats were counted on the strip

questions.explanation: Key C is right: the 6-second method counts QRS complexes in 6 seconds (30 large boxes at 25 mm/s) and multiplies by 10, so 8 x 10 = 80 bpm. A is wrong because 300 is divided by large boxes between R waves in the 300 method, not by the 30-box segment length. B is wrong because 1500 is divided by small boxes between consecutive R waves in the 1500 method, not by a QRS count. D is wrong because the raw count must be scaled to a full minute by multiplying by 10.

questions.question: An unresponsive adult with no pulse receives a shock from an AED after analysis advises one. A coworker is managing the airway. What should the person doing compressions do immediately after the shock is delivered?

answers.text: Stop compressions for a full minute to check for a pulse
Leave the patient to document the shock time before anything else
Wait for the next AED analysis before touching the patient again
Resume chest compressions immediately, beginning with compressions rather than a pulse check

questions.explanation: D is correct: after a shock, compressions resume immediately to restore perfusion; rhythm and pulse checks wait for the next scheduled analysis cycle. A is wrong because a prolonged pause for a pulse check leaves the heart and brain unperfused. B is wrong because documentation never takes priority over compressions during an arrest. C is wrong because waiting idle until the next analysis wastes the minutes when compressions matter most.

questions.question: In a paper-chart clinic, a technician finds that a tracing was mounted upside down and the mount sheet's label covers the first complexes of the strip. What is the correct way to fix the mounting?

answers.text: Leave it as mounted, since the date and name are still readable somewhere on the sheet
Staple the strip flat through the waveform area so it cannot shift again
Remount the strip flat and right-side up on the mount sheet with the full tracing visible and the identifying label on the sheet where it does not cover any complexes
Trim off the covered complexes so the remaining strip lies flat

questions.explanation: C is correct: a mounted paper tracing must lie flat, be oriented correctly for review, show the complete tracing, and carry its identification on the mount sheet without obscuring any part of the recording. A is wrong because an upside-down strip with hidden complexes cannot be reviewed reliably even if the name is visible. B is wrong because stapling through the waveform damages and obscures the tracing itself. D is wrong because cutting away complexes destroys part of the diagnostic record.

questions.question: A reusable electrode clip has visible corrosion and dried gel on its contact surface, and recent tracings from that lead show intermittent signal dropouts. What should the technician do?

answers.text: Clean the contact surface as the manufacturer directs; if corrosion or pitting remains, replace the clip and verify good contact before patient use
Clip it on more tightly so pressure overcomes the poor contact
Apply extra electrode gel over the corrosion to bridge the connection
Move the clip to a different lead without cleaning it, so a less important lead is affected

questions.explanation: A is correct: corrosion and dried gel raise contact resistance and cause the dropouts, so manufacturer-directed cleaning is first, and a clip that stays pitted must be replaced and its contact verified before use.
