B is wrong because extra pressure does not restore a corroded contact surface and can damage the electrode tab. C is wrong because gel over corrosion does not remove the resistive layer and leaves an unreliable connection. D is wrong because it spreads a known defective clip to another lead and leaves contamination in place.

questions.question: Telemetry shows atrial deflections occurring regularly at 200 per minute. Only every second deflection is followed by a QRS, giving a regular ventricular rate of 100 bpm. Each conducted beat has a constant PR interval of 0.18 seconds and a QRS of 0.08 seconds. Which rhythm should be reported?

answers.text: Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction
Sinus tachycardia at 100 bpm
Complete heart block
Atrial tachycardia with atrioventricular block

questions.explanation: D is correct: a rapid atrial rhythm at 200 per minute with a fixed 2:1 conduction pattern and a constant PR interval on conducted beats is atrial tachycardia with AV block. A is wrong because flutter has a sawtooth baseline at about 300 flutter waves per minute. B is wrong because sinus tachycardia has one P wave per QRS at the ventricular rate, not atrial activity at twice that rate. C is wrong because complete heart block has atria and ventricles beating independently, not a fixed every-second-beat relationship.

questions.question: On a telemetry unit, a monitor alarm sounds repeatedly from a room the EKG technician is passing. A busy staff member says, 'Just silence that alarm for the rest of the shift — it keeps going off.' What should the technician do?

answers.text: Silence the alarm for the shift as requested to reduce alarm fatigue
Turn the alarm volume down so it can still be seen but not heard
Go to the patient, assess the situation, and promptly notify the responsible nurse of the alarm and what was found, rather than disabling it
Disconnect the lead causing the alarm until the nurse's next rounds

questions.explanation: C is correct: alarms signal findings that require assessment and escalation; the technician checks the patient and notifies the responsible nurse instead of disabling a safety device. A is wrong because silencing an alarm for a whole shift could hide a life-threatening rhythm change. B is wrong because an inaudible alarm is effectively disabled. D is wrong because disconnecting monitoring removes surveillance of the patient and is outside the technician's authority in this situation.

questions.question: A tracing is unusable because the left leg lead shows no signal, while the other limb leads record. Checking the electrodes, the technician finds the left leg electrode has lifted off the skin. What is the appropriate response?

answers.text: Interpret leads II and III from the remaining electrodes without repeating
Attach the left leg wire to the right leg electrode so recording can finish quickly
Move V6 to the left leg to substitute for the missing lead
Re-prep the skin, apply a fresh electrode at the left leg site, and repeat the tracing

questions.explanation: D is correct: loss of contact requires restoring proper skin preparation and a fresh electrode at the correct site, then repeating so all leads record. A is wrong because leads II and III require the left leg electrode and cannot be derived without it. B is wrong because sharing one electrode for two limbs produces invalid limb leads. C is wrong because V6 is a precordial electrode and cannot substitute for a limb electrode.

questions.question: An underlying sinus rhythm at 72 bpm (PR 0.16 seconds, QRS 0.08 seconds) is interrupted by wide premature beats of 0.18 seconds. One additional beat looks different from both: it is preceded by a P wave with a shorter PR interval of 0.10 seconds, and its QRS measures 0.12 seconds with a shape halfway between the normal beats and the wide premature beats. What is that in-between beat?

answers.text: A premature atrial contraction with aberrancy, because a P wave before a beat always makes it atrial
A second, unrelated PVC focus, because every non-sinus shape is its own focus
A fusion beat — the sinus impulse and a ventricular impulse activated the ventricles at the same time, blending the two shapes
Artifact on a normal beat, because an intermediate QRS width cannot occur

questions.explanation: C is correct: a fusion beat occurs when an impulse from above and a ventricular ectopic impulse activate the ventricles simultaneously, so the QRS blends both morphologies and measures between the two; the preceding P wave with a shortened PR interval fits the sinus impulse arriving just as the ectopic fires. A is wrong because aberrancy alone would give a bundle-branch pattern from a fully conducted beat, not a shape blended with the PVC morphology after a shortened PR. B is wrong because a separate focus would produce its own consistent shape, not an exact intermediate. D is wrong because fusion beats are a genuine, well-described event with consistent measurements.

questions.question: A technician has helped a patient into a gown and is about to begin chest electrode placement in a room whose door opens onto a busy hallway and is standing ajar, with the curtain pulled only halfway. What should happen before placement begins?

answers.text: Close the door and fully draw the curtain so the patient is shielded from hallway view during placement
Begin placement at once, since the gown alone provides all the privacy required
Ask passing staff in the hallway to avoid looking in while placement is done
Move the patient, still in the gown, to stand behind the exam table for placement

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: securing the physical space — closed door and fully drawn curtain — is the basic privacy safeguard before a patient is exposed for electrode placement. B is wrong because a gown does not shield a patient from view through an open door. C is wrong because relying on passersby to look away is not a privacy safeguard. D is wrong because standing placement is not the position for a resting recording and does not fix the sightline problem.

questions.question: Marcus, an adult patient with a developmental disability, arrives for a resting EKG with his sister, who answers most questions for him. He appears calm and can answer simple questions when given extra time. How should the EKG technician communicate with Marcus?

answers.text: Direct all questions to his sister, since she knows his history best
Speak directly to Marcus in short, simple sentences, allow extra time for answers, and involve his sister only as he wishes or as needed
Use medical terminology so his sister can translate it accurately for him
Skip explanations to Marcus and explain the procedure only after it is finished

questions.explanation: B is correct because developmental level affects communication: speaking directly to the patient in plain, short sentences, allowing extra response time, and including a family member only with the patient's involvement respects his autonomy and improves understanding. A is wrong because directing everything to his sister excludes the patient from his own care. C is wrong because medical terminology makes instructions harder, not easier, for him to follow. D is wrong because explaining afterward denies him the chance to understand and cooperate during the test.

questions.question: On a routine outpatient 12-lead tracing from an adult who feels well, a technician checks the frontal-plane QRS axis, the mean direction of ventricular depolarization, using the net QRS deflections in leads I and aVF. In lead I the QRS is mainly negative, with the S wave deeper than the R wave is tall. In lead aVF the QRS is mainly positive, with the R wave taller than the S wave is deep. How should the technician classify this axis, and what should the technician do next?

answers.text: A normal axis; transmit the tracing to the chart with no further check, because a mainly upright QRS in aVF is expected
Left axis deviation; tell the patient the tracing shows a ventricular conduction disorder and that a specialist must clear the tracing before the patient leaves

Right axis deviation; first verify that the limb electrodes are on the correct limbs and repeat the tracing if any are misplaced, and if the marked deviation persists on a correctly recorded tracing, report the axis finding to the provider
Extreme (northwest) axis deviation; move the precordial electrodes to the right side of the chest and record a right-sided tracing before reporting anything

questions.explanation: C is correct: a mainly negative QRS in lead I with a mainly positive QRS in aVF places the mean QRS axis between +90 and +180 degrees, which is right axis deviation, well outside the normal range of -30 to +90 degrees. Because misplaced limb electrodes can falsely shift the limb-lead axis, the technician first verifies limb-electrode placement and repeats the tracing if any electrode is misplaced; a deviation that persists on a correctly recorded tracing is then reported to the provider, without the technician naming a cause. A is wrong because this quadrant pattern falls outside the normal -30 to +90 degree range, so filing it unchecked could pass a technical error or a genuine finding forward without review. B is wrong because left axis deviation shows the opposite pattern, mainly positive in lead I and mainly negative in aVF, and because telling the patient a diagnosis is outside the technician's scope. D is wrong because extreme axis deviation requires a mainly negative QRS in both lead I and aVF, while aVF here is mainly positive, and moving the chest electrodes changes the precordial view rather than checking the limb-lead axis.

questions.question: At a pre-test screening, a 17-year-old athlete scheduled for exercise testing reports two episodes in the past month of racing, pounding heartbeat during practice that ended with feeling about to pass out. The resting pulse today feels regular. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

answers.text: The episodes can be disregarded because today's resting pulse is regular
The history matters only if the athlete also reports chest pain
Exertional palpitations with near-fainting are a significant history that must be passed to the supervising provider before exercise testing
The technician should clear the athlete because teenagers commonly feel their heart pound

questions.explanation: C is correct: palpitations with near-syncope during exertion can signal a serious rhythm problem and must reach the provider before a stress test adds workload. A is wrong because a normal resting pulse does not erase episodic exertional symptoms. B is wrong because near-fainting with palpitations is concerning even without pain. D is wrong because clearing a patient for exercise testing is outside the technician's scope.

new-york-mpje.quiz_title: New York MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A practitioner in Glens Falls handwrites a paper controlled-substance prescription and asks pharmacist Petra Novak what form the quantity must take on the face of the prescription. What is correct?

answers.text: Quantity may appear in numerals alone, because numerals are unambiguous
Quantity may appear in words alone, because words cannot be altered
Quantity may appear either way, at the prescriber's preference
Quantity must appear in both numeric form and written-word form

questions.explanation: A paper controlled-substance prescription must state the quantity in both numeric form and written-word form, so the two representations check each other on the face of the prescription. Numerals alone and words alone each omit one of the two required representations, and the prescriber has no preference-based option to choose only one.

questions.question: A collaborative protocol in a Schenectady hospital authorizes regimen titration and monitoring but contains no language about laboratory testing. The pharmacist wants to order a disease-state test that would help guide titration. What is correct?

answers.text: The pharmacist may order it because titration implies testing authority
The pharmacist may order it if the laboratory is located inside the facility
The pharmacist may order it only if the protocol specifically authorizes laboratory ordering and the test is necessary
The pharmacist may order it whenever the physician is off site for the day

questions.explanation: Disease-state laboratory tests may be ordered only when specifically authorized by the protocol and only as necessary, so a protocol silent on testing provides no authority. Titration authority does not imply testing authority, the laboratory's location does not supply authorization, and a physician's absence does not expand the protocol.

questions.question: A pharmacist in Buffalo is asked which site could participate in New York collaborative drug therapy management. Which site qualifies on the facts given?

answers.text: A dental clinic that employs a pharmacist part time
A rehabilitation center with a consulting pharmacist
A residential health care facility that contracts for pharmacy services
A nursing home that has an on-site pharmacy staffed by a licensed pharmacist

questions.explanation: A nursing home qualifies only when it has an on-site pharmacy staffed by a licensed pharmacist, alongside teaching and general hospitals and their specified hospital-based settings. Dental clinics and dispensaries are expressly excluded, rehabilitation centers are expressly excluded, and residential health care facilities are expressly excluded even if pharmacy services are contracted.

questions.question: A website-based pharmacy in Oregon takes orders from patients in Buffalo, mails prescription drugs to them weekly, and has never registered with the New York department, arguing that a website has no physical presence in New York. What is the legal assessment?

answers.text: Lawful, because internet sales have no physical presence to register
Lawful for the first 600 prescriptions each year without any application
Lawful if the website discloses that it is not registered in New York
A violation, because an internet pharmacy that ships prescription drugs into New York must be registered with the department

questions.explanation: An internet pharmacy that ships, mails, or delivers prescription drugs into New York must be registered with the department, so ongoing weekly shipments without registration are a violation. Lack of a physical storefront does not remove the registration duty, the isolated-transaction relief requires an application and is not a blanket allowance for this ongoing operation, and disclosing non-registration does not cure it.

questions.question: A product is recalled for a labeling irregularity, and the notice states that use of the product is not likely to cause adverse health consequences. Which recall class fits?

answers.text: Class III
Class I
Class II
No class, because a recall requires proof of death

questions.explanation: A recall where harm is unlikely is a Class III recall. Class I requires a reasonable probability of serious harm or death, and Class II involves temporary or reversible harm, neither of which matches a product unlikely to cause adverse consequences. Proof of death is not required for a recall to be classified.

questions.question: A patient in Buffalo presents after a potential HIV exposure. Under a non-patient-specific order from a licensed physician, what may the pharmacist dispense for post-exposure prophylaxis?

answers.text: A full 28-day course with no further prescriber involvement required by this authority
Up to a 7-day starter pack of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis drugs under the non-patient-specific order or protocol
A single dose only, because starter packs are not authorized
Any antiretroviral the pharmacist selects, in any quantity, for 90 days

questions.explanation: Under a non-patient-specific order or protocol from a licensed physician or certified nurse practitioner, a pharmacist may dispense up to a 7-day starter pack of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis drugs after a potential exposure. That authority is for a starter pack, not a full course or a 90-day supply under this mechanism, and it is more than a single dose.

questions.question: Mid-shift, the pharmacist-in-charge observes that a staff pharmacist is slurring his speech, unsteady, and about to begin final verification of prescriptions, with clear signs of impairment while on duty. What must happen first?

answers.text: He may finish the shift as long as he verifies only non-controlled prescriptions
He should be moved to inventory duties and allowed to verify prescriptions again after lunch
The concern should be documented and raised at the next quarterly staff meeting
He must be removed from dispensing duties immediately, before he verifies or dispenses further prescriptions

questions.explanation: An impaired pharmacist on duty presents an immediate patient-safety risk, so the first step is removing him from dispensing duties at once rather than letting verification continue in any category of prescriptions. Reassigning him temporarily and returning him to verification later the same shift leaves the risk in place, and deferring the response to a future meeting allows an impaired practitioner to keep practicing in the meantime; reporting and recovery or monitoring channels follow from that immediate removal.

questions.question: In Buffalo, an adult recipient with a cognitive impairment is brought for vaccination by a family member, and the pharmacist cannot obtain the recipient's own meaningful consent to the injection. What must the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Follow the written consent and attendance requirements that apply to a person unable to consent before administering
Proceed on the family member's verbal nod alone, with nothing in writing
Vaccinate without any consent because a family member brought the recipient in
Delegate the consent decision to the technician who checked the recipient in

questions.explanation: For a person unable to consent, the pharmacist follows the written consent and attendance rules provided for that situation before administering, rather than improvising a substitute. A verbal nod without the required writing, vaccination with no consent at all, and delegating the consent determination to support staff each bypass those requirements.

questions.question: A practitioner in Manhattan is about to prescribe a Schedule III controlled substance for a patient in the ordinary course of clinic practice, and no exception applies. What does New York require before prescribing?

answers.text: The practitioner shall consult the registry before prescribing a Schedule II, III, or IV controlled substance
The practitioner may consult the registry, but consultation is entirely optional for prescribers
The practitioner must consult the registry only for Schedule II substances, never for Schedule III or IV
The practitioner need not consult if a pharmacist will later dispense the prescription

questions.explanation: Every practitioner must consult the registry before prescribing or dispensing a Schedule II, III, or IV controlled substance, subject to the enumerated exceptions. Consultation is mandatory rather than optional for practitioners, the duty expressly reaches Schedules III and IV as well as Schedule II, and a later pharmacy dispensing does not substitute for the practitioner's own pre-prescribing consultation.

questions.question: A patient asks a pharmacy technician detailed questions about a new medication's side effects and whether it is safe with the patient's other drugs. What should the technician do?

answers.text: Answer the clinical questions if the technician has many years of experience
Offer the pharmacist's counseling and refer the clinical questions to the pharmacist
Answer only the side-effect question and refer the interaction question to the prescriber next month
Tell the patient counseling is optional and hand over the medication without involving the pharmacist

questions.explanation: Technicians may offer the pharmacist's counseling but may not counsel or answer clinical questions; those questions belong to the pharmacist. Experience does not expand a technician into the counseling role, splitting the questions still leaves the technician counseling, and bypassing the pharmacist denies the patient the required clinical review.

questions.question: In Albany, a prescriber hands a patient a routine paper prescription for a non-controlled blood pressure medicine and tells her to take it to pharmacist Nora's pharmacy. No exception is documented and none is claimed. What should Nora do?

answers.text: Decline to dispense from the paper form and ask the prescriber to transmit the prescription electronically
Dispense it, because the mandate applies only to controlled substances
Dispense it, because a patient may always choose a paper prescription instead of an electronic one
Dispense a 30-day supply and require electronic transmission only for any refill

questions.explanation: New York's mandate covers controlled and non-controlled prescriptions alike, so a routine paper prescription outside a statutory exception is not dispensable and the prescriber should transmit it electronically. Limiting the mandate to controlled substances understates its scope, a patient's preference for paper creates no exception, and dispensing even a first supply from the non-exempt paper form does not cure the defect.

questions.question: At one visit a prescriber hands a patient four sequential Schedule II prescriptions, each for a 30-day supply with staggered start dates, for a combined 120 days of therapy. Pharmacist Nadia Brooks is asked to file all four for future filling. What should she do?

answers.text: Accept all four because each prescription individually covers only 30 days
Accept only a set whose combined supply stays within 90 days and return the excess prescription for the prescriber to address
Fill all four immediately so the patient does not need to return
Accept all four if the patient signs a waiver accepting the extra supply

questions.explanation: The combined supply from multiple Schedule II prescriptions issued at one visit may not exceed a 90-day supply, so a four-prescription set totaling 120 days goes beyond the permitted total even though each prescription alone is for 30 days. Filling the entire set at once also defeats the staggered dates, and a patient's waiver cannot expand the prescriber's authority to issue the excess.

questions.question: A pharmacy in Glens Falls cannot obtain the interchangeable biological product that would ordinarily be substituted, but the originally prescribed biological product is in stock and there is no medical emergency. On what terms may the pharmacist dispense the prescribed biological product?

answers.text: At no more than the price that would have been charged for the interchangeable substitute, if the pharmacist agrees to dispense it at that price
At the regular price, with no agreement about price required
At the regular price plus a documented stocking fee
Only after the prescriber issues a new prescription marked for the brand

questions.explanation: When an interchangeable biological product is not available and the prescribed biological product is, substitution is not required if the pharmacist agrees to dispense the prescribed product for a price not exceeding what the interchangeable substitute would have cost. Outside a medical emergency the regular price cannot simply be charged, no stocking fee may be added on top, and no new brand-marked prescription is a condition of this contingency.

questions.question: A man representing an unfamiliar company offers a pharmacy deeply discounted brand-name medication, but the pharmacy cannot confirm the seller is an authorized trading partner. A buyer argues the sealed packaging looks genuine. What is the status of product from this source?

answers.text: It is suspect product from an unverified source and may not be dispensed
It is acceptable stock because sealed packaging proves legitimacy
It may be dispensed to cash-paying patients only
It may be dispensed if the price savings are passed to patients

questions.explanation: Pharmacies must deal only with authorized trading partners, and product offered by a seller whose authorized status cannot be verified is suspect product that must not enter dispensing stock. Intact-looking packaging does not establish a legitimate source, and neither the patient's payment method nor a lower price cures a broken chain of custody.

questions.question: A pharmacist at a community pharmacy in Albany proposes a collaborative arrangement with a nearby physician under which the pharmacist would evaluate walk-in patients, diagnose new conditions, and start new drug therapy on the pharmacist's own assessment, outside any hospital. Why is this proposal not permitted?

answers.text: It is permitted if the physician signs the agreement, because a signed agreement creates collaborative authority in any setting
It is permitted if the pharmacist is board certified, because certification removes the setting limits
It is barred only because the patients are walk-ins; scheduled community-pharmacy patients could be diagnosed

Collaborative drug therapy management is a facility-based demonstration program limited to hospitals and teaching institutions and their affiliates under voluntary written agreements and physician-directed protocols, and a pharmacist may never diagnose or initiate therapy outside a protocol

questions.explanation: Collaborative drug therapy management in New York operates only as a facility-based demonstration program in hospitals, teaching institutions, and affiliates, under a voluntary written agreement and physician-directed protocols, and pharmacists acting under it may not diagnose or initiate therapy outside the protocol. A signed agreement therefore cannot create community-pharmacy authority, board certification addresses qualification rather than the setting limit, and the walk-in character of the patients is not the defect — diagnosis itself is outside the pharmacist's role in this program.

questions.question: A pharmacy returns an unopened, in-date bottle to its wholesaler as a saleable return, and the wholesaler plans to resell it to another pharmacy. A warehouse worker argues that because the bottle is sealed and in date, nothing further is needed before it re-enters commerce. What is required?

answers.text: Nothing further, because a sealed, in-date bottle is automatically saleable
Only a visual check that the outer carton is uncreased
Only the returning pharmacy's assurance that the bottle was stored on a shelf
The saleable return must be verified through the verification system before it can be resold

questions.explanation: Saleable returns must be verified — through the verification router service — before the product can be treated as saleable and resold. A sealed container, an in-date status, a visual carton check, or a storage assurance does not substitute for that verification step. Verification is what allows returned product to re-enter the supply chain with confidence in its legitimacy.

questions.question: Pharmacist Hannah Cole is a party to a collaborative practice agreement authorizing her to adjust doses for enrolled clinic patients. During her lunch break, she asks an experienced pharmacy technician to make a dose adjustment the agreement contemplates, saying she will review it when she returns. What is correct?

answers.text: Make the adjustment, because the agreement covers the clinic's patients regardless of who acts
Do not make the adjustment through the technician, because the agreement delegates the specified functions to the pharmacist party to it, not to support staff
Make the adjustment if the patient has been enrolled for more than a year
Make the adjustment and have the prescriber co-sign the technician's note next week

questions.explanation: The agreement is between the pharmacist and the prescriber and delegates the specified patient-care functions to that pharmacist, so a technician cannot exercise them on the pharmacist's behalf. Enrollment length does not transfer delegated authority to another person, and a later co-signature does not cure an adjustment made by someone the agreement never authorized. The adjustment must wait for, or be performed by, a pharmacist acting within the agreement.

questions.question: Pharmacist Sam Whitaker discovers on June 1 that an unencrypted backup drive containing patient information was lost, and the incident is a breach of unsecured protected health information. His manager proposes finishing a leisurely internal review first and notifying people sometime in the fall. What does breach notification require?

answers.text: Notification only if a patient complains or a newspaper reports the loss
Notification to the pharmacy's wholesaler, which then notifies patients on the pharmacy's behalf
Notification of affected individuals generally within 60 days of discovery, and notification to HHS
No notification, because the drive was lost rather than deliberately stolen

questions.explanation: A breach of unsecured protected health information requires notifying affected individuals, generally within 60 days of discovery, and notifying HHS, so waiting until the fall breaches that timeline. Notification is not triggered only by complaints or publicity, and it is the pharmacy's duty rather than its wholesaler's. An accidental loss is still a breach when unsecured information is involved; deliberate theft is not the only qualifying event.

questions.question: A pharmacy's contract with an outside management company states that the company assumes all responsibility for regulatory compliance, staffing oversight, and recordkeeping. When the board cites serious compliance failures, the pharmacist-in-charge argues the contract transferred his accountability to the company. Is he correct?

answers.text: No. The pharmacist-in-charge's accountability to the board cannot be contracted away to a management company
Yes, because a signed contract binds the board as well as the parties
Yes, because the management company becomes the pharmacist-in-charge once the contract is signed
Yes, unless the board objects in writing within thirty days of the contract

questions.explanation: The pharmacist-in-charge remains accountable to the board for the pharmacy's compliance, security, records, and supervision of personnel, and a private contract with a management company cannot transfer that regulatory accountability. The board is not a party to the contract and is not bound by how the parties allocate duties between themselves, signing a management agreement does not make the company the licensed pharmacist-in-charge, and board silence after a contract is signed does not ratify such a transfer.

questions.question: Pharmacy A performs central processing for Pharmacy B, and a data-entry error made at Pharmacy A leads to a wrong strength being filled and dispensed at Pharmacy B. Pharmacy B's owner argues that because the error originated at Pharmacy A, Pharmacy B bears no responsibility for the dispensed prescription. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Pharmacy B is correct, because responsibility follows the employee who made the original keystroke
Neither pharmacy is responsible, because shared processing divides accountability until it disappears
Only the technician who entered the data is responsible, since pharmacists do not answer for processed orders

Responsibility is allocated under the shared-services arrangement and Pharmacy B, as the dispensing pharmacy operating under its license, retains responsibility for what it dispenses, including its pharmacist's verification

questions.explanation: In a shared-services arrangement each participating pharmacy remains accountable under its own license for the functions it performs, and the dispensing pharmacy cannot shed responsibility for a prescription its pharmacist verified and dispensed merely because an upstream step contributed to the error. Accountability does not vanish when work is shared, does not rest solely on the person who typed the entry, and is not limited to technicians when pharmacists retain verification duties.

pennsylvania-mpje.quiz_title: Pennsylvania MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: The individual permit holder of a pharmacy in State College dies, and the personal representative asks how long an extension of the pharmacy permit may last. What is the maximum?

answers.text: No extension is available and the pharmacy must close at once
At most 6 months from the date of death
At most 2 years from the date of death
At most 1 year from the date of death

questions.explanation: On a permit holder's death, the personal representative may obtain an extension of at most 1 year from the date of death. Six months understates the allowance, 2 years overstates it, and immediate closure ignores the extension the law makes available.

questions.question: Under the direct and immediate personal supervision of the pharmacist on duty in a Scranton pharmacy, which set of tasks may a registered pharmacy technician perform?

answers.text: Accepting a prescriber's telephone prescription and transcribing the order
Counseling a patient on how a new medication interacts with the patient's other drugs
Making the final verification decision on a filled prescription before it is dispensed
Carrying containers, counting tablets into containers, typing and printing labels, and entering prescription information into the patient profile

questions.explanation: Under direct and immediate personal supervision, a Pennsylvania technician may perform mechanical and clerical tasks such as carrying containers, counting pills or tablets into containers, typing or printing labels, maintaining practice records, and entering prescription, drug order, and patient information into a patient profile. Accepting or transcribing an oral order, counseling a patient, and exercising the pharmacist's verification judgment are all outside technician scope.

questions.question: A pharmacist in Erie is asked which setting falls outside Pennsylvania's bar on supplying a Schedule V narcotic cough preparation without a prescription. Which setting is excepted?

answers.text: A retail sale to a regular customer known to the pharmacist
A sale to a traveler who left a prescription at home
A mail-order sale to an established patient
Institutional use

questions.explanation: The prescription requirement for Schedule V narcotic cough preparations carries an exception for institutional use. Familiarity with a retail customer, a traveler's circumstances, and an established mail-order relationship are retail settings, and none of them is the institutional use the rule excepts.

questions.question: A patient declines the pharmacist's offer to counsel on a new prescription. What should happen next?

answers.text: The refusal ends the matter with no record of any kind
The drug must be withheld until the patient accepts counseling
The counseling offer and the patient's refusal should be documented
The technician should counsel the patient instead at pickup

questions.explanation: Counseling itself or the patient's refusal of counseling is documented, which preserves a record that the offer was made. Leaving no record loses that documentation, withholding the drug penalizes a permissible refusal, and a technician cannot be substituted to provide counseling the patient declined from the pharmacist.

questions.question: An inspector finds that a drug product was prepared under insanitary conditions and is contaminated. How is the product classified?

answers.text: Misbranded only, because contamination is a labeling problem
Properly dispensed, because the label is accurate
Adulterated, because it is contaminated and was prepared under insanitary conditions
Recalled as Class III in every case, regardless of the risk presented

questions.explanation: A product that is contaminated or prepared under insanitary conditions is adulterated. Misbranding concerns false or misleading labeling or missing required label information, not contamination of the product itself. An accurate label does not cure adulteration, and recall classification depends on the health risk rather than applying automatically to every adulterated product.

questions.question: Pharmacist Marta Kowalski is counseling a patient on the last fill of a maintenance prescription that has no refills remaining. Which refill counseling should the patient receive?

answers.text: No refill discussion is needed, because the prescription has been filled before
The patient should be told the pharmacy will automatically continue the drug when it runs out
The patient should be told no refills remain and to contact the prescriber before running out, so a new authorization can be obtained in time
The patient should be told to borrow the same drug from a family member if it runs out

questions.explanation: Refill information is a counseling point, and when no refills remain the patient needs to know to contact the prescriber before the supply runs out so therapy is not interrupted. Prior fills do not remove the need for that discussion, the pharmacy cannot continue the drug without authorization, and sharing another person's medication is unsafe and impermissible.

questions.question: A Pennsylvania dispenser submitted information to the monitoring system and, on another occasion, did not seek information from it, in both instances acting under the program law and keeping information confidential. What liability protection applies?

answers.text: The dispenser is civilly liable for not seeking information in all cases
There is no civil liability or licensing discipline for submitting information, or for not seeking or obtaining information, when acting under the program provisions and maintaining confidentiality
Immunity applies only if the dispenser queried before every dispensing
Immunity applies only to prescribers and never to dispensers

questions.explanation: There is no civil liability or licensing discipline for submitting information to the system, or for not seeking or obtaining information from it, when the prescriber or dispenser acts under the program's dispenser and prescriber provisions and keeps information confidential. Liability in all cases for not seeking information contradicts that protection, conditioning immunity on universal querying imports a duty the law does not impose, and the protection covers dispensers as well as prescribers.

questions.question: A pharmacist in Sunbury files a Schedule II prescription in the general prescription file and a Schedule IV prescription in the usual numbered file with no marking, and plans to keep distribution records for 5 years. Which correction is required?

answers.text: No correction, because all prescriptions may share one file and 5 years is the Pennsylvania period

Schedule I and II orders are kept in a file separate from all other records, Schedule III through V orders are kept separately or made readily retrievable by marking the face in red ink with a letter C at least 1 inch high in the lower right corner when filed in the usual file, and distribution records are kept 2 years
Only Schedule II needs a red C marking, and distribution records are kept 7 years
The Schedule IV prescription must be destroyed after filling

questions.explanation: Schedule I and II prescription orders are maintained in a file separate from all other pharmacy records, while Schedule III, IV and V orders are maintained separately or in readily retrievable form, which includes the red-ink C marking at least 1 inch high in the lower right corner when filed in the usual consecutively numbered file. Records of controlled-substance purchases, sales and distributions are kept for 2 years, not 5 or 7 years.

questions.question: During an internal audit in Altoona, pharmacist Grace Liu finds a refill entry that shows the quantity dispensed and the drug, but the entry does not show when the refill occurred or which pharmacist dispensed it. Which elements must each refill record show?

answers.text: The date of the refill, the dispensing pharmacist's name or initials, and the quantity dispensed
The patient's insurance claim number and the prescriber's fax number
The original prescription's expiration date and the technician's initials only
The wholesaler invoice number and the patient's date of birth

questions.explanation: Each refill record must show the date, the name or initials of the dispensing pharmacist, and the quantity dispensed, and this record is missing two of those three elements. Claim numbers and fax numbers, a technician-only entry, and invoice or birth-date data do not supply the required refill-record contents.

questions.question: A registered pharmacy technician applicant in Allentown asks whether any training beyond the board-approved technician program is required as part of qualification. Which additional training does Pennsylvania require?

answers.text: At least 3 hours of approved training in child abuse recognition and reporting
At least 8 hours of training in controlled-substance diversion prevention
A current advanced cardiac life support certification
No additional training of any kind is required beyond the technician program

questions.explanation: Pennsylvania's technician qualification regulation includes at least 3 hours of approved child abuse recognition and reporting training in addition to the age, diploma, training-program, and criminal history elements. Diversion-prevention hours and advanced cardiac life support are not technician qualification elements, and it is incorrect that no additional training is required.

questions.question: Pharmacist Hannah Lee learns that a patient was hospitalized with liver injury two weeks after starting a new drug, but she cannot tell whether the drug caused the injury. What should she do about reporting?

answers.text: Report the serious event through MedWatch even though causality is uncertain
Wait until a specialist proves the drug caused the injury before reporting anything
Report it only if the prescriber agrees the drug was at fault
Do not report it, because uncertain events are excluded from safety reporting

questions.explanation: A pharmacist should report a serious adverse event through MedWatch even when it is uncertain whether the drug caused it, because the reporting system is designed to collect suspected events for evaluation. Waiting for proof of causation or for the prescriber's agreement would defeat that purpose, and uncertainty is not a ground for withholding a serious-event report.

questions.question: A prescriber's office telephones pharmacist Grace Lin with a routine oral prescription for a Schedule III medication for one of the prescriber's established patients. A technician says oral orders are barred for every controlled substance. What is correct?

answers.text: Oral orders are barred for all controlled substances, so a written prescription is required
A routine oral prescription for a Schedule III drug may be accepted from the prescriber's office and reduced to writing; the routine oral-order bar applies to Schedule II
An oral Schedule III order may be accepted only in a true emergency
An oral Schedule III order may be accepted only if the prescriber delivers a signed original within 7 days

questions.explanation: Routine oral orders are barred for Schedule II outside the emergency pathway, but a prescriber's office may phone in an oral prescription for a Schedule III drug through the ordinary telephone-order process. The emergency limitation and the seven-day follow-up duty belong to the emergency oral Schedule II rule, not to a routine Schedule III order.

questions.question: Routine environmental monitoring in pharmacist Ingrid Voss's cleanroom returns results outside the acceptable range for the compounding area. A technician proposes filing the report without comment and continuing the normal compounding schedule indefinitely. What does the quality framework require instead?

answers.text: Discard the result as a presumed laboratory error, with no follow-up of any kind
Stop all environmental monitoring, because the program has now produced a failure
Clean the room once and destroy the monitoring report so the file stays clean
Investigate the out-of-range result, take corrective action, and document the response in the quality records

questions.explanation: Environmental monitoring is part of sterile compounding quality assurance, so an out-of-range result triggers investigation, corrective action, and documentation rather than silent filing. Presuming laboratory error without investigation, ending the monitoring program, or destroying the report each defeat the quality purpose the monitoring serves.

questions.question: A pharmacy director in Philadelphia asks which agency action keeps prescribers and pharmacies informed as interchangeable biological products are added to or deleted from recognition in Pennsylvania, and how often that notice must appear. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: The State Board of Pharmacy must mail a notice to every pharmacy after each individual change
The Department of Health publishes notice in the Pennsylvania Bulletin of additions and deletions of interchangeable biological products at least every 3 months
The Attorney General publishes the notice once a year in a general circulation newspaper
No agency notice is required, because pharmacies must monitor federal listings on their own

questions.explanation: The Department of Health administers the substitution act and publishes notice in the Pennsylvania Bulletin of additions and deletions of generically equivalent drugs and interchangeable biological products at least every 3 months. The duty belongs to the Department rather than to the Board of Pharmacy or the Attorney General, the interval is quarterly rather than annual, and the published-notice duty exists alongside any federal monitoring a pharmacy chooses to do.

questions.question: The only bottle of a maintenance drug on pharmacist Ryan Patel's shelf passed its expiration date yesterday. A technician notes it was stored perfectly, in a sealed container, and proposes printing a new label with a later date so a waiting patient is not inconvenienced. What must the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Refuse the relabeling; expired medication may not be dispensed and must be removed from active inventory
Approve the relabeling, because proper sealed storage preserves a drug past its printed date
Dispense half the quantity, because a smaller amount limits the patient's exposure
Dispense it this once if the patient is told the printed date has passed

questions.explanation: Expired medication may not be dispensed, and expired stock is removed from active inventory; storage conditions and container seals do not extend a manufacturer's expiration date, and staff may not redate the product. Dispensing a partial quantity or disclosing the expired status to the patient does not make an expired drug dispensable. The waiting patient's fill must wait for in-date stock.

questions.question: Pharmacist Samir Haddad must compound a sterile hazardous infusion. The only free workstation is a sterile primary engineering control that provides an ISO-classified work zone but has no hazardous-drug containment features. A colleague argues sterility is the only concern for an infusion. What is correct?

answers.text: Compound there, because sterile technique alone satisfies every standard for an infusion
Compound only where sterile compounding requirements are met inside a containment primary engineering control, because the preparation is both sterile and hazardous
Compound on the open counter instead, because containment matters more than the sterile work zone
Send the infusion out as a nonsterile preparation, because hazardous drugs are exempt from sterile compounding rules

questions.explanation: A sterile hazardous preparation must satisfy the sterile compounding standard and the hazardous-drug standard together, which means sterile conditions provided within containment. Sterility alone ignores occupational exposure, abandoning the sterile work zone ignores the patient's infection risk, and a hazardous infusion does not become nonsterile or exempt because it is hazardous.

questions.question: A patient with a terminal illness who is being cared for at home has a Schedule II prescription for 90 tablets. Pharmacist Grace Liu's pharmacy has only 30 tablets today. The patient will need the medication continuously over the coming weeks. Which plan fits the federal partial-fill rules?

answers.text: Supply the 30 tablets now and provide the remaining installments in partial fills spread over the next 60 days, up to the prescribed quantity
Decline to dispense anything until the full 90 tablets are in stock, because partial fills are not allowed for patients at home
Supply the 30 tablets and treat the remaining 60 as refills that can be drawn down over the next six months
Supply the 30 tablets and complete the balance within 72 hours, the same deadline that applies to every partial fill

questions.explanation: Partial fills of a Schedule II prescription for a terminally ill patient may be provided in installments over 60 days rather than being confined to the ordinary 72-hour remainder rule. The installments are not refills — Schedule II prescriptions have no refills — and the 72-hour deadline is the standard outpatient rule, not the one governing terminally ill or long-term care patients.

questions.question: A board inspector arrives at pharmacist Paul Mercer's pharmacy at mid-morning, while the pharmacy is open and dispensing, and asks to inspect the pharmacy's prescription records. The store manager proposes telling the inspector that records can only be reviewed after closing, when staff are less busy, and that she should return that evening. How should Paul respond?

answers.text: Agree, because inspectors may enter only when the pharmacy is closed to patients
Agree, because a pharmacy may set any single weekly hour for record inspection
Refuse access until the pharmacy's attorney can be present the following week
Make the records available, because the board's inspection authority operates during the pharmacy's business hours and prescription records must be available for inspection then

questions.explanation: Boards exercise entry and inspection authority during business hours, and prescription records must be available for inspection during those hours rather than only at the pharmacy's convenience. Postponing to after closing, inventing a weekly inspection hour, or conditioning access on counsel arriving days later all defeat the during-business-hours standard.

questions.question: Over several months, a pharmacist repeatedly releases filled prescriptions to patients without performing any pharmacist review of the filled product, despite being reminded of the board's practice rules, and documents that checks were done when they were not. Which ground for discipline most directly fits this pattern?

answers.text: Unprofessional conduct, including violating board rules governing practice
No ground, because no ground exists until a patient proves injury in a malpractice suit
Only a federal ground, because dispensing standards are set exclusively by the FDA
A ground exists only if the pharmacist also held an expired license during the same period

questions.explanation: Repeatedly bypassing required pharmacist review and falsifying the record of it is unprofessional conduct and a violation of board rules, both recognized grounds for discipline. Board discipline does not wait for a malpractice judgment or proof of injury, because the board protects the public through licensure standards. Dispensing practice standards are enforced by the state board, and an expired license is a separate ground that need not be present.

questions.question: A community pharmacy uses a central processing service that enters prescription data and performs an initial clinical review, after which the order returns to the community pharmacy for filling. The store's manager proposes that the filling pharmacist skip personal verification of these orders because the central site already reviewed them. Is the proposal acceptable?

answers.text: Yes, because one pharmacist verification anywhere in the chain satisfies the requirement for the whole process
No, because pharmacist verification is retained at each step, and the pharmacist at the dispensing pharmacy must still verify the order before it is dispensed
Yes, provided the central processing site keeps a log showing its review was completed
No, because central processing of prescription data is prohibited in all circumstances

questions.explanation: Shared and central processing arrangements operate under the responsible pharmacy's license with pharmacist verification retained at each step, so a review upstream does not retire the dispensing pharmacist's own verification duty. A central-site log documents the earlier step but does not substitute for the final check, and central processing itself is a permitted arrangement rather than a prohibited one when it is properly authorized.

georgia-mpje.quiz_title: Georgia MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A pharmacist is found working while impaired and diverting controlled substances, creating an immediate risk to patients who will be served that same day. What expedited board action is available?

answers.text: Summary suspension of the license where there is imminent danger
No action until the pharmacist is convicted of a felony
A product recall issued by the board for the diverted drugs
Transfer of the pharmacist's license to another state board for review

questions.explanation: A board may summarily suspend a license where imminent danger is present, rather than waiting for the ordinary timeline to run while patients remain at risk. A felony conviction is a separate ground and process and is not a prerequisite for this expedited action, a recall addresses products rather than a dangerous licensee, and transferring the license does not protect the public the board serves.

questions.question: A Columbus pharmacy is receiving a transferred prescription from another store, and the sending pharmacy calls to convey it. The pharmacist is verifying a fill nearby. Who at the receiving pharmacy may take the transfer?

answers.text: The senior registered technician, because receiving information is a clerical task
The technician on duty, if the sending pharmacy is part of the same chain
A pharmacist or intern, because a technician may not receive a transferred order
Either the technician or the pharmacist, whichever answers first

questions.explanation: Taking a transferred order is receiving a prescription drug order, and Georgia prohibits technicians from transferring orders in either direction, including the receiving end. Chain affiliation and the pharmacist's proximity do not change that limit, and characterizing the call as clerical does not make it a technician task. A pharmacist or intern must handle the communication.

questions.question: A Georgia pharmacist launches an advertising campaign urging members of the general public to ask for a specific prescription-only drug by name. Which statement best describes this conduct under the discipline statute?

answers.text: It is permitted because advertising is commercial speech with no pharmacy-law limit
Promoting prescription-only drugs to the public is a ground for discipline
It is a ground only if a patient is actually harmed by the advertised drug
It is governed solely by federal advertising law, with no Georgia disciplinary consequence

questions.explanation: Promoting prescription-only drugs to the public is an enumerated ground for discipline under Georgia's pharmacist discipline statute. It is not insulated as ordinary advertising, it does not require proof that a patient was harmed by the drug, and Georgia law supplies its own disciplinary consequence rather than leaving the matter entirely to federal advertising rules.

questions.question: A pharmacy installs receiving software that automatically rewrites certain fields of incoming electronic prescriptions to match the pharmacy's internal formatting before the pharmacist sees them. Why is this arrangement improper?

answers.text: It is improper only if the software also changes the price charged to the patient
An electronic prescription's content may not be altered by the pharmacy's receiving system; the prescription must reach the pharmacist as the prescriber transmitted it
It is acceptable as long as the changes make the directions easier to read
It is improper only when the prescription is for a non-controlled drug

questions.explanation: A valid electronic prescription is transmitted directly from the prescriber's system without intermediaries or receiving systems altering its content. Readability improvements are still alterations of what the prescriber sent, pricing is unrelated to content integrity, and the no-alteration principle is not limited to one drug category.

questions.question: A new pharmacist in Decatur is building a label template for controlled-substance dispensing. Which addition belongs on that template because the drug is a controlled substance?

answers.text: The date the prescription was written in place of the fill date
Cautionary statements
A statement of the patient's diagnosis
The name of the technician who counted the tablets

questions.explanation: Cautionary statements are one of the three additions required on a controlled-substance label, together with the pharmacy telephone number and the expiration date of the dispensed drug. A diagnosis statement and the counting technician's name are not label requirements, and the added elements supplement rather than replace the ordinary fill-date information.

questions.question: A patient returns to the pharmacy asking pharmacist Elena Ruiz to refill a Schedule II pain medication because one refill remains noted in the patient's own records. What must the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Explain that Schedule II prescriptions have no refills and a new prescription from the prescriber is required
Refill it once and document the patient's request
Refill it if the prescriber gave verbal permission last month
Transfer the refill from another pharmacy that filled it previously

questions.explanation: Schedule II prescriptions may never be refilled, so continued therapy requires a new prescription from the prescriber. A single courtesy refill is still a prohibited refill, verbal permission from an earlier encounter does not create a refill, and a Schedule II prescription can never be transferred between pharmacies.

questions.question: An audit shows pharmacist David Kim has been taking controlled substances from his employer's stock for his own use over several months and altering counts to conceal the shortage. Which exposure best describes his situation?

answers.text: He faces only an internal employment review, because the drugs were for personal use
He faces board discipline and potential criminal exposure for the diversion
He faces exposure only if a patient received a shorted prescription
He is protected from discipline if he enters treatment voluntarily afterward

questions.explanation: Diverting controlled substances, including for personal use, and falsifying counts to conceal it are grounds for board discipline, and the same conduct can also carry criminal exposure because civil, administrative, and criminal tracks are independent. Personal use does not confine the matter to an employer review, patient harm is not a prerequisite, and later treatment does not erase the disciplinary and criminal consequences, though boards may address impairment through monitoring.

questions.question: A scheduled stock examination at a pharmacy in Newnan turns up a deteriorated device and several outdated drugs, which a technician proposes returning to the dispensing shelves after wiping the containers. What is the correct handling?

answers.text: Return them to the shelves if they still look usable
Dispense the outdated drugs first to clear them from inventory
Sell the deteriorated device at a discount with a warning
Remove them from dispensing stock, because an expired or deteriorated drug or device may never be dispensed

questions.explanation: Stock examinations exist to pull outdated and deteriorated items out of circulation, and an expired or deteriorated drug or device may never be dispensed, so the items must be removed from dispensing stock. Appearance of usability does not restore an outdated product, dispensing outdated drugs first and discount-selling a deteriorated device both put barred items into patients' hands.

questions.question: A pharmacist-in-charge in Warner Robins proposes shredding signed pseudoephedrine logbooks after one year and letting experienced sales staff skip training because they have sold the products for years. What does Georgia require?

answers.text: Logbooks may be shredded after one year if the pharmacy keeps a summary count of sales
The signed logbook must be retained at least two years, and pharmacy personnel who sell these products must complete the DEA self-certification training
Logbooks must be retained five years, and only pharmacists need any training to sell the products
No logbook retention period applies, because the logbook is a federal formality with no Georgia requirement

questions.explanation: The signed pseudoephedrine logbook must be retained at least two years, and pharmacy personnel selling these products must complete the DEA self-certification training, so experience does not excuse the training and one year is too short for the records. A summary count does not replace the retained logbook, a five-year period overstates the retention while wrongly narrowing who needs training, and the logbook carries a Georgia retention requirement rather than none.

questions.question: A patient in Griffin presents a refill of a medication on which appropriate counseling was already given at the original dispensing. How is counseling on this refill governed in Georgia?

answers.text: Counseling is mandatory in full on every refill regardless of prior counseling
Counseling is prohibited on refills
A technician must counsel on every refill
Counseling on refills rests on the dispensing pharmacist's professional judgment, and it is not required for a refill on which appropriate counseling has already taken place or been declined

questions.explanation: Under the Georgia counseling rule, refill counseling is governed by the dispensing pharmacist's professional judgment and is not required for a refill on which appropriate counseling has already taken place or been declined. A full mandatory session on every refill, a technician-delivered requirement, and a prohibition on refill counseling all misstate that judgment-based rule.

questions.question: At a pharmacy in Valdosta, pharmacy intern Sarah Lindqvist is working under the direct supervision of the pharmacist on duty when a patient picking up a new prescription needs professional consultation. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An intern may never provide professional consultation under any circumstances
An intern may consult only if a registered technician is also present at the counter
An intern may consult only when the supervising pharmacist has left the premises
An intern under direct supervision may provide professional consultation and counseling

questions.explanation: Georgia reserves professional consultation and counseling to a pharmacist or an intern under direct supervision, so a supervised intern may counsel the patient. A blanket ban on intern counseling misstates that authority, a technician's presence is not a condition of it, and counseling while the pharmacist is away inverts the direct-supervision requirement.

questions.question: A patient is picking up a first prescription for ophthalmic drops and tells pharmacist Mateo Reyes she has never used eye drops before. Which part of counseling is most directly required by her situation?

answers.text: A review of the pharmacy's return policy for opened eye products
A demonstration and explanation of how to instill the drops correctly, as part of counseling on the dosage form and its administration
A comparison of the drop's price with the ointment form of the same drug
Instructions to share the bottle with a spouse who has similar eye symptoms

questions.explanation: Counseling includes the dosage form and route of administration, so a first-time user of ophthalmic drops should be shown and told how to instill them correctly. Return policies and price comparisons are not administration counseling, and sharing a prescription eye product with another person is improper rather than a counseling point.

questions.question: At final check, pharmacist Luis Herrera sees that a sealed, properly stored vial ready for a patient was labeled without several pieces of information the dispensed container label is required to carry. The drug itself is sound and in date. How is the drug in this container classified?

answers.text: Adulterated, because any labeling omission changes the drug's quality
Counterfeit, because the container came from the pharmacy rather than the manufacturer
Misbranded, because a dispensed container missing required label information makes the labeling deficient
Acceptable for dispensing, because labeling omissions matter only for over-the-counter products

questions.explanation: A drug whose labeling is missing required information is misbranded, and a dispensed prescription container that lacks required label information renders the drug misbranded even when the product itself is sound. Adulteration concerns contamination, decomposition, or quality defects in the drug itself, counterfeiting concerns falsified product or identity, and required labeling applies to dispensed prescriptions as well as over-the-counter products.

questions.question: The pharmacist-in-charge of a Douglasville pharmacy learns that the employment information the Board holds for two of the pharmacy's registered technicians no longer matches who actually works there. Whose duty is it to keep that registry information current, and what must the pharmacist-in-charge do?

answers.text: Each technician's own duty only, with no role for the pharmacist-in-charge
The pharmacy owner's duty only, because the owner holds the permit
The pharmacist-in-charge's duty; the pharmacist-in-charge must keep the Board's technician-registry information current
No one's duty until the Board asks for an update at renewal

questions.explanation: Georgia places the duty on the pharmacist-in-charge to keep the Board's technician-registry information current for the pharmacy. Technicians have their own update obligations, but those do not erase the pharmacist-in-charge's registry duty, and the permit holder's status does not transfer it to the owner alone. Waiting for a renewal inquiry also fails the ongoing duty to keep the information current.

questions.question: A mail-service pharmacy prepares a refill shipment of a drug for which a Medication Guide is required. The operations manager proposes saving the printing cost by noting on the invoice that the guide is available on the manufacturer's website. What must the pharmacy do?

answers.text: Print the website address more prominently so patients can find the guide
Enclose the Medication Guide with the drug in the shipment
Send the guide only with the first shipment and omit it from refills
Ask the patient to request the guide if she wants a copy

questions.explanation: A required Medication Guide must be dispensed with the drug, which for a mail shipment means enclosing it in the package. Directing the patient to a website does not satisfy the duty to provide the guide with the medication. The obligation is not limited to a first fill, and it does not depend on the patient requesting a copy.

questions.question: At a Sandy Springs pharmacy, pseudoephedrine products are stocked on an open aisle shelf, and a sales clerk proposes selling a customer enough product to total 4 grams in one day, recording it in a logbook the store discards each year. Which statement identifies the Georgia violations in this plan?

answers.text: There are none, because pseudoephedrine is not a controlled substance in Georgia
Pseudoephedrine must instead be sold in the emergency department of a hospital

The plan violates Georgia law because the products must be stored in the prescription department, sales are capped at 3.6 grams per 24 hours, and the signed logbook must be retained at least two years
The only violation is the storage location, because Georgia sets no quantity caps for pseudoephedrine

questions.explanation: Pseudoephedrine is an exempt Schedule V substance in Georgia, and its products must be stored in the prescription department and sold only by a pharmacist, intern, or extern under direct supervision. Sales are capped at 3.6 grams per 24 hours and 9 grams per 30 days per customer, with a government photo identification check and a signed logbook retained at least two years. The plan therefore fails on storage, on the daily quantity cap, and on logbook retention, and hospital-only sale is not the rule.

questions.question: A prescriber's office faxes a signed Schedule II prescription to pharmacist Ingrid Solberg for a walk-in outpatient who is not in long-term care, hospice, or home infusion. The patient asks to pick it up tonight and says the paper original will be dropped off next week. What must happen?

answers.text: The fax alone authorizes immediate dispensing for any patient
The patient may take a three-day supply and return with the original for the rest
The pharmacist may dispense once the prescriber confirms the fax by telephone
The pharmacist must have the signed original prescription before dispensing to this patient

questions.explanation: Outside the long-term care, hospice, and home-infusion exceptions, a fax does not serve as the original Schedule II prescription, so the signed original must be presented before dispensing to an ordinary outpatient. A fax alone, a partial supply pending the original, and a telephone confirmation do not substitute for that original in this setting.

questions.question: An internal audit at pharmacist Ben Carter's pharmacy establishes that one of its own technicians has been diverting controlled substances over several months. The store manager proposes handling the matter quietly as an internal personnel issue, with no outside report, since the loss was discovered by the pharmacy itself. What must the pharmacy do?

answers.text: Follow the manager's plan, because internally discovered losses need not be reported
Report the significant loss to the DEA in writing within one business day of discovery, because theft or diversion by an employee is still a reportable significant loss
Wait until the technician's final paycheck is issued, then decide whether to report
Report only if a local newspaper learns of the diversion first

questions.explanation: Theft or significant loss of controlled substances must be reported to the DEA in writing within one business day of discovery, and diversion by the pharmacy's own employee is a significant loss even though the pharmacy discovered it internally. Handling the matter as a purely internal personnel issue, tying the report to payroll timing, or waiting for press attention all miss the one-business-day duty.

questions.question: Pharmacist Sara Lindqvist fills a prescription exactly as written, with no dispensing error of any kind. The patient's profile documents a condition that makes this drug unusually risky for this particular patient, but she says nothing about the risk, and the patient is harmed by it. In the resulting lawsuit, her defense is that an accurate fill ends a pharmacist's responsibility. How does that defense fare?

answers.text: It succeeds, because liability requires a miscount, wrong drug, or wrong strength
It succeeds, because the learned-intermediary doctrine shields dispensing pharmacists the same way it shields manufacturers
It succeeds, because warning about risks is solely the prescriber's legal duty
It fails, because a pharmacist's duty extends beyond accurate filling, and a pharmacist who knows of a patient-specific risk and fails to warn can be liable

questions.explanation: A pharmacist's duty is not exhausted by filling accurately; it extends to drug utilization review and counseling, so knowing of a patient-specific risk and remaining silent can create liability even when the correct drug and strength were dispensed. Limiting liability to physical dispensing errors ignores that broader duty, the learned-intermediary doctrine generally shields manufacturers rather than a dispensing pharmacist aware of the individual risk, and the prescriber's own duties do not erase the pharmacist's.

questions.question: On Monday morning, pharmacist Sarah Kim finds that the refrigerator holding insulin and vaccines warmed above its labeled range for several hours over the weekend. A technician has already returned the products to the refrigerator and suggests simply resuming dispensing, since the vials look normal. What should the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Resume dispensing, because appearance is a reliable test of temperature damage
Discard every product in the refrigerator immediately without recording anything
Backdate the weekend temperature log so the record appears continuous
Document the temperature excursion in the monitoring records and set the affected products aside pending an assessment of their condition before any dispensing

questions.explanation: Drugs must be stored at their labeled conditions, refrigerator temperatures are monitored, and excursions are documented, so the weekend event belongs in the monitoring record and the affected products should be held from dispensing until their condition is assessed. A normal appearance does not establish that a temperature-sensitive product remained usable. Discarding stock without documentation destroys the record of the event, and backdating the log falsifies the monitoring history the pharmacy is required to keep.

new-jersey-mpje.quiz_title: New Jersey MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: The New Jersey Board contracts with an outside testing service to help prepare and grade its licensure examinations. Who retains the authority to determine which applicants have passed?

answers.text: The testing service makes the final pass determination for each applicant
The Governor reviews and approves each passing determination
The Board retains sole discretion and responsibility for determining which applicants passed
Each applicant's pharmacy school certifies whether its graduates passed

questions.explanation: Even when the Board contracts for examination preparation or grading, it retains sole discretion and responsibility for determining which applicants passed. The testing vendor does not make the final determination, the Governor plays no role in individual pass decisions, and pharmacy schools do not certify examination passage.

questions.question: A pharmacist in New Brunswick counsels a patient starting a new oral medication. Which set of points falls within the counseling topics New Jersey enumerates?

answers.text: Only the price of the medication and the pharmacy's return policy
The name and description of the medication, and its dosage form, dosage, route of administration, and duration of therapy
Only the prescriber's qualifications and office hours
The patient's insurance deductible and the pharmacy's store hours

questions.explanation: The enumerated counseling topics include the name and description of the medication and its dosage form, dosage, route of administration, and duration of therapy. Price, return policy, prescriber credentials, insurance amounts, and store hours are not among the enumerated clinical counseling topics.

questions.question: A clinic wants to begin sending electronic controlled-substance prescriptions to pharmacist Priya Shah's pharmacy. Before the pharmacy may receive and process those orders, what must be true of the pharmacy's own system?

answers.text: It must be DEA-compliant software for electronic controlled-substance prescriptions
It only needs a working fax line as a backup channel
It must be the same brand of software the clinic uses
Nothing special is required; any e-prescribing inbox may receive them

questions.explanation: Electronic prescribing of controlled substances requires DEA-compliant software on the receiving side as well as the sending side, so the pharmacy's system must meet those requirements before it receives and processes such orders. A fax backup and brand matching are irrelevant to that compliance, and an ordinary inbox without the required safeguards is not sufficient.

questions.question: A pharmacist in Cherry Hill asks a registered technician for help starting a refill. Which task may the technician perform?

answers.text: Decide whether the refill is therapeutically appropriate for the patient
Call the prescriber to change the medication to a stronger strength
Retrieve the prescription file, patient profile, and other Board-determined records the pharmacist needs
Counsel the patient on how the medication should be taken

questions.explanation: Technicians may assist with retrieval of prescription and patient files, profiles, and other Board-determined records. Judging therapeutic appropriateness requires the pharmacist's professional judgment, changing a strength is a prescriber and pharmacist matter rather than a technician task, and patient counseling is expressly outside technician duties.

questions.question: A prescriber sends a prescription for clozapine, a drug subject to a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program. What must the pharmacist do before dispensing?

answers.text: Dispense it as an ordinary prescription with no special conditions
Waive the program conditions because the patient has taken the drug before
Follow the special dispensing conditions imposed by the drug's REMS program
Substitute a different antipsychotic that has no program conditions

questions.explanation: REMS programs impose special dispensing conditions, and drugs such as clozapine and isotretinoin under its program must be dispensed in compliance with those conditions. Prior use by the patient does not waive the conditions, and treating the prescription as ordinary ignores the program. Substituting a different drug is a prescriber decision, not a way to bypass the requirements for the drug prescribed.

questions.question: A patient starting a new medication asks what problems to watch for and how to know the therapy is working. Which counseling content answers her within New Jersey's enumerated topics?

answers.text: Common adverse or severe side effects, interactions, and therapeutic contraindications, including their avoidance and the action to take if they occur, plus techniques for self-monitoring of drug therapy and any special directions and precautions for preparation, administration, and use
Only a statement that all medications carry some risk, with no specifics
A referral to read the manufacturer's advertising material
