An explanation of the pharmacy's dispensing fees and delivery charges

questions.explanation: The enumerated topics include common adverse or severe side effects, interactions, and therapeutic contraindications, including their avoidance and the action to take if they occur, techniques for self-monitoring of drug therapy, and special directions and precautions for preparation, administration, and use. A vague risk statement, advertising material, and fee information do not supply that enumerated content.

questions.question: An extern in Jersey City is helping in the dispensing area while the supervising pharmacist reviews labels from a private office outside that area and does not inspect the finished containers. Which requirement is not being met?

answers.text: No requirement is missed, because an extern may complete the final label check alone
The pharmacist may supervise from any room in the building as long as a phone is available
Immediate personal supervision requires the pharmacist to be physically present in the dispensing area and to conduct in-process and final checks, including of the finished label
Only the pharmacist-in-charge may ever look at a finished label, so the supervising pharmacist should not check it at all

questions.explanation: Immediate personal supervision requires physical presence in the compounding and dispensing area together with in-process and final checks, expressly including the finished label. An extern does not supply that check alone, telephone availability from another room is not physical presence in the area, and the duty belongs to the supervising pharmacist performing the supervision rather than being reserved exclusively to the pharmacist-in-charge.

questions.question: After a Toms River pharmacy's permit is revoked, its drug stock is placed under seal. The owner wants to dispose of the sealed stock right away to recover its value, although the time to appeal has not run. What is the rule?

answers.text: The owner may dispose of the stock after 30 days whether or not an appeal is pending.
The owner may donate the sealed stock to a charitable clinic immediately.
Sealed items generally may not be disposed of until Administrative Procedure Act appeal rights expire or an appeal is determined.
The Board must purchase the sealed stock at fair market value.

questions.explanation: Items placed under seal generally may not be disposed of until the Administrative Procedure Act appeal rights expire or an appeal is determined, so the owner's wish to recover value does not permit immediate disposal or donation. There is no 30-day free-disposal window and no obligation for the Board to buy the stock.

questions.question: A newly registered pharmacy in Newark asks what standard governs its controlled dangerous substances records and inventories, and how often a CDS inventory must be taken. Which answer is correct?

answers.text: Records and inventories follow the pharmacy's own internal policy, and an inventory is required only when stock is moved
Records and inventories must conform to federal recordkeeping and inventory requirements, inventoried once every 5 years
Records and inventories are governed solely by a freestanding New Jersey inventory code that displaces federal law

Records and inventories must conform to the recordkeeping and inventory requirements of federal law plus any additional rules issued by the Director, and a CDS inventory must be taken every 2 years (on May 1 for a registrant registered on or before May 1, 1971, otherwise every 2 years from first registration)

questions.explanation: The CDS Act incorporates the federal standard: registrants must keep records and maintain inventories in conformance with federal recordkeeping and inventory requirements, plus any additional rules issued by the Director, rather than under a freestanding State code or internal policy. The inventory is biennial — every 2 years, anchored to May 1 for registrants registered on or before May 1, 1971 and otherwise running every 2 years from the date first registered — not a 5-year cycle.

questions.question: A patient in Cherry Hill lawfully keeps a prescribed CDS at home for use by a member of her household and for administration to the family's dog. Which status describes her under the CDS Act?

answers.text: She is a distributor because others may use the medication
She is a practitioner because she administers medication to an animal
She is an ultimate user, because she lawfully possesses the CDS for her own use, for a household member's use, or for administration to an animal owned by her or a household member
She is an unregistered dispenser because the medication was not consumed by her alone

questions.explanation: An 'ultimate user' is a person who lawfully possesses a CDS for the person's own use, for the use of a member of the person's household, or for administration to an animal owned by the person or a household member. Lawful household and animal use within the definition does not make her a distributor, practitioner, or dispenser.

questions.question: A pharmacy mails most prescriptions to patients who live far from the store. The manager proposes dropping the counseling offer for mailed orders because the patient is not at the counter. What is correct?

answers.text: The offer is unnecessary whenever a prescription leaves the store by mail or delivery
Dispensing by mail or delivery does not eliminate the offer to counsel; the offer is made by telephone for delivered prescriptions
The offer can be replaced by the delivery driver's explanation of the medication
The offer applies only to the first mailed order and not to any later ones

questions.explanation: The duty to offer counseling follows the dispensing, not the patient's physical presence, so a mailed or delivered prescription still requires the offer, made by phone. A delivery driver cannot provide the pharmacist's counseling, and the offer is not a one-time courtesy limited to a first order.

questions.question: A patient returns to the pharmacy asking pharmacist Elena Ruiz to refill a Schedule II pain medication because one refill remains noted in the patient's own records. What must the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Explain that Schedule II prescriptions have no refills and a new prescription from the prescriber is required
Refill it once and document the patient's request
Refill it if the prescriber gave verbal permission last month
Transfer the refill from another pharmacy that filled it previously

questions.explanation: Schedule II prescriptions may never be refilled, so continued therapy requires a new prescription from the prescriber. A single courtesy refill is still a prohibited refill, verbal permission from an earlier encounter does not create a refill, and a Schedule II prescription can never be transferred between pharmacies.

questions.question: A prescription arrives for a drug whose Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program requires pharmacies to be specially certified to dispense it. This pharmacy has never enrolled in that program, though its pharmacists have dispensed similar drugs for years. What must happen first?

answers.text: The pharmacy may dispense once and complete enrollment afterward
Any licensed pharmacist on staff may dispense it because licensure satisfies the program
The pharmacy must be enrolled and certified in the drug's REMS program before it may dispense the drug
The pharmacy may dispense if the prescriber confirms enrollment is unnecessary

questions.explanation: Where a REMS program conditions dispensing on pharmacy certification, enrollment and certification are prerequisites that must be in place before the pharmacy dispenses the drug. Dispensing first and enrolling later reverses that order, general pharmacist licensure does not substitute for program certification, and a prescriber cannot waive a dispensing condition the program imposes on the pharmacy.

questions.question: During a stock inspection, pharmacist Grace Okafor finds a bottle whose contents show visible breakdown from age and heat exposure, with discolored, crumbling tablets. A staff member asks whether the product can still be dispensed at a discount. How is this product classified, and what follows?

answers.text: It is merely mislabeled, so it may be dispensed once a new label is printed
It is a recalled product, so it may be dispensed until the recall notice arrives
It is an expired generic, so it may be dispensed if the patient consents in writing
It is adulterated because the drug has decomposed, and it may not be dispensed

questions.explanation: A drug that has decomposed is adulterated, and adulterated product may not be dispensed, discounted or otherwise. Relabeling addresses labeling defects rather than decomposition, a recall notice is not what creates this defect, and a patient's written consent does not make an adulterated drug dispensable.

questions.question: A prescription names a specific drug product, and the pharmacy stocks only a version of the drug made with a different salt form. A staff member proposes dispensing the stocked version as the generic substitute because the active ingredient name looks nearly the same. What should pharmacist Laura Bennett do?

answers.text: Decline to treat the different salt form as an interchangeable generic substitute for the prescribed product
Dispense the different salt form, because any product sharing the same base drug name is interchangeable
Dispense the different salt form if it is priced lower than the prescribed product
Dispense half the quantity of the different salt form as a trial until the prescriber's office reopens

questions.explanation: A different salt form of a drug is a different product, not an interchangeable generic substitute for the prescribed product, so it may not be dispensed as a substitution. A similar base name and a lower price do not create interchangeability, and dispensing a partial trial quantity of a different product is still an unauthorized substitution.

questions.question: A patient in Hackensack continues to receive an opioid for chronic pain from the same prescriber over many months. How often must the prescriber or an authorized person access the patient's prescription monitoring information during that continued treatment?

answers.text: Only at the first prescription
Every twelve months
Every three months (quarterly) during the period the patient continues to receive the prescription
Never, once the first check is documented

questions.explanation: For a patient who continues to receive a Schedule II CDS or opioid for acute or chronic pain, or a Schedule III or IV benzodiazepine, the practitioner or authorized person must access prescription monitoring information on a quarterly basis, every three months, during the period the patient continues to receive the prescription. A first-prescription-only, annual, or no-further-check approach understates the prescriber duty.

questions.question: Pharmacist Renata Cole learns that a well-known local official fills controlled substances at a competitor pharmacy. Out of curiosity, and with no prescription pending for that person, she considers looking the official up in the prescription drug monitoring program. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The lookup is permissible, because pharmacists may browse program data for anyone in their community
The lookup is permissible if she tells no one what she finds
The lookup is permissible once, as long as she documents her curiosity as the reason
The lookup is improper, because program access is limited to authorized purposes such as a dispensing decision, and the data is confidential

questions.explanation: Monitoring program data is confidential and access is limited to authorized purposes; curiosity about a person for whom the pharmacist has no dispensing decision is not such a purpose. Keeping the results secret does not cure an unauthorized access, because the access itself is the violation. Documenting an improper reason does not convert curiosity into an authorized use.

questions.question: A prescriber's electronic prescribing system sends a new prescription through a network service that routes the message, unchanged, directly into pharmacist Sofia Marino's pharmacy system, where she can read every field exactly as the prescriber entered it. A colleague objects that any service between the two systems destroys the prescription's status. How should the prescription be treated?

answers.text: As invalid, because a valid electronic prescription may pass through no network of any kind
As a telephone order, because it arrived through a communications service
As a fax prescription, subject to the rules for paper facsimiles
As a valid electronic prescription, because it was transmitted directly from the prescriber's system without an intermediary altering its content

questions.explanation: The validity requirement is that an electronic prescription be transmitted directly from the prescriber's system and not be converted or altered by an intermediary, and routing that leaves the content exactly as entered satisfies that requirement. Ordinary network transmission is how such prescriptions travel and does not invalidate them, and a message that was never converted to a fax image or phoned in is neither a fax nor a telephone order.

questions.question: A patient-specific compounding pharmacy has filled about twenty prescriptions a month for an established preparation over the past year. The owner directs the compounder to prepare five hundred units in advance, explaining that a new clinic opening nearby is expected to triple demand. How much may the pharmacy compound in advance?

answers.text: Five hundred units, as long as the preparation is stored under labeled conditions
Only a limited quantity supported by the pharmacy's history of valid prescriptions received for the preparation; an expected-demand forecast does not justify a large speculative stockpile
Five hundred units, if the clinic's medical director confirms the expected volume in writing
A full year's projected supply, which is the customary advance-compounding allowance

questions.explanation: Anticipatory compounding is limited to quantities grounded in the pharmacy's history of valid prescriptions actually received, so a forecast of future demand cannot support a stockpile far beyond that demonstrated history. Proper storage does not cure an excessive quantity, a prescriber's written prediction is still a prediction rather than prescription history, and there is no standard allowance to compound a year's projected supply in advance.

questions.question: A new pharmacist-in-charge, Carla Nguyen, is writing her pharmacy's privacy and security compliance plan. She lists staff privacy training and access policies, locked record rooms and controlled workstation placement, and unique user logins with encryption for electronic records. Which framework do these three groups represent?

answers.text: The three classes of recall the pharmacy must be ready to handle
The administrative, physical, and technical safeguards HIPAA requires for protected health information
The three categories of sterile compounding environments
The three schedules of drugs the pharmacy may stock without additional registration

questions.explanation: HIPAA safeguards fall into administrative safeguards such as training and access policies, physical safeguards such as locked record areas and workstation controls, and technical safeguards such as unique user identification, access controls, and encryption. The three groups in the plan match those safeguard categories. They do not describe recall classes, sterile compounding categories, or drug scheduling tiers.

alabama-mpje.quiz_title: Alabama MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Recent graduate Lena Kovacs took her national licensing examination after designating Alabama for score transfer, and she asks whether she must retake that examination to be licensed in Alabama. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: She must retake the national examination in Alabama regardless of the designation
She is licensed automatically once the score is transferred, with no further testing or interview
She must pass an Alabama practical examination but is excused from any law examination
She need not take an additional national examination, but she must still take the Alabama pharmacy law examination, earn an average of 75, and participate in a Board oral interview

questions.explanation: When Alabama was designated for score transfer at the time of the examination, the Board may license without an additional national examination, but the applicant must still take the Alabama pharmacy law examination with an average of 75 and participate in a Board oral interview.

questions.question: A prescriber confirms to pharmacist Robert Hayes by phone that the quantity and directions on a Schedule II prescription should both be revised to match a new dosing plan. What may the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Refuse both changes because no Schedule II element may ever be altered
Change only the directions and leave the quantity permanently unchanged
Change both the quantity and the directions after that prescriber consultation
Change both without documenting any prescriber contact, to save time

questions.explanation: Quantity and directions are elements a pharmacist may change on a Schedule II prescription after consulting the prescriber. Refusing all changes and changing only one of them both understate that permitted authority, while making the changes without prescriber consultation removes the condition that makes them permissible.

questions.question: A prescriber telephones in a prescription for a biological product to pharmacist Sam Ortiz, but the caller never mentions substitution. What is required of an oral or electronic prescription of this kind?

answers.text: It must instruct the pharmacist whether or not a less expensive interchangeable biological product may be dispensed
It needs no substitution instruction, because oral orders are always filled with the brand product by default
It needs a substitution instruction only when the patient is paying cash
It must be converted to a written prescription before any substitution instruction can apply

questions.explanation: An oral or electronic prescription for a biological product must instruct the pharmacist whether or not a less expensive interchangeable biological product may be dispensed. The instruction is part of the order itself, not an optional add-on.

questions.question: A company that is not physically part of any licensed healthcare facility wants to provide centralized services to an institutional pharmacy serving Alabama facility patients. Does it need an institutional pharmacy permit?

answers.text: Yes, an institutional pharmacy permit is required for a pharmacy that is not a physical portion of a licensed facility but provides centralized services to an institutional pharmacy
No, because only pharmacies inside a facility building can hold that permit
No, because centralized services are exempt from permitting
Yes, but only if it also operates a retail storefront open to the public

questions.explanation: An institutional pharmacy permit is required not only for a pharmacy that is a physical portion of a licensed healthcare facility, but also for a pharmacy that is not a physical portion of such a facility yet provides centralized services to an institutional pharmacy. Lack of a facility address does not remove the permit requirement.

questions.question: A Mobile pharmacy repeatedly fails to transmit its database reports, and the health department becomes aware of the gap. Under the reporting rule's compliance mechanism, what happens next?

answers.text: The department notifies the appropriate licensing board of the failure to report, and that board investigates and reports the outcome back to the department
The department fines the pharmacy directly without involving any licensing board
The pharmacy's wholesaler is ordered to suspend all shipments permanently
Nothing happens unless a patient files a complaint

questions.explanation: Licensing boards supply the database program, monthly or as designated, an electronic listing of the entities and practitioners required to report, and the program monitors that list for compliance. When a failure to report is found, the department notifies the appropriate licensing board, which investigates and reports the outcome to the department.

questions.question: An authorized representative of a state certifying board asks the database for information about a physician who is licensed by a different board, explaining that the physician sometimes works with her board's licensees. How is board access limited?

answers.text: A certifying board may access information about any practitioner who works in the state

Access is limited to information concerning licensees of that certifying board, with medical-examiner representatives also able to inquire about mid-level registrants holding the controlled-substances registration certificate
A certifying board may access any record if it gives the other board written notice first
A certifying board may access only de-identified aggregate information

questions.explanation: Authorized representatives of a certifying board may access database information concerning licensees of that board. Representatives of the Board of Medical Examiners may additionally inquire about certified registered nurse practitioners and certified nurse midwives holding the controlled-substances registration certificate.

questions.question: A single pharmacist is on duty in a retail prescription department. The manager wants four technicians working with that pharmacist and wants one of them to log a newly arrived controlled substance into inventory. Which arrangement complies with Board rule?

answers.text: Four technicians may work with no certification requirement, and a technician may log the controlled substance receipt
Four technicians may work only if two of them are certified, and a technician may not document receipt of the controlled substance into inventory
Only two technicians may ever work with one pharmacist, regardless of certification
Four technicians may work if one is certified, and the senior technician may log the controlled substance receipt

questions.explanation: Board rule permits four technicians per pharmacist only when two are certified, and technicians are expressly prohibited from documenting the receipt of a controlled substance into inventory.

questions.question: Pharmacist Hannah Lee learns that a patient was hospitalized with liver injury two weeks after starting a new drug, but she cannot tell whether the drug caused the injury. What should she do about reporting?

answers.text: Report the serious event through MedWatch even though causality is uncertain
Wait until a specialist proves the drug caused the injury before reporting anything
Report it only if the prescriber agrees the drug was at fault
Do not report it, because uncertain events are excluded from safety reporting

questions.explanation: A pharmacist should report a serious adverse event through MedWatch even when it is uncertain whether the drug caused it, because the reporting system is designed to collect suspected events for evaluation. Waiting for proof of causation or for the prescriber's agreement would defeat that purpose, and uncertainty is not a ground for withholding a serious-event report.

questions.question: A man in Mobile is convicted of practicing pharmacy without first obtaining a license from the Board, and no other penalty is specifically provided for his conduct. What criminal exposure does he face?

answers.text: A Class A misdemeanor with a fine of not more than $500 for each offense
A Class B misdemeanor, with a fine of not more than $1,000 for each offense, and the court may in its discretion also sentence him to hard labor for the county for not more than 12 months
A Class C felony with a mandatory term of imprisonment
A civil infraction punishable only by a fine of not more than $10,000

questions.explanation: Practicing pharmacy without first obtaining a license, permitting prescriptions to be compounded or dispensed by unauthorized persons, or willfully violating the chapter or a Board rule where no other penalty is specifically provided is a Class B misdemeanor. On conviction the fine is not more than $1,000 for each offense, and the court may in its discretion add hard labor for the county for a period not to exceed 12 months.

questions.question: A pharmacy hires two beginners on the same day: a first-time intern/extern permit applicant and a first-time technician registration applicant. The manager asks about criminal background checks for the pair. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Only the intern applicant is subject to a background check, and the Board pays for it
Both applicants must consent to a Board-approved criminal background check at the applicant's own cost
Neither applicant may be asked for a background check until after a full renewal cycle
Background checks apply only to applicants with a prior out-of-state license

questions.explanation: An intern/extern applicant consents on initial application to a Board-approved criminal background check at the applicant's cost, and each technician applicant must likewise consent to and be subject to such a check at the applicant's cost as a prerequisite to registration or reinstatement.

questions.question: While reconciling a rejected transmission in Troy, pharmacist Noah Bennett checks which identifiers the database submission is required to carry for each dispensing. Which of the following must be included in the transmitted information?

answers.text: The National Drug Code of the controlled substance dispensed
The name of the patient's employer
The patient's diagnosis code for the condition being treated
The pharmacy's wholesaler account number

questions.explanation: Transmitted prescription information must include the prescribing practitioner's identifying designation, the date the prescription was filled or medication dispensed, the name and full address of the person for whom it was written or to whom it was dispensed, the National Drug Code of the substance dispensed, the quantity dispensed, the dispensing pharmacy or practitioner, other elements consistent with the national pharmacy automation standards as designated by regulation, and the method of payment with third-party payor identification. The National Drug Code is one of those required elements.

questions.question: A trustee schedules a public auction that will include a failed store's stock of narcotics and dangerous drugs, and the sale is not the ordinary-course sale of a pharmacy as a business. What notice and reporting does the seller owe the Board?

answers.text: Written notice of the sale at least one week before the sale day, and a complete written report within 10 days after the sale identifying the parties who received any narcotics, exempt narcotics, or dangerous drugs, with an itemized inventory
Notice only if the Board asks about the sale afterward
A telephone call to the Board on the morning of the sale, with no later report
A report within 60 days after the sale, with buyer names kept confidential from the Board

questions.explanation: In a sale in bankruptcy, at public auction, or any other sale except in the normal course of business, the seller must give the Board written notice at least one week before the sale and make a complete written report within ten days after the sale showing the names and addresses of parties to whom any narcotics, exempt narcotics, or dangerous drugs were sold, with an itemized inventory. The bona fide sale of a pharmacy as a business, with the Board notified of the proposed sale, is excepted.

questions.question: Pharmacist Daniel Okafor is the only pharmacist scheduled at a Montgomery store on Saturday morning. The district manager asks him to also cover a second store across town during the same hours by phone and video, with both stores open for dispensing. What limit applies to Daniel's coverage?

answers.text: He may cover both stores so long as a registered technician is present at each one
He may have personal supervision of only one pharmacy at the same time, so both stores cannot be open under his supervision at once
He may cover both stores if neither store compounds sterile preparations
He may cover both stores for up to three hours before another pharmacist must relieve him

questions.explanation: Every pharmacy, when open for business, must be under the personal supervision of a duly licensed pharmacist, and that pharmacist may have personal supervision of not more than one pharmacy at the same time. Remote check-ins do not multiply the one-pharmacy limit.

questions.question: A prescriber's office faxes a prescription for a non-controlled medication directly to pharmacist Rachel Kim's pharmacy. The fax shows the prescriber's name printed by the office software, but the prescriber has not signed it by hand. What makes a faxed prescription of this kind valid?

answers.text: It is valid as sent, because a printed name carries the same weight as a signature on a fax
It is valid if the patient confirms the prescriber intended to send it
It is valid once a technician initials the fax to show it was received
It is valid when it originates from the prescriber's office and bears the prescriber's manual, handwritten signature

questions.explanation: A faxed prescription must originate from the prescriber's office and bear the prescriber's manual signature or a compliant electronic signature. A software-printed name is not that signature, a patient's confirmation cannot supply the prescriber's signing act, and a technician's receipt initials document arrival rather than prescriber authorization.

questions.question: Pharmacist Hannah Cole is a party to a collaborative practice agreement authorizing her to adjust doses for enrolled clinic patients. During her lunch break, she asks an experienced pharmacy technician to make a dose adjustment the agreement contemplates, saying she will review it when she returns. What is correct?

answers.text: Make the adjustment, because the agreement covers the clinic's patients regardless of who acts
Do not make the adjustment through the technician, because the agreement delegates the specified functions to the pharmacist party to it, not to support staff
Make the adjustment if the patient has been enrolled for more than a year
Make the adjustment and have the prescriber co-sign the technician's note next week

questions.explanation: The agreement is between the pharmacist and the prescriber and delegates the specified patient-care functions to that pharmacist, so a technician cannot exercise them on the pharmacist's behalf. Enrollment length does not transfer delegated authority to another person, and a later co-signature does not cure an adjustment made by someone the agreement never authorized. The adjustment must wait for, or be performed by, a pharmacist acting within the agreement.

questions.question: Pharmacist Ben Whitaker must compound a hazardous drug into a nonsterile ointment for a named patient, manipulating the drug's powder to incorporate it into the base. A technician suggests that because the ointment is nonsterile, only the nonsterile standard matters. What is correct?

answers.text: Both the nonsterile compounding standard and the hazardous-drug standard apply, because the preparation is nonsterile and the drug is hazardous and manipulated
Only the nonsterile standard applies, because a hazardous drug loses its hazardous character in an ointment base
Only the sterile standard applies, because manipulating a powder is treated as aseptic work
Neither standard applies, because a prescription for a named patient exempts the preparation

questions.explanation: The preparation is nonsterile compounding and it involves manipulating a hazardous drug, so the nonsterile standard and the hazardous-drug standard apply together, including containment, protective equipment, and decontamination duties. Incorporation into a base does not strip a drug of its hazardous character, powder manipulation for an ointment is not sterile compounding, and a patient-specific prescription is the normal basis for compounding rather than an exemption from its standards.

questions.question: During a remodel of a Huntsville pharmacy, operations manager Dana Ruiz proposes moving legend-drug stock into a locked cage in the public retail aisle to free up back-room space. Pharmacist Luis Herrera is asked whether the plan is acceptable. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: The plan is acceptable because the cage would remain locked at all times
Legend drugs must be stored within the confines of the prescription department or its storage room
The plan is acceptable if the relocated stock is entered in the pharmacy's inventory log
The plan is acceptable during business hours, provided the stock is returned each night

questions.explanation: Legend drugs must be kept within the confines of the prescription department or its storage room. Placing them in a public retail area, even in a locked cage, does not satisfy that storage requirement.

questions.question: A patient telephones a compounding pharmacy about a first-time, customized preparation her prescriber says he will order later today. The prescription itself has not yet reached the pharmacy, and the compounder wants to begin making her preparation now so it is ready the moment the order arrives. What governs the timing?

answers.text: Patient-specific compounding for her begins only after the pharmacy receives her prescription; the separate anticipatory-compounding allowance does not cover a first-time preparation with no prescription history behind it
Compounding may begin as soon as the patient describes what the prescriber intends to order
Compounding may begin once the prescriber's office confirms by phone that an order is planned, with no prescription ever required
Compounding may begin a full day in advance for any preparation a patient requests by name

questions.explanation: Traditional compounding is patient-specific, so compounding an individual patient's preparation begins once the pharmacy has received that patient's prescription. A patient's description of an intended order is not a prescription, a prescriber's stated plan does not eliminate the prescription requirement, and the limited anticipatory allowance rests on a history of valid prescriptions for an established preparation, which a first-time custom order does not have.

questions.question: A patient asks to move the remaining refills of a Schedule III prescription to pharmacist Sofia Marino's pharmacy. The original pharmacy emails Sofia a completed transfer form with all refill details, but no pharmacist from that pharmacy ever speaks with her, and its pharmacist says the form 'says everything.' Under the original federal transfer framework, what is missing?

answers.text: Nothing; a complete written form carries the same weight as a conversation between pharmacists

Direct communication of the transfer information between the transferring pharmacist and the receiving pharmacist; refill information for a Schedule III through V transfer is communicated pharmacist-to-pharmacist
A countersignature from the prescriber authorizing the change of pharmacy
A new prescription from the prescriber, since Schedule III refill information cannot move between pharmacies at all

questions.explanation: Under the original transfer rules, Schedule III through V refill information is communicated directly between the pharmacist giving up the prescription and the pharmacist receiving it; an unattended form with no pharmacist-to-pharmacist communication does not meet that standard. No prescriber countersignature or new prescription is required for a transfer of refills that remain valid.

questions.question: The owner of a retail pharmacy chain offers a physician a salaried position whose stated purpose is to enter into collaborative practice agreements with the chain's pharmacists. A second offer would hire a different physician only to perform quality-assurance reviews of collaborative pharmacists. How do the two offers compare?

answers.text: Both offers are prohibited
Both offers are permitted
The agreement-purpose employment is prohibited, while hiring a physician for quality-assurance reviews of collaborative pharmacists is not prohibited
The agreement-purpose employment is permitted, while the quality-assurance hiring is prohibited

questions.explanation: A retail pharmacy may not employ a physician for the purpose of maintaining, establishing, or entering into a collaborative practice agreement. Hiring a physician to perform quality-assurance reviews of collaborative pharmacists is expressly not prohibited.

colorado-mpje.quiz_title: Colorado MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A new intern asks what initial interpretation means in Colorado dispensing practice. Which answer is correct?

answers.text: Checking only that the container is sealed
Counting tablets at the final check
The review of an order accompanied by order entry, with the pharmacist conducting it accountable for entry accuracy and drug regimen review
Delivering the finished prescription to the patient

questions.explanation: Initial interpretation is the review of an order accompanied by order entry, and the pharmacists conducting it are accountable for the accuracy of the electronic entry or manual transcription and for drug regimen review. Sealing checks, counting, and delivery belong to later dispensing steps. The definition centers on order review and regimen review, not on physical handling alone.

questions.question: A facility applying for registration stores controlled substances. What must it show about its premises?

answers.text: Nothing about controlled substances is relevant to registration
Only a promise to buy a safe within the first year is required
A locked car trunk used for overflow storage satisfies the standard
It must have adequate and proper facilities for handling and storing controlled substances and maintain proper control over them so they are not illegally dispensed or distributed

questions.explanation: An applicant for registration must have adequate and proper facilities for handling and storage of controlled substances and maintain proper control over them to ensure they are not illegally dispensed or distributed. Controlled-substance readiness is therefore part of registration rather than irrelevant. Vehicle overflow storage and a deferred promise to buy a safe do not show presently adequate facilities and control.

questions.question: Why does a patient profile include date of birth or age and gender, in addition to medication history?

answers.text: To determine the patient's prescription copay
To support prospective review screens that depend on age and gender, along with the medication history
To decide whether child-resistant packaging is requested
To replace the need for any prospective review

questions.explanation: Age or date of birth and gender in the profile support prospective review screens for age and gender contraindications, and medication history supports interaction and duplication screens. Copay, packaging requests, and eliminating prospective review are not the purposes for which those profile elements are maintained.

questions.question: Which operation qualifies for the central fill supervision ratio?

answers.text: A non-hospital, non-public-facing pharmacy that only acts as agent of an originating pharmacy to fill or refill a prescription
A retail pharmacy that also takes walk-in customers between mail orders
Any hospital inpatient pharmacy with a busy dispensing volume
A wholesaler that ships stock to pharmacies

questions.explanation: A central fill pharmacy is a non-hospital, non-public-facing pharmacy that only acts as agent of an originating pharmacy to fill or refill prescriptions. Hospital status and direct public service both take an operation outside that definition. A wholesaler distributes stock rather than filling patient prescriptions as another pharmacy's agent.

questions.question: Before denying an application or revoking a registration, what process must the board or administration provide?

answers.text: An order to show cause stating the grounds and directing appearance at a time and place not less than thirty days after service, and a renewal refusal must be served not later than thirty days before expiration, with the existing registration staying in effect while that proceeding is pending
A telephone call giving the registrant one week to respond
No notice, because registration is a privilege
A notice served the day after the registration expires

questions.explanation: Due process in this scheme runs through a written order to show cause with at least thirty days between service and the directed appearance, and renewal refusals carry their own thirty-day-before-expiration service deadline while the existing registration continues during the proceeding. A one-week phone call and after-expiration notice both fail the timing rules. The privilege label does not erase the process the statute prescribes.

questions.question: Intern Carla's approved curriculum places her with a registered nurse whose professional scope overlaps a pharmacist's scope in the activities she performs. How are those hours treated?

answers.text: They count double because two professions are involved
They never count, because no non-pharmacist can ever supervise intern hours
They count only if the nurse also holds technician certification
They can count, because direct supervision by a regulated individual whose scope overlaps a pharmacist's, as part of an approved curriculum, is a recognized route

questions.explanation: Intern hours may be earned under the direct supervision of a regulated individual, such as a nurse, dentist, physician, or veterinarian, when the placement is part of an approved curriculum and that individual's scope overlaps a pharmacist's scope. Non-pharmacist supervision is therefore not automatically disqualifying. Technician certification for the supervisor is not the stated condition, and overlapping-scope hours are credited normally rather than doubled.

questions.question: A newly licensed Colorado pharmacist tells a colleague that her state license now lets her handle controlled substances to the full extent she wishes, regardless of her federal registration. Why is that incorrect?

answers.text: State licensure expands federal controlled-substance authority
A state license or registration does not entitle the holder to handle controlled substances beyond the scope of the holder's federal registration
Federal registration is irrelevant once a state license issues
Controlled substances require only a state outlet registration, never federal registration

questions.explanation: Issuance of a Colorado license or registration does not entitle the holder to wholesale, manufacture, distribute, dispense, or professionally use controlled substances beyond the scope of the holder's federal registration, so the federal scope remains the ceiling. State licensure therefore does not expand federal authority, and federal registration cannot be treated as irrelevant. A state outlet registration alone likewise does not substitute for the federal registration that defines the permitted scope.

questions.question: A pharmacy opens a detached building across the parking lot, not a satellite, where its pharmacists will provide pharmacist care services. What registration is required for that area?

answers.text: None, because the main outlet's registration covers every nearby building
Only a local business license
A separate registration for the area outside the outlet where pharmacist care services are provided
Registration is required only if controlled substances will be stored there

questions.explanation: A separate registration is required for any area outside the outlet that is not a satellite where pharmacist care services are provided. The main registration therefore does not automatically blanket nearby buildings. A local business license is not the Board registration, and the duty turns on the care services provided rather than on controlled-substance storage.

questions.question: A manufacturer applying for Colorado registration shows weak safeguards against diversion of controlled substances and little past experience maintaining anti-diversion controls. How should the Board evaluate those facts?

answers.text: They are irrelevant because registration is purely ministerial
They matter only after the registration has been granted and a violation occurs
The Board may consider only the applicant's Colorado tax status

The Board considers maintenance of effective controls against diversion and the applicant's past experience and existing anti-diversion controls when deciding whether issuance is consistent with the public interest

questions.explanation: The public-interest review for manufacturer and wholesaler registration expressly includes maintenance of effective controls against diversion of controlled substances and the applicant's past experience in, and existing controls for, that area. Registration is therefore not purely ministerial, diversion-control weakness is considered at the application stage, and tax status is not the sole or stated criterion.

questions.question: A licensed psychologist who holds prescriptive authority asks whether the opioid limits law's prescriber definition reaches that practice. What is the answer?

answers.text: Yes, a licensed psychologist with prescriptive authority is included in the definition
No, psychologists are never included
Only if the psychologist also holds a medical license
Only for benzodiazepines, never opioids

questions.explanation: A licensed psychologist with prescriptive authority is included in the prescriber definition for the limits law. Never-included and dual-license answers both deny an express addition to the list. The inclusion is not split so that it covers one drug class but not the other.

questions.question: Patient Maria Santos is relocating and asks pharmacist Ben Whitaker to send the remaining refills of her non-controlled blood pressure prescription to a pharmacy near her new home. What is the proper response?

answers.text: Refills on a non-controlled prescription can never move between pharmacies
Honor the patient's request and transfer the remaining refill information to the new pharmacy
The prescriber must reissue the prescription in the new city before any refill moves
Transfer only if the patient has filled at the original pharmacy for a full year

questions.explanation: A patient may have the remaining refills of a transferable prescription, including a non-controlled maintenance prescription, transferred to a new pharmacy at the patient's request, with the refill information communicated between the pharmacies. No rule confines non-controlled refills to the original store or conditions transfer on a year of history. Reissuance by the prescriber is unnecessary where refills remain.

questions.question: Pharmacist Jordan knows a prescription was not issued in the usual course of professional practice, but the prescriber demands that it be filled exactly as written. What should Jordan do?

answers.text: Fill it because a prescriber's demand overrides the pharmacist's judgment
Not fill it as a valid prescription, because the pharmacist shares responsibility for whether it was issued for a legitimate medical purpose in the usual course of practice
Fill it and shift all responsibility to the patient who requested it
Fill it once and refuse all future prescriptions from that prescriber without review

questions.explanation: Corresponding responsibility means the pharmacist shares responsibility with the prescriber for a prescription's legitimacy, so a known illegitimate order is not valid to fill on demand. A prescriber's demand and a patient's request do not override that shared responsibility, and refusing all future orders without review substitutes a blanket rule for the required prescription-by-prescription judgment.

questions.question: A new prescription for pharmacist Jonas Weber names the patient and the drug, gives a quantity and directions, and is dated and signed, but states no strength, and the drug is marketed in several strengths. The patient says, 'Just use the strength I had last year.' What must Jonas do?

answers.text: Dispense the strength from the patient's prior-year fill
Dispense the lowest marketed strength as the safest default
Dispense the most commonly stocked strength and note the assumption
Contact the prescriber to establish the intended strength before dispensing, because drug strength is a required element the pharmacist cannot assume from the patient's history

questions.explanation: A valid prescription must state the drug name and strength, and a missing strength cannot be supplied by copying an old fill, defaulting to the lowest or most common strength, or relying on the patient's recollection. The pharmacist must establish the intended strength with the prescriber before dispensing.

questions.question: Patient Harold Finch learns that the tablets he prefers were recalled and asks pharmacist Becca Nolan to sell him one of the recalled bottles anyway, offering to sign a waiver accepting the risk. The bottles are still in the back room. What must Becca do?

answers.text: Sell one bottle once the signed waiver is placed in Harold's file
Refuse, because recalled stock is quarantined and may never be dispensed, even at the patient's insistence
Sell one bottle at a discount with extra counseling about the recall
Sell one bottle if Harold's prescriber telephones approval that day

questions.explanation: Recalled stock is quarantined and may not be dispensed, and a patient's insistence, waiver, discount arrangement, or prescriber call does not restore recalled product to dispensable status. The refusal protects the patient regardless of how willing the patient is to accept the risk.

questions.question: During an end-of-day review, pharmacist Daniel Okafor discovers that a drug dispensed that morning, for which a Medication Guide is required, left the pharmacy without the guide because the bag was sealed before it was added. The patient is reachable by phone. What should Daniel do?

answers.text: Note the omission in a log and wait until the patient's next refill to include the guide
Contact the patient promptly to provide the required Medication Guide for the dispensed drug rather than leaving the patient without it until a later fill
Take no action, because the patient can find the same information on the manufacturer's website
Ask the patient to return the medication so the entire dispensing can be voided and repeated

questions.explanation: A required Medication Guide must be dispensed with the drug, so discovering that a dispensing went out without it calls for promptly getting the guide to the patient, not deferring it to a future refill. A website reference does not satisfy the duty to provide the guide with the medication, a log entry alone leaves the patient without required information, and voiding a dispensing the patient already has does not itself put the guide in the patient's hands.

questions.question: Pharmacist Ben Whitaker must compound a hazardous drug into a nonsterile ointment for a named patient, manipulating the drug's powder to incorporate it into the base. A technician suggests that because the ointment is nonsterile, only the nonsterile standard matters. What is correct?

answers.text: Both the nonsterile compounding standard and the hazardous-drug standard apply, because the preparation is nonsterile and the drug is hazardous and manipulated
Only the nonsterile standard applies, because a hazardous drug loses its hazardous character in an ointment base
Only the sterile standard applies, because manipulating a powder is treated as aseptic work
Neither standard applies, because a prescription for a named patient exempts the preparation

questions.explanation: The preparation is nonsterile compounding and it involves manipulating a hazardous drug, so the nonsterile standard and the hazardous-drug standard apply together, including containment, protective equipment, and decontamination duties. Incorporation into a base does not strip a drug of its hazardous character, powder manipulation for an ointment is not sterile compounding, and a patient-specific prescription is the normal basis for compounding rather than an exemption from its standards.

questions.question: On the same day, pharmacist Aisha Khan learns of a serious reaction to a newly dispensed non-vaccine drug and a serious reaction following a vaccine given at the pharmacy. A colleague proposes filing both events together through MedWatch for simplicity. What is correct?

answers.text: Each event goes to its own channel: the drug reaction through MedWatch and the vaccine reaction through VAERS
Both events go through VAERS, because they were learned of on the same day
Only the drug event is reported, because one federal report per day is permitted
Both events are handled by a single call to the vaccine manufacturer

questions.explanation: Federal adverse-event reporting separates the channels by product type, with drug events reported through MedWatch and vaccine events through VAERS, even when they surface on the same day. Filing both through either single system misroutes one of them. No one-report-per-day limit applies on these facts, and a manufacturer call does not replace either federal submission.

questions.question: Pharmacist Dana Whitfield needs to send a patient's prescription information to the patient's prescriber to coordinate therapy, submit a claim to the patient's health plan, and use records internally to review dispensing quality. The patient has signed no special authorization form. May the pharmacy do these things?

answers.text: Yes, protected health information may be used and disclosed for treatment, payment, and health care operations without patient authorization
No, every use or disclosure of protected health information requires a signed patient authorization first
Only the internal quality review is allowed, because treatment and payment disclosures always need authorization
Only if the patient first pays a disclosure processing fee set by the pharmacy

questions.explanation: Protected health information may be used and disclosed for treatment, payment, and health care operations without patient authorization, which covers coordinating care with the prescriber, billing the health plan, and internal operations review. A blanket authorization requirement would block those routine functions, and no disclosure fee is a precondition for them.

questions.question: A registrant reassigns a staff member away from ordering duties and tells her in the hallway, in front of a witness, that she may no longer sign controlled-substance orders. Nothing is put in writing. The staff member signs an order the following week, explaining that she believed her authority was still in place. Which statement best describes the revocation problem?

answers.text: There is no problem, because an oral statement in front of a witness revokes the authority
There is no problem, because reassignment to other duties automatically revokes a power of attorney
The authority ended when the registrant stopped scheduling the employee for ordering shifts
The revocation was not properly accomplished, because a power of attorney for controlled-substance ordering is revoked in writing

questions.explanation: Revocation of a power of attorney to sign controlled-substance orders must be made in writing; an oral hallway statement, even if witnessed, does not accomplish it. A job reassignment or a change in shift scheduling likewise does not by itself revoke the written grant. The registrant should issue a written revocation so the end of signing authority is documented.

questions.question: Pharmacist Sam Whitaker discovers on June 1 that an unencrypted backup drive containing patient information was lost, and the incident is a breach of unsecured protected health information. His manager proposes finishing a leisurely internal review first and notifying people sometime in the fall. What does breach notification require?

answers.text: Notification only if a patient complains or a newspaper reports the loss
Notification to the pharmacy's wholesaler, which then notifies patients on the pharmacy's behalf
Notification of affected individuals generally within 60 days of discovery, and notification to HHS
No notification, because the drive was lost rather than deliberately stolen

questions.explanation: A breach of unsecured protected health information requires notifying affected individuals, generally within 60 days of discovery, and notifying HHS, so waiting until the fall breaches that timeline. Notification is not triggered only by complaints or publicity, and it is the pharmacy's duty rather than its wholesaler's. An accidental loss is still a breach when unsecured information is involved; deliberate theft is not the only qualifying event.

connecticut-mpje.quiz_title: Connecticut MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Pharmacist Fran reviews the sign posted at the dispensing counter about substitution. What must it look like and say in substance?

answers.text: A sign easily seen at the dispensing counter, in block letters not less than one inch high, stating the pharmacy may be able to substitute a less expensive therapeutically equivalent drug product or interchangeable biological product unless the patient does not approve
A handwritten note of any size behind the register
A sign posted only in the pharmacy's back office
A sign in letters at least three inches high mentioning only generic drugs

questions.explanation: The substitution sign must be easily seen at the dispensing counter and printed in block letters not less than one inch high, conveying that the pharmacy may be able to substitute a less expensive therapeutically equivalent drug product or interchangeable biological product unless the patient does not approve. Back-office posting, smaller handwriting, and generic-only wording all miss the requirement.

questions.question: Immediately after administering a vaccine under protocol, pharmacist Rosa Delgado completes the record of the administration. Which set of details belongs in that documentation?

answers.text: Only the patient's name and the date, since product details are kept by the wholesaler
The patient's insurance claim number and the pharmacy's register total for the day
The date of administration, the vaccine's lot number, and the site of administration, as part of the documented record
A note that a vaccine was given, with product details added at the end of the quarter

questions.explanation: Immunization practice includes documenting each administration with the identifying details of the event, including the date, the lot number of the vaccine given, and the administration site. A name-and-date-only entry, billing data, or a vague note reconstructed months later do not create the record needed to trace a specific dose to a specific patient.

questions.question: A hospital prescriber enters an original order for a Schedule II drug and wants it to run for three weeks without further action. What limits the order?

answers.text: Hospital Schedule II orders may run 30 days
They expire after 24 hours
They run until discharge with no limit
Original and continuing Schedule II hospital orders are limited to 7 days from entry, extendable for additional 7-day periods by the prescriber signing or initialing the order

questions.explanation: Original and continuing hospital orders for Schedule II substances are limited to seven days from entry and may be extended for additional seven-day periods only by the prescriber signing or initialing the order. Thirty days is the outer limit for Schedule III, IV, and V hospital orders, 24 hours is the oral-order confirmation window, and an unlimited until-discharge duration contradicts the seven-day limit.

questions.question: Pharmacist Morgan fills a controlled substance prescription written by a dentist. A trainee checks the dispensing label and asks which elements it must show. Which list is complete?

answers.text: The prescriber's full address and the patient's date of birth instead of the serial number
Pharmacy name only
Patient name and drug name only

The pharmacy's name and address, the patient's full name, the prescriber's last name, the directions, the prescription serial number, the date of filling or refilling, and any legally required cautionary statement

questions.explanation: The pharmacist's dispensing label must show the pharmacy's name and address, the patient's full name (or for an animal, the owner's name and the species), the prescriber's last name, the directions, the serial number, the date of filling or refilling, and any cautionary statement required by law. Pharmacy name alone and a two-item list omit required elements, and swapping in a full address and birth date does not replace the serial number, and no one may alter, deface, or remove that label.

questions.question: A pharmacist commits three separate unlawful patient consultations. How are they counted under the default criminal penalty rule?

answers.text: As one combined offense
Consultations can never be offenses
Each instance of patient contact or consultation in violation is a separate offense
Only the first consultation counts

questions.explanation: Under the default penalty rule, each instance of patient contact or consultation in violation is a separate offense. The three consultations are therefore counted individually rather than combined into one, consultations can constitute offenses, and later instances count alongside the first.

questions.question: A hospice patient in a long-term care facility needs a Schedule II medication, and the pharmacy can supply only part of the quantity today. Over what period may the remaining partial fills be provided for this patient?

answers.text: Only within 72 hours, with no exception
Only on the day the prescription was written
Up to 6 months from the issue date
Up to 60 days, because terminally ill and long-term care patients have an extended partial-fill period

questions.explanation: For terminally ill and long-term care facility patients, Schedule II partial fills are permitted over 60 days. The ordinary 72-hour remainder rule does not govern this patient category, same-day-only filling is not the standard, and six months is the refill window for lower schedules rather than this partial-fill period.

questions.question: A licensee lets an unlicensed person use their pharmacist display document and hold themselves out with pharmacist signage. Which ground is implicated?

answers.text: No ground covers lending a display document

Permitting a person not licensed to practice pharmacy in Connecticut to practice in violation of the practice rules, use a license or display document improperly, or use protected words, displays, or symbols is a discipline ground
Only the unlicensed person faces any consequence
Signage misuse is governed only by local zoning

questions.explanation: Permitting a person not licensed to practice pharmacy in Connecticut to practice pharmacy, to use a pharmacist license or display document, or to use words, displays, or symbols in violation of the governing provisions is a discipline ground for the licensee. The lending licensee therefore faces consequences alongside the unlicensed person, and the signage misuse is a pharmacy-law ground rather than only a zoning issue.

questions.question: An entrepreneur sells vitamins and sundries from a storefront and wants to call the business a pharmacy and sell prescription drugs at retail. What must be true first?

answers.text: Nothing, if a pharmacist visits weekly
Registration of one technician is sufficient
A nonlegend drug permit covers retail prescription sales
A pharmacy license must have been issued for that place of business

questions.explanation: A pharmacy is a place of business where drugs and devices may be sold at retail and for which a pharmacy license has been issued. Occasional pharmacist visits do not substitute for licensure, technician registration does not license a premises, and a nonlegend permit does not authorize retail legend drug sales as a pharmacy.

questions.question: A vending operator stocks a machine with a product that requires age verification at the register, plus several loose tablets in a plain bag. What is wrong?

answers.text: No product subject to a sale restriction such as age verification, identification proof, or a quantity limit may be placed in a vending machine, and products must be sold only in the manufacturer's clearly labeled, original, unbroken, tamper-proof, expiration-dated packaging
Nothing is wrong with either choice
Only the plain bag is a problem
Only the restricted product is a problem

questions.explanation: No product subject to a sale restriction — age verification, identification proof, or a quantity limit — may be placed in a vending machine, and nonlegend products must be stored per manufacturer recommendations and sold only in the manufacturer's clearly labeled, original, unbroken, tamper-proof, expiration-dated packaging. Both choices therefore violate the rules, so neither single-item answer captures the full defect.

questions.question: A graduate begins performing pharmacist duties at a store while their license application is still pending, holding neither a license nor a temporary permit. What is the problem?

answers.text: No problem until the first refill is dispensed
No individual may engage in the practice of pharmacy unless they hold a current license or temporary permit to practice pharmacy issued by the Department
Pending applications authorize practice automatically
Only the store needs licensure

questions.explanation: Practice requires a current Department-issued pharmacist license or temporary permit, so practicing on a pending application alone is unauthorized. The prohibition attaches to engaging in practice itself rather than to a later refill milestone, a pending filing confers no automatic authority, and premises licensure does not substitute for the individual's own credential.

questions.question: A pharmacy installs an automated prescription dispensing machine. Under the current Connecticut definition, what must the qualifying prescription have completed before the machine may be used for it?

answers.text: Final verification by any technician
Order entry verification performed by a pharmacist
A second pharmacist's independent double check
Patient counseling at the machine

questions.explanation: The current definition requires order entry verification performed by a pharmacist for the qualifying prescription. The older formulation tied to a different verification label no longer states the standard, a technician cannot supply the pharmacist verification, and neither a routine double check nor machine-side counseling is the stated prerequisite.

questions.question: A Schedule II substance used medically under practitioner supervision is federally approved and then federally reclassified to a lower schedule. The Commissioner has not specifically designated otherwise. What happens for Connecticut purposes?

answers.text: It stays in Schedule II forever
It is removed from all control immediately with no designation
It takes the federal designation for state purposes under the Schedule II regulation's follow-the-federal rule
Each pharmacy decides its state schedule

questions.explanation: The Schedule II regulation provides that such an FDA-approved, medically used substance that is federally reclassified or unscheduled takes the federal designation for state purposes unless the Commissioner specifically designates otherwise. It does not remain frozen in Schedule II, reclassification is a designation change rather than an automatic absence of any designation, and individual pharmacies do not set schedules.

questions.question: Pharmacist Helen Cho quarantined a shipment as suspect product under the supply-chain law and investigated it with her trading partners. The investigation confirms the product is illegitimate. A receiver asks whether the bottles can now go back on the shelf since the investigation is finished. What must happen?

answers.text: The product stays out of commerce; it must not be dispensed or returned to saleable stock, and the illegitimate finding is reported through the required channels
The product returns to the shelf because completing the investigation clears it
The product may be dispensed at a discount with a warning to patients
The product may be given to a neighboring pharmacy that is willing to accept the risk

questions.explanation: Under the DSCSA, suspect product is quarantined and investigated, and product confirmed to be illegitimate must not be dispensed or returned to commerce; it is handled and reported as illegitimate product. Finishing an investigation does not clear a product the investigation condemned. Discounting it to patients or passing it to another pharmacy would put illegitimate product into the supply chain.

questions.question: A technician tells pharmacist Marcus Hale that a prescription cream applied to the skin must be dispensed in a child-resistant container because, in the technician's words, every prescription requires one. How should the pharmacist evaluate that claim?

answers.text: The technician is correct, because the child-resistant default covers topical products in the same way as oral products
The technician is incorrect, because the child-resistant packaging default applies to oral prescriptions, and this topical prescription falls outside that oral-packaging default
The technician is correct only if the cream is kept in the patient's bathroom
The technician is incorrect only when the patient lives alone

questions.explanation: The child-resistant packaging default is tied to oral prescriptions, so a topical prescription is outside that oral-packaging default and the technician's blanket claim is wrong. Bathroom storage and living alone do not change the scope of the default, and the default does not extend to topical products in the same way it covers oral ones.

questions.question: Pharmacist Yusuf Rahman receives a Schedule II prescription written for 60 tablets. He calls the prescriber about a dosing concern, and the prescriber confirms the intended quantity was actually 30 tablets and asks Yusuf to correct the prescription. What may Yusuf do?

answers.text: Refuse, because no element of a Schedule II prescription may ever be altered
Make the change only if the patient also agrees in writing
Send the prescription back and wait for a couriered replacement before any dispensing this week
Change the quantity to 30 tablets after that prescriber consultation and dispense the corrected quantity

questions.explanation: Quantity is among the elements a pharmacist may change on a Schedule II prescription after consulting the prescriber, so the prescriber-confirmed correction to 30 tablets may be made and dispensed. The prescription is not wholly unalterable, the patient's written agreement is not the source of the pharmacist's authority to make the change, and returning the prescription for a replacement is unnecessary once the prescriber has confirmed the correction.

questions.question: While filling an oral prescription, a technician notices the patient's intake form says no children live in the home and suggests switching to a plain snap cap for convenience. Neither the patient nor the prescriber has asked for non-child-resistant packaging. What should pharmacist Tom Becker do?

answers.text: Keep the child-resistant container, because that packaging remains the default unless the patient or the prescriber requests otherwise
Use the snap cap, because a household with no children is automatically exempt from child-resistant packaging
Use the snap cap whenever the intake form lists only adult residents, without asking anyone
Let the technician decide based on how crowded the packaging shelf is that day

questions.explanation: Child-resistant packaging is the default for most oral prescriptions, and the absence of children in the household does not by itself remove that default. The packaging changes when the patient or the prescriber requests otherwise, not when staff infer an exemption from an intake form or choose based on convenience or shelf space.

questions.question: To process one current claim, a health plan asks pharmacist Hugo Almeida to send the patient's complete prescription history covering the past five years. The claim itself concerns a single recent fill. What does the minimum necessary standard require?

answers.text: Limit the disclosure to the information necessary for the payment purpose, rather than the full five-year history
Send the complete history, because payment disclosures are exempt from any scope limit
Send the history only after the patient signs an authorization, because payment always requires one
Refuse to send anything, because no information may ever be shared for payment

questions.explanation: The minimum necessary standard applies to payment uses and disclosures, so a request tied to a single current claim should be answered with the information that payment purpose requires, not an entire five-year history. Payment disclosures are permitted without patient authorization, so authorization is not the missing step, but permission to disclose for payment is not permission to disclose without limit. Refusing all sharing would defeat a permitted payment function.

questions.question: A shipment arrives with mismatched product identifiers and packaging that does not match the manufacturer's presentation, and pharmacist Helen Brooks suspects the product may be illegitimate. A technician proposes returning it to the regular shelves while someone calls the supplier next week. What must happen instead?

answers.text: The product may be dispensed first to established patients while the inquiry proceeds
The product may be returned to saleable stock if the supplier later says by phone that it is probably fine
The product must be quarantined and investigated, and it must not be dispensed or returned to saleable stock unverified
The product may be sold at the front counter as a nonprescription item to clear it out

questions.explanation: Suspect or illegitimate product must be quarantined and investigated, and it must never be dispensed or returned to saleable stock without verification. Dispensing it to any patient, relying on an unverified phone assurance, or diverting it to front-counter sale all allow product whose legitimacy is in doubt to reach the public.

questions.question: Pharmacist Dana Whitaker faces board charges over repeated recordkeeping violations. Rather than contest the charges at a formal hearing, she is offered a written agreement that resolves the case if she accepts probation, a monetary fine, and periodic record audits. May board charges be resolved in this way?

answers.text: Only if a criminal court approves the agreement first
Yes. A licensee may resolve board charges through a consent agreement or consent order that imposes conditions such as probation, a fine, and monitoring
No. Every board charge must be decided at a full contested hearing, even when the licensee agrees to the outcome
Yes, but a consent agreement may only dismiss the charges outright and can never include conditions

questions.explanation: A licensee may settle board charges through a consent agreement or consent order, accepting enforceable conditions such as probation, a fine, and monitoring instead of litigating the case. Criminal-court approval is not part of this administrative resolution, a contested hearing is unnecessary when the licensee voluntarily agrees to the terms, and an agreement that imposed no conditions at all would fail to address the violations that prompted the charges.

questions.question: Pharmacist-in-charge Alan Foster has just completed the pharmacy's biennial controlled-substance inventory, with counts taken and the working tally sheets signed. A staff member asks whether the finished inventory record can be discarded once the state inspector's visit ends next month. What is the correct treatment of the record?

answers.text: It may be discarded once any single inspection is over
It may be kept at the pharmacist-in-charge's home instead of at the pharmacy
It needs to be retained only until the next order of Schedule II drugs arrives
It must be documented and retained with the pharmacy's controlled-substance records

questions.explanation: The biennial inventory is a controlled-substance record: completing it is not enough, because the documented inventory must be retained with the pharmacy's controlled-substance records. Tying retention to one inspection or to the next drug order shortens the record's life without authority, and removing it to a home separates it from the records it belongs with.

district-of-columbia-mpje.quiz_title: District of Columbia MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement accurately places HIV prophylaxis in District pharmacy practice?

answers.text: Pharmacists have no role in HIV prophylaxis
Pharmacists may initiate prophylaxis without any protocol
Pharmacy-based prophylaxis was never enacted in the District

Initiation of pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV prevention, pursuant to a protocol, is an element of the practice of pharmacy as determined through the Mayor's clinical-services authority

questions.explanation: The practice-of-pharmacy clinical-services list includes initiation of PrEP and PEP for the prevention of HIV/AIDS pursuant to a protocol. Denying any pharmacist role and repeating the claim that no District legislation exists contradict the current statute, while dropping the protocol condition overstates the element as written.

questions.question: Who must direct compounding, repackaging, and prepackaging, and what final step is required?

answers.text: The most senior technician, with no verification step
The proprietor, whether or not a pharmacist
A pharmacist must direct and supervise the work, make the final verification of the prepackaged product, and document that verification
Verification is optional if a log is kept

questions.explanation: A pharmacist directs and supervises compounding, repackaging, and prepackaging, performs the final verification of the prepackaged product, and documents it. Technician seniority does not transfer pharmacist supervision. A nonpharmacist proprietor cannot supply it. A log does not replace the documented final verification.

questions.question: A pharmacist-in-charge is auditing report quality. Which statement about the regulatory data set is correct?

answers.text: It adds items such as the patient's telephone number, the dispenser's name, address and telephone number, the prescriber's full name, and which refill is being dispensed, and the dispenser must ensure reported information is correct
It is narrower than the statute's list and drops the days supply
