It requires reporting the patient's diagnosis for every covered drug
It forbids correcting a report once submitted

questions.explanation: The regulation's data set is broader than the statute's list, adding items such as patient telephone number, dispenser contact details, the prescriber's full name, and the number of the refill being dispensed, and each dispenser must ensure the information is correct and submit corrections when needed. The set is broader rather than narrower, it does not add a diagnosis element, and corrections are required rather than forbidden.

questions.question: Pharmacist Aisha Grant dispensed a Schedule II medication under the emergency oral authorization rule. What must the prescriber do next?

answers.text: Deliver a written or electronic prescription to the pharmacy within 7 days
Deliver a written prescription within 30 days
Telephone the pharmacy again within 72 hours to confirm the order
File the follow-up prescription only with the state board

questions.explanation: After an emergency oral Schedule II dispensing, the prescriber must deliver a written or electronic prescription within 7 days. Thirty days is too long, a second telephone call does not substitute for the required written or electronic prescription, and filing only with a board does not satisfy the duty to deliver it to the pharmacy.

questions.question: Staff discover a burglary and a significant inventory shortage on Monday morning. By when must the Director be told?

answers.text: Within 30 days after discovery

Within 48 hours after discovery, for burglaries, thefts, suspected diversions, significant inventory losses or inability to account for inventory, and fire, flood, or other damage to the pharmacy or its inventory
Only at the next annual inspection
Within 7 days, and only for controlled substances

questions.explanation: The reporting deadline is forty-eight hours after discovery for the listed loss, diversion, and damage events. Thirty days is far too late. Waiting for inspection defeats prompt reporting. The duty is not limited to controlled substances or stretched to seven days.

questions.question: A new patient presents a first prescription and reports several current medications and a drug allergy. What must the pharmacy maintain to support review and counseling for this patient?

answers.text: A patient profile with name, address, date of birth or age, gender, medication history, allergies, and relevant conditions
Only the patient's name and insurance information
A profile only if the patient is enrolled in Medicaid
A profile that lists allergies but omits medication history

questions.explanation: A patient profile maintained for drug utilization review and counseling includes name, address, date of birth or age, gender, medication history, allergies, and relevant conditions. Name and insurance alone, a Medicaid-only limitation, and a profile without medication history all omit information needed for screening and counseling.

questions.question: When the Board decides a denial or discipline case based on a conviction, what must it consider, and what annual report follows?

answers.text: Only the fact of conviction; no report is required
Only letters of reference; the report goes to the Mayor by July 1
Only elapsed time; the report is optional

Factors including relatedness to the occupation's duties, nature and seriousness, elapsed time, age at the offense, rehabilitation and fitness evidence, related work history, and references; the Mayor reports conviction-based denials and revocations or suspensions to the Council by January 1 each year

questions.explanation: Conviction-based decisions require consideration of the listed factors, including relatedness, seriousness, elapsed time, age at the offense, rehabilitation evidence including recidivism and supervision compliance, work history, and references. The Mayor's annual report of conviction-based denials and revocations or suspensions goes to the Council by January 1, so a conviction-alone test, a references-only test, and a July or optional report are all wrong.

questions.question: Pharmacy staff will begin handling a corrosive material as part of a new preparation process. Pharmacist-in-charge Monica Reyes is preparing the workplace before the work starts. Which preparation is required?

answers.text: Staff may learn the hazards by trial and error during the first week of handling
Gloves and other protective equipment are optional courtesies the pharmacy may skip to save cost
Staff must be trained on the hazards, provided with protective equipment, and eyewash must be available where corrosive materials are handled
The only preparation needed is posting the material's price list near the work area

questions.explanation: Hazard communication requires that staff be trained on the hazards of materials they handle, that they be provided protective equipment, and that eyewash be available where corrosive materials are handled. Learning by trial and error, treating protective equipment as optional, and posting pricing information leave the actual safety duties unmet.

questions.question: Pharmacist-in-charge Dana Whitaker is redesigning her pharmacy's controlled-substance filing system. Which plan satisfies the federal record requirements?

answers.text: Keep all controlled-substance records for one year, with Schedule II records filed together with Schedule III through V records
Keep the records for at least two years, but file Schedule II records in the same folder as the other controlled-substance records
Keep the records for at least two years and maintain Schedule II records separately from the other controlled-substance records
Keep Schedule II records separately, but destroy all controlled-substance records after 18 months to limit storage

questions.explanation: The federal floor requires controlled-substance inventories and records to be kept for at least two years, and Schedule II records must be maintained separately from other controlled-substance records. A one-year or 18-month destruction schedule falls short of the two-year minimum. Holding records for two years but filing Schedule II records together with Schedule III through V records fails the separation requirement.

questions.question: A large compounding operation that supplies office stock to hospitals and clinics completes the federal registration required for its category of facility. With which agency is that registration held?

answers.text: The state board of pharmacy in its home state only
The Drug Enforcement Administration
The Food and Drug Administration
The United States Pharmacopeia

questions.explanation: An outsourcing facility registers with the Food and Drug Administration and operates under federal current good manufacturing practice requirements, which distinguishes it from a traditional patient-specific compounding pharmacy regulated primarily by the state board. The Drug Enforcement Administration handles controlled-substance registration, and the United States Pharmacopeia sets standards but does not register facilities.

questions.question: A physician sends a valid prescription directing a vaccine for a specific patient who falls outside the pharmacist's usual walk-in bands. May a Board-certified pharmacist administer it?

answers.text: No, pharmacists may only vaccinate walk-ins
Yes, the practice of pharmacy separately includes administering immunizations and vaccinations to any individual pursuant to a valid prescription, when the pharmacist is Board-certified
Yes, but only if the pharmacist is not Board-certified
No, prescriptions for vaccines must be sent to a clinic

questions.explanation: Separate from the order-and-administer bands, the practice of pharmacy includes administering immunizations and vaccinations to any individual pursuant to a valid prescription when the pharmacist is certified by the Board. Walk-in-only practice understates the authority, certification is required rather than disqualifying, and there is no clinic-only routing rule.

questions.question: The Board approved Ellis to sit for the examinations on March 1. Ellis has passed neither examination by the following March. What is the status of the application?

answers.text: It is considered abandoned and closed; Ellis must reapply, meet current requirements, and pay required fees
It stays open indefinitely while Ellis keeps trying
It converts automatically into a technician registration
The Board must grant a one-year extension on request

questions.explanation: The applicant must successfully complete both examinations within one year from the date the Board approves the applicant to take them; failure means the application is considered abandoned and closed, and the applicant must reapply, meet current requirements, and pay required fees. An indefinite open period contradicts the one-year deadline. No automatic conversion to a technician credential occurs. No extension on request is stated in this rule.

questions.question: A pharmacy technician with no compounding background is assigned to prepare nonsterile capsules and oral liquids. No training record exists for her, and the pharmacist-in-charge argues documented competency is a sterile-compounding concern only. What is correct?

answers.text: The technician may compound freely, because nonsterile compounding has no training documentation expectations
Compounding personnel require training and documented competency for nonsterile compounding as well, before compounding for patients
The pharmacist-in-charge's license alone documents the technician's competency
Documentation may be created at year-end describing training that was never actually given

questions.explanation: Competency training and documentation are compounding quality requirements that reach nonsterile compounding personnel, not only the cleanroom. A supervisor's license does not demonstrate a technician's training, and back-created paperwork without actual training is not documentation of competency.

questions.question: A technician tells pharmacist Marcus Hale that a prescription cream applied to the skin must be dispensed in a child-resistant container because, in the technician's words, every prescription requires one. How should the pharmacist evaluate that claim?

answers.text: The technician is correct, because the child-resistant default covers topical products in the same way as oral products
The technician is incorrect, because the child-resistant packaging default applies to oral prescriptions, and this topical prescription falls outside that oral-packaging default
The technician is correct only if the cream is kept in the patient's bathroom
The technician is incorrect only when the patient lives alone

questions.explanation: The child-resistant packaging default is tied to oral prescriptions, so a topical prescription is outside that oral-packaging default and the technician's blanket claim is wrong. Bathroom storage and living alone do not change the scope of the default, and the default does not extend to topical products in the same way it covers oral ones.

questions.question: A pharmacy manager asks pharmacist Julia Moreno to strike a drug from the pharmacy's hazardous-drug list because the store fills it only a few times a year and senior staff are comfortable handling it. The drug appears on the national hazardous drug list. What should the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Keep the drug on the pharmacy's hazardous list, because listing follows the NIOSH list rather than local volume or staff comfort
Remove the drug, because low dispensing volume exempts a pharmacy from the list
Remove the drug for senior staff only, keeping it listed for new hires
Remove the drug once the manager documents that staff feel comfortable handling it

questions.explanation: The NIOSH list identifies hazardous drugs, and a pharmacy cannot delist a drug by local preference, volume, or staff familiarity. Handling controls for a listed drug are addressed through the standard and, where permitted, an assessment of risk for a dosage form, not by erasing the listing for some staff or some months.

questions.question: A 15-year-old customer selects levonorgestrel emergency contraception from the over-the-counter shelf. A technician tells pharmacist Aisha Rahman the sale must wait until a parent arrives to consent, and offers to hold the package at the register until then. What should Aisha do?

answers.text: Allow the sale without requiring a parent's presence or consent, because the product is available over the counter with no federal age restriction
Hold the package until a parent consents, as the technician proposed
Sell the product only after the customer calls a prescriber for authorization
Refuse the sale and refer the customer to a clinic, because minors may not purchase the product

questions.explanation: Levonorgestrel emergency contraception is available over the counter with no age restriction under federal law, so a sale may not be conditioned on parental consent, a parent's presence, or a prescriber's authorization. Refusing the sale to a minor imposes exactly the age-based barrier the federal framework does not contain.

questions.question: An adult aged 22 asks a pharmacist informally what District law treats as lawful personal conduct: carrying just under two ounces, giving a friend aged 25 half an ounce for free, growing plants at home, and selling a small amount to a neighbor. Which summary is correct?

answers.text: All four acts are lawful, including the sale, under the personal-use initiative
Only possession is lawful; any free transfer and any home growing remain offenses

Possessing, using, purchasing, or transporting two ounces or less is lawful, transferring one ounce or less without pay to another adult 21 or older is lawful, and home growing at a principal residence is capped at six plants per person with no more than three mature or flowering and twelve per household with no more than six mature — but sale is expressly not made lawful, and marijuana that is sold or offered for sale counts as a controlled substance Code-wide
Growing is capped at twelve plants per person with six mature, and sale under one ounce is lawful

questions.explanation: The personal-use provisions written into the controlled-substances law itself allow an adult 21 or older to possess or transport up to two ounces, transfer up to one ounce without remuneration to another adult, and grow at a principal residence up to six plants per person — three or fewer mature — within a household cap of twelve plants and six mature. Sale is expressly excluded from legality, and the Code-wide definition excludes compliant personal marijuana while including any marijuana sold or offered for sale.

questions.question: Pharmacist-in-charge Alan Foster has just completed the pharmacy's biennial controlled-substance inventory, with counts taken and the working tally sheets signed. A staff member asks whether the finished inventory record can be discarded once the state inspector's visit ends next month. What is the correct treatment of the record?

answers.text: It may be discarded once any single inspection is over
It may be kept at the pharmacist-in-charge's home instead of at the pharmacy
It needs to be retained only until the next order of Schedule II drugs arrives
It must be documented and retained with the pharmacy's controlled-substance records

questions.explanation: The biennial inventory is a controlled-substance record: completing it is not enough, because the documented inventory must be retained with the pharmacy's controlled-substance records. Tying retention to one inspection or to the next drug order shortens the record's life without authority, and removing it to a home separates it from the records it belongs with.

questions.question: Jamie holds a pharmacist license in good standing in a neighboring state whose credentialing requirements were substantially equivalent to the District's when Jamie was licensed, and that state admits District-credentialed professionals in a like manner. Which credentialing concept describes Jamie's route?

answers.text: Endorsement by a national accrediting association
Temporary licensure by examination
Reciprocity
Foreign equivalence review

questions.explanation: Reciprocity means issuing a credential to an applicant licensed and in good standing in another state whose requirements were substantially equivalent at credentialing and which admits District-credentialed professionals in a like manner; Jamie's facts match that definition. Endorsement rests on credentialing by a recognized accrediting association or state board under the endorsement definition, framed differently. Temporary licensure is a short-term status, not this route. Foreign equivalence review concerns education abroad, not a sister-state license.

questions.question: A data logger shows that a refrigerator at pharmacist Oliver Grant's pharmacy spent nine hours above its labeled temperature range overnight, and the excursion is documented in the log. A technician has already put the affected insulin back on the pick shelf 'since the vials look fine.' What should Oliver do?

answers.text: Leave the vials in service, because appearance is a reliable test of potency
Erase the logger entry so the record does not create questions later
Discard every product in the refrigerator immediately without any assessment or record
Assess the excursion's impact, keep the affected stock out of use pending that determination, and document what was decided and why

questions.explanation: A documented excursion calls for assessment, not silent return to use: the affected stock is held out of service while its usability is determined, and the determination is documented. Vial appearance cannot establish that a temperature-sensitive product retained potency. Blanket discarding without assessment or records wastes product that may be usable and leaves no account of the event, and falsifying the log destroys the documentation the process depends on.

delaware-mpje.quiz_title: Delaware MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which pharmacist's conduct presents a recognized ground for board discipline?

answers.text: A pharmacist who diverts controlled substances and practices while impaired
A pharmacist who dispenses an AB-rated generic equivalent when the prescriber has not prohibited substitution
A pharmacist who offers counseling to a patient on a new prescription
A pharmacist who reports a suspected adverse event through the FDA reporting program

questions.explanation: Impairment and diversion are recognized grounds for discipline, along with unprofessional conduct, fraud in obtaining a license, certain convictions, and violating board rules. Dispensing an interchangeable AB-rated generic when substitution has not been prohibited is lawful practice, offering counseling is an expected practice standard, and reporting adverse events is proper professional conduct.

questions.question: A pharmacist asks how often and by what transmission method monitoring data must be sent. Where does the statute direct that pharmacist for the answer?

answers.text: The statute itself fixes a single daily deadline for every dispenser
Each pharmacy chooses its own frequency in its policy manual
The prescriber sets the frequency for prescriptions they wrote
The transmission methods and frequency are established by regulation of the Office of Controlled Substances

questions.explanation: The statute assigns the how and how-often questions to Office of Controlled Substances regulation rather than stating them itself. No single statutory daily deadline exists to quote, and neither store policy nor an individual prescriber supplies the method or frequency. Looking to the regulation is the legally correct move.

questions.question: A candidate who failed an examination asks where the frequency and conditions for retesting are established. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: The candidate's preceptor sets them case by case
Federal law sets one uniform retest schedule for every state
The testing vendor may change them without Board rules
The Board determines retest frequency and conditions in its rules and regulations

questions.explanation: The statute directs the Board to determine, in its rules and regulations, the frequency and conditions under which a candidate may retest after a failure. A preceptor and a testing vendor have no such authority, and no single federal schedule displaces the Board's rules. Retesting is conditioned, not unlimited.

questions.question: A new patient starting HIV prevention services signs a form waiving consultation to save time. How must the pharmacist respond?

answers.text: Accept the waiver, because a signed form controls
Provide consultation only if the patient later asks questions
Skip consultation for new patients but require it for returning ones
Consultation is required for these services, and a new patient may not waive consultation, so the pharmacist must provide it despite the signed form

questions.explanation: The consultation duty for HIV prevention and post-exposure services cannot be waived by a new patient, making the signed waiver ineffective for that purpose. Later questions and returning-patient status do not change the new-patient rule. Time pressure is not an exception the provision recognizes.

questions.question: A reporter files a public-records request for monitoring data on a named patient. How must the request be handled?

answers.text: The data must be released with the patient's name redacted only
The data is a public record once it is a year old
The pharmacy may release it if the reporter pays the copying fee
Monitoring information is not subject to disclosure as a public record, and data maintained in the program is protected health information

questions.explanation: Program data carries two protections: it is not disclosable as a public record, and it is protected health information. Redaction, age of the record, and copying fees do not convert protected health information into a public record. The request must be refused on those grounds.

questions.question: At 2 a.m., a nurse and a physician enter the closed hospital pharmacy for a needed drug, and a security guard waits outside. A second nurse should have joined them. What does the entry rule require?

answers.text: One clinician may enter alone if the need is urgent

Entry requires 2 persons, such as a registered nurse or physician plus another nurse, physician, or security guard, and the entrants must record the drug name, strength, amount, date and time taken, their signatures, and the patient name and location, with pharmacy review of the record upon reopening
Entry is allowed with no record if the drug is inexpensive
Three persons are required, and no record is kept

questions.explanation: After-hours entry is a two-person rule, pairing a nurse or physician with another nurse, physician, or security guard, so the guard should have been one of the entrants rather than waiting outside. The record is detailed: drug, strength, amount, date and time, signatures, and patient name and location. Urgency and drug price create no solo-entry or no-record exceptions.

questions.question: A pharmacist whose license lapsed two and a half years ago asks whether they must retake and pass the jurisprudence examination to renew. What is the answer on these facts?

answers.text: Yes, every lapse over one year requires the retake
No, the jurisprudence retake is added only for a lapse longer than four years
Yes, because any lapse over two years requires it
No, and no other reinstatement steps are required either

questions.explanation: The track for a lapse over one year but under four years requires a late fee, education proof, fingerprints, and clearinghouse review, without a jurisprudence retake. The retake is the added step for lapses longer than four years, so a two-year threshold is also wrong. The other reinstatement steps are still required, and clearinghouse results do not control whether the retake applies.

questions.question: A unit-dose prepacked container was packed on January 1. The pharmacist assigns a beyond-use date 18 months out, citing habit, with no stability data. What does the rule say?

answers.text: Eighteen months is the standard prepack dating period
Prepack dating always follows the manufacturer's expiration date exactly
No beyond-use date is needed for unit-dose containers

The beyond-use date for a unit-dose or single-dose prepacked container may not exceed 1 year from the date of prepacking unless manufacturer stability data combined with compendial standards supports a longer date, and storage temperature must not exceed 25 degrees Celsius in containers with moisture-permeation properties better than polyvinyl chloride

questions.explanation: The default ceiling is one year from prepacking, extendable only on manufacturer stability data combined with compendial standards, neither of which habit supplies. Container and storage conditions are part of the same rule: better moisture protection than polyvinyl chloride and storage at or under 25 degrees Celsius. Copying the manufacturer's expiration date wholesale ignores the one-year cap.

questions.question: While taking inventory, a pharmacist reaches an ordinary stock bottle of a Schedule IV anxiolytic containing a few hundred tablets. Which counting approach is permitted for this bottle?

answers.text: An exact count is mandatory for every controlled substance, whatever the schedule
The bottle may be skipped entirely if it was counted at the last inventory
The contents may be weighed and the weight recorded in place of any count
The contents may be estimated, because Schedule III through V substances may generally be counted by estimate

questions.explanation: Schedule III through V substances may generally be counted by estimate at inventory, unlike Schedule II substances, which always require an exact count. Estimation is not mandatory exact counting, it does not excuse skipping the bottle, and substituting a weight for a count is not the permitted estimation method described in the inventory rules.

questions.question: Jordan becomes a pharmacist-in-charge for the first time in Delaware after being licensed. By when must Jordan appear for an interview similar to the permit interview?

answers.text: Within 90 days of licensure
Within 10 days of licensure
Within 1 year of licensure
Only at the next biennial renewal

questions.explanation: A pharmacist who is a pharmacist-in-charge for the first time in Delaware must appear for a similar Board interview within 90 days of licensure. Ten days is the window used for several notice duties, not this interview, and waiting a year or until renewal would miss the early review the rule sets. The interview follows soon after taking on the role.

questions.question: A clinic is credentialing a new prescriber to sign controlled-substance orders electronically. The prescriber asks pharmacist Dana Whitfield what identity check the prescriber must complete when signing such orders. What is required?

answers.text: A single password entered once at the start of each work shift
Two-factor authentication by the prescriber
A PIN supplied by the patient at the pharmacy counter
Approval of each order by the receiving pharmacist before signing

questions.explanation: Electronic prescribing of controlled substances requires the prescriber to authenticate with two-factor authentication. A single shift password is only one factor, a patient's PIN is not prescriber authentication, and pharmacist approval at receipt does not substitute for the prescriber's signing authentication.

questions.question: A medical practice wants to begin sending controlled-substance orders electronically and asks pharmacist Colin Reyes whether any ordinary office software may be used to create and transmit them. What requirement applies to the prescribing application?

answers.text: The application must be DEA-compliant, using certified software for controlled-substance prescribing
Any word-processing program may be used if the document is saved before sending
A general fax application is sufficient because it produces a readable copy
No software standard applies if each prescriber uses a personal password

questions.explanation: The prescribing application for electronic controlled-substance orders must be DEA-compliant certified software. Saving a word-processing document, producing a fax copy, or relying on a personal password alone does not satisfy the application requirement that accompanies two-factor authentication.

questions.question: A licensed nonresident pharmacy sits on a home-state inspection report for three months, keeps Delaware patient records mixed with all other records retrievable only after a month, and a separate unlicensed operator ships into Delaware for ten days. What exposures accumulate?

answers.text: The report deadline is 6 months, records may stay mixed for 30 days, and unlicensed operation is fined once per month
Only the unlicensed operator faces consequences; record and report lapses are not discipline grounds

Grounds include failing to give the Board inspection reports within 60 days of receipt and failing to keep Delaware-patient records readily retrievable within 15 days and segregated from other residents' records, sanctions may reach $250,000 per violation with each continuing day separate, and unlicensed operation draws up to $10,000 for each day
Inspection reports go to the home-state board only, with no Delaware deadline at all

questions.explanation: Nonresident discipline adds two operational grounds to the facility grounds: inspection reports must reach the Board within sixty days of the pharmacy receiving them, and records of drugs provided to Delaware residents must stay readily retrievable within fifteen days and separate from non-Delaware records. Sanctions for violations reach $250,000 per violation with each continuing day counted separately, and operating without a Delaware license adds up to $10,000 for each day of unlicensed operation. Three-month and one-month delays both miss their respective clocks.

questions.question: An auditor reviewing compounder Omar Farouk's file finds a single passed written quiz and no records of observed garbing, fingertip sampling, or media-fill testing, although Omar has compounded sterile preparations for months. How should the pharmacist-in-charge characterize the file?

answers.text: Complete, because a written quiz is the whole of sterile compounding competency
Incomplete, because competency must be demonstrated and documented across the hands-on elements, not shown by a quiz alone
Complete, because months of compounding without a complaint prove competency retroactively
Irrelevant, because competency documentation is optional for experienced compounders

questions.explanation: Sterile compounding competency is demonstrated through hands-on elements including garbing and hand hygiene observation, fingertip sampling, and media-fill testing, each documented in the competency file. A quiz tests knowledge only, an absence of complaints is not a competency demonstration, and documentation duties are not waived by experience.

questions.question: A hospital satellite pharmacy compounds a low-risk sterile preparation inside an ISO Class 5 primary engineering control that sits in a segregated compounding area rather than a full cleanroom suite. The preparation will be kept at room temperature. How must it be categorized and dated?

answers.text: Category 1, with a room-temperature beyond-use limit of no more than 12 hours
Category 2, with a room-temperature beyond-use limit of 30 days
Category 1, with a room-temperature beyond-use limit of 7 days
Category 3, because any ISO 5 device creates the longest dating

questions.explanation: Category 1 preparations are made in an ISO Class 5 primary engineering control within a segregated compounding area and carry short dating, no more than 12 hours at room temperature. Category 2 work occurs in a cleanroom suite and is the route to longer dating, a 7-day room-temperature period far exceeds the Category 1 cap, and the device alone does not create a longer-dating category.

questions.question: After a hazardous-drug compounding session ends, technician Grace Liu wipes the work surface once with a general-purpose cleaner and announces the area is ready for non-hazardous compounding. Pharmacist Tom Becker stops her. What must happen to the surface first?

answers.text: The hazardous-drug deactivation and decontamination steps must be performed for the residues left by the session
Nothing further, because a single wipe with any cleaner satisfies hazardous-drug procedures
The surface must be covered with a clean drape so residue is sealed underneath
The area must simply air out overnight, with no cleaning steps recorded or performed

questions.explanation: Hazardous-drug procedures require deactivation and decontamination steps that address drug residues, not a single general-purpose wipe. Covering residue with a drape leaves it in place, and passive airing performs neither deactivation nor decontamination.

questions.question: Pharmacist David Osei counsels a patient in the designated consultation area using a lowered voice. Despite those measures, a customer passing nearby briefly overhears part of the conversation, and the patient complains that any overhearing is automatically a privacy violation. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Any overhearing is a violation, regardless of the safeguards used
The pharmacy must stop all counseling at the counter permanently
An incidental disclosure that occurs despite reasonable safeguards is permitted; the safeguards David used are what the standard expects
The customer who overheard must be given the patient's records so the disclosure is equal

questions.explanation: Incidental disclosures are permitted when reasonable safeguards are in place, and counseling in a designated area with a lowered voice is the kind of safeguard expected for everyday communications. The standard does not demand that overhearing be made impossible, so a brief overhearing despite those measures is not automatically a violation. Ending all counseling would sacrifice a required practice function, and giving the bystander records would compound a limited overhearing into a full improper disclosure.

questions.question: A newly hired pharmacist finds that her pharmacy files its Schedule II prescription records in the same undifferentiated sequence as all of its other controlled-substance records, so a Schedule II record can be located only by reading through the entire file. Her pharmacist-in-charge says separation is optional for a small store. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Schedule II records must be maintained separately from the pharmacy's other records, so the mixed filing must be corrected
Separation is genuinely optional, and small pharmacies are exempt from it
Separation is required only for pharmacies that also sell Schedule I substances
The mixed filing is acceptable if the pharmacy performs a biennial inventory on schedule

questions.explanation: Federal recordkeeping requires Schedule II records to be maintained separately from other records, unlike Schedule III through V records, which have the readily-retrievable alternative. Store size creates no exemption, pharmacies do not sell Schedule I substances, which have no accepted medical use, and completing inventories does not substitute for the separate-records requirement.

questions.question: At pickup, a pharmacist says nothing to a patient about a critical precaution for a newly dispensed drug, even though sharing it is part of proper counseling. The patient, unaware of the precaution, is harmed in exactly the way the warning would have prevented. What is the pharmacist's position?

answers.text: The pharmacist is immune because counseling is a courtesy rather than a professional duty
Only the drug's manufacturer can be liable when a warning was omitted
The prescriber absorbs all liability because the prescriber selected the therapy
The pharmacist may be civilly liable because a counseling failure, like a review failure, can breach the duty of care

questions.explanation: Counseling failures can create civil liability when the omitted information was material and the patient is harmed as a result, because the duty of care reaches counseling as well as filling accuracy. Counseling is a professional obligation rather than a courtesy, manufacturer liability does not displace the pharmacist's own duty, and the prescriber's choice of therapy does not absorb the pharmacist's counseling responsibility.

questions.question: A prescriber's electronic prescribing system sends a new prescription through a network service that routes the message, unchanged, directly into pharmacist Sofia Marino's pharmacy system, where she can read every field exactly as the prescriber entered it. A colleague objects that any service between the two systems destroys the prescription's status. How should the prescription be treated?

answers.text: As invalid, because a valid electronic prescription may pass through no network of any kind
As a telephone order, because it arrived through a communications service
As a fax prescription, subject to the rules for paper facsimiles
As a valid electronic prescription, because it was transmitted directly from the prescriber's system without an intermediary altering its content

questions.explanation: The validity requirement is that an electronic prescription be transmitted directly from the prescriber's system and not be converted or altered by an intermediary, and routing that leaves the content exactly as entered satisfies that requirement. Ordinary network transmission is how such prescriptions travel and does not invalidate them, and a message that was never converted to a fax image or phoned in is neither a fax nor a telephone order.

hawaii-mpje.quiz_title: Hawaii MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What makes a generic product an equivalent generic drug product for substitution purposes?

answers.text: Any generic with the same active ingredient, whether listed or not
Any product the wholesaler labels as equivalent
A generic approved only by a neighboring state for its own list
It has been approved by the director of health as substitutable and is included in the state list of substitutable products

questions.explanation: An equivalent generic is one the director of health has approved as substitutable and included in the state list. Same-ingredient status alone, a wholesaler label, and another state's list do not confer that status, and a discounted brand is not a generic equivalent. List inclusion is the gateway to substitution.

questions.question: A patient's identification number reaches its five-year purge date, but the patient's data are part of an active investigation. What happens?

answers.text: The number must be purged anyway, and investigators lose access
The purge does not apply while the information is part of an active investigation
The number is transferred to the investigating agency permanently
The purge clock restarts for another five years

questions.explanation: The five-year purge of a patient's identification number is subject to an exception: it does not apply while the information is part of an active investigation. Investigators therefore do not lose the identifier mid-investigation. The exception is a hold on purging, not a permanent transfer or an automatic five-year restart.

questions.question: The board proposes new rules governing pharmacy practice and wholesale distribution standards. Under what authority and process may it act?

answers.text: The board may issue binding rules by press release with no procedure
Only the legislature may ever change any pharmacy requirement
The board may adopt, amend, and repeal rules under the administrative procedure chapter as it deems proper for the pharmacy chapter, the cited federal law, and the cited federal wholesale regulations
The board may adopt rules only for technician certificates

questions.explanation: The board may adopt, amend, and repeal rules under the state administrative procedure chapter as it deems proper for the pharmacy chapter, Public Law 100-293, and the federal wholesale distributor regulations in 21 CFR part 205. A press release bypasses the required procedure, legislative action is not the exclusive route because rulemaking is delegated, and the rulemaking power extends well beyond technician certificates.

questions.question: Which topics must a wholesaler's written policies and procedures cover?

answers.text: Receipt, security, storage, inventory, and distribution, including identifying and reporting loss or theft and correcting inventory errors
Only pricing, marketing, and customer credit
Receipt and storage, with security handled informally
Procedures may be entirely oral if staff are experienced

questions.explanation: Written procedures must address receipt, security, storage, inventory, and distribution, including loss and theft identification and reporting and inventory-error correction. Commercial and routing topics do not cover the required operational areas. Security cannot be left informal, and experienced staff do not excuse the written form the rule requires.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly identifies the administrator and the designated state agency under the controlled substances chapter?

answers.text: The administrator heads the Narcotics Enforcement Division within the Department of Public Safety
The designated state agency is the Board of Pharmacy
The administrator heads the Narcotics Enforcement Division, and that division is the designated state agency, within the Department of Law Enforcement
The designated state agency is the state police narcotics bureau of the counties

questions.explanation: The administrator is the administrator of the Narcotics Enforcement Division of the Department of Law Enforcement, and that division is the designated state agency. Placing the division in Public Safety repeats the pre-2024 structure, and neither the pharmacy board, the health director, nor county bureaus hold those chapter roles.

questions.question: A complete prescription for a non-controlled blood pressure drug contains every required element but no DEA number. A technician flags it as invalid for that omission alone. Is the flag correct?

answers.text: Yes, because every prescription for any drug must carry the prescriber's DEA number
Yes, unless the patient supplies the DEA number verbally
No, because a DEA number is required for controlled-substance prescriptions, not for a non-controlled drug prescription
No, because non-controlled prescriptions need no prescriber identification at all

questions.explanation: A prescriber's DEA number is required on controlled-substance prescriptions, so its absence alone does not invalidate an otherwise complete prescription for a non-controlled drug. That does not remove the ordinary prescriber name, address, and signature elements, and a patient supplying a number verbally is irrelevant to a requirement that does not apply here.

questions.question: An authorized professional prescribes naloxone by standing order to people positioned to help at-risk individuals. How is that prescribing characterized?

answers.text: It is treated as prescribing without any medical purpose
It is deemed a legitimate medical purpose in the usual course of professional practice
It is allowed only as an experiment under a research protocol
It counts as dispensing, never as prescribing

questions.explanation: Prescribing, dispensing, and distributing an antagonist to an at-risk individual, a person positioned to assist, or a harm-reduction organization, directly or by standing order, is deemed a legitimate medical purpose in the usual course of practice. Calling it purposeless, experimental only, mere dispensing, or a law-enforcement function mischaracterizes the deeming rule.

questions.question: A technician's certificate approaches its expiration at the end of an odd-numbered year, and the technician plans to keep working into the next biennium. What must occur?

answers.text: Nothing; certificates continue automatically while employed
The pharmacy's permit renewal renews all staff certificates with it
The technician may work until the board sends an expiration warning
The certificate must be renewed under the biennial renewal scheme; failure to pay the biennial fee forfeits it as of expiration

questions.explanation: Technician certificates renew within the same biennial scheme as other credentials, and failure to pay the biennial fee forfeits the certificate as of expiration. Continued employment does not auto-renew it, the struck lapse-and-new-registration rule is gone, an employer's permit renewal does not carry staff credentials, and no warning precedes forfeiture.

questions.question: A companion provision in the board's own rules addresses fines after a hearing. Which statement about fines must be avoided when drafting or applying these provisions?

answers.text: Blending the pharmacy chapter, board-rules, general-act, and food-and-drug fine figures into a single generic state fine, because each figure belongs to its specific provision
Noting that the pharmacy chapter range is one hundred to one thousand per violation
Keying a general-act fine question to its no-less-than-one-hundred, no-stated-maximum structure
Keying a food-and-drug administrative question to its ten-thousand-per-offense ceiling

questions.explanation: The fine figures must never be merged into one generic fine, because the pharmacy chapter, board rules, general act, and food and drug chapter each state their own amounts, units, and processes. Stating the chapter range, the general-act floor structure, and the food-and-drug ceiling with their own citations are exactly the provision-specific readings required. Blending is the error to avoid.

questions.question: A large compounding operation that supplies office stock to hospitals and clinics completes the federal registration required for its category of facility. With which agency is that registration held?

answers.text: The state board of pharmacy in its home state only
The Drug Enforcement Administration
The Food and Drug Administration
The United States Pharmacopeia

questions.explanation: An outsourcing facility registers with the Food and Drug Administration and operates under federal current good manufacturing practice requirements, which distinguishes it from a traditional patient-specific compounding pharmacy regulated primarily by the state board. The Drug Enforcement Administration handles controlled-substance registration, and the United States Pharmacopeia sets standards but does not register facilities.

questions.question: A licensed practitioner dispenses drug samples of a designated controlled substance directly to a patient and assumes samples escape monitoring because no pharmacy was involved. What does the reporting provision say?

answers.text: The seven-day reporting covers dispensing of drug samples by a licensed practitioner as well as filled prescriptions for designated substances
Samples are never reportable under any circumstances
Samples are reported only if the patient pays for them
Samples are reported by the patient, not the practitioner

questions.explanation: The reporting duty covers filled prescriptions for designated controlled substances and dispensing of drug samples by a licensed practitioner, so direct sample dispensing is included. A never-reportable rule and a payment trigger both contradict that inclusion, and the reporting responsibility rests with the dispenser rather than the patient.

questions.question: Two cases arrive together: one involves a deceptive newspaper advertisement, the other a dishonest private dealing with no advertisement. How do the grounds sort them?

answers.text: Both fit only the advertising ground
Both fit only the dealings ground, because advertisements are dealings
The advertisement fits false, fraudulent, or deceptive advertising, while the private dealing fits the separate ground for other fraudulent or dishonest dealings
Neither fits any ground without a drug-law violation

questions.explanation: Deceptive promotion fits the advertising ground, and a non-advertising dishonest transaction fits the separate ground for any other fraudulent or dishonest dealings. Collapsing both into either single ground erases the distinction the enumeration draws. Neither requires a drug-law violation to be disciplinable, and procurement fraud concerns obtaining the credential.

questions.question: An 82-year-old patient who lives alone presents a new oral prescription. A technician, noting the patient's age and household, reaches for an easy-open cap without asking the patient anything about packaging. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: Use child-resistant packaging by default, because age and living alone do not themselves waive the default; non-child-resistant packaging requires a request
Use the easy-open cap, because patients over 65 are automatically exempt
Use the easy-open cap, because a household with no children is automatically exempt
Ask the prescriber to note the patient's age on every prescription so caps can be waived

questions.explanation: The child-resistant default applies unless the patient or prescriber requests otherwise, and neither advanced age nor living alone is itself such a request, so the default packaging is used until a request is made. Automatic exemptions based on age or household composition, and routing the question through the prescriber on every fill, replace the patient's actual choice with assumptions.

questions.question: Pharmacist Colin Barrett is training a new hire on will-call audits and pulls a ready vial whose label shows the patient, prescriber directions, and fill date, but no number linking the vial back to the pharmacy's dispensing record for that fill. Which correction is required?

answers.text: None, because the fill date alone links the vial to the dispensing record
Add the prescriber's telephone number so the office can be called to trace the fill
Add the manufacturer's lot number in place of any pharmacy reference number
Add the prescription number assigned to that fill before the vial is released

questions.explanation: The dispensed container label must carry the prescription number for the fill, which is the link between the vial in the patient's hands and the pharmacy's record. The fill date, the prescriber's telephone number, and the manufacturer's lot number each serve other purposes and do not substitute for that number.

questions.question: A pharmacy technician with no compounding background is assigned to prepare nonsterile capsules and oral liquids. No training record exists for her, and the pharmacist-in-charge argues documented competency is a sterile-compounding concern only. What is correct?

answers.text: The technician may compound freely, because nonsterile compounding has no training documentation expectations
Compounding personnel require training and documented competency for nonsterile compounding as well, before compounding for patients
The pharmacist-in-charge's license alone documents the technician's competency
Documentation may be created at year-end describing training that was never actually given

questions.explanation: Competency training and documentation are compounding quality requirements that reach nonsterile compounding personnel, not only the cleanroom. A supervisor's license does not demonstrate a technician's training, and back-created paperwork without actual training is not documentation of competency.

questions.question: An auditor reviewing compounder Omar Farouk's file finds a single passed written quiz and no records of observed garbing, fingertip sampling, or media-fill testing, although Omar has compounded sterile preparations for months. How should the pharmacist-in-charge characterize the file?

answers.text: Complete, because a written quiz is the whole of sterile compounding competency
Incomplete, because competency must be demonstrated and documented across the hands-on elements, not shown by a quiz alone
Complete, because months of compounding without a complaint prove competency retroactively
Irrelevant, because competency documentation is optional for experienced compounders

questions.explanation: Sterile compounding competency is demonstrated through hands-on elements including garbing and hand hygiene observation, fingertip sampling, and media-fill testing, each documented in the competency file. A quiz tests knowledge only, an absence of complaints is not a competency demonstration, and documentation duties are not waived by experience.

questions.question: Patient Devon Park asks pharmacist Alicia Tran to move his Schedule IV prescription to a pharmacy across town and wonders whether Alicia must mail the original paper prescription to the receiving store. What actually transfers in a proper transfer?

answers.text: The original paper prescription itself, sent by certified mail
Nothing transfers; the patient must obtain a brand-new prescription
A photocopy of the paper prescription, which the new pharmacy files as its original
The prescription and refill information, communicated between the pharmacies

questions.explanation: What moves in a transfer of a Schedule III, IV, or V prescription is the prescription and refill information, communicated between the pharmacies — not the physical paper prescription. Mailing the original or a photocopy does not accomplish a transfer, and a transferable prescription with refills remaining does not require the patient to start over with a new order.

questions.question: A prescriber's electronic prescribing system sends a new prescription through a network service that routes the message, unchanged, directly into pharmacist Sofia Marino's pharmacy system, where she can read every field exactly as the prescriber entered it. A colleague objects that any service between the two systems destroys the prescription's status. How should the prescription be treated?

answers.text: As invalid, because a valid electronic prescription may pass through no network of any kind
As a telephone order, because it arrived through a communications service
As a fax prescription, subject to the rules for paper facsimiles
As a valid electronic prescription, because it was transmitted directly from the prescriber's system without an intermediary altering its content

questions.explanation: The validity requirement is that an electronic prescription be transmitted directly from the prescriber's system and not be converted or altered by an intermediary, and routing that leaves the content exactly as entered satisfies that requirement. Ordinary network transmission is how such prescriptions travel and does not invalidate them, and a message that was never converted to a fax image or phoned in is neither a fax nor a telephone order.

questions.question: When the pharmacist-in-charge of a hospital pharmacy takes an extended leave, staff pharmacist Brian Kessler agrees to be designated as acting pharmacist-in-charge. He assumes the 'acting' label means the compliance duties stay with the absent pharmacist-in-charge. Is he right?

answers.text: Yes, because an acting designee carries the title but none of the accountability
Yes, because accountability attaches only to a permanent appointment

No, because the pharmacist designated as in charge — including an acting designee — bears the pharmacist-in-charge's responsibility for the pharmacy's compliance, security, records, and supervision of personnel
No, but only because hospital pharmacies are exempt from pharmacist-in-charge designation

questions.explanation: The pharmacist-in-charge role carries responsibility for the pharmacy's compliance, security, records, and supervision of personnel, and that responsibility attaches to whoever is designated in charge, acting or permanent. An absent predecessor cannot retain duties for a pharmacy she is not running, and no setting is exempt from having a designated pharmacist in charge.

questions.question: Pharmacist Tomas Rivera's pharmacy is located inside a grocery store that is open until midnight, while the pharmacy closes at 8 p.m. The grocery manager proposes propping the pharmacy's gate open after 8 p.m. so grocery staff can reach a stockroom door behind the pharmacy counter. What must Tomas maintain instead?

answers.text: The prescription department must be secured when the pharmacy is closed, even though the surrounding store stays open
The gate may stay open because the grocery staff are all store employees
The pharmacy may close without securing the department if a camera covers the area
Only the controlled-substance cabinet needs locking; the department itself may stay open

questions.explanation: When the pharmacy is closed, the prescription department itself must be secured — the fact that the host store remains open and staffed does not extend pharmacy access to store personnel. Employment by the same store is not authorization to enter the department. A camera records a breach but does not secure the space, and locking one cabinet leaves the rest of the department's stock and records exposed.

kentucky-mpje.quiz_title: Kentucky MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What must a pharmacist do with the pocket certificate the Board issues?

answers.text: Leave it with the pharmacist-in-charge
Carry it and exhibit it on request
Surrender it at each renewal and practice without one
Display it in a vehicle window

questions.explanation: The pocket certificate travels with the pharmacist and is shown when asked. Leaving it with a supervisor, surrendering it for the practice year, and vehicle display are none of them the carry-and-exhibit duty stated.

questions.question: A pharmacist earns twenty contact hours in one licensing year and asks to apply the extra five to the next year. What is the answer?

answers.text: Excess hours carry over for one year only
Excess hours may not be transferred or applied to future years
Excess hours carry over without limit
Excess hours convert to a fee credit

questions.explanation: Hours earned beyond the annual requirement expire with the year; they cannot be banked forward. One-year and unlimited carryover both contradict the no-transfer rule, and hours do not convert into money off the renewal fee.

questions.question: A charitable pharmacy's board proposes adding a small dispensing fee to cover operating costs. Is that permitted?

answers.text: A fee up to five dollars is permitted
No dispensing fee may be charged
A fee is permitted if patients are told in advance
A fee is permitted only for non-indigent patients

questions.explanation: A charitable pharmacy may not charge a dispensing fee at all. A five-dollar cap, advance disclosure, and charging only patients outside the eligible group each invent exceptions that the no-fee rule does not contain, and the pharmacy serves only qualified indigent patients in any event.

questions.question: A permit holder's policy delays patients' access to their own pharmacy records for weeks without justification. What is correct?

answers.text: Unreasonably restricting a patient's timely access to records or services is unprofessional conduct for the permit holder
Patients have no timely-access interest the rule protects
Record delays matter only for controlled substances
The policy is improper only during an inspection

questions.explanation: A permit holder commits unprofessional conduct by unreasonably restricting a patient's timely access to records or services. The protection is not limited to controlled-substance records or to inspection periods, and patients' timely access is exactly what the rule guards.

questions.question: A pharmacist is asked to serve as pharmacist-in-charge for two unrelated pharmacies at the same time. What is correct?

answers.text: They may serve two pharmacies freely if each gets ten hours weekly
They may not serve as pharmacist-in-charge for more than one pharmacy at a time except on written board approval
They may serve up to three pharmacies without approval
They may serve two pharmacies if the owners agree in writing

questions.explanation: Serving as pharmacist-in-charge is limited to one pharmacy at a time unless the board gives written approval. Meeting the ten-hour floor at both sites, a three-pharmacy allowance, and private owner agreement do not substitute for the board's written approval.

questions.question: A pharmacist is asked to sell a controlled substance directly to an unregistered acquaintance who promises to use it responsibly. Which pharmacist sales are proper?

answers.text: Dispensing pursuant to a conforming prescription, or selling to a federally registered person
Any sale the pharmacist personally supervises
Sales to acquaintances if the quantity is small
Sales to anyone who presents photo identification

questions.explanation: A pharmacist's lawful channels are prescription-based dispensing and sales to federally registered persons. Personal supervision, a small quantity, and identification do not substitute for one of those channels, so the acquaintance sale is improper.

questions.question: A clinician providing charitable care under Kentucky's charitable health care services framework issues a paper controlled-substance prescription in 2026. How is that treated under the mandate?

answers.text: It violates the mandate because no charitable exception exists
It is allowed only if the clinic also holds a waiver
It is allowed only for Schedule V substances
It falls within the charitable-care exception added to the mandate in 2026

questions.explanation: Charitable care under the Kentucky charitable health care statute was added to the exception list by the 2026 amendment, effective in mid-2026. The exception does exist, it operates without layering a separate waiver on top, and it is not confined to one schedule.

questions.question: A prescriber's office asks the Board for a copy of the nonequivalent formulary outside the regular distribution. How does the Board handle individual requests?

answers.text: Copies are never released outside the annual distribution
Copies are free but only to pharmacies
Requests must go through a legislator
The Board supplies copies on request at a price the Board sets

questions.explanation: On-request copies are supplied at the Board-set price, so the prescriber's office can obtain one. The annual mailing is not the only channel, the price term applies rather than free pharmacy-only access, and no legislative intermediary is involved.

questions.question: A pharmacy holds a bulk container with 1,500 tablets of a Schedule III medication, and the pharmacist is completing the biennial inventory. How must this container be counted?

answers.text: An exact count is required, because a container holding more than 1,000 units may not be estimated
An estimate is always permitted, because Schedule III drugs never require an exact count
An estimate is permitted as long as the container has not been opened
No count is required, because bulk containers are covered by the supplier's invoice

questions.explanation: Although Schedule III through V substances may ordinarily be estimated, a container holding more than 1,000 units requires an exact count. The schedule alone does not guarantee estimation, and the container being unopened does not restore the estimate option at this size. Supplier invoices document orders and do not replace counting the stock on hand.

questions.question: A newly licensed pharmacist authorized to dispense controlled substances to humans asks about monitoring-system registration. What does the law require?

answers.text: Register once, with no duty to keep the account active
Register with the Cabinet and maintain an active account continuously during licensure
Registration is optional for pharmacists
Registration is required only after a first dispensing error

questions.explanation: Every practitioner or pharmacist authorized to prescribe or dispense controlled substances to humans must register and keep an account active continuously during licensure. A one-time registration that lapses ignores the active-account duty, the duty is not optional, and it does not wait for an error to attach.

questions.question: A prescription directs a dose well above the usual range and a duration far longer than appropriate for the stated therapy. Which prospective review screens are triggered?

answers.text: Only allergy and therapeutic duplication
Incorrect dosage and incorrect duration
Only age and gender contraindications
Only abuse and misuse

questions.explanation: Prospective review includes screening for incorrect dosage and incorrect duration, both of which are presented by an excessive dose paired with an excessive treatment length. Allergy, duplication, age, gender, abuse, and misuse are separate screens and do not describe a dose-and-duration problem on these facts.

questions.question: Pharmacist Daniel Okafor is evaluating whether an electronically received prescription for a non-controlled drug qualifies as a valid e-prescription. Which transmission path satisfies the requirement?

answers.text: The prescription is transmitted directly from the prescriber's system to the pharmacy's system
A staff member at an intermediary retypes the order and sends the retyped version onward
The prescriber's office prints the order and a courier delivers the printout
The patient forwards a screenshot of the order from a patient portal

questions.explanation: A valid electronic prescription is transmitted directly from the prescriber's system to the pharmacy's system, preserving the prescriber's order as sent. A retyped intermediary version, a couriered printout, and a patient-forwarded screenshot each break that direct system-to-system transmission and are not the e-prescription itself.

questions.question: While facing shelves, technician Ruth Adler finds four bottles that passed their expiration dates last month still standing among current stock, each flagged with a small sticker. She asks whether the stickers are enough. What should pharmacist Samir Haddad direct?

answers.text: Leave the bottles in place, since the stickers warn anyone who reaches for them
Move the bottles to the front of the active shelf so they are used before newer stock
Pull the bottles from the active shelf and segregate them away from dispensable inventory
Return the bottles to the active shelf after wiping off the printed dates

questions.explanation: Expired stock may not remain in active, dispensable inventory, and a warning sticker does not change that status. The bottles must be removed and segregated from current stock; featuring them for early use or erasing their dates would move expired product toward patients.

questions.question: A temperature-sensitive injection that must stay refrigerated until use is ready for a patient who will not reach home for several hours on a hot day. The patient suggests carrying it loose in a shopping bag. What should pharmacist David Kim arrange at dispensing?

answers.text: Provide the medication in a way that maintains its labeled refrigerated storage conditions during the patient's trip, such as an insulated container with cold packs, with counseling on prompt refrigeration at home
Hand it over loose, because storage conditions stop applying once a product is dispensed
Freeze the vial solid before handover so it thaws slowly on the trip
Tell the patient storage no longer matters because the first dose is due that evening

questions.explanation: Drugs must be kept at their labeled storage conditions, and that obligation extends to how a temperature-sensitive product is handed over and transported at dispensing. A loose bag on a hot day breaks the cold chain, freezing a refrigerated product violates its labeled conditions in the opposite direction, and an imminent first dose does not waive proper handling.

questions.question: After a hazardous-drug compounding session ends, technician Grace Liu wipes the work surface once with a general-purpose cleaner and announces the area is ready for non-hazardous compounding. Pharmacist Tom Becker stops her. What must happen to the surface first?

answers.text: The hazardous-drug deactivation and decontamination steps must be performed for the residues left by the session
Nothing further, because a single wipe with any cleaner satisfies hazardous-drug procedures
The surface must be covered with a clean drape so residue is sealed underneath
The area must simply air out overnight, with no cleaning steps recorded or performed

questions.explanation: Hazardous-drug procedures require deactivation and decontamination steps that address drug residues, not a single general-purpose wipe. Covering residue with a drape leaves it in place, and passive airing performs neither deactivation nor decontamination.

questions.question: To save money, a pharmacy director proposes compounding hazardous preparations on an open counter and relying entirely on the gloves, gowns, and other protective equipment staff will wear. Pharmacist Aisha Rahman reviews the proposal. How should she evaluate it?

answers.text: Approve it, because protective equipment and containment controls are interchangeable
Approve it if two staff members wear protective equipment at the same time
Reject it, because protective equipment supplements containment engineering controls and does not replace them
Approve it for experienced compounders, whose technique removes the need for containment

questions.explanation: Protective equipment is one layer of hazardous-drug handling alongside containment engineering controls, and it does not substitute for a containment primary engineering control. Adding a second wearer or relying on experience leaves the missing engineering containment unaddressed.

questions.question: A prescriber insists that pharmacist Ben Okafor fill a controlled-substance prescription, saying, 'I wrote it, so any problem with it is mine alone.' Ben has information indicating the prescription lacks a legitimate medical purpose. How does the law treat Ben's position?

answers.text: Ben shares a corresponding responsibility for the prescription's legitimacy, independent of the prescriber's, so the prescriber's assurance is not a defense to filling it
Ben is protected, because responsibility rests entirely with the person who wrote the prescription
Ben is responsible only if he also examined the patient
Ben's responsibility ended once he confirmed the prescriber's signature was genuine

questions.explanation: The pharmacist shares corresponding responsibility with the prescriber for a prescription's validity, and that duty is the pharmacist's own. It is not removed by the prescriber's willingness to accept blame, it does not depend on the pharmacist having examined the patient, and verifying a signature addresses authenticity of the document, not the legitimacy of the prescribing.

questions.question: A purchasing technician at pharmacist Amy Lindqvist's pharmacy prepares two orders: one for a Schedule II analgesic and one for a Schedule V cough preparation. Remembering that the analgesic needs special ordering documentation, she prepares a DEA Form 222 for both orders to be safe. Which correction is needed?

answers.text: The Schedule V order is placed on an ordinary invoice like other Schedule III through V orders; Form 222 or CSOS documentation is used for the Schedule II order
Both orders need Form 222, because any controlled substance may be ordered that way
Neither order needs any documentation, because both come from the same wholesaler
The Schedule II order goes on an invoice, and the Schedule V order needs the Form 222

questions.explanation: Form 222 and CSOS are the ordering route for Schedule II drugs, while Schedule III through V drugs are ordered on invoices, so the Schedule V order belongs on the pharmacy's ordinary invoice documentation. Applying Schedule II paperwork across all schedules misstates the system, ordering from one wholesaler does not erase the documentation for either order, and reversing the two routes gets both orders wrong.

questions.question: A pharmacy installs a barcode system that confirms the correct product, strength, and label for every filled prescription. The pharmacist-in-charge proposes that, when the system shows a match, experienced technicians may perform the final verification and release prescriptions so pharmacists can concentrate on clinical work. May this proposal be adopted?

answers.text: Yes, because a confirmed barcode match is equivalent to pharmacist verification
Yes, as long as it applies only to refills rather than new prescriptions
Yes, if the pharmacy documents the policy in its procedure manual
No, because final verification is always the pharmacist's responsibility, and technology that assists the process does not transfer it to technicians

questions.explanation: Final verification is always the pharmacist's function; barcode technology supports that verification but does not replace the pharmacist's professional check, and documenting the transfer in a policy manual cannot authorize it. The limit applies to refills as well as new prescriptions. Freeing pharmacist time for clinical work must be achieved within, not by abandoning, the verification structure.

questions.question: A business with no pharmacy permit offers to run a shared prescription-processing operation for several independent pharmacies, performing order entry and refill processing entirely under its own business registration, with each client pharmacy treating the arrangement as the vendor's independent operation. What is wrong with this structure?

answers.text: Nothing, because prescription processing is clerical work that any registered business may operate independently
The client pharmacies may use the service only if the vendor hires its own pharmacist-in-charge
Shared services and central processing must operate under the license and responsibility of a pharmacy, not as an independent unlicensed operation detached from a responsible pharmacy
The arrangement fails only if the vendor also delivers finished prescriptions to patients

questions.explanation: Central processing and shared services operate under the responsible pharmacy's license, so the work cannot be spun off as an independent operation answerable to no pharmacy license. Calling the tasks clerical does not remove them from the licensed arrangement, hiring a pharmacist-in-charge does not give a non-pharmacy a pharmacy license, and the structural defect exists in the processing arrangement itself regardless of whether deliveries are added.

louisiana-mpje.quiz_title: Louisiana MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A pharmacist transferring a license into Louisiana from another state asks the operative schedule fee for the transfer. What applies?

answers.text: The schedule fee for a license transfer is $450
The schedule fee for a license transfer is $300
The schedule fee for a license transfer is $50
The schedule fee for a license transfer is $150

questions.explanation: The fee schedule sets license transfer at $150. The $450 figure appears as a published application quote that exceeds the schedule and is not the schedule figure, $300 is the new-license-by-examination figure, and $50 is the intern and candidate registration figure.

questions.question: A pharmacist asks which agency now runs medical marijuana retail permitting and production licensing. What is correct?

answers.text: Those functions sit with the Board of Pharmacy under its pharmacy permit system
Those functions sit with the health department, including the retail permits and the two production licenses
Those functions sit with the State Police
Those functions were abolished, so no agency runs them

questions.explanation: Medical marijuana retail permitting and production licensing moved to the health department. The older Board-run marijuana pharmacy model no longer supplies the structure, the State Police role is pseudoephedrine monitoring, and the program continues under the health department rather than having been abolished.

questions.question: Reese buys a DME pharmacy business and assumes the seller's DME permit transfers with the sale. What is correct?

answers.text: The permit transfers automatically with the business assets
The permit transfers if the seller signs a notarized assignment
The permit transfers after one year of joint operation
DME permits are not transferable, so the permit does not pass to the buyer through the sale

questions.explanation: DME permits are expressly non-transferable. An automatic transfer on sale, a notarized assignment, and a transition year of joint operation all describe transfer mechanisms the rule does not allow.

questions.question: Quinn asks what physical and identification features define the automated medication system device. Which pairing is correct?

answers.text: Individual medication storage compartments within the device, together with bar-code scanning
One open bulk bin for all medications, with identification left to the user's memory
Compartments are forbidden, because doses must be stored loose for faster access
Bar-code scanning is optional and may be replaced by handwritten labels alone

questions.explanation: The statutory device description pairs individual medication storage compartments with bar-code scanning. A bulk bin with memory-based identification defeats both features, loose storage contradicts the compartment design, and scanning is a defining feature rather than an option replaceable by handwriting.

questions.question: An over-the-counter product on the shelf lacks required label information and does not provide adequate directions for use. How is this product classified?

answers.text: Adulterated, because inadequate directions always mean the product is decomposed
Misbranded, because required label information is missing and directions for use are inadequate
AB-rated, because it can be sold without a prescription
Exempt from labeling rules because it is sold over the counter

questions.explanation: Missing required label information and inadequate directions for use for an over-the-counter product make it misbranded. Decomposition is an adulteration defect in the product itself and is a different problem from the labeling failures described. Over-the-counter status does not create an Orange Book rating or exempt the product from labeling requirements.

questions.question: A pharmacist working under a collaborative practice agreement orders a lab test and changes a therapy in a way the agreement does not authorize, reasoning that the change was clinically appropriate. How is this conduct best characterized?

answers.text: Acceptable, because a good clinical outcome cures any paperwork problem
Practicing outside the delegated authority of the agreement
A minor documentation error with no practice consequences
Permitted whenever the pharmacist documents the clinical reasoning

questions.explanation: Authority under a collaborative practice agreement ends at the agreement's boundaries, so acting beyond them is practicing outside delegated authority regardless of clinical intent.
