A favorable outcome or thorough documentation does not retroactively authorize functions the agreement never granted.

questions.question: Nia asks which controlled substance schedules generate eligible transactions that a dispenser must report to the monitoring program. Which answer is complete?

answers.text: Schedules II, III, and IV only
Schedules II and III only
Schedules II, III, IV, and V
Schedule II only

questions.explanation: Eligible transactions cover all of Schedules II through V, not a subset of them. Stopping at Schedule IV omits Schedule V, stopping at Schedule III omits two schedules, and a Schedule II-only rule would exclude most of the transactions the program collects.

questions.question: A prescriber starts a patient on a non-opioid controlled substance, and Ira asks whether the mandatory query statute was triggered by that prescribing alone. What is correct?

answers.text: Yes, because the query duty covers every controlled substance
No, because the mandatory query duty is tied to opioid prescribing
Yes, because the query duty covers every prescription of any kind
No, because the query duty applies only to pharmacists

questions.explanation: The codified query duty is an opioid-prescribing duty, so starting a non-opioid controlled substance does not by itself trigger it. Extending the mandate to all controlled substances or all prescriptions broadens it beyond its text, and assigning it only to pharmacists reverses the duty's actual bearer.

questions.question: During the biennial inventory, a pharmacist is counting several bottles of morphine, a Schedule II drug, including sealed stock bottles. How must these drugs be counted?

answers.text: They may be estimated whenever the container is still sealed
An exact count is required for Schedule II substances
They may be estimated unless a single container holds more than 1,000 units
Only opened containers need to be counted, because sealed bottles are presumed full

questions.explanation: Schedule II substances require an exact count at inventory. Estimating a sealed container is not permitted for this schedule, and the more-than-1,000-units exact-count rule is the exception that applies within the Schedule III through V estimation framework, not a relaxation for Schedule II. Sealed Schedule II bottles are counted exactly along with opened ones rather than presumed full.

questions.question: An investor asks a pharmacist how Louisiana's medical marijuana retail program is structured and who runs it. Which description is correct?

answers.text: The Board of Pharmacy issues unlimited marijuana pharmacy permits, and pharmacists recommend the product to patients
The Department of Health issues fifty retail permits, and there is no patient quantity cap
Retail permits sit with the Board, production with the Department of Health, and the program is permanent

Retail permitting and production licensing sit with the Department of Health, with at most ten retail permits statewide at twenty-two thousand five hundred dollars per year and two production licenses, a designated responsible pharmacist for each retail permit holder, a patient cap of two and one-half ounces of raw marijuana per fourteen days, and a program sunset of July first, twenty thirty

questions.explanation: Since the twenty twenty-five restructuring, the health department issues at most ten retail permits statewide at twenty-two thousand five hundred dollars per year plus the two production licenses, and the pharmacist's statutory role is the permit holder's designated responsible pharmacist, reachable by phone or video during open hours. Pharmacists are not authorized recommenders, the patient cap is two and one-half ounces per fourteen days, and the authorizing section sunsets July first, twenty thirty rather than running permanently.

questions.question: After speaking with the prescriber, pharmacist Laura Nguyen learns the prescribed dosage form of a Schedule II drug is unavailable and the prescriber agrees to a different dosage form of the same drug. May the pharmacist make that change?

answers.text: No, dosage form can never be changed on a Schedule II prescription
Yes, after consulting the prescriber, the pharmacist may change the dosage form
Yes, without contacting the prescriber, whenever stock is short
Yes, and the pharmacist may also change the drug to a different therapeutic agent

questions.explanation: For a Schedule II prescription, dosage form is among the elements a pharmacist may change after consulting the prescriber. The change is not categorically barred, prescriber consultation is required rather than optional, and changing to a different drug altogether goes beyond a dosage-form change of the same drug.

questions.question: Skyler manages a community pharmacy that dispenses controlled substances and asks whether the pharmacy counts as a dispenser for monitoring program reporting. What is correct?

answers.text: Yes, because pharmacies that dispense controlled substances or drugs of concern are dispensers who must report
No, because only individual practitioners count as dispensers
No, because pharmacies report only through their wholesalers
Yes, but only hospital pharmacies count as dispensers

questions.explanation: A pharmacy that dispenses controlled substances or drugs of concern is a dispenser with reporting duties. The category is not limited to individual practitioners, reporting is the pharmacy's own duty rather than something routed through a wholesaler, and community pharmacies are included rather than only hospital pharmacies.

questions.question: During receiving, pharmacist Marcus Yeung identifies a bottle whose packaging and identifiers show it is counterfeit. His assistant proposes sending it back to the supplier for credit so the pharmacy does not lose money on it. What must the pharmacist do instead?

answers.text: Dispense it only to patients who are told about the packaging problem
Send it back for credit, because returning it removes it from the pharmacy
Quarantine the counterfeit product and report it; it must not be dispensed or sent back into commerce
Move it to a back shelf and decide about it at the next quarterly inventory

questions.explanation: Suspect and counterfeit product must be quarantined and reported, and it must never be dispensed. Returning it to the supplier for credit puts the product back into commerce channels rather than isolating it. Leaving it on a back shelf until a quarterly inventory leaves counterfeit product unsecured and unreported in the meantime.

questions.question: During a stock inspection, pharmacist Grace Okafor finds a bottle whose contents show visible breakdown from age and heat exposure, with discolored, crumbling tablets. A staff member asks whether the product can still be dispensed at a discount. How is this product classified, and what follows?

answers.text: It is merely mislabeled, so it may be dispensed once a new label is printed
It is a recalled product, so it may be dispensed until the recall notice arrives
It is an expired generic, so it may be dispensed if the patient consents in writing
It is adulterated because the drug has decomposed, and it may not be dispensed

questions.explanation: A drug that has decomposed is adulterated, and adulterated product may not be dispensed, discounted or otherwise. Relabeling addresses labeling defects rather than decomposition, a recall notice is not what creates this defect, and a patient's written consent does not make an adulterated drug dispensable.

questions.question: A sterile compounding manager proposes keeping only failed environmental monitoring reports in the quality file and discarding passing results, competency passes, and routine documentation to reduce clutter. Pharmacist Helen Osei reviews the proposal. What is correct?

answers.text: The quality file must retain the compounding quality records, including monitoring results and competency documentation, not only failures
The proposal is sound, because only failures have any quality value
The quality file may consist of the manager's verbal assurance that checks occurred
Routine documentation may be discarded once the next compounding session begins

questions.explanation: Quality assurance depends on retained records of the monitoring and competency program as a whole, so passing results and competency documentation are kept alongside failures. Failures alone cannot show the program operated routinely, verbal assurance is not a record, and beginning a new session does not end the duty to retain the last session's documentation.

questions.question: A prescription names a specific drug product, and the pharmacy stocks only a version of the drug made with a different salt form. A staff member proposes dispensing the stocked version as the generic substitute because the active ingredient name looks nearly the same. What should pharmacist Laura Bennett do?

answers.text: Decline to treat the different salt form as an interchangeable generic substitute for the prescribed product
Dispense the different salt form, because any product sharing the same base drug name is interchangeable
Dispense the different salt form if it is priced lower than the prescribed product
Dispense half the quantity of the different salt form as a trial until the prescriber's office reopens

questions.explanation: A different salt form of a drug is a different product, not an interchangeable generic substitute for the prescribed product, so it may not be dispensed as a substitution. A similar base name and a lower price do not create interchangeability, and dispensing a partial trial quantity of a different product is still an unauthorized substitution.

questions.question: A prescriber insists that pharmacist Ben Okafor fill a controlled-substance prescription, saying, 'I wrote it, so any problem with it is mine alone.' Ben has information indicating the prescription lacks a legitimate medical purpose. How does the law treat Ben's position?

answers.text: Ben shares a corresponding responsibility for the prescription's legitimacy, independent of the prescriber's, so the prescriber's assurance is not a defense to filling it
Ben is protected, because responsibility rests entirely with the person who wrote the prescription
Ben is responsible only if he also examined the patient
Ben's responsibility ended once he confirmed the prescriber's signature was genuine

questions.explanation: The pharmacist shares corresponding responsibility with the prescriber for a prescription's validity, and that duty is the pharmacist's own. It is not removed by the prescriber's willingness to accept blame, it does not depend on the pharmacist having examined the patient, and verifying a signature addresses authenticity of the document, not the legitimacy of the prescribing.

questions.question: A cardiologist treating a shared patient calls pharmacist James Okafor to ask what medications the patient is currently taking, so she can avoid a harmful interaction before prescribing. James's manager asks whether he must first obtain the patient's written authorization and limit the disclosure to the minimum necessary. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: He may share the information for treatment without patient authorization, and the minimum-necessary standard does not apply to treatment disclosures
He may share it only after the patient signs a written authorization naming the cardiologist
He may share it for treatment, but he must first strip the record down to the minimum necessary
He may not share it at all because disclosures to another practice always require authorization

questions.explanation: Protected health information may be used and disclosed for treatment without patient authorization, and the minimum-necessary standard applies to payment and operations rather than to treatment. Requiring a signed authorization first, reducing the disclosure to a minimum-necessary subset, and refusing the disclosure outright all impose limits that do not govern a treatment disclosure between treating providers.

questions.question: When the pharmacist-in-charge of a hospital pharmacy takes an extended leave, staff pharmacist Brian Kessler agrees to be designated as acting pharmacist-in-charge. He assumes the 'acting' label means the compliance duties stay with the absent pharmacist-in-charge. Is he right?

answers.text: Yes, because an acting designee carries the title but none of the accountability
Yes, because accountability attaches only to a permanent appointment

No, because the pharmacist designated as in charge — including an acting designee — bears the pharmacist-in-charge's responsibility for the pharmacy's compliance, security, records, and supervision of personnel
No, but only because hospital pharmacies are exempt from pharmacist-in-charge designation

questions.explanation: The pharmacist-in-charge role carries responsibility for the pharmacy's compliance, security, records, and supervision of personnel, and that responsibility attaches to whoever is designated in charge, acting or permanent. An absent predecessor cannot retain duties for a pharmacy she is not running, and no setting is exempt from having a designated pharmacist in charge.

questions.question: Pharmacy A performs central processing for Pharmacy B, and a data-entry error made at Pharmacy A leads to a wrong strength being filled and dispensed at Pharmacy B. Pharmacy B's owner argues that because the error originated at Pharmacy A, Pharmacy B bears no responsibility for the dispensed prescription. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Pharmacy B is correct, because responsibility follows the employee who made the original keystroke
Neither pharmacy is responsible, because shared processing divides accountability until it disappears
Only the technician who entered the data is responsible, since pharmacists do not answer for processed orders

Responsibility is allocated under the shared-services arrangement and Pharmacy B, as the dispensing pharmacy operating under its license, retains responsibility for what it dispenses, including its pharmacist's verification

questions.explanation: In a shared-services arrangement each participating pharmacy remains accountable under its own license for the functions it performs, and the dispensing pharmacy cannot shed responsibility for a prescription its pharmacist verified and dispensed merely because an upstream step contributed to the error. Accountability does not vanish when work is shared, does not rest solely on the person who typed the entry, and is not limited to technicians when pharmacists retain verification duties.

massachusetts-mpje.quiz_title: Massachusetts MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A prescriber tells a pharmacist that gabapentin is a Schedule V controlled substance in Massachusetts. What is correct?

answers.text: Gabapentin is not a scheduled controlled substance in Massachusetts
The prescriber is right, because gabapentin is Schedule V here
Gabapentin is Schedule IV here
Gabapentin is Schedule II here

questions.explanation: Gabapentin carries no schedule as a controlled substance in Massachusetts. Placing it in Schedule V, Schedule IV, or Schedule II each assigns it a controlled substance status it does not hold.

questions.question: Devon assumes the Board runs the state prescription monitoring program because it licenses pharmacists, and asks whether that assumption is right. What is correct?

answers.text: No, because the Department of Public Health administers the prescription monitoring program, not the Board
Yes, because the Board administers the program through its licensing staff
Yes, because the Board and the Department share administration equally
No, because a private vendor administers the program with no state agency involved

questions.explanation: The prescription monitoring program is administered by the Department of Public Health rather than the Board of Registration in Pharmacy. Board administration and shared administration both misassign the program, and no private vendor administers it free of the responsible state department.

questions.question: A pharmacist fills a methylphenidate prescription and asks which single filling ceiling applies to it under current law. What is correct?

answers.text: Up to a 60-day supply, under the stimulant-specific ceiling
Up to a 30-day supply, like every other Schedule II drug
A 14-day supply, because stimulants are limited to two weeks
Up to a 90-day supply in a single filling, because it is a non-opioid drug in the covered schedules

questions.explanation: Methylphenidate is expressly within the non-opioid category that carries the 90-day single filling ceiling. The 60-day stimulant figure comes from dead text, a universal 30-day rule ignores the enumerated categories, and a two-week cap appears in neither the current nor the superseded framing.

questions.question: Casey asks what duty the prescription monitoring program law places on pharmacists themselves. What is correct?

answers.text: Pharmacists must query the program before every dispensing
Pharmacists must administer the program for the Board
Pharmacists must complete training related to the prescription monitoring program
Pharmacists have no program-related duty of any kind

questions.explanation: The monitoring program law imposes a training requirement on pharmacists. A query before every dispensing is a mandate the law does not place on pharmacists, administering the program belongs to the state health department rather than to individual pharmacists or the Board, and the training duty means pharmacists are not free of program obligations altogether.

questions.question: Reese asks whether the shield label substitution is available for every prescription the pharmacy fills. What is correct?

answers.text: Yes, because any prescriber may use a practice name on any label for convenience
Yes, because the substitution is mandatory for every controlled substance label
No, because the substitution applies only to prescriptions written outside Massachusetts
No, because the substitution applies to prescriptions for reproductive and gender-affirming health care services

questions.explanation: The shield substitution is tied to reproductive and gender-affirming care prescriptions rather than to labeling generally. Convenience use on any label and mandatory use on controlled substance labels both detach it from that subject matter, and its scope turns on the kind of care rather than on where the prescription was written.

questions.question: A patient's profile shows relevant medical conditions and a complete medication history, and the patient is starting a drug affected by one of those conditions. How should pharmacist Elena use the profile?

answers.text: Use the profile's conditions and medication history in prospective review and counseling before dispensing
Ignore the conditions because profiles are kept only for billing
Delete the conditions from the profile to avoid an alert
Use the profile only after the patient reports a problem at home

questions.explanation: The patient profile is maintained for drug utilization review and counseling, so its relevant conditions and medication history must be used prospectively and in counseling before dispensing. Billing is not the profile's purpose here, deleting conditions destroys information needed for review, and waiting for a problem at home abandons prospective use.

questions.question: Vale holds a pharmacist license from another state that was granted without any examination and asks whether it supports Massachusetts reciprocity. What applies?

answers.text: Yes, because any current out-of-state license supports reciprocity
Yes, if Vale has practiced for at least ten years on that license
No, because reciprocity requires licensure by examination in another jurisdiction
No, because reciprocity requires licensure in Massachusetts first

questions.explanation: Reciprocity rests on holding licensure by examination in another jurisdiction, which a license granted without examination does not supply. Any current license and long practice on an unexamined license both overlook the examination basis, and requiring Massachusetts licensure first would make reciprocity circular.

questions.question: Quinn searches the Board's establishing provisions for a general quorum rule covering all Board business and asks what they contain. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The establishing provisions set a general quorum of seven members for all Board business
There is no general quorum provision for the Board in its establishing provisions, and the stated quorum rule is the three-member rule for discipline hearings
The establishing provisions set a general quorum of a majority of the pharmacist members only
The establishing provisions require all thirteen members for any Board action

questions.explanation: The Board's establishing provisions contain no general quorum rule, and the quorum figure the law states is the three-member rule tied to discipline hearings. A seven-member general quorum and a pharmacist-only majority both invent a provision that is not there, and requiring all thirteen members contradicts the narrower hearing rule that does exist.

questions.question: Pharmacist-in-charge Dana Whitaker is redesigning her pharmacy's controlled-substance filing system. Which plan satisfies the federal record requirements?

answers.text: Keep all controlled-substance records for one year, with Schedule II records filed together with Schedule III through V records
Keep the records for at least two years, but file Schedule II records in the same folder as the other controlled-substance records
Keep the records for at least two years and maintain Schedule II records separately from the other controlled-substance records
Keep Schedule II records separately, but destroy all controlled-substance records after 18 months to limit storage

questions.explanation: The federal floor requires controlled-substance inventories and records to be kept for at least two years, and Schedule II records must be maintained separately from other controlled-substance records. A one-year or 18-month destruction schedule falls short of the two-year minimum. Holding records for two years but filing Schedule II records together with Schedule III through V records fails the separation requirement.

questions.question: Two board inspectors arrive at a retail pharmacy during regular business hours and ask to inspect the prescription department and its records. What is the pharmacy's obligation?

answers.text: The pharmacy may postpone any inspection until a complaint against it has been closed
The pharmacy must permit board entry and inspection during business hours
The pharmacy may refuse inspection unless the inspectors schedule an appointment at least 30 days ahead
Only the Food and Drug Administration may inspect a pharmacy, so the inspectors must leave

questions.explanation: State boards have authority to enter and inspect a pharmacy during business hours, and to investigate complaints. That authority is not conditioned on a complaint first being closed or on a lengthy advance appointment, and inspection of licensed pharmacies is a board function rather than an exclusively FDA function.

questions.question: After consulting the prescriber, pharmacist David Lindqvist changes the strength and directions on a Schedule II prescription to match the prescriber's revised plan. Beyond making the changes themselves, what must David do with them?

answers.text: Nothing further; changes agreed by phone need no record on the prescription
Wait for a brand-new prescription before recording anything
Ask the patient to confirm the changes in writing at pickup instead
Document the changes on the prescription record

questions.explanation: Changes a pharmacist makes to a Schedule II prescription after prescriber consultation are documented on the prescription record, so the dispensed order can be audited against what the prescriber authorized. An undocumented phone agreement leaves no trail. The patient's pickup confirmation is not a substitute, and obtaining a new prescription is unnecessary where the change is one the pharmacist may make after consultation.

questions.question: A newly licensed pharmacist with strong supervisory training is offered a Manager of Record position, and a colleague claims the appointment is impossible because new licensees are barred from the role for a set period. What is correct?

answers.text: The claim is unfounded, because the codified rules set no minimum practice period before a registered pharmacist may serve as Manager of Record
The claim is right, because a pharmacist must practice three years before managing
The claim is right, because a pharmacist must hold a management certificate first
The appointment is barred for a different reason, because only pharmacy owners may manage

questions.explanation: The codified rules impose no minimum years-of-practice condition on serving as Manager of Record, so length of licensure alone does not bar the appointment. A three-year practice floor and a management certificate requirement are both conditions the rules do not contain, and ownership is not the credential the manager role requires.

questions.question: At final check, pharmacist Luis Herrera sees that a sealed, properly stored vial ready for a patient was labeled without several pieces of information the dispensed container label is required to carry. The drug itself is sound and in date. How is the drug in this container classified?

answers.text: Adulterated, because any labeling omission changes the drug's quality
Counterfeit, because the container came from the pharmacy rather than the manufacturer
Misbranded, because a dispensed container missing required label information makes the labeling deficient
Acceptable for dispensing, because labeling omissions matter only for over-the-counter products

questions.explanation: A drug whose labeling is missing required information is misbranded, and a dispensed prescription container that lacks required label information renders the drug misbranded even when the product itself is sound. Adulteration concerns contamination, decomposition, or quality defects in the drug itself, counterfeiting concerns falsified product or identity, and required labeling applies to dispensed prescriptions as well as over-the-counter products.

questions.question: Prescriber Dr. Hannah Brooks marks a prescription so the brand product must be dispensed as written, prohibiting substitution. At pickup, the patient asks pharmacist Luis Ortega to dispense the lower-cost AB-rated generic instead and offers to sign a note accepting the switch. What should the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Dispense the generic, because the patient's signed note overrides the prescriber's direction
Dispense the generic, because an AB rating makes substitution mandatory
Dispense the generic if the pharmacist documents the cost savings for the patient
Dispense the brand product, because the prescriber's prohibition controls despite the patient's request

questions.explanation: A pharmacist may dispense an FDA-approved generic equivalent only unless the prescriber prohibits substitution; here the prescriber has prohibited it, so the brand must be dispensed as written. A patient's request or signed note cannot override that prohibition. An AB rating establishes that a generic is interchangeable when substitution is permitted — it never makes substitution mandatory against a prescriber's direction.

questions.question: A pharmacy repackages tablets from a manufacturer's bottle that expires in four months. A technician proposes assigning the repackaged units a beyond-use date nine months out because the repackaging room is well controlled. What must the pharmacist do?

answers.text: Approve nine months because repackaging resets the expiration clock
Approve nine months if the units are kept refrigerated
Keep the assigned date at or before the manufacturer's expiration date
Use the date the pharmacy received the stock bottle instead

questions.explanation: A repackaged product's assigned beyond-use date may never exceed the manufacturer's expiration date, so a date nine months out cannot stand when the original product expires in four months. Repackaging does not reset the manufacturer's clock, refrigeration does not extend that ceiling, and the receipt date is not the controlling limit.

questions.question: A compounding pharmacy prepares an oil-based oral liquid for patient Andre Boateng. The formulation contains no water and the pharmacy has no stability data for it. A technician proposes dating it 180 days because the batch is large. What is the correct default beyond-use date?

answers.text: 90 days, the default limit for a non-aqueous liquid without stability data
14 days refrigerated, the default for any compounded oral liquid
35 days, the default for any liquid that contains a preservative
180 days, because batch size determines the dating of liquids

questions.explanation: A non-aqueous liquid compounded preparation carries a default beyond-use date of 90 days when no stability data support a longer period, and batch size does not change that limit. The 14-day refrigerated limit applies to non-preserved aqueous preparations and the 35-day limit to preserved aqueous preparations, while this formulation contains no water. The 180-day limit applies to solid dosage forms, not to a liquid.

questions.question: A prescriber telephones a pharmacy and orally instructs the pharmacist not to substitute a particular biologic for one named patient, and Quinn asks whether that instruction bars substitution and what the substitution rules require afterward. What is correct?

answers.text: The oral instruction bars substitution completely, because any prescriber instruction in any form defeats the permission

The oral instruction does not bar substitution, because only a written patient-specific instruction bars it, and after substituting the pharmacist must notify the prescriber within a reasonable time, give the patient written notice, and keep substitution records for at least one year
The oral instruction does not bar substitution, but the prescriber must be notified within five days and records kept for five years
The oral instruction bars substitution for that patient, and no notice or records duties exist for biologics at all

questions.explanation: Biologics substitution is defeated only by a written, patient-specific prescriber instruction, notice to the prescriber runs within a reasonable time with no fixed day-count, the patient receives written notice, and substitution records are kept at least one year by the pharmacist, the prescriber, and the administering practitioner. Treating an oral instruction as a complete bar contradicts the written-instruction requirement, the five-day notice figure is another jurisdiction's rule and five-year records overstate the one-year period, and denying the notice and records duties ignores obligations the substitution provision imposes.

questions.question: Peyton attends a conference offering twelve hours of credit in one day and asks how many of those hours can count toward the annual requirement. What is correct?

answers.text: All twelve hours can count, because they were earned at one accredited event
No more than five hours earned in a single day can count
No more than ten hours earned in a single day can count
No more than eight hours earned in a single day can count

questions.explanation: Credit is limited to eight hours per day, so four of the conference hours cannot count toward the requirement. Accreditation of the event does not lift the daily cap, and five and ten hours are not the stated daily ceiling.

questions.question: New hire Jordan Ellis proudly shows his manager a national pharmacy technician certification certificate and asks to begin counting and preparing prescriptions that afternoon. The pharmacy has not yet confirmed any state credential for him. May he begin technician duties on the strength of the national certificate?

answers.text: Yes, because national certification authorizes technician practice in every state
Yes, if the pharmacist-in-charge verbally approves him for that shift
No, because national certification alone does not authorize practice; state registration or licensure is also required
No, because a certified technician must first work a full year as a trainee before touching prescriptions

questions.explanation: National certification and state authorization are separate credentials, and certification alone does not authorize a person to practice as a pharmacy technician; state registration or licensure through the board is also required. Treating the national certificate as a nationwide practice license confuses a private credential with state authorization, a pharmacist-in-charge's verbal approval cannot substitute for the state credential, and the barrier here is the missing state registration rather than any mandatory year of traineeship.

questions.question: A newly hired pharmacist finds that her pharmacy files its Schedule II prescription records in the same undifferentiated sequence as all of its other controlled-substance records, so a Schedule II record can be located only by reading through the entire file. Her pharmacist-in-charge says separation is optional for a small store. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Schedule II records must be maintained separately from the pharmacy's other records, so the mixed filing must be corrected
Separation is genuinely optional, and small pharmacies are exempt from it
Separation is required only for pharmacies that also sell Schedule I substances
The mixed filing is acceptable if the pharmacy performs a biennial inventory on schedule

questions.explanation: Federal recordkeeping requires Schedule II records to be maintained separately from other records, unlike Schedule III through V records, which have the readily-retrievable alternative. Store size creates no exemption, pharmacies do not sell Schedule I substances, which have no accepted medical use, and completing inventories does not substitute for the separate-records requirement.

maine-mpje.quiz_title: Maine MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Gamma hydroxybutyrate is placed in which Maine schedule?

answers.text: Schedule W
Schedule Y
Schedule Z
Schedule X

questions.explanation: Gamma hydroxybutyrate is listed in Schedule X. Schedule W overstates its placement, and Schedule Y and Schedule Z both contradict the express listing.

questions.question: A pharmacy manager setting up vaccine documentation asks about reporting to the state system. What does the law require?

answers.text: Since August 1, 2023, the pharmacist shall report administration of a vaccine to the state immunization information reporting system within 72 hours of administering it
Reporting is required once a month in a batch summary
Reporting is required within 30 days after administration
Reporting to the state system is voluntary for community pharmacies

questions.explanation: Vaccine administrations are reported to the state immunization information system within 72 hours, under the requirement in effect since August 1, 2023. Monthly batching and a thirty-day window both miss that deadline, and the reporting is a duty rather than a voluntary practice.

questions.question: What could move the veterinarian electronic prescribing duty earlier than July 1, 2025?

answers.text: A vote of the state veterinary association
A determination by the Commissioner of Health and Human Services that an electronic platform is widely available for veterinarians
The opening of a new veterinary school in Maine
A request from any single veterinary practice

questions.explanation: The veterinarian e-prescribing date can arrive earlier if the Commissioner of Health and Human Services determines an electronic platform is widely available for veterinarians. An association vote, a new school, and a single practice's request are not the trigger the section states.

questions.question: Under the rule, before the department notifies a licensing entity of a check or reporting violation, what must the prescriber or dispenser receive?

answers.text: No notice, because notification is immediate and confidential
Six months of advance notice and a full trial
Notice only after the licensing entity has already acted
Two weeks of advance notice and an opportunity to comment

questions.explanation: The rule gives the prescriber or dispenser two weeks of advance notice and an opportunity to comment before the department notifies the licensing entity. Immediate secret notification and after-the-fact notice both defeat the advance process, and a six-month trial procedure far exceeds what the rule provides.

questions.question: Alex asks what fixes the date on which a Maine pharmacist license expires. What is correct?

answers.text: The license expires two years after issuance on the anniversary of the examination
The license expires on the pharmacist's birthday each year
The license expires on the date set by the commissioner under the OPOR framework statute
The Board president sets a different expiration date for each pharmacist

questions.explanation: A pharmacist license expires on the date set by the commissioner under the OPOR framework statute. A biennial examination anniversary and a birthday cycle both invent calendars the provision does not use, and the date is a uniform commissioner-set date rather than an individual presidential choice.

questions.question: A prescriber's office faxes a signed Schedule II prescription for a general outpatient who is not in long-term care, hospice, or home infusion. Pharmacist Miguel Santos asks what the fax lawfully lets the pharmacy do tonight. Which answer is correct?

answers.text: Use the fax to prepare the prescription, but wait for the signed original before dispensing
Dispense from the fax, since it bears the prescriber's signature
Dispense half the quantity from the fax and the rest when the original arrives
Refuse the order entirely, because a faxed Schedule II prescription has no lawful use

questions.explanation: For a Schedule II patient outside the long-term care, hospice, and home-infusion exceptions, a fax may be used to prepare the prescription so it is ready, but dispensing must wait until the signed original is presented. The fax alone does not authorize dispensing any portion of the quantity. It is not useless, however — preparation in advance is precisely what it permits.

questions.question: Under prevailing principles, a pharmacy intern is on duty with a supervising pharmacist. Which statement correctly describes the intern's role?

answers.text: The intern may perform most pharmacist functions under direct supervision, but may not perform final verification
The intern may perform final verification whenever the supervising pharmacist is busy
The intern may counsel patients with no pharmacist supervision at all
The intern may operate the pharmacy alone during the pharmacist's meal break

questions.explanation: Under prevailing principles, interns may perform most pharmacist functions under direct supervision, with final verification reserved to the pharmacist. A busy pharmacist does not transfer final verification, counseling by an intern remains a supervised function, and an intern's presence does not allow the pharmacy to operate without a pharmacist on duty.

questions.question: During the biennial inventory, a pharmacist is counting several bottles of morphine, a Schedule II drug, including sealed stock bottles. How must these drugs be counted?

answers.text: They may be estimated whenever the container is still sealed
An exact count is required for Schedule II substances
They may be estimated unless a single container holds more than 1,000 units
Only opened containers need to be counted, because sealed bottles are presumed full

questions.explanation: Schedule II substances require an exact count at inventory. Estimating a sealed container is not permitted for this schedule, and the more-than-1,000-units exact-count rule is the exception that applies within the Schedule III through V estimation framework, not a relaxation for Schedule II. Sealed Schedule II bottles are counted exactly along with opened ones rather than presumed full.

questions.question: A prescription was written for thirty tablets and the patient requested and received ten in a partial fill. What quantity must the practitioner notice state?

answers.text: The quantity actually dispensed, which is ten tablets
The quantity originally prescribed, which is thirty tablets
The quantity remaining, which is twenty tablets
No quantity, because the notice states only the date

questions.explanation: The notice after a partial fill states the quantity actually dispensed, so it reports the ten tablets the patient received. The prescribed quantity and the void remainder describe amounts the patient did not receive in the fill, and the notice does carry a quantity.

questions.question: Pharmacist Tomas Reed completes the period and conditions stated in a board order that took away his right to practice for eight months, and the board restores his license. Which sanction did he serve?

answers.text: Suspension of the license for a defined period
Revocation of the license
A reprimand recorded on his license file
Denial of his original license application

questions.explanation: Suspension is temporary: the licensee loses the right to practice for a period or until conditions are met and may then return to practice. Revocation permanently removes the license, a reprimand leaves the license in effect with a formal warning on record, and denial concerns an application rather than an existing license held by a practicing pharmacist.

questions.question: During prospective review, pharmacist Tom sees early fills, escalating use, and a pattern suggesting the patient is misusing a prescribed drug. Which screen captures this concern?

answers.text: Child-resistant packaging compliance
Expiration-date verification
Abuse and misuse screening before dispensing
Manufacturer labeling verification

questions.explanation: Prospective drug utilization review includes screening for abuse and misuse, which is the concern raised by early fills and escalating use. Packaging compliance, expiration verification, and manufacturer labeling checks are important dispensing tasks but do not screen a patient's pattern of use.

questions.question: At pickup, a technician tells a patient, 'The pharmacist can counsel you on this new drug if you would like,' and the patient asks a follow-up clinical question. What is correct about the technician's role here?

answers.text: The technician exceeded the role by making the offer
The technician may now answer the clinical question because the technician made the offer
The technician must counsel because the patient accepted the offer
The technician may offer the pharmacist's counseling but may not counsel or answer the clinical question, which goes to the pharmacist

questions.explanation: Technicians may offer the pharmacist's counseling but cannot counsel or answer clinical questions, so the follow-up question must go to the pharmacist. Making the offer itself is within the technician's role, and neither making the offer nor the patient's acceptance converts the technician into the counselor.

questions.question: During a routine inventory audit, pharmacist Marcus Lee pulls a sealed bottle from the shelf and notices that the product identifier printed on the container does not match the identifier shown in the product's labeling. What is the correct classification and handling of this bottle?

answers.text: It is merely mislabeled stock that may be dispensed once the pharmacist corrects the label by hand
It is a saleable return that may be sent back through the verification router for credit
It is suspect product under the DSCSA and must be quarantined while the discrepancy is investigated
It is expired product and must be moved to the disposal bin without further review

questions.explanation: A mismatch between a container's product identifier and its labeling makes the product suspect under the DSCSA track-and-trace framework, so it must be quarantined and investigated rather than dispensed. Hand-correcting the label would put a questionable product into use, saleable-return verification applies to returns being resold rather than to an identifier discrepancy found in inventory, and nothing in the scenario shows the product is expired.

questions.question: A retail pharmacy's pharmacist in charge resigns and the owner proposes operating for a month with only technicians and a relief pharmacist who has not registered as pharmacist in charge, and Wren asks whether that works. What applies?

answers.text: Yes, because a relief pharmacist's presence alone satisfies the requirement
Yes, because a pharmacy may operate without a pharmacist in charge for up to ninety days

No, because a retail pharmacy's business is conducted under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist who has registered as the pharmacist in charge with the Board, and no retail pharmacy may operate without one
No, because the pharmacy must instead register its senior technician as pharmacist in charge

questions.explanation: A retail pharmacy operates under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist registered as its pharmacist in charge, and it may not operate without one. An unregistered relief pharmacist and a ninety-day gap both leave the pharmacy without the registered pharmacist in charge the rule requires, and a technician cannot hold the position.

questions.question: While filling an oral prescription, a technician notices the patient's intake form says no children live in the home and suggests switching to a plain snap cap for convenience. Neither the patient nor the prescriber has asked for non-child-resistant packaging. What should pharmacist Tom Becker do?

answers.text: Keep the child-resistant container, because that packaging remains the default unless the patient or the prescriber requests otherwise
Use the snap cap, because a household with no children is automatically exempt from child-resistant packaging
Use the snap cap whenever the intake form lists only adult residents, without asking anyone
Let the technician decide based on how crowded the packaging shelf is that day

questions.explanation: Child-resistant packaging is the default for most oral prescriptions, and the absence of children in the household does not by itself remove that default. The packaging changes when the patient or the prescriber requests otherwise, not when staff infer an exemption from an intake form or choose based on convenience or shelf space.

questions.question: A drug dispensed by pharmacist Hannah Lindqvist is one for which a Medication Guide must be dispensed with the drug. The pharmacy has run out of that guide, but a clerk offers to enclose the product's patient package insert instead, arguing both are FDA patient paperwork. What is correct?

answers.text: The insert is an acceptable substitute whenever the guide is out of stock
Either document satisfies the requirement, because both are written for patients
The Medication Guide requirement is not met by substituting a different document, so the required guide itself must be provided with the drug
The guide requirement disappears for this fill if the insert is enclosed and the substitution is documented

questions.explanation: A Medication Guide that is required for a drug must itself be dispensed with the drug; a patient package insert is a different required document for other products and does not satisfy the guide requirement. Stock shortages and documentation of a substitution do not convert one document into the other or waive the guide for that dispensing.

questions.question: A pharmacy receives a faxed prescription that was generated by an outside fax service from a scanned note, and it does not bear the prescriber's signature. The prescriber's office confirms by phone that the prescriber did intend the medication. May the fax itself serve as the prescription?

answers.text: Yes, because the prescriber's intent was confirmed by phone
Yes, because any fax received on pharmacy letterhead paper is valid
No, because a valid faxed prescription must originate from the prescriber's office and bear the prescriber's signature, and a fax generated by an intermediary is not valid
No, but only because the medication is not a controlled substance

questions.explanation: A faxed prescription must originate from the prescriber's office and bear the prescriber's signature; a fax generated by an intermediary rather than the prescriber's office is not a valid faxed prescription. Verbal confirmation of intent does not cure the defective fax itself, the paper it arrives on is irrelevant, and the origin-and-signature defects are not limited to controlled substances.

questions.question: A remote dispensing site is staffed on site by a pharmacy technician, with a pharmacist supervising from the main pharmacy by live link. The technician asks whether a filled prescription can be handed to a waiting patient right away to keep the line moving, before the pharmacist's check. What governs the handoff?

answers.text: The technician may hand it over, because working at a remote site removes the verification step
The technician may hand it over if the patient signs a waiver of pharmacist review
The technician works under the pharmacist's supervision, and dispensing requires the pharmacist's verification before the medication is handed over
The site's landlord may authorize the handoff when the pharmacist's link is busy

questions.explanation: At a remote or telepharmacy site the technician works under a pharmacist's supervision, and dispensing still requires pharmacist verification, so a filled prescription is not handed over before that check. Distance from the main pharmacy does not remove verification, a patient waiver cannot waive it, and a landlord holds no authority over dispensing decisions.

questions.question: A pharmacist is found to have violated Maine's prohibition on conversion therapy. What follows for the license?

answers.text: Nothing follows, because the prohibition carries no licensing consequence
The violation is a pharmacist-specific ground for discipline
The license is automatically revoked with no disciplinary proceeding of any kind
The violation matters only if it occurred inside a pharmacy building

questions.explanation: Violation of the conversion-therapy prohibition is a stated pharmacist-specific ground for discipline. It is not consequence-free for licensure, it operates as a ground within the discipline framework rather than as an automatic revocation without process, and no pharmacy-building location condition is stated.

questions.question: A cardiologist treating a shared patient calls pharmacist James Okafor to ask what medications the patient is currently taking, so she can avoid a harmful interaction before prescribing. James's manager asks whether he must first obtain the patient's written authorization and limit the disclosure to the minimum necessary. What is the correct answer?

answers.text: He may share the information for treatment without patient authorization, and the minimum-necessary standard does not apply to treatment disclosures
He may share it only after the patient signs a written authorization naming the cardiologist
He may share it for treatment, but he must first strip the record down to the minimum necessary
He may not share it at all because disclosures to another practice always require authorization

questions.explanation: Protected health information may be used and disclosed for treatment without patient authorization, and the minimum-necessary standard applies to payment and operations rather than to treatment. Requiring a signed authorization first, reducing the disclosure to a minimum-necessary subset, and refusing the disclosure outright all impose limits that do not govern a treatment disclosure between treating providers.

minnesota-mpje.quiz_title: Minnesota MPJE Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Blair asks who appoints the program's Advisory Task Force and how long it lasts. What is correct?

answers.text: The governor appoints the task force, which expires every two years unless renewed
The task force is appointed by the commissioner of health and has five members serving at the commissioner's pleasure
The task force appoints itself from program users and expires when the database is replaced
The Board appoints the task force, which is drawn from ten representative categories and never expires

questions.explanation: The Board appoints the Advisory Task Force, which is drawn from ten representative categories and never expires. Appointment by the governor or the health commissioner moves the power away from the Board, and an expiring or self-appointed body contradicts the task force's standing structure.

questions.question: Riley asks which examinations a Minnesota pharmacist applicant must pass before licensure. What is correct?

answers.text: Both the NAPLEX and the MPJE must be passed
Only the NAPLEX must be passed
Only the MPJE must be passed
Either the NAPLEX or the MPJE may be passed, at the applicant's choice

questions.explanation: Minnesota requires the applicant to pass both the NAPLEX and the MPJE before licensure. Passing only one of the two examinations, or treating them as alternatives, omits a required examination.

questions.question: A prescriber concludes that an adult patient genuinely needs more than a 7-day supply for acute pain. What does the statute allow?

answers.text: The limits are absolute and may never be exceeded
A practitioner may exceed a limit when, in the practitioner's professional clinical judgment, more is required to treat the patient's acute pain
The prescriber must obtain a Board waiver before exceeding a limit
Only a second practitioner's written approval allows exceeding a limit

questions.explanation: A practitioner may exceed an acute-pain limit when professional clinical judgment finds more is required to treat the patient's acute pain. Absolute limits, a Board waiver, and a second-approval requirement all add machinery the override does not contain.

questions.question: An out-of-state pharmacy licensed to dispense into Minnesota asks what toll-free telephone service it must provide. What is required?

answers.text: A toll-free telephone service on weekdays only, for at least 20 hours per week
A toll-free telephone service 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
A toll-free telephone service at least 6 days per week and at least 40 hours per week, with pharmacist access to records
An email contact service instead of a telephone service

questions.explanation: A nonresident pharmacy must provide a toll-free telephone service at least 6 days per week and at least 40 hours per week with pharmacist access to records. Weekday-only service at half the hours understates the duty, round-the-clock service overstates it, and email is not the telephone service the statute describes.

questions.question: A licensing-board staff member reviewing PMP data spots a prescriber the staff member suspects of misconduct. What use limit applies?

answers.text: Licensing-board personnel may not use PMP access to initiate a disciplinary action
Board personnel may open a disciplinary case directly from any data they view
Board personnel must initiate discipline whenever data looks unusual
Board personnel may share the data publicly to prompt a complaint

questions.explanation: Licensing-board personnel may not use their PMP access to initiate a disciplinary action. Opening a case directly from viewed data and treating unusual data as a mandatory case both contradict that limit, and public sharing is not a permitted use.

questions.question: For which vaccine-and-age combination is the pre-administration registry assessment NOT required?

answers.text: All vaccines for individuals age nine and older
Influenza vaccines for individuals age nine and older
Influenza vaccines for individuals under age nine
COVID-19 vaccines for individuals age nine and older

questions.explanation: The assessment exception covers influenza vaccines for individuals age nine and older. Extending it to all vaccines widens it beyond its terms, applying it to younger children inverts it, and the exception names influenza rather than COVID-19 vaccines.

questions.question: An application was received by the Board twenty months ago and was never completed. What is its status under the Board's rule?

answers.text: The application remains valid until the applicant withdraws it
The application is invalid only after 3 years
The application is invalid, because an application becomes invalid 18 months after the Board receives it
The application remains valid because examination fees were paid

questions.explanation: An application becomes invalid eighteen months after the Board receives it, so a twenty-month-old incomplete application is invalid. Validity until withdrawal and a three-year life both extend the stated period, and paid fees do not keep an application alive past it.

questions.question: Following a documented spillage, a pharmacist is deciding what happens to the destroyed controlled-substance stock. What is the correct disposition?

answers.text: The recovered tablets may be swept up and returned to the stock bottle
The damaged tablets may be dispensed at a discount with a warning to the patient
The destroyed stock is disposed of through the registrant disposal process
The destroyed stock may be set aside indefinitely with no further handling

questions.explanation: Stock destroyed by breakage or spillage is disposed of through the registrant disposal process, after the event is documented in the pharmacy's records. Contaminated tablets from a spill must never return to a stock bottle or be dispensed to a patient, discounted or otherwise. Setting the destroyed stock aside indefinitely is not a disposition and leaves the disposal step unfinished.

questions.question: A pharmacist is temporarily suspended without a prior hearing under the pharmacy discipline statute's own temporary-suspension provision. How long does that suspension last?

answers.text: For a fixed period of 60 days, after which it expires on its own
Until the Board issues its final order after a hearing
Until the pharmacist files an appeal, at which point it lifts automatically
For one year, renewable by the Board without a hearing

questions.explanation: A temporary suspension under the pharmacy discipline statute lasts until the Board's final order after hearing. It is not a fixed-day suspension, and filing an appeal does not lift it.

questions.question: The PMP system is unavailable when a prescriber attempts a required check, and the prescriber asks how the failure fits the mandate. What applies?

answers.text: A technological failure reported to the Board is one of the stated exceptions
Any system slowdown automatically excuses the check with no report
A technological failure is never an exception
The prescriber must wait until the system returns, however long that takes

questions.explanation: A technological failure reported to the Board is a stated exception to the query mandate. An unreported slowdown does not carry the reporting element the exception includes, the exception does exist, and an indefinite wait is not the mechanism the exception describes.

questions.question: Pharmacist Marta Kowalski is counseling a patient on the last fill of a maintenance prescription that has no refills remaining. Which refill counseling should the patient receive?

answers.text: No refill discussion is needed, because the prescription has been filled before
The patient should be told the pharmacy will automatically continue the drug when it runs out
The patient should be told no refills remain and to contact the prescriber before running out, so a new authorization can be obtained in time
The patient should be told to borrow the same drug from a family member if it runs out

questions.explanation: Refill information is a counseling point, and when no refills remain the patient needs to know to contact the prescriber before the supply runs out so therapy is not interrupted. Prior fills do not remove the need for that discussion, the pharmacy cannot continue the drug without authorization, and sharing another person's medication is unsafe and impermissible.

questions.question: A pharmacist asks whether a delegate may access prescription monitoring program data on the pharmacist's behalf for a current patient. What is correct?

answers.text: Delegates may never access program data under any circumstances
A delegate may access program data for any person, whether or not a current patient
Dispensers and their delegates are permissible users for a current patient, for dispensing or considering dispensing
A delegate may access program data only for research purposes

questions.explanation: Dispensers and their delegates may access program data for a current patient, for the purpose of dispensing or considering dispensing. A total bar on delegates contradicts their place on the list, access for non-patients exceeds the current-patient limit, and research is not the dispensing purpose the statute names.

questions.question: A prescription arrives marked by the prescriber to be dispensed as written, with substitution prohibited. At pickup, the patient asks pharmacist Frank Delgado to switch to the cheaper AB-rated generic instead and says cost matters more than the notation. What must Frank do?

answers.text: Dispense the brand as directed, because a prescriber's dispense-as-written direction bars substitution even when the patient requests it
Substitute the generic, because the patient's preference overrides the prescriber's notation
Substitute the generic after documenting the patient's request in the profile
Substitute the generic for this fill only and restore the brand on refills

questions.explanation: When the prescriber directs that a prescription be dispensed as written, the pharmacist may not substitute, and the patient's cost preference or a documented request does not override that direction. A one-fill exception would still be a substitution the prescriber prohibited.

questions.question: Pharmacist Sofia Marino dispenses a product that is required to be accompanied by a patient package insert, although the product carries no Medication Guide requirement. A technician sets the insert aside, saying only Medication Guides are legally required paperwork. What must Sofia do?

answers.text: Ensure the patient package insert accompanies the dispensing, because a required insert must be provided to the patient when the product is dispensed
Discard the insert, because technician judgment determines which paperwork is required
Provide the insert only if the patient asks for written information
Substitute a Medication Guide for a different drug, since any FDA paperwork satisfies the requirement

questions.explanation: Patient package inserts are required for certain products and must reach the patient when the product is dispensed; the absence of a Medication Guide requirement for the same product does not make its required insert optional. Waiting for a patient request withholds required information, paperwork for a different drug does not substitute for this product's insert, and a technician's view does not override the dispensing requirement.

questions.question: A mail-service pharmacy ships a filled vial in a box that carries the pharmacy's return address on the outer shipping label, but the vial inside identifies only the drug and the patient. A reviewer flags the vial itself. What is missing from the dispensed container?

answers.text: The pharmacy's name and address on the container label itself
The wholesaler's name and address that supplied the stock bottle
The prescriber's office address on the container label
The carrier's tracking address printed on the vial

questions.explanation: The label on the container dispensed to the patient must itself show the dispensing pharmacy's name and address, and an address on the outer shipping carton does not satisfy that container-label requirement. The wholesaler, the prescriber's office, and the carrier are not the dispensing pharmacy whose identification belongs on the vial.

questions.question: A traveler shows pharmacist Erin Walsh a sealed bottle of an unapproved foreign version of a drug, saying she brought back a six-month supply for herself and asking the pharmacy to keep it behind the counter and dispense it to her monthly. What is the correct response?

answers.text: Accept the bottle, because any amount a traveler brings in is automatically permitted
Decline; importing unapproved drugs is generally prohibited, the personal-use enforcement discretion typically reaches only up to a 90-day supply, and it is not a channel for pharmacy dispensing
Accept the bottle if the patient signs a waiver accepting the risk
Buy part of the supply from the patient so other patients can benefit from it

questions.explanation: Importing unapproved drugs is generally prohibited. The FDA's enforcement discretion for personal use typically covers up to a 90-day supply under conditions and does not make the product a pharmacy-dispensable item — a six-month supply held and dispensed by the pharmacy falls outside it. A patient waiver does not change the product's status, and purchasing the supply for resale would turn personal importation into an unlawful resale channel.

questions.question: A patient whose prescriber is unreachable asks pharmacist James Carter for an emergency supply of a Schedule IV anxiety medication, citing the emergency-refill rule he used last month for a blood pressure drug. How does the rule apply here?

answers.text: The same 72-hour emergency supply is available for any maintenance drug
A 72-hour supply is allowed if the patient pays cash
A seven-day supply is allowed for Schedule IV drugs specifically
Emergency refills do not extend to controlled substances outside the specific federal emergency Schedule II oral-order rule

questions.explanation: The prevailing emergency-refill principle never extends to controlled substances beyond the specific federal emergency Schedule II oral-order rule, so it cannot supply a Schedule IV drug here. Cash payment and the schedule of the drug do not create an exception, and no seven-day emergency supply exists for this situation.

questions.question: Pharmacist-in-charge Greg Halvorsen took his pharmacy's last biennial controlled-substance inventory in May two years ago. Facing a busy spring, he proposes postponing the next inventory to 25 months after the last one. A staff pharmacist proposes taking it a few weeks before the two-year mark instead. Which plan complies?

answers.text: Postponing to 25 months, because the biennial inventory is approximate
Either plan, because only the initial inventory date is regulated
Taking it a few weeks early, because a biennial inventory may be taken on any date within two years of the previous one
Skipping this cycle, because a recent state inspection reviewed the records

questions.explanation: A biennial controlled-substance inventory may be taken on any date within two years of the previous inventory, so taking it a few weeks early complies while waiting 25 months exceeds the window. The schedule is a firm two-year limit, not an approximation, and it applies to every biennial cycle, not just the initial inventory. A state inspection does not substitute for the pharmacy's own required inventory.

questions.question: A prescriber telephones Greenleaf Compounding, a traditional compounding pharmacy, asking it to prepare a batch of a customized cream this week for patients the clinic expects to see next month, with individual names to be supplied later. How must the pharmacy respond under its compounding category?

answers.text: It may prepare the batch now and match names to units when patients arrive
It may prepare the batch if the prescriber promises names within thirty days
It may compound only pursuant to a prescription for an individual, identified patient
It may prepare the batch if each container is labeled with the clinic's name

questions.explanation: A traditional compounding pharmacy compounds pursuant to patient-specific prescriptions for identified patients, so it cannot build a batch for unnamed future patients even if names are promised later. Labeling containers for the clinic does not cure the absence of individual prescriptions, and supplying stock for general office use belongs to a different, federally registered type of facility.

questions.question: Pharmacist Paul Nguyen is setting up a compounding corner where staff will regularly handle a corrosive cleaning agent and a corrosive drug ingredient. A coworker says the sink in the break room two doors away is good enough if anyone splashes something in an eye. What safety equipment must be available where the corrosive materials are handled?

answers.text: A first-aid kit containing eye drops, kept in the manager's office
A bottle of sterile water that staff may carry to the break room
An eyewash station available where the corrosive materials are handled
No equipment, because corrosive materials in a pharmacy are too dilute to matter

questions.explanation: Where corrosive materials are handled, an eyewash station must be available at that work area so an exposed eye can be flushed immediately. Eye drops in an office kit are not an eyewash station, a carried bottle does not provide the needed flushing capability at the point of exposure, and the corrosive nature of the materials is exactly what triggers the requirement rather than excusing it.

fnp.quiz_title: FNP Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A 58-year-old woman with no urinary symptoms has a urine dipstick showing 2+ blood at a wellness visit. She is not menstruating and has not exercised vigorously in the past 2 days. Which assessment step best confirms microscopic hematuria?

answers.text: Accepting the single dipstick result alone as confirmation of microscopic hematuria
Treating for a urinary tract infection and not repeating the urine testing
Confirming at least 3 red blood cells per high-power field on microscopy of a properly collected specimen
Reassuring her that blood in the urine without pain never requires microscopic confirmation, risk assessment, or any follow-up

questions.explanation: C is correct: microscopic hematuria is a microscopic diagnosis, confirmed by finding at least 3 red blood cells per high-power field in a properly collected specimen; the dipstick detects heme pigment and can be positive from hemoglobin, myoglobin, or contamination. A is wrong because a dipstick alone cannot confirm true hematuria. B is wrong because she has no infection symptoms and empiric treatment without confirmation abandons the hematuria evaluation. D is wrong because painless hematuria can signal serious urinary tract disease and always warrants confirmation and risk-based follow-up.

questions.question: After several episodes in which distressed patients and visitors have threatened staff, a clinic serving many middle-aged adults decides to strengthen safety. Which approach reflects an effective workplace violence prevention program?

answers.text: Rely on individual staff members to judge which threats are serious and handle them on their own

Build a program that combines hazard and environmental assessment, a clear non-retaliatory way to report threats and incidents, staff training in recognition and de-escalation, and a planned response with support after any incident
Post a notice that aggressive behavior will not be tolerated and consider the program complete
Restrict the program to employed security staff, since violence prevention is not a clinical or leadership responsibility

questions.explanation: The key is B: effective healthcare workplace violence prevention is a system — leadership commitment, hazard assessment, environmental and administrative controls, accessible reporting without retaliation, training in recognition and de-escalation, and post-incident response and support. A is wrong because leaving threat assessment to isolated individuals is exactly the gap such programs close. C is wrong because a posted notice alone changes neither reporting, training, nor response. D is wrong because prevention requires interdisciplinary and leadership ownership, not security staff alone.

questions.question: A 55-year-old with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and no diabetes is starting dapagliflozin 10 mg daily. Which counseling point should the nurse practitioner implement at initiation?

answers.text: Stop the medication permanently if blood glucose readings are in the normal range
Take an extra dose on days when ankle swelling is worse than usual

Take it once daily for heart failure even though blood glucose may be normal, keep up genital hygiene and hydration, and hold it and contact the clinic during an acute illness with vomiting or poor fluid intake
Expect it to replace the daily loop diuretic, which should be stopped today

questions.explanation: Key C is correct: dapagliflozin benefits heart failure independent of diabetes, so normal glucose is expected and is not a reason to stop; counseling covers perineal hygiene against mycotic infection, adequate hydration, and temporarily holding the drug during dehydrating acute illness to reduce kidney and ketoacidosis risk. A is wrong because glycemic effect is not the treatment goal here. B is wrong because it is a fixed once-daily dose, not a symptom-titrated diuretic. D is wrong because it does not replace loop diuretics for congestion.

questions.question: A 48-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation has a 20-minute episode of right arm weakness and inability to find words, which resolves completely. She has no headache, jerking movements, or confusion afterward, and her glucose during the episode was 118 mg/dL. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Transient ischemic attack
Migraine aura without headache
Hypoglycemia
Focal seizure with postictal weakness

questions.explanation: A is correct: a brief, focal neurologic deficit in a vascular distribution that resolves within 24 hours in a patient with atrial fibrillation is a transient ischemic attack. B is wrong because migraine aura typically produces gradually marching positive symptoms (such as flashing lights or tingling), often with headache, rather than abrupt loss of speech and strength. C is wrong because the glucose was normal and hypoglycemia tends to cause global rather than focal findings. D is wrong because there were no rhythmic jerking movements and no postictal confusion.

questions.question: A 28-year-old man is evaluated after fainting during sleep while febrile with influenza. His brother died suddenly at age 32. Electrolytes and echocardiogram are normal. The ECG shows a downsloping, coved ST-segment elevation in leads V1 through V3 followed by an inverted T wave. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Long QT syndrome
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Brugada syndrome
Benign early repolarization

questions.explanation: Brugada syndrome is correct: syncope at rest or during fever, a family history of early sudden death, and the coved type 1 ST elevation in V1-V3 with inverted T wave and a structurally normal heart are diagnostic features. Long QT syndrome shows a prolonged QT interval and torsades-type syncope usually triggered by exertion, startle, or drugs. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy produces left ventricular hypertrophy on imaging and usually exertional symptoms. Benign early repolarization shows concave ST elevation without syncope, family sudden death, or the coved right-precordial pattern.

questions.question: A 27-year-old woman presents with 7 weeks of amenorrhea, unilateral pelvic pain, and light vaginal spotting. She is hemodynamically stable. Serum human chorionic gonadotropin is 2,800 mIU/mL, and transvaginal ultrasound shows no intrauterine gestational sac and a small amount of free fluid in the pelvis. Which diagnosis must be prioritized until proven otherwise?

answers.text: Ectopic pregnancy
Threatened abortion of an intrauterine pregnancy
Ovarian torsion
Pelvic inflammatory disease

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: a positive pregnancy test with pain, spotting, no intrauterine pregnancy on transvaginal ultrasound at a hormone level where an intrauterine sac should usually be seen, plus free pelvic fluid, makes ectopic pregnancy the priority diagnosis because of rupture risk. B is wrong: threatened abortion presumes a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy, which ultrasound has not shown. C is wrong: torsion causes acute severe pain often with nausea and an adnexal mass, but does not explain a positive pregnancy test with no intrauterine sac. D is wrong: pelvic inflammatory disease does not explain amenorrhea with this hormone level and ultrasound pattern.

questions.question: A 31-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis has taken a platform injectable disease-modifying therapy for 18 months with good adherence. In that period she has had two clinical relapses, and surveillance MRI shows three new T2 lesions and one gadolinium-enhancing lesion compared with last year. What is the correct evaluation of her treatment response?

answers.text: The therapy is working adequately, because relapses that occur on treatment are always milder than the relapses she would have had without it

She has breakthrough disease activity — clinical relapses plus new and enhancing MRI lesions — indicating inadequate response, so refer promptly to neurology to escalate to a higher-efficacy disease-modifying therapy
Wait for at least two more clinical relapses before judging her response, because new MRI lesions by themselves do not count as disease activity
Stop all disease-modifying therapy, because continued relapses and MRI lesions prove that this class of medication does not work for her disease

questions.explanation: Continued clinical relapses accompanied by new T2 and gadolinium-enhancing lesions on a faithfully taken therapy define breakthrough disease and inadequate treatment response in relapsing multiple sclerosis; contemporary practice escalates to higher-efficacy therapy rather than accumulating disability (B). Relapse occurrence on therapy is not itself evidence of benefit (A). MRI activity is a core component of response assessment, so waiting for more relapses (C) forfeits the window to prevent injury. Abandoning disease-modifying therapy entirely (D) leaves inflammatory activity untreated.

questions.question: A 26-year-old woman reports menses every 40 to 60 days, worsening acne, and coarse hair growth on her chin requiring frequent removal. Body mass index is 31 kg/m2. TSH and prolactin are normal, pregnancy test is negative, and pelvic ultrasound shows increased ovarian volume with numerous small peripheral follicles. Which diagnosis best fits this presentation?

answers.text: Hypothyroidism
Hyperprolactinemia
Polycystic ovary syndrome
Cushing syndrome
