questions.explanation: Key C is correct: she meets diagnostic criteria for polycystic ovary syndrome with ovulatory dysfunction (infrequent menses), clinical hyperandrogenism (hirsutism and acne), and polycystic ovarian morphology, after exclusion of thyroid disease and hyperprolactinemia. A is wrong because her TSH is normal, excluding hypothyroidism as the cause of the cycle irregularity. B is wrong because her prolactin is normal and she has no galactorrhea. D is wrong because she lacks the proximal weakness, wide violaceous striae, and other systemic features of cortisol excess.

questions.question: An infant receives the wrong vaccine product during a busy immunization session, and review shows several similar near misses in the clinic. The family nurse practitioner leads the system redesign. Which change most directly prevents this class of error?

answers.text: Separate look-alike products in labeled storage, and check a single prepared dose against the order and the record before administration
Ask staff to simply be more careful during busy sessions, supported by a reminder sign posted in the medication room and a mention at the next staff meeting
Have one staff member prepare and administer all vaccines entirely alone, deliberately removing second checks so that no one else's handling can introduce confusion into the process
Store all infant vaccine products together in a single shared bin so that staff can find whichever product they need faster during a busy session

questions.explanation: A is correct because vaccine errors are usually system failures: look-alike products stored together and rushed preparation invite mix-ups, and standardizing separation, labeling, and a pre-administration check against the order removes the opportunity for error. B is wrong because exhortations to be careful do not change the conditions that produced the error. C is wrong because removing independent checks increases, rather than decreases, risk. D is wrong because co-storing look-alike products is the hazard itself, not a remedy.

questions.question: A 29-year-old woman reports that since a physical assault 3 months ago she has had recurrent nightmares about the event, avoids the neighborhood where it occurred, startles easily, and feels constantly on guard. Which specialized assessment is most appropriate?

answers.text: A validated trauma symptom screen such as the Primary Care PTSD Screen, with a trauma-informed history
Reassurance that these symptoms always resolve, with no screening
A urine drug screen as the sole assessment
A depression questionnaire only, ending the assessment if it is negative

questions.explanation: A is correct: intrusive nightmares, avoidance, and hypervigilance persisting months after a traumatic event call for a validated post-traumatic stress screening instrument and a trauma-informed history covering symptom duration, function, safety, and supports. B is wrong because persistent, functionally impairing symptoms 3 months after trauma require assessment, not dismissal. C is wrong because a drug screen does not evaluate trauma symptoms and cannot substitute for a symptom history. D is wrong because depression screening alone misses the trauma-specific symptom clusters that define this presentation.

questions.question: A 14-year-old boy's height has crossed downward across two percentile lines in 2 years. He has no pubic hair development and his testes are prepubertal in volume, while most classmates have entered puberty. Which assessment is most appropriate to evaluate his pubertal status?

answers.text: Reassurance without any growth or pubertal documentation
A single random testosterone level as the sole defining assessment
Brain magnetic resonance imaging as the first assessment step
Tanner staging including testicular volume, with plotting of growth velocity on a growth chart

questions.explanation: D is correct: absent pubertal development by age 14 years in a boy with slowing growth is evaluated first by formal Tanner staging, testicular volume measurement (the earliest sign of central puberty), and growth-velocity plotting, which together distinguish delayed puberty patterns and direct any laboratory workup. A is wrong because downward percentile crossing plus absent puberty at 14 is not a pattern to dismiss undocumented. B is wrong because a single random testosterone is often low and pulsatile in early puberty and cannot by itself stage or define pubertal status. C is wrong because neuroimaging is reserved for specific indications after clinical and biochemical assessment, not a first step.

questions.question: A 39-year-old woman who smokes about 15 cigarettes daily asks to start 'the pill' for contraception. Her blood pressure is 128/78 mm Hg, she has no history of thrombosis or migraine, and her pregnancy test is negative. Which contraceptive prescription is appropriate?

answers.text: A combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive, because her blood pressure is normal
A combined oral contraceptive at the lowest estrogen dose, with a plan to reassess in a year
A progestin-only oral contraceptive, because estrogen-containing contraception is unacceptable at her age combined with her smoking intensity
No prescription method, because all hormonal contraception is contraindicated for smokers

questions.explanation: C is correct: smoking 15 or more cigarettes daily at age 35 or older makes estrogen-containing contraception an unacceptable health risk because of myocardial infarction and stroke, so a progestin-only pill provides hormonal contraception without estrogen. A and B are wrong because normal blood pressure and lower estrogen dose do not remove the age-plus-smoking contraindication. D is wrong because progestin-only and long-acting methods remain safe options; only the estrogen component is the problem.

questions.question: On day 3 of life, a well, afebrile newborn who is feeding normally develops blotchy red patches over the trunk and face with small white-yellow papules and pustules in the centers. The palms and soles are spared, and there are no vesicles. Which plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Start intravenous acyclovir and perform a full sepsis evaluation
Reassure the parents that this is erythema toxicum neonatorum, a benign eruption that resolves on its own without treatment, with routine newborn follow-up
Start oral cephalexin for bacterial pustulosis
Apply a potent topical corticosteroid to all affected areas

questions.explanation: B is correct: erythema toxicum neonatorum is a common benign newborn eruption appearing in the first days of life in a well infant, sparing palms and soles, and it resolves spontaneously without therapy. A is wrong because herpes simplex would show grouped vesicles, often in an ill or at-risk infant; empiric acyclovir and sepsis workup are not warranted for this classic benign picture in a well newborn. C is wrong because there are no signs of bacterial infection — the baby is afebrile and feeding well — and antibiotics are not indicated. D is wrong because potent topical steroids are unnecessary for a self-limited eruption and are inappropriate on newborn skin.

questions.question: A 49-year-old woman reports 4 months of frequent large-volume watery stools. The diarrhea wakes her from sleep and continues unchanged during a 48-hour period when she ate nothing during a hospital observation. She has no blood in the stool and only mild cramping. Which history feature most supports a secretory diarrhea?

answers.text: Diarrhea that persists during fasting and occurs at night
Diarrhea that stops completely when she fasts
Bloating and diarrhea that follow only large loads of fruit juice and sugar-free gum
Bulky, greasy stools that are hard to flush and float

questions.explanation: A is correct: secretory diarrhea is driven by intestinal secretion, so it persists despite fasting and typically continues at night, often with large stool volumes. B is wrong because diarrhea that resolves with fasting characterizes an osmotic diarrhea, the opposite pattern. C is wrong because symptoms tied only to poorly absorbed sugars or sugar alcohols also indicate an osmotic mechanism. D is wrong because bulky, greasy, floating stools indicate fat malabsorption rather than a secretory process.

questions.question: A 76-year-old man with Parkinson disease takes carbidopa-levodopa three times daily. Over 4 months he reports that each dose now 'wears off' after about 3 hours: tremor and stiffness return, and he freezes when walking just before the next dose. He has no hallucinations, confusion, or troublesome dyskinesia. What is the best evaluation and next step?

answers.text: Conclude levodopa has stopped working entirely and discontinue it
Advise him to double each dose on his own when symptoms return
Recognize motor fluctuations (wearing-off); adjust the levodopa schedule (e.g., more frequent dosing) and coordinate with neurology about adjunctive options
Add a dopamine-blocking antiemetic for the freezing episodes

questions.explanation: The key is correct: predictable return of parkinsonian features before the next dose is the wearing-off phenomenon of advancing disease and shorter levodopa duration; shortening the dosing interval and involving neurology about adjuncts (e.g., COMT or MAO-B inhibitors) is standard management. A is wrong because each dose still works for about 3 hours, so the drug has not failed; stopping it would cause severe immobility. B is unsafe self-titration that increases dyskinesia and confusion risk. D is wrong because dopamine blockers worsen parkinsonism and freezing is not nausea.

questions.question: A 15-year-old boy is found on imaging done for abdominal pain to have a congenital solitary left kidney. He is healthy, blood pressure and urinalysis are normal, and he wants to keep playing school sports, including soccer and weight training. Which plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Prohibit all organized sports permanently because he has one kidney
Clear him for sports only after a kidney biopsy confirms normal tissue
Restrict him to swimming, the only sport considered safe with a solitary kidney
Use shared decision-making to permit most sports with counseling on protective gear and hydration, and monitor blood pressure and urinalysis at least annually

questions.explanation: A healthy adolescent with a solitary kidney and normal blood pressure and urinalysis can participate in most sports after individualized shared decision-making, with attention to protective padding for contact sports and hydration; periodic blood pressure and urine monitoring is part of the plan. A blanket permanent ban on sports is unnecessarily restrictive and harmful to health and quality of life. Kidney biopsy is invasive and not a prerequisite for sports clearance in a healthy teen with normal findings. Limiting him to swimming alone is not evidence-based.

questions.question: A 63-year-old woman has symptomatic knee osteoarthritis. She also has stage 3 chronic kidney disease, hypertension, and a history of peptic ulcer disease. She wants medication for knee pain in addition to exercise therapy. Which analgesic strategy is safest and most appropriate to start?

answers.text: Scheduled oral ibuprofen taken daily on a long-term basis
Tramadol as the first-line long-term analgesic
Topical diclofenac gel applied to the knee, combined with quadriceps-strengthening physical therapy, weight management, and activity modification
Intra-articular corticosteroid injections repeated every week indefinitely

questions.explanation: C is correct: topical diclofenac delivers effective knee osteoarthritis analgesia with far lower systemic exposure than oral nonsteroidal drugs, making it preferred when chronic kidney disease, hypertension, and ulcer history raise oral NSAID risk, and exercise and weight measures are core therapy. A is wrong because chronic oral ibuprofen risks kidney decline, blood pressure elevation, and ulcer bleeding in this patient. B is wrong because tramadol is not first-line for osteoarthritis and carries dependence, fall, and other risks. D is wrong because intra-articular steroids are intermittent adjuncts for flares, not weekly indefinite therapy, which can harm cartilage and soft tissue.

questions.question: A 36-year-old woman is admitted at 35 weeks and 3 days of gestation with regular contractions, cervical dilation of 3 cm with 80% effacement, and intact membranes. She has received no antenatal corticosteroids in this pregnancy. She has no diabetes, no signs of infection, and delivery is anticipated within the next several days. Working with the obstetric team, which medication plan should the FNP help implement?

answers.text: No corticosteroids, because antenatal steroids have no role after 34 weeks of gestation under any circumstances, including imminent late preterm delivery
Weekly repeated corticosteroid courses continued until she reaches 37 weeks, since more courses provide more fetal lung benefit
A single course of betamethasone now, with notification to the neonatal team that the newborn will need glucose monitoring
Magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection as the priority medication at 35 weeks, given for 24 hours before the anticipated delivery

questions.explanation: C is correct: a single course of betamethasone is recommended in the late preterm period (34 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks) for patients at risk of preterm delivery within 7 days who have not previously received corticosteroids; it reduces neonatal respiratory complications, and transient neonatal hypoglycemia is the main effect to monitor. A is wrong because the late-preterm course is an established exception to the usual under-34-weeks window when delivery is anticipated. B is wrong because rescue or repeated weekly courses are not the plan here; a single late-preterm course is what the evidence supports. D is wrong because magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection is used at earlier gestations (before about 32 weeks), not at 35 weeks.

questions.question: A 74-year-old woman is found to have primary hyperparathyroidism: serum calcium 11.4 mg/dL on repeat testing, elevated parathyroid hormone, replete vitamin D, and eGFR 58 mL/min/1.73 m2. She feels well, has never had a kidney stone, and her dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scan shows a femoral neck T-score of -2.6. Which plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Start cinacalcet to lower the calcium and avoid any referral
Refer for parathyroid surgery evaluation because her bone density meets a surgical criterion even without symptoms
Start an oral bisphosphonate alone, which corrects the underlying parathyroid disease
Repeat calcium in 1 year with no referral, because surgery is considered only for symptomatic disease

questions.explanation: Parathyroidectomy is indicated in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism when any surgical criterion is present, including a T-score of -2.5 or lower at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, total hip, or distal radius, so referral (B) is correct. Cinacalcet (A) lowers calcium but does not improve bone density and is reserved for patients who cannot have surgery. A bisphosphonate (C) may raise bone density but does not cure the parathyroid disease or address hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria. Annual monitoring alone (D) ignores a met surgical criterion; asymptomatic disease with such a criterion is an indication for surgery, not observation.

questions.question: A 74-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents to clinic with 2 days of markedly increased dyspnea, increased sputum volume, and sputum that has changed from white to green. He is afebrile, alert, speaks in full sentences, and his oxygen saturation is 91% on room air, near his baseline. He uses a long-acting bronchodilator daily. Which treatment is most appropriate now?

answers.text: Increase the frequency of his maintenance long-acting bronchodilator for 1 week and reassess
Start a 5-day course of oral prednisone together with an oral antibiotic active against typical exacerbation pathogens
Start oral prednisone alone, reserving antibiotics unless fever develops
Arrange same-day chest computed tomography before starting any therapy

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: he has all three cardinal exacerbation features—increased dyspnea, increased sputum volume, and increased sputum purulence—which is the presentation in which adding an antibiotic to a short systemic corticosteroid course improves outcomes; a 5-day prednisone course is standard for an outpatient exacerbation of this severity. A is wrong because simply intensifying maintenance bronchodilation does not treat the acute inflammatory and bacterial components. C is wrong because with all three cardinal symptoms present, withholding antibiotics until fever appears undertreats the exacerbation; fever is not required. D is wrong because uncomplicated exacerbations are treated clinically; imaging is reserved for suspected pneumonia or another diagnosis and should not delay therapy.

ccrn.quiz_title: CCRN Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: On an Impella device, purge pressure has risen steadily, purge flow has fallen, and a low-purge-flow alarm sounds. The catheter position is confirmed correct. What is the appropriate response?

answers.text: Address the purge system promptly — inspect for kinks and change the purge cassette/fluid as directed — because purge failure risks motor thrombosis and device stoppage
Turn the purge system off for several hours to let the pressure normalize on its own, and maintained even if repeat imaging shows progression of the underlying problem in the meantime
Increase the performance level to maximum to force purge fluid through the motor, combined only with reassurance to the patient that the finding is expected and self-limited
Remove the device immediately without attempting any purge-system correction, with the abnormal finding attributed to monitor artifact until the next routine device interrogation

questions.explanation: The purge fluid (dextrose-based, with heparin per protocol) keeps blood out of the motor; rising purge pressure with falling flow signals obstruction or cassette/fluid problems that must be corrected promptly or the motor can thrombose and stop. Turning purge off (B) accelerates exactly that failure. Raising performance level (C) does not clear a purge obstruction and raises other risks. Immediate removal (D) skips simple corrective steps in a patient who still needs support.

questions.question: A 60-year-old man with diabetic ketoacidosis that has now resolved (anion gap closed, pH normal) is eating meals. His insulin infusion has been steady at 1.8 units/hr over the past 6 hours with glucose values of 148 to 172 mg/dL. Which transition plan is best?

answers.text: Stop the infusion and rely on correction-scale insulin alone for the next 24 hours, adding scheduled insulin only if glucose exceeds 300 mg/dL on two consecutive checks
Continue the infusion indefinitely until discharge, because subcutaneous insulin cannot maintain control after ketoacidosis
Give his first subcutaneous basal dose at the exact moment the infusion is stopped, because any overlap would cause dangerous insulin stacking in a patient just recovering from ketoacidosis
Convert using about 80% of his stable 24-hour infusion requirement (about 35 units daily) split between basal and mealtime insulin, giving basal 1 to 2 hours before stopping the infusion

questions.explanation: Key D is correct: a stable rate of 1.8 units/hr projects to about 43 units over 24 hours; standard transition practice gives roughly 80% of that projected total (about 35 units) as scheduled subcutaneous insulin split between basal and mealtime doses, with the basal dose given 1 to 2 hours before the infusion stops so there is no gap in coverage once the gap has closed and the patient is eating. A is wrong because correction-only therapy after ketoacidosis leaves him without basal coverage and invites rebound hyperglycemia and recurrent ketosis. C is wrong because intravenous insulin clears within minutes; without an overlap, subcutaneous insulin has not yet taken effect and coverage lapses. D is wrong because a resolved, eating patient is exactly the candidate for transition, and indefinite infusion needlessly prolongs intensive monitoring and immobility.

questions.question: A 44-year-old man arrives after a traumatic below-knee amputation from industrial machinery. Direct pressure has not controlled brisk arterial bleeding from the stump and BP is 84/50 mmHg. What should the nurse do first?

answers.text: Pack the stump loosely and reassess the bleeding in 15 minutes after fluids
Apply a proximal tourniquet until bleeding stops
Elevate the stump and wait for the surgical team before intervening
Apply a loose dressing and give analgesia before addressing bleeding

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: life-threatening extremity hemorrhage uncontrolled by direct pressure requires an immediate proximal tourniquet tightened until bleeding stops, with the time documented. A is wrong because loose packing and delayed reassessment allow continued exsanguination. C is wrong because elevation alone and waiting do not control arterial bleeding. D is wrong because analgesia and a loose dressing must not precede hemorrhage control in a hypotensive patient.

questions.question: A patient taking a daily SSRI plus linezolid develops symptomatic methemoglobinemia. Before methylene blue is given, the team pauses to consider a drug-interaction caution. What is it?

answers.text: Methylene blue has no known interactions with serotonergic drugs at any therapeutic dose used
The only concern is that methylene blue turns the urine and stool blue-green for a day or two, which can alarm the patient and family
Methylene blue inhibits MAO-A and can precipitate serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs; weigh risks and alternatives
SSRIs must be continued at double the usual dose to offset any effect of the antidote on mood

questions.explanation: Methylene blue is a potent reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase A; combined with serotonergic agents (SSRIs, linezolid) it can precipitate serotonin syndrome, a boxed-warning interaction. In symptomatic methemoglobinemia the team weighs this risk, considers alternatives, and monitors — the urine color change is trivial by comparison.

questions.question: A patient with a new colostomy has already learned to empty and change the pouch. At the discharge teaching session, the nurse focuses on the skin barrier. Which teaching point is most important for preventing the most common cause of pouch leakage?

answers.text: Change the pouch on a fixed schedule at the same time every morning, first thing after waking, whether or not it is leaking, so the routine becomes automatic for the patient at home.
Apply extra adhesive paste over the whole barrier whenever a small leak appears, to seal it.
Cut the barrier opening to fit the stoma, inspect the skin at each change, and treat a recurring leak as a sign the fit needs reassessment rather than just more adhesive.
Wear the pouch as long as possible between changes to reduce skin irritation from removal.

questions.explanation: Most leakage traces to barrier fit and peristomal skin condition, so discharge teaching should cover cutting the opening to fit the stoma (which changes size as swelling resolves), inspecting the skin at every change, and reading recurrent leakage as a fit problem needing reassessment. A rigid schedule ignores the barrier's actual condition, layering paste over a failing fit masks the cause, and stretching wear time invites leakage and skin breakdown under a saturated barrier.

questions.question: Minutes after receiving a cephalosporin infusion, a patient develops urticaria, wheezing, angioedema, hypotension, and ischemic chest pain with ST elevation. Which recognition and immediate priority pair is correct?

answers.text: This is simple contrast allergy; give an antihistamine alone and continue the antibiotic infusion slowly, with reassessment deferred until the next scheduled set of rounds and routine laboratory review

This is anaphylaxis only, so coronary ischemia should be ignored until allergy symptoms fully resolve, documented as the sole plan while the current vital-sign trend is simply observed without escalation

This is a primary plaque-rupture infarction, so the allergic signs should be treated as incidental, carried out as a complete standalone strategy with no additional imaging, consultation, or monitoring added
This is Kounis syndrome — allergic coronary spasm/ischemia — so treat anaphylaxis including epinephrine while simultaneously managing the acute coronary syndrome

questions.explanation: Kounis syndrome is acute coronary syndrome triggered by an allergic/anaphylactic reaction, via spasm, plaque disruption, or stent thrombosis. Anaphylaxis with hypotension still requires epinephrine — the coronary event does not remove that indication — alongside ACS care. Antihistamine alone while continuing the trigger (A) is dangerous. Ignoring ischemia (B) misses infarction in progress. Calling it incidental plaque rupture (C) misses the allergic driver and the need to stop the offending agent.

questions.question: A 68-year-old man is 1 day post right upper lobectomy. He is dyspneic with pink frothy sputum, crackles bilaterally, SpO2 87%, BP 168/94 mm Hg, and a new irregular rapid pulse at 132/min. Chest film shows diffuse pulmonary edema. In addition to oxygen and sitting him upright, what should the nurse anticipate?

answers.text: A fluid bolus for presumed postoperative hypovolemia losses
Immediate chest tube clamping to prevent further fluid shifts
Diuresis and afterload reduction for acute pulmonary edema
Bronchodilators alone as the sole treatment for the edema

questions.explanation: Key C is correct: hypertension, crackles, pink frothy sputum, and diffuse edema after thoracic surgery indicate acute (cardiogenic/fluid-overload) pulmonary edema with likely atrial fibrillation with rapid response; treatment centers on oxygen, upright positioning, diuresis, and vasodilation/afterload reduction plus rate evaluation. A is wrong because additional fluids worsen pulmonary edema in a hypertensive, overloaded patient. B is wrong because clamping a postoperative chest drain does not treat pulmonary edema and risks retained air/blood complications. D is wrong because bronchodilators do not remove pulmonary edema fluid or reduce afterload and are insufficient as sole therapy.

questions.question: Four days after abdominal surgery, a 66-year-old woman has massive painless colonic dilation with a cecal diameter of 11 cm. CT shows no mechanical obstruction and no perforation, and she takes opioids and an anticholinergic. Conservative measures for 24 hours have not helped. What is the next appropriate step?

answers.text: Give neostigmine with cardiac monitoring after excluding contraindications
Proceed directly to total colectomy as the first treatment for the dilation
Give an oral contrast challenge to push through the presumed blockage
Increase her opioid dose so she can rest while the colon decompresses

questions.explanation: Key A: Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome) without mechanical blockage that fails conservative care is treated with neostigmine under cardiac monitoring, alongside stopping opioids and anticholinergics and correcting electrolytes. B is wrong because surgery is reserved for perforation, ischemia, or failure of medical and endoscopic therapy. C is wrong because there is no mechanical obstruction to push through. D is wrong because opioids worsen colonic dysmotility.

questions.question: A 63-year-old woman is receiving an intravenous phenytoin load at 75 mg/min through a pump. Ten minutes in, her blood pressure falls from 138/80 to 92/56 mmHg and the monitor shows a slowed, widened rhythm. She has no rash and her airway is patent. What should the nurse do?

answers.text: Speed the infusion up so the load finishes before her pressure falls further and the drug can start working
Give an intravenous antihistamine first, because this pattern is an allergy that must be treated before touching the infusion
Stop or slow the infusion, monitor ECG and blood pressure, and notify the provider: phenytoin loads must not exceed 50 mg/min in adults
Switch the tubing to a faster-flowing vein and continue at the same rate, because the reaction depends only on vein size or on the patient's age

questions.explanation: C is correct: intravenous phenytoin is limited to no more than 50 mg/min in adults (slower in older or cardiac patients) because its propylene glycol diluent and the drug itself cause rate-related hypotension and cardiac conduction slowing, including bradycardia and widening; hypotension with rhythm change during a 75 mg/min infusion is that reaction, and the response is to stop or slow the infusion, monitor the ECG and pressure continuously, and notify the provider, with many teams preferring fosphenytoin for its better infusion tolerance. A is wrong: a faster rate delivers more diluent per minute and deepens the hypotension and conduction block. B is wrong: there are no allergic features, and delaying the rate correction to give an antihistamine leaves the cause running. D is wrong: the reaction is systemic and rate dependent; vein choice does not change the milligrams per minute reaching the heart.

questions.question: A 76-year-old man has had 2 days of fluctuating dizziness, double vision, slurred speech, and unsteadiness that repeatedly resolve and return. Today he is drowsy, his pupils are small, he cannot move his eyes vertically, and he has weakness on both sides. Which vascular territory best explains this evolving picture?

answers.text: The anterior cerebral artery, supplying the medial frontal lobe and the leg area of cortex
The middle cerebral artery, supplying the lateral frontal and temporal lobes and language cortex
The ophthalmic artery, supplying the retina and producing transient monocular visual loss
The basilar artery and posterior circulation, supplying the brainstem, cerebellum, and occipital lobes

questions.explanation: D is correct: fluctuating vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria, and ataxia that progress to drowsiness, small pupils, vertical gaze failure, and bilateral weakness localize to the brainstem — the basilar artery territory — because the posterior circulation supplies the brainstem, cerebellum, and occipital lobes, and crossed or bilateral signs with altered consciousness are its hallmark. A is wrong: anterior cerebral lesions cause leg-predominant weakness and abulia, not gaze palsies or bilateral brainstem signs. B is wrong: middle cerebral lesions cause unilateral face-and-arm deficits and aphasia, not fluctuating brainstem prodromes. C is wrong: ophthalmic ischemia causes monocular visual loss only, without dysarthria, ataxia, or depressed consciousness.

questions.question: A unit plots its monthly ventilator-associated event rate on a run chart for a quality project. For 14 months the points wander above and below the median with no pattern; in month 15 one point is the highest yet, though still within the range of earlier variation. A colleague wants to declare the prevention practice a failure. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: Treat the single high month as proof the practice has failed, discontinue it immediately, and begin searching for a replacement intervention before the next month's data are available to the project team or unit leadership for review.

Conclude the practice must actually be working better than ever, on the grounds that a month this extreme is usually followed by a better one, and report that expected improvement to leadership as an achieved result of the project.

Remove the high month from the chart as an outlier before presenting the data, since one unusual month unfairly distorts the picture of an otherwise stable process and could mislead the committee reviewing the project results this quarter.

Read it as common-cause variation unless run-chart rules are met - such as a sustained run on one side of the median or a clear trend - and keep collecting data while checking for any special cause in that month.

questions.explanation: Key (D): Run charts distinguish common-cause variation - the stable wandering seen for 14 months - from special-cause signals defined by rules such as shifts, trends, or astronomical points beyond the process's demonstrated range; one high point inside prior variation does not prove failure. A is wrong because reacting to noise discards a practice on a single unproven signal. B is wrong because predicting regression to the mean as an achieved improvement invents a result. C is wrong because deleting inconvenient points falsifies the very record the project depends on.

questions.question: A nurse reviews her unit's catheter-associated urinary tract infection data and notices her own patient has had an indwelling catheter for four days after surgery, with no documented ongoing indication and a nurse-driven removal protocol in place. What should she do?

answers.text: Leave the catheter in place until the provider's next routine round, since it was placed by the surgical team and removing another service's device without discussion is presumptuous
Assess the catheter against the removal protocol, remove it the same day if no indication is met, document the removal, and monitor for voiding — and raise the pattern at the unit huddle
Keep the catheter in place but obtain a urine culture today and repeat it every few days, so that any developing infection is detected and treated at the earliest possible stage
Clamp the catheter for lengthening intervals during the day to retrain the bladder while keeping it available, which simulates the benefits of removal without losing venous-like access

questions.explanation: B is correct: bundle ownership means the bedside nurse acts on the daily-necessity review the protocol authorizes — removing a catheter without indication is the single strongest CAUTI prevention step — and feeds the pattern back to the unit. A is wrong because deference to the placing team perpetuates the exact drift the protocol exists to interrupt. C is wrong because culturing a colonized catheter invites overtreatment and does not reduce device days. D is wrong because clamping retains the infection risk of an indwelling device while adding retention risk.

questions.question: A 78-year-old man with severe calcific aortic stenosis (valve area 0.7 cm2) is admitted for the third time in 4 months with melena. Endoscopy each time shows bleeding cecal angiodysplasia treated with cautery, yet the bleeding recurs, and testing shows loss of high-molecular-weight von Willebrand factor multimers. Which treatment most definitively addresses the cause of his recurrent bleeding?

answers.text: Lifelong iron infusions alone, with no change to his cardiac management plan at all
Repeated colonoscopic cautery every month on a fixed schedule regardless of bleeding
Aortic valve replacement to correct the shear stress destroying von Willebrand factor
High-dose desmopressin before every endoscopy as his permanent long-term strategy

questions.explanation: Option C is correct: in Heyde syndrome, the stenotic valve's shear stress cleaves high-molecular-weight von Willebrand factor multimers, producing an acquired bleeding defect that drives angiodysplasia bleeding; replacing the valve removes the shear and is the definitive treatment for recurrence. Option A is wrong because iron replaces losses without correcting the factor defect or the valve lesion causing them. Option B is wrong because cautery treats individual lesions that keep recurring while the hematologic defect persists, as his three admissions show. Option D is wrong because desmopressin gives only a transient rise in von Willebrand factor and is at best a short-term adjunct, not a durable strategy.

questions.question: A 49-year-old man with alcohol use disorder is admitted after a drinking binge followed by 2 days of vomiting and almost no food intake. Glucose is 138 mg/dL, pH 7.21, bicarbonate 12 mEq/L, anion gap 26, and beta-hydroxybutyrate is markedly elevated; his ethanol level is now undetectable. Which diagnosis best explains this picture?

answers.text: Alcoholic ketoacidosis: a high-gap ketotic acidosis with a near-normal glucose, driven by starvation and alcohol metabolism after intake stops
Diabetic ketoacidosis, because any high anion gap acidosis with elevated ketones is diabetic ketoacidosis by definition, whatever the glucose and history show
Lactic acidosis from sepsis, because the size of the anion gap alone identifies lactate as the acid present and no ketone result changes that conclusion
Uremic acidosis, because a gap of this size in a vomiting, volume-depleted patient is most often from acute kidney failure and retained acids

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: alcoholic ketoacidosis follows a binge that ends in vomiting and starvation - low insulin, high counter-regulatory hormones, and alcohol metabolism drive ketogenesis while glucose stays normal or only mildly elevated, and ketones (predominantly beta-hydroxybutyrate) produce the high-gap acidosis. B is wrong because diabetic ketoacidosis is characteristically accompanied by substantial hyperglycemia, which is absent here, and the history is the alcohol-starvation pattern. C is wrong because the markedly elevated beta-hydroxybutyrate identifies ketones, not lactate, as the dominant acid. D is wrong because no kidney failure is described, and uremia does not produce this degree of ketone elevation.

questions.question: A 29-year-old man had a commercial tourniquet applied high on the thigh 90 minutes ago for uncontrolled bleeding from a mangled lower leg after a machinery injury. Bleeding is controlled, he is resuscitated and stable, and the operating room is being prepared. He is now in a trauma center with surgical capability. What is the correct approach to the tourniquet?

answers.text: Loosen it for 5 minutes every hour on the ward to let the leg 'breathe', then retighten it, continuing this cycle until surgery the next day, documenting each loosening carefully in the chart, because a well-documented cycle of release and retightening is considered equivalent to formal conversion
Remove it immediately on arrival without preparation, because any tourniquet that has stopped bleeding has finished its job and the wound will stay dry

Attempt timely conversion in a controlled setting with the surgical team ready — expose and assess the wound, and replace the tourniquet with direct pressure, packing, or a pressure dressing if bleeding can be controlled that way — rather than leaving it on for many more hours

Add a second tourniquet below the first one and leave both in place for 24 hours, because more compression always protects an injured limb better, and covering both with a tight circumferential dressing, because layered compression over two tourniquets distributes the pressure more safely across the thigh

questions.explanation: Key C is correct: a tourniquet that has controlled bleeding should be converted to a less ischemic method as soon as the setting allows — ideally within about 2 hours — by exposing the wound with help and resuscitation ready, then controlling bleeding with direct pressure, hemostatic packing, or a dressing; if conversion fails, the tourniquet is reapplied. A is wrong because periodic loosening causes repeated blood loss without restoring meaningful perfusion and is explicitly not done. B is wrong because unprepared removal can release uncontrolled hemorrhage before the team can react. D is wrong because prolonged total ischemia beyond several hours increasingly costs the limb, and a second tourniquet adds ischemia without benefit.

questions.question: A 71-year-old man is admitted with accidental hypothermia, core temperature 29.4 C, and is being rewarmed with warmed intravenous fluids and forced-air warming. Thirty minutes into rewarming his core temperature falls further to 28.7 C and his BP drops from 104/66 to 88/54 mmHg. What best explains this and guides the response?

answers.text: Afterdrop and rewarming vasodilation; continue core rewarming with volume support and monitoring
The warmed fluids were too hot and caused thermal injury; stop all rewarming immediately and cool him
This pattern proves internal bleeding; stop rewarming and give a large rapid cold fluid bolus now
Peripheral rewarming should be intensified first to raise the skin temperature as fast as possible

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: afterdrop occurs as cold, acidotic peripheral blood returns to the core when peripheral vessels dilate during rewarming, transiently lowering core temperature and blood pressure; management is continued gentle core-first rewarming, warmed fluids, volume support, and continuous core (esophageal/bladder) monitoring. B is wrong because therapeutic warmed fluids do not cause this pattern, and abandoning rewarming worsens hypothermia. C is wrong because there is no bleeding evidence and cold fluids would deepen hypothermia. D is wrong because aggressive peripheral-first rewarming worsens afterdrop and rewarming shock.

questions.question: A nurse reviewing her own small unit's data notes its central-line infection count went from 0 infections in 40 line-days one month to 2 infections in 35 line-days the next, and a colleague concludes the unit's line care 'has collapsed' and needs emergency retraining. Which interpretation is most sound?

answers.text: With denominators this small, one or two events swing the rate enormously; the sound response is to review the two cases for real defects, aggregate data over a longer period with counts and denominators shown, and watch the trend before declaring a practice collapse

The colleague is right: any month with two infections after a zero month proves practice has deteriorated and warrants immediate unit-wide retraining, because a rate that doubles from zero represents a genuine doubling of risk regardless of how many line-days the unit accumulated that month
Small units should stop tracking infection data altogether, because numbers this small can never contribute anything useful to safety work on the unit
The rate should be reported to leadership as a precise percentage with two decimal places, so the size of the deterioration can be compared exactly with larger units

questions.explanation: The key is right: small denominators make rates unstable — a single event moves the rate dramatically — so case review for genuine defects plus longer aggregation, with numerators and denominators visible, precedes any conclusion about practice. B is wrong because it treats random swing as proven collapse. C is wrong because small-unit data remain useful when interpreted with their denominators and over time. D is wrong because false precision on tiny denominators misleads comparison rather than informing it.

questions.question: A 62-year-old woman ventilated for 7 days was noted yesterday to have fever and purulent secretions with a clear chest radiograph, assessed as ventilator-associated tracheobronchitis. Today she has a NEW right-lower-lobe infiltrate, her PaO2/FiO2 ratio has fallen from 280 to 170, PEEP has been increased from 5 to 10 cm H2O, and secretions remain purulent with a temperature of 39.1 C. What has changed, and what is now indicated?

answers.text: Nothing has changed since yesterday; continue observation only, because yesterday's tracheobronchitis assessment carries forward regardless of today's new findings
She now meets criteria for ventilator-associated pneumonia — obtain lower-respiratory sampling and start empiric antibiotics promptly as ordered
She has developed a pneumothorax, because only pleural air can raise PEEP requirements this quickly
She should be extubated immediately, because a new infiltrate means the tube is now doing more harm than good

questions.explanation: Key (B): The discriminating features have appeared: a new infiltrate plus significant worsening of oxygenation (falling PaO2/FiO2, doubled PEEP) on top of fever and purulent secretions converts the picture from tracheobronchitis to ventilator-associated pneumonia. That change triggers prompt lower-respiratory tract sampling and empiric antibiotics as ordered, alongside bundle measures — delay risks progression to sepsis. A is wrong: yesterday's tracheobronchitis assessment depended on the absent infiltrate and stable oxygenation, both of which have now reversed. C is wrong: pneumothorax causes unilateral findings and does not produce a new lobar infiltrate with purulent secretions and fever. D is wrong: she is more, not less, dependent on ventilatory support today.

questions.question: A 46-year-old woman is confused with hemoglobin 7.6 g/dL, schistocytes on smear, platelets 16,000/mm3, and lactate dehydrogenase markedly elevated — thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is strongly suspected and plasma exchange is being arranged for within hours. She has no active bleeding. A covering provider orders a platelet transfusion 'for the low count' before a central line is placed. What should the nurse do?

answers.text: Give the platelets, because any count below 20,000/mm3 must be corrected before a line is placed
Give the platelets together with plasma to balance the clotting risk
Question the order: platelets are withheld in TTP without life-threatening bleeding, as they can worsen microvascular thrombosis
Delay the plasma exchange until the platelet count rises above 50,000/mm3

questions.explanation: Key (C): In TTP the thrombocytopenia reflects platelet consumption into microthrombi, and transfused platelets can add substrate for thrombosis and worsen organ injury, so they are generally withheld unless there is life-threatening bleeding; urgent plasma exchange must not be delayed for a platelet target. A applies a generic threshold that does not fit this disease. B is wrong: adding plasma does not make platelet transfusion safe here, and plasma exchange itself supplies the needed plasma therapy. D reverses priorities: exchange is the lifesaving treatment and waiting for a count threshold increases mortality.

questions.question: A 59-year-old man has received a high-dose sodium nitroprusside infusion for 4 days for hypertensive emergency. Blood pressure is now controlled and PaO2 is normal, but he has become confused, lactate has risen from 1.8 to 7.4 mmol/L, pH is 7.22 with a widening metabolic acidosis, and central venous oxygen saturation is 88% with a narrowed arteriovenous oxygen difference. There is no fever or new source of infection. What should the nurse do first?

answers.text: Increase the nitroprusside rate to improve perfusion and clear the lactate
Stop nitroprusside and give hydroxocobalamin for cyanide toxicity
Continue the infusion and give sodium bicarbonate alone for the acidosis
Continue the infusion and start antibiotics for presumed new sepsis

questions.explanation: Key B is correct: prolonged high-dose sodium nitroprusside releases cyanide, which inhibits mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase so tissues cannot extract oxygen. That produces rising lactate and metabolic acidosis, altered mentation, a high venous oxygen saturation, and a narrowed arteriovenous oxygen difference despite adequate blood pressure and PaO2. The infusion must be stopped at once and hydroxocobalamin given, because it binds cyanide to form cyanocobalamin, while an alternative antihypertensive is substituted. A is wrong because increasing nitroprusside delivers more cyanide and worsens the poisoning. C is wrong because bicarbonate alone neither stops cyanide delivery nor removes cyanide. D is wrong because there is no fever or infectious source, the pattern fits cyanide toxicity, and continuing the infusion while treating presumed sepsis leaves the poison running.

pmp.quiz_title: PMP Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Capture effort is scarce on a predictive brewery expansion, so choices must be made about what knowledge to secure first. Which of the following qualify as knowledge critical to capture? Select the appropriate responses.

answers.text: The wort-cooling failure decision rules that only two brewers currently apply
The excise-duty evidence trail that revenue inspectors will audit at commissioning
The staff party preferences collected by the social committee
The delivery drivers' personal holiday rota
The label colour opinions gathered at a marketing workshop

questions.explanation: Cooling-failure decision rules held by two people and the audit-facing duty evidence trail are knowledge whose loss threatens production and compliance, so both are critical to capture. Party preferences, personal holiday arrangements, and label colour opinions are neither scarce nor decision-shaping and can be recreated trivially, so capture effort spent on them is wasted.

questions.question: A change to a telecommunications billing project has just been approved. Which of the following actions correctly follow from that approval? (Select three.)

answers.text: Update the affected project documents and baselines to reflect the change
Leave the original documents in place so the team can compare later
Treat the change as implemented as soon as the approval email is sent
Communicate the approved change and its effects to the affected stakeholders
Plan and schedule the implementation work for the change

questions.explanation: After approval, the project documents and baselines are updated, affected stakeholders are told what changed and what it means for them, and the implementation work is planned. Leaving original documents in place as the working record creates conflicting versions. Approval alone does not implement anything; the work still has to be planned and performed.

questions.question: A construction project's field and office teams are in persistent conflict. Which findings point to the real sources the project manager should address? (Select TWO.)

answers.text: Both team leads have strong personalities and enjoy debating
The project uses a new document system that some staff find unfamiliar
Field instructions reach crews through two different channels with conflicting revision dates
Office staff prefer email while field staff prefer radio updates
The schedule gives the office team review time that overlaps the field team's only procurement window

questions.explanation: Conflicting instruction channels and a schedule that pits the two groups against the same window are structural sources that will keep generating conflict. Strong personalities may color the tone but do not explain persistent, predictable friction. Unfamiliarity with a new system is a training need, not a conflict source between these teams. Different communication preferences are a tailoring issue the teams can bridge without conflict.

questions.question: A scrum team is adopting story-point estimation for its backlog. Which practices support sound estimation? (Select all that apply.)

answers.text: Estimate against shared reference stories the team has already delivered, so points stay consistent over time
Have the whole team estimate together so different perspectives on the work surface before a size is agreed
Let the product owner assign the points alone, since the product owner owns the backlog
Convert every story point into a fixed number of hours so progress can be tracked by timesheet
Revisit an item's estimate when genuinely new information about the work emerges

questions.explanation: Sound relative estimation uses reference stories for consistency, involves the whole team so knowledge and disagreement surface, and updates estimates when real new information appears. Product-owner-only assignment removes the team's knowledge of the work from the estimate. Converting points to fixed hours destroys the relative sizing the technique depends on and turns estimates back into timesheet commitments.

questions.question: A team building a flood-warning app has no member who has worked with river-gauge telemetry, and its first two sprints produced sensors misread by a factor of ten in test data. What is the best knowledge-gathering step?

answers.text: Bring in operational hydrologists for structured sessions on gauge data behaviour, and capture the conversion rules and edge cases in the team's working documentation
Let the team keep debugging conversions until the readings look plausible
Search a general programming forum whenever a reading looks wrong
Delay telemetry work until a hydrologist can be hired permanently

questions.explanation: Structured sessions with practising hydrologists gather the domain knowledge the team demonstrably lacks and leave it captured for future sprints. Continued debugging by trial risks plausible-looking but wrong safety data. Forum searches answer isolated questions without building reliable domain understanding. Waiting for a permanent hire stalls delivery when targeted expert input can close the gap sooner.

questions.question: A project manager is setting up routine financial monitoring for a state agency modernization. Which practices support monitoring variations and working with governance? (Select all that apply)

answers.text: Compare earned value, planned value, and actual cost at agreed intervals and investigate significant variances
Adjust the baseline quietly whenever a variance grows large enough to attract attention
Report only favorable variances so governance confidence stays high
Report forecasts and reserve status to the governance body in the format and cadence it requires
Escalate funding or baseline decisions that exceed the project manager's authority to the governance process

questions.explanation: Monitoring works when performance is compared regularly against plan, variances are investigated, forecasts and reserves are reported as governance requires, and decisions beyond the project manager's authority are escalated. Quietly moving the baseline hides the performance governance must judge. Selective reporting of good news destroys the trust and the early warning the process exists to provide.

questions.question: A team's decision log is meticulously maintained, yet the same decisions are reopened in meeting after meeting because nobody consults it. What should the project manager do?

answers.text: Add more fields to the log to make it more comprehensive
Assess why the artifact is not being used, and change how decisions are surfaced and referenced so the log actually informs the work
Require the team to read the entire log before every meeting
Delete the log, since documentation clearly does not work for this team

questions.explanation: Assessing artifact effectiveness means fixing the usage problem: decisions must be visible and referenced where work happens. More fields worsen the burden without addressing use, full-log readings are impractical, and deleting the record removes the memory the team needs.

questions.question: A pharmaceutical packaging project is entering planning. The sponsor wants inspection added at the end of the line to catch labeling defects. What should the project manager do first to plan quality properly?

answers.text: Identify the quality requirements and standards that apply to the labels and packaging from regulators, the customer, and organizational standards
Approve the end-of-line inspection plan and hire additional inspectors
Ask the packaging vendor to guarantee zero defects in the supply contract
Benchmark a competitor's defect rate and adopt it as the project target

questions.explanation: Quality planning starts by identifying the applicable quality requirements and standards so prevention and appraisal activities can be designed around them. Hiring inspectors first builds appraisal cost before requirements are known. A vendor guarantee does not define measurable requirements. A competitor benchmark is not a substitute for the regulatory and customer requirements that actually govern the deliverable.

questions.question: A newbuild ferry project is about to start construction. Its project manager is writing the document that will govern how risks are scored, funded, escalated, and reviewed. Which of the following provisions belong in that document? (Select three.)

answers.text: A forecast naming the exact dates on which the top risks will occur
The scoring scales and escalation thresholds that define when a risk goes to the steering group
A commitment that the risk register will never need updating after planning
Funding arrangements for risk responses, including who may authorize response spending
How contingency will be sized, held, and released

questions.explanation: The scoring scales and escalation thresholds that define when a risk goes to the steering group belong because consistent analysis and timely escalation require them before risks arrive. Funding arrangements for risk responses, including who may authorize response spending, belong because responses stall when nobody knows who can pay for them. Rules for how contingency will be sized, held, and released belong because reserves are part of the risk approach. A forecast naming the exact dates on which the top risks will occur claims a precision risk planning cannot have. A commitment that the register will never need updating contradicts the living nature of risk work, since new risks emerge throughout delivery.

questions.question: A hybrid hospital-at-home service has a governance board that approves each expansion cohort, but expansion requests arrive as slide decks with different measures each time, so the board defers most decisions. What should the project manager introduce?

answers.text: Longer board meetings so each differently-shaped request can be debated fully
A standard expansion pack with agreed measures, submitted on a fixed cycle, so the board can compare cohorts and decide at the meeting
A rule that expansion requests come only from the clinical director
Verbal briefings instead of packs, to keep the board discussion flexible

questions.explanation: A standard pack on a fixed cycle supports the governance process by making decisions comparable and timely. Longer meetings accommodate inconsistency rather than removing it. Restricting who may request expansion does not fix the incomparable evidence. Verbal briefings remove the record a governance decision needs.

questions.question: A product squad estimating a set of data-migration stories keeps producing estimates that ignore the effort of reconciling records rejected by automated matching, which historically consumes a third of migration time. What estimation change addresses this?

answers.text: Estimate only the automated matching, since reconciliation varies too much to count
Add a flat fifty percent to every estimate without explaining why
Include reconciliation work explicitly in the effort estimates, using the historical proportion as a reference until the squad's own data replaces it
Let the squad commit first and discover reconciliation effort during the sprint

questions.explanation: Making a known, historically large work component explicit in estimates corrects a systematic underestimation. Omitting variable work guarantees the shortfall the history predicts. An unexplained flat uplift hides the reasoning and cannot improve as data matures. Committing before counting known work repeats the failure inside the sprint.

questions.question: A fertiliser producer must reline storage silos at four depots without interrupting supply during the planting season, combining fixed depot shutdowns with trial relining at one site first. Which execution strategy should the plan recommend?

answers.text: Sequence the depots outside the planting peak, proving the relining method at the trial site before each subsequent depot starts
Reline all four depots simultaneously to shorten the programme
Close all depots for one long shutdown spanning the planting season
Begin with whichever depot manager shouts loudest and improvise the order from there

questions.explanation: Sequencing depots outside the supply peak with a proven trial protects the constraint that dominates this strategy. Simultaneous relining risks every depot's supply on an unproven method. A season-long total closure violates the continuity requirement outright. A loudest-first order lets pressure, not supply risk, set the sequence.

questions.question: A dual-sourcing response for a furniture maker's board supplier is partly working: one of two product lines is now qualified with the second supplier, while the other line failed its quality trials and still depends on the original supplier. The sponsor asks whether the supply risk is handled. What is the accurate communication?

answers.text: A split picture: the qualified line's exposure has fallen as planned, the unqualified line remains fully exposed, and the next step is a further trial or an alternative for that line, with its timing
Yes, the risk is handled, because dual sourcing has been implemented
No progress has been made, because dual sourcing only counts when every line is covered
The risk no longer needs reporting, because a response is under way

questions.explanation: Honest status communication distinguishes what a partial response has actually achieved from what remains: one line protected, one line exposed, with the next step and its timing. Claiming the risk is handled overstates the position for the exposed line. Claiming no progress understates a real reduction and misleads in the opposite direction. A response under way is a reason to keep reporting, not to stop.

questions.question: Quality reviewers in a contact center keep conflicting with team trainers. Reviewers fail calls for being too long; trainers coach agents to stay on calls until the customer's issue is fully resolved. What is the most likely source the project manager should address?

answers.text: The reviewers' personalities, which trend toward fault-finding
Incompatible measures: the scorecard rewards short calls while training and customer outcomes reward full resolution
The trainers' refusal to attend reviewer calibration sessions
The age of the call recording system, which frustrates both groups

questions.explanation: The source is incompatible measurement: a scorecard rewarding short calls directly opposes coaching that rewards full resolution, so each group is doing what it is measured on. Attributing the pattern to reviewer personalities ignores that the conflict follows the measures, not the individuals. Calibration attendance may contribute but does not create the underlying contradiction. Recording-system age frustrates everyone equally and does not set the two groups against each other.

questions.question: Exhibit - A regional bakery chain is replacing ovens in 12 production sites while launching a pre-order app. Oven replacement follows fixed vendor installation windows and food-safety inspections; the app evolves through two-week iterations with store managers. Both streams share one refrigeration contractor and one training team, and the sponsor reviews an integrated plan monthly. At consolidation, which dependency most needs explicit management in the integrated plan?

answers.text: The bakery's flour supplier, which neither stream's plan mentions
The sponsor's monthly review meeting, which both streams attend
The shared refrigeration contractor and training team, whose capacity both streams draw on at overlapping points
The app store's release calendar, which only the app stream uses

questions.explanation: Consolidation exists to surface shared-resource dependencies; one contractor and one training team serving both streams is the clash risk the plan must sequence. The flour supplier is outside both streams' work. A shared meeting is governance rhythm, not a delivery dependency. The release calendar constrains one stream only, so it is not a cross-plan dependency.

questions.question: Several autonomous product teams in a bank each invented their own way of approving production releases, and an auditor cannot trace who authorized two of them. Leadership wants consistency without removing team autonomy over their internal work. What governance design fits?

answers.text: A single detailed procedure prescribing every step of every team's release work
No framework, since team autonomy is incompatible with governance
Authorization by the most senior engineer present on release day

A lightweight common framework that fixes the non-negotiables — who may authorize a release, the evidence required, and where the authorization is recorded — while leaving teams free in how they organize work inside that frame

questions.explanation: Governance for autonomous teams works by establishing the structure and rules at the points of accountability — authorization, evidence, and record — using organizational assets, while preserving team discretion elsewhere. Prescribing every step abolishes the autonomy leadership wants to keep and invites workarounds. Treating autonomy and governance as incompatible abandons the traceability the auditor found missing. Seniority-on-the-day is the untraceable arrangement that produced the audit finding.

questions.question: Emergency repair work on a pumping station must start immediately after storm damage. The full extent of the damage cannot be defined until equipment is opened up, the work is expected to last only a few weeks, and the utility needs a ceiling on its exposure. Which contract approach best fits?

answers.text: A time-and-materials arrangement with a not-to-exceed ceiling and active surveillance of hours and materials, because the work cannot yet be defined but exposure must be capped
A firm-fixed-price contract covering all damage, including damage not yet discovered
A cost-plus-percentage arrangement with no ceiling, so the contractor is rewarded as costs grow
No contract at all until the damage is fully defined, leaving the station out of service meanwhile

questions.explanation: Undefined urgent work of short duration suits time-and-materials, but only with a ceiling and active surveillance to control the buyer's exposure. A fixed price for undiscovered damage prices a guess and invites disputes. Cost-plus-percentage rewards higher costs and removes any economy incentive. Waiting for full definition leaves a critical station idle.

questions.question: Guides on a museum travelling-exhibition project keep making opposite calls on how much handling school groups may do with replica artefacts, although the exhibition vision stresses hands-on learning within conservation limits. What should the project manager do?

answers.text: Work the vision into the guides' handling decisions by reviewing real cases against it at team huddles until the pattern of calls becomes consistent
Email the conservation policy again and ask guides to confirm they have read it
Let each venue set its own handling practice because local judgement matters most
Remove replica handling from the exhibition to end the inconsistency

questions.explanation: Reviewing real handling cases against the vision in huddles promotes the vision as a decision tool and aligns judgement across guides. Re-sending a policy repeats information transfer that already failed to change behaviour. Venue-by-venue practice abandons the shared vision for local variation. Removing handling deletes a core element of the vision instead of promoting it.

questions.question: Interest rates have risen sharply since a housing developer's project was approved. At the new rates, the later phases of a three-phase housing scheme no longer meet the developer's return threshold, while phase one, already under construction, still does. Lenders are asking for the developer's position. What should the project manager do?

answers.text: Assure the lenders the full scheme will proceed as approved, to protect confidence

Assess the rate change's impact phase by phase and bring the sponsor prioritised options, such as completing phase one as planned, redesigning or deferring later phases, with the numbers for each, before the lenders are answered
Stop phase one as well, because the scheme was appraised as a whole
Increase the planned selling prices on paper until all phases pass the threshold again

questions.explanation: A financing-environment change that affects phases differently calls for phase-level assessment and costed options for the decision-makers, before external commitments are made. Assuring lenders of an unchanged scheme misstates a position the analysis does not support. Stopping a phase that still meets the threshold destroys value the change has not touched. Inflating price assumptions to pass a threshold manufactures the answer the appraisal exists to test.

questions.question: A grain export terminal project involves a rail operator that can halt all grain movements to the port, farming cooperatives that support the project but are fragmented across many small groups, and a port union that is undecided and influential with the workforce. What analysis best supports the project manager's engagement planning?

answers.text: Treat all three parties equally, since each can affect the project in some way
Focus engagement on the farming cooperatives because they are the most numerous
Defer analysis of the union until it declares a position

Assess each party's power, interest, and current stance, so engagement effort concentrates on the rail operator's concerns, organises the cooperatives' support, and addresses the union's undecided position

questions.explanation: Engagement planning needs differentiated analysis: power, interest, and stance together show where effort changes outcomes: close attention to the party that can halt the project, structure for the fragmented supporters, and early work with the undecided but influential union. Equal treatment wastes effort on parties whose stance is already secure and starves the one relationship that can stop the project. Numbers alone mislead; a thousand fragmented supporters move less than one operator's timetable decision. Waiting for the union to declare itself surrenders the period when its position is most open to influence.

alabama-hvac.quiz_title: Alabama HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: In a pumpdown system, the thermostat is satisfied. Put the control sequence in the correct order of events.

answers.text: The liquid-line solenoid closes, the compressor pumps the low side down, and the low-pressure switch stops the compressor
The low-pressure switch opens first while the solenoid stays open, and the compressor continues running until the high-pressure switch stops it at the end of the cycle
The compressor stops immediately on the thermostat, and only afterward does the solenoid close so liquid can continue feeding the evaporator during the off cycle
The solenoid opens wider on the thermostat call ending, so the evaporator fills with liquid that the compressor will clear on the next start before cooling resumes

questions.explanation: Pumpdown works by closing the liquid solenoid first, letting the running compressor evacuate the low side into the receiver, then stopping on the low-pressure cutout. The low-pressure switch responds to the pumpdown rather than initiating it while the solenoid stays open, stopping the compressor first would leave the low side full of refrigerant, and filling the evaporator during the off cycle is the migration problem pumpdown exists to prevent.

questions.question: A P-trap at the base of a suction riser serves to:

answers.text: Trap a small pool of oil/refrigerant that helps oil move up the riser in slugs and prevents oil from draining back down during the off cycle
Stop refrigerant vapor from rising to the compressor
Remove moisture from the suction vapor
Measure the oil level in the riser

questions.explanation: Oil collects in the trap until gas velocity carries it upward as a slug, and the trap keeps that oil from falling back when flow stops. Option B is wrong because vapor must flow freely through the trap, option C is a drier's job on the liquid line, and option D describes a sight glass or oil-level regulator, not a trap.

questions.question: What does it mean that a split system is an AHRI-rated combination?

answers.text: Any indoor and outdoor units of equal nominal tonnage are considered rated together once they are installed and started
The outdoor unit alone carries the rating, so the indoor section can be any coil with a matching refrigerant connection size
The installer creates the rating by recording startup pressures and signing the installation invoice at the end of the job
That specific indoor and outdoor pairing was tested together, and its published capacity and efficiency apply to that pairing

questions.explanation: Published ratings belong to the tested pairing of outdoor unit, indoor coil, and often the furnace or air handler. Equal tonnage alone creates no rating, the indoor section materially affects results, and field paperwork cannot create a tested rating.

questions.question: Which set of duct locations must all be included when a duct system is sealed to its specified class?

answers.text: Only the transverse joints, because longitudinal seams are factory-sealed
Transverse joints, longitudinal seams, and branch tap-ins and other duct wall penetrations
Only the connections at the air handler, because the rest of the system leaks negligibly
Only fittings, because straight duct sections never leak at their seams

questions.explanation: Leakage occurs at every discontinuity in the duct wall, so the sealing class applies to joints, seams, taps, and penetrations alike. Option A is wrong because longitudinal seams such as Pittsburgh and snap-lock seams do leak and are explicitly part of sealing requirements; option C is wrong because field joints throughout the run typically outnumber and out-leak the equipment connections; option D is wrong because straight sections are joined by longitudinal seams, which are a primary leakage path when left unsealed.

questions.question: How does an electronic expansion valve (EEV) differ from a TXV in how it controls refrigerant flow?

answers.text: An EEV has no moving parts and relies on a fixed factory-drilled opening
An EEV uses inlet water pressure from the condensate drain to position its needle
An EEV responds only once per day when its controller updates the superheat setting, at a scheduled overnight check of the system's operating program as a whole
An EEV is positioned by an electronic controller using sensor inputs such as suction pressure and line temperatures to hold a superheat target

questions.explanation: An EEV's controller reads pressure and temperature sensors and drives a motorized valve in small steps to maintain the programmed superheat. Option A describes a fixed orifice, not an electronic valve, and option B invents a water-pressure mechanism that does not exist. Option C is wrong because the controller adjusts the valve continuously during operation, not on a daily cycle.

questions.question: An ECM blower ramps slowly, delivers steady airflow as duct static rises, and its control module has failed while the motor windings test good. What is the best repair approach?

answers.text: Install a PSC motor without changing the control or wiring
Replace the module or motor assembly with the manufacturer-matched ECM component and program it correctly
Bypass the module and connect line voltage directly to the motor windings without any electronic commutation or speed control in place
Add a larger run capacitor to restore electronic control

questions.explanation: ECM performance depends on its matched electronic module and programming, so that component must be restored correctly. Substituting a PSC motor changes controls, wiring, and airflow behavior. Direct line voltage to ECM windings can destroy the motor and will not provide control, and ECM motors do not use an external run capacitor in that way.

questions.question: A designer uses the extreme record low temperature instead of the recommended winter design temperature for a city. What is the likely result?

answers.text: A smaller, more efficient furnace selected from the next size down in the product line
No effect on equipment size
Better humidity control in summer
An oversized heating system that short-cycles most of the season

questions.explanation: Design temperatures represent near-extreme but statistically appropriate conditions; using the record low inflates delta T and load, oversizing equipment, so D is correct. A reverses the effect, B ignores the larger delta T, and C confuses heating sizing with summer latent control.

questions.question: During a duct replacement, the owner asks for added insulation that was not in the original scope. How should the contractor price the change?

answers.text: Absorb the full cost as goodwill and record nothing, so the original job-cost report remains unchanged
Price the added labor, materials, overhead, and profit, and get written approval before doing it
Charge only for the insulation material at supplier cost, with no recovery for the crew time to install it
Double the original contract price regardless of the size of the addition, as a standard penalty for any change

questions.explanation: B is correct because a change order should recover its full cost plus overhead and profit and be approved in writing first. A is incorrect because absorbing the cost hides a real job cost and gives away recoverable work. C is incorrect because it omits the labor and overhead the added work consumes. D is incorrect because pricing must relate to the actual added scope, not an arbitrary doubling.

questions.question: A rooftop gas heat section lights reliably but produces low heat rise and a lazy, yellow-tipped flame. Supply gas pressure to the unit is within range. What measurement most directly confirms a likely cause?

answers.text: Manifold pressure at the gas valve compared with the rating plate value, because low manifold pressure underfires the burner and softens the flame

Blower motor nameplate amps compared with locked-rotor amps, because flame appearance on a rooftop burner is set by blower electrical load while the rest of the system continues to operate normally through a complete cycle of operation

Economizer damper angle compared with its minimum position, because damper angle is the adjustment that meters gas flow to the burner section even after the obvious maintenance items at the unit have already been checked and corrected first
Condensate trap depth compared with pan pressure, because trap depth determines the gas pressure delivered to the burners during heating

questions.explanation: Low heat rise with a lazy flame and adequate inlet pressure points to underfiring, confirmed by manifold pressure against the rating plate. Blower locked-rotor amps, damper angle, and trap depth do not meter gas to the burner.

questions.question: A candidate who failed the written examination writes to the Board asking for the hands-on alternative instead of another written sitting. Which path does the law provide?

answers.text: He may take a practical examination at any time within two years, with no written request needed, because the request is implied by his failure notice. The Board's office confirms the date by letter, and the examination is scheduled from that confirmation rather than from the original written sitting.
