He must first pass the written examination, because the practical examination is an additional test given only to candidates who already passed. Once he passes that later test, the earlier written failure is treated as erased from his record for every licensing purpose.
He may, on specific written request to the Board, take a practical examination equivalent to the written examination within six months of the last unsuccessful written attempt.

He may substitute employer references for any further examination, because documented field experience replaces testing after one written failure. His employer may certify the experience in a sworn statement, and the Board accepts that statement in place of any further testing.

questions.explanation: C is correct: An applicant who fails the written examination may, on specific written request to the Board, take a practical examination equivalent to the written examination, held within six months from the date of the last unsuccessful written examination. A is wrong: The window is six months from the last unsuccessful written attempt, not two years, and a specific written request is required. B is wrong: The practical route is an alternative for an applicant who failed the written exam, not an add-on after passing it. D is wrong: Experience and references do not replace the required examination after a failure.

questions.question: A foreman is planning refrigerant work on a rooftop unit and asks what safety-and-environmental preparation the crew should complete before opening the system. Which plan is soundest?

answers.text: Skip the briefing when the crew is experienced, because hazard communication is required only for first-year employees on a jobsite.

Vent any inconvenient residual refrigerant quickly at the start, because recovery is required only when a full system is being scrapped. Experienced technicians are presumed to know the hazards, so the briefing and equipment checks are documented only for new hires.

Brief the crew on the job hazards and protective equipment, confirm refrigerant recovery equipment and procedures are in place so refrigerant is recovered rather than vented, and verify the work area is safe before starting.

Rely on the building owner's safety program entirely, because a visiting contractor has no safety duties on another party's premises. The owner's written safety plan is filed with the job paperwork, and the contractor's crew follows that plan instead of its own procedures.

questions.explanation: C is correct: Safety and environmental practice for HVAC work combines hazard briefing and protective equipment with lawful refrigerant handling, including recovering refrigerant before opening a charged system rather than venting it; experience and premises ownership do not remove the contractor's own duties. A is wrong: Hazard communication is not limited to first-year employees. B is wrong: Refrigerant must be recovered before a charged system is opened; venting as a shortcut is not the lawful procedure. D is wrong: A contractor retains safety responsibilities for its own crew even when working on an owner's premises.

questions.question: A candidate wants to know how Alabama lien law will reach him on the heating and air conditioning examination and which listed reference covers the business and law material. Which answer is correct?

answers.text: Lien law is not tested at all on the examination, because the Alabama examination is confined to trade topics and the business areas were removed from it when the examination moved to computer-based delivery at testing centers.

Lien Laws is one of the embedded business areas, accounting for 2 of the examination's 115 questions, and the NASCLA Contractors Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, 14th edition, is an open-book reference for this same examination.

Lien law is tested in a separate afternoon session of 25 questions devoted to it, and candidates must bring a state lien statute book of their own because that book does not appear on the examination's reference list.

Lien Laws accounts for 10 of the 115 questions, which makes it the largest single business area on the examination, ahead of both contracts and licensing laws in the weight the outline assigns to business topics.

questions.explanation: B is correct: the content outline places Lien Laws among the embedded business and law areas with 2 questions of the 115, and the examination's reference list includes the NASCLA Contractors Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, 14th edition, marked open book for this same exam. A is wrong because the business areas, including lien laws, are part of the single examination. C is wrong because there is no separate lien session; all business areas are embedded in the one exam. D is wrong because Lien Laws carries 2 questions, not 10, and is among the smaller business areas.

questions.question: An electronic oil primary goes to lockout, and pressing reset repeatedly makes the burner fire briefly and lock out again with a smoky, rumbling start each time. The technician should:

answers.text: Keep resetting until the burner stays lit so the fault clears itself, pressing the reset as many times as needed during a single visit without checking ignition, fuel delivery, or the amount of oil already sprayed into the chamber
Stop resetting, because repeated trials can load the chamber with unburned oil and cause a severe puffback, and diagnose ignition, fuel delivery, and flame sensing first
Replace the thermostat because lockout is a control-voltage issue
Close the combustion-air opening to enrich the mixture

questions.explanation: Repeated resets without diagnosis risk accumulating oil that can ignite violently; lockout is a safety response requiring fault-finding, not persistence. Option A describes the dangerous practice itself. Option C is wrong because the control is sequencing and locking out as designed, indicating a burner-side fault. Option D starves combustion air and worsens sooting and ignition.

questions.question: On a cold morning a water heater spills briefly at the draft hood for the first minute after firing, then establishes steady draft and spills no more. The flue is clear and zone pressure is near neutral. What best fits this pattern?

answers.text: Cold flue with delayed draft
A blocked flue, which characteristically spills only at startup and then clears itself completely once the burner has run for about a minute
A cracked heat exchanger in the nearby furnace, which pushes flue gas out of the water heater hood only while both appliances start at the same time
Excessive combustion-appliance zone depressurization, which is known to disappear on its own as soon as the burner warms regardless of exhaust operation

questions.explanation: A cold flue has little initial draft, so brief startup spillage that clears as the chimney warms fits a cold-flue, delayed-draft pattern. A blocked flue spills persistently rather than clearing, a furnace heat-exchanger crack does not produce this timed water-heater pattern, and depressurization-driven spillage continues while the exhaust load continues instead of resolving with warm-up.

questions.question: A chilled-water pump has begun rattling like gravel is passing through it, vibrating, and losing discharge pressure, especially when the water is warm and the suction strainer is partly clogged. What is happening?

answers.text: Cavitation — vapor bubbles form at the impeller eye because suction pressure fell too low, then collapse violently in the higher-pressure region of the pump

Normal operation, because a rattling pump with falling discharge pressure is how a centrifugal pump signals that it is fully primed and loaded, and the strainer condition, suction pressure, and water temperature have all just been verified normal
A failed mechanical seal only, which always raises discharge pressure while making the pump run quieter and smoother than before
Water hammer in the discharge piping several floors above, which cannot affect conditions at the pump suction or the impeller eye

questions.explanation: When inlet pressure drops below what the pump needs, water flashes to vapor at the eye and the bubbles implode downstream, producing the gravel noise, vibration, and lost head. Option B dismisses classic damage symptoms, option C describes a leak path that does not explain the noise or lost pressure, and option D is a discharge-side surge phenomenon unrelated to suction conditions.

questions.question: A communicating residential system displays a manufacturer fault indicating low indoor airflow on cooling, though the filter is clean. What is the most productive next step?

answers.text: Replace the outdoor unit, because communicating faults always originate outdoors
Clear the fault repeatedly until the message stops appearing
Disconnect the communicating bus entirely and wire the system as a conventional 24-volt system permanently, discarding all of its built-in diagnostic reporting
Use the system's reported airflow and static data and inspect the blower, coil, and duct restrictions the diagnostics point to

questions.explanation: Communicating diagnostics narrow the search, and reported airflow data should guide inspection of the indoor air path. The fault described is an indoor airflow issue, not grounds to replace the outdoor unit. Clearing codes without repair leaves the cause in place, and abandoning communicating control discards its diagnostic and performance benefits.

questions.question: A contractor wins nearly every bid but finishes most jobs with little or no profit. What estimating problem is most likely?

answers.text: The overhead rate is set too high, causing the company to win work it should have declined at those prices
Prices are too low because costs such as burden or overhead are being understated
The quantity takeoffs are too detailed, giving the estimator an unrealistically precise view of material needs
Change orders are being documented too carefully, which consumes profit in administrative time on each job

questions.explanation: B is correct because consistently winning while earning little suggests prices are set below the true cost of labor burden, overhead, and direct costs. A is incorrect because an excessive overhead rate would tend to lose bids, not win nearly all of them. C is incorrect because detailed takeoffs improve accuracy rather than erase profit. D is incorrect because careful change documentation protects profit by capturing added work.

questions.question: Two identical supply trunks are sealed the same day. On one, foil tape was pressed over dusty, slightly oily galvanized joints and burnished lightly; on the other, joints were wiped clean and dry and sealed with mastic reinforced at the corners. A year later the taped trunk leaks noticeably more. The best explanation is:

answers.text: Tape adhesion depends entirely on a clean, dry surface and firm burnishing, so the contaminated application failed progressively, while mastic bonds to the prepared surface and tolerates joint movement better
Tape always fails within a year regardless of how it is applied

Mastic works because it dissolves the galvanizing and welds the joint shut, fusing the two metal edges into a single continuous surface that no longer needs tape, fasteners, or any separate seal once the coating has fully cured in the field
The taped trunk leaked because tape adds thickness that narrows the duct

questions.explanation: Listed tapes are legitimate sealants only when their listing conditions are honored — clean, dry metal and full contact — whereas mastic on a prepared joint forms a durable, slightly flexible seal. Option B is wrong because properly listed and applied tape on clean duct can last for years; the failure here traces to the contaminated surface; option C is wrong because mastic is an adhesive sealant that cures on the surface; it does not dissolve zinc coatings or weld metal; option D is wrong because a few thousandths of tape thickness has no meaningful effect on duct area or leakage.

questions.question: A mechanical room contains a deep pit below a chiller, and signage and a permit program treat the pit as a confined space requiring controls for entry. What defines the safe approach for a technician asked to retrieve a dropped tool from the pit?

answers.text: Climb in quickly and climb back out before any hazardous atmosphere could affect a healthy worker, since short entries do not count as entries
Send the smallest crew member, because a smaller person uses less oxygen and can safely work in the space for the few minutes the task requires
Follow the permit entry procedure rather than entering on impulse
Prop the door open and rely on natural air movement through the doorway, which is considered equivalent to a tested and permitted entry in a pit

questions.explanation: A space controlled by a permit program is entered only under that procedure, with testing, an attendant, and rescue arrangements in place. Speed, body size, and a propped door do not make an uncontrolled atmosphere safe or turn an unpermitted entry into a permitted one.

questions.question: In the weeks after tornadoes sweep through the northern part of the state and the Governor declares a state of emergency, a repair operator with a prior conviction for noncompliance with a state occupational license requirement knowingly conceals that noncompliance while contracting to repair a damaged home. Which classification fits these facts?

answers.text: Ordinary unlicensed practice only, a Class A misdemeanor with no felony exposure on these facts.
A Board administrative violation only, punishable solely by a fine of up to $2,000 per violation.
Aggravated home repair fraud in the declared emergency, a Class C felony.
A local ordinance violation only, because state licensing law does not reach disaster home repairs.

questions.explanation: C is correct: Knowingly committing listed deceptive acts, including violating the licensing chapter after a prior conviction for noncompliance with a state occupational license requirement or knowingly concealing such noncompliance, in home repair of a residence damaged by an event under a Governor-declared emergency is aggravated home repair fraud, a Class C felony. A is wrong: The emergency declaration, residential damage, prior conviction, and knowing concealment together trigger the felony carve-out rather than the ordinary misdemeanor alone. B is wrong: The Board fine track does not displace the felony classification supplied by the emergency-fraud statute. D is wrong: State law expressly reaches this conduct; it is not left to local ordinances alone.

texas-hvac.quiz_title: Texas HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Where is a suction accumulator installed, and what is its main job?

answers.text: In the liquid line just after the receiver, to store extra liquid refrigerant so the expansion valve always sees a completely solid column of liquid
In the suction line just before the compressor, to catch liquid and meter it back as vapor and oil
In the discharge line just after the compressor, to separate oil from hot gas and return that oil directly to the compressor crankcase by a float
In the condenser outlet ahead of the receiver, to subcool the liquid further whenever the ambient temperature around the unit rises above design

questions.explanation: The accumulator sits in the suction line at the compressor inlet, trapping liquid slugs and returning them gradually through a small orifice with oil. A liquid-line vessel after the receiver describes receiver/storage duty, a discharge-line float device describes an oil separator, and extra subcooling at the condenser outlet is not the accumulator's location or function.

questions.question: What information does an inverter compressor's variable operating frequency give the technician, at a practical level?

answers.text: The exact refrigerant charge in ounces, because drive frequency is calibrated against charge weight during the factory test of each individual unit
The supply voltage quality at the building, because any frequency other than line frequency proves the incoming power is outside its tolerance
A direct indication of the speed the drive is commanding
The indoor blower's airflow in cubic feet per minute, because both motors are locked to one shared frequency in every communicating design

questions.explanation: Drive frequency sets compressor motor speed, so it shows how hard the system is being driven at that moment. It is not a charge scale, a commanded frequency different from line frequency is the normal purpose of the drive, and the indoor blower runs on its own control rather than sharing the compressor's frequency.

questions.question: Why must rooftop equipment be placed and secured so service work near a roof edge can be done safely?

answers.text: Rooftop units must sit directly at the edge so condensate can fall clear of the building without any drain piping at all
Roof edges eliminate fall concerns because technicians are trained to balance while carrying tools and replacement parts
Workers need safe access and, where the location creates a fall exposure, an approved means of protection.
Equipment may overhang the roof edge if its weight is supported mainly by the curb and shipping brackets left in place

questions.explanation: Placement must allow servicing without creating an unprotected fall hazard, and equipment must be fully supported. Edge placement for drainage is unsafe and unnecessary, training does not remove fall exposure, and shipping brackets are not structural support.

questions.question: What is the on-time contractor renewal fee, and how long must a CE certificate be retained?

answers.text: Renewal fee $65, and the CE certificate must be retained for one year after course completion
Renewal fee $115, and the CE certificate must be retained for three years after course completion
Renewal fee $65, and the CE certificate must be retained for three years after course completion
Renewal fee $50, and the CE certificate must be retained for one year after course completion

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: renewal $65; CE certificate retained 1 year and produced on request. B uses the $115 application fee and the 3-year business-record period. C pairs the right fee with the wrong retention. D uses the $50 certified-technician application fee.

questions.question: An electronic bypass arrangement uses a plenum static pressure sensor wired to the control. What does the control do with that signal?

answers.text: It uses the signal only to log pressure for a service report, because electronic bypass dampers are positioned by zone thermostat count and never by measured duct pressure
It converts the pressure signal into a call for second-stage heat, because high plenum pressure is the panel's standard indication that more capacity is needed in the zones
It modulates the bypass damper to hold the set static pressure
It shuts the bypass damper tighter as pressure rises, because relieving a zoned system requires forcing all blower airflow through whichever zones remain open

questions.explanation: In an electronic bypass system the sensor reports plenum static pressure and the control drives the modulating bypass damper to hold the chosen setpoint. The signal is a working control input rather than a log entry, high pressure calls for relief rather than more capacity, and closing the bypass further would raise pressure instead of relieving it.

questions.question: A technician needs to pressurize a repaired, empty system for leak testing. Which practice is safe and appropriate?

answers.text: Pressurize with oxygen to a high pressure for a sensitive test

Pressurize with shop compressed air and leave the moisture in the system, relying on the filter drier alone to remove all of the water, oil contamination, and noncondensable gases introduced during a long, high-pressure leak test at maximum shop pressure
Use dry nitrogen, regulated to a safe test pressure, optionally with a small trace amount of the system refrigerant for an electronic leak detector, then follow with proper evacuation
Use discharge gas from a running compressor to pressurize the empty system

questions.explanation: Dry nitrogen is inert and moisture-free, and a regulator keeps test pressure controlled; a trace of refrigerant lets an electronic detector pinpoint leaks before evacuation. Option A is dangerous because oxygen under pressure with oil can explode, option B introduces moisture and air that must be removed, and option D cannot pressurize an empty, repaired system and risks contamination.

questions.question: Water drips from the outside of a bare-metal supply duct crossing a humid attic in summer, while the air inside the duct is 55°F and attic dew point is near 70°F. What is occurring?

answers.text: Condensate is leaking out through duct joints from inside, because supply ducts normally carry liquid water that escapes wherever joints are not taped
The duct is sweating because humid attic air is reaching a surface chilled by the cold supply air, and the water is refrigerant condensing through the metal wall
Missing insulation lets surface chill
The roof is leaking directly onto that duct section, which is why the dripping only happens during the cooling season and not during dry winter heating

questions.explanation: Without insulation the metal surface falls below the attic dew point, so moisture from attic air condenses on the outside of the duct. Supply ducts carry air, not liquid water, refrigerant cannot pass through the duct wall, and a roof leak tied to cooling-season runtime, rather than rain, does not fit the pattern.

questions.question: A bypass steam humidifier's electrode canister is scaled, output has fallen, and the water panel light is on. What service is indicated?

answers.text: Replace the canister per the manufacturer schedule and check water quality and drain operation.
Soak the sealed canister in descaler and reinstall it indefinitely, because steam canisters are lifetime parts with no replacement interval
Increase the humidistat setting to maximum so the scaled electrodes draw more current and burn the mineral scale off by themselves
Disconnect the drain line so minerals stay dissolved in the boiling chamber instead of concentrating during the automatic flush cycles

questions.explanation: Steam canisters are consumable: mineral scale insulates the electrodes and the canister must be renewed, with feed-water quality checked. Descaling a sealed canister is not the prescribed service, overdriving scaled electrodes does not clean them, and blocking the drain concentrates minerals faster.

questions.question: In general terms, an indemnification clause in a contract does which of the following?

answers.text: Sets the daily amount payable if the project finishes later than the contract completion date requires
Lists the equipment models that are approved as substitutions for the products named in the specifications
Allocates responsibility for certain losses or claims to a specified party
Requires the owner to obtain the building permit and schedule every inspection for the mechanical work

questions.explanation: C is correct because indemnification allocates who bears specified losses, claims, or damages arising from the work. A is incorrect because daily amounts for late completion describe liquidated damages. B is incorrect because approved substitutions are handled through submittals and specifications. D is incorrect because permit and inspection duties are scope assignments, not indemnification.

questions.question: A manufactured home's heating bills jump after a winter storm, and the under-home inspection finds belly material torn open with insulation hanging down around the ducts. Why does this explain the bill increase?

answers.text: The torn belly lets the furnace draw return air from under the home, and cold return air is more efficient, so the bill rise must come from the thermostat
The exposed ducts and floor lose heat directly to outdoor air and the unprotected ductwork leaks and cools supply air before it reaches the registers
The hanging insulation blocks the crossover duct inlet completely in every case, so the furnace short-cycles and the blower's electricity dominates the bill
The belly material is structural, and its loss lets the home settle so the gas line sags, reducing manifold pressure and therefore heating efficiency

questions.explanation: The belly encloses and insulates the floor and duct system; tearing it exposes ducts to outdoor conditions, wasting heat and cooling supply air in transit. It does not convert the return to an efficient under-home source, does not block the crossover in every case, and does not sag the gas line by settlement.

questions.question: A sidewall vent termination is installed just above grade in a snow climate. The first winter, the furnace locks out repeatedly after heavy snowfalls. What install error best explains this?

answers.text: The exhaust was terminated with PVC instead of stainless steel, so snow was able to cool the pipe and condense extra water inside
The intake and exhaust were terminated on opposite sides of the house, so wind pressure kept reversing the inducer flow pattern
The furnace was leveled perfectly flat, so condensate backed up into the inducer housing whenever outdoor temperatures fell low
Termination placed too low for snow depth

questions.explanation: A termination set too low for expected snow accumulation gets buried and starved or blocked, producing repeated lockouts after snowfalls. Option A is wrong because PVC is the specified material for this vent class, option B does not match a shared low termination, and option C concerns internal drainage rather than a snow-correlated pattern.

questions.question: A proposed tank location puts the container and its relief discharge close beside a basement window well and a ground-level ignition source. Why should the designer move it?

answers.text: Relief discharge and leaked vapor are heavier than air and can collect at low openings and ignition sources
The window well would shade the tank in summer, and a cooler tank cannot reach the pressure needed to open a second-stage regulator on warm afternoons
Basement windows are required to stay available as fresh-air intakes for the tank itself, because the container draws combustion air through the building when it vaporizes
The only concern is delivery access for the hose, because vapor released at grade disperses upward immediately and cannot linger near a low opening or ignition source

questions.explanation: Propane vapor sinks, so a release near a low building opening can enter and collect, and a nearby ignition source can ignite vapor that reaches it. The hazard is the behavior of released vapor at grade, not tank shading or delivery convenience, and the tank itself uses no combustion air.

questions.question: A system shows suction 96 psig, superheat 5°F, subcooling 11°F, head 270 psig, and a temperature split of 24°F. The filter is new, blower speed and amps are correct, duct static is normal up to the coil, but pressure drop across the indoor coil is double its rated value and the coil face is visibly matted between the fins. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A blower motor losing speed under load, which is contradicted by the verified correct blower amps and delivered airflow up to the coil
A fouled evaporator coil
A TXV stuck open, which would also drop superheat but would not double the air-side pressure drop across the coil
An undercharge, which would raise superheat well above the 5°F measured rather than leave the coil overfed relative to its airflow

questions.explanation: Low superheat and low suction with correct blower delivery but double the rated coil pressure drop place the airflow blockage inside the fouled coil itself. The blower is proven by its amps and upstream static, an undercharge raises superheat, and a stuck-open valve cannot create an air-side pressure-drop signature.

questions.question: A crew is joining copper lines in an occupied hospital area where an open-flame permit is difficult to obtain, and the fitting manufacturer lists the product for the refrigerant and pressure involved. What joining method fits this situation?

answers.text: Soft solder with a small handheld torch, because it needs only a small, brief flame that can be shielded from nearby occupants
Solvent cement, as used on plastic pipe
Press fittings installed with the manufacturer's tool and verified jaws, following its listing and instructions
Threaded black iron with pipe dope

questions.explanation: Listed press fittings avoid open flame while providing a rated mechanical joint when installed with the correct tool and procedure, option C. Soft solder (A) still needs a flame and is not suitable here, solvent cement (B) is for plastics and has no place on copper refrigerant lines, and threaded black iron with dope (D) is a steel-piping practice, not a copper refrigerant-line joint.

questions.question: During commissioning of a new split air conditioner, the installer wants to adjust the refrigerant charge right after first starting the compressor. What must be verified first, and why?

answers.text: Indoor airflow at the design volume and a clean, fully wetted coil must be verified first, because superheat and subcooling readings are meaningless if airflow is wrong
The thermostat must be set to its lowest temperature first, because that alone guarantees correct airflow
The outdoor fan must be blocked first, because that stabilizes head pressure for charging
The condensate drain must be primed first, because a dry trap changes superheat

questions.explanation: Charge is judged by superheat or subcooling, and both shift when airflow is low or uneven, so airflow, filter, blower setting, and coil condition come before any charge adjustment. Option B changes the call for cooling but proves nothing about airflow, option C artificially raises head pressure and corrupts the readings, and option D affects drainage, not the refrigerant measurements.

questions.question: A newly tested gas line is ready to be placed in service. The crew plans to purge the air from the line by opening a union inside the mechanical room and letting the gas-air mixture blow into the room until gas is smelled. Why is this purge plan prohibited?

answers.text: Purging must discharge to the outdoors, with ignition sources controlled and the discharge point kept away from air intakes, never into a confined indoor space
Purging is prohibited altogether, so new piping must be placed in service with its air still inside and let the appliances clear it in use
The plan is prohibited only because the crew used smell as the endpoint; purging into the room is acceptable with a combustible gas indicator
The plan is prohibited only on lines over 2 inches, because small lines may be purged indoors where the volume of gas released is minor

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: purging removes air and gas mixtures that pass through the flammable range, so the discharge must be vented outdoors at a controlled point, away from ignition sources and building intakes, not released into a room where it can accumulate and ignite. Option B denies a step that is required before placing piping in service, option C accepts the indoor discharge and changes only the endpoint detection, and option D invents a small-line indoor exception that the purging rules do not contain.

questions.question: A company wants its office manager, who holds no ACR credential, to perform routine maintenance work on customers' systems. Who may a company use to perform maintenance work?

answers.text: Only licensed contractors, registered technicians, certified technicians, or students who meet the student-exemption conditions may perform maintenance work

Any employee who has worked for the company for at least one year, provided a licensed contractor reviews the completed maintenance work each week and signs off on the maintenance records for that week
Any employee the assigned licensee has trained in-house, provided the training is documented in the employee's personnel file at the main office
Any employee, provided the customer is told before the visit that the worker performing the maintenance holds no credential under the licensing law

questions.explanation: Key A is correct: a company may use only licensed contractors, registered technicians, certified technicians, or qualifying students to perform maintenance work. B is wrong because length of employment and weekly review do not substitute for a credential. C is wrong because in-house training and documentation do not substitute for registration or licensure. D is wrong because customer disclosure does not authorize an uncredentialed person to perform maintenance work.

questions.question: A furnace is found locked out on an open rollout switch. There is scorch discoloration above one burner opening, flames were reported 'rolling out' before shutdown, manifold pressure is correct, vent draft is strong, and the heat exchanger passages on that cell are heavily soot-restricted on borescope inspection. What is the underlying cause?

answers.text: Soot-blocked heat exchanger passages
A disconnected vent pipe spilling flue gas at the furnace, which is contradicted by the strong measured draft and intact vent connections
A failed rollout switch that opened spuriously at normal temperatures, which cannot explain the scorch marks and witnessed rollout flames
Excessive manifold pressure blowing flames out of the cell, which is excluded by the verified correct 3.5 in. wc manifold reading

questions.explanation: Flames rolling out of a cell whose passages are soot-choked is a flow problem inside the exchanger: combustion products cannot leave, so they exit the front. Manifold pressure is correct, the switch has physical scorch evidence that it tripped honestly, and draft is strong with the vent intact.

questions.question: A completed system delivers only 950 CFM against a 1,200 CFM design. Static readings show the duct system itself is within its budget, but total external static is well above the blower's rating point because the installed wet coil and filter drops are much higher than the values used in design. What went wrong at the design stage?

answers.text: The ducts shrank after installation, which raised the total static
The blower lost capacity because the thermostat was set to cooling
Nothing went wrong; blowers deliver design CFM at any external static

The static budget was built on optimistic component values instead of the actual selected coil's wet-coil drop and the real filter drop at design airflow, so the blower was asked to work beyond the point where it can deliver design CFM

questions.explanation: A blower delivers its rated airflow only up to its rated external static; if real component drops push the total past that point, airflow falls — and the budget is only as honest as the component data in it. Option A is wrong because installed sheet metal does not shrink; the discrepancy was in the design inputs, not the duct dimensions; option B is wrong because thermostat mode does not change a blower's pressure capability; option C is wrong because blower tables show airflow falling as static rises beyond the rating point — that relationship is the whole basis of the budget.

questions.question: Unsteady cooling. Superheat hunts between 8 and 28 degrees F over a single steady call, subcooling sits at 14 degrees F, and suction pressure swings with the superheat. In the air handler, the expansion valve sensing bulb is found hanging loose beside the suction line, its strap broken and insulation tape fallen away. Warming the bulb by hand drives superheat down promptly. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A moisture-contaminated system freezing at the valve orifice intermittently, which would block flow in longer episodes and would not respond immediately to hand-warming a sensing bulb hanging in the airstream
A detached expansion valve sensing bulb sensing air temperature instead of suction-line temperature
An undercharge making the valve hunt for refrigerant, which would hold subcooling low rather than at the healthy 14 degrees measured during the hunting
A compressor whose valves leak on a repeating cycle, which would produce a steady capacity loss and pressure pattern rather than superheat that answers directly to bulb temperature

questions.explanation: The loose bulb senses warm cabinet air instead of the suction line, so the valve opens and closes against the wrong signal and superheat hunts widely; hand-warming it changes superheat on cue, confirming the diagnosis. Moisture icing blocks flow in longer episodes and ignores the bulb, an undercharge cannot hold 14 degrees of subcooling, and leaking compressor valves cause a steady loss, not bulb-responsive hunting.

florida-hvac.quiz_title: Florida HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: On a pressure-enthalpy diagram for a vapor-compression cycle, what do the two axes represent?

answers.text: Temperature on the vertical axis and entropy on the horizontal axis, so every heat transfer process in the cycle is read as a change in entropy alone
Pressure on the horizontal axis and volume on the vertical axis, with enthalpy calculated afterward from a separate table for each plotted state point
Suction pressure on one axis and discharge pressure on the other, so compressor ratio can be read directly without knowing any heat content values at all
Pressure vertically and enthalpy horizontally

questions.explanation: A pressure-enthalpy chart plots pressure on the vertical axis against enthalpy on the horizontal axis, letting cycle work and refrigeration effect be read as enthalpy differences. Temperature-entropy and pressure-volume diagrams are different charts, and the two pressures alone do not define the cycle states.

questions.question: In conventional thermostat wiring, which terminal letters correspond to the heating call and the cooling compressor call?

answers.text: G for heat and W for cooling
R for heat and C for cooling
W for heat and Y for cooling
Y for heat and G for cooling

questions.explanation: W energizes heating and Y energizes the cooling contactor in conventional wiring. G controls the indoor fan, not heat. R supplies power and C is common, neither of which is a heat or cooling call, and swapping Y with G misassigns both functions.

questions.question: Wood-fiber duct board and other combustible materials are proposed inside a commercial supply plenum. What governs acceptance?

answers.text: Any material is acceptable in a plenum once it is painted with ordinary latex paint, because paint seals the surface against flame spread
Combustible plenum materials are allowed whenever the building is only one story and the exits are within a short travel distance
Plenum rules apply only to return plenums in hospitals, so supply plenums in offices may use any low-cost combustible lining
Materials in a plenum must meet strict flame-spread and smoke-developed limits; unlisted combustibles are not permitted.

questions.explanation: Plenum materials are limited to very low flame-spread and smoke-developed ratings because a plenum can distribute fire and smoke building-wide. Paint does not confer a listing, building height does not waive the limit, and the rule covers plenums generally, not one occupancy or one airstream.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the short on-delay or interstage timer commonly found between stages on a multi-stage rooftop unit?

answers.text: To keep the blower running for several minutes after cooling stops so the evaporator coil can freeze solid and store cold for the next cycle during a full-load test on a warm afternoon with the space calling continuously
To prevent both stages from starting at the same instant and to give the first stage time to handle the load before the next stage is allowed in

To hold the economizer dampers closed during the first hour after startup regardless of outdoor conditions or ventilation requirements below when measured at the unit with the blower running and all access panels secured in place
To lock out gas heat whenever cooling has run that day, so heating and cooling can never be available within the same twenty-four hours

questions.explanation: Interstage timing staggers stage starts, limiting inrush and letting the running stage prove whether it can carry the load. It does not aim to freeze the coil, does not impose an hour-long economizer lockout, and does not create a day-long heat lockout after cooling.

questions.question: In an oil burner primary control system, what does the cad cell do?

answers.text: It pumps oil from the tank to the nozzle through the suction line, using the gear set in the fuel unit to raise the oil to atomizing pressure
It generates the spark for ignition
It senses light from the flame, and its resistance drops when flame is present, telling the primary control combustion is established
It opens the oil solenoid valve on a call for heat

questions.explanation: The cad cell is a light-sensitive resistor: bright flame lowers its resistance and proves flame to the primary control. Option A describes the fuel unit (oil pump). Option B describes the ignition transformer or igniter. Option D describes the solenoid valve, which the control may energize but which does not sense flame.

questions.question: A manifold gauge set is being selected for regular R-454B work. Beyond pressure rating, what compatibility point should be checked?

answers.text: Nothing at all, because gauge sets carry no refrigerant-specific components and any set from any era is automatically suitable for every refrigerant
That the hoses are the shortest available, because hose length alone determines whether a manifold set may be used with a flammable refrigerant
Hoses and seals suited to the refrigerant and oil in use, alongside a pressure rating adequate for the system's pressures
That the set includes a sight glass filled with mineral oil, because mineral oil in the hoses is required to protect POE systems from contamination

questions.explanation: Elastomers, hoses, and seals should be compatible with the refrigerant and oil in service, alongside an adequate pressure rating. Gauge components are not universal across all refrigerants and eras, hose length is a convenience rather than a compatibility rating, and introducing mineral oil would contaminate a POE system rather than protect it.

questions.question: A tester needs leakage to outside only, not total leakage, on a house where many ducts run inside the conditioned space. Which test setup isolates leakage to outside?

answers.text: Equalize house and duct pressure
Pressurize the ducts alone with the house left open to outdoors, then subtract the supply-register airflow from the return-register airflow measured with a flow hood
Run the air handler on high speed and compare its blower-table airflow with the sum of all supply registers, treating any shortfall as leakage to outside specifically
Seal every register, pressurize the ducts to 50 Pa instead of 25 Pa, and report that higher-pressure reading because doubling test pressure cancels leaks to the inside

questions.explanation: With a blower door holding the house at the same pressure as the duct tester, no air flows through leaks to the inside, so the duct tester measures only leaks to outside. Ducts alone measure total leakage, a flow-hood shortfall cannot separate inside from outside leaks, and raising test pressure changes the reading's magnitude without cancelling inside leakage.

questions.question: A clinic asks why its ultrasonic humidifier leaves white dust and why steam is often preferred in healthcare settings. What is the correct explanation?

answers.text: White dust is harmless metal flake from the ductwork, and humidifier type has no relationship to what is carried into the airstream
Steam units aerosolize more minerals than ultrasonic units, because boiling concentrates minerals and then ejects them as a fine white powder
The dust comes from the air filter shedding fibers, which happens only when an ultrasonic humidifier is installed in the same building
Ultrasonic units aerosolize the minerals and microbes in their water, while steam humidification boils water and does not carry those contents into the air the same way.

questions.explanation: Mist-type humidifiers put their water's dissolved minerals and any microbes into the air as droplets that dry to dust; boiling separates water vapor from those contents. The dust is humidifier-borne, not duct metal or filter fiber, and steam carries fewer, not more, mineral particles.

questions.question: A variable-capacity outdoor unit is installed but controlled by the homeowner's basic single-stage legacy thermostat. What is lost?

answers.text: Modulating and staging control, tailored airflow, and much of the diagnostic and dehumidification functionality
Nothing is lost, because the outdoor unit's internal board reconstructs full communicating control from a simple on-off call
The system cannot run at all, since variable-capacity equipment will not start without its proprietary communicating control
The warranty is automatically void the moment any non-communicating thermostat is connected to the equipment for any period

questions.explanation: A legacy thermostat reduces a modulating system to crude staged or single-stage operation and hides its advanced features. The equipment cannot recreate data it never receives, many systems can run in a legacy mode rather than not at all, and control choice alone does not automatically void coverage.

questions.question: A typical contractor workmanship warranty differs from a manufacturer's equipment warranty in which way?

answers.text: The workmanship warranty covers the contractor's installation work; the manufacturer's covers its equipment defects
The workmanship warranty covers the factory's equipment defects, while the manufacturer covers the contractor's labor errors
Both warranties are identical in coverage, and the distinction exists only for marketing purposes in the proposal
The manufacturer's warranty covers the contractor's installation workmanship for as long as the building remains standing

questions.explanation: A is correct because the contractor warrants its own installation work while the manufacturer warrants defects in its equipment. B is incorrect because it reverses the two parties' responsibilities. C is incorrect because the coverage, responsible party, and claim route genuinely differ. D is incorrect because a manufacturer does not warrant the installing contractor's workmanship.

questions.question: In a pumpdown system, when the thermostat is satisfied, the liquid-line solenoid closes and the compressor keeps running briefly until a low-pressure control stops it. The purpose of this sequence is to:

answers.text: Charge the system automatically from a cylinder
Pump most refrigerant into the condenser and receiver, leaving the evaporator and suction line at low pressure so liquid cannot migrate to the compressor during the off cycle

Defrost the evaporator coil with hot gas diverted from the compressor discharge through a separate hot-gas bypass line, solenoid, and check-valve arrangement while the fans are stopped and the box temperature is rising well above its normal setpoint
Raise head pressure to seat the compressor valves

questions.explanation: Pumpdown stores the charge on the high side and leaves little refrigerant in the low side to migrate or flood back at restart. Option A describes a charging procedure, option C describes hot-gas defrost which uses a different valve arrangement, and option D is wrong because the compressor stops on low pressure, not on raised head pressure.

questions.question: An electric furnace delivers very hot air for a few minutes, trips its limit, then delivers lukewarm air. Only the first strip seems to cycle. What staging fault fits best?

answers.text: All strips are energized together with no staging delay
The thermostat anticipator is set for gas heat, causing the strips to short-cycle in a pattern unrelated to the limit trips seen
The blower is running at cooling speed, which cools the strips so fast that the limit opens from rapid temperature change
The sequencer for the later stages is holding every strip on continuously, so the limit never has a reason to open at all

questions.explanation: If all strips come on at once instead of staging, discharge temperature overshoots, the limit trips, and heat output collapses until reset, matching the hot-then-lukewarm pattern. Option B concerns cycle timing, not a single overshoot and trip, option C would lower rather than spike air temperature, and option D contradicts the observed cycling off.

questions.question: A system shows suction 96 psig, superheat 5°F, subcooling 11°F, head 270 psig, and a temperature split of 24°F. The filter is new, blower speed and amps are correct, duct static is normal up to the coil, but pressure drop across the indoor coil is double its rated value and the coil face is visibly matted between the fins. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A blower motor losing speed under load, which is contradicted by the verified correct blower amps and delivered airflow up to the coil
A fouled evaporator coil
A TXV stuck open, which would also drop superheat but would not double the air-side pressure drop across the coil
An undercharge, which would raise superheat well above the 5°F measured rather than leave the coil overfed relative to its airflow

questions.explanation: Low superheat and low suction with correct blower delivery but double the rated coil pressure drop place the airflow blockage inside the fouled coil itself. The blower is proven by its amps and upstream static, an undercharge raises superheat, and a stuck-open valve cannot create an air-side pressure-drop signature.

questions.question: A replacement system was connected to an existing suction line that is one size too small for its capacity and run length. Capacity is down, suction pressure drop is excessive, and compressor superheat runs high. What is the underlying mechanism?

answers.text: The small line adds refrigerant charge automatically
Excessive friction pressure drop in the undersized suction line reduces mass flow and capacity at the compressor
The liquid line is far too large for the system and is flashing all of the refrigerant to vapor before it can reach the metering device
The metering device is responding to suction-line color

questions.explanation: Undersized suction piping creates friction loss, so pressure and density at the compressor fall, mass flow drops, and capacity suffers with high compressor superheat, option B. Line size does not add charge (A), the symptoms center on the suction side rather than liquid-line flashing (C), and metering devices respond to pressures, temperatures, and flow - not pipe color (D).

questions.question: On the first cold night of the year, a system without head-pressure control shows very low discharge pressure, a starved expansion valve, and poor case temperatures, although the summer charge was verified. The correct service direction is:

answers.text: Remove refrigerant to match the low pressure
Replace every expansion valve with a capillary tube

Seal the condenser fan motor so it runs slower in summer, reducing outdoor airflow across the coil during the hottest afternoons when head pressure and compressor amp draw are already at their seasonal peak
Fit or restore low-ambient head-pressure control so a minimum condensing pressure is maintained for proper valve feed

questions.explanation: The fault is condensing pressure collapsing in low ambient, so maintaining a minimum head pressure restores pressure difference and feed across the valve. Removing charge in option A makes feed worse, option B abandons superheat control without fixing pressure, and option C addresses summer fan operation, not winter head pressure.

questions.question: A hospital adds pneumatic controls to its air handlers, and certified Class A contractor Devon is hired to install the pneumatic control piping for the controls. Is that piping within Devon's scope?

answers.text: No, because pneumatic control piping belongs to the plumbing category and must be subcontracted on a hospital project of this kind.
Yes, but only for the portion of the piping located outside the building, because interior control piping is outside Class A scope.
Yes. Pneumatic control piping is listed within Class A scope, together with piping and insulation of pipes, vessels, and ducts.
No, because Class A piping scope is limited to condensate and refrigerant piping connected directly to the equipment being serviced.

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Class A definition lists piping, insulation of pipes, vessels and ducts, pressure and process piping, and pneumatic control piping. A is wrong because the piping is listed in the Class A definition rather than assigned to the plumbing category. B is wrong because the listing contains no inside-versus-outside-the-building split. D is wrong because Class A piping scope extends well beyond condensate and refrigerant piping, as the listed categories show.

questions.question: An approved provider has a contractor teach the same four-hour course three separate times during one renewal cycle, and the contractor claims twelve hours of instructor credit. What credit is actually available?

answers.text: Twelve hours, because instructors receive hour-for-hour credit every time they present the course during the cycle.
Eight hours, because instructors receive credit for the first two presentations of a course in each renewal cycle.
No hours, because teaching a course can never substitute for attending one as a student in a renewal cycle.
Four hours, because instructors receive hour-for-hour credit for the first presentation of the course in the cycle.

questions.explanation: D is correct: instructors, teachers, lecturers, panelists, and discussion leaders receive hour-for-hour credit for the first presentation of a course in each renewal cycle, so one four-hour presentation earns four hours and the repeats earn none. A is wrong because repeat presentations in the same cycle do not earn additional credit. B is wrong because the rule credits the first presentation only, not the first two. C is wrong because the first presentation does earn credit.

questions.question: A legacy mercury thermostat short-cycles a gas furnace: burners run about seven minutes, shut off with the room still roughly 2 degrees below setpoint, and restart soon after. The gas valve circuit measures 0.78 A. The thermostat's heat anticipator dial is set at 0.25 A. Furnace temperature rise and limit operation test normal. What is the correct adjustment?

answers.text: Set the anticipator near 0.1 A to add more anticipator heat so the burners run longer and finally bring the room fully up to setpoint before shutting off
Replace the thermostat because anticipator settings do not affect cycle length on gas equipment, and the short cycles must come from the furnace limit circuit instead
Set the anticipator to about 0.8 A to match the measured circuit current
Remove the anticipator from the circuit so the thermostat responds only to room air, accepting the wide temperature swings that follow on this type of control

questions.explanation: The anticipator is set at 0.25 A while the circuit actually draws 0.78 A, so the anticipator heater produces too much heat, satisfies the thermostat early, and short-cycles the furnace short of setpoint; matching the dial to the measured 0.8 A corrects it. Setting it lower adds still more anticipator heat and worsens the early shutoff, the limit circuit tests normal so the thermostat setting is the fault, and removing the anticipator trades short cycles for overshoot swings.

questions.question: Humidity complaint. A 4-ton air conditioner serves a house whose calculated cooling load is about 2.6 tons. It reaches the temperature setpoint in roughly eight-minute runs, cycles off for long stretches, and holds the house at setpoint, yet indoor relative humidity sits at 63 percent and the occupants feel clammy. Refrigerant readings, airflow per ton, and drain operation all test normal. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A low refrigerant charge reducing latent capacity first, which would also show abnormal superheat and subcooling and long, weak cooling runs rather than eight-minute satisfied cycles
A condensate drain that holds water in the pan and re-evaporates it, which would need a drainage fault, while drain operation and pan condition test normal on this visit
A thermostat set to run the blower continuously in the on position, which can re-evaporate coil moisture, but here the blower is verified running in auto with normal cycling behavior
Equipment oversized for the load, short-cycling before it can dehumidify

questions.explanation: The 4-ton unit satisfies the 2.6-ton sensible load in eight minutes, so the coil barely stays wet long enough to remove moisture and humidity stays at 63 percent despite normal refrigerant and airflow readings. Low charge would distort the refrigerant readings and lengthen runs, the drain tests normal, and the blower runs in auto, leaving oversizing and its short latent run time as the explanation.

questions.question: A retail sales floor in Miami expects 40 occupants in 3,000 square feet. Using people rate 7.5 cfm per person and area rate 0.12 cfm per square foot, what breathing-zone outdoor airflow is required?

answers.text: 300 cfm, from the people component alone, because retail spaces are ventilated on occupancy count only here
360 cfm, from the area component alone, because retail spaces are ventilated on floor area only in this table
660 cfm, from 40 people at 7.5 cfm (300 cfm) plus 3,000 square feet at 0.12 cfm (360 cfm)
560 cfm, from 40 people at 7.5 cfm (300 cfm) plus 3,000 square feet at 0.06 cfm (260 cfm by rounding)

questions.explanation: Both components apply: 7.5 x 40 = 300 cfm for people and 0.12 x 3,000 = 360 cfm for area, totaling 660 cfm. A and B each omit one required component. D uses the 0.06 office area rate instead of the 0.12 retail rate (and misfigures even that product, which would be 180 cfm, not 260 cfm).

north-carolina-hvac.quiz_title: North Carolina HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A hermetic compressor's motor windings are cooled primarily by:

answers.text: Outdoor air blown over the shell by the condenser fan while the fan cycles on and off with the compressor during normal cooling operation on a mild day
Water circulating through a jacket around the shell
Oil sprayed continuously over the windings
Cool suction vapor returning from the evaporator and passing over the motor before compression

questions.explanation: In a hermetic compressor the returning suction vapor flows over the motor before it is compressed, which is why loss of charge or mass flow can overheat the motor. Option A may cool the shell surface slightly but is not the design cooling path, option B describes water-cooled equipment, and option C is wrong because oil circulation alone does not provide the main motor cooling.

questions.question: A replacement motor has a nameplate FLA of 10 A and a 1.15 service factor. Overload protection is properly based on:

answers.text: The locked-rotor current divided by six, because that arithmetic shortcut is accepted instead of reading the rating printed on the motor nameplate
The nameplate FLA, with any service-factor allowance applied by the protection rules, not on measured amps alone
The branch breaker rating, because the overload device is set to match whatever breaker happens to be installed in the panel feeding the motor
A single clamp-meter reading taken at light load, because the lowest measured current is the safest basis for setting motor overload protection

questions.explanation: The nameplate FLA, with any service-factor allowance applied by the protection rules, not on measured amps alone. Locked-rotor arithmetic, breaker size, and a light-load snapshot are not the basis; nameplate FLA governs overload selection.

questions.question: Refrigerant piping passes through wood framing and runs exposed where it can be struck in a garage. What protection is required?

answers.text: No protection is needed once the system holds pressure, because a passing pressure test also proves the piping can withstand vehicle impact
Soft copper may be notched into the face of a stud without a plate, provided the notch is filled later with construction adhesive
Piping in a garage should be buried in the concrete slab without a sleeve so vehicles cannot reach it under any circumstances
Shield plates at framing penetrations where piping is close to the edge, and guards or placement that protects piping from physical damage.

questions.explanation: Piping near a framing edge must be shielded from nails and screws, and exposed piping subject to impact must be protected. A pressure test says nothing about impact resistance, unshielded notching invites fastener damage, and unsleeved burial is not the required protection method.

questions.question: Which set of acts is grouped together as criminal unlicensed-practice conduct for heating contracting?

answers.text: Charging a customer more than the original estimate, finishing a job one week late, and declining to offer an extended warranty.
Failing to display a license number in an advertisement, renewing ten days late in January, and moving a shop without updating a phone number.
Bidding slightly below a competitor, hiring a licensed subcontractor for permitted help, and requesting an inspection after start-up.
Contracting without a license, falsely impersonating another practitioner, and using an expired or revoked license to perform work.

questions.explanation: D is correct: engaging or offering to engage without the required license, practicing beyond a limited license, giving false evidence to obtain a license, falsely impersonating another practitioner, using an expired or revoked license, or violating the licensing law is a Class 2 misdemeanor. A is wrong because pricing and scheduling disputes are not in that criminal list. B is wrong because those paperwork and timing lapses are rule or fee matters, not the listed misdemeanor conduct. C is wrong because competitive bidding and lawful subcontracting are not criminal conduct.

questions.question: How does a barometric bypass damper decide when to open?

answers.text: It opens in response to supply pressure acting against an adjustable weight or counterbalance
It opens when the zone panel counts more satisfied thermostats than calling thermostats, using a relay output that drives the bypass blade to a preset angle
It opens on a fixed time schedule after the blower starts, regardless of the pressure actually present in the supply plenum during that equipment cycle
It opens when discharge air temperature falls below its setpoint, because temperature, not pressure, is the variable a barometric damper is built to sense and relieve

questions.explanation: A barometric bypass is a mechanical pressure device; rising supply pressure overcomes its adjustable weight or counterbalance and pushes the blade open. It needs no panel relay or timer, and the temperature-based description confuses it with discharge-air limit control.

questions.question: How do mainstream equipment standards treat installing R-454B into an existing air conditioner that was designed and listed only for R-410A?

answers.text: Not permitted; the equipment must be designed and listed for the mildly flammable refrigerant it will contain
Permitted as a routine retrofit whenever the pressures are similar, provided the oil is changed and the nameplate is updated by the installing contractor
Permitted only in commercial buildings, because occupancy rules rather than equipment listing determine whether a different refrigerant may be used
Permitted if the charge is reduced by a small percentage, because a reduced charge converts an unlisted refrigerant change into an approved application

questions.explanation: Equipment must be designed and listed for the mildly flammable refrigerant, including its sensors, controls, and electrical components. Similar pressures do not create a retrofit approval, building type does not override equipment listing, and trimming the charge does not make an unlisted conversion acceptable.

questions.question: A large single-stage air conditioner is zoned, and the small bedroom zone overshoots its setpoint and short-cycles the equipment whenever it calls alone. What is the root mismatch?

answers.text: The bedroom thermostat is too sensitive, because a single-stage system delivers capacity in small increments that a properly placed thermostat would never overshoot on a short call
The bedroom zone has too much duct area for its load, so the equipment runs long and slowly rather than satisfying the zone quickly at full capacity output
Full single-stage capacity is delivered into a small zone, satisfying it quickly and cycling the equipment
The zone panel adds capacity when only one zone calls, raising a single-stage unit above its rated output so the small zone receives more than nameplate cooling

questions.explanation: A single-stage unit has only full capacity, and delivering all of it into the smallest zone satisfies that zone very quickly, producing overshoot and short cycles. The thermostat is reporting the rapid temperature change rather than causing it, the zone's duct and load are small rather than large, and a panel cannot raise a single-stage unit above its rated output.

questions.question: A home installs a 600 cfm kitchen range hood in a tight new house with a natural-draft water heater. What concern must be addressed?

answers.text: Makeup air is needed so the hood does not depressurize the house and backdraft combustion appliances
The hood will over-ventilate the bedrooms with fresh air
The water heater will produce too much combustion air on its own
No concern exists because a ducted range hood only moves air around inside the kitchen and never removes any air from the house or changes indoor pressure

questions.explanation: Large exhaust can pull the house negative and reverse flow in natural-draft flues, spilling combustion products, so makeup air is required at larger hood capacities. The risk is depressurization, not over-ventilation of bedrooms. The water heater does not supply makeup air, and a ducted hood exhausts air out of the house rather than merely moving it indoors.

questions.question: What is the minimum defensible basis for equipment size on a changeout where no prior load calculation exists and the home's history is unknown?

answers.text: The size of the neighboring home's system, adjusted by the installer's judgment about which house feels larger inside
A current load calculation performed from measured dimensions, construction, and local design conditions
The old nameplate size, doubled-checked against the square footage divided by a standard regional tons-per-foot factor
The largest system that fits the existing closet and duct connections, so capacity is never the limiting factor later

questions.explanation: Without records, sizing must be built from an actual calculation on the house as it stands. Neighbor comparisons and square-foot factors are rules of thumb, the old nameplate may itself be wrong, and fitting the closet is a physical constraint rather than a load basis.

questions.question: A complete bid for a rooftop unit replacement should include which set of cost elements?

answers.text: Direct labor, materials, equipment, permits, overhead, and profit
Only the purchase price of the rooftop unit and the sales tax charged on that equipment purchase
Direct labor and materials only, because overhead and profit are handled separately after the job is awarded
Materials, advertising expense for the season, and office rent, with field labor treated as an owner draw

questions.explanation: A is correct because a complete bid recovers direct job costs plus permits, overhead, and profit. B is incorrect because it omits labor, overhead, and profit needed to perform the work. C is incorrect because excluding overhead and profit from the bid understates the selling price. D is incorrect because it mixes period marketing costs into job cost while misclassifying field labor.

questions.question: A low-water cutoff on a hot-water boiler is tested and the burner keeps firing as water is drawn down past the probe level. The required response is to:

answers.text: Raise the aquastat setting so the test finishes faster, then return it to its original setting and put the boiler back in service without repairing the cutoff as long as the burner eventually stops at the high limit
Ignore it if the pressure gauge still shows normal pressure
Adjust the fill valve to a higher pressure and retest later
Shut the boiler down and repair or replace the cutoff, because it must interrupt the burner before the boiler can fire dry and be damaged or become unsafe

questions.explanation: The low-water cutoff is a safety control that must stop firing on low water; a failed test means the boiler stays out of service until the control works. Option A does not restore low-water protection. Option B is wrong because normal pressure can exist while water level is unsafe in the boiler. Option C changes fill pressure but leaves a dead safety in place.

questions.question: A system with a plain steel compression tank has rising pressure as it heats, frequent relief-valve weeping, and the tank feels full of water to its top. The diagnosis is:

answers.text: The tank is oversized for the system volume, with an acceptance capacity several times larger than the total expansion of all the water in the boiler, piping, and radiators combined
The tank is waterlogged — it has lost its air cushion — so expanded water has nowhere to go and pressure climbs to the relief setting
The circulator is pumping toward the boiler
The air separator is removing too much air

questions.explanation: A compression tank works only while it holds an air cushion; absorbed air leaves it full of water, so thermal expansion spikes pressure and lifts the relief valve. Option A would lower, not raise, pressure rise. Option C affects air removal efficiency, not the tank's lost cushion. Option D is backwards, because air leaving system water is exactly what this tank has lost.

questions.question: A system short-cycles on its low-pressure control on a warm day. Superheat is high, subcooling is low, and airflow and coil condition check out normal. After leak repair and proper evacuation, the correct way to restore charge in this fixed-orifice system is to:

answers.text: Charge by head pressure alone until the low-pressure switch stops opening, while watching only the high-side gauge and never measuring evaporator superheat at any point
Weigh in the nameplate charge (adjusted for line length as specified), then verify operation with superheat under the stated indoor and outdoor conditions
Add refrigerant until the suction line feels beer-can cold at the compressor
Charge until subcooling reaches the highest value the condenser can produce

questions.explanation: Weighing in the specified charge gives a known-correct starting point, and superheat verification under rated conditions confirms the fixed-orifice system is truly correct. Option A ignores superheat entirely and can badly overcharge a piston system, while option C uses touch in place of measurement and routinely floods compressors. Option D pursues maximum subcooling, which on this metering type simply means severe overcharge.

questions.question: A condensing furnace's condensate drain has a long flat section that sags, and the furnace intermittently locks out with water backing up into the collector box. What correction best addresses the cause?

answers.text: Raise the gas manifold pressure well above the manufacturer's specification so the furnace runs hotter and dries itself out from the inside during every cycle
Plug the secondary drain port so water cannot back up
Re-pitch the drain so it slopes continuously downhill to its termination, support it so it cannot sag, and keep required traps in place
Connect the condensate line directly into a gas vent

questions.explanation: Condensate must flow by gravity through a continuously sloped, supported drain with its required trap, option C; a sagging flat run pools water that eventually backs up and trips the furnace. Manifold pressure (A) has nothing to do with drainage, plugging a drain port (B) worsens backup, and tying condensate into a gas vent (D) mixes drainage with combustion venting and is prohibited practice.

questions.question: A walk-in cooler holds product temperature except after busy delivery periods, when box temperature rises for hours. The coil, fans, and refrigerant readings check normal, but a door sweep is torn and the gasket pulls away at one corner. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.text: Warm, moist outside air infiltrating through the door leaks, adding latent and sensible load and frosting the coil
A failed evaporator pressure regulator that is holding suction pressure too high at all hours, including overnight periods when the doors remain closed and no warm product is loaded
An oversized compressor that short-cycles too often to dehumidify the box
A liquid-line sight glass that has become too clear during operation

questions.explanation: Infiltration through a torn sweep and leaking gasket admits warm, moist air, which loads the box and frosts the coil, especially after frequent door use. A regulator fault in option B would show in suction-pressure readings, an oversized compressor in option C would short-cycle even without delivery periods, and option D describes a normal clear glass, not an air leak.

questions.question: A clothes dryer exhaust duct in a North Carolina home has 25 feet of straight duct and two 90-degree elbows. The code maximum exhaust length is 35 feet, with each 90-degree elbow counted as 5 feet of equivalent length. Does this installation comply, and why?

answers.text: It does not comply, because elbows are not counted at all and the straight length alone already uses the allowance, including where the equipment involved was installed during an earlier phase of the work
It complies with length to spare, because the two elbows together add only 2 feet of equivalent length to the run
It complies exactly at the limit, because 25 feet plus two elbows at 5 feet each gives 35 feet of equivalent length
It does not comply, because each elbow counts as 10 feet and the equivalent length therefore reaches 45 feet total

questions.explanation: C is correct: equivalent length = 25 ft of straight duct + (2 elbows x 5 ft each) = 25 + 10 = 35 ft, which equals, and therefore does not exceed, the 35 ft maximum. A is wrong because elbows do count, at 5 ft each, and the straight run alone is 25 ft, not 35 ft. B is wrong because each 90-degree elbow deducts 5 ft, not 1 ft. D is wrong because the deduction for a 90-degree elbow is 5 ft, not 10 ft.

questions.question: A person holds a Heating Group 1 Technician license but wants to work full-time for a Heating Group 3 contractor while keeping that Group 1 technician status. What does the rule require instead?

answers.text: The technician may work for any group contractor, because technician licenses are not tied to employers.
The Group 1 Technician must be a full-time employee of a Heating Group 1 Contractor to hold that status.
The technician must be a part-time employee of at least two different heating group contractors.
The technician must own part of the Group 3 firm before working there as a Group 1 Technician.

questions.explanation: B is correct: the holder of a Heating Group 1 Technician license shall be a full-time employee of a Heating Group No. 1 Contractor, and the same tie applies group-by-group for Groups 2 and 3. A is wrong because the license is expressly tied to a same-group contractor employer. C is wrong because the rule requires full-time employment with the matching-group contractor. D is wrong because ownership is not the stated requirement.

questions.question: A heat pump blows warm air on a cooling call on an 88-degree day. The compressor and both fans run, the reversing valve solenoid measures 24 V and its coil pulls a screwdriver magnetically, yet tube temperatures at the valve match the heating position: the line to the indoor coil is hot and the house keeps warming. Refrigerant charge was verified by weight earlier in the visit. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A reversing valve spool stuck in the heating position despite an energized solenoid, its internal slide remaining in the heating position and routing hot discharge gas to the indoor coil throughout the cooling call
A dead reversing valve solenoid coil, ruled out because the coil is energized at 24 V and demonstrably magnetizes, pulling on a screwdriver held to it

A thermostat wired to energize the valve in the wrong mode, which would leave the solenoid de-energized on this cooling call for this unit's energize-in-cooling configuration rather than powered and magnetic
A low refrigerant charge making cooling feel like heating, which cannot deliver genuinely hot air to the indoor coil and is ruled out by the weighed-in verified charge

questions.explanation: The electrical side of the valve works (24 V, magnetic coil) but the refrigerant side never shifts: tube temperatures show the valve still routing hot gas to the indoor coil in the heating position, so the spool itself is stuck. The solenoid is proven live and magnetic, the thermostat is delivering the correct energized state for cooling on this configuration, and low charge cannot produce hot supply air.

questions.question: A ventilation design uses the rate formula: CFM = 0.03 x floor area + 7.5 x (bedrooms + 1). For a 1,600 sq ft house with 3 bedrooms, what is the required continuous ventilation rate?

answers.text: 55.5 CFM, because only the floor-area term applies to houses
70.5 CFM, because the bedroom term uses bedrooms minus 1
78 CFM, because 0.03 x 1,600 = 48 and 7.5 x 4 = 30, totaling 78
108 CFM, because the floor-area coefficient is 0.05 for houses over 1,500 sq ft

questions.explanation: Both terms of the given formula count: the area term contributes 48 CFM and the occupant term, using bedrooms + 1 = 4, contributes 30 CFM. Option A is wrong because dropping the occupant term understates the rate — people, not just floor area, generate the contaminants ventilation dilutes; option B is wrong because the formula as given adds 1 to the bedroom count to represent the primary suite's two occupants; option D is wrong because the coefficient in the stated formula is 0.03; substituting 0.05 changes the given method rather than applying it.

questions.question: A technician watches an air-cooled condenser on a hot day. The first passes of the coil are cooling hot discharge gas, the middle passes are changing state at a nearly constant temperature, and the last passes cool the liquid a few degrees further. What are those three processes, in order?

answers.text: Subcooling, desuperheating, then condensing
