Change orders are being documented too carefully, which consumes profit in administrative time on each job

questions.explanation: B is correct because consistently winning while earning little suggests prices are set below the true cost of labor burden, overhead, and direct costs. A is incorrect because an excessive overhead rate would tend to lose bids, not win nearly all of them. C is incorrect because detailed takeoffs improve accuracy rather than erase profit. D is incorrect because careful change documentation protects profit by capturing added work.

questions.question: A technician finishes a cooling-season service on a heat pump and wants to confirm the reversing valve fully shifts to cooling. Energizing the valve produces a distinct whoosh and the suction and discharge line temperatures swap roles correctly, but capacity is still slightly low with normal superheat, normal subcooling, and correct airflow. What is the best next diagnostic step?

answers.text: Replace the reversing valve, because any capacity loss after a shift test is a valve fault, without testing the check valve or the cooling metering device path any further first
Check the outdoor coil and metering circuit serving cooling mode (including the cooling-side check valve and metering device path) for a partial restriction or bypass fault
Add refrigerant until capacity returns, regardless of the normal charge indicators
Disable the defrost board so the valve cannot move during cooling season

questions.explanation: With the valve proven to shift, charge indicators normal, and airflow correct, the remaining suspects are in the cooling-mode refrigerant path itself, such as a check valve that does not seat or open fully. Option A replaces a component the shift test just cleared, and option C overcharges a system whose superheat and subcooling both say the charge is right. Option D disables a needed heat-pump function instead of diagnosing the capacity loss.

questions.question: No-cool call. Line voltage at the disconnect is 238 V. With the contactor pulled in, voltage measured across its closed compressor contacts drops 4.6 V, the compressor sees only about 233 V under load, contact faces are dark and pitted, and the compressor occasionally chatters at startup. The contactor coil measures a steady 24.3 V. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Burned, pitted contactor contacts
A failing contactor coil that is dropping out under load, which would show control voltage collapsing at the coil rather than a steady 24.3 V with a large drop across the closed power contacts
Low utility voltage at the service, which would show the same depressed voltage at the disconnect before the contactor instead of a healthy 238 V arriving at it
A compressor with shorted windings, which would trip the breaker or draw locked-rotor current continuously rather than run with a measurable voltage loss across the switching contacts

questions.explanation: A healthy closed contact drops well under a volt; 4.6 V lost across pitted faces leaves the compressor undervoltaged and explains the startup chatter and heat-darkened contacts. The coil holds a steady 24.3 V, so the coil is not dropping out, the disconnect delivers a full 238 V, so the utility supply is not low, and shorted windings would trip protection or draw locked-rotor current rather than produce this contact voltage drop.

questions.question: A new furnace is commissioned with correct gas input, but its temperature rise measures above the nameplate range and the high-limit switch trips on long cycles. Airflow settings are at the factory default. What is the most likely fix?

answers.text: Increase airflow by selecting a higher blower speed or correcting duct restriction so rise falls within the listed range
Raise manifold pressure so the furnace fires harder and cycles shorter, turning the gas valve regulator up beyond the listed setting until the short cycles bring the measured rise down
Close several supply registers to build pressure in the duct
Replace the high-limit switch with one rated for a higher temperature

questions.explanation: With input correct, excessive rise means too little air is carrying the heat away, so raising airflow or removing restriction brings rise into range and stops limit trips. Option B adds more heat to an already overheated exchanger, option C reduces airflow further and worsens the rise, and option D defeats a safety control instead of fixing its cause.

connecticut-hvac.quiz_title: Connecticut HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A medium-temperature evaporator must be defrosted periodically because frost on the coil:

answers.text: Raises the refrigerant boiling temperature
Turns refrigerant into a noncondensable gas that collects in the condenser, raises head pressure, and must be purged from the top of the system with a recovery machine
Acts as insulation and blocks airflow, reducing capacity until the coil can no longer absorb heat effectively
Increases subcooling in the condenser

questions.explanation: Frost insulates the tubes and chokes the air passages, so heat transfer and capacity fall even though the coil surface is very cold. Option A is backwards because a frosted coil tends to run at a lower, not higher, boiling temperature, option B is false because frost does not change refrigerant into air, and option D concerns the condenser, not the frosted evaporator.

questions.question: A furnace repeatedly trips its flame rollout switch near the burner compartment. What is the correct response?

answers.text: Investigate the cause, such as a blocked heat exchanger or venting problem, rather than repeatedly resetting or bypassing it
Bypass the switch with a jumper wire and return the furnace to service because rollout switches are nuisance devices that often trip without any real flame problem present
Reset it each visit until the heating season ends
Replace it with a higher-temperature limit so it stops tripping

questions.explanation: Rollout indicates flame escaping where it should not, often from blockage or venting faults, and the cause must be found. Bypassing removes a critical fire safety. Repeated resetting without diagnosis leaves a hazardous condition, and a higher-temperature device defeats the intended protection.

questions.question: A condensing unit is set at grade in a known flood-hazard area, below the required flood elevation. What must be done?

answers.text: Raise the equipment on a platform or support so it sits at or above the required elevation.
Leave it at grade but wrap the electrical compartment in plastic sheeting, which is accepted as flood protection for mechanical equipment
Install it in a shallow pit so floodwater drains away from the unit toward the street during and after a storm event
Rely on the unit's factory weatherproof rating, because outdoor equipment ratings already account for being submerged in floodwater

questions.explanation: Flood provisions require mechanical equipment to be elevated or protected to the design flood level to prevent damage and hazards. Plastic wrap is not approved protection, a pit collects water at the unit, and weatherproofing resists rain, not submersion.

questions.question: A shop hires a new trainee and tells the trainee that shop employment alone makes the trainee an apprentice for licensing purposes. What does the definition actually require?

answers.text: Two years of employment with one contractor, since the definition ties apprentice status to a minimum period of continuous service with a single sponsoring heating firm in the trade
Enrollment in any private trade school, since school enrollment is the registration event the definition points to, and Labor Department records are not part of the apprentice definition
Passing a preliminary skills test given by the examining board, since the board's testing of a trainee's starting ability is what converts an employee into a registered apprentice
Registration with the Labor Department for the purpose of learning a skilled trade, since an apprentice is a person so registered, not merely a person a shop chooses to call a trainee

questions.explanation: D is correct: an apprentice means any person registered with the Labor Department for the purpose of learning a skilled trade, so registration, not the employer's label, is the defining element. A is wrong because no two-year single-employer service period appears in the definition. B is wrong because the registration named is with the Labor Department. C is wrong because no board skills test is part of the apprentice definition.

questions.question: How does a fire damper in a duct penetration of a rated wall normally close, and why does it need an access provision?

answers.text: A smoke detector signals a motor that drives the blade closed, and no access is needed because the motor self-tests, runs a full closure cycle on its own schedule, and reports any fault directly to the building panel without anyone opening the ceiling to reach it
The blade closes when duct pressure rises during a fire, and access is only for painting the frame
A thermostat in the airstream closes the blade electrically whenever return air gets warm
A fusible link melts at its rated temperature and releases the blade to close by spring or gravity, and access is needed so the damper can be inspected, tested, and reset or replaced after operation

questions.explanation: A fire damper is a passive heat-actuated device: the fusible link is the sensor, and periodic inspection rules assume someone can physically reach it. Option A is wrong because detector-actuated motorized closure describes a smoke or combination damper, not a standard fusible-link fire damper; option B is wrong because duct pressure does not trip a fire damper, and access exists for inspection and testing, not painting; option C is wrong because ordinary warm return air must not close a fire damper — its link is rated well above normal airstream temperatures.

questions.question: A manifold gauge set is being selected for regular R-454B work. Beyond pressure rating, what compatibility point should be checked?

answers.text: Nothing at all, because gauge sets carry no refrigerant-specific components and any set from any era is automatically suitable for every refrigerant
That the hoses are the shortest available, because hose length alone determines whether a manifold set may be used with a flammable refrigerant
Hoses and seals suited to the refrigerant and oil in use, alongside a pressure rating adequate for the system's pressures
That the set includes a sight glass filled with mineral oil, because mineral oil in the hoses is required to protect POE systems from contamination

questions.explanation: Elastomers, hoses, and seals should be compatible with the refrigerant and oil in service, alongside an adequate pressure rating. Gauge components are not universal across all refrigerants and eras, hose length is a convenience rather than a compatibility rating, and introducing mineral oil would contaminate a POE system rather than protect it.

questions.question: A duct pressurization test at 25 Pa measures 180 CFM25 of total leakage on a system that moves 1,200 CFM at the air handler. How should this result be interpreted?

answers.text: Leakage is negligible because any reading taken at only 25 Pa is too low a test pressure to reveal real operating losses in a residential duct system
Leakage is about 1.5% of system airflow, since the test result in CFM is divided by ten times the air-handler flow before it is expressed as a percentage
The system passes easily because leakage up to one-quarter of delivered airflow is normally expected even in a well-sealed, newly installed duct system
Leakage is high at 15% of airflow

questions.explanation: 180 divided by 1,200 is 0.15, so leakage is 15% of system airflow, a high value that wastes delivered capacity. The 25 Pa test pressure is the standard reference pressure, not a pressure too low to be meaningful, the 1.5% figure misplaces the decimal in the same calculation, and one-quarter leakage would be a major defect, not a normal expectation for sealed ducts.

questions.question: A portable air cleaner's clean-air delivery rate is far below the room's volume needs, and the owner expects hospital-grade air. What limit must be explained?

answers.text: Portable cleaners treat the whole house equally from any location, because cleaned air displaces dirty air in every room within a few minutes
Doubling the fan speed on an undersized unit multiplies its clean-air delivery by ten, closing any sizing gap the room presents
A portable unit can only clean the air that passes through it, so an undersized unit cannot achieve the room air changes needed for a large reduction in airborne particles.
Particle removal does not depend on airflow through the unit at all, since the cleaner's field effect treats air in rooms behind closed doors

questions.explanation: Air cleaning is a rate problem: room volume times desired air changes sets the delivery rate the device must meet. One small unit does not serve a whole house uniformly, fan speed cannot multiply capacity tenfold, and air behind closed doors never reaches the device.

questions.question: A heat pump is being set in a snowy climate where defrost water must drain away from the base. Which pad and placement choice is correct?

answers.text: Set the unit flat on the ground so defrost water soaks into the soil under it, letting each defrost cycle drain straight into the earth beneath the base with no elevated pad, stand, or drainage path provided
Set the unit inside a solid enclosure so snow cannot reach the coil
Bury the base rails in mulch to insulate the bottom of the unit
Raise the unit on a pad or stand above the expected snow line with a clear path for defrost water to drain away and not refreeze under the coil

questions.explanation: Elevation keeps the coil and base above snow, and open drainage lets defrost meltwater escape instead of building ice that chokes the coil and fan. Option A invites ice buildup at ground level, option B starves airflow and traps discharge air, and option C holds moisture against the base and can block drainage openings.

questions.question: In general terms, a performance bond on a project guarantees which of the following?

answers.text: That the equipment will operate at its advertised efficiency rating in the customer's building for its full service life
That the contractor will complete the contract, backed by a surety if it defaults
That employees will receive benefits if they are injured while performing work covered under the bonded contract
That the owner will never owe progress payments until every punch-list item on the project has been fully corrected

questions.explanation: B is correct because a performance bond backs the contractor's completion of the contract, with the surety stepping in on default. A is incorrect because equipment efficiency over its life is a product performance matter, not a bond guarantee. C is incorrect because employee injury benefits are provided by workers' compensation insurance. D is incorrect because progress payment timing is a contract term, not something a performance bond eliminates.

questions.question: A condensing furnace locks out on its pressure switch shortly after a summer shutdown. The condensate trap is found completely dry. Why can a dry trap prevent startup?

answers.text: A dry trap raises manifold gas pressure above the high-fire setting because the drain line connects the condensate trap directly to the outlet side of the gas valve regulator
A dry trap opens the rollout circuit directly
Without a water seal, the inducer can draw air through the drain line instead of developing the negative pressure needed to close the pressure switch
A dry trap causes the flame sensor to read zero microamps

questions.explanation: The trap's water seal blocks air from being pulled through the drain, so the inducer can pull the heat exchanger and vent under vacuum and prove the pressure switch; priming the trap restores it. Option A is wrong because the trap has no effect on gas pressure. Option B is wrong because the trap is not wired in the rollout circuit. Option D is wrong because flame sensing occurs only after ignition, which never occurs here.

questions.question: A furnace shows a temperature rise well below the nameplate minimum while delivering weak, lukewarm air at the registers. Which pairing is a plausible cause?

answers.text: A restricted return grille combined with a dirty filter choking airflow down to a fraction of what the blower requires for cooling
A blocked vent termination that raises combustion temperatures and forces the high limit to cycle the burners off repeatedly
Underfiring or excess airflow
A cracked heat exchanger leaking supply air outdoors through the vent, which cools the remaining air delivered to the house only

questions.explanation: Low rise results when heat input is too low for the airflow, or airflow is too high for the input, so underfiring and excess airflow both fit. Option A describes low airflow, which raises rise, option B describes a venting fault that causes limit cycling, and option D misdescribes how an exchanger breach presents.

questions.question: A system short-cycles on its low-pressure control on a warm day. Superheat is high, subcooling is low, and airflow and coil condition check out normal. After leak repair and proper evacuation, the correct way to restore charge in this fixed-orifice system is to:

answers.text: Charge by head pressure alone until the low-pressure switch stops opening, while watching only the high-side gauge and never measuring evaporator superheat at any point
Weigh in the nameplate charge (adjusted for line length as specified), then verify operation with superheat under the stated indoor and outdoor conditions
Add refrigerant until the suction line feels beer-can cold at the compressor
Charge until subcooling reaches the highest value the condenser can produce

questions.explanation: Weighing in the specified charge gives a known-correct starting point, and superheat verification under rated conditions confirms the fixed-orifice system is truly correct. Option A ignores superheat entirely and can badly overcharge a piston system, while option C uses touch in place of measurement and routinely floods compressors. Option D pursues maximum subcooling, which on this metering type simply means severe overcharge.

questions.question: Existing appliances work alone, but when the furnace and water heater fire together, manifold pressure at the furnace collapses. This pattern points to:

answers.text: A defective furnace gas valve, because a valve fault would be expected to appear only when a second appliance happens to fire at the same time
Undersized common piping or a supply restriction under combined load
An oversized vent common to both appliances, because vent interaction is the usual cause of gas pressure loss measured at the burner manifold
A clocking error at the meter, because measurement mistakes during setup change the actual pressure available to appliances in simultaneous operation

questions.explanation: Undersized common piping or a supply restriction under combined load. A single-appliance valve fault does not wait for a second load, vent size does not set gas pressure, and a measurement error does not change delivered pressure.

questions.question: A refrigerated display case keeps product at correct temperature and all refrigerant readings are normal, but water and sheet ice keep forming under the case and spilling onto the floor. The drain pan is full, the drain outlet is blocked with slime and debris, and the coil itself is clean with normal frost pattern between scheduled defrosts. What is the correct repair?

answers.text: Replace the evaporator fan motors, which are moving air normally across a clean coil and cannot explain a drain pan overflowing with meltwater
Clear the blocked case drain
Add refrigerant to improve case temperature, when product temperature and every refrigerant reading are already normal and the fault is water handling, not cooling
Replace the TXV for overfeeding the coil, which would show as collapsed superheat and abnormal pressures rather than a full drain pan with normal readings

questions.explanation: Normal temperatures and refrigerant readings with a full drain pan and a blocked outlet localize the fault to meltwater disposal: defrost water cannot leave, so it refreezes and spills. A TXV fault would distort superheat, added charge cannot fix drainage when cooling is already normal, and healthy fans do not fill a drain pan.

questions.question: A load calculation for a West Hartford house gives a total cooling design load of 33,800 Btu/h. Two candidate condensing units are on the table: a nominal 3-ton unit whose capacity at the design conditions is 34,500 Btu/h, and a nominal 4-ton unit rated 42,000 Btu/h at those conditions. Which selection follows sound sizing practice?

answers.text: The 4-ton unit, because selecting a full nominal size above the calculated load is the standard safety practice for hot spells that exceed the design temperature used in the calculation
The 3-ton unit: its capacity at design conditions (34,500 Btu/h) meets the 33,800 Btu/h load with only a small margin, while the 4-ton unit overshoots the load by about 24 percent
Neither unit until the load is recalculated with a 25 percent safety factor added, because equipment may only be selected against a load that has been padded by that amount beforehand
The 4-ton unit if the ducts are also upsized, because oversized equipment performs correctly at part load so long as the duct system is made larger to match its airflow

questions.explanation: B is correct: equipment is selected on its capacity at the actual design conditions against the calculated load; 34,500 Btu/h covers the 33,800 Btu/h load with a margin under 3 percent, while 42,000 Btu/h oversizes the job by roughly 24 percent, inviting short cycling and poor dehumidification. A is wrong because a full extra nominal ton is not a safety practice; design conditions already represent the sizing weather. C is wrong because the load calculation is not padded with a blanket safety factor before selection. D is wrong because larger ducts do not cure the part-load cycling and latent-load problems of grossly oversized equipment.

questions.question: A carbon dioxide sensor using automatic background calibration is installed in a space occupied around the clock that never returns to outdoor background levels. What error can develop?

answers.text: The sensor can drift low over time because its calibration logic assumes the lowest reading equals fresh-air concentration
The sensor will read exactly double the true concentration every night
The calibration feature makes the sensor immune to all drift in any application
Continuous occupancy actually improves the automatic calibration, because having more people in the space produces more carbon dioxide and gives the sensor a stronger signal

questions.explanation: Automatic background calibration needs periodic exposure to true background air; without it, the assumed baseline is too high and readings skew low. The error is a gradual low drift, not a nightly doubling. The feature is not drift-proof, and constant occupancy removes the clean reference the logic depends on.

questions.question: Which conversion approach is correct for a furnace listed as convertible to propane?

answers.text: Drill the existing natural gas orifices to a size chosen from a generic chart, then set manifold pressure by flame appearance alone without a manometer reading
Leave the burner orifices unchanged and raise manifold pressure until the flame looks blue, because pressure adjustment alone converts any listed furnace safely to propane
Use the manufacturer kit for that model, including its orifices and regulator conversion parts
Swap only the gas valve nameplate label and record the fuel change in the job file, because the internal regulator spring and orifices are identical for both fuels

questions.explanation: A listed conversion uses the appliance manufacturer kit for that model, with the specified orifices and the regulator spring or conversion parts that set propane pressure. Drilling orifices, converting by pressure alone, or changing only the label leaves the appliance outside its listed conversion instructions.

questions.question: A zoned system's smallest zone has ducts designed for 350 CFM. The two-stage air conditioner delivers 800 CFM on low stage. With only the small zone calling and its damper fully open while the others are closed, low-stage airflow still tries to force roughly 800 CFM toward a 350-CFM path. Which design correction addresses the root cause?

answers.text: Ensure the combination of equipment turndown, modulating dampers, and zone sizing keeps delivered airflow within what the smallest calling zone combination can accept at acceptable static pressure — for example by using variable-speed equipment with deeper turndown or enlarging the minimum zone grouping
Install a higher-pressure blower so it can force the full 800 CFM through the small zone
Close the small zone's damper partway so the excess air has somewhere to go
Remove the small zone's thermostat so it can never call by itself

questions.explanation: The root cause is a capacity-to-zone mismatch at minimum call; the fix is at the design level — turndown, modulation, and zone grouping — not forcing more pressure into an undersized path. Option B is wrong because more pressure means more noise, more leakage, and possible equipment trips — it intensifies every symptom; option C is wrong because throttling the only open damper raises static further and gives the excess air no destination at all; option D is wrong because defeating the zone's thermostat abandons the zoning the owner paid for instead of designing the match correctly.

questions.question: A compressor will not start after a long off period in a cold equipment room. The crankcase heater is found open-circuit, the oil sight glass shows a high, foamy level, and the compressor draws locked-rotor current briefly before tripping. What follow-up is most appropriate before returning it to regular service?

answers.text: Immediately add a full supplemental oil charge, because a foamy sight glass always means the crankcase is low on oil and needs additional volume right away
Replace the expansion valve with a smaller one, because migration during the off cycle is controlled entirely by the size of the valve orifice at the evaporator
Jumper the overload and force several long runs, because sustained running under load is the fastest way to prove the compressor has not been damaged by liquid
Restore the heater, warm and clear the oil of refrigerant, and verify oil condition before normal operation

questions.explanation: A dead heater allowed migration, so the heater must be restored and the refrigerant boiled out of the oil gently, with oil condition checked, before trusting the machine. A foamy glass reflects refrigerant in the oil, not a low oil charge needing more oil, migration is driven by temperature differences rather than expansion-valve orifice size, and forcing runs with an overload jumper risks destroying a possibly liquid-damaged compressor.

delaware-hvac.quiz_title: Delaware HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the purpose of a liquid receiver in a system that has one?

answers.text: To store liquid refrigerant leaving the condenser and supply a steady liquid seal to the liquid line as load and charge requirements vary
To prevent liquid from reaching the compressor on the suction side by trapping it in a large accumulator vessel installed immediately before the compressor inlet
To remove moisture and acid from the refrigerant
To measure refrigerant flow to the evaporator

questions.explanation: The receiver is a high-side storage vessel that holds condensed liquid and keeps liquid, not vapor, feeding the expansion device across varying conditions. Option B describes a suction accumulator, option C describes a filter drier, and option D describes the metering device or a flow measurement, not storage.

questions.question: What does an air pressure switch in a modern induced-draft furnace prove before ignition continues?

answers.text: That the gas valve has the correct manifold pressure
That the flame is present in the main burner
That the inducer is creating the required pressure or vacuum for venting
That the circulating blower is moving enough air for cooling

questions.explanation: The pressure switch senses inducer pressure or vacuum to prove the venting system is operating before and during firing. Manifold pressure is set and measured at the gas valve, flame is proved by the flame sensor, and cooling airflow is a different function from inducer proving.

questions.question: A replacement water heater is installed with no readily accessible gas shutoff valve serving it. What is required?

answers.text: An accessible shutoff valve in the same room, within the prescribed reach of the appliance, ahead of its union or connector.
A valve at the gas meter is sufficient for every appliance in the building, no matter how far the heater is from the meter location
A shutoff is required only on appliances over a certain input, so smaller heaters may rely on turning off the main building valve
The valve may be hidden behind the heater's jacket panel, provided a sticker on the front tells a technician that it is located inside

questions.explanation: Each appliance needs its own accessible shutoff nearby so it can be isolated quickly for service or emergency. A distant meter valve does not serve that purpose, the requirement is not limited to large inputs, and a valve behind a jacket panel is not accessible.

questions.question: Gross profit on a job is best defined as which of the following?

answers.text: Contract price minus direct job costs
Contract price with no deduction at all, because deductions are only tracked at the company level at year end
Total company revenue minus office rent, advertising, and administrative salaries for the entire fiscal year
Cash collected to date minus only the material invoices that have already been paid to suppliers

questions.explanation: A is correct because gross profit is the contract price less the direct costs of performing that job. B is incorrect because gross profit requires deducting direct job costs from the price. C is incorrect because deducting company overhead from total revenue describes a broader company-level result. D is incorrect because cash timing and paid-only invoices do not measure job gross profit.

questions.question: A supply outlet measures 600 FPM average velocity through a free area of 1.0 sq ft. How much air is it delivering?

answers.text: 60 CFM
160 CFM
600 CFM

questions.explanation: CFM = velocity x area = 600 FPM x 1.0 sq ft = 600 CFM, so D is correct. A divides by ten incorrectly, B adds unrelated numbers, and C overstates the product by nearly three times.

questions.question: What design feature distinguishes recovery equipment that is suitable for A2L refrigerants from older recovery units?

answers.text: Ignition-protected, spark-free motors, switches, and controls, so the machine cannot ignite vapor it draws in
A larger recovery rate in pounds per minute, because moving refrigerant faster is the feature that makes a unit acceptable for flammable refrigerants
A painted steel housing in a warning color, because the housing color is the rating that determines whether internal switches may spark in use
An automatic purge that vents a small amount of refrigerant at startup, because clearing the unit that way is required before flammable vapor can be recovered

questions.explanation: A2L-rated recovery machines use spark-free switches, motors, and controls so the machine itself cannot ignite vapor it draws in. Recovery speed and housing color do not provide ignition protection, and a unit that vents refrigerant at startup would violate no-venting rules rather than qualify the machine.

questions.question: A communicating zoned system is set up with an airflow target for each zone. Only the smallest zone calls. What should the blower do differently from a non-communicating setup?

answers.text: Deliver full whole-house airflow anyway, because zone airflow targets are used only for balancing reports and do not change blower operation during a live call
Stop entirely until a second zone calls, because variable-speed blowers in communicating systems are not permitted to serve a single zone at reduced airflow
Deliver approximately that zone's target airflow, reducing static pressure and noise on the small call
Deliver the sum of all zone targets plus the bypass target, because communicating controls add every programmed value together whenever any one zone is calling

questions.explanation: Zone-based airflow control lets the blower match delivery to the calling zones, so a single small zone receives roughly its own target airflow instead of the whole-house total. That is an operating function rather than a reporting feature, single-zone service at reduced airflow is the point of the setup, and targets for non-calling zones are not added to the call.

questions.question: A new whole-house dehumidifier is plumbed into the return duct but its condensate line has no trap or slope and the unit backs up. What is the installation lesson?

answers.text: Dehumidifiers produce pure water that evaporates inside the cabinet, so drainage piping is optional on ducted whole-house models
The backup proves the unit should drain into its own supply duct, where moving air will carry the moisture back into the house
Backups are cured by raising the unit's humidity setpoint above the house level so the machine simply never produces condensate
A dehumidifier is condensate-producing equipment and needs the same sloped, trapped, approved drainage as other cooling equipment.

questions.explanation: A ducted dehumidifier removes pints of water daily and must drain reliably by gravity with proper slope and trapping. Its water does not evaporate in the cabinet, draining into the supply defeats its purpose, and defeating the setpoint abandons humidity control rather than fixing drainage.

questions.question: A customer asks the technician to 'just keep adding R-22' to a leaking system instead of replacing it. Which fact most changes that conversation?

answers.text: R-22 is still manufactured domestically in unlimited quantities, so its price is expected to fall steadily every year
Virgin R-22 production and import ended in the United States, so supply is reclaimed stock at rising and uncertain cost
Adding refrigerant to a leaking system is prohibited in all cases, including small appliances with no leak-repair options
R-22 can be freely mixed with newer refrigerants in the same system to stretch the remaining supply at lower cost

questions.explanation: New R-22 supply ended, leaving reclaimed material whose price and availability drive replacement economics. It is not still produced without limit, leak and service rules are more nuanced than a blanket ban on charging, and refrigerants must never be mixed in a system.

questions.question: A water chiller produces 44°F leaving chilled water while the evaporator saturated refrigerant temperature is 38°F. What is the evaporator approach, and what does it describe?

answers.text: 6°F — the difference between leaving chilled-water temperature and evaporating refrigerant temperature
82°F — the sum of the leaving water and refrigerant temperatures added together
38°F — the refrigerant temperature alone, regardless of the water temperature measured at the outlet
44°F — the leaving water temperature alone, regardless of what the refrigerant is doing inside the evaporator

questions.explanation: The approach is 44 minus 38, or 6°F, and a widening approach at the same load points to poor heat transfer. Option B adds the temperatures, which has no diagnostic meaning, option C names only the refrigerant temperature, and option D names only the water temperature, so neither describes a difference between the two.

questions.question: A system holds test pressure overall, but a slight odor near one union suggests a tiny leak to pinpoint. Which method fits propane service?

answers.text: Pass a lit lighter slowly around the union, because a small leak will lift the flame visibly before the surrounding vapor concentration can reach a hazardous level in open air
Drill a small sampling hole in the pipe beside the union, because direct access to the pipe interior gives the fastest confirmation of which side of the joint is leaking
Raise the test pressure to tank pressure with propane and listen for a hiss, because increasing the pressure is the standard way to make a suspected pinhole reveal itself
Apply approved leak-detection fluid to the joint and watch for bubbles, or use a combustible gas detector

questions.explanation: Approved noncorrosive leak fluid bubbling at a joint, or a combustible gas detector, pinpoints a leak without adding an ignition source or damaging the piping. A flame at a suspected leak is an ignition source at the worst location, drilling the pipe destroys its integrity, and raising pressure with fuel turns a search into a release.

questions.question: During a basement furnace replacement, a technician notices an open sump pit and cracked slab joints. Why mention soil gas to the owner?

answers.text: An open sump proves the house has a carbon monoxide problem, because sumps are the primary source of combustion gases in basements
The sump should be connected to the furnace return so soil gas is diluted continuously by the air distribution system each cycle
Cracks should be widened so soil gas can enter freely and be detected sooner by a monitor placed across the basement room
Open sumps and slab cracks are entry routes for soil gases such as radon and moisture, and sealing or covering them as directed helps limit entry.

questions.explanation: Soil-gas entry points matter to indoor air quality, and an open sump is a direct pathway from below the slab. A sump is not a combustion-gas source, returning soil gas through the ducts would distribute it, and widening entry routes increases rather than controls entry.

questions.question: A system shows suction 94 psig, superheat 22°F, subcooling 18°F, head 330 psig, and a 9°F temperature drop measured across the liquid-line filter drier with light frost forming on its outlet side only. Airflow is normal and the evaporator is clean. What is the correct repair decision?

answers.text: Replace the liquid-line filter drier
Add refrigerant until superheat falls, which would mask the starvation while pressures downstream of the restriction remained low and the real blockage stayed in place
Replace the TXV, since a starved evaporator always means the valve has failed, even when a 9°F drop across the drier localizes the restriction upstream of it
Raise condenser airflow to lower the head pressure, which does nothing for a liquid-line blockage that is already proven by the temperature drop

questions.explanation: High subcooling with a starved evaporator seems contradictory until the 9°F drop across the drier localizes a liquid restriction: liquid backs up in the condenser while little reaches the coil. Adding charge only masks the starvation, the TXV sits downstream of the proven restriction, and condenser airflow cannot clear a blocked drier — the drier is replaced and the system rechecked.

questions.question: Corrugated stainless steel tubing (CSST) is used for part of a home's gas distribution. Besides following the manufacturer's instructions for fittings and support, what widely required safety measure applies to the CSST system?

answers.text: Electrical bonding of the gas piping system to reduce lightning-related damage risk
Painting the tubing black so it looks like iron pipe
Burying it without any protective sleeve or coating wherever it passes through concrete, masonry, or underground soil
Testing it with oxygen at high pressure

questions.explanation: Mainstream fuel-gas practice and CSST manufacturers require bonding of the piping system, in part to address lightning energy, option A. Painting for appearance (B) provides no safety function, unprotected burial through concrete (C) violates protection requirements, and oxygen testing (D) is prohibited because oxygen creates a severe fire and explosion hazard.

questions.question: A reach-in freezer was 'topped off' twice this season. Now head pressure is high, subcooling measures 28°F, the sight glass is solid clear, discharge temperature is elevated, box temperature is marginal, and a recovery check confirms the charge is 22% over nameplate. What is the correct diagnosis?

answers.text: A restricted cap tube, which would starve the evaporator and raise superheat rather than stack liquid and raise subcooling
A dirty condenser as the whole story, when the coil was cleaned last month and subcooling of 28°F specifically indicates excess liquid stacked in the system
Refrigerant overcharge
Noncondensables alone, which usually follow opening the system and would not be confirmed by a recovered charge weighing 22% over nameplate

questions.explanation: A weighed charge 22% over nameplate with 28°F subcooling and a solid glass is direct evidence of excess refrigerant stacked in the condenser. Noncondensables are not confirmed by an overweight charge, the cleaned coil cannot create 28°F subcooling, and a cap-tube restriction starves rather than stacks the high side.

questions.question: A master HVACR licensee in good standing in Maryland applies to Delaware by reciprocity and asks whether years of post-licensure practice must be proven. Maryland is on DPR's published list. What applies?

answers.text: Seven years of practice must be proven, because every reciprocity applicant owes the same experience proof to Delaware
Two years of practice must be proven, matching the post-certificate experience required of examination applicants in Delaware
No proof of experience is required on that point, because Maryland is published by DPR as substantially similar to Delaware
Reciprocity is unavailable from Maryland, because Delaware grants reciprocity only to states that border Delaware directly

questions.explanation: C is correct: DPR publishes Connecticut, Iowa, and Maryland as substantially similar, for which no proof of experience is required; the applicant still presents proof of current licensure in good standing and the other statutory qualifications. A is wrong because the 7-year practice proof applies to jurisdictions that are not substantially similar. B is wrong because the 2-year figure belongs to the examination eligibility route. D is wrong because Maryland is expressly on the substantially-similar list.

questions.question: A 600 CFM commercial-style range hood is installed in a tight house with a natural-draft water heater. When the hood runs on high, the house goes strongly negative and the water heater backdrafts. What does the hood installation need?

answers.text: A smaller water heater with a shorter flue, because reducing appliance size is the standard way to make natural draft resist a large exhaust appliance
A warning label on the hood telling occupants not to use the high setting, which satisfies the makeup-air requirement without any ducted air supply
Provide makeup air for the hood
A tighter house envelope, because reducing envelope leakage raises the house pressure and prevents the hood from pulling the house negative at all

questions.explanation: A large exhaust hood in a tight house needs ducted makeup air, interlocked with the hood, so it does not depressurize the house and backdraft other appliances. Appliance size does not make natural draft resist that depressurization, a label does not supply air, and a tighter envelope makes the same hood pull the house even more negative.

questions.question: No-heat call on a cold furnace that sat overnight. On a heat call the indoor blower starts and runs continuously, but the inducer never starts and there is no ignition sequence. The high-limit switch, which should be closed at room temperature, measures open circuit with the furnace cold, and its terminals show heat discoloration. All other safeties in the string measure closed. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A thermostat that is not calling for heat, ruled out because the blower responds to the call and the rest of the safety string measures closed and ready
A failed inducer motor that cannot start the sequence, which would stop the sequence at its own step but would not hold a cold limit switch open or run the blower continuously
An open pressure switch keeping the board in a fault state, ruled out because the pressure switch is among the safeties that measure closed at rest during this check
A high-limit switch failed in the open position

questions.explanation: A limit that reads open on a cold furnace has failed mechanically or thermally from past overheating (note the discoloration), and the board responds by running the blower with no heat sequence. The thermostat is calling, the inducer cannot be reached in sequence until the safety string is satisfied, and the pressure switch measures closed, leaving the failed-open limit as the break in the string.

questions.question: A 3-ton nominal air conditioner is being selected for a desert home with an outdoor design temperature of 108 degrees F. The manufacturer's extended performance table shows that at 108 degrees outdoors and the design indoor wet bulb, this model delivers 31,800 Btu/h total capacity. The house load at design is 33,500 Btu/h. What should the designer conclude?

answers.text: The model is acceptable because 3-ton nominal always equals 36,000 Btu/h at any outdoor temperature, with nameplate tonnage guaranteeing the same delivered capacity in desert heat, mild weather, and humid coastal conditions alike, so no extended table lookup is ever needed before approving the selection
The model exceeds the load, because capacity rises as outdoor temperature rises
The shortfall can be ignored because it is less than 5 percent of nominal tonnage

This model does not meet the design load — nominal tonnage is rated at milder standard conditions, and selection must use the capacity at the actual design conditions, so a model whose table value meets 33,500 Btu/h is required

questions.explanation: Capacity falls as outdoor temperature climbs, which is why selection uses extended rating tables at the project's design conditions rather than the nameplate's nominal tonnage. Option A is wrong because 36,000 Btu/h is the rating at standard test conditions, not a guarantee at 108 degrees; option B is wrong because air-cooled condensing capacity decreases with hotter outdoor air, since the condenser rejects heat less easily; option C is wrong because the comparison that matters is table capacity versus load at the same conditions — 31,800 against 33,500 is a real shortfall regardless of percentages of nominal.

questions.question: A resistive duct heater in a Middletown office draws 15 amps at 208 volts single phase. How much heat does it produce in watts, and about how much is that in Btuh?

answers.text: 3,120 watts, which is 3,120 x 3.41 = about 10,639 Btuh of electric heat output from the element bank
223 watts, found by dividing the voltage by the current and then multiplying the result by the number of phases
13.9 watts, found by dividing the voltage by the current alone, which actually gives the element's resistance in ohms
9,360 watts, found by tripling the single-phase product on the assumption that every duct heater is a three-phase load

questions.explanation: A is correct: for a resistive single-phase load, P = V x I = 208 x 15 = 3,120 watts, and 3,120 x 3.41 Btu per watt-hour = about 10,639 Btuh. B is wrong because its arithmetic does not follow the power relationship and its result is far below the V x I product. C is wrong because 208 / 15 = 13.9 is the resistance in ohms, not the power. D is wrong because the stem states a single-phase load, so no three-phase multiplier applies.

hawaii-c40-hvac.quiz_title: Hawaii C-40 HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: On a pressure-enthalpy diagram for a vapor-compression cycle, what do the two axes represent?

answers.text: Temperature on the vertical axis and entropy on the horizontal axis, so every heat transfer process in the cycle is read as a change in entropy alone
Pressure on the horizontal axis and volume on the vertical axis, with enthalpy calculated afterward from a separate table for each plotted state point
Suction pressure on one axis and discharge pressure on the other, so compressor ratio can be read directly without knowing any heat content values at all
Pressure vertically and enthalpy horizontally

questions.explanation: A pressure-enthalpy chart plots pressure on the vertical axis against enthalpy on the horizontal axis, letting cycle work and refrigeration effect be read as enthalpy differences. Temperature-entropy and pressure-volume diagrams are different charts, and the two pressures alone do not define the cycle states.

questions.question: A condensing unit nameplate lists MCA 32 A and MOP 50 A. Which pairing is correct when installing it?

answers.text: Size the conductors for 50 A and use a 32 A breaker as the maximum
Size the conductors for the compressor locked-rotor current shown in a generic table and ignore the equipment nameplate ratings entirely
Use 32 A overcurrent protection and conductors rated only for the fan current
Size the conductors for at least 32 A ampacity and use overcurrent protection no larger than 50 A

questions.explanation: MCA sets minimum conductor ampacity and MOP sets the maximum overcurrent device, so 32 A conductors with protection up to 50 A is correct. Reversing the two values misapplies both ratings. Locked-rotor current is a starting value, not the branch-circuit sizing basis, and the fan alone does not represent the whole load.

questions.question: A replacement water heater is installed with no readily accessible gas shutoff valve serving it. What is required?

answers.text: An accessible shutoff valve in the same room, within the prescribed reach of the appliance, ahead of its union or connector.
A valve at the gas meter is sufficient for every appliance in the building, no matter how far the heater is from the meter location
A shutoff is required only on appliances over a certain input, so smaller heaters may rely on turning off the main building valve
The valve may be hidden behind the heater's jacket panel, provided a sticker on the front tells a technician that it is located inside

questions.explanation: Each appliance needs its own accessible shutoff nearby so it can be isolated quickly for service or emergency. A distant meter valve does not serve that purpose, the requirement is not limited to large inputs, and a valve behind a jacket panel is not accessible.

questions.question: On a rooftop unit, a pleated filter has collapsed inward and dirty air has bypassed around the rack, coating the coil. Airflow is low. What is the complete service response?

answers.text: Replace the filter, clean the fouled coil as needed, and check why the filter collapsed, including excessive pressure drop across a clogged or wrong filter
Straighten the collapsed filter and reinstall it, because a pleated filter that has held its frame shape once will resist collapse on the second use
Remove the filter entirely for the cooling season, because a coated coil loses less airflow than any filter the rack can hold in this unit size
Increase blower speed two steps to pull through the bypass, because raising speed restores design airflow regardless of coil fouling above it

questions.explanation: A collapsed filter means the rack saw excessive pressure drop and the coil has been fouled by bypassed air; both must be corrected and the collapse cause addressed. A collapsed filter cannot be straightened back into service, running without filtration fouls the coil further, and raising blower speed does not clean a coated coil.

questions.question: Which description best fits a Category I gas appliance?

answers.text: Positive vent pressure with flue gas temperature low enough to condense continuously inside a sealed plastic vent that drains back to the furnace
Negative vent pressure with flue gas temperature high enough to avoid sustained condensation in the vent
A sealed-combustion appliance that draws all combustion air through a pipe from outdoors
An unvented appliance that discharges products into the room

questions.explanation: Category I appliances operate with negative vent pressure and flue temperatures that avoid sustained condensation, which is option B. Positive pressure with condensing temperatures (A) describes Category IV, sealed combustion-air piping (C) may apply to several categories and is not the defining test, and unvented operation (D) is not Category I venting at all.

questions.question: A technician must pinpoint a suspected R-454B leak inside a small indoor mechanical closet. Which leak-detection approach fits A2L service?

answers.text: A lit propane torch passed slowly along each joint, because the flame color method remains acceptable when the room is small and the door is left open
A standard combustible-gas lighter used as a test flame at each fitting, because a small flame presents less risk than a full-size torch flame
An ultrasonic detector alone with no confirmation, because sound-based tools also measure refrigerant concentration against the lower flammability limit
An electronic detector rated for A2L refrigerants

questions.explanation: Electronic detectors listed or rated for A2L use detect the leak without introducing ignition. Any open-flame method adds an ignition source regardless of flame size or door position, and an ultrasonic tool hears leak noise but does not measure concentration or confirm refrigerant identity by itself.

questions.question: Duct leakage results are reported at 25 Pa, about 0.10 in. w.c., even though operating duct pressures vary by location and system. Why is 25 Pa used?

answers.text: It is a standardized reference pressure
It is the exact pressure found at every register in every residential system, so test results at 25 Pa need no interpretation to reflect operating leakage rates
It is the highest pressure a residential duct can withstand, chosen so the test doubles as a structural proof test of the duct joints and seams
It is the pressure at which leakage stops changing with pressure, so readings taken there equal the leakage that occurs at any other operating pressure

questions.explanation: Twenty-five pascals is an agreed reference pressure that makes leakage results comparable between houses, testers, and before-and-after sealing work. Operating pressures vary widely and are not uniformly 25 Pa, residential ducts withstand far more than this gentle test pressure, and leakage does change with pressure, which is exactly why a fixed reference is needed.

questions.question: Why do traditional combustion air methods provide two openings, one high and one low, between a furnace room and the rest of the building or outdoors?

answers.text: Both openings are drains for condensate from the appliance
The high opening lets hot air and flue-related gases escape the enclosure while the low opening supplies cooler combustion air
The high opening is provided for cooling-season supply airflow and the low opening serves as the return-air path back to the air handler for the rest of the house
Two openings are required only so one can be blocked as a spare

questions.explanation: Warm air rises out the upper opening while denser supply air enters low, supporting both combustion supply and enclosure relief. Neither opening is a condensate drain. They are not the building's cooling or return-air system, and neither opening is intended to be blocked as a spare.

questions.question: A system has always short-cycled and left the home humid, and the owner asks for 'the same size again.' What should the contractor do?

answers.text: Install the same size, because the equipment that was there longest defines the correct size for that house by precedent
Go one size larger so the system satisfies the thermostat faster, which is the usual cure for humidity complaints in summer
Run a load calculation and select from its results, because repeating the old size perpetuates the oversizing problem
Go two sizes smaller without a calculation, since humidity complaints always mean the system is exactly two sizes too big

questions.explanation: Documented short-cycling and poor dehumidification are classic oversizing symptoms that a calculation can quantify and correct. Long service does not validate a wrong size, larger equipment short-cycles worse, and arbitrary downsizing without numbers risks undercapacity on design days.

questions.question: Under a lump-sum contract for a defined scope, the contractor agrees to which arrangement?

answers.text: Complete the defined scope for a fixed price
Be reimbursed for every actual cost incurred plus an hourly fee that the owner may revise at any time
Work without a stated total and invoice at the end for whatever amount the contractor considers reasonable
Provide labor only, with the owner supplying all materials, equipment, permits, and insurance for the work

questions.explanation: A is correct because a lump-sum contract sets one fixed price for a clearly defined scope of work. B is incorrect because reimbursement of actual costs plus a fee describes cost-plus contracting. C is incorrect because a lump sum requires a stated price agreed before the work proceeds. D is incorrect because a lump sum does not by itself limit the contractor to labor only.

questions.question: A system using a fixed metering device has an evaporator saturation temperature of 40 degrees F and a measured suction-line temperature at the evaporator outlet of 52 degrees F. What is the evaporator superheat?

answers.text: 92 degrees F
12 degrees F
40 degrees F
52 degrees F

questions.explanation: Superheat is suction-line temperature minus saturation temperature, so 52 minus 40 equals 12 degrees F. Option A adds the two temperatures instead of subtracting, option C is only the saturation temperature, and option D is only the line temperature, neither of which is a temperature difference.

questions.question: On a very cold morning, a large furnace on a small, nearly empty propane tank loses pressure and locks out, and frost covers the tank shell up to a low line. What is happening?

answers.text: The tank is overfilled for cold weather, and the frost line marks liquid propane leaking through the steel shell at the point where the tank is beginning to split
The tank cannot vaporize liquid fast enough for the load in that cold, low-level condition
The second-stage regulator is freezing outdoor air into the yard line, and the tank frost is a separate cosmetic effect that has no relationship to appliance pressure loss
Cold weather makes propane liquid expand against the relief valve, so the lockout is caused by the tank venting vapor faster than the furnace can use it at full fire

questions.explanation: Vapor supply depends on liquid surface area, liquid level, and outdoor temperature, and a small, low tank in deep cold may not boil off vapor fast enough for a large load, which also explains frost up to the liquid level. The frost line marks chilled liquid level rather than a leaking split, and cold contracts the liquid instead of expanding it.

questions.question: A fixed-orifice R-410A system frosts the evaporator. Readings: suction 90 psig, head 258 psig, superheat 4°F, subcooling 12°F, supply-air temperature split 26°F, measured airflow only 215 cfm/ton, and the filter is packed solid with dust while the coil and charge history are unremarkable. What should the technician correct first?

answers.text: Recover part of the charge to raise superheat, which treats the symptom while leaving the coil starved of the air it needs to boil refrigerant
Replace the fixed orifice with a larger size, which would feed still more refrigerant into an evaporator that cannot absorb heat at this airflow
Restore evaporator airflow
Add refrigerant to raise the suction pressure, even though the low 4°F superheat shows the evaporator is already overfed relative to its heat load

questions.explanation: Low suction, low superheat, a wide air-side temperature split, and measured airflow near half of normal identify an air-side starvation problem, here a packed filter. Adding refrigerant or enlarging the orifice would flood the coil further at 4°F superheat, and removing charge cannot restore the missing heat load — airflow must be restored and the readings rechecked.

questions.question: A tall suction riser is piped with no intermediate traps, and the compressor gradually loses oil that is found spread through the riser and evaporator. The piping correction is to:

answers.text: Remove the trap at the base of the riser as well
Slope the entire riser backward toward the evaporator, so any oil carried partway up the vertical run drains away from the compressor and collects in the coil whenever the system cycles off at night
Fill the riser halfway with oil before start-up
Add traps at the base and at intervals up the tall riser so oil is lifted in stages rather than having to climb the full height at once

questions.explanation: Intermediate traps break a tall lift into stages, collecting oil and letting gas carry it upward step by step instead of falling back. Removing the base trap in option A worsens drainage control, sloping toward the evaporator in option B sends oil away from the compressor, and option C overfills piping with oil that belongs in the crankcase.

questions.question: A reach-in freezer was 'topped off' twice this season. Now head pressure is high, subcooling measures 28°F, the sight glass is solid clear, discharge temperature is elevated, box temperature is marginal, and a recovery check confirms the charge is 22% over nameplate. What is the correct diagnosis?

answers.text: A restricted cap tube, which would starve the evaporator and raise superheat rather than stack liquid and raise subcooling
A dirty condenser as the whole story, when the coil was cleaned last month and subcooling of 28°F specifically indicates excess liquid stacked in the system
Refrigerant overcharge
Noncondensables alone, which usually follow opening the system and would not be confirmed by a recovered charge weighing 22% over nameplate

questions.explanation: A weighed charge 22% over nameplate with 28°F subcooling and a solid glass is direct evidence of excess refrigerant stacked in the condenser. Noncondensables are not confirmed by an overweight charge, the cleaned coil cannot create 28°F subcooling, and a cap-tube restriction starves rather than stacks the high side.

questions.question: A service technician in Hilo advertises that he holds a Hawaii journeyman refrigeration license and will contract walk-in repairs directly with store owners. What is wrong with that position?

answers.text: Nothing, because Hawaii licenses refrigeration journey workers individually and they may contract directly once they complete a registered apprenticeship program in the trade and may contract directly with owners for repair and installation work in the trade in which that license was earned and documented over the years
The problem is that journeyman refrigeration licenses are issued by the counties, so he must obtain his license from the county where each store is located instead
The only problem is the advertising wording, because a technician may contract directly with owners as long as the advertisement does not use the word journeyman in it

Hawaii has no journeyman refrigeration license; outside the RME and sole proprietor licenses, an unlicensed individual may do the regulated work only as an employee with wages as the person's sole compensation

questions.explanation: D is correct: neither the contractor statute nor its rules creates any journeyman, apprentice, technician, or helper license for refrigeration work; the individual licenses are the RME license and the sole proprietor's license, and chapter 444 does not apply to a person who engages in the regulated activities as an employee with wages as the person's sole compensation. A is wrong because no such journeyman license exists. C is wrong because direct contracting, not just wording, requires a contractor license. B is wrong because counties do not issue a Hawaii journeyman refrigeration license.

questions.question: A filter shows an unusually low pressure drop for its rating, yet the evaporator coil is fouling with dust as if no filter were installed. The filter is found sitting loosely with a wide gap along one edge of the rack. What is the diagnosis?

answers.text: Air is bypassing the filter
The filter media is too efficient, so it captures dust before the pressure drop can develop and then releases that dust onto the coil during blower off-cycles
The coil is fouling from refrigerant oil that migrated out of the sealed system and coated the fins, attracting dust that the filter never had a chance to catch
The low pressure drop proves the blower is moving too little air to carry dust to the coil, so the fouling must predate the current filter installation entirely

questions.explanation: Air follows the low-resistance gap around a loose filter, which explains both the low measured drop and dust reaching the coil as if unfiltered. Efficient media raises rather than lowers pressure drop and does not release dust downstream, refrigerant oil stays inside the sealed circuit, and low airflow from blower problems would not create a rack gap or this bypass pattern.

questions.question: A gas furnace lights, runs 4 seconds, and shuts down, repeating three times before lockout. The igniter glows normally, manifold pressure is 3.5 in. wc, the flame looks strong and blue while lit, and the flame-sense microamp reading is 0.4 µA against a control spec of at least 2 µA; the flame sensor rod is visibly coated with white oxide. What is the correct repair?

answers.text: Clean the flame sensor rod
Replace the gas valve, which is delivering a full 3.5 in. wc manifold pressure and a strong flame every time the burners light
Replace the hot-surface igniter, which is glowing normally and successfully lighting the burners on every attempt
Replace the control board, which is correctly shutting the burner down because the flame-proving signal it receives is genuinely too weak

questions.explanation: A strong flame that the control cannot see — 0.4 µA against a 2 µA minimum — with an oxide-coated rod is a flame-sensing fault, cured by cleaning the sensor. The gas valve and igniter both prove themselves each cycle, and the board is responding correctly to a genuinely weak signal rather than failing.

questions.question: Humidity complaint. A 4-ton air conditioner serves a house whose calculated cooling load is about 2.6 tons. It reaches the temperature setpoint in roughly eight-minute runs, cycles off for long stretches, and holds the house at setpoint, yet indoor relative humidity sits at 63 percent and the occupants feel clammy. Refrigerant readings, airflow per ton, and drain operation all test normal. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A low refrigerant charge reducing latent capacity first, which would also show abnormal superheat and subcooling and long, weak cooling runs rather than eight-minute satisfied cycles
A condensate drain that holds water in the pan and re-evaporates it, which would need a drainage fault, while drain operation and pan condition test normal on this visit
A thermostat set to run the blower continuously in the on position, which can re-evaporate coil moisture, but here the blower is verified running in auto with normal cycling behavior
Equipment oversized for the load, short-cycling before it can dehumidify

questions.explanation: The 4-ton unit satisfies the 2.6-ton sensible load in eight minutes, so the coil barely stays wet long enough to remove moisture and humidity stays at 63 percent despite normal refrigerant and airflow readings. Low charge would distort the refrigerant readings and lengthen runs, the drain tests normal, and the blower runs in auto, leaving oversizing and its short latent run time as the explanation.

questions.question: A walk-in box measures 10 feet by 12 feet inside with an 8-foot ceiling. Panels come in 4-foot widths and cover the full wall height. Ignoring doors and corners, how many wall panels are needed for the four walls?

answers.text: 44 panels, found by dividing the total wall length of 176 feet by the 4-foot panel width
24 panels, found by dividing the floor area of 120 square feet by a 5-square-foot panel face
11 panels, found by dividing the total wall length of 44 feet by the 4-foot panel width
22 panels, found by dividing the total wall area of 352 square feet by a 16-square-foot coverage

questions.explanation: C is correct: the wall perimeter is 10 + 12 + 10 + 12 = 44 feet, and 44 divided by the 4-foot panel width equals 11 full-height panels for the four walls. A is wrong because 176 is not the perimeter; it multiplies the wall length by an extra factor of four. B is wrong because wall panels are counted from wall length, not from the floor area. D is wrong because a 4-foot-wide, 8-foot-tall panel covers 32 square feet, not 16, so the area method as stated misstates panel coverage.

iowa-hvac.quiz_title: Iowa HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How does a capillary tube or fixed-orifice metering device differ from a thermostatic expansion valve?

answers.text: It actively senses superheat at the evaporator outlet with a remote bulb and adjusts flow continuously to hold a preset superheat under all load conditions
It contains a sensing bulb and external equalizer
It uses a diaphragm and push pins to modulate flow
It is a fixed restriction with no moving parts and no superheat control, so superheat varies with load and charge

questions.explanation: A capillary tube or fixed orifice is simply a fixed restriction; flow changes only with pressure difference, so superheat floats with conditions. Options A, B, and C all describe parts or behavior of a thermostatic expansion valve, not a fixed restriction.

questions.question: For reliable building pressure control, where should the indoor pressure sensor reference be placed?

answers.text: Inside the supply duct, where pressure is highest and easiest to read
In a representative interior location away from doors, diffusers, and direct drafts, referenced to a stable outdoor pressure tap shielded from wind
Directly in the blast of an entrance door that opens frequently
Outdoors on the roof in a fully exposed location where wind gusts strike the pressure tap directly and the reading follows every change in wind speed and direction

questions.explanation: Space pressure sensing must reflect the building, not local air movement, and wind on the outdoor reference corrupts the differential. Duct pressure is a different, much larger variable. Door drafts and wind gusts are exactly the disturbances good placement avoids.

questions.question: Before leaving a new installation, which combustion-related checks belong on the startup record for a gas furnace?

answers.text: Only that the burners lit on the first attempt
Only the color of the flame as seen through the sight glass
Manifold pressure, temperature rise against the nameplate range, vent draft or pressure-switch operation as applicable, and a carbon monoxide check of the supply air or flue as directed
Only the gas meter size and the length of the gas line

questions.explanation: A complete combustion startup verifies fuel pressure, heat-exchanger airflow by temperature rise, proper venting operation, and the absence of carbon monoxide where the maker directs the check. Option A proves ignition only, option B relies on appearance, which cannot confirm safe combustion, and option D records supply piping facts without any operating verification.

questions.question: An Iowa-based contractor applicant is assembling its filings. Which pairing correctly states the minimum public liability insurance and the minimum surety bond for the contractor license itself?

answers.text: Liability insurance of $250,000 and a surety bond of $25,000, with the bond amount taken from the contractor registration schedule for all applicants
Liability insurance of $1,000,000 and a surety bond of $5,000, with the higher insurance figure required of every contractor regardless of the size of its work
Liability insurance of $500,000 and a surety bond of $25,000, because the out-of-state registration bond sets the bond floor for in-state applicants as well
Liability insurance of $500,000 and a surety bond of $5,000, each providing that cancellation requires 10 days' written notice to the Board

questions.explanation: D is correct: the contractor applicant must show a public liability policy with minimum coverage of $500,000 and a surety bond in a minimum amount of $5,000, each providing that it will not be canceled without the issuer first giving 10 days' written notice to the Board. A is wrong on both figures for this license. B is wrong because the insurance minimum is $500,000, not $1,000,000. C is wrong because the $25,000 bond belongs to the separate out-of-state contractor registration instrument, not the contractor license bond.

questions.question: After a three-phase condenser fan motor is replaced, it runs backward. What is the standard correction?

answers.text: Swap the run capacitor leads and reverse the thermostat Y wire
Swap any two of the three power leads to the motor
Reverse the transformer primary leads
Move all three leads one terminal clockwise

questions.explanation: Swapping any two line leads reverses the phase sequence and therefore rotation of a three-phase motor. Capacitor and thermostat wiring do not set three-phase rotation. Reversing a control transformer does not change motor rotation, and rotating all three leads preserves the same sequence.

questions.question: Before opening a refrigerant circuit for repair or disposing of an appliance, the technician is required to:

answers.text: Vent the charge if it is less than the system nameplate amount, if the job is outdoors on a windy day, or if the technician believes the amount released will be too small to matter under the handling rules
Recover refrigerant to the required recovery level using certified recovery equipment, rather than knowingly venting it
Add nitrogen to dilute the refrigerant before release
Recover only the liquid portion and release the vapor

questions.explanation: Handling rules prohibit knowingly venting refrigerant and require recovery to specified levels with certified equipment before a system is opened or disposed of. Option A invents a small-charge venting exception that does not exist in this form, option C still releases refrigerant, and option D is wrong because the entire charge, vapor included, must be recovered.

questions.question: Water drips from the outside of a bare-metal supply duct crossing a humid attic in summer, while the air inside the duct is 55°F and attic dew point is near 70°F. What is occurring?

answers.text: Condensate is leaking out through duct joints from inside, because supply ducts normally carry liquid water that escapes wherever joints are not taped
The duct is sweating because humid attic air is reaching a surface chilled by the cold supply air, and the water is refrigerant condensing through the metal wall
Missing insulation lets surface chill
The roof is leaking directly onto that duct section, which is why the dripping only happens during the cooling season and not during dry winter heating

questions.explanation: Without insulation the metal surface falls below the attic dew point, so moisture from attic air condenses on the outside of the duct. Supply ducts carry air, not liquid water, refrigerant cannot pass through the duct wall, and a roof leak tied to cooling-season runtime, rather than rain, does not fit the pattern.

questions.question: A supply duct in a crawlspace drips steadily in summer. Crawlspace dew point is about 68°F and a thermometer on the duct insulation surface reads 58°F. What is the diagnosis?

answers.text: The duct is leaking cold air that freezes crawlspace moisture into frost, which then melts and drips whenever the blower cycles off in the afternoon
Groundwater is wicking up through the duct supports and running down the duct, which is why the dripping follows the cooling season so closely
Condensate from the indoor coil is draining into the duct and out through its seams, collecting on the outside surface as it escapes the duct interior
Surface is below the dew point

questions.explanation: Any surface held at 58°F in air with a 68°F dew point will condense moisture continuously, so the duct surface is simply below the dew point. Leaking cold air would chill a spot rather than wet the whole surface, groundwater wicking does not track cooling runtime, and coil condensate belongs in the drain system, not spread over the duct exterior.

questions.question: After a refrigerant safety toolbox talk, what documentation practice best supports the business's compliance efforts?

answers.text: Discard attendance records once the talk ends, because only the content of the training matters and never who received it
Ask employees to sign a single undated sheet covering every training topic planned for the remainder of the year
Have the supervisor rely on memory to recall attendance if a question about the training arises months later
Record the date, topic, trainer, and attendees, and keep the record on file

questions.explanation: D is correct because a dated record of topic, trainer, and attendees proves who received the training and when. A is incorrect because discarding the record destroys the evidence the training occurred. B is incorrect because an undated blanket sheet does not show a specific session or actual attendance. C is incorrect because memory months later is unreliable compared with a contemporaneous record.

questions.question: A rooftop gas heat section lights reliably but produces low heat rise and a lazy, yellow-tipped flame. Supply gas pressure to the unit is within range. What measurement most directly confirms a likely cause?

answers.text: Manifold pressure at the gas valve compared with the rating plate value, because low manifold pressure underfires the burner and softens the flame

Blower motor nameplate amps compared with locked-rotor amps, because flame appearance on a rooftop burner is set by blower electrical load while the rest of the system continues to operate normally through a complete cycle of operation

Economizer damper angle compared with its minimum position, because damper angle is the adjustment that meters gas flow to the burner section even after the obvious maintenance items at the unit have already been checked and corrected first
Condensate trap depth compared with pan pressure, because trap depth determines the gas pressure delivered to the burners during heating
