answers.text: Outdoor air blown over the shell by the condenser fan while the fan cycles on and off with the compressor during normal cooling operation on a mild day
Water circulating through a jacket around the shell
Oil sprayed continuously over the windings
Cool suction vapor returning from the evaporator and passing over the motor before compression

questions.explanation: In a hermetic compressor the returning suction vapor flows over the motor before it is compressed, which is why loss of charge or mass flow can overheat the motor. Option A may cool the shell surface slightly but is not the design cooling path, option B describes water-cooled equipment, and option C is wrong because oil circulation alone does not provide the main motor cooling.

questions.question: When soft-soldering (sweating) a copper joint for HVAC water-side work, what sequence produces a sound joint?

answers.text: Clean and flux the surfaces, assemble, heat the fitting, and let capillary action draw solder into the joint
Heat the solder rod directly with the torch until it drips and runs onto a cold, uncleaned fitting that was never fluxed or prepared
Apply flux after the joint has cooled to seal the outside
Melt solder into the gap with no flux on oxidized tubing

questions.explanation: Soldering depends on clean, fluxed surfaces and heating the fitting so capillary action pulls molten solder through the joint, option A. Heating solder over a cold dirty fitting (B) produces a weak surface blob, flux after cooling (C) cannot clean oxides or promote flow inside the joint, and omitting flux on oxidized copper (D) prevents wetting and bonding.

questions.question: In a primary-secondary chilled-water plant, what does the common (decoupler) pipe between the two loops allow?

answers.text: It lets each loop circulate at its own flow rate; the direction of flow in the common pipe shows which loop is producing more
It forces both loops to run at exactly the same flow at all times, because any difference would immediately air-lock both pumps
It replaces the expansion tank, air separator, and all balancing valves in both loops with a single short piece of pipe
It mixes supply and return water deliberately so the chillers always see the warmest possible return water at low load

questions.explanation: Decoupled loops run independently; excess production one way or the other simply passes through the low-pressure-drop common pipe. Option B defeats the entire purpose of decoupling, option C assigns the pipe jobs belonging to other components, and option D misstates the goal, since uncontrolled mixing and warm returns are problems, not design intent.

questions.question: In an air-cooled condenser, which condition most directly reduces the coil's ability to reject heat?

answers.text: A clean coil with full airflow
A layer of dirt and debris insulating the fins and blocking airflow through the coil
A liquid line that is a few degrees subcooled below saturation as it leaves the condenser and travels through a long, well-insulated run to the indoor coil
An evaporator with correct superheat

questions.explanation: Dirt both insulates the fin surface and restricts airflow, so heat rejection falls and head pressure rises. Option A is the desired condition, option C describes normal subcooled liquid leaving a condenser, and option D is an evaporator measurement that does not impair the condenser itself.

questions.question: Why does a condensing furnace's condensate trap need to be installed and primed correctly?

answers.text: It prevents flue gases from escaping through the drain while allowing condensate to flow out
It stores water to humidify the house during dry weather
It filters particles from the flue gas before venting
It raises the temperature of the condensate as it leaves the furnace so that standard PVC drain piping will not soften or melt from the heat of the flue gases

questions.explanation: The water seal in the trap blocks positive-pressure flue gas from leaving via the drain line while passing condensate. The trap is not a humidifier reservoir. It does not filter flue gas, and condensate is cool, so melt protection is not its purpose.

questions.question: A technician wants to dehydrate a system that was open in humid weather and may contain moisture. The most effective approach is:

answers.text: Pull a quick vacuum to 28 inches of mercury and charge immediately
Deep vacuum to 500 microns or below with large-diameter hoses and valve cores removed, using nitrogen sweep and repeat evacuation if moisture is stubborn, verified with a micron gauge on the system

Pressurize with refrigerant and vent it several times to flush moisture out, repeating the cycle until the vented gas appears dry, regardless of the prohibition on knowingly venting refrigerant during service and maintenance procedures
Run the compressor to boil moisture out of the oil

questions.explanation: Moisture boils and leaves only under a deep vacuum measured in microns at the system, and nitrogen sweeping plus repeated evacuation helps remove stubborn moisture without venting refrigerant. Option A stops far short of dehydration vacuum, option C is prohibited venting and poor drying, and option D circulates moisture through the compressor instead of removing it.

questions.question: A freeze-stat trips repeatedly on an air handler on cold mornings, stopping the fan. What is the correct technician response?

answers.text: Treat it as a real low-temperature warning: check outdoor-air damper control, preheat operation, and coil conditions rather than raising the setting or bypassing it

Bypass the freeze-stat for the entire winter by jumpering its contacts so morning startups are never interrupted, and rely on the operator to watch coil temperatures manually on the coldest days instead
Raise its setpoint well above freezing so it trips earlier and more often
Jumper the heating valve closed so cold water stops circulating in the coil

questions.explanation: Repeated trips signal air that is too cold reaching the coil, and the damper, preheat, and coil causes must be corrected. Bypassing removes coil protection and risks a burst coil, raising the setpoint makes trips more frequent, and closing off heating water removes the very heat that protects the coil.

questions.question: Before raising an aerial lift to set a curb adapter, the operator walks around the machine and finds a hydraulic leak and a worn tire. What should the operator do?

answers.text: Operate the lift at reduced height all day, because hydraulic leaks and tire wear only become dangerous when the platform is near its maximum elevation
Tag the lift out of service and report the defects before use
Top off the hydraulic fluid and proceed, since a leak that can be refilled during the shift does not count as a defect requiring the lift to be removed
Swap the lift's parking spot with another crew's machine without mentioning the defects, letting the next operator discover the problems during their own work

questions.explanation: A pre-use inspection that finds defects like hydraulic leaks or damaged tires takes the lift out of service until repaired. Reduced height does not make a failing lift safe, refilling does not fix a leak, and silently passing a defective machine to another crew just moves the hazard.

questions.question: Two sets of drawings are on the jobsite trailer table. One sheet shows a revision cloud around the duct routing with a later revision date in the title block. Which set should the crew build from?

answers.text: The set carrying the latest revision of that sheet
The older set, because revisions issued after bidding are advisory only and the contract can only be built from the documents priced at bid time
Whichever set the crew started with, because consistency within a crew matters more than incorporating design changes issued during construction
Both sets at once, building each half of the run from a different revision so the final installation averages the old and new routing decisions

questions.explanation: Crews must build from the current revision, and the revision cloud and title block date identify what changed and which sheet is current. Older sets are superseded rather than advisory, habit does not outrank issued revisions, and mixing revisions produces a run that matches neither design.

questions.question: A Louisiana firm preparing to seek a mechanical license wants to confirm which body licenses contractors in the state and where that body is domiciled. Which answer is accurate?

answers.text: Contractors are licensed by the State Plumbing Board in New Orleans, because mechanical work grew out of plumbing regulation and that board retained authority over both trades statewide.
Contractors are licensed by the State Licensing Board for Contractors, whose domicile is Baton Rouge.
Contractors are licensed by the Department of Labor in Shreveport, because contractor licensing is administered as part of the state's workforce and employment programs for the construction trades.
Contractors are licensed parish by parish by local licensing boards, because Louisiana has no single state board and each parish issues the contractor licenses valid within its own borders.

questions.explanation: B is correct: Louisiana contractors are licensed by the State Licensing Board for Contractors, created within the office of the governor, and the Board's domicile is Baton Rouge. A is wrong because the State Plumbing Board handles plumbing licensure, such as the master plumber credential, not general contractor licensing. C is wrong because contractor licensing is not a Department of Labor workforce program. D is wrong because Louisiana licensing is state-level through this Board, not a parish-by-parish system.

questions.question: After repairs, a long underground-to-indoor gas run must be purged before the appliance is lit. Safe purging means:

answers.text: Open the appliance union indoors and let the gas flow until it can be smelled strongly at the furnace, then light the appliance immediately
Purge into a closed garage with the doors shut, because keeping the mixture contained is considered safer than releasing it outside the building
Use the appliance's own ignition trial to burn off the air in the line, repeating trials as many times as needed until the burners stay lit
Discharge the gas-air mixture outdoors at a controlled point away from ignition and openings

questions.explanation: Discharge the gas-air mixture outdoors at a controlled point away from ignition and openings. Indoor release, release into an enclosed space, and repeated ignition trials all create an uncontrolled fuel-air hazard instead of a controlled outdoor purge.

questions.question: Clocking a gas meter, the 1-cubic-foot dial takes 36 seconds to complete one revolution with only the furnace firing. The furnace input is about:

answers.text: 50,000 Btu/hr, found by dividing the seconds per revolution directly into the heating value without converting the dial volume to an hourly rate
200,000 Btu/hr, found by assuming the 1-cubic-foot dial actually delivers 2 cubic feet per revolution because it is read at both the start and finish marks
36,000 Btu/hr, found by treating the 36 seconds of dial time as if it were itself the hourly fuel consumption in thousands of Btu per hour

questions.explanation: The furnace input is about 100,000 Btu/hr. One cubic foot in 36 seconds is 100 cubic feet per hour, and at roughly 1,000 Btu per cubic foot that is about 100,000 Btu/hr; the other figures come from the stated conversion errors.

questions.question: A hydronic loop is filled with 50% propylene glycol where 30% would provide the needed freeze protection. Compared with water, the excess glycol will most likely:

answers.text: Lower heat output and raise pumping work, because excess glycol is more viscous and carries less heat per gallon, while adding unnecessary cost
Increase heat transfer and reduce circulator load
Have no effect on system performance at any concentration
Eliminate the need for corrosion inhibitors in the loop

questions.explanation: Glycol solutions transfer less heat and are more viscous than water, and the penalty grows with concentration, so over-concentrating derates coils and loads the circulator. Option B reverses both effects. Option C denies measured fluid properties that sizing must account for. Option D is wrong because glycol still requires maintained inhibitors, which degrade over time.

questions.question: A metal supply duct in a humid crawlspace sweats every summer despite a layer of duct insulation. Inspection shows the insulation's outer jacket is torn and its seams are unsealed. What is the most effective repair?

answers.text: Add a second layer of insulation over the torn jacket without sealing anything, because total thickness alone determines whether the outer surface stays warm
Puncture the low points of the jacket so condensed water can drain out of the insulation instead of accumulating inside it over the summer
Seal the outer vapor jacket
Remove the insulation entirely so the duct surface warms to crawlspace temperature and stops condensing moisture from the surrounding air

questions.explanation: Humid air is reaching the cold metal through jacket tears and open seams and condensing there; sealing the outer vapor jacket keeps that air off the cold surface so the jacket exterior stays above the dew point. Added thickness over an open jacket still admits humid air, drainage holes invite more vapor in, and a bare duct in humid air sweats worst of all.

questions.question: A field supervisor verbally agrees to a costly extra the owner requested, with nothing in writing. What risk has the contractor created?

answers.text: No risk at all, because verbal extras are always paid at the amount the contractor later decides to charge
The risk that retainage will automatically double on every unrelated project the company currently has under contract
The risk that the equipment warranty will be extended indefinitely because the change was not documented properly
A payment dispute because the extra's scope and price were not authorized in writing

questions.explanation: D is correct because an undocumented extra leaves scope and price open to dispute when the bill is presented. A is incorrect because verbal extras are a common source of nonpayment disputes, not guaranteed payment. B is incorrect because retainage on other projects is governed by their own contracts. C is incorrect because warranty duration is set by warranty terms, not by change documentation.

questions.question: A PSC blower delivers too little air against 0.7 in. w.c. external static, though the wheel is clean. Using the manufacturer's blower table, what should the technician do?

answers.text: Select a higher speed tap or correct the high static, verifying amps stay within rating
Block part of the return opening with a panel to raise airflow through the remaining registers
Remove the filter permanently
Lower the charge to compensate

questions.explanation: PSC airflow falls as static rises, so the fix is a higher speed tap per the blower table or reducing static, while checking motor amps, making A correct. Blocking the return raises static further, removing the filter is not a permanent correction, and refrigerant charge does not change blower delivery.

questions.question: A boiler fires to its high limit at 205°F and shuts down while every zone stays cold. The circulator has 120 V at its terminals but draws 0 amps, its shaft will not turn by hand, pipes beyond the pump are cold, and the boiler itself shows no pressure or combustion problems. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Three failed zone valves failing simultaneously, which is improbable and would not explain the circulator's seized shaft and zero amp draw
A seized circulator pump
An air-bound system, which can stop flow but would not leave a pump drawing zero amps with a shaft that physically will not rotate
A failed boiler aquastat firing the boiler too long, which is contradicted because the limit correctly stops the boiler at 205°F with no flow

questions.explanation: Voltage present with zero amps and a mechanically seized shaft is a dead circulator; with no flow, boiler heat has nowhere to go and the limit does its job. Air binding does not seize a shaft, simultaneous zone-valve failure does not fit the pump evidence, and the aquastat/limit behaved correctly.

questions.question: A supply duct crosses an unconditioned garage in a cold climate carrying warm air in winter. It is insulated, but the insulation stops short at each hanger and at the register boot connections, leaving bare metal bands. Besides heat loss in winter, what problem do those bare bands create in summer cooling?

answers.text: Bare bands make the duct too warm in summer for condensation ever to occur
The bands will freeze the supply air solid where insulation is missing

In cooling, the bare bands are cold surfaces exposed to humid garage air with no vapor barrier, so they become the first places condensation forms and drips, even though the rest of the duct is protected

Missing insulation at hangers only matters for appearance once the duct is painted, since the bare bands are too narrow to lose meaningful heat, collect meaningful moisture, or affect the rooms served, even when humid summer air washes over them for months at a time

questions.explanation: Continuity is the point of an insulation and vapor-barrier system: any exposed cold band is a condensing surface, regardless of how well the rest of the run is wrapped. Option A is wrong because in cooling the duct surface is cold, not warm — that is precisely why humid air condenses on it; option B is wrong because supply air at normal cooling temperatures does not freeze, and no solid ice forms inside the duct; option D is wrong because dripping condensate on garage contents and corrosion of the duct are functional failures, not appearance issues.

questions.question: A thermostatic expansion valve system is specified to run at 12 degrees F subcooling. After airflow is verified and the system stabilizes, condensing saturation temperature is 110 degrees F and liquid-line temperature is 104 degrees F. What should the technician do?

answers.text: Add charge in small amounts and recheck, because measured subcooling is only 6 degrees F, below the 12-degree target
Recover charge, because measured subcooling is above the target
Leave the charge alone, because any subcooling above zero is correct for a TXV system, no matter how far the measured value sits below the subcooling target specified for this equipment
Adjust the TXV superheat setting to raise subcooling to the target

questions.explanation: Subcooling is 110 minus 104, or 6 degrees F, and on a TXV system low subcooling is corrected by adding charge in small increments with stabilization between checks. Option B is backwards because subcooling is low, not high, option C ignores the specified target that ensures a solid liquid seal at the valve, and option D confuses the valve superheat setting with the charge-controlled subcooling value.

questions.question: Comfort complaint. A system satisfies its thermostat in about seven minutes and shuts off while far bedrooms remain 4 degrees warm. The thermostat sits on a wall directly in the discharge path of a nearby supply register, and a thermometer held at the thermostat reads several degrees cooler than a thermometer in the room center while the system runs. Between cycles the two readings converge. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: An oversized air conditioner short-cycling on capacity, which would satisfy the whole house's sensible load quickly and would not leave the thermostat reading colder than the room only while air is moving
A thermostat with a drifting sensor reading low, which would read off from room temperature at all times, including between cycles when these two readings converge
Supply air washing over the thermostat and satisfying it early
A weak compressor losing capacity mid-cycle, which would lengthen rather than shorten run times and would warm the supply air instead of cooling the thermostat's wall

questions.explanation: Discharge air blows straight onto the thermostat, cooling its sensor below true room temperature while the system runs, so it satisfies in minutes while distant rooms stay warm; between cycles the sensor recovers and readings converge. Oversizing satisfies the whole space, not just the thermostat wall, a drifting sensor would disagree with room temperature at rest too, and a weak compressor extends run time instead of cutting it to seven minutes.

ohio-hvac.quiz_title: Ohio HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How does a capillary tube or fixed-orifice metering device differ from a thermostatic expansion valve?

answers.text: It actively senses superheat at the evaporator outlet with a remote bulb and adjusts flow continuously to hold a preset superheat under all load conditions
It contains a sensing bulb and external equalizer
It uses a diaphragm and push pins to modulate flow
It is a fixed restriction with no moving parts and no superheat control, so superheat varies with load and charge

questions.explanation: A capillary tube or fixed orifice is simply a fixed restriction; flow changes only with pressure difference, so superheat floats with conditions. Options A, B, and C all describe parts or behavior of a thermostatic expansion valve, not a fixed restriction.

questions.question: A large commercial restroom with a row of water closets needs a makeup-air path for its exhaust fan. Which arrangement works?

answers.text: Seal the restroom completely — undercut, grille, and gaps all closed — so the exhaust fan can pull the room to its deepest possible vacuum, caulking every wall joint and fitting a sealed, gasketed door with a closer that pulls it fully shut against the frame
Vent the exhaust fan into the corridor ceiling so the corridor, rather than the restroom, receives the odors being removed
Provide transfer air — a door undercut, transfer grille, or ducted path sized so makeup air can enter as the fan exhausts, keeping the room slightly negative to contain odors
Supply the restroom with more air than the fan exhausts so odors are pushed out into the corridor whenever the door is opened

questions.explanation: Exhaust can only remove the air that can get in; a sized transfer path keeps flow moving and the room negative to its neighbors. Option A starves the fan so it moves little air, option B relocates the contaminant to another occupied space, and option D pressurizes the odorous room in exactly the wrong direction.

questions.question: In a ground-source (geothermal) heat pump system in heating mode, the ground loop does what?

answers.text: Burns a small amount of fuel underground to warm the circulating fluid before it returns to the heat pump indoors
Supplies all of the building's heating energy by itself, so the compressors in the heat pumps never need to run at all
Absorbs low-grade heat from the earth and delivers it to the heat pumps' source-side heat exchangers
Rejects the building's heat to the earth, which is the loop's function in every season including the middle of winter

questions.explanation: In heating, the loop is the heat source: circulating fluid picks up earth heat and carries it to the units, which upgrade it with the compressor. Option A invents underground combustion that does not exist, option B ignores that the compressor does the work of lifting the heat, and option D describes the loop's cooling-mode role, not its heating role.

questions.question: In an oil burner primary control system, what does the cad cell do?

answers.text: It pumps oil from the tank to the nozzle through the suction line, using the gear set in the fuel unit to raise the oil to atomizing pressure
It generates the spark for ignition
It senses light from the flame, and its resistance drops when flame is present, telling the primary control combustion is established
It opens the oil solenoid valve on a call for heat

questions.explanation: The cad cell is a light-sensitive resistor: bright flame lowers its resistance and proves flame to the primary control. Option A describes the fuel unit (oil pump). Option B describes the ignition transformer or igniter. Option D describes the solenoid valve, which the control may energize but which does not sense flame.

questions.question: On a 100 degree F day, a rooftop technician feels dizzy, nauseated, and stops sweating. What is the best immediate response?

answers.text: Push through to finish the job quickly
Drink an energy drink and keep working on the roof
Stop work, move to shade or a cool area, cool the person, and seek emergency care for suspected heat stroke
Wait alone on the roof until symptoms pass

questions.explanation: Dizziness, nausea, and stopped sweating in extreme heat signal possible heat stroke, a life-threatening emergency requiring stopping work, cooling, and emergency care, so C is correct. Continuing work or relying on an energy drink worsens the condition, and waiting alone on a hot roof delays treatment and adds fall risk.

questions.question: In a classic stack-relay primary control, what event causes the control to keep the burner running after the trial-for-ignition period?

answers.text: The thermostat contacts cooling and opening at the end of the call for heat, which mechanically latches the stack relay closed until the next heating cycle begins
The cad cell heating the bimetal switch
Room air rising past the limit control
Heat from flue gases warming a heat-sensitive element in the stack switch, which holds the safety switch in the run position

questions.explanation: Stack controls prove flame by flue-gas heat: the stack element warms, expands, and holds the control in run; if heat does not rise, the safety switch trips. Option A ends the call for heat rather than proving flame. Option B mixes two systems, because cad cells are electronic sensors used with electronic primaries, not stack relays. Option C describes the limit control's normal heat sensing, not flame proof.

questions.question: CSST runs through a house with several metal systems. The bonding jumper for the CSST is installed primarily to:

answers.text: Carry the normal return current of the HVAC circuits, so that a separate equipment grounding conductor is no longer needed for the furnace
Replace the grounding electrode conductor for the whole house, because bonding the gas tubing satisfies every grounding requirement by itself
Equalize electrical potential and reduce arcing damage from induced voltage
Prevent corrosion of the tubing by draining stray direct current from the gas line into the soil outside the building foundation wall

questions.explanation: Equalize electrical potential and reduce arcing damage from induced voltage. Bonding does not carry circuit return current, replace the service grounding system, or serve as a corrosion drain to soil.

questions.question: A crew is about to work from a scaffold erected beside an air handler. Which condition must be met before the scaffold is used each shift?

answers.text: The scaffold only needs a fresh inspection when it is first erected, after which daily conditions such as weather and impacts cannot affect its safety
Workers may use the scaffold while it is still being moved into position, provided they hold the frame and keep their weight near the casters
Guardrails can be left off the top level whenever ductwork is being passed up, because material handling temporarily overrides fall protection needs
A competent person inspects it and footing and planking are sound

questions.explanation: Scaffolds are inspected by a competent person before each shift and after events that could affect them, with firm footing and proper planking and guardrails. One-time inspection misses later damage, riding a moving scaffold is prohibited practice, and material handling never suspends fall protection.

questions.question: Two years after being licensed as an HVAC contractor, a licensee is approved to sit for the refrigeration examination. Must he pass the business and law examination again?

answers.text: Yes, because the business and law examination must be passed separately for each trade, with no credit carried from one trade's licensure to another, even when the second trade's examination is taken well within three years of the first license.
No, because once both parts are passed, the business and law part counts as a passing score for three years from the date the first license is issued.
No, because a passed business and law part counts as a passing score for five years from the date the first license is issued under the chapter.
Yes, because business and law credit expires one year after it is earned, matching the one-year validity of the examination approval itself.

questions.explanation: B is correct: the examination consists of a trade part and a business and law part, seventy percent on each part is required, and once both parts are passed the business and law part is deemed a passing score for three years from the date the license is issued if the applicant is later approved to sit for another examination under the chapter. A is wrong because business and law credit does carry across trades within the stated period; it is not a per-trade examination each time. C is wrong because the credit period is three years, not five years. D is wrong because the one-year figure is the validity of an examination approval, not the life of a passed business and law part.

questions.question: A commercial facility applies chemicals in a process area served by a hazardous exhaust system, and the operator proposes cycling the exhaust off between applications to save energy. What do Ohio's provisions require?

answers.text: Ohio added a requirement that the controls keep the hazardous exhaust system operating at all times during chemical application, so cycling it off during application is not permitted

Ohio permits the exhaust to cycle freely during application, because the added control provision addresses only the hours when the facility is closed to the public and on weekends when staffing is reduced
Ohio deleted the hazardous exhaust control provisions, leaving run-time decisions entirely to the facility's own energy management policy and procedures
The exhaust may be cycled off during application if a portable fan is placed in the room, because Ohio recognizes portable ventilation as equivalent to the fixed system

questions.explanation: A is correct: Ohio's provisions add a section requiring controls so the hazardous exhaust system operates at all times during chemical application, so the system cannot be cycled off while chemicals are being applied. B is wrong because the added provision is aimed precisely at the application period, not closed hours. C is wrong because Ohio added, rather than deleted, this control requirement. D is wrong because a portable fan is not a substitute for the required fixed hazardous exhaust system operating during application.

questions.question: A hood passes its airflow test yet smoke still spills at the front edge over a charbroiler line. Which change most directly improves capture?

answers.text: Raise the exhaust rate until the kitchen is so negative that smoke is pulled away from the cooks and toward the dining room doors, and aim a portion of the kitchen exhaust toward the dining room to relieve the pressure felt at the pass window
Increase hood overhang over the appliances, add end (side) panels to block cross-drafts, and keep supply air from blowing across the hood face
Move the makeup-air diffusers directly in front of the hood and aim them downward so replacement air pushes the smoke upward
Remove the grease filters so the plume can enter the duct collar without any resistance at the hood's capture opening

questions.explanation: Capture improves with geometry and calm air around the plume: more overhang, side panels against cross-drafts, and undisturbed rising air. Option A trades spillage for a severe pressure problem, option C aims supply air to disrupt the plume it should protect, and option D removes required grease extraction while doing nothing for the spill at the edge.

questions.question: A supply duct in a crawlspace drips steadily in summer. Crawlspace dew point is about 68°F and a thermometer on the duct insulation surface reads 58°F. What is the diagnosis?

answers.text: The duct is leaking cold air that freezes crawlspace moisture into frost, which then melts and drips whenever the blower cycles off in the afternoon
Groundwater is wicking up through the duct supports and running down the duct, which is why the dripping follows the cooling season so closely
Condensate from the indoor coil is draining into the duct and out through its seams, collecting on the outside surface as it escapes the duct interior
Surface is below the dew point

questions.explanation: Any surface held at 58°F in air with a 68°F dew point will condense moisture continuously, so the duct surface is simply below the dew point. Leaking cold air would chill a spot rather than wet the whole surface, groundwater wicking does not track cooling runtime, and coil condensate belongs in the drain system, not spread over the duct exterior.

questions.question: An installer must choose between sealing a set of accessible metal duct joints with brush-on mastic alone, or mastic embedded with fiberglass mesh tape over the wider gaps at a fitting. When is the mesh-reinforced application the right call?

answers.text: Where gaps are wide or the joint can move slightly, the mesh bridges the opening and gives the mastic a reinforced membrane instead of a thin film that could crack across the gap

Mesh is only decorative and is used when the job will be photographed, giving the finished joints a neat woven pattern that looks professional in closeout pictures and inspection reports even though it adds nothing to how the seal itself performs
Mesh replaces the need for any mechanical fastening of the joint
Mesh should be used dry, without mastic, as a stand-alone seal

questions.explanation: Mastic alone seals tight, well-fitted joints; reinforcing mesh lets the cured seal span and survive gaps and movement that would split an unreinforced coating. Option B is wrong because the mesh serves a structural role in the seal, not an appearance role; option C is wrong because sealant systems never substitute for screws, drives, or other mechanical joint fastening; option D is wrong because dry mesh is an open weave that leaks freely — the mastic is what makes it a seal.

questions.question: A room's design heating load requires 180 CFM of supply air, while its cooling load requires 260 CFM, and the branch will have one fixed duct size and damper setting. On what basis should the branch airflow be designed, and what handles the other season?

answers.text: Size it to the 180 CFM heating value, since heating always governs duct design
Size it to the average, 220 CFM, so both seasons are equally short
Install two separate branch ducts, one for each season, in every such room
Size the branch to deliver the larger requirement — 260 CFM for cooling — and let seasonal balancing trim delivery for heating, rather than sizing to the smaller value and starving cooling

questions.explanation: A single fixed branch must satisfy the season that needs it most; designing to the smaller load guarantees the room fails in the governing season. Option A is wrong because cooling governs here because 260 exceeds 180 — whichever load is larger sets the branch, not a fixed rule for heating; option B is wrong because averaging underserves both seasons and fully satisfies neither; option C is wrong because duplicate seasonal branches are not standard practice; one correctly sized branch with balancing serves both.

questions.question: An owner wants time-and-materials work but is concerned about an open-ended total. What contract feature best addresses that concern?

answers.text: A clause that lets the contractor extend the schedule indefinitely without notifying the owner of any delay
A not-to-exceed cap that requires approval to go beyond it
An agreement to stop keeping time records once the job passes the halfway point of the estimated duration
A promise that material will be billed at a later date, so its cost does not appear in the running job total

questions.explanation: B is correct because a not-to-exceed cap limits the owner's exposure and requires approval before the cap is exceeded. A is incorrect because indefinite schedule extension does not control the total cost. C is incorrect because abandoning time records removes the basis for time-and-materials billing. D is incorrect because deferring material billing hides, rather than caps, the true total.

questions.question: Attic air temperature measures 105°F, but an uninsulated supply duct in that attic gains heat faster than attic air temperature alone predicts. The roof deck above it measures 145°F. What additional transfer path is at work?

answers.text: Convection currents from the attic floor insulation are rising through the duct wall and carrying stored heat from the ceiling below into the airstream
The duct metal is generating heat by friction as air moves through it, an effect that grows stronger directly under the hottest part of the roof deck
Ultraviolet light passing through the roof deck is heating the duct directly, because shingles and decking transmit most solar radiation into the attic
Radiant gain from hot roof deck

questions.explanation: A 145°F roof deck radiates heat directly to the duct surface, adding a radiant load on top of conduction from 105°F attic air. Floor insulation does not convect stored ceiling heat into a duct, friction heating at duct velocities is negligible, and roof assemblies block rather than transmit most solar radiation as light.

questions.question: A converted propane furnace has correct manifold pressure, yet temperature rise is well above the rating plate range. What should the technician verify next about the firing rate?

answers.text: Only the thermostat anticipator or cycle rate, because correct manifold pressure guarantees correct input no matter which orifices or gas the burners are using
That the vent connector is one size smaller than listed, because restricting the vent is the approved way to trim an excessive temperature rise on a converted furnace
The installed orifice size against the rating plate for propane at that altitude
The color of the flame through the sight glass only, because a blue flame proves the input is correct even when measured temperature rise is outside the plate range

questions.explanation: Manifold pressure alone does not set input; the orifice size for the fuel and altitude must also match the rating plate, and a wrong orifice can overfire at correct pressure. Thermostat settings and flame color cannot prove firing rate, and downsizing a vent is never a method for trimming input or temperature rise.

questions.question: No-cool call. The control board's cooling terminal delivers 24 V leaving the air handler, the indoor blower runs, but the outdoor contactor shows 0 V at its coil. The coil itself ohms at 14 ohms in its normal range, and pushing the contactor in manually starts the outdoor unit, which then cools normally. Continuity testing of the outdoor control cable shows one conductor open, with chewed insulation found at the wall penetration. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A failed contactor coil that cannot pull in, ruled out because the coil ohms in its normal range and the unit runs correctly when the contactor is pushed in by hand
An open conductor in the control cable to the outdoor unit
A control board relay that never sends the cooling signal, ruled out because 24 V is measured leaving the board on its cooling terminal during the call
A float switch holding the outdoor unit off, which would show its contacts open at the pan rather than an open conductor with chewed insulation at the wall penetration

questions.explanation: Signal leaves the board at 24 V and never arrives; the coil is good, the unit runs when the contactor is closed manually, and continuity testing finds the open conductor with physical damage at the penetration. The coil, the board output, and the float switch are each ruled out by a direct measurement, leaving the broken control conductor.

questions.question: A new three-phase scroll compressor starts but is unusually loud, draws low amperage, and produces almost no pressure difference between suction and discharge. What is the most likely cause and correction?

answers.text: The compressor is running in reverse because two power leads are swapped; correct the phase order and recheck operation
The system is overcharged; recover half the charge and restart it
The metering device is stuck closed; replace it before running the compressor again
The condenser fan is cycling; replace the fan control and leave the compressor wiring alone, then run the system again to see whether the pressure difference returns once fan operation is corrected

questions.explanation: A scroll running backwards cannot build pressure, sounds harsh, and draws low amps, and swapping any two line leads restores the correct rotation. Option B would create an undercharge without changing rotation, option C would still leave a reversed compressor unable to pump, and option D addresses the fan while the symptoms point to compressor rotation.

questions.question: A three-phase motor runs but vibrates and draws noticeably higher current on one leg, while average voltage looks normal. The supply shows a significant voltage imbalance between phases. What is the most likely effect if operation continues?

answers.text: No effect at all, because only the average voltage across the three legs matters to a three-phase motor and individual leg differences can safely be ignored
Automatic reversal of rotation until balance returns
Motor overheating and reduced life because current imbalance is much larger than voltage imbalance
Lower current on all legs because resistance rises evenly

questions.explanation: Even a modest voltage imbalance produces a much larger current imbalance and extra heating, which shortens motor life. Average voltage alone does not protect the motor. Imbalance does not reverse rotation, and heating and current do not fall evenly across all legs.

south-carolina-hvac.quiz_title: South Carolina HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Inside an evaporator coil, most of the cooling of the air passing over the coil is accomplished by refrigerant that is:

answers.text: Being subcooled as a liquid in the last passes of the condenser coil before it reaches the metering device outdoors
Being compressed as a vapor
Flowing through the metering device
Boiling from a liquid to a vapor at low pressure, absorbing heat from the air

questions.explanation: Low-pressure liquid boils in the evaporator and the latent heat for that change of state comes from the air, which is the cooling effect. Subcooling in option A happens in the condenser and removes heat outdoors, compression in option B adds work in the compressor, and option C occurs before the evaporator, not inside it.

questions.question: Why do kitchen grease exhaust fans typically discharge upward at the roof with grease containment at the fan?

answers.text: Because the building code requires all rooftop fans of every type to blow upward regardless of what airstream they are moving

Because a side-discharge fan would cool the grease too quickly, and warm grease is easier for the duct cleaners to remove later, which is why the fan curb for a grease fan is always specified taller than any other equipment curb on the roof
Because discharge direction is purely cosmetic and owners choose upblast fans only to match the other equipment on the roof
To throw grease-laden air up and away from the roof surface and intakes, with containment keeping discharged grease off the roof membrane

questions.explanation: Upblast discharge plus a grease collector protects the roof and nearby intakes from a flammable contaminant. Option A overgeneralizes a grease-specific practice to every fan, option B invents a grease-temperature rationale unrelated to fire and roof protection, and option C dismisses a safety-driven selection as decoration.

questions.question: In general terms, what is the purpose of a mechanic's lien?

answers.text: To guarantee that a project will be completed on its original schedule regardless of weather or supply delays
To secure payment for labor or materials furnished to improve property
To exempt the property owner from paying sales tax on equipment installed during the improvement project
To transfer ownership of installed equipment back to the supplier automatically at the end of the warranty period

questions.explanation: B is correct because a mechanic's lien is a security claim against the improved property for unpaid labor or materials. A is incorrect because a lien secures payment; it does not guarantee the schedule. C is incorrect because a lien has no effect on sales tax obligations. D is incorrect because a lien is a claim for payment, not an automatic transfer of equipment ownership.

questions.question: CSST runs through a house with several metal systems. The bonding jumper for the CSST is installed primarily to:

answers.text: Carry the normal return current of the HVAC circuits, so that a separate equipment grounding conductor is no longer needed for the furnace
Replace the grounding electrode conductor for the whole house, because bonding the gas tubing satisfies every grounding requirement by itself
Equalize electrical potential and reduce arcing damage from induced voltage
Prevent corrosion of the tubing by draining stray direct current from the gas line into the soil outside the building foundation wall

questions.explanation: Equalize electrical potential and reduce arcing damage from induced voltage. Bonding does not carry circuit return current, replace the service grounding system, or serve as a corrosion drain to soil.

questions.question: A concentric direct-vent kit passes both pipes through one wall penetration. Its field advantage is:

answers.text: The exhaust pipe can be omitted whenever the intake pipe is present, because the appliance can discharge flue gases around the intake annulus
The two air streams are mixed inside the kit before reaching the burner, so the furnace burns a blend of outdoor air and its own exhaust
The kit allows the vent to be run at any length without counting fittings, because a single penetration removes all equivalent-length limits
Intake and exhaust share one termination point as designed

questions.explanation: Intake and exhaust share one termination point as designed. The exhaust is not omitted, the streams are kept separate rather than mixed, and vent-length and fitting limits still apply to a concentric kit.

questions.question: Refrigerant that has been reclaimed differs from refrigerant that has merely been recovered or recycled because reclaimed refrigerant:

answers.text: Is simply removed from a system and stored in a recovery cylinder

Is cleaned on site, typically with filtration and oil separation, for reuse only in the same owner's equipment, without any laboratory analysis or verification that it meets virgin-product purity specifications for general resale
Has been reprocessed off site and verified by chemical analysis to meet virgin-product purity specifications, so it can be used in any owner's equipment
Is destroyed by high-temperature incineration

questions.explanation: Reclaim means reprocessing to virgin purity specifications with verified analysis, which is a higher standard than recovery or on-site recycling. Option A is the definition of recovery, option B is the definition of recycling, and option D describes destruction, not reclaim.

questions.question: A designer considers greatly oversizing a suction line to cut its pressure drop to near zero on a long run. The hidden penalty of a much-too-large suction line is:

answers.text: Refrigerant velocity falls so low that oil is not carried along and can log in the line and evaporator
Discharge pressure rises to match the larger pipe volume
The liquid line begins to flash in the condenser

Superheat at the compressor becomes impossible to measure because the larger pipe diameter prevents a service gauge and a temperature clamp from being attached to the suction line at the same service port location

questions.explanation: Suction sizing balances pressure drop against velocity; an oversized line drops velocity below what entrains oil, starving the compressor over time. Option B invents a link between suction pipe volume and discharge pressure, option C misplaces flashing, which occurs after a pressure drop in liquid, and option D is false because superheat is measured from pressure and temperature regardless of pipe size.

questions.question: A long flexible duct run sags between widely spaced supports and is compressed where it crosses a truss. What is the likely result and fix?

answers.text: Restore full support at close intervals and a fully extended, uncompressed duct to recover design airflow.
Leave the sag, because pooled low spots in flex duct increase velocity and therefore improve airflow to distant registers
Replace the flex duct with a longer run routed in a wide loop, since extra length compensates for the pressure lost in sagging sections
Crush the duct further at the truss so it fits the space, because flex duct airflow is unaffected by changes in its internal diameter

questions.explanation: Sagging and compression add friction and sharply cut airflow; proper support and full extension restore the duct's rated performance. Sag does not raise useful velocity, extra length adds more loss, and crushing reduces the flow area the duct depends on.

questions.question: An oil burner gradually starves and locks out as the tank empties past half, and the tank top is slightly drawn inward. Vacuum readings are excessive. What is the likely cause?

answers.text: A nozzle one size too large, which consumes oil faster than gravity can replace it in the tank during long firing cycles
A deaerator that returns too much oil, pressurizing the tank and forcing the burner pump into a flooded suction condition
An oversized vent alarm tube that lets too much air escape during firing, pulling the tank into a deep vacuum by itself alone
A blocked tank vent creating vacuum

questions.explanation: A blocked vent prevents air from entering as oil leaves, so vacuum builds, the tank can deform inward, and the pump eventually cannot draw fuel. Option A describes consumption rate, not vacuum, option B reverses deaerator return behavior, and option C treats the alarm as a firing vent, which it is not.

questions.question: With a blower door holding the house at -50 Pa with respect to outdoors, an attached garage zone reads -25 Pa with respect to outdoors. How should this zonal reading be interpreted?

answers.text: The garage is connected only to the house, because any reading below zero means the zone has no openings at all to the outdoors or to other zones
The garage is connected only to outdoors, since an intermediate reading is produced when a zone is fully vented and the gauge averages house and outdoor pressure
Garage connects to both sides
The reading is a gauge error, because a zone can only ever read either the full house pressure or zero, never a stable value in between the two

questions.explanation: A reading halfway between house and outdoor pressure indicates the garage has meaningful connections to both the house and outdoors, splitting its pressure between them. A house-only connection would read near -50 Pa, an outdoors-only connection would read near zero, and stable intermediate zonal readings are a normal, informative result of the method.

questions.question: In a pressure-pan survey with the house depressurized to -50 Pa, most registers read between 1 and 3 Pa in magnitude. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: Every register is leaking badly to the attic, because any measurable pan pressure at all proves the boot has separated from the duct behind the ceiling
The ducts are disconnected inside the walls, since a connected duct would pull the pan reading all the way up to the full 50 Pa house pressure
Ducts are well sealed to outdoors
The blower door was set to the wrong pressure, because valid pressure-pan readings must always fall between 20 and 30 Pa regardless of duct condition

questions.explanation: Pan readings near zero mean each register is connected mainly to the house and poorly connected to outdoors, the signature of ducts well sealed to outside. Bad leakage to outside drives readings toward the house pressure, a disconnected duct leaking outside would also read high rather than explain low readings, and there is no fixed 20 to 30 Pa valid band for this test.

questions.question: A pressure-pan survey shows readings of 2 to 4 Pa at most registers, but every register fed by one attic trunk reads 30 Pa or more. Where should sealing effort be focused first?

answers.text: Leak is on that trunk run
Every register boot in the house should be resealed first, because uniform low readings elsewhere prove the boots are the weakest point in the whole system
The return plenum at the air handler is the priority, since high supply-register readings are generated by return leakage pulling the pans toward outdoor pressure
The duct tester fan needs recalibration, because a cluster of high readings on one run is a known sign of instrument drift during a long survey

questions.explanation: Pan readings cluster by duct run, so one trunk with uniformly high readings is strongly connected to outdoors and is where the leakage, and the sealing effort, belongs. Low readings elsewhere argue against a house-wide boot problem, return leakage does not create this supply-trunk pattern, and consistent clustering by run points to the duct, not instrument drift.

questions.question: A technician ohm-tests a cad cell in a brightly burning oil flame and reads a very high resistance, nearly the same as in darkness. The burner locks out on safety shortly after light-off. The correct conclusion is:

answers.text: The cad cell or its sighting/wiring is faulty, so the control cannot see a flame that is actually present
The nozzle is oversized for the firing rate, delivering more oil than the chamber was designed for and producing an oversized flame that overheats the cad cell
The stack draft is excessively high
The oil supply contains too much air

questions.explanation: A good cad cell in flame should read low resistance, typically a few hundred to about 1,500 ohms; a dark-level reading in flame means the cell is dirty, misaimed, failed, or its leads are open. Option B changes firing rate but would not keep cell resistance high. Option C affects combustion efficiency, not light sensing. Option D causes flame sputter, not a stable flame the cell cannot see.

questions.question: A furnace blower is rated to deliver design airflow at a maximum total external static pressure of 0.80 in. w.g. The wet evaporator coil drops 0.28, the filter drops 0.12, and the supply and return grilles together drop 0.08. How much static pressure remains available for the ductwork itself?

answers.text: 0.48 in. w.g., because only the coil loss is subtracted from the blower rating
0.80 in. w.g., because component losses are included in the blower rating already
0.20 in. w.g., because the filter loss must be subtracted twice, once per side

questions.explanation: An external static budget subtracts every non-duct component from what the blower can overcome; what is left is what the duct runs may consume. Option A is wrong because subtracting only the coil leaves the filter and grille losses unaccounted for, so the ducts would be sized with pressure that does not exist; option C is wrong because the blower rating is a total budget for everything external to the unit, not a duct-only allowance; option D is wrong because the filter is a single component with one pressure drop, counted once.

questions.question: A Group 3 mechanical licensee with documented net worth of $35,000 is offered a single $210,000 project in its classification. The owner argues the firm's net worth is more than enough, so the job should be allowed. How should the licensee respond?

answers.text: Accept the job, because once net worth exceeds the group minimum by any amount, the job-cost ceiling for that group no longer limits the size of a single project
Accept the job if the owner signs a waiver, because a private agreement between the parties can expand a license group's statutory job limit for one project at a time
Decline or qualify higher first, because Group 3 caps a job at $200,000, and moving to Group 4 requires net worth of $60,000 or working capital of $40,000, which this firm does not show

Decline the job permanently, because a licensee that is once offered work above its group limit loses the ability to upgrade its group at any later renewal or application, no matter how strong its later financial statements become or how the project itself is structured

questions.explanation: C is correct: a licensee is confined to its group's job-cost limits; Group 3 ends at $200,000, so a $210,000 job requires Group 4, whose financial test is net worth of $60,000 or working capital of $40,000 — above this firm's $35,000 net worth. A is wrong because exceeding a minimum does not erase the separate job ceiling. B is wrong because a private waiver cannot expand a statutory license limit. D is wrong because nothing bars the firm from later qualifying in a higher group.

questions.question: A public toilet room in a Spartanburg office building contains four water closets. The mechanical code exhaust rate for this room is 70 cfm per water closet. What exhaust airflow must the room's exhaust system provide?

answers.text: The room requires 280 cfm of exhaust: four water closets x 70 cfm per water closet = 280 cfm of exhaust airflow for the room
The room requires 70 cfm of exhaust, because the per-fixture rate is a single flat quantity that covers the whole room regardless of fixture count
The room requires 140 cfm of exhaust, found by counting only two of the four water closets because adjoining fixtures share one exhaust allowance in the table
The room requires 560 cfm of exhaust, found by applying the per-fixture rate twice to each water closet to cover both the bowl and the room volume

questions.explanation: A is correct: the exhaust requirement scales with fixture count: 4 water closets x 70 cfm = 280 cfm. B is wrong because the 70 cfm figure is a per-fixture rate, not a flat whole-room allowance. C is wrong because every water closet in the room counts toward the exhaust total; fixtures do not share an allowance. D is wrong because the rate is applied once per fixture, not doubled.

questions.question: A two-zone system with a single-stage blower serves a small zone calling alone. Airflow noise rises sharply. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: The thermostat is set too low
Return ducts are oversized
Full blower airflow is forced through only the open zone ducts, raising velocity and static
Zone dampers always reduce total static pressure, even when only one small zone is calling and the other damper is fully closed

questions.explanation: With one zone closed, full airflow through half the duct system raises velocity and static, causing noise, so C is correct. Thermostat setting and oversized returns do not explain it, and D is false because closing dampers raises, not lowers, static unless airflow is reduced or bypassed properly.

questions.question: A house has two duct leakage problems: a disconnected supply branch blowing into the attic, and a leaky return plenum in the same attic. Both leak roughly the same amount of air. Why is the return leak usually the bigger comfort and energy problem on a peak summer afternoon?

answers.text: The return leak pressurizes the attic, which forces heat through the ceiling

Return leaks do not matter because the fan simply pulls the same air back out of the house, since any air drawn in at the plenum mixes with house air returning through the grilles and reaches the coil at essentially the same temperature and moisture content as normal return air

The return leak pulls superheated attic air directly into the system, adding a large sensible and moisture load the equipment must remove, while the supply leak mainly wastes air that was already conditioned
The supply leak is harmless because the attic eventually returns that air to the house

questions.explanation: Air entering a return leak comes from wherever the return sits — on a summer afternoon that is the hottest, most humid air available — and it becomes an added load on every pass through the system. Option A is wrong because a return leak does not work by pressurizing the attic and forcing ceiling heat flow; the mechanism is hot air entering the airstream directly; option B is wrong because air pulled from the attic is not house air recirculating; it is new hot, humid air the system must condition; option D is wrong because conditioned air blown into a vented attic is lost to the outdoors, not recovered by the house.

questions.question: A boiler's relief valve (30 psi) discharges on nearly every heating cycle. System pressure reads 12 psi cold but climbs to 29 psi at temperature; tapping the expansion tank shows it heavy and waterlogged with no air cushion, and the fill valve holds a steady 12 psi with no creep when the boiler is cold and isolated. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A leaking fill (pressure-reducing) valve, which would creep the cold pressure upward too, but cold pressure here holds steady at 12 psi when isolated
A waterlogged expansion tank
An overheating aquastat driving pressure up with temperature, when boiler temperature is verified within its normal operating range during these cycles
An undersized relief valve, which is a standard 30 psi residential valve correctly opening only when system pressure truly reaches its rating

questions.explanation: Pressure that is stable cold but soars hot means expanding water has no air cushion to absorb it — the tank is waterlogged. A leaking fill valve would raise cold pressure too, boiler temperature is normal, and the relief valve is honestly opening at its rating.

questions.question: A completed system delivers only 950 CFM against a 1,200 CFM design. Static readings show the duct system itself is within its budget, but total external static is well above the blower's rating point because the installed wet coil and filter drops are much higher than the values used in design. What went wrong at the design stage?

answers.text: The ducts shrank after installation, which raised the total static
The blower lost capacity because the thermostat was set to cooling
Nothing went wrong; blowers deliver design CFM at any external static

The static budget was built on optimistic component values instead of the actual selected coil's wet-coil drop and the real filter drop at design airflow, so the blower was asked to work beyond the point where it can deliver design CFM

questions.explanation: A blower delivers its rated airflow only up to its rated external static; if real component drops push the total past that point, airflow falls — and the budget is only as honest as the component data in it. Option A is wrong because installed sheet metal does not shrink; the discrepancy was in the design inputs, not the duct dimensions; option B is wrong because thermostat mode does not change a blower's pressure capability; option C is wrong because blower tables show airflow falling as static rises beyond the rating point — that relationship is the whole basis of the budget.

virginia-hvac.quiz_title: Virginia HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What does the float inside a typical discharge-line oil separator do when collected oil reaches its level?

answers.text: It closes the discharge line to the condenser so gas pressure builds in the separator shell and forces the collected oil out through the suction line
It opens a return line so oil flows back to the compressor crankcase
It energizes the crankcase heater so the returned oil is warmed before it is allowed to re-enter the compressor through the suction service valve
It opens a drain to a waste oil container so separated oil is removed from the refrigeration system permanently after each operating cycle

questions.explanation: The separator float rises with collected oil and ports it back to the crankcase, where it is reused. It does not block the main discharge flow to the condenser, it does not control the crankcase heater, and separated oil is returned for reuse rather than drained away as waste.

questions.question: After a three-phase condenser fan motor is replaced, it runs backward. What is the standard correction?

answers.text: Swap the run capacitor leads and reverse the thermostat Y wire
Swap any two of the three power leads to the motor
Reverse the transformer primary leads
Move all three leads one terminal clockwise

questions.explanation: Swapping any two line leads reverses the phase sequence and therefore rotation of a three-phase motor. Capacitor and thermostat wiring do not set three-phase rotation. Reversing a control transformer does not change motor rotation, and rotating all three leads preserves the same sequence.

questions.question: How does hot-gas defrost melt frost from an evaporator?

answers.text: Cold liquid refrigerant is sprayed over the outside of the coil
Hot discharge vapor is routed into the evaporator so its heat melts frost from inside the tubes
Room air is heated by a separate furnace and blown backward through the fans
The compressor is reversed so the condenser becomes the evaporator for a full cooling cycle

questions.explanation: Hot-gas defrost diverts warm compressor discharge vapor through the evaporator, warming the tubes so frost releases quickly. Option A would make the coil colder, option C invents a separate furnace system, and option D describes reverse-cycle operation rather than the hot-gas bypass used on these systems.

questions.question: On the shared journeyman and master HVAC portion, the test has 85 items and a 210-minute limit. What raw score must a journeyman candidate reach to pass?

answers.text: 64 correct answers, a figure the candidate may have seen quoted in connection with this same examination portion and its two license levels
60 correct answers, the raw passing score set for the journeyman level on this 85-item examination portion administered by the vendor
39 correct answers, a figure the candidate may have seen quoted in connection with a different HVAC examination portion in Virginia
72 correct answers, because the bulletin converts every tradesman passing score to a flat eighty-five percent of the items presented

questions.explanation: B is correct: journeyman and master candidates take the same 85-item, 210-minute portion, and the journeyman passing score is 60 correct. A is wrong because 64 is the master passing score on the same portion. C is wrong because 39 is the passing score for the separate Residential HVAC portion. D is wrong because the bulletin states raw passing scores, not a flat percentage conversion.

questions.question: Occupants report headaches and a carbon monoxide alarm is sounding. A technician is dispatched. What is the correct first protocol?

answers.text: Get occupants out, advise calling emergency services from outside, and do not re-enter or run appliances until the space is cleared by responders or verified safe.
Reset the alarm, open one window, and restart the furnace to see whether the alarm sounds again during a supervised test run
Tell occupants to stay indoors with the doors closed so the technician can measure an undisturbed carbon monoxide level on arrival
Move the alarm to another room to confirm it is not a faulty sensor before taking any other action on the service call

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide incidents are life-safety events: evacuate, summon emergency help, and keep combustion equipment off until cleared. Test-running a suspect appliance re-exposes occupants, staying inside for a cleaner measurement risks poisoning, and relocating the alarm delays the response to a possible real leak.

questions.question: What distinguishes self-contained (active) recovery equipment from system-dependent (passive) recovery equipment?

answers.text: Self-contained equipment has its own compressor or pump to draw refrigerant out of a system
Self-contained equipment relies entirely on the appliance compressor and pressure differences to move refrigerant
Self-contained equipment can only be used on appliances holding less than five pounds of refrigerant
Self-contained equipment recovers refrigerant as a liquid on every job regardless of system condition

questions.explanation: Self-contained equipment carries its own compressor or pump, so it can pull refrigerant from a system that is dead or leaking. Option B describes system-dependent equipment, which needs the appliance compressor or pressure differential to work. Option C is wrong because charge size does not define the equipment class, and option D is wrong because recovered phase depends on method and conditions, not on the machine alone.

questions.question: With the air handler running, a large supply trunk joint in the attic is found disconnected. The house measures slightly negative with respect to outdoors while the system runs. Why?

answers.text: The return grille is oversized, so the blower moves extra outdoor air into the house and the attic joint is merely venting that surplus air back outside
Supply air lost in the attic is replaced by air the return side no longer gets back, which would pressurize the house because the blower is still delivering its full rated flow

The house goes negative relative to outdoors, because supply air dumped into the attic never comes back through the return side, so the blower pulls replacement air in through leaks in the building shell
The disconnected joint acts like a second return that draws attic air into the supply stream and pushes the house positive whenever the blower runs

questions.explanation: Supply air dumped outside the envelope never returns, so the house loses air and drifts negative while the system runs. An oversized return grille does not import outdoor air, the lost supply cannot pressurize a house it is leaving, and a supply-side opening blows air out rather than drawing attic air in as a return would.

questions.question: A customer expects a UV-C lamp in the supply plenum to remove cooking odors, carbon monoxide, and dust from the house air. What is the accurate correction?

answers.text: UV-C inactivates microbes on irradiated surfaces and in the airstream within its limits; it does not remove particles, gases, odors, or carbon monoxide.
UV-C does remove odors and gases, so the customer's expectation is correct and no filtration or source control is needed in the home
UV-C replaces the air filter entirely, because irradiated dust is rendered harmless and may accumulate on the coil without consequence
UV-C generates fresh oxygen that neutralizes carbon monoxide in the duct, making a separate carbon monoxide alarm unnecessary

questions.explanation: UV-C is a disinfection technology with line-of-sight and dose limits, not a filter or gas remover. Odors and gases need ventilation and source control, filters are still required for particles and coil protection, and UV-C has no effect that substitutes for a carbon monoxide alarm.

questions.question: A contractor marks up a $1,000 job cost by 20% to set the price. What is the resulting price and its gross margin?

answers.text: $1,200 price; about 16.7% margin
$1,200 price and a 20.0 percent margin, because markup on cost and margin on price are always identical
$1,250 price and a 20.0 percent margin, found by using the margin divisor formula instead of the stated markup
$1,020 price and a 2.0 percent margin, found by adding the markup rate as a flat dollar amount

questions.explanation: A is correct because a 20 percent markup gives $1,200, and the $200 profit divided by $1,200 is about 16.7 percent margin. B is incorrect because a 20 percent markup does not produce a 20 percent margin. C is incorrect because it prices with the margin formula when the problem states a markup. D is incorrect because it treats 20 percent as $20 rather than 20 percent of $1,000.

questions.question: A firm holds both a contractor license and, through its Qualified Individual, a tradesman license, and assumes both run on the same cycle. How long is the contractor license's own term?

answers.text: Contractor licenses expire two years from the last day of the month in which issued, a shorter cycle than the tradesman license carries
Contractor licenses expire three years from the last day of the month in which issued, exactly matching the tradesman license cycle length
Contractor licenses expire one year from the last day of the month in which issued, because firm licenses renew more often than individual ones
Contractor licenses have no fixed term and remain valid indefinitely while the firm keeps the same designated employee and qualified individual

questions.explanation: A is correct: contractor licenses expire two years from the last day of the month in which issued, while HVAC tradesman licenses run three years, so the two cycles differ. B is wrong because three years is the tradesman figure, not the contractor figure. C is wrong because no one-year contractor term applies. D is wrong because the contractor license has a fixed two-year expiration.

questions.question: A vent table gives different capacities for the same vent diameter at different vent heights. Why does a taller vent usually carry more flue gas?

answers.text: A taller vent cools the flue gases so much that they become denser and fall upward through the connector by themselves
A taller vent raises gas pressure in the appliance, forcing more flue gas into the same connector regardless of temperature difference
Greater height strengthens draft
A taller vent eliminates connector resistance, so diameter and lateral length no longer matter in the sizing method

questions.explanation: Greater height strengthens draft. Cooling alone weakens draft, gas pressure does not drive venting, and connector resistance still counts in a taller system.

questions.question: A commercial kitchen exhaust system removes a large volume of air through its Type I hood. What does the mechanical code require regarding replacement (makeup) air?

answers.text: Makeup air is optional, because the building's general ventilation system will always supply enough air through door undercuts to satisfy a commercial hood of any size
Makeup air need only be supplied when the kitchen is in a basement, because grade-level kitchens can draw replacement air through the dining room without a dedicated system

Replacement air must be supplied, roughly in balance with the exhaust, and where it is introduced at the hood it must not be so cold that it disrupts capture; the code limits the temperature difference between makeup air and the room to 10 degrees F unless the air is part of the air-conditioning supply
Makeup air must exceed the exhaust rate by at least 25 percent so the kitchen stays at a positive pressure that pushes odors into the dining area for removal at the front of the house

questions.explanation: C is correct: commercial kitchen exhaust systems require makeup air approximately equal to the exhaust, and makeup air discharged into the hood area must be tempered so its temperature is not more than 10 degrees F below the room temperature (unless supplied as part of the air-conditioning system), so it does not defeat hood capture. A is wrong because dedicated makeup air is required, not optional. B is wrong because the requirement is not limited to basement kitchens. D is wrong because the kitchen is kept near neutral to slightly negative relative to dining areas, and excess pressurization is not required.

questions.question: A 5-ton system serves a 1,250 sq ft home whose calculated load is 2 tons. It satisfies the thermostat in 6-minute cycles, indoor humidity sits at 68%, supply air is cold, and all pressures, superheat, subcooling, and airflow per ton are normal. Occupants complain the home feels clammy. What is the correct diagnosis?

answers.text: Oversized equipment short-cycling
A blower speed set far too low, which would lengthen runtimes and wring out more moisture, the opposite of the 6-minute cycles observed
A dirty evaporator coil reducing dehumidification, which would distort airflow and superheat readings that here are entirely normal
Low refrigerant charge causing poor latent removal, which is contradicted by the normal superheat, subcooling, and pressures measured on this call

questions.explanation: Normal refrigerant readings with very short cycles and high indoor humidity are the signature of gross oversizing: sensible load is met before the coil runs long enough to remove latent load. Charge, blower speed, and coil condition all show normal measurements, and low blower speed would extend runtime rather than shorten it.

questions.question: On a furnace changeout, the only gas shutoff valve for the new appliance is nine feet away, around a corner in the next room, behind stored boxes. What does fuel-gas installation practice under the mechanical code require instead?

answers.text: The valve is acceptable because any shutoff within the same building satisfies the requirement for service access to the appliance
A shutoff valve must be located in the same room as the appliance, within six feet of it, and accessible for operation and service
A second shutoff must be added at the meter, after which the remote interior valve location no longer matters for compliance
The valve may stay if it is painted a bright color and tagged, because visibility substitutes for the distance requirement

questions.explanation: B is correct: each appliance must have an accessible shutoff valve in the same room, within 6 feet of the appliance it serves, so fuel can be cut quickly for service or an emergency. A is wrong because 'same building' is far looser than the same-room, six-foot rule. C is wrong because a meter valve does not replace the required appliance shutoff at the appliance. D is wrong because painting and tagging do not cure a valve that is too far away and obstructed by storage.

questions.question: A variable-speed drive slows a chilled-water pump to 90% of full speed. Using the pump affinity laws, about how much pump power is saved?

answers.text: About 3%, because pump power falls only in direct one-to-one proportion to the drop in pump rotational speed
About 10%, because pump power falls in proportion to the square of the speed ratio at reduced flow conditions
About 19%, because pump head and pump power always change by exactly the same percentage as each other
About 27%, because power varies with the cube of speed: 0.9 cubed is about 0.73 of full power
