questions.explanation: Power follows the cube law: 0.9^3 = 0.729, so roughly 27% of the power is saved. Option A uses the flow relationship, option B uses the head (square) relationship, and option C wrongly equates head and power changes, which follow different exponents.

questions.question: Outdoor temperature has fallen well below the point where a heat pump alone can carry the house, and indoor temperature is dropping despite the compressor running continuously. What should the control bring on?

answers.text: The defrost board, as the sole source of heat
Auxiliary electric strip heat, staged with the heat pump still running to meet the load
The outdoor fan at higher speed to extract more heat
Emergency heat only, with the compressor locked out for the entire winter whenever outdoor temperatures fall below freezing

questions.explanation: Below the balance point the heat pump keeps running and auxiliary strips stage on to make up the shortfall, option B. The defrost board (A) controls defrost timing and is not a heat source, faster outdoor fan speed (C) cannot create capacity the cycle lacks at that temperature, and emergency heat with compressor lockout (D) is reserved for compressor failure or manual selection, not routine cold weather.

questions.question: A technician must open a disconnect enclosure on a large air handler where an arc-flash hazard exists. The unit can be shut down for the task. What is the safest course?

answers.text: De-energize, lock out, and verify absence of voltage before touching conductors
Work energized with insulated gloves alone, because shutting the unit down for a short inspection task creates more schedule risk than electrical risk
Open the enclosure quickly and keep one hand in a pocket, a technique that by itself brings the arc-flash exposure within acceptable limits
Have a coworker hold a flashlight from the doorway, since having a second person nearby is the main control required for energized electrical work

questions.explanation: Putting equipment in an electrically safe condition by de-energizing, locking out, and testing removes the arc-flash exposure for the task. Gloves alone do not control arc energy, hand position is not a substitute for de-energizing, and a bystander with a flashlight provides no protective control.

questions.question: A 15 kW electric furnace has three equal 5 kW elements. On a heat call all sequencer contacts close, supply voltage is correct, but total current draw equals only two-thirds of the expected value and supply air is cooler than normal. What is the most likely fault?

answers.text: One heating element is open and producing no heat
The sequencer is energizing an extra element
The blower is running too fast for any heating to occur
The thermostat is set to emergency heat on a gas furnace

questions.explanation: Losing exactly one of three equal elements removes one-third of capacity and current while voltage and controls remain normal, matching option A. An extra element (B) would raise current above expected, blower speed (C) affects temperature rise but not element current, and the system described (D) is electric resistance heat, not a gas furnace.

questions.question: A condensate drain line is installed dead level for a long run and plugs with slime every season. What installation defect is most likely?

answers.text: The line was made from approved drain material instead of thin-wall tubing that stays warmer and therefore resists biological growth
The drain terminates at an approved receptor instead of discharging directly onto the roof membrane below the condensing unit
The trap was installed at the unit rather than at the far end of the run near the floor drain, where traps are most effective
The line lacks continuous downward slope in the direction of flow.

questions.explanation: Condensate drains must fall continuously, about an eighth inch per foot, so water and debris do not stand in the line. Approved material and an approved receptor are correct practice, not defects, and the trap belongs at the unit to prevent air issues.

questions.question: One bedroom is always warm in cooling while the rest of the house is comfortable. Its register delivers about 18 CFM against a design of roughly 95 CFM; all other registers measure near design, system static pressure is normal, and the branch damper is verified open. In the attic, that bedroom's flex duct makes a sharp bend at a truss and is visibly crushed where it crosses it. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: The kinked and crushed flex branch duct serving that room
A system-wide airflow shortage from the blower, which would depress airflow at every register in the house rather than leave all but one branch at its design flow
A closed zone damper starving one side of the house, ruled out because the branch damper is verified open and neighboring branches on the same trunk measure normally
An undersized supply trunk for the whole system, which would show elevated static pressure and broadly weak registers instead of one crushed branch at normal static

questions.explanation: Only the one branch is starved, total static is normal, and the physical inspection finds that branch kinked and crushed at a truss, throttling its roughly 95 CFM design flow down to 18 CFM. A blower or trunk problem would depress many registers and change static pressure, and the branch damper is proven open.

tennessee-hvac.quiz_title: Tennessee HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: When does a TXV need an external equalizer connection?

answers.text: On every installation regardless of coil size, because an internally equalized valve cannot operate at all unless an external equalizer line is also connected
Only when the system uses a suction accumulator, because the accumulator creates the pressure drop that the external equalizer is designed to compensate for
When evaporator pressure drop is significant, as with a distributor or a large coil
Only on systems with a liquid receiver, because the receiver pressure must be sensed at the valve diaphragm for the valve to open against spring pressure

questions.explanation: With a distributor or large coil, outlet pressure is well below inlet pressure, so the valve must sense true outlet pressure through an external equalizer to hold correct superheat. Small coils with negligible drop work with internal equalization, the accumulator is downstream protection rather than the reason for equalizing, and the equalizer senses evaporator outlet pressure, not receiver pressure.

questions.question: After responders clear a carbon monoxide incident, what must happen before the gas furnace returns to normal service?

answers.text: The furnace may restart immediately once the alarm stops, because silence proves the earlier reading was a transient sensor malfunction
Only the thermostat batteries need changing, since low batteries are the most common cause of genuine carbon monoxide production in furnaces
A qualified technician must find and correct the source, verify safe combustion and venting, and confirm carbon monoxide is not being produced or spilled.
The vent connector should be sealed with tape and the furnace run at high fire for an hour to burn out any residue in the heat exchanger

questions.explanation: Clearing the building air does not fix the appliance fault; the cause, such as a blocked vent, cracked heat exchanger, or negative-pressure spillage, must be repaired and verified. A silent alarm does not prove safety, batteries do not cause carbon monoxide production, and taping a vent and over-firing a suspect furnace is dangerous.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a submittal in project documentation?

answers.text: To record daily weather and crew size so the project schedule can be reconstructed at the end of the job
To request final payment and certify that every item on the punch list has already been completed and accepted
To release retainage early in exchange for storing equipment off site rather than at the project location
To show the equipment and materials proposed for approval before installation

questions.explanation: D is correct because submittals present proposed products and data for review and approval before they are installed. A is incorrect because daily conditions are recorded in daily reports, not submittals. B is incorrect because final payment requests and punch completion occur at closeout, after installation. C is incorrect because retainage release and stored materials are payment matters, not the purpose of a submittal.

questions.question: On a mild spring morning in Nashville, outdoor air is cooler and drier than the return air in a small commercial building served by a packaged unit with an economizer. How should the economizer respond to the cooling call?

answers.text: It should close the outdoor-air damper fully so the compressor alone handles the entire cooling load for the rest of the occupied period that day
It should open the relief damper and hold the outdoor-air damper at its minimum position all day
It should bring in up to full outdoor air for free cooling, reducing or replacing mechanical cooling as conditions allow
It should start the heating circuit to temper the outdoor air before admitting any of it to the building

questions.explanation: C is correct: an economizer uses favorable outdoor air as the first stage of cooling, modulating the outdoor-air damper up to full open when outdoor conditions are suitable, which cuts compressor run time. A is wrong because closing the damper discards the free-cooling opportunity the economizer exists to capture. B is wrong because holding minimum position is the response for unsuitable outdoor conditions, not favorable ones. D is wrong because no heating is needed when the outdoor air itself satisfies the cooling demand.

questions.question: Which statement correctly states the net positive suction head (NPSH) requirement for a pump?

answers.text: Available NPSH must exceed the pump's required NPSH, with margin, at the actual operating flow
Required NPSH is a property of the piping only and is never published by the pump manufacturer for a given flow rate
Available NPSH must be kept as low as possible so the pump inlet stays close to the water's vapor pressure at all times
NPSH matters only for steam condensate pumps and has no bearing on chilled-water or condenser-water pumps of any size

questions.explanation: The system must deliver more inlet head than the pump requires at that flow or the pump cavitates. Option B reverses the roles, since required NPSH comes from the manufacturer's pump curve, option C invites exactly the flashing that causes cavitation, and option D wrongly exempts hydronic pumps from a basic suction requirement.

questions.question: A long yard line serves a house from an outdoor tank, and appliance pressure used to swing widely between a cold morning and a warm afternoon. Why does splitting regulation into two stages help?

answers.text: Two stages let the building line run at full tank pressure on cold mornings, which increases appliance input exactly when the tank itself produces the least vapor
Two stages eliminate the need for any regulator vent protection, because a regulator with two diaphragms cannot be affected by water, ice, or insects at its vent
The first stage absorbs most tank-pressure variation, so the second stage holds steadier outlet pressure
Two stages double the heat content delivered per gallon, because each regulator pass concentrates the vapor before it reaches the appliance gas controls

questions.explanation: Staging the reduction means the second-stage regulator sees a fairly steady intermediate inlet pressure instead of raw tank pressure that swings with temperature. That steadies the final outlet pressure, while vents still need protection and no regulator changes the heat content of the fuel.

questions.question: Before a new section of gas piping is put into service, what must be done to prove its integrity under mainstream fuel-gas practice?

answers.text: Paint all joints and look for bubbles while the appliances fire
Pressure-test the piping with air or an inert gas at the required test pressure for the required duration and inspect for leaks; never test with fuel gas or oxygen
Open the meter valve briefly and smell each joint
Test only the appliance connectors, since new pipe cannot leak

questions.explanation: New gas piping is pressure-tested with air or inert gas and held to verify tightness before being charged with fuel gas, and oxygen is never used, option B. Firing appliances during a bubble check (A) puts unproven piping into service, smelling joints after opening the meter (C) is not a test and exposes the building to gas, and untested new pipe (D) can and does leak at joints.

questions.question: A mechanical system is complete, but the owner wants the required inspection skipped to move tenants in sooner. What is the contractor's correct course?

answers.text: Conceal the work and photograph it, because photographs are accepted everywhere as a full substitute for an in-person inspection
Keep the work exposed as required and obtain the inspection and approval before concealment and occupancy use.
Move tenants in and schedule inspection within the following year, since occupancy does not change the inspection requirement's timing
Have the owner sign a form accepting the work, which transfers the authority having jurisdiction's approval power to the property owner

questions.explanation: Permitted mechanical work must be inspected and approved at the required stages; deadlines do not waive it. Photographs do not replace inspection, occupancy before approval reverses the required sequence, and an owner's signature cannot assume the inspector's authority.

questions.question: An applicant is wholly owned by a parent company, and its own financial statement is mostly cash with few fixed assets. Its president asks whether the Board can demand support beyond the company's own statement. What may the Board require?

answers.text: The Board may require a Guaranty Agreement in addition to the financial statement; the parent may have to file its own statement and guaranty the subsidiary's contracting debts, and a Board-format bond requested instead of the guaranty is not accepted in lieu of a statement

The Board may not require anything further, because a statement that satisfies the tier for the requested limit exhausts the Board's financial-review authority over subsidiary applicants in Tennessee under the Board's financial rules, regardless of how the parent company chooses to structure its support of the subsidiary
The Board may require the parent to take the trade examination, because parent-company support for a subsidiary applicant is provided through an additional qualifying agent rather than a guaranty
The Board may require only a larger cash deposit with the state, because guaranty agreements are available solely to individual guarantors and never to parent companies of applicants

questions.explanation: A is correct: a Guaranty Agreement, line of credit, bond or other indemnity may be required in addition to the financial statement where the statement is primarily cash without fixed assets, or where a parent company owns the applicant; the parent may be required to file its own statement plus a guaranty of the subsidiary's contracting debts, and a bond requested instead of the guaranty is not accepted in lieu of a financial statement. B is wrong because the rule expressly reserves this additional-support authority. C is wrong because parent support runs through statements and guaranties, not an extra qualifying agent. D is wrong because guaranties are the stated tool for parent-owned applicants, not cash deposits.

questions.question: At renewal, a licensee seeks to keep a $1,200,000 monetary limit. What is the minimum financial filing the current renewal structure accepts at that limit?

answers.text: A CPA-audited statement, because renewal at any limit above $500,000 requires the highest level of CPA assurance under the current Board financial rules
A CPA-reviewed statement, because renewal limits above $1,000,000 were moved to the reviewed tier when the financial rules were last updated by the Board
A self-prepared balance sheet with the required notarized statement that the information is true and correct, unless the Board requires more in the case
A surety bond only, because renewal applicants below the unlimited tier must now replace all financial filings with the in-lieu bond on file with the Board

questions.explanation: C is correct: at renewal, limits of $1,500,000 or less may be supported by a self-prepared balance sheet with the required notarized statement that the information is true and correct, unless the Board requires more; above $1,500,000 a CPA compilation is the minimum. A is wrong because audit is not the renewal minimum at $1,200,000. B is wrong because the $1,500,000 line, not $1,000,000, separates the self-prepared tier. D is wrong because the in-lieu bond is an option from July 1, 2026, not a mandatory replacement for renewal financials.

questions.question: Before raising an aerial lift to set a curb adapter, the operator walks around the machine and finds a hydraulic leak and a worn tire. What should the operator do?

answers.text: Operate the lift at reduced height all day, because hydraulic leaks and tire wear only become dangerous when the platform is near its maximum elevation
Tag the lift out of service and report the defects before use
Top off the hydraulic fluid and proceed, since a leak that can be refilled during the shift does not count as a defect requiring the lift to be removed
Swap the lift's parking spot with another crew's machine without mentioning the defects, letting the next operator discover the problems during their own work

questions.explanation: A pre-use inspection that finds defects like hydraulic leaks or damaged tires takes the lift out of service until repaired. Reduced height does not make a failing lift safe, refilling does not fix a leak, and silently passing a defective machine to another crew just moves the hazard.

questions.question: A dryer duct run uses several elbows and exceeds the length the appliance listing allows, and clothes take two cycles to dry. What are the accepted remedies?

answers.text: Install a smaller-diameter duct for the whole run, because higher velocity in a restricted duct always restores dryer performance
Shorten or reroute the run, reduce fitting losses, or use a listed booster arrangement permitted by the listing.
Terminate the excess length into a garage so the remaining outdoor run falls within the length limit on the appliance label
Add an inline lint filter at mid-run and leave the length unchanged, since filtering is treated as equivalent to shortening the duct

questions.explanation: Equivalent length, including fittings, must stay within the listing unless an approved booster method is used. Smaller duct raises resistance further, a garage termination discharges lint and moisture indoors, and a mid-run filter adds restriction rather than removing length.

questions.question: A return grille that is too small for the required CFM will most likely cause:

answers.text: Lower velocity and quieter operation
No change in static pressure
High velocity, noise, and increased pressure drop
Higher refrigerant superheat directly, with no change in airflow or noise

questions.explanation: Forcing required CFM through too little free area raises velocity, which creates noise and pressure drop, so C is correct. A and B describe the opposite of the actual effect, and superheat is a refrigeration measurement not directly set by grille size.

questions.question: Midway through a design, the owner upgrades from a basic filter at 0.10 in. w.g. pressure drop to a deep-media high-efficiency filter rated at 0.25 in. w.g. at design airflow. Nothing else changes. What must the designer do to the duct design?

answers.text: Nothing, because filter pressure drop is internal to the equipment and outside the duct budget
Increase the available duct static by 0.15, since a better filter helps the blower
Leave the friction rate unchanged but shrink all ducts one size to restore velocity
Reduce the static pressure available for the ductwork by the added 0.15 in. w.g. and recompute the friction rate, because the filter upgrade spends part of the blower's fixed external static budget

questions.explanation: Every external component draws from the same blower budget; a filter that costs 0.15 in. more leaves 0.15 in. less for the ducts, and the friction rate must be recalculated on the smaller remainder. Option A is wrong because the filter sits in the external airstream and its drop is a standard line item in the external static budget; option B is wrong because a higher-drop filter burdens the blower more, it does not assist it; option C is wrong because shrinking ducts raises their pressure drop — the opposite response when less pressure is available.

questions.question: The specifications state that motor starters are furnished under the mechanical division and installed under the electrical division. A starter is missing at rough-in inspection. Why does that split matter for resolving the problem?

answers.text: It defines which trade furnishes and which trade installs the starter
It means neither trade is responsible, because any item mentioned by two divisions is automatically supplied by the building owner after occupancy
It proves the starter was deleted from the project, since equipment cannot legally be furnished by one trade and installed by another trade
It transfers the inspection failure to the general contractor's safety record, after which the starter no longer needs to be provided at all

questions.explanation: Division-of-work language assigns furnishing and installing responsibility, which is exactly what resolves a missing-item dispute. Split responsibility is common and enforceable, it does not make the owner the supplier, and it does not erase the requirement after an inspection finding.

questions.question: A shop is joining large rectangular duct sections on a higher-pressure system and chooses a flanged transverse connection with a gasket instead of a simple slip-and-drive joint. The main reason is that the flanged joint:

answers.text: Is the only joint permitted on round spiral duct
Provides a stiffer, stronger connection with a compressible gasket surface that seals more reliably at larger sizes and higher pressures

Eliminates the need for sealant or gasket material at any pressure, since the bare metal flange faces seal themselves when the sections are pulled together and normal duct pressure keeps the joint faces pressed tightly shut
Lets the sections be joined with no mechanical fasteners at all

questions.explanation: Slip-and-drive joints suit smaller, lower-pressure rectangular work; flanged systems add rigidity and a gasketed face that holds its seal as size and pressure grow. Option A is wrong because flanged rectangular connections are a rectangular-duct method, not the standard joint for round spiral duct; option C is wrong because the gasket is the sealing element of this joint — the joint exists partly to compress it properly; option D is wrong because flanges are bolted or clamped together, so fasteners are central to how the joint works.

questions.question: A compressor is located below its air-cooled condenser, so discharge gas must rise through a vertical discharge riser before reaching the condenser. Oil management on this discharge riser should include:

answers.text: No provisions, because hot gas always carries oil at any velocity, including at the low mass flow of a lightly loaded system on a cold night when discharge velocity in the riser falls to its minimum
A liquid receiver installed in the discharge line
An EPR valve at the top of the riser
A trap at the base of the discharge riser and correct sizing so oil is carried upward rather than falling back toward the compressor at low flow

questions.explanation: Discharge risers face the same oil-lift physics as suction risers, so base trapping and adequate velocity keep oil moving toward the condenser and separator instead of slugging back. Option A ignores low-load velocity loss, option B puts a liquid vessel in a hot-gas line, and option C places a suction-side regulator where it cannot manage oil.

questions.question: Intermittent no-cool. The system cools well for about an hour, then the outdoor unit stops for roughly 20 minutes and restarts on its own, repeating through hot afternoons. During a dropout, the contactor coil has a full 24 V at its terminals yet is not pulled in, indoor blower and thermostat call continue normally, and compressor pressures are equalizing normally (not a pressure trip). Pulled after a dropout, the coil measures open circuit while hot but returns to about 16 ohms after cooling on the bench. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A thermostat with an anti-short-cycle delay that lengthens in heat, which would remove the 24 V call during its delay rather than leave full voltage sitting at a coil that will not pull in
A high-pressure switch tripping on hot afternoons, which would open the control circuit and remove coil voltage instead of leaving 24 V present at the terminals during the dropout
A compressor internal overload cycling the unit, which would stop the compressor only while the condenser fan kept running and the contactor stayed pulled in
A contactor coil that opens thermally when hot and recovers as it cools

questions.explanation: Voltage is present but the coil will not pull in, and the coil itself proves open while hot and normal at 16 ohms when cool, a classic thermal intermittent that matches the run-an-hour, rest-20-minutes rhythm. A thermostat delay or pressure switch would remove coil voltage during the dropout, and a compressor overload leaves the contactor pulled in with the fan still running.

questions.question: A boiler's relief valve (30 psi) discharges on nearly every heating cycle. System pressure reads 12 psi cold but climbs to 29 psi at temperature; tapping the expansion tank shows it heavy and waterlogged with no air cushion, and the fill valve holds a steady 12 psi with no creep when the boiler is cold and isolated. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A leaking fill (pressure-reducing) valve, which would creep the cold pressure upward too, but cold pressure here holds steady at 12 psi when isolated
A waterlogged expansion tank
An overheating aquastat driving pressure up with temperature, when boiler temperature is verified within its normal operating range during these cycles
An undersized relief valve, which is a standard 30 psi residential valve correctly opening only when system pressure truly reaches its rating

questions.explanation: Pressure that is stable cold but soars hot means expanding water has no air cushion to absorb it — the tank is waterlogged. A leaking fill valve would raise cold pressure too, boiler temperature is normal, and the relief valve is honestly opening at its rating.

questions.question: During evacuation, the vacuum pump has run for hours but the micron gauge mounted at the pump reads 300 microns while the system was only briefly opened. To know the system's true vacuum level, the technician should:

answers.text: Measure with the micron gauge connected to the system (valved off from the pump for a decay reading), using large, short hoses and removed valve cores to reduce restriction
Trust the pump-mounted gauge reading as the system reading
Add a small refrigerant charge to push air out

Judge dryness by how long the pump has run, regardless of gauge placement, hose size, valve-core restriction, system volume, ambient temperature, or whether a decay test was ever performed with the pump valved off from the system

questions.explanation: Gauges at the pump read the pump, not the far system; system-mounted measurement, isolation for decay, and low-restriction connections reveal the real level and speed evacuation. Option B is the error described, option C contaminates an evacuated system instead of drying it, and option D substitutes elapsed time for the measurement that proves dryness.

michigan-hvac.quiz_title: Michigan HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How does a digital scroll compressor vary its capacity during a control cycle?

answers.text: It reverses the direction of the orbiting scroll for part of each cycle so compressed gas flows backward through the discharge port toward the suction side
It briefly separates the scrolls so compression stops for part of the cycle
It varies the voltage and frequency supplied to the motor so shaft speed changes continuously in direct proportion to the cooling load on the building
It opens and closes a hot-gas bypass valve in the discharge line while the scrolls themselves remain loaded and compressing at full displacement continuously

questions.explanation: A digital scroll uses a solenoid to axially separate the scrolls for timed intervals, so average capacity follows the loaded fraction of the cycle at constant speed. It does not reverse rotation, it is not a variable-frequency speed control, and its scrolls themselves unload rather than relying on a discharge hot-gas bypass.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a heat anticipator in a traditional electromechanical thermostat?

answers.text: To open the heating contacts slightly early to prevent temperature overshoot from residual heat
To increase the furnace firing rate automatically whenever outdoor temperature falls below a set balance point during cold weather
To delay the blower until the heat exchanger is fully hot
To add resistance so the thermostat can operate without a common wire

questions.explanation: The anticipator warms the sensing element so contacts open before residual heat overshoots the setpoint, which is correct. Increasing firing rate is a burner control function, not the anticipator. Blower delay is handled by a fan control or board timing, not the anticipator. Operating without a common wire relates to power-stealing or batteries, not anticipation.

questions.question: An appliance in an attic is reached through a small scuttle with no walkway and no lighting. Which condition must be corrected?

answers.text: Move the appliance disconnect to the living room so the technician never needs to enter the attic for any service operation
Provide a safe passageway, a service platform where required, lighting, and a receptacle at the appliance.
Require the homeowner to supply a flashlight and a loose sheet of plywood each time a technician visits the property
Enlarge the scuttle only if the appliance is replaced, because access rules apply solely on the day of original installation

questions.explanation: Technicians must be able to reach and service the appliance safely, with passage, platform, light, and power. A remote disconnect does not make the attic workable, borrowed plywood and flashlights are not permanent access, and access requirements are not waived between replacements.

questions.question: After replacing a rooftop blower belt, how should correct tension be judged before returning the unit to service?

answers.text: By twisting the belt a full half-turn at mid-span, with any belt that resists twisting considered correctly tensioned for service
By running the blower for one hour and retightening only if the belt has stretched until it touches the guard at the bottom of its travel
By pressing the belt until it feels as tight as a guitar string, because tighter tension always improves airflow and bearing life together
By measuring deflection at mid-span under the specified force and comparing it with the unit or belt maker's deflection specification

questions.explanation: Belt tension is set by measured deflection under a specified force at mid-span, compared with the published specification. Twist feel is not a measurement, waiting for visible stretch leaves the unit running loose, and over-tightening overloads bearings and shafts rather than improving service life.

questions.question: What does a low-water cutoff protect a boiler against?

answers.text: High gas pressure at the manifold caused by a failed regulator that is delivering full inlet pressure directly to the burners
Frozen coils in the air handler
Excessive circulator speed
Firing or overheating when boiler water level falls too low, which can damage the boiler and create a hazard

questions.explanation: The low-water cutoff interrupts burner operation when water level is unsafe, preventing dry-firing damage and hazard, option D. Gas manifold pressure (A) is governed by the regulator and gas valve, frozen air-handler coils (B) concern a different system, and circulator speed (C) is set by the pump and its controls, not a water-level safety.

questions.question: How do mainstream equipment standards treat installing R-454B into an existing air conditioner that was designed and listed only for R-410A?

answers.text: Not permitted; the equipment must be designed and listed for the mildly flammable refrigerant it will contain
Permitted as a routine retrofit whenever the pressures are similar, provided the oil is changed and the nameplate is updated by the installing contractor
Permitted only in commercial buildings, because occupancy rules rather than equipment listing determine whether a different refrigerant may be used
Permitted if the charge is reduced by a small percentage, because a reduced charge converts an unlisted refrigerant change into an approved application

questions.explanation: Equipment must be designed and listed for the mildly flammable refrigerant, including its sensors, controls, and electrical components. Similar pressures do not create a retrofit approval, building type does not override equipment listing, and trimming the charge does not make an unlisted conversion acceptable.

questions.question: Instead of bypassing to the return, a designer relieves excess air into a hallway and basement area that tolerate extra conditioning. What is this strategy called, and what is its main trade-off?

answers.text: A dump zone; the relieved area may be overconditioned while it absorbs excess air
A dead zone; the relieved area receives no air at all, and the trade-off is that the excess blower airflow is absorbed by raising static pressure in the trunk instead
A purge zone; the relieved area is ventilated outdoors, and the trade-off is the energy cost of discarding conditioned air through an exterior wall opening on every cycle
A staging zone; the relieved area is heated by a separate appliance, and the trade-off is the fuel cost of running two heat sources whenever only one thermostat is calling

questions.explanation: A dump zone gives excess supply air a harmless destination instead of short-circuiting it into the return, at the cost of overconditioning that tolerant area. The other descriptions send the air nowhere, outdoors, or to a second appliance, none of which describes relieving air into a non-critical conditioned area.

questions.question: In a hot-humid climate, a vented crawlspace gets wetter in summer the more its vents are opened, and ducts there sweat heavily. Why does ventilation worsen it?

answers.text: Vent air adds moisture that condenses
Opening vents raises crawlspace temperature above the dew point of the outdoor air, which forces moisture out of the soil and into the framing
Wind through the vents pressurizes the crawlspace and squeezes liquid water out of the soil through the foundation walls into the space
The vents admit insects whose activity generates the extra moisture, and the duct sweating is a separate refrigerant-side problem

questions.explanation: Humid outdoor air entering the crawlspace contacts ducts and framing cooled by the house above, falls below its dew point, and deposits moisture, so more ventilation means more condensation. Ventilation does not heat surfaces above dew point in a way that draws water from soil, wind pressure does not squeeze liquid water through foundation walls, and insects do not generate this volume of moisture.

questions.question: To use the target-superheat charging method on a fixed-orifice system, which two air temperatures must the technician measure at the time of charging?

answers.text: Supply-air dry bulb and return-air dry bulb
Liquid-line temperature and suction-line temperature only, measured at the service ports with the system running and stabilized under a steady indoor load
Compressor discharge temperature and outdoor wet bulb
Indoor wet-bulb temperature at the return and outdoor dry-bulb temperature at the condenser

questions.explanation: The target-superheat chart or formula is entered with indoor wet bulb, which reflects indoor load and humidity, and outdoor dry bulb, which reflects condensing conditions. Option A gives temperature split, not the chart inputs, option B is used to compute actual superheat rather than the target, and option C pairs a refrigerant temperature with the wrong outdoor measurement.

questions.question: A typical contractor workmanship warranty differs from a manufacturer's equipment warranty in which way?

answers.text: The workmanship warranty covers the contractor's installation work; the manufacturer's covers its equipment defects
The workmanship warranty covers the factory's equipment defects, while the manufacturer covers the contractor's labor errors
Both warranties are identical in coverage, and the distinction exists only for marketing purposes in the proposal
The manufacturer's warranty covers the contractor's installation workmanship for as long as the building remains standing

questions.explanation: A is correct because the contractor warrants its own installation work while the manufacturer warrants defects in its equipment. B is incorrect because it reverses the two parties' responsibilities. C is incorrect because the coverage, responsible party, and claim route genuinely differ. D is incorrect because a manufacturer does not warrant the installing contractor's workmanship.

questions.question: Hot-gas bypass gas is introduced directly into the suction line far from the evaporator on a system that then logs oil in the evaporator during long bypass hours. Why can the injection point matter?

answers.text: Bypass into the distributor or evaporator inlet keeps refrigerant velocity through the coil up, helping oil return, while suction-only injection can leave coil velocity too low
The injection point never matters, because hot gas entering anywhere in the low side produces identical evaporator velocities and identical oil-return behavior at all loads
Injecting into the suction line raises evaporator velocity the most, because the gas passes through the entire coil twice before it reaches the compressor inlet
Injecting at the distributor stops all oil movement in the coil, because the added gas pressure holds the oil stationary against the tube walls during bypass operation

questions.explanation: Feeding bypass gas through the coil maintains mass flow and velocity that sweep oil back, whereas suction-line-only injection satisfies the compressor while the coil itself sees very low flow and can log oil. Injection location changes coil velocity and oil behavior materially, suction-only gas does not pass through the coil at all, and distributor injection promotes rather than prevents oil movement through the coil.

questions.question: On a new condensing furnace, the PVC exhaust vent runs 18 feet horizontally to the sidewall. How should that horizontal run be pitched, and why?

answers.text: Pitched away from the furnace so condensate runs outdoors, where it can drip freely off the termination fitting
Pitched back toward the furnace
Pitched exactly level so condensate can sit in the pipe and evaporate slowly during the off cycle between calls for heat
Pitched away from the furnace on the first half and back toward it on the second half, forming a shallow low point in the middle

questions.explanation: The exhaust is pitched back toward the furnace, typically about 1/4 inch per foot, so condensate formed in the vent drains to the furnace drain system. Option A sends acidic condensate outdoors to drip and freeze at the termination, option C lets water pool and block vent area, and option D creates a trap in the middle that can fill and trip the pressure switch.

questions.question: A 5-ton system serves a 1,250 sq ft home whose calculated load is 2 tons. It satisfies the thermostat in 6-minute cycles, indoor humidity sits at 68%, supply air is cold, and all pressures, superheat, subcooling, and airflow per ton are normal. Occupants complain the home feels clammy. What is the correct diagnosis?

answers.text: Oversized equipment short-cycling
A blower speed set far too low, which would lengthen runtimes and wring out more moisture, the opposite of the 6-minute cycles observed
A dirty evaporator coil reducing dehumidification, which would distort airflow and superheat readings that here are entirely normal
Low refrigerant charge causing poor latent removal, which is contradicted by the normal superheat, subcooling, and pressures measured on this call

questions.explanation: Normal refrigerant readings with very short cycles and high indoor humidity are the signature of gross oversizing: sensible load is met before the coil runs long enough to remove latent load. Charge, blower speed, and coil condition all show normal measurements, and low blower speed would extend runtime rather than shorten it.

questions.question: A masonry chimney is relined for a mid-efficiency furnace. A liner much larger than the vent connector is proposed to 'give the gases room.' The main risk is:

answers.text: Excessive draft that pulls too much dilution air through the draft hood and raises the appliance firing rate above its nameplate input
Flue gases moving so fast in the large liner that they cannot transfer heat and instead melt the liner joints within one heating season
A pressure increase inside the chimney that forces the furnace pressure switch to stay closed after the inducer has shut down
Slow, cool flue gases with weak draft and condensation

questions.explanation: Slow, cool flue gases with weak draft and condensation. A large liner does not raise firing rate or flue-gas speed, and it does not create pressure that holds a pressure switch closed.

questions.question: An ice machine makes thin, weak ice and cycles off on high head pressure on warm afternoons. Its air-cooled condenser is packed with grease and dust. The best first action is:

answers.text: Increase the ice thickness setting to compensate
Shorten the harvest cycle
Add water to the sump until the pump overflows
Thoroughly clean the condenser and verify airflow, then recheck pressures and production

questions.explanation: A fouled air-cooled condenser cannot reject heat, so head pressure rises and freeze efficiency falls; cleaning restores heat transfer before judging other parts. Thicker settings in option A lengthen an already stressed cycle, option B changes harvest rather than heat rejection, and option C overfills the water system without addressing pressure.

questions.question: A license was not renewed and became void after the October 31, 2028 deadline. The former licensee files a reinstatement application in 2030. Which determination is correct?

answers.text: Reinstatement requires passing the examination again, since any voided license must be re-earned
Reinstatement in 2030 is within 3 years after voiding, so reexamination is not required, and until reinstated the void license cannot be used to obtain a permit

Reinstatement in 2030 is within 3 years after voiding, so the license was never void for permit purposes, and the former licensee may obtain permits while the reinstatement application is being processed
Reinstatement is impossible after a license becomes void, and a new application is the only route

questions.explanation: A license not renewed is void for the purpose of obtaining a permit, and a reinstatement filed within 3 years after voiding, as a 2030 filing is after the 2028 voiding, does not require reexamination. A filing after that 3-year period, such as in 2032, would require meeting the examination requirement.

questions.question: Total external static pressure on a PSC-blower system rises from 0.50 in. w.c. to 0.74 in. w.c. over a season, filter pressure drop accounts for most of the increase, and rooms are getting less air. What is happening?

answers.text: Airflow falls as static rises
The blower is delivering more air than before, because a PSC motor speeds up automatically to overcome added resistance and maintain its original operating point
The refrigerant charge is migrating to the filter, which raises its pressure drop and reduces airflow by starving the evaporator coil of refrigerant flow
The ducts are leaking less than when new, so the higher static pressure is simply proof that sealing work has succeeded and airflow should be unchanged

questions.explanation: A loaded filter adds resistance; on a PSC blower the operating point moves to higher static and lower airflow, which matches the comfort complaint. A PSC motor does not speed up to compensate, refrigerant does not migrate into an air filter, and reduced duct leakage would not selectively raise the filter's share of pressure drop.

questions.question: No-heat call. A furnace completes prepurge, proves its pressure switch, and glows its igniter on every trial, but the burners never light and no gas smell is present. A meter shows 24 V delivered to the gas valve terminals during the trial, manifold pressure reads zero, and the gas valve coil measures open circuit against a specified resistance in the tens of ohms. Inlet gas pressure is normal. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: An open gas valve coil
A failed igniter that never reaches lighting temperature, ruled out because the igniter glows visibly on every trial and the failure includes zero manifold pressure with full valve voltage
A control board that never calls for gas, ruled out because 24 V is measured at the gas valve terminals during the ignition trial window
A closed manual gas cock starving the valve, ruled out because inlet pressure at the valve measures normal while the manifold side stays at zero

questions.explanation: Voltage arrives, inlet pressure is normal, and the coil is electrically open, so the valve can never open and manifold pressure stays at zero despite a glowing igniter. The igniter performs, the board delivers its call, and gas reaches the valve inlet, leaving the open coil as the single failed link in the sequence.

questions.question: A designer's worksheet shows: blower maximum external static 0.70 in. w.g.; available for ducts listed as 0.70; friction rate computed from 0.70 over a TEL of 200 feet, giving 0.35 in. per 100 feet. The selected coil drops 0.30 and the filter 0.15. Identify the design error and its consequence.

answers.text: The designer spent the blower's whole budget on the ducts without subtracting the coil and filter; only 0.25 in. is truly available, so the correct friction rate is 0.125 in. per 100 feet and the ducts as sized will be far too small, producing high static and low delivered airflow
There is no error, because coil and filter drops are paid from a separate budget
The only error is arithmetic: 0.70 over 200 feet gives 0.70 per 100 feet
The consequence will be oversized ducts and excessive airflow at the registers

questions.explanation: Available static for ducts is what remains after non-duct components are subtracted: 0.70 - 0.30 - 0.15 = 0.25 in., and 0.25 x 100 / 200 = 0.125 in. per 100 feet — the as-designed rate is nearly three times too high. Option B is wrong because coil and filter are external components drawing on the same single blower budget — there is no second budget; option C is wrong because the arithmetic (0.70 x 100 / 200 = 0.35) is internally consistent; the flaw is the 0.70 input, not the division; option D is wrong because an inflated friction rate sizes ducts too small, which restricts airflow rather than increasing it.

questions.question: An appliance's vent operates under positive pressure, yet its vent gases leave hot enough that they do not condense in the vent. Which venting category is it?

answers.text: It is a Category III appliance with positive vent pressure and noncondensing gases
It is a Category I appliance with a fan-assisted burner and a draft hood fitted
It is a Category II appliance venting by nonpositive pressure through the vent
It is a Category IV appliance whose condensate must be drained from the vent run at every stage of normal equipment operation outdoors

questions.explanation: Positive vent pressure combined with noncondensing vent gases is the definition of Category III. Category I and II both operate nonpositive, and Category IV is the condensing positive-pressure category.

mississippi-hvac.quiz_title: Mississippi HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why is the suction line normally insulated between the evaporator and an outdoor compressor?

answers.text: To keep heat from the surrounding air from adding unwanted superheat and to prevent condensation sweating on the cold line
To keep liquid refrigerant from boiling in the liquid line as it travels from the outdoor condenser through a hot attic to the indoor metering device
To raise discharge pressure in cold weather
To silence compressor vibration

questions.explanation: The suction line carries cold vapor, so insulation limits heat gain that would reduce capacity and cause the line to sweat and drip. Option B concerns the separate liquid line, option C is unrelated to suction insulation, and option D may be a side benefit of some supports but is not the purpose of the insulation.

questions.question: A replacement disconnect is selected for a condensing unit with MCA 28 A and MOP 45 A. Selection must satisfy:

answers.text: Only the physical size of the enclosure, because any disconnect marked for outdoor use is automatically rated for every residential condensing unit
Amp rating adequate for the load and a fused/breaker size not exceeding MOP where protection is in the disconnect
A fuse size equal to the locked-rotor current, because the disconnect fuses must allow the compressor to start without ever opening on inrush
The smallest available rating to save cost, because a disconnect switch is not required to be rated for the current it will actually carry

questions.explanation: Amp rating adequate for the load and a fused/breaker size not exceeding MOP where protection is in the disconnect. Enclosure size, locked-rotor fusing, and lowest cost do not set the rating; the switch must carry the load and any protection in it must respect the MOP.

questions.question: A standard-efficiency furnace with an open draft hood is proposed inside a small bedroom closet. What is the correct position?

answers.text: It is permitted without restriction, because a bedroom closet counts as a mechanical room once a louvered door is installed on the closet
That appliance type is not permitted to draw combustion air from and serve that sleeping space in that way; a permitted listed arrangement, such as sealed/direct-vent where allowed, is required.
It is permitted if the bedroom door is left open at night so the furnace can share the whole house's air while occupants are sleeping
It is permitted whenever the furnace is the smallest model in the product line, regardless of its venting or combustion-air arrangement

questions.explanation: Open combustion appliances are restricted in bedrooms and bathrooms because of carbon monoxide and air-supply risks; only specifically permitted listed configurations may be used. A louver does not convert a bedroom closet into a safe location, an open door is not a combustion-air design, and small size does not waive the restriction.

questions.question: Which residential actors must hold a residential license?

answers.text: Builders must be licensed only on work over $100,000.
Remodelers must be licensed only on improvements over $50,000, regardless of how long the licensee has been in business.
Neither builders nor remodelers require a residential license.
Builders on work over $50,000 and remodelers on improvements over $10,000 must be licensed.

questions.explanation: On the residential track, builders over $50,000 and remodelers over $10,000 in improvements must be licensed. The higher thresholds in the other options are not the residential figures.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a transverse joint in a sheet-metal duct run?

answers.text: It is a decorative seam that covers the edge of the insulation jacket
It is the opening left in the duct wall for a balancing damper
It connects one duct section to the next across the run, and it must be mechanically fastened and then sealed so the joint is both strong and airtight

It is a flexible connector that isolates fan vibration from the building structure, installed at the fan outlet in place of a rigid joint so equipment movement never reaches the duct or the framing it passes through along the run

questions.explanation: A transverse joint joins duct sections end to end, so it carries both a structural and an air-sealing duty. Option A is wrong because that describes a jacket trim piece, not a joint between duct sections; option B is wrong because a damper opening is a branch or in-duct cut, not the connection between two sections; option D is wrong because vibration isolation is the job of a flexible canvas connector at the equipment, not a transverse joint.

questions.question: Before opening a refrigerant circuit for repair or disposing of an appliance, the technician is required to:

answers.text: Vent the charge if it is less than the system nameplate amount, if the job is outdoors on a windy day, or if the technician believes the amount released will be too small to matter under the handling rules
Recover refrigerant to the required recovery level using certified recovery equipment, rather than knowingly venting it
Add nitrogen to dilute the refrigerant before release
Recover only the liquid portion and release the vapor

questions.explanation: Handling rules prohibit knowingly venting refrigerant and require recovery to specified levels with certified equipment before a system is opened or disposed of. Option A invents a small-charge venting exception that does not exist in this form, option C still releases refrigerant, and option D is wrong because the entire charge, vapor included, must be recovered.

questions.question: Water drips from the outside of a bare-metal supply duct crossing a humid attic in summer, while the air inside the duct is 55°F and attic dew point is near 70°F. What is occurring?

answers.text: Condensate is leaking out through duct joints from inside, because supply ducts normally carry liquid water that escapes wherever joints are not taped
The duct is sweating because humid attic air is reaching a surface chilled by the cold supply air, and the water is refrigerant condensing through the metal wall
Missing insulation lets surface chill
The roof is leaking directly onto that duct section, which is why the dripping only happens during the cooling season and not during dry winter heating

questions.explanation: Without insulation the metal surface falls below the attic dew point, so moisture from attic air condenses on the outside of the duct. Supply ducts carry air, not liquid water, refrigerant cannot pass through the duct wall, and a roof leak tied to cooling-season runtime, rather than rain, does not fit the pattern.

questions.question: A balanced ventilation system is preferred over exhaust-only ventilation in a very cold climate home with natural-draft combustion equipment mainly because it:

answers.text: Supplies about as much air as it exhausts, limiting house depressurization
Heats all of the incoming outdoor air fully up to room temperature without any heat loss or energy use of any kind during cold weather operation
Eliminates the need for local bathroom exhaust
Allows the combustion appliance to share the ventilation duct

questions.explanation: Matching supply and exhaust keeps pressures near neutral, protecting natural-draft appliances from backdrafting. Incoming air is tempered by heat recovery at best, not heated for free to room temperature. Balanced systems do not replace local exhaust, and combustion vents must never be combined with ventilation ducts.

questions.question: Before a subcontractor starts work, why does a contractor typically collect a current certificate of insurance?

answers.text: To verify the subcontractor carries the coverage the subcontract requires
To transfer the contractor's own license obligations to the subcontractor for every project currently under contract
To guarantee the subcontractor's work will need no inspection, because insured work is exempt from code review
To set the subcontractor's labor rates for the project, since insurance certificates include a schedule of wage charges

questions.explanation: A is correct because the certificate provides evidence the subcontractor carries the insurance the subcontract requires before work begins. B is incorrect because an insurance certificate does not transfer licensing duties between businesses. C is incorrect because insured work remains subject to inspection and code requirements. D is incorrect because certificates evidence coverage limits and dates, not labor pricing.

questions.question: A replacement rooftop unit is set on an adapter curb over an older curb footprint. Rainwater is entering the duct drop and airflow is uneven between supplies. What adapter-curb issue best explains both symptoms?

answers.text: The adapter was painted a different color than the original curb, changing solar gain on the roof enough to drive rain into the supply opening
The adapter's internal turning vanes are too efficient, accelerating air so unevenly that rain is pulled upward through the return drop in storms
Poorly sealed and misaligned transitions in the adapter can leak air and water at the joints while distorting flow into the existing duct drops
The adapter raised the unit several inches, and any height increase alone guarantees both water entry and uneven supply distribution below

questions.explanation: Adapter curbs must align with the old supply and return openings and be sealed and flashed at every joint; gaps there leak water and air and disrupt distribution. Paint color does not drive rain entry, efficient vanes do not pull rain upward, and added height alone causes neither symptom when transitions are sealed.

questions.question: An upstairs baseboard loop is air-bound and cold while lower loops heat normally, and automatic vents at the high point are crusted shut. The correct service is to:

answers.text: Raise boiler pressure to 30 psi to force the air out
Vent or purge the air from the high loop and repair or replace the failed high-point vents so air is removed where it naturally collects
Drain the entire system and refill it without venting
Install a larger circulator to push water past the air pocket

questions.explanation: Air collects at high points and blocks circulation there; it must be vented or purged and the automatic vent restored so the problem does not recur. Option A risks lifting the relief valve and still leaves trapped air in place. Option C reintroduces fresh air with the refill water and repeats the fault. Option D cannot circulate water through a loop fully blocked by an air pocket.

questions.question: First-stage electric heat works normally, but the second stage never comes on even on the coldest design days. The thermostat is a two-stage model. What should be investigated first?

answers.text: Whether the outdoor condenser contactor is pulling in, because second-stage strip heat is interlocked through the cooling circuit
Whether the return grille is painted shut, because second-stage heat is enabled by a pressure switch sensing return airflow only
The W2 call, second-stage sequencer, and its wiring
The refrigerant metering device, because a restricted device signals the control board to hold off auxiliary heat indefinitely on

questions.explanation: A dead second stage with a healthy first stage points first to the second-stage control path: the W2 call, its wiring, and the second sequencer or relay and link. Option A ties strip staging to a cooling contactor, option B invents a return-pressure interlock, and option D imports a refrigeration fault into a resistance-heat staging problem.

questions.question: A 5-ton system serves a 1,250 sq ft home whose calculated load is 2 tons. It satisfies the thermostat in 6-minute cycles, indoor humidity sits at 68%, supply air is cold, and all pressures, superheat, subcooling, and airflow per ton are normal. Occupants complain the home feels clammy. What is the correct diagnosis?

answers.text: Oversized equipment short-cycling
A blower speed set far too low, which would lengthen runtimes and wring out more moisture, the opposite of the 6-minute cycles observed
A dirty evaporator coil reducing dehumidification, which would distort airflow and superheat readings that here are entirely normal
Low refrigerant charge causing poor latent removal, which is contradicted by the normal superheat, subcooling, and pressures measured on this call

questions.explanation: Normal refrigerant readings with very short cycles and high indoor humidity are the signature of gross oversizing: sensible load is met before the coil runs long enough to remove latent load. Charge, blower speed, and coil condition all show normal measurements, and low blower speed would extend runtime rather than shorten it.

questions.question: A long suction run was undersized, creating a large suction pressure drop between evaporator and compressor. Even if evaporator temperature looks right, system capacity and efficiency suffer because:

answers.text: The compressor must work against a higher compression ratio from its lower inlet pressure, moving less refrigerant per revolution

The condenser receives more heat than it was designed for from the pipe itself, because the long, undersized suction run absorbs enough mechanical-room heat along its length to overload the outdoor condensing coil at the roof
The expansion valve gains pressure difference and overfeeds
Oil viscosity increases in the warmer evaporator

questions.explanation: Pressure drop lowers the density and pressure of vapor actually entering the compressor, raising its compression ratio and cutting mass flow and efficiency. Option B blames pipe heat that is not the mechanism, option C is wrong because suction drop does not add feed pressure at the valve, and option D misstates both where the oil problem arises and its cause.

questions.question: A TXV system with verified airflow shows subcooling well above the specified target while superheat at the evaporator outlet stays near its normal controlled value. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: The system is undercharged, because high subcooling always means low charge

The TXV has failed closed, because subcooling can only rise when the valve closes, so the valve should be replaced before any charge is removed or added and before the condenser is checked for stacked liquid
The indoor coil is dirty, because fouling raises liquid-line subcooling directly
The system is likely overcharged; the valve holds superheat while excess liquid backs up in the condenser, so charge should be recovered to the target subcooling

questions.explanation: A working TXV masks overcharge at the evaporator by holding superheat, so the excess shows up as liquid stacked in the condenser and high subcooling, corrected by recovering to target. Option A reverses the subcooling relationship, option B ignores that a failed-closed valve would starve the evaporator and raise superheat, and option C describes an air-side fault that lowers capacity rather than stacking liquid.

questions.question: On a residential duct system built to the duct construction standard listed for the residential exam, how must horizontal flexible duct be supported?

answers.text: It is supported at close intervals so the duct stays nearly level, with only slight sag between supports
It is supported only at its two ends, with the middle of each run left to sag as low as the attic insulation and ceiling framing will allow it to
It is supported by resting the full run on the bottom chords of the roof trusses, with no straps or saddles used anywhere along the flexible duct
It is supported at intervals of one support per room served, regardless of how long the run is or how much the duct sags between the supports

questions.explanation: Flexible duct must be supported frequently enough that it runs nearly straight with minimal sag, since sag and compression add friction the design did not allow. End-only support, resting unstrapped on framing, or one support per room all leave long sagging spans that choke airflow.

questions.question: A building is losing its slight positive pressure whenever exhaust fans run, and doors stand ajar with wind noise at entrances. The relief and exhaust controls are not tracking supply airflow. What is the control goal that fixes this?

answers.text: Seal the relief path completely shut so building pressure rises without any limit whenever the supply fan runs at full speed on a windy day
Modulate relief or exhaust in step with supply and outdoor airflow to hold a small, steady positive building pressure
Drive building pressure strongly negative so entrance doors pull themselves closed
Control pressure from a sensor placed in the supply duct instead of in the building space

questions.explanation: Tracking relief to airflow holds the intended slight positive pressure across operating conditions. Sealing relief invites over-pressurization, strong negative pressure causes infiltration and can affect combustion appliances, and duct pressure is a different variable from space pressure.

questions.question: A furnace call: the inducer runs, the pressure switch proves closed, 120 V is delivered to the igniter terminals at the right point in the sequence — but there is no glow, no ignition, and the igniter measures open (infinite resistance) on a cool ohmmeter check. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A pressure switch stuck open, which is contradicted because the switch proved closed and the sequence advanced to energizing the igniter
An open hot-surface igniter
A dirty flame sensor, which causes shutdown seconds after a successful light, not a complete absence of ignition and glow
A failed gas valve coil, which would prevent gas flow but cannot explain an igniter that never glows and measures electrically open

questions.explanation: Voltage present at the igniter with no glow and an open resistance reading condemns the igniter itself; the sequence never reaches gas flow or flame sensing. A gas valve fault acts later in the sequence, the pressure switch demonstrably closed, and a dirty flame sensor only matters after a flame exists.

questions.question: A ventilation design uses the rate formula: CFM = 0.03 x floor area + 7.5 x (bedrooms + 1). For a 1,600 sq ft house with 3 bedrooms, what is the required continuous ventilation rate?

answers.text: 55.5 CFM, because only the floor-area term applies to houses
70.5 CFM, because the bedroom term uses bedrooms minus 1
78 CFM, because 0.03 x 1,600 = 48 and 7.5 x 4 = 30, totaling 78
108 CFM, because the floor-area coefficient is 0.05 for houses over 1,500 sq ft

questions.explanation: Both terms of the given formula count: the area term contributes 48 CFM and the occupant term, using bedrooms + 1 = 4, contributes 30 CFM. Option A is wrong because dropping the occupant term understates the rate — people, not just floor area, generate the contaminants ventilation dilutes; option B is wrong because the formula as given adds 1 to the bedroom count to represent the primary suite's two occupants; option D is wrong because the coefficient in the stated formula is 0.03; substituting 0.05 changes the given method rather than applying it.

questions.question: A compressor will not start after a long off period in a cold equipment room. The crankcase heater is found open-circuit, the oil sight glass shows a high, foamy level, and the compressor draws locked-rotor current briefly before tripping. What follow-up is most appropriate before returning it to regular service?

answers.text: Immediately add a full supplemental oil charge, because a foamy sight glass always means the crankcase is low on oil and needs additional volume right away
Replace the expansion valve with a smaller one, because migration during the off cycle is controlled entirely by the size of the valve orifice at the evaporator
Jumper the overload and force several long runs, because sustained running under load is the fastest way to prove the compressor has not been damaged by liquid
Restore the heater, warm and clear the oil of refrigerant, and verify oil condition before normal operation

questions.explanation: A dead heater allowed migration, so the heater must be restored and the refrigerant boiled out of the oil gently, with oil condition checked, before trusting the machine. A foamy glass reflects refrigerant in the oil, not a low oil charge needing more oil, migration is driven by temperature differences rather than expansion-valve orifice size, and forcing runs with an overload jumper risks destroying a possibly liquid-damaged compressor.

new-jersey-hvac.quiz_title: New Jersey HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why are tandem (paired) compressors used instead of one large compressor on some packaged units?

answers.text: Because two compressors piped together always use exactly half the energy of one compressor of the same total capacity at every possible operating condition
Because a tandem pair eliminates the need for any oil equalization or shared oil management between the two crankcases under all load combinations
Because a single compressor cannot be manufactured above a very small size, so any unit over a few tons must always use two compressors in tandem
Staged capacity and redundancy, with each compressor sized for part of the total load

questions.explanation: Tandem pairs stage capacity to match part load and keep partial cooling if one machine fails. They do not halve energy use at every condition, their shared piping still requires careful oil equalization, and large single compressors are readily available, so pairing is a staging choice, not a size limit.

questions.question: After a severe hermetic compressor burnout, the replacement plan that best protects the new compressor is:

answers.text: Change only the compressor and reuse all driers unchanged

Flush the system with liquid refrigerant from a charging cylinder, pushing the full cylinder contents through the suction and liquid lines, out through the evaporator, and venting the contaminated mixture at the far end of the run before installing the new compressor
Test the oil/refrigerant for acid, install new liquid-line and suction cleanup driers/filters sized for cleanup, run, retest, and replace cleanup cores/driers until tests stay clean
Add extra oil to dilute any acid so no driers are needed

questions.explanation: Burnout debris and acid circulate system-wide, so cleanup driers on both lines, acid testing, and repeat checks until clean are the standard protection for the new compressor. Option A leaves contamination to kill the replacement, option B is an improper and wasteful flushing method, and option D dilutes nothing safely because acid remains active in the oil.

questions.question: Where must an appliance fuel-gas shutoff valve be located?

answers.text: In a different room from the appliance, behind a locked panel, so it cannot be reached while the appliance is operating at full input
At the meter set only, since individual appliance shutoffs are not permitted anywhere downstream of the meter in a building system
Inside the appliance cabinet, reachable only after the burner access panel and the blower panel have both been removed by a technician
Accessible, in the same room as the appliance, within 6 feet of the appliance it serves

questions.explanation: An appliance shutoff valve must be accessible, in the same room as the appliance, and within 6 feet of the appliance it serves. That accessible same-room placement within 6 feet is the keyed requirement.

questions.question: In the field, a duct main was rerouted around a new opening and now sits 4 feet from its drawn location. What must happen to the record documents?

answers.text: Nothing, because field reroutes under ten feet are considered too minor to document and future crews are expected to locate concealed duct by sounding walls
The original plan should be destroyed and replaced with a verbal description given to the building engineer during the final walkthrough meeting
The change should be photographed for the crew's own files but kept off the record set so the drawings continue to match the approved permit documents exactly
The as-built set must show the duct in its actual location

questions.explanation: Record drawings must reflect what was actually built, including a 4-foot reroute, so future work can find the duct. Minor-change exemptions, verbal descriptions, and private photographs all leave the official record wrong.

questions.question: What is the employer's basic duty for workplace safety and protective equipment?

answers.text: To post a safety policy at the office, after which each employee bears sole responsibility for recognizing and avoiding every job hazard
To require employees to buy their own protective equipment in all cases, since providing equipment is treated as a voluntary benefit
To act only after an injury occurs, since the safety duty arises from the injury report rather than from known hazards in the work
To provide a workplace free from recognized hazards and supply needed personal protective equipment and training for its use

questions.explanation: The employer must provide a workplace free from recognized hazards and supply needed personal protective equipment and training for its use. That duty is proactive; it does not wait for an injury to occur.

questions.question: A compressor fails with washed-out bearings and scored surfaces, and service history shows months of operation with superheat near zero at the compressor inlet. What mechanism connects that history to this failure?

answers.text: High discharge temperature from chronic overheating thinned the oil
Excessive subcooling hardened the bearing surfaces over time
Low suction pressure raised the compression ratio until the bearings scored, until the suction pressure recovered on its own
Liquid refrigerant returning to the compressor diluted and washed oil off the bearing surfaces (floodback)

questions.explanation: Sustained floodback sends liquid refrigerant into the crankcase, diluting the oil and stripping the lubricating film from bearings until they score and fail. Option A describes an overheating failure, but near-zero superheat means the suction gas was cold and saturated, not overheated. Option B names a condenser-side condition with no such bearing effect, and option C contradicts the history, since floodback conditions accompany ample, not low, suction-side refrigerant.

questions.question: After electrical service work, a three-phase scroll compressor starts and runs loudly with no cooling, and suction pressure rises instead of falling. The first check is:

answers.text: Manifold gas pressure, because a reversed scroll compressor changes the gas valve setting of the furnace sharing the same gas line in the building
The thermostat anticipator setting, because incorrect anticipation causes compressors to run backward for complete cooling cycles at a time
Phase rotation; a scroll running backward produces little compression and can be damaged
The sediment trap at the furnace, because debris in the gas line is a common cause of electrical phase reversal at a compressor motor

questions.explanation: Phase rotation; a scroll running backward produces little compression and can be damaged. Gas pressure, thermostat anticipation, and a gas-line trap have nothing to do with rotation; reversed phases after service work are the prime suspect.

questions.question: Why do refrigerant records for purchases, recovery, and appliance service need dates, quantities, and the identity of the parties involved?

answers.text: They create an auditable trail showing refrigerant was bought, handled, recovered, and disposed of through proper channels
They are used by suppliers to set the retail price of refrigerant each season, based on the total quantities each contractor reports purchasing during the previous year
They replace the need for certified technicians to handle refrigerant
They prove a system was charged correctly without any gauge readings

questions.explanation: Traceable records demonstrate compliant handling across the refrigerant's path. Pricing is a market matter unrelated to record fields, certification requirements still apply to handlers, and paperwork alone cannot prove a correct charge, which is verified by measurement.

questions.question: A contractor marks up a $1,000 job cost by 20% to set the price. What is the resulting price and its gross margin?

answers.text: $1,200 price; about 16.7% margin
$1,200 price and a 20.0 percent margin, because markup on cost and margin on price are always identical
$1,250 price and a 20.0 percent margin, found by using the margin divisor formula instead of the stated markup
$1,020 price and a 2.0 percent margin, found by adding the markup rate as a flat dollar amount

questions.explanation: A is correct because a 20 percent markup gives $1,200, and the $200 profit divided by $1,200 is about 16.7 percent margin. B is incorrect because a 20 percent markup does not produce a 20 percent margin. C is incorrect because it prices with the margin formula when the problem states a markup. D is incorrect because it treats 20 percent as $20 rather than 20 percent of $1,000.

questions.question: A contractor operates as a sole proprietor. What is the owner's liability position for the business?

answers.text: The owner is liable only up to the value of the equipment the business owns, and personal assets are protected by the business registration alone
The owner shares liability equally with every employee, so no single person is responsible for the whole of a business debt or obligation
The owner is personally liable for the debts and obligations of the business
The owner has no liability for business debts once the business obtains its own tax identification number and a separate business bank account

questions.explanation: In a sole proprietorship there is no legal separation between owner and business, so the owner is personally liable for the debts and obligations of the business. That unlimited personal liability is the form's defining risk.

questions.question: Why do contracting businesses retain job, payroll, and tax records for a set period after a project ends?

answers.text: So the supplier can reuse the customer's equipment selections as a template for quoting unrelated future customers
