To support audits, warranty questions, tax filings, and dispute resolution
Only to fill archive space required by the office lease, with no business or legal purpose served by keeping them
To allow employees to revise their recorded hours after final pay whenever they disagree with the original timesheets

questions.explanation: B is correct because retained records substantiate taxes, payroll, warranty history, and the facts if a dispute or audit arises. A is incorrect because a customer's project records are not a supplier quoting template. C is incorrect because retention serves compliance and business purposes, not lease space requirements. D is incorrect because records are kept to preserve an accurate history, not to permit after-the-fact timesheet changes.

questions.question: A typical contractor workmanship warranty differs from a manufacturer's equipment warranty in which way?

answers.text: The workmanship warranty covers the contractor's installation work; the manufacturer's covers its equipment defects
The workmanship warranty covers the factory's equipment defects, while the manufacturer covers the contractor's labor errors
Both warranties are identical in coverage, and the distinction exists only for marketing purposes in the proposal
The manufacturer's warranty covers the contractor's installation workmanship for as long as the building remains standing

questions.explanation: A is correct because the contractor warrants its own installation work while the manufacturer warrants defects in its equipment. B is incorrect because it reverses the two parties' responsibilities. C is incorrect because the coverage, responsible party, and claim route genuinely differ. D is incorrect because a manufacturer does not warrant the installing contractor's workmanship.

questions.question: A condensing furnace develops intermittent pressure-switch trips in mid-winter that clear when the technician drains a large amount of water from the secondary heat exchanger area. The root cause is:

answers.text: An oversized vent termination screen that gradually collects frost and lint outdoors until it blocks the entire vent outlet and shuts the furnace down on every call for heat
A high-fire manifold pressure set too low
A flame sensor coated with silica
A partially blocked condensate drain or trap that lets condensate back up into the secondary exchanger and venting path, restricting draft

questions.explanation: Backed-up condensate occupies exchanger and vent passages, so draft falls intermittently until the water is drained — the drain or trap restriction is the fault to clear. Option A can restrict the vent but would not explain water draining from the exchanger. Option B affects heat output, not draft proving. Option C causes flame-proving shutdowns after ignition, not pressure-switch trips before it.

questions.question: An ERV serving a northern building loses capacity and shows rising pressure drop across the core every cold snap, recovering each thaw. What is happening and what is the standard remedy?

answers.text: The wheel motor is failing only in cold weather, and replacing the motor each winter is the accepted maintenance practice
Frost is building up in the core as moist exhaust air freezes — use a designed frost-control strategy such as preheat, bypass, or defrost cycle
The outdoor-air filters are loading with snow dust, which is cured by removing the filters for the entire heating season

The building is over-ventilated, and permanently closing the outdoor-air intake each winter is the standard operating remedy, and post a laminated sign instructing the operators to keep the outdoor-air intake closed until the spring thaw arrives

questions.explanation: Exhaust moisture condenses and freezes in the core at low outdoor temperatures; engineered defrost or preheat keeps the unit running. Option A misdiagnoses a thermal problem as a recurring motor failure, option C sacrifices filtration for the season and still leaves frost forming, and option D abandons required ventilation instead of controlling frost.

questions.question: After passing, what general liability insurance certificate must be submitted by an applicant who will offer services to the public?

answers.text: A certificate for $3,000 in combined coverage, matching the surety bond amount, from any insurer the applicant chooses in any state
A certificate for $160,000 in combined coverage, matching the biennial renewal fee multiplied across the licensing period, from a NJ insurer
A certificate for $500,000 for combined property damage and bodily injury in any one accident or occurrence, from an insurer authorized in New Jersey
No certificate at all, since general liability coverage is optional for a master who acts as a bona fide representative of a licensed entity

questions.explanation: The certificate must show $500,000 for combined property damage and bodily injury to or death of one or more persons in any one accident or occurrence. The insurer must be authorized and licensed to do business in New Jersey, or DOBI-approved proof of self-insurance may be submitted.

questions.question: After a fuel change to propane, a furnace soots, rolls flame out of the heat exchanger openings, and trips its rollout switch. The gas valve was converted, but the original natural gas orifices are still installed. What best explains the symptoms?

answers.text: The furnace is underfired because propane orifices were required to be larger, so the weak flame is being pulled out of the openings by excessive induced draft at the vent connector
The rollout trips are an electrical coincidence, because orifice size has no effect on input, flame shape, or heat exchanger temperature once the gas valve regulator is converted
Sooting after conversion is expected break-in behavior for propane, and the correct response is to reset the rollout switch repeatedly until the soot burns off the heat exchanger
The oversized natural gas orifices overfire the burners on propane

questions.explanation: Natural gas orifices are too large for richer propane at propane manifold pressure, so the burners are heavily overfired, producing soot, distorted flame, and rollout. The fault is excessive rather than weak input, orifice size directly sets firing rate, and repeated rollout resets ignore a hazardous firing condition.

questions.question: An HVACR contractor licensed in another state wants a New Jersey license without taking the examination. When is that possible?

answers.text: The license is available without examination only if the other state's standards are equal or comparable to New Jersey's and that state permits New Jersey licensees to obtain licensure there based on a New Jersey license

The license is available without examination whenever the other state's standards are equal or comparable, even if that state does not license New Jersey licensees in return, and the applicant need not show any proof that the other state would license a New Jersey master on the same terms
The license is available without examination whenever the other state licenses New Jersey licensees in return, even if that state's standards fall below New Jersey's
The license is never available without examination, and every out-of-state applicant must pass both portions regardless of the other state's standards or treatment

questions.explanation: Reciprocity requires both prongs: standards equal or comparable to New Jersey's, and the other state permitting New Jersey licensees to obtain licensure there based on a New Jersey license. The applicant submits the Board form with a full street name and number, proof of age 21, a passport-size photo taken within the last six months, proof of the education requirements, proof of the other state's reciprocal treatment and of licensure, and the application fee, and after the Board determines comparability the applicant submits the bond, insurance, and licensing fee.

questions.question: Airflow complaint. With bedroom doors open the system heats and cools evenly, but with doors closed the bedrooms go stuffy, airflow at their registers drops noticeably, and a whistle sounds under the doors. There is no ducted return in the bedrooms. A manometer reads each closed bedroom about +4 Pa relative to the hallway, and the hallway side goes slightly negative. Door undercuts measure only about half an inch. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Supply dampers to the bedrooms closing on their own, which would cut register airflow whether the doors were open or closed rather than track door position exactly
A return duct leak in the hallway zone, which would depressurize the main body regardless of bedroom door position and would not pressurize each closed bedroom in turn
A blower that slows when back pressure rises on its control board, which would reduce airflow to the whole house rather than redistribute it based on which doors are shut
Closed bedrooms pressurizing because they have no return-air path

questions.explanation: Supply air enters each closed bedroom with no way back except a half-inch undercut, so the room pressurizes to about +4 Pa, supply flow into it falls, and air whistles under the door. Dampers would not track door position, a return leak would not pressurize individual rooms, and a blower response would change total airflow rather than create room-by-room pressure differences.

questions.question: A new draw-through air handler on a cooling coil pulls air across the coil, so its drain pan is under negative pressure. It is piped with a straight pipe from the pan to the drain with no trap, and at startup air is sucked up the drain line and condensate overflows the pan. What was missed?

answers.text: The drain needed a larger diameter so air could enter faster
A trap of adequate depth is needed so its water seal resists the negative pressure and lets condensate drain instead of being held in the pan
The pan needed a safety switch instead of any trap

The drain should have been connected to the liquid line to equalize pressure, tying the condensate piping directly into the sealed refrigerant circuit so the two pressures balance each other at startup

questions.explanation: On a draw-through unit the fan can draw air up an untrapped drain and hold water in the pan until it overflows; a trap with enough depth holds a seal against that pressure difference. Option A would admit more air, option C adds protection against overflow but does not make the drain work, and option D would join condensate piping to refrigerant piping, which is never correct.

questions.question: A replacement job involves connecting wiring for a 20-ton unit on a 240-volt system from an adequately sized equipment service disconnect. Which conditions must all be met for this replacement-wiring scope?

answers.text: The work may be new installation wiring, the equipment may exceed 25 tons, and the voltage may exceed 240 volts if the disconnect is new
The work must be performed by an apprentice alone, the disconnect may be replaced as part of the job, and no code provision needs to be followed
The case must be a replacement, each piece of equipment must be 25 tons or less, the voltage must be 240 volts or less, and the connection must follow the Uniform Construction Code
The case must be a replacement, and no tonnage limit, voltage limit, or code requirement applies to wiring run from a service disconnect box

questions.explanation: Replacement wiring is allowed in replacement cases only, from an equipment service disconnect box of adequate size. Each piece of equipment must be 25 tons or less, the system voltage must be 240 volts or less, and the connection must be performed according to all relevant Uniform Construction Code provisions; the 20-ton, 240-volt facts fit those limits.

new-mexico-hvac.quiz_title: New Mexico HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Where is a suction accumulator installed, and what is its main job?

answers.text: In the liquid line just after the receiver, to store extra liquid refrigerant so the expansion valve always sees a completely solid column of liquid
In the suction line just before the compressor, to catch liquid and meter it back as vapor and oil
In the discharge line just after the compressor, to separate oil from hot gas and return that oil directly to the compressor crankcase by a float
In the condenser outlet ahead of the receiver, to subcool the liquid further whenever the ambient temperature around the unit rises above design

questions.explanation: The accumulator sits in the suction line at the compressor inlet, trapping liquid slugs and returning them gradually through a small orifice with oil. A liquid-line vessel after the receiver describes receiver/storage duty, a discharge-line float device describes an oil separator, and extra subcooling at the condenser outlet is not the accumulator's location or function.

questions.question: Why does a small voltage imbalance cause a much larger current imbalance in a three-phase motor?

answers.text: Because the overload heaters are sized differently on each leg, so the currents are forced apart by the protective devices rather than the motor itself
The motor's low impedance to unbalanced currents multiplies the effect, adding heat
Because the equipment grounding conductor carries one phase of the imbalance, which unbalances the currents measured in the three supply conductors
Because the contactor poles wear at different rates every cycle, which continuously changes the phase sequence seen by the motor while it is running

questions.explanation: The motor's low impedance to unbalanced currents multiplies the effect, adding heat. Heater sizing, grounding conductors, and contactor wear do not create the effect; unbalanced voltage drives disproportionate unbalanced current and heating.

questions.question: Why does the furnace or air handler blower matter to a cooling system's rated combination?

answers.text: The blower matters only for heating season, because cooling capacity is set entirely at the outdoor unit and airflow is secondary
Blower airflow across the coil is part of the tested combination, and wrong airflow changes capacity, efficiency, and dehumidification
A stronger blower always raises the rating, so oversizing the air handler is a reliable way to gain extra efficiency points
Blower selection affects only noise level, since the coil removes the same moisture regardless of the air volume crossing it

questions.explanation: Rated performance assumes a specified airflow; too much or too little distorts sensible and latent capacity. The blower is central in cooling as well as heating, more airflow is not automatically better, and moisture removal is strongly airflow-dependent.

questions.question: In an estimate, what is the purpose of an allowance?

answers.text: A penalty amount withheld from a subcontractor whenever a scheduled milestone is missed on the project
A guaranteed profit amount the contractor may keep even if the selected item is never purchased
A budgeted placeholder amount for a selection not yet made
A contingency reserve the owner controls exclusively for correcting defective work after final payment

questions.explanation: C is correct because an allowance reserves a stated amount in the price for an item the owner has not yet selected. A is incorrect because withholding for missed milestones describes a different contract remedy. B is incorrect because an allowance is tied to the cost of the selected item, not guaranteed profit. D is incorrect because an allowance is set at pricing time for an undecided selection, not a post-payment defect fund.

questions.question: Which basic license fee pairing is correct under the CID fee rule?

answers.text: MM-3 and the other non-98 classifications cost $50.00 per year or $100.00 for two years, while MM-98 costs $100.00 per year or $200.00 for two years
MM-3 and the other non-98 classifications cost $100.00 per year or $200.00 for two years, while MM-98 costs $50.00 per year or $100.00 for two years
Every mechanical classification, including MM-98, costs $75.00 per year or $150.00 for two years under a single uniform basic license fee
MM-3 costs $50.00 per year with no two-year option, while MM-98 costs $200.00 per year with a mandatory four-year payment at initial licensure

questions.explanation: Non-98 classifications run $50.00 per year or $100.00 for two years, and the -98 classifications, including MM-98, run $100.00 per year or $200.00 for two years.

questions.question: A service van is being stocked for the first A2L jobs of the season. Which addition most directly addresses the new hazard?

answers.text: A larger halide torch kit with spare tips, because flame-based detection will be needed more often as flammable refrigerants become more common
A set of ungrounded extension cords for recovery equipment, because flexible power arrangements matter more than atmosphere monitoring on these jobs
Extra venting hose for releasing small charges outdoors, because small A2L quantities may be released when a recovery cylinder is unavailable
A combustible-gas / A2L leak monitor for the work area

questions.explanation: Monitoring the work area for flammable concentration is a core A2L-era addition to the truck. Flame detection moves in the wrong direction, damaged or ungrounded power arrangements add ignition risk, and releasing even small charges is prohibited venting regardless of cylinder availability.

questions.question: With the air handler running, a large supply trunk joint in the attic is found disconnected. The house measures slightly negative with respect to outdoors while the system runs. Why?

answers.text: The return grille is oversized, so the blower moves extra outdoor air into the house and the attic joint is merely venting that surplus air back outside
Supply air lost in the attic is replaced by air the return side no longer gets back, which would pressurize the house because the blower is still delivering its full rated flow

The house goes negative relative to outdoors, because supply air dumped into the attic never comes back through the return side, so the blower pulls replacement air in through leaks in the building shell
The disconnected joint acts like a second return that draws attic air into the supply stream and pushes the house positive whenever the blower runs

questions.explanation: Supply air dumped outside the envelope never returns, so the house loses air and drifts negative while the system runs. An oversized return grille does not import outdoor air, the lost supply cannot pressurize a house it is leaving, and a supply-side opening blows air out rather than drawing attic air in as a return would.

questions.question: An energy recovery ventilator fitted with an enthalpy (total-energy) wheel does what that a plain plate heat exchanger handling only sensible heat does not?

answers.text: It generates chilled water as a byproduct of spinning the wheel through the two opposing airstreams in the unit
It removes grease from kitchen exhaust so the exhaust can be routed through occupied space without a rated duct
It transfers moisture as well as heat between the exhaust and outdoor airstreams, reducing the latent load in humid weather
It raises the outdoor-air temperature above the exhaust-air temperature in winter using only the energy in the exhaust stream

questions.explanation: An enthalpy medium exchanges water vapor along with heat, trimming both sensible and latent loads. Option A invents a refrigeration byproduct the wheel cannot produce, option B assigns it a grease-cleaning role it does not have, and option D claims a temperature lift beyond what passive recovery from the exhaust stream can deliver.

questions.question: Under the longest-length method for gas piping, which run establishes the length used to size the piping?

answers.text: The length used is the run from the meter to the hydraulically most remote appliance outlet.
The length used is the shortest branch run in the system, since it carries gas with the least resistance.
The length used is the average of all branch lengths, rounded down to the nearest listed increment.
The length used is the vent connector length of the largest appliance served by the piping system.

questions.explanation: The longest-length method sizes from the meter, or point of delivery, to the farthest appliance outlet, so every branch has adequate pressure available.

questions.question: Which conviction falls on New Mexico's list of felonies that may disqualify a contractor license applicant?

answers.text: A conviction for embezzlement is on the list of disqualifying felonies
A conviction for a non-listed misdemeanor traffic offense is on the list of disqualifying felonies for every applicant in all classifications
A conviction under a municipal noise ordinance is on the list of disqualifying felonies, ranked alongside fraud and racketeering offenses
A juvenile adjudication for a school disciplinary offense is on the list of disqualifying felonies used for contractor applicants

questions.explanation: The disqualifying-felony list includes embezzlement along with offenses such as robbery, fraud, forgery, arson, and racketeering. Traffic misdemeanors and juvenile adjudications are not on that list.

questions.question: Which finding during a heat exchanger inspection is grounds for taking the furnace out of service until the exchanger or furnace is addressed?

answers.text: Light surface discoloration on the outside of one cell with no holes, cracks, distortion, or flue-gas leakage demonstrated at all
A thin layer of dust on top of the exchanger that wipes off easily and matches dust found throughout the blower compartment area
Slightly uneven burner flame color between two burners that disappears after the burner faces are cleaned and aligned properly
A visible crack or hole through the exchanger wall

questions.explanation: A through-wall crack or hole lets flue gas and carbon monoxide enter the supply airstream and requires removing the furnace from service pending repair or replacement. Option A describes cosmetic discoloration, option B describes ordinary dust, and option C describes a cleanable burner issue, none of which breach the exchanger wall.

questions.question: Which risk does a commercial general liability policy primarily cover for an HVAC contractor?

answers.text: It primarily covers the contractor's own tools stolen from the shop, replacing them at full purchase price with no deductible or depreciation applied
It primarily covers third-party claims for bodily injury and property damage arising from the contractor's operations
It primarily covers the contractor's unpaid supplier invoices, guaranteeing payment to every material supplier on every project the firm undertakes that year
It primarily covers the cost of redoing the contractor's own defective work, including tear-out and replacement of the contractor's installed equipment itself

questions.explanation: General liability responds to claims by others for bodily injury and property damage from the firm's operations; tools, supplier credit, and the firm's own defective work sit elsewhere.

questions.question: A rooftop R-410A unit trips toward high head on a 98°F afternoon. Readings: head 448 psig, suction 136 psig, superheat 11°F, subcooling 8°F, discharge line 212°F, condenser fan running at full speed with normal amps, and the condenser coil face matted with cottonwood and dirt. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A fouled condenser coil
A stuck-open expansion valve flooding the evaporator, which would collapse superheat toward zero and frost the suction line back to the compressor
An undercharge, which would lower both head and suction pressure and raise superheat well above the 11°F measured here
A weak compressor with leaking discharge valves, which cannot build head pressure and would show a low head with an abnormally high suction pressure

questions.explanation: High head pressure with normal superheat, normal subcooling, and a very hot discharge line points to heat rejection failure at a visibly fouled condenser. An undercharge lowers both pressures and raises superheat, an overfeeding valve collapses superheat, and weak compressor valves prevent head pressure from building at all — none matches a 448 psig head.

questions.question: Suction piping passing through a warm, humid mechanical room sweats and drips onto equipment below, even though the insulation is thick. Inspection finds gaps at joints and an unsealed vapor barrier. The fix is to:

answers.text: Remove the insulation so the line can dry in room air
Paint the pipe with standard latex paint only
Restore continuous insulation with sealed joints and an intact outer vapor barrier so moist air cannot reach the cold pipe surface

Raise suction pressure until the line is above room temperature by restricting the compressor suction service valve and holding it partly closed through all operating conditions, including full-load pulldown

questions.explanation: Condensation forms when humid air reaches a surface below its dew point, so insulation must be continuous and vapor-sealed at every joint and fitting. Removing insulation in option A exposes more cold surface, option B alone is not a vapor-sealed insulation system, and option D would destroy the refrigeration temperatures the line must carry.

questions.question: Water stains appear on a ceiling below a rooftop unit only during windy rainstorms, never during cooling operation, and the drain pan is dry at inspection. What source is most likely?

answers.text: Wind-driven rain entering at curb flashing, a cabinet seam, or an unsealed adapter joint rather than condensate produced by the cooling process

Condensate overflowing the pan only while the blower is off, with the water traveling upward through the duct to stain the ceiling from above even after the obvious maintenance items at the unit have already been checked and corrected first

Refrigerant oil leaking from the coil and being mistaken for water, since oil stains spread only during storms when roof traffic is heaviest while the rest of the system continues to operate normally through a complete cycle of operation
Gas heat condensate forming in summer storms, because the idle gas section condenses moisture from humid air passing over its exchanger

questions.explanation: Staining tied to wind and rain with a dry pan points to the building envelope at the curb, flashing, or adapter seams, not to system condensate. Pan overflow does not travel upward, refrigerant oil is not storm-dependent, and an idle heat exchanger does not generate condensate in summer.

questions.question: SCENARIO: A two-person HVAC shop owner proposes skipping workers' compensation coverage to save money, arguing the crew is careful. What is the correct assessment?

answers.text: The proposal is acceptable for crews under three people, since very small employers are automatically excused from carrying workers' compensation coverage
The proposal is acceptable if each employee signs a waiver releasing the employer, since private waivers replace the statutory coverage requirement entirely
The proposal is acceptable during the shop's first year, since new businesses are granted a grace period before coverage duties attach to their payroll
Workers' compensation coverage is a legal obligation for the employer, and noncompliance carries penalties and, in New Mexico, invalidates the contractor license

questions.explanation: Workers' compensation is mandatory coverage, not an optional economy; New Mexico ties noncompliance to the validity of the contractor license itself.

questions.question: Halfway through a large job, job costing shows labor at 80% of budget while the work is only 50% complete. What is the best immediate response?

answers.text: Ignore the report until final billing, because mid-job figures almost always correct themselves without action
Bill the owner for the entire remaining contract balance immediately, whether or not that work has been performed
Reduce the crew's recorded hours retroactively so the cost report aligns with the original estimate on paper
Investigate the overrun cause and reforecast the cost to complete

questions.explanation: D is correct because a labor overrun at mid-job requires finding the cause and updating the forecast while corrective action is still possible. A is incorrect because waiting removes the chance to correct productivity or scope problems. B is incorrect because billing for unperformed work is not a response to a cost overrun. C is incorrect because altering time records falsifies the job-cost data the decision depends on.

questions.question: Intermittent no-heat. A furnace runs reliably on calm days but locks out on pressure-switch faults during gusty wind. Its vent terminates on a wall near an outside corner where gusts sweep past. Measured inducer vacuum hovers at about 1.15 in. w.c. against a switch rating of 0.95 in. w.c., dipping to 0.7 in. w.c. during gusts; with the vent temporarily disconnected at the furnace for testing, vacuum holds a steady 1.4 in. w.c. Drains and trap are clear and the inducer is strong. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A marginal inducer that weakens in cold wind, ruled out because the same inducer holds a steady 1.4 in. w.c. once the termination's wind exposure is removed from the test
A condensate trap that plugs only on windy days, which has no mechanism tying drain blockage to gusts and is verified clear during these windy-day failures
Wind at the vent termination disturbing inducer vacuum enough to trip the switch
A pressure switch whose contacts bounce in vibration, which would fault on calm days with blower vibration as well rather than correlate tightly with outdoor gusts

questions.explanation: Vacuum is marginal to begin with and gusts at the poorly placed termination push it from 1.15 down through the 0.95 in. w.c. trip point to 0.7, while the inducer proves strong and steady at 1.4 in. w.c. without the termination's influence. The inducer, trap, and switch each fail to explain the strict correlation with wind that the termination location explains directly.

questions.question: A technician fixes the same no-cooling symptom three times by replacing a capacitor, yet the unit keeps failing each heat wave. What does callback analysis say about this pattern?

answers.text: The capacitor is likely a victim rather than the root cause, so the investigation should look for what is stressing it, such as low voltage, heat, or a struggling compressor

Replacing the same capacitor repeatedly on every callback is the correct long-term strategy, and the technician should keep installing identical parts until one finally holds through an entire summer season
The customer is at fault because heat waves coincide with the failures
Warranty requires installing the same part a fourth time before deeper diagnosis

questions.explanation: Repeated failure of the same component signals an upstream cause that must be found. Continuing identical replacements wastes visits and leaves the fault. Heat waves expose the weakness but blaming the customer or the weather does not fix it, and no warranty rule forbids proper diagnosis.

questions.question: On a duct layout, a small diamond symbol on a branch duct is noted as a volume damper, and the branch serves a room that is overheating. What does that symbol tell the balancing technician?

answers.text: An adjustable damper at that location can throttle the branch
The branch contains a fire damper that must be removed from the airstream before any additional cooling can reach the overheated room
The diamond marks a test port where static pressure is recorded once at startup and the branch airflow itself can never be adjusted afterward
The branch is a spare takeoff capped inside the main, and the overheating must be corrected by increasing total fan speed for the whole system

questions.explanation: The symbol identifies an adjustable volume damper the technician can throttle to reduce airflow to the overheating room. It is not a fire damper, a fixed test port, or a capped spare, and raising total fan speed would add air where it is not wanted.

nevada-hvac.quiz_title: Nevada HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: In an air-cooled condenser, which condition most directly reduces the coil's ability to reject heat?

answers.text: A clean coil with full airflow
A layer of dirt and debris insulating the fins and blocking airflow through the coil
A liquid line that is a few degrees subcooled below saturation as it leaves the condenser and travels through a long, well-insulated run to the indoor coil
An evaporator with correct superheat

questions.explanation: Dirt both insulates the fin surface and restricts airflow, so heat rejection falls and head pressure rises. Option A is the desired condition, option C describes normal subcooled liquid leaving a condenser, and option D is an evaporator measurement that does not impair the condenser itself.

questions.question: A critical exhaust fan on a VFD is specified with a bypass. The bypass exists so the fan can:

answers.text: Continue at variable speed after the drive has failed, because the bypass contains a second complete drive in the same enclosure package
Run across the line at full speed if the drive fails
Operate without any overload protection, because bypass contactors are permitted to carry motor current with no protective device in the circuit
Be serviced while energized, because selecting bypass removes the need to lock out the equipment before opening the drive enclosure

questions.explanation: Run across the line at full speed if the drive fails. A bypass is a full-speed fallback, not a second drive, and it removes neither overload protection nor lockout requirements.

questions.question: During an R-22 system replacement, what must happen to the refrigerant in the old unit?

answers.text: It may be vented slowly after dark, provided the amount is small and the technician stands upwind of the release point
It must be recovered into approved cylinders and not vented, then handled through proper reclaim or disposal channels
It should be pumped into the new system's lines to top off the factory charge and reduce the cost of new refrigerant
It can be released into a bucket of water, which absorbs the refrigerant and makes the release acceptable in the field

questions.explanation: Recovery without venting is required, and recovered refrigerant goes to reclaim or approved disposal. Venting is prohibited regardless of timing or amount, old R-22 must not be put into a system built for another refrigerant, and water does not make a release acceptable.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the purpose of a preliminary notice in lien practice?

answers.text: The notice transfers the sender's lien rights to the lender financing the project for the remainder of the work.
The notice converts an unpaid invoice into a judgment without any further legal step by the sender.

The notice releases every lien right the sender holds on the project, in exchange for a promise of future payment from the owner, and the release takes effect even if that promised payment is never actually made to the sender.
The notice alerts the owner that the sender furnished labor or materials to the project, preserving and publicizing the sender's potential lien rights.

questions.explanation: Preliminary notice puts the owner on record that a potential lien claimant contributed to the project, which is how rights are preserved and surfaced early. The key states that purpose.

questions.question: General liability insurance for a contractor primarily protects against which risk?

answers.text: The cost of redoing the contractor's own defective installation workmanship whenever the owner is dissatisfied with it
Third-party bodily injury or property damage claims arising from operations
Lost profit when a job takes longer than estimated and the crew must remain on site for additional weeks
The replacement cost of the contractor's own tools if they are stolen from a locked vehicle at the job site

questions.explanation: B is correct because general liability responds to third-party injury and property damage claims arising from the contractor's operations. A is incorrect because repairing the contractor's own defective work is generally a workmanship cost, not a liability claim. C is incorrect because schedule overruns and lost profit are business risks, not covered third-party claims. D is incorrect because theft of the contractor's own tools is a property or inland marine concern.

questions.question: A technician must pinpoint a suspected R-454B leak inside a small indoor mechanical closet. Which leak-detection approach fits A2L service?

answers.text: A lit propane torch passed slowly along each joint, because the flame color method remains acceptable when the room is small and the door is left open
A standard combustible-gas lighter used as a test flame at each fitting, because a small flame presents less risk than a full-size torch flame
An ultrasonic detector alone with no confirmation, because sound-based tools also measure refrigerant concentration against the lower flammability limit
An electronic detector rated for A2L refrigerants

questions.explanation: Electronic detectors listed or rated for A2L use detect the leak without introducing ignition. Any open-flame method adds an ignition source regardless of flame size or door position, and an ultrasonic tool hears leak noise but does not measure concentration or confirm refrigerant identity by itself.

questions.question: Registers whistle and doors slam under pressure only when the smallest zone calls alone; with all zones calling the system is quiet. What best explains the pattern?

answers.text: The refrigerant charge is correct only when all zones call, because zone dampers meter refrigerant between the indoor coil and the registers serving each part of the house
The smallest zone's thermostat is wired to raise blower speed above its setting whenever it is the only thermostat in the entire house asking for conditioning
The outdoor unit becomes louder indoors on single-zone calls, and the whistling is compressor sound transmitted through the line set rather than air moving in the ducts
Full equipment airflow forced through the smallest duct path raises velocity and static pressure there

questions.explanation: With only the smallest path open, the same blower output must pass through far less duct area, so velocity, static pressure, register noise, and room pressurization all rise. The pattern follows the open duct area rather than refrigerant charge, thermostat wiring, or compressor sound.

questions.question: A cold-climate house with winter window condensation improves when a properly sized exhaust ventilation system runs steadily. Why does ventilation act as a moisture cure here?

answers.text: Exhaust fans warm the window glass by circulating indoor air faster, raising the glass above the dew point so condensation cannot form on it
Dry outdoor air dilutes indoor moisture
Ventilation pressurizes the house with outdoor air, which pushes indoor moisture back into the wall cavities where it can no longer reach the windows
The fans remove the coldest indoor air first because it pools at the exhaust grilles, leaving warmer, drier air behind in the living spaces

questions.explanation: Cold outdoor air holds very little moisture, so when it replaces exhausted indoor air and is heated, indoor RH falls and window condensation eases. Exhaust fans do not meaningfully warm glass, exhaust-only ventilation depressurizes rather than pressurizes the house, and fans remove mixed room air, not a selectively cold layer at the grille.

questions.question: Which statement correctly gives the passing standard for the Construction Management Survey examination?

answers.text: The CMS minimum passing score is 45 of 60 questions, which the bulletin states as 75 percent correct.
The CMS minimum passing score is 60 of 85 questions, matching the raw-count standard used for the C-21 trade examination.
The CMS minimum passing score is 50 of 60 questions, which the bulletin states as a passing standard for first-time candidates only.
The CMS minimum passing score is 42 of 60 questions, stated in the bulletin as a raw count with no percentage attached to it.

questions.explanation: Fact 9 gives the CMS standard as a minimum passing score of 45, stated in the bulletin as 75 percent of the 60 scored questions; the largest CMS outline cell is Financial Management at 12 questions (fact 10).

questions.question: In general terms, an employer's duties under occupational safety rules include which of the following?

answers.text: Requiring employees to purchase all of their own protective equipment with no guidance about its proper use
Reporting only those injuries that result in a customer complaint, and keeping all other incidents unrecorded
Delegating all safety responsibility to the newest employee, because that person is closest to the daily hazards
Providing a workplace free of recognized hazards and training employees on hazards of their work

questions.explanation: D is correct because employers must address recognized hazards and train employees about the hazards and protections of their work. A is incorrect because the employer is responsible for providing required protective equipment and instruction. B is incorrect because injury reporting and recording duties do not depend on customer complaints. C is incorrect because safety responsibility rests with the employer and cannot be handed to the newest hire.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes claims against a Nevada contractor's surety bond?

answers.text: An action on the bond must be brought within 2 years of the act, employee labor claims are preferred, and the Board may not claim against the bond for administrative fines.
Employee labor claims are paid after all other claims against the bond, and an action on the bond must be brought within 1 year of the act.
The bond runs only in favor of the State, so owners, employees and suppliers injured by a contractor's unlawful acts have no claim against it.

An action on the bond may be brought at any time within 5 years of the act, and the Board may claim against the bond to collect its administrative fines including fines the Board has already assessed against the contractor for earlier violations of the licensing law.

questions.explanation: Fact 19 states the 2-year action window, the preference for employee labor claims, and the bar on the Board claiming against the bond for administrative fines; the bond runs in favor of the State for owners, employees, suppliers and injured persons.

questions.question: Which statement correctly gives the format and passing standard of the C-21 trade examination?

answers.text: The C-21 trade examination has 60 questions, a minimum passing score of 45 questions, a time limit of 2 hours, and an open-book format.
The C-21 trade examination has 100 questions, a minimum passing score of 60 questions, a time limit of 4 hours, and an open-book format.
The C-21 trade examination has 85 questions, a minimum passing score of 60 questions, a time limit of 3 hours, and an open-book format.
The C-21 trade examination has 85 questions, a minimum passing score of 65 questions, a time limit of 3 hours, and a closed-book format.

questions.explanation: Fact 6 and fact 24 both state the trade standard as a raw count: 85 questions, a minimum passing score of 60, 3 hours, open book.

questions.question: A system shows suction 94 psig, superheat 22°F, subcooling 18°F, head 330 psig, and a 9°F temperature drop measured across the liquid-line filter drier with light frost forming on its outlet side only. Airflow is normal and the evaporator is clean. What is the correct repair decision?

answers.text: Replace the liquid-line filter drier
Add refrigerant until superheat falls, which would mask the starvation while pressures downstream of the restriction remained low and the real blockage stayed in place
Replace the TXV, since a starved evaporator always means the valve has failed, even when a 9°F drop across the drier localizes the restriction upstream of it
Raise condenser airflow to lower the head pressure, which does nothing for a liquid-line blockage that is already proven by the temperature drop

questions.explanation: High subcooling with a starved evaporator seems contradictory until the 9°F drop across the drier localizes a liquid restriction: liquid backs up in the condenser while little reaches the coil. Adding charge only masks the starvation, the TXV sits downstream of the proven restriction, and condenser airflow cannot clear a blocked drier — the drier is replaced and the system rechecked.

questions.question: A long suction run was undersized, creating a large suction pressure drop between evaporator and compressor. Even if evaporator temperature looks right, system capacity and efficiency suffer because:

answers.text: The compressor must work against a higher compression ratio from its lower inlet pressure, moving less refrigerant per revolution

The condenser receives more heat than it was designed for from the pipe itself, because the long, undersized suction run absorbs enough mechanical-room heat along its length to overload the outdoor condensing coil at the roof
The expansion valve gains pressure difference and overfeeds
Oil viscosity increases in the warmer evaporator

questions.explanation: Pressure drop lowers the density and pressure of vapor actually entering the compressor, raising its compression ratio and cutting mass flow and efficiency. Option B blames pipe heat that is not the mechanism, option C is wrong because suction drop does not add feed pressure at the valve, and option D misstates both where the oil problem arises and its cause.

questions.question: A walk-in freezer's compressor shows a frosted suction line back to the compressor shell, superheat near 1°F at the evaporator outlet, and a cool, sweating compressor crankcase. Which fault do those signs point to?

answers.text: A restricted liquid-line filter drier is starving the evaporator, so almost no refrigerant reaches the coil during the cooling cycle.
A failed condenser fan motor is raising head pressure, so hot gas backs up through the discharge line into the compressor crankcase.
Liquid refrigerant is flooding back from an overfed evaporator, diluting the compressor oil and risking mechanical damage.
Noncondensable gas is trapped in the condenser, so discharge pressure stays high even while the box temperature continues to fall.

questions.explanation: Superheat near zero with frost and sweat reaching the compressor means liquid is leaving the evaporator unevaporated; sustained floodback washes oil from bearings and can slug the compressor.

questions.question: A plan shows a thermostat symbol on an interior wall of a classroom, but the installer's rough-in placed the sensor on an exterior wall in direct afternoon sun. Why does the symbol location matter?

answers.text: It does not matter, because modern thermostats recalibrate themselves to cancel out solar heat gain on any wall within the first day of operation
The exterior wall placement is actually preferred, since a warmer sensor location makes the cooling system run longer and dehumidify the room better
Sensor location affects control accuracy, and sun exposure skews readings
The symbol only shows where the display screen will be viewed from, while the actual temperature sensor is always located inside the air handler

questions.explanation: A sensor reads the air and surface conditions around it, so sun exposure on an exterior wall skews the reading and the control response. Thermostats do not self-correct for solar gain, a warmer location causes false calls rather than better control, and the wall device is the sensing point shown.

questions.question: A contractor reviews a job-cost report and finds the duct-material cost code running well past its budgeted amount while labor codes track the budget. What does job costing give the contractor here?

answers.text: An automatic transfer of the overrun to the owner's account, since cost codes assign any excess material cost to the client, together with a credit for the labor savings the report shows in the other codes for the same period.
A comparison of actual costs against the estimate by cost code, showing which part of the job is overrunning so corrective action can target it.
A revised contract price, since the job-cost report by itself amends the agreement whenever actual costs exceed the estimate.
A guarantee that the job will finish at a profit once the remaining invoices are entered into the accounting system at closeout.

questions.explanation: Job costing tracks actual cost against budget by code, isolating the duct-material overrun from the labor codes that are holding. The key states that diagnostic use.

questions.question: A furnace call: the inducer runs, the pressure switch proves closed, 120 V is delivered to the igniter terminals at the right point in the sequence — but there is no glow, no ignition, and the igniter measures open (infinite resistance) on a cool ohmmeter check. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A pressure switch stuck open, which is contradicted because the switch proved closed and the sequence advanced to energizing the igniter
An open hot-surface igniter
A dirty flame sensor, which causes shutdown seconds after a successful light, not a complete absence of ignition and glow
A failed gas valve coil, which would prevent gas flow but cannot explain an igniter that never glows and measures electrically open

questions.explanation: Voltage present at the igniter with no glow and an open resistance reading condemns the igniter itself; the sequence never reaches gas flow or flame sensing. A gas valve fault acts later in the sequence, the pressure switch demonstrably closed, and a dirty flame sensor only matters after a flame exists.

questions.question: A condensate drain line is installed dead level for a long run and plugs with slime every season. What installation defect is most likely?

answers.text: The line was made from approved drain material instead of thin-wall tubing that stays warmer and therefore resists biological growth
The drain terminates at an approved receptor instead of discharging directly onto the roof membrane below the condensing unit
The trap was installed at the unit rather than at the far end of the run near the floor drain, where traps are most effective
The line lacks continuous downward slope in the direction of flow.

questions.explanation: Condensate drains must fall continuously, about an eighth inch per foot, so water and debris do not stand in the line. Approved material and an approved receptor are correct practice, not defects, and the trap belongs at the unit to prevent air issues.

questions.question: No-heat call on a cold furnace that sat overnight. On a heat call the indoor blower starts and runs continuously, but the inducer never starts and there is no ignition sequence. The high-limit switch, which should be closed at room temperature, measures open circuit with the furnace cold, and its terminals show heat discoloration. All other safeties in the string measure closed. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A thermostat that is not calling for heat, ruled out because the blower responds to the call and the rest of the safety string measures closed and ready
A failed inducer motor that cannot start the sequence, which would stop the sequence at its own step but would not hold a cold limit switch open or run the blower continuously
An open pressure switch keeping the board in a fault state, ruled out because the pressure switch is among the safeties that measure closed at rest during this check
A high-limit switch failed in the open position

questions.explanation: A limit that reads open on a cold furnace has failed mechanically or thermally from past overheating (note the discoloration), and the board responds by running the blower with no heat sequence. The thermostat is calling, the inducer cannot be reached in sequence until the safety string is satisfied, and the pressure switch measures closed, leaving the failed-open limit as the break in the string.

oklahoma-hvac.quiz_title: Oklahoma HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An air conditioner has an EER of 12.0 at its rating point. What is its COP at that same operating point?

answers.text: About 12.0 as well, because EER and COP are two names for the identical number and are interchangeable without any unit conversion between the ratings
About 41.0, found by multiplying 12.0 by 3.412 in the wrong direction, which would claim the unit moves forty-one units of heat per unit of work input
About 3.52
About 0.29, found by dividing 3.412 by 12.0, which inverts the conversion and understates the unit's efficiency by more than a factor of ten at the rating point

questions.explanation: COP is EER divided by 3.412, so 12.0 divided by 3.412 is about 3.52, a dimensionless ratio of heat moved to work in consistent units. Treating the two as identical skips the Btu-to-watt conversion, and the other answers multiply or divide in the wrong direction.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a service disconnect located within sight of an air-conditioning unit?

answers.text: To regulate refrigerant pressure during service
To let a servicing technician shut off and control power to the equipment while working on it
To serve as the unit's normal everyday on-off control in place of the thermostat, cycling the equipment on and off to maintain the indoor temperature
To increase the available voltage at the unit

questions.explanation: A nearby disconnect gives the technician a local means to isolate and control the power source during service. It has no role in refrigerant regulation. It is not a substitute thermostat for daily operation, and a disconnect cannot raise supply voltage.

questions.question: Why is changing from an R-22 system to a POE-oil system a special concern for a reused line set?

answers.text: POE oil instantly dissolves copper piping, so any line that carried mineral oil will leak within the first season
Residual mineral oil and sludge from the old system can circulate with the POE oil and foul valves and driers
Mineral oil residue turns the new refrigerant into a blend with a different pressure-temperature relationship
The old lines become electrically conductive once POE oil contacts them, creating a shock hazard at the service valves

questions.explanation: POE oil is an effective solvent that mobilizes old mineral-oil sludge, which can plug metering devices and driers. It does not dissolve copper, it does not change the refrigerant into a different blend, and oil residue does not make piping a shock hazard.

questions.question: Which cost is a direct job cost rather than an indirect overhead cost?

answers.text: Annual rent for the main office and warehouse space used by the entire company throughout the year
Duct material installed on that specific job
The bookkeeper's salary for processing payroll and accounts payable for all jobs in the company
General advertising that promotes the company as a whole rather than any one contracted project

questions.explanation: B is correct because material installed on a specific job is traceable directly to that job. A is incorrect because office and warehouse rent supports all work and is overhead. C is incorrect because bookkeeping for the whole company is an indirect administrative cost. D is incorrect because company-wide advertising cannot be traced to one job.

questions.question: What approval and time rules govern continuing education credit?

answers.text: Courses may be approved after they are completed, and one credit hour is any 30 minutes of attendance in the room, because attendance alone proves the material was covered
No advance approval is needed for either one if the provider advertises the course to licensees as approved, when the provider's catalog says so
Only the instructor needs advance approval, and scheduled breaks count in full as instruction time for credit, because the break falls inside the credited hour
Both the course and the instructor must be approved in advance by the Committee, and one credit hour is 50 minutes of instruction plus a 10-minute break

questions.explanation: Continuing education counts only when both the course and the instructor were approved in advance by the Committee, and a credit hour consists of 50 minutes of instruction plus a 10-minute break.

questions.question: A technician must pinpoint a suspected R-454B leak inside a small indoor mechanical closet. Which leak-detection approach fits A2L service?

answers.text: A lit propane torch passed slowly along each joint, because the flame color method remains acceptable when the room is small and the door is left open
A standard combustible-gas lighter used as a test flame at each fitting, because a small flame presents less risk than a full-size torch flame
An ultrasonic detector alone with no confirmation, because sound-based tools also measure refrigerant concentration against the lower flammability limit
An electronic detector rated for A2L refrigerants

questions.explanation: Electronic detectors listed or rated for A2L use detect the leak without introducing ignition. Any open-flame method adds an ignition source regardless of flame size or door position, and an ultrasonic tool hears leak noise but does not measure concentration or confirm refrigerant identity by itself.

questions.question: A flex duct run delivers far less air than its size suggests. Inspection shows excess length coiled and sagging between supports. What is the correction?

answers.text: Cut excess, pull it taut, support it properly, and keep bends gentle
Compress it further to shorten the run and leave the extra length coiled at the plenum
Add another coil to smooth flow
Raise refrigerant pressure

questions.explanation: Flex duct has high resistance when slack, sagging, or sharply bent; cutting excess, stretching it taut, and supporting it restores rated airflow, so A is correct. More compression or coiling worsens resistance, and refrigerant pressure is unrelated to duct geometry.

questions.question: A hood passes its airflow test yet smoke still spills at the front edge over a charbroiler line. Which change most directly improves capture?

answers.text: Raise the exhaust rate until the kitchen is so negative that smoke is pulled away from the cooks and toward the dining room doors, and aim a portion of the kitchen exhaust toward the dining room to relieve the pressure felt at the pass window
Increase hood overhang over the appliances, add end (side) panels to block cross-drafts, and keep supply air from blowing across the hood face
Move the makeup-air diffusers directly in front of the hood and aim them downward so replacement air pushes the smoke upward
Remove the grease filters so the plume can enter the duct collar without any resistance at the hood's capture opening

questions.explanation: Capture improves with geometry and calm air around the plume: more overhang, side panels against cross-drafts, and undisturbed rising air. Option A trades spillage for a severe pressure problem, option C aims supply air to disrupt the plume it should protect, and option D removes required grease extraction while doing nothing for the spill at the edge.

questions.question: At what pressure does the relief valve on a typical residential hot-water boiler open to protect the boiler?

answers.text: 15 psi
30 psi
100 psi
50 psi

questions.explanation: Residential hot-water boilers are protected by a relief valve set to open at 30 psi, well above normal fill and operating pressures but below the boiler's safe limit.

questions.question: How do Ground Source Piping and Medical Gas licenses qualify, if not by a PSI examination?

answers.text: Both categories require only an attestation from the applicant's employer, with no outside certification of any kind needed, with the employer judging the background alone
Both categories use the standard HVACR trade examination administered by PSI, taken at a PSI testing site in the usual way, exactly as the standard HVACR categories are earned
Ground Source uses certification under NFPA 99, and Medical Gas uses a ground-loop installer test from an approved group, with their certifications effectively swapped
Ground Source uses installation certification from a Committee-approved organization, and Medical Gas uses certification in accordance with the most current NFPA 99

questions.explanation: Ground Source Piping qualifies through installation certification by a Committee-approved organization, while Medical Gas qualifies through certification under the most current NFPA 99, so neither relies on a PSI examination.

questions.question: A furnace nameplate lists a temperature rise of 30 to 60°F. The return air is 70°F and the supply air, measured away from radiant heat, is 115°F. What is the finding?

answers.text: Rise is 45°F, within range
Rise is 115°F, far above range, because supply temperature alone is always reported as the temperature rise for the furnace
Rise cannot be determined until the outdoor temperature is known, because rise is measured against ambient conditions outside
Rise is 185°F, the sum of supply and return temperatures, and it exceeds the listed maximum by a very large margin indeed

questions.explanation: Temperature rise is supply minus return, 115 minus 70, which is 45°F and inside the 30 to 60°F nameplate range. Option B reports supply temperature as rise, option C wrongly brings in outdoor air, and option D adds the temperatures instead of subtracting them.

questions.question: Which set lists the essential elements of an enforceable contract?

answers.text: A handshake, a verbal promise, good faith, and the parties' long business relationship
A written document, a notary's seal, two witnesses, and registration with the state
An estimate, an invoice, a purchase order, and payment of the first installment
Offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties, and a legal purpose

questions.explanation: An enforceable contract requires an offer, acceptance, consideration, parties competent to contract, and a purpose that is legal.

questions.question: After a repair in which the system was opened and evacuated only briefly, a unit runs with head 472 psig, suction 146 psig, subcooling 23°F, superheat 12°F, discharge temperature 225°F, and poor cooling. The refrigerant charge was weighed in exactly to nameplate. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A TXV stuck closed, which would starve the evaporator and show low suction pressure with very high superheat instead of these values
A condenser fan running backwards after motor replacement, which would raise head pressure but was verified correct rotation and full airflow on this call
Noncondensables in the system
A simple overcharge, which is unlikely because the charge was weighed to nameplate and overcharge alone rarely drives discharge temperature this high

questions.explanation: Very high head pressure and subcooling with a weighed-in charge and a history of a rushed evacuation point to air trapped in the condenser, where it adds its partial pressure and blankets condensing surface. Overcharge is contradicted by the weighed charge, fan rotation and airflow were verified, and a stuck-closed TXV would starve the low side rather than inflate the high side.

questions.question: A gas line that fed one furnace adequately is extended a long distance with several added elbows to serve a second appliance, and now both appliances starve for gas when firing together. What sizing principle explains this?

answers.text: Pipe capacity falls as total developed length and fitting losses increase and as simultaneous demand rises, so the line must be sized for total load at the actual length
Gas pressure increases with distance, so the appliances are overfired
Elbows add capacity by slowing the gas down
Only the appliance closest to the meter counts in sizing

questions.explanation: Gas piping must be sized for the combined connected load over the full developed length, including fitting losses, option A; longer, more restricted runs deliver less gas at usable pressure. Pressure drops - not rises - with distance and flow (B), elbows add resistance and reduce capacity rather than adding it (C), and every simultaneously firing appliance counts toward demand (D).

questions.question: A rooftop unit shows low supply airflow, a clean filter, correct belt tension, and a blower wheel whose scoops are heavily coated with packed dirt. Why is cleaning the wheel the priority repair?

answers.text: A dirt-packed wheel moves far less air at the same speed because the blade shape is effectively lost, so cleaning restores airflow without changing pulleys or charge

Dirt on the wheel raises its weight enough to increase airflow by centrifugal effect, so cleaning is needed only to reduce noise at the curb opening after the system has been running long enough for pressures and temperatures to stabilize fully

Wheel dirt insulates the motor from airstream cooling, and cleaning matters only because the motor would otherwise trip on its internal protector on a unit that has otherwise been keeping the space comfortable through the rest of the season
Packed dirt changes refrigerant metering in the coil above the blower, so cleaning is required before any superheat reading can be trusted at all

questions.explanation: Packed dirt fills the blower scoops and destroys the blade profile, sharply reducing air moved at a given speed even with good filters and belts. The dirt does not increase airflow by weight, motor cooling is not the primary airflow issue, and wheel condition does not change refrigerant metering in the coil.

questions.question: An employee works 46 hours in a workweek at a regular rate of $20 per hour. How is the employee's gross pay for the week correctly structured?

answers.text: 46 hours at one and one-half times the regular rate, since any overtime re-rates the whole week
46 hours at the regular rate, with the extra 6 hours paid in the following pay period
40 hours at the regular rate plus 6 hours at the regular rate, since the premium is optional
40 hours at the regular rate plus 6 hours at one and one-half times the regular rate

questions.explanation: Overtime structure is 40 hours at the regular rate plus the 6 hours over 40 at the time-and-one-half premium rate.

questions.question: An owner wants time-and-materials work but is concerned about an open-ended total. What contract feature best addresses that concern?

answers.text: A clause that lets the contractor extend the schedule indefinitely without notifying the owner of any delay
A not-to-exceed cap that requires approval to go beyond it
An agreement to stop keeping time records once the job passes the halfway point of the estimated duration
A promise that material will be billed at a later date, so its cost does not appear in the running job total

questions.explanation: B is correct because a not-to-exceed cap limits the owner's exposure and requires approval before the cap is exceeded. A is incorrect because indefinite schedule extension does not control the total cost. C is incorrect because abandoning time records removes the basis for time-and-materials billing. D is incorrect because deferring material billing hides, rather than caps, the true total.

questions.question: A furnace with a new flame sensor and a clean burner still drops out seconds after light-off intermittently. Flame signal fluctuates between 0.8 and 3 µA, gas pressure and sensor position are correct, and electrical checks find hot and neutral reversed at the furnace junction box (120 V from neutral to ground). What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A cracked heat exchanger, which disturbs flames and raises CO but does not reverse electrical polarity or make the microamp signal unstable
A weak gas valve coil dropping out under load, which would show manifold pressure collapsing at dropout rather than a fluctuating flame signal
A defective new flame sensor, which is unlikely because the signal fluctuates with the wiring fault and the sensor was just replaced with no change
Reversed polarity defeating flame rectification

questions.explanation: Flame rectification depends on correct polarity and grounding; reversed hot/neutral makes the sense signal weak and unstable even with a new sensor correctly positioned. The replacement sensor changed nothing, manifold pressure holds through dropout, and a cracked exchanger cannot produce the measured polarity reversal.

questions.question: A technician fixes the same no-cooling symptom three times by replacing a capacitor, yet the unit keeps failing each heat wave. What does callback analysis say about this pattern?

answers.text: The capacitor is likely a victim rather than the root cause, so the investigation should look for what is stressing it, such as low voltage, heat, or a struggling compressor

Replacing the same capacitor repeatedly on every callback is the correct long-term strategy, and the technician should keep installing identical parts until one finally holds through an entire summer season
The customer is at fault because heat waves coincide with the failures
Warranty requires installing the same part a fourth time before deeper diagnosis

questions.explanation: Repeated failure of the same component signals an upstream cause that must be found. Continuing identical replacements wastes visits and leaves the fault. Heat waves expose the weakness but blaming the customer or the weather does not fix it, and no warranty rule forbids proper diagnosis.

questions.question: An equipment schedule gives minimum circuit ampacity and maximum overcurrent protection for each fan-powered unit. The electrical contractor asks the mechanical contractor where that data came from. What is the correct use of those schedule values?

answers.text: They coordinate the electrical rough-in with the mechanical equipment
They allow the electrician to ignore the nameplate on the delivered unit, because schedule values always override the listing of the actual equipment
They set the size of the duct connections on each unit, since ampacity and duct diameter both increase in direct proportion to fan horsepower
They are used only for utility rebate paperwork after the building opens and have no role in sizing conductors or breakers during construction

questions.explanation: Publishing ampacity and overcurrent data in the schedule lets the electrical scope be roughed in to match the mechanical equipment. The delivered unit nameplate still governs final connections, the values have nothing to do with duct sizing, and they are construction data rather than rebate paperwork.

utah-hvac.quiz_title: Utah HVAC Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: In an air-cooled condenser, which condition most directly reduces the coil's ability to reject heat?

answers.text: A clean coil with full airflow
A layer of dirt and debris insulating the fins and blocking airflow through the coil
A liquid line that is a few degrees subcooled below saturation as it leaves the condenser and travels through a long, well-insulated run to the indoor coil
An evaporator with correct superheat

questions.explanation: Dirt both insulates the fin surface and restricts airflow, so heat rejection falls and head pressure rises. Option A is the desired condition, option C describes normal subcooled liquid leaving a condenser, and option D is an evaporator measurement that does not impair the condenser itself.

questions.question: Where does a fan-powered humidifier belong, and why does placement matter?

answers.text: In the return drop only, because fan-powered models depend entirely on the return airstream being warmer than the supply airstream
Loose in the blower compartment, where unducted air movement across the panel provides enough evaporation for a whole house
On the outdoor condensing unit, where weather provides airflow and the moisture can be piped indoors with the refrigerant lines
On the supply plenum, where its own fan pushes air through the water panel independent of bypass duct pressure differences.

questions.explanation: A fan-powered unit is a supply-plenum appliance with its own fan, so it does not rely on supply-to-return pressure difference like a bypass model. It is not a return-only or loose-in-cabinet device, and humidification is an indoor air-side function, not an outdoor refrigerant-side one.

questions.question: What minimum remuneration must an H100 qualifier receive from the licensee?

answers.text: No minimum — any nominal payment satisfies the qualifier requirement
Remuneration for not less than 30 hours of work per week
A flat annual salary set by the Division, regardless of hours worked
Remuneration for not less than 12 hours of work per week

questions.explanation: A qualifier must receive remuneration for not less than 12 hours of work per week for the licensee.

questions.question: What background-check change has DOPL announced, and when does it take effect?

answers.text: A fingerprint-based requirement that applies only to out-of-state applicants
A credit-based background check requirement effective at the next renewal
A fingerprint-based background check requirement effective January 1, 2027
Elimination of the background check requirement effective January 1, 2027

questions.explanation: DOPL has announced a fingerprint-based background check requirement effective January 1, 2027.

questions.question: What experience does the statute itself require of an H100 qualifier applicant?

answers.text: Four years of any construction employment, whether the work was paid or unpaid and whether or not it involved heating or cooling systems at all
Two years of full-time paid employment of HVAC-specific experience, plus passing the required examinations
Two years of experience in any building trade, including electrical or plumbing work, so long as the employment was full-time and paid
One year of HVAC-specific experience together with completion of an approved training program, with no examination requirement imposed by the statute

questions.explanation: The statutory floor is two years of full-time paid HVAC-specific experience plus passing the examinations.

questions.question: A TXV system shows low suction pressure, superheat of 26°F, and normal-to-slightly-high subcooling. There is a measurable 6°F temperature drop across the liquid-line filter drier. How do these findings separate a restriction from a simple undercharge?

answers.text: They do not; a temperature drop across a drier is normal and charge should simply be added
The high subcooling proves undercharge, because undercharge always stacks liquid in the condenser, since a restriction would prevent liquid from reaching the condenser outlet at all
Restriction and undercharge are the same fault, so the drier reading can be ignored
Normal subcooling shows liquid is available up to the restriction, and the drier temperature drop locates it, whereas an undercharge would show low subcooling

questions.explanation: Liquid stacking ahead of a restriction keeps subcooling normal or high while the evaporator starves, and a temperature drop across the drier pinpoints where flashing begins. Option A is wrong because a healthy drier has essentially no temperature drop, and adding charge would overcharge the system once the restriction is cleared. Option B reverses the subcooling signature of an undercharge, and option C ignores a finding that changes both the diagnosis and the repair.

questions.question: A replacement condensing unit has a higher MCA than the unit it replaces, but the existing branch-circuit conductors are smaller than the new MCA. What must the installer do?

answers.text: Keep the old conductors in place because the breaker never tripped while the old, smaller unit was running on them for several seasons
Raise the breaker size so the smaller conductors run cooler
Install conductors with ampacity at least equal to the new MCA before energizing the unit
Use the old conductors if the run is mostly in free air

questions.explanation: Conductors must meet the new equipment's MCA regardless of the previous unit's history. Past non-tripping does not make undersized wire compliant or safe. A larger breaker makes protection worse, not cooler, and free-air assumptions do not override the nameplate requirement for this installation.

questions.question: On a changeout, unsealed duct joints in an unconditioned attic are found while the air handler is out. Why is this the best time to seal them?

answers.text: Sealing is only cosmetic at changeout, because duct leakage stops mattering once new high-efficiency equipment is installed
Access is open during the changeout, and sealing reduces the capacity and efficiency losses the new system would otherwise inherit
The joints should be left open so attic air can supplement return air and reduce the load on the return duct system
Sealing must wait a full season so the new system can establish a baseline before any duct changes are allowed to be made

questions.explanation: Changeout access makes sealing cheap, and leakage in unconditioned space wastes delivered capacity regardless of equipment efficiency. New equipment does not cancel leakage losses, attic air drawn in through leaks adds heat and moisture rather than helping, and there is no required waiting season.

questions.question: Which set lists the essential elements of an enforceable contract at principle level?

answers.text: A sealed written document and payment in full before any work begins
Offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties, and a legal purpose
A verbal promise, a handshake, and possession of a business license
A notarized signature, a sworn witness, and a filing of the signed agreement with a state agency

questions.explanation: An enforceable contract rests on offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties, and a legal purpose. Notarization, seals, advance payment in full, and handshakes are not required elements.

questions.question: A circulator-zoned system heats an idle upstairs zone whenever the downstairs circulator runs. The upstairs circulator is off and its piping gets hot. The missing or failed component is:

answers.text: A check valve (flow check) in the idle zone that should prevent gravity and induced flow when its circulator is off
The air separator on the supply main
The boiler high-limit aquastat
A zone-valve end switch in the upstairs thermostat

questions.explanation: Each circulator zone needs a check to stop hot water migrating through idle loops by gravity or by pressure from running circulators. Option B removes air centrally and does not select zones. Option C limits boiler temperature for all zones, not flow in one. Option D belongs to zone-valve systems and cannot stop hydraulic migration here.

questions.question: Before an H100 license issues, and again at renewal, what financial-responsibility showings are required?

answers.text: Before issuance, the applicant registers only with the exam vendor, and at renewal the only showing required is proof of completed prelicensure coursework
