Before issuance, proof of registrations with the Department of Commerce, Division of Corporations, Unemployment Insurance Division, State Tax Commission, and IRS; at renewal, evidence of continuing financial responsibility
Before issuance, the applicant files an audited financial statement, and at renewal the qualifier must complete a new criminal background check and fingerprinting
Before issuance, only proof of liability insurance is required, and at renewal no financial-responsibility showing of any kind is required from the licensee

questions.explanation: Pre-issuance filings include registrations with the Department of Commerce, Division of Corporations, Unemployment Insurance Division, State Tax Commission, and IRS, and renewal requires evidence of continuing financial responsibility.

questions.question: Which set of documents may support an H100 qualifier petition or application as proof of qualification?

answers.text: A personal resume, three customer references, and photographs of completed installations the applicant worked on during the claimed employment period
Tax documents showing employment by a licensed contractor, affidavits from contractors or direct supervisors, and an attestation under oath
Exam score reports for both required examinations, with no employment documentation of any kind needed to support the experience claimed in the petition
Bank statements showing the applicant's income, a written business plan, and a letter of good standing from the applicant's liability insurance carrier

questions.explanation: Petition proof may include tax documents, affidavits from contractors or direct supervisors, and an attestation under oath.

questions.question: A homeowner complains the heat pump 'stopped working' at 20 degrees F because supply air feels cool and run times are long, yet the house holds setpoint without auxiliary heat running excessively. What is the best explanation?

answers.text: The reversing valve must be leaking because supply air should feel as hot as a gas furnace
Heat pump capacity and supply-air temperature fall as outdoor temperature drops, so long run times with lukewarm air can be normal if setpoint is maintained
The system is in permanent defrost
The thermostat should force strip heat below 40 degrees F in all cases

questions.explanation: As outdoor temperature falls, a heat pump moves less heat and delivers cooler supply air, so long cycles that hold setpoint are expected behavior, option B. A leaking valve (A) would show capacity loss and failure to hold setpoint, permanent defrost (C) would fail to heat normally and cycle auxiliaries constantly, and forcing strips in all cases below 40 degrees (D) wastes energy when the heat pump is still carrying the load.

questions.question: In proportional balancing, a branch reads 60 percent of design flow while the main reads 90 percent of design. What does proportional method direct the balancer to do first?

answers.text: Close the main damper until the main also reads 60 percent so everything matches

Set the branch reading 60 percent to exactly 100 percent of its design flow by opening its damper fully and leaving it there, regardless of how short the total system flow is or what happens to every other branch
Work with the ratios: set the outlets in proportion to each other starting from the least-favored run, rather than forcing any single outlet to full design flow while the total is short
Abandon the job, because any branch below design means the fan must be replaced

questions.explanation: Proportional balancing equalizes percentages so that a final fan adjustment brings all outlets to design together. Throttling the main to the lowest ratio wastes capacity, forcing one branch to design while the total is low starves the rest, and a short branch is a distribution problem to correct, not automatic grounds for a new fan.

questions.question: A contractor prices 120 feet of line-set work at a firm rate per foot that includes labor and materials. What pricing method is this?

answers.text: A lump-sum method with no measurable quantity, where the entire project is priced as one indivisible total
A cost-plus method where the owner reimburses every invoice plus a separate negotiated percentage fee
An allowance method where the per-foot figure is only a placeholder until the owner selects a finish
Unit pricing

questions.explanation: D is correct because unit pricing charges a set rate per measurable unit, here per foot, covering labor and materials. A is incorrect because a lump sum does not break the price into a rate per unit of quantity. B is incorrect because no reimbursement of actual invoices plus a fee is described. C is incorrect because the rate is stated as firm, not as a placeholder for an unmade selection.

questions.question: A field supervisor verbally agrees to a costly extra the owner requested, with nothing in writing. What risk has the contractor created?

answers.text: No risk at all, because verbal extras are always paid at the amount the contractor later decides to charge
The risk that retainage will automatically double on every unrelated project the company currently has under contract
The risk that the equipment warranty will be extended indefinitely because the change was not documented properly
A payment dispute because the extra's scope and price were not authorized in writing

questions.explanation: D is correct because an undocumented extra leaves scope and price open to dispute when the bill is presented. A is incorrect because verbal extras are a common source of nonpayment disputes, not guaranteed payment. B is incorrect because retainage on other projects is governed by their own contracts. C is incorrect because warranty duration is set by warranty terms, not by change documentation.

questions.question: What distinguishes the H100 qualifier's examination burden from that of the other classifications that take the Business and Law Exam?

answers.text: The H100 qualifier is the only one who must also pass a trade exam in addition to the Business and Law Exam
Every other classification's qualifier takes two trade exams in addition to the Business and Law Exam, while the H100 qualifier takes the business exam alone
The H100 qualifier takes the Business and Law Exam twice — once for the business and once personally — while other qualifiers take it a single time
The H100 qualifier is the only one excused from the Business and Law Exam, precisely because the H100 qualifier must already pass a separate HVAC trade exam

questions.explanation: The H100 is the only contractor qualifier with a trade exam in addition to the Business and Law Exam.

questions.question: Two identical supply trunks are sealed the same day. On one, foil tape was pressed over dusty, slightly oily galvanized joints and burnished lightly; on the other, joints were wiped clean and dry and sealed with mastic reinforced at the corners. A year later the taped trunk leaks noticeably more. The best explanation is:

answers.text: Tape adhesion depends entirely on a clean, dry surface and firm burnishing, so the contaminated application failed progressively, while mastic bonds to the prepared surface and tolerates joint movement better
Tape always fails within a year regardless of how it is applied

Mastic works because it dissolves the galvanizing and welds the joint shut, fusing the two metal edges into a single continuous surface that no longer needs tape, fasteners, or any separate seal once the coating has fully cured in the field
The taped trunk leaked because tape adds thickness that narrows the duct

questions.explanation: Listed tapes are legitimate sealants only when their listing conditions are honored — clean, dry metal and full contact — whereas mastic on a prepared joint forms a durable, slightly flexible seal. Option B is wrong because properly listed and applied tape on clean duct can last for years; the failure here traces to the contaminated surface; option C is wrong because mastic is an adhesive sealant that cures on the surface; it does not dissolve zinc coatings or weld metal; option D is wrong because a few thousandths of tape thickness has no meaningful effect on duct area or leakage.

questions.question: A mechanical combustion air supply must serve appliances with a total input of 80,000 Btu/h. At the required rate of 0.35 cfm per 1,000 Btu/h, how much air must the supply fan deliver?

answers.text: 14 cfm
35 cfm
28 cfm
80 cfm

questions.explanation: The total input is 80 units of 1,000 Btu/h. Multiplying 80 by 0.35 cfm gives 28 cfm of mechanically supplied combustion air.

questions.question: A prime contractor plans to rely on a subcontractor's price in its bid. What should the prime contractor confirm before submitting that bid?

answers.text: That the subcontractor will accept a materially lower price after award in exchange for the promise of future work on other projects the prime contractor may win
That the subcontractor's price covers the assigned scope, terms, and qualifications, and that the subcontractor can perform as priced
That the subcontractor's name can be withheld from the bid documents until the contract is signed
That the subcontractor submitted the lowest price received, with no review of scope or qualifications at all

questions.explanation: Before relying on a subcontractor's number, the prime contractor confirms the price covers the assigned scope on the stated terms and that the subcontractor is able to perform. Price alone, with no scope check, invites gaps and defaults.

alabama-refrigeration.quiz_title: Alabama Refrigeration Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What happens during the initialization (homing) routine of a stepper-motor EEV when power is first applied?

answers.text: The controller drives the valve fully closed (often with extra steps) to establish a known zero position, then opens to the calculated steps
The controller opens the valve fully and leaves it there until suction pressure rises, using that pressure rise as the only reference for valve position thereafter
The controller counts the steps the valve took during the last power failure and restores that exact count without ever driving the valve to a mechanical stop
The controller spins the stepper freely in both directions for several minutes to warm the motor windings before it attempts any refrigeration control at all

questions.explanation: Steppers have no absolute position feedback, so the controller overdrives the valve to its closed stop to zero the step count, then counts steps to the target opening. It does not use a pressure rise as a position reference, it cannot trust a remembered count after power loss, and homing is a brief positioning routine, not a winding warm-up.

questions.question: A pressure test holds steady on the gauge, but a soap check bubbles slowly at one threaded joint. The correct action is:

answers.text: Accept the test, because a gauge that does not move over the test period proves that any bubbling at a joint is only trapped air escaping
Repair the joint and retest the section
Tighten the joint under full test pressure until the bubbles stop, then record the original test as a pass without repeating it
Coat the joint with additional pipe sealant on the outside and retest only if the customer later reports a gas odor at that fitting

questions.explanation: Repair the joint and retest the section. A steady gauge does not override a positive bubble leak, tightening under pressure is unsafe practice, and surface sealant is not a repair for a leaking threaded joint.

questions.question: In a primary-secondary chilled-water plant, what does the common (decoupler) pipe between the two loops allow?

answers.text: It lets each loop circulate at its own flow rate; the direction of flow in the common pipe shows which loop is producing more
It forces both loops to run at exactly the same flow at all times, because any difference would immediately air-lock both pumps
It replaces the expansion tank, air separator, and all balancing valves in both loops with a single short piece of pipe
It mixes supply and return water deliberately so the chillers always see the warmest possible return water at low load

questions.explanation: Decoupled loops run independently; excess production one way or the other simply passes through the low-pressure-drop common pipe. Option B defeats the entire purpose of decoupling, option C assigns the pipe jobs belonging to other components, and option D misstates the goal, since uncontrolled mixing and warm returns are problems, not design intent.

questions.question: A refrigeration contractor is lettering two new service vans. Which lettering plan satisfies the Board's vehicle display rule?

answers.text: The company name on both vans and the certification number in one-inch letters on the rear door only, because vehicle display is satisfied by any legible placement of the number on the vehicle., with the number repeated on the fuel tank and the trailer hitch so that an inspector approaching from behind can identify the contractor at a job site.
The certification number in three-inch letters on the tailgate and the company name on the roof, because height above two inches on any single panel meets the prominence requirement.

The certification number and company name displayed prominently and legibly, at least two inches high, on at least two sides of each vehicle, with AL Number, AL No., or AL# immediately before the number in equal-sized print.
The certification number displayed only inside the cargo area next to the refrigerant recovery equipment, because the display rule for vehicles is directed at inspectors rather than the public.

questions.explanation: C is correct: the certification number and company name must be displayed prominently and legibly on all service and installation vehicles, at least two inches in height, on at least two sides of the vehicle, with the phrase AL Number, AL No., or AL# immediately before the certification number in equal-sized print. A is wrong on height (one inch is under the two-inch minimum), on placement (one panel rather than two sides), and it omits the required prefix. B is wrong because a single rear or roof panel does not meet the two-sides requirement even at a larger letter height. D is wrong because the display must be prominent and legible on the vehicle's exterior sides, not hidden inside the cargo area.

questions.question: A contractor marks up a $1,000 job cost by 20% to set the price. What is the resulting price and its gross margin?

answers.text: $1,200 price; about 16.7% margin
$1,200 price and a 20.0 percent margin, because markup on cost and margin on price are always identical
$1,250 price and a 20.0 percent margin, found by using the margin divisor formula instead of the stated markup
$1,020 price and a 2.0 percent margin, found by adding the markup rate as a flat dollar amount

questions.explanation: A is correct because a 20 percent markup gives $1,200, and the $200 profit divided by $1,200 is about 16.7 percent margin. B is incorrect because a 20 percent markup does not produce a 20 percent margin. C is incorrect because it prices with the margin formula when the problem states a markup. D is incorrect because it treats 20 percent as $20 rather than 20 percent of $1,000.

questions.question: A fixed-orifice system's suction pressure corresponds to an evaporator saturation temperature of 40°F, and the suction line at the evaporator outlet measures 52°F. What is the evaporator superheat?

answers.text: 12°F, found by subtracting the saturation temperature from the suction-line temperature
92°F, found by adding the two temperatures
52°F, because superheat equals the suction-line temperature itself, at the evaporator outlet coil
40°F, because superheat equals the saturation temperature itself

questions.explanation: Superheat is the vapor temperature above saturation, so 52 minus 40 gives 12 degrees of superheat. Option B adds the values, which is not how any refrigerant temperature difference is calculated, and options C and D each substitute a single temperature for the required difference.

questions.question: In a ladder diagram, switches and controls are drawn on the left portion of a rung and the load is drawn on the right. A rung shows a pressure switch and a coil. If the pressure switch is open, what is true?

answers.text: The coil cannot be energized through that rung regardless of other rungs' loads
The coil is energized anyway because connected loads elsewhere in the circuit draw power around any open switches in the rung
The pressure switch is acting as the load
The transformer secondary is shorted

questions.explanation: An open switch in series with a coil breaks that rung, so the coil stays de-energized. Loads cannot draw power around an open series switch. The coil, not the switch, is the load in this rung, and an open circuit is the opposite of a short.

questions.question: A load calculation shows 28,500 Btuh total cooling with 21,000 Btuh sensible. When selecting equipment per Manual S, the technician should:

answers.text: Choose equipment whose total and sensible capacities at design conditions match the loads without gross oversizing
Always choose the largest unit available
Match only the nameplate tonnage to the square footage
Ignore sensible capacity if total capacity matches

questions.explanation: Manual S requires matching both total and sensible capacity at actual design conditions to the calculated loads, avoiding gross oversizing, so A is correct. B invites short-cycling, C uses a rule of thumb instead of a load calc, and D risks failing to meet the sensible load or control humidity.

questions.question: Halfway through a large job, job costing shows labor at 80% of budget while the work is only 50% complete. What is the best immediate response?

answers.text: Ignore the report until final billing, because mid-job figures almost always correct themselves without action
Bill the owner for the entire remaining contract balance immediately, whether or not that work has been performed
Reduce the crew's recorded hours retroactively so the cost report aligns with the original estimate on paper
Investigate the overrun cause and reforecast the cost to complete

questions.explanation: D is correct because a labor overrun at mid-job requires finding the cause and updating the forecast while corrective action is still possible. A is incorrect because waiting removes the chance to correct productivity or scope problems. B is incorrect because billing for unperformed work is not a response to a cost overrun. C is incorrect because altering time records falsifies the job-cost data the decision depends on.

questions.question: A rooftop gas heat section lights reliably but produces low heat rise and a lazy, yellow-tipped flame. Supply gas pressure to the unit is within range. What measurement most directly confirms a likely cause?

answers.text: Manifold pressure at the gas valve compared with the rating plate value, because low manifold pressure underfires the burner and softens the flame

Blower motor nameplate amps compared with locked-rotor amps, because flame appearance on a rooftop burner is set by blower electrical load while the rest of the system continues to operate normally through a complete cycle of operation

Economizer damper angle compared with its minimum position, because damper angle is the adjustment that meters gas flow to the burner section even after the obvious maintenance items at the unit have already been checked and corrected first
Condensate trap depth compared with pan pressure, because trap depth determines the gas pressure delivered to the burners during heating

questions.explanation: Low heat rise with a lazy flame and adequate inlet pressure points to underfiring, confirmed by manifold pressure against the rating plate. Blower locked-rotor amps, damper angle, and trap depth do not meter gas to the burner.

questions.question: A trainee proposes pressurizing a newly brazed refrigerant circuit with shop air indefinitely, and filling new gas piping with natural gas to soap the joints. Why must both proposals be rejected?

answers.text: Both are acceptable if done quickly
Shop air introduces moisture and oxygen into a refrigerant circuit (regulated dry nitrogen is the proper medium), and gas piping must be proven with air or inert gas before fuel gas is introduced
Soap solution is forbidden on all piping of any kind
Nitrogen cannot be used on either system under any circumstances

questions.explanation: Refrigerant circuits are pressure-tested with regulated dry nitrogen to avoid moisture and contamination, and fuel-gas piping is proven tight with air or inert gas before it is ever charged with gas, option B. Speed does not make either shortcut acceptable (A), approved leak-detection solution is a standard inspection method when testing is done properly (C), and nitrogen (D) is precisely the correct medium for refrigerant-circuit testing.

questions.question: Which statement correctly states a general employer duty under OSHA that applies to a refrigeration contractor's shop and field crews?

answers.text: The employer's only duty is to report injuries after they happen, because jobsite methods are left entirely to each crew, an approach the owner supports by pointing to the experience level of the senior technicians on staff.
The employer must provide a workplace free from recognized hazards, furnish needed personal protective equipment, and train employees on the hazards of their work.
The employer may delegate its safety duties to the employees themselves by posting the OSHA poster in the shop.
The employer's duties apply only on jobs over a stated dollar size, so small service calls carry no OSHA obligations.

questions.explanation: B is correct: Under OSHA's general duty and its standards, the employer must provide employment and a place of employment free from recognized hazards, comply with applicable standards, furnish and require appropriate personal protective equipment, and train employees so they understand the hazards and protections involved. A is wrong: Injury reporting is one requirement, but prevention — hazard control, PPE, and training — is the employer's primary duty. C is wrong: Posting notices informs employees; it does not transfer the employer's nondelegable duties. D is wrong: OSHA duties are not triggered by job dollar size (and Alabama HACR law likewise sets no dollar threshold for its duties).

questions.question: A furnace inducer runs at full speed but the pressure switch never closes. With a manometer teed into the switch tubing, vacuum is well below the switch setpoint and the vent is clear. The next best step is to:

answers.text: Check for a cracked or water-filled pressure-switch hose, a blocked heat-exchanger condensate drain, or a weak inducer producing insufficient draft
Replace the gas valve because manifold pressure must be low after checking that the igniter glows, the flame sensor is clean, and the burners have failed to light for three consecutive trials
Adjust the thermostat anticipator to a lower setting
Replace the flame sensor and clean the burners

questions.explanation: Insufficient vacuum with a clear vent directs diagnosis to the sensing hose, condensate blockage in the secondary exchanger, or an inducer too weak to develop draft. Option B concerns gas delivery after ignition, which is never reached. Option C affects thermostat cycling only. Option D concerns flame proving after light-off, not draft proving before it.

questions.question: In January a house shows heavy window condensation and RH of 55% indoors at 70°F, with no plumbing or roof leaks found. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.text: Outdoor winter air leaking in is humidifying the house, because cold outdoor air holds more moisture than warm indoor air and releases it at the windows
The windows are defective and are generating moisture at the glass, which is why condensation appears there first instead of anywhere else in the rooms
The furnace humidifier has failed empty and is somehow adding moisture, since window condensation in winter is a standard symptom of too little indoor humidity
Indoor vapor condensing on cold glass

questions.explanation: At 55% RH the indoor dew point is high enough that cold window glass falls below it, so indoor-generated vapor condenses on the coldest surface. Winter outdoor air is dry and dilutes indoor moisture when it leaks in, glass does not generate moisture, and a failed-empty humidifier would lower rather than raise indoor humidity.

questions.question: Torch brazing is planned inside a finished tenant space where cardboard, wood trim, and solvent-based materials are stored nearby. What must happen before the torch is lit?

answers.text: The torch operator should work quickly and keep the flame small, which is considered sufficient protection regardless of what is stored around the work area
The stored materials should be covered with a drop cloth borrowed from the painters, since any fabric covering makes combustibles safe from brazing sparks
Combustibles are moved or shielded, a permit is obtained, and an extinguisher is at hand
The tenant should be asked to leave the space, after which brazing may proceed with the materials in place because an empty room presents no fire risk

questions.explanation: Hot-work practice clears or shields combustibles, authorizes the work through a permit, and stages an extinguisher before ignition. A small flame still throws sparks, an ordinary drop cloth burns, and removing people does nothing to stop the stored materials from catching fire.

questions.question: A refrigeration firm's only person in responsible charge resigns on Monday. The office has unsigned proposals it wants to send out on Tuesday while it looks for a replacement. What is the firm's position under Board rules?

answers.text: The firm has a 90-day grace period to keep bidding while an emergency replacement is arranged after a resignation.

The firm may keep signing contracts for work it already bid, because proposals sent before the resignation remain valid indefinitely, and it may also accept new verbal work orders because no paperwork has been signed on those jobs yet.
The firm must immediately cease entering contracts and performing refrigeration work until the Board approves a certified contractor as person in responsible charge.
The firm may continue operating as long as it notifies the Board at its next annual renewal that the resignation occurred.

questions.explanation: C is correct: When the person in responsible charge separates from the entity, the contractor and the entity must notify the Board within five days, and the entity must immediately cease entering all contracts, verbal and written, and all installation, service, and repair work until a certified contractor is approved by the Board as person in responsible charge. A is wrong: The 90-day emergency certification applies to death or incapacitation, not to a resignation. B is wrong: The cease requirement covers entering new contracts, not merely performing unsigned proposals. D is wrong: Notice is due within five days, and work stops immediately — renewal-time notice is far too late.

questions.question: Two refrigeration contractors are both 67 years old. One holds an active certification and the other has held inactive status for several years. Which statement about the age-based continuing-education exemption is correct?

answers.text: Both are exempt, because the exemption turns on the contractor's age alone and applies in the same way to every certification status a contractor over 65 may hold.

Neither is exempt, because the age-based exemption was written for heating and air conditioning contractors and has no application to the refrigeration credential at all., so a refrigeration contractor of any status who is past that birthday renews without completing the annual education hours.
Only the inactive contractor can claim the exemption, because it applies to inactive contractors aged 65 or older and expressly does not apply to a contractor holding an active certification.
Only the active contractor can claim the exemption, because inactive contractors must complete continuing education every year to preserve their ability to reactivate later.

questions.explanation: C is correct: the exemption covers an inactive contractor who is 65 years of age or older, and it expressly does not apply to contractors 65 or older holding an active certification, so the active 67-year-old must still complete the annual hours. A is wrong because status matters as well as age. B is wrong because the exemption sits in the continuing-education rules governing certified contractors generally, including refrigeration contractors. D reverses the rule: inactive status is the qualifying status, and it is the active contractor who remains obligated.

questions.question: Two identical supply trunks are sealed the same day. On one, foil tape was pressed over dusty, slightly oily galvanized joints and burnished lightly; on the other, joints were wiped clean and dry and sealed with mastic reinforced at the corners. A year later the taped trunk leaks noticeably more. The best explanation is:

answers.text: Tape adhesion depends entirely on a clean, dry surface and firm burnishing, so the contaminated application failed progressively, while mastic bonds to the prepared surface and tolerates joint movement better
Tape always fails within a year regardless of how it is applied

Mastic works because it dissolves the galvanizing and welds the joint shut, fusing the two metal edges into a single continuous surface that no longer needs tape, fasteners, or any separate seal once the coating has fully cured in the field
The taped trunk leaked because tape adds thickness that narrows the duct

questions.explanation: Listed tapes are legitimate sealants only when their listing conditions are honored — clean, dry metal and full contact — whereas mastic on a prepared joint forms a durable, slightly flexible seal. Option B is wrong because properly listed and applied tape on clean duct can last for years; the failure here traces to the contaminated surface; option C is wrong because mastic is an adhesive sealant that cures on the surface; it does not dissolve zinc coatings or weld metal; option D is wrong because a few thousandths of tape thickness has no meaningful effect on duct area or leakage.

questions.question: A fixed-orifice system is charged by target superheat. Indoor wet-bulb temperature is 67 degrees F and outdoor dry-bulb temperature is 95 degrees F. Using target superheat equals ((3 times wet bulb) minus 80 minus outdoor dry bulb) divided by 2, what is the target?

answers.text: 26 degrees F
13 degrees F
8 degrees F
21 degrees F

questions.explanation: Three times 67 is 201, minus 80 minus 95 leaves 26, and divided by 2 gives a target superheat of 13 degrees F. Option A stops before dividing by 2, option C does not follow the stated formula from the given temperatures, and option D results from using the wrong outdoor temperature in the formula.

questions.question: Intermittent no-cool. The system cools well for about an hour, then the outdoor unit stops for roughly 20 minutes and restarts on its own, repeating through hot afternoons. During a dropout, the contactor coil has a full 24 V at its terminals yet is not pulled in, indoor blower and thermostat call continue normally, and compressor pressures are equalizing normally (not a pressure trip). Pulled after a dropout, the coil measures open circuit while hot but returns to about 16 ohms after cooling on the bench. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: A thermostat with an anti-short-cycle delay that lengthens in heat, which would remove the 24 V call during its delay rather than leave full voltage sitting at a coil that will not pull in
A high-pressure switch tripping on hot afternoons, which would open the control circuit and remove coil voltage instead of leaving 24 V present at the terminals during the dropout
A compressor internal overload cycling the unit, which would stop the compressor only while the condenser fan kept running and the contactor stayed pulled in
A contactor coil that opens thermally when hot and recovers as it cools

questions.explanation: Voltage is present but the coil will not pull in, and the coil itself proves open while hot and normal at 16 ohms when cool, a classic thermal intermittent that matches the run-an-hour, rest-20-minutes rhythm. A thermostat delay or pressure switch would remove coil voltage during the dropout, and a compressor overload leaves the contactor pulled in with the fan still running.

alaska-plumbing.quiz_title: Alaska Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A crew is setting a 6-inch horizontal building drain across a parking-lot trench. What minimum slope must they hold?

answers.text: 1/4 inch per foot
1/16 inch per foot
1/8 inch per foot
No slope is needed at this size

questions.explanation: Pipe 4 inches through 6 inches requires at least 1/8 inch per foot, about a 1% grade. The 1/4-inch rate applies to pipe 2-1/2 inches and smaller, 1/16 inch per foot is reserved for 8-inch and larger pipe, and a level drain would not move waste by gravity at all.

questions.question: Which statement correctly states the shared pressure rule for building water distribution?

answers.text: Maximum static pressure is 100 psi, with a regulator recommended above it
Pressure may reach 125 psi as long as fixtures are rated for it
There is no maximum; pressure is limited only by the water heater's relief valve
Maximum static pressure is 80 psi, and a pressure-reducing valve is required where the service pressure exceeds it

questions.explanation: Both code families cap building distribution static pressure at 80 psi and require an approved pressure-reducing valve where street or service pressure exceeds it. The 100 psi and 125 psi figures exceed that cap, and the heater relief valve is a safety device, not a pressure-regulation method.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the competent person's inspection duty for an excavation?

answers.text: Inspections are needed only on the first day the trench is opened
Inspections are needed only after a cave-in has occurred
Any worker may substitute a visual glance for the competent person's inspection
The competent person must inspect daily and before worker entry, and again after rain or another event that could increase hazards

questions.explanation: Daily and pre-entry inspection by the competent person, plus re-inspection after rain or other hazard-increasing events, is the stated duty. A first-day-only or after-the-fact inspection misses changing soil and water conditions.

questions.question: What approval must be obtained before a combination waste and vent system is installed?

answers.text: Verbal approval from the inspector at rough-in is sufficient, provided the installation matches the approved fixture schedule
The construction documents for each system must be approved by the Authority Having Jurisdiction before any portion is installed
Approval of the fixture schedule only, obtained after the piping is roughed in but before it is covered or tested
No approval, provided the system passes its final test and the vents are each provided with an accessible cleanout

questions.explanation: The construction documents for each combination system need approval from the Authority Having Jurisdiction before any part of the system goes in. A rough-in conversation or a passing final test does not replace that advance document approval.

questions.question: A dwelling has 3.5 bathrooms and 4 bedrooms. What minimum first-hour rating must its storage water heater have?

answers.text: 49 gallons
62 gallons
74 gallons
38 gallons

questions.explanation: For 3 to 3.5 bathrooms with 4 bedrooms, the required first-hour rating is 74 gallons. The 62-gallon rating covers smaller combinations such as 3 to 3.5 bathrooms with 3 bedrooms, and 49 and 38 gallons serve one-bathroom dwellings.

questions.question: Three drinking fountains on one corridor branch drain through a common segment. What load does that segment carry from the fountains alone?

answers.text: 1.5 DFU
0.5 DFU — grouped fountains share one rating
3 DFU
6 DFU

questions.explanation: Each fountain is 0.5 DFU and loads add along the flow: 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.5 DFU. Counting the group once ignores additivity, while 3 or 6 DFU would require per-fountain values of 1 or 2 DFU that the shared table does not assign.

questions.question: A dishwasher is added under a remodeled counter and tapped off a convenient 3/8-inch line. What is the minimum supply size for a domestic dishwasher?

answers.text: 3/8 inch
1/2 inch
3/4 inch
1 inch

questions.explanation: A domestic dishwasher requires a minimum 1/2-inch supply, the same minimum shared by several common residential fixtures. The 3/8-inch tap is undersized, and 3/4 inch or 1 inch are larger than the minimum required.

questions.question: Hot water at 165 °F is mixed with cold water at 65 °F to produce 125 °F water. What percentage of the mix is hot water?
questions.explanation: Hot fraction = (125 − 65) ÷ (165 − 65) = 60 ÷ 100 = 0.60, or 60%. The 40% option is the cold fraction, and 76% wrongly divides the mix temperature by the hot temperature (125 ÷ 165).

questions.question: A shower compartment has one main shower head and two additional heads, all draining to the same shower drain. What is the total drainage fixture unit load of the shower?

answers.text: 4 DFU
3 DFU
2 DFU
6 DFU

questions.explanation: The base single-head shower contributes 2 DFU and each additional head adds 1 DFU, so two extra heads add 2 DFU for a total of 4 DFU. Counting only the base head ignores the additional-head rule, and charging 2 DFU per head double-counts the base rating.

questions.question: A 2-inch vent is laid out to serve 20 fixture units, which is within its load rating, but its developed length comes to 150 feet. How must the design be corrected?

answers.text: Increase the vent to 3 inches, whose 212-foot length limit covers the run while its load rating also covers 20 units
Leave the 2-inch vent, because meeting the load rating makes the length limit advisory only
Increase the vent to 2-1/2 inches, a size the combined table lists with a 150-foot vent limit
Keep the 2-inch size but split the run with a second trap arm so the length limit resets

questions.explanation: Both limits in the combined table must be satisfied at once: a 2-inch vent is capped at 120 feet, so 150 feet fails on length even though 20 units is within its 24-unit load. A 3-inch vent, rated 84 units and 212 feet, covers both; the table lists no 2-1/2-inch vent row, and no trap-arm change resets a vent's developed length.

questions.question: An apprentice reads the branch sizes in the fixture-unit table as outside diameters and orders tube accordingly. What is wrong with that reading?

answers.text: The listed sizes are nominal (inside diameter) pipe sizes
The listed sizes are thread sizes for the fixture stops
The listed sizes are outside diameters of copper tube only
The listed sizes are minimum drainage sizes, not supply sizes

questions.explanation: The table's minimum fixture branch pipe sizes are nominal (inside diameter) pipe sizes. Treating them as outside diameters or thread sizes misreads the table, and the sizes belong to the water-supply side of the system, not the drainage side.

questions.question: An applicant asks where to apply for an Alaska master plumber license so they can perform code work. What is the correct response?

answers.text: Apply to the commerce department for the master plumber license
Apply to Mechanical Inspection for a master plumber license after passing the administrator exam
A master plumber license is issued automatically with an administrator license
There is no such license; performing code work is authorized by the journeyman certificate of fitness

questions.explanation: No master plumber license exists in Alaska. Performing code work is authorized by the journeyman certificate of fitness, while an administrator license covers supervision and sign-off only, so directing the applicant to a master license program would be wrong.

questions.question: A dry vent serves a group whose highest flood-level rim is at 40 inches above the floor. The vent is roughed to turn horizontal at 44 inches. How much higher must the vertical rise go before the turn is permitted?

answers.text: At least 2 inches more, to reach 6 inches above the rim
It may turn now; it is already above the rim
At least 6 inches more, for a full second clearance
It must rise to the ceiling regardless of rim height

questions.explanation: The vent must rise at least 6 inches above the flood-level rim of the highest fixture served: 40 plus 6 is 46 inches, and the rough-in at 44 inches is 2 inches short. Merely clearing the rim is not enough, adding a full extra 6 inches overshoots the requirement, and ceiling height plays no part in the rule.

questions.question: On a 45° offset with an 11-inch set in a soffit, the travel piece is measured between two fittings that each have a take-out of 1.25 inches. What is the cut length of the piece between the fittings?
questions.explanation: Travel = 11 × 1.414 = 15.55 in. Cut length = 15.55 − (2 × 1.25) = 15.55 − 2.50 = 13.05 in. The 15.55 in. option deducts nothing and 14.30 in. deducts only one fitting.

questions.question: A private bathroom in an older home contains a water closet flushing more than 1.6 gallons per flush, a single lavatory, and a single-head shower. What is the total drainage fixture unit load of the room?

answers.text: 6 DFU
5 DFU
9 DFU
7 DFU

questions.explanation: Summing the individual fixtures: the older water closet rates 4 DFU in private use above 1.6 gpf, the lavatory 1 DFU, and the shower 2 DFU, for 7 DFU total. The familiar 6 DFU sum belongs to the same room fitted with a 1.6 gpf closet.

questions.question: A vertical stack drops into a horizontal drain through a combination wye and 1/8-bend branch. An apprentice objects that only a long-turn tee wye should be used. What is the correct ruling?

answers.text: The objection stands; vertical-to-horizontal joints need a sanitary tee.
The objection stands; combination branches are for horizontal joints only.
The joint is approved only if the stack is 2 inches or smaller.
The combination branch is an approved pattern for a vertical line entering a horizontal line.

questions.explanation: Vertical drainage entering horizontal drainage uses the same fitting families as horizontal joints, and the combination wye and 1/8-bend is expressly among them. Sanitary-tee patterns are absent from the list for this direction as well, and no small-stack exception is involved.

questions.question: During a remodel, a plumber finds a shutoff valve installed between a water heater and its relief valve, placed there so the valve can be serviced without draining the heater. What is required?

answers.text: Leave it, provided the valve is left locked in the open position
Remove the shutoff valve; no shutoff may be placed between the relief valve and the heater or on the discharge pipe to the atmosphere
Leave it, provided a second relief valve is installed downstream of it
Replace it with a check valve so flow can only move toward the heater

questions.explanation: No shutoff valve may sit between a relief valve and the water heater, or on the discharge piping between the valve and the atmosphere, because isolating the relief device defeats overpressure protection. Locking it open, adding a second valve downstream, or substituting a check valve all leave a prohibited obstruction in the relief path.

questions.question: In a strip-mall tenant build-out, the tenant's plumber vents all the new fixtures into the ceiling vent piping but makes no connection to any vent that reaches outdoors, planning to tie in during a later phase. The space is otherwise ready to open. What is the status of the vent system?

answers.text: Complete, because the tie-in is planned for a later phase and the branch vents are already installed and safely capped
Complete, because branch vents are all a tenant space needs when a landlord vent system exists somewhere in the building
Incomplete only if an odor complaint is filed
Incomplete — the building's venting must include at least one main vent extending to the open air outdoors, and this system currently has none in service

questions.explanation: A vent system with no main vent to the open air cannot admit or emit air as venting requires, so it is incomplete now, not at some later phase. A planned connection is not a connection, branch vents alone never satisfy the through-to-outdoors requirement, and compliance does not wait on a complaint.

questions.question: A supply connector burst in a laundry room. The static pressure gauges a normal 60 psi, and the owner insists 'the pressure is fine, so the piping can't be over-stressed.' The washer's solenoid valve snaps shut at the end of every fill. What explains the burst?

answers.text: The gauge must be broken - static pressure is secretly above 150 psi
The connector burst from thermal expansion of the hot line
Vibration from the washer's spin cycle fatigued the connector
Water hammer - the surge from the quick-closing valve can reach many times the normal static pressure, and that transient spike, not the 60 psi static reading, burst the connector

questions.explanation: Water hammer is a shock wave: stopping moving water suddenly generates a surge many times the static pressure, enough to burst piping and damage fixtures even when the resting pressure is a normal 60 psi. A static gauge cannot see the transient spike that did the damage.

questions.question: On one floor, a horizontal branch joins a horizontal main, and directly above, a vertical line drops into the same main. The installer uses a combination wye and 1/8-bend at the first joint and a 45-degree wye at the second. Judge the pair.

answers.text: Only the first complies; vertical lines need sanitary tees to enter a main.
Only the second complies; combination branches are barred at horizontal joints.
Both joints comply; each uses a pattern from the approved families for its connection.
Neither complies; both joints require double fixture fittings.

questions.explanation: Horizontal-to-horizontal and vertical-to-horizontal connections draw on the same approved families, 45-degree wyes and combination wye and 1/8-bend branches or equivalents, so both choices fit their joints. Sanitary tees appear on neither list, and double fixture fittings belong to back-to-back fixture connections, not these joints.

arizona-plumbing.quiz_title: Arizona Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A cleanout is specified for a 3-inch horizontal drain in a restaurant kitchen. What size cleanout must be furnished?

answers.text: 2 inches — one size below the pipe is standard
4 inches — every cleanout is 4 inches
3 inches — the same nominal size as the pipe
1-1/2 inches, to match the largest trap on the line

questions.explanation: A cleanout must be the same nominal size as the pipe it serves, up to 4 inches, so a 3-inch drain takes a 3-inch cleanout. Reducing it restricts rodding access, the universal 4-inch answer confuses the cap for larger pipe with a universal size, and trap size does not set cleanout size.

questions.question: A hotel bathroom rough-in is at the parts-ordering stage. What minimum branch size must be ordered for the bathtub supplies?

answers.text: 1/2 inch
1 inch
3/4 inch
1-1/4 inches

questions.explanation: A bathtub's minimum fixture supply is 1/2 inch under the shared table values. The 1-inch size is the minimum for a flush-valve water closet, and 3/4 inch and 1-1/4 inches are not the bathtub's table minimum — the item asks for the minimum, not an upsized preference.

questions.question: Which termination gives an indirect waste line full protection against both backsiphonage and backpressure?

answers.text: An air break ending at the flood-level rim
An air gap, with the outlet terminating above the receptor's flood-level rim by the required distance
A deep trap seal on a directly connected drain
A check valve installed in the indirect waste pipe

questions.explanation: Only the air gap's physical separation above the flood-level rim blocks both mechanisms. An air break is incomplete, and mechanical devices in the waste line do not equal that open separation.

questions.question: Fixtures discharging to a wet vent total 10 DFU. What is the smallest wet vent size the IPC table permits for that load?

answers.text: 3 inches
2-1/2 inches
2 inches
1-1/2 inches

questions.explanation: The table capacities are 1-1/2 inch = 1 DFU, 2 inch = 4 DFU, 2-1/2 inch = 6 DFU, and 3 inch = 12 DFU. Only the 3-inch size covers a 10-DFU discharge to the wet vent; every smaller size is exceeded.

questions.question: What rules govern the shutoff valve on the cold-water branch serving a water heater?

answers.text: The valve may be located anywhere in the building as long as it is labeled
The valve may serve the heater and one additional appliance on the same branch
The valve must be near the equipment, serve only that equipment, be accessible on the same floor level as the heater, and must not disrupt cold-water supply to the rest of the system
The valve must be on the floor below the heater to drain the riser

questions.explanation: The cold-water branch to each heater or storage tank must have a valve located near the equipment, serving only that equipment, with access provided on the same floor level as the equipment, arranged so closing it does not disrupt the cold-water supply to the rest of the system. Remote labeled valves, shared-appliance valves, and a floor-below location each violate one of those conditions.

questions.question: A building owner asks why the new drains cannot simply be tied into a small booster pump so the pipes can run level. Which answer states the governing principle?

answers.text: Drainage piping may always run level if a pump is anywhere in the building
Drainage is a gravity system; its piping is sloped to maintain self-scouring flow rather than relying on pressure
Level drainage is allowed for runs under 20 feet
Pumps increase the required slope instead of replacing it

questions.explanation: Sanitary drainage is designed as a gravity system, with slope chosen to maintain a self-scouring velocity of about 2 ft/sec. The presence of a pump elsewhere, a short run length, or a supposed slope increase does not turn the gravity drainage piping itself into a level pressure system.

questions.question: In a closed mechanical-room system, pressure on a storage heater climbs while temperature stays normal. At what pressure will a standard T&P relief valve open on pressure?

answers.text: 80 psi
100 psi
150 psi
210 psi

questions.explanation: The standard T&P pressure setting is 150 psi. The 80 psi figure is the building distribution maximum — a different rule — 100 psi is below the stamped setting, and 210 is the valve's temperature number, not a pressure.

questions.question: A 22.5° offset has a set of 10 inches. Each of the two fittings has a take-out of 2 inches. What is the cut length of the travel piece?
questions.explanation: Travel = 10 × 2.613 = 26.13 in.; cut length = 26.13 − (2 × 2) = 26.13 − 4.00 = 22.13 in. The 26.13 in. option deducts nothing, and 24.13 in. deducts only one fitting.

questions.question: A branch carries 22 DFU of ordinary fixtures, and equipment on it adds a semicontinuous discharge of 5 gpm. The branch must be sized for:

answers.text: 27 DFU
32 DFU
22 DFU
47 DFU

questions.explanation: The semicontinuous flow converts at 2 DFU per gpm, adding 10 DFU to the 22 DFU of fixtures, for a design load of 32 DFU. The 27 DFU answer adds the flow one-to-one, and ignoring the equipment flow entirely leaves an undersized 22 DFU branch.

questions.question: A non-pneumatic ejector discharges 500 gpm. Its sump vent is proposed at 2-1/2 inches with a 20-foot developed length. What does the sump-vent table say?

answers.text: The 2-1/2-inch vent is permitted up to 25 feet
A 2-1/2-inch vent is not permitted at that discharge; a 3-inch vent allows up to 24 feet
A 2-inch vent allows up to 97 feet at that discharge
Any size is permitted because length is unlimited at high discharge

questions.explanation: At 500 gpm, vents of 2-1/2 inches and smaller are not permitted at all; the table first allows a 3-inch vent, capped at 24 feet. The 25-foot and 97-foot figures come from the 100-gpm row for smaller vents and do not transfer to this discharge.

questions.question: An indirect waste pipe has an effective opening of 3/4 inch and discharges through an air gap into a floor sink. What minimum air gap is required?

answers.text: 3/4 inch
1 inch
2-1/2 inches
1-1/2 inches

questions.explanation: The indirect-waste air gap must be not less than twice the effective opening of the pipe. Twice the 3/4-inch opening is 1-1/2 inches; an answer equal to the opening itself applies no multiplier at all.

questions.question: An over-rim bath filler with a 1-inch effective opening is installed with a single wall 2-1/2 inches from the outlet. What is the minimum required air gap?

answers.text: 2 in.
3 in.
4 in.

questions.explanation: First decide which column governs: a wall is close to the outlet when it lies within three times the opening diameter, and 3 x 1 = 3 inches, so a wall 2-1/2 inches away is close. Over-rim bath fillers and fixtures with openings up to 1 inch require 3 inches close to a wall. The 2-inch answer is the away-from-wall value for the same row, which would govern only if the wall were more than 3 inches away.

questions.question: A remodel keeps a fixture on a 4-inch drain. The stock on the truck is 1-1/4-inch, 1-1/2-inch, 2-inch, and 3-inch vent pipe. Applying the half-diameter rule, what is the smallest stock size the vent may be?

answers.text: 1-1/4 inches, because that is the minimum vent size anywhere
2 inches
1-1/2 inches
3 inches

questions.explanation: Half of the 4-inch drain diameter is 2 inches, so the vent may not be smaller than 2 inches, and that size also clears the 1-1/4-inch system minimum. The 1-1/4-inch and 1-1/2-inch choices satisfy or approach the general minimum but fail the half-diameter rule for this drain, and 3 inches is larger than the rule requires.

questions.question: A tempering valve blends 160 °F hot water with 55 °F cold water to deliver 105 °F water. A process needs 90 gallons of the mixed water. How many gallons of hot water are required?

answers.text: 47.1 gal
60.0 gal
42.9 gal
45.0 gal

questions.explanation: Hot fraction = (105 − 55) ÷ (160 − 55) = 50 ÷ 105 = 0.476. Hot gallons = 0.476 × 90 = 42.86 ≈ 42.9 gal. The 47.1 gal option is the cold-water share, and 60.0 gal wrongly reuses the two-thirds example fraction.

questions.question: In a split-level restaurant, only the basement fixtures sit below the elevation of the next upstream manhole cover; the dining-level fixtures sit above it. Which arrangement complies?

answers.text: Route every fixture in the building through one backwater valve on the main drain
No backwater valve is needed anywhere in the building
Protect the basement fixtures with a backwater valve in the horizontal branch serving them, and keep the dining-level fixtures off that valve
Put the backwater valve only on the dining-level branch

questions.explanation: Fixtures below the manhole-cover elevation must be protected by a backwater valve in the building drain or the horizontal branch serving them, and fixtures above that elevation must not discharge through a backwater valve. Protecting only the basement branch satisfies both halves of the rule; valving the whole building impermissibly routes the upper fixtures through the valve, and valving only the upper branch protects the wrong fixtures.

questions.question: A fire-protection branch without chemical additives presents only a low (non-health) hazard, but both backpressure and backsiphonage are possible. Which testable assembly fits this application?

answers.text: A reduced-pressure principle assembly is the only assembly ever permitted on any hazard
An atmospheric vacuum breaker (ASSE 1001)
A spill-resistant vacuum breaker assembly (ASSE 1056)
A double-check valve assembly (ASSE 1015)

questions.explanation: The double-check valve assembly is the testable assembly rated for low hazard against both backpressure and backsiphonage — exactly this application. A reduced-pressure assembly would also protect here but is not the only permitted choice, and both vacuum breakers protect against backsiphonage only, leaving the backpressure threat uncovered.

questions.question: A valve-predominant transportation terminal contains thirty public flushometer-valve water closets and twenty public urinals with 1-inch flushometer valves. What is the estimated demand?

answers.text: 143 gpm
127 gpm
177 gpm
108 gpm

questions.explanation: The load is 30 x 10.0 + 20 x 10.0 = 500 WSFU, and the flushometer-valve curve reads 500 WSFU as 143 gpm. The neighboring valve-curve values frame the schedule: 108 gpm is the value at 300 WSFU, 127 gpm at 400 WSFU, and 177 gpm at 750 WSFU. Reading a curve cell beside the actual load, rather than at it, produces each of those answers.

questions.question: A remodel moves a sink to a new wall. The drain is reconnected the same day, but the vent tie-in is left for the following week, and the owner uses the sink in the meantime, judging it by its free drainage. What is the plumber's obligation?

answers.text: None; no obligation arises until the final inspection is called and an inspector actually orders the vent connection to be made
Leave the sink in service through the week; its free drainage and lack of odor prove the trap is safe until the vent crew returns, and interim use is the owner's choice
Take the position that the trap is unprotected until its vent is connected — every fixture trap must be protected by a vent — and complete the vent connection rather than relying on interim drainage
Add a second trap under the sink for the interim week, so the fixture has double seal protection until the vent is connected and the extra trap can be removed

questions.explanation: A trap without its vent is an unprotected trap from the first discharge, however freely the sink seems to drain; the standard is the rule — every fixture trap protected by a vent — not a week of apparently normal use. Waiting for inspection does not change the trap's exposure, and an interim second trap would be prohibited double-trapping.

questions.question: At a cafe's final inspection, the drain from a beverage machine is discovered ending down inside its floor sink, its outlet below the sink's flood-level rim and sometimes sitting in standing water. The installer shrugs: 'Close enough - that is basically an air gap.' What is the correct ruling?

answers.text: He is right - any open, unsealed termination counts as an air gap
It is a direct connection, and it must be sealed to the sink with a coupling
It is only an air break, not an air gap - its backsiphonage protection is incomplete, and the outlet must be raised above the rim to gain full protection
It is acceptable because the floor sink is trapped and vented

questions.explanation: Classification turns on where the outlet ends: at or below the flood-level rim is an air break, whose protection is incomplete because receptor water can reach - or even submerge - the outlet; only a termination above the rim by the required distance is an air gap. The receptor being trapped and vented does not upgrade the classification.

questions.question: Using the IPC Appendix E fixture-unit table, a private bathroom group with a flush-tank water closet is assigned cold, hot, and total water supply fixture unit loads. A small addition combines two identical groups on one branch. What total load does the branch carry?

answers.text: 3.6 WSFU
7.2 WSFU
8.0 WSFU
16.0 WSFU

questions.explanation: One private flush-tank bathroom group totals 3.6 WSFU (cold 2.7, hot 1.5), so two groups load the branch with 2 x 3.6 = 7.2 WSFU. The 3.6 figure counts only one group, 8.0 WSFU is the total for a single flushometer-valve group, and 16.0 doubles that valve-group value instead.

florida-plumbing.quiz_title: Florida Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A junior designer asks why simply enlarging a nearly flat drain does not fix its fouling problem. Which principle answers the question?

answers.text: Drainage is a gravity system whose slope must maintain a self-scouring velocity of about 2 ft/sec; a flatter oversized run still lets solids settle
Larger pipe always flows slower, so diameter must never be increased
Fouling is caused only by vent sizing, never by slope
Solids float to the top of any drain regardless of velocity

questions.explanation: Minimum slopes exist to keep gravity flow at a self-scouring velocity of about 2 ft/sec so solids stay entrained. Enlarging a flat run does not restore that velocity, vent sizing does not cause this fouling, and solids do not reliably float clear — they settle when flow slows.

questions.question: In a coin laundry, each commercial automatic clothes washer is rated at what drainage fixture unit value?

answers.text: 2 DFU
4 DFU
6 DFU
3 DFU

questions.explanation: A commercial automatic clothes washer is rated 3 DFU. The 2 DFU value is the residential clothes washer rating, so the use, not just the appliance, decides the value.

questions.question: A lavatory faucet with a 1/2-in. effective opening is installed well away from any wall, farther than the close-to-wall distance. What is the minimum required air gap?

answers.text: 1 in.

questions.explanation: For lavatories and fixtures with effective openings of not more than 1/2 in., the required air gap away from a wall is 1 in. The 1-1/2-in. option is that row's close-to-wall value, which does not apply at this distance. The 2-1/2-in. option is the close-to-wall value for sinks with larger openings, and the 1/2-in. option merely repeats the opening size, which is not the gap for any row covering this fixture.

questions.question: How often must a Florida certified contractor's certification be renewed?

answers.text: Every year
Every 3 years
Every 2 years
Every 5 years

questions.explanation: Florida certification is renewed every 2 years. An annual cycle is too short, and 3-year and 5-year cycles are both longer than Florida's biennial renewal period.

questions.question: A gravity tank is filled from the potable system under the IPC. How must its inlet terminate, and where must the tank overflow discharge?

answers.text: The inlet may connect directly below the overflow rim, and the overflow may discharge at floor level
The inlet terminates with an air gap at least 1 inch above the overflow, and the overflow discharges at least 2 inches above a drain
The inlet terminates with an air gap at least 4 inches above the overflow, and the overflow discharges at least 6 inches above a roof, floor, drain, or open fixture
The inlet terminates with an air gap at least 4 inches above the overflow, and the overflow must be hard-piped directly into the drainage system

questions.explanation: The potable inlet to a gravity tank must end in an air gap of not less than 4 inches above the overflow so tank water can never siphon back, and the overflow itself must spill visibly at least 6 inches above a roof, floor, drain, or open fixture. A direct inlet connection defeats the backflow protection, the 1-inch/2-inch figures understate both clearances, and hard-piping the overflow removes the required visible air-gap discharge.

questions.question: Plans show a vent serving a 6-inch drain drawn at 2 inches. The reviewer applies the half-diameter rule. What correction must be entered on the plans?

answers.text: None; 2 inches exceeds the 1-1/4-inch vent minimum
Increase the vent to at least 2-1/2 inches
Increase the vent to at least 3 inches
Reduce the drain to 4 inches so the 2-inch vent works

questions.explanation: The vent may not be smaller than half the diameter of the drain it serves: half of 6 inches is 3 inches, so the 2-inch vent must grow to at least 3 inches. Clearing the 1-1/4-inch general minimum does not cure a half-diameter failure, 2-1/2 inches is still below half, and shrinking a designed drain to rescue an undersized vent reverses the sizing logic.

questions.question: A 15-foot-deep trench in Type C soil is being planned. A worker suggests benching the walls to save excavation width. Why must that suggestion be rejected?

answers.text: Benching is allowed in Type C if the benches are narrow
Benching is the preferred method for Type C soil
Benching is not permitted in Type C soil, so sloping at 1-1/2H:1V or another protective system must be used
The depth alone prohibits benching, but Type C would otherwise allow it

questions.explanation: The prohibition is tied to the soil: benching is not permitted in Type C, the least stable class. At 15 feet the excavation is within the tabulated range, so sloping, shoring, or shielding must provide protection instead.

questions.question: Tempered water is supplied to fixtures under the IPC. What is the maximum tempered-water temperature, and through what kind of device must it be delivered?

answers.text: 120 degrees F, through the water heater's thermostat
110 degrees F, through the water heater's thermostat
110 degrees F, through a temperature-limiting device conforming to ASSE 1070
140 degrees F, through a temperature-limiting device conforming to ASSE 1070

questions.explanation: Tempered water must be limited to not greater than 110 degrees F by a temperature-limiting device conforming to ASSE 1070 / ASME A112.1070 / CSA B125.70. The code expressly says a water-heater thermostat does not count as the temperature-limiting means, which rules out both thermostat answers, and 120 and 140 degrees exceed the tempered-water limit.

questions.question: Under the administrative chapter carried in the Florida plumbing code, which inspection covers the stage when trenches are excavated and piping is installed, before any backfill is placed?

answers.text: The rough-in inspection
The final inspection
The framing inspection
The underground inspection

questions.explanation: The underground inspection is the stage performed after trenches are excavated and piping is installed but before backfill. The rough-in inspection comes later, once roofing, framing, and fireblocking are in place, and the final inspection occurs when the building is complete and ready for occupancy; framing is not one of the three plumbing inspections in this sequence.

questions.question: An applicant for certification submits a forged letter to the board claiming years of experience the applicant never had. Which description fits this conduct?

answers.text: A routine application shortcut the board overlooks if the exam is passed
Permissible advocacy, because supporting letters are not evidence
A correctable defect that only delays the application by one cycle
Giving false or forged evidence to the board, which is a prohibited act

questions.explanation: Submitting forged documentation to the board is giving false or forged evidence, a prohibited act. Supporting letters are evidence, passing an exam does not erase the forgery, and the conduct is not treated as a harmless correctable defect.

questions.question: A sanitary tee is used to turn drainage flow from vertical to horizontal under a slab. Is that pattern permitted under the IPC fitting table?

answers.text: Yes — sanitary tees are permitted in all three directions of change
Yes — if the tee is one size larger than the drain
No — a sanitary tee is permitted only for a horizontal-to-vertical change of direction
No — sanitary tees are prohibited in drainage entirely

questions.explanation: The fitting-pattern table permits a sanitary tee only where drainage turns from horizontal to vertical. Using it vertical-to-horizontal or horizontal-to-horizontal is not permitted at any size, though the tee itself remains a lawful drainage fitting in its one permitted orientation.

questions.question: A gooseneck faucet with a 3/4-inch effective opening is installed in a corner, with two intersecting walls each 2-1/2 inches from the outlet. What is the minimum required air gap?

answers.text: 3 in.
2 in.

questions.explanation: With two intersecting walls, the outlet is close to a wall when the walls lie within four times the opening diameter: 4 x 0.75 = 3 inches, and walls at 2-1/2 inches are inside that distance, so the close-to-wall column governs. Sinks, laundry trays, gooseneck faucets and fixtures with openings up to 3/4 inch require 2-1/2 inches close to a wall. The 1-1/2-inch answer is the away-from-wall value for the same row, and 3 inches is the close value for the next larger opening row.

questions.question: A mechanical room's floor drain sits slightly uphill from the water heater, and the installer pitches the T&P discharge pipe up to reach it, figuring pressure will push any discharge through. What rule is violated?

answers.text: The discharge pipe must drain by gravity — a relief discharge cannot be pitched uphill or trapped on its way to the receptor
No rule — relief pressure overcomes any pitch
The pipe must be pitched up at least 1/4 inch per foot
Only metal discharge pipe may drain by gravity

questions.explanation: T&P discharge piping drains by gravity, so an uphill or trapped run that holds water against the valve violates the rule. The valve's lifting pressure is not a design basis for the discharge path, and no upward pitch is ever prescribed for it.

questions.question: In a horizontal wet-vent system, the dry vent is connected to a water closet fixture drain, and that drain is run vertically down into the wet-vented branch. What does the arrangement require instead?

answers.text: Where the dry vent connects to a water closet fixture drain, that drain must connect horizontally to the wet-vent system
A water closet drain carrying the dry vent may connect at any angle
The dry vent must be moved to the bathtub drain in all cases
The water closet must be relocated downstream of every other fixture

questions.explanation: The dry-vent rules single out the water closet connection: when the dry vent ties to a water closet fixture drain, that drain's connection to the wet-vent system must be horizontal. Letting it drop in vertically, forcing the dry vent onto a different fixture, or reordering the closet downstream are none of them the stated condition.

questions.question: A plumbing project includes fire line standpipes where the law authorizes that work for the trade, and excavation that is incidental to the plumbing installation. How does the plumbing scope treat those items?

answers.text: Both items are excluded, because standpipes and excavation are never treated as plumbing work
The standpipes are included on the project but excavation incidental to the work is always excluded
Standpipes and sprinklers are included where authorized by law, and incidental excavation is included
Both items are included only on jobs where the property owner acts as the project's own contractor

questions.explanation: The plumbing scope includes fire line standpipes and fire sprinklers where authorized by law, and excavation incidental to the work. Neither item is categorically excluded, incidental excavation is not carved out while standpipes are kept, and the owner acting as contractor is not the condition for either inclusion.

questions.question: A Category 2 facility proposes a single medical air compressor train and one alarm panel for its warning system. Which pair of conditions makes that proposal acceptable?

answers.text: Simplex sources are permitted with a facility emergency plan for loss of service, and the single panel sits under continuous surveillance while operating
Simplex sources are permitted with no emergency plan at all, and the single panel may sit in a locked room that staff visit only once each week or so
Simplex sources are permitted only in Category 1, and the single panel is permitted only where master alarms are omitted from the system entirely
Simplex sources require a duplicate standby building, and the single panel must be duplicated at two locations before the facility may open its doors

questions.explanation: In Category 2 and 3, sources such as medical air compressors may be simplex if facility staff develop an emergency plan for loss of that service, and the warning system may use a single alarm panel located in an area of continuous surveillance while the facility operates. No plan at all and a rarely visited locked room both fail those conditions, simplex permission belongs to Category 2 and 3 rather than Category 1, and neither a standby building nor a duplicated panel is the stated condition.

questions.question: A storage water heater is fed through a pressure-reducing valve, with no check valve anywhere in the supply. The crew argues no expansion control is needed because there is no check valve. What is required?

answers.text: No expansion control is required unless a check valve is present, because a pressure-reducing valve does not close the system to expansion back toward the street main
An expansion-control device is required, connected upstream of the pressure-reducing valve so the street side of the system absorbs the expansion volume
The relief valve must be upsized instead of adding an expansion device, and its discharge pipe must be increased one size to handle the expansion discharge
An expansion-control device is required, connected to the heater cold-water supply pipe downstream of the pressure-reducing valve

questions.explanation: Thermal expansion control is triggered where a storage water heater is fed through a check valve, a pressure-reducing valve, or a backflow preventer; a PRV alone creates the closed system. The device connects to the cold-water supply pipe downstream of the PRV, not upstream of it, and the relief valve must not be used to control thermal expansion.

questions.question: A trap arm for a 2-inch drain runs 9 feet at 1/4 inch per foot before reaching its vent. By how much does its total fall exceed one pipe diameter?
questions.explanation: Total fall = 9 × 1/4 = 2.25 in. One pipe diameter is 2.00 in., so the excess is 2.25 − 2.00 = 0.25 in. — the geometry that limits trap-arm length. The 2.25 in. option is the total fall, not the excess over the diameter.

questions.question: A 6,000-square-foot roof receives runoff diverted onto it by two vertical walls, one of 3,000 square feet and one of 1,000 square feet. The design rainfall rate is 3 inches per hour. What design flow must the storm system handle?

answers.text: 312 gpm
208 gpm

questions.explanation: Half the area of each vertical wall that diverts rainwater to the roof is added to the roof area, so the two walls add 1,500 and 500 square feet, for an effective area of 8,000 square feet. The 187.2 gpm answer omits the walls entirely, and 312 gpm wrongly adds the full wall areas instead of half.

questions.question: In a split-level restaurant, only the basement fixtures sit below the elevation of the next upstream manhole cover; the dining-level fixtures sit above it. Which arrangement complies?

answers.text: Route every fixture in the building through one backwater valve on the main drain
No backwater valve is needed anywhere in the building
Protect the basement fixtures with a backwater valve in the horizontal branch serving them, and keep the dining-level fixtures off that valve
Put the backwater valve only on the dining-level branch

questions.explanation: Fixtures below the manhole-cover elevation must be protected by a backwater valve in the building drain or the horizontal branch serving them, and fixtures above that elevation must not discharge through a backwater valve. Protecting only the basement branch satisfies both halves of the rule; valving the whole building impermissibly routes the upper fixtures through the valve, and valving only the upper branch protects the wrong fixtures.

north-carolina-plumbing.quiz_title: North Carolina Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An 8-inch horizontal building sewer is being graded with a laser level. What is the flattest slope that still meets the minimum?

answers.text: 1/4 inch per foot
1/8 inch per foot
1/2 inch per foot
1/16 inch per foot

questions.explanation: Horizontal drainage pipe 8 inches and larger requires at least 1/16 inch per foot. The steeper 1/8-inch and 1/4-inch rates are the minimums for mid-size and small pipe respectively — they would work hydraulically but they are not the minimum for this size, and the item asks for the minimum.

questions.question: A dental lavatory in a treatment room is counted at what drainage fixture unit value?

answers.text: 2 DFU
3 DFU
0.5 DFU
1 DFU

questions.explanation: A dental lavatory is rated 1 DFU. It is not rated 2 DFU like a service sink or bathtub, nor 0.5 DFU like a drinking fountain or nonwater urinal.

questions.question: A tank-predominant building has six public flush-tank water closets and no other fixtures. What is the estimated demand for this fixture schedule?

answers.text: 42.0 gpm
21.5 gpm
26.3 gpm
23.3 gpm

questions.explanation: The load is 6 x 5.0 (public flush-tank water closets) = 30 WSFU. On the tank-predominant conversion curve, 30 WSFU = 23.3 gpm. The 42.0-gpm option is the valve-predominant curve at 30 WSFU, which is the wrong curve for a flush-tank building. The 21.5-gpm option is the tank curve at 25 WSFU and the 26.3-gpm option is the tank curve at 40 WSFU; both are wrong-row reads.

questions.question: A lavatory is built into a freestanding vanity island in an open-plan bath. Which venting statement is correct for it?

answers.text: Island fixtures cannot be vented, so the trap goes unprotected
A loop vent is recognized for island lavatories, and its below-flood-level portion needs a rodding cleanout
The lavatory must be moved to a wall before it can be used
A second trap under the floor replaces the loop vent

questions.explanation: Loop (island fixture) venting is recognized for island sinks and lavatories in both code families, with a cleanout required so the below-flood-level portion can be rodded. Relocating the fixture, leaving the trap unprotected, or double-trapping are not the recognized solution.

questions.question: Under the IPC, what is the minimum fixture supply size for a domestic kitchen sink?

answers.text: 1/2 inch
3/8 inch
3/4 inch
1/4 inch

questions.explanation: The kitchen sink row is 1/2 inch in the IPC minimum fixture supply table (the same value covers laundry trays of one to three compartments). The kitchen sink is not among the five fixtures allowed at 3/8 inch, and 3/4 inch or 1/4 inch appear nowhere for this fixture.

questions.question: An island sink is vented with a loop vent, but the installer omitted the cleanout from the loop piping to save a fitting, arguing the sink's own cleanout plug is enough. What must be added, and why?

answers.text: A second loop vent for redundancy
Nothing; the sink cleanout serves the vent as well
A deeper trap seal to compensate
A cleanout positioned so the below-flood-level portion of the loop vent can be rodded
