questions.explanation: Island loop venting carries a specific extra requirement: a cleanout so the below-flood-level portion of the loop vent — the part waste can reach and foul — can be rodded clear. A drain cleanout at the sink does not give rod access into that vent portion, a duplicate vent is not the requirement, and seal depth has nothing to do with maintaining the loop.

questions.question: Excavation in Type C soil is planned at less than 20 feet deep using sloping alone. What slope is required, and what shaping method is off the table?

answers.text: Slope at 3/4H:1V, and benching is encouraged in Type C soil
Slope at 1H:1V, and benching may replace the slope in Type C soil
Slope at 1-1/2H:1V, and benching is not permitted in Type C soil
Vertical walls are allowed if benching is added in Type C soil

questions.explanation: Type C, the least stable class, requires the flattest slope at 1-1/2H:1V and benching is not permitted in Type C soil. Steeper Type A or B slopes do not protect workers in this soil.

questions.question: A pressure vacuum breaker assembly is installed to protect an irrigation zone under the IPC. How must the assembly be positioned relative to the downstream piping and outlets?

answers.text: Its critical level must be at least 6 inches above the flood-level rim of the highest fixture
Its critical level must be at least 12 inches above all downstream piping and outlets
It may be installed below the highest downstream outlet if a check valve is added
It must be installed between 12 and 60 inches above the floor, measured to its test cocks

questions.explanation: Pressure vacuum breaker (and spill-resistant vacuum breaker) assemblies must sit with the critical level at least 12 inches above all downstream piping and outlets, because the breaker only works if downstream water can never rise into it. The 6-inch figure is the flood-rim rule for vacuum breakers generally, installing the assembly below a downstream outlet defeats it entirely, and the 12-to-60-inch band is the general assembly mounting-height rule, not this placement rule.

questions.question: Which conditions must all hold for a licensed contractor to allow a permit to be obtained under the contractor's license?

answers.text: Performance by the contractor or its employees, general supervision by the contractor or a properly licensed technician until completion, an executed contract held by the contractor with the licensed GC or owner, and all payments received by the contractor

The property owner signs a waiver accepting the arrangement; the general contractor posts a payment bond for the job; the permit fee is paid in cash at the permit counter; the contractor visits the site at least once before completion; and the qualifier countersigns the application
The job lasts fewer than five days; the crew has worked for the contractor on earlier jobs; the owner is a repeat customer; and the contractor is notified before the permit is pulled
The contractor visits the site monthly; the subcontractor carries its own insurance; the payments are split evenly between them; and the permit is pulled in the subcontractor's trade name

questions.explanation: All four conditions must hold together: performance by the contractor or the contractor's employees, general supervision by the contractor or a properly licensed technician until completion, an executed contract held by the contractor with the licensed general contractor or property owner, and receipt by the contractor of all contractual payments. Waivers and bonds, job length and familiarity, or monthly visits with split payments are not the stated conditions.

questions.question: A master plumber is checking the load on a branch that collects a private 1.6 gpf water closet, a bathtub, and a lavatory before joining the stack. What total should the check show?

answers.text: 6 DFU
5 DFU
8 DFU
3 DFU

questions.explanation: Add the shared private-use values: water closet 3 DFU + bathtub 2 DFU + lavatory 1 DFU = 6 DFU. A total of 5 DFU drops one fixture's share, 8 DFU overstates the group, and 3 DFU counts the water closet alone.

questions.question: A small non-pneumatic ejector discharges only 10 gpm. What does the sump-vent table say about the maximum developed length of its vent, at any listed vent size?

answers.text: The limit is 72 feet for every size
The limit is 25 feet for every size
The vent is limited to 100 feet regardless of size
There is no limit at that discharge — every listed vent size shows no limit, meaning lengths greater than 500 feet

questions.explanation: At 10 gpm the table lists no limit for every vent size — the table's own note explains that no limit means the actual allowable values exceed 500 feet. The 72-foot and 25-foot figures are cells from higher-discharge rows, and no flat 100-foot cap appears in this table.

questions.question: An indirect waste receptor with a 2-inch trap receives fixtures whose drainage loads total 7 DFU. What load is assigned to the receptor itself for sizing the drain it discharges into?

answers.text: 3 DFU
2 DFU
10 DFU
7 DFU

questions.explanation: A receptor's load is the sum of the fixture loads discharging to it, but not less than the receptor's own value. By trap size a 2-inch trap is worth 3 DFU, and the 7 DFU inflow is greater, so the inflow sum governs at 7 DFU. The 3 DFU answer stops at the receptor's own value and ignores the greater inflow, while 10 DFU double-counts by adding the inflow and the receptor value together.

questions.question: A transit-center restroom uses flush-valve water closets, and the value-engineering list proposes trimming their supplies to match the 1/2-inch branches used elsewhere. Why must that line item be rejected?

answers.text: A flush-valve water closet requires a 1-inch minimum supply, larger than the ordinary fixture branches
Flush-valve closets may use any size as long as the valve is listed
The trim is fine because flush valves meter their own flow
A flush-valve closet needs a 2-inch supply, so both sizes fail

questions.explanation: The flushometer-valve water closet is the shared table's 1-inch-minimum fixture, reflecting the valve's high instantaneous demand. It cannot be trimmed to the smaller branch sizes used for tubs and sinks, and its minimum is 1 inch — not 2 inches.

questions.question: Back-to-back water closets are to connect to a double sanitary tee, with 20 inches of horizontal developed length between each closet outlet and the double-tee connection. What is the IPC position?

answers.text: It is prohibited in all cases under the IPC
It is permitted only if the length is 12 inches or less
It is permitted only for fixtures without pumping action, and water closets never qualify
The connection is permitted, because the general bar on double sanitary tees receiving back-to-back water closets has an exception where that horizontal developed length is 18 inches or greater

questions.explanation: The IPC bars double sanitary tee patterns from receiving back-to-back water closets and pumping-action fixtures, but expressly excepts back-to-back closets where the horizontal developed length from outlet to the double-tee connection is 18 inches or more — 20 inches qualifies. Treating the bar as absolute, or reversing the length condition, misses the exception.

questions.question: A homeowner asks a Restricted Limited Plumbing Contractor to install a water filtration system on the home's water distribution line. Is that work within the restricted license?

answers.text: Yes — water filtration systems or components installed on a water distribution line or water service piping are within the restricted license
No — filtration work is reserved to Class I contractors because it touches potable water and serves the home's drinking water supply
No — the restricted license covers exterior piping only and never any filtration equipment installed on any line
Yes, but only if the contractor also replaces the home's water heater during the same visit as part of the same job

questions.explanation: Water filtration systems or components installed on a water distribution line or water service piping are expressly within the Restricted Limited Plumbing Contractor's authority. Filtration work on those lines is not reserved to Class I, the restricted license is not limited to exterior piping in a way that excludes filtration, and no water heater replacement is required to make filtration work permissible.

questions.question: A contractor proposes a double-check valve assembly on a cross-connection classified as a high health hazard, arguing that its two checks protect against both kinds of backflow. How must the reviewer respond?

answers.text: Reject it — a double-check assembly may never be used on a high-hazard cross-connection
Approve it, because protection against both mechanisms is the only criterion
Approve it if the assembly is tested twice a year instead of once
Approve it if a strainer is installed ahead of the assembly

questions.explanation: Mechanism coverage is not the only criterion: a double-check valve assembly is approved for low (non-health) hazard only and may never protect a high-hazard connection, where a reduced-pressure assembly or an air gap is required. Extra testing or a strainer does not raise its hazard approval.

questions.question: A heater's cold-water feed passes first through a check valve and then through a pressure-reducing valve. The expansion tank is teed into the feed between the check valve and the PRV. What is wrong?

answers.text: Nothing is wrong, provided the expansion tank is on the cold-water pipe somewhere between the water service entrance and the heater itself
The device must be moved to the hot-water outlet pipe, where the expanded water actually collects during each heating cycle of the storage tank
The expansion-control device must connect downstream of all check valves, pressure-reducing valves and backflow preventers in the feed
The device must be moved upstream of the check valve, so that it remains on the street side of every device installed in the heater feed line

questions.explanation: The expansion-control device must connect to the cold-water supply pipe downstream of all check valves, PRVs and backflow preventers, so it can absorb expansion from the heater without a device isolating it. Teeing in between the check valve and the PRV leaves the PRV between the tank and the heater; the hot outlet and the upstream side of the check valve are both wrong locations.

questions.question: A full tank contains 35 cubic feet of water. Approximately how much does the water alone weigh?
questions.explanation: Weight = 35 × 62.4 = 2,184 lb. The 261.8 lb option is the gallon count (35 × 7.48) mistaken for pounds, 291.6 lb multiplies cubic feet by the per-gallon weight (35 × 8.33) without converting units, and 4,368 lb doubles the correct weight.

questions.question: A roof of 5,000 square feet is in an area with a design rainfall rate of 4 inches per hour. Using the IPC rainfall conversion, what flow must the storm system handle?

answers.text: 104 gallons per minute
312 gallons per minute
208 gallons per minute
500 gallons per minute

questions.explanation: Flow = R x A x 0.0104 = 4 x 5,000 x 0.0104 = 208 gpm. Halving the factor gives 104 gpm, using 0.0156 gives 312 gpm, and 500 gpm would require roughly 12,000 square feet at this rainfall rate.

questions.question: A basement lavatory and shower sit below the next upstream manhole-cover elevation, while the same project's ground-floor fixtures sit above it and share the designer's proposed single valved drain. What must change?

answers.text: Nothing; one valve on the shared drain protects everything
Separate the flows: the basement branch discharges through a backwater valve, and the ground-floor fixtures discharge without passing through a backwater valve
Remove the valve and protect the basement with a check valve in each fixture trap
Raise the manhole cover so both floors are above it

questions.explanation: The basement fixtures, being below the manhole-cover elevation, require backwater-valve protection in the drain or branch serving them, while the ground-floor fixtures above that elevation must not discharge through a backwater valve. A single shared valved drain cannot satisfy both rules at once, so the flows must be separated; fixture traps are not a substitute for the required valve.

ohio-plumbing.quiz_title: Ohio Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A crew is setting a 6-inch horizontal building drain across a parking-lot trench. What minimum slope must they hold?

answers.text: 1/4 inch per foot
1/16 inch per foot
1/8 inch per foot
No slope is needed at this size

questions.explanation: Pipe 4 inches through 6 inches requires at least 1/8 inch per foot, about a 1% grade. The 1/4-inch rate applies to pipe 2-1/2 inches and smaller, 1/16 inch per foot is reserved for 8-inch and larger pipe, and a level drain would not move waste by gravity at all.

questions.question: What drainage load may a 4-inch building sewer carry when it is laid at 1/4 inch per foot?

answers.text: 180 DFU
216 DFU
250 DFU
160 DFU

questions.explanation: A 4-inch building drain or sewer at 1/4 inch per foot carries 216 DFU. The 180 DFU figure is its capacity at 1/8 inch per foot and 250 DFU at 1/2 inch per foot, while 160 DFU is the 4-inch horizontal fixture branch limit from the companion table.

questions.question: An over-rim bath filler with a 1-inch effective opening is installed with a single wall 2-1/2 inches from the outlet. What is the minimum required air gap?

answers.text: 2 in.
3 in.
4 in.

questions.explanation: First decide which column governs: a wall is close to the outlet when it lies within three times the opening diameter, and 3 x 1 = 3 inches, so a wall 2-1/2 inches away is close. Over-rim bath fillers and fixtures with openings up to 1 inch require 3 inches close to a wall. The 2-inch answer is the away-from-wall value for the same row, which would govern only if the wall were more than 3 inches away.

questions.question: A 2-1/2-inch horizontal drain is the largest small-size pipe on a cottage job. What minimum grade does it require?

answers.text: 1/4 inch per foot
1/8 inch per foot
1/16 inch per foot
Level is acceptable under 10 feet

questions.explanation: Pipe 2-1/2 inches and smaller sits in the 1/4-inch-per-foot group — the 2-1/2-inch size is the top of that group, not the bottom of the next one. The 1/8-inch rate starts at 4 inches, the 1/16-inch rate at 8 inches, and no horizontal drainage run is permitted dead level.

questions.question: A gravity water-closet flush tank needs its antisiphon protection identified on a plan. Which device row applies, and what are its limits?

answers.text: ASSE 1002 antisiphon fill valve; high hazard, backsiphonage only
ASSE 1011 hose-connection vacuum breaker; high hazard, backpressure or backsiphonage
ASSE 1024 dual check; low hazard, backpressure only
ASSE 1001 pipe-applied vacuum breaker; low hazard only

questions.explanation: The antisiphon fill valve for gravity flush tanks is the ASSE 1002 device, rated high hazard for backsiphonage only — it lives inside the tank and works by keeping the fill outlet above the water line, so it offers no backpressure protection. The other standards name hose, dual-check and pipe-applied devices with different ratings.

questions.question: A wall-hung fixture is mounted high for accessibility, and its trap ends up with a vertical outlet-to-weir distance of exactly 24 inches. A helper worries any distance over 18 inches fails. What is the correct call?

answers.text: It fails; 18 inches is the maximum vertical distance, and the fixture must be lowered until its trap sits within that distance
It fails; the distance must be kept under 12 inches, because any longer drop lets the discharge fall fast enough to harm the trap
It complies only if the trap seal is deepened past 4 inches to give the longer drop a larger reserve of water to work against
It complies; 24 inches is the maximum permitted vertical distance from fixture outlet to trap weir

questions.explanation: The limit is a maximum of 24 inches measured vertically from the fixture outlet to the trap weir, so a distance of exactly 24 inches complies. Neither 18 inches nor 12 inches is the stated maximum, and deepening a seal past the 4-inch maximum would create a second violation rather than cure one.

questions.question: Which fixture must discharge indirectly - through an air gap into a trapped, vented receptor - rather than by a direct connection to the sanitary drain?

answers.text: A water closet
A bathroom lavatory
A bathtub
A commercial ice machine

questions.explanation: Equipment handling potable water and food products - ice machines, beverage equipment, and food-preparation sinks - carries a contamination concern that requires indirect discharge through an air gap. Ordinary plumbing fixtures such as water closets, lavatories, and tubs connect directly to the sanitary system through their traps.

questions.question: Even at its best, street pressure at a hilltop building cannot deliver the flow pressures the fixture-outlet table requires. What must the design include?

answers.text: A larger water meter only
Oversized fixture supplies throughout
A pressure-reducing valve
A booster system

questions.explanation: Where street pressure cannot deliver the required flow pressures, a booster system is required. A pressure-reducing valve lowers pressure further, and a larger meter or larger fixture supplies cannot create pressure the street does not provide.

questions.question: How many contracting companies may hold an individual's assigned license for the same type of contracting at one time?

answers.text: Up to two, if the individual works for both companies
Only one
Up to three, with notice to the specialty section
An unlimited number, provided each company carries insurance

questions.explanation: A license may be assigned to only one contracting company at a time. Working for two companies, notifying the section, or having each company insured does not permit a second simultaneous assignment for the same type of contracting.

questions.question: What governs welding and brazing of metallic building services piping, including medical gas, that the Ohio plumbing code references?

answers.text: The installing contractor's own written welding procedure, filed with the building department for the project
The piping manufacturer's recommendations alone, which Ohio adopts as the sole governing requirement for the work
A section of the Ohio Revised Code that Ohio's plumbing code points to for that welding and brazing work
The model code's general workmanship language, because Ohio added no specific provision for welding or brazing

questions.explanation: Ohio provides that welding and brazing of metallic building services piping systems referenced by the plumbing code, including medical gas, is governed by the Revised Code section it names for that work. Contractor procedures and manufacturer recommendations do not replace that governing provision, and Ohio did add a specific provision.

questions.question: A 3-inch trap under the IPC is vented with the trap arm sloped at 1/8 inch per foot. What maximum trap-to-vent distance does the table allow?

answers.text: 8 feet
6 feet
16 feet
12 feet

questions.explanation: A 3-inch trap at 1/8 inch per foot may run 12 feet to the vent. Eight feet is the 2-inch limit at a steeper slope, 6 feet is for 1-1/2 inch, and 16 feet is reserved for a 4-inch trap.

questions.question: A fixture with a 1-1/4-inch trap has its vent fitting 6 feet from the trap weir, with the fixture drain graded at 1/4 inch per foot. Which single change brings the installation into compliance?

answers.text: Move the vent fitting to 4 ft from the trap weir and steepen the grade to 1/2 in. per foot
Move the vent fitting to 5 ft from the trap weir and keep the 1/4-in.-per-foot grade
Increase the fixture drain to 1-1/2 in., move the vent fitting to 6-1/2 ft, and keep the 1/4-in.-per-foot grade
Keep the 6-ft run and flatten the grade to 1/8 in. per foot

questions.explanation: For a 1-1/4-inch trap the vent fitting must be within 5 feet, and at 5 feet the total fall is 5 x 0.25 = 1.25 inches, exactly the drain diameter, so moving the vent to 5 feet complies on both checks. Steepening to 1/2 inch per foot at 4 feet gives a fall of 2 inches, exceeding the 1-1/4-inch diameter. The enlarged 1-1/2-inch drain allows only 6 feet, so 6-1/2 feet still fails on distance. Flattening to 1/8 inch per foot drops below the 1/4-inch-per-foot minimum slope for pipe of this size and is not a listed grade for this trap in the distance table.

questions.question: A heater's controls fail in the heating position overnight and the water temperature climbs steadily. At what temperature will a standard T&P relief valve open on temperature to protect the tank?

answers.text: 180 degrees Fahrenheit
210 degrees Fahrenheit
150 degrees Fahrenheit
250 degrees Fahrenheit

questions.explanation: The standard T&P temperature setting is 210°F, just below boiling at atmospheric pressure, so the valve opens before the tank's water can flash to steam. Settings of 150°F and 180°F are far too low, and waiting until 250°F would defeat the valve's purpose.

questions.question: A horizontal wet vent is roughed in so that its dry vent is taken from the drain of an emergency floor drain in the bathroom group, the only fixture the installer left near the vent stack. What must change?

answers.text: Nothing — an emergency floor drain is the preferred dry-vent fixture
The dry vent must instead be an individual or common vent for a bathroom group fixture other than an emergency floor drain
The emergency floor drain must be removed from the group entirely
A second dry vent must be added at the downstream end to balance the first

questions.explanation: For a horizontal wet vent, the dry-vent connection must come through an individual or common vent serving a bathroom group fixture — with the emergency floor drain expressly excepted from that role. The floor drain may remain in the group; what has to move is which fixture's vent supplies the dry vent, and a second downstream vent is not the remedy.

questions.question: An approved applicant neither obtains the background check nor takes the examination within a year of approval. What happens?

answers.text: The approval remains valid indefinitely, because approvals do not expire once granted
The approval is no longer valid and the applicant must reapply
The applicant may sit for the examination but must obtain the background check within 30 days afterward
The applicant's application fee is converted into a credit that keeps the approval open for a second year

questions.explanation: Approval is valid for one year; an approved applicant who has not obtained the background check or taken the examination within that year must reapply. Approvals do expire, so indefinite validity is wrong. The background check must come before sitting, not after. No fee-credit mechanism extends the approval into a second year.

questions.question: A master plumber is setting terminal heights on a mixed-use building. One vent exits a storage building's plain weather roof; another exits the roof of a dining pavilion whose roof is an occupied deck. Which pair of minimum heights is correct?

answers.text: 7 feet for both roofs
6 inches for the weather roof, and 7 feet for the occupied-deck roof
6 inches for both roofs
7 feet for the weather roof, and 6 inches for the occupied deck

questions.explanation: Terminal height follows roof use: at least 6 inches above a roof that serves only as weather protection, and at least 7 feet above a roof used for another purpose, such as an occupied deck, so people are not breathing vent gas at head height. Applying either single height to both roofs gets one of the two wrong, and swapping them gets both wrong.

questions.question: A relief valve discharges in a mechanical room next door to the room where its water heater sits, with the pipe passing through the wall to reach a floor drain there. How does the IPC treat this?

answers.text: It is permitted if the pipe is increased one size where it passes through the wall
It is permitted if the floor drain in the next room is trapped and vented
It is permitted if the termination in the next room is readily observable
It is not permitted; the discharge must pass through an air gap in the same room as the water heater

questions.explanation: IPC discharge piping must discharge through an air gap in the same room as the water heater. A trapped-and-vented receptor, an upsized wall penetration, or an observable termination in another room does not satisfy the same-room air-gap rule.

questions.question: Using the Hunter's flush-tank reference points of 43.5 gpm at 100 WSFU and 65 gpm at 200 WSFU, by approximately what percent does probable demand rise when the WSFU total doubles from 100 to 200?
questions.explanation: Percent increase = (65 − 43.5) ÷ 43.5 × 100 = 21.5 ÷ 43.5 × 100 ≈ 49%. Demand does not rise 100% — Hunter's curve flattens because simultaneous use becomes less likely as fixture count grows.

questions.question: After computing roof runoff with the rainfall conversion equation, what else must the designer check before finalizing the storm drain size?

answers.text: The flow must be converted to drainage fixture units and checked in the sanitary tables
The calculated flow must also be checked against the roof drain manufacturer's published flow rate for the specific drain model and size
The flow must be checked against the gutter table before any drain is sized
The flow must be doubled as a safety factor before the tables are entered

questions.explanation: In addition to the equation result, the IPC requires the flow to be checked against the roof drain manufacturer's published flow rate for the specific model and size, since the drain itself can be the bottleneck. Storm flow is never converted to DFU, no doubling factor is prescribed, and gutter sizing is a separate step that does not replace this check.

questions.question: One floor of a small inn has three bathroom groups with 1.6 gpf water closets on a common branch, along with a domestic kitchen sink, a domestic dishwasher, and a residential clothes washer. What is the total load on that branch?

answers.text: 24 DFU
19 DFU
21 DFU
27 DFU

questions.explanation: Each bathroom group counts at its group value of 5 DFU, and the kitchen sink, dishwasher and residential washer each add 2 DFU. The 24 DFU answer sums the group fixtures individually at 6 DFU per group instead of using the group value.

texas-plumbing.quiz_title: Texas Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A drinking fountain with a refrigerated water cooler is installed in a school corridor. What load and minimum trap go on the schedule?

answers.text: 1 DFU with a 1-1/2-inch trap
0.5 DFU with a 1-1/4-inch trap
2 DFU with a 1-1/2-inch trap
0.5 DFU with a 1-1/2-inch trap

questions.explanation: A drinking fountain / water cooler is 0.5 DFU with a 1-1/4-inch minimum trap. The DFU in the 1- and 2-DFU options belongs to lavatories and tubs/sinks respectively, and pairing the correct 0.5 DFU with a 1-1/2-inch trap overstates the fountain's minimum trap size.

questions.question: Cleanouts on a 5-inch building sewer must be installed at intervals of not more than:

answers.text: 100 feet
200 feet
400 feet
50 feet

questions.explanation: Building sewers smaller than 8 inches require cleanouts at intervals of not more than 100 feet. The 200-foot and 400-foot figures belong to the manhole spacing rules for sewers 8 inches and larger, not to cleanouts on a 5-inch sewer.

questions.question: An over-rim bath filler with a 1-in. effective opening is installed away from any wall. What is the minimum required air gap?

answers.text: 3 in.
1 in.
2 in.

questions.explanation: For over-rim bath fillers and fixtures with effective openings of not more than 1 in., the required air gap away from a wall is 2 in. The 3-in. option is that row's close-to-wall value, which does not apply to this installation. The 1-1/2-in. option is the away-from-wall value for the smaller 3/4-in.-opening row, and the 1-in. option is the lavatory row value.

questions.question: A clothes washer standpipe trap is roughed in 4 inches above the finished floor to gain fall on a tight retrofit. What does the installation require instead?

answers.text: The trap may sit 4 inches above the floor if the standpipe is shortened
The trap may be placed below the floor if a cleanout is provided
The trap roughed in not less than 6 inches and not more than 18 inches above the floor, and never below the floor
The trap must be roughed in at least 18 inches above the floor

questions.explanation: A clothes washer standpipe trap must be roughed in between 6 and 18 inches above the floor and must not be installed below the floor at all, so 4 inches is too low. Shortening the standpipe does not change the trap rule, and no cleanout exception permits a below-floor trap for this receptor.

questions.question: Which of the following locations is on the IPC's list of places where a full-open valve is required?

answers.text: On the supply pipe to every water heater
On the fixture supply to each lavatory
On every hose bibb branch
Inside each flush tank

questions.explanation: A full-open valve is required on the supply pipe to every water heater, one of the eight listed locations (which also include the building service near the curb, the distribution supply at the building entrance, and the discharge side of every meter). Fixture supplies and sillcock supplies take ordinary shutoff valves instead, and no valve is placed inside a flush tank.

questions.question: A vented group of fixtures drains through a long horizontal run in a commercial building, roughed at 240 feet between accessible points. Cleanout planning for that horizontal drain must respect which spacing limit?

answers.text: Cleanouts at least every 50 feet
Cleanouts only at the far end of the run
One cleanout anywhere on the run is enough
Cleanouts no more than 100 feet apart

questions.explanation: Cleanouts on horizontal drains are spaced no more than 100 feet apart, so a 240-foot run needs intermediate cleanouts, not just end access. Fifty feet is stricter than required, and a single cleanout cannot serve the whole run.

questions.question: On a repair, a plumber solvent-welds a new PVC drain fitting directly into an existing ABS hub using ABS cement, and the joint weeps within a week. What went wrong?

answers.text: The cement was the wrong color for a repair
The joint needed primer on the ABS side only
ABS and PVC are not solvent-welded to each other - a listed transition fitting or transition cement is required between the two plastics
ABS and PVC can be welded together, but only with PVC cement

questions.explanation: The two plastics use different cements that are not interchangeable, and ABS is never solvent-welded directly to PVC with either cement. A listed transition fitting or approved transition cement is the correct way to join them; primer and cement color do not fix a cross-plastic weld.

questions.question: A demand-controlled recirculation system is commissioned, and testing shows it is pushing 112-degree F water into the cold-water piping at the far fixtures. What is the verdict?

answers.text: Not acceptable — demand recirculation controls must limit water entering the cold-water piping to 104 degrees F
Acceptable if the pump stops within 5 minutes
Acceptable; demand systems have no temperature limit on the cold side
Not acceptable only if the temperature exceeds 120 degrees F

questions.explanation: Demand-recirculation controls must start the pump on user action, presence or flow sensing and must limit water entering the cold-water piping to 104 degrees F. At 112 degrees F the system exceeds that limit; the 5-minute rule governs pumps circulating between a heater and a storage tank, not this temperature limit.

questions.question: Two fixture vents are to be joined into a common vent overhead. What must happen before they connect?

answers.text: Only the larger of the two vents must reach 6 inches above its fixture's flood-level rim
Each vent must reach 6 inches above its own fixture's flood-level rim before connecting to any other vent
The vents may join at any height if the common vent is one size larger
The vents must join below the fixtures' flood-level rims to equalize pressure

questions.explanation: When vents converge, each one must first reach 6 inches above the flood-level rim of the fixture it serves. Upsizing the common vent does not waive the rise for either vent, and joining below the rims defeats the protection the rise provides.

questions.question: A horizontal drain run totals 101 ft in developed length. How does the spacing rule treat the final 1 ft?

answers.text: It requires a cleanout only if horizontal direction changes are also present somewhere along the same run.
It is ignored; only complete 100-ft segments count toward cleanout spacing, and the extra foot is absorbed by the first segment.
It counts as a fraction requiring its own cleanout coverage; the run needs coverage for two 100-ft segments.
It extends the first segment's allowance to 101 ft, because spacing is measured to the nearest whole segment reached.

questions.explanation: Runs over 100 ft need a cleanout for each 100 ft or fraction thereof, and 101 ft is one full segment plus a fraction. The fraction is never rounded away, and direction change is a separate, additional trigger.

questions.question: A dry vent is being connected to a horizontal drain and then run toward a vent stack. Which set of rules governs that dry vent?

answers.text: It connects below the centerline, may hold condensate, and may offset at flood level
It connects above the centerline of the horizontal drain, is graded to drain back by gravity, and rises at least 6 inches above the flood level rim of the highest fixture vented before offsetting
It connects at the centerline, slopes away from the drain, and rises 2 inches above the rim
It connects above the centerline but may offset horizontally at any height

questions.explanation: A dry vent must join above the drain's centerline so waste cannot enter it, must be graded back to the drainage pipe, and must rise 6 inches above the highest vented fixture's flood rim before offsetting. Connections below the centerline, trapped condensate, and offsets at rim level each break one of those rules.

questions.question: A locker-room building drain at 1/4 inch per foot serves eight public 1.6-gpf water closets, six lavatories and three floor drains. What is the smallest building drain size for the load?

answers.text: 3 in.
5 in.
4 in.

questions.explanation: The load is 8 x 4 + 6 x 1 + 3 x 2 = 44 DFU. A 3-in. drain at 1/4 inch per foot is capped at 42 DFU, so it falls 2 DFU short even though it looks close. A 2-1/2-in. drain carries only 24 DFU. The next size, 4 in., carries 216 DFU and complies. A 5-in. drain complies but is not the smallest permitted size.

questions.question: A facility survey classifies a closed heating loop with no chemical treatment as a low (non-health) hazard, but notes both backsiphonage and backpressure are possible on the makeup connection. Which assembly fits?

answers.text: A reduced-pressure principle assembly is the only assembly that stops backpressure
A pressure vacuum breaker, installed 12 inches above the loop
A double-check valve assembly — it protects against both mechanisms and is approved for low-hazard service
No assembly is needed for low-hazard connections

questions.explanation: The double-check valve assembly's two checks protect against both backsiphonage and backpressure, and its approval limit — low hazard only — matches this connection. A reduced-pressure assembly would also work hydraulically but is not the only choice, a vacuum breaker never protects against backpressure, and low hazard still requires protection.

questions.question: An inspector measures the developed length from a 1-1/4-inch trap weir to its vent fitting at 5 feet 6 inches, with the arm at 1/4 inch per foot. How should this IPC installation be judged?

answers.text: It exceeds the 5-foot maximum and the vent must be moved closer or the layout changed
It complies because trap-arm length is unlimited below 6 feet
It complies because the extra 6 inches is a construction tolerance
It exceeds the limit only if the fixture is a water closet

questions.explanation: A 1-1/4-inch trap is limited to 5 feet, so 5 feet 6 inches is over the maximum by 6 inches. There is no general 6-foot allowance or tolerance that rescues it, and the limit applies to this trapped fixture, not only to water closets.

questions.question: A 6-inch horizontal drain is run at 1/8 inch per foot instead of the standard slope. Applying the required adjustment, what is its maximum permitted load?

answers.text: 720 DFU
576 DFU
640 DFU

questions.explanation: The 6-inch horizontal rating of 720 DFU assumes 1/4 inch per foot; at 1/8 inch per foot it is multiplied by 0.8, giving 576 DFU. The 1,104 DFU figure wrongly reduces the pipe's vertical rating instead.

questions.question: An apprentice enrolled in good standing in a U.S. Department of Labor apprenticeship program asks whether the standard classroom-training hours still apply before testing. What is the rule?

answers.text: The apprentice must complete double the classroom hours because the program is federally run
The apprentice is exempt from the licensing examination but not from classroom training
The apprentice is exempt from the 24-hour and 48-hour classroom training requirement
The exemption begins only after the apprentice has become a journeyman plumber

questions.explanation: An apprentice enrolled in good standing in a Department of Labor apprenticeship program is exempt from the 24-hour and 48-hour classroom training requirement. The exemption concerns classroom training; it does not eliminate the examination, and it applies while the apprentice is in the program rather than only after promotion.

questions.question: A secondary parapet scupper is detailed with a width narrower than the roof drain serving the same roof area, on the theory that the scupper is only a backup. What width is required?

answers.text: The scupper width must be at least half the diameter of that roof drain, because the scupper is a backup device that flows only part of the time
The scupper width is not regulated; only its height of not less than 4 inches is, because width is a roofing detail left to the designer
The scupper width must equal the diameter of that roof drain, so the scupper opening matches the drain's throat size at the parapet
The scupper width must be not less than the circumference of a roof drain sized for the same roof area

questions.explanation: A parapet scupper opening must be not less than 4 inches in height, and its width must be not less than the circumference of a roof drain sized for the same roof area. Width is regulated alongside height, and both the half-diameter and equal-diameter answers fall well short of a full circumference.

questions.question: A cylindrical storage tank is 30 inches in diameter and 48 inches high. Approximately how many gallons does it hold when full?

answers.text: 36.7 gal

questions.explanation: Radius = 15 in. Volume = π × 15² × 48 = 33,929 cu in. Gallons = 33,929 ÷ 231 = 146.9 gal. Using the diameter (30 in.) as the radius quadruples the result to about 587.5 gal, halving the radius gives 36.7 gal, and 33,929 gal forgets the cubic-inch conversion.

questions.question: Two water heaters on the third floor share a single cold-water shutoff valve located in the basement. Each heater is replaced one at a time, and the crew wants to keep the shared basement valve. What is required?

answers.text: One shared valve is acceptable if it is a full-open valve, is located where it can be reached quickly, and shuts off both heaters at the same time
One shared valve is acceptable if it is labeled for both heaters and a second valve is provided on the hot-water outlet of each heater
Each heater must have its own valve on its cold-water branch, near that heater, on the same floor level, serving only that heater
Each heater needs its own valve, but the valves may be grouped together on any floor of the building if access to them is provided

questions.explanation: The cold-water branch to each heater or storage tank must have a valve near the equipment, serving only that equipment, with access on the same floor level as the heater. A shared basement valve fails the near-equipment, single-equipment, and same-floor conditions at once, whether or not it is full-open or labeled.

questions.question: A bathroom group built around a water closet flushing more than 1.6 gpf also has a bidet installed as an extra fixture beyond the group's fixtures. What is the total load for the group plus the added bidet?

answers.text: 7 DFU
6 DFU
8 DFU
5 DFU

questions.explanation: The group counts 6 DFU because its water closet flushes more than 1.6 gpf, and a fixture added to a bathroom group is added at its own value, so the bidet adds 1 DFU. The 6 DFU answer forgets the bidet, while 8 DFU comes from summing the group's fixtures individually (4 + 1 + 2 = 7) and then adding the bidet instead of using the group value.

virginia-plumbing.quiz_title: Virginia Plumbing Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A trainee assumes a lavatory rated at 1 DFU must be discharging exactly 1 gallon per minute whenever it runs. Why is that reading wrong?

answers.text: A DFU is a fixed meter reading taken at the fixture outlet
A DFU is a probability-based design factor that accounts for discharge rate, volume and duration, and how often the fixture is used
A DFU is the average flow measured over a full 24-hour day
A DFU only describes cold-water supply, not drainage

questions.explanation: A DFU is not a direct flow rate. It is Hunter's probability-based load factor built from how much a fixture discharges, for how long, and how often — which is why DFU totals predict probable peak load rather than adding up running flows. A fixed outlet reading (A), a 24-hour average (C), and a supply-only definition (D) all miss that probabilistic design purpose.

questions.question: A bidet installed in a residence is assigned what drainage fixture unit value?

answers.text: 2 DFU
0.5 DFU
3 DFU
1 DFU

questions.explanation: A bidet is rated 1 DFU, the same as a lavatory. It is not rated 2 DFU like a bathtub or sink, and the half-unit rating belongs to fixtures such as a drinking fountain.

questions.question: A lavatory faucet with a 1/2-in. effective opening is installed well away from any wall, farther than the close-to-wall distance. What is the minimum required air gap?

answers.text: 1 in.

questions.explanation: For lavatories and fixtures with effective openings of not more than 1/2 in., the required air gap away from a wall is 1 in. The 1-1/2-in. option is that row's close-to-wall value, which does not apply at this distance. The 2-1/2-in. option is the close-to-wall value for sinks with larger openings, and the 1/2-in. option merely repeats the opening size, which is not the gap for any row covering this fixture.

questions.question: A laundry tray in a basement utility room is roughed in last and left on a 3/8-inch branch. What minimum supply does a laundry tray require?

answers.text: 1/2 inch
3/8 inch
1 inch
3/4 inch

questions.explanation: A laundry tray requires a minimum 1/2-inch fixture supply, so the 3/8-inch branch must be upsized. The larger sizes offered are permissible pipe but are not the minimum the rule states.

questions.question: A designer is checking required outlet capacity for lavatories under the IPC. How do the private and public lavatory rows differ?

answers.text: Private lavatory: 0.4 gpm at 8 psi; public lavatory: 0.8 gpm at 8 psi
Private lavatory: 0.8 gpm at 8 psi; public lavatory: 0.4 gpm at 8 psi
Both require 0.8 gpm at 8 psi
Both require 0.5 gpm at 60 psi

questions.explanation: The capacity table gives the private lavatory 0.8 gpm at 8 psi and the public lavatory — typically a metering or self-closing faucet — only 0.4 gpm at 8 psi. Reversing the two values misstates both rows, the 'both 0.8' answer erases the public reduction, and 0.5 gpm at 60 psi is a maximum-consumption figure for a public lavatory faucet, not a required-capacity row.

questions.question: An island sink is vented with a loop vent, but the installer omitted the cleanout from the loop piping to save a fitting, arguing the sink's own cleanout plug is enough. What must be added, and why?

answers.text: A second loop vent for redundancy
Nothing; the sink cleanout serves the vent as well
A deeper trap seal to compensate
A cleanout positioned so the below-flood-level portion of the loop vent can be rodded

questions.explanation: Island loop venting carries a specific extra requirement: a cleanout so the below-flood-level portion of the loop vent — the part waste can reach and foul — can be rodded clear. A drain cleanout at the sink does not give rod access into that vent portion, a duplicate vent is not the requirement, and seal depth has nothing to do with maintaining the loop.

questions.question: Occupants report a loud bang and shaking pipes every time a single-lever washing machine shuts off at the end of fill. What phenomenon best explains the complaint?

answers.text: Water hammer, a pressure surge created when moving water is stopped suddenly by a quick-closing valve
Thermal expansion in a closed system slowly raising static pressure
A partially closed stop valve causing continuous low flow noise
Air trapped in a drain causing gurgling at fixtures

questions.explanation: Water hammer is the shock wave from suddenly stopping moving water, typical of quick-closing washer valves, and its surge can be many times normal pressure. Thermal expansion is gradual, and drain gurgling is a venting symptom, not a supply bang.

questions.question: A pump circulates water between a water heater and its storage tank. The heating cycle ends, but the pump is still running 12 minutes later. What requirement has been violated?

answers.text: None; heater-to-tank pumps run continuously
The pump must stop not more than 30 minutes after the heating cycle ends
The pump must stop not more than 5 minutes after the heating cycle ends
The pump must run at least 10 minutes after the cycle to prevent stagnation

questions.explanation: Pumps circulating between the heater and the storage tank must stop not more than 5 minutes after the heating cycle ends. Twelve minutes of overrun exceeds that limit; continuous running and a 30-minute allowance are not the rule.

questions.question: Grade stakes for a 96-foot run of 8-inch building sewer are set at minimum slope. What elevation difference should appear between the first and last stakes?

answers.text: 24 inches
12 inches
6 inches
96 inches

questions.explanation: Pipe 8 inches and larger grades at a minimum of 1/16 inch per foot, so 96 feet falls 6 inches. Twelve inches would be the fall at 1/8 inch per foot and 24 inches at 1/4 inch per foot — both rates for smaller pipe.

questions.question: Site conditions keep a vent terminal 8 feet horizontally from a dormer window, so the installer raises it until it ends 3 feet above the top of that window. Is the placement acceptable?

answers.text: No; a terminal must always be a full 10 feet away with no alternative
Yes; ending at least 3 feet above the top of the opening is the allowed alternative to 10 feet horizontal
No; it must also be 7 feet above the roof in every case
Yes, but only if the window is fixed shut afterwards

questions.explanation: The rule offers two ways to comply: 10 feet horizontally, or at least 3 feet above the top of the opening; the raised terminal uses the second. The 7-foot height applies to roofs used for other purposes, not to every terminal, and the window need not be sealed.

questions.question: A designer proposes a 3-inch single-stack vent system for a stack that will be 80 feet tall. What does the table say about that proposal?

answers.text: It is permitted with a maximum load of 24 DFU
It is permitted with a maximum load of 225 DFU
A 3-inch stack is not permitted at that height — its only allowance, 24 DFU, applies to stacks under 75 feet
It is permitted if it serves no water closets

questions.explanation: The 3-inch single-stack row has a value in only one band — 24 DFU for stacks under 75 feet — and is not permitted in either taller band, so an 80-foot stack cannot use this size at all. Neither the short-band load nor a water-closet restriction rescues a size the table excludes at that height.

questions.question: A building drain with no water closets, laid at 1/4 inch per foot, receives a continuous pump discharge of 10 gpm plus two general floor drains. What is the smallest building drain size for the load?

answers.text: 2 in.
3 in.

questions.explanation: Continuous flow converts at 2 DFU per gpm, so 10 gpm = 20 DFU, and the two floor drains add 2 x 2 = 4 DFU, for 24 DFU total. At 1/4 inch per foot a 2-in. drain carries only 21 DFU and a 1-1/2-in. drain only 3 DFU, so both fail. A 2-1/2-in. drain carries exactly 24 DFU and complies; because no water closet is served, the 3-in. minimum for water-closet drains does not apply. A 3-in. drain complies but is not the smallest.

questions.question: A turf irrigation zone has no pump or elevated storage downstream, so the only backflow mechanism possible is a supply-side vacuum during a main break. Which devices are legitimate candidates for this connection?

answers.text: A pressure vacuum breaker or an atmospheric vacuum breaker — both protect against backsiphonage, which is the only mechanism present
Only a reduced-pressure assembly may protect any irrigation system
A double-check assembly is the only choice because it is testable
No protection is needed where only backsiphonage is possible

questions.explanation: Where backsiphonage is genuinely the only mechanism, the vacuum breakers — PVB and AVB — are legitimate candidates, subject to their own installation limits. Testable assemblies also protect here but are not the only choices, and backsiphonage-only connections still require protection.

questions.question: An air admittance valve is sealed inside a finished wall cavity with no access opening, in a spot where almost no air can reach the valve. Which requirements does that installation violate?

answers.text: Only the access requirement; a valve needs no air supply because it is sealed
Neither — a valve inside a wall is protected and needs no access
Only the air-entry requirement; concealed valves never need access
Both of them — access must be provided to every air admittance valve, and the valve must be installed where air can enter it

questions.explanation: An air admittance valve is a maintainable device that works by admitting air, so the code demands both an access path to every valve and a location where air can actually enter it. A sealed, air-starved wall cavity fails on both counts — the valve can neither breathe nor be serviced or replaced.

questions.question: A helper performs electrical tasks while supervised by a tradesman who is licensed only as a plumber. Why does the supervision situation not fit here?

answers.text: Because a helper is never permitted to perform work connected with more than one trade during the course of a single project under any circumstances at all
Because the situation requires the helper to be a family member of the supervisor or to have worked for the same employing firm for a set minimum period of time
Because the situation rests on supervision by a tradesman licensed in the specialty for which the work is being performed, and a plumbing license is not the electrical specialty
Because the situation applies only to work performed on floating vessels and on single-family residences, and not to supervised trade work performed inside other buildings

questions.explanation: C is correct because the supervised individual is outside personal licensure only when working under a tradesman licensed in the specialty for which the work is being performed, and electrical work requires an electrically licensed supervisor for that fit. A is wrong because the problem is the supervisor's specialty, not a ban on helpers touching more than one trade. B is wrong because no family or length-of-employment condition is part of this rule. D is wrong because the vessel and small-residence provisions are separate exclusions, not the supervision rule.

questions.question: A mixing valve blends 150 °F hot water with 50 °F cold water to deliver 110 °F water, and 60 gallons of mixed water are needed. How many gallons of hot water are required?

answers.text: 24 gal
30 gal
36 gal
45 gal

questions.explanation: Hot fraction = (110 − 50) ÷ (150 − 50) = 60/100 = 0.60, so hot water = 0.60 × 60 = 36 gal. The 24 gal option is the cold-water share (0.40 × 60), and 30 gal assumes a 50/50 blend.

questions.question: A relief valve is piped onto the hot-water outlet line about a foot away from a storage tank, where the water it senses has already left the tank. What installation rule does this miss?

answers.text: The relief valve must be installed on the cold-water inlet instead, where it can sense the pressure of the incoming supply water
The relief valve must be installed at the lowest point of the tank, where pressure is greatest when the tank is full of water
The relief valve must be installed downstream of a shutoff valve for servicing, on a branch off the hot-water outlet line near the tank, and identified with a tag
The relief valve must be installed in the shell of the tank, with its temperature element actuated by water in the top 6 inches of the tank

questions.explanation: Relief valves are installed in the shell of the tank, and the temperature element must be actuated by water in the top 6 inches, where the hottest water collects. Piping the valve onto the outlet line moves the sensing element away from that water; the cold inlet and the bottom of the tank are colder still, and no shutoff may be placed between the valve and the tank in any case.

questions.question: A rolling offset in a parking-garage ceiling must shift 12 inches sideways and 16 inches up, using 45° fittings. Each fitting has a take-out of 2.25 inches. What is the cut length of the travel piece?
questions.explanation: True offset = √(12² + 16²) = √400 = 20 in. Travel = 20 × 1.414 = 28.28 in. Cut length = 28.28 − (2 × 2.25) = 28.28 − 4.50 = 23.78 in. The 28.28 in. option forgets both take-outs, 26.03 in. deducts only one, and 33.78 in. adds the take-outs instead of subtracting them.

questions.question: A roof of 5,000 square feet is in an area with a design rainfall rate of 4 inches per hour. Using the IPC rainfall conversion, what flow must the storm system handle?

answers.text: 104 gallons per minute
312 gallons per minute
208 gallons per minute
500 gallons per minute

questions.explanation: Flow = R x A x 0.0104 = 4 x 5,000 x 0.0104 = 208 gpm. Halving the factor gives 104 gpm, using 0.0156 gives 312 gpm, and 500 gpm would require roughly 12,000 square feet at this rainfall rate.

questions.question: In a hotel, the fixtures on each of five floors total 180 DFU, and all five floors drain into a single stack. Determine the smallest stack size that respects both the limit on any one floor's discharge into the stack and the limit on the whole stack's load.

answers.text: 4 inches
5 inches
6 inches
8 inches

questions.explanation: The total load is 900 DFU. A 4-inch stack fails both checks, allowing only 90 DFU per interval and 500 DFU total over more than three intervals. A 5-inch stack allows 200 DFU per interval and 1,100 DFU total, so it satisfies both; 6 and 8 inches work but are not the smallest.

maryland-hvac-master-restricted.quiz_title: Maryland HVAC Master Restricted Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An oil-fired furnace rumbles and puffs soot at startup, then settles into steady operation. Which condition best explains this delayed-ignition complaint pattern?

answers.text: The burner is firing with too much excess air, so the flame lifts off the nozzle and lights only after a long delay
The fuel pump is delivering oil at a pressure far above its rating, flooding the chamber on every start attempt
Oil is spraying into the chamber before the ignition arc is established, so accumulated oil lights off all at once
The draft regulator is stuck fully open, so the chamber cools between cycles and the oil cannot vaporize at start

questions.explanation: C is correct: delayed ignition occurs when oil sprays before the spark is present or effective, letting unburned oil accumulate and then ignite as a puffback. A is wrong: excess air causes flame lift and noise during running, not an accumulation-and-puff at startup. B is wrong: excessive pump pressure over-fires the burner and is not the classic delayed-ignition sequence. D is wrong: an open regulator weakens draft and affects running combustion, not the timing of ignition at start.

questions.question: The Board is weighing an applicant's prior conviction. Which set lists the considerations the Board applies?

answers.text: The nature of the crime, its relationship to the licensed activities, its relevance to fitness, the time since conviction, and the applicant's behavior before and after
The applicant's credit history, current employment status, years of trade experience, examination score, and standing with former employers in the trade
The county where the conviction occurred, the size of the fine imposed, the applicant's age at the time, and whether the case received local publicity
Whether the applicant completed a prep course, holds other state licenses, owns a business, and can post the required insurance before the hearing date

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Board considers the nature of the crime, its relationship to the licensed activities, its relevance to the applicant's fitness and qualification, the time elapsed since the conviction, and the applicant's behavior before and after the conviction. B is wrong: credit history, exam score, and employer standing are not among the conviction factors. C is wrong: fine size and publicity are not among the stated factors. D is wrong: prep courses and out-of-state licenses are not among the conviction factors.

questions.question: A residential hot-water boiler is fitted with a pressure relief valve at the factory. At what pressure is that valve typically set to open and protect the boiler?

answers.text: The valve is set to open at 15 psi, relieving the boiler well before a standard fill valve can raise system pressure
The valve is set to open at 50 psi, giving the circulator full head room before any relief of the system can occur
The valve is set to open at 30 psi, the standard residential hot-water boiler relief setting for this equipment class
The valve is set to open at 125 psi, matching the test pressure stamped on the boiler pressure vessel data plate

questions.explanation: C is correct: residential hot-water boilers carry a pressure relief valve set at 30 psi, which stands above normal fill and operating pressures and below the vessel rating. A is wrong: 15 psi is near a typical fill pressure and would weep in normal operation. B is wrong: 50 psi exceeds the standard residential relief setting for this class of boiler. D is wrong: vessel test pressure is a manufacturing figure and is far above any working relief setting.

questions.question: A single-pipe oil system runs its tank dry. After the tank is refilled, the burner starts, runs briefly, and locks out without firing. What is the correct service step?

answers.text: Replace the nozzle first, since running dry always destroys the nozzle's spray pattern
Replace the ignition transformer, since a dry run overheats and ruins the ignition system
Convert the installation to a two-pipe system, since a single-pipe system can never be restarted after a dry run
Bleed the air from the fuel pump at its bleeder fitting until a clear, foam-free stream of oil flows

questions.explanation: D is correct: a single-pipe system that has run dry draws air into the suction line and pump, and the pump cannot lift oil until that air is bled at the pump's bleeder fitting with the burner running, restoring a solid stream of oil. A is wrong: running dry does not inherently destroy a nozzle, and replacing it does nothing about the air in the line. B is wrong: the ignition system is not damaged by a dry tank, and the burner did run — it simply had no oil to ignite. C is wrong: single-pipe systems are routinely restarted after dry runs once primed and bled; conversion is unnecessary.

questions.question: A horizontal condensate drain line is being roughed in from an indoor coil. What minimum slope does the mechanical code require on that line?

answers.text: 1/4 inch per foot, the same minimum slope required for horizontal sanitary drainage piping
Dead level, provided a properly sized condensate trap is installed at the unit outlet
1/8 inch per foot (a 1 percent slope) in the direction of drainage
1/16 inch per foot, since condensate flows are small and intermittent in normal operation

questions.explanation: C is correct: condensate drain piping must be sloped not less than 1/8 unit vertical in 12 units horizontal — 1/8 inch per foot, a 1 percent slope — in the direction of flow. A is wrong: 1/4 inch per foot is a sanitary drainage figure, not the condensate minimum this code states. B is wrong: a trap does not substitute for slope; a level line holds water, grows slime, and overflows the pan. D is wrong: 1/16 inch per foot is half the required minimum and will not reliably drain the line.

questions.question: On an R-410A system the suction pressure corresponds to a saturation temperature of 40 degrees, and the suction line temperature at the sensing point is 52 degrees. What is the operating superheat?

answers.text: The superheat is 8 degrees, found by subtracting the line temperature from twice the saturation temperature value
The superheat is 12 degrees, found by subtracting the saturation temperature from the suction line temperature
The superheat is 92 degrees, found by adding the saturation temperature and the suction line temperature together
The superheat is 40 degrees, found by reading the saturation temperature alone as the completed superheat value

questions.explanation: B is correct: superheat = suction line temperature minus saturation temperature = 52 - 40 = 12 degrees. A is wrong: doubling the saturation temperature before subtracting is not part of the superheat calculation. C is wrong: the two temperatures are subtracted, never added, to find superheat. D is wrong: the saturation temperature alone states the boiling point, not the heat added past it.

questions.question: A sheet metal shop fabricates a supply duct run for a system designed at a 2-inch water column static pressure class. What governs the sheet gauge, joint, and reinforcement selections for that ductwork?

answers.text: The selections are governed by duct length alone, with longer runs receiving heavier gauge metal and added reinforcement
The selections are governed by the sheet metal supplier house standard, applied uniformly to every job the shop fabricates
The selections are governed by the insulation thickness specified, with the duct liner schedule setting the metal gauge used
The selections are governed by the pressure class together with the duct dimensions, per the duct construction standards

questions.explanation: D is correct: the SMACNA duct construction standards set gauge, transverse joint, and reinforcement requirements from the combination of static pressure class and duct width or diameter. A is wrong: run length does not set construction requirements in the standards tables. B is wrong: a house standard cannot replace the project pressure class and duct size lookup. C is wrong: liner and insulation schedules concern thermal and acoustic treatment, not structural gauge selection.

questions.question: Combustion air for a 200,000 Btu/h boiler room is supplied from outdoors through two horizontal ducts. What net free area is required for each duct under the two-opening outdoor method?

answers.text: Each duct must provide 400 square inches of net free area under the horizontal duct sizing ratio for outdoor air
Each duct must provide 50 square inches of net free area under the horizontal duct sizing ratio for outdoor air
Each duct must provide 100 square inches of net free area under the horizontal duct sizing ratio for outdoor air
Each duct must provide 200 square inches of net free area under the horizontal duct sizing ratio for outdoor air

questions.explanation: C is correct: horizontal ducts use 1 square inch per 2,000 Btu/h, so 200,000 / 2,000 = 100 square inches for each duct. A is wrong: 400 square inches applies a ratio four times larger than the horizontal duct ratio. B is wrong: 50 square inches is the vertical duct result (1 per 4,000 Btu/h), not the horizontal duct result. D is wrong: 200 square inches uses the indoor-opening ratio of 1 per 1,000 Btu/h, which does not govern ducts.

questions.question: A journeyman restricted licensee in ventilation offers to contract directly with a building owner for a duct replacement. Which statement correctly limits this offer?

answers.text: The offer is proper, and a journeyman restricted licensee may contract with the public in the examined specialty
A journeyman restricted licensee provides services only under the direction and control of a licensed contractor
The offer is proper if the journeyman restricted licensee first registers the contract with the county permitting office
The offer is proper for ventilation work, and the under-direction limit applies only to the heating specialties

questions.explanation: B is correct: the journeyman restricted license authorizes providing services in its specialty while under the direction and control of a licensed contractor; it is a worker-tier license, not a contracting license. A is wrong: contracting with the public requires a contractor-tier license such as master, master restricted, or limited. C is wrong: no county registration converts a worker-tier license into contracting authority. D is wrong: the direction-and-control condition applies across the restricted specialties, including ventilation.

questions.question: A master restricted license expired two years ago and the former licensee now applies to restore it. What does restoration require on these facts?

answers.text: Restoration on payment of the required renewal or reinstatement fee, within the four-year window
A completely new application with fresh experience proof and a new passing examination score
Restoration only after a hearing at which the Board votes on the reasons for the lapse
No restoration path, with a new license available only after a full waiting period runs

questions.explanation: A is correct: when application for restoration is made within 4 years after expiration, the license may be restored on payment of the required renewal or reinstatement fee. B is wrong: fresh experience proof and re-examination belong to the Board's options after the four-year window, not within it. C is wrong: no hearing vote is a stated condition of an in-window restoration. D is wrong: an in-window restoration path expressly exists.

questions.question: The owner of a Maryland HVACR company asks whether the company itself should apply for a business license from the Board. What is the accurate answer?

answers.text: The company must hold its own business license in addition to the licenses held by the individuals who work for it
The company must hold a business license only if it employs more than the threshold number of field employees
The company obtains one business license and every employee then works under that single company credential
Maryland licenses individuals only, and the business acts through a licensee it employs and designates

questions.explanation: D is correct: Title 9A licenses individuals and creates no separate business or entity license; the business provides services through a master, master restricted, or limited license holder it employs and designates to direct and control the work. A is wrong: no Board business license exists to hold alongside individual licenses. B is wrong: no employee-count threshold creates a business-license duty. C is wrong: employees hold their own individual licenses rather than working under a company credential.

questions.question: A candidate is allocating study time for the Air Conditioning specialty examination. Which topic distribution matches its published outline?

answers.text: Electrical 15, Piping 15, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning 15, and Safety 5 questions
Electrical 10, Piping 20, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning 7, Heating Systems 8, and Safety 5 questions
Electrical 15, Piping 10, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning 20, and Safety 5 questions
Electrical 15, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning 5, Heating Systems 25, and Safety 5 questions

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Air Conditioning outline is Electrical Knowledge, Motors, and Controls 15, Piping 10, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning 20, and Safety 5, totaling 50 questions. A is wrong: that even 15-15-15 split with Safety 5 is the Refrigeration outline. B is wrong: that distribution, with Piping heaviest, is the Hydronic outline. D is wrong: that distribution, dominated by Heating Systems, is the Forced Air outline.

questions.question: A replacement boiler rated at 150,000 Btu/h serves a building whose calculated design heat loss is 60,000 Btu/h. The boiler fires in bursts of about two minutes, and fuel use has risen compared with the old, smaller boiler. What is the root problem?

answers.text: The circulator is moving water too slowly, trapping heat inside the boiler jacket and forcing the operating control to end each firing cycle early, a suspicion the technician confirms by measuring the temperature rise across the boiler at full fire with strap-on sensors

The aquastat's differential is set too wide, causing long off-cycles that the burner then answers with short compensating bursts of firing, which the technician corrects by narrowing the aquastat's differential to its minimum available setting

The expansion tank is undersized, so each firing cycle relieves a little water and the fill valve answers with cold water that shortens the next cycle, a pattern the owner confirms by finding small puddles beneath the relief valve's discharge pipe after cold nights
The boiler is grossly oversized for the connected load, so each firing satisfies the control temperature almost immediately and the burner never settles into efficient steady operation

questions.explanation: D is correct: a boiler with two and a half times the capacity of the design load reaches its control temperature in very short runs, and the resulting short-cycling wastes fuel in repeated startup and standby losses. A is wrong: slow circulation raises the boiler's temperature rise across the heat exchanger but does not produce this firing pattern in an oversized boiler, and the old boiler behaved on the same piping. B is wrong: a wider differential lengthens both on- and off-cycles, the opposite pattern. C is wrong: relief weeping from an undersized tank is a pressure symptom that would be visible at the relief discharge, and it does not set burner cycle length.

questions.question: A local subdivision requires a surety bond under its local HVACR requirements for work a master restricted licensee will contract. How does the licensee's state insurance proof affect that local demand?

answers.text: It has no effect, and the licensee must post the local surety bond in addition to carrying the insurance
Proof of the required state insurance satisfies the local surety-bond requirement
It reduces the local bond amount by the amount of the property damage coverage the licensee carries
It satisfies the bond only for residential jobs, with commercial jobs still requiring a separate bond

questions.explanation: B is correct: where a local subdivision requires a surety bond under local HVACR requirements, proof of the required state insurance satisfies that bond requirement. A is wrong: the statute gives the insurance proof satisfying effect rather than leaving the bond fully additional. C is wrong: the rule is satisfaction of the requirement, not a dollar-for-dollar reduction. D is wrong: no residential-only limit narrows the satisfaction rule.

questions.question: A crew brazes the suction and liquid lines of a new walk-in system without flowing any gas through the tubing. Weeks later the expansion valve's inlet screen is found clogged with black, flaky scale. What practice would have prevented the scale?

answers.text: Brazing with a hotter flame and faster travel speed, keeping each joint at brazing temperature for the shortest possible time, since brief, fast heating of a joint raises far less internal oxide than the sustained heat of a difficult, slow joint

Applying flux to the inside of every fitting before assembly, so the flux dissolves oxides before they can flake into the refrigerant stream, applied with the same paste flux used for soft-soldering copper water tube in ordinary plumbing work

Using a filler metal with a lower melting point for every joint, producing a chemically cleaner joint interior at the lower temperature, at the cost of the pressure-containing joint strength that code-recognized brazing temperatures are specified to provide
Flowing dry nitrogen through the tubing during brazing to displace the oxygen, preventing the cupric-oxide scale that forms on hot copper exposed to air

questions.explanation: D is correct: brazing filler metals melt above 840 degrees F, and at brazing temperatures copper oxidizes rapidly in air, forming black cupric-oxide scale that later flakes off and plugs screens and valve ports; a low flow of dry nitrogen through the tubing during brazing displaces the oxygen and keeps the interior clean. A is wrong: oxide forms whenever copper is at brazing heat in air, regardless of travel speed. B is wrong: flux belongs on the joint exterior as the procedure requires, and coating fitting interiors introduces contamination rather than preventing scale. C is wrong: a joint made below the brazing temperature range with a lower-melting filler is a soldered joint, a different process, and the stem's joints still would have been heated in air.

questions.question: A technician is replacing a failed compressor on a split air-conditioning system and will have the sealed system open at several points. What must be done with the refrigerant charge before any line is cut?

answers.text: Release the charge slowly through the manifold gauge set so that the oil stays behind in the system
Recover the refrigerant into an approved recovery cylinder with recovery equipment, without venting it
Front-seat both service valves and leave the entire charge trapped in the condensing unit indefinitely
Blow the charge out of the lines with nitrogen into a bucket of water so it cannot reach the air

questions.explanation: B is correct: before a system is opened, its refrigerant must be recovered into an approved recovery cylinder using recovery equipment; federal rules prohibit knowingly venting refrigerant during service. A is wrong: venting the charge through a manifold is prohibited, regardless of how slowly it is released or what happens to the oil. C is wrong: front-seating service valves cannot lawfully substitute for recovery when the system will be opened at the compressor, and a condensing unit is not an approved storage vessel for an indefinite hold. D is wrong: blowing the charge out with nitrogen still vents the refrigerant, and water does not neutralize or capture it.

questions.question: A Maryland licensee who started in a restricted category later upgrades to a higher license category. What happens to the licensee's registration number at the upgrade?

answers.text: A new registration number is issued and the earlier number is retired from Board records permanently
The registration number stays the same as the licensee upgrades the license
The registration number changes to match the registration number of the contractor who supervised the upgrade
The licensee chooses a replacement registration number from numbers the Board has not yet assigned

questions.explanation: B is correct: the registration number is personal to the licensee and remains the same as the licensee upgrades the license; only the category number changes. A is wrong: upgrading does not retire the number or trigger a new one. C is wrong: the number belongs to the individual licensee, not to a supervising contractor. D is wrong: registration numbers are assigned by the Board, not selected by the licensee.

questions.question: Immediately after each defrost, a walk-in freezer's evaporator fans start with the compressor and blow warm, moist air across the stored product, frosting surfaces quickly and spiking box temperature. The circuit includes a fan-delay control. What is the fault?

answers.text: The defrost termination thermostat is ending defrost too late, so the fans are correctly removing the excess heat the long defrost put into the coil, and the fans are simply performing the heat-removal duty that the termination thermostat's timing dictates for this coil

The evaporator fans are oversized for the coil, so they move the post-defrost warm air into the box faster than the refrigeration system can remove it, a condition corrected by slowing the evaporator fans with a speed controller fitted to the fan motors for this purpose
The fan-delay control has failed, since its job is to hold the fans off after defrost until the coil is pulled back down toward operating temperature, protecting product and limiting frost

The time clock's defrost frequency is set too low, so each defrost must run longer and the fans cannot help but circulate warm air when it ends, so lengthening each defrost period is the remedy that restores normal fan behavior in the minutes after defrost ends

questions.explanation: C is correct: the fan-delay control exists to keep evaporator fans off after defrost until the coil is re-chilled, so warm moist air is not blown onto product; fans starting instantly with the compressor show that control has failed. A is wrong: even a long defrost would still be followed by a fan delay on a working control, so termination timing does not explain fans starting immediately. B is wrong: fan size does not change when the fans start; the fault is in start timing, not air volume. D is wrong: defrost frequency changes how often the event occurs, not the fan behavior in the minutes after each defrost.

questions.question: After a humidifier and an electronic air cleaner are wired into a furnace's 24-volt control circuit, the outdoor contactor begins to chatter and control voltage sags to about 19 volts whenever several accessories run together. The transformer is rated 40 VA. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: The combined VA load of the control devices now exceeds the transformer's 40 VA rating, so its output voltage collapses under load
