The thermostat is defective, since only a thermostat fault can make a contactor chatter on a cooling call regardless of how many accessories happen to be running at the time
Line voltage to the furnace is too high, forcing the transformer to shed the excess as a voltage sag
The contactor coil is wound for 120 volts, which explains the chatter whenever the accessories run

questions.explanation: A is correct: control transformers deliver their rated voltage only up to their VA rating; adding accessory loads beyond 40 VA overloads the transformer, its output sags (here to about 19 volts), and the contactor — the largest load — chatters as it drops in and out. B is wrong: a thermostat fault would not correlate with accessory operation or produce a measured system-wide voltage sag. C is wrong: high line voltage raises, not lowers, secondary voltage, and transformers do not shed excess as a sag. D is wrong: a 120-volt coil on 24 volts would never pull in properly at any time, not only when accessories run together.

questions.question: In a three-zone hot-water system, two zones heat normally but one zone stays cold. At the cold zone's valve, the thermostat is calling and the technician measures 24 volts at the valve motor terminals; the motor housing is warm, the valve does not open, and its end switch never closes to call the circulator for that zone. What is the correct repair?

answers.text: Replace the valve's powerhead — the motor assembly designed to be changed without draining the system — then verify the end switch closes and the zone circulates

Drain the system and replace the complete valve body, since a valve that will not open with voltage present has always failed in its internal waterway passages, including cutting out the sweat-connected valve body and sweating in a complete new valve assembly on the zone piping

Replace the circulator, since a zone that never starts its circulator call has lost pumping capacity even where other zones still heat, selected by horsepower from the boiler nameplate and replaced with the failed circulator during the same service visit

Replace the zone thermostat, since 24 volts measured at the valve motor proves the thermostat is sending a corrupted signal the motor cannot use, which the technician proves by swapping the zone thermostat with one taken from a zone that is heating normally

questions.explanation: A is correct: voltage present at the motor with a warm but non-operating motor identifies a failed powerhead, and zone valve powerheads are designed to be replaced without draining the system; end-switch closure is then verified. B is wrong: the valve body's waterway is moved by the powerhead, and a motor failure does not require disturbing the piping or draining the system. C is wrong: the other zones heat on the circulator's call path, and this zone's circulator never receives its end-switch call in the first place. D is wrong: a clean 24 volts at the motor terminals shows the thermostat and wiring are delivering the call correctly.

nmls-safe-mlo.quiz_title: SAFE MLO — Mortgage Loan Originator Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Hannah advertises a monthly payment example online. What makes the example non-deceptive?

answers.text: Showing the payment for the shortest term even when advertising a longer one
Stating the loan amount, term, and material assumptions behind the payment shown
Rounding the payment down so the figure is easier to remember
Omitting taxes and insurance without saying they are excluded

questions.explanation: A payment figure means little without the amount, term, and assumptions that produced it, and taxes or insurance cannot be silently left out. Rounding down or swapping terms turns an example into a lure.

questions.question: For rescission purposes, how is a business day generally counted?

answers.text: All calendar days except Sundays and federal public holidays
Only days when the creditor branch nearest the borrower is open
Monday through Friday, excluding every Saturday in all cases
Only days when mail is delivered to the creditor office

questions.explanation: The rescission business day counts every calendar day except Sundays and federal holidays, so a Saturday counts even if a particular branch is closed. The narrower branch-hours definition applies to some other disclosure rules, not to rescission timing.

questions.question: How do FHA and USDA guaranteed loans differ on household income limits, at a concept level?

answers.text: FHA has no maximum household income limit of the USDA kind, while USDA guaranteed eligibility requires income at or below its area limit
Both programs use the exact same income ceiling in every county
USDA has no income test and FHA has the strictest one
Income limits apply only to VA loans among government programs

questions.explanation: The USDA income ceiling is a distinctive gate for that program, while FHA eligibility does not hinge on staying under a comparable household maximum. VA eligibility instead turns on service-based entitlement.

questions.question: What continuance question is central when using child support income to qualify?

answers.text: Whether the child will attend a private school
Whether the paying parent lives in the same state
Whether the borrower prefers direct deposit
Whether payments will continue for the required period based on the child's age and the support order

questions.explanation: Continuance depends on how long the support obligation will remain in effect, which turns on the order and the child's age. Where the payer lives does not determine whether the income will continue.

questions.question: Which culture failure most enables pricing discretion abuse to persist across a sales force?

answers.text: Requiring written reasons for pricing exceptions
Auditing exception rates by loan officer each quarter
Publishing clear pricing policies to all originators
Rewarding volume and revenue per loan while ignoring disparity reports and treating compliance questions as obstacles

questions.explanation: Abuse persists when incentives reward revenue per loan and disparity findings are ignored, signaling that results matter more than equal treatment. Written exception reasons and regular audits are controls that work against the abuse, not causes of it.

questions.question: Which interview answer is a red flag that warrants further verification rather than immediate acceptance?

answers.text: The borrower explains a job change with an offer letter and a start date
The borrower provides two years of tax returns that match the stated income
The borrower cannot name the employer address, gives shifting income figures, and urges the officer not to verify anything
The borrower asks for a copy of the Loan Estimate

questions.explanation: Shifting figures, inability to give basic employer details, and resistance to verification together signal possible misrepresentation requiring further checks. Asking for the Loan Estimate is normal borrower behavior and is not a warning sign at all.

questions.question: Servicer Summit plans to charge borrower Karl for force-placed insurance. The first required written notice must generally be sent:

answers.text: On the same day the charge is imposed
Only after the policy has been renewed twice
Within 90 days after the charge is imposed
At least 45 days before the borrower is charged for the force-placed insurance

questions.explanation: The servicer must send the first force-placed insurance notice at least 45 days before charging the borrower. Notice on the day of the charge gives the borrower no chance to provide proof of coverage.

questions.question: In a seller-funded 2-1 buydown, where does the money that covers the borrower's reduced early payments come from?

answers.text: From the borrower's future tax refunds
From a subsidy account funded at closing, often by the seller or builder as a concession
From the lender forgiving part of the interest
From the borrower's retirement account by law

questions.explanation: The buydown subsidy is deposited into an escrow-like buydown account at closing, commonly funded by the seller or builder, and drawn each month to make up the difference. The lender does not forgive the interest; the account pays it.

questions.question: Noah Fitzgerald borrows $295,000 at 6.875% for 30 years. What is his monthly principal and interest payment?
questions.explanation: The amortization calculation for $295,000 at 6.875% over 360 months is $1,937.94. The $1,690.10 choice is interest only and omits the principal component entirely.

questions.question: Tom Young has $7,628 in annual escrow disbursements. What is the maximum two-month cushion permitted?
questions.explanation: Divide the annual total by six to get two months' worth: $7,628 / 6 = $1,271.33. Forgetting that the cushion is two months leads to the one-month amount.

questions.question: Before an originator joins a video call where a borrower will show tax documents on screen, what preparation matters most?

answers.text: Using a virtual background with the lender logo in every frame
Ensuring a private setting and confirming who else can see or hear the session
Asking the borrower to read every document aloud for the recording
Scheduling the call during lunch so fewer co-workers are nearby

questions.explanation: Screen-shared tax documents are highly sensitive, so privacy of the setting and audience comes first. A branded background does not stop a roommate, co-worker, or passerby from viewing the return.

questions.question: A homeowner cannot make payments and, to avoid foreclosure, voluntarily transfers title to the lender. What is this called?

answers.text: Lis pendens
Deficiency judgment
Deed in lieu of foreclosure
Wraparound transfer

questions.explanation: A deed in lieu voluntarily conveys title to the lender to satisfy the debt and avoid a foreclosure proceeding.

questions.question: A business with gross revenues above the large-business threshold in the prior fiscal year applies for mortgage credit and is denied. Which notification approach can comply with Regulation B for that business applicant?

answers.text: No notification of any kind is ever required for a business applicant

The creditor may notify the applicant orally or in writing within a reasonable time, and must provide a written statement of specific reasons and the ECOA notice if the applicant makes a written request within 60 days
The creditor must always send the identical consumer notice with no variations allowed for business credit
The creditor may wait until the applicant files a lawsuit before giving any reason

questions.explanation: For larger businesses, Regulation B allows oral or written notification within a reasonable time, with a written statement of reasons due after a timely written request. Business credit is still covered by ECOA, so giving no notice at all is not an option.

questions.question: A lender's own origination charge was estimated at one amount, and at closing the lender tries to charge more with no valid reason for a revision. How is that charge treated?

answers.text: It may increase by up to ten percent like other third-party fees
It may not increase, because fees paid to the creditor are subject to zero tolerance
It may increase freely because the Loan Estimate is only a rough guide
It may increase if the borrower signs a waiver at the closing table

questions.explanation: Charges paid to the creditor itself sit in the zero tolerance bucket and cannot grow from the estimate. The ten percent cushion belongs to a different category, and a closing-table waiver does not cure an increase.

questions.question: A buyer asks why she receives a preliminary title commitment before closing but a final owner's policy afterward. What explains the timing of the final policy?

answers.text: The final policy is issued after closing and recording, insuring title as of that point based on the completed transaction
The final policy is only a marketing document with no insurance function
The commitment and the final policy are the same document with different covers
The final policy must be issued before the title search is performed

questions.explanation: The commitment previews what will be insured and on what conditions; the final policy issues once the transaction closes and the instruments are recorded. A policy cannot precede the search and closing it insures.

questions.question: An originator wants to work from her home office in a state that permits remote origination work under stated conditions. Which setup best fits the typical concept-level conditions?

answers.text: Meeting borrowers at her kitchen table and storing paper files at home
Working through the employer's secure systems, not holding the home out as a business location, and not meeting consumers in person at the residence
Listing the home address as a branch to attract walk-in clients
Keeping the arrangement secret from the employer to avoid paperwork

questions.explanation: Remote-work permission typically hinges on secure company systems, no consumer meetings at the home, and no holding the residence out as an office. Walk-in traffic and home file storage are the features those conditions are designed to prevent.

questions.question: An adjustable-rate mortgage has an index of 5 percent, a margin of 2.5 percent, a start rate of 4 percent, and an initial cap that allows at most a 1 percent increase. What is the rate after the first adjustment?

answers.text: 6 percent
4.5 percent
5 percent
7.5 percent

questions.explanation: The fully indexed rate is 5 + 2.5 = 7.5 percent, and the capped rate is 4 + 1 = 5 percent. The actual rate is the lower of the two, 5 percent.

questions.question: Borrower Elena opens a new mortgage relationship with a lender she has never used before. Under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, when must she receive the lender's initial privacy notice?

answers.text: Only if she asks for it in writing after closing
Only at the first annual renewal of her loan
Only when the lender decides to sell her information
No later than when the customer relationship is established, such as at application or closing under the lender's delivery method

questions.explanation: GLBA requires a clear and conspicuous initial privacy notice no later than when the customer relationship is established. Waiting until an annual cycle or until information is sold would leave the consumer uninformed at the moment sharing practices begin.

questions.question: Sofia refinances her first mortgage, and her home equity lender agrees in writing to let the new first mortgage keep senior position ahead of the equity loan. What has the equity lender signed?

answers.text: A defeasance clause releasing its lien in full
A quitclaim deed transferring the equity loan to the new lender
An estoppel certificate confirming the equity balance
A subordination agreement keeping its lien in junior position behind the new first mortgage

questions.explanation: Subordination is the junior lienholder agreement to remain or move behind another lien, which a refinance of a first mortgage often requires. The equity lien is not released, so defeasance does not fit.

questions.question: A borrower considering a loan asks whether a qualified future buyer could assume it, and the originator reviews the actual loan terms and explains accurately what is and is not promised about assumption. What is this?

answers.text: Proper disclosure conduct regarding an assumable loan
A guarantee that any buyer will be approved to assume
Prohibited, because assumability may never be discussed
Sufficient only if the originator also sells the future home

questions.explanation: Accurately explaining actual assumability terms, without promising lender approval, is proper conduct.

nhie-home-inspector.quiz_title: National Home Inspector Examination (NHIE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What distinguishes a dry creek bed or drainage channel feature that is functioning properly?

answers.text: It holds standing water for several days after storms
It is filled with loose mulch up to the foundation
It conveys stormwater along a defined path away from structures and discharges without eroding
It directs water under the driveway slab

questions.explanation: A functioning drainage feature moves water along its intended path without ponding at buildings or eroding its channel. Standing water at the house signals failure.

questions.question: A balcony's floor slopes toward the house and its door threshold shows water damage. What is the primary defect?

answers.text: The balcony surface drains toward the structure instead of away, driving water at the threshold and wall
The balcony railing is too high for the door to open
The balcony door needs a storm door added
The balcony is missing a ceiling fan

questions.explanation: Elevated floors over or against walls must pitch away and be flashed at the wall line; reverse slope delivers water to the most vulnerable joint in the assembly.

questions.question: Geothermal (ground-source) heat pumps exchange heat with:

answers.text: A rooftop cooling tower
The earth or groundwater through buried loops
A gas-fired boiler
Solar panels directly

questions.explanation: Ground-source systems circulate fluid through buried piping, using the earth's stable temperature as a heat source in winter and a heat sink in summer. This typically yields very high efficiency.

questions.question: A report's recommendations should generally direct the client to:

answers.text: Perform the repair themselves using online videos
Ignore the finding if the seller disagrees
Negotiate a specific dollar credit
Have the condition further evaluated or corrected by a qualified professional in the relevant trade when it exceeds inspection scope

questions.explanation: Inspectors identify and describe conditions and recommend the appropriate next step — usually evaluation or repair by a qualified specialist. They do not design repairs, set credits, or assign DIY work.

questions.question: Which element distinguishes an exclusion from a limitation in an agreement?

answers.text: An exclusion is written and a limitation is only spoken
A limitation is more expensive than an exclusion
An exclusion removes an item from the service entirely, while a limitation describes a boundary or condition on how included work is performed
They are identical and interchangeable in all uses

questions.explanation: Exclusions take items off the table; limitations qualify the work that remains, such as visual-only access. Using the concepts precisely keeps client expectations accurate.

questions.question: A TPR valve discharge pipe terminates 18 inches above the floor and is threaded at its end. Why should the inspector report this?

answers.text: The pipe is too long to allow drainage
The termination height and threaded end create a scald and capping hazard
Discharge pipes must terminate outdoors
The pipe should be made of flexible tubing

questions.explanation: A discharge pipe must end close to the floor or a safe drain point, be unthreaded, and remain unobstructed so a discharge cannot scald occupants or be capped shut. A high, threaded end violates both principles.

questions.question: What should an inspector do when a home has a fire suppression system with a backflow preventer and pressure gauges showing zero pressure on the sprinkler side?

answers.text: Rebuild the backflow preventer during the inspection
Conclude the system is fine because gauges often read zero
Flow a head to test the actual pressure
Report the system as apparently not pressurized or impaired and recommend prompt evaluation by a qualified sprinkler contractor

questions.explanation: Zero indicated pressure, closed valves, and similar observations mean the system cannot be relied on. Inspectors report impairment and defer testing and repair to sprinkler professionals.

questions.question: An inspector finds a bottom chord of a roof truss has been cut to install an attic pull-down stair. How should this be reported?

answers.text: As a serious structural alteration requiring evaluation by a qualified professional
As acceptable if the stair operates smoothly
As a normal field adjustment for trusses
As a cosmetic attic access issue only

questions.explanation: Trusses are engineered systems; cutting any chord or web without an engineered repair can compromise the entire truss.

questions.question: Insulation missing or displaced above a dropped ceiling or around an attic hatch causes:

answers.text: No measurable heat loss
Improved attic ventilation
A vapor barrier failure only
A thermal bypass — a concentrated area of heat loss (and summer heat gain)

questions.explanation: Continuity matters: even small uninsulated gaps, such as an uninsulated hatch, leak disproportionate heat because heat flows preferentially through the weakest path. Weatherstripping and insulating the hatch is a standard fix.

questions.question: A range hood mounted far above the cooktop with a narrow canopy will perform poorly primarily because of which factor?

answers.text: Excessive grease filtration
Poor capture efficiency, since the rising plume spreads and escapes past the hood
Too much make-up air
Oversized duct diameter

questions.explanation: Capture depends on hood size, overhang, and height as much as fan cfm. A hood that covers the front burners and sits at the recommended height captures far more effluent at the same airflow.

questions.question: An inspector notes a missing bonding jumper appearance at the water heater piping and several outlets testing with no ground on a tester. What referral is correct?

answers.text: Diagnose the entire grounding system in the report
Recommend the buyer install jumpers personally with clamps
Recommend evaluation by a licensed electrician, reporting the tester observations and visible concerns without claiming to have verified the entire grounding and bonding system
State that ungrounded outlets are safe for all modern appliances

questions.explanation: Tester indications and visible bonding concerns justify an electrician referral, but full grounding-system verification exceeds a general inspection. The report should state observations and limits accurately.

questions.question: A wire enters a metal box through a knockout with no cable clamp or bushing, and the cable jacket is cut where it rubs the sharp edge. The defect is what?

answers.text: A normal method to strip cable automatically
Only a concern if the box is plastic
Damage limited to appearance
Unprotected cable entry that has damaged the conductors' protection and must be repaired

questions.explanation: Clamps and bushings protect cable from sharp metal edges; damaged jackets and insulation can progress to shorts and arcing.

questions.question: A smart thermostat is installed but the heating system short-cycles and the display goes blank during calls for heat. What should the inspector limit the report to?

answers.text: Observed malfunction of the heating operation and recommendation for HVAC evaluation
A full diagnosis of the control board electronics
Reprogramming the thermostat schedule
Replacing the thermostat during the inspection

questions.explanation: Inspectors test systems using normal controls and report observed behavior such as short-cycling without performing repairs or deep electronics diagnosis. A blanking display suggests a power or control issue for a technician to resolve.

questions.question: A roof surface measures 30 feet by 40 feet on one rectangular slope. How many roofing squares does that slope represent?

answers.text: 12 squares
120 squares
7 squares
1.2 squares

questions.explanation: Area is 30 times 40 equals 1,200 square feet. Dividing by 100 square feet per square gives 12 squares.

questions.question: During a heating inspection with the thermostat calling, supply air should feel warm and the temperature rise across a typical gas furnace is commonly in the range of:

answers.text: 5 to 10 degrees F
15 to 20 degrees F
About 30 to 60 degrees F above return air, per the data plate range
Over 150 degrees F

questions.explanation: Furnaces are rated for a specified temperature rise, commonly roughly 30 to 60 degrees F. Rise well outside the plate range signals airflow or firing-rate problems.

questions.question: A window unit air conditioner is the only cooling for a bedroom and it is unplugged with a damaged cord. How should cooling for that room be reported?

answers.text: Present but not operated due to a damaged cord — a safety-related condition to report along with the testing limitation
Fully functional because the room felt cool
Not present because it is a window unit
Inspected by plugging it in despite the damaged cord

questions.explanation: A damaged cord is both a finding and a reason not to operate the unit. Reports should capture both rather than energizing unsafe equipment.

questions.question: A client asks the inspector not to put a mold-like growth in writing, only to mention it verbally, fearing the lender will see the report. The inspector should:

answers.text: Comply, because the client pays the fee
Document observed conditions in the report as professional standards require, explaining that reports must be complete and accurate
Describe it as a 'decorative pattern' instead
Send two versions of the report

questions.explanation: A report with deliberate omissions is a false record that can mislead lenders and future parties and expose the client and inspector. Completeness is not optional at a client's request.

questions.question: A vented gas fireplace insert is installed in a masonry fireplace and the surrounding trim shows heat discoloration. The flue above the insert was never lined or connected. Why is this concerning?

answers.text: Inserts always heat trim, so no concern exists
Trim discoloration proves the room is well heated
An insert venting into an oversized unlined flue cavity will draft perfectly
An insert that dumps exhaust into the chimney cavity instead of a properly sized liner or connector can cause poor draft, condensation, and gas leakage into the home

questions.explanation: Inserts must vent through a properly sized liner or connector continuous to the top of the chimney as the maker directs. Venting into the large old flue cavity cools exhaust, harms draft, and can leak combustion products.

questions.question: A receptacle is installed in a floor in the middle of a living room with a standard wall-style cover and no listing for floor use, and its face is damaged. Floor receptacles require what special feature?

answers.text: Any receptacle may be laid in a floor opening
A rug placed over the receptacle as its cover
A listed floor box and cover assembly designed to protect the device and exclude moisture and debris
GFCI protection alone makes any floor install acceptable

questions.explanation: Floor outlets face foot traffic, mopping water, and debris, so listed floor assemblies with protective covers are required.

questions.question: Peeling paint, soft siding at the base of an exterior wall, and a moisture reading that is elevated together most likely indicate:

answers.text: The siding is a premium product
Moisture-related deterioration of the siding/trim that is defective and needs repair and source correction
The wall was recently renovated correctly
Insects are impossible in that wall

questions.explanation: Softness to probing plus finish failure and moisture evidence form a classic deterioration cluster. Reporting the cluster and recommending repair plus moisture-source correction addresses both symptom and cause.

north-carolina-home-inspector.quiz_title: North Carolina Home Inspector Licensing Examination Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the effect of a licensee's failure to notify the Board of a required change, such as a new business address?

answers.text: It automatically upgrades the license
It can be a rule violation and can cause the licensee to miss renewal or disciplinary notices
It transfers the license to the new address in another state
It has no possible consequence of any kind

questions.explanation: Current Board records are essential for renewal and legal notices. Failing to report required changes violates the rules and risks missed deadlines and default consequences.

questions.question: A client in Sanford asks the inspector to state the exact insulation R-value throughout the attic from a visual look. What is the proper response reflected in the report?

answers.text: Report the insulation type and approximate depth observed and note that exact R-value cannot be verified visually, rather than certifying a precise value
Invent a precise R-value to satisfy the client
Remove insulation samples for laboratory testing
Refuse to mention insulation at all

questions.explanation: Visual inspection can identify material and depth but not laboratory R-value, which varies with density and condition. Honest reporting states what was observed and its limits.

questions.question: Which best describes the Board's rulemaking authority?

answers.text: The Board may make any law, including criminal statutes, without the legislature
The Board has no authority to adopt rules
The Board may rewrite the Standards of Practice of other states for use in North Carolina
The Board may adopt administrative rules within the authority granted by the licensure law to implement it

questions.explanation: The Board rulemakes within its statutory grant to implement Article 9F, including the Standards of Practice and licensing procedures. It cannot enact criminal statutes or legislate beyond its authority.

questions.question: A kitchen range exhaust in a Burlington home recirculates through a charcoal filter, while heavy cooking moisture fogs nearby windows. What should the inspector note about moisture control?

answers.text: Recirculating hoods remove moisture as well as vented hoods
Cooking produces no moisture
Window fogging in a kitchen is always a window defect only
A recirculating hood does not remove moisture to the exterior, so cooking moisture remains indoors and the arrangement should be noted where moisture symptoms are present

questions.explanation: Charcoal filters trap some odors and grease but do not exhaust water vapor outdoors. In a home already showing condensation, noting the non-vented hood helps explain indoor moisture load.

questions.question: In an Outer Banks home in Kitty Hawk, wind-driven rain has wet the attic decking near gable vents and insulation is damp on that side. How should the inspector frame this?

answers.text: Attic moisture can only come from the living space
Report the damp materials and their location near the gable vent as moisture intrusion needing evaluation, without certifying the exact entry path if it cannot be confirmed visually
Guarantee the gable vent is the sole source
Damp insulation dries instantly and needs no mention

questions.explanation: Coastal wind-driven rain can enter at vents and penetrations, but inspectors distinguish observation from certainty. Reporting the damp location and recommending evaluation is accurate and defensible.

questions.question: Which statement about NC report timing and delivery is most consistent with the SoP framework?

answers.text: The written report, including the summary, is provided to the client as the deliverable of the inspection, following the agreement's terms
The report may be withheld until the seller approves it
Only the agent receives the report; the client receives a receipt
The report is optional if a verbal walkthrough occurred

questions.explanation: The written report with its summary page is the contracted deliverable to the client. A walkthrough conversation does not replace it, and the seller does not approve it.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why NC requires a summary page in addition to the full report?

answers.text: To replace the need for a written agreement
To provide the seller with a repair list only
To draw the client's attention to the most significant findings: items that are not functioning, materially defective, unsafe, or recommended for professional evaluation
To advertise additional inspection services

questions.explanation: The summary page exists to highlight the significant findings defined by the SoP so they are not buried in the full report. It supplements, and does not replace, the complete report.

questions.question: A seller offers to pay an NC inspector to omit a known defect from the report. What does the SoP require?

answers.text: The inspector may omit it if the omission is noted in the agreement
The inspector must report observed conditions honestly and must not be influenced by who pays the fee
The inspector must let the paying party edit the report
The inspector may omit defects the seller plans to repair later

questions.explanation: The inspector's duty is to report observed conditions objectively regardless of who pays. Allowing a party to suppress findings violates the SoP's scope and ethics of practice.

questions.question: A Winston-Salem home has a whole-house fan louver in the hallway ceiling, and the attic above has minimal insulation with a large uninsulated opening at the fan. In winter, what concern applies?

answers.text: The fan opening has no effect in winter
An uninsulated, leaky fan opening allows warm moist house air into the cold attic and loses heat, so its condition should be noted
Whole-house fans heat attics in winter
Louvers seal airtight by design

questions.explanation: A whole-house fan is a large hole between the house and attic unless covered and insulated in the heating season. Air leakage there wastes energy and can add moisture to the attic.

questions.question: Under the NC SoP, how are structural components concealed behind finished walls and ceilings treated?

answers.text: The inspector must open finished surfaces to inspect them
The inspector must report them as defective
The inspector must use X-ray equipment
They are not inspected because they are not readily accessible, and the inspection is limited to visible conditions

questions.explanation: Concealed structure is outside a visual inspection of readily accessible components. The inspector reports visible evidence, such as cracking or sagging, that suggests hidden problems.

questions.question: No kick-out flashing exists where a roof eave terminates at a sidewall in a Holly Springs home, and the siding and sheathing at that exact spot are rotted while the rest of the wall is sound. What does kick-out flashing do?

answers.text: It vents the attic at the eave
It diverts roof runoff at the end of a step-flashing run out away from the wall and into the gutter, instead of letting the concentrated flow run behind the siding
It holds the gutter to the fascia
It is an ice-dam device used only in northern states

questions.explanation: At the bottom of a roof-to-wall junction, all the water collected along the step flashing must be kicked out into the gutter. Without it, that stream pours behind cladding and rots a localized patch exactly as described.

questions.question: In a vented crawl space in Goldsboro, an inspector finds a slow drip from a supply fitting, dark staining and fungal-like growth on joists below it, and saturated soil. What two recommendations belong in the report?

answers.text: Paint the joists and add a second drip for balance
Ignore the drip because crawl spaces are expected to be wet
Repair of the plumbing leak by a plumber and correction and drying of the moisture condition affecting the wood structure
Install a garden sprinkler timer to match soil moisture

questions.explanation: A chronic supply leak both wastes water and keeps framing wet, promoting decay and microbial growth. The report needs the leak repaired and the moisture condition and affected materials addressed.

questions.question: A homeowner converted a natural gas furnace in a mountain home to propane by simply connecting the propane tank, and now the furnace soots heavily and produces a lazy, lifting flame. What fundamental mistake was made?

answers.text: Propane tanks must be painted a different color before use

Fuel conversion requires changing burner orifices and regulator settings because propane and natural gas operate at different pressures and energy content, and an unconverted appliance burns dangerously wrong
The furnace needs a larger flue for propane smoke
Sooting after conversion is normal for the first full year

questions.explanation: Propane is delivered at higher pressure and carries more energy per cubic foot than natural gas, so burners need different orifice sizes and settings. Running an unconverted appliance causes severe over-firing, soot, and carbon monoxide risk.

questions.question: In principle, which of the following is a core power of the North Carolina Home Inspector Licensure Board?

answers.text: Setting local property tax rates for inspected homes
Approving every home inspection report before it is delivered
Adopting rules, licensing qualified applicants, and disciplining licensees
Ordering sellers to make repairs identified in an inspection

questions.explanation: The Board rulemakes, examines and licenses applicants, renews licenses, investigates complaints, and imposes discipline. It does not approve individual reports or order repairs in private transactions.

questions.question: Under NC roofing practice, what should an inspector do when only part of the roof is visible due to the home's height and geometry?

answers.text: Report the entire roof as inspected in full
Report what was observed, state the viewing method and the extent of the limitation, and avoid characterizing unobserved areas
Refuse to mention the roof at all
Estimate the hidden areas' condition from the home's age

questions.explanation: Partial visibility yields partial findings plus explicit limitation language. Unobserved slopes are never characterized as sound or defective.

questions.question: Under a 1994 Clayton home, the inspector finds a polybutylene supply line actively spraying a fine mist from a split near a plastic fitting, soaking the insulation and subfloor. What immediate advice belongs in the inspector communication?

answers.text: Let it run until the plumber visit next week to keep the line flushed
Wrap the split in tape and report it as repaired
Photograph it for the report and say nothing until the report is delivered in two days
Shut off the water to the home if a working shutoff is accessible, because an active pressurized leak is causing damage now, and recommend emergency repair by a licensed plumber

questions.explanation: An active spray leak is an ongoing damage event, not a routine report item. Stopping the water through the normal shutoff within inspector scope and calling for emergency plumbing repair limits the loss.

questions.question: The large suction line running from a heat pump into a Concord home has long bare sections where the black insulation has rotted away, and the exposed copper sweats heavily, dripping onto the siding and foundation. Why is this reported beyond cosmetics?

answers.text: Sweating copper means the line is about to burst from pressure
The dripping indicates a plumbing leak inside the wall
Insulation on suction lines is purely decorative from the factory
Bare suction lines gain heat and lose efficiency, and the constant condensation wets building materials, so the deteriorated insulation should be replaced

questions.explanation: The suction line carries cold refrigerant vapor back to the compressor. Missing insulation wastes capacity as the line absorbs heat and produces heavy condensation that drips onto siding and foundation materials.

questions.question: An unlicensed person argues the licensure law does not apply because inspections are booked through an app. What is the correct principle?

answers.text: Online booking exempts a business from licensure
The licensing requirement follows the activity — compensated home inspections — regardless of how the work is booked
Only telephone-booked inspections require a license
Licensure applies only to firms with a physical office

questions.explanation: Licensure regulates the activity, not the booking channel. App-based, online, or office-based compensated inspections all require the same license.

questions.question: A gas water heater in a Salisbury home is found with its pilot out and its gas shutoff valve closed, tagged by the gas company. The listing agent asks the inspector to open the valve and relight the pilot so hot water can be tested. What should the inspector do?

answers.text: Decline to operate a shutoff or relight the appliance, report that the water heater could not be operated and why, and recommend evaluation by the gas utility or a licensed contractor
Open the valve and relight it, because testing is the job
Remove the utility tag to avoid alarming the buyer
Report the water heater as failed and defective with certainty

questions.explanation: Inspectors do not turn on utilities, open gas shutoffs, or light pilots, especially where a utility tag suggests a known problem. The correct action is to report the inoperative, untested condition and refer it to the responsible professionals.

questions.question: A rectangular crawl space in Thomasville measures 30 feet by 40 feet and its vapor retarder is sold in rolls covering 500 square feet each, with no waste allowance. How many rolls are minimally needed for single-layer full coverage?

answers.text: One roll
Two rolls
Three rolls, because 30 times 40 is 1,200 square feet and 1,200 divided by 500 rounds up to 3
Twelve rolls

questions.explanation: The area is 30 x 40 = 1,200 square feet. At 500 square feet per roll, 1,200 / 500 = 2.4, which rounds up to 3 rolls for full coverage.

texas-home-inspector-state-law.quiz_title: Texas State Law Exam (Home Inspector) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is a tie-in statute in the DTPA context, in principle?

answers.text: Another Texas law that expressly allows a violation of it to be pursued through the DTPAs consumer remedies
A rule tying inspection fees to home prices
A contract clause binding a client to one inspector
A federal law that replaces the DTPA entirely

questions.explanation: Tie-in statutes borrow the DTPAs enforcement power, letting consumers use its remedies for violations of the other law. They expand the DTPAs practical reach.

questions.question: Which conduct best reflects the independence expected of a Texas inspector?

answers.text: Accepting payment to change a finding
Performing an inspection objectively and reporting findings without improper influence from any party to the transaction
Letting the listing agent write the conclusions
Inspecting only homes sold by friends

questions.explanation: Inspectors serve their client with objective reporting. Improper influence, conflicts, and paid changes to findings undermine licensure duties.

questions.question: What distinguishes revocation from suspension in Texas license discipline?

answers.text: Suspension is permanent and revocation is temporary
Revocation terminates the license, while suspension pauses practice authority for a period or until conditions are met
They are identical sanctions with different names
Revocation applies only to apprentices

questions.explanation: Revocation ends the license, whereas suspension is a temporary removal of authority. The distinction matters for whether and how a person may return to practice.

questions.question: What is required for electrical receptacles during a Texas inspection?

answers.text: Inspect a representative approach to accessible receptacles and report deficiencies such as damage, incorrect wiring indications, or missing cover plates
Remove every receptacle from the wall
Test only one receptacle per home
Replace any receptacle that looks old

questions.explanation: Accessible receptacles are checked for condition and tester-indicated problems, and deficiencies are reported without dismantling the wiring system.

questions.question: How is a garage door opener handled under the Texas standards?

answers.text: Inspect its operation and safety features and report deficiencies such as a photoelectric sensor that does not reverse the door
Never inspect garage doors
Reprogram the opener remotes for the buyer
Only check the door if it is wooden

questions.explanation: Garage doors and openers are inspected for operation and safety reversal features, and failures are reported because they present a safety risk.

questions.question: A candidate fails the Texas licensing examination. What is the correct principle?

answers.text: The candidate must meet the examination requirement through the authorized retake process before licensure is granted
Failing once grants a temporary license forever
The sponsor may waive the examination
The candidate may practice while studying indefinitely

questions.explanation: Passing the required examination is a condition of licensure. A candidate who has not passed is not yet licensed to practice.

questions.question: A consumer claims mental anguish damages in a DTPA case involving knowing conduct. What is the principle?

answers.text: Mental anguish is automatic in every contract dispute
Mental anguish can never be recovered by a consumer
Only businesses may recover mental anguish
Mental anguish may be recoverable where the statute allows, particularly with knowing or intentional conduct and proof of a high degree of mental pain

questions.explanation: DTPA principles allow mental anguish in defined circumstances tied to culpable conduct and real proof. It is neither automatic nor categorically barred.

questions.question: Stairways, handrails, and guardrails are inspected in Texas primarily for what reason?

answers.text: Decorative consistency
Paint quality only
Historical authenticity
Safety and function, with deficiencies such as loose or missing rails reported

questions.explanation: Stairs and rails are safety components. Loose, missing, or improper rails and related deficiencies are reported on the form.

questions.question: How are windows that are painted shut or have failed insulated glazing units reported?

answers.text: As satisfactory because they are closed
As deficiencies affecting window operation or condition
As roof deficiencies
They are never reported

questions.explanation: Inoperable windows and failed glazing affect function, egress considerations, and energy performance, and are reported as deficiencies.

questions.question: An applicant fails the licensing examination. What is the general principle that follows?

answers.text: The applicant may practice while studying for a retake
Failure in one state section waives all other requirements
The applicant is not yet licensed and must pass as required before performing regulated inspections
The sponsor may sign reports in the applicants name until a pass

questions.explanation: Passing the required examination is a condition of licensure. Until licensed, the applicant cannot perform work that requires the license.

questions.question: What does the professional inspector level represent in the Texas licensing structure?

answers.text: The highest inspector license level, reflecting the most education and experience and the ability to sponsor others where permitted
A temporary permit for a single inspection
A license that exempts the holder from the standards of practice
A title any experienced contractor may use without licensure

questions.explanation: The professional inspector is the top rung of the Texas inspector ladder and can include sponsorship responsibilities. Higher licensure never exempts an inspector from the standards of practice.

questions.question: What do the four report designations on the Texas form allow the inspector to communicate?

answers.text: Whether each item was inspected, not inspected, not present, or deficient
The price to repair each item
Which party should pay for repairs
The inspector personal rating of the seller

questions.explanation: Each listed item is marked as inspected, not inspected, not present, or deficient, giving the reader a complete picture of scope and condition.

questions.question: A client pressures an inspector to soften a report in exchange for future repair referrals. What is the professional-conduct answer?

answers.text: Soften only minor defects
Trade report language for referrals if disclosed later
Refuse the bargain and report findings honestly, because report integrity cannot be traded for business benefits
Let the referring agent edit the report

questions.explanation: Professional conduct rules protect report independence. Future business is exactly the kind of benefit that must not shape findings.

questions.question: A Texas inspector reuses one clients glowing testimonial but fabricates the clients name and transaction. Which principle is broken?

answers.text: Only a spelling rule
Testimonials are banned even when genuine
Advertising must be truthful; invented endorsements mislead consumers just as false credentials do
Fabrication is allowed for privacy reasons

questions.explanation: Truthfulness in advertising covers endorsements as well as credentials. A fabricated testimonial deceives consumers about real client experience.

questions.question: A Texas inspector is asked to perform a partial inspection of only the roof for a client. What is the sound rule principle?

answers.text: Partial inspections are never lawful in any form
The inspector must secretly inspect the whole home anyway
A limited-scope service should be clearly agreed and reported as limited, without implying a full standard inspection was performed
The full standard form must claim all systems were inspected

questions.explanation: Limited services are handled by clear scope and honest reporting of what was and was not done. The report must never overstate the work performed.

questions.question: An inspector agrees to pay a fine and accept a reprimand to resolve a complaint. What type of resolution is this in concept?

answers.text: A criminal plea bargain in district court
A private settlement that binds future consumers
An agreed administrative order resolving an enforcement matter without a fully contested hearing
An appeal that overturns the complaint automatically

questions.explanation: Many enforcement matters resolve through agreed orders in the administrative process. Such an order is a regulatory resolution, not a criminal plea or a private contract with consumers.

questions.question: Cooling equipment produces almost no cooling and the indoor coil is frozen. The inspector should:

answers.text: Defrost it with a torch
Report that the system did not function as intended and note the observed icing as a deficiency
Add refrigerant from a personal tank
Mark it inspected with no deficiency

questions.explanation: Failure to cool and visible coil icing show the system is not functioning as intended and must be reported deficient.

questions.question: A condition prevents inspection of part of the electrical system. How should that limitation be handled in the Texas report?

answers.text: Mark the item deficient without comment
Omit the electrical section entirely
Indicate the item was not inspected and explain the reason
Assume the hidden part is satisfactory

questions.explanation: When an item is not inspected, the Texas form requires the inspector to check the not-inspected designation and explain why inspection was not possible.

questions.question: An elderly first-time buyer is pressured into paying for duplicate inspections the inspector knows are unnecessary, at inflated prices. Which DTPA theory is most plausible in principle?

answers.text: No theory, because the buyer signed
Unconscionable conduct, because the inspector exploited the consumers inexperience for unnecessary services
A theory limited to the inspectors advertising font
A claim belonging only to the Texas attorney general in every case

questions.explanation: Exploiting inexperience to sell needless services for excessive gain is the heart of unconscionability. A signature obtained through that exploitation does not end the inquiry.

questions.question: Which action is NOT required of a Texas inspector in the electrical system?

answers.text: Inspecting accessible receptacles for deficiencies
Observing the service panel condition
Reporting a visibly damaged service mast
Determining whether the electrical service is adequate for a planned future addition

questions.explanation: Determining adequacy for future loads goes beyond the standards. The inspection is a visual, functional check of existing conditions, not an engineering adequacy study.

south-carolina-residential-business-law.quiz_title: South Carolina Residential Business Management and Law Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is a business's break-even point?

answers.text: The sales level at which total revenue just covers total costs, with no profit or loss
The date a contractor license must be renewed
The point at which a job is half completed
The maximum amount a bank will lend the business

questions.explanation: At break-even, revenue equals fixed plus variable costs. Knowing it helps an owner set sales targets and evaluate whether pricing is sustainable.

questions.question: When are toolbox talks or short safety meetings most effective as a business practice?

answers.text: When held regularly, documented, and tied to the specific hazards of the work being performed
When held once at the founding of the company
When conducted only after a serious accident
When attendance records are never kept

questions.explanation: Brief, task-focused safety meetings reinforce training and surface site-specific hazards before work begins. Documenting attendance and topics supports the employer's training compliance.

questions.question: What is an express warranty in a construction contract?

answers.text: A guarantee the law imposes even if the parties never mention it
Insurance coverage purchased after a loss occurs
A promise that a payment bond will be issued
A specific promise or statement in the agreement about the quality, materials, or performance of the work

questions.explanation: An express warranty arises from the contractor's own statements or contract terms. Implied warranties, by contrast, arise by operation of law.

questions.question: What is a resale certificate used for?

answers.text: Certifying a home for resale
Waiving income tax
Licensing a subcontractor
Buying goods tax-free that will be resold to customers, rather than consumed by the buyer

questions.explanation: A resale certificate lets a retailer buy inventory for resale without paying sales tax at purchase. It does not exempt materials the contractor consumes in a lump-sum construction job.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a mechanic's lien for a residential builder or supplier?

answers.text: To provide security for payment for labor or materials that improved real property
To transfer ownership of the property to the contractor
To exempt the property from property taxes
To replace the need for a written contract

questions.explanation: A mechanic's lien secures payment for work or materials that improved the property. It does not transfer ownership or replace a contract.

questions.question: What is the effect of both parties signing a contract amendment that changes the completion date?

answers.text: The original contract is destroyed and unenforceable
Only the party who proposed the change is bound by it
The contract is modified as stated in the amendment, with the remaining terms continuing in effect
The amendment is valid only if filed with the building department

questions.explanation: A signed amendment is itself a contract change supported by the parties' agreement. Keeping amendments with the contract documents preserves a complete record.

questions.question: What does a performance bond guarantee?

answers.text: That materials will be cheapest
That employees will not be injured
That the building will appreciate
That the contract will be completed according to its terms, or the surety will arrange or pay for completion

questions.explanation: A performance bond protects the owner if the contractor defaults. The surety may complete the work, tender a new contractor, or pay the bond amount.

questions.question: What is the completed-contract method of accounting?

answers.text: Recognizing income monthly
Recognizing costs but never income
Recognizing all income and costs of a contract only when the job is finished
A method only for payroll

questions.explanation: Completed-contract defers profit recognition until the job ends. It contrasts with percentage-of-completion, which recognizes profit as work progresses.

questions.question: Who may typically claim a mechanic's lien on a residential project?

answers.text: Only the property owner
A party who furnished labor or materials for the improvement under contract
Any neighbor affected by construction noise
Only a licensed attorney

questions.explanation: Lien rights generally belong to those who furnished labor or materials for the improvement. Neighbors and unrelated parties have no lien right from that work.

questions.question: What is the key difference between insurance and a surety bond regarding expected losses?

answers.text: Insurers expect no losses ever
Bonds are a form of gambling
Neither involves payment of claims
Insurance pools expected losses across many insureds; a surety expects no loss and seeks reimbursement from the principal

questions.explanation: Insurance pricing assumes some insureds will have losses. Surety underwriting assumes the principal will perform, and the principal indemnifies the surety if it must pay.

questions.question: What records must an employer keep to comply with wage-and-hour requirements?

answers.text: Only the total annual payroll for the whole company
Only records of employees who filed complaints
Accurate records of hours worked each day and week, rates of pay, and wages paid for each employee
No records, if employees are paid a salary

questions.explanation: Time and payroll records prove compliance with minimum wage and overtime rules and are required to be retained. In disputes, missing records are held against the employer's position.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an employer identification number (EIN) for a residential building business?

answers.text: It is the business's building permit
It grades the business's credit
It is the federal tax identification number used for payroll, tax filings, and business accounts
It replaces the state license

questions.explanation: An EIN identifies the business to the IRS for payroll taxes, returns, and banking. It does not replace state licensure or permits.

questions.question: Why must an employer deposit withheld employee taxes promptly rather than using them for business expenses?

answers.text: Withheld amounts are optional until the end of the year
Withheld amounts are trust funds belonging to the employee and government, and misuse brings severe penalties and possible personal liability
Deposits are only required for corporations, not sole proprietors
Late deposits simply earn the business extra interest income

questions.explanation: Amounts withheld from wages are held in trust for the government. Responsible persons can be personally liable for unpaid trust fund taxes.

questions.question: Which South Carolina body licenses residential builders, home inspectors, and residential specialty contractors?

answers.text: The South Carolina Residential Builders Commission
The county tax assessor
The local building inspections department
The South Carolina Secretary of State alone

questions.explanation: The Residential Builders Commission, within the state's licensing structure, issues and regulates those residential licenses. Local offices handle permits and inspections, not state licensure.

questions.question: Under the federal Fair Labor Standards Act concept, which employees are generally entitled to overtime pay?

answers.text: Nonexempt employees, paid at least one and one-half times their regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek
Only employees who work on holidays
Every salaried employee regardless of duties
Employees who volunteer to work extra hours

questions.explanation: The FLSA generally requires overtime at time-and-a-half over 40 hours in a workweek for nonexempt employees. Certain executive, administrative, and professional employees may be exempt if salary and duties tests are met.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a fixed-price (lump sum) contract from the contractor's estimating perspective?

answers.text: The contractor bears no cost risk because the owner pays all overruns
The price adjusts automatically with every material price change
The contractor is paid only for hours worked, with no set total
The contractor agrees to complete described work for a set total price and bears the risk if actual costs exceed the estimate

questions.explanation: In a lump sum contract the total price is fixed for the defined scope, so estimating errors fall on the contractor. Scope changes are handled through change orders.

questions.question: Why might a lender require evidence of insurance before funding a construction loan draw?

answers.text: To delay the project
Insurance evidence is a formality with no purpose
To confirm its collateral, the partially built structure, is protected against loss
To set the interest rate daily

questions.explanation: The structure under construction is the lender's collateral. Proof of builder's risk and liability coverage protects that collateral during the loan.

questions.question: A supplier delivered materials that were never incorporated into the project and were returned unused. What is the likely effect on a lien claim for those materials?

answers.text: The lien amount doubles
The lien may fail for those materials because they did not improve the property
The lien automatically attaches to another property
No effect at all

questions.explanation: Lien rights rest on improving the property. Materials returned and never used in the improvement generally do not support a lien.

questions.question: Which coverage protects a contractor when a third party claims bodily injury or property damage caused by the contractor's operations?

answers.text: Workers' compensation insurance
A payment bond
Commercial general liability insurance
Builder's risk insurance only

questions.explanation: Commercial general liability covers third-party bodily injury and property damage claims arising from operations. Workers' compensation instead covers injuries to the contractor's own employees.

questions.question: A homeowner says, 'I will pay $500 if you inspect and report on the roof by Friday,' and the inspector agrees. The homeowner's statement is best described as what?

answers.text: An acceptance
A counteroffer to an earlier price
A revocation
An offer, because it proposes terms the other party can accept to form a contract

questions.explanation: An offer is a proposal with definite terms that, if accepted, creates a contract. The inspector's agreement would be the acceptance of those terms.

washington-home-inspector-state.quiz_title: Washington Home Inspector State Portion (Laws and Rules) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement about Washington exam retakes is correct in concept?

answers.text: A candidate who fails a portion must retake and pass that portion, paying the applicable exam fee for the retake
A failed portion is passed automatically after 30 days
Both portions must always be retaken even if one was passed
Retakes are free and unlimited without scheduling

questions.explanation: Only the failed portion needs to be retaken and passed, and retakes carry the applicable fee and scheduling requirements.

questions.question: What is the core education concept a Washington applicant must complete before licensure regarding fundamentals instruction?

answers.text: An approved fundamentals course of 120 hours of home inspection training
A 12-hour weekend seminar of the applicant's choosing
Any 120 hours of general college credit in any subject
No classroom instruction if the applicant has construction experience

questions.explanation: Washington's pathway includes an approved 120-hour fundamentals course in home inspection. Unrelated college credit or informal experience does not substitute for that approved instruction.

questions.question: Who holds final regulatory authority over Washington home inspector licenses, including discipline?

answers.text: Each client's real estate broker
A private trade association chosen by the inspector
The county sheriff
The Director of the Department of Licensing

questions.explanation: The Director of the Department of Licensing is the regulator for home inspector licensure and discipline. Private associations and transaction participants do not exercise that authority.

questions.question: Before performing a Washington home inspection, what agreement concept should be in place with the client?

answers.text: A written pre-inspection agreement describing the scope and terms of the inspection
A verbal promise that the inspector will find every defect
A purchase and sale agreement signed by both buyer and seller
A hold-harmless note written by the listing agent

questions.explanation: Washington practice expects a written pre-inspection agreement before the work begins, setting out scope, standards, and terms. It aligns expectations and documents what the inspection will and will not cover.

questions.question: What access expectation applies to attics and crawl spaces under the Washington standards?

answers.text: Inspectors enter readily accessible attics and crawl spaces when it can be done safely and without damage
Inspectors must cut new access openings where none exist
Attics and crawl spaces are never part of any inspection
Inspectors enter only if the seller requests it

questions.explanation: Where access is provided and entry is safe, attics and crawl spaces are inspected as part of the structural and systems review. Inspectors are not required to create openings or enter unsafe spaces, but must report such limits.

questions.question: An applicant is 17 years old and asks about a basic eligibility concept for Washington licensure. Which requirement is relevant?

answers.text: There is no minimum age in Washington
An applicant must be at least 18 years old
An applicant must be at least 25 years old
Age matters only for renewals, not initial licensure

questions.explanation: Washington requires an applicant to be at least 18 years old. The applicant would need to wait until meeting that basic eligibility requirement.

questions.question: A consumer asks how to verify a Washington home inspector is licensed. The best answer is:

answers.text: Trust the inspector's business card alone
Ask the seller's agent to vouch verbally
Licenses cannot be verified by the public
Check the inspector's license status through the Department of Licensing's public license lookup

questions.explanation: Licensure is a public record maintained by the Department, and consumers can verify status through its lookup resources.

questions.question: Which Washington organisms or conditions fall under the wood-destroying organism concern for inspectors?

answers.text: Only honeybees in wall voids
Termites, carpenter ants, wood-boring beetles, and wood decay fungi, among others
Only rodents and birds
Garden weeds touching a fence

questions.explanation: Washington WDO practice centers on insects that destroy wood and on wood decay fungi, not on nuisance wildlife or yard weeds.

questions.question: An applicant who failed the Washington state portion but passed the national portion asks whether licensure can issue now. What is correct?

answers.text: Yes, the national pass is sufficient for Washington practice
Yes, if the applicant promises to retake the state portion within five years
No, both portions must be passed, each at the required scaled score
Yes, if the applicant completed extra field training

questions.explanation: Washington requires passing each portion separately at a scaled score of 70. Field training or promises to retest do not substitute for the missing state-portion pass.

questions.question: During a Washington inspection, no water comes from a showerhead although other fixtures work. What is the proper approach?

answers.text: Report the inoperative fixture and recommend repair or further evaluation
Disassemble the shower valve to find the cause
Ignore it because other fixtures function
Reduce the inspection fee automatically

questions.explanation: An inoperative fixture within scope is reported as a defect with a recommendation for correction; disassembly is beyond a visual inspection.

questions.question: Under Washington's Standards, which interior condition is a safety issue that must be reported?

answers.text: A missing handrail on an open staircase
Faded paint in a bedroom closet
A squeaky interior door hinge
Carpet that is worn but intact in a hallway

questions.explanation: Missing handrails on stairs present a fall hazard and are reportable safety defects, unlike cosmetic wear.

questions.question: What must a Washington inspector report about the electrical service when the service capacity cannot be determined?

answers.text: Guess the amperage from the age of the home
State that the capacity was not determined and note what limited the determination
Omit any mention of service capacity
Report the capacity of a typical neighboring home

questions.explanation: When a required item cannot be verified, the inspector describes the limitation rather than guessing or omitting the system from the report.

questions.question: An inspector observes a horizontal crack with measurable displacement in a foundation wall. What reporting approach fits the Washington standards?

answers.text: Call it cosmetic and exclude it from the report
Provide a full engineering design for the repair in the report
Guarantee the wall will not move further
Report the cracking and displacement as a significant structural observation and recommend evaluation by a qualified professional

questions.explanation: Displaced foundation cracking is a material structural finding that belongs in the report with a recommendation for qualified evaluation. It is neither cosmetic nor a subject for guarantees or engineering design by the inspector.

questions.question: A Washington inspector cannot operate the furnace because the gas supply is shut off. What does the Standards of Practice require?

answers.text: Report that the system was not operated and state the reason
Turn on the utility gas supply at the meter
Assume the furnace works because it looks new
Skip the heating section of the report entirely

questions.explanation: Systems that are shut down are not turned on by the inspector; the report states the system was not inspected or operated and why.

questions.question: Furniture and stored boxes completely block access to an electrical panel. Under the Washington standards, how should the inspector handle this limitation?

answers.text: Move all of the owner's belongings without permission
Report the panel as satisfactory without seeing it
Note in the report that the panel was not inspected because access was blocked
Cancel the entire inspection and leave without a report

questions.explanation: Inspectors are not required to move personal property to gain access, but uninspected items and the reason must be disclosed in the report. Claiming an unseen component is satisfactory is improper.

questions.question: Vegetation grows directly against siding and shrubs block a crawl space vent. How should the inspector address this under the exterior and related standards?

answers.text: Trim the vegetation personally and bill the seller
Treat heavy vegetation contact as purely decorative
Report vegetation conditions that trap moisture against the home, damage materials, or block ventilation as items to correct
Refuse to inspect any home with landscaping

questions.explanation: Vegetation in contact with the structure or blocking vents creates moisture and pest-conducive conditions and impedes ventilation, so it is reported as a correctable condition. Landscaping work itself is not performed by the inspector.

questions.question: What cooling-system duty applies under the Washington Standards of Practice when outdoor temperatures are too low to operate air conditioning safely?

answers.text: Operate the compressor anyway to complete the checklist
Report the cooling system as defective
State that the system was not operated because of temperature and note the limitation
Waive the entire mechanical inspection

questions.explanation: Inspectors do not operate cooling equipment when conditions could damage it; they document the limitation in the report instead.

questions.question: A Washington home inspector holds both a home inspector license and a structural pest inspector license. When performing a complete WDO inspection, the inspector acts under:

answers.text: The home inspector license alone
The structural pest inspector license and its reporting requirements, as a distinct regulated service
No license, because holding two cancels both
The real estate broker's license

questions.explanation: Dual licensees perform complete WDO work under the agriculture licensing framework, which is a distinct service from the home inspection.

questions.question: A Washington inspector lets the license expire and keeps performing inspections for a fee. What is the licensing problem?

answers.text: There is no problem if clients consent
Only the first expired-license inspection is a violation
Performing home inspections for a fee without a current license is unlicensed activity subject to discipline
Expired licenses remain valid for two extra years

questions.explanation: A current license is required to inspect for a fee; practicing on an expired license is unlicensed activity and grounds for enforcement.

questions.question: An inspector performs an inspection substantially below the Washington standards of practice and omits major required systems without explanation. Besides a dissatisfied client, what exposure does the inspector face?

answers.text: None, because standards are merely suggestions
Discipline by the licensing department for failing to meet the required standards of practice
Only loss of trade association membership
Automatic transfer of the client to another inspector

questions.explanation: The Washington Standards of Practice are enforceable minimums, not optional suggestions. Materially falling below them can support department discipline.

illinois-home-inspector-section.quiz_title: Illinois Home Inspector Licensing Exam — Illinois Section Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which inspector action most clearly complies with the Illinois Human Rights Act in everyday practice?

answers.text: Offering different levels of thoroughness based on a buyer religion
Quoting higher fees because of a client disability
Providing the same professional service, scope, and honest reporting to every client regardless of protected characteristics
Steering clients toward or away from homes based on national origin

questions.explanation: Equal professional service — same scope, care, fees based on legitimate factors, and honest reporting for all — is the practical meaning of fair-housing compliance for an inspector.

questions.question: Which fee practice is most consistent with inspector independence?

answers.text: A bonus for finding no defects
A discount if the buyer waives the report
Payment from the seller for a favorable summary
A flat inspection fee agreed in advance that does not depend on findings or whether the sale closes

questions.explanation: A predetermined fee unrelated to results or closing preserves neutrality. Payments tied to findings or closing give the inspector a stake in the outcome.

questions.question: What is the record retention principle for Illinois inspectors under Part 1410 concepts?

answers.text: Records may be discarded the day after delivery
Inspection records, agreements, and reports must be retained for a required period and be producible to IDFPR as required
Only photographs need to be kept, never reports
Records belong to the seller and must be surrendered

questions.explanation: Retention rules preserve the evidence of what was agreed, inspected, and reported, for client follow-up and Department review. Early destruction defeats accountability.

questions.question: What about vapor retarders in Illinois inspections?

answers.text: They must be removed to check behind them
They must be laboratory tested on every job
Where visible in readily accessible unfinished areas, vapor retarders are observed and described as part of insulation and ventilation reporting
They are inspected only in new construction

questions.explanation: Vapor retarders are evaluated only as visible components of accessible areas. Removal and laboratory testing are outside the noninvasive scope.

questions.question: How must roof drainage components be handled in Illinois?

answers.text: They must be cleaned by the inspector during the visit
They must be tested by running a hose for an hour
They are ignored because they are not part of the roof
Gutters and downspouts that are present are inspected and their observed condition reported

questions.explanation: Roof drainage is part of the roofing system observation. Cleaning or flood-testing gutters is not required; their visible condition is reported.

questions.question: What best explains the consumer-protection purpose of licensing home inspectors in Illinois?

answers.text: To set minimum competence and accountability for a service buyers rely on in a major purchase
To guarantee every home sold is defect-free
To fix the price of inspections statewide
To replace the need for any disclosure by sellers

questions.explanation: Licensing establishes verified qualifications, standards, and a discipline system for an influential service. It does not guarantee a defect-free home or set prices.

questions.question: A buyer who uses a wheelchair asks the inspector to describe accessibility features and barriers observed in the home. The inspector should:

answers.text: Describe the observed physical features and barriers factually as part of a professional inspection
Refuse because disability may not be discussed at all
Guarantee the home complies with accessibility law
Tell the buyer to look only in 'disabled housing'

questions.explanation: Factually reporting door widths, steps, and other observed physical features the client asks about is legitimate service. Refusing service or channeling the buyer by disability would be discriminatory.

questions.question: An inspector notices a sagging ceiling with water staining. What does Illinois require?

answers.text: Report the observed sagging and staining as conditions present at the inspection
Open the ceiling to find the source as part of the standard inspection
Paint over the stain to test if it returns
Attribute the stain to a specific hidden leak with certainty
