A detached wiper leaves the primary seal exposed to weather and the rim space open. The strongest distractor — 'Nothing, because the primary seal alone provides all required sealing' — fails because the secondary seal is a working part of the sealing system — it sheds rainwater off the primary seal and closes the rim vapour space — not a spare that can be left failed.

questions.question: An owner-operator has just acquired a tank with no inspection history. What is the best-practice first step?

answers.text: Place the tank in service indefinitely without inspection because it has not leaked
Establish a baseline by reviewing any available records and performing a thorough initial inspection
Rely solely on the seller's verbal assurance of condition
Defer all inspection until the next scheduled turnaround several years away

questions.explanation: Establish a baseline by reviewing any available records and performing a thorough initial inspection — this is correct because without history there is no basis for intervals or remaining-life judgments, so a documented baseline inspection is needed first. The strongest alternative, 'Place the tank in service indefinitely without inspection because it has not leaked', loses because verbal assurance loses because RP 575 practice requires objective evidence and records, not unsupported statements.

questions.question: Globular transfer in GMAW is best avoided on a critical tank weld mainly because it tends to produce what?

answers.text: A fine, stable droplet stream
Complete absence of spatter
Automatic slag coverage of the bead
Irregular large drops, heavy spatter and inconsistent fusion

questions.explanation: Large gravity-driven drops make globular transfer erratic and prone to spatter and fusion problems. The strongest alternative — A fine, stable droplet stream — loses because a fine stable stream describes spray transfer, not globular transfer.

questions.question: An inspector is told a tank had bottom settlement near the shell, but the only record is a single elevation reading at the center. What is the correct evaluation response?

answers.text: Require a proper profile or survey around the perimeter and across the bottom so the settled zone near the shell can actually be located and measured
Accept the center reading as proof the edge is acceptable
Judge settlement solely from the age of the tank
Judge settlement solely from whether product has leaked

questions.explanation: A is correct because settlement near the shell is a perimeter and profile condition that a center point cannot characterize. The strongest distractor loses because the center can be level while a damaging dip exists at the edge.

questions.question: Shell settlement survey points for Tank 2205 (diameter 120 ft) must be spaced no more than 32 ft apart around the circumference, with no fewer than 8 points in total. How many survey points are required?

answers.text: 10 points
16 points
12 points
8 points

questions.explanation: Circumference = π × D = 3.1416 × 120 = 377.0 ft. Points by spacing = 377.0 / 32 = 11.78, rounded up to 12 points. Compare with the 8-point minimum: max(12, 8) = 12 points. Rounding down, or using a 50 ft spacing, would leave gaps wider than permitted.

questions.question: Pits in Tank 1806 intersect a straight line within an 8 in. (200 mm) length with individual pit lengths of 0.55 in., 0.50 in., 0.45 in., 0.60 in. The acceptance limit for the summed pit length in any 8 in. is 2.00 in. What is the determination?

answers.text: Acceptable — summed length 2.10 in. is within the 2.00 in. limit
Acceptable — summed length 0.55 in. (largest pit only) is within the limit
Not acceptable — summed length 2.10 in. exceeds an 8.00 in. limit
Not acceptable — summed length 2.10 in. exceeds the 2.00 in. limit

questions.explanation: Add the pit lengths lying within the 8 in. (200 mm) length: 0.55 + 0.50 + 0.45 + 0.60 = 2.10 in. Compare with the 2.00 in. limit: 2.10 > 2.00 in. by 0.10 in., so the pitting pattern fails this summed-length criterion. Counting only the largest pit would incorrectly pass it.

questions.question: Tank 808 has a measured shell-course thickness of 0.580 in. The calculated t-min for the evaluated fill height is 0.595 in. What is the correct continued-service determination and margin?

answers.text: Not acceptable — short by 0.015 in.
Acceptable — margin 0.015 in. above t-min
Not acceptable — short by 0.055 in.
Acceptable with no margin

questions.explanation: Compare actual with required: 0.580 - 0.595 = -0.015 in. Because the result is negative, the measured thickness is 0.015 in. below t-min = 0.595 in., so the course is not acceptable for continued service at the evaluated fill height and the fill height must be reduced or the course repaired or replaced.

questions.question: The widely used protection criterion expressed as a potential more negative than a stated value versus a copper/copper-sulfate electrode is fundamentally a check that what condition exists?

answers.text: The structure has been polarized sufficiently negative to indicate cathodic protection is being achieved
The structure is carrying no current of any kind
The soil has been dried to a nonconductive state
The anodes have been completely consumed

questions.explanation: The key is right because the negative-potential criterion is evidence the steel surface has been polarized into the protected range. The consumed-anodes distractor loses because fully consumed anodes would mean protection is ending, not that the criterion is satisfied.

questions.question: At a post-lining inspection before the tank is filled, the inspector finds areas of lining that are soft and tacky well after the expected cure time. The best interpretation is what?

answers.text: Softness is the desired final state for flexible service
The areas will certainly cure once product covers them
Cure is incomplete in those areas — from mix ratio error, low temperature, or expired material — and they are not ready for service until the cause is corrected and cure is verified
Tackiness proves extra resin was applied, which is always beneficial

questions.explanation: The key is right because persistent tackiness signals a cure defect with a discoverable cause that must be fixed before immersion. The product-will-cure-it distractor loses because product exposure of under-cured film causes damage rather than completing the cure.

questions.question: Tank 305 (diameter 15.0 m) stores process water with specific gravity 0.74. The evaluated shell thickness is 7.0 mm, allowable stress S = 160 MPa and joint efficiency E = 0.85. Using the rearranged SI minimum-thickness relationship, what is the maximum permitted liquid fill height H?
questions.explanation: Rearrange t-min = 4.9·D·(H-0.3)·G / (S·E) to H = t·S·E / (4.9·D·G) + 0.3. Substitute: H = 7.0 × 160 × 0.85 / (4.9 × 15.0 × 0.74) + 0.3 = 952.0 / 54.39 + 0.3 = 17.50 + 0.3 = 17.80 m, about 17.8 m. Omitting the 0.3 m term understates the height.

questions.question: What does a satisfactory external inspection NOT establish about a tank?

answers.text: That the shell exterior was examined
That the roof and vents were checked
That the foundation showed no obvious distress
That the tank bottom is fit for a full further internal interval, because the bottom's condition cannot be fully determined from outside

questions.explanation: External success cannot certify the hidden bottom. Treating it as proof of bottom fitness is the scope error that lets floor failures develop unseen.

questions.question: Concentrated pits form under a tank bottom where groundwater chemistry varies along a drainage path beneath the pad, while adjacent areas are sound. Which in-scope mechanism describes attack driven by differing chemical conditions in contact with the steel?

answers.text: Brittle fracture driven by groundwater
Caustic stress corrosion cracking from soil alone in every case
Uniform atmospheric rusting of the underside
Concentration cell corrosion, where differences in the environment at the metal surface create anodic areas that corrode preferentially

questions.explanation: D is correct because concentration cells form where oxygen or chemistry differs point to point, localizing attack. The strongest distractor loses because the finding is localized and cell-driven, not uniform rusting.

api-936-refractory-personnel.quiz_title: API 936 Refractory Personnel Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How is a ramming mix typically placed and consolidated?

answers.text: It is sprayed at high velocity so compaction occurs only on impact
It is poured as a self-leveling liquid that needs no compaction
It is unrolled and left uncompacted so it remains a soft insulation layer
It is placed in relatively thin layers and compacted by pneumatic or hand ramming to achieve density

questions.explanation: Ramming mixes depend on layer-by-layer mechanical compaction to develop density and eliminate voids. The strongest distractor, self-leveling pouring, is wrong because a mix that flows and levels itself is a flowable castable, not a ramming mix.

questions.question: What is the framework reason materials from different families are not interchangeable in a lining design?

answers.text: Families are interchangeable; only brand names differ
Each family differs in bonding, placement, density, and service behavior, so the design's performance assumptions are family- and product-specific
Interchangeability is prevented only by purchasing policy, not by technical reasons
Materials become interchangeable once they reach operating temperature

questions.explanation: Non-interchangeability is technical, not bureaucratic. Firing does not erase differences in density, chemistry, and structure that were built into each family's design role.

questions.question: What is the panel's role when a new anchor type is introduced to an established crew?

answers.text: It provides the first controlled opportunity to install and place around the new anchor and to examine coverage and consolidation before production use
It proves the new anchor needs no examination
It allows the crew to skip learning the anchor's installation requirements
It transfers the manufacturer's anchor testing to the field unchanged

questions.explanation: New hardware changes installation behavior even for experienced crews. Skipping the learning and examination, reflected in the distractors, would debut an unproven detail in the vessel.

questions.question: Why should batch size be matched to the placement rate?

answers.text: So the mixer is always completely full regardless of crew size
So fewer batch records need to be kept
So each batch can be placed and consolidated within its working time
Batch size has no relationship to placement rate

questions.explanation: Material begins changing as soon as water is added, so a batch larger than the crew can place in time will stiffen before it is fully placed. The strongest distractor, always filling the mixer completely, is wrong because mixer capacity is a maximum, not a requirement, and it ignores working time.

questions.question: What is the first principle for repairing a defective area in a regenerator head?

answers.text: Remove the defective lining back to sound, well-bonded material before reinstalling
Cover the defect with a thin cosmetic skim
Repair only the visible surface regardless of subsurface condition
Patch new material over loose or delaminated lining

questions.explanation: A repair bonded to unsound material inherits the failure; sound substrate material is the foundation of a durable repair. The strongest distractor — "Patch new material over loose or delaminated lining" — is wrong because a skim over a delamination leaves the separation in place beneath the patch.

questions.question: What feature of brick construction most affects its QC compared with a monolithic lining?

answers.text: Brick linings have no joints, so QC focuses only on anchor welding
The many mortar joints between units must be controlled for joint thickness, mortar consistency, and unit alignment, since joints are potential weak paths
Brick units change size after laying, so QC measures them only after firing
Brick cannot be inspected until the unit has operated at full temperature

questions.explanation: Brick systems under API 975 live or fail at their joints and coursing, unlike a jointless monolithic mass. The strongest distractor, that brick has no joints, denies the defining feature of an assembled shaped system.

questions.question: Which packaging condition on receipt most directly threatens a dry castable's quality?

answers.text: A scuffed outer pallet wrap with bags intact
Torn or punctured bags that have allowed moisture to reach the mix
A label printed in a different color than usual
Bags stacked in a different orientation than expected

questions.explanation: Damage matters in proportion to exposure of the material itself. Scuffed outer wrap with intact bags is cosmetic; breached bags expose hygroscopic dry mix to the moisture that degrades it.

questions.question: How does material qualification differ from production or as-installed sampling?

answers.text: Qualification qualifies the material before the job, while production sampling verifies the work as it is installed
Qualification happens after dryout, while production sampling happens before purchase
They are the same activity performed under two different names
Qualification verifies the installer, while production sampling verifies only the manufacturer

questions.explanation: The timing and object differ: qualification approves the material in advance; production sampling checks material as placed during the job. The strongest distractor reverses that timing.

questions.question: What must happen to a defective anchor weld found before lining installation?

answers.text: The defective weld must be repaired or the anchor rewelded before lining covers it
The lining should cover it quickly so it is not seen again
The anchor should be bent over flat and left in place
The defect should be recorded and the area lined without repair

questions.explanation: Defective welds are repaired or rewelded while they are still accessible. Recording a defect and covering it anyway leaves a known weak anchor in service.

questions.question: What QC check during mixing verifies that a fiber castable is behaving as intended before placement?

answers.text: Checking only the color of the dry bags
Weighing the mixer before and after the shift
Inspecting the cured lining weeks later as the first check
Consistency/flow checking of the fresh mix, which reveals both water problems and fiber-related workability problems

questions.explanation: Fresh-state checks are the last chance to catch a batch problem before it is built into the lining. The strongest distractor, waiting for cured inspection, is wrong because by then a defective batch is installed and its internal distribution cannot be corrected.

questions.question: What role do anchors play in a rammed plastic lining, and how does installation respond?

answers.text: Voids around anchors in plastic help the lining expand
Plastic should be kept clear of anchors to avoid damaging them
Anchors are unnecessary in plastic linings because the material is sticky
Anchors support and retain the lining, and plastic must be rammed or hand packed tightly around them so they are fully embedded without voids

questions.explanation: Retention only works through full embedment. The strongest distractor, that stickiness replaces anchors, confuses placement convenience with the mechanical support anchors provide in service.

questions.question: Whose instructions govern the curing method and duration for a specific castable product?

answers.text: The refractory manufacturer's instructions for that product
The personal preference of the individual installer
A general rule copied from an unrelated lining material
The heating contractor's dryout schedule alone

questions.explanation: Each product has its own water, placement, and curing requirements set by its manufacturer. A rule for a different material cannot substitute, because formulations differ.

questions.question: A shipment arrives and its identification does not match the certification paperwork. The documentation-correct action is to:

answers.text: Install it and fix the paperwork later
Discard the certification and proceed
Hold the material from installation, document the mismatch, and resolve traceability before use
Relabel it in the field to match

questions.explanation: A mismatch breaks traceability, so the material must be held and the discrepancy resolved and documented before use. Relabeling in the field would falsify the traceability chain.

questions.question: A lab uses excess mixing water to make specimens easier to form, beyond the intended range. What is the likely consequence?

answers.text: Specimen properties can shift, so the results may not represent the material as it will be installed
Excess water guarantees higher strength in every case
The specification comparison becomes more reliable
Results will be identical regardless of water content

questions.explanation: Water content influences properties. Intentionally departing from the intended mixing makes the specimen unrepresentative and the comparison unreliable.

questions.question: A designer reviews two zones of the same lining, one much hotter at the anchor depth than the other. What material approach follows?

answers.text: Both zones must always use the least heat-resistant alloy
The hotter zone needs a more heat-resistant alloy than the cooler zone
The cooler zone needs the more heat-resistant alloy
Anchor material need is identical regardless of temperature

questions.explanation: Hotter anchor locations require more heat-resistant alloys. Using the least resistant alloy everywhere is wrong because it would fail first where anchors are hottest.

questions.question: How does casting differ from gunning in how material reaches its final position, and why does that change the defect focus?

answers.text: Casting and gunning have identical defect profiles in all respects
Neither method has characteristic defects worth distinguishing

Casting flows and is vibrated into forms, so its characteristic defects are cold joints, voids, and segregation, while gunning's impact placement makes rebound and laminations its characteristic concerns
Casting's main defect is rebound, and gunning's main defect is cold joints

questions.explanation: Placement physics dictates defect families. The strongest distractor swaps the families — rebound belongs to gunning's impact and cold joints to casting's interruptions.

questions.question: What condition of the substrate temperature in a rotary kiln section can affect placement on a freezing morning?

answers.text: A frozen or near-frozen substrate can impair bonding and curing, so conditions must be brought within the procedure's requirements
Ice on the substrate melts into useful mixing water
Substrate temperature never affects a hot-service lining
Frozen substrates improve bond by roughness

questions.explanation: Bond forms at installation temperatures, not service temperatures, so a frozen interface is a real defect risk. The strongest distractor — "Frozen substrates improve bond by roughness" — is wrong because ice at the interface prevents direct bond to the substrate.

questions.question: In an API 936 refractory quality program, who is primarily responsible for defining the project requirements and specifications that the work must meet?

answers.text: The owner
The contractor/applicator
The manufacturer
The inspector

questions.explanation: The owner defines requirements and specifications, setting the criteria everyone else works to. The contractor executes to those requirements and the inspector verifies against them, so neither of those roles replaces the owner as the source of requirements.

questions.question: An applicator's qualification is approved. Midway through production the specified material is discontinued and a replacement is approved by the owner. What follows for the applicator?

answers.text: The applicator should demonstrate the replacement material, through requalification as directed, before installing it in production
The applicator installs the replacement under the old qualification without discussion
The replacement needs no one's review because it is newer
Production stops permanently with no path forward

questions.explanation: A material change changes a qualified variable, so demonstration must be renewed for it. Installing under the old qualification, the strongest distractor, assumes two different materials place identically.

questions.question: At a wall base, an inspector finds a soft, sandy layer buried under sound gunned material. What most likely happened?

answers.text: The layer is a cold joint from interrupted casting
Excess vibration compacted the base layer too much
The base was intentionally designed with a soft starter layer
Rebound collected at the base and was gunned over instead of being removed

questions.explanation: A buried sandy layer at the base is trapped rebound — gunning's characteristic entrapment defect. The strongest distractor, a casting cold joint, is wrong because this is gunned work and the soft sandy nature identifies rebound, not a placement plane.

frm-part-i.quiz_title: FRM Part I (Financial Risk Manager) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the slope of the security market line?

answers.text: The risk-free rate
The market risk premium, E(Rm) - Rf
The beta of the market portfolio, which is zero
The standard deviation of the market

questions.explanation: Rising from beta 0 to beta 1 raises expected return from Rf to E(Rm), so the slope is E(Rm) - Rf.

questions.question: Why does binomial variance np(1-p) peak at p = 0.50 for fixed n?

answers.text: Because the mean np is largest at p = 0.50
Because trials become dependent near p = 0.50
Because p(1-p) is maximised at p = 0.50, where outcomes are most uncertain
It does not peak there; variance grows monotonically in p

questions.explanation: For fixed n, variance is proportional to p(1-p), a parabola with maximum at p = 0.5 (value 0.25). Near p = 0 or p = 1 outcomes are nearly certain, so variance is small even though the mean keeps rising with p.

questions.question: Storage costs are paid by the spot holder carrying a commodity. In forward pricing they:

answers.text: Decrease F0 by the full storage amount
Increase F0, because the short who delivers later must be compensated for the cost of holding the asset until delivery
Have no effect if the commodity is storable
Are paid by the exchange to both parties

questions.explanation: Storage is a cost of carry added to spot (along with financing, net of benefits): higher storage means a higher forward price, other things equal.

questions.question: A covered call combines long stock with a short call. The writer's trade-off is to:

answers.text: Collect premium income while capping upside above the strike
Gain unlimited upside while eliminating downside risk
Avoid owning the stock while receiving dividends
Hedge a short stock position against a price rise

questions.explanation: Writing a call against owned shares brings in premium that cushions small declines. In exchange, shares may be called away above the strike, capping further gains.

questions.question: A bond has a Macaulay duration of 2.90 years and a yield of 5%. What is its modified duration?

answers.text: 2.36 years
2.90 years
2.76 years
3.04 years

questions.explanation: Modified duration = Macaulay / (1+y) = 2.90 / 1.05 = 2.76 years. Using Macaulay directly would overstate price sensitivity.

questions.question: Which statement about financial disasters is most accurate as a general lesson?

answers.text: Most combine an adverse market move with pre-existing leverage, concentration, and control or governance failures
Most are caused by a single unforeseeable market move in otherwise well-controlled firms
Market moves alone explain losses, so controls are secondary
Disasters occur only in institutions that use derivatives

questions.explanation: Post-mortems consistently show market moves are the trigger, but leverage, concentration, concealment, and governance determine whether the move becomes a disaster.

questions.question: Which scenario combines credit and market risk in a way managers must handle carefully?

answers.text: A plain cash deposit in a vault
A fire in an office building
A derivative whose value moves with market prices and whose counterparty may default when the contract is in the firm's favour
A change in the firm's logo

questions.explanation: Derivatives create market-driven exposure whose size changes over time, and loss occurs if the counterparty defaults when replacement cost is positive. This counterparty credit risk depends on market movements.

questions.question: The autocorrelation function of an MA(1) process typically:

answers.text: Decays slowly over many lags
Cuts off after lag 1
Rises to 1
Is undefined

questions.explanation: An MA(1) only shares shocks up to one period apart, so autocorrelation is nonzero at lag 1 and essentially zero beyond it.

questions.question: When a swap is novated to a central counterparty, the effect is similar to futures clearing in that:

answers.text: The CCP becomes counterparty to both sides, margining replaces bilateral exposure, and netting can apply across positions
All future payments are cancelled
The swap becomes an equity contract
No margin is ever required

questions.explanation: Cleared swaps gain the CCP protections described for other cleared products: novation, netting, initial and variation margin, and a default waterfall.

questions.question: Which feature most distinguishes exchange-traded contracts from OTC contracts?

answers.text: Customized terms negotiated privately between two parties
Standardized terms traded on a centralized venue, typically with clearing and margining
Absence of any margin or collateral requirements
Single settlement negotiated at maturity with no daily settlement

questions.explanation: Exchange-traded contracts have standardized size, maturity and terms and trade on a venue, whereas OTC contracts are privately negotiated and customized.

questions.question: Barbell versus bullet portfolios of equal duration: which typically has more convexity and why?

answers.text: The bullet, because it has shorter maturity
The barbell, because its cash flows are more dispersed around duration
They always have identical convexity
The bullet, because its cash flows are concentrated

questions.explanation: Dispersion of cash flows raises convexity at a given duration. The barbell's short- and long-end cash flows are more spread out than the bullet's concentrated intermediate flows.

questions.question: What happens to a long portfolio's parametric VaR when volatility doubles, mean and value unchanged?

answers.text: VaR falls by half
VaR quadruples
VaR doubles
VaR is unchanged

questions.explanation: Parametric VaR = (z*sigma - mu) x value is linear in sigma (with mu near zero), so doubling volatility doubles VaR; the relationship is linear, not quadratic.

questions.question: A portfolio returns 12%, exactly equal to its CAPM-required return. Its Jensen's alpha and interpretation are:

answers.text: Alpha is 12%; performance is exceptional
Alpha is zero; performance matches the return required for its systematic risk
Alpha is negative; the manager underperformed
Alpha cannot be zero if the return is positive

questions.explanation: Alpha = 12% - 12% = 0%. The portfolio delivered precisely the return CAPM requires for its beta.

questions.question: Output table: Intercept 5.0 (SE 1.0), Slope  -2.0 (SE 0.5). Predicted Y at X=3 and the slope t-statistic are:

answers.text: Y-hat 11 and t -0.25
Y-hat -1 and t -4.0
Y-hat 5 and t 4.0
Y-hat 0 and t -2.0

questions.question: The correlation between spot and futures price changes is 0.8, the spot volatility is 20% and the futures volatility is 25%. What is the minimum-variance hedge ratio?

answers.text: 16.00, because volatilities are multiplied without dividing
1.00, because the volatility ratio is inverted
0.80, because the hedge ratio always equals the correlation

questions.explanation: h* = ρ × (σS / σF) = 0.8 × (20 / 25) = 0.8 × 0.800 = 0.64. The ratio scales the futures position to the relative volatility of the two prices.

questions.question: In a one-step binomial model, the stock can rise by factor u = 1.25 or fall by factor d = 0.90, and e^(r*dt) = 1.0000 (r = 0). What is the risk-neutral probability of an up move?
questions.explanation: Risk-neutral probability p = (e^(r*dt) - d)/(u - d) = (1.0000 - 0.90)/(1.25 - 0.90) = 0.1000/0.35 = 0.2857. Inverting the formula or using 1 - p gives the distractors.

questions.question: A trader is long 2,000 calls (position 3) with delta 0.35 per option (one share per option). How many shares must the trader hold to be delta-neutral?

answers.text: 800 shares
-700 shares
700 shares
-350 shares

questions.explanation: Delta hedging requires holding -delta per option: -(0.35) x 2,000 = -700 shares. A negative sign means a short share position; for long puts with negative delta the hedge is a long share position.

questions.question: A second-line team sets a framework but never challenges first-line decisions or reports breaches. What is the weakness?

answers.text: The second line is too independent
Oversight without challenge and escalation fails the core second-line purpose
The first line should be abolished
Internal audit should take over daily risk decisions

questions.explanation: The second line must monitor and challenge, not merely publish policies. Moving daily decisions to audit, the strongest distractor, would destroy third-line independence rather than fix oversight.

questions.question: A floating-rate note with par $1000 resets to a reference rate of 4.2% plus a spread of 1.5%. What is the annual coupon rate and annual coupon amount for the next period?
questions.explanation: FRN coupon = reference + spread = 4.2% + 1.5% = 5.70%. Annual amount = 1,000 x 5.70% = $57.00.

questions.question: A bond with face value $100, an annual coupon rate of 6% paid annually, and 3 years to maturity is priced at a yield to maturity of 4%. What is its price?
questions.explanation: Price is the present value of all cash flows discounted at 4%: 6/1.04^1 = 5.77 + 6/1.04^2 = 5.55 + 106/1.04^3 = 94.23 = 105.55. Price exceeds/falls short of par depending on coupon versus yield.

frm-part-ii.quiz_title: FRM Part II (Financial Risk Manager) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which outcome is most concerning for a 250-day 99% VaR backtest?

answers.text: 12 exceptions, placing the model in the red zone
4 exceptions, at the top of the green zone
2 exceptions, below the expected count but within green
0 exceptions in a very calm year with a conservative model

questions.explanation: The expected count is 2.5, green allows up to 4, yellow runs 5 to 9, and red begins at 10. Twelve exceptions is well into the red zone and signals serious underestimation of tail risk.

questions.question: The LIBOR market model (BGM) models which quantities directly?

answers.text: A single constant swap rate for all maturities
The instantaneous short rate only
A set of forward LIBOR rates, each with its own volatility, under dynamics that keep each rate consistent with its own forward measure
The prices of equity index options

questions.explanation: The LIBOR market model specifies lognormal dynamics for discrete forward LIBOR rates spanning the curve, which makes it natural for pricing caps, floors and swaptions.

questions.question: How do variation margin and initial margin differ in purpose?

answers.text: Both settle current value, but initial margin is paid in securities and variation margin in cash only
Initial margin is exchanged only at maturity while variation margin is exchanged daily
Variation margin settles current mark-to-market moves; initial margin is a buffer against future moves during the margin period of risk
Variation margin covers future moves while initial margin settles today's value

questions.explanation: Variation margin keeps collateral aligned with today's exposure; initial margin is over-collateralisation held against the gap risk that arises before close-out can occur.

questions.question: What does subordination provide to a senior tranche?

answers.text: Exemption from any rating review after issuance
A guarantee from the originator that the pool cannot default
A higher coupon than every junior tranche in all circumstances
Credit enhancement: junior tranches absorb losses first, protecting the senior tranche up to its attachment point

questions.explanation: Subordination is internal credit enhancement. The thickness of tranches below the senior tranche is the loss cushion that must be exhausted before senior principal is impaired.

questions.question: What horizon and minimum define the Net Stable Funding Ratio for Union Trust?

answers.text: A five-year horizon, with a minimum of 75%
A stressed 30-day horizon, with a minimum of 100%
A one-year horizon, with available stable funding at least 100% of required stable funding
A one-week horizon, with a minimum of 150%

questions.explanation: The NSFR is a one-year structural measure: ASF must be at least 100% of RSF. The stressed 30-day horizon defines the LCR instead.

questions.question: If a loss distribution is shifted by adding a fixed certain loss of $10,000 to every outcome, a coherent risk measure should:

answers.text: Stay unchanged
Increase by $10,000 multiplied by the confidence level
Increase by exactly $10,000
Decrease by $10,000

questions.explanation: This follows from translation invariance applied in reverse: a certain added loss raises required capital one-for-one. Both VaR and ES satisfy this particular axiom; VaR's coherence failure lies in subadditivity.

questions.question: A portfolio worth $5,000,000 has daily returns with mean 0.20% and standard deviation 3.0%. Using the parametric (delta-normal) method, what is the one-day 90% VaR?
questions.explanation: VaR = (z x sigma - mu) x V = (1.282 x 3.0% - 0.20%) x $5,000,000 = 3.646% x $5,000,000 = $182,300. The distractors use the wrong z-value, omit the mean adjustment, or use sigma alone.

questions.question: Implied volatility is 30% for a 0.25-year option. What is total implied variance, and what standard deviation of returns does it imply over that quarter?

answers.text: Total variance is 0.075, implying a quarterly standard deviation of 27.4%
Total variance is 0.0225, implying a quarterly standard deviation of 15%
Total variance is 0.09, implying a quarterly standard deviation of 30%
Total variance is 0.0225, implying a quarterly standard deviation of 2.25%

questions.explanation: Total variance = volatility squared times time = 0.30^2 x 0.25 = 0.09 x 0.25 = 0.0225. The standard deviation over the quarter is sqrt(0.0225) = 0.15, or 15%.

questions.question: A CDS allows an investor to take a short credit view without borrowing a bond. This is possible because:

answers.text: CDS contracts include ownership of the bond's voting rights
Buying protection pays off when the reference credit deteriorates or defaults, mimicking a short bond credit position
Shorting bonds is the only legal use of CDS
The protection seller lends the bond to the buyer

questions.explanation: The buyer profits from widening spreads and from the protection payment on default, without sourcing or borrowing the cash bond. That ease of shorting is a defining feature of the CDS market.

questions.question: A bank wants to reduce credit VaR without changing total lending volume. The most effective route is to:

answers.text: Raise every borrower's PD assumption
Shorten every loan's documentation
Replace all secured loans with unsecured loans
Diversify across borrowers, industries and regions and reduce single-name concentrations

questions.explanation: Credit VaR is driven by tail co-movement. Spreading exposure and cutting concentrations lowers the high-quantile loss for the same expected loss and the same total volume.

questions.question: Summit Bank funds 30-year mortgages primarily with short-term wholesale borrowing. What ALM problem does this create?

answers.text: Severe maturity mismatch: funding must be rolled many times before assets mature
No problem, because asset and liability maturities need not be considered
An excess of stable funding that must be invested overnight
A guaranteed profit because short-term rates are always lower

questions.explanation: Funding long assets short creates maturity transformation risk: liabilities reprice and can run long before assets repay. Matching funding tenor to asset tenor mitigates this core ALM risk.

questions.question: Why are long-only and position-limit constraints often helpful in optimisation despite appearing to reduce efficiency?

answers.text: They guarantee higher expected returns than the unconstrained optimum
They eliminate the need to estimate covariances
They ensure every asset receives an equal capital weight
They prevent the optimiser from exploiting estimation error with extreme long-short or concentrated positions

questions.explanation: Unconstrained optima look efficient in-sample but often reflect noise in expected returns. Realistic constraints act as a form of regularisation, producing portfolios that are more robust out of sample even though in-sample efficiency is lower.

questions.question: A position is worth $4,000,000 and its ordinary value-at-risk is $300,000. The bid-ask spread is 0.5% of the position value. What is the exogenous liquidity-adjusted value-at-risk?
questions.explanation: Liquidity add-on = 0.5 x 0.0050 x $4,000,000 = $10,000. LVaR = VaR + add-on = $300,000 + $10,000 = $310,000. Using the full spread instead of half would double the add-on.

questions.question: An option position has a delta of 0.6 on 100,000 shares with the underlying priced at $50. The underlying's daily volatility is 2.0%. Using the delta-equivalent mapped position, what is the approximate one-day VaR using z = 1.645?
questions.explanation: Delta-equivalent position = |delta| x shares x price = 0.6 x 100,000 x $50 = $3,000,000. Mapped VaR = $3,000,000 x 2.0% x 1.645 = $98,700, ignoring gamma and other higher-order effects.

questions.question: A company has equity of $25 million and total assets of $100 million. What proportion of assets is funded by creditors?
questions.explanation: Assets = debt + equity, so creditor funding = (100 - 25) / 100 = 75%.

questions.question: A borrower's hazard rate is 4% and loss given default is 60%. Using spread approx hazard rate x LGD, what is the approximate credit spread?

answers.text: 120 basis points
600 basis points
240 basis points
400 basis points

questions.explanation: Spread approx lambda x LGD = 0.04 x 0.6 = 0.0240 = 240 basis points. Using the hazard rate alone would ignore loss severity.

questions.question: High information ratio over a short period with very few independent bets should be treated cautiously because:

answers.text: Information ratio cannot be calculated for short periods
Skill estimates need breadth and time; a few correlated bets can produce a high ratio by luck
Few bets guarantee a sustainably high ratio
Tracking error is undefined when bets are few

questions.explanation: The fundamental law of active management links information ratio to skill per bet and the number of independent bets. A high ratio built on a handful of correlated wagers has a wide confidence interval and often mean-reverts.

questions.question: A structured note has a payoff linked to an underlying that is not directly traded and cannot be replicated. In the standardised approach this feature most likely triggers what?

answers.text: A zero capital charge, because untraded underlyings are riskless
The residual risk add-on, because the risk cannot be adequately captured by standard sensitivities
The default risk charge as the sole charge
Only a delta charge on the note's issuer

questions.explanation: Payoffs on non-replicable or exotic underlyings leave residual risks outside the sensitivities-based method, which is exactly the gap the residual risk add-on is designed to capitalise.

questions.question: In a simplified single-period calculation ignoring discounting, expected exposure is $10.0 million, the marginal probability of default for the period is 1.5%, and loss given default is 40%. What is the credit valuation adjustment (CVA) for the period?
questions.explanation: CVA is approximately LGD x EE x PD = 0.40 x $10.0 million x 0.015 = $60,000. Omitting LGD would overstate the charge.

questions.question: A vendor's employee, working on the bank's premises, steals bank-owned laptops. The bank bears the loss of the equipment and related costs. Which classification question matters most?

answers.text: Whether the theft happened during business hours
Whether the laptops were new or old
Whether the bank has insurance
Whether the act was intentional theft by a party acting from outside the bank's own staff

questions.explanation: Loss classification follows the nature and perpetrator of the event. Theft by someone who is not the bank's own employee points toward external fraud rather than internal fraud; value, timing and insurance do not determine the event type.

garp-scr-sustainability-and-climate-risk.quiz_title: GARP Sustainability and Climate Risk (SCR) Certificate Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Net zero carbon dioxide emissions, at concept level, means:

answers.text: No human activity produces any carbon dioxide anywhere
Anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions are balanced by anthropogenic removals over a specified period, so net addition to the atmosphere stops
Each individual company must physically capture its own emissions on site
Carbon dioxide already in the atmosphere is instantly removed

questions.explanation: Net zero is a balance: residual emissions continue but are matched by removals, halting further accumulation. It does not require zero gross emissions, on-site capture by every emitter, or instant removal of the existing atmospheric stock.

questions.question: In financed emissions calculations for listed companies, the attribution denominator is commonly based on what?

answers.text: The company's number of employees
The company's total value, such as enterprise value including cash, so the investor's share reflects its proportion of that value
The company's total office floor space
The length of time the investor has held the shares

questions.explanation: For listed holdings, attribution typically divides the value of the investment by the company's enterprise value including cash, giving the financed share. Employees, floor space and holding period do not determine the ownership share of emissions.

questions.question: In PCAF financed-emissions accounting, the attribution factor generally expresses:

answers.text: The borrower's total revenue share
The share of a borrower's or asset's emissions attributed to the financier based on its share of financing
The percentage of branches using renewables
The assurance provider's sampling rate

questions.explanation: Attribution allocates emissions in proportion to the financier's share of the financing. Revenue share, branch energy and sampling rates are unrelated.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the accuracy principle in emissions accounting?

answers.text: Estimates should be sufficiently accurate that systematic over- or under-estimation is reduced as far as practicable
Rounding all values to the nearest thousand satisfies accuracy
Accuracy means reporting only metered data and omitting all estimates
Accuracy is achieved when totals match the prior year exactly

questions.explanation: Accuracy means quantifying emissions without systematic bias and reducing uncertainty where practicable, while still using reasonable estimates where needed. Rounding rules, omitting estimates, or matching last year do not establish accuracy.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches a measure with its primary purpose?

answers.text: Mangrove restoration for timber revenue — mitigation only
Early-warning system for heatwaves — mitigation
Energy-efficiency retrofit — adaptation
Water-efficient irrigation in a drying region — adaptation

questions.explanation: Efficient irrigation helps a farming system cope with reduced water availability, a classic adaptation goal. Early-warning systems are also adaptation, not mitigation. Efficiency retrofits primarily cut energy use and emissions, so they are mitigation. Mangroves can serve both purposes, not mitigation only.

questions.question: Which statement best captures how PRI signatories are expected to apply the six principles?

answers.text: Apply only the principles that are convenient in a given year
Apply them only to equity holdings, never to other asset classes
Treat them as legal rules with fines for any deviation
Act in the best long-term interests of beneficiaries, recognizing that ESG issues can affect investment performance

questions.explanation: D is correct: the PRI preamble ties the principles to fiduciary duty and long-term beneficiary interests, with ESG issues recognized as relevant to performance. A contradicts the commitment to implement the principles as a set. B is wrong because responsible investment practice extends across asset classes. C mischaracterizes a voluntary framework as an enforced legal code.

questions.question: What role do minimum safeguards commonly play in a sustainable finance taxonomy?

answers.text: They set baseline expectations on matters such as human rights and governance that an activity must respect to qualify
They guarantee the financial performance of qualifying activities
They exempt qualifying activities from all other laws
They apply only to product advertising

questions.explanation: Minimum safeguards set baseline expectations an activity must respect. They do not guarantee performance, exempt activities from law, or apply only to advertising.

questions.question: Why might a company set separate targets for different scopes or gases within an overall net zero goal?

answers.text: To hide poor performance in one area inside an average
Because a single combined figure is prohibited in all reporting
To avoid setting any long-term target
Because sources differ in size, measurability, and abatement options, so separate targets improve management and transparency

questions.explanation: Separate targets can reflect different levers and timelines, for example methane versus energy carbon dioxide, while still rolling up to the overall goal. They should increase, not reduce, transparency.

questions.question: Which action is an operational, rather than purely strategic, sustainability step for a manufacturer?

answers.text: Announcing a long-term ambition to be a sustainable company
Redesigning processes to cut waste, water use, and energy use on the factory floor
Changing the mission statement wording
Hiring a consultant to draft a vision document

questions.explanation: Operations concern how work is actually done day to day, such as process changes that reduce resource use and waste. Ambitions, mission wording, and vision documents are strategic or communicative steps that matter only if operations follow.

questions.question: What does it mean to say that physical risk is location-specific in a way that portfolio averages can hide?

answers.text: A portfolio with low average hazard can still contain a concentrated cluster of highly exposed assets whose losses dominate in an event
Every asset in a portfolio always has identical risk
Averages are prohibited in risk reports
Location matters only for residential property

questions.explanation: A is correct: averaging can mask concentrations that drive event losses. B is the opposite of the point. C overstates the lesson; averages are useful but insufficient. D wrongly limits location effects to one asset class.

questions.question: In a hot-house narrative, which risk pattern is generally expected relative to an orderly narrative?

answers.text: Higher physical risk and comparatively lower transition risk
Higher transition risk and lower physical risk
Equal levels of both risks in all years
Neither risk present because markets adapt automatically

questions.explanation: Hot-house pathways trade low transition disruption for high warming and physical risk. Disorderly pathways show the reverse emphasis, and markets do not automatically eliminate risk.

questions.question: Why can repeated small floods be financially significant even when no single flood is catastrophic?

answers.text: Cumulative repair costs, repeated interruptions, rising insurance costs, and gradual value erosion can add up to a large total burden
Small floods always destroy entire buildings
Repetition turns an acute hazard into a policy risk
Small floods matter only if they are reported together in one year

questions.explanation: A is correct: frequency matters as well as severity, and repeated losses accumulate and erode value and insurability. B overstates single-event damage. C mislabels the risk type. D makes reporting, not economic burden, the criterion.

questions.question: An invented logistics firm, SwiftHaul, must replace diesel trucks earlier than planned because cities restrict diesel access. The trucks' resale value collapses. This is mainly an example of what?

answers.text: A gain from technology risk
Physical chronic risk from rising temperatures
Stranded assets caused by policy-driven restrictions shortening useful life
Liability risk from a customer lawsuit

questions.explanation: Access restrictions strand the diesel fleet: its useful life and resale value fall because of policy. It is a loss, not a gain (A), no temperature hazard is involved (B), and no lawsuit is described (D).

questions.question: Which design choice most affects whether a scenario exercise reveals long-term physical risk to a mortgage portfolio?

answers.text: The font used in the board presentation
The number of scenarios printed in the appendix
The time horizon chosen, since many physical impacts grow substantially beyond typical planning horizons
Whether the exercise is run in the morning or afternoon

questions.explanation: Horizon selection determines whether slow-building physical risks become visible. Presentation formatting and scheduling have no analytical effect.

questions.question: What do ice cores show about the relationship between greenhouse gases and temperature in past climate swings?

answers.text: The two never changed at the same time in the past
Temperature always changed with no change in any gas
Greenhouse gas levels and temperature rose and fell together across glacial cycles, consistent with gases amplifying climate change
Past carbon dioxide levels were always higher than today's

questions.explanation: Across glacial cycles gases and temperature moved together, consistent with feedback amplification, so C is correct. The records do show co-movement, and past levels in those cycles were not always above today's.

questions.question: What should an investor conclude if a labelled sustainable fund is later found to breach its label criteria?

answers.text: Labels make breaches impossible, so the finding must be ignored
The breach tests the label's monitoring and enforcement, and the label may need review or withdrawal
The investor should assume all sustainable funds are fraudulent
The fund's disclosure obligations end after labelling

questions.explanation: A breach tests monitoring and enforcement and may lead to review or withdrawal. Breaches are possible, one breach does not prove universal fraud, and disclosure duties continue.

questions.question: A clothing maker uses the phrase people, planet, and profit in its sustainability report. What framework is it invoking in plain language?

answers.text: A framework covering only shareholder returns
A three-part view aligning social, environmental, and economic performance
A legal test for product labeling
A method for setting executive pay

questions.explanation: People, planet, and profit is a plain-language expression of the social, environmental, and economic dimensions. It is broader than shareholder returns alone and is neither a labeling test nor a pay-setting method.

questions.question: A company's base-year emissions are 100,000 tCO2e. In the current year, Scope 1 is 42,000, Scope 2 is 18,000, and Scope 3 is 55,000 tCO2e. What is the current-year total footprint?
questions.explanation: Total = 42,000 + 18,000 + 55,000 = 115,000 tCO2e. Omitting Scope 3 gives 60,000, and the other options result from adding only two scopes or mis-adding the three figures.

questions.question: CASE - Verdant Vale Foods sets a target to restore 120 hectares of riverside buffer habitat by 2030 and reports progress annually. Which disclosure element does the annual progress figure serve?

answers.text: A governance biography
A product label claim
Metrics and targets, showing a measurable goal and tracked performance against it
An unrelated marketing metric

questions.explanation: A quantified target with reported progress is core metrics-and-targets disclosure. It is measurable and tied directly to the assessed nature risk.

questions.question: A stress test shows large losses under a disorderly transition pathway. The most appropriate management response is to:

answers.text: Discard the result because the pathway has not happened
Consider adjustments such as exposure limits, hedging, or strategy changes, and report findings to senior governance
Hide the result from the board
Assume the pathway is a forecast and book the loss today

questions.explanation: B is correct: results should inform risk actions and reach governance bodies. A dismisses forward-looking analysis, C breaches governance, and D confuses a scenario with a forecast.

asis-cpp-certified-protection-profession.quiz_title: ASIS Certified Protection Professional (CPP) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A university security department's metric set has grown to ninety measures, none of which leadership can recall. The remedy is to:

answers.text: Add a ninety-first summary measure
Print the measures on a larger poster
Rotate which measures are ignored each month
Prune to a small set of measures tied to the program's stated objectives, each with an owner who reviews and acts on it

questions.explanation: Measurement serves management only when it is few, owned, and connected to objectives; volume without attention is decoration.

questions.question: Which metric BEST shows whether a contract guarding budget is being consumed as planned during the year?

answers.text: The vendor's total annual contract value alone
Actual hours worked and billed by post compared with authorized hours by post
The number of invoices received each month
The guard company's years in business

questions.explanation: Hours by post against authorized hours connects money to the actual service delivered and reveals unauthorized posts, excess hours, or missing coverage early.

questions.question: A hospital forms a multidisciplinary threat assessment team. Which composition best supports sound decisions about a concerning employee case?

answers.text: Only security staff, to keep the process confidential and fast
Security, human resources, legal counsel, and appropriate clinical or employee-assistance expertise, with others added as the case requires
The employee's immediate coworkers, voting on the outcome
An outside vendor with no access to internal employment context

questions.explanation: Threat cases blend safety, employment, legal, and behavioral-health dimensions that no single function can evaluate alone. A multidisciplinary team brings those lenses together while controlling information on a need-to-know basis.

questions.question: A security manager proposes removing classification markings from internal email 'to reduce clutter.' What is lost if this is adopted?

answers.text: The ability to search old messages
Nothing; email is automatically secure inside the company
Only the legal department's formatting preference
Recipients lose the at-a-glance handling cue that governs forwarding, printing, and storage decisions — the point where most information changes hands

questions.explanation: Email is the highest-volume disclosure channel in most firms. Markings matter most exactly where handling decisions are fastest and least considered.

questions.question: A first-arriving officer at a stadium gate collapse transmits an initial report to the EOC. Which content makes that size-up most useful?

answers.text: What happened, where, the scale of casualties and damage, hazards present, actions underway, and resources needed
The officer's theory about who is legally responsible
A prediction of tomorrow's weather at the stadium
A list of spectators the officer recognizes

questions.explanation: A good size-up gives decision-makers the incident's nature, location, scale, hazards, current actions, and needs. Theories of liability and speculation belong to later investigation, not the opening report.

questions.question: A middle school adjacent to your office campus goes into lockdown, and anxious employees begin calling security about their children. What liaison action is appropriate?

answers.text: Send company officers to the school to help search the building
Contact the school district and police liaison for verified status information, share only confirmed guidance with employees, and keep campus entrances clear for responders
Tell employees the lockdown is probably a drill so they calm down
Open campus gates so parents can cut through to reach the school faster

questions.explanation: In a neighboring emergency the company role is verified information and unobstructed responder access, not speculation or freelance assistance. Confirmed updates through the school and police liaison prevent rumor-driven panic among employees.

questions.question: An annual refresher has not changed in four years, and completion stays high while tailgating and unreported incidents stay flat. What should the program owner conclude?

answers.text: Completion is the outcome that matters, so the program is working
Employees are deliberately resisting and need disciplinary warnings
Lengthen the same refresher to ninety minutes to increase its impact
The refresher is measuring attendance, not behavior; redesign it around the persistent behaviors using fresh scenarios and measure those behaviors directly

questions.explanation: High completion with unchanged behavior shows the program optimizes the wrong metric. Effective refreshers target the specific behaviors that are not changing and are evaluated by observation and incident data, not seat time.

questions.question: An international school screens teachers hired from several countries and finds some jurisdictions cannot provide the same records. What documentation practice maintains program integrity?

answers.text: Mark all foreign files incomplete and bar international hiring
Accept any document a candidate provides without review
Record files as fully equivalent with no notation
Record which components were completed, which equivalents were used, and which were unavailable, with a risk decision by the designated authority

questions.explanation: Transparency about what was and was not verified preserves the meaning of a completed file. Documented equivalents and explicit risk acceptance are defensible; silent equivalence is not.

questions.question: Surveying a pharmaceutical warehouse, the assessor observes high-value cage inventory counts that do not match system records. What should the survey do?

answers.text: Recommend a larger cage as the remedy for count differences
Conclude theft has occurred and name suspects in the survey report
Limit the report to noting the mismatch without further inquiry
Expand the survey to cage access logs, key custody, and count procedures to find where control breaks down.

questions.explanation: Count discrepancies are a control signal; the survey traces access, custody, and counting practice rather than leaping to accusations.

questions.question: At a university research building, there are card readers on laboratory doors that log entries but whose exit buttons fail intermittently. What is the best action?

answers.text: Tell researchers to knock for exit when buttons fail
Add exit-device checks to the maintenance rounds and repair failing buttons before staff start propping lab doors.
Ignore exit faults since entry logging works
Remove exit buttons and use keys instead

questions.explanation: Failed exit hardware drives door-propping; maintaining the full portal, entry and exit, preserves the control.

questions.question: A company leases two floors in a multi-tenant tower and writes its response plan without contacting building management. Why is this a serious planning gap?

answers.text: Evacuation, alarm systems, stairwell control, and building systems are managed at the building level, so plans must be coordinated with the property operator
Building management is responsible for all tenant emergencies, so no tenant plan is needed
Coordination would reveal the company's presence in the building
Tenants are forbidden from speaking to building management about safety

questions.explanation: In multi-tenant buildings, life-safety systems and evacuation are controlled centrally. A tenant plan written in isolation will conflict with building procedures precisely where coordination matters most.

questions.question: A data center's assessment identifies a single access road that floods in heavy rain, cutting off fuel deliveries. Why does this detail matter to prioritization?

answers.text: It is only a facilities maintenance concern, not a security issue
It proves the site should relocate immediately
It affects only the landscaping contract
It reveals a cascading vulnerability where one hazard disables a critical support function

questions.explanation: A hazard that cuts off fuel deliveries creates cascading failure of backup power. Identifying such dependencies raises the priority of both the hazard and the mitigation for the support function.

questions.question: A jewelry manufacturer's security program defines competencies for each role, then finds supervisors cannot coach officers on report quality. The competency model should drive which follow-on action?

answers.text: Lowering the report standard to match current skill
Targeted development for supervisors in the identified gap, with the model updated as roles evolve
Outsourcing all report writing to a clerical pool
Removing report quality from the competency list

questions.explanation: A competency model earns its keep by directing development where gaps appear; erasing the standard instead of building the skill weakens the program quietly.

questions.question: A site manager proposes paying a local official a 'facilitation fee' in cash to speed a routine permit the company is entitled to. What is the correct characterization?

answers.text: An improper payment risk — cash payments to officials for official action must be refused and escalated under anti-corruption policy, whatever the local label
A normal courtesy where such fees are common
Acceptable if the amount is small and no receipt is expected
A vendor cost that can be hidden in petty cash

questions.explanation: Payments to officials to influence or speed official duties — especially in cash, off the record — are the core anti-corruption concern. Custom and small size do not cure them.

questions.question: Natural surveillance is a priority for a new transit station. Which design delivers it?

answers.text: Mirrors installed instead of lighting and staffing
High solid walls around platforms with cameras on top
Open sightlines, windows overlooking platforms, staffed kiosks positioned to see waiting areas, and lighting without dark pockets.
Tinted enclosures that hide waiting passengers from view

questions.explanation: Natural surveillance puts legitimate eyes on the space through layout, transparency, staffing position, and even lighting.

questions.question: A survey of a state agency finds citizens' application files, including financial details, stored in open shelving in a public waiting area during a renovation. What is the most urgent survey action?

answers.text: Photograph the shelving for the report cover
Note the finding and include it in the report due next quarter
Wait until the renovation ends, when the finding will resolve itself
Immediate interim protection — relocate or secure the files now rather than waiting for the final report, because exposure is active and ongoing

questions.explanation: Surveys are not purely observational when harm is in progress. Active exposure of sensitive records warrants same-day escalation and interim controls.

questions.question: As a resort prepares to reopen after a hurricane, guests with reservations receive no information and cancel en masse, while employees report to a closed entrance. What recovery element was neglected?

answers.text: The design of the reopening celebration
The wording of the property's advertising slogan
Planned communication of resumption status, timing, and instructions to employees, customers, and suppliers
The order in which parking lots are swept

questions.explanation: Resumption must be communicated as deliberately as the original emergency. Stakeholders who hear nothing make their own decisions, and avoidable confusion becomes additional business loss.

questions.question: An assessment of a university archive treats a disgruntled former employee and an organized theft ring as identical threats because both 'might steal.' The analysis is weak because it ignores:

answers.text: The archive's shelf arrangement
Whether theft is rated on a five-point scale
Differences in actor capability, resources, and intent, which change both likelihood and the controls that would deter or detect each
The color of the rating matrix used

questions.explanation: Threat characterization distinguishes actors by capability and intent; lumping them produces generic controls fitted to no real adversary.

questions.question: A protection program evaluates adding a second principal — the chief financial officer — after a threatening incident targeting her during a labor dispute. An executive suggests simply splitting the existing detail in half. What is the better analysis?

answers.text: Assess the new principal's distinct threat, schedule, and exposure, and resource the requirement on its own merits rather than diluting existing coverage by half
Split the detail equally because fairness requires identical teams
Deny protection because only one principal can ever be covered
Assign the new principal the detail on the chief executive's days off

questions.explanation: Each principal's risk and itinerary differ, and halving a detail can leave both principals under-protected. A separate assessment produces a right-sized, defensible allocation.

questions.question: A technology company adopts cloud storage chosen independently by product teams. The security manager learns of new services only when contracts renew. What program mechanism fixes this discovery problem?

answers.text: Block all cloud services at the network edge
Hire an analyst to search the internet for the company's data
Require teams to confess unauthorized services in an annual survey
Tie information-system adoption to a visible process — procurement and expense checkpoints that route new services holding company data through security review at adoption, not renewal

questions.explanation: Shadow adoption is a process gap, not mainly a discipline problem. Checkpoints where money and contracts move are where governance reliably intercepts new information flows.

asis-psp-physical-security-professional.quiz_title: ASIS Physical Security Professional (PSP) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What distinguishes a structured checklist method from an unstructured walkthrough at a power plant?

answers.text: Only the checklist requires the assessor to be present on site
The checklist predefines items to verify, promoting consistent coverage, while the walkthrough depends heavily on what catches the observer's eye
The unstructured walkthrough always takes longer
The checklist guarantees no finding will be missed

questions.explanation: Predefinition is the structural difference and buys consistency, though no checklist guarantees completeness; duration and presence claims do not distinguish the methods.

questions.question: What geographic factor most affects a rural clinic's physical security planning compared with an urban one?

answers.text: The clinic's distance from the assessor's office
Rural clinics need no planning because crime is urban
Distance — long emergency response times and isolation that leave the clinic self-reliant during incidents
Rural patients are inherently less threatening

questions.explanation: Isolation and response distance are defining rural environment facts; crime-free assumptions, assessor convenience, and patient stereotyping are not planning factors.

questions.question: Which of these is the clearest example of a 'functional requirement' in an access control design?

answers.text: The system shall cost less than the approved budget line
The head-end server shall sit in a locked room
The system shall support anti-passback so a credential cannot be passed back for a second entry
The vendor shall provide two years of warranty coverage

questions.explanation: Functional requirements describe what the system must be capable of doing; anti-passback is a capability, while the other statements concern cost, siting, or contract terms.

questions.question: In CPTED terms, a 'natural access control' measure is best illustrated by:

answers.text: A guard checking badges at a desk
A single, well-defined entrance path created by fencing, landscaping, and lighting that channels visitors past the reception point
A biometric reader on the server room
A policy forbidding visitors after 6 p.m.

questions.explanation: Natural access control designs the environment itself to route people where the organization wants them, reducing dependence on staff intervention at every arrival.

questions.question: Which factor most strengthens the defensibility of a bid evaluation if a losing bidder protests?

answers.text: A contemporaneous scoring record tied to the published criteria
Destruction of notes once the award is announced
The evaluators' private recollections of the discussion
A statement that the winner felt like the right fit

questions.explanation: Written scores linked to criteria published in advance show the decision followed the announced process rather than preference.

questions.question: An assessor is planning work at a stadium that hosts events only part of the year. Which asset identification nuance matters most?

answers.text: Assets such as broadcast infrastructure and cash handling surge in importance on event days, so identification must reflect both event and non-event states
Event-day assets belong to visiting teams and can be ignored
The stadium has no assets on non-event days
Only permanent office furniture counts as an asset

questions.explanation: Criticality at event venues shifts with operating state, and the plan must capture both; empty-day denial, furniture-only views, and ignoring event assets would misstate what needs protection.

questions.question: A food processing plant proposes cameras inside employee locker rooms to stop a rash of locker thefts. What should the assessor recommend instead?

answers.text: Reject in-locker-room cameras because the expectation of privacy there is high and recording creates severe legal exposure; pursue lockers with better locks, camera coverage of the locker room entrance, and controlled access to the area
Install the cameras but angle them at the ceiling
Install the cameras and post no notice to catch the thief
Record only during the night shift when fewer staff are present

questions.explanation: Some locations carry a privacy expectation that no theft problem overrides. Entrance coverage and stronger lockers attack the same theft pattern while keeping the program inside lawful bounds.

questions.question: A mall assessor learns shoplifting rings have hit three nearby malls in two months but not this one yet. How should that affect likelihood?

answers.text: It raises the judged likelihood for this mall because capable actors are demonstrably active in its immediate operating area
It converts shoplifting into a natural hazard
It lowers likelihood because lightning never strikes nearby twice
It has no bearing until this mall is hit

questions.explanation: Proximate, repeated activity by the same threat type is strong likelihood evidence; folk sayings, wait-until-hit logic, and hazard reclassification discard that signal.

questions.question: A designer places a panic button under the counter of a late-night convenience store and a second button in the back office. Two locations are specified because:

answers.text: Buttons are sold in pairs
An alarm reachable only at the counter is useless to an employee who has retreated from a robbery; coverage follows where staff may actually be during an incident
One button is a decoy
The alarm panel has exactly two spare inputs

questions.explanation: Duress devices protect only if reachable in the moment of need; placement is designed around realistic staff positions during the incident, not around the panel's convenience.

questions.question: A performance requirement for a hospital's wireless infant tags sets a maximum location-refresh interval. The clinical reason for a tight interval is:

answers.text: Tags look better when they blink often
Battery vendors prefer rapid discharge
Nurses enjoy watching screens update
Staff must see an infant's movement toward an exit in near-real time to intervene before the exit is reached

questions.explanation: Location data protect only if they are current enough to act on; the refresh interval is derived from how fast a person can carry an infant to an exit versus how fast staff can respond.

questions.question: A plant must run a camera and gate intercom to a guardhouse 400 meters from the main building, across an area with frequent lightning strikes. Which transmission medium best fits that run?

answers.text: Standard copper network cable buried in a shared trench with power lines
Fiber optic cable, which covers the distance without repeaters and is immune to electrical interference and lightning-induced surges
Coaxial cable extended with consumer-grade signal boosters
A series of short copper segments joined in outdoor junction boxes

questions.explanation: Fiber handles long distances in a single run and, being non-conductive, does not carry lightning energy or suffer electromagnetic interference—two decisive advantages for a long outdoor run in a strike-prone area. Copper solutions inherit both the distance and the surge problems.

questions.question: A biotech firm assigns two officers to a night patrol of a large research park and gives them overlapping, identical routes. What is the main weakness of this patrol design?

answers.text: Two officers cannot legally patrol the same property at once
Identical simultaneous routes waste coverage—both officers are always in the same place, leaving the rest of the park unobserved for long stretches
Overlapping routes make guard tour checkpoints impossible to install
Officers on identical routes cannot communicate with each other by radio

questions.explanation: Patrol value comes from distributed, unpredictable presence. Staggering or splitting routes spreads observation across the park and varies timing; duplicated routes double the cost of covering one area while the remainder gets none.

questions.question: An assessor must rank a hotel's assets for protection priority. Which ranking logic is soundest?

answers.text: Rank by the size of each asset in square feet
Rank alphabetically by department name
Rank by which assets photograph best for the report
Rank by guest life safety first, then by functions whose loss closes the property or destroys guest trust

questions.explanation: Protection priority follows harm to people and mission-ending consequences; floor area, alphabet, and photogenic quality carry no protective logic.

questions.question: A utility substation assessment relies partly on trouble tickets for its intrusion alarm. The tickets show the alarm was in a bypassed state for six weeks awaiting a part. How should the assessor treat protection during that period?

answers.text: Treat the substation as effectively unmonitored for intrusion during the bypass, regardless of what the design documents describe
Credit the site with full alarm protection because the system was installed and owned
Average the protection level across the year so the six weeks have little effect
Ignore the bypass because parts delays are outside the operator control

questions.explanation: Vulnerability reflects conditions as they existed, not as designed. A bypassed alarm provides no detection, so the site carried an unmonitored interval that must be stated plainly.

questions.question: A designer for a stadium project prepares enlarged plans of the command center and each gate screening area within the drawing set. What do enlarged plans accomplish that the overall floor plans cannot?

answers.text: They show device placement, operator positions, and clearances at a scale where the working relationships in dense areas can actually be designed and built
They replace the need for specifications in those rooms
They satisfy a page-count requirement for public projects
They allow the architect to delete the corresponding areas from the base plans

questions.explanation: Dense functional areas—command centers, screening lanes—cannot be designed at small scale: equipment relationships, sightlines, and working clearances need room to be drawn precisely. Enlarged plans give those areas the resolution their complexity demands.

questions.question: During cost estimation for a stadium's screening system, the estimator separates costs into equipment, installation labor, infrastructure modifications, training, and first-year support. What estimating practice does this categorization support?

answers.text: Guaranteeing the low bid wins
Hiding the total price from the owner
Avoiding the need for quantities
A structured cost breakdown that lets reviewers verify each category, spot omissions, and compare competing proposals on equal terms

questions.explanation: Categorized estimates are auditable: a missing line—training forgotten, support unpriced—shows as an empty category rather than hiding inside a lump sum. The same structure later becomes the project's cost-control skeleton.

questions.question: During vendor evaluation for a campus camera maintenance contract, the team visits a finalist's service center unannounced during business hours. What does this due diligence reveal that paper review cannot?

answers.text: The firm's advertising budget
Actual staffing, parts stocking, and dispatch practices behind its service claims
The owner's own response-time needs
Its proposal's binding quality
