questions.explanation: A site visit tests whether the operation behind the proposal — technicians, spares, and dispatch — matches what was promised.

questions.question: An analyst for a water utility assigns likelihood ratings using a five-level defined scale where each level names a frequency range, instead of letting each reviewer use personal judgment of words like 'likely'. Why does the defined scale improve the analysis?

answers.text: Defined levels remove the need for any supporting data
Five levels are required by law for utility analyses
Different reviewers attach the same meaning to the same rating, so ratings can be compared and combined across scenarios and sites
Defined scales always produce more optimistic results

questions.explanation: Undefined words mean different things to different people. Anchoring each level to a frequency range makes ratings consistent enough to aggregate, which is the point of a shared scale.

questions.question: An assessor comparing a tenant improvement plan with the base building standard finds the tenant proposes a glass-walled server room on the building perimeter with blinds. Which base-building security expectation does this design strain?

answers.text: The building standard for window film on south-facing glass
The building janitorial access schedule for tenant spaces
The parking allocation formula for tenant employees
Perimeter rooms holding sensitive equipment expose it to outside observation and to attack through the exterior wall, contrary to the usual practice of keeping critical functions off the perimeter

questions.explanation: Critical functions belong in the interior where walls and distance protect them. A glazed perimeter server room advertises its contents and puts them one pane away from the street.

questions.question: System A costs $80,000 installed and $6,000 per year to maintain. System B costs $95,000 installed and $3,000 per year. Over an 8-year life, which has the lower total cost and by how much?

answers.text: System A, by $9,000
System B, by $9,000
They are exactly equal
System A, by $24,000

questions.explanation: System A totals $80,000 + (8 × $6,000) = $128,000. System B totals $95,000 + (8 × $3,000) = $119,000. System B is lower by $128,000 − $119,000 = $9,000 despite its higher purchase price.

acams-cafs-certified-anti-fraud-speciali.quiz_title: ACAMS Certified Anti-Fraud Specialist (CAFS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A team wants to test a challenger rule set against the current champion on live traffic. What is a sound approach?

answers.text: Replace the champion everywhere at once with no comparison
Test only on cases already known to be fraud
Run a controlled champion-challenger test with defined measures, limits and rollback, comparing fraud, false positives and friction
Let the challenger block payments with no limit on errors

questions.explanation: Controlled testing shows whether a challenger truly improves outcomes without exposing all customers to unproven logic. Testing only on known fraud proves nothing about false positives, and uncontrolled replacement risks harm.

questions.question: When a fraud team classifies a case as second-party, which control implication follows most directly?

answers.text: Focus exclusively on restoring a stolen identity for the account holder
Review only the account holder's income documents from origination
Limit action to changing the account holder's password
Examine linked accounts, recruiters, shared devices, and cash-out behaviour to disrupt the wider facilitation network

questions.explanation: Second-party cases are network cases: facilitators connect victims, organisers, and cash-out channels. Identity-restoration or password steps alone would leave recruiters, linked accounts, and repeat facilitation untouched.

questions.question: Why do models need confirmed genuine behaviour as well as confirmed fraud?

answers.text: Only fraud cases contain useful data
Genuine behaviour never changes
Genuine outcomes calibrate what normal variation looks like and reduce false positives
Feeding genuine outcomes makes rules unnecessary

questions.explanation: Confirmed genuine outcomes teach the model the range of normal variation, cutting false positives. Fraud cases alone would make the model treat too much legitimate behaviour as suspicious. This keeps routine customers moving while focusing effort where risk is genuinely higher.

questions.question: Analyst Ken needs to test whether a new fraud pattern affects mobile only or all channels. He should:

answers.text: Look only at branch transactions
Assume mobile is affected without data
Segment the analytic results by channel — online, mobile, telephone and face-to-face — and compare rates
Stop the analysis

questions.explanation: Segmenting by channel shows where the pattern concentrates and where controls are needed. Looking only at branch data cannot answer a mobile-versus-all-channels question. The outcome should then be monitored so the control can be adjusted as behaviour changes.

questions.question: Which outcome best demonstrates corroboration of an OSINT lead before an account exit decision?

answers.text: A public review, a registry filing showing the same dissolved status, and internal transaction patterns inconsistent with the stated business all align
One anonymous review states the business is a scam
The investigator's supervisor agrees the lead feels right
A search returns many results for the business name

questions.explanation: Independent sources of different types converging on the same conclusion, supported by internal data, is corroboration. A single anonymous claim, search volume or a colleague's impression does not test the lead.

questions.question: Luis is designing control testing for a new account-opening identity check. Which design element should be settled first?

answers.text: The precise control objective and the criteria for pass or fail evidence
The date the final audit report will be published
The name of the executive who will receive a summary slide
A target number of failures the team hopes to find

questions.explanation: Testing must start from a clear control objective and defined pass or fail criteria, otherwise evidence cannot be judged consistently. Report dates and recipients matter for planning, but hoping for a set number of failures would distort objective testing.

questions.question: A bank's fraud policy has no named owner and has not been reviewed in four years. What is the main governance risk?

answers.text: The policy may no longer match current products, threats or regulations, with no one accountable for fixing it
The document will automatically expire and stop all payments
Staff will be unable to open the file without the owner present
Regulators will fine the bank solely for the document's age

questions.explanation: Without an owner and review cycle, the policy drifts away from current threats, products and rules with no accountability. The risk is misalignment and inaction, not an automatic shutdown or an age-based fine.

questions.question: Following a widely reported data breach, a bank sees credential-stuffed logins succeed on accounts that reused passwords. What trend response is most effective?

answers.text: Force password resets and step-up checks on affected accounts, and monitor for contact-detail changes after login
Publish a press statement and make no account changes
Lower transaction limits for all customers permanently, including unaffected ones
Wait for customers to report losses before acting

questions.explanation: A breach creates a predictable takeover wave, so resetting credentials and watching post-login changes targets the actual risk. Press statements alone do not protect accounts, and blanket limits punish unaffected customers without stopping takeovers.

questions.question: Before adding a purchased list of suspected mule accounts to its screening, what should a bank assess first about the list?

answers.text: Whether the list is the cheapest available on the market
Whether the vendor offers the list in a spreadsheet format
Its provenance, accuracy, bias and the legal basis for using it against customers
Whether other banks have already bought the same list

questions.explanation: External data used to act against customers must be checked for where it came from, how accurate and biased it may be, and whether using it is lawful. Price and format do not address the risk of acting on unreliable or unlawfully obtained data.

questions.question: Fraudsters send a series of small test payments, each slightly larger, before a large authorised push payment scam attempt. What behaviour are they showing?

answers.text: Normal customer saving behaviour
Chargeback abuse after a genuine purchase
Staff collusion inside the bank
Probing to learn detection thresholds before committing the main fraud

questions.explanation: Incrementally increasing test payments are used to discover where controls trigger, so the main attempt can stay beneath them. Detecting the probing pattern itself is often the earliest warning. That balance is central to keeping the control proportionate.

questions.question: An investigator wants to include a recommendation that a product feature be changed after repeated scam abuse. Who should be involved before finalising?

answers.text: Only the investigator
The customer who was scammed
No one, recommendations need no consultation
Relevant product, risk and legal colleagues so feasibility, impact and unintended consequences are assessed

questions.explanation: Product, risk and legal input tests feasibility and unintended consequences of a feature change. Solo recommendations risk being impractical or creating new vulnerabilities elsewhere.

questions.question: Legal, fraud and HR meet after an internal-fraud investigation substantiates deliberate circumvention by a supervisor. What must conclusions balance?

answers.text: Immediate public disclosure of the supervisor's name
Only the financial loss, ignoring control fixes
Evidence-based findings, fair process for the individual, control remediation and any referral or reporting decisions
A decision made before the evidence review is complete

questions.explanation: Substantiated internal cases require fair process, remediation and referral decisions grounded in evidence. Public naming or loss-only conclusions neglect duties and fixes. This framing keeps the focus on the mechanism of the fraud rather than on the size of the loss alone.

questions.question: A small bank outsources its fraud hotline to a vendor whose staff give customers incorrect advice about recall deadlines. Who carries the regulatory responsibility?

answers.text: The vendor alone is responsible because its staff spoke
The bank remains responsible for outsourced activities and must oversee the vendor, correct the advice and remediate affected customers
Customers are responsible for checking the advice themselves
Responsibility transfers to the vendor once a contract is signed

questions.explanation: Outsourcing does not outsource accountability: the firm must monitor the provider and fix harm from wrong advice. A contract allocates tasks, not the firm's regulatory duties.

questions.question: Priya at a retail bank sees card-not-present fraud rising on e-commerce purchases while in-store chip fraud stays flat. What is the best first control adjustment?

answers.text: Add step-up authentication for higher-risk online card transactions
Remove transaction limits from all in-store card purchases
Turn off card alerts to reduce customer contacts
Require branch visits for every online purchase

questions.explanation: Step-up authentication targets the risky channel without blocking all commerce, matching control strength to risk. Removing limits or disabling alerts weakens protection, and branch visits for every purchase create friction fraudsters can still bypass online.

questions.question: Several customers who were tricked by a lookalike banking website entered their credentials there, and logins using those credentials follow within the hour. Which data most helps the bank find the victims quickly?

answers.text: Waiting for each customer to notice a loss and phone the bank individually.
Correlating the timing of the phishing campaign with subsequent logins, resets and new-payee activity to prioritise accounts for outreach and protection.
Reviewing only accounts that have already lost money, since the rest are unaffected.
Blocking the lookalike website's address and assuming no credentials were captured.

questions.explanation: Victims are identifiable before losses occur by linking campaign timing to risky account events, allowing protection while funds remain. Waiting for reports or losses wastes the window when intervention can still prevent harm.

questions.question: Investigator Dan interviews a victim who authorised payments while being coached, but now insists 'the bank told me to move it.' How should Dan explore this claim?

answers.text: Accept the claim and record the bank as the instructing party
Ask open questions about who called, what number appeared, what was said and what the victim saw on screen, then compare the account with call and warning records
Tell the victim they are lying because the bank never calls
Refuse to record the claim so the report stays simple

questions.explanation: Open exploration followed by record comparison establishes who actually instructed the payment. Accepting or rejecting the claim without testing it, or omitting it from the record, leaves a central fact about instruction and liability unexamined.

questions.question: A payments firm finds its staff use three different templates for interbank recovery requests, causing missing information. What improvement aligns with scheme practice?

answers.text: Let each analyst invent their own format to encourage creativity
Remove payment identifiers from templates to protect privacy in all cases
Send recovery requests by personal email to avoid record keeping
Adopt one standard request template capturing payment identifiers, fraud basis, amounts, contact point, and indemnity wording where needed

questions.explanation: A standard, complete template reduces errors and speeds beneficiary-bank matching and assessment. Ad hoc formats, missing identifiers, and unrecorded personal emails undermine the process. Clear recording of that reasoning supports audit, complaints, and learning.

questions.question: A non-bank lender assesses application fraud risk by customer segment and finds thin-file applicants targeted by impersonators far more than existing customers. What should follow?

answers.text: Apply identical checks to all segments regardless of findings
Remove thin-file applicants from the market entirely
Strengthen identity proofing for the higher-risk segment in a proportionate, fair way
Lower checks for thin-file applicants to boost approvals

questions.explanation: Segment-level assessment lets controls match where impersonation actually concentrates, with stronger proofing for the exposed segment. Identical treatment everywhere ignores the finding, while blanket exclusion goes beyond what the risk requires.

questions.question: A customer is wrongly blocked, loses a supplier discount and pays a late fee. What remediation is most appropriate where the firm was at fault?

answers.text: A generic apology with no practical remedy
An apology plus reasonable redress such as reimbursing the fee, restoring access and correcting any adverse records the block created
Telling the customer losses are never the firm's concern
A voucher that can only be used by opening a new account

questions.explanation: Where the firm's error caused loss, apology should be matched with practical redress and record correction. A generic apology alone leaves the customer bearing the cost of the firm's mistake. The same balance applies when the next rule, threshold or warning for this channel is reviewed.

questions.question: A threshold policy says cases over a set loss value get full investigation and smaller cases get a light review. A pattern of many small first-party fraud claims by one customer emerges. The investigator should:

answers.text: Keep each claim in light review forever
Ignore the pattern because each claim is small
Aggregate the pattern and consider a full investigation based on total exposure and behaviour
Pay all claims to close the cases

questions.explanation: Repeated small claims can form a significant pattern, so aggregation by customer and behaviour is proper analysis. Reviewing each in isolation misses first-party fraud conducted in small amounts. That discipline protects both the customer and the institution if the finding is later questioned.

acams-cams.quiz_title: ACAMS CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why might a launderer accept lower returns when integrating funds into a legitimate business?

answers.text: Lower returns exempt the funds from monitoring
Legitimate businesses never produce high returns
The goal is to make the wealth appear legitimate and usable, not to maximize profit
Integration requires investing only in failing companies

questions.explanation: At integration, legitimacy and usability matter more than yield. A plausible business holding lets the criminal enjoy and explain the wealth.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of aggregating currency transactions under the BSA?

answers.text: To increase fee income from large depositors
To allow customers to choose their reporting day
To tax cash transactions above a monthly limit
To prevent evasion of the over-$10,000 report by splitting a large amount into smaller same-day transactions

questions.explanation: Aggregation defeats the simplest evasion technique: splitting one large cash movement into pieces on the same business day. Without it, the over-$10,000 report would be easily avoided.

questions.question: Which statement about customer risk rating timing is most accurate?

answers.text: A rating is assigned once and never revisited
Ratings are updated only when the customer changes products
Ratings are assigned only after suspicious activity is confirmed
A rating is assigned at onboarding and then updated as new information, reviews or transaction behavior warrant

questions.explanation: Ratings start at onboarding but live with the relationship. Confirmed suspicion is too late a trigger, and product change is only one of several events that can require an update.

questions.question: A written program should be best described as which of the following?

answers.text: As detailed as possible, regardless of the institution's actual business
Risk-based, board-approved, tailored to the institution, and implemented through procedures staff actually follow
Identical in structure for every institution of any type
Primarily a response document prepared for examiners

questions.explanation: Those four features together define a sound written program. Length alone, examiner-only preparation, and one-size-fits-all structure each miss the risk-based tailoring requirement.

questions.question: What distinguishes a well governed perpetual KYC exception?

answers.text: Exceptions are deleted if not reviewed within one day
An alert or trigger that could not be resolved automatically is routed to an analyst with the underlying data and a tracked outcome
Exceptions are hidden from management reporting to keep metrics clean
All exceptions are resolved by lowering the customer's risk rating

questions.explanation: Exceptions are where automation hands off to judgment; routing them with data and tracking preserves the control. Deleting or hiding them destroys it.

questions.question: An MSB agent processes many small money orders for different senders that all benefit one recipient. Which concern is MOST relevant?

answers.text: Proof that money orders cannot be misused
Evidence of casino chip laundering
Opening a savings account with documented salary credits
Possible structuring and layering through the agent network to obscure the true beneficiary

questions.explanation: The keyed answer reflects the sector-specific risk in the fact base for real estate, casinos, MSBs, or hawala. The strongest distractor is weaker because it describes ordinary, documented activity or misstates how the sector operates.

questions.question: When a US financial institution blocks property under OFAC rules, by when must it report the blocked property to OFAC?

answers.text: Reporting is never required for blocked property
Within 10 calendar months
Only at the end of the fiscal year
Within 10 business days

questions.explanation: Blocked property must be reported to OFAC within 10 business days. Ongoing reporting obligations also apply while property remains blocked.

questions.question: During EDD, a high-risk customer's stated source of funds is inconsistent with known occupation and account activity. What should happen next?

answers.text: Seek additional information and corroboration, and escalate for a decision on establishing or continuing the relationship if the inconsistency cannot be resolved
Ignore the inconsistency if the customer has been polite and responsive
Close the file with no documentation to avoid offending the customer
Immediately tell the customer they are suspected of money laundering

questions.explanation: An unexplained inconsistency goes to the heart of EDD and must be pursued and escalated if unresolved. Ignoring it defeats EDD, and accusing or tipping off the customer is inappropriate.

questions.question: Aisha Rahman, in the compliance team at a community bank, is handling a filing question. What should board and senior management training focus on?

answers.text: How to operate the transaction monitoring software day to day
Detailed instructions for completing individual customer onboarding forms
Nothing, because the board has no role in the compliance program
Their oversight responsibilities, the institution's risk profile and appetite, and significant compliance issues and findings

questions.explanation: Board training supports oversight: risk appetite, program status, and material findings. Operational software detail is the wrong depth for directors, and the board does have a defined oversight role.

questions.question: Marta Ellis, a screening analyst at an online payments firm, receives a potential match involving Cascade Textiles Inc.. When must sanctions screening occur?

answers.text: Only at onboarding, because lists rarely change
Only at year-end for annual reporting
At onboarding and again when sanctions lists are updated, as well as on transactions as they occur
Only when a regulator specifically asks for a screening run

questions.explanation: Lists change frequently, so onboarding-only screening quickly goes stale. Re-screening on list updates and screening transactions in flight are both essential controls.

questions.question: A customer's risk rating has not been refreshed despite two changes of business activity notified to the bank. This is a failure of what?

answers.text: Keeping scoring inputs current through event-driven and periodic updates
Transaction threshold tuning
Phonetic name matching
Case aging management

questions.explanation: Notified changes are trigger events that should refresh inputs and possibly the rating. Leaving stale inputs in place degrades both scoring and the monitoring baseline.

questions.question: A threshold sat above a structuring pattern's typical amounts for two years and the pattern was missed. This is best described as what?

answers.text: A false positive from a threshold set too low
Successful risk-based tuning
A fuzzy matching failure
A false negative from a threshold set too high

questions.explanation: A threshold above the typology's amounts lets it pass silently. That is under-detection in transaction monitoring, not a name-matching issue.

questions.question: A car wash with legitimate customers has  inflated daily cash receipts far above the number of vehicles washed. Investigators suspect illicit cash is being added to genuine takings before banking. Which typology does this BEST describe?

answers.text: A shell company with no operations holding assets on paper
Phantom shipment trade-based money laundering
Hawala settlement between trusted brokers
A front company commingling illicit funds with legitimate revenue

questions.explanation: A front company is a real operating business used to commingle illicit funds with legitimate revenue, and inflating cash receipts is the classic mechanism for cash-intensive fronts. A shell company is weaker here because the business clearly operates and serves real customers.

questions.question: A compliance officer identifies a transaction pattern that raises suspicion of terrorist financing in an otherwise low-risk account. What does the FATF approach require?

answers.text: Simplified measures continue because the account was originally rated low risk
The institution may ignore the pattern if the amounts are small
The account risk rating prevents any further review until the next annual cycle
The suspicion overrides any simplified treatment and the matter must be handled as higher risk

questions.explanation: Suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing removes the basis for simplified measures. The institution must escalate and apply appropriate enhanced scrutiny.

questions.question: Risk assessment review: a savings bank experiences a surge in politically exposed customers after a nearby government project. What is the most appropriate assessment action?

answers.text: Wait several years to see whether the trend continues before assessing it
Record the growth as a commercial success with no assessment change
Score the new exposure as low risk to keep onboarding smooth
Update the enterprise-wide assessment for the changed customer risk concentration and recalibrate affected controls

questions.explanation: A material change in customer risk concentration alters the institution's inherent risk and may change residual risk. Deferring for years or scoring for convenience leaves CDD, monitoring and staffing calibrated to the former business.

questions.question: An investigation is complete and the activity appears genuinely suspicious. What is the next step?

answers.text: Exit the account first and consider reporting only if the customer complains
Escalate for a suspicious activity report decision through the institution's designated process
Send the investigation file to the customer for comment before deciding
Wait until the customer transacts again to be extra certain

questions.explanation: Confirmed suspicious activity moves to the formal filing decision process without delay. Exiting first or waiting for more activity risks missing the filing deadline and losing evidence.

questions.question: A true sanctions match is confirmed for an existing customer. What is the immediate priority?

answers.text: Wait for the next periodic review
Ask the customer to explain before any escalation
Escalate under the sanctions procedure, block or report as required, and preserve records
Lower the customer's risk score

questions.explanation: Confirmed sanctions matches require prompt action under legal obligations, including blocking and reporting timeframes. Delay or informal handling can compound the breach.

questions.question: An employee discovers a manager instructing staff to skip customer diligence for a favored client and fears retaliation if they report it. What governance feature should protect this employee?

answers.text: A requirement to confront the client directly
A policy that reports must go through the manager involved
Automatic promotion for the manager
Confidential whistleblower channels that allow escalation outside the chain involved, with protection from retaliation

questions.explanation: Effective programs provide whistleblower channels that bypass the implicated chain and protect reporters from retaliation. Routing a report through the person reported on would defeat the channel.

questions.question: Account-opening scenario: an elderly customer without a current driving licence presents with another acceptable government-issued document or non-documentary checks under policy. What is the correct CIP handling?

answers.text: Delay all identification steps until suspicious activity occurs
CIP allows documentary and non-documentary routes; lack of one specific document is handled through the program's alternatives, not by waiving verification.
Open the account with no records so the customer is not inconvenienced
Waive identification and verification because the circumstances are unusual

questions.explanation: CIP allows documentary and non-documentary routes; lack of one specific document is handled through the program's alternatives, not by waiving verification. Unusual circumstances change the method or handling, not the obligation: required information, verification, list checks and records remain the foundation, and suspicion is not the trigger for basic identification.

questions.question: An analyst notices a customer's transactions are normal in amount but now occur through a previously unseen intermediary in another country. Which analytic approach is most likely to surface the significance of this change?

answers.text: A static rule that only checks transaction amounts
Network analytics showing the new counterparty relationship and its connections
A review limited to the customer's onboarding form
Averaging the customer's balances over the past year

questions.explanation: The change is relational, so network analysis of the new counterparty link is the revealing tool. Amount-only rules and balance averages would miss a relationship shift.

acams-ccas-certified-cryptoasset-afc-spe.quiz_title: ACAMS Certified Cryptoasset AFC Specialist (CCAS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of address clustering in blockchain analytics?

answers.text: To group addresses likely controlled by the same entity based on shared spending patterns and transaction links
To prove the legal identity of a wallet owner without any off-chain information
To merge separate blockchains into a single ledger for faster searching
To anonymize addresses so investigators cannot follow fund flows

questions.explanation: Clustering groups addresses that behave as if under common control, which helps trace an entity's activity. It does not by itself prove legal identity, merge different ledgers, or anonymize activity for investigators.

questions.question: What is an oracle in the context of a DeFi lending protocol, and why does it matter for risk?

answers.text: A data feed that brings external information, such as asset prices, on-chain; manipulated feeds can trigger wrongful liquidations or under-collateralized borrowing
A government official who approves each loan the protocol issues
A hardware device that stores the protocol's private keys offline
A marketing term for the protocol's largest liquidity provider

questions.explanation: Protocols cannot see off-chain prices, so oracles supply them, and a corrupted feed can cascade into bad liquidations and losses. An oracle is data infrastructure rather than an approving official, a key-storage device, or a liquidity provider.

questions.question: Which finding BEST supports closing an alert as explainable?

answers.text: The customer said the activity should not be questioned
No adverse media was found in a single quick search
The activity matches a documented life event, such as verified redundancy pay invested over several weeks, with amounts and timing consistent with records
The customer threatened to move their account elsewhere

questions.explanation: Closure needs positive evidence tying activity to a documented, consistent explanation. A customer's instruction, a cursory media check, and commercial pressure are not evidence that the activity is explained.

questions.question: What is the BEST way to preserve blockchain evidence so it remains usable months later at audit?

answers.text: Keep only a verbal summary in the case file
Rely on a live explorer link that may later show different labels
Delete raw exports once a chart is drawn
Save dated exports or screenshots with hashes, addresses and the source and time of capture

questions.explanation: Dated, sourced captures with core identifiers let an auditor reconstruct what the analyst saw. A verbal summary lacks verifiable detail, live links and third-party labels can change, and deleting raw material after charting removes the underlying support for conclusions.

questions.question: Why should a crypto firm test business continuity for its screening systems?

answers.text: Continuity testing is only about office furniture and lighting
If screening fails, the firm needs a governed fallback so deposits and withdrawals do not proceed unscreened unnoticed
Screening outages never affect financial crime risk
Customers will not notice if screening stops for a week

questions.explanation: A governed fallback ensures activity is not processed unscreened without anyone noticing when systems fail. Continuity here concerns control continuity, not furniture, and outages directly raise sanctions and laundering exposure.

questions.question: Which event would most directly challenge a claim that a particular public chain's history cannot be rewritten?

answers.text: A new wallet application is released
An attacker or coalition controlling a majority of validation power builds a longer alternative chain that nodes accept
A customer loses their exchange password
An explorer experiences downtime for an hour

questions.explanation: Majority control can enable history revision by producing an accepted competing chain, which is why decentralization matters. Wallet releases, password loss, and explorer downtime do not rewrite ledger history.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly shows a firm acting as a broker rather than as an exchange operator?

answers.text: The firm runs an order book where customers trade with each other
The firm operates kiosks that sell cryptoassets for inserted cash
A representative takes a client instruction and arranges the purchase through a venue for that client account
The firm safeguards private keys for hundreds of account holders

questions.explanation: Arranging a transaction for a specific client on instruction is brokerage. Running an order book is exchange operation, kiosks are ATM exchange activity, and safeguarding keys is custody, each a distinct VASP function.

questions.question: Which counterparty relationship presents the HIGHEST inherent red-flag risk for an exchange?

answers.text: A regulated pension fund buying through a prime broker
A long-standing customer using a hardware wallet for savings
A university endowment with audited financial statements
An unlicensed nested exchange routing many unidentified users through one omnibus account

questions.explanation: A nested, unlicensed service hides the underlying users behind a single account, defeating customer identification and monitoring. Regulated institutions with transparent records, and an individual using cold storage for savings, present far lower counterparty opacity and risk.

questions.question: A customer whose case has been escalated internally asks why extra questions are being asked about a transfer. How should staff respond?

answers.text: Confirm that a suspicious activity report is being prepared about them
Tell them another customer reported them to the authorities
Give a neutral explanation about routine reviews without disclosing any escalation or filing
Share the investigator's notes so the customer can correct them

questions.explanation: Staff should use a neutral, routine-review explanation and disclose nothing about escalation or filing, which could amount to tipping off. Confirming a report, inventing another source, or sharing investigator notes all compromise confidentiality and the case.

questions.question: What should happen when the same root cause produces findings in AML monitoring, sanctions screening, and onboarding at the same time?

answers.text: Each team fixes its own finding with no coordination
The findings are closed separately to improve closure rates
Only the smallest finding is addressed
A single coordinated remediation addresses the shared root cause, with progress reported centrally

questions.explanation: A shared root cause needs one coordinated fix reported centrally, otherwise each team patches symptoms while the cause persists. Separate closures, cosmetic closure rates, or fixing only the smallest finding leave the underlying weakness intact.

questions.question: What should happen when a trigger event raises a customer's rating to high at a crypto firm?

answers.text: Nothing changes until the customer asks for a review
The customer is automatically reported to law enforcement
All historical transactions are deleted from monitoring systems
Enhanced measures follow, such as refreshed diligence, closer monitoring, and any required approvals to retain the relationship

questions.explanation: A higher rating must drive proportionate action: refreshed diligence, intensified monitoring, and retention approvals where policy requires them. It does not by itself mandate a law-enforcement report, inaction, or destruction of monitoring history.

questions.question: Which pattern in stablecoin monitoring MOST suggests trade-based value transfer rather than ordinary payments?

answers.text: A freelancer receiving the same monthly amount from one client
A family sending a modest remittance each month
Repeated transfers between the same two businesses with amounts that do not match any invoices, goods movement, or stated trade relationship
A customer cashing out a long-held stablecoin position once

questions.explanation: Value moving between businesses without matching commercial substance suggests invoices or trade are being used as cover for transfer. Regular salary-like, remittance, and one-off cash-out patterns have clear economic explanations.

questions.question: A law enforcement request seeks assets in a self-custody wallet whose owner refuses to cooperate. What limitation should be communicated?

answers.text: The exchange can reset the wallet and transfer the funds
The assets can be moved by knowing the public address alone
A freeze can be applied inside the wallet software by any analyst
Without the key, seed phrase, or a custodian able to act, on-chain transfer of the assets may not be technically possible

questions.explanation: Self-custody removes any intermediary who can execute a freeze or transfer, so key access is the practical bottleneck. No exchange reset, public-address transfer, or analyst-side wallet freeze exists for such holdings.

questions.question: A compliance analyst at a virtual asset service provider notices a deposit has one confirmation. Why do many firms wait for more confirmations before crediting it?

answers.text: Additional confirmations increase the market price of the deposited asset
Exchanges are legally required to wait exactly twenty-four hours in all cases
Confirmations convert a private key into a public address for screening
Each added block makes reorganizing the chain to reverse the transaction harder and costlier

questions.explanation: Each added block makes a reorganization that reverses the transaction harder and costlier, so waiting lowers risk. Confirmations do not set prices, impose a universal 24-hour rule, or convert keys into addresses.

questions.question: An analyst notices a customer receiving many small crypto payments from unrelated senders, consolidating them, and forwarding the total abroad weekly. This resembles:

answers.text: A payroll service with full employer records
Long-term retirement saving
Ordinary staking rewards distribution
A funnel or mule aggregation pattern used to collect and forward fraud or scam proceeds

questions.explanation: Many-to-one collection followed by regular onward forwarding is the funnel pattern typical of mule aggregation of illicit proceeds. Payroll has identifiable employers and records, retirement saving accumulates rather than forwards, and staking rewards come from a protocol, not unrelated senders.

questions.question: While supporting a restraint order, an operations analyst at Fenwick Row notices the in-scope wallet received additional funds after the freeze took effect. What should happen?

answers.text: Record the post-freeze receipts, preserve them within the freeze scope as legal directs, and alert legal and the case investigator promptly
Return the new funds to the sender to keep the wallet tidy
Ignore them because the freeze date has passed
Let the customer withdraw the new funds since they arrived later

questions.explanation: Post-freeze inflows are material events that must be recorded, preserved as legal directs and escalated, since they may be further proceeds or third-party funds. Returning or releasing them without direction can breach the order, and ignoring them leaves the restrained position misstated.

questions.question: Alder Creek Exchange is offered a white-label arrangement where a partner onboards customers under Alder Creeks licence. What is the key risk question?

answers.text: What colour the partners website uses
Whether Alder Creek retains visibility and control over customer identification and monitoring under the arrangement
Whether the partner has more social media followers
Whether the partner prefers weekly or monthly invoicing

questions.explanation: The firm remains responsible for who its customers are, so visibility and control over identification and monitoring are decisive. Branding colours, follower counts and invoicing cycles have no bearing on financial crime risk.

questions.question: A payment processor offers instant crypto-to-fiat conversion at checkout. What risk does instant conversion add?

answers.text: No risk, because conversion speed removes exposure
The processor must mine the crypto it receives
Merchants can no longer receive chargebacks of any kind
The processor briefly holds market and counterparty exposure and must screen the payer before funds become fiat

questions.explanation: Instant conversion means the processor takes possession and price exposure at the moment of payment, so payer screening must occur before value is transformed. Speed increases rather than removes the need for controls, and mining is not involved.

questions.question: During a periodic review, a customer's screening produces a possible sanctions name match with a similar name but a different date of birth. What is the correct handling?

answers.text: Treat it as a confirmed match and block everything permanently
Clear it without looking because the birth dates differ
Compare all available identifiers, document why the match is or is not the customer, and escalate if the match cannot be resolved
Ask the customer whether they are the sanctioned person and accept their answer alone

questions.explanation: Potential matches are resolved by comparing identifiers — name variants, birth date, nationality, documents — and documenting the reasoning, escalating unresolved cases. Auto-blocking on a partial match harms innocent customers, dismissing it unexamined misses true matches, and the customer's own denial is not evidence.

questions.question: A group moves its nominal headquarters to a lightly regulated jurisdiction but keeps staff, customers, and servers in stricter markets. How will regulators in those markets likely view the structure?

answers.text: They must accept the headquarters jurisdiction's rules as the only applicable rules
They may assert jurisdiction based on where activity, customers, and harm occur, and treat the structure as arbitrage risk
They lose all authority once a foreign headquarters is announced
They can act only if the group voluntarily submits to examination

questions.explanation: Regulators commonly assert jurisdiction where business is conducted and customers are located, regardless of a nominal headquarters. A foreign headquarters does not extinguish local authority, compel deference to its rules, or make supervision depend on voluntary submission.

acams-cgss-certified-global-sanctions-sp.quiz_title: ACAMS Certified Global Sanctions Specialist (CGSS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why are correspondent banking relationships described as a transmission channel for extraterritorial sanctions risk?

answers.text: Correspondent accounts are legally invisible to regulators
Only the respondent bank's home regulator may examine correspondent activity
Correspondent fees are denominated only in local currency
A respondent bank's payments clear through the correspondent's jurisdiction, importing that jurisdiction's sanctions rules into transactions that otherwise look purely local

questions.explanation: Clearing through a correspondent subjects the payment to the clearing jurisdiction's sanctions regime, so a foreign respondent inherits that exposure. Correspondent activity is examinable and supervised, fees are irrelevant to jurisdiction, and regulators in the clearing jurisdiction can and do scrutinize these flows.

questions.question: When should synthetic and known-name screening tests be repeated outside their regular schedule?

answers.text: Only at year-end, regardless of events
Never, because repetition invalidates earlier results
After tuning changes, list-source changes, system upgrades, or a production miss, because each can alter what screening actually catches
Only when a regulator schedules an examination

questions.explanation: Event-driven re-testing is needed whenever configuration, data sources, or the platform change, and after any miss reveals a possible gap. A fixed year-end-only rule, refusing repetition, or waiting for an exam leaves changed screening unverified.

questions.question: A screening analyst is unsure whether a name match is a true match. What should training instruct the analyst to do FIRST?

answers.text: Follow the defined escalation and review procedure, gathering identifiers and holding the transaction rather than releasing or rejecting it unilaterally
Release the payment to avoid customer complaints
Delete the alert so queue statistics improve
Ask the customer whether they are a sanctioned party

questions.explanation: Uncertain matches must be held and escalated under procedure so a qualified review weighs the identifiers. Releasing to avoid complaints, deleting alerts and asking the customer all bypass the control the training exists to support.

questions.question: Which feature BEST distinguishes a likely false positive from possible wilful evasion in a flagged case?

answers.text: The customer responds quickly to information requests
The transaction amount is small
The customer is based in a low-risk jurisdiction
Cooperative, consistent explanations supported by documents versus shifting stories, missing records and instructions to conceal parties or routes

questions.explanation: Behaviour and evidence quality distinguish error from evasion: consistency and corroboration point to a false positive, while shifting explanations and concealment instructions point to intent. Speed of response, amount size, and home jurisdiction alone do not reliably separate the two.

questions.question: Invented Larchmont Bank redesigns screening QA after reviewers overturned many analyst dispositions. Which QA design is BEST?

answers.text: QA reviews only alerts the analysts themselves select
Independent sampling of closed alerts, blind re-performance of a subset, error feedback to analysts, and tracking of overturn rates by reason
QA limited to checking that disposition forms are fully completed
QA performed once at the end of remediation and then discontinued

questions.explanation: Effective QA independently samples closures, re-performs some blind, feeds errors back as coaching, and trends overturn reasons to fix systemic causes. Self-selected samples bias results, form-checking ignores judgment quality, and one-off QA cannot sustain the improvement.

questions.question: A bank relies on an OFAC general license that requires periodic reports. What happens if the bank completes the transactions but never files the required reports?

answers.text: Nothing, because reporting is voluntary once the transaction is complete
The general license automatically converts into a specific license
The bank has failed to comply with a condition of the authorization and may face enforcement exposure
Only the customer, never the bank, is responsible for the report

questions.explanation: Reporting and recordkeeping are binding conditions of reliance on a general license, not optional extras, so failure to file can undermine the authorization and create enforcement risk. The license does not convert form, and the party relying on and processing under the license cannot shift its compliance duty entirely to the customer.

questions.question: A government closes its airspace to a target state's aircraft as a sanctions measure. How does this differ from a military no-fly zone?

answers.text: Airspace closure is a civil regulatory denial of access to national airspace, while a military no-fly zone is enforced by armed forces to prohibit flights in a conflict area
There is no difference; both require Security Council air strikes
Airspace closure freezes the aircraft as financial assets
A military no-fly zone is administered by commercial airlines

questions.explanation: Sanctions airspace closures are sovereign regulatory measures denying entry to national airspace, whereas military no-fly zones are coercive operations enforced by armed forces. Neither concept depends on airlines administering force, and closure does not itself freeze aircraft as assets.

questions.question: A European bank clears U.S. dollar payments through a correspondent in New York. Why does this matter for its sanctions risk assessment?

answers.text: Dollar clearing through the United States can bring transactions within U.S. sanctions jurisdiction even when neither party is American
Dollar payments are exempt from sanctions because they are wholesale
Only the New York correspondent needs to assess this exposure
Currency choice affects credit risk but never sanctions jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Using the U.S. financial system for dollar clearing can create a U.S. jurisdictional nexus, extending the bank's exposure beyond its home regime. Wholesale payments are not exempt, the European bank retains its own assessment duty, and currency routing is a recognised driver of sanctions jurisdiction.

questions.question: Who should make the final decision to exit a long-standing customer relationship after repeated sanctions near-misses and one confirmed rejected transaction?

answers.text: Senior management, informed by sanctions operations and legal, because exit decisions weigh enterprise risk appetite
The alert analyst, because they know the case history best
The relationship manager, because they own the client commercially
The screening vendor, because its scoring flagged the pattern

questions.explanation: Relationship exit is a risk-appetite decision belonging to senior management with compliance and legal input. Analysts supply facts, relationship managers supply commercial context, and vendors supply tooling, but none of them owns the enterprise decision.

questions.question: A sanctions team sets its AIS-gap alert at any silence longer than a few minutes anywhere in the world. What is the flaw in this design?

answers.text: AIS gaps should never generate alerts at all
Short gaps are always evidence of evasion
Satellite coverage means gaps cannot occur innocently
Undifferentiated thresholds create noise from ordinary coverage and equipment gaps; alerts should be risk-based, weighing duration, location, vessel type and cargo sensitivity

questions.explanation: Brief signal loss is common for benign technical and coverage reasons, so effective monitoring calibrates by context such as time dark, proximity to sanctioned ports and cargo type. Gaps do merit alerts when risk-based, short gaps are not automatic proof, and coverage limitations are precisely why calibration is needed.

questions.question: The invented firm Aldergrove University accepted research funding channelled from a blocked person through an intermediary foundation and performed no donor diligence. Which lesson applies?

answers.text: Non-profit and academic institutions are outside sanctions enforcement
Donations are exempt because no goods are sold
Sanctions duties reach non-commercial actors too, and accepting value from blocked sources without diligence can produce enforcement exposure
Only the intermediary foundation can be liable for routed funds

questions.explanation: Sanctions apply across sectors, and dealings involving blocked property include receiving funds or services, not only commercial sales. Academic status confers no exemption, the donation label does not remove the dealing, and the recipient's own diligence failure matters.

questions.question: After a consent-order-style outcome, invented Aldgate Bank must remediate years of missed sanctions screening. Which remediation design is MOST complete?

answers.text: A memo reminding staff to be careful, with no review of historical transactions
An independent consultant overseeing a risk-based lookback, system replacement or tuning, enhanced controls, and board-tracked milestones
A voluntary staff survey asking whether anyone recalls problematic payments
A new logo and public statement announcing a fresh start for the compliance team

questions.explanation: Credible remediation combines independent oversight, a lookback to find and report historical violations, fixed or replaced screening systems, and milestones the board tracks to verified completion. Reminders, surveys, and public statements do not test the past, repair the control, or prove the fix worked.

questions.question: A sanctions dashboard reports only green ratings for two years while audit later finds serious breaches. Which MI design flaw most likely contributed?

answers.text: The dashboard used too many charts relative to tables
The dashboard was produced monthly rather than quarterly
The indicators measured activity and self-assessment rather than outcomes such as breaches, near misses, and overdue remediation
The dashboard was circulated to too many senior managers

questions.explanation: MI built on activity and self-assessment can stay green while real outcomes deteriorate; breach, near-miss, and remediation-ageing data would have surfaced the problem. Format choices, production frequency, and wide circulation do not explain systematically misleading content.

questions.question: Before a rewritten alert-handling procedure goes live, a sanctions manager arranges for working analysts to walk through realistic alerts using only the draft text. What is the purpose of this step?

answers.text: To let analysts rewrite the policy's risk appetite
To satisfy a training attendance requirement
To replace the need for formal approval of the procedure
To test usability: ambiguous steps, missing system details, and unrealistic sequences surface while the text can still be corrected

questions.explanation: A practical walkthrough reveals where desk-level wording fails the people who must follow it under time pressure. It does not change risk appetite, substitute for approval, or serve as mere attendance-taking.

questions.question: A fintech's new feature lets users buy fractional interests in tokenized real-world assets. A designated person attempts to invest through a nominee. The control that MOST directly addresses this is:

answers.text: Reducing minimum investment amounts
Displaying asset valuations more frequently
Offering more asset categories
Beneficial-ownership verification and screening of investors and their funding wallets, not just the nominee account holder

questions.explanation: Nominee arrangements are defeated by verifying and screening the true beneficial owner and the source wallet, not only the named holder. Valuation displays, product range, and minimums do not address hidden designated ownership.

questions.question: A letter-of-credit presentation contains a bill of lading dated before the vessel's first recorded call at the load port, and the discrepancy was waived without inquiry. What risk did the waiver create?

answers.text: None, because banks deal only in documents and dates never matter
Duplicate financing of the same cargo by two banks
A small delay in reimbursement to the beneficiary
Accepting an impossible chronology can let a fabricated or diverted shipment pass as genuine trade

questions.explanation: A loading document that predates the vessel's arrival is chronologically impossible, and waiving it without inquiry removes the one check that would expose a false shipment. Banks do deal in documents, which is why document integrity matters; duplicate financing and reimbursement delay are secondary and do not describe this chronology problem.

questions.question: Fictional Ironhaven Bank screened IMO numbers for owned vessels but not for vessels carrying collateralized cargo on third-party ships. A designated vessel carried the cargo. What gap does this reveal?

answers.text: Cargo insurance was priced too low for the route
The crew nationality was not recorded in the loan file
Screening scope was drawn around the banks own assets rather than all sanctioned-party touchpoints in the transaction
The cargo description used a generic commodity code

questions.explanation: Sanctions exposure follows the transaction, including the carrying vessel, not just assets the bank owns. Insurance pricing, crew details, and commodity coding do not explain why a designated carrier escaped screening.

questions.question: A blocked person owns 30 percent of an investment vehicle, and that vehicle owns 80 percent of a port operator. No other blocked interest exists. Applying OFAC's indirect-ownership approach, what is the port operator's status?

answers.text: It is blocked, because any chain touching a blocked person blocks every entity below it
It is blocked, because the vehicle's 80 percent stake is attributed in full regardless of the blocked person's minority stake in the vehicle
It is not automatically blocked through that chain, because the vehicle is not itself a blocked entity whose stake counts toward the threshold
It is blocked at a deemed 24 percent level, which still triggers blocking

questions.explanation: Indirect ownership counts through entities the blocked person owns 50 percent or more of; at 30 percent the vehicle is not blocked, so its 80 percent stake is not attributed as blocked ownership of the operator. Chains are not automatically tainted, full attribution does not apply, and a multiplied percentage is not how the rule works.

questions.question: The same corporate customer generates separate alerts in its payments account, its trade account, and its treasury relationship, each worked by a different analyst. What case-management practice BEST improves this?

answers.text: Requiring each analyst to close their alert without seeing the others
Deleting two of the three alerts as duplicates
Linking the alerts into a single case on the party, so one analyst sees the full relationship and dispositions stay consistent
Rotating the alerts daily so no analyst sees the whole picture

questions.explanation: Party-level case consolidation gives one reviewer the complete context, prevents contradictory dispositions, and builds a single audit record. Fragmented or blinded review invites inconsistency, related alerts are evidence rather than duplicates to delete, and deliberate rotation away from full context defeats the purpose.

questions.question: An aid agency's shipment of shelter kits is authorized in the EU and UK, but its bank's sole correspondent for the destination has exited the corridor entirely. Agency staff propose using a money-service business that asks no sanctions questions. What should the bank advise?

answers.text: Decline the unquestioning channel, help document the authorized shipment, and support the search for a regulated alternative corridor or regulator-facilitated solution
Endorse the money-service business because the aid is authorized
Endorse it if the agency uses several small transfers instead of one
Advise the agency to label the kits as commercial samples

questions.explanation: Corridor exit requires finding a regulated, transparent alternative, not an unquestioning channel that creates evasion and financial-crime risk. Small transfers and false labelling compound the problem even for authorized aid.

aee-certified-energy-auditor.quiz_title: AEE Certified Energy Auditor (CEA) Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Before a walk-through at an operating factory, what should the audit team complete on arrival?

answers.text: Begin opening equipment guards to save time
Attend the site safety briefing, confirm personal protective equipment, and agree on communication and muster procedures
Tour the plant unescorted to observe natural behavior
Shut down a production line to test motor loads

questions.explanation: A safety briefing, correct protective equipment, and agreed communications are prerequisites for any work in an operating plant.

questions.question: For a lighting audit in a warehouse, where should lux measurements be taken to be comparable to recommended levels?

answers.text: Directly under each fixture, as close to the lamp as possible
At the workplane height where tasks are performed, on a grid across the space, with daylight conditions noted
Only at the doorway, where light is dimmest
At eye level facing a window at noon

questions.explanation: Illuminance recommendations apply at the task plane. A grid at workplane height, with daylight contribution recorded, shows whether areas are over- or under-lit.

questions.question: Why do you use lighting power density as an audit metric when comparing two floors of the same building?

answers.text: It measures the color quality of the light on each floor
It proves which floor has the better daylight design
It replaces the need to count fixtures or operating hours
It normalizes connected lighting load by area, so a larger floor is not penalized for higher total watts when efficiency is compared

questions.explanation: Dividing watts by area puts spaces of different sizes on a common basis. The auditor pairs the density figure with hours and controls to explain energy use, rather than treating density alone as consumption.

questions.question: When an auditor recommends tank insulation on an older water heater, what check must come first?

answers.text: Insulate immediately regardless of tank condition
Confirm the manufacturer's guidance and the tank's condition, and do not insulate over controls, vents, or a tank that should be replaced due to corrosion or age
Cover the burner access and flue for maximum saving
Set the thermostat to its maximum before insulating

questions.explanation: Insulation only pays on a tank worth keeping and must never block controls or combustion air paths. The auditor documents condition and safe coverage limits.

questions.question: A client asks why you photograph and probe window units instead of relying only on the window schedule. What do you explain?

answers.text: Schedules always list a better U-factor than was installed, so field work raises savings
Field checks are only needed to confirm the frame color for the report
Installed units may differ from the schedule, seals fail, and glazing may have been replaced, so observed condition determines the U-factor and infiltration you credit
Window field work replaces the need to examine walls and roofs

questions.explanation: As-built windows often differ from design documents, and failed seals and replacement glazing change performance. The auditor bases loads on what is actually installed and its condition.

questions.question: A warehouse owner will use audit results to support a loan application for a major HVAC replacement. Which level best fits that decision?

answers.text: A Level 1 walk-through assessment
A Level 3 investment-grade audit
A benchmarking exercise with no engineering analysis
A lighting-only spot survey

questions.explanation: Lending and major capital decisions need the detailed data, refined costing, and risk treatment of an investment-grade Level 3 audit.

questions.question: A residual plot from an office building's regression fans out and curves upward at high degree days. What should the auditor suspect?

answers.text: The model fits perfectly at all loads
The intercept should be reported as the savings
A missing driver or a non-linear relationship is distorting the fit
The weather data should be discarded without review

questions.explanation: Patterned residuals, rather than random scatter, signal model misspecification such as an omitted occupancy or production driver.

questions.question: A $90,000 measure saves $20,000 in year 1, with savings escalating 3% yearly. Why is a flat $20,000-per-year NPV in a draft understated?

answers.text: Flat savings always overstate NPV when prices rise
Escalation applies only to costs, never to savings
It omits the escalation the analysis assumes, so later years' savings are valued too low
The first-year saving should be doubled instead

questions.explanation: If energy prices escalate at 3%, each later year's avoided cost grows. Holding savings flat contradicts the stated escalation assumption and understates present value.

questions.question: An auditor notes a chilled-water system operating with a 6°F temperature difference across coils instead of the design 12°F. This low delta-T condition causes what?

answers.text: Lower pumping energy
Higher flow and pumping energy for the same cooling delivered
Improved chiller efficiency
Reduced fan energy

questions.explanation: Delivering the same cooling at half the temperature difference requires roughly double the flow, raising pumping energy.

questions.question: An auditor measures supply air at 55°F and room air at 75°F with 3,000 cfm delivered. What is the sensible cooling provided? Use Q = 1.08 × cfm × ΔT.
questions.explanation: Q = 1.08 × 3,000 × 20 = 64,800 Btu/h of sensible cooling.

questions.question: Belt losses in a well-maintained synchronous belt drive compared with a worn V-belt drive are generally what, and what should the auditor do?

answers.text: Identical, so no action
Higher for synchronous belts
Unmeasurable
Lower for synchronous belts; the auditor notes drive type and condition when estimating transmitted power

questions.explanation: Synchronous belts avoid slip and typically transmit power more efficiently than worn or slipping V-belts. Recording drive type and condition refines the auditor's estimate of how much shaft power reaches the load.

questions.question: A gymnasium's demand-controlled ventilation holds CO2 well below target at full occupancy while the fan runs at maximum speed. What should the auditor investigate?

answers.text: Whether the CO2 setpoint is far lower than the design intent requires, causing unnecessary ventilation and fan energy
Whether spectators prefer maximum airflow
Whether the fan motor should be enlarged
Whether CO2 control should be banned from gymnasiums

questions.explanation: An overly conservative CO2 setpoint ventilates for air quality already achieved, at real fan and conditioning cost. The auditor compares the programmed setpoint with the design basis for the space.

questions.question: Spot measurements and schedules suggest a school's plug loads total 180,000 kWh per year while whole-building use is 1,200,000 kWh. What plug-load share should appear in the auditor's end-use breakdown?

answers.text: 15 percent
18 percent
12 percent
25 percent

questions.explanation: The share is 180,000 / 1,200,000 = 0.15, or 15 percent of annual use.

questions.question: While auditing a community clinic, you find a utility prescriptive program that pays a fixed dollar amount per qualifying fixture installed. How does this differ from a custom program when you document it?

answers.text: Prescriptive incentives use a pre-set payment for a listed measure, while custom incentives are calculated from the project's estimated or measured savings
Prescriptive incentives always require a year of post-installation metering, while custom incentives never do
Prescriptive incentives are paid only to the utility, while custom incentives are paid to the contractor
Prescriptive incentives cover the full installed cost, while custom incentives cover none of it

questions.explanation: A prescriptive program lists eligible measures and a fixed payment per unit, so the auditor can estimate the incentive from the inventory count. A custom program bases payment on project-specific savings, which requires a savings calculation and usually closer utility review.

questions.question: An auditor trends a variable-air-volume system and finds supply air cooled to 55 degrees F while many zones simultaneously fire electric reheat to stay warm at low load. Which measure should be investigated?

answers.text: Lower the supply-air temperature further so reheat coils cycle less often
Raise the supply-air temperature and reduce zone minimum airflow where ventilation allows, so cooling and reheat stop fighting each other
Set every zone minimum damper to its maximum position for stability
Replace the chiller with a larger unit to support the combined load

questions.explanation: Simultaneous cooling and reheat wastes energy on both sides of the coil, a classic auditor finding from trend data. Supply-air reset and right-sized zone minimums attack the waste while preserving required ventilation.

questions.question: A hotel's two 400,000 Btu/h water heaters both fire for only 3 to 4 minutes at a time throughout a low-occupancy week, and metered hot water use is about one-third of design. What sizing evidence should the auditor record?

answers.text: The heaters are undersized because they fire frequently
Frequent firing proves the heaters are operating at peak efficiency
Short cycling at low load combined with metered use well below design capacity indicates substantial oversizing and high standby loss
Metered use below design proves the meters are faulty

questions.explanation: Short, frequent burns at a fraction of design load show capacity far exceeds actual demand. The auditor logs firing patterns, occupancy, and metered use to quantify standby and cycling losses.

questions.question: You blower-door test a multifamily building and find high leakage at elevator shafts, pipe chases, and recessed lights, while windows are relatively tight. Where do you direct the air-sealing recommendation?

answers.text: Sealing the shafts, chases, and ceiling penetrations first
Sealing only the window perimeters
Adding weatherstripping to exterior doors only
Full window replacement as the first measure

questions.explanation: The test and visual inspection locate the dominant leakage paths at shafts, chases, and penetrations, so sealing those paths captures most of the saving. Window work would address a minor share at much higher cost.

questions.question: A chiller measure reduces demand by 120 kW at the building's own afternoon peak, but the utility's system peak, which sets the coincident demand charge, occurs two hours later when the reduction is only 40 kW. What demand saving should the auditor claim for that charge?

answers.text: 120 kW
80 kW, the average of the two
160 kW
40 kW

questions.explanation: Coincident charges are set at the utility's system peak time, so only the 40 kW reduction present at that hour counts for that charge. Claiming the building-peak reduction would overstate the saving.

questions.question: In a hospital, which lighting areas offer the auditor the least controls savings opportunity, and how should that shape the report?

answers.text: All hospital areas equally, because occupancy patterns are uniform across a hospital
Only the parking structure, because interior hospital lighting cannot be controlled at all
Surgical suites, which should be placed on standard occupancy sensors immediately
24-hour clinical and egress areas, where lights must run continuously; the report focuses those areas on wattage reduction and assigns controls savings mainly to offices, waiting, and support spaces

questions.explanation: Continuous-operation areas have few off-hours for controls to capture. The auditor avoids inflating controls savings there and instead emphasizes efficacy, while targeting controls where occupancy actually varies.

questions.question: A plant has a large variable-speed compressor and two smaller fixed-speed machines, and all three often run partly loaded. What control finding do you most likely document?

answers.text: The dryers are oversized for the receiver volume
The leak tags were placed too close together
The receiver is painted a color that absorbs heat
Poor sequencing is wasting energy, and the audit should recommend a control scheme that keeps one machine as trim and avoids multiple partly loaded units

questions.explanation: Multiple partly loaded fixed-speed machines draw high unloaded power. Sequencing so base machines run fully loaded and one unit trims the load is a standard, high-value audit recommendation.

certified-fraud-examiner.quiz_title: ACFE Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a trial balance in detecting accounting fraud?

answers.text: To prove that no fraud has occurred
To replace the need for source documents
To value inventory for tax purposes
To check that total debits equal total credits and surface out-of-balance manipulations

questions.explanation: A trial balance verifies the mechanical equality of debits and credits; imbalances can reveal posting manipulations, though balanced entries can still be fraudulent.

questions.question: Tokenization reduces card fraud risk in stored payments because:

answers.text: It stores the full card number in more places
It replaces the card number with a substitute value that is useless to thieves if the merchant's stored data is breached
It eliminates the need for authorizations
It guarantees every transaction is legitimate

questions.explanation: Tokens have no value outside their intended context, so a breach of stored tokens does not yield usable card numbers. Authorization and fraud checks still apply to each transaction.

questions.question: An examiner needs to annotate relationships between documents while analyzing them. Where should those annotations go?

answers.text: On sticky notes attached to the originals
In pencil on the backs of originals
In the evidence log's description field
On working copies or in a separate analysis file, never on the original evidence

questions.explanation: Analysis belongs on copies and in workpapers so the originals remain exactly as collected and available for independent examination.

questions.question: What are compensatory damages in a civil fraud case intended to do?

answers.text: Punish the defendant in proportion to their wealth regardless of loss
Pay the plaintiff a fixed statutory bonus for filing suit
Reimburse the court for the cost of the trial
Make the injured party whole for actual losses caused by the fraud, such as funds taken, costs incurred, and proven consequential losses

questions.explanation: Compensation ties recovery to proven, caused loss. Punishment is the separate function of punitive damages, which have their own requirements.

questions.question: Communicating the program to employees should emphasize:

answers.text: Technical descriptions of audit sampling methods
Threats of prosecution as the sole message
What the standards are, that monitoring and proactive audits occur, how to report, and that reports are protected and acted upon
Communication only when a fraud case becomes public

questions.explanation: Communication drives both deterrence and reporting: employees must know the rules, believe detection is real, and trust the reporting route. Fear-only messaging suppresses tips.

questions.question: Reviewing the payroll master file change log for after-hours changes by the payroll processor is a detection step for:

answers.text: Unauthorized rate, deduction, or employee-record changes that enable payroll schemes
Vendor invoice duplication
Customer payment lapping
Inventory shrinkage

questions.explanation: Payroll schemes often require standing-data changes; logs showing who changed what and when expose unauthorized modifications.

questions.question: A casino patron buys chips with a large amount of illicit cash, gambles minimally, and redeems the chips for a check. The stage of laundering this best illustrates is:

answers.text: Integration only, because a check was issued
Structuring of bank deposits
Layering through international trade
Placement, because illicit cash is being introduced into a financial channel in a form that looks like legitimate winnings

questions.explanation: Placement is getting criminal proceeds into the legitimate system. Converting cash to chips and then to a check disguises the cash's origin as gambling proceeds.

questions.question: A subject is suspected of stealing to cover a family medical crisis. Which statement best reflects theme development?

answers.text: 'We will prosecute unless you confess in five minutes.'
'Sometimes good people under enormous pressure at home make a decision they would never normally make; help me understand what was happening then.'
'Your coworkers all say you are a thief.'
'Only a criminal would do what you did.'

questions.explanation: The statement offers a sympathetic rationalization tied to the subject's circumstances, lowering the barrier to admission; the alternatives shame or threaten.

questions.question: A witness asks to have their union representative or attorney present. How should the examiner handle the request?

answers.text: Cancel the entire investigation
Follow applicable law, policy, and counsel guidance, and document how the request was addressed
Interview the representative instead about all topics
Refuse and lock the interview room door

questions.explanation: Representation rights vary by setting and jurisdiction; handling the request lawfully and on the record protects the interview's product.

questions.question: A suspended employee asks whether suspension means the company has decided they stole funds. How should the suspension be framed and handled to reduce legal risk?

answers.text: As a neutral, documented interim measure to protect people, assets, and evidence while facts are gathered, without prejudging the outcome
As punishment that will be announced to customers
As a finding that will be reversed only if they confess
As an unpaid penalty with no written record

questions.explanation: Framing suspension as a neutral protective step, consistently applied and documented, avoids converting an interim measure into a prejudgment that supports defamation or wrongful-discipline claims.
