questions.explanation: Producers capture the most energy; only ~10% passes to each successive trophic level (the rest is lost as heat, respiration, and waste). Energy is conserved physically but degraded to unusable heat — it is not recycled like nutrients.

questions.question: Two resistors of 2 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in series. What is their equivalent resistance, in ohms?
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: 2 + 12 = 14 Ω, because the same current traverses both and their voltage drops sum.

questions.question:
Apprenticeship is the oldest educational technology and the one our age finds hardest to defend, because its central transaction looks, to modern eyes, like exploitation: the apprentice gives years of cheap labor; the master gives — what, exactly, that a book could not? The answer is tacit knowledge, the vast submerged portion of any craft that its practitioners know but cannot say. The master joiner hears when the plane is right; she cannot fully tell you what right sounds like, but she can stop your hand when it is wrong, ten thousand times, until your hand knows. Apprenticeship is the transmission system for knowledge that lives in correction rather than in statement. This is why its decline, lamented as a loss of tradition, is more precisely a loss of bandwidth: schools and manuals transmit the statable with wonderful efficiency and the tacit hardly at all, and a civilization that educates only through statement will find its crafts thinning — each generation restarting closer to the book and further from the hand. The revival of apprenticeship in unlikely places — surgery, software, cooking — is the market rediscovering what the lecture cannot carry.

Which of the following most accurately describes the main idea of the passage?

answers.text: Apprenticeship transmits tacit knowledge — what practitioners know but cannot state — through correction, which books and lectures cannot carry, explaining its modern revival
Schools transmit tacit knowledge as efficiently as masters do
All craft knowledge can be fully written in manuals
Apprenticeship is simply a system of exploitation

questions.explanation: The thesis: the master's payment is tacit knowledge, transmitted by ten thousand corrections; statement-based education loses that bandwidth — hence apprenticeship's return in surgery, software, and cooking.

questions.question: Counting glycolysis, the citric acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation, one glucose gives roughly:

answers.text: About 12-14 ATP
About 38-40 ATP
About 30-32 ATP
Exactly 2 ATP

questions.explanation: Modern accounting (≈2.5 ATP per NADH, ≈1.5 per FADH2, minus transport costs) gives roughly 30-32 ATP per glucose. The older textbook figure of 36-38 used integer P/O ratios of 3 and 2; 2 ATP is glycolysis's net alone.

questions.question: In a cross Aa x Aa, what percentage of the offspring are expected to be the dominant phenotype?
questions.explanation: The cross Aa x Aa gives AA and Aa (3 of 4) show the dominant phenotype, so the expected share is 75%. Mendelian probabilities come from the Punnett square's equally likely genotype classes.

questions.question:
Apprenticeship is the oldest educational technology and the one our age finds hardest to defend, because its central transaction looks, to modern eyes, like exploitation: the apprentice gives years of cheap labor; the master gives — what, exactly, that a book could not? The answer is tacit knowledge, the vast submerged portion of any craft that its practitioners know but cannot say. The master joiner hears when the plane is right; she cannot fully tell you what right sounds like, but she can stop your hand when it is wrong, ten thousand times, until your hand knows. Apprenticeship is the transmission system for knowledge that lives in correction rather than in statement. This is why its decline, lamented as a loss of tradition, is more precisely a loss of bandwidth: schools and manuals transmit the statable with wonderful efficiency and the tacit hardly at all, and a civilization that educates only through statement will find its crafts thinning — each generation restarting closer to the book and further from the hand. The revival of apprenticeship in unlikely places — surgery, software, cooking — is the market rediscovering what the lecture cannot carry.

The author describes apprenticeship as a transmission system for knowledge that lives in:

answers.text: Lectures and demonstrations
Silent observation alone
Correction rather than in statement
Written examinations

questions.explanation: 'Apprenticeship is the transmission system for knowledge that lives in correction rather than in statement.'

questions.question:
The professions maintain their status by a bargain that is rarely stated outright. Society grants a profession a monopoly — only its members may practice — plus the right to discipline its own, and in exchange the profession undertakes to police competence and ethics from within, sparing the state the cost of doing it badly from without. The bargain's weak point is structural: the body that judges is composed of the judged. Peer review of a surgeon's outcomes, a bar association's inquiry into a lawyer — these are conducted by people whose own reputations are entangled with the collective reputation they are asked to police. The predictable result is a disciplinary system that is vigorous against outsiders practicing without a license — a threat to the monopoly — and lenient toward insiders whose misconduct is merely a threat to the public. This is not hypocrisy so much as incentive: institutions reliably protect the asset they exist to protect. Reform, if it is to work, must therefore change the composition of the judging body — importing lay members with no stake in the collective reputation — rather than exhorting the insiders to be braver.

The author says professional discipline is predictably vigorous against:

answers.text: Members who charge low fees
Insiders whose misconduct endangers the public
Retired members of the profession
Outsiders practicing without a license, who threaten the monopoly

questions.explanation: Discipline is 'vigorous against outsiders practicing without a license — a threat to the monopoly — and lenient toward insiders whose misconduct is merely a threat to the public.'

questions.question:
Investigators compared enzyme activity in wild-type cells and in cells carrying a mutation in gene Q, measuring 50 independent samples per group. Wild-type cells averaged 84 units of activity and the mutant cells averaged 27 units; the difference had a p-value of 0.003.

With this study in mind, does this experiment establish that the mutation CAUSES the lower activity?

answers.text: Yes — any observed association between a gene and a trait proves causation automatically
Only if the same result is obtained in human patients
No — experiments can never support causal conclusions of any kind
It supports a causal effect, provided the groups differed only in the mutation (controlled genetic background and conditions)

questions.explanation: A controlled experiment that manipulates one variable (the mutation) while holding background and conditions constant does support causation; mere association would not. Experiments are precisely the tool for causal inference — human replication is not required for the causal logic.

questions.question:
A map, Borges famously suggested, that perfectly reproduced its territory would be useless — a mile-to-the-mile cartography collapsing under its own completeness. The fable is usually told as a joke about representation, but it conceals a working principle of the mapmaker's art: every map is a theory of what matters. To map a coastline for sailors is to privilege soundings and hazards; to map it for generals is to privilege anchorages and approaches; the coastline itself is indifferent to both. Trouble begins when one map's theory is mistaken for the territory's truth. The road atlas taught generations of drivers to experience their countries as networks of highways joining cities, with the land between reduced to green interval. That is not a false picture — the highways are really there. It is a partial picture worn smooth by use into invisibility, and its partiality has consequences: we govern, fund, and imagine the mapped world more readily than the unmapped one. Cartography's power lies not in its inaccuracies but in its selections.

Borges's fable of the mile-to-mile map is introduced in order to establish that:

answers.text: Fiction writers understand geography better than mapmakers
Completeness in a map would destroy its usefulness — selection is the essence of the art
Ancient cartographers attempted full-scale maps
Territory is more interesting than representation

questions.explanation: The fable 'conceals a working principle': because a complete map is useless, every map must select — it is a theory of what matters.

questions.question:
A research team measured social media use and self-reported loneliness in a large sample of adults and found a correlation of r = 0.62 between them: people with higher social media use tended to report higher self-reported loneliness.

In this study, why can the researchers NOT conclude from this study alone that one variable causes the other?

answers.text: The sample of adults is too small to study
A third variable might influence both, or the causal direction might run the other way
Correlations are never statistically significant
Self-report measures cannot be correlated with anything

questions.explanation: Correlational designs leave directionality and third-variable explanations open — the two classic reasons correlation is not causation. Correlations can be significant, large samples help precision, and self-reports are legitimately correlated in many studies.

questions.question: An organic synthesis has a theoretical yield of 100 g of product, but the isolated yield is 70% of theoretical. How many grams of product were actually isolated?
questions.explanation: Actual yield = percent yield x theoretical yield = 70% x 100 = 70 g. The percent yield compares what was isolated against the stoichiometric maximum.

questions.question: The process by which children learn the cultural expectations of masculinity and femininity is:

answers.text: Biological maturation of secondary sex characteristics
Gender socialization — learning the norms and roles associated with one's gender through family, peers, school, and media
Sex determination, which is purely chromosomal
Occupational segregation in adult employment

questions.explanation: Sex is the biological category; gender is the cultural meaning attached to it, transmitted through socialization from birth (clothing, toys, praised behaviors). Occupational segregation is one adult outcome of the process, not the process itself.

questions.question: A 50 mL sample of HCl is titrated with NaOH. If the HCl concentration is 0.5 M and the titration requires 20 mL of NaOH to reach the equivalence point, what is the NaOH concentration?
questions.explanation: At equivalence, moles of acid equal moles of base: (50 mL x 0.5 M) = (20 mL x Mb), so Mb = (50 x 0.5)/20 = 1.25 M.

questions.question: According to Weber's law, if the just noticeable difference for a 500 g weight is 10% of the standard weight, what is the JND in grams?
questions.explanation: JND = k x I = 10% x 500 g = 50 g. Weber's fraction gives the increment as a proportion of the standard stimulus.

questions.question:
Every reader of biography knows the experience: three hundred pages into a life, the evidence thins, and the biographer's voice, hitherto discreet, begins to swell. 'She must have felt...' 'Surely he.' The subjunctive creep is not a failure of diligence but a structural temptation of the genre, which promises a whole person and inherits only paper. The honest biographers signal the gap; the dishonest pave it. Yet the reader's complicity deserves notice too. We do not buy biographies to be told where the letters end. We buy the illusion — skillfully maintained — that a stranger's interior can be recovered entire, and we punish, with our indifference, the scrupulous biographer who keeps pointing at the holes. The market thus selects against the virtue it praises. Biography's golden ages are not those with the most archives but those whose readers were most willing to be pleased by plausible connective tissue and least inclined to ask what it was made of.

The author's attitude toward biographers who fill gaps without signaling them is best described as:

answers.text: Indifferent, since all biography is fiction
Fully approving, since readers demand it
Critical of the dishonesty, while acknowledging the pressures that produce it
Surprised, since the practice is rare

questions.explanation: The passage calls such writers 'the dishonest [who] pave it' — critical — while framing the practice as a structural temptation reinforced by the market.

ap-psychology.quiz_title: AP Psychology Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A neuron at rest is stimulated and its membrane suddenly becomes much less negative inside as sodium ions rush in through opened channels. This rapid change that launches the impulse is called

answers.text: depolarization
repolarization through sodium influx
the refractory period
reuptake of sodium

questions.explanation: Depolarization is the rapid reduction in the neuron's internal negative charge caused by sodium ions flowing into the cell.

questions.question: Two travelers cross six time zones, one flying east and one flying west. The eastward traveler typically has the harder adjustment mainly because it is harder for the circadian system to:

answers.text: Fall asleep later than usual than earlier
Advance the sleep schedule earlier than to delay it later
Produce melatonin at any time of day
Enter REM sleep after travel

questions.explanation: Most people's internal clock runs slightly longer than 24 hours, so delaying sleep westward is easier than advancing it earlier eastward, making eastward jet lag worse.

questions.question: A hospital wants to ease night-shift nurses' adaptation using circadian principles. The most directly supported strategy is to manage the timing of:

answers.text: Caffeine doses only, ignoring light
Bright light exposure during the shift and darkness during daytime sleep
Extra REM sleep by napping at random times
Growth hormone supplements

questions.explanation: Light is the strongest cue resetting the circadian clock, so bright light at work and dark conditions for daytime sleep help shift workers align sleep with their schedule.

questions.question: Kept in constant dim light with no clocks, a volunteer's sleep-wake cycle settles into a rhythm slightly longer than 24 hours. The brain structure whose activity generates this internal rhythm is the:

answers.text: Hippocampus
Cerebellum
Suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus
Amygdala

questions.explanation: The suprachiasmatic nucleus acts as the master circadian clock, generating a roughly 24-hour rhythm that light normally entrains to the day.

questions.question: Light entering the eye produces vision through an ordered sequence in the retina. Which sequence correctly orders the first stages of processing?

answers.text: Ganglion cells, then photoreceptors, then bipolar cells
Photoreceptors, then bipolar cells, then ganglion cells, whose axons form the optic nerve
Bipolar cells, then ganglion cells, then photoreceptors
Photoreceptors, then ganglion cells, then the lens

questions.explanation: Rods and cones transduce light first and pass signals to bipolar cells, which in turn activate ganglion cells. The axons of ganglion cells leave the eye as the optic nerve.

questions.question: An axon wrapped in myelin conducts impulses far faster than a bare axon of the same diameter, largely because the electrical signal effectively jumps between the exposed gaps in the insulation. Those gaps are the

answers.text: synaptic vesicles
nodes of Ranvier
dendritic spines
terminal buttons

questions.explanation: Nodes of Ranvier are the unmyelinated gaps where the action potential is regenerated, producing fast saltatory conduction.

questions.question: A researcher needs to know the exact millisecond at which the brain first responds differently to an unexpected tone, even though pinpointing the precise patch of cortex responsible is less important. Which method best fits this need?

answers.text: A CT scan, because it gives detailed images of brain structure
An EEG, because its electrical recording has excellent temporal resolution
A PET scan, because it tracks radioactive glucose use over minutes
A lesion study, because removing tissue reveals its function

questions.explanation: EEG records electrical activity with millisecond precision, making it ideal for timing brain responses, though it localizes their source only roughly.

questions.question: After a head injury, a physician mainly needs a detailed picture of the brain's anatomy to locate a possible bleed, and does not need to measure moment-to-moment activity. The most appropriate tool is:

answers.text: A structural MRI scan
An EEG recording
A PET scan of glucose metabolism
Single-neuron recording

questions.explanation: Structural MRI produces detailed anatomical images without measuring activity, which suits locating physical damage such as a bleed.

questions.question: A team wants to scan the same volunteers many times over several weeks to watch activity change as they learn a skill, and wants to avoid repeated exposure to a radioactive tracer. Which method should they choose?

answers.text: An EEG, because it images deep structures directly
A CT scan, because it measures blood oxygen levels
A PET scan, because it requires no injected substance
An fMRI, because it tracks blood-oxygen changes without radioactivity

questions.explanation: fMRI detects activity indirectly through blood-oxygen changes and uses no radioactive tracer, so it can be repeated safely across many sessions.

questions.question: In a bakery quality lab, staff can just barely detect a 4-gram increase in a 200-gram roll. Assuming Weber's law holds for this judgment, how large an increase should they just barely detect in a 1,000-gram loaf?

answers.text: 4 grams
10 grams
100 grams
20 grams

questions.explanation: Weber's law says the just noticeable difference is a constant proportion of the original intensity. The fraction here is 4/200, or 1/50, and 1/50 of 1,000 grams is 20 grams.

questions.question: No single neuron can fire much faster than about 1,000 times per second, yet listeners hear pitches well above 1,000 cycles per second through timing codes. Groups of neurons solve this problem by taking turns firing in rotation, a mechanism called:

answers.text: The volley principle, in which alternating groups of neurons fire in sequence
Sensory adaptation of the auditory nerve
Lateral inhibition in the cochlea
The gate-control mechanism applied to hearing

questions.explanation: Under the volley principle, groups of neurons alternate firing so their combined rate can follow frequencies no single cell could match. This extends timing-based pitch coding to higher frequencies.

questions.question: Shown a classic Kanizsa figure, viewers clearly see the edges of a bright triangle in the middle even though no lines are drawn there and the region is the same white as the background. Perceiving contours that do not physically exist shows that perception:

answers.text: Actively constructs organization beyond the information directly present in the stimulus
Is a passive recording of every line on the page
Depends entirely on rods in the peripheral retina
Occurs only when sensory adaptation has taken place

questions.explanation: Illusory contours are perceived edges with no corresponding change in the retinal image. The visual system infers an occluding surface and constructs the boundary.

questions.question: A researcher briefly disrupts activity in a small cortical area with magnetic pulses while volunteers perform a visual task, and their accuracy drops only during the disruption. This design is stronger than a brain scan alone because it can support a conclusion about:

answers.text: Which neurotransmitter the area releases
The exact age at which the area matured
Whether activity in that area is causally necessary for the task
Which genes built that area

questions.explanation: Temporarily disrupting an area and observing a performance change provides causal evidence about that area's role, whereas scans alone show only correlation between activity and behavior.

questions.question: A student has red-green color deficiency: one cone type is missing, and reds and greens are confused, yet blue-yellow discrimination is completely normal and complementary afterimages still occur in the intact pairings. This full pattern is best explained by:

answers.text: Combining trichromatic processing at the receptors with opponent-process organization at later stages
Trichromatic theory alone, with no opponent organization anywhere
Opponent-process theory alone, with no specialized cone types
Feature detectors for lines, which also code all color information

questions.explanation: Three cone types explain receptor-level color coding and the effects of a missing cone type, while opponent pairing explains afterimages and why intact pairings remain normal. The two theories describe successive stages.

questions.question: Participants who are sleep-deprived before viewing an event, and again before a suggestive interview, later endorse more suggested details as genuinely seen than rested participants do. The integrated explanation is that sleep loss both weakens encoding of the original event and:

answers.text: Improves source monitoring
Impedes the source monitoring needed to tell suggested details from perceived ones
Eliminates suggestibility entirely
Makes all memories uniformly accurate

questions.explanation: A weak original trace leaves gaps, and sleep-deprived source monitoring is poor at tagging where a detail came from. Together the two deficits make misinformation easier to absorb and harder to detect.

questions.question: Even after being told that debaters were assigned their positions by a coin flip, audience members still rated the debater who argued for a policy as personally favoring it more than the assigned opponent. Persisting in explaining assigned behavior by personal views illustrates:

answers.text: A self-serving bias in the debaters
The fundamental attribution error, underestimating the situational constraint of an assigned role
An informational influence on the audience's factual beliefs
A door-in-the-face effect on the audience

questions.explanation: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency to underestimate situational influences and overestimate personal dispositions when explaining others' behavior. Here the role assignment is a powerful situational constraint that observers still discount.

questions.question: A screening test is given to 1,000 people. The condition's prevalence is 10%, so 100 people have it; the test detects 90% of true cases. Of the 900 without the condition, 10% test positive anyway. Of all people who test positive, the proportion who actually have the condition is:

answers.text: 50%: 90 true positives out of 90 + 90 = 180 total positives

questions.explanation: True positives number 90; false positives number 10% of 900, also 90. A positive result is therefore correct 90 out of 180 times — 50% — despite the test's 90% accuracy rates, because the condition is uncommon.

questions.question: A researcher tests whether background music helps or hurts proofreading. Every participant proofreads one passage in silence first and then a second passage with music. Scores with music are higher, but participants may simply have warmed up. Which change would best address this order problem?

answers.text: Counterbalance the order so half the participants get music first and half get silence first
Give every participant three passages instead of two
Tell participants that music is expected to help
Remove the silent condition so only music is tested

questions.explanation: Counterbalancing distributes practice and fatigue effects evenly across conditions, so an order effect cannot systematically favor one condition.

questions.question: A hospital changes its policy so that a radiologist who misses a tumor faces a far larger penalty than one who orders an unnecessary follow-up scan. With her eyesight and training unchanged, the radiologist begins flagging many more scans, catching more real tumors but also ordering many more needless follow-ups. Signal detection theory attributes the change to:

answers.text: Her sensory sensitivity to faint tumors has increased
She has lowered her response criterion, producing more hits and more false alarms
Her absolute threshold for visual stimuli has been permanently lowered
She has eliminated false alarms by improving her sensory receptors

questions.explanation: Sensitivity and decision criterion are separate in signal detection theory. Costly misses shift the criterion toward saying the signal is present, which raises hits and false alarms together without any change in the senses.

questions.question: A clinician reports that clients high in 'aggressiveness' also smash the most plates in a frustration task, but aggressiveness was measured solely by that same plate-smashing task administered a week earlier. Claiming the trait 'predicts' the behavior is weak because:

answers.text: A single method and a single act cannot establish a trait: the claim needs the construct measured independently and behavior aggregated across situations
Traits can never predict behavior
Plate smashing is too violent to study
A week is too short an interval

questions.explanation: This design is mono-method and mono-act: predictor and outcome are essentially the same observation. Trait claims require independent measurement and aggregation across occasions, which average out situational noise.

ap-biology.quiz_title: AP Biology Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A solution has pH 11. Using pH + pOH = 14 and [OH-] = 10^-pOH, what is its hydroxide ion concentration?

answers.text: 3 M

questions.explanation: pOH = 14 - 11 = 3, so [OH-] = 10^-3 M. The trap answer 10^-11 M is [H+], not [OH-]; confusing the two ions reverses the result.

questions.question: How much does the temperature of 100 g of water rise when it absorbs 4,180 J? Use q = mc(delta T) with c = 4.18 J/g per degree C for water.

answers.text: 10 degrees C
1.0 degree C
0.10 degree C
41.8 degrees C

questions.question: A Lineweaver-Burk plot (1/v versus 1/[S]) for an enzyme has a y-intercept of 0.02 min/micromol. Since the y-intercept equals 1/Vmax, the enzyme's Vmax is:

answers.text: 0.02 micromol/min
50 micromol/min
20 micromol/min
500 micromol/min

questions.explanation: Vmax = 1/0.02 = 50 micromol/min.

questions.question: A cellular process requires +13.0 kcal/mol. Each ATP hydrolysis releases 7.3 kcal/mol under the stated conditions. Coupling the process to two ATP hydrolyses gives a net delta G of:

answers.text: +5.7 kcal/mol
-14.6 kcal/mol
-1.6 kcal/mol, so the coupled process is exergonic
+27.6 kcal/mol

questions.explanation: Two ATP provide -14.6 kcal/mol; +13.0 - 14.6 = -1.6 kcal/mol. One ATP (-7.3) would not suffice, which is why the number of ATP matters.

questions.question: On a pigment chromatogram, the solvent front traveled 7.0 cm from the origin and a pigment band traveled 4.2 cm. The Rf value of the pigment is:
questions.explanation: Rf = distance moved by pigment / distance moved by solvent = 4.2/7.0 = 0.60.

questions.question: For a sphere, SA = 4 pi r^2 and V = (4/3) pi r^3, so SA/V = 3/r (formulas given). Compare a spherical cell of radius 1 micrometer with one of radius 3 micrometers. What are their SA/V ratios, and which exchanges materials more effectively per unit volume?

answers.text: Both are 3 per micrometer, so they exchange equally
Radius 1: 1 per micrometer; radius 3: 3 per micrometer; the larger cell exchanges better
Radius 1: 3 per micrometer; radius 3: 1 per micrometer; the smaller cell exchanges better
Radius 1: 9 per micrometer; radius 3: 3 per micrometer; the smaller cell exchanges better

questions.explanation: SA/V = 3/r: for r = 1 it is 3 per micrometer, and for r = 3 it is 1 per micrometer. The smaller sphere has three times as much membrane per unit volume, so exchange per unit volume is more effective.

questions.question: A rod-shaped cell is modeled as a cylinder of radius 1 micrometer and length 8 micrometers, ignoring the end caps. For a cylinder's side, SA = 2 pi r h and V = pi r^2 h (formulas given). What is its approximate SA/V ratio?

answers.text: 8 per micrometer
0.25 per micrometer
4 per micrometer
2 per micrometer

questions.explanation: SA = 2 pi (1)(8) = 16 pi; V = pi (1)^2 (8) = 8 pi; SA/V = 16 pi / 8 pi = 2 per micrometer. The pi factors and units cancel in the ratio.

questions.question: A beaker contains a 0.30 M glucose solution at 25 C (298 K). Glucose does not ionize (i = 1). Using Psi_s = -iCRT with R = 0.0831 L bars/(mol K), the solute potential of the solution is closest to:

answers.text: -7.4 bars
-2.5 bars
-14.9 bars
+7.4 bars

questions.explanation: Psi_s = -(1)(0.30)(0.0831)(298) = -7.43 bars. The -14.9 value wrongly uses i = 2; solute potential is always zero or negative.

questions.question: Cubical cell A has side 2 units (SA 24, V 8, SA:V = 3.0). Cubical cell B has side 6 units (SA 216, V 216, SA:V = 1.0). Per unit of volume, exchange of materials across the membrane can proceed in cell A at up to:

answers.text: The same rate as in B
One-third the rate in B
Three times the rate in B
Nine times the rate in B

questions.explanation: Exchange capacity per volume scales with SA:V: 3.0/1.0 = 3, so the smaller cell supports about three times the exchange per unit volume.

questions.question: Cells are exposed to a hormone at several concentrations, and the percent of cells showing the response is recorded: 1 nM gives 4%, 3 nM gives 14%, 10 nM gives 48%, 30 nM gives 82%, 100 nM gives 96%. The concentration at which the response is approximately half-maximal is closest to:

answers.text: 10 nM
1 nM
30 nM
100 nM

questions.explanation: Half of the ~96-100% maximum is about 50%; the measured response closest to 50% is 48% at 10 nM. The 100 nM value is where the response is nearly maximal, not half-maximal.

questions.question: DNA content is measured for thousands of cells from a growing culture. The results: 60% of cells have 2C DNA content, 15% have intermediate values, and 25% have 4C. The cells with 4C DNA content are cells that:

answers.text: Are in G1 with unreplicated chromosomes
Have replicated their DNA but have not yet divided (G2 or M phase)
Are gametes produced by meiosis
Have permanently left the cell cycle in G0

questions.explanation: DNA content doubles during S phase, so 4C cells have finished replication but not yet divided; they are in G2 or M. G1 and G0 cells are 2C (options A and D), and gametes would be 1C (option C).

questions.question: A cell has a chromosomal lac operon whose repressor gene is completely deleted (no repressor is made from it), plus a plasmid carrying a normal repressor gene but no structural genes. No lactose is present. What is predicted?

answers.text: Both the chromosomal operon and any normal operon stay fully on, because a deleted repressor gene cannot be complemented
The chromosomal operon is on only if its operator is also deleted
The chromosomal operon is repressed, because normal repressor protein made from the plasmid can diffuse and bind its operator
The chromosomal operon is on, because repressor acts only in cis on the DNA that encodes it

questions.explanation: Repressor is a diffusible protein, so it acts in trans: a normal copy anywhere in the cell supplies repressor that can bind the chromosomal operator. This contrasts with an operator mutation, which acts only in cis.

questions.question: A flattened cell is modeled as a box 10 x 10 x 1 micrometers. Its surface area is 2(10x10) + 4(10x1) = 240 square micrometers and its volume is 100 cubic micrometers (values given). A cube with the same volume of 100 cubic micrometers has a surface area of about 129 square micrometers. What does the comparison show?

answers.text: Flattening raises SA/V from about 1.29 to 2.4 per micrometer, improving exchange without changing volume
Flattening lowers SA/V, which is why flat cells exchange poorly
Shape has no effect on SA/V at constant volume
The cube must have the larger surface area because cubes are compact

questions.explanation: SA/V for the flat box = 240/100 = 2.4 per micrometer versus about 129/100 = 1.29 for the cube. Spreading the same volume thin increases surface relative to volume — the strategy of flat cells such as epithelial cells.

questions.question: Two ligands act on the same receptor in the same cell type. Ligand X reaches a half-maximal response at 2 nM and a maximal response of 100 units. Ligand Y reaches a half-maximal response at 2 nM but a maximal response of only 55 units, even at saturating concentrations. Which statement correctly compares the two ligands?

answers.text: Y is more potent than X because its maximum is lower
Y is more efficacious than X because it binds at low concentration
Y cannot bind the receptor at all
X and Y have similar potency, but Y has lower efficacy

questions.explanation: Potency is read from the half-maximal concentration (2 nM for both, so similar), while efficacy is the maximal response (100 vs 55 units), so Y's efficacy is lower. Option A confuses potency with efficacy, and Y clearly binds the receptor since it produces a response.

questions.question: A culture is treated with a drug that prevents DNA replication from initiating. After 24 hours, DNA-content measurement shows almost all cells at 2C, with very few cells at intermediate or 4C values, whereas an untreated culture shows all three populations. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: Treated cells accumulate in G1 because they cannot enter or progress through S phase
Treated cells accumulate in mitosis
The drug forces cells to divide faster
Treated cells have become haploid

questions.explanation: With replication blocked, cells that finish division return to 2C and stay there; no new cells reach 4C, so the 4C population drains away and cells pile up at 2C in G1. They remain diploid (option D); 2C is the normal G1 content.

questions.question: A monohybrid cross is expected to give a 3:1 ratio. Among 376 offspring, 290 show the dominant phenotype and 86 show the recessive phenotype (expected: 282 and 94). The chi-square terms are (64/282) and (64/94). With 1 degree of freedom the critical value at p = 0.05 is 3.84 (given). What is the correct chi-square value and conclusion?

answers.text: chi-square is about 0.91, so the data are consistent with a 3:1 ratio
chi-square is about 9.10, so the 3:1 hypothesis is rejected
chi-square is about 0.91, so the 3:1 hypothesis is rejected
chi-square is about 3.64, so the data are consistent with a 3:1 ratio

questions.explanation: Each term is (O-E)^2/E: 64/282 = 0.227 and 64/94 = 0.681, summing to about 0.91. Because 0.91 is far below the critical value 3.84, the deviation is attributable to chance and the 3:1 hypothesis is not rejected. A small chi-square never justifies rejection.

questions.question: A template DNA segment within a gene reads 3'-CTT-5' at one position, so the mRNA codon there is 5'-GAA-3' (glutamate). A mutation changes the first base of this template segment - the base at its 3' end - from C to A, making the template 3'-ATT-5'. Codon excerpt: GAA = Glu, UAA = Stop, AUU = Ile. What is the consequence?

answers.text: The codon becomes UAA, a stop codon, so the protein is truncated at this position (a nonsense mutation)
The mutation is silent, because the amino acid is unchanged
The codon becomes AUU, changing glutamate to isoleucine
A frameshift scrambles all downstream amino acids

questions.explanation: Working from the template: 3'-ATT-5' is complementary to mRNA 5'-UAA-3', which is a stop codon. A single base substitution in the template has converted a glutamate codon into a termination signal - a nonsense mutation. (Note the result must be derived from the template strand, not read off it directly.)

questions.question: In a cultured cell line, binding of ligand L to its surface receptor triggers response R through three relay proteins, J, K, and M. Researchers obtain these results: (1) cells lacking J do not respond to L, but directly activating K restores the full response; (2) cells lacking K do not respond to L, and directly activating J does not restore the response; (3) a permanently active form of M produces response R even in cells lacking both J and K. Which order of action is consistent with all three results?

answers.text: Receptor, then K, then J, then M, then response
Receptor, then J, then K, then M, then response
Receptor, then J, then M, then K, then response
Receptor, then M, then K, then J, then response

questions.explanation: Activating a downstream component bypasses loss of an upstream one: K activation rescues loss of J, so K is downstream of J, and J activation cannot rescue loss of K, confirming J is upstream. Permanently active M works without J or K, placing M last. Option A reverses J and K, which contradicts result (2).

questions.question: In a signaling pathway, one activated receptor activates 5 effector enzymes. Each effector enzyme produces 40 molecules of a second messenger, each second-messenger molecule activates one kinase, and each activated kinase phosphorylates 15 target proteins. Ignoring losses, how many target proteins are phosphorylated as a result of one activated receptor?
questions.explanation: 5 x 40 = 200 second messengers, activating 200 kinases, and 200 x 15 = 3,000 target proteins. Option A stops after the second-messenger step; option D (40 x 15) forgets the 5 effector enzymes; option B adds the factors instead of multiplying them.

questions.question: A treated cell population shows a large increase in cells with 4C DNA content. A second stain specific to a protein found only in mitotic cells shows that very few of those 4C cells are actually in mitosis. What is the most likely state of the accumulated 4C cells, and what does it suggest?

answers.text: They are in mitosis, and the marker stain must be faulty
They are in cytokinesis, which the DNA measurement cannot detect
They are arrested in G2, suggesting the treatment triggers the G2 checkpoint or blocks mitotic entry
They are in S phase, still copying their DNA

questions.explanation: DNA content alone cannot distinguish G2 from M (both are 4C). The mitosis-specific marker shows the cells are not in M, and a full 4C content rules out S phase (option D), so the cells are held in G2.

ap-human-geography.quiz_title: AP Human Geography Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A road map states that 1 inch equals 2 miles. Expressed as a representative fraction, the scale is closest to (1 mile = 63,360 inches)
questions.explanation: Two miles contain 2 times 63,360, or 126,720, inches, so 1 inch on the map represents 126,720 inches on the ground.

questions.question: A team must model soil moisture, a quantity that varies continuously across every part of a field with no natural boundaries. The most natural data model is

answers.text: vector polygons with one moisture value per farm
a flow line from wet to dry areas
vector points at each farmhouse
raster cells, each storing a moisture value for its location

questions.explanation: Continuous fields are represented as rasters, where each cell carries the value measured or estimated for that location.

questions.question: A raster layer uses square cells 30 metres on a side. How much ground does one cell cover, and what happens to file size if the team switches to 10-metre cells over the same area?

answers.text: 900 square metres per cell; the file grows about ninefold
30 square metres per cell; the file grows about threefold
900 square metres per cell; the file shrinks about ninefold
60 square metres per cell; the file is unchanged

questions.explanation: A 30-metre cell covers 30 times 30, or 900, square metres; dividing cell side by three multiplies the number of cells by nine.

questions.question: A country of 5,000,000 people records 120,000 births and 80,000 deaths in a year, with migration ignored. Its rate of natural increase is:

answers.text: 4.0 percent
0.8 percent
0.04 percent
2.4 percent

questions.question: Country X grows at 1.0 percent per year and Country Y at 3.5 percent per year. Using the rule of 70, Y's doubling time is shorter than X's by approximately:

answers.text: 2.5 years
25 years
50 years
90 years

questions.explanation: X doubles in 70 / 1.0 = 70 years and Y in 70 / 3.5 = 20 years, a difference of about 50 years.

questions.question: A country has an arithmetic density of 400 people per square kilometre and a physiological density of 2,000 people per square kilometre of arable land. Arable land therefore makes up approximately what share of its total area?

answers.text: 5 percent
50 percent
20 percent
80 percent

questions.explanation: The ratio of arithmetic to physiological density equals the arable share of total land: 400 / 2,000 = 0.20, so about 20 percent of the country is arable.

questions.question: Two pairs of cities have identical population products. The cities in Pair 2 are twice as far apart as the cities in Pair 1. Under an inverse-square gravity model, the predicted interaction for Pair 2 is:

answers.text: One-quarter of Pair 1's interaction
One-half of Pair 1's interaction
Equal to Pair 1's interaction
Twice Pair 1's interaction

questions.explanation: With population held constant, interaction varies with the inverse square of distance, so doubling the distance reduces the predicted flow to one-quarter.

questions.question: A household moves from an apartment in a city's historic core to a house in a suburb of the same metropolitan area, keeping the same jobs and schools. In migration terminology this is:

answers.text: Interregional migration
International migration
Step migration
Intraregional migration, a move within the same region or metropolitan area

questions.explanation: Moves within a single region, such as within a metropolitan area, are intraregional and typically involve housing and life-cycle motives rather than labour-market relocation.

questions.question: A textbook claims unitary government works best in states that are small and culturally homogeneous. Which case would most weaken a claim that homogeneity is necessary for a unitary system to function?

answers.text: A small homogeneous country governed unitarily for decades
A large, multilingual country governed unitarily for decades without breaking apart
A federation whose provinces follow language boundaries
A confederation of small homogeneous states

questions.explanation: A long-functioning unitary system in a large, multilingual country is direct counterevidence to the claim that cultural homogeneity is necessary for unitary government.

questions.question: A market gardener's crop earns $1,800 per hectare before transport and loses $90 per hectare for each kilometre hauled to market. The maximum rent the gardener can bid for land 12 km from the market, while just breaking even, is

answers.text: $540 per hectare
$900 per hectare
$720 per hectare
$1,080 per hectare

questions.explanation: Transport over 12 km consumes 12 x $90 = $1,080, leaving $1,800 - $1,080 = $720 per hectare as the break-even bid rent.

questions.question: A researcher overlays a 1990 floodplain layer with a 2024 housing layer and reports that 3,000 current homes sit in the floodplain, recommending the figure for this year's insurance maps. The most serious methodological flaw is

answers.text: GIS cannot overlay layers from different decades
Housing built after 1990 should have been excluded
The floodplain itself was mapped from 1990 channels and land cover, so pairing a 34-year-old hazard layer with current housing misstates which homes face the present-day flood risk
Insurance maps require paper cartography rather than GIS

questions.explanation: Rivers migrate, levees are built, and land cover changes over three decades, so the hazard layer no longer describes current conditions even though the housing layer does.

questions.question: A city legalises duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes on every residential lot, where previously only detached single-family houses were allowed. The most likely change to the urban landscape is

answers.text: A ring of high-rise towers at the city edge
Scattered small multi-unit buildings appearing within existing neighbourhoods, adding homes through gentle, distributed density
Immediate conversion of downtown offices to housing
A decline in total housing units as lots are combined

questions.explanation: The missing middle is the range of small multi-unit housing between detached houses and apartment blocks; legalising it produces dispersed small buildings, not towers.

questions.question: A weighted-overlay site model gives slope a weight of 50 percent, road access 30 percent, and land price 20 percent, and ranks a steep but cheap site first after the weights are accidentally entered in reverse. The episode best illustrates that suitability results

answers.text: are objective once data are digital
are invalid whenever three or more layers are used
cannot be produced from raster data
depend on the analyst's weighting choices, which must be justified and checked

questions.explanation: Weighted overlays encode judgement in their weights; different or erroneous weights produce different rankings from identical data.

questions.question: Two brothers face identical conditions: the same drought at home and the same job offer abroad. One migrates; the other stays because he is the sole carer for their disabled father. Lee's model explains the different outcomes through:

answers.text: Different gravity-model populations
Different intervening obstacles in the two countries
A counterstream affecting only one brother
Personal factors that filter the same pushes and pulls differently for each individual

questions.explanation: Lee included personal circumstances and obligations among his model's elements precisely because identical external conditions produce different decisions for different people.

questions.question: A large, culturally diverse country adopts a federal constitution whose provincial boundaries deliberately follow the homelands of its major language groups, giving each group control of schooling in its own province. The design most directly uses federalism to

answers.text: eliminate the language groups through assimilation
move the capital to the geographic center
draw maritime boundaries among the provinces
accommodate territorially concentrated diversity by matching self-government to cultural regions

questions.explanation: Federal systems can accommodate diversity by giving territorially concentrated cultural groups self-government within their own constituent units.

questions.question: A cocoa-growing country exports nearly all its beans unprocessed; chocolate making, branding and most profit happen abroad. Using core-periphery reasoning applied to this commodity chain, the single move that most increases the country's capture of value is

answers.text: Growing still more beans for export
Building domestic grinding and chocolate manufacture so higher-value stages of the chain occur inside the country
Lowering the farm-gate price of beans
Exporting beans to more countries at the same stage

questions.explanation: In the chain as described, value is added where processing and branding occur, which is the core side of the exchange. Moving those stages onshore is what changes the country's share, not expanding raw output.

questions.question: An Indigenous community preparing for land negotiations draws its own maps showing seasonal hunting, fishing and gathering sites that government topographic and cadastral maps have never recorded. The maps' main geographic value in the negotiations is that they

answers.text: Replace the need for any surveyed boundary evidence
Prove the community's legal title under international law by themselves
Make locally held spatial knowledge of resource use visible in a form officials must engage with, documenting occupation and use that official data omit
Show that the territory is a formal region

questions.explanation: Official surveys record parcels and terrain, not lived resource use; counter-mapping converts community knowledge into spatial evidence of that use.

questions.question: A minority language is taught two hours a week in schools, yet children's home use keeps falling and grandparents report speaking the national language to grandchildren 'to help them succeed.' Which additional program most directly targets the mechanism actually driving the decline?

answers.text: Parent-and-toddler heritage-language playgroups and coaching that help families use the language at home from infancy
A new dictionary of the language for university libraries
Renaming streets in the heritage language
A televised awards ceremony honoring elderly speakers

questions.explanation: Decline is driven by interrupted transmission in the home, so effective intervention must restore child-directed heritage-language use in families.

questions.question: Members of the Velari linguistic community live in the mountain valleys where three neighboring countries meet. Each country's census counts Velari speakers, their kinship and market networks cross all three borders, and no country is governed by Velari institutions. As a political-geographic classification, the Velari are best described as

answers.text: a nation-state divided by a relic boundary
a perforated nation enclosed by three states
a city-state with exclaves in each country
a multi-state nation, because one nation is divided among more than one state

questions.explanation: A multi-state nation is a single nation whose homeland and population are split among two or more sovereign states.

questions.question: A territory elects its own assembly, runs its own schools and police, and collects local taxes, but a neighboring country's parliament must approve its laws, conducts its foreign relations, and can dissolve its assembly at will. Other countries do not treat it as an independent country. The territory is not a sovereign state primarily because it lacks

answers.text: a permanent population, since its residents also hold foreign passports
a defined territory, since its borders are internationally surveyed
sovereignty, since final authority over its affairs rests outside the territory
a government, since its assembly passes local laws

questions.explanation: Sovereignty means supreme, independent authority over a territory; a government whose decisions can be overridden by an outside power is not sovereign.

comptia-a-plus.quiz_title: CompTIA A+ Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A high-end graphics card has an eight-pin socket on its top edge. What must the technician connect there?

answers.text: A SATA data cable so the card can read game files faster
A PCIe power lead from the power supply, because slot power alone is not enough for the card
A front-panel audio lead so the card can output sound
Nothing, because those sockets are decorative on most cards

questions.explanation: Powerful graphics cards draw more than the slot provides, so they need a direct PCIe power lead from the supply. Leaving the connector empty typically prevents the card from starting at all.

questions.question: A laptop's DHCP lease is halfway through its lease period. What does the laptop normally do at this point?

answers.text: It broadcasts a Discover to find a completely new server
It assigns itself an APIPA address until the lease expires
It releases the address and requests a different one
It asks the leasing server to renew the same address

questions.explanation: At about half the lease time, a client asks its DHCP server to renew the lease on the same address, keeping connectivity uninterrupted. Broadcasting a new Discover is what happens when renewal fails or no address is held.

questions.question: At the objectives level, what is the best short description of a container?

answers.text: A full virtual computer with its own hardware emulation
A backup copy of a physical server stored offsite
A lightweight package that runs an application and its dependencies in isolation while sharing the host kernel
A remote desktop session delivered to a thin client

questions.explanation: A container packages an application with its dependencies and runs it in isolation while sharing the host operating system kernel. A remote desktop session delivers a user interface and is not a packaging format for applications.

questions.question: Which command would a Linux administrator use to change the owner of a file named report.txt to a different user?

answers.text: chmod report.txt
grep report.txt
chown report.txt
passwd report.txt

questions.explanation: chown changes file ownership, while chmod changes permissions without changing who owns the file. grep only searches text content and does not alter ownership or permissions.

questions.question: Which phone setting prevents a device from silently joining unknown open networks while the owner travels?

answers.text: Turn off automatic joining of unknown networks and approve new networks manually
Set the phone to prefer the strongest open signal available
Save every open network the phone has ever encountered
Disable the phone screen lock while traveling

questions.explanation: Auto-joining unknown networks can connect the phone to an attacker hotspot without the owner noticing. Manual approval keeps the owner in control of which networks are trusted.

questions.question: After fitting a maintenance kit, the printer still displays its maintenance-due message. What step completes the service?

answers.text: Replace the kit again with a second new kit
Disconnect the printer from the network for a day
Reset the maintenance counter as directed in the service procedure
Print one hundred pages to clear the message automatically

questions.explanation: The maintenance message is driven by a counter that must be reset manually after the kit is installed, otherwise the printer assumes the old parts remain. Replacing good parts again wastes a kit.

questions.question: An office cable run exceeds the maximum length for its Ethernet standard and the link drops intermittently at the far end. What is the appropriate remedy?

answers.text: Assign two IP addresses to the far PC
Change the DNS server to a public one
Install a switch or repeater mid-run so each segment stays within the length limit
Rename the far PC with a shorter hostname

questions.explanation: Over-length copper runs suffer signal degradation, so breaking the run with a switch keeps each segment in spec. Addressing and naming changes cannot restore a degraded signal.

questions.question: An inkjet printer produces pages with white horizontal streaks through text, and a nozzle check shows missing segments. What is the best first remedy?

answers.text: Replace the paper tray springs
Run the printer's printhead cleaning cycle and re-test with a nozzle check
Change the printer's default gateway
Install a larger hard drive in the PC

questions.explanation: Missing segments on a nozzle check indicate clogged nozzles, addressed first by the built-in cleaning cycle. Gateway and storage changes do not clear ink passages.

questions.question: A technician needs to see which users are currently signed in to a shared computer and sign one of them out. Which Task Manager tab provides that?

answers.text: Processes
Users
App history
Details

questions.explanation: The Users tab in Task Manager lists signed-in users, their resource use, and options to disconnect or sign out a session. App history shows resource totals for apps over time, not live user sessions.

questions.question: A manager wants Microsoft Defender Antivirus scans to run every Sunday evening on office PCs. Where is a recurring scan schedule like that typically set?

answers.text: In Windows Security virus and threat protection settings or via Task Scheduler for the scan task
In the printer sharing dialog
In the mapped drive wizard
In Disk Cleanup settings

questions.explanation: Defender scan scheduling is managed through Windows Security settings or its scheduled task in Task Scheduler. Printer sharing and mapped drives deal with network resources, not antivirus timing.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a one-time passcode delivered by an authenticator app as an authentication factor?

answers.text: It is something the user has, tied to the registered device or app
It is something the user is, like a facial feature
It is a permanent password that never changes
It counts as two factors by itself because it has six digits

questions.explanation: A time-based code from an authenticator app proves possession of the registered device, so it is a 'something you have' factor. A biometric trait would be something the user is, and a single code is still just one factor.

questions.question: Maya installs a new graphics driver and the PC then blue-screens shortly after sign-in on every boot. What is the most direct corrective action?

answers.text: Reinstall Windows from installation media immediately
Boot into Safe Mode and roll back the graphics driver in Device Manager
Disable Windows Firewall and restart the PC
Format a secondary data drive to free space

questions.explanation: Safe Mode loads minimal drivers, allowing the faulty new driver to be rolled back without triggering the crash. Reinstalling Windows is disproportionate before a driver rollback has been tried.

questions.question: Since a memory upgrade last week, a workstation intermittently shows stop errors under heavy load, while light tasks run fine. Which troubleshooting approach best isolates the cause?

answers.text: Replace the power supply before testing anything else
Test with a memory diagnostic and try one module at a time in the primary slot to find a faulty module or slot
Reinstall the display driver repeatedly until the errors stop
Assume the processor has failed and order a replacement

questions.explanation: Load-dependent stop errors after a memory change point first at the new modules or their seating, and diagnostics plus one-at-a-time testing isolate the culprit methodically. Replacing unrelated parts such as the power supply skips the evidence the recent change provides.

questions.question: A server's RAID 6 array reports one drive failed and a second drive showing predictive failure warnings, though the array is still online and serving data. Why is this situation treated as urgent?

answers.text: RAID 6 arrays stop serving data the moment any warning appears
The array can tolerate two drive losses, but if both drives fail before a rebuild finishes the data is lost
Predictive warnings on a second drive always mean the first failure was misreported
The array's parity can only be rebuilt on weekends by design

questions.explanation: RAID 6 survives two concurrent drive failures, but with one drive already out and a second deteriorating, losing the second during the stress of a rebuild would exceed the array's tolerance and lose data. The array is still serving data, so the urgency is preventing a second failure, not an outage that already happened.

questions.question: A junior technician is told to use xcopy rather than copy for a migration because the job includes subfolders and hidden structure. What is the key advantage being relied on?

answers.text: Xcopy compresses the files as it copies
Xcopy repairs file system errors while copying
Xcopy joins the computer to a domain
Xcopy can copy folders and their subfolders, not just individual files

questions.explanation: Xcopy extends copy by handling directories and subdirectories, which a folder migration needs. Plain copy is oriented to files, and neither command repairs a file system.

questions.question: A data center's temperature sensors alarm on a hot aisle reading that keeps climbing. What is the most appropriate immediate concern?

answers.text: The paint color of the racks
Overheating can throttle or damage servers, so cooling and airflow need prompt attention
The alarm sound annoys nearby staff only
Higher heat improves processor speed

questions.explanation: Rising temperatures can cause throttling, shutdowns, and permanent hardware damage, so cooling faults need urgent response. Heat never improves processor speed; sustained overheating degrades reliability and lifespan.

questions.question: A technician plans to degauss a batch of drives for disposal. Which drives will degaussing NOT reliably sanitize?

answers.text: Traditional magnetic hard disk drives
Magnetic backup tapes
Older magnetic storage media
Solid-state drives that store data in flash chips

questions.explanation: Degaussing disrupts magnetic storage, but SSDs hold data electronically in flash, so a magnet has no sanitizing effect. SSDs need an approved erase method or physical destruction.

questions.question: A technician notices a desktop's processor fan cable is pinched flat under a drive cage edge and its insulation is worn through where it crosses the metal. The machine intermittently reports fan failures. What is the best action?

answers.text: Ignore it because fan cables carry no meaningful current
Raise the fan failure warning threshold in setup to hide the alerts
Replace or reroute the damaged fan lead so it cannot short against the chassis
Move the memory modules farther from the fan cable

questions.explanation: Worn insulation against a metal edge can short the fan's power or sense line, explaining intermittent failure reports, so replacing or rerouting the lead fixes the hazard. Raising the warning threshold would hide alerts while leaving a short that could damage the board.

questions.question: Before crimping a connector, a technician removes a short section of the cable's outer jacket while taking care not to nick the inner conductors. Which tool is designed for this preparation step?

answers.text: A cable stripper
A toner generator
A cable tester
A PoE injector

questions.explanation: A cable stripper is sized to cut through the outer jacket cleanly without damaging the conductors inside. A cable tester verifies a finished run and does not remove jacket material.

questions.question: A school secretary gets a call from someone claiming to be a parent who urgently needs another student's home address, offering a convincing story about a playdate emergency. What is the correct handling?

answers.text: Provide the address because the story sounds caring
Decline to release another student's private information and direct the caller to official school procedures
Provide only the street name as a partial answer
Ask the caller to phone back later and give it then

questions.explanation: A convincing story is a pretext, and private information about a third party must not be released on the strength of a story alone. Partial disclosure still leaks protected information and rewards the manipulation.

itil-4-foundation.quiz_title: ITIL 4 Foundation Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Coral Bay Resorts scenario: which role authorizes budget for service consumption?

answers.text: User
Sponsor
Service provider
Customer

questions.explanation: At Coral Bay Resorts, the sponsor role is held by whoever authorizes the budget that pays for consuming a service.

questions.question: During service review, which statement gives the purpose of it asset management?

answers.text: Ensure suppliers and their performance are managed to support seamless quality services
Protect the information needed to conduct business
Plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets
Establish and nurture links with stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels

questions.explanation: The question here, during service review, is 'which statement gives the purpose of it asset management'. IT asset management exists to plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets. Neither alternative fits: one belongs to supplier management and the other to information security management.

questions.question: Which outcome best shows problem management succeeding over several months?

answers.text: More incidents logged per week
Fewer repeat incidents because underlying causes were removed
More emergency changes raised
Faster password resets for users

questions.explanation: Problem management reduces the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying and addressing their causes.

questions.question: Which offering element consists of activities the provider performs for the consumer?

answers.text: Goods
Service consumption
Service actions
Access to resources

questions.explanation: Work the provider carries out for the consumer - maintenance visits and the like - counts as service actions. The provider performs them; the consumer benefits from them.

questions.question: While triaging requests, what makes the principles universal?

answers.text: They fit one project type
They cover one technology only
They suit one industry only
They apply in all circumstances

questions.explanation: The question here, while triaging requests, is 'what makes the principles universal'. The point here is that universality comes from applying in all circumstances, regardless of goals, strategy, work type or structure. 'They cover one technology only' does not match what the stem describes.

questions.question: During capacity planning, a team works across departments to get better buy-in. Which principle is this?

answers.text: Optimize and automate
Think and work holistically
Collaborate and promote visibility
Keep it simple and practical

questions.explanation: In short, collaborate and promote visibility means collaboration across boundaries for better buy-in and information, involving the right people in the right roles and making work and data visible. The behaviour described here — a team works across departments to get better buy-in — is the giveaway. The alternatives, Think and work holistically and Keep it simple and practical, name other principles whose behaviours differ from the one shown.

questions.question: Before proposing changes, improve at a school district reviews what coming from deliver and support and stakeholders?

answers.text: Performance information and feedback
Delivered services
Agreed specifications
New service components

questions.explanation: Performance information and feedback are inputs to improve, arriving from other value chain activities. Other value chain activities supply them.

questions.question: A routine, low-risk memory upgrade follows a fully documented, previously assessed procedure. What type of change is it?

answers.text: An emergency change
A normal change
A standard change
A major incident

questions.explanation: Standard changes are low-risk, pre-authorized, well understood and fully documented, like a routine memory upgrade.

questions.question: A provider rebrands its desk as a practice rather than just a function. What changes in how it is understood?

answers.text: It is a practice within the service value system, working with many other practices
It stops capturing requests
It becomes solely a phone team
It replaces all other practices

questions.explanation: In ITIL 4 the service desk is a practice within the SVS, working with practices such as incident, service request and problem management.

questions.question: Breaches are reported, but nobody manages follow-up actions, so breaches repeat. Which purpose element is weakest?

answers.text: Defining the SLA document
Writing targets in plain language
Managing delivery against the targets, not only measuring it
Setting the targets initially

questions.explanation: Service level management ensures delivery is assessed, monitored and managed against targets; reporting alone does not manage performance.

questions.question: Fill in the role: the _____ defines requirements for a service and takes responsibility for outcomes of its consumption.

answers.text: Service provider
Customer
Sponsor
User

questions.explanation: A customer defines the requirements for a service and takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption. The customer role is the one that sets what a service must achieve and owns the results of using it.

questions.question: While mapping stakeholders, documentation and processes are moved to live use. Which practice is this?

answers.text: Continual improvement
Release management
Service configuration management
Deployment management

questions.explanation: Broadly, deployment management moves new or changed hardware, software, documentation, processes or other components to live environments, or to testing and training environments. Look at the behaviour in the stem: documentation and processes are moved to live use. That separates Deployment management from Release management and Service configuration management, the other practices offered.

questions.question: Riverdale Schools upgrades its workflow tool, knowledge base and messaging systems used to manage services. Which dimension is this?

answers.text: Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
Organizations and people
Value streams and processes

questions.explanation: At Riverdale Schools, workflow tools, knowledge bases, communication systems and the information they carry all sit in the information and technology dimension.

questions.question: Business needs keep shifting and services must keep up. Which statement best captures the purpose of continual improvement?

answers.text: To authorize all changes centrally
To maximize the number of successful changes
To restore normal service as quickly as possible
To align practices and services with changing business needs through ongoing improvement

questions.explanation: Continual improvement aligns practices and services with changing business needs through ongoing improvement of products, services and practices.

questions.question: A printer is broken and printing has stopped for a whole department. A colleague says to raise it as a service request. What is wrong?

answers.text: Incidents must go through the catalogue
Requests cannot be raised by departments
A failure is an incident, not a service request
Printers are never supported

questions.explanation: Requests are not a report of failure, unlike incidents. A broken printer stopping work is an incident.

questions.question: Following a cost review, a team notes a process works but could still be improved after assessment. Which principle is this?

answers.text: Focus on value
Collaborate and promote visibility
Progress iteratively with feedback
Start where you are

questions.explanation: What the stem shows is this: a team notes a process works but could still be improved after assessment. Not starting from scratch without considering what is already available to leverage, assessing the current state objectively through measurement and direct observation — that is what start where you are means. The alternatives, Focus on value and Progress iteratively with feedback, name other principles whose behaviours differ from the one shown.

questions.question: Before a procurement decision, workarounds and known errors are managed to reduce incident impact. Which practice is this?

answers.text: Relationship management
Supplier management
Problem management
Information security management

questions.explanation: What the stem shows is this: workarounds and known errors are managed to reduce incident impact. In short, problem management reduces the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying actual and potential causes, and managing workarounds and known errors. That separates Problem management from Information security management and Relationship management, the other practices offered.

questions.question: QuickShip Couriers wants a single model showing how its components and activities combine to create value, and how it interfaces with other organizations. Which model is this?

answers.text: Governance
Service value chain
Service value system
Continual improvement

questions.explanation: How an organization's components and activities combine as one system to enable value creation is described by the service value system. No single component is the SVS; it is the system as a whole.

questions.question: Priority drives which operational decisions?

answers.text: Baseline and target setting
Change authorization and scheduling
Target timescales, response speed and escalation
Register prioritization by value

questions.explanation: Priority determines timescales and drives faster response and escalation for higher priorities.

questions.question: During a benefits review, services are aligned to changing business needs through ongoing improvement. The purpose of continual improvement is best described by which option?

answers.text: Establish and nurture links with stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
Ensure suppliers and their performance are managed to support seamless quality services
Align practices and services with changing business needs through ongoing improvement
Plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets

questions.explanation: For continual improvement, the stated purpose is to align practices and services with changing business needs through ongoing improvement. The behaviour described here — services are aligned to changing business needs through ongoing improvement — is the giveaway. 'Ensure suppliers and their performance…' is the purpose of supplier management, not of continual improvement.

slla.quiz_title: SLLA Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of the following is the soundest guidance on handling values conflicts openly?

answers.text: The leader should quietly adopt the position of the most influential group.
Values conflicts should be avoided in meetings because they damage morale.
Pretending consensus exists is the fastest route to unity.
When stakeholders disagree about values, a leader surfaces the disagreement, clarifies what is negotiable, and decides transparently rather than letting conflict go underground.

questions.explanation: Unspoken value conflicts resurface as resistance and rumor; honest treatment builds the trust that implementation needs.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with effective practice in observing for student evidence?

answers.text: Observation evidence should focus on the teacher's presentation polish.
Strong observers record what students say, do, and produce as the primary evidence of learning, rather than rating teacher performance alone.
Seating charts and board work are sufficient evidence of learning.
Student confusion during a lesson is irrelevant if the teacher covered the plan.

questions.explanation: Teaching is the cause under review, but learning is the effect that counts; student evidence keeps observation honest.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with effective practice in preventing bullying systematically?

answers.text: Bullying prevention works as a system — clear definitions, taught expectations, supervised hot spots, consistent adult response, and support for targets and offenders alike.
Bullying is best handled case by case with no schoolwide system.
Assemblies alone are a sufficient bullying prevention strategy.
Targets should be coached to ignore bullying until it stops.

questions.explanation: Isolated responses leave the ecology that produces bullying untouched; systems change supervision, norms, and response together.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with effective practice in transparent hiring and assignment?

answers.text: Criteria may be written after interviews to fit the preferred candidate.
A leader may reserve key assignments for trusted allies without process.
Transparency in hiring is unnecessary when the leader's judgment is strong.
Hiring and coveted assignments follow posted criteria and consistent process, so outcomes can be defended as merit-based to anyone who asks.

questions.explanation: Processes that cannot be explained cannot be trusted; criteria-first selection protects the chosen candidate as much as the passed-over.

questions.question: Which of the following is the soundest guidance on designing the master schedule?

answers.text: Teacher preferences for planning periods are the schedule's first design constraint.
The master schedule should roll forward unchanged each year for stability.
Singleton courses for small groups of students should be cut before the schedule is built.
The master schedule is built from student course needs and program priorities first, then adjusted for staffing and space — not assembled around adult preferences.

questions.explanation: A schedule is the school's values in timetable form; building it student-first is an instructional decision disguised as logistics.

questions.question: Regarding setting measurable improvement goals, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: Vague goals such as 'do better in math' motivate more because they never declare anyone a failure.
Measurable goals should avoid dates so staff do not feel pressured.
Effective improvement goals state the outcome, the measure, the baseline, and the target date so progress can be checked honestly.
A goal without a baseline is acceptable because the target number alone shows ambition.

questions.explanation: A goal that cannot be measured cannot be managed; baselines and dates turn aspirations into commitments that can be reviewed.

questions.question: During a leadership review of protecting instructional time, which of the following should a school leader affirm?

answers.text: Instructional time is fixed by the bell schedule and cannot be influenced by leaders.
Frequent pull-outs and assemblies cost little because students catch up quickly.
Leaders protect learning time by auditing interruptions, streamlining transitions and announcements, and defending the master schedule's instructional blocks.
Protecting time means forbidding all enrichment activities during the school day.

questions.explanation: Minutes lost to friction compound into weeks across a year; time protection is one of the cheapest achievement strategies available.

questions.question: Regarding teaching students to use feedback, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: Students improve fastest when feedback tells them where they are against the goal, and they get class time to revise work in response.
Students should not see success criteria, because that makes tasks too easy.
Revision time is a reward for students who finished early.
Feedback is complete when the teacher returns papers with comments, whether or not students act on them.

questions.explanation: Feedback that students cannot act on is decoration; structured revision converts comments into learning.

questions.question: Regarding recruiting and retaining a diverse staff, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: Retention of diverse staff requires no attention once hiring improves.
