questions.question: Which activity adds value in a loan processing operation?

answers.text: Moving files between two in-trays adds value because motion keeps staff occupied on every run.
Photocopying every document twice adds value through extra handling of the file.
Verifying an applicant's income adds value by enabling a sound lending decision.
Waiting three days for a signature adds value by ageing the application properly.

questions.explanation: Value-adding steps change the input toward what the customer wants. Income verification advances the decision; transport and waiting do not.

questions.question: After a packaging process was shown capable and stable, what monitoring approach keeps capability from quietly slipping?

answers.text: Repeating a full capability study each morning before the first production run begins each day.
Plotting results on an appropriate control chart over time and reacting only to genuine signals.
Inspecting every finished pack forever, since sampling can never confirm that quality is holding.
Freezing all process settings permanently so no operator adjustment of any kind is ever allowed.

questions.explanation: Capability is a snapshot. Ongoing charting separates routine noise from real shifts, protecting the gains already demonstrated.

questions.question: A small sample of 10 cycle times is badly skewed, and the deadline forbids collecting more data. What is the defensible posture?

answers.text: Run the t-test and report certainty, because deadlines suspend the assumptions statistics requires.
Report the mean alone as proof, because summaries presented confidently become findings over time.
Duplicate the fastest five times to balance the skew, because symmetry matters more than honesty.
Acknowledge the limitation and favour a rank approach or cautious language about any conclusion.

questions.explanation: Ten badly skewed observations give a t-test little protection, since one extreme time can dominate. A rank-based approach or plainly cautious wording is the defensible course under the deadline.

questions.question: How are the zones on a variables chart constructed between the centre line and each three-sigma limit?

answers.text: Each side is split by the specification limits, so zone widths follow customer tolerance rather than sigma.
Each side is split into halves at the two-sigma line only, giving two bands named after their distance.
Each side is split into three one-sigma bands: zone C nearest the centre, then B, then A by the limit.
Each side keeps one single band, because zones are simply another name for the whole control region.

questions.explanation: Zones are one-sigma slices: C spans zero to one sigma, B spans one to two, and A spans two to three, on each side of the centre line.

questions.question: A manufacturer fits energy use = 200 + 12 x where x is production in hundreds of units. What is the fitted energy use at 500 units of production?

answers.text: 212 units of energy — the output for just one hundred units of production: 200 + 12 with x set to 1.
6200 units of energy — obtained by feeding the raw count 500 into the slope term: 200 + 12 x 500.
60 units of energy, from 12 x 5 = 60 with the base consumption of the plant left aside.
260 units of energy, from 200 + 12 x 5 = 200 + 60 = 260, since 500 units is 5 hundreds.

questions.explanation: Mind the units: x counts hundreds, so 500 units gives x = 5. Then 12 x 5 = 60 and 200 + 60 = 260.

questions.question: For a hospital pharmacy project tackling late discharge medications, a sponsor asks where a sentence about wanting discharge orders filled within 45 minutes belongs. Where should that sentence sit?

answers.text: It belongs in the goal statement because it expresses a desired future condition with a measurable threshold.
It belongs in the problem statement because any mention of timing automatically describes present-day suffering.
It belongs in the scope paragraph because time limits define which activities the team may touch.
It belongs in the business impact note because faster discharge directly frees beds for incoming admissions.

questions.explanation: Desired future performance with a numeric target is goal language. Problem language reports what hurts now, scope draws boundaries, and impact language quantifies organisational consequence.

questions.question: The gage R&R report for cap torque at Canyon Westbrook Products shows percent study variation of 9% for the plastic bottles measurements. How should Stefan Umar read that figure?

answers.text: Reading 9% as marginal treats percent study variation as a comparison against the specification width for cap torque.
Reading 9% as unacceptable grades an R&R percentage against customer returns, not against the study variation in plastic bottles.
At 9%, the measurement system is comfortably acceptable: the figure sits just under the 10% guidepost, meaning gage variation is a minor part of everything the study observed.
The 9% figure cannot be judged at all, because percent study variation guideposts apply only to attribute gages, never to variable data like cap torque at the Harborview Street plant.

questions.explanation: Stefan sees cap torque consume merely 9 percent for plastic bottles, squeaking beneath ten, so Canyon Westbrook's gage contributes only a minor slice of observed variation.

questions.question: A team has continuous cycle-time data for two independent shifts and wants to compare typical performance. Which test family fits first?

answers.text: A chi-square test on categories fits first, because shift names provide two neat group labels.
A two-sample comparison of means fits first, because the outcome is continuous across two groups.
A paired comparison fits first, because both shifts work inside the same building each day.
A variance-only test fits first, because averages are irrelevant whenever shifts are compared.

questions.explanation: Continuous outcome plus two independent groups points to a two-sample t-test family. Pairing would need the same units measured twice.

questions.question: A single case in a twelve-predictor shipping model has an enormous residual and sits at an extreme combination of predictor values. Why does that case deserve special scrutiny?

answers.text: Extreme observed cases must always be deleted before reporting, because regression standards cap permissible residual size relative to predictor extremes.
It combines a poor fit with potential leverage over the fitted surface, so the reported slopes might hinge on that one unusual shipment record.
The case proves the twelve predictors are collinear, because leverage can only arise when predictors duplicate each other's information heavily.
Scrutiny is unnecessary, because with twelve predictors the influence of any single case is mathematically guaranteed to be negligible.

questions.explanation: In higher dimensions a case can be both badly fitted and highly influential. Checking whether conclusions survive its removal is basic diligence, not data tampering.

questions.question: An operator doing autonomous maintenance finds a frayed belt during the daily clean and inspection round, before it fails. Which TPM idea does this illustrate?

answers.text: Operators should now take over belt replacement design, because finding a fault qualifies them as engineers
Daily operator care doubles as early defect detection, catching deterioration while repair is still cheap and plannable
Planned maintenance has become unnecessary on this machine, since operator rounds find every problem
The cleaning standard was too thorough, because inspections that find faults create unplanned work for technicians

questions.explanation: The clean-and-inspect routine exists precisely to surface such findings. Early detection converts an emergency stoppage into a planned repair.

questions.question: A bottling line produces drinks with underfilled bottles at a rate of four per hundred, and those bottles are scrapped or reworked every shift. Which waste category captures the underfills?

answers.text: Inventory waste, because scrapped bottles accumulate in a skip behind the bottling hall.
Overproduction waste, because the line must run longer to replace each scrapped bottle.
Motion waste, because operators carry rejected bottles from the line to the scrap area.
Defects waste, because output failing its specification consumes resources without serving customers.

questions.explanation: Output that fails requirements is defects waste, whether scrapped or reworked. Extra running and carrying are secondary ripples; the primary classification follows the failed specification.

questions.question: Chemical batches give one purity value each: mean 95.0 percent, mean moving range 4.0 percent. With the 2.66 factor, state the individuals limits.

answers.text: The band is tighter, running from 91.00 percent at its base to 99.00 percent at its peak.
Band edges sit at 108.07 percent and 81.93 percent.
Purity results signal outside the band running from 84.36 percent up to 105.64 percent.
Edges of 100.32 percent (top) and 89.68 percent (bottom) govern the chart.

questions.explanation: The allowance is 2.66 times 4.0, or 10.64, so the limits are 95.0 plus or minus 10.64, giving 105.64 and 84.36 percent.

questions.question: A newly drawn map of permit approvals shows files crossing between planning, legal, and finance eleven times before a decision issues. What improvement signal does the team read first?

answers.text: Eleven crossings prove each department distrusts the others and deliberately delays every file.
Frequent handoffs multiply queues and error chances, flagging transfer points as improvement targets.
Eleven crossings show the process is healthy, because many reviews guarantee very careful decisions.
Frequent handoffs mean the map is drawn wrongly, since real processes move in straight lines only.

questions.explanation: Each handoff risks delay, loss, and misunderstanding, so dense crossing patterns highlight where redesign may consolidate or sequence work better. Distrust motives and straight-line assumptions go beyond the evidence.

questions.question: Operators sample at random times they personally choose whenever the line seems calm. Why does this undermine subgroup logic?

answers.text: Choosing personal times improves alertness, so the chart gains sensitivity because operators engage more deeply.
Choosing calm moments randomises conditions, so the chart benefits from a broader mix of operating states sampled.
Choosing personal times affects only staffing, so the chart's statistical properties remain entirely untouched here.
Choosing calm moments biases subgroups toward good conditions, so the chart understates ordinary process variation as described.

questions.explanation: Subgroups should follow a planned schedule or scheme. Cherry-picking quiet moments gives a flattering, false baseline.

questions.question: A courier analyst plots parcels carried against route distance and sees points sweeping upward in a broad band that bends slightly near the longest routes. What should be concluded before fitting a straight line?

answers.text: The broad band means the variables are unrelated, because genuine relationships always appear as points hugging a narrow track.
A straight line is ideal precisely because the bend appears only at long distances, where fitted values matter least to the model.
The relationship looks mostly positive but the bend at long distances warns that a single straight line may misdescribe the far end.
The bend proves distance has no real association with parcels carried, so the analysis should stop before any line is attempted.

questions.explanation: Scatter inspection comes first: a generally rising pattern with curvature at the extremes cautions against blindly fitting one straight line across the whole range.

questions.question: In a control plan, the specification column for fill volume reads 500 ml plus or minus 10 ml. What job does that column perform during routine monitoring?

answers.text: It states the control limits the chart must use, replacing any need to calculate limits from process data.
It states the average fill the line achieved last quarter, kept as a historical note for annual reviews.
It states the gauge resolution required, expressed in millilitres so operators can select an instrument.
It states the customer-facing requirement against which individual results are judged for acceptance.

questions.explanation: Specifications voice the requirement; control limits, calculated separately from process behaviour, must never be copied from the specification column.

questions.question: An indicator for a rare supplier appears in only three of 400 observations in a parts-quality model, and its slope estimate is enormous with a huge standard error. What caution should attach?

answers.text: Three observations cannot support a reliable category contrast, so that slope should be flagged as unstable or the category grouped with others thoughtfully.
The enormous resulting estimated slope should headline the reported findings, because rare categories produce the most dramatic and therefore most valuable coefficients.
The standard error must be a misprint, because categories with few cases yield the tightest estimates in indicator modelling practice.
The supplier should be made the reference category, because baselines estimated from three cases anchor the remaining contrasts securely.

questions.explanation: Tiny category counts leave contrasts hostage to a few points. Huge standard errors are the output honestly reporting that fragility.

questions.question: Historical data at Juniper Stanton Foods show that 4% of bolts develop a surface flaw during curing. If the plant cures 250 units next week under the same conditions, how many flawed units should the team expect?

answers.text: 4 flawed units would treat the stated percentage itself as a count, ignoring that the run contains two hundred fifty units, not one hundred in the bolts operation.
25 flawed units would apply the flaw rate to the wrong base, overstating the expectation by a factor that the run size does not support.
10 flawed units is the expectation, because an expected count multiplies the flaw probability by the run size: 0.04 x 250 units at the Cobalt Street plant.
100 flawed units would multiply the percentage by the run size without converting 4% into its decimal form of 0.04 first.

questions.explanation: Curing 250 bolts while flaws strike 4 percent predicts 0.04 multiplied by 250, giving ten flawed bolts as Juniper Stanton's long-run expectation for next week.

questions.question: A paired t-test on 15 technicians shows mean error rate fell by 2.1 points, with the interval for mean change running from a fall of 3.8 to a fall of 0.4. How does that interval inform the verdict?

answers.text: The interval suggests errors rose, because negative thinking dominates the lower bound value listed.
The interval proves every technician improved equally, because ranges describe individuals directly.
The interval must be ignored, because paired tests communicate exclusively through t-statistics alone.
The interval excludes zero change, supporting a genuine average reduction in errors after training.

questions.explanation: An interval for the mean difference that stays clear of zero aligns with rejecting no change. It also bounds the plausible size of the average fall.

questions.question: A manager assumes buyers want the cheapest model, but interviews show durability matters more. What lesson follows?

answers.text: Checking assumptions against real customer input prevents optimising the wrong characteristic.
Interviews should be discounted whenever they contradict a manager's market intuition.
The lesson is that price never influences purchasing decisions in any product category.
Durability should now be maximised regardless of cost, segment, or stated trade-offs.

questions.explanation: Assumed priorities often miss. Gathering actual voice of the customer redirects effort toward characteristics buyers truly value.

nate-certification.quiz_title: NATE Certification Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: When a technician says a room is at 50 percent relative humidity at 75 degrees, what two instrument-derived values were combined to state that condition?

answers.text: Supply static pressure and return static pressure from a manometer
Dry-bulb temperature and a moisture measure (wet-bulb, dew point, or a direct humidity sensor reading)
Suction pressure and discharge pressure from the outdoor unit gauges
Blower amperage and supply temperature from the air handler

questions.explanation: Relative humidity is a state description requiring temperature plus moisture information. It can come from wet-bulb/dry-bulb psychrometry, a dew-point measurement, or a calibrated electronic humidity sensor read at that temperature. Pressures and amperage describe equipment operation, not the room air state occupants experience.

questions.question: A motor branch in a loading study draws 12 amps at 230 volts with a measured power factor of 0.85, and the engineer wants the true watts rather than the volt-ampere product. What real power is being delivered?

answers.text: The real power is 195.5 watts.
The real power is 2760 watts.
The real power is 2346 watts.
The real power is 325 watts.

questions.explanation: True power in an inductive motor circuit is the volt-ampere product reduced by the power factor, because part of the alternating current shuttles energy to and from the magnetic field without producing shaft work.  Calculation: 230 * 12 * 0.85 = 2346.

questions.question: A thermostat in Boulder is switched to emergency heat after a compressor failure in a cold snap. What changes in system operation, and why does the power bill jump?

answers.text: Emergency heat runs the compressor at double speed for extra output
The heat pump is locked out entirely and resistance strips carry the whole load at roughly three times the cost per unit of heat
Emergency heat burns natural gas in the air handler as a backup
The bill jumps because emergency heat disables the indoor blower

questions.explanation: Emergency heat exists to keep a house warm with a dead refrigeration side: the thermostat bypasses the compressor call and heats with strips alone. Resistance heat delivers one unit of heat per unit of electricity, versus roughly three for a heat pump in mild weather, so operating cost climbs steeply until the compressor is repaired.

questions.question: After a duct-modification project, a furnace that never previously tripped now opens its limit on long cycles, while its firing rate, filter, and blower all test exactly as before. What changed in the system to produce the new symptom?

answers.text: Ductwork changes can raise manifold pressure by back-pressuring the gas valve
The duct changes reduced delivered airflow, so a previously adequate heat balance now overheats the exchanger
New duct metal magnetizes the limit switch so it opens at lower temperatures
The furnace aged a full service life during the week of duct construction

questions.explanation: Limit behavior is a system outcome, not a part personality: identical burners and blower with new, more restrictive ductwork deliver less air, and less air over the same fire means higher exchanger temperature. The post-modification timing identifies the air-distribution change as the variable that must be corrected.

questions.question: A moisture indicator sight glass is fitted downstream of a filter-drier. What is the technician actually reading when checking it?

answers.text: The exact refrigerant charge in ounces, shown by a numbered scale
The color element that changes with the moisture content of the liquid refrigerant passing the glass
The oil level inside the compressor crankcase
The superheat value at the evaporator outlet

questions.explanation: The indicator's chemical element changes color with the moisture level in the liquid stream; bubbles seen in the glass can suggest low charge or a restriction, but the color itself reports moisture, not charge weight.

questions.question: What happens to relative humidity inside a cold storage room when warm humid air enters and is chilled toward the room temperature without moisture removal at first?

answers.text: Relative humidity climbs toward saturation as the air cools, and condensation or frost may form on cold surfaces
Relative humidity falls steadily because cold rooms are always dry in relative terms
Relative humidity stays fixed at the outdoor value regardless of temperature change
The air becomes superheated vapor as it contacts cold stored products

questions.explanation: Cooling at constant moisture content raises relative humidity because saturation capacity shrinks. Cold rooms therefore battle condensation and frost at door openings and on evaporators, even though their absolute moisture may be low. Dehumidification and air sealing, not just refrigeration, manage that moisture load.

questions.question: A heat pump's reversing-valve solenoid is wired to be energized during cooling on this particular manufacturer's system, and the unit heats when set to cool with correct refrigerant pressures verified. What control-side check comes first?

answers.text: Add refrigerant until the reversing valve is forced to shift mechanically.
Replace the compressor because its rotation determines heating versus cooling.
A reversing valve can never cause a heat-instead-of-cool complaint.
Confirm whether the thermostat's changeover output is actually energizing the solenoid circuit in cooling mode as that brand requires.

questions.explanation: Brands differ: some energize the solenoid in cooling, others in heating, so the stat's O/B output and its configuration must match the equipment. A valve stuck or unpowered stays in its default mode, producing exactly this swapped-operation complaint.

questions.question: Immediately after startup on a cool morning, a fixed-orifice system shows very high superheat that settles to normal within fifteen minutes. What is the disciplined interpretation?

answers.text: Morning air permanently changes the refrigerant's properties
Startup readings taken before pressures, oil and charge distribution stabilize are not charge evidence; only stabilized values may be judged
The metering device is failing and must be replaced at once
The system is undercharged every morning and corrects itself daily

questions.explanation: A system needs real run time for refrigerant to distribute, oil to return and coil temperatures to settle. Superheat chased during warm-up leads to phantom additions; the professional habit is to let the plant stabilize, then measure once and decide once.

questions.question: A trainee in Paris, Texas asks why heat pump charging instructions forbid using heating-mode readings to set charge on most residential systems in winter, even with gauges already connected. Give the core technical reason.

answers.text: Heating pressures are secret and gauges cannot display them in winter
Refrigerant refuses to circulate measurably when a system heats

Heating targets shift strongly with outdoor temperature and many makers publish no heating charging chart, while the weighed inventory method stays accurate in any weather, making winter running adjustments guesswork against moving targets
Winter charging is discouraged only to sell spring service visits

questions.explanation: In cooling, manufacturers map charge to measurable targets across conditions. In heating, the evaporator is outdoors in uncontrolled weather, loads swing with every degree, and published targets are scarce. Weighing the specified inventory sidesteps all that variability. Running checks still diagnose health in winter; they simply should not steer the scale.

questions.question: A burner compartment is found dusted with black soot and the flame picture has degraded over one heating season since a new, much larger gas range was added to the same meter. Which diagnostic direction connects those facts?

answers.text: Soot after adding an appliance is always caused by a failing indoor blower
Check total gas supply capacity and firing input — an overtaxed or misadjusted supply can distort burner operation and produce sooting incomplete combustion
The new range has magnetized the furnace burners so flames lean and soot
Sooting proves the furnace vent is oversized and nothing else need be checked

questions.explanation: Soot is a symptom of incomplete combustion, and changed gas demand can expose undersized piping or regulation that starves or destabilizes the furnace at full load; input must also be verified because overfiring soots as well. Treating soot as dirt to vacuum without combustion and supply diagnosis leaves a CO-producing fault in place.

questions.question: Condenser flooding for head-pressure control in cool weather deliberately backs liquid into the condenser. Which normal charging reading does that strategy intentionally distort?

answers.text: Subcooling and apparent charge inventory, because liquid is being stored in the condenser on purpose
Indoor wet-bulb temperature at the return grille
Blower motor amperage on the indoor unit
Suction-line insulation thickness

questions.explanation: Flooding controls hold head pressure by filling part of the condenser with liquid; that stored inventory makes subcooling look like an overcharge, so charge must be judged with the control's operation in mind.

questions.question: Cold-climate model in Burlington, Vermont: at five degrees outdoors it still delivers most of its rated heating capacity and rarely calls strips, unlike the older single-stage unit it replaced. Which design ideas explain that cold-weather stamina?

answers.text: The new unit burns a small amount of fuel inside the outdoor cabinet for boost
Its reversing valve is larger, which alone multiplies heating capacity in cold air
Cold air in Vermont contains extra heat that older units could not detect
Variable-speed compression that can overspeed in cold weather plus enhanced vapor injection keeps refrigerant mass flow and capacity up as outdoor temperature falls

questions.explanation: Cold-climate designs attack the real problem: thin cold air and high lift reduce how much refrigerant mass the compressor moves. Running the compressor faster and injecting vapor mid-compression restores flow and tames discharge temperature, holding capacity far down the thermometer. That is equipment capability, not a control trick, and it changes balance-point expectations for the house.

questions.question: A pressure-temperature chart shows that raising the pressure on a refrigerant raises its saturation temperature. If a condenser operates at unusually high pressure, what follows for condensing temperature?

answers.text: Condensing temperature stays fixed because pressure and temperature are unrelated in a condenser
Condensing occurs at a higher temperature, making heat rejection to outdoor air harder on a hot day
Condensing occurs at a lower temperature, which improves heat rejection in all weather
The refrigerant stops condensing and remains vapor regardless of coil size

questions.explanation: Pressure and saturation temperature move together for a refrigerant. Higher condensing pressure means a higher condensing temperature, which shrinks the temperature difference driving heat into outdoor air and raises compressor work. This relationship explains why dirty condensers and high head pressure hurt capacity and efficiency.

questions.question: A technician measures duct leakage only at the equipment and declares the system tight, yet rooms at the ends of long attic runs receive little air. Which blind spot invalidates that declaration?

answers.text: Attic runs lose air only through their register grilles
Long runs deliver more air because velocity builds with distance
Leakage and friction losses accumulate along the runs themselves, so an equipment-only check cannot see the pressure and volume surrendered before the far registers
Equipment readings include every downstream loss automatically

questions.explanation: A blower can be honest and the registers can still starve. Each joint along an attic run leaks a little and each foot of flex adds friction, so the far end inherits whatever pressure and volume remain; only measurements at the runs themselves expose where the delivery went.

questions.question: A homeowner in Christiansburg keeps a log: defrosts at almost the same run-time intervals all winter, lasting almost the same minutes, whether the week was drizzly or desert-dry. Which control family produces that metronome pattern, and what is its known trade-off?

answers.text: Time-temperature control, which checks on a schedule and can waste cycles on dry days while occasionally lagging heavy frost, trading simplicity for precision
Demand control, which is famous for ignoring actual frost completely
Manual control, since only a person could keep such regular timing
Pressure control, which defrosts by suction pressure alone on a clock

questions.explanation: Scheduled initiation cannot see moisture, so its calendar looks the same in a drought as in a drizzle. That regularity in the log is the fingerprint of timed control. The trade-off is accepted for simplicity and cost, but recognizing it prevents a technician from hunting sensor faults on a system that has no frost-sensing strategy to fail.

questions.question: While inspecting burner tubes on a ten-year-old furnace, a technician finds the flame sensor mounted so its rod passes through the edge of one burner's flame rather than sitting well inside the flame envelope. What operating symptom matches that placement?

answers.text: Marginal, intermittent flame proving with occasional dropouts even though combustion looks healthy
Continuous overheating of the gas valve regulator diaphragm
A pressure switch that chatters whenever the inducer reaches full speed
Steady limit tripping caused by excess heat at the sensor location

questions.explanation: The rod must be enveloped by flame to carry a strong rectification current; sitting at the flame edge produces a weak, unstable microamp signal that dips below the board threshold and causes intermittent lockouts. Repositioning or correcting burner alignment restores a solid signal without changing unrelated parts.

questions.question: Outdoor sensor strategy in Jackson, Wyoming: the changeover sensor is accurate, but afternoon sun strikes the west-facing outdoor unit and delays furnace changeover on bright cold days, leaving rooms chilly until sunset. What correction respects both sensor and sun?

answers.text: Relocate or shield the sensor to sample shaded ambient air as the manufacturer specifies, because solar loading makes any sensor report the sun's temperature instead of the air's
Raise the changeover setting by the exact sunny-day error permanently
Cover the entire outdoor unit with a box to keep it in shade
Accept chilly bright afternoons as the price of solar energy generally

questions.explanation: Sensors report their own temperature, hoping it equals the air's. Sunlight breaks that equality by several degrees. A shaded, ventilated mounting away from the cabinet and exhaust restores the measurement the control math assumes. Compensating the setpoint instead would corrupt every cloudy day to fix the sunny ones.

questions.question: A replacement transformer for a packaged unit has a 240-volt primary, a 24-volt secondary rating, and a nameplate showing 10 secondary turns in this training example using 100 primary turns. If the primary is actually energized at 240 volts, what secondary voltage follows from that turns relationship?

answers.text: The secondary delivers 2400 volts.
The secondary delivers 100 volts.
The secondary delivers 24 volts.
The secondary delivers 10 volts.

questions.explanation: Secondary voltage scales with the turns ratio, so a ten-to-one step-down from the primary produces one-tenth of the primary voltage at the secondary. Inverting the ratio would dangerously suggest a step-up that this transformer cannot provide.  Calculation: 240 * 10 / 100 = 24.

questions.question: A technician compares two vessels found on different systems: a large tank on the liquid line after the condenser, and a smaller tank in the suction line at the compressor inlet. Which pairing of roles is correct?

answers.text: Both tanks are receivers, and both store high-pressure liquid for the metering device
The liquid-line tank is an accumulator, and the suction-line tank sets the system charge
The liquid-line tank is a receiver storing liquid inventory; the suction-line tank is an accumulator trapping liquid so only vapor reaches the compressor
Both tanks are oil separators returning lubricant to the crankcase

questions.explanation: Location defines the job. A receiver sits in the high-pressure liquid stream and banks liquid inventory for a modulating valve. An accumulator sits in the low-pressure suction stream and intercepts liquid leaving the evaporator, metering it back slowly so the compressor is never slugged.

questions.question: The guesthouse over the garage hosts exchange students each summer, and the host family scheduled a pre-season verification. A blower delivers 1400 cfm into the supply ducts of a 5-ton split system at a farmhouse, and testing shows 20% of that air leaks into the attic before reaching the registers. How much airflow is being lost to the attic?

answers.text: 420 cfm, adding a fixed allowance to the percentage loss
280 cfm is lost, the delivered airflow multiplied by the leakage percentage
1320 cfm, which is closer to the air still reaching the rooms plus an allowance
200 cfm, found by multiplying the percentage number by ten regardless of total flow

questions.explanation: Leakage loss = 1400 cfm × 20% = 1400 × 0.20 = 280 cfm. That air was cooled at full energy cost but never reaches a register, which is why duct sealing can recover capacity that no equipment change could provide.

iassc-lean-six-sigma-black-belt.quiz_title: IASSC Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why does the hidden factory resist ordinary improvement prioritization in many plants?

answers.text: Operators hide rework deliberately to protect overtime earnings, and only surveillance reveals the true scale of the activity
Its work is normalized inside standard routings and labor standards, so no report ever isolates it as waste available for elimination
Hidden-factory output is sold as seconds at a discount, making its economics look attractive in contribution reports, if the budget holder approves
Accounting standards forbid separating rework labor, so managers must estimate the hidden factory from scrap value alone

questions.explanation: Rework embedded in standard times and routings becomes invisible by design; deliberate concealment, seconds sales, and accounting prohibitions misdescribe a structural visibility problem.

questions.question: A centered process has limits exactly four overall standard deviations on each side of the mean. What is its Pp?

answers.text: Pp is 2.67, because the full width of eight sigma divided by three gives the performance index for this process
Pp is 4.00, because the index reports the sigma distance from the mean to each limit without further adjustment
Pp is 0.75, because performance indices invert the ratio of tolerance width to the natural process spread used
Pp is 1.33, because the tolerance width of eight sigma divided by six sigma gives the performance index value

questions.explanation: Pp = (USL-LSL)/(6 x overall sigma) = 8 sigma / 6 sigma = 1.33. Centering makes Ppk equal to Pp in this symmetric case.

questions.question: Which phrasing correctly states what a Kruskal-Wallis rejection supports, absent any shape assumptions?

answers.text: The group with the largest sample has the largest median, because rank sums grow automatically with the size of each group
Every pair of groups differs significantly, because omnibus rejection is defined as all pairwise differences holding at once
All group means are different from one another in a specified direction that the statistic prints alongside its p-value here
At least one group's distribution is stochastically different, with values from it tending to sit higher or lower than others

questions.explanation: The defensible omnibus claim is distributional: at least one population tends to produce larger (or smaller) values than another. Pairwise and median-specific claims each demand further work or further assumptions.

questions.question: A grower tests five two-level inputs on tomato yield in a single replicate of a full factorial. How large is the run list?

answers.text: Thirty-two runs, from 2 multiplied by itself five times, covering each of the five factors' level pairings
Ten runs are enough, since five factors with two levels apiece contribute two runs per factor to the total
Sixty-four runs are required, which is the count belonging to six two-level factors rather than five here
Twenty runs result, because five factors at two levels produce four runs for every factor in the design

questions.explanation: With k=5, runs = 2^5 = 32, the full set of level combinations for five two-level factors.

questions.question: Which operators need control-plan training first when a plan launches across three shifts with limited trainer capacity?

answers.text: The day shift only, because night and weekend shifts can copy day-shift practice from the posted charts
Supervisors exclusively, since floor operators absorb plan requirements by imitating their supervisor, leaving direct operator instruction for a later training round
The newest hires, because experienced operators can be assumed competent on any new plan by default
Those covering the checks and reactions for critical characteristics on every shift, so no shift ever runs a critical control with untrained cover here

questions.explanation: Coverage logic governs sequencing: every shift needs certified capability on the highest-risk controls from the first day the plan is live.

questions.question: A Black Belt presents savings using straight wages while finance insists on loaded rates including benefits and payroll taxes. Whose convention governs the charter?

answers.text: Finance's loaded-rate convention, agreed and recorded at charter time, because benefit figures must be comparable across every project the portfolio reports
The Black Belt's wage figure, because improvement teams best understand what an hour in their process is actually worth
Whichever rate produces the larger benefit, since the charter's purpose is to win approval for worthwhile projects, because unwinding it later is somebody else's problem
A midpoint between the two rates, splitting the difference so neither party's convention dominates the calculation

questions.explanation: Comparability across the portfolio requires one agreed rate convention, set with finance before work starts; local knowledge, approval-seeking, and midpoint splits sacrifice that consistency.

questions.question: A Black Belt needs a quick check of a new fixture and runs a short study: 2 operators, 5 parts, 2 trials. The results look poor. What is the right weight to give this outcome?

answers.text: Treat it as a screening signal: a poor result warrants a fuller study, but the small design's estimates carry wide uncertainty
Treat it as definitive, because gage estimates stabilize completely once total measurements reach twenty in a study
Ignore it, because studies below ten parts are incapable of detecting even a completely unusable measurement system
Treat the poor result as proof the fixture is worse than the old one, since small studies bias estimates upward

questions.explanation: Small designs give imprecise variance estimates, so a poor screening result is a warning that justifies a proper study rather than a final verdict — but it is a real signal, not noise to be ignored.

questions.question: A team tests a claim that a process mean exceeds a regulatory floor. The analyst writes the alternative as 'mean equals the floor' by mistake, computes a tiny p-value, and claims victory. What went wrong conceptually?

answers.text: The boundary claim sat in the wrong seat: p-values flow from the default's distribution, so the scrambled setup voids the meaning
Nothing went wrong, because p-values are symmetric and can be computed from whichever statement the analyst finds convenient
The only slip is labeling, which a footnote can repair while preserving the victory claim and its supporting arithmetic
The floor should have been replaced by the sample mean in both statements, which would have made the victory claim rigorous

questions.explanation: Every p-value is anchored to the default position's sampling distribution; swapping the statements changes the anchor, so the tiny value no longer testifies about the claim being advanced.

questions.question: A predictor's variance inflation factor is 10, computed from an auxiliary R-squared of 0.90 when that predictor is regressed on the others. Verify and interpret.

answers.text: VIF = 1/(1 - 0.90) = 10 confirms it: the predictor is heavily explained by its companions, inflating its coefficient's variance
VIF = 1 - 0.90 = 0.10, so the predictor is nearly independent and its standard error is comfortably small, and the line crews would work to it
VIF = 1/(1 - 0.90) squared = 100, meaning the coefficient is ten times less precise than reported
VIF = 0.90/0.10 = 9, close to the threshold but computed by dividing the wrong pair of quantities here

questions.explanation: 1/(1 - 0.90) = 10 exactly; a VIF at that level says the coefficient's variance is inflated tenfold by overlap with other predictors.

questions.question: A study of solder defects uses each printed board twice: once as its own experimental unit and again after rework as a second unit. Why does a reviewer object?

answers.text: The objection is misplaced, because defect counts from the same board are actually more comparable than across boards
The reworked board is not an independent unit, so treating it as one understates error and overstates the evidence
Boards may be reused freely provided the run order is shuffled, which restores independence between the two passes
Rework is objectionable only because it doubles the study cost without adding any new factor combinations

questions.explanation: Experimental units must be independent; a reworked board carries its history with it, so its second result is correlated with the first.

questions.question: Phase I data for a new chart included a weekend when a substitute resin was used. Limits computed from all the data are wide, and phase II rarely signals. What went wrong?

answers.text: Phase I data must contain no special causes whatsoever, so the chart has to be discarded and the process requalified from scratch after that resin weekend.
Wide limits are correct here because phase II limits are required to widen every time phase I grows longer
The substitute resin weekend should have been charted as its own subgroup, which alone would have fixed the limits
The contaminated phase I sample inflated the variation estimate, so the trial limits are too generous and real departures hide inside them

questions.explanation: Phase I exists to estimate the stable process; leaving a known disturbed period in the estimate bakes its extra variation into every future limit.

questions.question: A Black Belt reviewing a supplier's CuSum finds the target was set to the average of the last month, which included a known bad week. What is the core defect?

answers.text: The defect is that targets must be specification midpoints, and using an observed monthly average is prohibited in CuSum work even when that week is excluded.
The target absorbed the bad week's bias, so the chart now treats a shifted level as normal and accumulates evidence against the wrong centre
A one-month baseline is too short by rule; CuSum targets require a minimum of twelve months of history before use
Including the bad week only affects the first plotted point, after which the statistic corrects itself automatically

questions.explanation: A CuSum measures departure from its target; a contaminated target shifts the zero point and the chart will defend the wrong level as if it were the aim.

questions.question: A fishbone session for invoice errors produces 60 candidate causes. The sponsor asks which three matter. The Black Belt's next step should be:

answers.text: Ask each participant to defend their own suggestions, then keep the three argued most persuasively in the room
Keep all sixty in scope until Improve, because narrowing causes early risks discarding the true root cause unknowingly, since missing it costs far more
Pareto the candidates against occurrence data — error logs, stratification by type and source — to shortlist causes for verification
Select the three causes cheapest to fix, since early wins matter more than causal importance at this stage of DMAIC

questions.explanation: Brainstormed volume must be reduced with evidence: error records stratified by type, shift, or source show where occurrences concentrate, pointing verification at plausible major causes.

questions.question: To estimate defect rates across three plants with very different volumes, a team samples proportionally within each plant. Which method and benefit?

answers.text: Cluster sampling, chosen because sampling whole plants is cheaper than sampling within every plant in the study
Stratified sampling, ensuring each plant is represented in proportion and plant-level comparisons remain possible
Simple random sampling across the pooled output, which automatically guarantees the proportional plant mix desired
Systematic sampling from the combined shipping stream, which represents plants in proportion to their shipment timing

questions.explanation: Dividing the population into plant strata and sampling within each is stratified sampling; it guarantees representation and supports per-stratum estimates.

questions.question: Two candidate fits for the same data differ only in that one was estimated on 18 points and the other on 60 points spanning the same x range. Why will the larger study's slope interval usually be tighter?

answers.text: More observations shrink the slope's standard error, since residual noise averages down while the x spread stays comparable
Larger samples raise the critical t value sharply, and that increase is what narrows intervals in practice
Sixty points guarantee a higher R-squared, and higher explained variation is what mechanically tightens slope intervals
The interval narrows because the slope estimate itself must grow with sample size, dwarfing its standard error

questions.explanation: Slope standard error falls roughly with the square root of n; more points over the same range pin the line's tilt down harder.

questions.question: A fractional screen estimates a contrast labelled A at 14 units, where A is aliased with BC. Later work shows the BC interaction is actually 10 units. What follows?

answers.text: A's effect must be 24, because aliased effects always add constructively in fractional designs
The later finding invalidates the screen retroactively, so all its other contrasts must also be discarded
A remains 14 regardless, because aliasing affects only the interpretation of inactive effects
Much of the 14 may belong to BC, so A's own contribution could be as small as roughly 4 units

questions.explanation: The contrast estimated A + BC = 14; if BC = 10, the portion attributable to A is about 14 - 10 = 4.

questions.question: A Black Belt sees a histogram of bolt torque with a sharp cutoff at the lower specification and a normal-looking body above it. What likely happened?

answers.text: The process naturally produces truncated data, because torque distributions terminate at specification limits physically
Parts below the limit were screened out before the histogram, so the data describe inspected output, not the process itself
The gauge cannot read below the limit, which proves the measurement system needs a wider range instrument installed
The cutoff proves the process is incapable, because capable processes never show abrupt edges in their histograms

questions.explanation: A hard edge at the spec is the signature of prior sorting: the process distribution was amputated by inspection, and capability read from it would be flattered.

questions.question: A call center's handle-time data fail every normality test, with p-values below 0.01 in samples of 30, 80, and 200 calls drawn weeks apart. A manager suggests collecting a much larger sample so the data themselves will become normal. Why is that reasoning wrong?

answers.text: Larger samples do become normal, but only after the count passes one thousand calls in a single uninterrupted sample
The reasoning is right for handle times because service data always converge to a bell shape as volume grows
Larger samples reveal the true skewed shape more clearly; the central limit effect applies to sample means, not to the raw call times
The tests fail only because of the small samples, and at 200 calls a p-value below 0.01 carries no information at all, across all shifts

questions.explanation: Collecting more calls sharpens the picture of a skewed population rather than changing it; the central limit theorem describes averages of samples, so raw handle times keep their skew no matter how many are gathered.

questions.question: A Black Belt sizes a two-sample t study to detect a 0.4-standard-deviation mean difference with power 0.80 at alpha 0.05. A planning table suggests about 100 observations per group. The client offers 40 per group 'to start.' What consequence should be spelled out?

answers.text: Power stays at 0.80 because the planning table's figures embed a safety factor of more than two that real studies never actually consume
At 40 per group, power for the targeted difference sinks toward roughly 0.40, so a null outcome leaves the question genuinely open
The smaller study becomes a pilot whose significant results are trustworthy but whose null results are even more decisive than the full study's
Reducing group size raises power in two-sample designs, because fewer observations tighten the sampling distribution of the difference

questions.explanation: Power curves are unforgiving at small standardized effects: 0.4 sigma needs roughly 100 per group for 80% power, and 40 per group buys little better than a coin flip weighted toward missing.

questions.question: A molding plant wants its andon escalation to be economically rational. Pulls currently stop the whole line for any fault, including faults one operator can clear in seconds. What refinement preserves the system?

answers.text: Abolish line stops entirely and log every fault for weekly review, since stop costs always exceed defect costs in high-volume molding operations
Tier the response: operator-clearable faults get a brief signal and local fix, while faults beyond a defined time or scope escalate to a full stop
Charge the cost of each stop to the pulling operator's department budget, creating a financial incentive to reserve pulls for severe faults only
Require supervisor pre-approval before any pull, ensuring only economically justified stops interrupt the line during scheduled production time

questions.explanation: Tiered escalation keeps fast local response cheap and reserves expensive full stops for faults that need them. Pre-approval or abolition would destroy the signal's immediacy.

The association may self-insure all risks without any statutory process, regardless of filing status, and the same result follows in each later year as well, even when the amount involved is small compared with the taxpayer's total income, and the treatment does not change merely because the taxpayer also has wage income

A condominium association must use its best efforts to obtain and maintain adequate property (hazard) insurance covering all association property and the common elements at full replacement value as the statute requires — the declaration and statute together allocate which parts of the buildings the association insures versus which fall to unit owners

questions.explanation: Best efforts, full replacement value, statutory allocation — the association carries the building's risk program.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Savannah, Drew Bennett — the senior CAM — is handling a question on grounds for discipline of a CAM. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Minor bookkeeping sloppiness can never be a disciplinary matter, whether or not the taxpayer itemizes deductions or claims any related credit for the year, including when the underlying payment was made electronically rather than by check

A CAM's license may be disciplined for fraud, deceit, gross negligence, incompetence, or misconduct in practice — including misusing association funds, failing to account for money and property, and violating the governing statutes and rules

Discipline is handled by the association's board rather than the Department, whether or not the taxpayer itemizes deductions or claims any related credit for the year, whether or not the taxpayer itemizes deductions or claims any related credit for the year
A licensee may be disciplined only after a criminal conviction, even when the amount involved is small compared with the taxpayer's total income

questions.explanation: Fraud, deceit, negligence, incompetence, misconduct — and mishandling the association's money sits at the center.

questions.question: Emerson Clark, a community association manager, must apply the correct practice for annual financial reporting tiers. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Each year the association must prepare a financial report whose required level of rigor scales with total annual revenue — from a report of cash receipts and expenditures at the lowest revenues, through compiled and reviewed statements, to a full audit at the highest tier — and must deliver it (or notice of its availability) to owners within the statutory period

Every association must obtain a full audit regardless of revenue, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history, and no additional documentation, statement, or approval is required to reach that result, and no additional documentation, statement, or approval is required to reach that result, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history

Financial reports are prepared for the board only and never shared with owners, for all taxpayers in this situation, with no case-by-case variation permitted, in every case and without regard to the taxpayer's other income or deductions for the year, even when the amount involved is small compared with the taxpayer's total income

The reporting level is chosen freely by the manager each year, with no exception available on these facts and no election that changes the outcome, regardless of filing status, and the same result follows in each later year as well, including when the underlying payment was made electronically rather than by check

questions.explanation: Revenue sets the rigor: report, compilation, review, audit — and owners get it on the statutory clock.

questions.question: During an operations review in Bangor, Jesse Alvarez raises the topic of suspension of rights for nonpayment. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: An association may suspend an owner's voting rights and common-area use rights when the owner is more than 90 days delinquent in a monetary obligation, following the required board action at a duly noticed meeting — but may not suspend access to the unit, parking, utilities, or ingress and egress

Suspension may cut off an owner's access to their own unit, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history, for all taxpayers in this situation, with no case-by-case variation permitted, in every case and without regard to the taxpayer's other income or deductions for the year

Rights may be suspended the day a payment is late, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history

Suspension requires no board action if the manager documents the delinquency, regardless of filing status, and the same result follows in each later year as well, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history

questions.explanation: Ninety days delinquent, board action at a noticed meeting, and never the owner's access to their home.

questions.question: Kai Watanabe is a newly licensed CAM at a Florida management firm and is asked about board meeting notice — condominiums. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Notice is required only for annual meetings, including when the underlying payment was made electronically rather than by check, for all taxpayers in this situation, with no case-by-case variation permitted, and no additional documentation, statement, or approval is required to reach that result

Board meetings require no notice if the agenda is routine, and no additional documentation, statement, or approval is required to reach that result, and no additional documentation, statement, or approval is required to reach that result, regardless of filing status, and the same result follows in each later year as well

For a condominium board meeting, notice must be posted in a conspicuous place in the condominium at least 48 continuous hours before the meeting (with additional mailed or delivered notice for meetings adopting budgets, levying special assessments, or considering certain rules, at least 14 days ahead)

Posted notice 24 hours in advance is sufficient for all board business, even when the amount involved is small compared with the taxpayer's total income, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history

questions.explanation: Forty-eight continuous posted hours for board meetings — fourteen days' written notice for the money meetings.

questions.question: Kai Watanabe is a newly licensed CAM at a Florida management firm and is asked about life-safety systems and inspections. Records on the point are kept in the HR system and agree with the paper file. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Elevator and fire system testing is optional if no incident has occurred, with no exception available on these facts and no election that changes the outcome, including when the underlying payment was made electronically rather than by check, whether or not the taxpayer itemizes deductions or claims any related credit for the year

The manager must calendar and document the association's life-safety obligations — fire alarm and sprinkler systems, elevators, pools, and (for taller condominiums) milestone inspection deadlines — because missed life-safety compliance is the association's gravest liability exposure

Life-safety inspections are the unit owners' shared responsibility individually, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history, whether or not the taxpayer itemizes deductions or claims any related credit for the year

Milestone inspection deadlines may be extended by board resolution, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history, and no additional documentation, statement, or approval is required to reach that result

questions.explanation: Fire, elevator, pool, structure — life-safety dates are the least forgiving entries on the manager's calendar.

questions.question: Sage Kowalski is a newly licensed CAM at a Florida management firm and is asked about association liens and foreclosure. The employee has several years of service and a clean record apart from the matter described. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Unpaid assessments are secured by the association's continuing lien on the unit or parcel; the association must follow the statutory notice steps (including the notice of intent to lien and notice of intent to foreclose, each with its cure window) before foreclosing, and association liens are generally subordinate to a first mortgage of record

Association assessment liens outrank first mortgages in all cases, in every case and without regard to the taxpayer's other income or deductions for the year, and the treatment does not change merely because the taxpayer also has wage income, for all taxpayers in this situation, with no case-by-case variation permitted, for all taxpayers in this situation, with no case-by-case variation permitted

Lien notices are courtesy letters with no statutory content or timing, including when the underlying payment was made electronically rather than by check, in every case and without regard to the taxpayer's other income or deductions for the year, without any need to consider the taxpayer's prior-year return or filing history

An association may foreclose immediately upon a missed payment without notice, whether or not the taxpayer itemizes deductions or claims any related credit for the year, including when the underlying payment was made electronically rather than by check, in every case and without regard to the taxpayer's other income or deductions for the year

questions.explanation: Intent to lien, intent to foreclose, cure windows between — collections is a notice discipline.

nccco-mobile-crane.quiz_title: NCCCO Mobile Crane Operator Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: At a substation job, the utility offers to install protective line coverings on a section of conductor for a week of crane work. How should the crew treat those coverings in their planning?

answers.text: As insulation that permits deliberate boom contact
As armor that raises the line's voltage rating
As an added safeguard that reduces risk from incidental contact but does not replace required clearance and planning
As decoration marking the utility's work zone

questions.explanation: Line coverings are a supplementary barrier against incidental brushing, not rated permission to touch or crowd the conductor. Clearances, spotters, and planning stay in force; treating covers as armor or insulation for deliberate contact defeats their purpose.

questions.question: An operator receives a clear 'swing' hand signal but cannot tell in which direction the finger is pointing because of backlight glare. What is required?

answers.text: Ask the signal person to point with the other hand while swinging slowly
Hold the load still and have the ambiguity resolved, by repositioning, shading, or switching to confirmed voice signals, before any swing begins
Swing a short distance as a test and watch for a stop signal
Swing in the direction the load was traveling on the previous pick

questions.explanation: Direction is the content of the swing signal; if it cannot be read, the signal has not been received. Test swings and momentum from previous picks gamble the load's path on a guess, and mid-motion clarification still starts with an unread instruction. The load waits until the direction is certain.

questions.question: A fictional 78-ton crane will use a spreader bar weighing 900 pounds plus slings weighing 260 pounds as rigging, with a block of 880 pounds, against a chart gross of 19,800 pounds from the chart reproduced in this question. What is the net capacity?

answers.text: 19,800 pounds
17,760 pounds
18,920 pounds
18,040 pounds

questions.explanation: Spreader bars are rigging and deduct in full: 19,800 − 880 − 900 − 260 = 17,760 pounds. Omitting the bar gives 18,920 pounds, omitting bar and slings gives a still higher wrong figure, and 19,800 pounds is gross capacity before any deduction is taken.

questions.question: Why is a crane that has been involved in any contact with an energized line inspected before returning to service, even if it appears to work normally afterward?

answers.text: Inspection is unnecessary if the contact lasted less than a second
Inspection is required only if the operator felt a shock
Inspection is a formality performed for the utility's records

Electrical contact can damage wire rope, electronics, bearings, and hydraulic components in ways that are not visible or immediate, so apparent normal operation is not evidence the machine is undamaged

questions.explanation: Current through a crane can pit bearings, anneal or fuse rope wires internally, and destroy electronic aids while leaving the machine superficially functional. Duration and the operator's sensations do not measure that damage. A competent inspection is what separates a machine that survived from one carrying hidden failures into its next picks.

questions.question: A fictional 45-ton crane is reeved with 3 parts of line at a stated single-line pull of 6,100 pounds, while its chart net capacity at the radius is 19,800 pounds. Total suspended weight for the planned pick is 18,900 pounds. What limits the pick?

answers.text: The chart limits it, and the pick is fine at 18,900 pounds
The reeving limits it: 3 parts hold 18,300 pounds by line pull, so the planned 18,900 pounds exceeds the line limit despite fitting the chart net
Neither limit applies, because the two nearly agree
The pick may proceed if the third part is treated as a spare

questions.explanation: Line-pull capacity is 3 × 6,100 = 18,300 pounds, which the planned 18,900-pound suspended weight exceeds by 600 pounds, so the pick cannot go as reeved even though the 19,800-pound chart net would allow it. Every part in the reeving works; none is a spare, and near-agreement between two limits does not waive the lower one.

questions.question: A lift plan for a courthouse clock-tower repair specifies cribbing built from sound, dry, full-dimension timbers laid in alternating layers. What performance does that layered cribbing provide at each float?

answers.text: It decorates the setup for a historic building
It creates a broad, stable, interlocked base that spreads the jack reaction and resists shifting
It allows the operator to skip using the float entirely
It raises the crane enough to clear the courthouse steps

questions.explanation: Alternating sound timbers interlock into a wide, stable platform that spreads load and resists lateral shifting under the float. Decoration and step clearance are incidental, and cribbing never replaces the float; the float and cribbing work together as one support system.

questions.question: Following a tip-over in which nobody was hurt, the crane lies on its side and the load is on the ground. The owner wants the machine righted immediately with another crane so work can resume. What must precede any recovery lifting?

answers.text: A fresh coat of paint on scraped panels so damage is less visible

A competent assessment of the damage, the cause, and a planned recovery, with the machine inspected before any return to service; an overturned crane is evidence and damaged equipment, not just an obstacle
Only the operator's statement that the machine felt normal before the tip
Nothing; righting it quickly erases the incident's disruption

questions.explanation: A tip-over means the machine absorbed forces it may not have survived intact, and the cause must be understood before the same configuration is trusted again. Recovery is itself a planned lift of a damaged machine. Rushing to right it, relying on feel, or cosmetically hiding damage destroys both the investigation and the inspection the machine needs.

questions.question: A torque check program marks swing bearing bolts with paint lines across bolt and joint after torquing. What does a broken paint line tell a later inspector at a glance?

answers.text: Paint lines are decoration showing the crane was serviced recently
A broken line proves the bolt has gained clamping force with use
That bolt has rotated since it was torqued, so its clamping has changed and the bolt set needs proper re-checking
Only bolts without paint lines ever need torque attention later

questions.explanation: Torque stripe is a witness mark: alignment means nothing moved, misalignment is instant evidence of rotation. It turns a hidden preload loss into something any walkaround can spot, provided inspectors know what the line is telling them.

questions.question: For a fictional 68-ton lattice crane, the chart reproduced in this question gives jib capacities for offset angles of 5 degrees and 25 degrees, rating 7,600 pounds and 6,300 pounds at the working radius. The jib is rigged at a 20-degree offset, which is not a listed angle. Which value must be used?

answers.text: 7,600 pounds, because 20 degrees is closer to 5 than the chart intends
7,600 pounds, the value at the next smaller listed offset
6,300 pounds, the value at the next greater listed offset angle
6,950 pounds, interpolated between the offsets

questions.explanation: Unlisted offset angles follow the same conservative rule as radius and boom length: use the next more severe listed condition, the 25-degree offset rating of 6,300 pounds. The 5-degree value and any interpolation such as 6,950 pounds claim capacity for a geometry the chart rates lower once the offset grows.

questions.question: A telescopic crane offers a free-fall lowering feature on its auxiliary drum. A rigger suggests using it to drop an empty spreader bar quickly back to the rigging deck between picks. What governs that suggestion?

answers.text: Free-fall may be used freely whenever the hook carries no rated load

Free-fall lowering is used only where the manufacturer permits it, never with personnel, and never as a shortcut when precise control is needed, because a falling hook or bar can accelerate beyond what the brake can smoothly arrest
Free-fall is the preferred method for any empty hook travel
The signal person may authorize free-fall use verbally for one cycle

questions.explanation: Free-fall trades control for speed: the drum pays out under gravity and the brake alone must catch the mass, which can overheat, grab, or overshoot. Manufacturers restrict where the feature may be used at all, personnel are never lowered by free-fall, and no verbal authorization expands those limits. An empty bar still carries injurious mass and momentum.

questions.question: A mechanic must pull a boom foot pin to replace a bushing, and the boom section involved will be supported for the job. What support principle governs that work from start to finish?

answers.text: The boom hoist brake alone is trusted to hold the section while the pin is out
Hydraulic pressure in the lift cylinder is a complete and sufficient support during pin work
A second worker holds the section steady by hand while the pin is driven out

The section is landed on sound blocking or a proper stand that carries its weight without any hydraulic help, because a pin can only move freely, and a section can only stay put, when no load is hanging on valves, seals or brakes

questions.explanation: Maintenance removes the very parts that hold loads, so the weight must first be given a dumb, solid path to the ground. Blocking and stands do not leak, drift or get bumped by a control lever. Any pin pulled against a suspended load binds, then releases violently when it finally moves.

questions.question: For a fictional 92-ton lattice crane with an erected 33-foot jib offset at 15 degrees, the notes state jib radius is measured to the jib tip sheave and the offset table already reflects that geometry. A planner instead enters the offset table with the main-boom radius, which is 14 feet shorter. What error results?

answers.text: The planner reads a conservative capacity and merely loses margin
No error, because jib and boom radius are interchangeable entries
The planner reads a capacity for a much smaller radius than the jib load occupies, overstating the jib rating
The planner understates the radius and therefore understates capacity

questions.explanation: Offset jib geometry places the load well beyond the main-boom radius, and the table is keyed to the jib radius the notes define. Entering with a radius 14 feet short lands on a stronger column than the load's position earns, which is the unsafe direction: the pick would be planned against capacity belonging to a load hanging much closer to the crane.

questions.question: Steel trucks queueing for a downtown project regularly spill back and block the driveway of the bakery next door, whose owner has begun complaining to the city. What should the project's traffic plan change?

answers.text: Move the queue into a managed holding pattern that keeps neighboring driveways clear, with arrivals scheduled so trucks never stack onto the bakery's access
Give truck drivers the bakery owner's number to apologize directly
Accept the blockage as an unavoidable cost of downtown construction
Ask the bakery to schedule its own deliveries around the project queue

questions.explanation: A queue is part of the site's footprint whether the plan admits it or not. Scheduling arrivals and holding trucks properly keeps the project's traffic on the project's space; exporting the queue onto a neighbor's driveway exports the conflict, the complaints, and eventually enforcement attention with it.

questions.question: A crane works a dusty plant job for a single long shift. Midway, the foreman asks whether any inspection thinking applies between morning and night checks. What is correct?

answers.text: Once the morning check is signed, nothing found later can require action until tomorrow
Mid-shift defects are the next operator's problem by custom in crane work
Only scheduled monthly crews may declare a defect found during working hours
Operators stay alert to new leaks, noises, damage and ground changes during the shift and stop to evaluate anything that develops

questions.explanation: Inspection is not a single morning ritual. Loads, weather, ground and the machine itself change during work, and a defect that appears at midday has the same consequence as one found at dawn, so it is acted on when it appears.

questions.question: For a fictional 92-ton crawler crane working from mats, the extended-track table rates the set at 18,200 pounds, the retracted-track table rates it at 12,700 pounds, and the suspended total is 13,400 pounds. The tracks are extended but one side sits on a mat stack noticeably lower than the other, leaving the upper visibly tilted. What must happen before the set?

answers.text: The tilt must be corrected first, because every track table presumes a level machine and no table rates a tilted stance
Use the extended table, because extension was achieved and tilt is a separate comfort issue
Use the retracted table as the automatic rating for a tilted extended stance
Proceed, because crawler tracks forgive tilt that outriggers would not

questions.explanation: Level is a condition written into every capacity the book prints: a visibly tilted upper shifts the load outward and consumes stability margin that neither the 18,200-pound extended value nor the 12,700-pound retracted value accounts for. There is no tilted-stance table to fall back on for any carrier type, so the mats are rebuilt and the machine leveled before the 13,400-pound total is lifted.

questions.question: A delivery driver waiting near the landing zone sees a sling leg slip as a crate is being lowered and throws both hands up in a stop gesture, shouting at the same time. The designated signal person has not reacted yet. What must the operator do?

answers.text: Keep lowering, since only the designated signal person may direct the crane
Lower faster to get the crate past the slipping leg's danger height
Wait for the designated signal person to confirm before changing anything
Stop the motion at once, because a stop signal is obeyed no matter who gives it, and sort out the rigging problem before any movement resumes

questions.explanation: Stop is the universal exception to the one-signal-person rule: anyone who sees an immediate hazard can halt a lift, and the operator obeys first and investigates second. The driver's alarm here is about a failing sling during a descent, where extra seconds of lowering could drop the crate. Resuming requires the actual problem to be fixed, not merely a confirmation ritual.

questions.question: On a fictional 175-ton crawler crane, the extended-track table rates a pick at 16,800 pounds and the retracted-track table rates it at 11,900 pounds. The crew extends the tracks fully and confirms the stance before lifting a 15,600-pound total. A trainee insists the retracted table must be used for safety. What is correct?

answers.text: The trainee is right, because the lowest table in the book is always the legal rating
Both tables must be satisfied simultaneously, so the effective rating is 11,900 pounds
The extended-track table governs because the stance was actually extended and verified, and its 16,800 pounds covers the total
The tables should be combined into a single working figure of 28,700 pounds

questions.explanation: Deliberately choosing a table for a stance the crane is not in is still using the wrong table: the verified extended stance owns the 16,800-pound rating. Conservatism means honoring margins and conditions, not misdescribing the machine; requiring both tables at once and adding tables together are both methods no chart recognizes.

questions.question: Maneuvering a glass curtain-wall unit toward a facade, the operator must watch two moving clearances at once: the unit near the building face and the counterweight sweeping an interior courtyard behind. How is this dual-clearance move properly staffed?

answers.text: The operator watches the load and guesses the tail clearance from swing count
One spotter watches the facade while the load's own signal person directs, with the tail-swing zone barricaded and its clearance positively confirmed before the swing begins
A worker stands in the courtyard holding a radio to shout if the tail gets close
The swing is made quickly so both clearances are exposed only briefly

questions.explanation: A crane has two strike zones moving in opposite directions, and the operator can see only one of them; the tail zone is therefore excluded by barricade and verified clear, while a spotter guards the facade gap the signal person cannot judge alone. Guessing tail clearance, posting a person inside the sweep, or hurrying both exposures turn two manageable checks into one blind maneuver.

questions.question: A bridle's two legs meet the hook at 60 degrees from horizontal on a 10,000 pound load, and the crew's angle factor for that angle is 1.15 applied to each leg's vertical share. What is each leg's tension?

answers.text: 5,000 pounds
10,000 pounds
4,350 pounds
5,750 pounds

questions.explanation: Start with the vertical share: half of 10,000 is 5,000 pounds per leg. Steep 60 degree legs add only a modest multiplier. Math: 10000 / 2 x 1.15 = 5750. Comparing this with a flat 30 degree lift shows how much headroom, and leg length, buys safety.

questions.question: A mobile crane will work from a barge-adjacent dock where the chart requires outriggers fully extended, but space forces one beam to stay partly in. What must the operator do?

answers.text: Use the full-extension chart and keep loads a little lighter by feel
Average the full and retracted chart values for a fair number
