Selective highlighting distorts that balance by steering attention to selling points and away from risks, even when no words are actually changed. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for handling of prospectus copies.

questions.question: During an account review meeting, the representative is addressing dividend income taxation concept. Which condition is a problem that must be corrected?

answers.text: The representative follows the established practice covering tax-exempt municipal interest concept
A representative tells a customer that dividends they reinvested will not be taxed because the customer never received any cash.
The representative follows the established practice covering cost basis concept for investments
The representative follows the established practice covering dividend income taxation concept

questions.explanation: A dividend is income when it is paid, and the tax result does not depend on what the investor does with it next. Taking cash and reinvesting both leave the investor with taxable dividend income for that year. Reinvestment does add to the investor's cost basis over time, which is a separate point from the tax owed on the dividend itself. The problem condition is the one that breaches the practice for dividend income taxation concept; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: During an account-opening interview, the representative is addressing income and liquidity needs in the profile. Which practice should the representative accept as correct?

answers.text: A customer's income is irrelevant to the profile if their net worth is above average.
Liquidity needs matter only for customers who state that they plan to withdraw funds within the first month.
The firm should assume every customer can leave invested funds untouched indefinitely unless the customer objects in writing.

The profile should capture the customer's income and liquidity needs, including how soon they may need money back and for what, because a recommendation must not lock up funds the customer will shortly require.

questions.explanation: Money earmarked for a near-term obligation has to stay accessible and stable, while money not needed for years can accept more fluctuation. Learning the customer's income and when they will need cash back prevents the classic mismatch of trapping short-term funds in long-term or penalized products. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to income and liquidity needs in the profile.

questions.question: During a customer outreach campaign, a problem involving resale limits on private placement securities must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: Securities bought in a private placement are restricted, meaning they cannot be freely resold to the public and are generally held with limited liquidity.
Securities bought in a private placement may be resold to the public the day after purchase.
The resale restriction on private placement securities applies only to the original issuer, not to buyers.
Restricted securities become freely tradable as soon as the buyer has held them for a few weeks.

questions.explanation: The restricted status travels with the securities, limiting resale and making the investment hard to exit quickly. Promising easy resale misleads the buyer about one of the most important practical features of a private placement and can leave them holding an investment they cannot sell. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for resale limits on private placement securities.

questions.question: While resolving a transaction question, the representative is addressing routing orders for execution quality not firm compensation. Which condition is a problem that must be corrected?

answers.text: The representative follows the established practice covering duty of best execution when handling orders
The representative follows the established practice covering handling orders promptly without holding them for firm advantage
The representative follows the established practice covering routing orders for execution quality not firm compensation
A firm changes its routing to a venue that pays more while providing customers noticeably worse executions, and documents compensation as the reason.

questions.explanation: Routing determines the prices and fills customers actually receive, so it cannot be treated as a private revenue decision. When compensation drives routing, the firm profits from a choice paid for by its customers' poorer results, which is the conflict best execution forbids. The problem condition is the one that breaches the practice for routing orders for execution quality not firm compensation; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: During a prospect meeting, a problem involving balanced discussion of risks alongside benefits must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: A communication satisfies the balance requirement by stating once that all investments involve risk, with no product-specific discussion.
Risks need to be mentioned only when a customer asks about them directly during a conversation.
Benefits may be presented alone in an advertisement if the prospectus, delivered later, discusses the risks.
When a communication discusses the benefits of a product, it must also give a balanced discussion of the associated risks rather than presenting benefits in isolation.

questions.explanation: A generic warning that investing involves risk does not explain the particular risks of the product being promoted. Balance has to occur within the communication itself, where the benefits are being used to attract the reader. Deferring all risk discussion to a later document leaves the promotional message itself one-sided and misleading. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for balanced discussion of risks alongside benefits.

questions.question: During an account review meeting, a problem involving changing the beneficiary on a 529 account must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: The account owner may change the beneficiary of a 529 account to another eligible family member of the original beneficiary without treating the change as a taxable withdrawal.
Only the beneficiary, and never the account owner, may request a change of beneficiary on a 529 account.
Changing a 529 beneficiary to a sibling always requires closing the account and paying tax on all earnings.
A 529 account beneficiary can never be changed once the account is opened.

questions.explanation: Flexibility on beneficiaries protects families when one child needs less help than expected. The owner can redirect the account to another eligible family member, such as a sibling, and continue the education purpose without the change itself being treated as a distribution. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for changing the beneficiary on a 529 account.

questions.question: During a recommendation review, the representative is addressing interest-rate risk in strategy choice. Which practice should the representative accept as correct?

answers.text: Bond prices are unaffected by changes in market interest rates once the bonds are issued.
When market rates rise, existing bonds with lower coupons become more valuable to buyers.

Interest-rate risk is the tendency of existing bond prices to fall when market rates rise and to rise when market rates fall, with longer maturities generally more sensitive, and it shapes how much bond exposure of what maturity a strategy should hold.
Short-term bonds are more sensitive to rate changes than long-term bonds.

questions.explanation: A bond paying a fixed coupon competes with new bonds issued at current rates; when new rates are higher, the older bond must fall in price to attract a buyer. The longer the wait for repayment, the bigger that price adjustment, which is why maturity choice is a deliberate part of bond strategy rather than an afterthought. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to interest-rate risk in strategy choice.

questions.question: During a recommendation review, a problem involving local government investment pool characteristics must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: A local government investment pool invests public cash primarily in long-term speculative equities for maximum growth.
A local government investment pool guarantees participants a fixed profit regardless of the pool's investment results.
Local government investment pools are individual brokerage accounts owned by retail investors for retirement saving.

A local government investment pool is a municipal fund security that pools cash from participating public entities and invests it in short-term, high-quality instruments to provide liquidity and preserve principal.

questions.explanation: These pools exist to manage public cash, not to chase growth. Participating governments need ready access to funds and protection of principal, so the pool concentrates on short-term quality holdings, and describing it as a speculative growth vehicle reverses its purpose and risk profile. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for local government investment pool characteristics.

questions.question: While explaining a fund to a customer, the representative is addressing separate account concept for variable products. Which condition is a problem that must be corrected?

answers.text: A representative tells a customer that variable contract assets sit in the insurer's general account alongside its other business funds.
The representative follows the established practice covering separate account concept for variable products
The representative follows the established practice covering variable products are securities requiring a prospectus
The representative follows the established practice covering contract owner bears investment risk

questions.explanation: The separate account is the structural heart of variable products: premiums directed to it are invested apart from the insurer's general business and are not used to satisfy the insurer's unrelated debts. That separation is also why contract values move with the underlying investments instead of being fixed by the insurer. The problem condition is the one that breaches the practice for separate account concept for variable products; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: Regarding asset allocation matched to the profile, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Asset allocation is concerned only with which individual securities a fund manager buys inside one fund.
Asset allocation means choosing the single best-performing fund each year and placing the entire portfolio in it.
Asset allocation divides a portfolio among asset classes such as stock funds, bond funds, and cash equivalents in proportions matched to the customer's objectives, horizon, and risk tolerance.
Every customer should receive the same standard allocation regardless of their profile.

questions.explanation: Allocation is the top-level decision about how much of the portfolio rides on growth assets versus steadier ones, and that balance drives most of the portfolio's behavior. Matching the mix to the customer's profile aligns the expected fluctuation with what the customer can accept and the goal actually requires. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the practice for asset allocation matched to the profile: asset allocation divides a portfolio among asset classes such as stock funds, bond funds, and cash equivalents in proportions matched to the customer's objectives, horizon, and risk tolerance.

questions.question: Regarding money market fund characteristics, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Money market funds invest in short-term, high-quality debt instruments and seek to maintain a stable share value, while offering no guarantee against loss.
Money market funds invest mainly in long-term bonds to seek the highest possible yield.
Money market funds are insured by the federal government against any loss of principal.
Money market funds hold volatile growth stocks to keep their share value stable.

questions.explanation: Money market funds limit themselves to short-maturity, high-quality debt so price swings stay small and a stable value can be pursued. That conservative design lowers risk but does not eliminate it, and no government insurance stands behind the shares an investor buys. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the practice for money market fund characteristics: money market funds invest in short-term, high-quality debt instruments and seek to maintain a stable share value, while offering no guarantee against loss.

questions.question: While discussing investments with a customer, the representative is addressing capital gains holding period distinction. Which practice should the representative accept as correct?

answers.text: A gain on an asset held for one year or less is generally treated as short-term, while a gain on an asset held for more than one year is generally treated as long-term, and the two are taxed differently.
Short-term and long-term gains are always taxed in exactly the same way at the same rates.
A gain is long-term whenever the asset was held for any period at all, even a single day.
The holding period of an asset has no effect at all on how a gain on its sale is taxed.

questions.explanation: Tax treatment of a gain turns in part on how long the investor held the asset. Short holding periods produce short-term gains, while holding beyond the one-year mark produces long-term gains, which generally receive more favorable treatment. That distinction gives investors a concrete tax reason to pay attention to timing when they sell. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to capital gains holding period distinction.

questions.question: While discussing investments with a customer, a problem involving disclosing material facts before a purchase must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: Material facts may be omitted if the representative believes the customer would not understand them.
A representative may disclose material facts after the purchase as long as they are disclosed eventually.
A representative must disclose all material facts about a recommended product before the customer decides to purchase, including facts that could influence a reasonable investor's decision.
Only favorable material facts need to be disclosed before a purchase.

questions.explanation: Timing matters because disclosure is meant to inform the decision itself. Facts that a reasonable investor would consider important must be available before the customer commits, since learning them afterward leaves the customer with a decision made without the full picture. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for disclosing material facts before a purchase.

questions.question: While processing a customer order, the representative is addressing reporting trade errors through the firm error process. Which practice should the representative accept as correct?

answers.text: When a trade error occurs, the representative must report it promptly through the firm's error process so a principal can decide how it is corrected.
A representative should correct trade errors quietly on their own without informing the firm.
Small trade errors may simply be ignored because reporting them creates paperwork.
Trade errors need to be reported only if the customer notices them first.

questions.explanation: Errors are corrected fairly only when the firm can see them and apply a consistent process. Prompt reporting lets a principal determine the proper correction and who bears any cost, while a quiet personal fix hides the event from supervision and from the firm's records. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to reporting trade errors through the firm error process.

questions.question: During a customer outreach campaign, the representative is addressing exchange and replacement communications for variable contracts. Which practice should the representative accept as correct?

answers.text: Lost benefits under the existing contract are immaterial once the customer has shown interest in exchanging.
A communication may describe an exchange as costing the customer nothing whenever no check is written at the time.
An exchange communication may list only the new contract's features, since surrender charges belong to the contract being left.

Communications encouraging a customer to exchange or replace an existing variable contract must present the costs and consequences of the exchange, such as new surrender charges and lost benefits, alongside any advantages of the new contract.

questions.explanation: An exchange restarts surrender schedules and can surrender guarantees the customer already owns, so those consequences are central facts, not details of the old contract alone. A pitch that shows only the new contract's attractions hides the price of switching. Absence of an immediate payment does not make an exchange costless when charges and lost benefits follow from it. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to exchange and replacement communications for variable contracts.

questions.question: A contract owner withdraws $15,000 that is subject to a surrender charge of 5 percent. Using surrender charge dollars equals the chargeable withdrawal times the surrender charge percentage, how much surrender charge applies?
questions.explanation: The surrender charge is $15,000 x 5% = $750. The representative verifies this computed figure against the customer records.

soa-exam-p-probability.quiz_title: SOA Exam P (Probability) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Parker Novak must identify the correct statement about independent versus mutually exclusive events. A fellow candidate has asked for the precise statement. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together, so if both have positive probability they are necessarily dependent: learning that one occurred drives the other's probability to zero.

If two events with positive probability are mutually exclusive, learning that one occurred leaves the other's probability unchanged, which is the definition of independence as the idea is used when probability is applied to insurance risk problems

Mutually exclusive events are always independent as well, because events that never overlap cannot influence each other's probabilities in any way as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

Mutually exclusive and independent are two names for the same property, and textbooks use them interchangeably when the events come from one experiment as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

questions.explanation: Disjoint with positive probabilities implies dependence: P(B|A) = 0, which differs from P(B).

questions.question: Umar Farouk, an Exam P candidate in a study group, double-checks the standard statement for the definition of conditional probability. The candidate is building a one-line summary for a flashcard. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The conditional probability of A given B equals the probability of A whenever B is known to have occurred at least once in a long series of past experiments as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

The conditional probability of A given B is the probability of their intersection divided by the probability of B, provided B has positive probability; conditioning means restricting the sample space to the outcomes where B occurred.

The conditional probability of A given B is the probability of B divided by the probability of their intersection, which is why conditional probabilities can exceed one in the standard treatment of this topic in actuarial probability

The conditional probability of A given B is the probability of their union divided by the probability of B, provided the union is computed over the full sample space in the sense the term carries throughout the probability syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

questions.explanation: P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B). Conditioning rescales probabilities to the reduced sample space B.

questions.question: A probability exercise for an Exam P candidate states the following. A random variable X has a binomial distribution with n = 39 and p = 0.5. What is the mean of X?
questions.explanation: Binomial mean = np = 19.50.

questions.question: Val Osei must identify the correct statement about order statistics and the minimum. The concept connects directly to actuarial risk problems. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: The minimum of independent variables exceeds x whenever the average of the variables exceeds x, so its probability is computed from the distribution of the sample mean instead in the sense the term carries throughout the probability syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

For independent identically distributed variables, the probability that the minimum exceeds x equals the probability that a single variable exceeds x, raised to the number of variables, because every variable must clear x for the smallest to clear it.

The probability that the minimum exceeds x equals the probability that a single variable is at most x raised to the number of variables, mirroring the maximum's formula exactly in the sense the term carries throughout the probability syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

The probability that the minimum exceeds x equals the probability that a single variable exceeds x divided by the number of variables, sharing the exceedance among them as a complete statement of the concept, with no qualifying condition omitted or added

questions.explanation: P(min > x) = (1 - F(x))^n for iid variables. Min and max have mirror-image formulas.

questions.question: Nadia Petrov must identify the correct statement about using independence to simplify conditional distributions. The question comes from the candidate's concept review notes. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: When two variables are independent, the conditional distribution of each given the other equals its marginal distribution: knowing the other's value provides no information, so the slice distribution is the same for every slice.

When two variables are independent, the conditional probabilities are all zero except on the diagonal of the joint table, where the two variables take matching values in the ordinary usage of the term among candidates preparing for this examination

Independence changes the marginal distributions when conditioning is applied, because the conditioning variable's values reweight the other's marginal probabilities as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

When two variables are independent, the conditional distribution of Y given X is concentrated at the mean of Y, because independence removes all variation linked to X in the standard treatment of this topic in actuarial probability

questions.explanation: Independence  every conditional equals the marginal. Any slice that differs from the marginal proves dependence.

questions.question: A practice reviewer asks Farah Haddad, a trainee actuary refreshing core probability, about the general addition rule. The discussion takes place during a weekly study session. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: For any two events, the probability of their union equals the sum of their probabilities in all cases; subtracting an intersection applies only to independent events in the sense the term carries throughout the probability syllabus
For any two events, the probability of their union equals the sum of their probabilities minus the probability of their intersection, because the overlap is counted twice in the sum.

For any two events, the probability of their union equals the larger of the two probabilities whenever one event is contained in the other experiment's outcome list as the statement would be understood in a first course in probability for actuaries

For any two events, the probability of their union equals the sum of their probabilities plus the probability of their intersection, because the overlap deserves extra weight as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

questions.explanation: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). The subtraction is needed only when the intersection is non-empty.

questions.question: A practice reviewer asks Owen Gallagher, a candidate reviewing probability fundamentals, about counting with the multiplication principle. The question is part of a self-test on fundamentals. Which of the following is the correct statement?

answers.text: The multiplication principle requires the stages to be performed in a specific chronological order, and reversing the stages always changes the total number of outcomes as the idea is used when probability is applied to insurance risk problems

The multiplication principle applies only when every stage has exactly the same number of options; otherwise the counts must be averaged before combining them as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

The multiplication principle states that if a task is done in stages with a fixed number of options at each stage, the total number of outcomes is the product of the stage counts, provided each stage's count does not depend on earlier choices.

The multiplication principle states that the total number of outcomes is the sum of the stage counts, because each stage contributes its options independently to a combined list as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

questions.explanation: Multiply stage counts when the number of options at each stage is constant regardless of earlier choices.

questions.question: Stefan Braun, a candidate working through a practice set, is asked about the cumulative distribution function. The review covers material from the current syllabus. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: For a continuous random variable, the probability that X lies between a and b equals F(b) minus F(a) plus the density at b, since the endpoint itself carries probability under the usual definitions adopted in introductory actuarial probability in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam P purposes

The cumulative distribution function gives the probability that the random variable is greater than x, so interval probabilities are computed by subtracting it from itself at the endpoints under the conventions normally used when this concept is introduced

The cumulative distribution function can decrease over intervals where the density is small, because accumulation slows whenever the density falls below its average level as the statement would be understood in a first course in probability for actuaries

The cumulative distribution function F(x) gives the probability that the random variable is less than or equal to x; it is non-decreasing, starts at zero, approaches one, and the probability of an interval is the difference of its endpoint values.

questions.explanation: P(a < X <= b) = F(b) - F(a). F is non-decreasing with limits 0 and 1.

questions.question: A probability exercise for an Exam P candidate states the following. A waiting time X has an exponential distribution with rate 1.0 per hour. What is the probability that the waiting time is less than 0.5 hours?

A risk modeller sets up the following calculation. A policy has a deductible of 500. The loss distribution is: loss 0 with probability 0.307, loss 500 with probability 0.308, loss 2000 with probability 0.231, loss 8000 with probability 0.154. What is the variance of the insurer's payment per loss?
questions.explanation: Payments are 0, 0, 1500, 7500; E[payment] = 1501.50; Var = E[payment^2] - (E[payment])^2 = 6927747.75.

questions.question: Nadia Petrov, a candidate working through a practice set, double-checks the standard statement for when a joint distribution factors into marginals. The review covers material from the current syllabus. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Two random variables are independent when their joint table has no zero entries, because zeros are what create the dependence between the variables' outcomes as the idea is used when probability is applied to insurance risk problems
Two random variables are independent exactly when their joint probabilities sum to the product of their marginal totals, a condition checked only on the table's overall sum.

Independence holds whenever the marginal distributions are identical, since variables with the same marginal behaviour cannot influence each other's values as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example
Two random variables are independent exactly when their joint probability function equals the product of their marginal probability functions at every combination of values.

questions.explanation: Independence  p(x,y) = pX(x) pY(y) for ALL (x,y). One failing cell is enough to establish dependence.

questions.question: Yusuf Rahman, a candidate working through a practice set, is asked about covariance of a variable with itself and scaling rules. The concept is being reviewed before a timed practice exam. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: Covariance is antisymmetric: swapping the two variables reverses the sign of the covariance, which is why the order of the arguments must be recorded carefully as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

Scaling a variable by a constant leaves its covariance with another variable unchanged, because covariance is a standardised measure like the correlation coefficient as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

The covariance of a variable with itself is one, by the same normalisation that makes a variable's correlation with itself equal to one in all cases in the sense the term carries throughout the probability syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

The covariance of a variable with itself is its variance, covariance is symmetric in its two arguments, and scaling either variable scales the covariance by the same factor, with signs following the scaling constants.

questions.explanation: Cov(X,X) = Var(X); Cov(aX, bY) = ab Cov(X,Y); Cov(X+a, Y+b) = Cov(X,Y) — shifts do not matter.

questions.question: A risk modeller sets up the following calculation. A portfolio draws 40% of its policies from Region 1 and the rest from Region 2. The claim rate is 0.05 in Region 1 and 0.1 in Region 2. Given that a randomly selected policy has a claim, what is the probability it comes from Region 1? The discussion follows a review of claim-count and claim-size examples.

An analyst at an insurer works with the following model. Events occur as a Poisson process with mean 3.0 per period. The candidate's study plan reserves the final review week for mixed problem sets. What is the probability that exactly 5 events occur in one period?

Elif Yilmaz, a student in a probability course for actuaries, double-checks the standard statement for the coefficient of variation. A fellow candidate has asked for the precise statement. Which of the following is the correct statement?

answers.text: The coefficient of variation carries the units of the original variable, which is why it is mainly used to compare variables that share the same measurement scale in the way the idea is presented in standard probability references for actuaries

The coefficient of variation is the mean divided by the standard deviation, expressing how many standard deviations fit inside one unit of the variable's average level in the standard treatment of this topic in actuarial probability
The coefficient of variation is the standard deviation divided by the mean, a unit-free measure of relative spread used to compare variability between variables measured on different scales.

The coefficient of variation is the variance divided by the mean squared plus one, a unit-free measure defined so it always lies between zero and one for positive variables in the standard treatment of this topic in actuarial probability

questions.explanation: CV = sigma/mu (for mu > 0). It is dimensionless, unlike variance and standard deviation.

questions.question: An actuary reviewing a block of policies models the following. Claim counts for each of 100 similar policies are independent with a Poisson distribution with mean 4. The total count S has mean 400 and standard deviation 20.00. Use the central limit theorem and the given value Phi(1.5) = 0.9332 to approximate P(S is at most 430).
questions.explanation: z = (430 - 400)/20.00 is approximately 1.5; P(S <= 430) is approximately Phi(1.5) = 0.9332.

questions.question: Sage Kowalski, an actuarial student preparing for Exam P in Portland, is consulted on variance of a conditional distribution. The candidate is checking a statement found in study notes. Which of the following is the correct statement?

answers.text: The variance of Y given X = x always equals the unconditional variance of Y, because conditioning rescales probabilities without altering the spread around the mean as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

The variance within a slice — the variance of Y under its conditional distribution given X = x — measures the spread of Y among outcomes sharing that value of X, and it generally differs from slice to slice.

Conditional variances are defined only for the slice with the largest marginal probability, since smaller slices lack the mass needed for a variance calculation in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam P purposes

The variance of Y given X = x is the conditional expectation of Y squared minus the joint probability of the slice, following the pattern of the product rule as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

questions.explanation: Var(Y|X=x) uses the conditional distribution exactly like an ordinary variance, inside that slice.

questions.question: While preparing for Exam P, Mateo Rossi — a candidate preparing for the Probability Exam — reviews the axioms of probability. The study group is checking the standard statement of the concept. The discussion follows a review of claim-count and claim-size examples. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Probability is a set function on events satisfying three axioms: probabilities are non-negative, the probability of the whole sample space is 1, and the probability of a countable union of mutually exclusive events equals the sum of their probabilities.

Probability requires that every individual outcome have strictly positive probability, so an event with probability zero can never be part of the sample space under the usual definitions adopted in introductory actuarial probability in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam P purposes

Probability is defined so that the probability of a union of any two events always equals the sum of their probabilities, whether or not the events overlap under the usual definitions adopted in introductory actuarial probability in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam P purposes

Probability is a set function satisfying two axioms only: probabilities lie between 0 and 1, and equally likely outcomes always receive equal probability by definition in the sense the term carries throughout the probability syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

questions.explanation: The third axiom (countable additivity) is stated only for mutually exclusive events; overlapping events need the addition rule correction.

questions.question: An actuary reviewing a block of policies models the following. A loss of 12000 occurs under a policy with a deductible of 1000 and a coinsurance rate of 80% payable by the insurer on the amount above the deductible. A fellow candidate has mixed this idea up with a neighbouring one, so precision matters here. What does the insurer pay on this loss?

A candidate practising for the Probability Exam considers the following. Independent random variables X and Y are normal with means 10 and 25 and standard deviations 3 and 6, respectively. The sum S = X + Y is normal with mean 35 and standard deviation 6.71. Use the given standard normal value Phi(0.5) = 0.6915. What is the approximate probability that S exceeds 38?

cscs.quiz_title: NSCA Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding bone adaptation specificity to load magnitude direction and novelty, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Bone adapts most to static, low-magnitude loading held for very long periods, and high-impact dynamic loading produces no bone benefit.
Once any exercise is performed regularly, continuing the identical routine produces ever-increasing bone gains without any progression.

Bone adapts most to loading that is dynamic, relatively high in magnitude, applied in varied or novel directions, and progresses over time, while routine low-magnitude loading produces little additional adaptation.
Bone adaptation is identical regardless of the direction loads are applied, so novel multidirectional loading offers no stimulus advantage.

questions.explanation: Bone cells desensitize to routine strain signals, so the stimulus must be sufficiently large, dynamic, and somewhat unfamiliar to keep driving formation. Progressive resistance and impact work in varied directions meet those conditions. Repeating an unchanging light routine falls below the effective stimulus once the tissue has adapted to it. This is the governing practice for bone adaptation specificity to load magnitude direction and novelty.

questions.question: Regarding training monotony and strain in load monitoring, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Strain depends only on total weekly load, so the distribution of load across days has no effect on the athlete.

Monotony describes how unvarying daily training load is across a week, and strain combines that monotony with total load, so a high-load week with little day-to-day variation carries greater strain than the same load spread unevenly.
Monotony is high when hard and easy days alternate strongly, and that pattern produces the greatest training strain.
Keeping every day at the same high load lowers strain because the athlete's body adapts to a predictable rhythm.

questions.explanation: The body tolerates stress better when hard days are balanced by lighter ones that permit recovery, so repeating similar high loads daily removes the variation adaptation depends on. Monotony and strain capture that risk by combining how much training is done with how evenly it is piled up, explaining why two weeks with equal totals can affect athletes very differently. This is the governing practice for training monotony and strain in load monitoring.

questions.question: Regarding kettlebell swing as a hip hinge not a squat, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The kettlebell swing is performed by squatting down deeply and lifting the bell with the shoulders to above the head.
In a correct swing the athlete pulls the bell upward primarily with the arms and front of the shoulders on every repetition.

The kettlebell swing is a powerful hip hinge in which the hips snap forward to drive the bell up to about chest height while the arms act mainly as straps, rather than the movement being a squat or a front raise.
The kettlebell swing should be done with a rounded back and loose hips so the bell can swing between the legs without effort.

questions.explanation: The swing is a ballistic hinge, and its training value comes from the hips producing force rapidly. When the athlete hinges, loads the hamstrings and glutes, and snaps the hips forward, the bell floats up from hip power and the arms simply connect the bell to the body. Squatting the movement or lifting with the shoulders removes the hip stimulus, slows the motion, and overloads the shoulder, which is why the hinge pattern defines the exercise. This is the governing practice for kettlebell swing as a hip hinge not a squat.

questions.question: During a movement assessment, a problem involving dip and push-up progression and regression options must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: Push-ups and dips are progressed by adding load, slowing the tempo, or increasing the range of motion, and regressed by elevating the hands, reducing the range, or adding assistance, all while the athlete keeps sound body positions.
Progressing dips means letting the shoulders shrug to the ears and dropping as deep as possible regardless of shoulder position or pain.
A beginner who cannot perform a full push-up should simply attempt maximal sets to failure on the floor every day until they succeed.
The only way to progress a push-up is to add weight, and there is no way to make the exercise easier for a beginner.

questions.explanation: Bodyweight exercises are useful across a whole team only when their difficulty can be scaled. Regressions such as elevating the hands let a weaker athlete practice the same sound pattern at a load they can manage, while progressions such as added load or slower tempos keep stronger athletes challenged. Scaling both directions keeps technique as the constant, so strength is built on good positions instead of on repeated failed or sloppy repetitions. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for dip and push-up progression and regression options.

questions.question: Regarding ventilation responses to increasing exercise, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Ventilation stays at resting levels until exercise ends, and then rises briefly to remove carbon dioxide that was stored unchanged in the blood.
Ventilation rises with exercise intensity through increases in breathing rate and tidal volume, tracking the body's need to take in oxygen and remove the carbon dioxide produced by working muscle.
Ventilation increases only by breathing faster, because tidal volume cannot increase above its resting depth during any form of exercise.
Carbon dioxide removal is unrelated to ventilation, since carbon dioxide leaves the body mainly through the skin during exercise.

questions.explanation: Breathing must match metabolic demand: as muscle produces more carbon dioxide, deeper and faster breathing clears it and keeps blood chemistry stable. Ventilation therefore climbs in step with intensity and rises especially steeply at very hard efforts. Coaching an athlete to suppress that response works against the physiology the session depends on. This is the governing practice for ventilation responses to increasing exercise.

questions.question: During a coach-athlete check-in, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing the coach role in rebuilding return-to-play confidence. Which practice should the professional accept as correct?

answers.text: Return-to-play confidence is rebuilt by having the coach clear the athlete for competition based on how confident the athlete appears.

The coach supports return-to-play confidence by setting graded, achievable training challenges within medical clearance, highlighting the athlete's demonstrated progress, and normalizing cautious feelings, while clearance decisions themselves remain with the medical team.
Confidence returns best when the returning athlete's first session replicates the exact maximal demands of competition without progression.
A coach should hide all information about the athlete's progress from them, because knowing progress undermines confidence on return.

questions.explanation: Confidence after injury is rebuilt the same way it is built anywhere: through evidence of capability gathered on tasks that increase in demand step by step. Working inside medical clearance, the coach can engineer those successes, make progress visible, and treat caution as normal rather than weak. Keeping clearance with the medical team protects the athlete, because confidence alone is not evidence that tissue is ready for competition loads. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to the coach role in rebuilding return-to-play confidence.

questions.question: During a technique session in the weight room, a problem involving kettlebell swing as a hip hinge not a squat must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: The kettlebell swing is performed by squatting down deeply and lifting the bell with the shoulders to above the head.
The kettlebell swing should be done with a rounded back and loose hips so the bell can swing between the legs without effort.

The kettlebell swing is a powerful hip hinge in which the hips snap forward to drive the bell up to about chest height while the arms act mainly as straps, rather than the movement being a squat or a front raise.
In a correct swing the athlete pulls the bell upward primarily with the arms and front of the shoulders on every repetition.

questions.explanation: The swing is a ballistic hinge, and its training value comes from the hips producing force rapidly. When the athlete hinges, loads the hamstrings and glutes, and snaps the hips forward, the bell floats up from hip power and the arms simply connect the bell to the body. Squatting the movement or lifting with the shoulders removes the hip stimulus, slows the motion, and overloads the shoulder, which is why the hinge pattern defines the exercise. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for kettlebell swing as a hip hinge not a squat.

questions.question: During a pre-competition meeting with an athlete, a problem involving intrinsic versus extrinsic motivation in athlete training must be addressed. Which practice must the corrected work follow?

answers.text: Intrinsically and extrinsically motivated athletes respond identically, so the source of motivation does not affect coaching choices.
Intrinsic motivation comes only from trophies and selection, while extrinsic motivation comes from enjoying the training itself.
Athletes who are extrinsically motivated have no interest in the activity itself and will always stop training when a reward ends.

Intrinsic motivation comes from interest, enjoyment, and satisfaction in the activity itself, while extrinsic motivation comes from outside outcomes such as rewards, praise, selection, or avoiding punishment.

questions.explanation: Motivation source shapes persistence and effort quality. Athletes who value the activity itself tend to sustain effort when external rewards fade, while rewards and consequences can support short-term compliance. Effective coaching uses outside incentives sparingly and builds genuine interest, competence, and ownership so motivation does not collapse when a prize or threat is removed. Correction is complete only when the corrected work follows the practice for intrinsic versus extrinsic motivation in athlete training.

questions.question: During a program audit, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing sliding filament cross-bridge cycle during contraction. Which condition is a problem that must be corrected?

answers.text: The professional follows the established practice covering sliding filament cross-bridge cycle during contraction
The professional follows the established practice covering pennation angle and fascicle architecture in pennate muscle
A coach explains to an athlete that their filaments shrink during each repetition and that ATP plays no role in detaching cross-bridges between strokes.
The professional follows the established practice covering combined proprioceptive feedback from spindles and golgi tendon organs

questions.explanation: The sliding filament model holds that filament length stays constant while overlap increases. Cross-bridge cycling requires ATP both for the cocking of the myosin head and for detachment from actin, which is why fatigued muscle with low ATP availability cannot sustain repeated forceful contractions or relax fully. The problem condition is the one that breaches the practice for sliding filament cross-bridge cycle during contraction; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: During a program-planning meeting, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing assigning training load from repetition maximum testing. Which condition is a problem that must be corrected?

answers.text: A coach assigns all working loads from a guess made on the first day and never tests or updates them, so half the team is underloaded and the other half cannot complete their sets.
The professional follows the established practice covering relative intensity for novice versus advanced athletes
The professional follows the established practice covering assigning training load from repetition maximum testing
The professional follows the established practice covering cluster sets with intra-set rest for power output

questions.explanation: Testing anchors prescription to what the athlete can actually do on that exercise. A measured or estimated maximum lets the coach compute loads that match the intended repetitions and intensity, and retesting updates those loads as ability changes. Without that anchor, loading is guesswork that systematically misses the target for many athletes. The problem condition is the one that breaches the practice for assigning training load from repetition maximum testing; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: While adjusting an athlete's program, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing evaluating sport injury profile in needs analysis. Which condition is a problem that must be corrected?

answers.text: A coach builds a program with no review of the sport common injury sites or the athlete history of repeated strains, and loads the previously injured area aggressively from the first week.
The professional follows the established practice covering evaluating sport injury profile in needs analysis
The professional follows the established practice covering training age and training status in needs analysis
The professional follows the established practice covering athlete profiling and testing battery selection in needs analysis

questions.explanation: Knowing where and how injuries typically occur in the sport, and what the individual athlete has already sustained, allows sensible exercise selection, preparatory strengthening, and load progression. It does not turn the coach into a clinician; diagnosis and rehabilitation remain referral matters. Ignoring the profile risks re-injury and misses a legitimate performance benefit of durable, available athletes. The problem condition is the one that breaches the practice for evaluating sport injury profile in needs analysis; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: During a preseason testing review, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing evidence basics for common recovery modalities. Which practice should the professional accept as correct?

answers.text: Cold-water immersion after every lifting session improves long-term strength and muscle growth, and it should replace sleep and nutrition as the main recovery strategy.
All recovery modalities produce identical effects, so the choice among them never matters for either soreness or long-term adaptation.

Recovery methods differ in their evidence and trade-offs: sleep, nutrition, and planned rest are the foundation, while methods such as cold-water immersion can reduce soreness yet may blunt strength and hypertrophy adaptations when used routinely right after lifting.
Compression garments, massage, and cold exposure can fully compensate for chronic sleep loss, making total recovery equal regardless of rest.

questions.explanation: Recovery is hierarchical: the basics of sleep, energy, protein, and sensible load management deliver most of the benefit, and add-on modalities offer smaller, mixed effects. Cold exposure illustrates the trade-off, easing soreness while potentially dampening the very signals that drive muscle adaptation. A coach who orders priorities correctly spends effort on the foundation first and uses modalities deliberately. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to evidence basics for common recovery modalities.

questions.question: While giving general nutrition guidance to an athlete, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing documenting and communicating nutrition concerns for referral. Which condition is a problem that must be corrected?

answers.text: A strength and conditioning professional notices repeated signs of underfueling, labels the athlete with a diagnosis in the training file, and takes no step to communicate or refer the concern.
The professional follows the established practice covering documenting and communicating nutrition concerns for referral
The professional follows the established practice covering referral to a registered dietitian for individualized nutrition needs
The professional follows the established practice covering general nutrition education within cscs scope

questions.explanation: Objective documentation records what was observed, such as missed meals, fatigue, or declining performance, without assigning a diagnosis the coach is not qualified to make. Sharing that record through proper channels lets medical and nutrition professionals evaluate promptly, while private speculation or informal comments can delay care and create inaccurate records that mislead the team. The problem condition is the one that breaches the practice for documenting and communicating nutrition concerns for referral; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: While evaluating an athlete's training response, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing glycogen depletion during prolonged work and repletion afterward. Which practice should the professional accept as correct?

answers.text: Muscle glycogen stores cannot be depleted by exercise, so prolonged work never reduces an athlete's capacity through fuel availability.
Only fat stores are used during prolonged exercise, and glycogen depletion is unrelated to the fatigue athletes feel late in long events.

Prolonged or repeated high-intensity exercise depletes muscle glycogen, reducing the capacity for further hard work, and glycogen is restored afterward through carbohydrate intake over the following hours.
Glycogen is restored instantly when exercise stops, with no need for carbohydrate intake in the hours after a depleting session.

questions.explanation: Glycogen is the muscle's local high-speed fuel store, and it is finite. As it empties, the athlete loses access to the fast glycolytic supply that hard efforts require, which is felt as a sharp drop in sustainable pace or power. Repletion needs dietary carbohydrate and time, a practical reason fueling between sessions shapes the next session's quality. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to glycogen depletion during prolonged work and repletion afterward.

questions.question: An athlete's standing reach is 240 centimeters and their highest jump reach is 330 centimeters. Using vertical jump height equals jump reach minus standing reach, what is the vertical jump height?

answers.text: 100 cm
330 cm
82 cm
90 cm

questions.explanation: Vertical jump height is 330 - 240 = 90 cm. The professional verifies this computed figure against the athlete's records.

questions.question: While running a team training session, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing gps and accelerometer data use and limitations. Which practice should the professional accept as correct?

answers.text: Accelerometer counts measure the internal physiological cost of a session directly, including heart and metabolic strain.
GPS data give a complete picture of training stress, making perceived exertion and wellness monitoring unnecessary for field athletes.

GPS and accelerometer data quantify external training load such as distance, speed, accelerations, and impacts, but they do not directly capture internal responses, technical quality, or strength-training stress, so they are interpreted alongside other monitoring information.
A drop in GPS running distance proves an athlete is fatigued, with no need to consider position, tactics, or drill design.

questions.explanation: Wearable sensors are excellent at recording what the body did externally, from total distance to high-speed efforts and collisions, but a session can impose large internal or muscular stress while producing modest movement data, as heavy lifting shows. Reading sensor output beside exertion, wellness, and performance measures prevents one convenient number from standing in for the whole training load. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to gps and accelerometer data use and limitations.

questions.question: While writing the next training block, the strength and conditioning professional is addressing training frequency by training status and split routine. Which practice should the professional accept as correct?

answers.text: Training frequency should be as high as physically possible for every athlete, regardless of soreness, performance, or recovery between sessions.
A split routine means training the same muscles in every session while calling the days by different names.

Training frequency is set by training status and recovery, with novices often training the whole body a few times per week and advanced athletes using split routines that train muscle groups on different days to manage higher volumes.
Advanced athletes must train every muscle group every day to progress, because split routines exist only for beginners with low work capacity.

questions.explanation: Frequency balances stimulus against recovery. Full-body sessions suit lower volumes and less experienced athletes, while splitting the body across days lets advanced athletes accumulate more work per muscle group without overloading a single session. Matching frequency and split to status keeps each session productive instead of merely frequent. Applied here, the correct practice is the one that matches the established approach to training frequency by training status and split routine.

questions.question: Regarding preparatory competition and transition period purposes, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The transition period is when the athlete trains hardest at maximum intensity to set personal records immediately after the season.
During the competition period the main goal is to build large amounts of new general fitness with very high training volumes.
The preparatory period should be skipped so the athlete can spend the entire year in the competition period at peak intensity.

The preparatory period builds general fitness first and then more specific fitness, the competition period emphasizes expressing peak performance while maintaining key qualities, and the transition period provides active recovery after the competitive season ends.

questions.explanation: Each period has a distinct job. Preparation creates the fitness base and then sharpens it toward the demands of the sport, competition is about performing and holding on to what was built rather than building large new capacities, and transition restores the athlete physically and mentally before the next cycle. Blurring these purposes, such as chasing peak loads year-round, leaves no time to build fitness or to recover from expressing it. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the practice for preparatory competition and transition period purposes: the preparatory period builds general fitness first and then more specific fitness, the competition period emphasizes expressing peak performance while maintaining key qualities, and the transition period provides active recovery after the competitive season ends.

questions.question: Regarding work to rest ratios for conditioning by energy system, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Conditioning intervals match work-to-rest ratios to the energy system targeted, with brief maximal efforts needing relatively long recovery and longer aerobic efforts tolerating shorter, more equal recovery periods.
Every conditioning session should use the same work-to-rest ratio, because the energy system being trained has no bearing on how much recovery an interval needs.
The shortest, most explosive intervals need the least rest, since very brief efforts restore their energy supply almost instantly with no recovery time.
Work-to-rest ratio refers to the proportion of a session spent coaching versus training, and it does not describe interval recovery at all.

questions.explanation: Different energy systems restore at different rates. Short explosive efforts depend on rapidly depleting stores that need proportionally generous recovery to repeat quality work, while aerobic intervals can continue with briefer pauses. Setting the ratio by the system targeted keeps interval quality aligned with the adaptation sought instead of letting fatigue redefine the session. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the practice for work to rest ratios for conditioning by energy system: conditioning intervals match work-to-rest ratios to the energy system targeted, with brief maximal efforts needing relatively long recovery and longer aerobic efforts tolerating shorter, more equal recovery periods.

questions.question: A muscle group can produce a maximum voluntary force of 1500 newtons. Using force produced equals maximum force times the stated percentage, how much force is produced at 80 percent of maximum?
questions.explanation: Force produced is 1500 x 80% = 1200 N. The professional verifies this computed figure against the athlete's records.

soa-exam-fm-financial-mathematics.quiz_title: SOA Exam FM (Financial Mathematics) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An Exam FM study problem states the following. The effective annual rate of discount is 5.00%. What is the equivalent effective annual rate of interest?
An analyst at an insurer sets up the following calculation. An annuity pays $400 at the end of each year for 23 years. At an effective annual rate of 5.5%, what is the present value of the annuity?
Yuki Tanaka must identify the correct statement about a sinking fund with a different deposit frequency. The candidate is building a one-line summary for a flashcard. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Deposit frequency must match the loan interest payment frequency by the definition of the method under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam FM purposes as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

The deposit uses the loan rate whenever deposits are more frequent than annual, regardless of the fund's earnings as the idea is used when cash flows are valued in actuarial work under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory

Deposits are always annual; other frequencies convert the arrangement into amortization as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added in the ordinary usage of the term among candidates preparing for this examination

Sinking fund deposits may be made more often than the interest payments on the loan; the deposit is then set by the annuity symbol matching the deposit frequency and the fund's own rate, independently of the loan's interest schedule.

questions.explanation: Deposit solves Deposit x s_N(j per deposit period) = L, using the fund rate j and deposit count N.

questions.question: Nia Thompson must identify the correct statement about coupon and coupon rate. The review covers material from the current syllabus. Which of the following is the correct statement?

answers.text: A bond's coupon per period is the face value multiplied by the coupon rate per period (Fr when F is face and r the per-period coupon rate); the coupon is a fixed dollar amount set at issue and does not change with market yields.

The coupon varies with the market yield so that the price stays at par throughout the bond's life as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added in the ordinary usage of the term among candidates preparing for this examination

The coupon is the redemption value multiplied by the yield rate, recalculated each period as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added in the ordinary usage of the term among candidates preparing for this examination

Coupon rate and yield rate are two names for the same quantity once the bond is trading under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam FM purposes as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

questions.explanation: Coupon = F*r per period (g = coupon/C on redemption basis). Yield is the buyer's earned rate at the price paid.

questions.question: Chiamaka Eze, a candidate working through a practice set, is asked about why the duration-only approximation errs. The review covers material from the current syllabus. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: The linear approximation is exact for small changes and errs only when the change exceeds the yield itself in the sense the term carries throughout the financial mathematics syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

The linear approximation overvalues the stream after any yield change, because it ignores discounting of distant flows in the ordinary usage of the term among candidates preparing for this examination as the statement would be understood in a first course in financial mathematics for actuaries

The error direction depends on the sign of the yield change: overvalue for rises, undervalue for falls in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam FM purposes as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

The duration-only (linear) approximation undervalues an option-free cash flow stream after a yield change in either direction, because the true price-yield curve is convex and lies above its tangent line.

questions.explanation: Convex price curve > tangent line everywhere except tangency: linear estimate is always too low for positive flows.

questions.question: Amara Diallo, an Exam FM candidate in a study group in Columbus, is consulted on net present value. The candidate is building a one-line summary for a flashcard. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: A negative net present value means the project earns more than the valuation rate, because the sign convention is reversed as a complete statement of the concept, with no qualifying condition omitted or added in the standard treatment of this topic in financial mathematics

Net present value is the accumulated value of all cash flows at the end of the project, with no discounting applied in the standard treatment of this topic in financial mathematics as the idea is used when cash flows are valued in actuarial work

Net present value subtracts undiscounted total inflows from undiscounted total outflows, so it ignores the timing of payments as the idea is used when cash flows are valued in actuarial work under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory

Net present value is the present value of all cash inflows minus the present value of all cash outflows at the valuation rate; a positive net present value means the inflows are worth more than the outflows at that rate.

questions.explanation: NPV = PV(inflows) - PV(outflows), all discounted at the same valuation date and rate.

questions.question: A study partner asks Ximena Torres, a candidate reviewing financial mathematics, to confirm the correct statement for an arithmetic decreasing annuity. The question is part of a self-test on fundamentals. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The decreasing annuity's present value is n times a-angle-n, because the first payment is n as the idea is used when cash flows are valued in actuarial work under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory
Decreasing and increasing annuities over the same term always have equal present values, because they make the same total of payments in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam FM purposes

A decreasing annuity paying n down to 1 has present value (a-angle-n minus n v to the n) divided by i, the same as the increasing annuity under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory
An arithmetic decreasing annuity-immediate pays n, n-1, down to 1 at successive period ends; its present value (Da)-angle-n equals (n minus a-angle-n) divided by i.

questions.explanation: (Da)_n = (n - a_n)/i. (Ia)_n + (Da)_n = (n+1)*a_n, a useful check.

questions.question: A trainee actuary is given the following information. An annuity pays a total of $6,000 per year, paid in equal instalments monthly at the end of each period, for 8 years. At an effective annual rate of 6.0%, what is the present value?

During a study session in Toronto, Omar Haddad raises the topic of the effect of a longer term on a level loan payment. The question arises while reviewing the exam syllabus topics. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: Extending the term raises the payment, because more interest must be covered per period as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added in the ordinary usage of the term among candidates preparing for this examination
Extending the term lowers both the payment and the total interest, because interest is spread more thinly in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam FM purposes
Extending the term leaves total interest unchanged, since the principal and rate are unchanged as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example
Extending the term of a loan at the same rate lowers the level payment but increases the total interest paid, because the principal is outstanding for longer on average.

questions.explanation: R = L/a_n falls as n rises; total interest = nR - L rises.

questions.question: Yuki Tanaka, a student in an interest theory course for actuaries, double-checks the standard statement for when an issuer calls a bond. A fellow candidate has asked for the precise statement. Which of the following is the correct statement?

answers.text: Investors price callable bonds assuming the call date most favourable to themselves, since the issuer must act fairly in the standard treatment of this topic in financial mathematics as the idea is used when cash flows are valued in actuarial work

Call decisions depend only on the time elapsed, never on interest rates in the sense the term carries throughout the financial mathematics syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example in the way the idea is presented in standard interest theory references for actuaries

An issuer tends to call a premium bond when rates have fallen, refinancing more cheaply; investors therefore assume a callable premium bond may be redeemed at the earliest advantageous-to-issuer date when setting a price for a target yield.

Issuers call discount bonds first, because retiring cheap debt early improves their reported yield in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam FM purposes as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added in the ordinary usage of the term among candidates preparing for this examination

questions.explanation: Falling rates -> call premium bonds and refinance. Yield-to-worst pricing reflects the issuer's advantage.

questions.question: A practice reviewer asks Zain Malik, a candidate preparing for the Financial Mathematics Exam, about immunization limitations. The tutor has asked the group to identify the correct statement. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Immunization eliminates default and liquidity risk as well as interest-rate risk under the conventions normally used when this concept is introduced in the sense the term carries throughout the financial mathematics syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

Once immunized, a portfolio never needs rebalancing, because the three Redington conditions are self-maintaining under the conventions normally used when this concept is introduced in the sense the term carries throughout the financial mathematics syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

Immunization protects against small, parallel shifts in a flat yield structure at the immunizing yield and must be maintained by rebalancing as time passes and rates move, because durations drift; it does not by itself protect against arbitrary non-parallel curve changes.

Immunization protects against any pattern of rate changes, including twists of the yield curve, by its three conditions in the sense the term carries throughout the financial mathematics syllabus as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

questions.explanation: Redington is a local, flat-curve, parallel-shift result. Durations change with time/yield -> rebalance.

questions.question: Quinn Adams, an actuarial student preparing for Exam FM in Portland, is consulted on modified duration. The candidate is checking a statement found in study notes. Which of the following is the correct statement?

answers.text: The sign is positive: value rises with yield at a rate given by modified duration in the way the idea is presented in standard interest theory references for actuaries as a complete statement of the concept, with no qualifying condition omitted or added in the standard treatment of this topic in financial mathematics

Modified duration measures the dollar change in value per unit yield change, with no division by value as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example in the way the idea is presented in standard interest theory references for actuaries

Modified duration equals Macaulay duration multiplied by (1 + yield), because modification amplifies the average time in the standard treatment of this topic in financial mathematics as the idea is used when cash flows are valued in actuarial work under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory

Modified duration equals Macaulay duration divided by (1 + yield per period), and it measures the proportional sensitivity of present value to a small change in yield: the percentage change in value is approximately minus modified duration times the yield change.

questions.explanation: ModD = MacD/(1+j) (per-period yield j). Approx: dP/P = -ModD * dj. Modified < Macaulay for positive yield.

questions.question: Alex Morgan, an actuarial student preparing for Exam FM, is asked about the accumulation function a(t). The question comes from the candidate's concept review notes. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The accumulation function a(t) gives the accumulated value at time t of an initial investment of 1 made at time 0, so a(0) equals 1 and the accumulated value of a principal P is P times a(t).

The accumulation function a(t) gives the present value at time 0 of 1 payable at time t, so a(0) equals the discount factor for the longest term available under the usual definitions adopted in introductory interest theory

The accumulation function a(t) is the effective rate of interest earned in year t, so it is measured as a percentage rather than as an amount in the sense the term carries throughout the financial mathematics syllabus

The accumulation function a(t) equals the total interest earned on a principal of 1 over t years, so a(0) equals 0 by definition in the way the idea is presented in standard interest theory references for actuaries

questions.explanation: a(0) = 1 by definition; AV of P after t years is P*a(t), and the interest earned is P*(a(t) - 1).

questions.question: An analyst at an insurer sets up the following calculation. Cash flows of $600 at the end of year 1, $300 at the end of year 2, $800 at the end of year 3, $500 at the end of year 4 are to be valued at an effective annual rate of 5.0%. What is their total present value?
questions.explanation: PV = sum of each cash flow discounted for its own term = 1945.96.

questions.question: A candidate reviewing financial mathematics considers the following. A loan of $25,000 is repaid by 18 level payments of $1,667.55 at the end of each year at an effective annual rate of 2.0%. What is the total amount of interest paid over the life of the loan?

While preparing for Exam FM, Tatum Herrera — an actuarial analyst checking a concept — reviews a bond selling at a premium. The scenario is drawn from the candidate's formula review session. What is the correct statement?

answers.text: A bond sells at a premium (price above redemption value) when its coupon rate per period exceeds the yield rate per period, because its coupons are more generous than the market requires.

Premium means the redemption value exceeds the face value, regardless of coupon and yield in the standard treatment of this topic in financial mathematics as the idea is used when cash flows are valued in actuarial work

A bond sells at a premium when its yield exceeds its coupon rate, because investors pay extra for high-yield bonds as a statement about the concept itself rather than about any single numerical example

A bond is at a premium whenever its term is long, because long bonds are riskier in the form in which the concept is stated for Exam FM purposes as a general statement that holds without extra conditions being added

questions.explanation: Premium iff coupon rate g (on redemption basis) > yield j. Discount iff g < j; par iff equal (see premium formula).

questions.question: While preparing for Exam FM, Marco Silva — a trainee actuary refreshing interest theory — reviews pricing with a yield curve compared with a single rate. The discussion takes place during a weekly study session. Which of the following is the correct statement?
