questions.question: All of the following support the principle of indemnity EXCEPT:

answers.text: A policy clause allowing the insured to keep duplicate full recoveries for one loss
Deductibles that leave part of the loss with the insured
Actual cash value settlement that accounts for depreciation
The insurer's right of subrogation after payment

questions.explanation: Duplicate full recovery would let the insured profit, contradicting indemnity. Deductibles, depreciation-based valuation, and subrogation all help keep recovery at the true loss amount.

questions.question: A Jacksonville ski shop closes entirely during coastal storm season and earns no income from that location to eliminate its coastal storm exposure. This is an example of:

answers.text: Risk transfer to a reinsurer
Risk retention
Risk reduction
Risk avoidance

questions.explanation: Giving up the activity that creates the exposure avoids the risk entirely. Reduction would keep operating but lessen the exposure, for example with defensible space and fire-resistant roofing.

questions.question: All of the following are common reasons an insurer may cancel mid-term, subject to required notice and applicable law, EXCEPT:

answers.text: The insurer's preference for a different logo on its policy forms
A substantial increase in the hazard insured against
Nonpayment of premium
Material misrepresentation in obtaining the policy

questions.explanation: Nonpayment, material misrepresentation and substantial hazard increase are recognized cancellation grounds when statutory notice rules are followed. Branding preferences about policy-form logos are not a ground to cancel a customer's coverage mid-term.

questions.question: A policy change request to correct the named insured from a sole proprietor to a newly formed corporation is significant because it may

answers.text: Never matter, since entity form has no effect on coverage
Change the insured entity itself, requiring underwriting approval rather than a simple clerical correction
Automatically transfer all prior policies to the corporation without notice
Cancel the need for any insurable interest in the property

questions.explanation: The legal entity that owns property and faces liability changed, which affects insurable interest, underwriting, and who holds policy rights. Insurers treat genuine entity changes as substantive, not typographical.

questions.question: An insured carries $160,000 on a building valued at $250,000. The policy states an 80% coinsurance requirement, a covered loss is $50,000, and no deductible is stated in this question. What is the insurer's payment?
questions.explanation: Required insurance is 80% of $250,000, or $200,000. The ratio of insurance carried to insurance required is $160,000 divided by $200,000, or 80%. Eighty percent of the $50,000 loss is $40,000.

questions.question: A Greensboro warehouse is valued at $1,000,000 as stated in the stem. The policy requires 80% coinsurance and the owner carries a $600,000 limit as stated in the stem. A covered partial loss of $100,000 occurs as stated in the stem, ignoring any deductible. The coinsurance-adjusted payment is:
questions.explanation: Required insurance is 80% of $1,000,000, or $800,000. The recovery ratio is $600,000 divided by $800,000, or 75%, so 75% of the $100,000 loss is $75,000. Paying the full loss ignores the underinsurance penalty.

questions.question: All of the following statements about a competent party to a contract are generally true EXCEPT:

answers.text: A minor's contract is generally voidable by the minor
Parties must be of legal age to be fully bound in most cases
A person under the influence may lack capacity in some circumstances
A person adjudicated mentally incompetent can bind an insurer by signing an application alone

questions.explanation: Someone adjudicated incompetent generally lacks capacity to form a binding contract alone. A minor's voidable contract status, the closest contrast, is a recognized capacity limitation rather than full binding power.

questions.question: A Jacksonville landlord is an additional insured on its tenant's liability policy. The tenant's employee negligently injures a customer, who sues the landlord claiming the landlord is responsible for the tenant's operations. The landlord's additional insured status is relevant because:

answers.text: The suit is automatically dismissed whenever a landlord is an additional insured
The landlord's status converts the tenant's policy into a property policy for the building
Additional insured status makes the landlord responsible for the tenant's premium
The claim arises from the named insured tenant's operations, which is the kind of liability additional insured endorsements are designed to reach

questions.explanation: The endorsement responds to liability asserted against the additional insured arising from the named insured's operations — exactly this suit's theory. It does not shift premium duty, change the policy type or dismiss the case.

north-carolina-building-contractor.quiz_title: North Carolina Building Contractor Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Building pad compaction on a student housing project in Boone is verified how?

answers.text: By driving over it and judging the feel
By the color of the soil after rolling
By field density testing of the compacted lifts against the specified density, lift by lift
By counting the roller's passes alone

questions.explanation: Passes and feel do not prove density. Testing each lift is what shows the specification was actually met.

questions.question: A roof cricket or saddle on a school building project in Charlotte is built where, and why?

answers.text: At the ridge for decoration
Under every skylight curb
Inside the gutter
Behind a chimney or other wide obstruction on the slope, to split and divert water around it instead of letting it pond against the uphill flashing

questions.explanation: Any wide uphill obstruction is a dam. The cricket is the small roof that moves the water around it.

questions.question: A plan's scale is used by the estimator on a retail center project in Asheville to do what?

answers.text: Decorate the title block
Convert measurements taken from the drawing into real dimensions of the work, checking them against figured dimensions wherever the drawings give them
Replace all written dimensions
Measure only when no dimensions exist and trust the scale over the figures

questions.explanation: Figured dimensions govern over scaled ones. Scaling is a check and a fallback, not the authority.

questions.question: High-strength bolting on a dealership building project in Goldsboro achieves its clamping force how, in principle?

answers.text: By using the largest wrench available once
By painting the bolts after snugging them by feel
By welding every bolt after installation
By tightening the bolt assembly to a verified tension using an approved method, so the connected plies are clamped together as the design assumes

questions.explanation: Pretensioned joints work by clamping force, and that force must be achieved by a verified method, not by feel.

questions.question: Hot weather concreting on a school building project in Charlotte calls for extra care mainly because of what?

answers.text: Concrete never sets in hot weather
Hot weather always doubles the strength
Forms cannot be used above mild temperatures
Rapid moisture loss and faster setting, which can cause plastic shrinkage cracking and a weaker surface if curing is not protected

questions.explanation: Heat accelerates both setting and drying. Protecting moisture and timing the finishing are the countermeasures.

questions.question: Post-tensioning tendons on a distribution center project in Salisbury may be stressed only when what condition is met?

answers.text: The crew has a free afternoon
The forms look dry
The tendons have been in place a full month
The concrete has reached the strength the design specifies for stressing, verified as the documents require

questions.explanation: Stressing too early can crush or crack immature concrete. The specified strength is the gate.

questions.question: Roof trusses on a clinic building project in Lumberton arrive on site and one is damaged in unloading. The framer should do what?

answers.text: Nail a board alongside the break and set it
Use it in the middle of the roof where it is hidden
Cut out the damaged web and continue
Keep it out of the structure and get a repair designed or approved by the truss designer or engineer rather than sistering boards by guess

questions.explanation: A truss is an engineered system whose members work together. Field-designed repairs guess at forces the designer calculated.

questions.question: A payment bond on a municipal building project in Wilmington on public work protects whom, and why does that matter more there?

answers.text: Only the owner's lender
Subcontractors and suppliers, who cannot lien public property — the bond is their substitute remedy for getting paid
The general contractor's own profit
No one; it is a formality

questions.explanation: Public property cannot be liened, so the bond stands in the lien's place for the people who furnished the work.

questions.question: Sports lighting on a dealership building project in Goldsboro must be aimed and shielded to achieve what two goals at once?

answers.text: The brightest possible light in all directions
Light aimed at the spectators for visibility
Only the field's centre needs light
Even, glare-controlled light on the playing surface for the athletes, and minimal spill and glare onto neighbours and the sky

questions.explanation: Good sports lighting is precision optics on poles: bright where the game is, dark where it is not.

questions.question: A pump is used to place concrete on a mixed-use building project in Cary. The mix must be adjusted how, compared with chute placement?

answers.text: Any mix pumps if enough water is added
It must be a pumpable mix — cohesive and properly graded — approved for pumping, not simply the chute mix with water added at the pump
Pumping needs no mix change and no approval
The pump operator may redesign the mix freely

questions.explanation: Pumping is a different placement method with its own mix requirements. Water is not the adjustment.

questions.question: Soil and existing-conditions information in the documents on a warehouse project in Durham is handled by the prudent bidder how?

answers.text: He studies what is furnished, visits the site, and prices the conditions he can foresee, while noting the contract's rules for conditions that differ from those indicated
He assumes perfect conditions in every bid
Site visits are a waste of bid time
Differing conditions are always the contractor's cost by law

questions.explanation: Ground risk is allocated by the documents and priced by the informed. The site visit is part of the estimate.

questions.question: Soil and existing-conditions information in the documents on a laboratory building project in Durham is handled by the prudent bidder how?

answers.text: He assumes perfect conditions in every bid
Site visits are a waste of bid time
Differing conditions are always the contractor's cost by law
He studies what is furnished, visits the site, and prices the conditions he can foresee, while noting the contract's rules for conditions that differ from those indicated

questions.explanation: Ground risk is allocated by the documents and priced by the informed. The site visit is part of the estimate.

questions.question: Grouting of reinforced masonry on a courthouse annex project in Asheville must be consolidated and the cells must be kept how before grouting?

answers.text: Partially filled with rubble to save grout
Wet with standing water
Clean and free of mortar fins and debris that would block the grout, so the grout fully fills the cells around the reinforcement
Blocked at random to create chambers

questions.explanation: Grouted reinforcement only works if grout actually surrounds the steel. Cleanouts and inspection exist for that reason.

questions.question: Refrigerant and condensate lines on a student housing project in Boone from rooftop and air-handler equipment must be routed and supported so that what is avoided?

answers.text: The lines looking untidy
Any need for a drain at all
Noise from the equipment
Condensate overflow into ceilings and walls, and refrigerant line damage — water from a clogged or badly sloped drain is one of the commonest building leaks

questions.explanation: Condensate is a plumbing problem attached to a mechanical system. Its drains deserve the same respect as any waste line.

questions.question: Marks on a bank building project in Burlington have faded or been destroyed by site traffic before the dig is finished. The excavator should do what?

answers.text: Have the facilities re-marked through the one-call process rather than digging from memory of where the marks were
Dig from the superintendent's recollection
Assume the lines follow the old marks exactly
Repaint the marks himself where he thinks they were

questions.explanation: Only the operators' locators can restore authoritative marks. Memory is not a marking system.

questions.question: Truss bracing on a parking deck project in Charlotte — temporary during erection and permanent in the finished roof — is required because of what?

answers.text: Bracing is only to keep trusses from blowing off the truck
Trusses are stable as soon as they touch the walls
Bracing replaces the roof sheathing
Individual trusses are slender and unstable out of plane; bracing ties them into a system that can carry its design loads and survive erection

questions.explanation: A truss alone is a mechanism waiting to fold sideways. Bracing is what makes the roof a structure.

questions.question: Steel lintels, shelf angles, and embed plates for masonry on a warehouse project in Durham must be coordinated early primarily because of what?

answers.text: They are cast or built into other trades' work on a schedule — a missed embed cannot be added after the concrete or masonry has closed over its location
They are the most expensive items on the job
They can always be surface-mounted later with equal performance
Coordination is a paperwork formality

questions.explanation: Embeds are one-way doors in the schedule. Coordination is how they exist when the pour or the wall arrives.

questions.question: A takeoff finds a net quantity of 300 units and the estimate adds a waste allowance of 15 percent. Using order quantity = net quantity + net quantity x waste percent / 100, how many units should be ordered?

answers.text: 390 units
345 units
370 units
300 units

questions.explanation: Allowance = 300 x 15 / 100 = 45. Order quantity = 300 + 45 = 345 units.

questions.question: A worker on a laboratory building project in Durham is found operating equipment he is not trained or authorized to run. The supervisor's correct action is to do what?

answers.text: Stop the work, remove him from the equipment, and address it as a training and enforcement failure — not let it continue because the work is behind
Look the other way if he seems capable
Punish only if an accident happens
Let him finish the shift first

questions.explanation: Unauthorized operation is a system failure caught in time. Stopping it is the supervisor's core function.

questions.question: A contractor bidding work on a community college building project in Gastonia must include in his price the costs of supervision, temporary facilities, insurance, and taxes — not only direct labor and materials — because of what?

answers.text: Owners reimburse them separately by law
Those job and overhead costs are real costs of delivering the work; a bid that omits them wins the job and loses the money
They are optional courtesies
They are covered by the performance bond

questions.explanation: Underpricing indirect costs is how profitable-looking bid days become losing jobs. The full cost is the only honest base.

louisiana-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: Louisiana Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: When does a binder typically provide temporary evidence of insurance?

answers.text: From binding until the policy is issued or the binder expires or is replaced
Only after the first claim is paid
For exactly ten years regardless of its terms
Never; binders have no legal effect in any state

questions.explanation: A binder is temporary proof of coverage pending policy issuance, governed by its own stated period and conditions. It does have legal effect, contrary to the final distractor.

questions.question: The policy period is important to the adjuster primarily because:

answers.text: Losses are covered whenever they are discovered, even decades after expiration, under every property form
The period determines the insured's mailing address
A loss one day before inception is covered if the claim is filed during the period
Property coverage generally responds only to losses that occur during the policy period stated in the declarations

questions.explanation: Occurrence within the stated period is a threshold coverage requirement for property forms. Filing a claim during the period does not pull a pre-inception loss into coverage.

questions.question: A loss payee endorsement on equipment in Shreveport primarily protects whom, and how?

answers.text: The insured's customers, by paying them for late deliveries
The producer, by guaranteeing commission after a loss
The lender or lessor, by directing loss payment for that equipment to it as its interest appears
The equipment vendor, by guaranteeing its sales price on every return

questions.explanation: Loss payee status is about the property claim check, not liability status. It ensures a party with a financial interest in damaged equipment is paid to the extent of that interest.

questions.question: What does the abandonment condition state?

answers.text: The insured may leave all debris for the insurer to own
The insurer must buy every damaged item at new price
There is no abandonment of damaged property to the insurer, meaning the insured cannot force the insurer to take the property in place of settlement
Salvage value can never be considered

questions.explanation: No-abandonment prevents an insured from dumping damaged property on the insurer as the settlement itself. Salvage and its value remain part of settlement accounting rather than a forced transfer.

questions.question: What is the 'garage' concept adjusters most often test in family auto claims?

answers.text: Whether the home has a driveway
Whether the car is washed inside the garage
Whether the garage has two doors
Whether youthful or household drivers and regularly used vehicles were disclosed, because the family car risk is the household's combined exposure

questions.explanation: Household composition drives auto risk; undisclosed resident drivers and regular-use cars are material underwriting facts the adjuster must verify at claim time.

questions.question: An insurer cedes part of its risk to another insurer so a single coastal storm-interface catastrophe near Slidell does not overwhelm its surplus. That arrangement is:

answers.text: A binder issued by a producer
Reinsurance, used to spread risk and stabilize results
A deductible charged to policyholders
A form of applicant misrepresentation

questions.explanation: Reinsurance transfers part of an insurer's exposure to another carrier, smoothing catastrophe impact. It operates between insurers, unlike deductibles that operate between insurer and insured.

questions.question: A condition that requires the insured to protect property from further damage after a loss is an example of:

answers.text: A definition of an insured location
An exclusion that removes the original loss from coverage
A declaration that sets the policy limit
A post-loss duty imposed on the insured by the policy conditions

questions.explanation: Protecting property from further harm is a classic insured duty after loss found in conditions. It does not exclude the original loss; it governs conduct after it happens.

questions.question: A New Orleans logistics manager wants the certificate to state a limit higher than the policy provides so a contract can be signed. What is the proper response?

answers.text: Refuse to misstate the limit; a certificate must accurately reflect the policy or be corrected by endorsement first
Issue it and note the difference only in an internal file
Issue the higher limit because the certificate does not affect coverage anyway
Issue it with a verbal warning that the real limit is lower

questions.explanation: Knowingly overstating limits on a certificate is misrepresentation even though the document does not change coverage. Accuracy is required, and any real increase must come through the policy.

questions.question: A dwelling policy shows Coverage A of $300,000 and the insured asks what the automatic other-structures amount is. The adjuster should state:

answers.text: $150,000, which is half the dwelling limit
$30,000, which is 10 percent of the dwelling limit
$90,000, which is 30 percent of the dwelling limit
$300,000, equal to the dwelling limit

questions.explanation: Ten percent of $300,000 is $30,000 for other structures. The one-half and 30-percent figures are derivations used for other coverages and would overstate this particular automatic limit.

questions.question: Priya adjusts a severe storm roof claim in Shreveport on a DP-2 policy. Wind lifts shingles and rain enters through the wind-created opening. Why does the broad form matter here?

answers.text: Rain alone, with no covered peril, automatically creates coverage
Windstorm is never covered under any dwelling form
The loss must be handled only as a flood claim
Windstorm is a covered broad-form peril, so ensuing water damage through the opening the wind created is analyzed as part of that covered loss

questions.explanation: Windstorm coverage is central here because the interior water damage followed a wind-created opening. Rain entering with no covered cause and no opening would present a very different and generally uncovered fact pattern.

questions.question: What does salvage value do in a total loss where the insured retains the vehicle?

answers.text: Salvage is added to the payment as a bonus
The retained salvage value is deducted from the settlement because the insured keeps an asset with remaining value
Salvage has no effect when the owner keeps the car
The insurer must pay the loan balance instead

questions.explanation: Owner-retained salvage prevents double recovery: the insured receives value in cash plus the wreck itself, so the wreck's value offsets the cash payment.

questions.question: Why does Part A exclude liability assumed under a contract in many situations?

answers.text: Because property damage is excluded from Part A entirely
Because contracts are never relevant to auto accidents
Because the insured could otherwise create liability by agreement that the insurer never underwrote, subject to the form's exceptions
Because the insured is never liable when a contract exists

questions.explanation: The contractual liability concept prevents an insured from volunteering the insurer into obligations beyond tort liability, while the form preserves certain defined exceptions.

questions.question: All of the following support the principle of indemnity EXCEPT:

answers.text: A policy clause allowing the insured to keep duplicate full recoveries for one loss
Deductibles that leave part of the loss with the insured
Actual cash value settlement that accounts for depreciation
The insurer's right of subrogation after payment

questions.explanation: Duplicate full recovery would let the insured profit, contradicting indemnity. Deductibles, depreciation-based valuation, and subrogation all help keep recovery at the true loss amount.

questions.question: All of the following describe the Basic form EXCEPT:

answers.text: It names fire and lightning as covered perils
It automatically covers accidental discharge of water from a plumbing system
It is the narrowest of the three standard causes of loss forms
It names smoke as a covered peril

questions.explanation: Accidental water discharge from plumbing is a Broad-form addition, not a Basic-form peril. Basic is the narrowest form and does name fire, lightning and smoke.

questions.question: All of the following are differences between a loss payee and an additional insured EXCEPT:

answers.text: An additional insured is usually added by endorsement at the request of the named insured under a contract
A loss payee's interest is in receiving property loss proceeds
An additional insured receives liability protection under the policy
A loss payee is entitled to set the policy premium and choose the insurer

questions.explanation: Neither a loss payee nor an additional insured sets premiums or selects the insurer; that is the named insured's and insurer's role. The real distinction is proceeds interest versus liability protection.

questions.question: A Slidell home suffers a frozen pipe burst after the insured shut off heat and left for a month in winter with no precautions. Which condition or exclusion is most relevant?

answers.text: The freezing peril's requirement that the insured use reasonable care to maintain heat or shut off and drain the water system
The ordinance exclusion as the sole issue
The nuclear hazard clause
The war exclusion

questions.explanation: Freezing coverage is conditioned on reasonable care to keep heat on or drain the system. Leaving a mountain home unheated and undrained in winter is the textbook failure of that condition.

questions.question: EXCEPT — Which act is NOT a proper insured duty after loss?

answers.text: Giving prompt notice of the accident
Cooperating with the insurer's investigation
Voluntarily paying the claimant's full demand and signing a release without the insurer's consent
Protecting the damaged vehicle from further loss

questions.explanation: Voluntary payments and unauthorized settlements breach the conditions and can destroy subrogation; notice, cooperation, and loss protection are the duties the form actually imposes.

questions.question: A Lafayette condo owner asks why his claim payment was less than his repair bill even though the damage was below the limit. The adjuster's most likely correct explanations involve:

answers.text: The insurer's right to keep part of every payment for overhead
The deductible and any depreciation or coinsurance adjustment provided by the policy
A requirement that insureds absorb half of every loss by law
A rule that adjusters always subtract an arbitrary percentage

questions.explanation: Shortfalls below the limit normally trace to the deductible, depreciation under an actual-cash-value basis, or coinsurance. Arbitrary withholdings and invented half-loss laws are not legitimate explanations.

questions.question: All of the following are typically required considerations before punitive damages are awarded EXCEPT:

answers.text: There generally must be an underlying compensable injury or compensatory award
The conduct must be shown to be malicious, wanton, reckless or otherwise more culpable than ordinary negligence
The amount must bear a reasonable relationship to the harm and the conduct
The claimant must prove the exact dollar amount of punitive damages from an invoice

questions.explanation: Punitive damages are not invoiced items; the amount is set by the fact-finder within constitutional and legal limits tied to culpability and harm. Ordinary negligence alone is usually not culpable enough to support them.

questions.question: All of the following are broad-form named perils under HO-2 EXCEPT:

answers.text: Theft
Falling objects
Earth movement
Accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam

questions.explanation: Earth movement is excluded rather than listed as a broad-form peril. Theft, falling objects and accidental water discharge are all within the broad named-peril list, which is why earth movement stands out.

hawaii-business-law.quiz_title: Hawaii Business and Law Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What basic rights do shareholders hold in a Hawaii contracting business in Kailua as a corporation?

answers.text: They direct daily field operations on every project
They withdraw corporate funds freely for personal use
They elect directors, vote on major corporate changes, and share in distributions when declared
They sign contracts that bind the corporation whenever they wish

questions.explanation: Shareholders own and vote, while day to day direction sits with directors and officers.

questions.question: Which body licenses contractors statewide for a Hawaii contracting firm in Honolulu?

answers.text: The largest supplier the firm buys materials from
The Contractors License Board, acting within the professional and vocational licensing division of the state commerce and consumer affairs department
The county building department in the county where the work sits
The trade association the firm chooses to join

questions.explanation: Contractor licensing in Hawaii is a statewide function of the board within the licensing division.

questions.question: What are the employer duties around protective equipment at a Hawaii contracting business in Kailua?

answers.text: Workers must always supply and maintain their own required gear
Equipment condition is the worker concern alone
Providing equipment excuses the firm from checking its use
To provide the required equipment without shifting its cost burden improperly, maintain it, and ensure workers use it correctly

questions.explanation: Providing, maintaining, and enforcing equipment use belong together.

questions.question: What is the accounting equation that underlies the books of a Hawaii contracting business in Honolulu?

answers.text: What the firm owns equals what it owes plus the ownership interest, so every recorded event keeps the books in balance
Expenses end when a job ends
Profit equals the balance in the bank account
Revenue always equals cash received

questions.explanation: The equation keeps assets, obligations, and ownership interest in balance.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a written safety programme at a Hawaii design-build contracting firm in Kailua Kona?

answers.text: To create paperwork that substitutes for safe practice
To shift all safety duties onto the newest workers
To be written once and never revisited
To set out responsibilities, procedures, training, and review so hazard control is systematic rather than improvised

questions.explanation: A written programme turns safety into an organised system.

questions.question: How does arbitration differ from mediation for a dispute involving a Hawaii building contracting company in Kailua Kona?

answers.text: Arbitration produces only a nonbinding suggestion
An arbitrator hears the case and issues a binding decision, while a mediator helps the parties reach their own settlement
A mediator imposes a binding award on both parties
Both processes always end with a jury verdict

questions.explanation: Arbitration decides the dispute and mediation facilitates a voluntary settlement.

questions.question: How can a written agreement change at-will status at a Hawaii general contracting company in Kailua?

answers.text: Only a verbal promise can change at-will status
Written promises never bind an employer
A promise of continued employment or a stated process for ending it can bind the firm beyond ordinary at-will terms
Handbook wording can never create obligations

questions.explanation: Words the firm puts in writing can limit its own freedom to dismiss.

questions.question: What should a Hawaii general contracting company in Waianae do when materials arrive on site?

answers.text: Install materials immediately before any inspection occurs
Accept every delivery unchecked and store it wherever space exists
Inspect them against the accepted submittal and order, note damage or shortages at delivery, and store them protected as the manufacturer directs
Reject materials that match the order to keep suppliers alert

questions.explanation: Delivery inspection and proper storage protect material quality and payment accuracy.

questions.question: How does an express contract differ from an implied contract for a Hawaii design-build contracting firm in Aiea?

answers.text: An express contract is always oral and an implied contract is always written
An implied contract has no legal effect under any circumstances
An express contract states its terms in words, while an implied contract is shown by the conduct of the parties
An express contract needs no agreement on price or scope

questions.explanation: Express terms are stated directly and implied terms are inferred from behavior.

questions.question: How should a Hawaii contracting firm in Kailua-Kona separate direct costs from indirect costs in an estimate?

answers.text: Direct costs trace to specific work on the project, while indirect costs support the work without belonging to a single item
Direct costs include only office rent and company advertising
Indirect costs are the profit added at the end of the bid
Direct costs are always paid by the customer and indirect costs by subcontractors

questions.explanation: Direct costs attach to project work and indirect costs support performance more generally.

questions.question: Why should a Hawaii contracting business in Waianae investigate incidents and near misses?

answers.text: Near misses prove the system is working perfectly
Investigation is needed only when an insurer demands it
To find the causes and correct them, so the same weakness does not produce the next, larger loss
To find a person to blame and close the file

questions.explanation: A near miss is a free lesson; investigation is how the lesson is collected.

questions.question: How should a Hawaii contracting business in Kailua-Kona separate direct costs from indirect costs in an estimate?

answers.text: Direct costs include only office rent and company advertising
Indirect costs are the profit added at the end of the bid
Direct costs trace to specific work on the project, while indirect costs support the work without belonging to a single item
Direct costs are always paid by the customer and indirect costs by subcontractors

questions.explanation: Direct costs attach to project work and indirect costs support performance more generally.

questions.question: A job of a Hawaii building contracting company in Waipahu has a total estimated cost of $245,000 and costs incurred to date of $175,000. What is the cost to complete?
questions.explanation: Cost to complete = total estimated cost - costs incurred = 245,000 - 175,000 = $70,000.

questions.question: Why can a lien generally not attach to public property in work by a Hawaii building contracting company in Waipahu?

answers.text: Government owners are exempt from paying for work
Because public property is held for public use and may not be seized or sold to satisfy a private claim
Liens are unnecessary because public work is always prepaid
Public projects never leave anyone unpaid

questions.explanation: Public property is shielded from seizure for private claims.

questions.question: Why must withheld payroll amounts at a Hawaii building contracting company in Mililani never fund operations?

answers.text: Trust treatment applies only to large payrolls
Because they are trust amounts taken from worker pay for the government, and using them exposes the firm and those directing it to serious consequences
Successful trading excuses the borrowing
Temporary use is acceptable if repaid quietly

questions.explanation: Trust money is never working capital.

questions.question: A consumer complaint about the work of a Hawaii construction firm in Lihue reaches the board. How should the firm respond?

answers.text: Cooperate with the inquiry, respond as required, and produce its records, treating the complaint as part of licensed accountability
Destroy job records so the inquiry ends quickly
Ignore the inquiry because complaints are private disputes only
Refuse all contact until the customer withdraws the complaint

questions.explanation: Answering to the regulator is part of the bargain of holding a license.

questions.question: How does a force majeure clause help a Hawaii general contracting company in Lihue when extraordinary events beyond its control halt the work?

answers.text: It allocates relief, usually added time, for delays caused by events neither party controls, as the clause defines
It transfers all project risks to the customer permanently
It excuses the contractor from finishing the project at all
It guarantees added payment for every weather day

questions.explanation: Force majeure language defines relief for truly uncontrollable events.

questions.question: The balance sheet of a Hawaii building contracting company in Hilo shows total assets of $160,000 and equity of $120,000. Using assets = liabilities + equity, what are the firm's total liabilities?
questions.explanation: Liabilities = assets - equity = 160,000 - 120,000 = $40,000.

questions.question: When might a Hawaii building contracting company in Hanapepe need cover for errors in professional services it supplies, such as design work it undertakes?

answers.text: When the firm takes on design or professional duties, because general liability cover is aimed at injury and damage, not pure professional error
Never, because design mistakes cause no losses
Professional duties are covered by vehicle cover
Only if a customer insists in writing

questions.explanation: Taking on professional duty creates a distinct exposure needing its own treatment.

questions.question: On a job for a Hawaii design-build contracting firm in Honolulu, costs incurred to date are $680,000 and total estimated cost is $800,000. What is the percent complete, computed as costs incurred divided by total estimated cost?
questions.explanation: Percent complete = 680,000 / 800,000 = 85%.

new-hampshire-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: New Hampshire Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is ratification in agency law?

answers.text: An insurer's approval, after the fact, of an act its producer took without prior authority
A state hearing to set insurance rates
Automatic cancellation of a policy at renewal
A producer's refusal to follow the agency agreement

questions.explanation: Ratification retroactively validates an unauthorized act once the principal learns the facts and accepts it. It is approval after the fact, not refusal or rate-setting.

questions.question: An insurance binder is best defined as:

answers.text: A temporary agreement providing insurance coverage until the policy is issued or the binder expires or is replaced
A permanent policy that never needs to be issued in written form
A receipt proving the insured paid more premium than was owed
A certificate that guarantees coverage for losses before the binder date

questions.explanation: A binder is interim proof and evidence of coverage for a short period until the formal policy follows or the binder ends. It does not create permanent coverage or reach back to losses before it took effect.

questions.question: A loss payee endorsement on equipment in Nashua primarily protects whom, and how?

answers.text: The lender or lessor, by directing loss payment for that equipment to it as its interest appears
The equipment vendor, by guaranteeing its sales price on every return
The producer, by guaranteeing commission after a loss
The insured's customers, by paying them for late deliveries

questions.explanation: Loss payee status is about the property claim check, not liability status. It ensures a party with a financial interest in damaged equipment is paid to the extent of that interest.

questions.question: Which item is an additional coverage commonly found in the dwelling forms?

answers.text: Payment for gradual deterioration over many years
Debris removal after a covered loss, subject to the form's limit
Payment for flood damage with no endorsement
A guarantee of the home's resale value

questions.explanation: Debris removal is a standard additional coverage tied to a covered loss. Gradual deterioration is a classic noncovered cause, so pairing debris removal with deterioration confuses a covered extra with an excluded condition.

questions.question: What is the classic coverage structure of the HO-3 Special Form?

answers.text: Named perils for everything
No coverage for personal property
Open perils for the dwelling and other structures, and broad named perils for personal property
Open perils for everything including contents

questions.explanation: The special form's split treatment is its defining feature: structures on an open-perils basis and contents on named perils. Giving contents the same open-perils grant describes the comprehensive form instead.

questions.question: A Nashua claimant submits receipts for a hotel stay after a covered fire, but the dates include two nights before the fire occurred. Adjuster Lee should:

answers.text: Ask the claimant to explain the discrepancy, verify the records, and pay only the amounts properly supported as covered
Deny the entire claim automatically and report the claimant for prosecution
Pay the full receipts without questions to maintain goodwill
Add extra nights to the payment to offset the confusion

questions.explanation: A date mismatch may be error or padding; verification and a chance to explain come first, with payment limited to what is supported. Automatic prosecution referrals and unquestioning payment both skip the investigation.

questions.question: The insuring agreement of a liability policy most characteristically promises to:

answers.text: Pay damages the insured becomes legally obligated to pay for covered injury or damage, subject to the policy terms
Repair the insured's own building in every lawsuit
Set the insured's premium for the next five years
List the insured's mailing address and mortgagee

questions.explanation: Liability insuring agreements promise payment of legally obligated damages (and typically defense). Listing addresses and mortgagees is declarations work, not the liability promise.

questions.question: How does evidence of coverage for a condominium lender differ in purpose from a simple certificate holder's copy?

answers.text: It makes the lender a named insured for liability losses
It waives the borrower's deductible for the lender
Evidence forms for lenders identify the property, the mortgagee interest, and renewal or cancellation provisions relevant to that interest
It guarantees the loan balance will be paid after any fire

questions.explanation: Lender evidence is property-focused: it ties coverage to a specific building and loan interest so the mortgagee can protect its collateral, without turning the lender into a liability insured.

questions.question: Adjuster Noah is reviewing a claim under an open perils form for a Lebanon restaurant where a refrigeration unit malfunctioned in an unusual accidental way that the form never mentions. No exclusion fits. Noah should:

answers.text: Require the owner to add the cause by endorsement after the loss
Treat the cause as within the open perils grant and proceed to value the covered damage
Reclassify the claim as a named perils claim and apply the Basic list
Deny solely because the cause is not named in the form

questions.explanation: Denying an open-perils claim solely because the cause is unnamed misapplies the form. If the loss is fortuitous, direct and not excluded, Noah values the damage rather than demanding a post-loss endorsement.

questions.question: Landlord Rosa in Claremont knows a porch step is rotted, does nothing for weeks, and a guest falls when it gives way. The strongest negligence fact against Rosa is:

answers.text: She is liable only if she intended the guest to fall
The guest must prove Rosa owned the property for more than ten years
She had notice of a dangerous condition, owed guests reasonable care, and breached that duty by failing to repair or warn
A landlord can never be liable for a guest's injury

questions.explanation: Notice of the hazard plus inaction supports breach of the duty to keep premises reasonably safe or warn of hidden dangers. Negligence does not require intent to injure, and length of ownership is not an element.

questions.question: Governmental action exclusion in Section I generally excludes what?

answers.text: Any loss that a city inspector happens to view
Loss from destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of a governmental authority, subject to stated exceptions such as certain demolition to prevent fire spread
The cost of a building permit for voluntary remodeling
A traffic ticket owed by the insured

questions.explanation: The exclusion targets government-ordered destruction or seizure. A permit fee for voluntary work is not a loss by governmental destruction, though code-upgrade costs raise a separate ordinance issue.

questions.question: An insured acquires a car when the current policy provides liability only and asks for collision on day 20 for an accident that happened on day 5. What is the issue?

answers.text: Collision is automatic retroactively for any earlier loss
The day-5 loss creates the coverage by itself
Liability limits convert into collision coverage
Physical damage for the new auto generally requires a timely request and inspection conditions; coverage cannot be created after a known loss

questions.explanation: An insured cannot wait for a loss and then buy damage coverage for it; the request timing and the form's physical damage conditions decide the new auto's protection.

questions.question: A lender is named on a Laconia cabin policy. If the cabin is destroyed by a covered fire, the lender's insurable interest is best measured by:

answers.text: The full replacement cost in all cases regardless of debt
The amount of the borrower's life insurance
The outstanding loan balance secured by the cabin
The borrower's total net worth

questions.explanation: A mortgagee's interest is limited to its financial stake — the debt secured by the property. Replacement cost may exceed that stake and belongs to the owner's interest, not the lender's.

questions.question: A Manchester shop has Broad-form coverage. A plumbing supply line suddenly bursts and discharges water that ruins inventory. Which statement is most accurate, assuming no exclusion in the stem changes the result?

answers.text: The loss is covered only if the pipe was struck by lightning
Accidental discharge or leakage of water from a plumbing system is a Broad-form peril
Only fire and lightning losses are covered under Broad form
Water damage of any kind, including a river flood, is covered under Broad form

questions.explanation: Broad form includes accidental discharge or leakage from plumbing, heating, air-conditioning or similar systems. That protection is not the same as flood coverage, and a river flood remains a different cause of loss.

questions.question: An additional insured endorsement on a liability policy typically does NOT give the additional insured the right to:

answers.text: Cancel or materially change the named insured's policy
Be notified in the manner the endorsement or policy provides for certain changes
Receive a defense for a covered suit within the endorsement's scope
Present a covered claim under the endorsement

questions.explanation: Additional insured status grants specified coverage rights, not control over the named insured's contract. Cancellation and material changes remain the named insured's and insurer's province, subject to any notice the form promises.

questions.question: Priya adjusts a severe storm roof claim in Nashua on a DP-2 policy. Wind lifts shingles and rain enters through the wind-created opening. Why does the broad form matter here?

answers.text: Windstorm is never covered under any dwelling form
The loss must be handled only as a flood claim
Rain alone, with no covered peril, automatically creates coverage
Windstorm is a covered broad-form peril, so ensuing water damage through the opening the wind created is analyzed as part of that covered loss

questions.explanation: Windstorm coverage is central here because the interior water damage followed a wind-created opening. Rain entering with no covered cause and no opening would present a very different and generally uncovered fact pattern.

questions.question: Scenario: A total loss car in Concord has a supported market value of $14,200 in the stem. The collision deductible stated is $500. No other adjustments apply. What is the settlement?

answers.text: $13,700 — the supported value minus the stated deductible
$7,100, half the value
$14,700, value plus deductible
$14,200, with no deductible on a total loss

questions.explanation: Total losses still apply the applicable deductible: $14,200 minus $500 equals $13,700 payable before any separately handled tax or fee items.

questions.question: A Portsmouth condo owner asks why his claim payment was less than his repair bill even though the damage was below the limit. The adjuster's most likely correct explanations involve:

answers.text: A requirement that insureds absorb half of every loss by law
A rule that adjusters always subtract an arbitrary percentage
The insurer's right to keep part of every payment for overhead
The deductible and any depreciation or coinsurance adjustment provided by the policy

questions.explanation: Shortfalls below the limit normally trace to the deductible, depreciation under an actual-cash-value basis, or coinsurance. Arbitrary withholdings and invented half-loss laws are not legitimate explanations.

questions.question: All of the following are typically required considerations before punitive damages are awarded EXCEPT:

answers.text: There generally must be an underlying compensable injury or compensatory award
The conduct must be shown to be malicious, wanton, reckless or otherwise more culpable than ordinary negligence
The amount must bear a reasonable relationship to the harm and the conduct
The claimant must prove the exact dollar amount of punitive damages from an invoice

questions.explanation: Punitive damages are not invoiced items; the amount is set by the fact-finder within constitutional and legal limits tied to culpability and harm. Ordinary negligence alone is usually not culpable enough to support them.

questions.question: An adjuster asks homeowner Noah in Dover to separate damaged from undamaged property and make the damaged items available for inspection. Under what duty does this fall?

answers.text: The duty to show and preserve damaged property and cooperate with the investigation as the conditions require
The duty belongs only to the mortgage company
No duty, because inspection is optional for the insured
The liability defense duty

questions.explanation: Cooperation and inspection duties let the insurer verify the loss it is asked to pay. Refusing all inspection while demanding payment contradicts the conditions the insured agreed to.

nevada-business-law.quiz_title: Nevada Business and Law Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why does the licensing regime care how a Nevada construction firm in Fallon advertises?

answers.text: Because only licensed firms may advertise at all, in any medium

Because advertising is where the public meets the license: the firm's licensed identity must be presented honestly, so the public can tell who is licensed, for what, and under whose authority it contracts
Because advertising replaces the need for a license number anywhere else
Because the Board approves the firm's logo design

questions.explanation: Honest, identifiable advertising lets the public verify the license behind the offer.

questions.question: How should overtime be authorized and controlled at a Nevada construction firm in Elko without violating pay duties?

answers.text: By editing time records to the approved hours
By refusing to pay unapproved overtime
By averaging hours across the pay period
By requiring advance approval as a management rule and enforcing it through scheduling and discipline — while still paying for any overtime actually worked, approved or not

questions.explanation: Control the behavior, never the pay: the firm manages approval, the law manages payment.

questions.question: What is the annual summary duty that closes the recordkeeping year at a Nevada design-build contracting firm in Fallon?

answers.text: Posting only in years with no injuries
Destroying the log after review
Posting the year's injury and illness summary where employees can see it, for the posting period the rules prescribe, certified by a company executive as examined and true
Mailing the log to every client

questions.explanation: Posting makes the record visible to the workforce it describes, with an executive's certification behind it.

questions.question: How does the pay-period definition at a Nevada contracting firm in Winnemucca interact with overtime compliance?

answers.text: Only monthly-paid staff earn overtime
Overtime is computed on the workweek regardless of how often paychecks are issued; a biweekly pay period does not permit blending a heavy week with a light one
Pay periods erase weekly overtime
Overtime is computed per pay period by law

questions.explanation: The workweek is the unit of overtime law; the pay period is only a payment schedule.

questions.question: What must a Nevada contracting firm in Elko report to the Board between renewals?

answers.text: Nothing at all until the next renewal arrives
Every bid it submits, winning or not

Changes the Board's rules make reportable -- in its qualifiers, its ownership or control, its address, and its classification standing -- because the license on file must describe the firm as it actually is
The names of all its customers each month

questions.explanation: Licensure is a continuing representation; material changes are reported as they happen, not discovered at renewal.

questions.question: Why must the estimator and the field team of a Nevada construction firm in Reno reconcile estimated costs with actual job costs after completion?

answers.text: Because the surety sets next year's tax rate from it
Because the comparison calibrates the firm's cost data: variances show which production rates and prices were wrong, making the next estimate rest on the firm's own proven numbers
Because the board audits every completed job
Because owners require a post-job report

questions.explanation: Estimating improves only by feedback; actuals are the firm's private cost library.

questions.question: What does the unemployment-insurance tax on a Nevada contracting firm in Boulder City fund, and what drives the rate the firm experiences?

answers.text: It funds the firm's retirement plan
It is a voluntary charitable contribution
Every firm pays the founder's personal rate
It funds benefits for workers who lose jobs through no fault of their own, and the firm's experience — its history of claims — moves its rate, rewarding stable employment

questions.explanation: Experience rating ties the tax to the firm's own layoff history: steadier firms pay less.

questions.question: How should a Nevada building contracting company in Fernley handle a dispute with an owner while work remains unfinished?

answers.text: Remove materials from the site as leverage
Stop all work until the owner agrees to everything
Bill disputed amounts as retainage

Follow the contract's dispute process, keep performing as the contract requires unless lawfully excused, and document the dispute contemporaneously — self-help stoppages usually worsen both the legal position and the loss

questions.explanation: Contracts design dispute lanes precisely so projects finish while disagreements are resolved inside them.

questions.question: Why does a Nevada contracting business in Fallon confirm that its bid includes the correct sales and use tax treatment for materials?

answers.text: Because materials are never taxed in construction
Because the testing company grades tax treatment
Because owners reimburse all taxes separately by law
Because tax on materials is a real cost of the work in the applicable treatment, and omitting or misapplying it understates the bid by that amount on every affected item

questions.explanation: Tax treatment is a cost input like any other; the estimate must carry the treatment the law applies.

questions.question: Why does the choice of entity form matter to the surety and lender of a Nevada construction firm in Boulder City?

answers.text: Because lenders ignore entity form entirely
Because entity form sets trade exam scores
Because form shapes who is liable, how ownership transfers, and what the financial statements represent — underwriters read the entity to know whose credit and indemnity stand behind the firm
Because sureties lend only to sole proprietors

questions.explanation: Credit follows liability; form tells the underwriter where liability lives.

questions.question: How must a Nevada building contracting company in Spring Creek handle hazardous waste its work generates, in principle?

answers.text: Identify it, containerize and label it, store it safely for no longer than the rules allow, and ship it only through authorized transporters to authorized facilities, with the paperwork the law prescribes
Leave it on site for the owner to discover
Burn it at the site boundary
Mix it with ordinary debris to dilute it

questions.explanation: Hazardous waste is a chain of custody from generation to disposal; every link is a duty, not a preference.

questions.question: Why does a sole proprietorship offer a Nevada contracting firm in Yerington simplicity at the price of personal risk?

answers.text: Because the form requires no records at all
Because the state forbids proprietors from hiring
Because proprietors pay no taxes
Because no separate entity exists: the owner is the business, contracting, owning, and owing in one person — formation is effortless and liability is unlimited for the same reason

questions.explanation: One person, one legal identity: ease and exposure are the same fact viewed from two sides.

questions.question: A contract held by a Nevada construction firm in Yerington states a contract amount of $240,000 and retainage of 5% of the contract amount, using the rate stated in the contract here. How much retainage is withheld in total at that rate?
questions.explanation: Retainage withheld = 5% of 240,000 = $12,000.

questions.question: What is the manager's correct response at a Nevada design-build contracting firm in Mesquite when the schedule shows the critical path slipping?

answers.text: Act on the path itself: resequence, add resources, or recover time on critical activities, and address the contractual notice duties for delay — effort spent on non-critical work does not move the finish date
Extend the contract date unilaterally
Accelerate activities with the most float
Wait for the next monthly update

questions.explanation: Recovery must land on the critical chain; elsewhere it spends money without buying time.

questions.question: How should a Nevada construction firm in Laughlin treat a customer's request to split one job into smaller contracts, each under its monetary limit?

answers.text: As acceptable whenever separate invoices are issued
As a proper way to use the limit, if the customer asks
As a matter for the firm's bookkeeper alone
As an evasion to refuse: the limit measures the work the licensee undertakes, and dividing one undertaking on paper does not bring work beyond the limit inside the license

questions.explanation: Limits are applied to the substance of the undertaking, not to how the paperwork is sliced.

questions.question: Why does a Nevada building contracting company in Las Vegas verify identity and work authorization at hiring rather than after a problem arises?

answers.text: Because verification expires monthly
Because banks require it for direct deposit
Because the verification duty attaches at hire, with prescribed documents examined and the form completed and retained then; later reconstruction does not satisfy a duty timed to the hiring event
Because the board assigns crews

questions.explanation: Timing is part of the duty: at hire, documented, retained.

questions.question: A contract held by a Nevada contracting firm in Carson City has a price of $600,000. The job is 90% complete. What is the earned revenue, computed as contract price times percent complete?
questions.explanation: Earned revenue = 600,000 x 90% = $540,000.

questions.question: The current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities. A nevada contracting business in pahrump reports current assets of $125,000 and current liabilities of $100,000. What is its current ratio?
What is professional liability (errors and omissions) coverage's place for a design-build firm like a Nevada design-build contracting firm in Mesquite?

answers.text: It responds to claims from the firm's design and professional services — negligence in the professional work itself — which general liability does not cover
It replaces general liability entirely
It guarantees design approval by owners
It covers employee injuries

questions.explanation: When the firm designs as well as builds, a second liability family appears, needing its own policy.

questions.question: A contract held by a Nevada contracting firm in Gardnerville states a contract amount of $50,000 and retainage of 10% of the contract amount, using the rate stated in the contract here. How much retainage is withheld in total at that rate?
questions.explanation: Retainage withheld = 10% of 50,000 = $5,000.

new-york-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: New York Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Implied authority allows a producer to do which of the following?

answers.text: Perform acts reasonably necessary to carry out the express authority granted
Bind any risk at any limit the producer chooses
Change state licensing law for a single client
Waive the insurer's underwriting guidelines at will

questions.explanation: Implied authority covers incidental acts needed to exercise express powers, like completing standard forms. It does not stretch to unlimited binding or rewriting insurer guidelines.

questions.question: What is the practical difference between a misrepresentation and a breach of warranty for coverage?

answers.text: A warranty never affects coverage under any circumstances
Misrepresentation can only occur after a loss happens
A misrepresentation generally must be material to affect coverage, while a warranty is a strict condition of the contract
There is no difference; the terms are fully interchangeable

questions.explanation: Materiality is the gate for misrepresentation remedies, whereas warranties bind as contract conditions. Timing also differs: misrepresentation typically occurs in the application before inception, not only after a loss.

questions.question: A fraternal benefit society provides insurance benefits primarily to:

answers.text: Any member of the general public who walks in
Its members, who belong to the society's lodge or membership system
Only stockholders who buy shares
Employees of the state insurance department

questions.explanation: Fraternal insurers operate for their members under a lodge system. Membership, not share ownership, is the gateway to their insurance benefits.

questions.question: Nominal damages are best described as:

answers.text: A small symbolic award recognizing that a legal right was violated when little or no actual loss is proved
The largest possible punitive award in a case
A payment equal to the full policy limit
An advance payment for future medical treatment

questions.explanation: Nominal damages vindicate a right with a token amount when actual loss is minimal or unproved. They are the opposite of a maximum punitive award and are unrelated to policy limits or medical advances.

questions.question: Strict liability differs from negligence primarily because:

answers.text: Strict liability applies only to written contracts
Damages are never awarded under strict liability
The claimant must prove the defendant intended the exact injury
Liability can be imposed without proof of careless conduct for certain activities or defective products

questions.explanation: Strict liability focuses on the activity or product and the resulting harm rather than on whether the defendant behaved carelessly. It also does not require proof of intent to cause the specific injury.

questions.question: Why does insurance fraud matter to honest policyholders as a business matter?

answers.text: Fraud lowers everyone's premiums by increasing claim volume
Fraudulent payments raise loss costs, which are ultimately reflected in the premiums honest insureds pay
Fraud has no financial effect outside the single claim
Fraud only affects the insurer's advertising budget

questions.explanation: Claim costs feed pricing, so fraud losses are spread across the pool of honest customers. Fraud therefore harms the customer base, not just one file.

questions.question: The insuring agreement of a liability policy most characteristically promises to:

answers.text: Pay damages the insured becomes legally obligated to pay for covered injury or damage, subject to the policy terms
Repair the insured's own building in every lawsuit
Set the insured's premium for the next five years
List the insured's mailing address and mortgagee

questions.explanation: Liability insuring agreements promise payment of legally obligated damages (and typically defense). Listing addresses and mortgagees is declarations work, not the liability promise.

questions.question: A Albany fire loss is covered by two property policies on the same interest. The other-insurance clause in each policy primarily determines:

answers.text: How the loss is apportioned between the insurers
Which adjuster gets promoted after the claim
The resale value of the damaged building
Whether the insured must pay two deductibles to the state

questions.explanation: Other-insurance provisions allocate a shared loss among covering policies, commonly pro rata by limits. They do not govern personnel matters or state fees.

questions.question: An insured with Special-form coverage suffers direct physical loss from a cause the form does not name and does not exclude or limit. The usual result is:

answers.text: The loss is paid only at actual cash value even if the policy is on a replacement cost basis
The loss is covered because Special form is written on an open-perils basis
The loss is denied because every covered cause must be named
The loss is covered only if a Basic-form peril also occurred

questions.explanation: Under Special form, a cause does not need to be named to be covered; it needs to avoid the exclusions and limitations. Requiring the cause to be named would turn Special form back into a named-perils form.

questions.question: Which form is most commonly used as evidence of property insurance for a mortgagee with an interest in a Rochester office building?

answers.text: An evidence of property insurance form showing the mortgagee interest and property coverage
A liability certificate listing general liability limits only
An auto identification card for the building owner
A workers compensation certificate of coverage

questions.explanation: Property evidence forms are designed to show building coverage, mortgagee interests, and loss payee information, while a liability certificate addresses third-party liability limits instead.

questions.question: The phrase 'all risk' in connection with open perils coverage is potentially misleading because:

answers.text: Open perils coverage applies only to liability losses
Open perils policies cover fewer perils than Basic named perils policies
The policy still contains exclusions, limitations and conditions, so not literally every risk is covered
The phrase means the insured bears all the risk with no insurance

questions.explanation: All-risk is informal shorthand for open perils, not a promise to pay every loss. Reading the exclusions and conditions remains essential, which is why adjusters should use the term special or open perils in file notes.

questions.question: Efficient proximate cause doctrine holds that when a loss follows a chain of events:

answers.text: The adjuster may select the cause that produces the lowest payment
Every cause in the chain must be covered or nothing is covered
Coverage is determined by the peril that set the chain in motion, if that peril is the efficient or dominant cause
Coverage is always determined by the last event to touch the property, no matter what started the chain

questions.explanation: The doctrine looks to the cause that started the train of events in motion, not mechanically to the last link. It also forbids picking a cause based on which outcome is cheapest for the insurer.

questions.question: Adjuster Marco is handling a Buffalo fire claim. The insured demands payment from two insurers for the full amount of the same loss from each. Marco correctly explains that indemnity:

answers.text: Lets the insured choose the higher of the two payments plus the lower one
Requires each insurer to pay the full loss independently
Applies only to liability claims and never to property
Prevents recovering more than the actual loss for the same damage

questions.explanation: Other-insurance and indemnity principles coordinate payments so total recovery does not exceed the loss. Paying the full loss twice, the demand here, is exactly what indemnity forbids.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of a physical hazard EXCEPT:

answers.text: Worn tires on a delivery van
Icy steps outside a Kingston storefront
A frayed electrical cord in a Buffalo warehouse
A driver who regularly texts while driving on I-87 near Albany

questions.explanation: Texting while driving reflects careless behavior, a moral or morale concern, not a physical condition of property. Worn tires, icy steps, and frayed cords are tangible physical conditions that increase loss risk.

questions.question: All of the following are common reasons an insurer may cancel mid-term, subject to required notice and applicable law, EXCEPT:

answers.text: The insurer's preference for a different logo on its policy forms
A substantial increase in the hazard insured against
Nonpayment of premium
Material misrepresentation in obtaining the policy

questions.explanation: Nonpayment, material misrepresentation and substantial hazard increase are recognized cancellation grounds when statutory notice rules are followed. Branding preferences about policy-form logos are not a ground to cancel a customer's coverage mid-term.

questions.question: EXCEPT — Which of the following is NOT accomplished by an endorsement?

answers.text: Retroactively erasing a loss that has already occurred from the claim record
Adding an additional insured for liability coverage
Adding a newly purchased vehicle to a commercial auto policy
Raising a property limit after a values increase

questions.explanation: Endorsements change contract terms going forward or as agreed from an effective date, but they do not rewrite history to make a known, already-occurred loss disappear.

questions.question: All of the following are characteristics of an agreed value provision EXCEPT:

answers.text: When it applies, a coinsurance penalty is typically suspended for covered losses
The insurer and insured agree in advance on the value used for loss settlement
It is commonly used for unique or hard-to-value property
It requires the insured to prove the property's value again after every loss before payment

questions.explanation: Agreed value is set before the loss, so the parties do not re-prove that agreed value after the loss in order to use it. The advance agreement is precisely what distinguishes this method, and it commonly suspends a coinsurance penalty while it is in effect.

questions.question: A Syracuse condo owner asks why his claim payment was less than his repair bill even though the damage was below the limit. The adjuster's most likely correct explanations involve:

answers.text: A requirement that insureds absorb half of every loss by law
The insurer's right to keep part of every payment for overhead
The deductible and any depreciation or coinsurance adjustment provided by the policy
A rule that adjusters always subtract an arbitrary percentage

questions.explanation: Shortfalls below the limit normally trace to the deductible, depreciation under an actual-cash-value basis, or coinsurance. Arbitrary withholdings and invented half-loss laws are not legitimate explanations.

questions.question: All of the following statements about a competent party to a contract are generally true EXCEPT:

answers.text: A minor's contract is generally voidable by the minor
Parties must be of legal age to be fully bound in most cases
A person under the influence may lack capacity in some circumstances
A person adjudicated mentally incompetent can bind an insurer by signing an application alone

questions.explanation: Someone adjudicated incompetent generally lacks capacity to form a binding contract alone. A minor's voidable contract status, the closest contrast, is a recognized capacity limitation rather than full binding power.

questions.question: A Kingston landlord is an additional insured on its tenant's liability policy. The tenant's employee negligently injures a customer, who sues the landlord claiming the landlord is responsible for the tenant's operations. The landlord's additional insured status is relevant because:

answers.text: The landlord's status converts the tenant's policy into a property policy for the building
The suit is automatically dismissed whenever a landlord is an additional insured
Additional insured status makes the landlord responsible for the tenant's premium
The claim arises from the named insured tenant's operations, which is the kind of liability additional insured endorsements are designed to reach

questions.explanation: The endorsement responds to liability asserted against the additional insured arising from the named insured's operations — exactly this suit's theory. It does not shift premium duty, change the policy type or dismiss the case.

oregon-business-law.quiz_title: Oregon Business and Law Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What should an Oregon contracting firm in Medford verify before it starts any new category of work?

answers.text: Only that the customer can pay
That its license and endorsement cover that category, its bond and insurance are in force, and any project-level requirements are met
Nothing beyond its general experience
Only that materials are available

questions.explanation: Scope, bond, and insurance are checked before work begins, not after a problem arises.

questions.question: What is the difference between a conditional and an unconditional lien release for an Oregon construction firm in Klamath Falls?

answers.text: A conditional release takes effect when the payment it recites is actually received and clears; an unconditional one is effective as given, whether or not the money arrives
Unconditional releases wait for payment by definition
The two are identical in effect
Conditional releases are unenforceable

questions.explanation: Never give an unconditional release against money not yet in hand.

questions.question: What is the environmental duty of an Oregon general contracting company in Beaverton in its construction work?

answers.text: To leave environmental matters to the owner in all cases
To perform the work so that soil, water, and air are protected as the environmental laws and its permits require, treating those duties as part of the work itself
To landscape the site attractively at the end
To comply only when an inspector is present

questions.explanation: Environmental compliance is built into method, not added as decoration.

questions.question: Which statement about the license of an Oregon general contracting company in Roseburg is correct?

answers.text: The license is a continuing permission conditioned on ongoing compliance -- bond, insurance, truthful dealing, and work within endorsement -- not a one-time purchase of a permanent right
Compliance duties end after the first renewal
Once granted, a license can never be disciplined
The license guarantees the firm's workmanship

questions.explanation: Licensure is conditional and continuing; the Board's authority over the licensee does not lapse after grant.

questions.question: Which statement about the license of an Oregon contracting firm in Medford is correct?

answers.text: The license guarantees the firm's workmanship
Once granted, a license can never be disciplined
Compliance duties end after the first renewal
The license is a continuing permission conditioned on ongoing compliance -- bond, insurance, truthful dealing, and work within endorsement -- not a one-time purchase of a permanent right

questions.explanation: Licensure is conditional and continuing; the Board's authority over the licensee does not lapse after grant.

questions.question: What is an operating agreement for an Oregon design-build contracting firm in Corvallis if it is a limited liability company?

answers.text: A permit issued by the building department
The owners' own agreement governing management, contributions, distributions, and what happens when an owner leaves or the company winds up
A contract with the firm's largest customer
The company's advertising plan

questions.explanation: The operating agreement is the company's internal constitution among its owners.

questions.question: When may an Oregon design-build contracting firm in Albany suspend its work for non-payment?

answers.text: At any moment payment feels slow
Only if the crew votes for it
Never, under any circumstances
When the contract and the law give that right -- typically on defined notice after a payment default -- rather than by walking off at the first late day

questions.explanation: Suspension is a conditioned remedy, used by the contract's steps.

questions.question: Who administers the building code on a project of an Oregon contracting business in Roseburg?

answers.text: The project's lender
The material suppliers jointly
The local building department and its officials, who review plans, issue permits, and inspect the work under the code the jurisdiction has adopted
The firm's trade association

questions.explanation: The authority having jurisdiction administers the code locally.

questions.question: Why should equipment costs be charged to jobs by an Oregon general contracting company in Eugene?

answers.text: Charging equipment is double counting by definition
Only hired equipment has a cost
Because machines consumed by a project are a real cost of that project; uncharged equipment flatters job margins and starves replacement planning
Owned equipment works for free

questions.explanation: Owned steel still costs money every hour it turns.

questions.question: How much time do candidates have for this examination, and where is it given?

answers.text: Candidates have 180 minutes for the scored portion, at PSI test centers or remotely proctored
Candidates have 120 minutes, at a monthly paper sitting only
