Candidates have 330 minutes, twice a year at the Board's office
Time is unlimited on the day of the sitting

questions.explanation: The published sitting allows 180 minutes for the scored portion, at test centers or remotely proctored.

questions.question: Why must an Oregon general contracting company in Medford never discuss its bid with competitors?

answers.text: Coordination among bidders on price or allocation of work is unlawful bid rigging, destroying the competition the process exists to create
Only written collusion is a problem
Discussion is lawful if friendly
Competitors may set a floor price together

questions.explanation: Compete on your own figure, arrived at alone.

questions.question: Why may an Oregon construction firm in Klamath Falls not simply let its license lapse and keep working while a renewal is prepared?

answers.text: Because there is no grace in the work itself: contracting while unlicensed is unlicensed contracting, whatever the firm's intentions about renewing
Because a lapsed license doubles the firm's bond automatically
Because customers may not pay a renewing firm
Because renewal paperwork is quicker than working

questions.explanation: The right to contract flows from a live license; an expired license confers no more authority than none at all.

questions.question: Why must an Oregon contracting business in Pendleton classify each worker's duties honestly for workers' compensation purposes?

answers.text: Because premiums and coverage follow the real risk of the work performed; misdescribing duties understates premium and endangers cover when a claim comes
Classification for compensation is a marketing choice
Duties need not match the work actually done
The cheapest class may always be used

questions.explanation: Compensation classification must mirror the work as it truly is.

questions.question: What should an estimator for an Oregon building contracting company in Redmond do about items the documents describe unclearly?

answers.text: Omit the item and hope it vanishes
Assume the cheapest reading and stay silent
Seek clarification through the bid process, or qualify and price the risk openly -- never silently assume the cheapest reading
Price it at zero to win the work

questions.explanation: Unclear scope is a question to raise or a risk to price, never a gift to assume.

questions.question: Why must expansion and movement joints in the envelope of an Oregon construction firm in Corvallis be detailed, not just cut?

answers.text: Joints may be left open if narrow
Because the joint must keep water and air control while the building moves; an unsealed slot is a designed leak, not a movement provision
Movement joints are purely structural
Sealing a joint prevents its movement in all cases

questions.explanation: Accommodate movement and exclude weather: the detail must do both.

questions.question: Why should an Oregon design-build contracting firm in Bend pay workers through traceable payroll rather than in cash off the books?

answers.text: Cash pay is lawful if both sides agree
Off-book pay only risks a minor fee
Off-the-books pay defeats tax withholding, wage records, compensation cover, and the worker's own protections, and exposes the firm on every one of those fronts
Records are optional for small crews

questions.explanation: Payroll is a legal system, not a payment style.

questions.question: Why are the licensing duties of an Oregon contracting business in Ashland not waived when it works for a friend or a repeat customer?

answers.text: Repeat customers are deemed licensed themselves
Duties apply only to strangers
Small informal jobs are outside the law entirely
Because the duties protect the public and the integrity of the scheme, not merely the immediate customer, so private familiarity cannot displace them

questions.explanation: Licensing duties follow the work, whoever the customer is.

questions.question: A subcontractor offers an Oregon general contracting company in Medford a much lower price than every competitor. What is the prudent response?

answers.text: Award instantly; the lowest price is always best
Probe the bid for missed scope, misunderstanding, or unsustainable pricing before awarding, because a failing subcontractor costs more than a sound price saves
Assume the competitor bids were collusive
Ignore scope and rely on the subcontract to cure everything

questions.explanation: A price far below the field is a question to answer, not a gift to grab.

questions.question: Why must protective equipment be the last line, not the first plan, for an Oregon design-build contracting firm in Medford?

answers.text: Because the hierarchy of controls removes or engineers out the hazard before relying on what a worker wears; equipment fails, is forgotten, and fits imperfectly
Eliminating hazards is forbidden if equipment exists
Engineering controls are optional luxuries
Equipment is always the strongest control

questions.explanation: Remove the hazard first; dress the worker for what remains.

questions.question: A supplier invoice to an Oregon design-build contracting firm in Klamath Falls totals $8,000. The supplier's terms, as printed on the invoice, offer a discount of 2% for payment inside the discount period. If the firm pays inside the period, what net amount does it pay?

mississippi-business-law.quiz_title: Mississippi Law and Business Management Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is a qualifying party, in the licensure of a Mississippi construction firm in Vicksburg?

answers.text: The firm's outside accountant
The designated individual whose examinations and standing qualify the firm: the license is issued to the entity, but it rests on a named person the board has qualified for the work the firm performs
Any employee the firm designates for payroll purposes
The owner of the largest project the firm has built

questions.explanation: Entity licensure needs a competence anchor; the qualifying party is that anchor.

questions.question: What is substantial completion, and why does it matter to the managers of a Mississippi design-build contracting firm in Hattiesburg?

answers.text: Any date the contractor chooses
The day the contract is signed
The day the last invoice is paid

The stage at which the work is sufficiently complete for the owner to occupy or use it for its intended purpose — the point that typically starts warranties, shifts some risks, and triggers punch-list and payment milestones

questions.explanation: Substantial completion is the project's hinge: use begins, and many contractual clocks start.

questions.question: What is the published name of the examination this practice bank prepares candidates for?

answers.text: Mississippi Commercial Contractors Business Examination
Law and Business Management Examination -- that is its published name; the shorter label Mississippi Business and Law is a vendor shorthand, not the published name
The national business and law examination for Mississippi
Mississippi Business and Law Examination, as the shorthand has it

questions.explanation: The bulletin heads the examination Law and Business Management Examination; the shorter vendor label is not its published name.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the employment-eligibility verification duty when a Mississippi design-build contracting firm in Olive Branch hires?

answers.text: To register the employee with the licensing board
To confirm, through the prescribed documents and form completed at hiring, that each new employee is authorized to work — a record the firm must keep and be able to produce
To enroll the employee in the union
To set the employee's wage rate

questions.explanation: Verification at hiring, documented and retained, is the employer's proof of a lawful workforce.

questions.question: What is risk management's working definition at a Mississippi contracting firm in Jackson?

answers.text: Avoiding all risky work
Buying the cheapest insurance available
The discipline of identifying the losses the firm is exposed to, then deciding for each whether to avoid, reduce, transfer, or retain it — deliberately, before the loss chooses for the firm
Transferring every risk to subcontractors

questions.explanation: Management is decision before event: name the risk, pick the treatment, on paper.

questions.question: How should a Mississippi building contracting company in Southaven price work it will self-perform versus work it will subcontract when building a bid?

answers.text: Subcontracted work needs no verification
Self-performed work carries no overhead

Self-performed work is priced from the firm's own labor, material, and equipment costs; subcontracted work is priced from verified subcontractor quotes — and the estimate keeps the two visibly separate
Both are priced from subcontractor quotes for consistency

questions.explanation: The price source follows the performer: own costs for own work, checked quotes for others' work.

questions.question: How should a supervisor at a Mississippi construction firm in Olive Branch handle an employee who works through lunch without being asked?

answers.text: Pay double as a bonus
The time is still hours worked if the firm knows or should know the work was performed: the firm must pay for it and manage the behavior through discipline or scheduling, not by deleting the time
Delete the time; unapproved work is unpaid
Ignore it unless the client complains

questions.explanation: Suffered-or-permitted work is payable work; the remedy for unwanted hours is management, not non-payment.

questions.question: Why does the choice of entity form matter to the surety and lender of a Mississippi building contracting company in Olive Branch?

answers.text: Because sureties lend only to sole proprietors
Because lenders ignore entity form entirely
Because entity form sets trade exam scores
Because form shapes who is liable, how ownership transfers, and what the financial statements represent — underwriters read the entity to know whose credit and indemnity stand behind the firm

questions.explanation: Credit follows liability; form tells the underwriter where liability lives.

questions.question: How should a Mississippi building contracting company in Pascagoula price work it will self-perform versus work it will subcontract when building a bid?

answers.text: Self-performed work is priced from the firm's own labor, material, and equipment costs; subcontracted work is priced from verified subcontractor quotes — and the estimate keeps the two visibly separate
Self-performed work carries no overhead
Both are priced from subcontractor quotes for consistency
Subcontracted work needs no verification

questions.explanation: The price source follows the performer: own costs for own work, checked quotes for others' work.

questions.question: What does an overbilled position on a job of a Mississippi contracting firm in Gulfport represent on its balance sheet?

answers.text: A receivable from the surety
A liability: the firm has billed more than it has earned, so it owes the owner either the work or, in substance, the unearned difference
Proof the job is ahead of schedule
An asset the firm can spend freely

questions.explanation: Billings ahead of earnings are the owner's money in the firm's hands — an obligation, not income.

questions.question: What are the essential elements of an enforceable contract that a Mississippi design-build contracting firm in Pascagoula relies on in every deal?

answers.text: A written form, a witness, and a seal
Offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties, and a legal purpose — the elements whose absence makes an agreement a conversation rather than a contract
Registration with the licensing board
A deposit, a deadline, and a handshake

questions.explanation: The five elements are the checklist between talk and obligation.

questions.question: How should a Mississippi construction firm in Pearl price work it will self-perform versus work it will subcontract when building a bid?

answers.text: Self-performed work carries no overhead
Both are priced from subcontractor quotes for consistency
Subcontracted work needs no verification

Self-performed work is priced from the firm's own labor, material, and equipment costs; subcontracted work is priced from verified subcontractor quotes — and the estimate keeps the two visibly separate

questions.explanation: The price source follows the performer: own costs for own work, checked quotes for others' work.

questions.question: A job of a Mississippi contracting firm in Hernando has a total estimated cost of $215,000 and costs incurred to date of $110,000. What is the cost to complete?
questions.explanation: Cost to complete = total estimated cost - costs incurred = 215,000 - 110,000 = $105,000.

questions.question: A contract of a Mississippi design-build contracting firm in Hattiesburg contains an ambiguity that the parties dispute. What interpretive principle commonly decides it?

answers.text: Ambiguity voids every contract automatically
The owner's reading always wins
The longer document wins
Ambiguity is commonly read against the party that drafted the language, which is why careful parties define their terms and why the drafter bears the cost of its own vagueness

questions.explanation: The construction-against-the-drafter rule prices unclear drafting to its author.

questions.question: What separates a prime contractor from a subcontractor in this licensing scheme, as it applies to a Mississippi design-build contracting firm in Gulfport and the firms it hires?

answers.text: Prime contractors perform all work with their own forces
Prime contractors are always larger firms
The prime contractor contracts directly with the owner and superintends the work; the subcontractor contracts with the prime, or with another subcontractor, rather than with the owner
Subcontractors never need licenses of any kind

questions.explanation: The distinction is the contracting relationship: with the owner, or through the prime.

questions.question: An employee of a Mississippi contracting business in Pascagoula works 45 hours in one week at a regular rate of $32 per hour, with no overtime. What is the employee's gross pay for the week?
questions.explanation: Gross pay = hours x rate = 45 x 32 = $1,440.

questions.question: What should the crew of a Mississippi general contracting company in Greenville do first when a fuel spill reaches bare ground at the site?

answers.text: Stop the source, contain the spread, keep it from drains and waterways, and set the notification and cleanup duties in motion, because minutes decide whether a spill is an incident or a contamination case
Hose the area down into the nearest drain
Cover it with soil and continue work
Wait until the end of the week to report it

questions.explanation: Spill response is a race against migration; containment first, paperwork on its heels.

questions.question: For one pay period, a Mississippi contracting business in Biloxi has gross wages of $10,000. The employer's payroll burden is a charge of 10% of gross wages plus a charge of 4% of gross wages, using only the rates stated here. What is the employer's total payroll cost for the period?
How should a Mississippi contracting firm in Gulfport decide how much risk to retain through deductibles?

answers.text: Retain nothing; insure every dollar
Always choose the largest deductible offered
By matching retention to what the firm can absorb without distress: retain the small, frequent losses it can fund, and transfer the large, rare losses that could break it
Set deductibles by the estimator's preference

questions.explanation: Retention is a cash decision: keep the losses that inconvenience, transfer the ones that kill.

questions.question: On a job for a Mississippi building contracting company in Jackson, costs incurred to date are $180,000 and total estimated cost is $200,000. What is the percent complete, computed as costs incurred divided by total estimated cost?
questions.explanation: Percent complete = 180,000 / 200,000 = 90%.

new-mexico-business-law.quiz_title: New Mexico Business and Law Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why must bids and contracts of a New Mexico contracting firm in Gallup be made in the name on its license?

answers.text: Because any name is acceptable if the owners match
Because contracts require a trade name in all cases
Because the Division taxes names, not firms
So the contracting party the owner deals with is the very entity the Division licensed and can discipline: work offered under another name breaks the link between the license and the work

questions.explanation: The license names its holder; contracting in that name keeps the holder answerable for the work.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a request for information in the project administration of a New Mexico building contracting company in Silver City?

answers.text: To change the contract price automatically

To obtain a documented clarification of the contract documents where they are ambiguous or silent, routed and answered in the project record so the clarified understanding — not corridor conversation — directs the work
To replace the submittal process
To transfer design responsibility to the contractor

questions.explanation: An RFI freezes a question and its answer into the record; undocumented clarifications direct nothing provable.

questions.question: Which body licenses contractors for a New Mexico contracting firm in Hobbs and issues its contractor license?

answers.text: The city building department of its home city
The New Mexico Construction Industries Division, the state division that licenses contractors, sets the classifications under which they may work, and judges the qualifications applicants must meet
The county board of commissioners in the county where the firm is located
The national contractors association, which licenses firms in every state

questions.explanation: Contractor licensure in this state sits with one statewide division; local offices issue permits, not the contractor license.

questions.question: What makes a performance evaluation at a New Mexico construction firm in Los Lunas useful rather than decorative?

answers.text: Specific, contemporaneous observations tied to the job's standards, discussed with the employee and filed — so evaluations guide improvement and, when needed, support personnel decisions with facts
Evaluations written only at termination
Scores copied from the prior year
Vague praise recorded once a year

questions.explanation: An evaluation earns its keep when it is specific enough to act on and honest enough to rely on.

questions.question: Which body licenses contractors for a New Mexico contracting firm in Albuquerque and issues its contractor license?

answers.text: The national contractors association, which licenses firms in every state
The New Mexico Construction Industries Division, the state division that licenses contractors, sets the classifications under which they may work, and judges the qualifications applicants must meet
The city building department of its home city
The county board of commissioners in the county where the firm is located

questions.explanation: Contractor licensure in this state sits with one statewide division; local offices issue permits, not the contractor license.

questions.question: Why does the estimator at a New Mexico construction firm in Farmington note the validity period of each material quote?

answers.text: Because owners require validity certificates
Because validity periods set the project schedule
Because a quote is a price with an expiry: if award or purchasing slips past it, the material may reprice, and the estimate must carry either the firmer quote or an allowance for the movement
Because expired quotes are void as contracts in all cases

questions.explanation: A price is only as good as its dates; the bid inherits every expiry inside it.

questions.question: How should a supervisor at a New Mexico construction firm in Roswell handle an employee who works through lunch without being asked?

answers.text: The time is still hours worked if the firm knows or should know the work was performed: the firm must pay for it and manage the behavior through discipline or scheduling, not by deleting the time
Ignore it unless the client complains
Pay double as a bonus
Delete the time; unapproved work is unpaid

questions.explanation: Suffered-or-permitted work is payable work; the remedy for unwanted hours is management, not non-payment.

questions.question: What does surety prequalification examine before bonding work for a New Mexico contracting firm in Farmington?

answers.text: Only the lowest bid it has submitted
Only the firm's advertising
The firm's financial statements, work in progress, experience, organization, and references — the character, capacity, and capital on which the surety decides the firm finishes what it starts
The personal hobbies of the owners

questions.explanation: Bonding is earned before the bid: the surety underwrites the firm first and the project second.

questions.question: What must the owners of a New Mexico general contracting company in Hobbs file to keep a corporation or LLC in good standing?

answers.text: Copies of all subcontracts

The periodic reports and fees the formation state requires, plus maintaining a registered agent and office — because an administratively dissolved entity loses the standing its contracts and shield presume
Nothing after formation
Daily activity reports

questions.explanation: Good standing is a maintained condition, not a formation souvenir.

questions.question: How should a New Mexico general contracting company in Las Cruces handle a final paycheck and withholdings when an employee leaves mid-project?

answers.text: By the same rules as any payroll: compute gross from hours worked, apply the required withholdings, pay within the applicable pay-timing rules, and keep the records — departure changes nothing about the trust duties
Skip reporting because the job ended
Pay cash without withholdings for simplicity
Withhold the entire check as a completion bond

questions.explanation: Exit is an administrative event, not an exemption: the last check is a payroll like any other.

questions.question: How does a surety bond differ from an insurance policy for a New Mexico building contracting company in Silver City?

answers.text: A bond is a three-party guarantee of the contractor's obligation to another, with the contractor expected to repay the surety; insurance is a two-party transfer of the insured's own loss risk to the insurer
Insurance guarantees contract completion
They are interchangeable products
Bonds cover employee injuries

questions.explanation: Beneficiary and repayment divide them: bonds guarantee performance to others; insurance absorbs the insured's own losses.

questions.question: What does an entire-agreement (merger) clause do to the earlier negotiations of a New Mexico construction firm in Los Lunas?

answers.text: It makes the signed document the whole bargain: prior promises and understandings outside it are superseded, which is why every commitment that matters must be inside the signed text
It incorporates every earlier draft automatically
It voids the written contract in favor of the talks
It merges the two companies into one

questions.explanation: After merger, the document is the deal; anything left outside was left behind.

questions.question: Why does depreciation matter to the estimating and financial work of a New Mexico general contracting company in Tucumcari even though it is not a cash expense?

answers.text: Because equipment is consumed by use and time; charging depreciation spreads that consumption into job and period costs so prices and profits reflect the true cost of using the fleet
Because depreciation increases cash
Because it lowers the firm's license fee
Because the board buys used equipment

questions.explanation: Depreciation prices the wearing-out of assets into the work that wears them out.

questions.question: Why do construction contracts for a New Mexico general contracting company in Artesia insist on written change orders when both parties trust each other?

answers.text: Because oral changes are always void
Because the written order fixes the changed scope, price, and time before performance, when agreement is easy — trust does not prevent honest memory differences about what was authorized
Because change orders raise the contract sum automatically
Because the board must pre-approve each change

questions.explanation: Writing is not a symptom of distrust; it is how a changing bargain stays one bargain.

questions.question: Which job-related charges belong in an estimate by a New Mexico design-build contracting firm in Silver City as their own line items rather than buried in overhead?

answers.text: Charges the project itself causes and the documents make the contractor bear — permits, fees, testing, and temporary services — identified and priced so they are neither lost nor double-counted
The owners' personal expenses
The firm's income taxes
Costs already inside the subcontract prices, counted again

questions.explanation: Project-caused charges priced visibly are recovered once; buried, they are recovered never or twice.

questions.question: Why should a New Mexico construction firm in Taos calendar lien and bond-claim deadlines at job start rather than when payment trouble appears?

answers.text: Because the deadlines run from events like last furnishing, not from when a dispute ripens; by the time payment fails, uncalendared rights may already have expired
Because deadlines can be extended by request at any time
Because owners set the deadlines
Because the board requires a calendar filing

questions.explanation: These clocks start on furnishing events; only advance calendaring keeps the rights alive.

questions.question: Why should the owners of a New Mexico contracting firm in Las Cruces plan for succession and continuity at formation rather than at retirement?

answers.text: Because the plan sets the firm's prices

Because death, disability, or a falling-out can arrive at any time, and a firm whose ownership, authority, and license assignments have no continuity plan can lose its banking, bonding, and licensure footing in a single event
Because succession plans are required license exhibits
Because partners never disagree after formation

questions.explanation: Continuity is a formation decision; improvising it during a crisis is how sound firms unravel.

questions.question: For one pay period, a New Mexico contracting firm in Santa Fe has gross wages of $10,000. The employer's payroll burden consists of a charge of 6% of gross wages and a second charge of 2% of gross wages, using only the rates stated here. What is the total payroll burden for the period?
questions.explanation: First charge = 6% of 10,000 = $600. Second charge = 2% of 10,000 = $200. Total burden = 600 + 200 = $800.

questions.question: What is the employer's core safety duty to the employees of a New Mexico building contracting company in Deming under the general framework the examination assumes?

answers.text: To meet standards only on inspected days
To furnish a workplace free from recognized hazards likely to cause death or serious harm, and to comply with the safety standards that apply to the work — a duty owed to every employee on every site
To provide safety only when owners require it
To delegate the duty entirely to employees

questions.explanation: The duty is the employer's, continuous, and hazard-focused; it cannot be delegated away.

questions.question: A contract held by a New Mexico design-build contracting firm in Gallup states a contract amount of $200,000 and retainage of 5% of the contract amount, using the rate stated in the contract here. How much retainage is withheld in total at that rate?
questions.explanation: Retainage withheld = 5% of 200,000 = $10,000.

pennsylvania-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Pennsylvania Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the fitness standard for licensure. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The department may not consider an applicant's past prohibited acts.
Passing the exam alone entitles every applicant to the license.
Fitness is measured only by a credit score threshold in the statute.

The department issues the license when the applicant shows the general fitness, competence, and reliability sufficient to satisfy the department that the applicant is worthy of licensure, in addition to passing the exam and paying the fees.

questions.explanation: Exam passage is necessary but not sufficient — character and reliability are an independent licensing criterion.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes collapse coverage limits?

answers.text: Property forms cover collapse only when caused by specified perils or hidden decay and similar listed conditions; mere settling, cracking, shrinking, or bulging of foundations, walls, or roofs is not collapse.
Any wall crack qualifies as a collapse claim.
Collapse coverage pays for gradual settling over years.
A building that threatens to fall someday is a present collapse claim.

questions.explanation: Abrupt, caused, and sudden is the shape of collapse coverage — deterioration is maintenance, not collapse. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: Regarding the HO-2 form, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: The HO-2 is an open-perils form for the dwelling.
The HO-2 covers only fire and extended coverage perils.
The HO-2 (broad form) covers both the dwelling and personal property against the same list of named broad-form perils.
The HO-2 is designed for condominium unit owners.

questions.explanation: HO-2 names its perils for everything it covers — broader than the basic form, narrower than the HO-3's open-perils dwelling coverage. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of delay explanation letters?

answers.text: If an investigation cannot be completed in time, the insurer must give the claimant a reasonable written explanation for the delay, and repeat that explanation every forty-five days, stating when a decision may be expected.
Explanations may be given orally to the adjuster.
The interval for status letters is ninety days.
One delay letter covers the claim indefinitely.

questions.explanation: In one line: The forty-five-day drumbeat keeps a slow claim visible instead of forgotten.

questions.question: An examiner asks about direct versus indirect loss. Which response is correct?

answers.text: Property insurance distinguishes direct loss — physical damage to the property itself, like a building burned by fire — from indirect or consequential loss, like the income the business loses while the building is repaired.
Direct loss means any loss the insured discovers directly.
Indirect losses are never insurable under any form.
Lost income is a direct loss because the fire caused it.

questions.explanation: The adjuster's first sorting question on any file: what physically broke (direct) and what flowed from it (indirect, needing time-element cover). That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: A two-partner adjusting firm files for the entity and for both partners individually. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: before transacting any business under the license
individual licenses must be held or secured for each partner or member
when the home state does not license Pennsylvania residents on the same basis
the department may waive education and fee requirements for good cause

questions.explanation: The example points to individual licenses must be held or secured for each partner or member. The each-person rule follows the entity form: partners and members are individually licensed, just as corporate officers are.

questions.question: In a claim file, the adjuster notes the issue of how the FAIR Plan is supported. Which statement about it is correct?

answers.text: The FAIR Plan is operated through an association of the insurers licensed to write property insurance in the Commonwealth, which share in its results.
Only surplus lines insurers participate in the plan.
The plan is funded entirely by state tax revenue.
The federal government reinsures the plan directly.

questions.explanation: The key point: Residual-market plans spread the risk across the market that declined it — every licensed property writer participates.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing other structures on a dwelling form. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Detached structures are never covered by a dwelling form.
A garage rented to a neighbor is covered exactly like a private garage.
Structures coverage is unlimited under the dwelling form.

Dwelling forms cover other structures on the premises, such as detached garages and sheds, subject to the form's terms; renting the structure out or using it for business can defeat or limit that coverage.

questions.explanation: The key point: The adjuster asks what the detached building was used for before agreeing it is a covered other structure.

questions.question: Mr. Ferreira is adjusting a claim at a rental cottage after a hailstorm. The file raises the issue of builders risk coverage. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Coverage continues unchanged for years after occupancy.
Builders risk is the contractor's general liability policy.
Only the contractor, never the owner, may be insured.

Builders risk insurance covers a building or structure while it is under construction, including materials and supplies on site, in transit to the site, or stored for the project, usually ending when the project is completed or occupied.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: The adjuster watches the endpoints: when did coverage attach, and had the building been occupied or accepted before the loss.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes who the businessowners policy is designed for?

answers.text: Any business of any size or hazard class is eligible.
The BOP is written only for Fortune-scale manufacturers.

The businessowners policy packages property and liability coverage for eligible small and mid-sized businesses — offices, retailers, wholesalers, and small service operations — in a single simplified form.
It is a homeowners form sold to sole proprietors.

questions.explanation: Eligibility is the first BOP question: size and class limits keep heavy hazards in the commercial package market. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the definition of hazard. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A hazard is the uncertainty of financial loss.
A hazard is the cause of a loss, such as fire.
A hazard is a condition that increases the probability or severity of a loss from a peril.
A hazard is a loss that has already occurred.

questions.explanation: Hazards raise the odds or the size of a loss without being its cause — oily rags stored by a furnace are a hazard; the fire they help start is the peril. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: Mr. O'Brien is adjusting a claim at a rental cottage after a hailstorm. The file raises the issue of how applications are filed. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The department accepts applications only during a January filing window.
Pennsylvania license applications are filed electronically through the online licensing portals used by the department, rather than by paper, which is reserved for applicants unable to apply online.
Applications are filed at the examination site before testing begins.
Paper applications are the standard channel and are mailed to the commissioner.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: Electronic filing is the default path; paper is the exception and takes considerably longer.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of direct versus indirect loss. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Direct and indirect losses are paid from the same coverage in all cases.
Direct loss means loss caused without any peril involved.
A direct loss is the physical damage itself; an indirect (consequential) loss follows from the direct loss, such as lost rental income while a building is repaired.
Indirect loss is damage to property not listed in the policy.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: The distinction drives coverage placement: fire damage to the building is direct; the rent the landlord loses during repairs is indirect and needs its own coverage grant.

questions.question: Mrs. Lindqvist is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of salvage and abandonment. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An insured may always dump a total loss on the insurer.
The insurer must take title to all damaged property.
Property forms prohibit the insured from abandoning damaged property to the insurer; whatever salvage value remains belongs in the settlement accounting, reducing the net loss.
Salvage value is ignored in actual cash value settlements.

questions.explanation: No abandonment is why burned inventory stays the owner's problem to dispose of, with its remaining value credited. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: A fire closes a business for 4 months. The business's net income would have been $20,000 per month, and its continuing normal operating expenses are $8,000 per month. What is the business income loss for the closure?
questions.explanation: Business income loss combines lost net income and continuing expenses: ($20,000 + $8,000) x 4 months = $112,000.

questions.question: Mr. Whitfield is adjusting a claim at a small warehouse after a sprinkler leak. The file raises the issue of documenting the adjustment. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Only the final settlement sheet needs to be kept.
The department discourages keeping carrier correspondence.

A Pennsylvania public adjuster's file should let the whole adjustment be reconstructed: the signed contract with its initialed disclosures, the insurer notice, the estimates and documentation shared with the client, and every carrier communication tracked against the state timing standards.
Verbal updates replace file documentation for small claims.

questions.explanation: The key point: Good files win arguments about clocks, fees, and conduct all at once — documentation is the adjuster's proof of compliance.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a small warehouse after a sprinkler leak. The file raises the issue of the investigation clock. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Catastrophe claims have no investigation standard.
Every insurer must complete its investigation of a claim within thirty days after notification of the claim, unless the investigation cannot reasonably be completed within that time.
Investigations may run one hundred eighty days without explanation.
The standard is thirty working days after the proof of loss only.

questions.explanation: In one line: Thirty days is the investigation benchmark; more time is possible, but only with the required explanations.

questions.question: A buyer closes on a house Friday with a binder in hand; the fire that weekend is analyzed under the binder's coverage. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: a financial stake in the property's preservation
risk as the uncertainty of financial loss
liability without proof of negligence for abnormally dangerous activities
temporary proof of coverage before the policy issues

questions.explanation: The example points to temporary proof of coverage before the policy issues. Binders bridge the gap between agreement and issuance; claims in that window are tested against the binder's terms and the coverage contemplated.

questions.question: A family's normal monthly living expenses are $2,800. While their fire-damaged home is repaired, their temporary living costs are $3,700 per month for 2 months. How much additional living expense does Coverage D pay?
questions.explanation: Coverage D pays the increase over normal expenses: ($3,700 - $2,800) x 2 months = $1,800. It does not pay the family's normal expenses, which they would have had anyway.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Applicant fingerprints are submitted so the insurance department can receive national criminal history records information from the Criminal Justice Information Services Division of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

answers.text: conviction of, or a plea of nolo contendere to, a felony
any person signing the contract may rescind it
the applicant has not committed any act prohibited by the licensing law
so the department can receive national criminal history records from the federal bureau

questions.explanation: That description defines so the department can receive national criminal history records from the federal bureau. The fingerprint channel runs applicant -> department -> federal criminal history records; it is a fitness screen, not a formality.

kansas-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Kansas Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding newly acquired and construction reporting, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Values reporting has no penalty structure.
New locations are covered automatically for the whole term at full limits.
Acquired property never needs endorsement.

Commercial programs handle growth with reporting and extension mechanics — newly acquired buildings and business personal property receive automatic limited extensions for a short reporting window, and values-reporting forms tie premium and recovery to values the insured reports periodically, with penalties for material under-reporting.

questions.explanation: Static limits meet dynamic businesses through these mechanics — and the adjuster tests every location and value date against them before conceding coverage. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the appraisal clause. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: When the insured and insurer disagree on the value of the property or the amount of loss, the policy's appraisal clause lets either party demand, in writing, that each side select a competent, impartial appraiser; the appraisers choose an umpire, and an award agreed by any two of the three sets the amount of loss — appraisal decides value, not coverage.
An appraisal award may be set at any figure the umpire prefers.
Appraisal decides whether the loss is covered.
The insurer's appraiser must be its own employee.

questions.explanation: In one line: Appraisal is a valuation machine, not a coverage court — and in Kansas a public adjuster's own conduct rules forbid wearing the appraiser's hat on their own claim.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of matching and uniformity?

answers.text: Matching is never a legitimate valuation issue.

Valuation disputes often turn on matching: whether repairing only the damaged portion of a roof plane, facade, or floor leaves a reasonably uniform appearance, or whether the scope must extend so new work matches the surviving property in kind, quality, and appearance.
The scope always extends to the whole exterior automatically.
Contractors alone decide matching questions.

questions.explanation: Matching fights are scope fights: documented evidence of color, profile, and the availability of original materials is what resolves them. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: On the subject of equipment breakdown, which statement is right?

answers.text: The coverage excludes the failed object itself.
Spoilage extensions require no breakdown trigger.
Wear and tear is covered as breakdown.

Equipment breakdown coverage insures sudden and accidental mechanical breakdown, electrical arcing, and pressure-equipment failure of boilers and machinery, paying for repair or replacement of the equipment, resulting damage to other property, and related business income and spoilage where the form provides.

questions.explanation: Breakdown is the peril the standard form excludes and this coverage restores — with the failed machine, not just its consequences, at the center. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: On the subject of contract contents — the claim described, which statement is right?

answers.text: A Kansas public adjuster contract must contain the insured's full name and street address, the name of the insurer and the policy number, and a description of the loss and its location.
The insurer's identity is confidential and omitted.
The loss description may simply say 'property damage'.
The policy number may be added after settlement.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: The contract ties the engagement to one insured, one insurer, one policy, and one described loss at a stated location — specificity is the requirement.

questions.question: A covered item has a replacement cost of $30,000. Depreciation of 10% applies for its age and condition. What is the item's actual cash value?
questions.explanation: Actual cash value is replacement cost minus depreciation: $30,000 x (1 - 0.10) = $27,000. The depreciation withheld is $3,000.

questions.question: Ms. Chen is adjusting a claim at a single-family home after a kitchen fire. The file raises the issue of employee theft coverage. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The coverage requires the employee to be convicted first.
Employee theft covers any employee error that costs money.

The commercial crime form's employee theft coverage pays for loss of money, securities, and other property resulting directly from theft committed by an employee — a dishonest taking by someone in the insured's service — with discovery and prior-fraud provisions shaping which losses qualify.
Losses caused by the insured's partners are covered as employee theft.

questions.explanation: The embezzling bookkeeper is the archetypal crime claim: proof centers on the employee's dishonest act and the direct loss it caused. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the deductible's function. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Percentage deductibles are computed on the loss in every form.
The deductible is paid by the insurer to the insured.

A deductible is the stated amount or percentage of each covered loss the insured retains before the insurer pays — reducing small-claim costs, aligning the insured's care incentives, and lowering premium in exchange for retained risk.
The deductible applies once per policy term.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Retained risk is the price of the premium saved: every valuation ends by subtracting the retention the insured agreed to keep.

questions.question: Mr. Novak is adjusting a claim at a retail store after a windstorm. The file raises the issue of contract contents — identity and license. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A Kansas public adjuster contract must contain the legible full name of the public adjuster signing it, the adjuster's permanent home state business address and phone number, and the adjuster's license number.
The contract need not identify which individual adjuster signed it.
A trade name alone satisfies the identity requirement.
The license number is optional if the insured already knows it.

questions.explanation: The insured must be able to identify, locate, and verify the exact licensed individual they hired — from the face of the contract. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing no false or malicious statements. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Statements to prospective clients are unregulated.
Exaggerating an insurer's conduct is fair salesmanship.

A Kansas public adjuster may not knowingly make any oral or written material misrepresentations, or statements that are false or maliciously critical and intended to injure any person engaged in the business of insurance, to an insured client or a potential insured client.
Only written falsehoods are covered.

questions.explanation: In one line: Kansas polices the pitch as well as the practice: winning a client with knowing falsehoods about insurers is itself an ethics violation.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a condominium unit after a theft. The file raises the issue of attorney exemption. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The exemption lets attorneys employ unlicensed adjusters freely.
A license as a public adjuster is not required of an attorney-at-law admitted to practice in Kansas when acting in that professional capacity as an attorney.
A disbarred attorney keeps the exemption.
Any attorney from any state may adjust Kansas claims without a license.

questions.explanation: The exemption follows the law license and the legal work — it is the practice of law that is carved out, not the person in all they do. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: Mr. O'Brien asks how proof of loss works in a property claim. Which explanation is correct?

answers.text: The proof of loss may be submitted at any time before suit is filed, regardless of policy terms.
Verbal notice to an agent is a proof of loss.

A proof of loss is the insured's signed, sworn statement, submitted within the time the policy requires after the insurer's request, stating the time and origin of the loss, the insured's interest and all other interests in the property, the cash value of each item and the amount claimed, all other insurance, and the changes in title or occupancy since the policy issued.
A proof of loss is the adjuster's own estimate form.

questions.explanation: In one line: The proof is the insured's formal, sworn number — the claim the insurer must answer — which is why its contents and deadline are dictated by the policy.

questions.question: A family's normal monthly living expenses are $3,000. While their fire-damaged home is repaired, their temporary living costs are $4,100 per month for 6 months. How much additional living expense does Coverage D pay?
questions.explanation: Coverage D pays the increase over normal expenses: ($4,100 - $3,000) x 6 months = $6,600. It does not pay the family's normal expenses, which they would have had anyway.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of subrogation. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Subrogation lets an insurer that has paid a loss pursue the negligent third party to recover what it paid, standing in the insured's place.
Subrogation is the transfer of the policy to a new owner.
Subrogation is the insured's right to cancel mid-term.
Subrogation lets the insured collect twice for one loss.

questions.explanation: In one line: After paying, the insurer inherits the insured's claim against whoever caused the loss — and the public adjuster must protect that right, for example by preserving evidence and the salvage.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Kansas public adjusting concerns first-party claims: claims the insured makes under the insured's own insurance contract for loss or damage to the insured's own real or personal property.

answers.text: within twelve months, on proof and a reinstatement fee
public access in the home state
the insured's own claim under their own policy
helpers who only gather facts or give technical support

questions.explanation: That description defines the insured's own claim under their own policy. First-party is about whose policy and whose property: the adjuster stands on the insured's side of the insured's own contract.

questions.question: A business that sells its fire-damaged building along with the pending claim assigns the proceeds right — a transfer the form permits after loss. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the insured's rights may pass, duties may not be dumped
the statutory baseline behind property forms
who counts as an insured under the form
the policy's fact sheet: who, what, where, how much

questions.explanation: The example points to the insured's rights may pass, duties may not be dumped. Consent guards the risk the insurer agreed to take; the post-loss claim is a chose in action the insured may sell or pledge.

questions.question: A commercial building is valued at $1,000,000. Its policy has a 80% coinsurance clause. The owner carried $400,000 of insurance. A covered loss of $50,000 occurs, and the deductible is $500. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Coinsurance required 80% of $1,000,000, which is $800,000. The payment ratio is $400,000 / $800,000 = 0.50. Applied to the $50,000 loss gives $25,000, minus the $500 deductible = $24,500.

questions.question: After a moderate quake cracks a home's foundation, the owner learns her earthquake policy's 15% deductible applies before any payment. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible
defense costs and other supplementary payments are outside the limit
the policy is void as to an insured who intentionally conceals or misrepresents
Coverage C pays others' medical expenses without fault

questions.explanation: The example points to earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible. Percentage deductibles are the earthquake signature: 10% of a $600,000 limit means the insured absorbs the first $60,000 of quake damage.

questions.question: A report that fixes the night of the warehouse fire and maps damage to building, stock, and business income coverages gives the file its working structure. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: age, condition, and remaining service life
when repaired work must blend with the undamaged
occurrence date, coverages, and the facts of the loss
photographs, measurements, and preserved evidence

questions.explanation: The example points to occurrence date, coverages, and the facts of the loss. The outline names two of these expressly — occurrence date and coverages — because a report missing either cannot anchor deadlines or route damage to the right limits.

questions.question: A homeowner cannot know whether a kitchen fire will happen this year; that uncertainty is what she insures against. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: a financial stake in the property's preservation
risk as the uncertainty of financial loss
liability without proof of negligence for abnormally dangerous activities
the damage itself versus its consequences

questions.explanation: The example points to risk as the uncertainty of financial loss. Risk is the uncertainty itself — the chance that a loss may occur — not the cause of loss (the peril) or the condition that raises its likelihood (the hazard).

florida-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Florida Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing moral hazard. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Moral hazard is indifference arising from a physical defect.
Moral hazard arises from dishonesty or character defects in an insured that increase the chance of a loss or inflate its size.
Moral hazard is a physical condition of the property.
Moral hazard is carelessness caused by having insurance.

questions.explanation: Moral hazard is about intent and character — fraud and deliberate loss — as opposed to morale hazard (carelessness) and physical hazard (property conditions).

questions.question: Regarding the proof of loss, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: The insurer prepares and signs the insured's proof of loss.
A proof of loss is the insured's formal, sworn statement documenting the claim — the property, the loss, its cause, and the amount claimed — submitted within the time the policy requires.
A proof of loss is optional in every claim and never time-limited.
A proof of loss is the insurer's denial letter.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Public adjusters build proofs of loss that can survive scrutiny: complete inventories, documented values, and timely filing under the policy's clock.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the HO-6 form?

answers.text: The HO-6 insures the entire condominium building for the association.
The HO-6 provides no personal property coverage.
The HO-6 is written for condominium unit owners, covering the unit's interior items the owner is responsible for, personal property, and liability.
The HO-6 is a landlord's dwelling policy.

questions.explanation: Condo ownership splits the building (association's master policy) from the unit interior and contents (the owner's HO-6) — adjusters coordinate the two on every condo loss. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: When a claim turns on the apprentice's starting point, which statement governs?

answers.text: The apprentice license replaces the all-lines adjuster license.
Anyone may become an apprentice with no other license.
A Florida public adjuster apprentice must be licensed as an all-lines adjuster and hold a current appointment by a licensed public adjusting firm that has designated a primary adjuster.
Apprentices are appointed directly by the Department without a firm.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: The apprenticeship is built on top of the all-lines adjuster license and a firm's appointment — it is not an entry-level license standing alone.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes roof inducements?

answers.text: Roof-claim gift cards are allowed up to $100.
Waiving the deductible to win a roof claim is a permitted courtesy.

A Florida public adjuster or apprentice may not offer a rebate, gift, gift card, cash, coupon, deductible waiver, or anything else of value in exchange for allowing a roof inspection or making a roof-damage claim, nor offer or accept compensation for referrals of services paid from property insurance proceeds for roof repairs or replacement.
Only the contractor, never the adjuster, is bound by the roof rule.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: Roof claims were Florida's fraud frontier, so the inducement ban there is explicit and detailed — deductibles themselves became a banned bargaining chip.

questions.question: Mr. Novak is adjusting a claim at an office condo after vandalism. The file raises the issue of claims handling goals. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An insurer's claims organization aims to comply with the policy contract, satisfy its obligations to the policyholder fairly, and control loss costs — goals a public adjuster tests against the file on every claim.
Cost control excuses ignoring the contract.
The carrier's only goal is to pay nothing on every claim.
Claim goals never include fairness to the policyholder.

questions.explanation: Knowing the other side's legitimate goals — contract compliance, fair dealing, cost control — tells the public adjuster which arguments move a file.

questions.question: Mr. O'Brien is adjusting a claim at an office condo after vandalism. The file raises the issue of fidelity bonds. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Fidelity bonds are performance bonds for public works.
Fidelity bonds guarantee that a contractor will finish a project.
Fidelity bonds insure a building against fire.
Fidelity bonds protect an employer against loss caused by the dishonest acts of bonded employees.

questions.explanation: The key point: Where surety guarantees performance to a third party, fidelity protects the employer itself from its own employees' dishonesty.

questions.question: A home sits empty for four months awaiting sale; vandals strip the copper piping and the vacancy condition defeats that part of the claim. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: fire legal liability for premises the insured rents
earthquake, landslide, and earth sinking are excluded perils in standard homeowners forms
occurrence responds by injury date; claims-made by claim date
coverage restrictions after extended vacancy

questions.explanation: The example points to coverage restrictions after extended vacancy. Adjusters calendar vacancy carefully: beyond the form's 60-day line, whole peril categories fall away and remaining losses take a percentage reduction.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the thirty-day inspection. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The inspection window is six months.
When a Florida property claim investigation requires a physical inspection, the insurer must generally conduct the inspection within thirty days after receiving the proof-of-loss statement.
Only the insured's adjuster ever inspects in Florida.
Inspections may be scheduled at the carrier's leisure.

questions.explanation: Thirty days to put eyes on the damage keeps the carrier's valuation anchored to the actual loss rather than to photographs and delay. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: Regarding who may do this work for pay, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Except for an attorney at law, no one may, for compensation, prepare or file a claim, negotiate a settlement, offer to negotiate a claim, advertise public adjuster services, or solicit, investigate, or adjust a claim in Florida without being a licensed and appointed public adjuster.
Any contractor may adjust claims for a fee if the homeowner agrees.
Registration with a city is enough to adjust claims for pay.
Unlicensed adjusting is allowed for claims under $25,000.

questions.explanation: Florida reserves the whole compensated adjusting workflow — filing through negotiating through advertising — to licensees, and the Department can fine unlicensed practice.

questions.question: Ms. Kowalski is adjusting a claim at a rental cottage after a hailstorm. The file raises the issue of no obstructing inspection. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A Florida public adjuster may not act, or fail to act, in any way that obstructs or prevents the insurer from timely inspecting the claimed property; if the adjuster's or insureds' unavailability would delay a timely inspection, the insurer must be allowed access without them.
The inspection waits indefinitely for the adjuster's calendar.
The insurer needs the adjuster's permission to inspect at all.
Delaying inspection is a recognized negotiating tactic.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: The adjuster may attend and document the inspection — but may never become the reason it does not happen on time.

questions.question: Regarding who counts as a Florida public adjuster, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: In Florida, a public adjuster is a person who, for money, commission, or anything else of value, prepares or files a claim for an insured, helps an insured negotiate or settle a claim, advertises for such work, or solicits, investigates, or adjusts such claims for a public adjuster.
A public adjuster is only a person who owns a public adjusting firm.
A public adjuster is an unlicensed helper who works for free.
A public adjuster is any adjuster employed by an insurance company to settle its claims.

questions.explanation: Why it matters: Florida's definition turns on two things: compensation and working the claim for the insured's side — filing, negotiating, advertising, soliciting, investigating, or adjusting all count, however the person labels the service.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Insurance policies are contracts of adhesion drafted by the insurer, so genuinely ambiguous policy language is construed against the insurer and in favor of coverage.

answers.text: the cause of a loss
the insurer steps into the insured's shoes against the party at fault
ambiguous policy language is construed against the insurer
a financial stake in the property's preservation

questions.explanation: That description defines ambiguous policy language is construed against the insurer. Contra proferentem is the tiebreaker of coverage litigation: the side that wrote the confusing words bears their cost.

questions.question: A commercial building is valued at $400,000. Its policy has a 80% coinsurance clause. The owner carried $192,000 of insurance. A covered loss of $100,000 occurs, and the deductible is $2,500. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Coinsurance required 80% of $400,000, which is $320,000. The payment ratio is $192,000 / $320,000 = 0.60. Applied to the $100,000 loss gives $60,000, minus the $2,500 deductible = $57,500.

questions.question: Mrs. Lindqvist is adjusting a claim at a small warehouse after a sprinkler leak. The file raises the issue of low offers that force suit. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Litigation outcomes are irrelevant to claims-practice law.
Any settlement offer below the demand is automatically unfair.
Low offers are unfair only in auto claims.
Offering substantially less than the amount ultimately recovered in litigation, in a way that compels the insured to sue to recover what is due, is an unfair claims practice in Florida.

questions.explanation: Why it matters: The practice is judged by the pattern: offers so low they force suit, exposed when the eventual recovery dwarfs what was offered.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? A Florida public adjuster contract must contain the statutory fraud statement warning that knowingly filing a claim with false or misleading information is insurance fraud.

answers.text: written notice by certified mail or other proof of mailing
every contract must carry the public adjuster fraud statement
every public adjusting firm must designate a primary adjuster
1 percent when the insurer promptly pays a coverage part at its limit

questions.explanation: That description defines every contract must carry the public adjuster fraud statement. The fraud statement puts the insured on notice at the moment of engagement that claim honesty is a legal duty, not a negotiating tactic.

questions.question: Ms. Kowalski is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of insurable interest. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Anyone may insure any property they admire, stake or not.
Insurable interest is the insurer's right to set the premium.
Insurable interest must exist only when the policy is purchased, never at loss.
Insurable interest exists when a person benefits financially from the property's continued existence and would be harmed by its loss; for property it must exist at the time of loss.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: Property insurance is not a wager: the claimant must stand to lose financially from the property's damage, and that stake is measured when the loss occurs.

questions.question: A plumbing firm's apprentice floods a customer's home while on a service call, and the firm is vicariously liable. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the insured proves the loss; the insurer proves the exclusion
one party held liable for another's acts
principal, obligee, and surety
line-item estimating prices each repair operation separately

questions.explanation: The example points to one party held liable for another's acts. Employers answer for employees' on-the-job negligence — a doctrine that matters when a contractor's or firm's employee causes a client's loss.

questions.question: A family's normal monthly living expenses are $2,500. While their fire-damaged home is repaired, their temporary living costs are $4,100 per month for 4 months. How much additional living expense does Coverage D pay?
questions.explanation: Coverage D pays the increase over normal expenses: ($4,100 - $2,500) x 4 months = $6,400. It does not pay the family's normal expenses, which they would have had anyway.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? On a reopened or supplemental claim, the adjuster's compensation may be based only on claim payments obtained through the adjuster's work after the contract, may not be based on the previous settlement or payments for the same loss, and may not exceed 20 percent of the supplemental payment.

answers.text: misleading claims in adjuster advertising are prohibited
an itemized written estimate within 60 days, kept five years
no fee on payments to a named insured without a written contract
fees only on new money the adjuster's work obtains

questions.explanation: That description defines fees only on new money the adjuster's work obtains. Supplemental work is priced on the increment alone — the adjuster is paid for the additional recovery, never twice for the same dollars.

georgia-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Georgia Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: On the subject of direct versus indirect loss, which statement is right?

answers.text: A direct loss is the physical damage itself; an indirect (consequential) loss follows from the direct loss, such as lost rental income while a building is repaired.
Direct and indirect losses are paid from the same coverage in all cases.
Indirect loss is damage to property not listed in the policy.
Direct loss means loss caused without any peril involved.

questions.explanation: In one line: The distinction drives coverage placement: fire damage to the building is direct; the rent the landlord loses during repairs is indirect and needs its own coverage grant.

questions.question: Regarding Coverage A — Dwelling, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Coverage A covers the insured's furniture and clothing.
Coverage A pays for direct physical loss to the dwelling on the residence premises, including structures attached to it.
Coverage A covers the insured's liability to others.
Coverage A covers detached garages and fences.

questions.explanation: Coverage A is the house itself — the main structure and what is attached to it; detached structures move to Coverage B and contents to Coverage C. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the DP-1 basic form. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The DP-1 covers theft automatically.
The DP-1 covers open perils and replacement cost.
The DP-1 (basic form) covers the dwelling against fire, lightning, and internal explosion, plus the extended coverage perils if endorsed, and settles losses at actual cash value.
The DP-1 includes personal liability coverage.

questions.explanation: Dwelling policies are leaner than homeowners forms: the basic form names few perils and pays ACV, which is why landlords' claims are valued differently.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing communication duties. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Claimants are entitled to no explanations ever.
Silence is an accepted negotiation tool for adjusters.
An adjuster must communicate claim status honestly and promptly — acknowledging communications, returning calls, and explaining decisions — to the principal and, as the role allows, to the claimant.
Only written court filings count as communication.

questions.explanation: Unreturned calls are where claims become complaints: the communication duty is the profession's daily ethics in action. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: Ms. Kowalski is adjusting a claim at an office condo after vandalism. The file raises the issue of the protective safeguards endorsement. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Under a protective safeguards endorsement, if the insured fails to maintain the listed protective devices (such as an automatic sprinkler or central-station alarm) and notify the insurer of changes, fire coverage can be suspended for that location.
Disabling a sprinkler for repairs always voids the policy permanently.
Protective safeguards are suggestions with no coverage consequence.
The endorsement applies only to crime losses.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: A cheap premium bought with a sprinkler warranty becomes an unpaid fire claim when the system was shut off — adjusters verify safeguard status early.

questions.question: Mr. O'Brien is adjusting a claim at a farmhouse after a lightning strike. The file raises the issue of binders. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A binder is a premium invoice only.
A binder is a permanent policy.
A binder is a temporary contract of insurance — oral or written — that provides coverage from its effective date until the policy is issued or the binder expires or is cancelled under its terms.
Binders never bind the insurer.

questions.explanation: Binders bridge the gap between agreement and paperwork; a loss inside the binder period is a real claim under a real, if temporary, contract.

questions.question: A home has a replacement cost of $400,000. Its homeowners policy requires insurance of at least 80% of replacement cost for full replacement cost settlement. The owner carried $224,000. A covered partial loss of $40,000 occurs. Because the home was underinsured, how much will the insurer pay for the loss (before any deductible)?
questions.explanation: The 80% requirement is $320,000. The owner carried $224,000, a ratio of 0.70. The partial loss is scaled by that ratio: $40,000 x 0.70 = $28,000.

questions.question: Mr. Alvarez is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of concealment or fraud condition. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Minor paperwork errors automatically void every claim.
An insurer may void coverage for an honest mistake of memory.
The fraud condition applies only before the policy is issued.
If an insured intentionally conceals or misrepresents a material fact, engages in fraudulent conduct, or makes false statements relating to the insurance, coverage is void as to that insured.

questions.explanation: Fraud is the policy's capital offense — but it requires intentional, material deception, which the insurer must be prepared to prove. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: Mrs. Lindqvist is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of trees, shrubs and plants. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Homeowners forms cover trees, shrubs, and plants for specified perils (not wind) at a small percentage of Coverage A, with a per-item cap, commonly 5% of Coverage A overall and $500 per item.
Landscaping has no per-item limit.
Each tree is covered up to the full Coverage A limit.
Wind damage to trees is a covered cause under this additional coverage.

questions.explanation: Landscaping coverage is narrow on purpose: fire or lightning may qualify, wind does not, and the per-item cap controls most claims. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: A candidate is studying supplementary payments. Which of the following is a correct statement?

answers.text: Interest is never a supplementary payment.
Supplementary payments are deducted from the judgment.
Defense costs always erode the liability limit in every form.
Liability forms promise supplementary payments — such as defense costs, bail bonds, and interest — that the insurer pays in addition to, and not out of, the limit of liability.

questions.explanation: Knowing which dollars sit outside the limit changes settlement math: defense spend under a standard CGL does not shrink the indemnity pool.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing occurrence versus accident. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: An accident is a sudden, unexpected, unintended event; an occurrence is broader — an accident or continuous/repeated exposure to substantially the same harmful conditions — which is why liability forms are written on an occurrence basis.
The terms are interchangeable in every form.
Accident includes gradual damage over ten years by definition.
Occurrence means only a single sudden explosion.

questions.explanation: The occurrence definition is what pulls gradual-but-unintended harm inside liability coverage while 'accident-only' wording would leave it out. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: Regarding notice and proof of loss timing, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Property forms require notice of loss as soon as reasonably possible and a signed, sworn proof of loss within a set period — commonly sixty days after the insurer requests it — with extensions possible in writing.
Notice may wait until repairs are finished.
Proof of loss is due before the loss occurs.
No form anywhere sets a proof-of-loss deadline.

questions.explanation: In one line: Two clocks, two documents: notice opens the claim quickly, and proof of loss formalizes it on the form's own deadline.

questions.question: Ms. Chen is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of compensatory versus punitive damages. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Punitive damages reimburse the plaintiff's medical bills.
General damages are receipts for out-of-pocket costs.
Compensatory damages are meant to make the injured party whole (special damages for measurable losses, general damages for pain and suffering), while punitive damages punish egregious conduct.
Special damages cover pain and suffering that cannot be itemized.

questions.explanation: The key point: Adjusters valuing liability claims sort damages into these boxes: itemizable specials, intangible generals, and punitives that punish rather than compensate.

questions.question: Mr. Whitfield is adjusting a claim at a single-family home after a kitchen fire. The file raises the issue of the HO-3 form. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The HO-3 covers only named perils on both dwelling and contents.
The HO-3 is a renters form with no dwelling coverage.
The HO-3 insures the dwelling and other structures on an open-perils (special form) basis while covering personal property against the named perils.
The HO-3 excludes theft of personal property in all cases.
