questions.explanation: The key point: HO-3 is the workhorse owners form: the building gets open-perils protection, and contents get the broad named-peril list — the split adjusters check first on any contents claim.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a single-family home after a kitchen fire. The file raises the issue of occurrence versus claims-made triggers. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Both forms respond whenever the claim is reported, regardless of dates.

An occurrence CGL policy responds to bodily injury or property damage that occurs during the policy period, whenever the claim is later made; a claims-made policy responds when the claim is first made during the period, subject to its retroactive date.
Occurrence policies require the claim to be made before the period ends.
Claims-made coverage has no retroactive date concept.

questions.explanation: The key point: Trigger decides which year's policy answers a liability claim — the first question in any CGL tender, and a common source of reserving disputes.

questions.question: After the roof is replaced and the final invoice submitted, the carrier releases the depreciation it withheld from the first payment. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the adjuster reports findings to the principal who engaged the adjuster
the report identifies parties and any joint tortfeasors
withheld depreciation is recovered when repairs are completed
a line-item estimate of the work needed to restore the property

questions.explanation: The example points to withheld depreciation is recovered when repairs are completed. The two-step settlement — ACV now, depreciation on completion — is why adjusters drive the repair documentation to the finish line.

questions.question: A carrier that neither inspects nor answers for months is failing obligations the contract itself imposes. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: appraisal settles amount of loss when the parties disagree
concealment hides material facts; a warranty guarantees a fact
the insurer must investigate, decide, and pay what is owed
policy cancellation and nonrenewal follow statutory notice rules

questions.explanation: The example points to the insurer must investigate, decide, and pay what is owed. The obligations run both ways in the conditions: the insured owes notice and proof; the carrier owes investigation, decision, and payment.

questions.question: A commercial building is valued at $1,250,000. Its policy has a 80% coinsurance clause. The owner carried $700,000 of insurance. A covered loss of $60,000 occurs, and the deductible is $1,000. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Coinsurance required 80% of $1,250,000, which is $1,000,000. The payment ratio is $700,000 / $1,000,000 = 0.70. Applied to the $60,000 loss gives $42,000, minus the $1,000 deductible = $41,000.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Homeowners forms exclude loss caused by failure of utility services occurring away from the residence premises, subject to specific endorsements and ensuing-loss provisions.

answers.text: no liability coverage for property in the insured's custody
difference in conditions fills the gaps of underlying policies
off-premises utility failure is excluded unless endorsed
limited per-item coverage for trees and shrubs from specified perils

questions.explanation: That description defines off-premises utility failure is excluded unless endorsed. Food spoilage from a grid failure is the everyday version of this exclusion — small dollars, frequent surprise.

questions.question: A ten-year-old roof destroyed by hail is settled at its depreciated value under an ACV policy, putting the owner back where he was, not ahead. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: insurance purchased by an insurer to spread its own risk
dishonesty or character defects in the insured
vacancy means no people and no contents; unoccupancy means no people only
restoring the insured to the pre-loss financial position

questions.explanation: The example points to restoring the insured to the pre-loss financial position. Indemnity is the measuring rule of property claims: actual cash value settlements, deductibles, and other-insurance clauses all exist to prevent gain from a loss.

abpts-ocs.quiz_title: ABPTS Orthopaedic Clinical Specialist (OCS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Examine this short item. Which statement gives the primary action of the adductor magnus?

answers.text: Adducts the hip, with its hamstring part assisting hip extension
Extends the knee, with its oblique fibres guiding patellar tracking
Flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm
Flexes and ulnar-deviates (adducts) the wrist

questions.explanation: The adductor magnus acts to do the following: adducts the hip, with its hamstring part assisting hip extension. The other choices describe actions of other muscles.

questions.question: Consider the material below. Which finding constitutes a positive Yergason test?

answers.text: Pain in the bicipital groove, or palpable subluxation of the tendon
The thumb interphalangeal joint flexes (flexor pollicis longus compensating) to hold the paper
Reproduction of the patient's posterior pelvic pain during the thrust
Increased anterior translation with a soft or absent end point compared with the other side

questions.explanation: For the Yergason test (which assesses long head of biceps (and superior labral) pathology, using resisted supination and external rotation), the positive finding is: pain in the bicipital groove, or palpable subluxation of the tendon.

questions.question: Study the following item. The Ottawa ankle rules guide which decision?

answers.text: Whether surgery is needed
Whether to apply a cast
Whether the ligament is Grade II or III
Whether radiography is needed after acute ankle injury, based on bony tenderness and ability to bear weight

questions.explanation: Ottawa rules are a validated decision aid to reduce unnecessary ankle and foot radiographs.

questions.question: Here is an OCS practice item. Spondylolysis rehabilitation in a young athlete centres on what?

answers.text: A period of rest from extension-loading sport, trunk and hip strengthening in neutral ranges, and graded return including extension reintroduction criteria
Immediate return to bowling in cricket / gymnastics extension loads
Surgery for all cases
Complete rest for a year in all cases

questions.explanation: Bone stress needs rest from the provoking load plus capacity building.

questions.question: Review the item that follows. What does the Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM) measure?

answers.text: Shoulder pain and function combining a pain rating with daily-activity items
Pain intensity on a 0-10 scale, interpreted against the patient's own baseline and meaningful-change thresholds
Foot and ankle function in daily life and sport subscales
Disability from neck pain, scored 0-50 (or as a percentage) with higher scores meaning more disability

questions.explanation: The Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM) measures: foot and ankle function in daily life and sport subscales. It is re-administered at review points to judge change against meaningful thresholds.

questions.question: The item below tests specialist knowledge. Which statement gives the primary action of the tensor fasciae latae?

answers.text: Extends the great toe and dorsiflexes the ankle
Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot
Flexes and abducts the hip and tensions the iliotibial band
Extends the knee and flexes the hip

questions.explanation: The tensor fasciae latae acts to do the following: flexes and abducts the hip and tensions the iliotibial band. The other choices describe actions of other muscles.

questions.question: First read the material, then answer. Following lumbar microdiscectomy, standard early advice includes what?

answers.text: No walking until the three-month review
Early walking and gradual activity resumption, avoiding prolonged sitting and heavy lifting or loaded flexion-rotation early, per the surgeon's instructions
Immediate heavy deadlifting to strengthen the back
Strict bed rest for four weeks

questions.explanation: Early mobilisation after microdiscectomy supports recovery; loading restrictions in the first weeks protect against re-herniation while tissues heal.

questions.question: The short text below is followed by a question. Which finding constitutes a positive Hawkins-Kennedy test?

answers.text: Raising the unaffected leg reproduces pain in the affected leg
Reproduction of the patient's leg pain (not just back or hamstring pull) in the sensitive range, altered by ankle movement
Reproduction of shoulder pain during the manoeuvre
The elbow drops backward or the wrist flexes to compensate during the press

questions.explanation: For the Hawkins-Kennedy test (which assesses rotator cuff-related subacromial pain, using forced internal rotation at 90 degrees of flexion), the positive finding is: reproduction of shoulder pain during the manoeuvre.

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. Which finding constitutes a positive Valgus stress test (knee)?

answers.text: Pain, crepitus or reproduction of symptoms with axial compression and rotation of the thumb metacarpal
Tingling radiating into the median digits on tapping
Reproduction of shoulder pain near end-range elevation
Excessive medial joint opening or pain, with laxity graded against the other side

questions.explanation: For the Valgus stress test (knee) (which assesses medial collateral ligament and medial capsular integrity), the positive finding is: excessive medial joint opening or pain, with laxity graded against the other side.

questions.question: Read this item carefully. A patient with fibromyalgia is referred for knee pain. Planning should do what?

answers.text: Treat the knee as if the fibromyalgia does not exist
Refuse treatment
Apply maximal local loading immediately
Treat the knee within a whole-person plan — sleep, activity pacing and graded exercise — recognising central pain mechanisms amplify local symptoms

questions.explanation: Comorbid nociplastic pain changes dosage and expectations for local treatment.

questions.question: This item is part of OCS practice. Minimal detectable change (MDC) differs from MCID in that MDC is what?

answers.text: The maximum possible score
The average score of healthy people
The change patients find important
The smallest change that exceeds the instrument's measurement error — a statistical property, not a judgement of importance

questions.explanation: A change must first exceed MDC to be real, and exceed MCID to matter — both checks are applied at review.

questions.question: Examine the following item. Mentoring a junior colleague through a complex case is part of specialist practice because why?

answers.text: Mentoring is a management-only duty
Specialists should guard knowledge
It is unpaid extra with no professional standing
The DSP's professional roles include education and contributing to the body of knowledge and the profession's development

questions.explanation: Teaching is written into the specialist role definition, not an optional extra.

questions.question: This question practises a tested skill. Using standard goniometric reference values, what is the typical range for hip flexion with the knee flexed?

answers.text: 135 degrees
100 degrees
120 degrees
155 degrees

questions.explanation: Standard goniometric references put typical hip flexion with the knee flexed at about 120 degrees; the other values belong to other motions or exceed the normal arc.

questions.question: Study the material that follows. Which presentation warrants same-day emergency referral rather than routine therapy assessment?

answers.text: A patient with mild tennis elbow
A patient with back pain who cannot pass urine, with numbness in the saddle region
A patient with chronic knee stiffness
A patient with localised back ache after gardening

questions.explanation: Cauda equina features are the emergency; the rest are routine presentations.

questions.question: Here is another practice item. Planning for a young hypermobile patient with recurrent shoulder subluxations should emphasise what?

answers.text: Immobilisation as the long-term strategy
Progressive rotator cuff and scapular strengthening, proprioceptive training and activity modification, with surgical opinion if instability persists despite rehabilitation
Aggressive end-range stretching
Overhead throwing volume increases

questions.explanation: Dynamic stability substitutes for lax passive restraints — the core of hypermobility care.

questions.question: Consider each choice carefully here. For greater trochanteric pain syndrome, patient education must include which sleep and sitting modifications?

answers.text: Avoid lying on the painful side (or use a pillow between the knees side-lying on the other side) and avoid sitting with legs crossed or in low chairs that adduct the hip
Stand with weight always on the painful leg in adduction
Sit cross-legged for long periods
Sleep directly on the painful trochanter to desensitise it

questions.explanation: Compression avoidance extends into daily postures, not just exercise selection.

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. The highest level of evidence for a therapy question is generally considered to be what?

answers.text: A systematic review/meta-analysis of well-conducted randomised controlled trials (with individual high-quality RCTs just below)
A single expert's opinion
A case report
A cross-sectional survey

questions.explanation: The evidence hierarchy tops out at synthesised RCT evidence for intervention questions.

questions.question: The following item is original practice material. A child or adolescent athlete with extension-related low back pain and pain on single-leg hyperextension testing raises suspicion of what?

answers.text: Pars interarticularis stress reaction or spondylolysis
Lumbar disc herniation with radiculopathy in most cases
Sacroiliac joint infection
Hip labral tear

questions.explanation: Extension-loading pain in a young athlete is the classic presentation of a pars stress injury.

questions.question: Take a moment with this item. A physical therapist evaluates a 57-year-old man with diabetes who presents following months of finger stiffness in the mornings. Examination shows painful clicking and locking of the ring finger in flexion, with a tender nodule at the A1 pulley. Which diagnosis is MOST likely?

answers.text: Ankle osteoarthritis
Trigger finger
Lumbar radiculopathy (L5)
Mallet finger

questions.explanation: The combination — months of finger stiffness in the mornings, with painful clicking and locking of the ring finger in flexion, with a tender nodule at the A1 pulley — is the classic presentation of trigger finger. The other choices do not fit this finding pattern.

questions.question: Here is an item to work through. Superficial heat is most appropriate for which presentation?

answers.text: Over a suspected DVT
A fresh ankle sprain in the first hours
Subacute or chronic muscle spasm and stiffness before exercise, avoiding acute injury, insensate skin and areas of poor circulation
Over an insensate foot

questions.explanation: Heat eases stiffness to enable movement; its contraindications (acute trauma, sensory loss, thrombosis) are the examination point.

corrections-officer-ny-dcas.quiz_title: Corrections Officer Entrance — NY DCAS Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Passage: Order: Post Key Control. A key-control order states that the post key ring for a housing area holds 16 keys and that keys are never to leave the facility, be duplicated, or be left unattended. Officer Whitfield signs the ring out at the start of the tour, counts the keys in front of the relieving officer at tour change, and reports a missing key to the control room immediately — before any other task. A key found damaged is tagged, removed from service, and recorded in the key log the same tour. According to the passage, According to the order, when does Officer Whitfield count the keys on the ring?

answers.text: at the start of the tour only, alone
report it to the control room immediately, before any other task
in front of the relieving officer at tour change
it is tagged, removed from service, and recorded in the key log the same tour

questions.explanation: Keys are counted in front of the relieving officer at tour change. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: A housing unit has 4 tiers, and each tier holds 7 cells. How many cells does the unit hold in total?
questions.explanation: Multiply tiers by cells per tier: 4 x 7 = 28.

questions.question: Visualization: on a desk, from left to right, stand a cap, a log book, a radio, a flashlight. In a mirror facing the desk, which object appears second from the left in the mirror image?

answers.text: a radio
a cap
a log book
a flashlight

questions.explanation: Reversing the row for the mirror image puts the third object from the real left into the second position from the image's left. No outside information is needed; the stem supplies what matters.

questions.question: Passage: Standard: Log-Book Entries. A log-book standard states that entries in the Housing Area 3A log book must be made in ink, in chronological order, and initialed by the officer making them. Officer Hobson must never leave blank lines between entries, must draw a single line through any error and initial the correction, and must record every count, search, incident, and supervisory visit on the tour it occurred. An entry about another tour may be added only as a late entry labeled with the date and time it is actually written. Based on the passage, According to the standard, how must an error in a log-book entry be corrected?

answers.text: every count, search, incident, and supervisory visit on the tour it occurred
by tearing out the page and starting again
by drawing a single line through the error and initialing the correction
only as a late entry labeled with the date and time it is actually written

questions.explanation: The standard prescribes a single line through the error, initialed — never erasure or removal. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Memorization: a post telephone list gives the number sequence 6-8-8-1-1. What is the first digit in the sequence?
questions.explanation: Counting into the sequence 6-8-8-1-1, the first digit is 6.

questions.question: For a formal incident report, which sentence is punctuated correctly? The sentence in this set quotes a supervisor speaking about verifying counts.

answers.text: Supervisor Farrar said "All counts, must be verified before the tour ends."
Supervisor Farrar said, "All counts must be verified before the tour ends."
Supervisor Farrar said, "All counts must be verified before the tour ends".
Supervisor Farrar said "All counts must be verified before the tour ends".

questions.explanation: A direct quotation after 'said' takes a comma before the quote, and the period sits inside the closing quotation mark. Candidates should prefer the version that would be accepted unchanged in an official report.

questions.question: The following tasks appear on a tour schedule: inspect the tier and cells at 16:40; review the movement list at 14:40; sign the log book at 15:00; count and verify the area at 16:35. Putting the tasks in the order they must be performed, earliest first, gives which sequence?

answers.text: review the movement list, sign the log book, count and verify the area, inspect the tier and cells
review the movement list, sign the log book, inspect the tier and cells, count and verify the area
review the movement list, count and verify the area, sign the log book, inspect the tier and cells
review the movement list, inspect the tier and cells, count and verify the area, sign the log book

questions.explanation: Reading the printed times in order gives the sequence: review the movement list at 14:40; sign the log book at 15:00; count and verify the area at 16:35; inspect the tier and cells at 16:40.

questions.question: Using the facility map: the control room is directly north of the chapel, the recreation yard gate is directly east of the chapel, the visiting room entrance is directly south of the chapel, and the school area is directly west of the chapel. An officer at the chapel turns to face north. Which location is now on the officer's behind?

answers.text: the control room
the visiting room entrance
the school area
the recreation yard gate

questions.explanation: Facing north, the officer's behind points south, and the visiting room entrance is the location directly south of the chapel.

questions.question: For stated housing-area rules, the written rule for the area states: 'Complaints about medical care are recorded and forwarded to the clinic; officers do not judge their validity.' A person complains about a clinic decision the officer personally agrees was correct. Applying the rule, what must the officer do?

answers.text: hold the departure and reconcile the discrepancy with a supervisor before leaving
decline the gift and report the offer as procedure requires
refuse to hand over the key; the worker is escorted or the task is arranged through a supervisor
record the complaint and forward it to the clinic without judging it

questions.explanation: The rule separates recording from judging; the officer's own view of the merits is not a filter. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: For the DCAS Correction Officer exam, what does DCAS mean by the ability called Written Comprehension for a Correction Officer?

answers.text: they are sealed in a Yondr pouch until after the exam event, and using one can nullify the score and bar the candidate from civil service tests for up to five years
promotion to Captain (Correction), and from that title to Warden (Correction) at several assignment levels
two years of active service in a reserve component or the National Guard with an honorable discharge, not counting Individual Ready Reserve time
understanding written sentences and paragraphs, such as interpreting facility policies and regulations

questions.explanation: Written Comprehension is the reading ability — understanding written material and carrying out procedures based on it. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: At the start of the tour, Housing Area 2D held 25 sets of recreation equipment. During the period, 9 sets were signed out. How many sets remained in the storage room?
questions.explanation: Subtract what was signed out: 25 - 9 = 16. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Passage: Facility Notice: Counts and Verification. A facility notice on counts states that during the day tour, the officer assigned to Housing Area 5B must count and verify every person in custody in the area twice: once at 7:00 a.m. and once before the tour ends. At the 7:00 a.m. count, Officer Alvarez counted 22 people in the housing unit and 7 people who had returned early from a program area, for a verified total of 29. If the two counts disagree, the officer must recount immediately, notify the area supervisor, and record both counts and the recount in the log book before leaving the post. According to the passage, What is the main purpose of the notice?

answers.text: 29 people
to state how counts are taken, verified, and recorded when they disagree
recount immediately, notify the area supervisor, and record both counts and the recount in the log book
to announce a change in visiting hours

questions.explanation: Every sentence of the notice concerns counting, verifying, and recording counts. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: Under the area's assignment rule, a person may be assigned to the school program seats only if the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. In Housing Area 6C, one person has completed the program orientation but has no equivalency goal on file. Applying the rule, which conclusion must be true?

answers.text: That person may be assigned if a supervisor waives the rule verbally
That person may be assigned to the school program seats
The rule applies only to officers, never to assignments
That person may not be assigned to the school program seats

questions.explanation: For the school program seats, the rule requires every stated condition — that the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. This person misses one, so the assignment is barred.

questions.question: During one week, Officer Kowalski drove 3 escorted trips totaling 42 miles. What was the average number of miles driven for each trip?

answers.text: 14 miles
13 miles
42 miles
16 miles

questions.explanation: Average means total divided by trips: 42 / 3 = 14 miles per trip.

questions.question: During the evening tour, an officer notices that a normally busy dayroom is empty while a large group has gathered out of camera view in a corridor. What should the officer do, according to the standard reference material on the subject? Candidates meet the item in a practice review.

answers.text: treat the unusual gathering as a possible developing problem: observe, notify a supervisor, and do not enter the blind spot alone
the conflict between the verbal and written orders must be clarified with a supervisor so the officer follows the controlling instruction
assume the group is holding a meeting and ignore it
a sudden behavior change in one group can signal a planned disturbance or a medical emergency and warrants immediate attention

questions.explanation: Deliberate use of a blind spot plus an emptied common area is a warning pattern; the response is observation and backup, not a solo entry.

questions.question: A log-book entry must be spelled correctly. Which word below is spelled correctly? Choose the correct spelling of the word meaning: the gear issued for duty, such as radios and keys.

answers.text: equipment
equipmnet
equipmentt
equipement

questions.explanation: 'equipment' is the correct spelling of the word meaning the gear issued for duty, such as radios and keys; the other choices misplace or drop letters. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Which duties does the published Correction Officer job description assign around searches and safety? The question belongs to a general-knowledge drill.

answers.text: request medical assistance for inmates when necessary, and observe inmates to make recommendations concerning medical and psychiatric referrals
inspecting assigned areas for conditions threatening safety and security, and conducting searches to detect contraband
medical and psychological assessment, a qualifying physical test, drug screening before appointment with random testing during Academy training, and a background investigation
remembering information such as words, numbers, pictures and procedures, alone or in combination

questions.explanation: Inspection for hazards and searches for contraband are core published duties of the title. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: A tour commander in Housing Area 4B is shown this pattern: Four complaints in one week all describe cold food arriving in the same housing area; other areas served by the same kitchen reported no problem, and the area is the last stop on the cart route. Which conclusion follows best from the pattern?

answers.text: Something on the route to that area — timing or cart handling — is likely cooling the food
The observations show the facility should close the area involved
Every area in the facility has exactly the same problem at the same rate
The complaints must all be false because they agree

questions.explanation: Inductive reasoning combines separate observations into the general conclusion they jointly support: something on the route to that area — timing or cart handling — is likely cooling the food. The other choices either overstate the facts or ignore the pattern. This answer holds up under the facts as presented.

questions.question: Memorization: study this scene. In the visiting room, 7 people wore orange shirts, 3 wore blue shirts, and 8 wore yellow shirts. Seated nearest the door was Mr. Donnelly; seated in the middle was Mr. Castillo; seated nearest the window was Mr. Grimaldi. Who was seated nearest the window?

answers.text: Mr. Castillo
Mr. Farrar
Mr. Donnelly
Mr. Grimaldi

questions.explanation: The scene places the named person nearest the window in its final seating detail. No outside information is needed; the stem supplies what matters.

questions.question: The assignment rule for the area states that a person may be assigned to the school program seats only if the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. In the visiting area, one person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. Applying the rule, which conclusion must be true?

answers.text: The rule applies only to officers, never to assignments
The rule does not apply inside a housing area
That person may be assigned if a supervisor waives the rule verbally
That person may be assigned to the school program seats

questions.explanation: For the school program seats, the rule requires that the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation — and this person does, so the rule permits the assignment. It is the response a careful reviewer would expect on this fact pattern.

naa-camt.quiz_title: NAA CAMT — Certified Apartment Maintenance Technician Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which of these assertions about refrigerator cooling diagnosis fails to hold up?

answers.text: Poor refrigerator cooling can come from dirty condenser coils, blocked vents, or a failing door seal.
Food temperatures and air flow between compartments are checked before major parts are replaced.
Dirty condenser coils improve heat transfer and should never be cleaned.
The refrigerator is unplugged before fan blades or electrical covers are handled.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Most cooling complaints trace to airflow, coils, seals, or fans that can be checked in order, while blocked vents, dirty coils, and careless defrosting hide the real fault and can damage the appliance.

questions.question: On the subject of pool equipment mechanics, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Pool pumps lose prime when suction side air leaks or low water level let air enter the system.
High filter pressure always means the gauge is wrong and cleaning can be skipped.
Running a pool pump dry keeps the seals flexible and extends motor life.
A strainer basket can be removed and left out so water flows faster to the filter.

questions.explanation: Pool equipment depends on a full prime, clean baskets, and sound filtration, while dry running, missing baskets, and ignored pressure or air leaks damage motors and leave water cloudy and unsafe.

questions.question: One statement about energy and water conservation in repairs is not true. Which one is it?

answers.text: A running toilet or dripping faucet is treated as resource waste, not merely a minor annoyance, and prioritized accordingly.
When replacing components, the technician follows the property's efficiency standards rather than installing the least efficient option by default.
Repairs that conserve resources — fixing leaks promptly, sealing drafts, restoring insulation disturbed during work — are part of environmentally responsible maintenance.
Efficiency standards apply to new construction, never to replacement parts.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Responsible maintenance conserves by default: leaks fixed promptly, disturbed insulation restored, and replacements that respect the property's efficiency standards.

questions.question: Which claim about exterior lighting check should be discarded as false?

answers.text: Walkways, stairwells, and parking areas should all be included when checking exterior lighting.
Exterior lighting checks should be done after dark so burned out or dim fixtures are actually visible.
Burned out bulbs in stairwells can wait until a resident complains before being addressed.
The technician should report broken fixture covers and exposed wiring found during a lighting check as safety concerns.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Checking lighting after dark in all travel areas reveals dark spots and damaged fixtures that affect safety and security, allowing timely repair before residents are put at risk.

questions.question: For asking clarifying questions upward, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Restating an assignment wastes a supervisor time and adds no real value.
An unclear instruction should be guessed at so the day is not slowed down.
Asking for clarification signals incompetence and should be avoided at all costs.
Asking a supervisor to clarify an unclear instruction prevents work done the wrong way.

questions.explanation: Asking clarifying questions upward, and restating assignments to confirm priorities, prevents rework and unsafe assumptions, and supervisors view thoughtful questions as engagement rather than weakness.

questions.question: Among these statements on wall anchor and mounting, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: The correct anchor for a load depends on wall material, with hollow wall anchors, stud anchoring, and masonry anchors each suited to different conditions.
Heavy or safety related items such as grab bars and large fixtures should be anchored into framing or proper blocking whenever possible.
Before drilling, the technician should check for plumbing and wiring that may run behind the chosen mounting location.
Grab bars anchored only into drywall provide full support for a falling person.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Mounting safety rests on matching the anchor to both the wall and the load, preferring framing for anything a person may grab or that carries real weight. Checking for hidden pipes and wires before drilling prevents a simple mounting task from creating a plumbing or electrical emergency.

questions.question: Erin Sullivan is reviewing briefing material on airflow diagnosis. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Crushed, disconnected, or leaking ducts in attics or crawl spaces waste conditioned air and should be repaired and resealed.
Rooms that are far from the air handler or have closed doors and no return path often run warmer or cooler than the rest of the unit.
Weak airflow at registers prompts checks of the filter, blower operation, closed or blocked registers, and duct connections.
Blocking a return grille with furniture improves circulation by redirecting the air.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Airflow is half of comfort delivery, so the path from filter to blower to duct to register is checked as a chain. Finding crushed or disconnected ducts and blocked returns explains many uneven room complaints without touching the refrigeration circuit.

questions.question: A team discussion turns to winter pipe protection. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: A frozen pipe should be thawed gently with warm air, never with an open flame, and checked for splits once flow returns.
Insulation makes it impossible for any pipe to freeze regardless of temperature or exposure.
A pipe that froze but did not burst while frozen is guaranteed undamaged after thawing.
Turning heat completely off in a vacant unit during a freeze protects the plumbing system.

questions.explanation: Freeze protection focuses on the most exposed piping, gentle thawing, and a careful leak check after thaw, because splits often reveal themselves only when water flows again. Resident guidance and vacant unit heat are part of the same prevention system.

questions.question: A junior colleague makes several claims about glove selection for tasks. Which claim should a mentor correct?

answers.text: Thicker gloves always provide better protection for every kind of task.
Chemical resistant gloves are chosen based on the product being handled and its label guidance.
Cut resistant gloves suit sheet metal and glass handling where sharp edges are present.
Gloves are removed or changed when torn so hands are not exposed mid task.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Glove material and fit must match cuts, chemicals, or contamination risks and be changed when damaged, while loose gloves near rotating parts and one pair for every job spread harm instead of preventing it.

questions.question: Which claim about work order tracking for preventive tasks should be discarded as false?

answers.text: Preventive tasks should be entered as work orders so completion can be tracked like any other maintenance work.
Work order notes for preventive tasks should be left blank to keep the system tidy.
Notes on each preventive work order should include findings and parts used for future reference.
Tracking shows which homes or systems are overdue so the team can recover the schedule before gaps grow.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Entering preventive tasks as tracked work orders with findings and parts used makes overdue work visible, supports planning, and creates the history that proves the program is being followed.

questions.question: A study partner asks a fellow applicant about communicating delays promptly. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Revised times should be kept vague so the technician cannot be held to them.
Delay notices are the office job alone, even when the technician learns first.
Offering a revised time when communicating a delay gives the resident a clear expectation.
Giving a reason for a delay sounds like an excuse and should always be avoided.

questions.explanation: Communicating delays promptly means notifying the resident as soon as the delay is known, briefly explaining why, and offering a revised time, which respects the resident day and preserves trust.

questions.question: A team discussion turns to confidentiality of resident information. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: Confidentiality ends when a resident moves out, so old details can be shared freely.
A resident phone number from a work order may be used for personal contact later.
Discussing a resident payment or lease details with other residents is acceptable small talk.
Resident information seen on paperwork should be kept secure and out of public view.

questions.explanation: Confidentiality means using resident contact and schedule information only for the service task, keeping paperwork secure, and never sharing lease, payment, or personal details with others.

questions.question: Peter Lindqvist is walking the grounds on a daily property inspection. On the question of leaving entry notice behind, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Notices are only for repairs that failed, not for completed work.
Leaving the door unlocked after a visit helps the resident get in more easily.
The notice includes how to contact the office if the problem continues or returns.
A notice should list problems the technician noticed in the resident housekeeping.

questions.explanation: A clear notice and a relocked door tell an absent resident what was done and how to get help, while silence and unsecured doors create worry, callbacks, and avoidable security risk.

questions.question: What should a beginning maintenance technician understand about interior coating application? Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Interior paint should be applied in even coats, keeping a wet edge to avoid lap marks and uneven sheen.
Rolling in random directions with a dry roller produces the smoothest finish.
One very thick coat always looks better and lasts longer than thinner even coats.
A second coat can be applied immediately over a still tacky first coat in all conditions.

questions.explanation: Application technique shows in the finished wall, so wet edges, orderly cutting in, and respect for drying time produce an even sheen. Rushing recoats or laying paint too thick traps solvents and creates the lap marks and peeling that prompt repaint calls.

questions.question: A stakeholder repeats something they read online about inspection report writing. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Inspection reports record observed conditions precisely — location, condition, and severity — rather than conclusions the inspector did not verify.
Inspection reports are complete when the walk ends, even if entries are finished later from memory.
Recommended actions in a report are separated clearly from observed facts.
Life safety and water intrusion findings are flagged in the report with the urgency their risk deserves.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Inspection reports separate observation from recommendation, state severity honestly, and flag urgent risks plainly — the format that lets management act without a second visit.

questions.question: While preparing notes after a preventive maintenance day, Julia Santos double-checks notes on seasonal pool closing. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Closing procedures should include inspecting and securing the cover so it stays safe and in place through the off season.
Seasonal pool closing should include cleaning the pool, lowering or managing water as directed, and protecting equipment from freezing.
Pipes, pumps, and filters should be prepared for cold weather following the established closing checklist.
The pool gate can be left unlatched during winter because the pool is closed.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Proper seasonal closing protects the shell, plumbing, and equipment from freeze and debris damage, secures the cover and barrier, and makes the next opening faster, safer, and less costly.

questions.question: Michael Novak is reviewing briefing material on manufacturer training resources. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Checking manufacturer resources before servicing unfamiliar equipment reduces guesswork and errors.
Only sales staff benefit from reading manufacturer training materials.
Manufacturer videos and guides often show the exact service steps for a specific model.
Manufacturer updates can alert technicians to revised parts or changed service procedures.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Manufacturer training resources provide model specific steps, updated parts information, and approved procedures, so consulting them before unfamiliar work prevents avoidable errors and rework.

questions.question: David Osei, an aspiring maintenance technician, is learning the ropes in a first apartment maintenance role and reads a summary of lighting replacement safety. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: Broken glass from a lamp can be left in a fixture shade until the next scheduled visit.
The replacement lamp should match the fixture rating for wattage and type so heat does not damage the fixture or nearby materials.
A fixture with frayed wiring, a broken socket, or heat damage should be repaired or replaced rather than fitted with a new lamp alone.
Power to a light fixture should be turned off at the breaker and verified off before the fixture is handled.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Safe lighting work starts with verified power off and respects the fixture rating, because excess wattage creates heat that damages sockets and insulation. Flicker, water stains, and damaged wiring point beyond the lamp and require investigation rather than a simple relamp.

questions.question: While responding to an after hours maintenance emergency call, Peter Lindqvist double-checks notes on incident reporting duty to management. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Incident reports are management paperwork that technicians are not expected to contribute to.
Reporting an incident the technician caused is as required as reporting one the technician witnessed.
Accurate, same-day incident accounts protect residents, the technician, and the property if a claim follows.
A technician reports injuries, property damage, threats, and unusual incidents to management promptly through the property's reporting channel.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Prompt, honest incident reporting is a core compliance duty: it starts treatment, preserves evidence, and gives management the facts while they are still fresh and checkable.

questions.question: While responding to an after hours maintenance emergency call, Chris Delacroix double-checks notes on compatibility with existing systems. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Compatibility concerns should be omitted from the recommendation to keep it short.
The technician should flag added work a replacement would require, such as new venting, wiring, or structural changes.
A repair that preserves a well matched existing system can be wiser than a replacement that forces many changes.
A replacement should be checked for fit with existing connections, controls, space, and supporting systems before approval.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Checking fit, controls, space, and added work before approval prevents surprise costs and delays, and a well matched repair sometimes beats a replacement that would force changes everywhere.

cmca.quiz_title: Certified Manager of Community Associations (CMCA) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Knowledge check: on limits on officer authority, which statement passes?

answers.text: Any single officer may set association policy alone
The president's signature alone can amend the bylaws
Officers outrank the full board between board meetings
Officers carry out board decisions within the authority the bylaws and the board give them, and an officer acting alone cannot create new association policy.

questions.explanation: Officers are agents of the board, so their power is delegated and bounded, never independent.

questions.question: Which credential satisfies the third CMCA prerequisite pathway?

answers.text: A property management certificate from an unapproved provider
An expired state manager license kept in a drawer
Any real estate salesperson license from any state
An active, good-standing approved state community association manager license or credential, such as the Arizona, California, Florida, Illinois, or Nevada credential

questions.explanation: Holders of an active, good-standing approved state license or credential — Arizona CAAM, California CCAM, Florida CAM, Illinois CAM, or Nevada CAM — qualify through the license/credential pathway.

questions.question: A study review turns to common-area safety inspections. Which statement should a candidate select?

answers.text: Regular inspections of stairs, railings, walkways, pools, and play areas identify hazards such as broken surfaces and loose railings so they can be corrected before injuries occur
Safety inspections happen only after an injury is reported
Common areas are the owners' collective problem with no inspection role for management
Hazards are noted but correction is optional

questions.explanation: Finding and fixing hazards on a schedule is the most direct way to prevent the injuries that produce liability claims.

questions.question: Knowledge check: on assessments receivable under accrual accounting, which statement passes?

answers.text: Delinquent amounts are recorded as income already received
Accounts receivable is money the association owes its vendors
Unpaid assessments are never recorded until the cash arrives
Under accrual accounting, assessments that have been billed but not yet paid appear as accounts receivable on the balance sheet.

questions.explanation: Billing creates the receivable; collection later converts it to cash, which is why delinquency shows up on an accrual balance sheet.

questions.question: Of the statements offered on uniform application of the collections policy, which one is accurate?

answers.text: The policy applies only to owners who have complained
The collections policy is applied uniformly to every delinquent owner, including directors, so collection cannot become favoritism or retaliation.
The board may informally forgive the debts of friends
Directors are exempt from the collections policy while serving

questions.explanation: Uniform application, with no exceptions for insiders, is what makes a collections policy fair and enforceable.

questions.question: When a situation involving the assurance provided by an audit needs resolving at a master-planned community, which statement is correct?

answers.text: An audit guarantees that no fraud of any size exists
An audit is performed by the association's manager
An audit provides no assurance at all
An audit provides the highest level of assurance from a CPA, who expresses an opinion on whether the financial statements are fairly presented.

questions.explanation: An audit opinion is the strongest independent statement an association can give owners and lenders about its statements.

questions.question: When a situation involving deferred maintenance defined needs resolving at a suburban homeowners association, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Deferred maintenance refers only to optional cosmetic upgrades
Deferred maintenance is needed work that has been postponed beyond its recommended timing, usually to delay spending or because of other priorities
Deferred maintenance is work that was completed ahead of schedule
Deferred maintenance improves automatically the longer it is postponed

questions.explanation: Postponing needed work does not eliminate the need, and the underlying condition usually continues to worsen.

questions.question: A board president reviewing practice at a master-planned community asks about monthly reconciliation and independent review. Which response is correct?

answers.text: Bank accounts are reconciled every month, and someone other than the preparer, such as the treasurer, reviews the reconciliation.
Review is unnecessary whenever accounting software is used
The preparer reviewing their own work alone is the strongest control
Annual reconciliation is the standard practice for every association

questions.explanation: Monthly timing catches problems while they are small, and independent review is what makes the reconciliation a control rather than a chore.

questions.question: An auditor examining records at a master-planned community asks the manager about termination provision. Which reply is correct?

answers.text: Either side may walk away instantly for any reason under every contract
Termination rights exist even when the contract says nothing about them
Notice requirements for termination never need to be followed
A termination provision states the grounds and notice required to end the contract, including any right to terminate for convenience or for cause as negotiated

questions.explanation: Termination language determines how the association can exit a failing arrangement.

questions.question: During the start of a new fiscal year at a high-rise condominium association, a decision turns on the vice president's role. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The vice president performs the president's duties when the president is absent or unable to serve, as the bylaws provide.
The vice president's only duty is planning social events
The vice president outranks the president on all financial matters
The vice president automatically becomes the community manager

questions.explanation: The vice presidency exists for continuity of the chair, stepping in only when the president cannot serve.

questions.question: A study review turns to exterior painting and finish cycles. Which statement should a candidate select?

answers.text: Paint is renewed only after bare wood or metal is fully exposed and rotted
Painting cycles are set by whichever year a volunteer offers to help
Coating failure has no effect on the materials beneath it
Exterior paint and finishes are renewed on a planned cycle before coatings fail and expose underlying materials to weather damage

questions.explanation: Paint is a protective coating, and renewing it on schedule prevents substrate deterioration.

questions.question: An auditor examining records at a housing cooperative asks the manager about the purpose of a homeowner forum. Which reply is correct?

answers.text: A homeowner forum replaces the need for written owner communications
A homeowner forum gives owners a structured opportunity to address the board on association matters within a set time, while the board listens and may take items under advisement
A homeowner forum requires the board to answer every question immediately
A homeowner forum is where owners vote to overturn board decisions on the spot

questions.explanation: A forum channels owner input respectfully without turning an open comment period into unplanned decision-making.

questions.question: Omar is asked to justify a decision involving meeting logistics and room setup at a 240-unit condominium community. Which statement provides the correct basis?

answers.text: Room setup has no effect on meeting quality
Good logistics include a room arranged so participants can hear and see, working audio where needed, materials at hand, and accessibility for attendees
Accessibility is considered only if someone complains
Materials are located during the meeting as items arise

questions.explanation: Attention to the physical setting prevents the distractions and delays that derail otherwise well-planned meetings.

questions.question: While preparing for a board meeting at a high-rise condominium association, Marta reviews the prohibition on commingling association funds. Which statement applies?

answers.text: Several communities may share the manager's personal operating account
Commingling is acceptable if the manager keeps careful personal notes
A manager must never commingle association funds with the manager's own funds or with another community's funds.
A manager may borrow association funds for short periods

questions.explanation: Each association's money must stay separate and identifiable; mixing funds destroys accountability and breaches professional standards.

questions.question: Before signing off a trainee at a 240-unit condominium community, Ingrid tests their grasp of planning major repairs and replacements. Which statement shows it?

answers.text: Expected remaining life of components is irrelevant to planning
Major replacements are first considered on the day a system fails completely
Planning major work guarantees it will never be needed
Major repairs and replacements are planned in advance using condition assessments and expected remaining life so funding and scheduling can be arranged

questions.explanation: Advance planning spreads cost, avoids emergency pricing, and keeps essential systems reliable.

questions.question: Chris, the association manager for a master-planned community, is handling work involving using visuals in a board presentation. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: Effective visuals are simple, legible, and limited to the figures or points being decided, with the presenter explaining them rather than reading them aloud word for word
Visuals are decorative and unrelated to the decision
Visuals should pack every available number onto one slide
Visuals work best when the presenter reads each slide silently to the room

questions.explanation: Clear visuals help directors and owners grasp complex material such as budgets and project options quickly.

questions.question: Priya is asked to justify a decision involving who engages the association's CPA at a mid-size condominium association. Which statement provides the correct basis?

answers.text: The CPA reports only to the manager, who summarizes for the board
The CPA engagement is decided by the association's largest vendor
The manager engages the CPA to examine the manager's own work without telling the board
The board engages the CPA and receives the CPA's report, even though the manager coordinates schedules and provides the records.

questions.explanation: The CPA's independence depends on answering to the board, not to the manager whose work is being examined.

questions.question: A fellow manager double-checking Lena's work at a single-family homeowners association raises contents of an emergency communication plan. Which statement settles it?

answers.text: The plan lists only the manager's home number
An emergency communication plan includes current contact information for board members, staff, vendors, and emergency services, plus how owners will be notified and updated
Owners are notified only after recovery is complete
Emergency contacts are collected during the emergency itself

questions.explanation: Reaching the right people quickly is the backbone of an effective response, so contact lists are maintained before they are needed.

questions.question: Marcus, the association manager for a housing cooperative, is handling work involving delivering an effective presentation to owners. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: An effective presenter uses jargon to appear expert
An effective presenter organizes points in a logical order, speaks plainly, watches the audience's understanding, and leaves time for questions within the meeting's structure
An effective presenter avoids all questions to save time
An effective presenter reads a long report word for word

questions.explanation: Plain language, structure, and managed questions turn information into understanding and support for decisions.

questions.question: At a manager training session drawn from a master-planned community's operations, the instructor quizzes staff on identifying loss exposures. Which statement earns the point?

answers.text: Loss exposures are identified by reading only the prior year's claims
Loss exposure identification inventories what could be lost — property, income, liability, and personnel — and the events that could cause each loss
Loss exposure means listing the association's bank accounts only
Only exposures that have already caused losses count

questions.explanation: A complete inventory of what is at risk is the starting point for deciding what to insure, prevent, or retain.

crcr.quiz_title: HFMA Certified Revenue Cycle Representative (CRCR) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Examined closely, fraud, waste, and abuse awareness comes down to one correct statement. Which is it?

answers.text: Only auditors need any awareness of fraud, waste, and abuse
Fraud, waste, and abuse awareness helps staff recognize intentional deception, unnecessary cost, and careless practices that harm program integrity.
Fraud, waste, and abuse are acceptable when they increase revenue
Waste means any service a payer dislikes after the fact

questions.explanation: Revenue cycle staff who recognize warning signs can raise concerns before improper billing becomes widespread.

questions.question: Of the statements offered on a coinsurance-only estimate after the deductible is met, which one is accurate?

answers.text: The patient's estimated responsibility is $45
The patient's estimated responsibility is $1,050
The patient's estimated responsibility is $1,500, because coinsurance is added on top of the full amount
On an allowed amount of $1,500 with the deductible met and 30% coinsurance, the patient's estimated responsibility is $450.

questions.explanation: With the deductible met, responsibility is 30% of $1,500, which is $450.

questions.question: On the subject of who initiates a referral, which statement is right?

answers.text: The patient issues their own referral by calling the specialist
The referral is typically initiated by the patient's primary care provider, while the specialist's office verifies that it has been received and is valid before service.
The billing department issues referrals after the visit
The payer initiates all referrals automatically

questions.explanation: Referrals flow from the primary care relationship, and the receiving office confirms them rather than creating them.

questions.question: Focus on charity care prescreening at intake for a moment — which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: Charity prescreening uses basic information gathered at intake, such as household size and income indicators, to flag patients who should complete a full assistance application.
Charity prescreening is performed only by outside collection agencies
Prescreening replaces the formal assistance application in all cases
Prescreening guarantees every flagged patient receives free care

questions.explanation: Prescreening is a first filter that routes likely-eligible patients into the full application process before service.

questions.question: How many multiple-choice questions does the HFMA CRCR certification assessment contain?

answers.text: 150 multiple-choice questions
100 multiple-choice questions
75 multiple-choice questions
50 multiple-choice questions

questions.explanation: HFMA publishes the CRCR certification assessment as 75 multiple-choice questions.

questions.question: Examined closely, the effect of rescheduling on an existing authorization comes down to one correct statement. Which is it?

answers.text: A rescheduled service never needs an authorization check
The payer adjusts authorization dates without being contacted
Authorizations automatically follow a patient to any new date
When a service is rescheduled, staff check whether the existing authorization's approved dates still cover the new date and seek an extension or new authorization if they do not.

questions.explanation: Authorizations are date-bound, so a schedule change can silently invalidate approval unless staff recheck it.

questions.question: When a situation involving cost to collect as a performance indicator needs resolving at a multi-specialty clinic system, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Cost to collect reflects the expense of operating the revenue cycle compared with the revenue those operations bring in.
Cost to collect measures how much patients owe on one account
Cost to collect measures only the price of postage
Cost to collect is unrelated to staffing and technology expense

questions.explanation: Leaders use this measure to balance service quality and accuracy against the cost of revenue cycle operations.

questions.question: A problem surfaces at a community hospital that involves measuring back-end performance. Which statement reflects the correct understanding?

answers.text: Performance measures are reported only when results are favorable
Back-end performance is measured with indicators such as days in accounts receivable, denial rate, clean claim rate, and net collection rate, reviewed as trends over time.
A single day's results are enough to judge back-end performance
Back-end performance is measured by counting the statements mailed each week

questions.explanation: Trend-level indicators show whether billing, denial, and follow-up work is actually improving collections.

questions.question: A new team member at a rural hospital asks Marcus about front-end errors as a denial root cause. Which guidance is correct?

answers.text: Many back-end denials originate in front-end errors, such as wrong insurance information captured at registration, which is why denial data is fed back to patient access.
Feeding denial data back to registration is prohibited
Front-end accuracy has no measurable effect on denials
Denials almost always originate with the payer's payment system

questions.explanation: The revenue cycle is connected: intake mistakes surface weeks later as denied claims.

questions.question: A patient account dispute at an academic medical center makes training for revenue cycle staff the central issue. Which statement is right?

answers.text: Training is a substitute for accurate source information
Experienced staff never need updates when rules change
Training is needed only on the first day of employment
Ongoing training keeps staff current on payer rules, systems, compliance duties, and communication skills as requirements change.

questions.explanation: Revenue cycle requirements change frequently, so proficiency depends on continuing education and coaching.

questions.question: While orienting a new registrar at a community hospital, Chris explains information used in financial assistance screening. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Assistance screening considers household income, household size, and related circumstances, compared against the organization's financial assistance policy criteria.
Assistance decisions are based on the patient's type of diagnosis
Screening considers only whether the patient owns a car
Income is never relevant to assistance eligibility

questions.explanation: Financial assistance is designed around ability to pay, so income and household circumstances are its core screening elements.

questions.question: In a competency review at a community hospital, a question addresses an authorization denial. Which answer is right?

answers.text: An authorization denial means the claim format failed clearinghouse edits
An authorization denial means the payer already paid the claim once
An authorization denial means the patient was not covered on the date of service
An authorization denial means the payer refused payment because a required prior authorization was missing, expired, or did not match the service billed.

questions.explanation: Authorization denials connect the billed service to the approval that should have been obtained before care.

questions.question: During a busy registration week at an academic medical center, a decision turns on a deductible plus copayment amount due at service. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: When a patient owes a $100 deductible amount and a $25 copayment at service, the total amount due at service is $75
When a patient owes a $100 deductible amount and a $25 copayment at service, the total amount due at service is $250
When a patient owes a $100 deductible amount and a $25 copayment at service, the total amount due at service is $125.
When a patient owes a $100 deductible amount and a $25 copayment at service, the total amount due at service is $35

questions.explanation: Adding the $100 deductible amount and the $25 copayment gives $125 due at service.

questions.question: A problem surfaces at a rural hospital that involves a copayment plus coinsurance amount due at service. Which statement reflects the correct understanding?

answers.text: When a patient owes a $30 copayment and $50 in coinsurance at service, the total amount due at service is $80.
When a patient owes a $30 copayment and $50 in coinsurance at service, the total amount due at service is $20
When a patient owes a $30 copayment and $50 in coinsurance at service, the total amount due at service is $130
When a patient owes a $30 copayment and $50 in coinsurance at service, the total amount due at service is $800

questions.explanation: Adding the $30 copayment and the $50 coinsurance gives $80 due at service.

questions.question: A fellow representative double-checking Victor's work at a regional medical center raises late arrival check-in handling. Which statement settles it?

answers.text: When a patient arrives late, staff check them in courteously, confirm how the delay affects the appointment with the clinical area, and update the record accurately.
A late arrival automatically cancels all coverage for the visit
Staff should scold the patient before checking availability
Late patients should be registered for the original time without noting the delay in all systems

questions.explanation: Honest communication and coordination give the patient a clear next step without falsifying the record.

questions.question: While orienting a new registrar at a large physician practice group, Henry explains date of birth verification at arrival. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Date of birth is used only to send birthday greetings
Discrepancies can be ignored if the name looks right
A guessed date of birth is acceptable for billing
Staff confirm the patient date of birth at arrival and correct discrepancies before the encounter and claim are built on the record.

questions.explanation: Date of birth is a key identifier used by payers and by staff to distinguish patients with similar names.

questions.question: A patient account dispute at a specialty surgical hospital makes identifying an underpayment from a remittance the central issue. Which statement is right?

answers.text: Underpayments cannot be identified until the account reaches collections
An underpayment is identified by comparing the payer's allowed and paid amounts on the remittance against the contracted rates for the service.
An underpayment is identified by asking the patient whether the payment seems low
Any payment below the billed charge is automatically an underpayment

questions.explanation: Contract terms define what should have been allowed, so variance from the contract is what makes a payment an underpayment.

questions.question: Priya works in the revenue cycle at a regional medical center and must apply the principles of the coder's primary responsibility. Which statement gives the correct guidance?

answers.text: A coder's primary responsibility is to negotiate payer contract rates
A coder's primary responsibility is to approve financial assistance applications
A coder's primary responsibility is to call patients about overdue balances
A coder's primary responsibility is to review the medical record and assign accurate codes that reflect the documented diagnoses and services.

questions.explanation: Coding work centers on the record and code accuracy, while payment and assistance tasks belong to other revenue cycle roles.

questions.question: At a staff training session drawn from a specialty surgical hospital's operations, the instructor quizzes staff on the account resolution stage of the cycle. Which statement earns the point?

answers.text: Account resolution forbids correcting billing errors
Account resolution is complete when the first statement is ignored
Account resolution means abandoning every unpaid account immediately
Account resolution addresses remaining balances, denials, and questions until the account reaches a proper final outcome.

questions.explanation: Resolution closes the loop opened at scheduling and may involve patients, payers, and several departments.

questions.question: Sofia works in the revenue cycle at a regional medical center and must apply the principles of charge capture after services are rendered. Which statement gives the correct guidance?

answers.text: Charge capture is the payer's process for setting allowed amounts
Charge capture refers to deleting charges that a payer questions
Charge capture is the process of recording every billable service provided so that nothing performed is left off the account.
Charge capture means collecting cash from the patient at discharge

questions.explanation: Complete charge capture protects revenue and accuracy because services that are never captured can never be billed.

nabcore.quiz_title: NAB Core of Knowledge (Nursing Home Administrator) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Focus on the role of consultant pharmacist reviews for a moment — which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: The consultant pharmacist reviews only medications kept in the emergency box
Pharmacist review findings are filed without being shared with prescribers
The consultant pharmacist reviews resident medication regimens regularly, looks for problems such as unnecessary or interacting medications, and reports findings to the care team.
The consultant pharmacist prescribes all medications instead of the physician

questions.explanation: Regular independent review catches medication risks that busy prescribers and nurses may not notice.

questions.question: Knowledge check: on the managed care reimbursement concept, which statement passes?

answers.text: Managed care reimbursement follows the contract between the facility and the plan, including authorization, network, and payment terms in that contract.
Managed care reimbursement ignores the contract and always pays full charges
Managed care plans never require authorization for facility services
Managed care reimbursement is set by the resident at admission

questions.explanation: Plan contracts govern how services are authorized and paid, so staff must follow the specific terms that apply to each plan.

questions.question: Regarding the root cause analysis after an adverse event, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Root cause analysis means repeating the same work process unchanged
Root cause analysis is unnecessary when the resident recovers quickly
Root cause analysis examines the systems and processes that allowed an adverse event to happen so corrections address underlying causes rather than only individual error.
Root cause analysis stops once a single person is found to blame

questions.explanation: Looking beyond the immediate action reveals training, staffing, equipment, and process factors that can be fixed.

questions.question: Regarding the pain management oversight principles, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Non-drug comfort measures have no place in pain care
Once a pain medication is ordered, no follow-up on its effect is needed
Pain management oversight ensures pain is assessed regularly, treated through a combination of medication and non-drug approaches as appropriate, and re-evaluated for relief and side effects.
Pain is treated only when a resident repeatedly demands attention

questions.explanation: Effective pain care is a cycle of assessment, intervention, and reassessment rather than a single order.

questions.question: On the subject of the communication support for residents with impairments, which statement is right?

answers.text: If a resident cannot communicate easily, staff should decide without them
Communication aids are personal luxuries outside facility responsibility
Speaking louder solves all hearing and understanding difficulties

Residents with speech, hearing, vision, or cognitive impairments receive aids such as glasses, hearing devices, picture boards, large print, and extra time so they can express needs and take part in decisions.

questions.explanation: The right to be understood does not depend on how easily a person communicates.

questions.question: A new department head at a long-term care organization asks Marta about the income statement overview. Which guidance is correct?

answers.text: The income statement is a roster of unpaid vendor invoices
The income statement reports only cash in the bank on the last day
The income statement lists the personal property owed to residents
The income statement reports revenue earned and expenses incurred over a period and shows whether operations produced a gain or a loss for that period.

questions.explanation: By matching revenue and expenses for the same period, the statement shows the operating result for that period.

questions.question: While orienting a new manager at a nursing home, Lena explains the incident reporting in clinical care. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Reporting is mainly about assigning fault to the nearest staff member
Incidents should be reported only if someone outside the facility saw them
Minor incidents need no review because they caused no injury this time

Incidents such as falls, injuries, and errors are reported promptly, the resident is assessed and cared for, families and physicians are notified as appropriate, and the event is reviewed for prevention lessons.

questions.explanation: Honest, prompt reporting turns individual events into organizational learning and repeated-harm prevention.

questions.question: A resident or family concern at a senior care organization makes the purpose of ethical census development the central issue. Which statement is right?

answers.text: Growing census justifies admitting residents whose needs exceed staff capability
Ethical census development grows occupancy by honestly presenting services, building referral trust, and matching admissions to the care the organization can truly provide.
Ethical census development relies on disparaging competitors with false claims
Ethical census development permits promising services the organization cannot deliver

questions.explanation: Sustainable growth comes from trust and a good fit between resident needs and organizational ability.

questions.question: A resident or family concern at a skilled nursing facility makes the management of unintended weight loss the central issue. Which statement is right?

answers.text: Unintended weight loss is investigated for medical, dental, medication, mood, and dining-related causes, and the care plan is adjusted with added support and closer monitoring.
Unintended weight loss is ignored unless the resident mentions it
The only response to weight loss is to record it without any follow-up
Unintended weight loss is always desirable in long-term care

questions.explanation: Weight loss often signals an underlying problem, so it calls for curiosity and coordinated action rather than simple documentation.

questions.question: In a competency review at a long-term care community, a question addresses the insurance risk transfer concept. Which answer is right?

answers.text: Insurance transfers part of the financial risk of specified losses to an insurer in exchange for premiums, while the facility retains the duty to prevent harm.
Insurance transfers the duty to provide safe care to the insurer
Buying insurance makes risk prevention unnecessary
Insurance pays for every loss regardless of its cause or terms

questions.explanation: Coverage limits financial exposure for covered events, but prevention and safe operations remain facility responsibilities.

questions.question: A problem surfaces at a nursing facility that involves the purpose of financial forecasting. Which statement reflects the correct understanding?

answers.text: Financial forecasting estimates future revenue, expenses, and cash needs using census trends, payer mix, and expected cost changes.
Financial forecasting guarantees that future results will match the estimate exactly
Financial forecasting replaces the need for an operating budget
Financial forecasting is used only to set resident room decorations

questions.explanation: Forecasting helps leaders plan ahead by projecting likely results rather than waiting until money has already been spent or received.

questions.question: Priya is asked to justify a decision involving the behavioral health care coordination at a nursing home. Which statement provides the correct basis?
