questions.question: During a competency assessment at a regional crematory in Canton, a decision turns on machine guarding on processing equipment. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Experienced operators are exempt from guarding rules
Guards on the processor and other moving equipment stay in place during operation, because they are the barrier between the operator and rotating or crushing parts
Guarding is only for visitors' protection
Guards may be removed to clear jams while running

questions.explanation: A guard removed for convenience is an injury scheduled for later.

questions.question: An inspector examining operations at a funeral home crematory in Cleveland asks the operator about receiving remains outside normal hours. Which reply is correct?

answers.text: Receipts are waived for night deliveries
After-hours cases are left at the door for morning staff
Identification checks wait until the office opens
After-hours deliveries follow the same acceptance, identification and receipt procedure, arranged under facility policy, rather than informal drop-offs

questions.explanation: The custody standard does not change with the clock.

questions.question: While orienting a new crematory operator at a crematory facility in Toledo, Lena explains housekeeping in the cremation room. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The cremation room is kept clean, dry and orderly — floors free of slip and trip hazards, tools stored, surfaces sanitised — as a continuous operating condition
A wet floor is marked by operator memory
Tools are stored wherever the last task ended
Housekeeping is a weekly cleaning contract's concern

questions.explanation: Order in the room is a safety control, not an aesthetic preference.

questions.question: Before signing off a trainee operator at a crematory facility in Toledo, Priya tests their grasp of documenting the cremation itself. Which statement shows it?

answers.text: The operator's identity is never recorded
Cremation records are completed in batches at month end
Times are estimated when forgotten
For each case the operator records the cremation — date, times, operator and case identification — in the facility's cremation record as it happens

questions.explanation: Contemporaneous records are evidence; reconstructed ones are guesses.

questions.question: A problem surfaces at an independent crematory in Dayton that involves receiving body parts for cremation. Which statement reflects the correct understanding?

answers.text: Receipts are not given for body parts
Body parts are cremated with the next full-body case
Body parts are accepted and cremated under their own authorization track, with the same identification, receipt and record discipline as a full body
Body parts need no paperwork because they are small

questions.explanation: The authorization track differs; the custody discipline does not.

questions.question: In a competency review at a cemetery crematory in Cincinnati, a question addresses cleaning and disinfecting surfaces that contact remains. Which answer is right?

answers.text: Rinsing with water is sufficient disinfection
Disinfectant contact time can be ignored if the surface looks clean
Tables, trays, transfer devices and holding surfaces are cleaned and disinfected between cases with approved products and contact times, protecting the next case and the staff
Surfaces are disinfected weekly regardless of use

questions.explanation: Cleaning between cases is infection control and dignity control at once.

questions.question: At a staff in-service drawn from a crematory in Columbus's operations, the instructor quizzes staff on shipping cremated remains. Which statement earns the point?

answers.text: Ordinary untracked post is acceptable for remains
When remains are shipped, they are packaged securely and sent by a traceable method, with a signed receipt obtained on delivery, so the remains can be tracked throughout
Shipping needs no receipt because loss is unlikely
Remains are shipped in the urn box without outer packaging

questions.explanation: Traceability and a signed delivery receipt are the shipping standard.

questions.question: Omar, a crematory operator at a crematory in Youngstown, is handling work involving the function of the cremated remains processor. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: The processor washes remains before they are returned
The processor, often called a pulverizer, mechanically reduces recovered bone fragments to the fine, uniform consistency expected for placement in an urn or temporary container
The processor separates families' remains that were mixed together
The processor burns remains a second time at higher heat

questions.explanation: Processing is mechanical size reduction after cremation — it is not a second burning.

questions.question: A problem surfaces at a funeral home crematory in Cleveland that involves separate equipment for human and animal cremation. Which statement reflects the correct understanding?

answers.text: A facility that cremates animals must use separate equipment for cremation and pulverization of human remains and of animals, so there is no opportunity for commingling between them
Shared processing equipment is acceptable if cleaned
Commingling safeguards are waived for small animals
Separation applies only to the chamber, not the processor

questions.explanation: Separate means separate — chamber and processor alike.

questions.question: A senior operator reviewing practice at a funeral home crematory in Cleveland asks about the implant disclosure on the authorization form. Which response is correct?

answers.text: The form must include a statement of whether the authorizing agent actually knows of a pacemaker, defibrillator or other mechanical or radioactive device or implant in the decedent that could endanger cremation personnel
The form asks only about jewellery and valuables
Disclosure is the crematory's guess, recorded later
Implant disclosure is limited to cosmetic implants

questions.explanation: The form asks what the agent actually knows about hazardous devices — because the chamber crew's safety depends on the answer.

questions.question: At a staff in-service drawn from a cemetery crematory in Cincinnati's operations, the instructor quizzes staff on insurance and risk awareness for operators. Which statement earns the point?

answers.text: Risk is a management topic with no operator role
Insurance covers any practice, however careless
Procedure departures are a private operator choice
Operators support the facility's risk position by following procedure exactly — departures from procedure are what turn an insured, defensible operation into an exposed one

questions.explanation: Procedure is the facility's defence; following it is the operator's contribution to that defence.

questions.question: Chris, a crematory operator at a regional crematory in Canton, is handling work involving accuracy of times and dates in case records. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: Dates can be regularised to the working week
Recorded times are internal conveniences only
Times and dates recorded for delivery, cremation and release are the actual times, because the record may be read in a courtroom or by a regulator years later
Approximate times are acceptable in busy periods

questions.explanation: A record's value years later depends on its accuracy on the day.

questions.question: Before signing off a trainee operator at a crematory facility in Toledo, Marcus tests their grasp of container combustibility and equipment protection. Which statement shows it?

answers.text: Any container a family supplies may be cremated without checking
Container material has no effect on the chamber
Metal caskets burn the same as combustible containers
Only containers approved for cremation are charged, because non-combustible or inappropriate containers can damage the hearth, block airflow and leave unburned material

questions.explanation: What goes into the chamber determines how the chamber performs — unsuitable containers are refused.

nyctg.quiz_title: New York City Tour Guide Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Examined closely, the origin of the Wall Street name comes down to one correct statement. Which is it?

answers.text: The wall in question was the wall of the first stock exchange building
Wall Street follows the line of a defensive wall the Dutch built across Manhattan's northern edge in the 1650s against possible English and Native attack
The street is named after a banker called Wall who lent money to the city
Wall Street is named for a market wall built by the British in 1800

questions.explanation: The street name is a fossil of the little walled town that once ended there.

questions.question: On the subject of the Bronx as the mainland borough, which statement is right?

answers.text: Staten Island is connected to the mainland by a land bridge
Queens is the only mainland borough
The Bronx is the only borough attached to the North American mainland; Manhattan and Staten Island are islands of their own and Brooklyn and Queens sit on Long Island
All five boroughs are separate islands

questions.explanation: Mainland Bronx, two island boroughs, two on Long Island: the geography orients every tour.

questions.question: How long does an applicant have to take and pass the examination?

answers.text: Sixty days from the time the applicant's information appears in the exam scheduler's system
There is no time limit of any kind
Seven days from the application date
One full year from the licence's expiration

questions.explanation: The sixty-day window runs from appearance in the scheduler, not from filing.

questions.question: Regarding Bryant Park behind the Public Library, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Bryant Park, the green salon behind the New York Public Library's main branch on 42nd Street, pairs its lawn and reading room with a winter village and ice rink in the cold months
Its lawn is a private garden closed to the public
The library branch stands in Central Park's centre
Bryant Park is a harbour pier in the Bronx

questions.explanation: Lunch crowds on the lawn show how a rescued park serves office New York.

questions.question: On the subject of the Cathedral of St. John the Divine, which statement is right?

answers.text: The cathedral was completed in a single decade in 1800
Its site is a converted ferry terminal in Brooklyn
It is the smallest church in Manhattan
St. John the Divine on Amsterdam Avenue, begun in 1892 and still unfinished, is among the world's largest cathedrals, an Episcopal landmark of Morningside Heights

questions.explanation: Unfinished by design for a century, the cathedral makes a fine story of patience.

questions.question: Examined closely, New York City Hall's age and use comes down to one correct statement. Which is it?

answers.text: City Hall, completed in 1812 downtown, is among the oldest American city halls still housing its municipal government, its mayor's office and council chamber in daily use
The mayor works from an office tower in Albany
City Hall stands abandoned on Governors Island
City Hall was built in 1970 and has never been used

questions.explanation: Two centuries of mayors in one small marble building surprises most visitors.

questions.question: Examined closely, the JFK AirTrain's connections to the city comes down to one correct statement. Which is it?

answers.text: JFK has no rail connection of any kind
The AirTrain links Kennedy Airport's terminals to the subway and Long Island Rail Road at Jamaica and to the subway at Howard Beach, giving arriving visitors a rail path into Manhattan
The AirTrain runs directly into Grand Central's main concourse
It connects the airport only to New Jersey stations

questions.explanation: Jamaica Station is the hinge between the airport and the city for budget travellers.

questions.question: While orienting a new tour guide, Lena explains the Cathedral of St. John the Divine. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: It is the smallest church in Manhattan
Its site is a converted ferry terminal in Brooklyn
The cathedral was completed in a single decade in 1800
St. John the Divine on Amsterdam Avenue, begun in 1892 and still unfinished, is among the world's largest cathedrals, an Episcopal landmark of Morningside Heights

questions.explanation: Unfinished by design for a century, the cathedral makes a fine story of patience.

questions.question: Focus on the Garment District's working heritage for a moment — which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: No clothing businesses remain anywhere in the district

Midtown's Garment District, west of Fifth Avenue around Seventh Avenue, was the nation's clothing workshop, and its sidewalks still carry fashion showrooms, fabric shops and a giant needle-and-button landmark
Seventh Avenue there is nicknamed for banking, not fashion
The Garment District manufactured only ships and steel

questions.explanation: Fashion Avenue's signs let guides tell an industry story at street level.

questions.question: When a situation involving Walt Whitman's Brooklyn years needs resolving on tour, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Whitman never lived in New York at any age
Walt Whitman, Brooklyn's poet of Leaves of Grass, worked as a printer and newspaper editor in Brooklyn and sang the city's crowds, ferries and carpenters into American poetry
Whitman was a Boston sea captain who wrote only of whaling
Leaves of Grass is a novel about the Civil War's generals

questions.explanation: Crossing Brooklyn Ferry lets a guide quote Whitman to commuters doing the same crossing.

questions.question: In a competency review, a question addresses the Flatiron Building's triangular form. Which answer is right?

answers.text: The Flatiron Building of 1902 fills the triangular wedge where Fifth Avenue crosses Broadway at 23rd Street, and its prow-like shape made it an early skyscraper celebrity
The building was named for its use as a laundry headquarters
The Flatiron is a round tower on the Upper West Side
It was built in 1980 as a shopping mall in Staten Island

questions.explanation: The triangle is the grid meeting Broadway's diagonal, frozen into a building.

questions.question: A fellow guide double-checking Priya's commentary raises how Times Square got its name. Which statement settles it?

answers.text: The name honours a mayor called Times who paved the square
The ball drop tradition began in 1999 for the millennium
Longacre Square was renamed Times Square in 1904 when the New York Times moved its headquarters there, and the New Year's Eve ball drop from the Times Tower began a few years later in 1907
Times Square is named for the clocks once manufactured there

questions.explanation: A newspaper's name on a tower renamed a crossroads the whole world now knows.

questions.question: A fellow guide double-checking Victor's commentary raises the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater. Which statement settles it?

answers.text: Alvin Ailey's company, founded in 1958, carried modern dance rooted in Black American experience worldwide, and its signature work Revelations closes performances to this day
The company was founded in 1900 as a ballet school in Boston
Revelations is an opera by the company's founder
Ailey's troupe performs only tap dance

questions.explanation: Revelations' rocking chairs and river imagery give guides a sure closing image.

questions.question: Ingrid is preparing for a tour day based in Queens and must apply the principles of the Apollo Theater on 125th Street. Which statement gives the correct guidance?

answers.text: The Apollo is a movie palace in Times Square built in 1980
Amateur Night began as a radio quiz about geography
The Apollo has never permitted live music
Harlem's Apollo Theater, which began showcasing Black performers in 1934, launched careers through its famous Amateur Night, where a young Ella Fitzgerald won an early victory

questions.explanation: Wednesday Amateur Night is living history guides can still send visitors to.

questions.question: While orienting a new tour guide, Nadia explains the Lenape name recorded for the island that became Manhattan. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The name Manhattan comes from an English duke's family estate
Manhattan is a Dutch word invented by the West India Company
The island's Lenape name meant island of beavers and was later dropped entirely
The island was called Mannahatta, commonly rendered as the island of many hills, a name that survives in the modern borough name Manhattan

questions.explanation: Mannahatta to Manhattan is one of the oldest name survivals a guide can point to in the city.

questions.question: A mentor asks why a point involving the New York subway's round-the-clock operation matters. Which explanation is correct?

answers.text: The subway closes citywide from midnight to six each night
It operates only on weekdays for commuters
The subway runs twenty-four hours a day, every day, one of the few big-city systems never to close nightly, which makes it the visitor's always-available way across the boroughs
Night service runs only on Staten Island

questions.explanation: Never closes is the promise guides can make about the subway at any hour.

questions.question: An examiner-style quiz on the licence syllabus asks about the guide's legal duty under city bus regulations. Which reply is correct?

answers.text: The study materials call the routing rules optional advice
Licensed guides are legally obligated to follow the transportation department's bus regulations when directing a driver, so a guide must never instruct a driver to break routing or stopping rules
Bus regulations bind drivers only, never the guides directing them
Guides may override road rules whenever a schedule is tight

questions.explanation: The licence itself carries the duty: the guide's directions must stay inside the law.

questions.question: Something has gone wrong during a mentoring session with a senior guide, and the Eldridge Street Synagogue's rose window over the tenements is at the center of it. Which statement points the right way?

answers.text: The building stands alone in a suburban field

From inside the restored Eldridge Street sanctuary, stained glass and carved wood rise above the surrounding tenement rooftops, showing how immigrant congregations built splendour into a poor district
Its windows were designed for a Midtown office tower
The sanctuary's interior was rebuilt as a parking garage

questions.explanation: Splendour on a tenement budget is the congregation's statement guides translate.

questions.question: At a study session for the guide examination, the instructor quizzes candidates on the Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine's scale. Which statement earns the point?

answers.text: St. John the Divine's nave is long enough to hold the Statue of Liberty laid on her side, a comparison guides use to give the vast interior a New York measure
The statue comparison belongs to a Brooklyn church
Its nave is the shortest of any American cathedral
The cathedral could fit inside a subway car

questions.explanation: Measuring a cathedral by a statue is measurement in the city's own units.

questions.question: Omar, a licensed guide preparing a guided visit in Central Park, is reviewing work involving the Buttonwood Agreement and the stock exchange's beginnings. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: The Buttonwood Agreement was a treaty ending the Revolutionary War
Brokers first organised on the Brooklyn waterfront in 1900
The stock exchange began as a coffee-house lottery in 1850
In 1792 a group of brokers signed the Buttonwood Agreement under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street, the founding compact of what became the New York Stock Exchange

questions.explanation: A tree-side handshake on Wall Street grew into the world's best-known securities market.

ntn-frontline-national.quiz_title: Police Officer Entrance — NTN FrontLine National Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: At a house party call, a dozen young people spill onto the lawn arguing with officers about shutting the party down, music still blasting from inside. Which action best handles this situation?

answers.text: Use a clear, calm voice to explain what is happening and what you need from the crowd, and give people a specific place to move to
Tell the crowd the investigation details of the collision to prove you are being fair
Ignore the problem entirely and clear the call, hoping it resolves itself
Take the side of whoever seems most sympathetic and order the other side to comply

questions.explanation: Crowds respond to clear information and a single calm voice. Threatening lawful recording or posturing for dominance reliably makes crowds angrier and scenes less safe. A party crowd needs a simple, repeated instruction and a face-saving way to comply. The other choices either escalate the encounter, exceed the officer's authority, or abandon the problem.

questions.question: The City of Marston's noise ordinance limits amplified sound and construction noise in residential areas between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. During those hours, sound from a residence must not be plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the property line. Construction work that produces audible noise at neighboring homes may begin at 7:00 a.m. on weekdays and 8:00 a.m. on weekends. Exemptions include emergency repairs, snow removal, and city-authorized special events. A first violation results in a written warning. A second violation within 12 months may result in a citation with a fine of up to $250. Officers responding to noise complaints measure audibility from the property line of the complaining residence and document the distance, time, and type of sound in their report. The ordinance does not apply to vehicle traffic noise on public streets. According to the passage, which choice correctly gives the audibility distance standard?

answers.text: 25 feet from the house
Across the street
50 feet from the property line
100 feet from the property line

questions.explanation: Sound must not be plainly audible at 50 feet — stated directly in the passage. The other choices change a detail — a date, a number, a condition, or a person — from what the passage actually says.

questions.question: While writing up an abandoned-vehicle investigation, an officer weighs four statements. Which statement is written as a fact rather than an opinion?

answers.text: The clerk clearly did not care about the theft.
The house looked like a drug house.
The suspect looked like a typical troublemaker.
The child was standing with a teacher when officers arrived.

questions.explanation: Reports record what was seen, heard, and done. Conclusions about motives, character, and guilt are opinions and are left out; the facts let readers draw their own conclusions. The factual statement here is: 'The child was standing with a teacher when officers arrived.'

questions.question: A trainee notices a senior officer regularly falsifying the start times on overtime slips by about an hour a week. Which action would be LEAST appropriate for the officer?

answers.text: Report what you observed through the proper internal channel promptly and factually, regardless of friendship or rank — silence makes you part of it
Answer investigators' questions fully and honestly if the matter is reviewed
Write down exactly what you saw, when, and who was present, while memory is fresh
Tell everyone involved to stop wasting police time, and walk away without taking any action

questions.explanation: Integrity systems run on reports from inside. Theft, unjustified force, and falsified time are career-ending for a reason — and witnessing without reporting is its own violation in most agencies. Overtime falsification is fraud, however routine it has become. Each remaining option is defensible; only the keyed action clearly harms the situation.

questions.question: Detectives are investigating a series of incidents in which counterfeit $20 bills were passed at small businesses along the Harbor Avenue corridor. In each incident, a suspect made a small purchase — usually under $5 — and paid with a counterfeit $20, receiving genuine currency as change. Most incidents occurred between 4:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. The bills share a repeating serial number, and the paper feels smoother than genuine currency. Clerks are advised to use the detection pens provided by the Business Association and to check the watermark by holding bills up to the light. Anyone who receives a suspected counterfeit bill should avoid returning it to the passer, note a description of the person and any vehicle, and call the non-emergency line. Retaining the bill, if it can be done safely, helps the investigation; clerks should never place themselves in danger over a bill. Which of the following statements appears in the passage?

answers.text: To build trust with clerks
Rapid-fire
Slow down but continue following closely
Mostly as fragments for speed

questions.explanation: To build trust with clerks — this is stated in the passage. The other statements come from different topics and are not stated anywhere in this passage.

questions.question: An officer moonlighting in security for a mall is asked by mall management to 'deal with' a shoplifter using police authority during security hours. What should the officer do?

answers.text: Take the side of whoever seems most sympathetic and order the other side to comply
Use police authority at the mall since it gets faster results for the client
Disclose the relationship or conflict and step away from the decision or enforcement role, letting an uninvolved officer handle it whenever the situation allows
Ignore the problem entirely and clear the call, hoping it resolves itself

questions.explanation: Even honest handling looks corrupt when the officer has a stake. Disclosure and recusal protect the case, the agency, and the officer's name. Two jobs, two authorities — mixing them serves neither. The other choices either escalate the encounter, exceed the officer's authority, or abandon the problem.

questions.question: A customer in a store demands an officer force the clerk to give a refund, threatening to 'have the officer fired' if the store's policy is not overridden. Which action best handles this situation?

answers.text: Tell everyone involved to stop wasting police time, and walk away without taking any action
Promise an outcome you cannot guarantee, just to end the conversation quickly
Explain that this is a civil matter outside police authority, describe the proper legal channel, and offer to keep the peace while the parties use it
Announce that this is not your problem and direct everyone to call a different agency

questions.explanation: Police authority has legal edges. Evictions, refunds, and HOA rules move through courts and contracts; an officer who enforces them anyway creates liability and can commit a violation personally. A store's refund policy is a contract dispute, not a crime. The distractors fail on judgment, legality, or professionalism — the keyed action satisfies all three.

questions.question: The City is accepting applications for Police Dispatcher through Friday, June 20. Dispatchers answer emergency and non-emergency calls, dispatch police and fire units by radio, and enter information into the computer-aided dispatch system. Applicants must be at least 18 years old, hold a high school diploma or equivalent, and type at least 40 words per minute. Because dispatchers handle sensitive information, finalists must pass a background investigation and a hearing test. The position works rotating 12-hour shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Starting pay is $26.40 per hour, with a raise after successful completion of the one-year probationary period. New dispatchers complete a 10-week paid training academy before working a console alone. Applications are submitted online through the City jobs portal; paper applications are not accepted. Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?

answers.text: The posting announces a new dispatch center building
The posting describes the dispatcher job, its requirements, and how to apply
The posting explains how dispatchers answer 911 calls step by step
The posting compares dispatcher pay across cities

questions.explanation: The main idea covers the whole passage: the posting describes the dispatcher job, its requirements, and how to apply The other choices are too narrow, off-topic, or contradict the passage.

questions.question: In a narrative mentioning the marina parking area, one sentence must be chosen. Which sentence is correctly written?

answers.text: After the briefing, the officers dispersed to their assigned areas quickly fast.
After the briefing, the officers dispersed to there assigned areas.
After the briefing the officers dispersed, to their assigned areas.
After the briefing, the officers dispersed to their assigned areas.

questions.explanation: An introductory phrase takes a comma, the possessive is 'their,' and 'quickly fast' is redundant. (Correct: "After the briefing, the officers dispersed to their assigned areas.")

questions.question: During a welfare check, the resident opens the door holding a kitchen knife she was using to cook, then freezes, unsure what to do, as the officer reacts with surprise. Which action best handles this situation?

answers.text: Create distance and time: slow your movements, give simple repeated instructions, and avoid rushing in while the person is still able to comply verbally
Tell everyone involved to stop wasting police time, and walk away without taking any action
Sprint in and grab for the waistband before the man can reach it again
Shout a stream of different commands from every officer at once

questions.explanation: Time and distance are the officer's allies. Rushed, chaotic encounters with overlapping commands are where avoidable injuries happen. A cook holding a knife needs one clear instruction — 'put it down' — not a tackle. The remaining options tend to make the situation worse, break trust, or create a safety risk.

questions.question: A vehicle matches the general description from a shots-fired call — same color and type — but the area has many such cars, and this one is driving normally. Which action would be LEAST appropriate for the officer?

answers.text: Slow down and build the safest plan the facts allow: call for backup, use distance and light, and gather more information before closing in
Wait for a second unit for the warehouse entry when policy and circumstances allow
Raise your voice and keep shouting until you are obeyed
Advise dispatch of the stop location and circumstances before approaching

questions.explanation: Unknown-risk encounters punish hurry. Backup, information, and positioning are the tools that keep a partial description from becoming a tragedy for anyone involved. A common car color is a reason to verify, not to search the neighborhood's cars. The other options are reasonable professional responses; the keyed action is the one that would make things worse.

questions.question: The Public Works Department will resurface Alder Street between 9th Avenue and 14th Avenue over five nights, beginning Tuesday, October 7. Work will take place from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. each night to reduce disruption to daytime traffic. During work hours, Alder Street will be closed to through traffic, but residents will be able to reach their driveways with the help of flaggers posted at both ends of the work zone. Street parking on Alder Street will be prohibited during work hours, and vehicles left on the street may be towed at the owner's expense. Bus Route 12 will detour onto Birch Street for the duration of the project. The work is expected to finish by Sunday morning, October 12, weather permitting. Residents with questions may call the Public Works information line on weekdays between 7:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. According to the passage, how residents can reach their driveways during work hours?

answers.text: They cannot reach them until the project ends
By parking on Birch Street
With the help of flaggers at both ends of the work zone
Only after 5:00 a.m.

questions.explanation: Flaggers help residents reach their driveways — stated directly in the passage. Each other choice alters something the passage states; close reading of the exact wording settles it.

questions.question: An off-duty officer sees a social-media thread about her own department full of false claims, and is tempted to reply from her personal account with inside details. Which of the following would be the worst response?

answers.text: Remember you represent the agency in and out of uniform: decline to share case information, correct nothing with insider facts, and refuse favors that misuse the badge
Post a correction using non-public details to stop the false claims quickly
Suggest the cousin follow the department's official releases like everyone else
Keep social-media activity within agency policy and free of case details

questions.explanation: Insider information and badge favors are the currency of corruption, even in small denominations. The uniform's credibility depends on declining both, kindly but completely. Fighting false claims with confidential facts trades one problem for a worse one. Each remaining option is defensible; only the keyed action clearly harms the situation.

questions.question: State law requires every vessel to carry one properly fitting life jacket for each person on board. Children under 13 must wear a life jacket at all times while a vessel is underway. Vessels 16 feet or longer must also carry a throwable flotation device. Motorboats must display navigation lights between sunset and sunrise and during periods of restricted visibility. Operating a vessel while intoxicated carries penalties similar to those for driving a vehicle while intoxicated, including fines and possible loss of boating privileges. A vessel's operator is responsible for keeping a proper lookout and maintaining a safe speed for conditions, including traffic, weather, and visibility. Accidents involving injury, death, or property damage over $2,000 must be reported to the marine patrol within 48 hours. As used in the passage, the word 'vessel' most nearly means —

answers.text: A boat or ship
A flotation cushion
A harbor
A life jacket

questions.explanation: In this passage, 'vessel' means a boat or ship. The surrounding sentences confirm that meaning.

questions.question: A radio broadcast described the person this way: at 4:45 p.m., a woman in her 20s wearing a yellow rain jacket and black slacks, with a rolling suitcase, walking two dogs. According to the observation, which item was the person carrying or accompanied by?

answers.text: a guitar case
a dog on a leash
a bicycle
a rolling suitcase

questions.explanation: The observation states the person was carrying or accompanied by a rolling suitcase. Small associated details often distinguish one sighting from another. Choosing well here depends on the details in front of you, not on habit.

questions.question: A resident stops an officer on foot patrol to complain that patrol cars 'never' come down her street and response times are 'a joke.' She is firm but polite. Which response is best in this situation?

answers.text: Listen fully, acknowledge the concern without being defensive, explain honestly what the department is doing, and pass the specific concern to the right supervisor or unit
Take the side of whoever seems most sympathetic and order the other side to comply
Tell everyone involved to stop wasting police time, and walk away without taking any action
Handle the whole matter by text message later instead of dealing with it in person

questions.explanation: Complaints are information and a relationship test. Listening, honesty about limits, and routing the concern onward build trust; arguing, blaming, and false promises destroy it. A foot-patrol complaint is best met with specifics — where and when — not defensiveness. The other choices either escalate the encounter, exceed the officer's authority, or abandon the problem.

questions.question: The Department's Community Policing Officer (CPO) program assigns one officer to each of the city's twelve neighborhoods for a minimum of two years. Unlike patrol officers, who respond to calls across a district, a CPO works a regular daytime schedule in the same neighborhood, attends community meetings, and follows up on recurring problems such as abandoned vehicles, repeat noise locations, and graffiti. CPOs do not replace patrol response: emergencies and in-progress crimes in the neighborhood are still handled by patrol units. Each CPO maintains an office hour each week at a library or community center where residents can raise concerns without an appointment. The program's goal is to solve recurring problems and build familiarity, so that residents know an officer by name before a crisis occurs. CPO performance is measured by problem-resolution and community-survey results, not by citation counts. According to the passage, who handles emergencies in a CPO neighborhood?

answers.text: The CPO alone
The fire department
No one; CPOs handle everything
Patrol units

questions.explanation: Patrol handles emergencies and in-progress crimes — stated directly in the passage. Each other choice alters something the passage states; close reading of the exact wording settles it.

questions.question: A partner conducting a stop is focused on the driver while a passenger quietly steps out on the far side and starts moving toward the rear of the car. What is the most appropriate action for the officer?

answers.text: Ignore the problem entirely and clear the call, hoping it resolves itself
Tell everyone involved to stop wasting police time, and walk away without taking any action

Move to assist immediately and communicate clearly: take a useful role — controlling a limb, watching the crowd or the passenger, calling updates — rather than watching or duplicating your partner's exact effort
Take the side of whoever seems most sympathetic and order the other side to comply

questions.explanation: Backup is active, not spectating: the second officer's eyes, voice, and hands each have a job. Hesitation and freelancing both endanger the partner. The far-side passenger is exactly what a cover officer exists to see. The remaining options tend to make the situation worse, break trust, or create a safety risk.

questions.question: The City is accepting applications for Police Dispatcher through Friday, June 20. Dispatchers answer emergency and non-emergency calls, dispatch police and fire units by radio, and enter information into the computer-aided dispatch system. Applicants must be at least 18 years old, hold a high school diploma or equivalent, and type at least 40 words per minute. Because dispatchers handle sensitive information, finalists must pass a background investigation and a hearing test. The position works rotating 12-hour shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Starting pay is $26.40 per hour, with a raise after successful completion of the one-year probationary period. New dispatchers complete a 10-week paid training academy before working a console alone. Applications are submitted online through the City jobs portal; paper applications are not accepted. A 19-year-old with a diploma who types 35 words per minute is?

answers.text: Qualified if they pass the hearing test
Not qualified, because of the background investigation
Not yet qualified, because the typing minimum is 40 words per minute
Qualified, because the age and education requirements are met

questions.explanation: For 'Recruitment Posting: Police Dispatcher (Excerpt)': not yet qualified, because the typing minimum is 40 words per minute — this follows from the passage's stated facts applied to the situation. The other choices contradict the passage or add information it does not give.

questions.question: An officer starting a shift finds the patrol car's fuel near empty, a low tire, and the previous shift's food wrappers in the back — none of it logged or reported. What is the most appropriate action for the officer?

answers.text: Handle your part and report the gap: complete the vehicle/equipment checks, log deficiencies for maintenance, and leave shared gear ready for the next officer
Threaten to arrest everyone present if the situation does not end immediately
Use the last charged battery and leave the rest for day shift
Handle the whole matter by text message later instead of dealing with it in person

questions.explanation: Shared equipment fails at the worst moments when everyone assumes someone else handled it. Checking, logging, and leaving gear ready is basic team care. An empty tank and low tire discovered at roll-out are a gift compared with discovering them mid-call. The other choices either escalate the encounter, exceed the officer's authority, or abandon the problem.

fbi-special-agent-phase-i.quiz_title: FBI Special Agent Phase I Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An office handbook gives these facts. If wind speeds pass the safety threshold, then crane work is suspended. Suppose crane work is suspended. Which statement MUST be true?

answers.text: Wind speeds pass the safety threshold
It cannot be concluded from these facts that wind speeds pass the safety threshold
Wind speeds pass the safety threshold is the only way that crane work is suspended can happen
It is not the case that crane work is suspended

questions.explanation: An if-then statement cannot be reversed: crane work is suspended happening does not prove wind speeds pass the safety threshold caused it, because the rule only states what follows when wind speeds pass the safety threshold happens. The facts leave the cause of this occurrence open.

questions.question: Your technical summary must also be read by community members with no background in the subject. Which action should be avoided most strongly?

answers.text: Rewrite in plain language — short sentences, terms explained, the key point first — while keeping every fact accurate
Simplify by removing the qualifications until the claims are stronger than the facts
Test the draft on a colleague from another unit and fix wherever they stumble
Lead with the conclusion, define each necessary technical term once, and cut the rest

questions.explanation: Communication means the audience actually receives the message: plain language that stays accurate, not simplification that bends the facts. Community members can act on the summary without a specialist translator. The keyed response is the single action a supervisor would counsel an employee never to take here.

questions.question: A pair of personality statements both feel true to a candidate. What does the format require?

answers.text: They may leave the slider exactly in the middle to show equal agreement
They should choose the statement that sounds more impressive
They should alternate sides to keep their answers balanced
They must move the slider toward one statement — a neutral position is not possible

questions.explanation: The guide is explicit: the selector cannot be left in the middle. When both statements feel true, the candidate chooses the degree toward the one that fits them more. Choosing well here depends on the details in front of you, not on habit.

questions.question: A planning memo states the following. If a shipment arrives without paperwork, then the shipment is held at the dock. Suppose the shipment is held at the dock. Which statement MUST be true?

answers.text: A shipment arrives without paperwork
It is not the case that the shipment is held at the dock
It cannot be concluded from these facts that a shipment arrives without paperwork
A shipment arrives without paperwork is the only way that the shipment is held at the dock can happen

questions.explanation: An if-then statement cannot be reversed: the shipment is held at the dock happening does not prove a shipment arrives without paperwork caused it, because the rule only states what follows when a shipment arrives without paperwork happens. The facts leave the cause of this occurrence open.

questions.question: Find the rule in the described figures. Letter sequence: E, H, K, N, Q, ? Which letter completes the sequence?

answers.text: T
U
W
Q

questions.explanation: Each letter advances 3 places in the alphabet. The next letter is T.

questions.question: Working only from the facts below, answer the question. No member of the Northgate Program works in the weekend roster. Every member of the Union Unit is a member of the Northgate Program. Which statement MUST be true?

answers.text: No member of the Union Unit works in the weekend roster
No member of the Northgate Program works anywhere except the weekend roster
Some members of the Union Unit work in the weekend roster
Everyone who works in the weekend roster is a member of the Union Unit

questions.explanation: Every Union Unit member is an Northgate Program member, and no Northgate Program member works in the weekend roster, so no Union Unit member can work there either. A 'no' statement means the two groups have no overlap at all.

questions.question: A row of figures is described as follows. Letter sequence: J, K, N, O, R, ? Which letter completes the sequence?

answers.text: T
R
V
S

questions.explanation: Letters come in adjacent pairs, and each new pair starts a fixed number of places after the previous pair began. The next letter is S.

questions.question: A shared inbox keeps receiving the same misdirected requests because an old instruction page still circulates. Which action best handles this situation?

answers.text: Wait for a supervisor to notice the pattern themselves
Handle the whole matter informally later instead of dealing with it now
Take the side of whoever seems most sympathetic and order the other side to comply
Document the pattern with examples and propose a root-cause fix to your supervisor

questions.explanation: Initiative is pattern ownership: documented examples plus a proposed fix turn a recurring annoyance into a solved problem — while unapproved solo fixes to shared materials create a different risk. The stale instruction page is proposed for correction through the right hands. The other choices either escalate the situation, breach a duty, or abandon the problem.

questions.question: From the FBI's official guidance, the PFT self-evaluation is completed —

answers.text: A Physical Fitness Test self-evaluation, to determine readiness to move forward in SASS
A medical examination at Quantico
A panel interview with field office leadership
A firearms qualification course

questions.explanation: Applicants complete a PFT self-evaluation before the Meet and Greet; an applicant who cannot yet meet the minimum is advised to consider withdrawing and re-applying, with their Phase I result remaining valid while they stay eligible. This is the standard the exam measures in this area.

questions.question: Under the published Phase I rules, a candidate who needs a testing accommodation should —

answers.text: Unavailable for computerized assessments
Requested for each test as needed, and decided case by case; each test in the process is evaluated differently
Granted automatically once for the entire process
Requested only after a first attempt without one

questions.explanation: The guide provides an FBI contact for accommodation requests, requires a request per test, and states each decision is case by case. The other choices fail on the facts given, on judgment, or on both.

questions.question: The sequence below describes one figure at a time. A 3-by-3 arrangement of figures follows one rule: every row and every column contains each shape exactly once. Row 1: circle, star, cross. Row 2: star, cross, circle. Row 3: ?, circle, star. Which shape belongs in the missing cell (row 3, column 1)?

answers.text: oval
cross
circle
star

questions.explanation: Row 3 and column 1 each already contain the other two values, so the only shape that completes both without repeating is cross. This is the standard the exam measures in this area.

questions.question: Reviewing a shared draft, you notice your teammate transposed two figures in a table. The draft goes to a supervisor in an hour. Which response is best in this situation?

answers.text: Quietly show your teammate the error right away so they can fix it before the product goes out
Take the side of whoever seems most sympathetic and order the other side to comply
Raise the error in front of the supervisor to show your own diligence
Leave the error in and let the supervisor's review catch it

questions.explanation: Teamwork protects the product and the teammate at the same time: a private, immediate flag lets the owner fix their own work before it matters. The figures reach the supervisor correct, and your teammate keeps ownership of their section. The remaining options trade a short-term reaction for a worse outcome.

questions.question: Assume all of the following are accurate. Some members of the Harbor Division handle the public counter. No one who handles the public counter is a member of the Harbor Squad. Which statement MUST be true?

answers.text: Some members of the Harbor Squad handle the public counter
All members of the Harbor Division are members of the Harbor Squad
Some members of the Harbor Division are not members of the Harbor Squad
It is false that any member of the Harbor Division is described this way

questions.explanation: The Harbor Division members described — those who handle the public counter — cannot be in the Harbor Squad, because nobody described that way is. So some Harbor Division members must fall outside the Harbor Squad.

questions.question: A partner's section of a joint memo cites the wrong date for a key event. Nobody else has caught it, and the memo is about to be sent. Which action would be LEAST appropriate?

answers.text: Quietly show your teammate the error right away so they can fix it before the product goes out
Flag the item to the whole team channel so anyone can correct it in time
Fix the error yourself and mention it to your teammate afterward so they know
Raise the error in front of the supervisor to show your own diligence

questions.explanation: Teamwork protects the product and the teammate at the same time: a private, immediate flag lets the owner fix their own work before it matters. The memo goes out with the right date because you spoke up privately and early. The other options are reasonable professional responses; the keyed action is the one that would make things worse.

questions.question: As the FBI publishes it, if honest answers could reduce a candidate's chances, the published approach remains —

answers.text: Adjust later answers to compensate for the earlier ones
Use the middle option for the rest of the section
Keep answering accurately — the option that most accurately describes them is always the instruction
Slow down and reconsider every earlier answer

questions.explanation: The preparation guidance never changes: choose the option that most accurately describes you. Compensation strategies are exactly the 'beating the test' behavior the guide warns against. The other choices fail on the facts given, on judgment, or on both.

questions.question: The following statements are all true. All members of the Summit Team are members of the Cobalt Cohort. Every member of the Cobalt Cohort is also a member of the Northgate Section. Lila is a member of the Summit Team. Based only on these facts, which statement MUST be false?

answers.text: Lila is a member of the Northgate Section
All members of the Summit Team are members of the Northgate Section
Some members of the Northgate Section are members of the Summit Team
Some members of the Summit Team are not members of the Northgate Section

questions.explanation: Because every Summit Team member is a Cobalt Cohort member and every Cobalt Cohort member is a Northgate Section member, it is impossible for any Summit Team member to fall outside the Northgate Section — that statement must be false. Each other statement must be true.

questions.question: Halfway through a project, your supervisor redirects it: the audience has changed, and two sections you finished no longer fit. Which action best handles this situation?

answers.text: Refuse the change until it is put in a formal order
Announce that this is not your problem and direct everyone elsewhere
Confirm the new requirements, salvage what still fits, and rebuild the rest against the new direction without dwelling on the sunk work
Handle the whole matter informally later instead of dealing with it now

questions.explanation: Flexibility and adaptability are core to the role: direction changes are normal, and the professional response re-aims the usable work at the new target. The project reaches its new audience with the salvageable sections intact. The other choices either escalate the situation, breach a duty, or abandon the problem.

questions.question: The following figures are presented in order. A 3-by-3 arrangement follows two rules at once: in every row and column, each of the three shapes appears once and each of the three shadings appears once. Row 1: white crescent; shaded circle; ?. Row 2: shaded cross; black crescent; white circle. Row 3: black circle; white cross; shaded crescent. Which figure belongs in the missing cell (row 1, column 3)?

answers.text: black circle
white circle
white cross
black cross

questions.explanation: Row 1 is missing one shape and one shading, and column 3 is missing the same pair; the only figure satisfying both is the black cross.

questions.question: A senior colleague suggests your draft summary 'go easier' on a subject your unit knows socially, before it goes to a decision-maker. What is the most appropriate response?

answers.text: Rewrite the finding to be technically true but misleading
Handle the whole matter informally later instead of dealing with it now
Keep the finding exactly as the facts support, and note the pressure through the appropriate channel if it continues
Promise an outcome you cannot guarantee, just to end the conversation quickly

questions.explanation: A report that bends under social pressure fails its only purpose. Stating the supported finding — and creating a record of the pressure — is the professional response. The decision-maker reads what the evidence supports, not what was comfortable to write. The remaining options trade a short-term reaction for a worse outcome.

questions.question: Working only from the facts below, answer the question. Some members of the Juniper Cohort are members of the Westbrook Section. All members of the Westbrook Section are members of the Ridgeline Panel. Which statement MUST be true?

answers.text: All members of the Juniper Cohort are members of the Ridgeline Panel
Some members of the Juniper Cohort are members of the Ridgeline Panel
Some members of the Juniper Cohort are not members of the Ridgeline Panel
No members of the Juniper Cohort are members of the Ridgeline Panel

questions.explanation: The Juniper Cohort members who are in the Westbrook Section are also in the Ridgeline Panel, because every Westbrook Section member is. So at least some Juniper Cohort members must be Ridgeline Panel members. 'Some' says nothing about the rest, so the stronger and negative claims do not follow.

The tow truck removed the vehicle at 9:02 a.m., and the service drive reopened at 9:07 a.m.. What type of vehicle was involved?

answers.text: A red SUV
A black motorcycle
A white delivery van
A white minivan

questions.question: Standing rule: Evacuation Rule. On a fire alarm, occupants leave by the nearest stairwell; elevators are not used. questions.question: The letter group AZM is hidden inside exactly one of these four strings (set 5): first string: JMSUMGSLDWMFFKD; second string: ZSZKWGKTKXKHFCT; third string: JJRAZMLBZJHKPRV; fourth string: UCRMSAGGTWHSXDU. Which string contains the group AZM?

answers.text: The fourth string (begins UCRM)
The third string (begins JJRA)
The first string (begins JMSU)
The second string (begins ZSZK)

questions.explanation: Scanning each string letter by letter, the group AZM appears only in the third string (set 5).

questions.question: Part 2 of the personality measure asks candidates to —

answers.text: A list of duties to memorize
Two essays to compare
A story to summarize
Two statements, choosing the one they most agree with

questions.explanation: Part 2 presents two statements; the candidate selects the one most agreed with.

questions.question: A paragraph about organizing a case file (set 1-8) needs a topic sentence. Which sentence best introduces the paragraph's main idea?

answers.text: Some people dislike organizing a case file for reasons that are never explained (note 1-8).
Careful preparation (guide 1) makes organizing a case file safer and more effective for everyone involved.
Nobody has ever thought about organizing a case file before today (note 1-8).
The history of organizing a case file began in another country long ago (note 1-8).

questions.explanation: The topic sentence must state the paragraph's main idea about organizing a case file; the keyed sentence does that, while the others are vague, off-topic, or unsupported.

questions.question: In a written report, the word "detain" is closest in meaning to —

answers.text: to keep someone in official custody, typically for questioning
to discourage someone from doing something by instilling doubt or fear of consequences
extreme tiredness resulting from mental or physical exertion
having no fixtures, furniture, or inhabitants; empty

questions.explanation: The word "detain" means: to keep someone in official custody, typically for questioning.

questions.question: Five applicants are interviewed in some order. Clues: Hana is in position 4. Rosa is last. Aaron comes somewhere before Hana. Aaron is first. Ivan comes immediately before Hana. Who is in position 2?

answers.text: Rosa
Vera
Hana
Aaron

questions.explanation: Applying every clue leaves one possible arrangement, and position 2 in it is Vera.

questions.question: 3-layer block stack, described in words: layer 1 (from the bottom) has 3 blocks; layer 2 (from the bottom) has 3 blocks; layer 3 (from the bottom) has 3 blocks. How many blocks are in the whole stack?
questions.explanation: Adding the layers (3 + 3 + 3) gives 9 blocks.

questions.question: Memorization scene — marina (described in words; study the details, then answer): Scene: A marina in the late afternoon. A white sailboat named WINDSONG is tied at dock 7. A man in a striped shirt is coiling a rope on its deck. To the right of the sailboat, a green canoe rests upside down on the dock. Five seagulls stand on the roof of the bait shop. A red fuel drum stands beside the shop door. In the water near the dock, two children in orange life jackets sit in a small rowboat. A lighthouse with black and white bands is visible across the harbor. A sign on the dock gate reads NO WAKE ZONE. Question: The children in the rowboat wear —

answers.text: Blue helmets
Red life jackets
Orange life jackets
Yellow raincoats

questions.explanation: The children wear orange life jackets. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Per the NYSP selection-process page, candidates on the eligibility list are —

answers.text: Ranking by county of residence
Order of application date, first come first served
Ranking candidates in order of exam scores, plus any applicable veteran's credit
Alphabetical order of application

questions.explanation: The list ranks candidates by exam score plus applicable veteran's credit.

questions.question: A proofreader is checking whom as an object. Which sentence needs no correction?

answers.text: She is the officer, whom the chief praised her at the ceremony.
She is the officer whom the chief praised at the ceremony.
She is the officer who the chief praised at the ceremony.
She is the officer whom the chief praised at the ceremony's.

questions.explanation: 'Whom' is correct because the pronoun is the object of 'praised.' Choosing well here depends on the details in front of you, not on habit.

questions.question: Passage — Middletown: A long-running effort by Troop F in the Middletown area is a bicycle-patrol community program. Trooper Alicia Gomez directs the program, which began in 2018. Over the whole summer, its daily afternoon patrols — held on weekdays at the downtown business district — have reached 46 shop owners. The troop reports that shoplifting reports on the main street fell by 22 percent. Its purpose is to make troopers more approachable to merchants while increasing visible patrols. Question: Based on the passage, the program's sessions take place at —

answers.text: the troop headquarters parking lot
six commuter rail stations
the county fairgrounds classroom
the downtown business district

questions.explanation: The passage states where the sessions are held. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the rule, or on both.

questions.question: Which option is the correct sentence? The point tested is agreement with 'each'.

answers.text: Each of the recruits, they was issued a uniform on the first day.
Each of the recruits was issued a uniform on the first day.
Each of the recruits was issue a uniform on the first day.
All of the sentences in this set are equally correct.

questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so 'was issued' is correct, and 'a uniform' takes 'a,' not 'an.' This answer holds up under the facts as presented.

questions.question: A supervisor reviews a case under the rule: If a report contains an error, then the writer files a corrected supplement. The record shows it did not happen that the writer files a corrected supplement. The valid conclusion is —

answers.text: Nothing at all can be concluded from a missing result.
In that case, it was not true that a report contains an error.
The rule must have been repealed.
In that case, a report contains an error anyway.

questions.explanation: This is the contrapositive: if the consequence did not occur, the condition that guarantees it cannot have occurred. The keyed answer is the only one consistent with every fact given.

questions.question: Starting at the village green flagpole, facing north: you turn right and walk 1 block, then walk 4 blocks, then turn right and walk 1 block, then walk 2 blocks, then walk 1 block. Where are you now relative to where you started? (Route 33)

answers.text: 4 blocks north and 5 blocks east of the start
4 blocks south and 5 blocks west of the start
5 blocks north and 4 blocks west of the start
4 blocks south and 5 blocks east of the start

questions.explanation: Tracking each leg from facing north gives a net offset of 4 blocks south and 5 blocks east of the start.

questions.question: Passage — Canandaigua: Troop E, based near Canandaigua, runs a boating-safety education program. The effort is led by Investigator Sarah Lindqvist. It began in 2023, when the troop looked for a practical way to address a local safety problem. So far the program has reached 260 boaters through six weekend courses held over eight weeks. Sessions are held on Sundays at the marina education center. Organizers report that boating warnings on the lake fell by 20 percent while registrations rose. The stated purpose of the program is to teach new boaters life-jacket rules and safe speeds near docks and swimmers. Question: The troop reports which result of the program?

answers.text: Funding for the program was tripled by the legislature
The program won a national award in its first year
Boating warnings on the lake fell by 20 percent while registrations rose
The program was expanded to every county in the state

questions.explanation: The reported outcome is stated in the passage; the other results are never mentioned. The distractors each miss a detail that decides the item.

questions.question: Premises: No drivers for the delivery cooperative are allowed to reserve the telescope. Tara Whitfield is one of the drivers for the delivery cooperative. Which conclusion must be true?

answers.text: Tara Whitfield is one of the members of the astronomy club.
Some drivers for the delivery cooperative are allowed to reserve the telescope.
Tara Whitfield is allowed to reserve the telescope.
Tara Whitfield is not allowed to reserve the telescope.

questions.explanation: If no member of the group has the second property and the person belongs to the group, the person cannot have that property.

questions.question: A supervisor asks for the steps in order. the task is responding to a disabled vehicle (round 1 variant for responding to a disabled vehicle). Numbered sentences: (1) Park behind the vehicle with emergency lights activated. (2) Ask the driver what help is needed. (3) Arrange a tow or assistance and stay until the roadway is clear. (4) Approach on the side away from moving traffic. Which numbered order puts the steps in the most logical sequence?

answers.text: 3, then 2, then 1, then 4
1, then 4, then 2, then 3
1, then 3, then 4, then 2
4, then 3, then 2, then 1

questions.explanation: For responding to a disabled vehicle, the logical sequence is: Park behind the vehicle with emergency lights activated. Approach on the side away from moving traffic. Ask the driver what help is needed. Arrange a tow or assistance and stay until the roadway is clear. That is numbered order 1, then 4, then 2, then 3.

questions.question: A sequence of shaded counters (described in words) changes as follows: 50, 46, 41, 35, ? The decreases grow by one each step (4, 5, 6, ...). What number comes next?
questions.explanation: The drops are 4, 5, 6, so the next drop is 7: 35 minus 7 equals 28.

questions.question: The definition "far away in distance; situated far from the main centers" belongs to the word —

answers.text: damage
urgent
occupy
remote

questions.explanation: "Far away in distance; situated far from the main centers" is the definition of "remote".

ahip-medicare-certification.quiz_title: AHIP Medicare Certification Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Among these statements on skilled nursing facility coverage, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: Part A covers skilled nursing facility care only after a qualifying inpatient hospital stay of at least three days, not counting the discharge day
Part A covers custodial nursing home care for up to 100 days per year
Skilled nursing coverage requires a daily need for skilled care related to the hospital condition, and it is not coverage for custodial care
In a benefit period, the first 20 days of covered skilled nursing care carry no coinsurance, a coinsurance amount applies to the following days, and coverage ends after day 100

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. SNF coverage needs a 3-day qualifying *inpatient* stay (observation does not count), a daily skilled need, and it runs at most 100 days per benefit period with coinsurance after day 20.

questions.question: Which statement about the MA out-of-pocket maximum is accurate?

answers.text: Drug copayments count toward the medical out-of-pocket maximum
Every Medicare Advantage plan must set an annual maximum out-of-pocket limit for Part A and Part B services, after which the plan pays the full cost of covered services for the rest of the year
Original Medicare has the same built-in out-of-pocket maximum as Advantage plans
Medicare Advantage plans may choose whether to have an out-of-pocket maximum

questions.explanation: A mandatory MOOP for Parts A/B services is Medicare Advantage's signature protection; premiums and Part D spending sit outside it.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes drugs Part D does not cover?

answers.text: A drug covered by Part B in a situation is also payable by Part D for the same use
By law, Part D excludes certain categories such as most drugs for weight loss or gain, fertility drugs, cosmetic or hair-growth drugs, and cough and cold symptom drugs
Part D covers every drug a doctor prescribes
Weight-loss drugs are a mandatory Part D category

questions.explanation: Statutory exclusions plus the Part B/Part D boundary define Part D's edge: excluded categories never count toward the cap, and B-covered uses stay in B.

questions.question: A beneficiary asks about permission to contact. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Documentation of permission is unnecessary if the agent remembers the conversation
Revocation of permission must be honored promptly and recorded
Revocation is effective at the end of the plan year
Permission transfers freely between unrelated agencies

questions.explanation: Permission is documented, bounded, and revocable — treated as the beneficiary's property, not the agent's asset.

questions.question: One statement about documenting SEP eligibility is not true. Which one is it?

answers.text: The agent's memory is sufficient documentation
Plans may request proof of the SEP event, and an enrollment without a valid event can be denied or reversed
An SEP enrollment should be supported by documentation of the qualifying event — a move record, a coverage-loss notice, or a status-change letter
Agents should record which SEP they relied on in the client file for every midyear enrollment

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Midyear enrollments stand on their qualifying events: name the SEP, keep the proof, and expect the plan to be able to ask.

questions.question: Walter Hughes is reviewing training material on age-based Medicare eligibility. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Most people become eligible for Medicare at age 65 if they are U.S. citizens or lawfully present residents who meet the residency requirements
Turning 65 is the most common path to Medicare, and the initial enrollment period is built around the 65th birthday month
A person can qualify for Medicare at 65 through their own work record or through a spouse's work record
Medicare eligibility at 65 requires passing a health screening

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Eligibility at 65 turns on age, citizenship/residency, and a qualifying work record (one's own or a spouse's) — not on retirement, health status, or collecting Social Security early.

questions.question: A new agent makes several claims about what Part D covers. Which claim should a trainer correct?

answers.text: Part D helps pay for outpatient prescription drugs, with each plan maintaining its own list of covered drugs called a formulary
A person with Part A and/or Part B may join a stand-alone Part D plan to add drug coverage to Original Medicare
Part D is Medicare prescription drug coverage, offered by private companies approved by Medicare, either as a stand-alone plan or inside a Medicare Advantage plan
Part D covers cosmetic drugs and fertility drugs as a standard benefit

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Part D is voluntary prescription drug coverage through approved private plans, each with its own formulary. Drugs given during a covered inpatient stay are paid under Part A, not Part D.

questions.question: A client wants to know about biosimilars and generic substitution counseling. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: Agents should explain that a formulary's shift toward a generic is a cost-design change, not a loss of Medicare coverage itself
Exceptions for brand products are decided by the agent
Generic substitution voids the member's Part D coverage
Brand drugs are always clinically superior to generics

questions.explanation: Generic and biosimilar steering is built into Part D economics; the member's protection is the prescriber-supported exception, not a right to the brand at generic cost.

questions.question: During a team huddle on prohibited terminology and superlatives, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Marketing may not claim a plan is the 'best' or 'highest rated' or use similar absolute superlatives unless the claim can be substantiated and properly sourced
Testimonials from agents can substitute for substantiation
Materials may not state or imply that Medicare or CMS endorses or recommends a specific plan
Agents may not call a plan 'Medicare-approved' in a way that suggests the government recommends choosing it

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. No unsubstantiated absolutes and no implied government endorsement — CMS contracts with plans; it does not recommend them.

questions.question: A beneficiary asks about misuse of the Medicare name, card and symbols. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Marketing may not be designed to look like official government mail — deceptive envelopes and 'open immediately' government styling are prohibited tactics
Medicare numbers may be requested by email for a quote
The Medicare logo may be used by any AHIP-certified agent
Official styling is a formatting choice, not a compliance issue

questions.explanation: Official identity is not a marketing costume: no look-alike government pieces, no casual handling of Medicare numbers, no implied officialdom.

questions.question: A client wants to know about when an enrollment can be denied. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: An agent who receives a denial should help the beneficiary understand the valid path — a correct period or a correct plan — rather than resubmitting the same request
Service-area denials can be overridden by the agent
Resubmitting an identical application cures a denial
Entitlement is verified after the plan year begins

questions.explanation: Denials police the gates — period, area, entitlement. The agent's job after a denial is diagnosis and a lawful alternative, not repetition.

questions.question: A colleague's notes on the compliance officer and committee contain an error. Which line is the error?

answers.text: Sales leadership cannot override a compliance determination to protect a sales goal
A sales vice president may veto compliance findings
A sponsor's compliance officer must be an employee of the sponsor organization with direct access to senior leadership
The compliance function must have the authority and resources to halt non-compliant activity, not merely advise about it

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Compliance needs a named owner inside the sponsor, a line to the top, and stop authority that sales targets cannot outrank.

questions.question: Kevin Doyle is reviewing a client's coverage before renewal season. On the question of retiree coverage and Medicare, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Retiree coverage is not coverage based on current employment, so it does not protect against the Part B late-enrollment penalty
Retiree plans are standardized by Medicare like Medigap plans
Delaying Part B is penalty-free whenever retiree coverage exists
A retiree plan can waive Medicare's late-enrollment penalties

questions.explanation: Retiree coverage supplements Medicare but carries no Part B delay protection. Its coordination terms are plan-specific and must be checked before any delay advice.

questions.question: Thomas Rivera, a licensed agent, is helping a client compare coverage options. Regarding MA plan service areas and availability, which guidance is correct?

answers.text: A member who moves keeps the same plan with no action needed
Not every plan type is available everywhere; rural areas may have few or no Medicare Advantage options
Plan availability is identical in every county
A person may join a plan in a county they visit frequently even if they live elsewhere

questions.explanation: MA is local: county-based service areas, uneven availability, and a move triggers both a duty to change plans and a special enrollment window.

questions.question: Nancy Fitzgerald is reviewing training material on helping a member who cannot afford a drug today. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Paying cash for a non-covered drug builds out-of-pocket credit for the year
A point-of-sale problem is often a coverage problem in disguise — a missing prior authorization or a non-formulary drug — and is solved at the plan, not the register
The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan can smooth a large bill across remaining months but cannot make a non-covered drug covered

An agent or pharmacist helping a member facing an unaffordable fill should check, in order, formulary status, tier exception options, Extra Help eligibility, manufacturer or charitable assistance, and the payment plan

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Unaffordable fills have a diagnostic order: coverage, exception, subsidy, assistance, smoothing. Cash for non-covered drugs buys no threshold progress — and skipping doses is never the advice.

questions.question: A beneficiary repeats something they read online about marketing materials created by TPMOs. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Review duties apply only to plan-created materials
A TPMO may not invent plan comparisons that present one sponsor's plan using another plan's outdated data
Multi-plan marketing materials created by a TPMO must meet CMS content requirements and go through the applicable review or acceptance process involving the plans whose products are marketed
Generic TPMO advertising that names no plan still must avoid implying Medicare endorsement

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. TPMO-created pieces play by the same review and accuracy rules as plan pieces — generic does not mean unregulated, and comparisons must be current and fair.

questions.question: What should an agent understand about enrollment during the first months of MA (the OEP safety valve)? Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A new MA member who discovers in January that a key doctor is out of network can use the MA Open Enrollment Period to change plans or return to Original Medicare
New members must wait until the next AEP for any correction
A January check-in is prohibited post-sale contact
The OEP is only for changing drug plans

questions.explanation: January surprises have a January remedy — if someone is watching the calendar. The new-member check-in is retention work and compliance work at once.

questions.question: Thomas Rivera, a licensed agent, is reviewing a client's coverage before renewal season and reads a summary of guaranteed issue rights for Medigap. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: Guaranteed issue rights arise in defined situations, such as when a Medicare Advantage plan leaves the area or an employer plan that supplemented Medicare ends
Losing employer coverage never creates a Medigap guaranteed issue right
Guaranteed issue means the insurer must sell the policy, cannot impose pre-existing condition waiting periods, and cannot price based on health
A person who tries Medicare Advantage for the first time and leaves within the trial period may have a right to return to a Medigap policy

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Guaranteed issue is situation-specific: plan exits, lost supplemental employer coverage, and first-time MA trial rights are classic triggers, and they suspend underwriting, waiting periods, and health-based pricing.
