questions.question: James Whitfield is preparing for an Annual Enrollment Period appointment. On the question of the annual plan-change cycle for Part D members, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Extra Help members are locked out of all midyear changes in all cases
Formulary stability makes the fall recheck unnecessary
Drug plan changes can be made only in January
The Annual Enrollment Period is the standard window to change drug plans for January 1

questions.explanation: Part D is an annual re-decision: formulary, tier, pharmacy, and premium all reset each year, with AEP as the universal correction window and extra windows for subsidy members.

questions.question: While documenting a client consultation, Grace Nakamura double-checks a fact sheet on enrollment period priority and conflicts. Which statement on it should be corrected?

answers.text: When more than one period could apply, the enrollment request is processed under the period that governs the election, and agents must identify a valid election period for every application
An application submitted without a valid election period cannot simply be processed because the beneficiary wants the plan
Period conflicts are resolved by the pharmacy
Documenting the election period used is part of a complete, auditable enrollment

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Every enrollment rides on a valid election period, identified at submission and documented — wanting a plan is not itself an election right.

us-customs-broker-license-exam.quiz_title: US Customs Broker License Exam (CBLE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes reinstatement after suspension for a late report?

answers.text: Suspension is permanent once it attaches, with no cure
A broker suspended for failure to file the triennial report can regain active status by filing the report and fee before revocation occurs
A suspended broker may keep operating and fix the report at leisure
Reinstatement after a report suspension requires retaking the license exam

questions.explanation: The cure is simple but time-limited: file the report and fee before the suspension ripens into revocation — and transact no business in the meantime.

questions.question: Among these statements on post summary corrections, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: Post summary correction is a paper form mailed to the surety
Matters that cannot be corrected by post summary correction, such as certain trade remedy or restricted issues, follow their own channels
Corrections that change duties are accompanied by payment of additional duties owed or support a refund at liquidation
A post summary correction is filed electronically to correct entry summary data before the entry liquidates

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. PSC is the pre-liquidation fix: electronic, documented, duties trued up with the filing — and it dies when liquidation becomes final.

questions.question: Which statement about textile mixtures and fiber content is accurate?

answers.text: Textile goods made of mixed fibers are generally classified by the fiber that predominates by weight, under the textile section's own rules
A garment's coating or special construction never affects its classification
Fiber content information is unnecessary because laboratories decide at the port
Mixed textiles are classified by the most valuable fiber regardless of weight

questions.explanation: Textiles have their own constitution: chief weight of fibers as the starting rule, overridden where notes send coated or specially constructed garments to their own headings.

questions.question: Which statement about transaction value defined is accurate?

answers.text: Transaction value is the price actually paid or payable for the merchandise when sold for exportation to the United States, plus the statutory additions
Transaction value is the price the importer later charges United States customers
Any transfer of goods, including gifts and consignments, has a transaction value
The price actually paid or payable excludes payments made to third parties for the seller's benefit

questions.explanation: Transaction value starts with a real sale for exportation and the real total price paid or payable to or for the seller — no sale, no transaction value.

questions.question: On the subject of marking exceptions and special marking rules, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Special marking rules are optional alternatives to the general statute
Excepted articles need no marking of any kind, including their containers
Any article that is inconvenient to mark is automatically excepted

Certain articles are excepted from individual marking because they are incapable of being marked, would be damaged by marking, or fall on the statutory list of excepted articles, though their containers may still require marking

questions.explanation: Exceptions are statutory and specific: the article may go unmarked, the container usually may not — and special products (watches, pipes, steel) follow their own prescribed methods.

questions.question: During a client consultation, the topic of triennial status reports comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The triennial report is filed by the broker's clients rather than the broker
Suspension for a late status report requires a full disciplinary hearing first
Only organization brokers file status reports; individual brokers are exempt
A license that stays suspended for failure to file the status report is revoked if the report is still not filed within the cure period that follows suspension

questions.explanation: The triennial cycle is unforgiving: report and fee due February 1 every three years; miss March 1 and the license suspends automatically by operation of law, then revokes if the failure is not cured.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the broker's own bonds and permits distinguished?

answers.text: A broker's license and permit are distinct from the bonds a broker's clients must post for their entries
Clients of a licensed broker are exempt from posting bonds
The broker's license serves as a bond for all the broker's clients
A broker must personally guarantee every client's duties

questions.explanation: Keep the instruments straight: license (who may broker), permit (authority to transact), bond (the client's financial guarantee, with the client as principal).

questions.question: A colleague's notes on zone-to-zone transfers and weekly entry contain an error. Which line is the error?

answers.text: Weekly entry eliminates entry summaries entirely
Merchandise may move between foreign trade zones under customs procedures without entering commerce
Zone operators with steady withdrawals may use weekly entry procedures, consolidating a week's consumption withdrawals onto one entry summary
Weekly entry streamlines filing but does not change the duty owed on the merchandise

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Zones have their own logistics: transfers between zones stay outside commerce, and weekly entry batches a week's withdrawals into one summary — efficiency, not exemption.

questions.question: A client wants to know about valuation of software and media. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: Carrier media are prohibited imports
Media valuation rules apply to all digital content without conditions
A broker should confirm how the specific media and content are treated before declaring a medium-only value
The value of data is always added to the medium's cost

questions.explanation: Carrier-media valuation is a defined exception: medium value only when the conditions are met and the data cost is genuinely distinguished — confirmed product by product.

questions.question: A client wants to know about duty on quantities and rounding in assessment. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: Quantity reporting has no audit significance
A broker verifies quantities against packing lists and weight records before summary, because quantity errors are duty errors
Shortages discovered by the importer a year later are deducted at liquidation on request
The carrier's guess at weight substitutes for the shipper's records

questions.explanation: Specific-rate duty is arithmetic on quantity: report it exactly, document true shortages at the right time, and remember post-importation losses are not customs events.

questions.question: During a client consultation, the topic of drawback timing and administration comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Accelerated payment requires no bond or qualification
The claim period runs from the date the claimant first considers filing
Drawback is administered by the Department of Commerce
Accelerated payment of drawback is available to qualified claimants who post the required bond and meet the program's conditions

questions.explanation: Drawback runs on a five-year claim clock, transferable rights, and optional accelerated payment for bonded, qualified claimants — administered by CBP.

questions.question: Which of these assertions about bond requirements for temporary and special entries fails to hold up?

answers.text: Failure to close a bonded transaction properly converts the bond into a source of liquidated damages
Temporary importations, warehouse entries, and in-bond movements each carry bond obligations sized to the risk of the transaction
A temporary importation bond is generally set at twice the estimated duties that would apply if the goods were entered for consumption
Warehouse entries are bonded at a flat one hundred dollars

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Deferred duty means bonded duty: TIB bonds run at double the estimated duties, and every special procedure carries bond conditions whose breach is billed as liquidated damages.

questions.question: While helping a client plan a new product import, Ingrid Johansson considers retaining powers of attorney and broker records. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Records kept by the client excuse the broker from keeping any records
Entry and broker records generally must be kept for five years and produced to Customs and Border Protection on demand
Customs and Border Protection may inspect broker records only with a court order
Electronic storage of broker records is never permitted

questions.explanation: Record retention is five years for entry and broker records, powers of attorney are kept while in effect, and CBP may demand production — inability to produce is itself a compliance failure.

questions.question: Nadia Rahman is reviewing training material on instruments of international traffic. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Instruments of international traffic must be in genuine international use and are expected to leave the United States in that service
Reusable containers and similar instruments of international traffic, such as pallets, racks, and shipping containers in international service, receive special admission treatment
Diverting an instrument of international traffic to purely domestic use can trigger entry and duty consequences
Domestic trucking equipment qualifies automatically as an instrument of international traffic

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. The containers that carry trade get streamlined treatment while they stay in international service — domestic diversion is where the duty bill arrives.

questions.question: Michael Russo, a licensed broker, is documenting advice given to a client. Regarding incomplete and unfinished articles, which guidance is correct?

answers.text: Unfinished goods are classified by their raw materials in all cases
Any collection of parts in one box is classified as the finished article, even parts of several different products
The same treatment covers articles presented unassembled or disassembled, which are classified as the assembled article
Essential character under this rule is determined solely by weight

questions.explanation: Rule two(a) looks through form to substance: essential character present (or all parts present for assembly) means the finished article's heading — a rough blank without that character stays a blank.

questions.question: An importer repeats something they read online about working a deductive value computation. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: If imported goods resell in the United States at 100 dollars per unit in the greatest aggregate quantity, and the deductions are 8 dollars of duty, 6 dollars of domestic transport, and 21 dollars of profit and general expenses, the deductive value is 65 dollars per unit
The computation subtracts all three deductions from the resale unit price: 100 minus 8 minus 6 minus 21
Using the single highest resale price instead of the greatest-aggregate-quantity price would misstate the starting point
The greatest aggregate quantity price is the price of the largest single sale regardless of unit price differences

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Deductive value works backward: $100 resale unit price − $8 duty − $6 U.S. transport − $21 profit and expenses = $65.

questions.question: While reviewing a client's shipment file before filing, Nadia Rahman considers exam registration and fees. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A foreign passport plus a driver's license proves United States citizenship for exam admission
The exam fee is 390 dollars, as published on the Customs and Border Protection registration page
Photocopies of identity documents are accepted if the originals are unavailable
The exam fee is waived for candidates who have failed a previous sitting

questions.explanation: Registration and the $390 exam fee run through eCBP. Admission requires original, unexpired, physical proof of identity and U.S. citizenship (a U.S. passport covers both); doors close at 8:30 a.m. with no exceptions and no refund.

questions.question: Thomas Berg, a licensed broker, is preparing a compliance briefing for their brokerage. Regarding broker cooperation with Customs and Border Protection inquiries, which guidance is correct?

answers.text: A broker may shade answers to protect a valued client without legal risk
Inquiries may be answered by an unlicensed employee inventing plausible details
Routine record destruction may continue unchanged during an investigation
False statements to Customs and Border Protection by a broker can support both criminal exposure and license discipline

questions.explanation: Truthful cooperation is mandatory: no privilege shields entry facts, false statements are independently punishable, and document preservation duties attach when an inquiry starts.

questions.question: While reviewing a client's shipment file before filing, Carmen Vega double-checks a fact sheet on the entry and entry summary forms in electronic filing. Which statement on it should be corrected?

answers.text: Entry data is transmitted electronically in the automated system on the electronic equivalents of the entry and entry summary forms
A broker transmitting entry data certifies the filing under the authority of the importer's power of attorney
The entry for release and the entry summary are distinct filings even though both are transmitted through the same automated environment
The entry summary replaces the entry, so only one filing ever occurs

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. ACE changed the medium, not the structure: an entry filing for release and a separate entry summary filing with duties, both transmitted electronically under the broker's authority.

questions.question: Daniel Reyes, a licensed broker, is preparing a compliance briefing for their brokerage and reads a summary of computing the harbor maintenance fee. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: The same cargo arriving by air would bear no harbor maintenance fee
The harbor maintenance rate is 1.25 percent
Vessel cargo valued at 80,000 dollars bears a harbor maintenance fee of 100 dollars at the 0.125 percent rate
The computation is 80,000 dollars times 0.00125

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. HMF math: $80,000 x 0.125% = $100 — vessel cargo only.

iiba-ccba.quiz_title: IIBA CCBA — Certification of Capability in Business Analysis Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding why analyst performance is assessed, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Assessing business analysis performance finds ways to make future analysis work more effective, not to assign blame
Performance assessment exists to rank analysts against each other for pay decisions
Assessment considers speed alone; quality of requirements is out of scope
Only failed initiatives deserve a performance review

questions.explanation: Performance assessment is improvement work: examine products and process, capture what worked and what did not, and carry the lessons into future analysis.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes logistics for elicitation sessions?

answers.text: An agenda discourages creativity and should never be shared with participants
Session planning covers participants, agenda, timing, and any materials stakeholders need beforehand
Inviting as many people as possible always improves a session
A scribe's notes are unnecessary because the facilitator will remember everything

questions.explanation: Logistics make sessions productive: the right participants, a shared agenda, assigned roles like scribe, and materials distributed early enough to be useful.

questions.question: Regarding risks of poor prioritization, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Marking everything critical is a safe strategy
Stakeholders restrain themselves naturally without prioritization
Order of delivery has no effect on realized value
Delivering low-value requirements first can exhaust budget before the value that justified the initiative arrives

questions.explanation: Skipping or inflating prioritization spends the budget on the wrong order and erases the signal the process exists to create.

questions.question: Which claim about metrics for the future state should be discarded as false?

answers.text: Baseline values from the current state make future targets meaningful
Targets without baselines are equally meaningful
Key performance indicators defined with the future state become the measures used later in solution evaluation
Metrics cover outcomes customers and the enterprise care about, not only delivery milestones

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Define the scoreboard with the future: indicators, baselines, and targets set now are exactly what solution evaluation will later judge.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes acceptance and evaluation criteria?

answers.text: Criteria chosen after seeing the options are equally fair
Acceptance criteria are invented during final testing
Stakeholders accept solutions by instinct; criteria add nothing
Acceptance criteria define the conditions under which stakeholders will accept a solution or requirement as satisfied

questions.explanation: Criteria come before verdicts: acceptance criteria define 'good enough to accept', evaluation criteria define 'better than the alternatives' — both fixed in advance.

questions.question: A junior analyst makes several claims about communicating issues and changes. Which claim should a mentor correct?

answers.text: A change notice needs no reason, only the new text
Raising a discovered problem early, with evidence, is part of communicating analysis information
Stakeholders need timely notice of requirement changes that affect their interests, with the impact explained
Communication includes bad news; hiding a conflict until delivery destroys trust and options

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Communication covers changes and problems too: early, evidence-based, and with impact explained, so stakeholders can respond while choices still exist.

questions.question: During a working session, the topic of managing collaboration over time comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Trust is irrelevant when the analyst has formal authority
Trust built through reliable follow-through is the foundation of sustained collaboration
Collaboration management means scheduling more meetings
Follow-through on small commitments has no effect on collaboration

questions.explanation: Collaboration is a living system: monitor who is engaged, follow through reliably, and intervene early when participation fades.

questions.question: During a team discussion on root causes behind change requests, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Understanding the cause improves the recommendation — fix, redesign, or process change
The cause of a change is irrelevant to how it should be handled
A change request sometimes signals that the underlying need was misunderstood, not merely extended
Repeated changes in one area may reveal an elicitation or analysis weakness worth addressing

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Change patterns are diagnostic: clusters point to misunderstood needs or weak analysis, and the right response may be deeper than approving each patch.

questions.question: During a working session, the topic of culture and mindset in current state analysis comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A single survey fully captures an organization's culture
Cultural assessment uses observation and conversation, not only surveys
Resistance discovered late is cheaper to fix than resistance found early
Culture is identical across all parts of a large enterprise

questions.explanation: Culture is current-state fact: it predicts adoption, varies across groups, and must be understood early enough to shape the change strategy.

questions.question: A colleague's notes on monitoring risks through the change contain an error. Which line is the error?

answers.text: A realized risk stays labelled a risk forever
A risk that materializes becomes an issue, handled through the change's governance
New risks emerge from the change itself and are added to the assessment
Risks are monitored as the change proceeds, because likelihood and impact shift

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Risk assessment is a living activity: re-weigh as conditions move, add what emerges, and convert what materializes into governed issues.

questions.question: A stakeholder asks about using the architecture in impact analysis. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Architecture quality is proven in change situations, not in the drawing
Structure adds time to impact analysis
Changes never respect architectural boundaries, so structure is useless
Architecture is judged by the elegance of its diagrams

questions.explanation: The architecture pays rent during change: neighbours found fast, examination scoped tightly, impact bounded by structure rather than by reading everything.

questions.question: A stakeholder asks about characteristics of good requirements. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Testability can be added later by the test team
Atomic requirements — one need per statement — are easier to verify, trace, and change
Consistency across the set is optional polish
Feasibility is the builder's concern, not a quality of the requirement

questions.explanation: Quality is checkable: unambiguous, complete, consistent, feasible, testable, and atomic. Verify against those characteristics, not against taste.

questions.question: While supporting a hospital scheduling improvement effort, Omar Haddad considers focus groups and collaborative games. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Game results should be adopted as decisions without further analysis
A focus group of whoever is available represents all user types
Collaborative games use structured play to surface priorities, risks, and hidden assumptions
Collaborative games are entertainment with no analysis purpose

questions.explanation: Focus groups and collaborative games surface perceptions, priorities, and assumptions qualitatively — valuable insight that is then tested and confirmed by other techniques.

questions.question: Tom Becker is preparing requirements for a new onboarding process. On the question of who approves requirements, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Approvers need no accountability for outcomes
Authority to approve is claimed by whoever attends the review meeting
Quality review and business approval are the same act
Technical reviewers may verify quality, but business approval belongs to those accountable for the outcomes

questions.explanation: Approval belongs to accountable authority: identified in advance, distinct from technical review, and held by those who own the outcomes being committed.

questions.question: A stakeholder repeats something they read online about the purpose of requirements traceability. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Traceability connects each requirement to the business need it serves and the solution elements that satisfy it
Tracing helps assess the impact of a proposed change before it is approved
Traceability supports coverage checks — showing which needs have no requirements and which requirements serve no need
Traceability replaces the need for requirement reviews

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Traceability is a working map from need to requirement to solution: it drives impact analysis and exposes both uncovered needs and orphan requirements.

questions.question: While documenting the needs for a customer portal upgrade, Kevin Doyle considers value analysis for compliance-driven change. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Compliance options are compared on benefits alone
The cost of non-compliance — penalties, licence risk — frames the value of every option
Non-compliance cost is irrelevant to option value
A mandate dictates exactly one possible response

questions.explanation: Mandates change the question, not the need for analysis: the value lies in cheaper, safer compliance — priced against the real cost of failing to comply.

questions.question: Hannah Kim is reviewing study material on validating with scenarios end to end. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Scenario validation involves the stakeholders who own each leg of the journey
A journey with a missing leg still validates if each step reads well
End-to-end scenarios test whether the requirements set handles a complete business journey without gaps
A scenario that crosses several departments is especially good at exposing missing handoffs

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Whole-journey scenarios are validation's stress test: follow one real case across every handoff and watch where the requirements set runs out.

questions.question: While supporting a claims-system replacement initiative, Julia Santos double-checks a fact sheet on confirmation records and open items. Which statement on it should be corrected?

answers.text: Pending items may be presented to designers as settled
An open-items list with owners and due dates keeps unresolved points from evaporating
The record shows which results are confirmed, which are pending, and which are disputed
Disputed items carry both positions until resolution, not just the analyst's preference

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Confirmation is tracked like any other work: status per item, owners for open points, and both sides preserved where stakeholders dispute a result.

questions.question: While analysing a retailer's returns process redesign, Sofia Marino double-checks a fact sheet on versions and baselines. Which statement on it should be corrected?

answers.text: After baselining, changes follow the change process rather than editing the snapshot directly
Version history lets the team see what changed, when, and why
Changes after baselining are applied silently to keep the document stable
A baseline is an agreed, controlled snapshot of requirements at a point in time

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Baselines create a stable reference: the snapshot is controlled, later changes go through assessment, and history explains how the set evolved.

questions.question: While reviewing requirements for a merged company's shared platform, Laura Chen double-checks a fact sheet on emerging and evolving options. Which statement on it should be corrected?

answers.text: An option may be eliminated early when it clearly fails a hard constraint, saving evaluation effort
New options can emerge during analysis — a vendor release, a partner offer — and are assessed by the same criteria
Early elimination is never justified
Elimination decisions are recorded so the option is not resurrected without new evidence

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Option sets breathe: late arrivals judged by the same criteria, clear failures eliminated early and on the record, returns requiring new evidence.

financial-paraplanner-qualified-professi.quiz_title: FPQP (Financial Paraplanner Qualified Professional) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: On the subject of what data gathering collects, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Data gathering needs only account balances; goals and attitudes are irrelevant
The paraplanner should estimate missing figures rather than ask the client
Data gathering collects both quantitative facts, such as account balances and income, and qualitative information, such as goals and concerns
Tax returns are never useful in financial planning data gathering

questions.explanation: Sound analysis starts with complete, current data: statements, policies, tax returns, and legal documents, plus the client's goals, concerns, and attitudes — gathered and refreshed, never guessed.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes cash management for windfalls?

answers.text: Taxes never apply to any windfall, so no reserve for them is needed
Windfalls should be spent quickly before they lose value
A windfall, such as a bonus or inheritance, is allocated deliberately across taxes, debts, reserves, and goals
A windfall eliminates the need for an emergency fund

questions.explanation: Windfalls are planned, not splurged: reserve for any taxes, retire expensive debt, top up reserves, and fund goals — in the order the household plan dictates.

questions.question: Which statement about testing plans against different return assumptions is accurate?

answers.text: A single optimistic projection is the most reliable planning method
Sensitivity testing is done only after a plan fails
Running a plan at more than one assumed return shows how sensitive the outcome is
Higher assumed returns require larger deposits for the same goal

questions.explanation: One projection is a guess; several are a plan. Testing lower returns exposes fragile goals early, while there is still time to save more or adjust the target.

questions.question: A colleague wants to know about term life insurance. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: Term premiums are refunded if the insured outlives the term under standard policies
Term insurance is always more expensive than permanent insurance for the same face amount
A term policy pays its face amount whenever the insured dies, even decades after expiry
Term insurance generally offers the most coverage per premium dollar for temporary needs

questions.explanation: Term insurance is pure protection for a set period: no cash value, no payout after expiry — and the lowest cost per dollar of coverage while the need is greatest.

questions.question: A client asks about types of investment risk. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Liquidity risk means an asset is too easy to sell
Business risk is identical to inflation risk
Interest rate risk hits bond prices when market rates rise
Interest rate risk increases bond prices when rates rise

questions.explanation: Risks come in kinds: market risk moves everything, inflation risk erodes purchasing power, and interest rate risk reprices bonds when rates change — each managed differently.

questions.question: A client repeats something they read online about common planning ratios. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: A savings ratio compares amounts saved to income over a period
Housing and debt payment ratios help flag households whose fixed obligations crowd out saving
An emergency fund is often gauged in months of essential expenses held in liquid savings
The savings ratio is calculated from the balance sheet alone

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Ratios are gauges, not verdicts: months of liquid reserves, savings as a share of income, and debt burdens as a share of income help spot households under strain and track improvement.

questions.question: Erin Sullivan is reviewing study material on paraplanner technical skills. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Paraplanners use financial planning software to model scenarios and projections
Accuracy habits — checking inputs and tying out totals — are core paraplanner skills
Typos in client data are harmless because the software corrects them
Spreadsheet skills matter because much analysis is checked and customized outside the planning software

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Paraplanning is technical work: software fluency, spreadsheet competence, and disciplined input-checking, backed by working knowledge of tax, insurance, investments, and retirement concepts.

questions.question: During a team working session, the topic of liquidity in a financial plan comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Liquidity and profitability are the same thing
Retirement accounts are poor emergency sources because withdrawals can trigger taxes and penalties
An asset-rich household never faces cash problems
Retirement accounts are the ideal first emergency source

questions.explanation: Liquidity is about speed and certainty of conversion to cash. Wealth tied up in property or retirement accounts cannot pay this month's bills without cost or delay.

questions.question: Among these statements on net present value thinking in household decisions, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: Prepaying a loan can never be compared with investing the same money
A decision whose benefits in today's dollars exceed its costs in today's dollars is financially favorable on its face
Refinancing, prepaying debt, and choosing payment plans all involve present value comparisons
Comparing costs and benefits in today's dollars is the household version of net present value thinking

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Discounting is a household tool too: refinancing, prepayment, and payment-plan choices all turn on comparing money at different times in today's dollars.

questions.question: A colleague wants to know about own-occupation and benefit definitions. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: Definitions are set by federal law uniformly for private policies
Own-occupation policies pay even when the insured works full time in their own job by standard terms
All disability policies use the identical definition
The definition of disability is one of the most important terms in a disability policy

questions.explanation: One phrase decides claims: own-occupation protects a career, any-occupation protects against total work incapacity — which is why the definition is read before the price.

questions.question: A client repeats something they read online about methods of handling risk. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Retaining a risk means the household bears the cost itself if the loss occurs
Transferring risk means the insured can never lose money from the event
Insurance is the classic method of transferring risk to an insurer for a premium
The basic methods of handling risk are avoidance, retention, reduction, and transfer

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Risk is avoided, retained, reduced, or transferred. Insurance transfers the financial consequence for a premium; retention keeps it at home; reduction lowers frequency or severity; avoidance gives up the activity itself.

questions.question: In a team discussion on growth and value styles, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Growth stocks are companies expected to expand earnings rapidly, often paying little or no dividend
Value stocks trade at prices considered low relative to measures like earnings or book value
Style diversification holds both because leadership rotates between styles over time
Growth companies never fail

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Growth buys tomorrow's earnings, value buys today's assets cheaply; each style leads in different seasons, which is why portfolios often hold both.

questions.question: A client repeats something they read online about the boundary between support work and licensed activity. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Paraplanners prepare analysis and drafts that a responsible planner reviews and delivers
Licensing boundaries are optional for experienced support staff
Support staff must not give personalized investment advice unless properly licensed or registered to do so
Selling insurance or securities requires the appropriate license, separate from holding FPQP

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. FPQP is an education credential, not a license: personalized advice, sales, and order-taking require the proper license or registration, and paraplanner work is reviewed and delivered by the responsible planner.

questions.question: David Osei, a paraplanner, is preparing for a client review meeting. Regarding credit reports and errors, which guidance is correct?

answers.text: Only lenders are allowed to dispute report errors
Errors on credit reports correct themselves within a month
Unfamiliar accounts on a report are always the consumer's own forgotten accounts
Errors on a report should be disputed with documentation

questions.explanation: Regular report reviews catch errors and identity theft early; consumers have the right to see their reports and dispute mistakes with supporting documents.

questions.question: A client repeats something they read online about discounting and opportunity cost. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Choosing a discount rate is an assumption that should fit the decision and be stated
Discounting converts today's amounts into future amounts
The discount rate represents the return given up by not having the money now — an opportunity cost
Riskier future amounts are commonly discounted at higher rates

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Discounting prices patience and risk: the rate stands for what the money could earn elsewhere, so it must fit the decision — and riskier promises warrant higher rates.

questions.question: A junior associate makes several claims about annuity surrender charges and taxation in plain terms. Which claim should a mentor correct?

answers.text: Unlike qualified accounts, nonqualified annuities are funded with after-tax money
Nonqualified annuities are funded with pre-tax payroll deductions
Surrender charges penalize early withdrawals from many deferred annuities during the early contract years
Annuity earnings grow tax-deferred but are taxed as ordinary income when withdrawn

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Deferred annuities defer, not forgive: earnings come out taxed as ordinary income, and leaving early during the surrender period costs a charge on top.

questions.question: Fatima Al-Sayed, a paraplanner, is helping a planning team prepare annual review packets. Regarding money market funds and cash vehicles, which guidance is correct?

answers.text: Money market funds invest primarily in long-term stocks
A money market fund's value can never fluctuate under any circumstances
They aim to maintain a stable value while paying a modest yield
Their yields typically exceed long-term stock returns

questions.explanation: Money market funds are the portfolio's parking place: short-term quality debt, stable value aims, modest yield — and investment products, not insured deposits.

questions.question: Nadia Hassan, a paraplanner, is helping a planning team prepare annual review packets and reads a summary of the FPQP final exam. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: A candidate must score at least 70 percent to pass the FPQP final exam
The FPQP final exam is a closed-book, multiple-choice exam taken online with remote proctoring
The FPQP final exam is administered by FINRA at testing centers
The FPQP final exam contains 75 multiple-choice questions with a three-hour time limit

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. The FPQP final exam is the College's closed-book, remotely proctored online exam: 75 multiple-choice questions, three hours, with a published passing score of 70 percent.

questions.question: Ingrid Bauer, a paraplanner, is helping a planning team prepare annual review packets and reads a summary of refinancing a mortgage. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: Cash-out refinancing increases the loan balance and the debt secured by the home
Closing costs mean the rate savings must be weighed against how long the borrower stays
Refinancing replaces an existing mortgage with a new one, ideally at a lower rate or better terms
Refinancing resets nothing about the loan's term in typical cases

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Refinancing is a break-even calculation: closing costs today against payment savings over the time the loan will actually be held — and cash-out versions add debt against the home.

questions.question: While helping a planning team prepare annual review packets, Laura Chen double-checks a fact sheet on flood and earthquake coverage. Which statement on it should be corrected?

answers.text: Standard homeowners policies exclude flood damage
Flood insurance is available through the National Flood Insurance Program and some private insurers
Earthquake coverage is typically added by endorsement or a separate policy
Flood insurance takes effect the moment it is purchased in all cases

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Water from outside and shaking ground sit outside standard homeowners coverage: flood needs its own policy (often federal), and earthquake needs an endorsement or separate policy.

finra-series-24.quiz_title: FINRA Series 24 — General Securities Principal Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of these assertions about retention periods and ready accessibility fails to hold up?

answers.text: Many account and order records must be preserved for six years, and customer account records are kept for six years after the account is closed
Readily accessible means stored anywhere in the world as long as it can be retrieved within a few months
A principal should apply the retention period that fits each record type rather than using one convenient period for every record in the file room
For records with a six year retention period, the first two years must be kept in a place that is readily accessible to the firm and its regulators

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Retention runs by record type: six years for many account and order records, with the early portion readily accessible, and six years after closing for account records.

questions.question: One statement about direct participation program suitability concerns is not true. Which one is it?

answers.text: Illiquidity is a minor feature that representatives may omit when the programs tax or income features are attractive
A principal should watch for customers overconcentrated in one program or sponsor, since diversification failures often surface first in illiquid products
Suitability for a direct participation program considers the customers income, net worth, liquidity needs, and concentration in illiquid holdings
Direct participation programs are generally illiquid, so a principal must ensure representatives present the lack of a ready market clearly before any sale

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. An illiquid, concentrated investment can trap a customer for years, so principals enforce honest illiquidity disclosure and real concentration and suitability review.

questions.question: Which statement about principal approval before use is accurate?

answers.text: Any change to a previously approved retail template, however substantive, qualifies automatically for an exception from prior approval.
A principal must approve each retail communication before use or before filing with the regulator, whichever comes first, unless a narrow exception applies.
A principal may delegate final approval of retail communications to an unregistered marketing contractor with no principal review.
A principal may approve a retail communication after it has already been in public use for several weeks in all circumstances.

questions.explanation: Retail communications generally require principal approval before use. Narrow exceptions, such as certain template updates, do not create a general right to use material first and approve it later.

questions.question: On the subject of naked short selling, which statement is correct?

answers.text: A principal may approve a short sale with no locate whenever the trader promises to decide later whether to borrow the shares
A principal prohibits naked short selling, where a seller shorts without arranging to borrow and fails to deliver shares by settlement
A principal may permit naked short selling by market makers and customers alike because the practice reliably improves liquidity in all cases
Naked short selling is abusive only when it is profitable, so a principal need not review unprofitable patterns of delivery failure

questions.explanation: Naked short selling, shorting without a borrow arrangement and failing to deliver, is an abusive practice under Regulation SHO concepts. A principal must detect fail patterns, investigate, and stop unsupported shorting.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes reasonable investigation of the issuer?

answers.text: A principal may approve sales before the use of proceeds has been reviewed or understood by the firm
A principal may limit the investigation to reading the summary page of the private placement memorandum
A principal may skip review of financial statements when the issuer management seems experienced and well known
A principal must ensure the firm conducts a reasonable investigation of the issuer and its management before recommending a private placement

questions.explanation: A member participating in a private placement must investigate the issuer, its management, its financial condition, the use of proceeds, and the offering documents. A principal supervises that work before approval.

questions.question: A junior associate makes several claims about non cash compensation conditions. Which claim should a mentor correct?

answers.text: Training and education meetings can support permissible non-cash arrangements when attendance and content conditions are satisfied
Non-cash compensation in connection with product sales is restricted and generally permitted only when specific conditions are met
A principal reviews proposed trips, gifts and entertainment tied to product sales before they are offered or accepted
Non-cash compensation rules apply only to cash payments and never to trips, meals or merchandise

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Non-cash compensation connected to product sales is tightly conditioned, and a principal must screen arrangements such as sponsor funded trips and training meetings in advance.

questions.question: A registered representative asks about short interest reporting. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Short interest reports are filed solely for the firm marketing department to use with customers
Accurate short interest data helps regulators and markets monitor selling pressure and settlement risk
Short interest is reported once at account opening and never needs to be updated afterward
A principal may omit customer short positions from the report to protect customer confidentiality from regulators

questions.explanation: Firms report aggregate short interest on a recurring schedule so regulators and the market can monitor outstanding short positions and related settlement risk.

questions.question: In a team discussion on options account approval and disclosure, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: The customer must be delivered the options disclosure document that explains the characteristics and risks of standardized options
A principal approving options should consider the customer investment profile, including experience and financial situation
An options account requires additional firm approval beyond approval of a general securities account
Delivery of a prospectus for an unrelated security satisfies the options disclosure delivery duty

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Options involve distinct risks and strategy levels, so a principal applies a separate approval based on the customer profile and ensures delivery of the options disclosure document.

questions.question: During a compliance working session, the topic of regular-way settlement timing comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Once a trade is executed, its settlement date is left to the discretion of the clearing clerk handling the booking
Regular-way settlement applies only to government securities and never to corporate or municipal securities
A principal may extend regular-way settlement informally for any customer without agreement at the time of the trade
A principal supervising settlement must treat a trade that has not settled by its regular-way date as an exception requiring follow-up rather than as a routine delay

questions.explanation: Regular-way settlement for most corporate securities is T plus one, the next business day after the trade date. Any other settlement must be agreed at the time of the trade, and a principal must escalate trades that miss their contractual date.

questions.question: Tom Becker is drafting supervisory review notes. On the question of market order handling, which statement holds true?

answers.text: A principal may convert a customer market order into a limit order without customer instruction to reduce the firm exposure
A market order carries a price limit that guarantees execution only at or better than the price stated on the order ticket
A principal directs that market orders from smaller customers wait until larger proprietary orders have been completed first
A principal ensures market orders receive priority handling consistent with the terms the customer gave and prevailing market conditions

questions.explanation: A market order seeks prompt execution at the best available price with no customer-set limit. A principal supervises handling so the order is not delayed, converted, or subordinated to firm trading.

questions.question: A registered representative asks about corporate financing rule fairness standard. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The principal escalates any term that appears unfair or unreasonable and does not proceed until the concern is resolved through review
A principal may approve unfair terms if the offering is small and the firm expects little public attention
The fairness standard applies only to offerings by first-time issuers and never to seasoned public companies
Unfair underwriting terms become permissible if they are disclosed in small print at the back of the prospectus

questions.explanation: The corporate financing rule imposes a substantive fairness standard on underwriting terms and arrangements. The principal reviews the whole arrangement, not just the discount, and escalates unfair terms.

questions.question: What should a principal understand about best execution duty? Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The best execution duty is met whenever an execution occurs at any price inside the quoted spread regardless of other available markets
A principal may satisfy best execution by always routing to the venue that pays the firm the most for its order flow
A principal ensures the firm uses reasonable diligence to ascertain the best market so the resulting price is as favorable as possible under prevailing conditions
A principal may limit best execution review to orders the firm executed as principal and ignore orders routed to other venues

questions.explanation: Under the best execution rule the firm must use reasonable diligence to find the best market and obtain a price as favorable as possible under prevailing conditions. Routing arrangements never transfer that duty away.

questions.question: During a compliance working session, the topic of heightened supervision for conduct red flags comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A principal may allow a person under heightened supervision to open accounts and handle funds with the same discretion as before the red flags appeared.
A principal may assign supervision under the plan to the subject person own producing manager without any independent review element.
A principal must document reviews under a heightened supervision plan, escalate new violations promptly, and keep the plan in place until the underlying risk is demonstrably resolved.
A principal may keep a heightened supervision plan undocumented to avoid creating a record that could be requested by a regulator.

questions.explanation: Red flags require a supervisory response proportionate to the risk, not routine oversight. A principal imposes a written, tailored heightened supervision plan and follows through until the risk is actually resolved.

questions.question: A representative repeats something they read online about delegation and evidence of reviews. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: A principal who finds a delegated task was not performed must address the gap and document the corrective steps
Supervisory reviews should leave evidence showing who reviewed what, when, and what action was taken
Documentation of supervisory reviews may be created later from memory at examination time without concern
A principal may delegate supervisory tasks but remains responsible for seeing that the delegated duties are performed

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Delegation does not relieve the designating principal, and supervisory work must be evidenced so the firm can prove the review actually happened.

questions.question: During a compliance working session, the topic of fair markups markdowns and commissions comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Disclosure duties disappear when a firm trades as principal with its own customer
Fair pricing is judged solely by whether a competing firm charged more on a different day
In a net transaction or principal capacity trade, required disclosure of capacity and price information supports fair pricing review
Commissions need no reasonableness review because representatives set their own charges

questions.explanation: A principal reviews pricing for fairness and reasonableness across the pattern of trades, with attention to capacity and the disclosures that accompany principal and net transactions.

questions.question: A representative repeats something they read online about principal review of reporting exceptions. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: A principal reviews exception reports for late, rejected, or inaccurate trade reports and follows up until each item is resolved.
A principal documents corrective action only for exceptions involving customer harm, and never for reporting accuracy alone.
Repeated reporting exceptions require the principal to find and correct the systemic cause, such as a workflow, system, or training failure.
A principal documents exception review and corrective action so supervision of trade reporting can be evidenced to examiners.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Exception reports are the principal early warning system for reporting failures. A principal resolves each item, corrects systemic causes, and documents the review and the fix.

questions.question: While drafting supervisory review notes, James Whitfield considers disclosures required in research reports. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Disclosures are required only in the first report on a company and may be dropped from all later reports
Rating definitions and distributions are marketing material that a principal may remove from reports at will
A principal must verify that reports disclose investment banking relationships with the subject company so readers can weigh the conflict
Market making activity in a subject security never needs to be disclosed in a research report

questions.explanation: Research disclosures let readers judge conflicts for themselves: analyst and firm ownership, market making, banking relationships, plus rating meanings, distributions, and price information. Principals verify they are present and current.

questions.question: While supervising a branch office of a regional broker-dealer, Marta Kowalski double-checks a fact sheet on failure to respond to finra requests. Which statement on it should be corrected?

answers.text: A principal must track FINRA requests centrally, assign responsibility and deadlines, and escalate any request at risk of going unanswered.
A principal may advise a person to wait for a second FINRA request before answering, since the first request is treated as preliminary.
A principal must ensure a former associated person still subject to FINRA jurisdiction is told promptly about a request and about the consequences of not responding.
A principal must warn associated persons that failing to respond to a FINRA request for information or testimony can itself bring sanctions, including a bar, separate from the underlying matter.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Failure to respond is an independent and serious violation that can end a career even when the original inquiry was minor. A principal manages requests actively so no deadline is missed by neglect.

questions.question: Ingrid Bauer, a principal, is working in the compliance department of a national firm and reads a summary of patriot act information sharing. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: The sharing provisions eliminated the need for firms to file Suspicious Activity Reports with FinCEN
The USA PATRIOT Act provides mechanisms for information sharing between financial institutions and the government about money laundering and terrorist financing
A principal must ensure the firm responds appropriately to government requests for account and transaction information under these provisions
Firms that follow the required procedures may share information with other financial institutions about suspected terrorist or money laundering activity

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. The USA PATRIOT Act created controlled channels for sharing laundering and terrorism financing information with the government and between firms, within strict procedural limits.

questions.question: Victor Petrov, a principal, is serving as the designated principal for a business line and reads a summary of research interaction during a distribution. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: A principal must coordinate research and other issuer communications during an offering so they do not undermine the prospectus based selling process
A principal must restrict communications by a firm participating in a distribution that could function as offering promotion outside the permitted documents
A principal may allow distribution staff to draft research content as long as an analyst name appears on it
A principal must escalate a proposed issuer communication from the distributing firm that has not been cleared through offering compliance review

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. A distributing firm communications about the issuer during an offering are restricted. A principal manages the interaction between research and offering communications so promotion stays within the permitted framework.

maryland-journey-plumber-gas-fitter.quiz_title: Maryland Journey Plumber/Gas Fitter Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who licenses Maryland plumbers?

answers.text: Maryland plumbers are licensed by the board that licenses Colorado plumbers.
The Maryland State Board of Plumbing, within the Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing at the Maryland Department of Labor, licenses and regulates plumbers in Maryland.
A national plumbing association issues Maryland plumber licenses.
Each Maryland county licenses plumbers with no state board involved.

questions.explanation: State licensing sits with the Board of Plumbing at the Department of Labor in Baltimore, not with counties or associations.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding drainage pipe slope for large Maryland drains?

answers.text: Horizontal drainage piping of eight inches and larger is sloped at one-sixteenth inch per foot in the direction of flow.
Large drainage piping needs no slope because of its size.
Large drainage piping is sloped at one-quarter inch per foot.
Large drainage piping is sloped at one inch per foot to prevent settling.

questions.explanation: The biggest drains run at the flattest permitted grade: a sixteenth of an inch per foot.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to purging a Maryland gas line into service. Which point is correct?

answers.text: When a gas line is placed in service, it is purged so air is expelled safely — discharged outdoors or burned off under control — and never released into a confined space where the mixture can accumulate and ignite.
Maryland gas work follows the Uniform Plumbing Code exclusively.
Purging is unnecessary if the line is short.
Purging uses a vacuum pump on the meter.

questions.explanation: Air out, gas in, discharge controlled and outdoors — purging is an ignition-management procedure.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about the sediment trap on Maryland gas appliances.

answers.text: A sediment trap is a type of water trap on the drain.

A sediment trap — a tee with a capped nipple pointing down at the appliance inlet — is installed where the fuel gas code requires it so dirt, scale, and moisture drop out before they can foul the appliance valve.
Sediment traps filter the combustion air.
Sediment traps are installed on the vent connector.

questions.explanation: Dirt leg, drip leg, sediment trap — one fitting, one job: catch debris before the valve does.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the standard combustion air room volume rule?

answers.text: Regulators are installed backwards if space is tight.
The standard volume is 10 cubic feet per 1,000 BTU per hour.
Under the standard method, an unconfined space for combustion air provides at least 50 cubic feet of room volume for each 1,000 BTU per hour of the appliances' combined input rating.
Manifold pressure is measured in pounds per square inch on residential appliances.

questions.explanation: Fifty per thousand is the benchmark number of gas fitting — it anchors the math portion too.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the Board office address in Baltimore. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: The Board keeps no Baltimore office and works only by mail from Salisbury.
An inspector keeps an active master license while inspecting their own work.
The Maryland State Board of Plumbing address published for examination matters is 100 S. Charles Street, Tower I, in Baltimore.
The Board office is inside the Maryland State House in Annapolis only.

questions.explanation: 100 S. Charles Street, Tower I, Baltimore is the Board address in the PSI bulletin; the insurance certificate holder address is a different, separately published address.

questions.question: A new apprentice needs to understand what the Maryland journey license allows. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: A Maryland journey plumber/gas fitter license allows the holder to provide plumbing services while under the direction and control of a master plumber or a holder of a limited master plumber license.
Leaving a voicemail the night before protects the fee.
A journey applicant needs 7,500 hours of any construction work, supervised or not.
A journey license allows the holder to contract plumbing work fully independently with no master involved.

questions.explanation: Direction and control by a master (or limited master) is written into the journey credential itself.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the four Maryland journey eligibility pillars is handled in practice.

answers.text: Journey eligibility requires a college degree plus the examination.
Journey eligibility requires ten years of experience and no examination.
Backflow training is required only for master applicants, never for journey applicants.

Journey eligibility in Maryland rests on four pillars: four years holding an apprentice license, 7,500 supervised training hours, 32 hours of backflow training, and passing the comprehensive written examination.

questions.explanation: Years, hours, backflow training, and the exam — all four are required; none substitutes for the set.

questions.question: Which description of the job of the drainage system in a Maryland building matches accepted Maryland practice?

answers.text: A drainage system returns waste water to the potable supply after settling.
A building drainage system conveys sewage and waste water from fixtures to the building sewer and on to the public sewer or an approved private disposal system, by gravity wherever the design allows.
A drainage system exists only to vent sewer gas outdoors.
A common vent joins two fixtures below their flood rims.

questions.explanation: Drainage is a one-way gravity path out of the building — nothing in it is stored or reused.

questions.question: Which description of why gas dominates the Maryland journey outline matches accepted Maryland practice?

answers.text: A vent may end inside a chimney cleanout.
The journey license excludes gas work entirely.
Gas items appear only on the master paper.

Gas appliances and piping carry 40 of the 100 items on the Maryland journey outline because the journey credential is a combined plumber/gas fitter license — the holder is examined as a gas fitter, not as an afterthought.

questions.explanation: Plumber/gas fitter is one Maryland credential; the outline weights gas like it matters, because it does.

questions.question: Which description of gas connector rules for Maryland appliances matches accepted Maryland practice?

answers.text: Flexible appliance connectors are listed for the appliance, sized so they do not restrict flow, kept to the length the code allows, and never passed through walls, floors, or appliance housings.
Clearance applies only to wood, never to other combustibles.
Vent limiters are used to plug vents permanently.
Connectors may run through walls if sleeved in tape.

questions.explanation: A connector is a listed appliance part with routing rules — not a universal hose.

questions.question: A trainee asks about combustion air for Maryland gas appliances. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Gas appliances draw combustion air from the space or from outdoors through openings sized by the fuel gas code's methods — by room volume, by indoor and outdoor openings, or by engineered design — so burners never starve and soot.
Combustion air openings may be blocked once the appliance passes inspection.
Generator gas lines need no shutoff of their own.
A small closet is always an adequate air source.

questions.explanation: Starved burners make carbon monoxide; the sizing methods exist to keep air ahead of demand.

questions.question: When checking work against the Maryland State Plumbing Code, which statement about the Maryland apprentice license minimum age is right?

answers.text: An apprentice applicant must be at least 21 years of age.
The Board, not PSI, reviews every uploaded document in person.
A journey license allows the holder to contract plumbing work fully independently with no master involved.
An applicant for a Maryland apprentice plumber/gas fitter license must be at least 16 years of age.

questions.explanation: Sixteen is the published floor for both the apprentice plumber and apprentice natural gas fitter licenses.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers drainage pipe slope for small Maryland drains. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Horizontal drainage piping of two and one-half inches and smaller is sloped at one-quarter inch per foot in the direction of flow under the code Maryland has adopted.
Island fixtures need no venting because they sit low.
Small drainage piping is sloped at one inch per foot.
Small drainage piping is installed dead level for quiet operation.

questions.explanation: Quarter-inch-per-foot fall for the smaller sizes keeps solids moving with the water.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how why drainage slope has both a floor and a ceiling in practice is handled in practice.

answers.text: Slope is set by the fixture manufacturer's color chart.
Drainage is graded so waste water moves fast enough to carry solids with it without racing ahead and leaving the solids behind; the adopted slope tables balance scour against separation.
Steeper is always better, so drains are pitched as sharply as possible.
Public and private fixtures always share the same values.

questions.explanation: Too flat strands solids; wildly steep lets water outrun them — the table grades are the engineered middle.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the code that governs Maryland gas piping. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Hood systems are unrelated to gas service.
LP gas in Maryland follows the International Plumbing Code water chapters.

Fuel gas piping and appliance installation in Maryland follow the 2018 International Fuel Gas Code as incorporated by the Maryland State Plumbing Code, with liquefied petroleum gas under the 2017 edition of the national LP-gas code.
Maryland gas work follows no adopted code, only utility rules.

questions.explanation: IFGC 2018 for fuel gas, NFPA 58 (2017) for LP — the pair Maryland actually adopted.

questions.question: When checking work against the Maryland State Plumbing Code, which statement about venting categories of Maryland gas appliances is right?

answers.text: Gas appliances vent by category according to their flue-gas temperature and vent pressure: natural-draft categories rely on buoyancy, fan-assisted and condensing categories use their own listed vent systems and materials.
Vent category is chosen by the appliance's color.
All gas appliances may share one venting method.
Condensing appliances vent through any single-wall pipe.

questions.explanation: Category follows physics: hot buoyant gas, fan pressure, and corrosive condensate each demand their own vent design.

questions.question: A licensed Maryland master plumber asks a journey licensee, the topic of drainage pipe slope for mid-size Maryland drains comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Mid-size drainage piping is sloped at one-thirty-second inch per foot.
Horizontal drainage piping from three to six inches is sloped at one-eighth inch per foot in the direction of flow.
Mid-size drainage piping is sloped at one-half inch per foot.
Mid-size drainage piping may slope against the flow if vented.

questions.explanation: Larger pipes carry solids at a gentler grade: one-eighth inch per foot for the three-to-six-inch range.

questions.question: A licensed Maryland master plumber asks a journey licensee, the topic of gas piping pressure test duty in Maryland comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Gas piping is tested with oxygen for a cleaner result.
Pressure testing is waived when the pipe is new.
Gas piping is tested by lighting each appliance once.

A new Maryland gas piping system is pressure-tested with air or an inert gas — never oxygen — at the pressure and duration the fuel gas code requires for its size and volume, and proven tight before any appliance is connected or the piping is concealed.

questions.explanation: Air or inert gas only, code pressure, proven tight before cover — the test is the license to conceal.

questions.question: For safe, code-compliant Maryland plumbing practice, which statement about the appliance shutoff valve rule in Maryland gas work holds true?

answers.text: Each gas appliance has its own shutoff valve in the same room, within the reach the fuel gas code allows from the appliance, so a single appliance can be isolated without killing gas to the building.
One valve at the meter satisfies every appliance.
Shutoff valves are optional on appliances with electronic ignition.
Appliance valves may be located in another locked room.

questions.explanation: Same room, reachable, per appliance — isolation is a service and emergency basic.
