Harnesses are only for scissor lifts
One foot out for every two feet of height

questions.explanation: The 4-to-1 rule sets an extension or straight ladder at a stable angle that resists sliding and tipping.

questions.question: On a written assessment, a question covers housekeeping benefit. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A paper mask alone always suffices
It only makes the site look better for visitors
Egress is only needed at shift end
Clear walkways and stored materials prevent trips, falls, and struck-by incidents

questions.explanation: Good housekeeping directly prevents trip, fall, and struck-by injuries by keeping paths and work areas clear.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about scaffold guardrails. Which statement should the mentor confirm?

answers.text: Only the erector needs protection
Scaffolds never need fall protection
Guardrails or personal fall arrest protect workers on scaffolds above the trigger height
A toe board alone is sufficient

questions.explanation: Scaffold platforms above the trigger height require guardrail systems or personal fall arrest for everyone on them.

questions.question: On a written assessment, a question covers respirator fit. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A fit test and medical evaluation are required before respirator use
Fit testing is done once in a career
A dust mask needs a fit test but a respirator does not
Any respirator fits any worker

questions.explanation: Respirators only protect when they seal to the face, so fit testing and medical evaluation come before use.

questions.question: On a written assessment, a question covers adjustable wrench jaw. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Face the adjustable jaw toward the direction of pull so it grips without slipping
Use it as a hammer in a pinch
Grip with the jaw fully open
Turning bolts

questions.explanation: Pulling so the movable jaw is loaded in the strong direction keeps an adjustable wrench from spreading and rounding the fastener.

questions.question: During a morning toolbox talk, the topic of fire extinguisher classes comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Class A is for electrical fires
Class A is for cooking oils only
Flush against the wall
Class A is for ordinary combustibles such as wood and paper

questions.explanation: Extinguisher classes match fuel types: A for ordinary combustibles, B for flammable liquids, C for energized electrical, K for cooking oils.

questions.question: An instructor is checking understanding, the topic of torque wrench purpose comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Loosens rusted bolts faster
Tightens a fastener to a specified tightness so joints clamp correctly
Works as a breaker bar
Measures bolt length

questions.explanation: A torque wrench measures tightening force so bolted joints get the clamping load the design requires.

questions.question: An instructor is checking understanding, the topic of fall protection threshold comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Only on the first day of a job
Only when working above a roof edge
Only when the worker feels unsteady
Working at heights where a fall could cause serious injury, as required by the site plan and OSHA rules

questions.explanation: Fall protection decisions follow the site safety plan and applicable rules for the height and task, never personal comfort alone.

uscg-able-seaman.quiz_title: USCG Able Seaman Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes bow and stern?

answers.text: The bow is the deepest part of the hull below the waterline
The bow is the forward end of the vessel and the stern is the after end
The bow is the after end and the stern is forward
Both terms describe the sides of the vessel

questions.explanation: Forward is toward the bow; aft is toward the stern. Every other directional term on board builds on this pair.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes bulkhead?

answers.text: Spring lines are only used by spring tide
A bulkhead is a vertical partition — a wall — inside the vessel
A bulkhead is a type of anchor
A bulkhead is the opening in a deck

questions.explanation: Bulkheads divide the hull into compartments; watertight bulkheads limit flooding. Decks are the horizontal surfaces.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding draft?

answers.text: Draft is the distance from the deck to the waterline
Draft is the vessel's overall length
Draft is the vertical distance from the waterline down to the bottom of the keel
Draft is the height of the mast above the deck

questions.explanation: Draft tells how much water the vessel needs. The distance from waterline up to the deck is freeboard — the two add to depth of hull.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about freeboard.

answers.text: Freeboard is the distance from the keel to the waterline
Freeboard is the vertical distance from the waterline up to the main deck
Freeboard is spare cargo capacity measured in tons
Freeboard is the width of the vessel at the deck

questions.explanation: As a vessel loads, draft increases and freeboard decreases. Minimum freeboard is assigned for safety and marked on the hull.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about ground tackle.

answers.text: Ground tackle refers only to the anchor windlass motor
Ground tackle is the collective term for anchors, chains, and the gear used for anchoring
Ground tackle is the tackle used to hoist the gangway
Spring lines are only used by spring tide

questions.explanation: Anchor, chain or rode, windlass, and associated fittings together are the ground tackle.

questions.question: Which of these statements about beam would a licensed officer agree with?

answers.text: The beam is a single deck plank at the stern
The beam is the depth of the hold
The beam is the vessel's greatest width
A vessel constrained by her draft is any vessel in a channel

questions.explanation: Beam is measured at the widest point of the hull and matters for berthing, drydocking, and stability.

questions.question: Which of these statements about anchor parts would a licensed officer agree with?

answers.text: Draft is the distance from the deck to the waterline
Freeing ports must be plugged before getting underway in any weather
The flukes are the rings connecting the chain
The flukes are the parts of the anchor that dig into the bottom; the shank is the long central arm and the stock crosses near the top on stocked anchors

questions.explanation: Holding power comes from the flukes burying in the bottom. The crown joins shank and arms; the ring (shackle) takes the chain.

questions.question: Which description of scope of chain matches accepted maritime practice?

answers.text: Scope is the distance the vessel swings at anchor
Scope is the ratio of the length of anchor chain paid out to the depth of water (plus height of the hawse above water)
Scope is the angle of the anchor flukes
Scope is the weight of the anchor in pounds

questions.explanation: More scope lays the pull more horizontal so the anchor holds instead of breaking out; typical scope is 5 to 7 times the depth.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers hawsepipe. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: The hawsepipe is the pipe through which the anchor chain runs from the deck to the hawse opening in the bow
The hawsepipe is the voice tube to the anchor detail
The hawsepipe carries fuel to the bow thruster
The hawsepipe vents the chain locker

questions.explanation: Chain travels from windlass through the hawsepipe to the anchor. The spurling pipe leads chain down into the chain locker.

questions.question: Which description of masthead light arc matches accepted maritime practice?

answers.text: A masthead light is red on the port side
A masthead light is a white light showing over an arc of 225 degrees, visible from ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on each side
NUC by day is a black diamond between two balls
A masthead light shows over 135 degrees like a sternlight

questions.explanation: Masthead (225°), sidelights (112.5° each), and sternlight (135°) together cover the full circle without overlap confusion.

questions.question: When checking a crew member's knowledge of anchor light, which response is correct?

answers.text: An anchored vessel shows its sidelights and masthead light
A vessel at anchor shows an all-round white light where it can best be seen (two, the forward one higher, if 50 meters or more), and by day a single black ball
A composite unit is lighted as a vessel NUC
A vessel under oars shows a red light only

questions.explanation: Anchor lights are all-round white; deck lighting may be added on larger vessels but the anchor lights/shapes remain the legal signal.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how power-driven underway lights is handled at sea.

answers.text: A flashing light is any aid to navigation that flashes
A power-driven vessel underway shows a masthead light forward, a second masthead light abaft and higher if 50 meters or more, sidelights, and a sternlight
A second masthead light is shown forward of and lower than the first
A power-driven vessel under 50 meters must show two masthead lights

questions.explanation: Length drives the second masthead light (≥50 m). Under 50 m she may show one masthead light plus sidelights and sternlight.

questions.question: A new ordinary seaman needs to understand bitts and chocks. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: Bitts are fairleads on the mast
Bitts are paired vertical posts for securing mooring lines; chocks are fittings that guide lines through the rail
Chocks are posts used to belay lines on deck
Bitts are openings in the bulwark for drainage

questions.explanation: Lines are made fast to bitts or cleats; chocks give the line a fair lead and protect it from chafe at the rail.

questions.question: When checking a crew member's knowledge of bulwark and freeing ports, which response is correct?

answers.text: The bulwark is the solid rail around the weather deck, and freeing ports let shipped water drain overboard
Freeing ports must be plugged before getting underway in any weather
The bulwark is the railing around the pilothouse only
Freeing ports are used to take on ballast water

questions.explanation: Green water shipped on deck must escape quickly; freeing ports (scuppers in the bulwark) drain it so it does not add weight and free surface.

questions.question: A new ordinary seaman needs to understand windlass and wildcat. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: The wildcat is a hand crank for emergency steering
The wildcat is the sprocketed wheel of the windlass that engages the links of the anchor chain
Amidships is the highest point of the superstructure
The wildcat is the brake that stops the propeller shaft

questions.explanation: The wildcat's pockets grip each chain link as the windlass heaves or pays out. Smooth drums (gypsy heads / warping heads) handle line instead.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers sidelight arcs. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Each sidelight shows over 112.5 degrees, from ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on its own side — green to starboard, red to port
Sidelights show from astern around to ahead
A composite unit shows two full sets of towing lights
The green light is on the port side

questions.explanation: Seeing red means you are on the other vessel's port side; green, her starboard side — the first clue to aspect and crossing geometry.

questions.question: A new ordinary seaman needs to understand sternlight arc. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: A fishing vessel shows no sidelights even when making way
A sternlight is yellow and shows over 225 degrees
A sternlight is a white light showing over 135 degrees, centered astern (67.5 degrees each side of dead astern)
A composite unit shows two full sets of towing lights

questions.explanation: An overtaking vessel sees the sternlight of the vessel ahead. A special yellow towing light is shown above the sternlight when towing astern (Inland).

questions.question: Charted depth is 17 feet, the height of tide is 2 feet, and the vessel's draft is 11 feet. What is the under-keel clearance in feet?
questions.explanation: Actual depth = 17 + 2 = 19; minus draft 11 = 8 feet under the keel.

questions.question: The water depth at the anchorage is 90 feet and the master orders a scope of 7 to 1 based on depth. How many feet of chain must be paid out?
questions.explanation: Chain = 7 x 90 = 630 feet.

questions.question: A vessel's moulded depth from keel to main deck is 29 feet and her freeboard is measured at 9.5 feet. What is her draft in feet?
questions.explanation: Draft = depth - freeboard = 29 - 9.5 = 19.5 feet.

uscg-qmed.quiz_title: USCG QMED Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How would an experienced QMED best explain the QMED rating?

answers.text: Heat flows from the colder fluid to the hotter one
A QMED is a licensed engineer officer
A QMED is a qualified member of the engine department, an unlicensed rating below officer and above wiper or coal passer
Viscosity has no effect on fuel injection

questions.explanation: QMEDs are the qualified unlicensed engine-room ratings; wiper and coal passer are the entry ratings below them, and licensed officers are above.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes rounds of the machinery spaces?

answers.text: Rounds consist of signing the log without leaving the control room
On rounds the watch checks running machinery for leaks, noise, vibration, temperature, and correct oil and water levels
The oiler alone is responsible for the plant on watch
Only stopped machinery is checked on rounds

questions.explanation: Touch, sight, sound, and smell on rounds catch the bearing going hot or the leak starting long before an alarm does.

questions.question: Which statement best captures flanged joints?

answers.text: Flanged joints use no gasket
A leaking flange is fixed by overtightening one bolt
Flange bolts are tightened fully one at a time around the circle
A flanged pipe joint is sealed by a gasket compressed evenly between the flange faces as the bolts are tightened in sequence

questions.explanation: Even, cross-pattern tightening compresses the gasket uniformly; one-sided tightening cocks the flange and guarantees a leak.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes diesel engine principle?

answers.text: Diesel fuel ignites from a glow of the exhaust
Compression in a diesel is lower than in a gasoline engine
A diesel engine uses spark plugs like a gasoline engine
A diesel engine ignites its fuel by the heat of compression alone, with no spark plug

questions.explanation: Air compressed to a small fraction of its volume gets hot enough (well above the fuel's ignition temperature) to ignite the injected spray.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about diesel fuel injection purpose.

answers.text: Atomization is done by the exhaust valve
Injection only stores fuel near the cylinder
Injection timing is fixed and unrelated to load
The injection system meters the fuel, atomizes it, and injects it at the correct time for the load and speed

questions.explanation: Meter, atomize, time: those three jobs of the injection system decide how completely and smoothly the fuel burns.

questions.question: A trainee asks about engine department organization. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The chief engineer heads the engine department and is responsible for the propulsion plant and all machinery
The bosun heads the engine department
The first assistant deck officer heads the engine department
The master heads the engine department directly

questions.explanation: The master commands the vessel, but the engine department works under the chief engineer, through the first assistant engineer and the watch engineers.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the engine room log is handled at sea.

answers.text: The deck log records engine room readings
Log entries may be invented when a round is missed
More grease in a bearing is always better
Readings such as pressures, temperatures, and tank levels are recorded in the engine room log at regular intervals

questions.explanation: The log is the plant's legal and operating record; trends in its readings give the first warning of developing trouble.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about bearing temperature checks earns credit?

answers.text: Bearing temperature is never checked while running
A hot bearing is cooled by stopping its oil supply
A bearing that is heating up is found by comparing its temperature with its normal running temperature and with sister bearings
All bearings normally run too hot to touch

questions.explanation: Rising bearing temperature means failing lubrication or overload; report it early — a wiped bearing is far costlier than a slowed engine.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how measuring with a micrometer is handled at sea.

answers.text: A micrometer measures small dimensions such as shaft journals and clearances to about a thousandth of an inch
A micrometer measures electrical resistance
Expansion is absorbed by tightening flanges harder
Grease and oil are interchangeable in every bearing

questions.explanation: Micrometers (and calipers for larger work) are the precision measuring instruments of the engine room; feeler gauges measure clearances between parts.

questions.question: Which description of calipers matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: Calipers measure temperature
Calipers transfer or take inside and outside dimensions of parts such as bores, journals, and pipe
Calipers are used only on electrical work
Calipers are cutting tools

questions.explanation: Inside calipers read bores, outside calipers read shafts; the measurement is then read against a rule or micrometer.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to trunk piston and crosshead designs. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Trunk pistons are used only in steam engines
Side thrust does not exist in diesel engines
Large slow-speed engines use a crosshead to take side thrust, keeping it off the cylinder liner, while smaller engines use trunk pistons
Scavenging applies only to gasoline engines

questions.explanation: The crosshead guide absorbs piston side thrust so the liner sees only vertical motion; trunk pistons take the thrust on the liner wall through the skirt.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about feeler gauge use. Which statement should the mentor confirm?

answers.text: A feeler gauge tightens pipe flanges
A feeler gauge measures shaft speed
A feeler gauge measures the small gap or clearance between two surfaces, such as valve clearance or bearing clearance
A feeler gauge measures fluid pressure

questions.explanation: The blade that slips in with light drag is the clearance. Valve lash, ring gaps, and coupling checks all depend on it.

questions.question: A new wiper needs to understand the engineering watch. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: The engineer on watch is responsible for the safe operation of the machinery plant during that watch
Overfilling a sump has no effect on the machine
Mechanical seals are used only on steam lines
The oiler alone is responsible for the plant on watch

questions.explanation: Watch engineers own the plant on their watch; QMEDs assist them, make rounds, and report abnormal conditions at once.

questions.question: When checking a crew member's knowledge of relieving the watch, which response is correct?

answers.text: Relief valve discharge is piped to the bilge
Water in lube oil is normal and harmless
Relief is complete when the off-going watch leaves the space
A relieving watchstander must be familiarized with the running machinery, orders in effect, and any abnormal conditions before taking over

questions.explanation: A proper relief passes the state of the plant — what is running, what is secured, what is abnormal — so nothing is lost at the changeover.

questions.question: A new wiper needs to understand lubricating oil levels. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: A sump may be run empty to clean it
Sump and header tank oil levels are kept within the marked working range and checked on every round
Oil levels are checked once a month
Overfilling a sump has no effect on the machine

questions.explanation: Too little oil starves bearings; too much causes foaming, overheating, and leaks. Levels falling steadily mean consumption or a leak to find.

questions.question: When checking a crew member's knowledge of hand tools care, which response is correct?

answers.text: Hand tools are cleaned, inspected, and returned to their stowage after use so they are ready and accounted for
Damaged tools are kept in service until they break
Tools are left where they were last used
Tools are stowed loose on top of machinery

questions.explanation: A tool left in machinery spaces can fall into equipment or be impossible to find in an emergency; damaged tools injure people.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers four-stroke cycle. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: The four-stroke cycle completes intake, compression, power, and exhaust in four piston strokes and two crankshaft revolutions
Low compression raises that cylinder's exhaust temperature sharply
Four-stroke means four cylinders
The four-stroke cycle has no separate exhaust stroke

questions.explanation: One power stroke per cylinder every two revolutions; separate valve events handle charging and scavenging across the four strokes.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about standing orders in engineering. Which statement should the mentor confirm?

answers.text: Tank tables are the same for every vessel
The chief engineer's standing orders give the watch instructions for routine operation and the conditions that require calling the chief
Standing orders apply only to the deck department
Tanks are filled to the top to save time

questions.explanation: Standing and night orders tell the watch when to act alone and when to call — unusual noise, low pressure, or any doubt means call.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers pipe threads and fittings. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Tapered pipe threads seal by the wedging action of the threads themselves, usually with thread compound or tape
Pipe size names give the exact outside diameter
Pipe threads seal only with a gasket
Straight and tapered pipe threads are interchangeable

questions.explanation: National pipe taper threads tighten and seal as they wedge; nominal pipe size is a name, not the measured diameter.

questions.question: An instructor is checking understanding, the topic of two-stroke cycle comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A two-stroke fires once every two revolutions
A two-stroke engine completes its cycle in one crankshaft revolution, using ports uncovered by the piston for exhaust and charging
A two-stroke engine needs four revolutions per cycle
Two-stroke engines have no lubrication concerns

questions.explanation: Ports in the liner and a scavenge blower or turbocharger clear exhaust and refill the cylinder each revolution — a power stroke every turn.

indiana-plumbing-contractor.quiz_title: Indiana Plumbing Contractor Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who licenses Indiana plumbers?

answers.text: The Indiana building commissioner licenses plumbers county by county
Plumbing in Indiana is licensed statewide by the Indiana Plumbing Commission under the Professional Licensing Agency
Each Indiana city licenses plumbers independently with no state license
Plumbers in Indiana need no license if they work only on private homes

questions.explanation: Indiana is unusual: plumbing is the one construction trade the state itself licenses, and the Commission's license is the credential that applies statewide.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the trade-experience route?

answers.text: Trade experience must be proven only by tax records
Temporary licenses renew without limit
A resident may instead present a notarized statement evidencing at least four years of experience in the plumbing trade
State licensure eliminates all local permit duties

questions.explanation: Experience outside a formal apprenticeship counts if it reaches the four-year floor and is sworn to in the notarized statement the statute requires.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the Commission's verification power?

answers.text: Only the applicant may be contacted during review
Verification ends once affidavits are filed
The Commission must accept application papers at face value
The Commission may seek additional information from the applicant, any employer, or any third party to decide whether examination requirements are met

questions.explanation: Eligibility is actively verified. The Commission's authority to go to employers and third parties is written into the admission rule.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes water closet flush volume?

answers.text: Dual-flush closets are prohibited
A standard water closet is limited to a maximum flush of 1.6 gallons per flush, with high-efficiency models flushing less
Water closets may flush up to 3.5 gallons as new fixtures
Flush volume has no maximum for commercial closets

questions.explanation: The 1.6 gallon maximum made the modern closet; older 3.5 and 5 gallon tanks are replacement-only history, not a new-installation option.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding acting without a license?

answers.text: A license is needed only to pull permits, not to do the work
Only commercial plumbing requires a license in Indiana
Acting as a plumbing contractor or journeyman plumber in Indiana without the corresponding Commission license is unlawful
Unlicensed plumbing is allowed for jobs under a set dollar amount

questions.explanation: The licensing statute covers the practice itself, not just the paperwork: holding out and working in either capacity requires the license.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about indiana's license ladder earns credit?

answers.text: Indiana's top grade is called master plumber
Indiana's ladder runs apprentice, then journeyman plumber, then plumbing contractor as the top individual grade
Applications remain open indefinitely once filed
A corporation needs no license if its owner is licensed in another state

questions.explanation: There is no master plumber grade in Indiana. The plumbing contractor is the top license and the only individual grade that may contract for plumbing work.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to what four years of experience means in hours. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Four years means 4,000 hours with no time span required
Four years of experience means a minimum of 6,400 hours in the plumbing trade over at least four years
There is no age requirement for the contractor examination
A failed candidate must wait four years before any retake

questions.explanation: The rule converts the year requirement into hours: 6,400 hours minimum, and they must still span at least four years.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the weekly counting cap is handled in practice.

answers.text: No more than 40 hours may be counted in any calendar week toward the apprenticeship or experience requirement
Notice is required within one year
Only commercial plumbing requires a license in Indiana
Up to 60 hours per week may be counted

questions.explanation: The 40-hour weekly cap is why the requirement cannot be compressed: even heavy overtime stretches across the full four years.

questions.question: Which description of employer affidavits matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: Affidavits are required only for out-of-state experience
An examination applicant must submit affidavits from employers verifying all experience claimed in the application
Only the most recent employer must verify experience
Employer verification is optional if the applicant signs the form

questions.explanation: Every claimed period of experience must be verified by the employer who supervised it; the Commission does not take the applicant's word alone.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers urinal flush volume. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Urinal flush volume is unlimited
Waterless urinals are prohibited everywhere
A urinal is limited to a maximum flush of 1.0 gallon per flush
Shower doors must swing inward to save space

questions.explanation: Urinals carry their own, tighter maximum; waterless designs satisfy it by using no water at all where they are approved.

questions.question: When checking a journeyman's knowledge of showerhead flow, which response is correct?

answers.text: Flush controls may be placed behind the user in all cases
Sealing the base is prohibited because it hides leaks
Showerheads may flow 5 gallons per minute as new fixtures
A showerhead is limited to a maximum flow of 2.5 gallons per minute at the standard test pressure

questions.explanation: The 2.5 gpm cap applies per shower compartment's outlet arrangement; body-spray designs must account for the combined flow the code allows.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how kitchen faucet flow is handled in practice.

answers.text: Kitchen faucets are limited to 1.5 gpm in all cases
Pull-out sprays are measured differently and unlimited
Rough-in dimensions never vary between brands
A kitchen sink faucet is limited to 2.2 gallons per minute at the standard test pressure

questions.explanation: Kitchen faucets share the lavatory-class maximum; temporary higher-flow features on some models are an engineered exception, not the rating.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how minimum age for the contractor examination is handled in practice.

answers.text: The minimum age is 17 years old
Indiana publishes a guaranteed passing score of 85 percent
There is no age requirement for the contractor examination
A plumbing contractor examination applicant must be at least 18 years old

questions.explanation: Eighteen is the floor for both the journeyman and contractor examinations; the younger age figure that appears in the application material belongs to apprentice registration.

questions.question: For code-compliant Indiana practice, which statement about the apprenticeship route to eligibility holds true?

answers.text: An Indiana resident qualifies through an approved apprenticeship by completing at least four years in a program approved by the Commission
Two years in any apprenticeship is enough in Indiana
Apprenticeship is not an accepted route to the contractor exam
The apprenticeship must be served entirely out of state

questions.explanation: The approved-apprenticeship route is the standard path: four years in a Commission-approved program, documented by the program sponsor.

questions.question: Which description of hours inside a four-year approved apprenticeship matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: A four-year approved apprenticeship means at least 576 hours of classroom instruction and 6,400 hours of related on-the-job training
Contractors register with the Commission instead of localities
Helpers may hold themselves out as plumbers without a license
It means 288 classroom hours and 4,000 hours on the job

questions.explanation: The rule quantifies the apprenticeship: 576 hours in the classroom and 6,400 hours of related on-the-job training spread over at least four years.

questions.question: Which of these statements about the work-under-a-contractor route would an Indiana inspector agree with?

answers.text: A state license forbids local registration requirements
Work under an unlicensed contractor qualifies equally
Such applicants need only a letter from an employer
Working in a plumbing business under the direction of a licensed plumbing contractor for at least four years is a qualifying route for the contractor examination

questions.explanation: The contractor exam recognizes time spent in a real plumbing business under a licensed contractor's direction — the journeyman-to-owner pathway.

questions.question: A journeyman asks the contractor, the topic of lavatory faucet flow comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Lavatory faucets have no flow limit
Public faucets flow more than private by rule
Metering faucets are prohibited in public restrooms
A private lavatory faucet is limited to 2.2 gallons per minute at the standard test pressure, and public lavatory faucets are limited much lower or are metering types

questions.explanation: Public lavatories are the conservation frontier: low maximum flows or self-closing metering faucets that deliver a fixed dose per cycle.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers prior-experience credit in an apprenticeship. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A failed candidate must wait four years before any retake
There is no weekly cap on counted hours
Prior credit may cover 100 percent of the apprenticeship
Credit for previous education, training, or experience toward an approved apprenticeship may not exceed 75 percent of the total required hours

questions.explanation: Credit is generous but capped: at most three-quarters of the program may be credited, and the credit must be granted through the federal apprenticeship bureau and approved by the Commission.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers when an employer affidavit cannot be obtained. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: An applicant who cannot obtain a required employer affidavit must file an affidavit stating the inability and the reason for it
A coworker's letter replaces the required affidavit automatically
The application is automatically denied without every employer affidavit
The applicant may simply omit that period with no explanation

questions.explanation: A defunct employer does not end an application — but the gap must be sworn to and explained, and the Commission may still investigate.

questions.question: For the expected temperature change, a piping material expands 0.12 inches per foot of run. How much does a 30-foot run grow, in inches?
questions.explanation: Growth = 0.12 x 30 = 3.6 inches.

massachusetts-journeyperson-sheet-metal.quiz_title: Massachusetts Journeyperson Sheet Metal Worker Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures licensure by examination only?

answers.text: A license may still be bought from the Board without an examination
Since the grandfathering period ended on February 18, 2011, journeyperson and master licenses may be obtained only by examination
Candidates schedule with PSI first and apply afterward
Only master licenses require examination; journeyperson licenses do not

questions.explanation: The grandfathering window closed in February 2011; every new journeyperson or master since then has qualified by passing the Board's examination.

questions.question: Which statement best captures what is not sheet metal work?

answers.text: Sheet metal work is limited to cutting flat stock in a shop
Residential duct systems are not sheet metal work
Duct or air exhaust systems for refrigeration and combustion units are not sheet metal work
J-1 eligibility has no minimum years, only total hours

questions.explanation: The refrigeration and combustion carve-out is express; ordinary commercial duct and remodeling ductwork are inside the definition.

questions.question: A trainee asks about the homeowner exception. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The restricted license is granted after a hands-on shop demonstration instead of a written test
No license is required for work by a homeowner inside their own one- or two-family owner-occupied building
A homeowner may do sheet metal work in a rental property they own
The J-1 course is 450 hours

questions.explanation: The exception is narrow: the owner's own one- or two-family owner-occupied home.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about function decides sheet metal work.

answers.text: Copper work is always sheet metal work and plastic never is
Whether work is sheet metal work is determined by its function and purpose, not by the material used
Only work in galvanized steel counts as sheet metal work
The heaviest material on a job decides which trade's work it is

questions.explanation: A plastic PVC or CPVC duct system serving a duct function is sheet metal work even though no metal is involved.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to non-metal roof coverings. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Retakes require a new course each time
Non-metal roof coverings and their associated flashing are not sheet metal work
Trade names need no connection to the license
All roofing of any material is sheet metal work

questions.explanation: Watershed roof systems are in the definition, but roof coverings and associated metal flashing within them are excepted, and non-metal coverings are outside entirely.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who licenses Massachusetts sheet metal workers?

answers.text: The Massachusetts building commissioner licenses sheet metal workers county by county
Sheet metal work in Massachusetts is licensed by the Board of Examiners of Sheet Metal Workers within the Division of Occupational Licensure
Each Massachusetts city licenses sheet metal workers independently with no state license
Sheet metal workers in Massachusetts need no license if they work only on homes

questions.explanation: The Board sits inside the Division of Occupational Licensure and licenses apprentices, journeypersons, masters, instructors, schools, and businesses statewide.

questions.question: A trainee asks about the Massachusetts sheet metal license ladder. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The ladder runs Class A Apprentice, then Class J-2 Restricted or J-1 Unrestricted Journeyperson, then Class M-2 Restricted or M-1 Unrestricted Master
An apprentice may step directly to master without a journeyperson grade
The ladder runs helper, then mechanic, then contractor with no restricted grades
Massachusetts licenses only a single all-purpose sheet metal grade

questions.explanation: Restricted and unrestricted grades exist at both the journeyperson and master levels; the apprentice grade is Class A.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how other trades' work boundary is handled in practice.

answers.text: Work of a licensed pipe fitter, oil burning technician, refrigeration technician, plumber, or gasfitter under those trades' own laws is not sheet metal work
Only work in galvanized steel counts as sheet metal work
A sheet metal license overrides every other trade license on a job
No photo or background authorization is required

questions.explanation: Each licensed trade's statutory work stays with that trade; the sheet metal definition yields to the neighboring licenses.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts journeyperson best explain tasks needing no license?

answers.text: No license is required for paid duct repair by a handyman
No license is required for any work under a set dollar amount
All licenses expire December 31
No license is required for transporting or non-professional handling of sheet metal fixtures, or operating heavy machinery to move fixtures to the installation point

questions.explanation: Logistics and rigging support are carved out; installing or repairing the work for the public is not.

questions.question: Which description of purpose of layout matches the governing Massachusetts rules and standards?

answers.text: Layout refers only to scheduling shop work
Layout is the shop process of developing flat patterns from drawings so fittings can be cut, formed, and assembled to finished size
Verification is the inspector's job, not the shop's
Layout is the final inspection of installed duct

questions.explanation: Every fitting starts as a flat pattern; layout converts the drawing's finished geometry into cuttable metal.

questions.question: When checking an apprentice's knowledge of radial line development, which response is correct?

answers.text: The Pittsburgh lock is a soldered corner joint
Radial line development suits cones and pyramids, whose element lines radiate from one apex point
Radial line development suits long straight duct runs
Caps are cut exactly to the opening with no allowance

questions.explanation: All surface lines of a cone meet at the apex, so the pattern is struck from that center.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how triangulation is handled in practice.

answers.text: Wired edges are glued
Triangulation develops irregular transitions by dividing the surface into triangles and finding each edge's true length
Triangulation avoids finding true lengths
Triangulation works only on cylinders

questions.explanation: Square-to-rounds and offset transitions have no parallel or radial order, so the surface is broken into triangles.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about testing adjusting and balancing in the definition earns credit?

answers.text: Balancing belongs exclusively to the refrigeration license
Air balancing is reserved to licensed engineers in Massachusetts
The testing, adjusting, and air-balancing of air-handling equipment is sheet metal work
Testing and adjusting duct systems is unlicensed work

questions.explanation: TAB work on air-handling equipment is written into the definition of sheet metal work itself.

questions.question: For correct Massachusetts sheet metal practice, which statement about electrical work boundary holds true?

answers.text: Electrical work is not authorized by a sheet metal license, and an electrician's license does not authorize sheet metal work
An electrician may perform duct work under the electrical license
Incomplete applications stay open indefinitely
Either license covers both trades on small jobs

questions.explanation: The trades are mutually exclusive: neither license reaches into the other's work.

questions.question: A new apprentice needs to understand who may perform sheet metal work for the public. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: J-1 eligibility requires 4,800 hours over three years
Only a master or journeyperson licensed by the Board, with the proper permit from the local building inspector, may perform sheet metal work for the public
A business license alone authorizes an individual to do the work
An unlicensed person may work if a licensee inspects afterward

questions.explanation: Both the license and the permit are required before a licensee performs work for the public.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the three pattern development methods. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Fittings are developed by parallel line development, radial line development, or triangulation, chosen by the fitting's shape
Patterns are developed by freehand sketching only
A cone's pattern is a rectangle
One method serves every fitting shape

questions.explanation: Rectangular-to-round transitions triangulate, elbows radiate from a center, and straight duct develops on parallel lines.

questions.question: During a journeyperson examination review, the topic of parallel line development comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Parallel line development requires a single apex point
Parallel line development suits prismatic shapes such as rectangular duct and square elbows, where element lines stay parallel
Parallel line development works only on round pipe
Parallel line development is used for cones

questions.explanation: When the fitting's edges run parallel, the pattern wraps those parallel elements onto the flat sheet.

questions.question: A metal roof covers 3600 square feet. How many squares of roofing is that? (1 square = 100 square feet.)
A rectangular duct measures 32 inches by 16 inches. What is its cross-sectional area, in square feet? (144 square inches = 1 square foot.)
questions.explanation: Area = 32 x 16 = 512 square inches = 3.56 square feet.

questions.question: A duct with a cross-sectional area of 2.5 square feet carries air at 700 feet per minute. What is the airflow, in cubic feet per minute?
questions.explanation: Airflow = 2.5 x 700 = 1750 cfm.

massachusetts-master-plumber.quiz_title: Massachusetts Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes board that licenses plumbers?

answers.text: The local plumbing inspector is the body that licenses plumbers statewide in Massachusetts.
The Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters is the body that licenses plumbers and gas fitters in Massachusetts.
A national plumbing association issues Massachusetts plumber licenses.
The building department in each city licenses plumbers for the whole Commonwealth.

questions.explanation: Licensing is a state function handled by the named Board, while local inspectors handle local permits and inspections.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes apprentice direct supervision rule?

answers.text: An apprentice needs supervision only on gas work and never on plumbing work.
An apprentice plumber works only under the direct supervision of a master plumber or a journeyman plumber.
An apprentice may be supervised by any licensed tradesperson in any trade.
Passing candidates receive a full review of every exam item.

questions.explanation: Direct supervision by a master or journeyman is a condition of lawful apprentice work.

questions.question: Which statement best captures separate gas fitter licenses?

answers.text: An apprentice license may be renewed forever with no time limit.
Only Part One must be passed because Part Two is not scored.
Massachusetts has separate gas fitter licenses, including journeyman gas fitter, master gas fitter, and liquefied petroleum gas installer credentials.
Massachusetts has no gas fitter license separate from plumbing licenses.

questions.explanation: Gas fitting has its own license types alongside the plumbing ladder.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to plumber seeking gas fitter license. Which point is correct?

answers.text: For a business, any employee may take out the permit in a personal name.
A licensed plumber who wants a journeyman gas fitter license must still apply, pay the required fees, and pass that exam, but needs no added education or experience for it.
Hours worked under an unlicensed person count toward the 6,800 hours.
A plumber automatically receives a gas fitter license with no application or exam.

questions.explanation: The plumbing background satisfies education and experience, but the separate application and exam still apply.

questions.question: Which statement best captures journeyman theory hours total?

answers.text: Journeyman eligibility requires 550 hours of theory in a single month.
Journeyman eligibility includes only 55 hours of theory instruction.
Theory instruction is optional and is never counted for journeyman eligibility.
Journeyman eligibility includes 550 hours of theory instruction.

questions.explanation: Classroom theory is a separate requirement from field hours, totaling 550 hours.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about division housing the board earns credit?

answers.text: For a business, the permit goes to the customer rather than the company.
The Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters sits within the Division of Occupational Licensure.
The Board sits within the Department of Public Safety as a local inspection office.
For a business, any employee may take out the permit in a personal name.

questions.explanation: The Board is a state board housed in the Division of Occupational Licensure.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how master work through journeymen is handled in practice.

answers.text: An incomplete application is approved automatically after 30 days.
A master plumber may lend their license to any independent journeyman business.
A master plumber may supervise apprentices in other businesses without employing them.
A master plumber may perform work personally or through journeymen in their employ.

questions.explanation: The master is responsible for the business and may work directly or through employed journeymen.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how master exam journeyman prerequisite is handled in practice.

answers.text: Eligibility for the master plumber exam requires holding a Massachusetts journeyman plumber license.
Master eligibility requires a 500-hour business course instead of Tier Five.
Any apprentice may sit for the master exam without a journeyman license.
The yearly credit cap is 550 education hours in one year.

questions.explanation: Master eligibility builds on the journeyman license already earned.

questions.question: Which description of tier five course requirement matches the Massachusetts uniform state plumbing code?

answers.text: Master eligibility requires a 500-hour business course instead of Tier Five.
Master exam eligibility includes completing the 110-hour Tier Five course, unless it was already finished during the apprenticeship.
No course work of any kind is required for the master exam.
The Tier Five course is a one-hour online orientation.

questions.explanation: Tier Five is the final education tier and its 110 hours are part of master eligibility.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts master plumber best explain black steel gas piping?

answers.text: Black steel pipe is an approved material for fuel gas piping inside buildings.
Black steel pipe is banned from all fuel gas use.
Accessibility matters only for the meter valve and no others.
Gas pipe may share an elevator shaft if it is labeled.

questions.explanation: Black steel is a standard fuel gas piping material, joined mainly with threaded or welded joints.

questions.question: A new apprentice needs to understand copper tubing for gas. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: Corrosion protection is needed only for pipe that will be removed weekly.
Copper tubing is the only material ever allowed for gas piping.
Copper tubing may be used for fuel gas where the gas and the code allow it, using approved joints for gas service.
A regulator filters sediment out of the gas stream.

questions.explanation: Copper has a limited, conditional place in gas work rather than a universal one.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how tracer wire for plastic piping is handled in practice.

answers.text: A tracer wire is needed only if the installer expects to dig the line up.
Underground plastic gas piping must be installed with a tracer wire so the line can be located later.
Painting the ground above plastic pipe replaces the tracer wire.
An elevator shaft is an approved vertical chase for gas piping.

questions.explanation: Because plastic cannot be found with a metal locator, the tracer wire provides the locating path.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers apprentice minimum age requirement. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Apprentices may wait five years after licensure before starting school.
The experience form needs no signatures from anyone at the school.
An apprentice license requires the applicant to be at least 21 years old.
An applicant for an apprentice plumber license must be at least 16 years old and must hold an apprentice license to do apprentice work.

questions.explanation: Apprentices are licensed learners, not unlicensed helpers, and the minimum age is 16.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about master experience time and hours. Which statement should the mentor confirm?

answers.text: A master applicant needs ten years as an apprentice and no journeyman hours.
Time worked in another trade counts hour for hour as journeyman plumbing time.
A master exam applicant must have at least one year and at least 1,700 clock hours working as a Massachusetts journeyman plumber.
A master applicant needs only 100 hours working as a journeyman.

questions.explanation: Both the one-year minimum and the 1,700-hour minimum as a Massachusetts journeyman must be met.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers journeyman apprentice hours total. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Journeyman eligibility is built on 6,800 apprentice clock hours worked under a master plumber, or under a journeyman employed by a master plumber.
Journeyman eligibility requires 6,800 hours of classroom theory and no field hours.
Journeyman eligibility requires only 680 apprentice clock hours.
Hours worked under an unlicensed person count toward the 6,800 hours.

questions.explanation: The field-experience foundation for the journeyman exam is 6,800 supervised apprentice hours.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers corrugated stainless steel tubing. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Corrugated stainless steel tubing is an approved gas piping system when it is installed according to its listing and the manufacturer instructions.
Corrugated stainless steel tubing never needs any fittings from its own system.
A low-pressure system may be tested at one-half pound because that is its working pressure.
Corrugated stainless steel tubing is approved only for underground burial.

questions.explanation: CSST is a listed system, so its listing and instructions control how it is routed, supported, and terminated.

questions.question: When checking a journeyman's knowledge of polyethylene pipe underground only, which response is correct?

answers.text: A pipe near the edge of a stud needs no plate because nails avoid it.
Polyethylene gas pipe is used underground only and is never run inside a building as interior gas piping.
CSST may be pulled tight against nail paths with no protection.
Polyethylene pipe is approved exposed inside a living room.

questions.explanation: Plastic gas pipe is an underground material, with the transition to approved material made as the code requires.

questions.question: A piping material grows 0.05 inches per foot for the design temperature change. By how many inches does a run of 110 feet grow?
questions.explanation: Growth = 0.05 x 110 = 5.5 inches.

questions.question: A dimension of 140 inches is given center to center. Each fitting takes out 5 inches at the first end and 5 inches at the second. What cut length is needed, in inches?
questions.explanation: Cut length = 140 - 5 - 5 = 130 inches.

questions.question: Filling a 825-gallon tank at a steady 25 gallons per minute, how many minutes are needed?
questions.explanation: Time = 825 / 25 = 33 minutes.

ase-a1-engine-repair.quiz_title: ASE A1 — Engine Repair Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A vehicle has an aftermarket remote starter and a new complaint of intermittent no-start. Why does this detail belong in the verification notes?

answers.text: Aftermarket devices always cause no-starts and should be removed immediately
It voids all manufacturer service information
It is unrelated to starting and should be omitted
Added equipment in the starting path is a variable that must be documented and considered when the symptom is intermittent and starter-related

questions.explanation: Any non-original device spliced into a starting or ignition path is a legitimate diagnostic variable for an intermittent no-start and must be recorded. It does not automatically prove causation as A claims, nor does it void service information as B claims.

questions.question: Before any vacuum diagnosis, the gauge needle sits at 1.5 in. Hg with the hose disconnected and open to atmosphere. What must be done first?

answers.text: Proceed, because 1.5 in. Hg is too small to matter
Subtract 1.5 from barometric pressure instead
Replace the engine's intake gaskets if readings look low
Zero the gauge (or account for the offset per its instructions); an open hose must read 0 in. Hg

questions.explanation: Open to atmosphere, a vacuum gauge must indicate zero. A 1.5 in. Hg offset would corrupt every pattern judgment, for example making a normal 19 in. Hg read as about 17.5, so the instrument is corrected before the engine is judged.

questions.question: While pressurizing a cylinder for leak-down, the engine suddenly rotates and the reading drops to near 100% leakage. No parts were changed. What happened?

answers.text: The piston ring broke at that moment
The head gasket failed under shop air pressure
Both valves opened because the timing chain jumped
The piston was not exactly at top dead center, so air pressure pushed it down, opening the test position and venting past valves as the crank turned

questions.explanation: If the piston is slightly off top dead center, air pressure acts on it like a power stroke and rotates the crank, moving the piston down and changing valve position, which destroys the test setup. The cylinder must be reset to top dead center compression and the crank held.

questions.question: Oil is puddling on top of the head around the springs and the engine smokes on start-up after sitting overnight. Which parts are most suspect?

answers.text: Valve seats
Stem seals that leak while the engine sits, letting oil drain down the guides
Head bolt threads
Spring shims

questions.explanation: Start-up smoke after sitting is the classic stem-seal pattern: oil pooled around the guides drains past hardened or loose seals overnight and burns at start-up. Seats, bolt threads, and shims do not meter oil at the guide.

questions.question: Intake guide clearance measures within the limit given, but the valve still shows heavy oil deposits on its back. Which other cause fits this evidence?

answers.text: Exhaust guide wear
A failed or loose intake stem seal letting oil past a good guide
Excessive deck flatness
A strong valve spring

questions.explanation: Oil control at the guide needs both correct clearance and a working seal. With clearance proven within limit, a hardened, torn, or loose seal explains oil on the intake valve back. Exhaust wear, flatness, and spring strength do not meter intake guide oil.

questions.question: An engine will not crank, the battery and starter pass all tests on the bench, cables pass voltage-drop tests on the vehicle, and the engine will not rotate by hand with the starter removed. What is the final separation this sequence achieves?

answers.text: The starting subsystem is proven good both on and off the vehicle, so the no-crank cause is engine-mechanical lock-up, confirmed by failure to rotate with the starter out of the way
The battery must still be the cause
The fuel system is the cause
Bench tests are invalid so nothing is proven

questions.explanation: Removing the starter eliminates any starter-engagement explanation for the failed hand rotation, completing the isolation: every electrical element passed, and the engine itself will not turn. That is a mechanical lock-up by exclusion and direct test.

questions.question: Translucent white vapor from the exhaust disappears within minutes of a cold start on a cool morning, coolant level is stable over 2,000 miles, and there is no sweet odor. What is the correct interpretation?

answers.text: Early head-gasket failure that must be repaired before it worsens
A leaking intake-manifold coolant passage burning coolant intermittently
Normal condensation in the exhaust system; no coolant consumption is demonstrated
Coolant consumption too small to measure, requiring engine teardown

questions.explanation: Water is a normal combustion product and condenses in a cold exhaust, clearing as it warms. Stable coolant level over 2,000 miles and no sweet odor give no evidence of coolant consumption, so no repair is justified.

questions.question: An inline PCV valve has a flow-direction arrow on its body. It is found installed with the arrow pointing toward the crankcase instead of toward the intake manifold. What is the fault and correction?

answers.text: The arrow is decorative and orientation does not matter
Backwards installation increases ventilation and is harmless
The valve is installed backwards, blocking normal flow from crankcase to intake; reinstall it in the marked flow direction
The correction is to remove the valve entirely

questions.explanation: PCV flow runs from the crankcase to the intake manifold, and a directional valve installed backwards acts as a blockage. Correcting orientation restores the designed flow path; this is a basic installation inspection point.

questions.question: A head has been resurfaced. The measured amount removed plus a previous resurfacing now leaves the head thickness below the minimum thickness given in the stem. What should be done?

answers.text: Install the head with two head gaskets
Install the head and advance the cam timing to compensate
Mill the intake manifold instead and reuse the head
Replace the head because minimum thickness has been violated

questions.explanation: Minimum head thickness protects deck stiffness, combustion chamber volume, and valve train geometry. Once total material removed puts thickness below the minimum given, the head is no longer serviceable regardless of how flat it is, and it must be replaced.

questions.question: Carbon is built up on the back of an intake valve and in the port. Which valve-train condition, besides mixture or oil control, can contribute by holding the valve off its seat?

answers.text: Insufficient valve lash or preload holding the valve slightly open
Excessive deck flatness
New stem seals
Correct seat concentricity

questions.explanation: If lash is too tight or preload too great, the valve may not fully seat, allowing hot gas and deposits to affect the face and port area and preventing heat transfer into the seat. Flatness, new seals, and concentric seats do not hold a valve open.

questions.question: In a cylinder power balance test at idle, disabling each cylinder in turn drops rpm by about 50 rpm for cylinders 1, 2, and 4, but only 5 rpm for cylinder 3. What does cylinder 3's small drop mean?

answers.text: Cylinder 3 is the strongest cylinder
Cylinder 3 was contributing very little power before it was disabled
The test failed because all drops must be identical
Cylinder 3's ignition is the only possible cause

questions.explanation: A power balance test measures each cylinder's contribution by the rpm lost when it is cut. Drops of about 50 rpm show normal contribution; a 5 rpm drop means cylinder 3 was doing almost no work already. The test localizes the cylinder, not yet the cause.

questions.question: Charging voltage reads 13.9 volts, but a scope shows one missing ripple hump in every cycle and the battery repeatedly tests marginal after charging. Which statement is most accurate?

answers.text: Average charging voltage in range proves the alternator is fully healthy
A single failed diode can keep average voltage near normal while reducing output capacity and adding ripple, so the alternator can be faulty despite a normal-looking voltage number
Ripple patterns have no diagnostic value
The battery causes the missing ripple hump

questions.explanation: A voltmeter reads the average, which one dead diode may barely move. The scope's ripple pattern exposes the missing phase contribution. Output capacity and cleanliness, not just average voltage, decide whether a charging system can support the vehicle.

questions.question: Technician A says hydraulic lifters compensate automatically for thermal expansion and minor wear. Technician B says hydraulic lifters never need any preload verification after valve work. Who is correct?

answers.text: Technician B only
Technician A only
Both technicians
Neither technician

questions.explanation: Technician A is correct: within their travel, hydraulic lifters self-adjust for expansion and wear. Technician B is wrong because valve work changes stem height and geometry, so the plunger's starting position (preload) must be verified to be inside its compensating range.

questions.question: After installing a new chain and sprockets, the cam timing marks align but the crank mark is half a tooth off when tension is applied to the drive side. What should the technician do?

answers.text: Recheck the installation with slack taken up on the tension side as specified, and correct sprocket positioning before final assembly
Accept the error because half a tooth does not matter
Rotate the engine backward to hide the error
File the timing marks to align

questions.explanation: Timing must be judged with the drive side taut, as it runs. A half-tooth error under proper tension is a real timing error that retards or advances every valve event. The sprockets are repositioned per the procedure and rechecked before covers go on.

questions.question: A block inspection finds a crack running from a water jacket opening toward a cylinder bore. Dye penetrant confirms it is open. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.text: Evaluate the block for approved crack repair or replace it — do not return it to service as-is
Cover the crack with formed-in-place sealant during assembly
Peen the crack closed and reinstall the head
Ignore it because water jacket cracks do not affect compression

questions.explanation: An open crack between a water jacket and a bore will leak coolant into the cylinder and grow under thermal cycling. Sealant on an internal crack and peening do not restore structural integrity.

questions.question: A bore shows vertical scoring deep enough to catch a fingernail, extending through the ring travel area. What is the most likely correct service?

answers.text: Polish the score with emery cloth and reuse the piston
Deglaze with a flex hone and install standard rings
Install a thicker oil ring to bridge the score
Bore and hone to the next oversize (or sleeve) — deglazing will not remove deep scoring

questions.explanation: Scoring that catches a nail is too deep for a deglazing hone, which removes only surface glaze. Leaving it gives oil and blow-by a direct path past the rings.

questions.question: Technician A says crankshaft journals should be measured with a micrometer in several positions. Technician B says plastigage alone tells journal size, taper and out-of-round. Who is correct?

answers.text: Both Technician A and Technician B
Neither Technician A nor Technician B
Technician A only
Technician B only

questions.explanation: Only a micrometer on the journal reveals size, taper and out-of-round. Plastigage shows installed bearing clearance at one spot; it cannot measure the journal itself, so Technician B overstates it.

questions.question: An engine shakes noticeably at idle in gear. Spark, compression and power balance are all even, the mounts are sound, and the tachometer shows idle at 550 rpm against a specification given as 700 to 800 rpm. Raising the idle to 750 rpm with the scan tool makes the shake disappear. The cause of the vibration is:

answers.text: A hidden misfire that only a road test can reveal
Worn engine mounts that pass a visual inspection
An idle speed well below specification, too slow for the engine to run smoothly under load
An unbalanced torque converter that smooths out at 750 rpm

questions.explanation: The comparison is decisive: 550 rpm measured against a 700 to 800 rpm specification. At that low speed, especially loaded in gear, power pulses are far apart and the engine shakes; restoring specified idle speed removes the vibration, so the idle control fault is corrected, not the mounts.

questions.question: On a relative compression scope pattern, the current humps are even except that the hump for cylinder 5 is about 40% lower than the rest. A gauge test then shows cylinder 5 at 100 psi versus 175 psi elsewhere. Technician A says the scope test alone identified which cylinder was low. Technician B says the scope test alone measures the exact psi in that cylinder. Who is correct?

answers.text: Technician A only
Technician B only
Both Technician A and Technician B
Neither Technician A nor Technician B

questions.explanation: Relative compression compares cylinders to each other, so it correctly flags cylinder 5 as low, which the gauge confirmed at 100 versus 175 psi. It does not measure absolute pressure; a gauge is still needed for the actual psi value. Technician B overstates the method.

questions.question: A vehicle returns twice for a coolant drip at the water pump area. The pump, gasket and bolts test good on the bench. Careful inspection finds a hairline crack in the front cover boss that one pump bolt threads into, weeping coolant beside the bolt. The repeat failure occurred because:

answers.text: Water pumps always leak twice before sealing
The actual leak source was in the mounting structure, not in the pump that was replaced
The coolant was the wrong color for the pump gasket
The pump bolts needed to be installed dry with no cleaning

questions.explanation: Coolant weeping from a cracked boss beside a bolt imitates a pump gasket leak. Replacing the pump cannot cure a leak whose source is the cover itself, which is why verifying the exact origin before parts replacement matters.

ase-a2-automatic-transmission.quiz_title: ASE A2 — Automatic Transmission/Transaxle Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A hybrid transaxle contains MG1 and MG2. The primary role of MG1 in many power-split designs is to:

answers.text: Serve as the parking pawl actuator
Drive the mechanical oil pump only
Act mainly as a generator and engine starter controlled to manage engine speed
Replace the final drive differential

questions.explanation: In power-split systems MG1 largely generates power, starts the engine, and controls engine operating point. It does not replace the differential, which still distributes torque to the wheels.

questions.question: Why does the controller compare commanded gear ratio to the ratio calculated from speed sensors?

answers.text: To set tire size automatically
To control the instrument cluster only
To adjust radio volume with speed
To detect incorrect gear ratio and slipping elements by seeing if the achieved ratio matches the command

questions.explanation: Ratio monitoring proves execution: if input and output speeds do not produce the commanded ratio, a gear or friction element is not holding. The strongest distractor B is wrong because the cluster merely displays information and is not the purpose of the ratio calculation.

questions.question: Governor pressure on a hydraulically controlled unit should relate to road speed in which way?

answers.text: It is highest at a standstill and falls with speed
It rises in proportion to output shaft/road speed and works against throttle pressure to time upshifts
It stays fixed at mainline pressure at all speeds
It changes only when the driver selects Reverse

questions.explanation: Governor pressure is generated by output-speed-driven weights/valve and increases with speed to push shift valves up. Highest at standstill is the exact reverse of the relationship and would prevent any normal upshift logic.

questions.question: Why is accumulator condition checked with the hydraulic pressure fully relieved before measuring gas precharge?

answers.text: The procedure is a formality with no effect on readings
Hydraulic pressure on the fluid side compresses the gas and would make a precharge reading falsely high and the check unsafe
The gauge only works at zero vehicle speed
Precharge changes with transmission temperature only

questions.explanation: Fluid-side pressure adds to gas compression, inflating the reading and storing hazardous energy. 'No effect' is the strongest distractor — skipping the relief step is both a measurement error and a safety hazard.

questions.question: A control system uses both feed-forward scheduling and feedback adaptation. In concept, what does each contribute?

answers.text: Both terms mean the same thing
Feed-forward scheduling picks shift points and pressures from current inputs and calibration tables; feedback adaptation corrects those choices over time based on measured results
Feed-forward repairs worn parts; feedback replaces fluid
Feedback chooses the gear; feed-forward chooses the gear ratio

questions.explanation: Tables decide in the moment; measured outcomes refine the tables' application over time. 'Same thing' is the strongest distractor — the distinction between deciding and learning from results is the core concept.

questions.question: Which visual inspection item directly relates to a complaint of vibration at highway speed that changes in Drive versus Neutral coast?

answers.text: Color of the shift knob
Condition of mounts, axles/CV joints, and driveline angles
Length of the dipstick
Type of pan bolts

questions.explanation: Mounts and driveline components influence vibration under load versus coast. Dipstick length has no effect on highway vibration.

questions.question: A single DMM reading of 0.0 volt on a solenoid control wire with the key on and the solenoid commanded ON by the scan tool most directly suggests:

answers.text: The solenoid is mechanically stuck in all cases
The control circuit is being pulled to ground/command path is active, or power is absent — the reading must be paired with a feed-side voltage check to separate the two
The transmission fluid is low
The battery is fully charged

questions.explanation: A zero reading alone is ambiguous between an active ground-side command and no power; checking the feed separates them. It does not by itself prove a mechanical stick or fluid level.

questions.question: A pressure tap test during a harsh shift event shows a sharp pressure spike in the element circuit at the moment of harshness. What does the spike prove?

answers.text: The harshness is caused by abrupt hydraulic apply, not by friction material grabbing alone
The gauge is defective whenever it spikes
Pressure spikes soften shifts
The element is slipping continuously

questions.explanation: A spike synchronized with the harsh event is direct evidence the apply was hydraulic and abrupt — accumulator, orifice, or valve control is at fault. The strongest distractor D would show low or falling pressure with flare, not a spike.

questions.question: A scan tool shows TCC duty cycle commanded at 95% and slip at 10 rpm on a level cruise, and no codes. How should this be reported?

answers.text: The TCC is slipping severely because duty is not 100%
Slip of 10 rpm means the clutch has failed
Lockup is applying and holding correctly — high command with near-zero slip is a pass
The converter must be replaced for preventive reasons

questions.explanation: 95% command with 10 rpm slip is controlled, essentially locked operation on a modulated system. Reading any duty below 100% as failure is wrong — modulated systems intentionally command less than full duty while holding slip near zero.

questions.question: A diagnostic flow chart for 'no movement in any range' lists fluid level and condition as the first check. Why is this step placed before pressure testing?

answers.text: Pressure gauges cannot be installed until fluid is drained
The pump cannot turn unless the chart is followed in order
Fluid inspection resets the transmission control module
Low or burnt fluid can cause loss of drive and invalidate pressure readings

questions.explanation: Checking fluid first is correct because a low level starves the pump so any later pressure reading would be misleading. Pressure testing first is the strongest distractor, but installing a gauge on a unit that is simply two quarts low wastes time and risks pump damage.

questions.question: Slip at full lockup measures 60 rpm. The specification allows up to 30 rpm. By what factor is slip over the limit, and what is the verdict?

answers.text: Within limits, because 60 is a small number
The limit does not apply at full lockup
2× the limit (60 ÷ 30); the clutch fails the slip test and needs apply-circuit and lining diagnosis
Half the limit; it passes

questions.explanation: 60 ÷ 30 = 2, so slip is double the allowance — a clear fail. 'Small number, passes' is the strongest distractor; specifications, not impressions of size, decide the verdict.

questions.question: A transmission temperature sensor circuit has a short to ground on the signal wire. On a negative temperature coefficient system, the module will interpret this as what?

answers.text: Extremely cold fluid, because shorts always read as opens
Normal temperature, because the module ignores shorts
A vehicle speed fault, because temperature and speed share a wire
Extremely hot fluid, because the short drives signal resistance and voltage low, the hot end of the sensor curve

questions.explanation: Low resistance equals hot on an NTC curve, and a ground short forces the lowest possible signal. Reading it as cold confuses a short's low resistance with an open's high resistance.

questions.question: A technician finds two procedures: a generic video and the OEM service information for the exact unit. For torque values and fluid type, priority goes to:

answers.text: The generic video
Social media comments
The OEM service information for that exact unit
The oldest forum post

questions.explanation: OEM data is unit-specific and authoritative for specs. A generic video may cover a different variant, making it risky for specs.

questions.question: Stall speed is 600 rpm above specification and the vehicle launches weakly, but highway cruise is normal once moving. What is most likely?

answers.text: A stuck closed thermostat
A slipping forward element or low apply pressure at launch
A locked torque converter clutch at launch
Correct stall for a performance converter in all cases

questions.explanation: High stall means the engine revs against an element that is not holding — a slipping forward clutch or low apply pressure — while cruise can feel normal once another element carries load. The strongest distractor C is wrong because a locked converter clutch at launch would stall or kill the engine, not raise stall speed.

questions.question: Converter stall is normal, launch is strong, but a scope/pressure review shows converter temperature climbing steadily at sustained 65 mph. Engine and cooler tests are pending. Which converter fault remains the prime suspect and why?

answers.text: A stator that will not freewheel — it is the only stator mode that leaves stall/launch normal while generating excess heat at speed
A stator freewheeling both ways, because it overheats at launch
Low line pressure inside the converter shell
A worn converter clutch that is not commanded on yet

questions.explanation: Symptom timing is the discriminator: normal stall excludes the freewheel fault; heat building specifically at sustained speed matches a stator obstructing flow past coupling. The freewheel distractor would have announced itself at every stop-light launch.
