questions.question: Using velocity in feet per second = 0.408 x flow in gallons per minute / (diameter in inches) squared, what is the velocity of 200 gallons per minute flowing in a 4-inch pipe, in feet per second?
questions.explanation: Velocity = 0.408 x 200 / (4 x 4) = 5.1 feet per second.

questions.question: A Kentucky plumbing permit for a building other than a one-family residence has a base fee of $50 plus $20 for each counted item. The job has 4 counted items and no other charges. What is the permit fee, in dollars?
questions.explanation: Fee = 50 + 20 x 4 = 130 dollars.

questions.question: A test gauge reads 60 pounds per square inch. Using 2.31 feet of head per pound per square inch, what head of water does that pressure equal, in feet?

tennessee-cmc-a-plumbing-gas-piping.quiz_title: Tennessee CMC-A (Plumbing and Gas Piping) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures the Tennessee contractor licensing threshold?

answers.text: A Tennessee contractor license is required only on public works projects
A Tennessee contractor license is required for a project whose total cost is twenty-five thousand dollars or more
Subcontractors never need a Tennessee contractor license because the prime is licensed
A Tennessee contractor license is required for every plumbing job of any size

questions.explanation: Twenty-five thousand dollars of total project cost is the line between the limited license world and the contractor license world.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the Limited Licensed Plumber license?

answers.text: CMC-A is a Tennessee certificate for apprentice plumbers
The Limited Licensed Plumber is an individual Tennessee license for plumbing work with a total cost under twenty-five thousand dollars in jurisdictions where the state handles permits or inspections
The Limited Licensed Plumber license is a business license issued to corporations
The Limited Licensed Plumber license is the first rung toward a Tennessee master license

questions.explanation: The LLP is a small-job individual license, not a contractor license and not a step on a grade ladder Tennessee does not have.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding slope for large drainage piping?

answers.text: Horizontal drainage piping of eight inches and larger is graded at not less than one-sixteenth inch per foot
Large drainage piping requires no slope because of its size
Large drainage piping is graded at one inch per foot
Large drainage piping is graded at one-quarter inch per foot minimum

questions.explanation: The largest drains need only a sixteenth-inch grade; oversloping wastes elevation and can outrun the liquid.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about the building drain.

answers.text: The building drain is the water service line entering the building
The building drain is the vent terminal through the roof
The building drain is the vertical pipe above the highest fixture
The building drain is the lowest horizontal drainage piping that receives discharge from waste and soil stacks and conveys it to the building sewer

questions.explanation: Drain language is positional: the building drain sits at the bottom of the system inside the building.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the small maintenance exemption?

answers.text: All repair work of any size is exempt from Tennessee plumbing licensing
The trade examination is an oral interview before the Board
General maintenance plumbing work under five hundred dollars is exempt from the Limited Licensed Plumber requirement
The qualifying agent must be an officer of the Board

questions.explanation: The exemption is narrow: small general maintenance only, not installations or larger repairs.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who licenses Tennessee plumbing contractors?

answers.text: Each Tennessee county licenses plumbing contractors with no state license at all
Plumbing contractors in Tennessee are licensed by the Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors in the Department of Commerce and Insurance
A private contractors association issues Tennessee plumbing contractor licenses
Tennessee plumbers are licensed by the plumbing examiners of the largest city in the county

questions.explanation: The Board for Licensing Contractors is the state licensing authority for contractor licenses, including the plumbing classification.

questions.question: A trainee asks about whether Tennessee has a master plumber license. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Tennessee has no statewide master plumber or journeyman plumber license; it licenses plumbing by project value through a limited license below the threshold and a contractor license at or above it
Tennessee issues a journeyman license after two years and a master license after five
Tennessee master plumbers are licensed by the State Fire Marshal
Tennessee licenses master plumbers who may then supervise licensed journeymen statewide

questions.explanation: The absence of a master/journeyman ladder is the defining feature of the Tennessee scheme: value, not grade, decides which license the work needs.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how what total cost includes in Tennessee is handled in practice.

answers.text: Tennessee has no adopted fuel gas code
Total cost excludes materials the owner buys directly
Total cost can be split across separate contracts to stay under the threshold
Total cost means the whole value of the work - labor, materials, equipment, subcontracted work, overhead, and profit - no matter who pays for each part or how many contracts cover the job

questions.explanation: The aggregate definition closes the splitting loophole: separate contracts and owner-purchased materials still count toward the threshold.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the scope of CMC-A plumbing work is handled in practice.

answers.text: A CMC-A contractor may install, repair, alter, remodel, or remove plumbing systems including water supply, waste, and storm drainage systems
A CMC-A contractor may perform only residential drain cleaning
Tennessee issues a journeyman license after two years and a master license after five
The Limited Licensed Plumber license authorizes contracting on projects of any size

questions.explanation: The classification covers the whole plumbing system - supply, waste, and storm - across residential, commercial, and industrial occupancies.

questions.question: How would an experienced Tennessee plumbing contractor best explain the full mechanical CMC classification?

answers.text: The Limited Licensed Plumber must also pass Business and Law
The full CMC covers plumbing only and excludes HVAC work
The full CMC is issued without any examination
The full CMC classification covers all mechanical contracting work - plumbing, HVAC, process piping, sprinklers, boilers, and the other mechanical categories - under one classification

questions.explanation: CMC is the umbrella mechanical classification; CMC-A is its plumbing and gas piping branch.

questions.question: How would an experienced Tennessee plumbing contractor best explain the purpose of drainage slope?

answers.text: Horizontal drainage piping is sloped so gravity moves waste and solids toward the sewer; slope is expressed in inches of fall per foot of run
A combination fitting is a type of trap
Drainage slope exists to increase water pressure at fixtures
A private water closet is rated at ten drainage fixture units

questions.explanation: Slope is the engine of a gravity system: too little strands solids, and the code fixes minimum grades by pipe size.

questions.question: A trainee asks about limited Licensed Plumber experience. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: A Limited Licensed Plumber applicant must show one year of verified plumbing experience
Examinations are offered only in Nashville on Board meeting days
A Limited Licensed Plumber applicant needs no experience at all
A Limited Licensed Plumber applicant must first hold a contractor license

questions.explanation: One verified year supports the limited license; the contractor classification examination demands three.

questions.question: When checking work against the adopted plumbing code, which statement about what the CMC-A classification means is right?

answers.text: CMC-A is the Plumbing and Gas Piping classification under Tennessee Mechanical Contracting, held on a contractor license
CMC-A is a county journeyman card recognized across Tennessee
CMC-A is a federal mechanical contractor registration
CMC-A is a Tennessee certificate for apprentice plumbers

questions.explanation: The letters name a classification on a state contractor license - the credential is the contractor license itself.

questions.question: Which of these statements about gas piping inside the CMC-A scope would a Tennessee plumbing inspector agree with?

answers.text: The trade examination fee is two hundred fifty dollars
CMC-A excludes all fuel gas piping, which needs a separate state license in every case
The Business and Law examination is built on the International Plumbing Code
CMC-A includes non-medical gas piping, including gas piping to water heaters, laundry and kitchen equipment, pool heaters, and gas logs

questions.explanation: Plumbing-related fuel gas work rides inside CMC-A; medical gas is a separate certified specialty outside it.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers who the contractor license is issued to. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: The Tennessee contractor license is issued to the business entity - sole proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, or corporation - in its exact business name
The license is issued to the project owner for the duration of the job
The license is issued jointly to the contractor and its bonding company
The license is issued to the individual qualifying agent as personal property

questions.explanation: Entity licensure is why a name change, a new entity, or a departing qualifying agent has licensing consequences.

questions.question: On a commercial service call in Tennessee, the topic of the qualifying agent comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The qualifying agent is an owner or a full-time employee of the entity who passes the required examinations for the license
The qualifying agent may be any licensed plumber hired for a single day to sit the exam
Medical gas piping is included in CMC-A with no extra credential
The license is issued to the project owner for the duration of the job

questions.explanation: The agent ties examination competence to the licensed business; the tie must be a genuine ownership or full-time employment link.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers slope for small drainage piping. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Horizontal drainage piping of two and one-half inches and smaller is graded at not less than one-quarter inch per foot
Small drainage piping may be graded back toward the fixture
Small drainage piping is graded at one inch per foot
A horizontal branch carries water supply to fixtures

questions.explanation: Small pipes need the steeper quarter-inch grade to keep solids suspended and moving.

questions.question: For safe, code-compliant Tennessee plumbing practice, which statement about the subcontractor licensing rule in Tennessee holds true?

answers.text: A plumbing subcontractor must hold a contractor license when its own portion of a project reaches twenty-five thousand dollars or more, counting materials, equipment, and labor
A subcontractor is covered automatically by the owner's building permit
Subcontractors never need a Tennessee contractor license because the prime is licensed
A subcontractor needs a license only when its portion exceeds one hundred thousand dollars

questions.explanation: The threshold follows the money at every tier: a large plumbing package needs a licensed plumbing contractor even under a licensed prime.

questions.question: A qualifying agent asks a project manager, the topic of slope for mid-size drainage piping comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Mid-size drainage piping is graded at two inches per foot
Horizontal drainage piping from three to six inches is graded at not less than one-eighth inch per foot
Mid-size drainage piping may be installed perfectly level
Mid-size drainage piping is graded at one-half inch per foot minimum

questions.explanation: Bigger waterways carry solids at the shallower eighth-inch grade - the classic IPC step-down.

questions.question: With gallons figured as 0.0408 times diameter in inches squared times length in feet, find the gallons standing in a 4-inch pipe 30 feet long.

minnesota-master-plumber.quiz_title: Minnesota Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who licenses Minnesota plumbers?

answers.text: Minnesota plumbers are licensed by the Department of Health
Plumbers in Minnesota are licensed by the Department of Labor and Industry, whose Construction Codes and Licensing Division administers the program
Each Minnesota city licenses its own plumbers with no state license
A private plumbing association issues Minnesota plumber licenses

questions.explanation: The Department of Labor and Industry is the state licensing authority for every class of Minnesota plumber.

questions.question: Which statement best captures whether electronic supervision counts?

answers.text: Results are posted publicly the same day
Video supervision counts if the camera feed is recorded
Electronic or remote supervision does not satisfy Minnesota's direct supervision requirement
The applicant certifies his or her own experience alone

questions.explanation: The rule is explicit that a screen is not supervision - the licensed plumber must be there.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to building drain basics. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Any pressure elbow may turn a drain
The building drain is the yard pipe between the house and the street main
The building drain is the lowest horizontal drainage piping inside the building that receives the discharge of soil, waste, and other drainage pipes and conveys it to the building sewer
The building drain is the vertical stack in a tall building

questions.explanation: Inside and lowest is the building drain; the yard run beyond the building is the building sewer.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes grades for larger drainage?

answers.text: Larger pipe needs steeper grade than smaller pipe
Large drainage may be installed dead level if it is oversized
Small drainage is graded at one inch per foot as a minimum

Larger drainage piping may run at the flatter grades the adopted tables allow - an eighth inch per foot at mid sizes and a sixteenth at large sizes - because a larger pipe carries its load at a shallower pitch

questions.explanation: Diameter buys flatness within the table's limits; it never buys a level drain.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about where a master plumber may work.

answers.text: A master license must be reissued by each city over five thousand people
A Minnesota master plumber license authorizes plumbing work statewide, inside buildings and outside to the water service, sanitary sewer, and storm sewer within the property lines
A master license is valid only in the county where it was issued
A master license covers interior work only, never yard piping

questions.explanation: The personal license travels statewide; it is the restricted licenses and contractor licenses that carry the population limits.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about the business-of-plumbing rule. Which statement should the master confirm?

answers.text: Licensed plumbers need no continuing education in Minnesota

No one may engage in the business of planning, superintending, or installing plumbing in Minnesota unless a licensed master plumber responsible for proper installation is in charge of the work at all times
A Minnesota master plumber may design plumbing but never install it
Any experienced journeyworker may run a plumbing business alone

questions.explanation: A master in charge at all times is the condition of doing plumbing business in Minnesota, whatever the job size.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who may perform plumbing work in Minnesota?

answers.text: Homeowners' employees may do commercial plumbing with no registration

Plumbing work requires a person who is at least eighteen, licensed or registered with the department or enrolled in a registered apprenticeship, and working as a W-2 employee of a licensed contractor or registered employer, or as a licensed owner or officer
Out-of-state licenses alone authorize plumbing work in Minnesota
The applicant certifies his or her own experience alone

questions.explanation: Age, status with the department, and the employment link must all line up before the work is lawful.

questions.question: A trainee asks about direct supervision in Minnesota. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Direct supervision means the supervising licensed plumber is physically present at the work location, immediately available for direction, and reviews the unlicensed worker's plumbing before it is operated
Direct supervision may be done by video call from another state
Direct supervision means the supervisor signs the paperwork at week's end
Both examinations are worth one hundred points

questions.explanation: Presence is physical in Minnesota: on site, available, and reviewing the work before it goes live.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the registered unlicensed plumber is handled in practice.

answers.text: A registered unlicensed plumber is a registered worker who performs plumbing for a contractor or employer without holding a plumber license, always under direct supervision
A master license covers interior work only, never yard piping
Minnesota recognizes no out-of-state master licenses for any purpose
A registered unlicensed plumber is licensed to contract for small jobs

questions.explanation: Registration is the entry status, not a license - it authorizes supervised work only.

questions.question: Which description of the purpose of a drainage system matches accepted Minnesota practice?

answers.text: A drainage system returns wastewater to the water supply for reuse
A drainage system carries wastewater and water-borne waste away from fixtures by gravity to the building drain and building sewer, keeping sewer gas out of occupied space
Trap shape has no effect on the seal
A drainage system exists mainly to vent steam from water heaters

questions.explanation: Gravity, fixture by fixture, to the sewer - with traps and vents keeping the gas on the drainage side.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about drainage fixture units earns credit?

answers.text: A cleanout may be concreted over once inspected
Drainage fixture units measure the water pressure at a fixture
Replaced drains need no test if the old one did not leak
Drainage fixture units measure the probable discharge load of fixtures so drain and vent piping can be sized from the adopted tables

questions.explanation: Load, not pressure: fixture units turn a building full of fixtures into pipe sizes.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how building sewer basics is handled in practice.

answers.text: The building sewer is inside the building under the slab
The building sewer begins outside the building and carries drainage from the building drain to the public sewer or other disposal point
Larger pipe needs steeper grade than smaller pipe
The building sewer is the water service pipe in the same trench

questions.explanation: The handoff at the building line separates drain from sewer, and the rules for each follow the pipe.

questions.question: A master plumber asks a journeyworker, the topic of the Minnesota license ladder comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Minnesota's ladder is helper, then contractor, then inspector
Minnesota has only a single plumber license with no grades
Minnesota licenses apprentices directly as master plumbers after one examination
Minnesota's ladder runs from registered unlicensed plumber, to journeyworker plumber, to master plumber, with a separate contractor license for the business

questions.explanation: Grade, registration, and business licensure are three distinct pieces of the Minnesota scheme.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about registering as an unlicensed plumber. Which statement should the master confirm?

answers.text: A worker may register after the first year of plumbing work
Registration is handled by the local union hall
A worker must register with the department and pay the fourteen dollar initial application fee before working as a registered unlicensed plumber
Registration is free and automatic when a contractor hires the worker

questions.explanation: No registration, no lawful unlicensed work - the fourteen dollars comes before the first hour.

questions.question: Which of these statements about drainage grades for small pipe would a Minnesota plumbing inspector agree with?

answers.text: Small horizontal drainage piping is graded at a quarter inch per foot so solids are carried along by the flow
Small drainage is graded at one inch per foot as a minimum
Small drainage slopes upward toward the stack
Trap seals never evaporate

questions.explanation: A quarter inch per foot keeps small drains self-scouring instead of settling.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers why excessive drainage slope hurts. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Drainage is sized by the number of fittings alone
Excessive slope lets liquid outrun solids, leaving waste behind to foul the line, so drainage grade is a band and not a race to steepness
An inch-and-a-half trap arm may run twelve feet
Steeper is always better in drainage design

questions.explanation: Grade is tuned: too flat settles, too steep strands - the code's slopes sit between the failures.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the role of the Minnesota Plumbing Board. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Restricted masters are barred from the full master examination
The Plumbing Board personally grades every licensing examination
The Minnesota Plumbing Board adopts and amends the Plumbing Code and the licensing rules and issues final interpretations of the code
The Plumbing Board sells plumbing permits for every Minnesota city

questions.explanation: Rule-writing and interpretation sit with the Board; day-to-day licensing administration sits with the department.

questions.question: When checking work against the Minnesota plumbing code, which statement about what a Minnesota master plumber is is right?

answers.text: A Minnesota master plumber is a retired journeyworker with an honorary title
One year of any construction work opens the journeyworker examination
The master examination is worth one thousand points
A Minnesota master plumber is skilled in the planning, superintending, and practical installation of plumbing and is qualified to contract for plumbing work and conduct the business of plumbing

questions.explanation: Planning and superintending join hands-on installation in the master definition - the master runs work, not just tools.

questions.question: A master plumber asks a journeyworker, the topic of common drainage fixture unit values comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Fixture units are assigned by the installing plumber's judgment

Under the adopted UPC-based code a lavatory counts one drainage fixture unit, a bathtub or shower two, a kitchen sink two, a service sink three, and a private water closet three while a public water closet counts four
A lavatory counts four units and a water closet counts one
Every fixture counts exactly two units regardless of type

questions.explanation: The small fixtures count small and the water closets count large - the table, not opinion, assigns the load.

questions.question: When checking work against the Minnesota plumbing code, which statement about who may supervise an unlicensed worker is right?

answers.text: An unlicensed worker may be supervised only by a licensed journeyworker or master plumber employed by the same employer
Any licensed plumber in the state may supervise any unlicensed worker
A licensed electrician may supervise plumbing apprentices
The property owner may supervise unlicensed plumbing workers

questions.explanation: Supervision runs inside the employment relationship: same employer, licensed supervisor, at all times.

new-jersey-master-plumber.quiz_title: New Jersey Licensed Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the code that governs New Jersey drainage design?

answers.text: New Jersey designs drainage to the Uniform Plumbing Code
New Jersey designs drainage to the International Plumbing Code
Each New Jersey town adopts its own drainage code
New Jersey drainage, waste, and vent work is designed to the National Standard Plumbing Code as adopted by the state plumbing subcode — not to the IPC or the UPC

questions.explanation: NSPC is the state's code family — the first distinction a New Jersey candidate must hold.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the New Jersey trap-arm length for three-inch pipe?

answers.text: Six feet is where three-inch arms must stop and vent
A dozen feet is the three-inch maximum in the state table
Vents are pitched toward the roof terminal
The three-inch row of the table tops out at 10 feet, weir to vent, before the arm overruns its vent

questions.explanation: Ten feet at three inches under the New Jersey table.

questions.question: Regarding why crown venting is prohibited in New Jersey, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Crown venting is the preferred method for tubs
A crown vent — a vent taken off the top of the trap's crown — is prohibited because waste flowing over the crown fouls and chokes the vent opening
Crown vents are required on all lavatories
Crown vents are prohibited because they are expensive

questions.explanation: The crown is where the waste stream rides highest; a vent opened there drinks waste instead of air.

questions.question: Which statement best captures common venting of paired fixtures?

answers.text: A common vent requires no vent pipe at all
A common vent serves two fixtures set back to back or side by side whose trap arms join at a shared fitting below one vent
A common vent serves fixtures on different floors
Any number of fixtures may share one common vent

questions.explanation: Two fixtures, one vent, one junction — the paired-bathroom workhorse.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to counting fixtures from a riser diagram. Which point is correct?

answers.text: On a riser diagram, every fixture symbol connected to the stack counts toward that stack's load, including fixtures on floors the drawing compresses
Each floor's fixtures are counted once per building, not per stack
Fixtures shown dashed are never counted
Pitch is whatever the note beside the pipe says, without checking

questions.explanation: The stack carries what connects to it — floor by floor, fixture by fixture.

questions.question: A trainee asks about the minimum pitch of small horizontal drainage in New Jersey. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Small drainage may be pitched one-sixteenth inch per foot
Pitch is optional on drainage shorter than ten feet
Horizontal drainage piping of 3 inches and smaller is pitched at least one-quarter inch per foot in the direction of flow
Small drainage is pitched one inch per foot as a minimum

questions.explanation: Quarter inch per foot at the small sizes: enough grade to keep solids moving with the water.

questions.question: Regarding the New Jersey trap-arm length for inch-and-a-half pipe, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: For inch-and-a-half work the limit is 5 feet, figured from the weir of the trap to where the vent takes off
Inch-and-a-half arms are allowed 8 feet in the New Jersey table
New Jersey lets a 1-1/4 inch arm reach a full 5 feet before venting
The building sewer is the piping inside the basement only

questions.explanation: Five feet at inch-and-a-half — the most common lavatory and tub arm in the field.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about the New Jersey trap-arm length for four-inch pipe earns credit?

answers.text: At four inches the table grants its longest reach: 12 feet from the fixture's trap to the vent connection
Twenty feet is allowed at four inches because the bore is generous
The four-inch maximum matches the two-inch maximum of eight feet
Four-inch arms are limited to ten feet like their smaller neighbors

questions.explanation: Twelve feet at four inches — the top of the New Jersey trap-arm ladder.

questions.question: Which description of what protects a trap seal from siphonage matches accepted New Jersey practice?

answers.text: A deeper trap alone prevents all siphonage
Nothing prevents siphonage in a tall building
Siphonage is prevented by oversizing the drain
A properly located vent connection breaks the siphon by admitting air behind the discharge, holding the trap seal at its level

questions.explanation: The vent, placed within its length limit, is the seal's bodyguard.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about individual venting in a New Jersey system earns credit?

answers.text: An individual vent serves one fixture's trap and rises to join a vent stack or terminate outdoors above the roof
Pitch is optional on drainage shorter than ten feet
An individual vent connects below the trap
An individual vent terminates under the floor

questions.explanation: One trap, one vent path to open air — the basic unit of vent design.

questions.question: Which description of what the Practical examination actually tests matches accepted New Jersey practice?

answers.text: The Practical part is an essay on plumbing history
The Practical part retests the Business and Law topics
Legends repeat the title block only
The Practical part tests whether the candidate can read a plumbing drawing — isometric and figure analysis — and extract sizes, lengths, and fixture counts from it accurately

questions.explanation: Reading is the skill: the drawing holds the answers, and the questions audit the reading.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how reading a fixture symbol against the schedule is handled in practice.

answers.text: Symbols are identified by their size on paper
As-builts are informal and unreliable by definition
The schedule lists only architectural finishes
A symbol is confirmed against the drawing's fixture schedule, because the same rough shape can stand for different fixtures in different sets of drawings

questions.explanation: The schedule is the drawing's dictionary — read the symbol through it.

questions.question: A new apprentice needs to understand pitch for larger drainage sizes in New Jersey. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: Two-inch arms stop at five feet under the state table
Larger drainage requires a half inch per foot minimum
Larger drainage sizes take the smaller grades the NSPC slope table allows — an eighth inch per foot at the larger sizes — and are never back-pitched against the flow
Each New Jersey town adopts its own drainage code

questions.explanation: Bigger pipe carries its load on less grade — the table steps down, never to zero or backwards.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about the New Jersey trap-arm length for two-inch pipe. Which statement should the master confirm?

answers.text: Every stack in a building must be 4 inches by rule
An AAV may be buried in a sealed wall anywhere
Two-inch arms stop at five feet under the state table
Two-inch arms are capped at 8 feet of developed distance between the trap and the vent fitting

questions.explanation: Eight feet at two inches — measured weir to vent, at the arm's proper grade.

questions.question: On a New Jersey plumbing jobsite, the topic of how a trap arm is measured in New Jersey comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Trap-arm length is measured to the center of the building drain
Trap-arm length is measured from the trap weir to the vent connection, along the arm at its required grade
Trap-arm length includes the vertical vent riser above the connection
Two-inch arms stop at five feet under the state table

questions.explanation: Weir to vent: the two points that decide whether the trap keeps its seal.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about the job of the vent system in New Jersey practice. Which statement should the master confirm?

answers.text: The vent system admits and circulates air so drainage flows without siphoning or blowing trap seals, and sewer gas is carried safely above the roof
Vents exist to let sewer gas into the attic for dilution
Vents are a decorative code formality
The vent system pressurizes the drainage to speed flow

questions.explanation: Air in, gas out, seals intact: the vent is the drainage system's lungs.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers what an isometric drawing shows a plumber. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Invert elevations describe water pressure
An isometric replaces the need for a floor plan entirely
An isometric drawing shows a piping system in three dimensions on one sheet, so runs, rises, drops, and fittings can be followed and measured as the system will actually be built
An isometric is a parts price list

questions.explanation: One sheet, three dimensions: the isometric is the system's portrait before it is its photograph.

questions.question: When checking work against the National Standard Plumbing Code, which statement about the New Jersey trap-arm length for inch-and-a-quarter pipe is right?

answers.text: Developed length matters only for water piping
Under the New Jersey NSPC trap-arm table, a 1-1/4 inch trap arm may run at most 2 feet 6 inches from trap weir to vent
The allowance for a 1-1/4 inch arm stretches to 3 feet 6 inches in New Jersey
Each New Jersey town adopts its own drainage code

questions.explanation: Two feet six — the New Jersey figure that differs from the UPC ladder used in other states.

questions.question: When checking work against the National Standard Plumbing Code, which statement about the two-diameter rule at the vent connection is right?

answers.text: The vent must sit at least ten diameters from the weir
Vent position relative to the weir is unregulated
The vent connection must sit at least two pipe diameters downstream from the trap weir, so discharge turbulence cannot wash across the vent opening
The vent may connect exactly at the trap weir

questions.explanation: Two diameters of calm pipe between the weir and the vent — a small distance with a large job.

questions.question: A licensed master plumber asks a registered journeyman, the topic of the first move in reading a figure on the exam comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Start by guessing the most common pipe size
Start from the roof terminal and work down for every question
Start by reading every note on the sheet first
Start by finding the fixture or section the question asks about, then trace its drain and vent paths completely before looking at the answer choices

questions.explanation: Locate, trace, then choose — answers picked before the trace are guesses wearing confidence.

alabama-master-plumber.quiz_title: Alabama Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who certifies Alabama master plumbers?

answers.text: A national plumbing institute issues Alabama master certificates
Master plumbers in Alabama are certified by the State of Alabama Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board
Master plumbers in Alabama are certified by the state contractors board for general construction
Each Alabama county certifies its own master plumbers

questions.explanation: One state examining board certifies every Alabama master plumber.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the Alabama master plumber defined?

answers.text: Master status is earned by owning a plumbing business for five years
A master plumber is defined solely by passing a practical piping test

A master plumber is a person or legal entity that engages in the actual installation, repair, or replacement of plumbing systems, has passed the board's examinations, and holds a valid current annual certificate
Candidates learn results only at renewal time

questions.explanation: Examination, issuance, and a current annual certificate — all three make the master.

questions.question: Which statement best captures master eligibility in Alabama?

answers.text: Any journeyman may sit the master exam immediately after passing
Master eligibility requires five years as a journeyman
Master eligibility is based on business ownership, not journeyman time
A master plumber applicant must show verifiable proof of one year of current work experience as a journeyman plumber

questions.explanation: One current, verifiable journeyman year stands between the two examinations.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the drainage slope for large pipe in Alabama?

answers.text: Large drainage slopes are left to the installer
Wet venting applies only to roof drains
Large drainage is laid dead level by design
Drainage pipe 8 inches and larger may be pitched as flat as one-sixteenth inch per foot

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about what Alabama calls its plumbing credential.

answers.text: Alabama issues only a single plumbing license with endorsements
Alabama issues certificates — apprentice registration, journeyman certification, and master certification — rather than licenses in the board's own terminology
Alabama calls every credential a permit
The board issues charters instead of certificates

questions.explanation: Certificate is the board's word at every rung of the ladder.

questions.question: A trainee asks about where the Alabama examining board sits. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The examining board's office is in Homewood, Alabama, and it examines, certifies, and regulates plumbers on a statewide basis
The board is a private trade association with an office in Birmingham
Each large city hosts its own examining board office
The board sits in Montgomery and regulates only state buildings

questions.explanation: Homewood hosts the board that regulates the trade statewide.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes whether the Alabama certificate works statewide?

answers.text: The certificate works statewide except in home-rule cities
An Alabama plumbing certificate is valid statewide and must be accepted by every city, town, and county
Large cities may refuse to honor the state certificate
The trade examination is 75 questions in 2 hours, closed book

questions.explanation: One certificate, every jurisdiction in the state.

questions.question: On an Alabama plumbing jobsite, the topic of carrying the Alabama certificate comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Only masters must carry a certificate; journeymen need not
The window is one year from the trade examination date
A photocopy at the shop satisfies the carry rule for apprentices
Every Alabama certificate holder must carry the current annual certificate and produce it for inspection on request

questions.explanation: The current certificate rides with the holder and comes out on request.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the Alabama journeyman plumber defined is handled in practice.

answers.text: A journeyman plumber engages in the actual installation, repair, or replacement of plumbing systems, has passed the board's examination for that level, and holds a valid current annual certificate
Military applicants are exempt from all examinations forever
A journeyman is an apprentice in the final training year
A business license from a city substitutes for the state certificate

questions.explanation: The journeyman is an examined, certificated rung — not a seniority title.

questions.question: How would an experienced Alabama master plumber best explain how an Alabama apprentice qualifies upward?

answers.text: Apprentice registration requires a practical soldering test
Calculators are banned entirely from the plumbing examinations
The apprentice examination is the same paper as the journeyman paper
An apprentice registers with the board without taking any written examination; the first examination in the ladder comes at the journeyman level

questions.explanation: No exam at registration — examinations begin at journeyman.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers journeyman eligibility in Alabama. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A journeyman applicant must show verifiable proof of two years of current work experience as an apprentice plumber, or completion of a board-approved apprentice training program
Journeyman eligibility requires a high school diploma and no experience
Five years as an apprentice are required before the journeyman exam
One year of any construction work qualifies a journeyman applicant

questions.explanation: Two documented apprentice years, or the approved program — verified, either way.

questions.question: Which description of the drainage slope for small pipe in Alabama matches accepted Alabama practice?

answers.text: Small drainage may be laid level if the run is short
Horizontal drainage of 2½ inches and smaller is pitched at one-quarter inch per foot under the plumbing code Alabama examinations use
Small drainage is pitched at one inch per foot
Floor drains need no traps in mechanical rooms

questions.explanation: A quarter inch per foot carries small drainage — flatter invites stoppage.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers local competency examinations in Alabama. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Master status is earned by owning a plumbing business for five years
Cities may add a harder local master examination
The trade examination is an oral board interview
No Alabama city or county may require its own competency examination for plumbing; competency certification belongs to the state board alone

questions.explanation: Local permits and inspections remain local; competency testing does not.

questions.question: Which of these statements about the Alabama apprentice plumber defined would an Alabama plumbing inspector agree with?

answers.text: An apprentice is any unregistered helper on a plumbing crew
All master fees together total $100
Business and law must be passed separately for each master certificate

An apprentice plumber is a person learning and assisting in installation who works directly under the supervision of a journeyman or master plumber and is registered with the board for the current year

questions.explanation: Registered, learning, and directly supervised — that is the apprentice.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the drainage slope for mid-size pipe in Alabama. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Drainage pipe from 3 to 6 inches is pitched at one-eighth inch per foot
Washer traps are 1¼ inches for all machines
Mid-size drainage has no minimum slope
Six-inch drainage is pitched at one-quarter inch per foot

questions.explanation: An eighth per foot is the mid-size standard.

questions.question: When checking work against the 2021 International Plumbing Code, which statement about why drainage pitch has a floor and a ceiling is right?

answers.text: Steeper is always better for every drainage line
Correct pitch keeps liquid and solids moving together; too flat strands solids, and grossly excessive pitch on small lines can outrun the solids the water must carry
Every fixture in a dwelling counts exactly 1 unit
Scuppers may discharge onto the sanitary vent

questions.explanation: Slope is a balance — the code numbers sit where flow carries its load.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the Alabama trap-arm distance for inch-and-a-quarter traps is handled in practice.

answers.text: Ten feet of reach is granted to the smallest trap arm in the table
Five feet is the longest run the IPC table allows a 1¼-inch trap arm at a quarter inch per foot, measured from the trap weir to the vent
Floor drains carry no drainage load value
Arms of that diameter are limited to the same reach as a four-inch arm

questions.explanation: Five feet — the IPC figure, longer than the NSPC and UPC figures in neighboring banks.

questions.question: A certified master plumber asks a journeyman, the topic of the statute behind Alabama plumbing certification comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: No statute governs Alabama plumbing; local custom controls
Certification rests on the state building code alone
A federal statute certifies Alabama plumbers
Alabama plumbing certification rests on the plumbers and gas fitters chapter of the state code's professions title, carried out through the board's administrative rules

questions.explanation: A professions statute plus the board's own rules — the building code governs work, the statute governs the certificate holder.

questions.question: Three straight sections measuring 10 feet, 6 feet, and 4 feet form one run in an Alabama building. What is the run's developed length, in feet?
questions.explanation: Developed length = 10 + 6 + 4 = 20 feet.

questions.question: Three straight sections measuring 14 feet, 9 feet, and 5 feet form one run in an Alabama building. What is the run's developed length, in feet?
questions.explanation: Developed length = 14 + 9 + 5 = 28 feet.

utah-master-plumber.quiz_title: Utah Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who licenses Utah master plumbers?

answers.text: Utah master plumbers are licensed by the state contractors board alone with no division involvement
Master plumbers in Utah are licensed by the Division of Professional Licensing in the Utah Department of Commerce
Each Utah county licenses its own master plumbers
A national plumbing board issues the Utah master license

questions.explanation: One state division in the Department of Commerce licenses every Utah master plumber.

questions.question: Which description of the Utah apprentice plumber matches accepted Utah practice?

Apprentice licensing requires the hands-on practical examination
An apprentice is an unregistered helper with no division record
The paper is entirely plumbing code doctrine and sizing

questions.explanation: Licensed, supervised, and documented — that is the Utah apprentice.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the governing drainage code in Utah?

answers.text: Utah uses the National Standard Plumbing Code
Utah drainage follows the Uniform Plumbing Code statewide
Each Utah city writes its own drainage code from scratch
Utah drainage work follows the International Plumbing Code as adopted into the State Construction Code with Utah amendments

questions.question: Which statement best captures grade for mid-size Utah drainage lines?

Mid-size lines fall one-half inch per foot
Mid-size lines may be laid dead level
Drainage piping from 3 to 6 inches is laid at a fall of one-eighth inch in every foot
