questions.question: A trainee asks about the Board office address. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The State Plumbing Board office is at 1560 Broadway, Suite 1350, in Denver, Colorado.
The Board office is at 525 West Jefferson Street in Springfield.
The Board keeps its only office inside the State Capitol basement.
The Board office is in Colorado Springs at 1560 Broadway.

questions.explanation: The Board sits with the Division at 1560 Broadway, Suite 1350, Denver — the address where the adopted codes are also open for public inspection.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about the journeyworker name change.

answers.text: Colorado abolished the middle grade in 2025 and kept only residential and master.

Colorado renamed the middle grade from journeyman plumber to journeyworker plumber throughout the plumbing law, effective July 1, 2025; older Board and testing documents may still print the old word for the same credential.
The name changed to journeyman senior, effective January 1, 2020.
The middle grade was renamed master assistant effective July 1, 2025.

questions.explanation: Journeyworker is the current statutory name; a document saying journeyman describes the same license.

questions.question: Which description of the journeyworker plumber definition matches accepted Colorado practice?

answers.text: A journeyworker plumber is a licensed plumber, other than a master, residential plumber, or apprentice, who engages in the actual installation, alteration, repair, and renovation of plumbing under the Board's standards and rules.
Endorsement is automatic for anyone holding any plumbing license anywhere.
A journeyworker plumber is an apprentice who has registered for a second year.
The master examination has 100 scored items and 240 minutes.

questions.explanation: The journeyworker is the full-scope working grade below the master: installation, alteration, repair, and renovation.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about the master plumber definition earns credit?

answers.text: A master plumber is a residential plumber with two extra years of any work.
A master plumber is simply any plumber who owns a plumbing business.

A master plumber has the qualifications, training, experience, and technical knowledge to properly plan, lay out, and install and repair plumbing apparatus and equipment, including supervising that work, under the Board's standards and rules.
A master plumber title is honorary and is granted after twenty years without an exam.

questions.explanation: Planning, laying out, installing, repairing, and supervising — that full span is what makes the grade a master.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how residential plumber experience requirement is handled in practice.

answers.text: A residential plumber applicant must verify two years, or 3,400 hours, of practical plumbing experience.
The tutorial is scored and counts toward the pass standard.
A residential plumber applicant needs five years, or 8,500 hours, of experience.
Examinations are offered in English and Spanish at every center.

questions.explanation: Two years and 3,400 hours is the first rung — half the journeyworker figure and well under the master figure.

questions.question: Which description of master plumber experience requirement matches accepted Colorado practice?

answers.text: A master plumber applicant needs 9,780 hours computed from sixty months at 163 hours.
A master plumber applicant must furnish evidence of five full-time years, or 8,500 hours, of practical plumbing experience.
A master plumber applicant needs four years, or 6,800 hours, of experience.
A master plumber applicant needs two years of experience after the journeyworker exam only.

questions.explanation: Five full-time years and 8,500 published hours is the master standard; the 9,780 figure is a secondary-source error the Board does not publish.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the 163-hour month. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Colorado counts one month of full-time plumbing experience as equivalent to 163 hours when experience is measured in months.
Colorado refuses to convert months to hours under any circumstance.
Colorado counts one month of full-time experience as 200 hours.
Colorado counts one month of full-time experience as 100 hours.

questions.explanation: 163 hours is the Board's month — a conversion for measuring experience, not a way to recompute the published grade totals.

questions.question: Which description of the job of the drainage system matches accepted Colorado practice?

answers.text: The drainage system treats wastewater to drinking quality inside the building.

The sanitary drainage system collects wastewater and waterborne waste from fixtures and conveys it by gravity to the building drain, building sewer, and the public sewer or an approved private disposal system.
A 2-inch trap arm may run 20 feet without a vent.
The drainage system pressurizes waste so it can flow uphill without slope.

questions.explanation: Drainage is a gravity conveyor to an approved disposal point — slope and venting make it work.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how why drainage slope matters is handled in practice.

answers.text: Steeper is always better, so drains should be pitched as sharply as possible.

Proper slope keeps the liquid stream moving at a self-scouring pace that carries solids along; too little slope lets solids settle, and excessive slope can let liquid outrun solids and leave them behind.
One air admittance valve can replace the entire vent system of a building.
Slope is a cosmetic concern handled by the finish grade of the floor.

questions.explanation: Grade is a balance — scour without separation is the goal on every horizontal run.

questions.question: For safe, code-compliant Colorado plumbing practice, which statement about the residential plumber scope holds true?

answers.text: A Colorado residential plumber installs plumbing and equipment in one-, two-, three-, and four-family dwellings that do not extend more than two stories aboveground.
A residential plumber may install plumbing in any building up to six stories.
A residential plumber is limited to single-family dwellings of one story only.
A residential plumber may supervise commercial work if a master signs the permit.

questions.explanation: The residential license is a dwelling license: one- to four-family, no more than two stories above ground.

questions.question: When checking work against the Colorado Plumbing Code, which statement about who must hold a license to do plumbing work is right?

answers.text: A person may not engage in or work at the trade of a residential, journeyworker, or master plumber in Colorado until licensed by the Division or holding a Board temporary permit; everyone else in the trade works as a registered apprentice under supervision.
Only business owners need licenses; employees may work unlicensed indefinitely.
A license is needed only for new construction, never for repair work.
Anyone may do plumbing work in Colorado if a licensed plumber inspects it afterward.

questions.explanation: Licensure (or a temporary permit) comes before the work, not after it.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about journeyworker plumber experience requirement. Which statement should the master plumber confirm?

answers.text: The journeyworker license requires two years, or 3,400 hours, like the residential license.
The journeyworker license requires five full-time years, or 8,500 hours.
The maximum experience the Board requires for a journeyworker license is four years, or 6,800 hours, of practical experience.
The journeyworker license requires ten years, or 17,000 hours, of experience.

questions.explanation: Four years and 6,800 hours caps the journeyworker requirement — the Board's own word for it is maximum.

questions.question: On a commercial service call in Colorado, the topic of the affidavit of experience comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Examination applicants verify their plumbing installation experience with an Affidavit of Experience form submitted from current and former employers who are plumbing contractors.
Incomplete applications are retained for five years at no charge.
Military plumbing service counts month-for-month without any cap.
Applicants verify experience with a notarized statement they write and sign themselves.

questions.explanation: The affidavit comes from the employing contractors — the people who supervised the work being claimed.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers minimum slope for small horizontal drains. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Horizontal drainage piping of 2 inches and smaller must be installed with a uniform slope of not less than one-quarter inch per foot toward the direction of flow.
Small drains may slope back toward the fixture if a trap is installed.
Small drains require one inch of slope per foot to stay clean.
The building sewer is any pipe the owner calls a sewer, regardless of location.

questions.explanation: A quarter inch per foot is the floor for small drains — enough velocity to carry solids without outrunning the liquid.

questions.question: A licensed Colorado master plumber asks a journeyworker, the topic of slope for a four-inch building drain comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A 4-inch drain must be installed dead level to slow the flow.
A 4-inch horizontal building drain may be installed at a slope of one-eighth inch per foot, the standard grade for mid-size drainage piping.
A 4-inch drain must slope one-half inch per foot in all cases.
A 4-inch drain requires two inches of slope per foot.

questions.explanation: Mid-size drains run at an eighth inch per foot; larger diameter carries the load at a gentler grade.

questions.question: A licensed Colorado master plumber asks a journeyworker, the topic of the purpose of the plumbing practice law comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The law declares plumbing an unregulated trade that anyone may enter freely.
The law's stated purpose is to keep plumbing wages uniform across Colorado.
The law exists mainly to collect registration fees for the general fund.

Colorado's plumbing law declares that improper plumbing can harm public health and that faulty plumbing is potentially lethal, so plumbing must be installed by people who have proven their knowledge of pneumatics and hydraulics and their skill in installing plumbing.

questions.explanation: The legislative declaration is a public-health declaration: proven knowledge and skill are the price of installing plumbing.

questions.question: A Colorado tempering mix blends 32 gallons at 132 degrees F with 24 gallons at 54 degrees F. Find the resulting temperature in degrees F.

maryland-master-plumber-gas-fitter.quiz_title: Maryland Master Plumber/Gas Fitter Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the Maryland journey time a master applicant must already hold?

answers.text: No minimum journey holding period applies to master applicants.
A Maryland master applicant must have held the journey plumber license for at least two years before qualifying for the master grade.
One year of journey licensure is enough for the master grade.
The master grade requires five years holding the journey license.

questions.explanation: Two journey years is the published holding floor for the master grade.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the out-of-state master's post-journey certification?

answers.text: Out-of-state applicants need no post-journey hours at all.
An applicant whose experience was earned outside Maryland also certifies at least two years including at least 3,750 hours of plumbing trade work after being licensed as a journey plumber.
The out-of-state post-journey leg may precede the journey license.
The master and journey outlines are identical in every area.

questions.explanation: Two years and 3,750 hours after the journey license — the second leg of the outside track.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the Maryland master examination's item count and time?

answers.text: The master examination carries 80 questions in 180 minutes.
The master examination is an untimed practical only.
The Master Plumber/Gas Fitter examination carries 100 questions with 240 minutes allowed — the same size and clock as the journey paper.
Passing the master examination issues the license automatically.

questions.explanation: 100 items, 240 minutes — master and journey papers share the format.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the one master-outline area the journey paper lacks?

answers.text: The master and journey outlines are identical in every area.
The master outline adds a second mathematics area.
The master outline adds a practical pipe-threading area.
The master outline adds a Special Topics area of three items that the journey outline does not carry — the only content area unique to the master paper.

questions.explanation: Special Topics, three items — the master paper's signature addition.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the master's response to a back-graded building drain?

answers.text: A building drain found back-graded is rejected on the master's review and re-laid to grade before cover — a directing master does not sign off on reverse fall.
Back-graded drains are noted and left for the owner.
A back grade corrects itself once flow begins.
A back grade is acceptable if the drain is oversized.

questions.explanation: Re-lay it. Reverse fall is a reject, never a sign-off.

questions.question: A journey licensee asks about the journey hours a Maryland master applicant must document. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The master applicant documents at least 3,750 hours of training as a licensed journey plumber under the direction and control of a licensed master plumber.
Only 1,875 journey hours are required for the master grade.
Journey hours for the master grade may be earned under any journey licensee.
The master applicant needs 7,500 fresh hours earned after the journey license.

questions.explanation: 3,750 journey hours under a master — half the apprentice total, at the higher grade.

questions.question: A pre-job briefing turns to the backflow course every Maryland master examination applicant files. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Every master examination applicant must submit a non-expired, approved 32-hour course in backflow prevention device testing — the same examination-applicant rule that governs the journey paper.
An expired backflow certificate is accepted for master applicants.
A 16-hour backflow refresher replaces the 32-hour course for masters.
Gas carries 55 items on the master outline.

questions.explanation: Non-expired and approved, 32 hours — for every examination applicant, master included.

questions.question: A journey licensee asks about the verification letter for the 11,250 out-of-state hours. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The out-of-state master applicant files an original letter of verification that all 11,250 required hours were worked under a licensed master whose own license was obtained by passing a written competency examination.
The letter need not address how the supervising master was licensed.
A study guide may be used during the master tutorial.
The verification letter may come from the applicant's office manager.

questions.explanation: Original letter, full 11,250 hours, supervising master licensed by written examination.

questions.question: For safe, code-compliant Maryland master practice, which statement about the master examination's book rule holds true?

answers.text: The master examination is open book: candidates bring their own unmarked code and reference books under the same rules as the journey paper.
Natural gas fitter credentials are grades of the plumbing inspector card.
Master candidates may bring any book including study guides.
The testing center lends master candidates a shared set of books.

questions.explanation: Open book at both grades — bring your own, unmarked, no study guides.

questions.question: How would an experienced Maryland master plumber best explain the references a Maryland master candidate brings?

answers.text: Master candidates may substitute a manufacturer's catalog for the fuel gas code.
Master candidates need no mathematics reference.
The newest book on the shelf wins any conflict on the master paper.

The master candidate's shelf mirrors the journey shelf: the 2018 plumbing code, the 2018 fuel gas code, a plumbing mathematics text, any standard backflow text, and the federal construction safety standards.

questions.explanation: Same published shelf at both grades — the master paper tests deeper use of it.

questions.question: How would an experienced Maryland master plumber best explain the master's drainage design duty before rough-in?

answers.text: The directing master verifies the drainage design — sizes, grades, venting, and cleanout access — before rough-in begins, because corrections after concealment fall on the master's license.
Double trapping is preferred for floor drains.
Indirect waste applies only to chemical fixtures.
Design verification happens at final inspection only.

questions.explanation: The master designs and checks first; the crew builds to the checked design.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the Maryland vent stack a master must recognize on plans is handled at master level.

answers.text: Grease is the health department's problem, not the design's.

In Maryland a vent stack is a pressure-relief device at the base of an individual drain stack serving five or more branch intervals — the master reads the term with the Maryland meaning, not the generic one.
The Maryland vent stack definition matches the generic vent-pipe meaning exactly.
Maryland abolished vent stacks in its code.

questions.explanation: Five or more branch intervals, pressure relief at the base — Maryland's own definition.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the combined career hours behind a Maryland master application is handled at master level.

answers.text: The journey leg adds nothing to the combined career total.
The combined total behind the master grade is 10,000 hours.
Insurance certificates go to the testing center's address.
The full Maryland route to the master grade totals 11,250 supervised hours: 7,500 apprentice hours plus 3,750 journey hours, each leg under a licensed master.

questions.explanation: 7,500 plus 3,750 equals 11,250 — the career total the master file documents.

questions.question: For safe, code-compliant Maryland master practice, which statement about the out-of-state master's pre-journey certification holds true?

answers.text: An applicant whose experience was earned outside Maryland files an original certification of at least four years and at least 7,500 hours under a licensed master before being licensed as a journey plumber.
The out-of-state pre-journey leg is 3,750 hours over two years.
Out-of-state applicants skip the pre-journey hours entirely.
Out-of-state applicants file a photocopy of their home license instead of hour certifications.

questions.explanation: The outside-Maryland track re-proves the whole ladder, starting with the 7,500-hour leg.

questions.question: On the master written examination, a question covers the tab rule on a master candidate's books. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Only permanent self-adhesive plastic tabs may mark a master candidate's books; removable flags are unacceptable and any tab a proctor can lift without tearing the page comes off.
Loose paper inserts may tab the master candidate's code book.
Tabs of any kind are banned on the master examination.
Paper flags are preferred on the master paper.

questions.explanation: Permanent tabs only — the rule does not soften at the master grade.

questions.question: On the master written examination, a question covers grade for smaller drainage piping the master lays out. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Drainage piping two and one-half inches and smaller is laid out at one-quarter inch of fall per foot so solids move with the liquid stream.
Smaller drainage is laid out at one inch per foot for speed.
Grade for small drainage is whatever the trench allows.
Existing drains are assumed adequate for any added load.

questions.explanation: Quarter-inch per foot for the small sizes — the master's layout standard.

questions.question: Which of these statements about vacuum breakers at hose connections, the master's measurement would a Maryland plumbing inspector agree with?

answers.text: Hose-attachment vacuum breakers sit at least six inches above the highest point of usage, on the discharge side of the last valve — the master measures both the height and the position.
Position relative to the last valve does not matter.
Hazard degree is a paperwork distinction.
Six inches is measured from the floor.

questions.explanation: Six inches above the highest usage, downstream of the last valve.

questions.question: A directing master needs the crew to understand whose direction the master applicant's journey hours run under. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: The 3,750 journey hours must be worked under the direction and control of a licensed master plumber — the directing grade the applicant is preparing to join.
The hours may run under a limited journey licensee.
Tabs of any kind are banned on the master examination.
Master applicants are excused from the backflow course.

questions.explanation: Journey hours count only under a licensed master's direction and control.

questions.question: On a Maryland commercial jobsite the master is directing, the topic of the experienced-master track for Baltimore County and WSSC holders comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Local-system holders need only the 32-hour backflow course to become state masters.
The limited master may direct any plumbing work statewide.
The local track waives all hour certifications.

A Baltimore County or WSSC journey holder applying toward the master paper certifies 7,500 hours under a master licensed by written examination plus 3,750 hours worked as a licensed master over two years since receiving the home master license.

questions.explanation: The local track is an experienced-master track: both hour legs are certified, not waived.

questions.question: A Maryland journey licensee asks the directing master, the topic of grade for mid-size drainage piping the master lays out comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Mid-size drainage grade is set by the fixture count alone.
Mid-size drainage piping in the three-to-eight-inch range is laid out at one-eighth inch of fall per foot under the adopted drainage table.
Mid-size drainage may be laid back-graded toward fixtures.
Mid-size drainage requires one-half inch per foot.

questions.explanation: Eighth-inch per foot for the mid sizes — checked on the master's grade layout.

arkansas-master-plumber.quiz_title: Arkansas Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures who an Arkansas apprentice plumber is registered under?

answers.text: Gas sizing uses a branch-length-only guess.
An Arkansas apprentice plumber is registered under an Arkansas master plumber and enrolled in the apprentice plumber training program provided in state law.
An apprentice is registered under the building owner.
An apprentice registers directly with a test vendor and needs no master.

questions.explanation: Registered under an Arkansas master and enrolled in the training program — both elements.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the hardship exception to the Arkansas one-year holding rule?

answers.text: Waiver documentation is never checked.
The one-year rule is waived whenever the fee is doubled.
In cases of extreme hardship, the Committee of Plumbing Examiners may waive the one-year journeyman holding requirement in whole or in part.
Any employer letter automatically waives the one-year rule.

questions.explanation: Extreme hardship only, Committee's call, in whole or in part.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes what an isometric DWV riser diagram shows a master reviewer?

answers.text: An isometric shows only the building's front elevation.
An isometric hides pipe sizes by design.
An isometric is a materials price list in drawing form.

An isometric riser diagram shows the drainage and vent piping in three-dimensional relationship — stacks, branches, vents, and fixture connections — so sizes, slopes, and vent paths can be checked from one drawing.

questions.explanation: One drawing, whole system in relief — the master's review tool.

questions.question: Which statement best captures what a size-change notation on a riser tells the installer?

answers.text: Fixture units are a billing device.
Notations mark only the stack base.
Notations record the pipe's color.
A size-change notation marks exactly where the piping changes diameter along the run, so the installer orders and sets the right fittings at the right point.

questions.explanation: The notation is the instruction: here the diameter changes.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about the professional-engineer route to the Arkansas master examination.

answers.text: Any engineer qualifies without plumbing expertise.
The Committee may consider applicants for the master plumber examination who are registered professional engineers with special expertise in plumbing engineering.
Engineers receive the master license without Committee consideration.
Candidates receive all four sections at once and choose the order.

questions.explanation: Registered professional engineer plus plumbing-engineering expertise — a consideration route, not an automatic license.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes what an Arkansas master plumber is, in the rules' own substance?

answers.text: An Arkansas master plumber is any journeyman with ten years on a crew.
An Arkansas master plumber is a person skilled in the planning, superintending, and practical installation of plumbing who is familiar with the laws and rules governing the same.
An Arkansas master plumber is defined only by passing the drawing section.
An Arkansas master plumber is a contractor licensed by the Contractors Licensing Board.

questions.explanation: Planning, superintending, and practical installation, plus knowledge of the governing laws and rules.

questions.question: A journeyman asks about how an Arkansas journeyman plumber differs from a master. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: An Arkansas journeyman plumber is any person other than a master plumber who is engaged in the practical installation of plumbing.
A journeyman is an apprentice in the fourth year of training.
A journeyman is a master who has not yet paid the license fee.
A journeyman in Arkansas plans and superintends all work independently by definition.

questions.explanation: Journeyman: practical installation, other than a master — the grade below the superintending master.

questions.question: How would an experienced Arkansas master plumber best explain the minimum experience for the Arkansas master examination?

answers.text: The master examination requires two years of experience.
The master examination requires ten years of experience.
No minimum experience applies to the master examination.
An applicant for the Arkansas master plumber examination must have a minimum of five years of plumbing experience.

questions.explanation: Five years minimum for master — one more than the journeyman floor.

questions.question: Which description of what a current Arkansas journeyman files for experience proof matches accepted Arkansas master practice?

answers.text: A current journeyman files no work history at all.
A current Arkansas journeyman applying for the master examination need only provide work history for the length of their journeymanship.
A current journeyman files only a photograph of the license.
A current journeyman must re-prove all five years from the first apprentice day.

questions.explanation: Journeymanship-length history suffices for the in-state journeyman — the earlier record already stands.

questions.question: A journeyman asks about why the Arkansas drawing separates vents and drains by color. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Colors replace the need for size notations.
Colors are decorative and carry no meaning.
Coloring vents blue and drains red lets the grader — and later the crew — follow each system's path through the riser without confusing a vent for a drain at a shared stack.
Red marks vents and blue marks drains.

questions.explanation: Blue vent, red drain: two systems, instantly separable on the page.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the minimum fall for small horizontal drainage piping is handled at master level.

answers.text: Candidates draw any building they prefer.
Horizontal drainage piping of two and one-half inches and smaller is laid at a minimum fall of one-quarter inch per foot under the adopted plumbing code.
Small drainage falls one-sixteenth inch per foot.
Small drainage falls one inch per foot minimum.

questions.explanation: Quarter-inch per foot for the small sizes — the classic drainage grade.

questions.question: Regarding the section that administers Arkansas plumber licensing day to day, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: An Arkansas master plumber is a contractor licensed by the Contractors Licensing Board.
A journeyman is a master who has not yet paid the license fee.
The Plumbing and Natural Gas Section of the Arkansas Department of Health is the Department for plumbing licensing: it administers the law, holds the examinations, and issues the licenses.
A private vendor administers Arkansas plumber licensing.

questions.explanation: Plumbing and Natural Gas Section, Department of Health — administrator, examiner, and issuer.

questions.question: An experienced journeyman is unsure about the committee that decides Arkansas examination eligibility. Which statement should the master confirm?

answers.text: Only a nickname and email are required.
The Committee of Plumbing Examiners — persons designated by the State Board of Health — determines the eligibility of applicants for the various plumbing and gas licenses.
Section 3 tests water heater branding.
The governor personally decides each applicant's eligibility.

questions.explanation: The designated Committee decides eligibility — fees alone never qualify an applicant.

questions.question: On the master examination, a question covers the minimum experience for the Arkansas journeyman examination. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Gas sizing uses the shortest-run method.
The journeyman examination requires one year of experience.
There is no December sitting in 2026.
An applicant for the Arkansas journeyman plumber examination must have a minimum of four years of experience or its equivalent.

questions.explanation: Four years or equivalent for journeyman; five for master.

questions.question: Which of these statements about how an Arkansas master applicant proves the five years would an Arkansas plumbing inspector agree with?

answers.text: The master examination requires two years of experience.
Experience is proven by an oral claim at the test center.
The journeyman examination has no experience floor.

Experience is proven with documentation submitted with the application: records, affidavits, bona fide evidence from licensing agencies, or qualified former employers who can attest to the work background.

questions.explanation: Paper proof travels with the application — records, affidavits, agency or employer evidence.

questions.question: On the master examination, a question covers what an out-of-state Arkansas master applicant adds. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: An out-of-state application must include a completed Verification of License Form or its equivalent, alongside the experience documentation.
Out-of-state applicants file only a resume.
Out-of-state applicants skip license verification.
Out-of-state verification is handled after licensure.

questions.explanation: Verification of the home license is part of the out-of-state file, not an afterthought.

questions.question: When signing off work against the Arkansas codes, which statement about the slope a master checks first on a horizontal drain in the drawing is right?

answers.text: Drainage slope is optional if the pipe is oversized.

A master reviewing the riser checks that horizontal drainage is drawn to fall at the code grade for its size — drainage moves by gravity, and a flat or back-pitched run in the drawing becomes a clogged run in the wall.
The stack vent supplies combustion air.
Size changes mark where pipe was cheapest.

questions.explanation: Gravity is the pump: the drawing's fall is the system's future performance.

questions.question: On an Arkansas commercial jobsite the master is superintending, the topic of the journeyman holding year before the Arkansas master examination comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The holding period before the master examination is three full years.
No holding period separates the journeyman and master examinations.
Exams are sat online from home.
A person who obtains an Arkansas Journeyman Plumber License must hold that license for one full year before becoming eligible for the master plumber examination.

questions.explanation: One full year licensed as a journeyman stands between the two examinations.

questions.question: On a commercial service call under an Arkansas master, the topic of the affidavit rule for an unlicensed Arkansas applicant comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An applicant who is not enrolled in the Arkansas apprenticeship program files affidavits from current or former employers attesting to the plumbing and gas fitting background — notarized and on company letterhead — and only legal work history is considered.
The master license is free after the first year.
Unnotarized notes from coworkers prove an unlicensed applicant's history.
Candidates may work two sections simultaneously.

questions.explanation: Notarized, on letterhead, legal history only — the unlicensed route is documented, not casual.

questions.question: At 0.0408 gallons per inch of diameter squared per foot of run, how many gallons fill a 4-inch Arkansas pipe 16 feet long?

uscg-lifeboatman.quiz_title: USCG Lifeboatman Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How would an experienced boat commander best explain form of the lifeboat credential?

answers.text: Only an engineer may be placed in command of a motor lifeboat.
Only mariners sailing from their home state are exempt from a state lifeboat license.
The lifeboat credential is a national endorsement placed on the Merchant Mariner Credential.
The lifeboat credential is a separate wallet card issued apart from the Merchant Mariner Credential.

questions.explanation: The endorsement lives on the mariner's Merchant Mariner Credential rather than standing alone.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes former title of the limited endorsement?

answers.text: An approved course can never count toward the examination requirement.
Lifeboat Operator-Limited is the current name for the endorsement formerly called Lifeboatman-Limited.
Lifeboat Operator-Limited has always carried exactly that printed title.
Lifeboat Operator-Limited was formerly called Lifeboatman Second Class.

questions.explanation: The limited endorsement also changed its printed name while keeping its limited scope.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to core charge of the lifeboat operator. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Each coastal state issues its own lifeboat license alongside the federal endorsement.
The Lifeboat Operator is in charge of a survival craft or rescue boat during and after launch.
Fast rescue boats are the only craft covered by this STCW endorsement.
The Lifeboat Operator is in charge only while the craft remains secured in its davits.

questions.explanation: Charge begins with the launch and continues after the craft is away.

questions.question: Which statement best captures general rule for unrigged vessels?

answers.text: Unrigged vessels require the full endorsement from every deck hand aboard.
Every person on an unrigged vessel must hold a lifeboat endorsement.
The unrigged vessel rule was removed and no longer applies to anyone.
As a general rule, no lifeboat endorsement is required of a person employed on an unrigged vessel.

questions.explanation: Unrigged vessels are the general exception to the endorsement requirement.

questions.question: Regarding former title of the full endorsement, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A union hall issues the lifeboat endorsement to its members.
Only the master may ever be placed in command of a lifeboat.
Lifeboat Operator is the current name for the endorsement formerly called Lifeboatman.
Lifeboat Operator is the current name for an endorsement formerly called Coxswain.

questions.explanation: The work did not change when the printed title changed from Lifeboatman to Lifeboat Operator.

questions.question: A trainee asks about everyday name still used for the endorsement. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Mariners and industry still commonly call the Lifeboat Operator endorsement lifeboatman in everyday speech.
Using the word lifeboatman now refers to a completely different rating.
Certificated persons are assigned to boats only to complete paperwork after drills.
Only retired mariners are permitted to use the word lifeboatman.

questions.explanation: The old word remains the familiar spoken name even though the printed title changed.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how vessels that call for the limited endorsement is handled in practice.

answers.text: Lifeboat Operator-Limited serves vessels that are fitted with liferafts but are not fitted with lifeboats.
Lifeboat Operator-Limited serves vessels that carry lifeboats but no liferafts.
A seagoing barge is the one vessel type that never needs any certificated person.
The lifeboat qualification is an optional add-on that Able Seaman applicants may skip.

questions.explanation: The limited scope follows the vessel's outfit, which has rafts and no lifeboats.

questions.question: Which description of limited holder charge of a liferaft matches accepted survival-craft practice?

answers.text: A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder takes charge of a liferaft only after it is recovered.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may take charge of a liferaft.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may watch a liferaft but never take charge of one.
Liferaft charge belongs only to the full Lifeboat Operator endorsement.

questions.explanation: Taking charge of a liferaft is central to the limited role.

questions.question: In a credentialing review, which statement about limited holder charge of other apparatus earns credit?

answers.text: Other lifesaving apparatus may be handled only by unlicensed crew members.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may touch no apparatus beyond a single named raft.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may take charge of other lifesaving apparatus besides a rescue boat or liferaft.
The current printed title of the full national endorsement is Able Lifeboatman.

questions.explanation: The limited charge extends to other lifesaving apparatus, not just rafts and rescue boats.

questions.question: How would an experienced boat commander best explain minimum age for the lifeboat family?

answers.text: The minimum age is 18 for Lifeboat Operator, Lifeboat Operator-Limited, Proficiency in Survival Craft, and Proficiency in Survival Craft-Limited.
Once the demonstration ended, all oar and sail questions left the written exam.
The minimum age is 16 for the limited endorsement and 21 for the full endorsement.
Ability is proved by a supervisor's letter while knowledge needs no proof.

questions.explanation: One age floor of 18 covers all four endorsements in the family.

questions.question: In a credentialing review, which statement about prescribed medical examination earns credit?

answers.text: Assessments are graded purely on the assessor's overall impression.
An applicant may self-certify fitness without any medical examination.
The transitional route was extended indefinitely by the National Maritime Center.
An applicant must pass the prescribed physical and medical examination for the endorsement.

questions.explanation: Medical fitness is examined, not assumed, before issuance.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how drug test timing and first endorsement is handled in practice.

answers.text: Taking charge is demonstrated only by a written essay about leadership.
Drug testing compliance must fall within 6 months, and the test is required for the first Lifeboat Operator endorsement unless the applicant is also renewing.
A mariner renewing nothing still never needs drug test evidence for a first endorsement.
The drug test is required only at the second renewal of the endorsement.

questions.explanation: Fresh compliance within 6 months is what the first endorsement calls for.

questions.question: A boat commander briefs the boat crew, the topic of no state lifeboat license comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Each coastal state issues its own lifeboat license alongside the federal endorsement.
A mariner needs a state license before the federal endorsement can be added.
Only mariners sailing from their home state are exempt from a state lifeboat license.
No state license is required to hold the federal lifeboat endorsement.

questions.explanation: Credentialing for this rating is entirely federal.

questions.question: For safe, compliant survival-craft practice, which statement about current printed title for the limited endorsement holds true?

answers.text: The current printed title of the limited national endorsement is Lifeboat Operator-Limited.
The current printed title of the limited national endorsement is Lifeboat Operator-Junior.
The current printed title of the limited national endorsement is Liferaft Operator.
The current printed title of the limited national endorsement is Survival Craft Attendant.

questions.explanation: The limited member of the family is printed as Lifeboat Operator-Limited.

questions.question: A crew member is unsure about limited holder charge of a rescue boat. Which statement should the boat commander confirm?

answers.text: A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may take charge only of the ship's workboat in port.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder takes charge of a rescue boat only on inland lakes.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may take charge of a rescue boat.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may never take charge of any boat of any kind.

questions.explanation: Rescue boat charge sits squarely inside the limited endorsement.

questions.question: A boat commander briefs the boat crew, the topic of valid medical certificate held comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An expired Medical Certificate is acceptable if renewal papers were mailed.
An applicant must hold a valid Medical Certificate when qualifying for the endorsement.
The Medical Certificate is needed only after the endorsement is issued.
A first aid card substitutes for the Medical Certificate.

questions.explanation: A current Medical Certificate is part of a complete application.

questions.question: When checking boat work against the lifeboat requirements, which statement about evidence of a passed drug test is right?

answers.text: A letter from an employer saying the applicant seems reliable replaces the drug test.
An applicant must provide evidence of having passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs or of qualifying for an exemption from that test.
The first topic area covers radio watchkeeping procedures.
STCW assessments may be signed by any shipmate who watched the task.

questions.explanation: Passed test evidence, or a genuine exemption, is the standard.

questions.question: When checking boat work against the lifeboat requirements, which statement about current printed title for the full endorsement is right?

answers.text: The current printed title of the full national endorsement is Boatswain.
The lifeboat qualification is an optional add-on that Able Seaman applicants may skip.
Survival craft refers to the mother ship after an abandonment.
The current printed title of the full national endorsement is Lifeboat Operator.

questions.explanation: Lifeboat Operator is the title now printed for the full endorsement.

questions.question: At the boat station during an abandon-ship drill, the topic of what the lifeboat operator fulfils aboard comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A Lifeboat Operator is the shore inspector who certifies the vessel's boats.
A raft-only vessel must still man every raft with a full Lifeboat Operator.
A Lifeboat Operator is any crew member who has once ridden in a lifeboat.
A Lifeboat Operator is the person who fulfils the manning requirement as lifeboat operator aboard the vessel.

questions.explanation: The endorsement exists because the vessel's manning calls for a qualified person in that role.

questions.question: Lifeboat falls were last turned end-for-end 7 months ago and the interval is 30 months. In how many months are they due again?
questions.explanation: Due in = 30 - 7 = 23 months.

ampp-cip1.quiz_title: AMPP Certified Coating Inspector Level 1 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the body that awards the credential?

answers.text: A state licensing board awards the Basic Coatings Inspector Certification.
AMPP, the Association for Materials Protection and Performance, awards the Basic Coatings Inspector Certification.
The coating manufacturer awards the Basic Coatings Inspector Certification.
Pearson VUE awards the Basic Coatings Inspector Certification.

questions.explanation: AMPP is the certifying body; testing centers and manufacturers do not award the credential.

questions.question: A toolbox talk turns to confined space hazard awareness. Which point is correct?

answers.text: A confined space is any room with a closed door.
Leaving keys in running equipment is standard practice.
Confined spaces can hold oxygen-deficient, toxic, or flammable atmospheres and require controlled entry procedures.
Confined space rules apply only to underground mines.

questions.explanation: Atmosphere and entry control are why confined spaces get special procedures.

questions.question: Which statement best captures supervision required in a shop setting?

answers.text: In a shop setting a Basic Coatings Inspector works entirely without supervision.
Total seat time for the theory exam is 90 minutes.
In a shop setting a Basic Coatings Inspector works under the supervision of a Level 2 or a Level 3 inspector.
A Basic Coatings Inspector certifies pressure vessels for service.

questions.explanation: Shop work at Level 1 is supervised by a Certified or Senior inspector.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about the level above Basic in the family.

answers.text: The level directly above Basic is Basic Coatings Inspector at Level 2.
The level directly above Basic Coatings Inspector is Certified Coatings Inspector at Level 2.
The level directly above Basic is Senior Coatings Inspector at Level 2.
There is no level above Basic in the coating inspector family.

questions.explanation: Level 2 carries the Certified title; Level 3 carries the Senior title.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the scope of a Level 1 inspection?

answers.text: A Basic Coatings Inspector inspects only concrete and masonry substrates.
A Basic Coatings Inspector performs basic coating inspections on steel substrates using nondestructive testing and instrumentation.
AMPP was formed by the merger of AWS and API.
A Basic Coatings Inspector certifies pressure vessels for service.

questions.explanation: Level 1 scope is basic, nondestructive inspection work on steel.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about the current awarded title at Level 1 earns credit?

answers.text: Two years of coating inspection experience is required before the course.
The credential awarded at CIP Level 1 is titled Basic Coatings Inspector.
Theory questions are all true-or-false items.
The credential awarded at CIP Level 1 is titled Certified Coatings Inspector.

questions.explanation: Basic is the Level 1 title; Certified and Senior belong to the higher levels.

questions.question: An applicator is unsure about the top level of the family. Which statement should the inspector confirm?

answers.text: The top of the family is the Basic Coatings Inspector at Level 3.
The top of the coating inspector family is the Senior Certified Coatings Inspector at Level 3.
The theory exam carries no test code or name in the guide.
The theory exam provides no result until the application is approved.

questions.explanation: Level 3 is the senior tier of the three-level family.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how prerequisites for the Level 1 course is handled in practice.

answers.text: There are no prerequisites to take the CIP Level 1 course.
Candidates must bring their own calculator to the CBT.
Candidates need five years of blasting experience before the Level 1 course.
The theory exam provides a percentage score at the end of the exam.

questions.explanation: AMPP publishes no prerequisites for taking the Level 1 course.

questions.question: How would an experienced coatings inspector best explain work experience required before the course?

answers.text: One year of welding experience is required before the course.
The course purchase includes the renewal fee for the first cycle.
Six months of painting experience is required before the course.
No prior work experience is required before taking the CIP Level 1 course.

questions.explanation: Experience is a renewal requirement, not an entry requirement at Level 1.

questions.question: Which description of the purpose of a safety data sheet matches accepted coating inspection practice?

answers.text: A safety data sheet is the inspector's daily production log.
A safety data sheet communicates a chemical product's hazards, handling, storage, and emergency measures.
A safety data sheet replaces the product data sheet for application values.
An inspector's duty covers only the inspector personally.

questions.explanation: The SDS is the hazard-communication document for the product.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers what HazCom requires. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Hazard communication requires that chemical hazards be identified and communicated through labels and safety data sheets.
Hazard communication applies only to office chemicals, not coatings.
Respirator fit does not matter if the straps are tight.
Hazard communication is satisfied by word of mouth alone.

questions.explanation: Labels and SDSs are the backbone of hazard communication.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how checking the atmosphere before entry is handled in practice.

answers.text: A single test a week before entry covers the whole job.
The atmosphere of a confined space is tested before and during entry for oxygen, flammables, and toxics.
Atmosphere testing is needed only after work finishes.
Fall protection is needed only above one hundred feet.

questions.explanation: Testing precedes entry and continues while people are inside.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the coatings a Level 1 inspector examines. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: The theory exam needs no scheduling because it is taken at home.
The Level 1 scope covers inspection of powder coatings on aluminum only.
In a field setting a Basic Coatings Inspector is supervised by the site owner alone.
The Level 1 scope covers nondestructive inspection of liquid coatings applied by brush, roller, or spray to steel surfaces.

questions.explanation: The guide frames Level 1 around liquid coatings on steel applied by brush, roller, or spray.

questions.question: When checking practice against the AMPP blueprint, which statement about supervision required in a field setting is right?

answers.text: In a field setting a Basic Coatings Inspector works under the supervision of a Senior Certified Coatings Inspector (Level 3).
In a field setting a Basic Coatings Inspector works under any Level 1 colleague.
In a field setting a Basic Coatings Inspector needs no supervision at all.
In a field setting a Basic Coatings Inspector is supervised by the site owner alone.

questions.explanation: Field supervision at Level 1 runs to the Senior (Level 3) inspector.

questions.question: An applicator is unsure about education required to enter the pathway. Which statement should the inspector confirm?

answers.text: An associate degree in chemistry is required to enter the pathway.
A bachelor's degree in engineering is required to enter the pathway.
No education requirement is published for entering the CIP Level 1 pathway.
A high school diploma is the published entry requirement for the pathway.

questions.explanation: Entry to Level 1 carries no published education gate.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the first course required for certification. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Certification requires successful completion of the CIP Level 1 Course.
Certification requires the Level 2 course taken before Level 1.
Certification requires only a self-study reading of the course manual.
Certification requires a manufacturer's product course instead of CIP Level 1.

questions.explanation: The CIP Level 1 Course is a named certification requirement.

questions.question: On a shop walkdown of coated steel, the topic of the ethics course requirement comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Certification requires the Ethics for the Corrosion Professional Course or an equivalent training.
References to NACE CIP Level 1 describe a program that was cancelled with no successor.
Certification requires a law degree module on contract ethics.
The course purchase includes a lifetime AMPP membership.

questions.explanation: An ethics course (or equivalent) is one of the two required courses.

questions.question: An experienced coatings inspector explains a point to a trainee, the topic of the inspector's personal safety responsibility comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Safety is solely the responsibility of the site owner.
Every inspector bears personal responsibility for working safely and stopping to address an unsafe condition.
Personal responsibility ends once a safety talk has been attended.
An inspector may ignore unsafe conditions outside the coating area.

questions.explanation: Personal responsibility is an explicit element of the safety domain.

questions.question: A steel area of 2600 square feet is to be coated at a practical coverage of 260 square feet per gallon. Compute the gallons of coating required.
questions.explanation: Gallons = 2600 / 260 = 10 gallons.

questions.question: An experienced coatings inspector explains a point to a trainee, the topic of the function of the solvent in a coating comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The solvent chemically becomes the pigment once the coating has cured.
The solvent dissolves or carries the binder, controls viscosity for application, and then evaporates to leave the dry film.
The solvent provides the color and opacity of the finished coating.
The solvent remains permanently as the main solid that protects the steel.

questions.explanation: Solvents are temporary carriers that leave the film by evaporation and are not part of the final solids.

wonderlic.quiz_title: Wonderlic Cognitive Ability Test Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What position is the letter O in the alphabet?
questions.explanation: O is letter number 15 in the alphabet, counting A as number 1.

questions.question: mountain is to valley as peak is to:

answers.text: trail
base
slope
rock

questions.explanation: The relation is 'high to low pair': mountain relates to valley the same way peak relates to base.

questions.question: 40% of 40 equals:
questions.explanation: Convert the percent to a fraction of 100: 40% of 40 = 40 × 40/100 = 16.

questions.question: What position is the letter U in the alphabet?
questions.explanation: U is letter number 21 in the alphabet, counting A as number 1.

questions.question: KEEN is most nearly the same in meaning as:

answers.text: calm
sharp
eager
reluctant

questions.explanation: The word most nearly the same in meaning as 'keen' is 'eager'.

questions.question: What does the proverb "A watched pot never boils" mean?

answers.text: Patience cooks food better
Watching a pot is dangerous
Time seems to pass slowly when you wait anxiously
Pots boil faster when covered

questions.explanation: The proverb means: time seems to pass slowly when you wait anxiously

questions.question: Which of these numbers is the largest? 0.75, 0.045, 0.8, 0.3
A ribbon costs $52.38 and a spool costs $15.72. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: Add the two prices column by column: $52.38 + $15.72 = $68.10.

questions.question: What number comes next in the series? 18, 28, 46, 74, 120, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 74 + 120 = 194.

questions.question: Which number does not belong with the others? 84, 39, 30, 37
questions.explanation: 84, 39, 30 are all multiples of 3; 37 is not.

questions.question: Which number completes the series 9, 68, 13, 66, 17, 64, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: one rises by 4 each time it appears (9, 13, 17, ...) while the other starts at 68; the next term belongs to the first series, so it is 21.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly opposite to poverty:

answers.text: debt
hardship
misery
wealth

questions.explanation: Of the options, only 'wealth' runs against the meaning of 'poverty', so it is the opposite.

questions.question: Follow the instructions: Start with 20. Then double it, then double it, then subtract 1. What is the final number?
questions.explanation: Step by step from 20: applying double it, double it, subtract 1 gives 79.

questions.question: Sam, a technician, sees a small puddle of water on the floor of a busy walkway. What is the best course of action?

answers.text: Wait for the cleaning staff at the end of the week
Wipe it up or place a warning sign and report it
Step over it and continue working
Tell customers to walk around it without marking it

questions.explanation: For Sam, working as a technician, the responsible action is to wipe it up or place a warning sign and report it; the other choices ignore the problem, conceal it, or act without checking.

questions.question: Which choice arranges the words into a proper sentence? Scrambled: glided across the marsh at dawn the heron

answers.text: The heron across the marsh glided at dawn the.
At dawn the across marsh heron glided.
The heron glided across the marsh at dawn.
Across the heron glided the marsh at dawn.

questions.explanation: The only grammatically complete arrangement is: The heron glided across the marsh at dawn.

questions.question: In a code where each letter is shifted forward by 2 in the alphabet, BOOK becomes:

answers.text: GTTP
DQQM
ERRN
FSSO

questions.explanation: Shifting each letter of BOOK forward by 2 gives DQQM.

questions.question: How many players from one soccer team are on the field at once (standard)?
questions.explanation: There are 11 players from one soccer team in the field at once (standard).

questions.question: Three of the following belong together. Which one does NOT belong? — Paris, London, Rome, Canada

answers.text: Paris
London
Rome
Canada

questions.explanation: Paris, London, Rome are all European capital cities; Canada is not.

questions.question: A rectangular garden is 25 feet long and 13 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
questions.explanation: Area = length × width = 25 × 13 = 325 square feet.

questions.question: A packer packs 4 gift boxes per hour. A coworker works 3 times as fast. How many boxes does the coworker assemble in 8 hours?
questions.explanation: A packer packs 4 boxes per hour, so the coworker's rate is 4 × 3 = 12 per hour; in 8 hours: 12 × 8 = 96 boxes.

parapro.quiz_title: ParaPro Assessment Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An aide asks, in a community-helpers unit: Which word has three syllables?

answers.text: banana
apple
cat
dog

questions.explanation: The correct choice is 'banana' — it is the only option that matches the sound pattern asked for; the other words have different vowel or consonant sounds. [Practice variant 4 — Phonics and Decoding.]

questions.question: Which fraction is equivalent to the decimal 0.75? (Item 57 in a practice set.)
questions.explanation: The decimal 0.75 equals the fraction 3/4; converting the decimal's place value to a fraction and simplifying gives 3/4.

questions.question: Solve for x: x + 14 = 36
questions.explanation: Subtract 14 from both sides: x = 36 − 14 = 22.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct? (Grammar check set while writing a lunch-menu notice.)

answers.text: Maria and I went to the fair.
Maria and me went to fair the.
I and Maria goes to the fair yesterday.
Me and Maria went to the fair first and then I.

questions.explanation: The correct sentence is "Maria and I went to the fair." — it follows standard subject–verb agreement, pronoun, and verb-form rules, while each other choice breaks at least one of those rules. [Practice variant 9 — Grammar.]

questions.question: What is the mode of this data set: 20, 14, 21, 19, 19?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often; 19 appears twice and every other value appears once.

questions.question: Sam asks: as used in "The generous donor gave books to every classroom." the word "generous" means

answers.text: careful with money
very wealthy only
giving freely
impossible to determine

questions.explanation: In context, "generous" means giving freely — the surrounding details in the sentence point to that meaning, while the other choices contradict or ignore those clues. [Practice variant 2 — Vocabulary in Context.]

questions.question: Read: "Omar studied every night for a month before the spelling bee." What can reasonably be inferred?

answers.text: Omar dislikes studying
The bee was canceled
Nothing at all can be inferred from the passage
Omar wants to do well in the bee

questions.explanation: The details in the passage support the inference that omar wants to do well in the bee. The other choices either contradict the details or go far beyond anything the passage suggests.

questions.question: A clock shows a start time, and 7 hours and 40 minutes pass. How many minutes is that in total?
questions.explanation: 7 hours = 420 minutes; adding 40 minutes gives 460 minutes.

questions.question: Ava helps students find the perimeter of a square tile with sides of 19 cm. What is the perimeter?
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides: 4 × 19 = 76 cm.

questions.question: Rosa records quiz scores 7, 11, 12, 17, 19 for a group. What is the group's median score?
questions.explanation: Ordered, the middle score of the five is 12 — the median.

questions.question: Owen buys 10 notebooks at $8 each and pays with $100. How much change should Owen receive?
questions.explanation: The notebooks cost 10 × $8 = $80; change from $100 is 100 − 80 = $20.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: We ate lunch, and ___ we played outside. (Word-usage drill set in a history-timeline activity.)

answers.text: them
then
than
too

questions.explanation: 'then' is the word that fits the sentence's meaning and grammar; the other choices are sound-alike or look-alike words whose meanings do not fit here.

questions.question: A paraprofessional is reviewing punctuation in a school-garden journal entry. Which sentence needs a comma added? (Choose the correctly punctuated version.)

answers.text: After, the rain stopped we went outside.
After the rain, stopped we went outside.
After the rain stopped we went, outside.
After the rain stopped, we went outside.

questions.explanation: The correct version is "After the rain stopped, we went outside." — its commas, apostrophes, end marks, and capital letters all follow standard written English; each other version misplaces or omits at least one of them. [Practice variant 2 — Punctuation and Capitalization.]

questions.question: In 'The book is on the table', the word 'on' is (Grammar drill set while preparing a cooking-club recipe card.)

answers.text: an adjective
a preposition
a conjunction only
a verb

questions.explanation: In that sentence the word functions as a preposition — its job in the sentence (naming, acting, describing, or relating) is what determines its part of speech. [Practice variant 4 — Parts of Speech.]

questions.question: What is the predicate (verb part) of 'The children laughed at the joke'? (Sentence drill set during a recycling-campaign activity.)

answers.text: The children
at the joke only, with no verb
it cannot be determined from any sentence
laughed at the joke

questions.explanation: The answer is 'laughed at the joke': a complete sentence needs a subject and a predicate expressing a complete thought, and fragments and run-ons fail that test in opposite ways. [Practice variant 4 — Parts of a Sentence.]

questions.question: A paraprofessional checks a word list during a science-fair project. Which word is spelled correctly? (Practice variant 2.)

answers.text: independent
indipendent
all three spellings are equally correct
independant

questions.explanation: 'independent' is the standard spelling; the other forms misplace, double, or drop letters compared with the accepted spelling of the word. [Practice variant 4 — Spelling.]

questions.question: A student cannot think of anything to write about pets. A good prewriting step is to (Prewriting scenario set during a plant-growth observation log.)

answers.text: skip prewriting and turn in a blank page
hand the student a finished essay to copy
freewrite for a few minutes, jotting down any ideas about pets without stopping to correct them
copy a published essay about pets word for word

questions.explanation: The supported step is: freewrite for a few minutes, jotting down any ideas about pets without stopping to correct them. Prewriting comes before drafting and is about generating and organizing ideas, not about correctness or copying. [Practice variant 6 — Prewriting and Planning.]

questions.question: Read this passage: 'A bike shop ran a free repair clinic, so riders learned to fix flat tires themselves. Earlier changes had been tried, but this step made the biggest difference.' Which sentence best summarizes the passage?

answers.text: The history of a bike shop since it was founded
Why a bike shop should be closed next year
A problem that a bike shop caused for visitors
The benefit of the change at a bike shop

questions.explanation: The passage centers on one change — a bike shop ran a free repair clinic — and its benefit: riders learned to fix flat tires themselves. The other choices name topics the passage never discusses, so the main idea is the benefit of that change at a bike shop. [Practice variant 3 — Main Idea and Purpose.]

questions.question: In a passage read while preparing a cooking-club recipe card, a writer states that the town's winter coat drive collected four hundred coats last year, accepts donations at the fire station, and distributes coats through local schools. According to the passage, which of the following is true of the town's winter coat drive? (Reader: Zoe)

answers.text: It is the largest of its kind in the state
It received a national award last spring
It was founded by Zoe
It distributes coats through local schools

questions.explanation: The passage states directly that the town's winter coat drive distributes coats through local schools. The other choices add claims — about a founder, an award, or a ranking — that the passage never makes, so only the stated detail is supported.

questions.question: An aide helps a student edit while writing a lunch-menu notice. A student is unsure whether 'affect' or 'effect' fits a sentence. The best reference is

answers.text: a dictionary, to compare the two words' meanings and uses
tell the student editing and references are unnecessary
a map, to find where the words come from
a calculator, to count the letters

questions.explanation: The correct editing/reference choice is: a dictionary, to compare the two words' meanings and uses. Editing fixes surface correctness and uses the reference built for that exact job.

rich

bold

intricate
harm
idea
leave

sand
hospital
leg

questions.explanation: The relation is covering and body part (shoe:foot :: glove:hand): shoe relates to foot in the same way glove relates to hand, so hand completes the pair; the other completions offered (fire, leg, sand, hospital) break that relation.

questions.question: A word meaning 'calm, peaceful and untroubled' is ___

answers.text: eloquent
ancient
serene
severe
abundant

questions.explanation: 'Serene' matches the definition exactly — calm, peaceful and untroubled — while each other choice names a different concept (definition 14).

questions.question: 115 items are shared equally among 5 people. How many items does each person get?
questions.explanation: Working the operation directly gives 23: each distractor results from a common slip such as adding instead of averaging or misplacing a digit, and none equals the computed value 23.

questions.question: Clara is 26 years old. Tara is 6 years older than Clara. How old is Tara?
questions.explanation: '6 years/inches older/taller' means add: 26 + 6 = 32. Subtracting would give the younger/shorter value, which answers the reverse question.

questions.question: Cubes are stacked 3 long, 2 wide and 4 layers high, with no gaps. How many cubes are in the stack?
questions.explanation: The stack is a rectangular solid: 3 × 2 × 4 = 24 unit cubes.

questions.question: Choose the completion: smile is to happy as frown is to ___

answers.text: sad
rope
drink
body
hunger

questions.explanation: The relation is expression and emotion (smile:happy :: frown:sad): smile relates to happy in the same way frown relates to sad, so sad completes the pair; the other completions offered (drink, body, hunger, rope) break that relation.

questions.question: Statements: (1) All tickets include parking. (2) This is a ticket. Which conclusion necessarily follows?

answers.text: The first statement must be false
The opposite of the second statement follows necessarily
Nothing at all can be concluded from the two statements
The conclusion holds only on weekdays
The second statement's subject has the property named in the first statement (it follows necessarily)

questions.explanation: From (1) and (2) together, the property in the first statement applies to the subject of the second, so the necessary conclusion is the one that restates that application; the negated version ('This ticket excludes parking') contradicts the premises rather than following from them.

questions.question: Because the road was ___, the delivery van took a different route. Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.

answers.text: paved
rural
blocked
straight
mapped

questions.explanation: 'Blocked' is the only choice that fits the sentence that begins 'ill in the blank with the most suitable word.': it matches the context clues in that sentence, while the alternatives contradict or ignore them.

questions.question: In a row of three, the pencil sits directly left of the mug, and the lamp is rightmost. What is in the middle position?

answers.text: Cannot be determined from the information given
mug
pencil
lamp
None of the three objects

questions.explanation: The lamp is fixed at the far right, and the pencil is immediately left of the mug; the only arrangement is pencil, mug, lamp, so the middle object is the mug.

questions.question: In a set where four figures are a red pentagon and one figure differs only in color, which figure is the odd one out?

answers.text: The red pentagon in the top-left position
The red pentagon drawn largest
The red pentagon in the center
The blue pentagon
The red pentagon drawn smallest

questions.explanation: Color is the only property that varies: four figures are red and one is blue, so the blue pentagon is the odd one out regardless of size or position.

questions.question: A class of 240 students has 15% absent one day (use the class size as the whole). How many students is that?
questions.explanation: 15% of 240 = 240 × 15/100 = 36. The other values come from using the wrong percentage or dropping a zero.

questions.question: The figure 'LETTER L' is reflected in a horizontal edge (flip top-to-bottom)2. What happens to it?

answers.text: Its top and bottom swap places, but its left and right stay the same
It stays exactly identical in every respect, including any lettering
It rotates 180 degrees in its plane
It becomes twice its original size
Its left and right sides swap places, but its top and bottom stay the same

questions.explanation: A flip over a horizontal edge is a top-bottom reversal of 'LETTER L': top and bottom exchange, left and right do not. That is different from a left-right mirror flip or a 180-degree rotation of 'LETTER L'.

questions.question: If 6 items cost the same ratio as 48 items scaled by 7, and the first group is 6, the second group is how many when the first becomes 42? (Solve the proportion 6:48 = 42:x)
questions.explanation: In the ratio 6:48, each step multiplies by 48/6 = 8; 42 × 8 = 336.

questions.question: A circle grows and shrinks in the pattern: small circle, medium circle, large circle, ___. If the size pattern (small, medium, large, medium) repeats, which figure comes next?

answers.text: medium triangle
small circle
medium circle
large circle
tiny circle

questions.explanation: The size cycle is small, medium, large, medium, then back to small, and the shape stays a circle throughout, so the next figure is a small circle.

questions.question: A sapling is 22 inches tall and grows to 13 inches taller than a second plant that is 22 inches. (Read carefully:) Priya's plant is 22 inches; Eli's is 13 inches taller. How tall is Eli's plant, in inches?
questions.explanation: Taller by 13 inches means add: 22 + 13 = 35. Subtracting would answer the reverse comparison.

parapathways.quiz_title: ParaPathways Assessment Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which sentence is correct? (Grammar and usage check set while writing a museum-visit report.)

answers.text: Whom did you invites to the ceremony?
Whom did you invite to the ceremony?
Who did you invite to the ceremony to whom's?
Who's invitation did you whom?

questions.explanation: The correct sentence is: "Whom did you invite to the ceremony?" It follows the rules of standard English grammar and usage — agreement, tense, pronoun case, and word choice — while each other sentence breaks one of those rules in a way a paraeducator should be able to spot. The setting for this item is the activity while writing a museum-visit report.

questions.question: During a library research lesson in a pen-pal letter exchange: A secondary source is

answers.text: ignore sources and evidence entirely
the original experiment data
a diary written at the time of the event
a work that analyzes or describes primary sources, such as a biography or history book

questions.explanation: In the activity in a pen-pal letter exchange, the supported answer is: a work that analyzes or describes primary sources, such as a biography or history book. Credible sources are authored, current, and evidence-based (journal articles and .edu/.gov sites over blogs, social posts, and tabloids), exact words require quotation and credit, and paraphrases still require citation.

questions.question: Which percent is equivalent to the fraction 16/5? (Ruth is converting between forms.)
questions.explanation: Convert the fraction to a percent: 16/5 = 3.2 as a decimal, and multiplying by 100 gives 320%.

questions.question: What is 667 rounded to the nearest ten? (Emma is rounding.)
questions.explanation: Look at the ones digit of 667: rounding to the nearest ten gives 670.

questions.question: Solve for x: x + 10 = 16 (Aaron is solving a one-step equation.)
questions.explanation: Undo the addition by subtracting 10 from both sides: x = 16 − 10 = 6.

questions.question: A paraeducator reviews word parts with students in a geography-quiz review. The word 'sunflower' is a compound word made from

answers.text: sunny + low
sun + flower
one root only
it has no effect on the word's meaning

questions.explanation: The correct answer is: sun + flower. Prefixes, suffixes, roots, and compound parts each carry a meaning, and using them is a standard word-analysis strategy for figuring out unfamiliar words. The setting for this item is the activity in a geography-quiz review.

questions.question: A reader is analyzing a text during a fire-safety poster activity. A fable ending with a stated lesson about honesty is mainly written to

answers.text: explain a scientific process
classify the text's binding
report a historical event
teach a moral while entertaining

questions.explanation: The best answer is: teach a moral while entertaining. Author's purpose (to inform, persuade, entertain, or instruct) and tone are read from the text's content and word choice, and this choice matches both the text type and its language. The setting for this item is the activity during a fire-safety poster activity.

questions.question: When a student misreads a word, a helpful prompt is to (Classroom reading-support item set during a space-unit lesson.)

answers.text: ignore every reading error permanently
tell the students to stop reading for the day
stop the student from reading aloud ever again
have the student look again at all the letters and sounds in the word

questions.explanation: The supported practice is: have the student look again at all the letters and sounds in the word. It builds the student's own reading skill — decoding, comprehension, discussion, and use of evidence — rather than bypassing the reading or doing the work for the student. The setting for this item is the activity during a space-unit lesson.

questions.question: Lena is working with integers on a number-line activity involving pencils. Calculate: (-6) ÷ (3) = ?
questions.explanation: For (-6) ÷ (3): applying the integer rules for the operation '÷' (same signs and different signs handled by the standard rules) gives (-6) ÷ (3) = -2, as Lena can check on the number line.
