questions.question: A recipe card Ravi is reading uses fractions of a cup. What is 4/6 + 3/6? Give the answer in simplest form.
questions.explanation: With the common denominator 6: 4/6 + 3/6 = 7/6, and simplifying that result gives 7/6.

questions.question: A storage box is 7 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 9 cm high. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters? (Caleb is packing the box.)
questions.explanation: Volume of a rectangular box is length × width × height: 7 × 3 × 9 = 189 cubic centimeters.

questions.question: During a phonics review during a map-skills lesson, an aide asks: Reading fluency is defined by which three basic components?

answers.text: the answer depends only on the word's spelling length
Letters, sounds, and spelling
Accuracy, rate, and expression
Speed, volume, and memorization

questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Accuracy, rate, and expression. This follows from how spoken words are built — phonemes (single sounds), syllables, digraphs, blends, and vowel patterns — and from the definition of fluency as accuracy, rate, and expression. The setting for this item is the activity during a map-skills lesson.

questions.question: A text shared with Elena (during a poetry-reading week) states that the school garden club plants seeds in March, waters the beds every morning, and sells herbs at the spring fair. According to the passage, which statement about the school garden club is true?

answers.text: It received a national award last spring
It was founded by Elena in 1950
It is the largest of its kind in the state
It waters the beds every morning

questions.explanation: The passage states directly that the school garden club waters the beds every morning. The other choices add claims — about a founder, an award, or a size ranking — that appear nowhere in the passage, so only the stated detail is supported. The setting for this item is the activity during a poetry-reading week.

questions.question: Read this passage, discussed while preparing class announcements: "After the power went out, Dad lit candles around the room." What can reasonably be inferred from the passage? (Ava is leading the discussion.)

answers.text: nothing at all can be concluded from the passage
The room has no windows at all
Dad is celebrating a birthday
The candles give light during the outage

questions.explanation: The details in the passage support the conclusion that the candles give light during the outage. The other choices either contradict those details or claim far more than the passage suggests. The setting for this item is the activity while preparing class announcements.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a comma after an introductory phrase correctly? (Punctuation and capitalization check set in a school-assembly announcement.)

answers.text: In the morning the students, gather in the hall.
In the morning, the students, gather in the hall.
In the morning, the students gather in the hall.
In, the morning, the students gather in the hall.

questions.explanation: The correctly punctuated and capitalized sentence is: "In the morning, the students gather in the hall." It applies the standard conventions — commas, apostrophes, quotation marks, end marks, and capital letters for proper nouns and sentence starts — while each other option misplaces or omits one of them. The setting for this item is the activity in a school-assembly announcement.

questions.question: During a writing mini-lesson while writing a birthday-book entry, an aide asks: Which sentence is punctuated as one complete sentence (not a run-on)?

answers.text: none of the choices can be correct
The library opens at nine, and it closes at five.
Opens at nine the library closes five.
The library opens at nine it closes at five.

questions.explanation: Working while writing a birthday-book entry, the right choice is: The library opens at nine, and it closes at five.. A complete sentence has a subject and a predicate and expresses a complete thought; fragments lack one of those, and run-ons jam two complete thoughts together without proper joining.

questions.question: A table shows books read: Monday 25, Tuesday 12, Wednesday 6, Thursday 12. What is the total number of books read in the four days shown? (Lena is reading the table.)
questions.explanation: Add the four daily figures: 25 + 12 + 6 + 12 = 55 books in total.

questions.question: Consider this passage (in a reading-buddy session): "In recent months, the school cafeteria changed in an important way: the cafeteria added a salad bar at lunch. As a result, students are choosing more vegetables with their meals." Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

answers.text: The benefit that followed when the school cafeteria made a change
The complete history of the school cafeteria since it was founded
A problem that the school cafeteria caused for the whole town
Why the school cafeteria should stop operating next year

questions.explanation: The passage is built around one change — the cafeteria added a salad bar at lunch — and the benefit that followed: students are choosing more vegetables with their meals. The other choices name topics (history, blame, closure) that the passage never raises, so the main idea is the benefit of the change at the school cafeteria. The setting for this item is the activity in a reading-buddy session.

questions.question: A student revises 'The cake was good' to 'The chocolate cake was moist and rich.' This revision improves the writing by (Writing-process focus while writing a birthday-book entry.)

answers.text: adding precise, descriptive details
making the sentence shorter in every way
removing all describing words
skip the writing process entirely

questions.explanation: In the activity while writing a birthday-book entry, the supported answer is: adding precise, descriptive details. The writing process moves from prewriting through drafting and revising (ideas, focus, organization) to editing and publishing, and each choice above belongs to exactly one of those stages.

questions.question: Convert: 56 days = how many weeks? (Irene is converting units.)
questions.explanation: Since 7 days make one unit, 56 days ÷ 7 = 8 weeks.

fcle.quiz_title: Florida Civic Literacy Exam (FCLE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A homework worksheet includes this item: an initiative allows citizens to?

answers.text: Remove a judge from a case
Veto a governor's bill
Propose a law or amendment and place it before the voters
Appoint cabinet members

questions.explanation: The initiative is a direct-democracy device letting citizens propose measures for a popular vote, used in many states but not at the federal level. This version of the item is set in a Saturday academy session, with Harper working through the question.

questions.question: In a tutoring session, the tutor asks: original jurisdiction means a court?

answers.text: Reviews a lower court's record
Has authority over all appeals
Hears a case first, at trial level
Decides only tax cases

questions.explanation: Cases begin in courts of original jurisdiction; the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction is narrow, covering disputes such as those between states. The setting for this item is a campus study session.

questions.question: The Mayflower Compact (1620) is significant because it?

answers.text: Established religious freedom for all
Ended taxation without representation
Was an early example of self-government by consent of the governed
Created the first Congress

questions.explanation: Plymouth's settlers agreed to form a civil body politic by mutual consent — an early social-contract act. The setting for this item is a high-school government class.

questions.question: For a civics study guide, complete the item: a recall election allows voters to?

answers.text: Remove an elected official before the term ends
Ratify a treaty
Choose a vice president
Fill a Supreme Court vacancy

questions.explanation: Recall lets voters remove certain state and local officials mid-term; it does not exist for federal officials. The setting for this item is an after-school review.

questions.question: A review app presents this prompt: the Constitutional Convention met in 1787 in?

answers.text: Boston
New York
Williamsburg
Philadelphia

questions.explanation: Delegates gathered in Philadelphia in the summer of 1787 — originally to revise the Articles, they instead drafted a new Constitution. The setting for this item is an after-school review.

questions.question: At a voter-education workshop, a participant asks: each state has equal representation in which chamber?

answers.text: The House of Representatives
The Supreme Court
The Cabinet
The Senate

questions.explanation: Every state elects two senators regardless of population — the equal-representation half of the Connecticut Compromise. The setting for this item is a campus study session.

questions.question: In a mock exam for Florida students, one question reads: the equal protection clause is found in?

answers.text: The First Amendment
The Preamble
The Tenth Amendment
The Fourteenth Amendment

questions.explanation: Equal protection of the laws is a Fourteenth Amendment command directed at the states, central to Brown v. Board of Education. This version of the item is set in a weekend study circle, with Marley working through the question.

questions.question: A homework worksheet includes this item: the Convention decided the president would serve?

answers.text: Four years, eligible for re-election
Life
Two years
One seven-year term

questions.explanation: Rejecting both life tenure and a single long term, the Framers chose four-year terms with re-eligibility; the two-term limit came in 1951. The setting for this item is a classroom discussion.

questions.question: Jordan is helping a friend prepare and asks: Medicare and Medicaid were created in 1965 to provide?

answers.text: Health savings accounts
Health coverage for the elderly (Medicare) and for low-income people (Medicaid)
Military health benefits only
Free health care for all workers

questions.explanation: The 1965 amendments to Social Security created Medicare (65+) and Medicaid (means-tested, state-administered). The setting for this item is a Saturday academy session.

questions.question: Which answer fits this question from a civics workbook: Executive Order 9066 (1942) led to?

answers.text: The forced relocation and internment of Japanese Americans during World War II
Desegregation of the military
The Manhattan Project
Rationing of gasoline

questions.explanation: President Franklin Roosevelt's order authorized exclusion zones; about 120,000 Japanese Americans, most of them citizens, were incarcerated. The setting for this item is a test-prep workshop.

questions.question: A classmate quizzes Logan with this question: the free exercise clause of the First Amendment protects?

answers.text: Exemption from every law
The right to practice one's religion
Government endorsement of religion
Tax exemptions for all activity

questions.explanation: The free exercise clause protects religious belief and practice, balanced against valid government interests. The setting for this item is a public-library program.

questions.question: In a mock exam for Florida students, one question reads: Marbury v. Madison (1803) established?

answers.text: The right to counsel
Judicial review
The exclusionary rule
School desegregation

questions.explanation: Chief Justice Marshall's opinion in Marbury claimed the courts' power to declare acts of Congress unconstitutional. The setting for this item is a dual-enrollment class.

questions.question: For a civics study guide, complete the item: literacy tests were historically used in some states in order to?

answers.text: Speed up elections
Improve reading skills
Prevent Black citizens from registering to vote
Translate ballots

questions.explanation: Literacy tests were administered discriminatorily to block Black registration until the Voting Rights Act suspended and then banned them. This version of the item is set in a peer tutoring hour, with Harper working through the question.

questions.question: Jordan poses this question to a study partner: the principal author of the Declaration of Independence was?

answers.text: George Washington
John Adams
Benjamin Franklin
Thomas Jefferson

questions.explanation: Jefferson drafted the Declaration for a committee that included Adams and Franklin; Congress then edited it before adoption. The setting for this item is a classroom discussion.

questions.question: Which option correctly answers this review question: Baker v. Carr (1962) opened the door to court review of?

answers.text: Foreign treaties
Legislative apportionment and redistricting
Impeachment trials
Pardons

questions.explanation: Baker held that equal-protection challenges to malapportioned districts are justiciable, leading to 'one person, one vote' in Reynolds v. Sims. The setting for this item is a library review group.

questions.question: Think about United States civics: powers shared by both federal and state governments, such as taxation, are called?

answers.text: Concurrent powers
Denied powers
Reserved powers
Implied powers

questions.explanation: Concurrent powers — taxing, building roads, establishing courts — may be exercised by both levels. The setting for this item is a library review group.

questions.question: During a classroom discussion, the teacher poses this question: Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) had established the doctrine of?

answers.text: Judicial review
'Separate but equal' segregation
Miranda warnings
One person, one vote

questions.explanation: Plessy upheld Louisiana's segregated railcars; its doctrine stood until Brown undermined it in 1954. The setting for this item is a dual-enrollment class.

questions.question: Which answer fits this question from a civics workbook: powers not listed in the Constitution but reasonably drawn from listed powers are called?

answers.text: Implied powers
Concurrent powers
Reserved powers
Denied powers

questions.explanation: Implied powers flow from the necessary and proper clause, as upheld in McCulloch v. Maryland. The setting for this item is a campus study session.

questions.question: Marley, a Florida college student, is reviewing civics notes and wonders: the Anti-Federalists opposed the Constitution mainly because they feared?

answers.text: A weak presidency
A strong central government threatening liberty, and the lack of a bill of rights
Too much power for state governments
Direct election of the House

questions.explanation: Anti-Federalists like 'Brutus' warned of consolidation and demanded explicit rights protections. The setting for this item is a test-prep workshop.

questions.question: In a printed study guide, one entry asks: the opening words 'We the People' in the Preamble reflect the principle of?

answers.text: Divine right
States' rights
Popular sovereignty
Judicial review

questions.explanation: By beginning 'We the People,' the Constitution grounds its authority in the people rather than in the states or a monarch. The setting for this item is a peer tutoring hour.

oet.quiz_title: Occupational English Test (OET) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A patient says, 'the cough is always worse when I lie flat at night' — the cough worsens?

answers.text: when the patient is lying flat
after drinking cold water
only during exercise
when the weather is hot

questions.explanation: The extract ties the worsening directly to lying flat. The setting for this item is a hospital-based OET preparation course.

questions.question: Someone studying for the test asks: the task asks for a transfer letter to a rehabilitation unit — the letter should focus on?

answers.text: the unit's building history
the admitting doctor's biography
the patient's current mobility and care needs
the patient's full childhood history

questions.explanation: A receiving rehabilitation unit needs current function and care needs above all. The setting for this item is a medical English conversation club.

questions.question: Which option correctly answers this revision question: non-verbal communication that supports rapport includes?

answers.text: sitting at the patient's level with an open posture
facing the computer throughout
avoiding all eye contact
standing over the patient with folded arms

questions.explanation: Position and posture are part of relationship building in the assessed criteria. The setting for this item is a one-to-one tutoring session.

questions.question: A ward sign states: 'hand sanitiser must be used on entering and leaving this ward' — the sanitiser must be used?

answers.text: by patients only
only on entering
only after meals
on entering and on leaving

questions.explanation: The sign covers both entry and exit. The setting for this item is a pharmacist English study group.

questions.question: A healthcare professional preparing for OET asks: which transition best links a history paragraph to the current problem?

answers.text: Anyway, stuff happened.
So yeah, pain now.
Whatever the case may be.
Since her last review, Mrs Owen's pain has increased significantly.

questions.explanation: A formal linking sentence maintains flow and register between paragraphs. The setting for this item is a one-to-one tutoring session.

questions.question: In a study group, the group leader asks: in a briefing you hear, 'the pharmacy delivery is running late, so the evening antibiotics may be delayed' — the risk identified is?

answers.text: a shortage of beds
a delay to the evening antibiotics
late visiting hours
a cancelled ward round

questions.explanation: The late delivery threatens the timing of the evening antibiotic doses. The setting for this item is a hospital-based OET preparation course.

questions.question: A memo states: 'due to building work, the main entrance will close at 6 p.m. this week; use the side entrance after that time' — after 6 p.m., people should?

answers.text: use the main entrance as usual
use the side entrance
enter through the pharmacy
wait until morning

questions.explanation: The memo redirects evening entry to the side entrance during building work. The setting for this item is a peer practice partnership.

questions.question: A practice booklet contains this question: an article states: 'the cost of the programme is offset by the reduction in emergency admissions' — 'offset' here means?

answers.text: hidden from managers
balanced or compensated for
increased further
paid in advance

questions.explanation: Savings from fewer admissions offset — balance out — the programme's cost. The setting for this item is a hospital-based OET preparation course.

questions.question: For an OET study guide, complete the item: the transition phrase 'now that I understand the background, may I examine your knee?' works because it?

answers.text: closes the consultation
gives the diagnosis
links the stages and seeks permission to proceed
avoids the examination

questions.explanation: Linking phrases plus consent manage stage transitions. The setting for this item is a hospital library study space.

questions.question: In a printed study guide, one entry asks: the nurse asks, 'and how long have you been feeling unwell like this?' — the nurse is asking about?

answers.text: the duration of the illness
the severity of the pain
previous admissions
the patient's address

questions.explanation: The question asks how long the current illness has lasted. The setting for this item is a nursing English workshop.

questions.question: A candidate preparing for OET asks: in a handover you hear, 'her daughter is her next of kin — call her overnight if there is any change' — overnight, staff should?

answers.text: ask the daughter to visit immediately
discharge the patient to the daughter
call the daughter every hour regardless
contact the daughter if the patient's condition changes

questions.explanation: The instruction is conditional: call the next of kin if there is any change. The setting for this item is a hospital-based OET preparation course.

questions.question: Marley poses this question to a study partner: in a presentation the speaker says, 'getting patients up and moving on day one shortens their recovery' — early mobilisation is said to?

answers.text: shorten recovery
reduce appetite
delay discharge
increase complications

questions.explanation: The benefit claimed for day-one mobilisation is a shorter recovery. The setting for this item is a college language laboratory.

questions.question: In a printed study guide, one entry asks: in a presentation you hear, 'patients who understood their discharge instructions were half as likely to be readmitted' — understanding discharge instructions was linked to?

answers.text: longer hospital stays
more outpatient visits
half the readmission rate
double the readmission rate

questions.explanation: Half as likely to be readmitted is the outcome stated in the extract. The setting for this item is a one-to-one tutoring session.

questions.question: Think about professional healthcare English: which opening is most appropriate for a formal referral letter?

answers.text: Mrs Ali. Knee. Please see.
I am writing to refer Mrs Ali for assessment of her persistent knee pain.
Hey, can you take a look at Mrs Ali's knee?
To whom it may concern-ish, about a knee.

questions.explanation: A formal opening names the patient, the problem, and the purpose in a complete professional sentence. The setting for this item is a community learning centre.

questions.question: Reese, a doctor preparing for registration abroad, asks in a revision session: a patient misunderstands and says, 'so I take four tablets at once?' — the professional should?

answers.text: confirm it to avoid embarrassment
end the consultation
calmly correct the misunderstanding and re-explain the dose clearly
blame the patient for not listening

questions.explanation: Correcting a dosage misunderstanding is safety-critical information giving. This version of the item is set in a medical English conversation club, with Reese working through the question.

questions.question: One question on a tutor-made quiz is: a memo states: 'due to building work, the main entrance will close at 6 p.m. this week; use the side entrance after that time' — after 6 p.m., people should?

answers.text: wait until morning
use the main entrance as usual
enter through the pharmacy
use the side entrance

questions.explanation: The memo redirects evening entry to the side entrance during building work. The setting for this item is a study circle of internationally trained nurses.

questions.question: Which answer fits this question from an OET skills workbook: a patient says, 'I just want to be able to walk my granddaughter to school again' — the professional should?

answers.text: promise it will definitely happen
acknowledge this personal goal and link the plan to it
note it is unrealistic
ignore it as irrelevant

questions.explanation: Incorporating the patient's own goals is central to the patient-perspective criterion. This version of the item is set in a language school classroom, with Jamie working through the question.

questions.question: Which answer fits this question from an OET skills workbook: a clinic leaflet states: 'if you cannot attend your appointment, please telephone at least 24 hours beforehand to rearrange' — patients who cannot attend should?

answers.text: send a friend instead
simply not turn up
write a letter afterwards
phone at least 24 hours ahead

questions.explanation: The leaflet asks for a phone call at least a day in advance. The setting for this item is a community learning centre.

questions.question: Morgan, an internationally trained nurse, is revising for OET and asks: choose the correctly spelled word to complete: 'the patient has a ___ appointment in June' (a routine check after treatment)?

answers.text: folow-up
follow-up
follow-upp
followup-appoinment

questions.explanation: Follow-up is the correctly spelled compound in this context. The setting for this item is a hospital-based OET preparation course.

questions.question: A healthcare professional preparing for OET asks: case notes include 'patient lives alone; daughter lives overseas' — for a discharge letter after a fall, this detail matters because it?

answers.text: predicts the weather
shows the level of support available at home
describes the daughter's job
explains the patient's accent

questions.explanation: Living alone with family overseas is directly relevant to safe discharge planning. The setting for this item is a language school classroom.

isee.quiz_title: Independent School Entrance Examination (ISEE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to JOLT?

answers.text: glide smoothly
rest quietly
rock gently
shake with a sudden movement

questions.explanation: A jolt is a sharp, sudden shake or jerk. This version of the item is set in a one-to-one tutoring session, with Mateo working through the question.

questions.question: What is 2,207 rounded to the nearest hundred?
questions.explanation: The tens digit decides: 2,207 rounds to 2,200. The setting for this item is an entrance-test preparation programme.

questions.question: The data set is 7, 9, 14, 23, 25. What is the median?
questions.explanation: In order, the middle (third) value is 14. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

questions.question: Column A: 11/6. Column B: 5/3. Which statement is true?

answers.text: The two columns are equal
Column B is greater
The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
Column A is greater

questions.explanation: Column A = 11/6 and Column B = 5/3, so column a is greater. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to RIDDLE?

answers.text: a simple fact
a puzzling question
a long speech
a clear instruction

questions.explanation: A riddle is a question designed to be hard to solve. This version of the item is set in a one-to-one tutoring session, with Mateo working through the question.

questions.question: In the pattern 3, 6, 9, 12, ..., what is the 9th term?
questions.explanation: Each term adds 3; term 9 = 3 + 8 × 3 = 27. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

questions.question: A rectangle has length 10 cm and width 7 cm. What is its perimeter?

answers.text: 34 cm
17 cm
38 cm
70 cm

questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (10 + 7) = 34 cm. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

questions.question: A train travels at 60 miles per hour for 3 hours. How far does it travel?

answers.text: 63 miles
180 miles
240 miles
120 miles

questions.explanation: Distance = 60 × 3 = 180 miles. The setting for this item is a summer preparation course.

questions.question: Which of the following fractions is the greatest: 5/8, 2/3, 7/12, 3/5?
questions.explanation: Comparing by converting to decimals or a common denominator, 2/3 is the largest. This version of the item is set in an after-school revision group, with Parker working through the question.

questions.question: x is a positive integer. Column A: x + 5. Column B: 2 × x. Which statement is true?

answers.text: Column B is greater
Column A is greater
The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
The two columns are equal

questions.explanation: If x = 1, Column A is greater; if x = 10, Column B is greater. The relationship cannot be determined. The setting for this item is a school study club.

questions.question: One ISEE candidate wonders: which word is closest in meaning to HARVEST?

answers.text: the planting of seeds
a farmers' market
a winter storm
the gathering of crops

questions.explanation: The harvest is the season's crops collected from the fields. The setting for this item is a one-to-one tutoring session.

questions.question: Which of the following fractions is the greatest: 3/5, 5/8, 2/3, 7/12?
questions.explanation: Comparing by converting to decimals or a common denominator, 2/3 is the largest. This version of the item is set in a summer preparation course, with Nia working through the question.

questions.question: Text: The sonnet is fourteen lines long because, poets say, that is about the length of one held thought — long enough to turn an idea over, short enough that the turn still surprises. Question: The sonnet's length is explained as matching

answers.text: the length of a song
a royal decree
an ancient page size
the span of a single developed thought

questions.explanation: One held thought, turned over, fits fourteen lines. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

questions.question: Text: A town that plants a tree is making a promise to people it will never meet; a town that cuts one is breaking a promise made by people it never knew. Shade, in this sense, is an inheritance that arrives on schedule. Question: Shade is called an inheritance because it is

answers.text: sold with houses
owned by the town
planted annually
received from earlier planters

questions.explanation: Trees outlive their planters for others' benefit. The setting for this item is an after-school revision group.

questions.question: A classmate quizzes Finley: which word best completes this sentence: the mayor's speech was ___; it said in fifty words what most speakers would need five hundred to say?

answers.text: concise
unclear
lengthy
rambling

questions.explanation: Saying much in few words is the definition of concise. This version of the item is set in a school study club, with Sofia working through the question.

questions.question: Someone studying for the test asks which word completes this sentence: the lecture was so ___ that half the audience quietly left before it ended

answers.text: engaging
brief
tedious
clear

questions.explanation: Audiences leave lectures that are tedious — long and boring. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

questions.question: In a race, Ruth finished immediately ahead of Emerson, and Noor finished last of the three. Who finished first of the three?

answers.text: Emerson
Noor
Ruth
the information given is not enough to decide

questions.explanation: Ruth is ahead of Emerson, and Noor is last, so Ruth finished first. The setting for this item is a school study club.

questions.question: Passage: Ice can flow. A glacier looks like frozen stillness, but set a marker on its surface and return in a year, and the marker will have travelled — metres in a slow glacier, a kilometre or more in a fast one. The ice moves in two ways at once. Deep inside, under its own weight, the ice slowly deforms, crystals sliding past each other like a deck of cards pushed across a table. At the base, where pressure and the Earth's warmth can melt a thin film of water, the whole glacier may also slide over its bed. Rocks frozen into that sliding base scrape the valley floor, which is why glaciated valleys bear long scratches aligned like the marks of a giant file. Question: The thin film of water at a glacier's base forms because of

answers.text: summer rain
pressure and the Earth's warmth
sunlight on the surface
wind erosion

questions.explanation: Pressure plus geothermal warmth melt the basal film. The setting for this item is a school study club.

questions.question: Text: The printing of banknotes is a war against imitation: watermarks, threads, inks that shift colour, and print so fine the eye gives up. Every feature exists because someone, somewhere, first succeeded in copying the simpler thing before it. Question: Each security feature on a banknote exists because

answers.text: earlier, simpler notes were successfully copied
governments compete in design
collectors demand variety
paper wears out quickly

questions.explanation: Counterfeits drive the arms race. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

questions.question: Passage: When the bakery's ovens failed on the morning of the village fair, Tomas did not panic; he did arithmetic. Forty loaves were promised by noon. The miller's wood oven, two lanes away, could bake twelve loaves an hour, but the miller needed it himself from ten o'clock. That left three hours of borrowed fire — thirty-six loaves if everything went perfectly, which it never did. Tomas sent his sister to the fair committee with a message he had written on the back of a flour sack: thirty-two loaves by noon, he promised, and four more by one o'clock, still warm. He would rather promise less and be believed, he told her, than promise forty and be doubted at thirty-nine. Question: The passage is mainly about

answers.text: how Tomas solves a baking problem by promising honestly
the history of the village fair
why bakery ovens break down
how wood ovens are built

questions.explanation: The story centres on his calculation and his adjusted promise. The setting for this item is an ISEE preparation class.

hsrt.quiz_title: Health Sciences Reasoning Test (HSRT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A report from a hospital ward gives this finding: 30% patients said they were seen within fifteen minutes of their appointment time of the patients surveyed. Which statement says the same thing in plain language? The review covered 40 cases in total.

answers.text: 12 out of every 40 cases in the review matched the description given
Exactly 30 cases in the review matched the description given
Every case in the review matched the description given
28 out of every 40 cases matched the description given

questions.explanation: 30% of 40 is 12, so the finding means 12 of the 40 cases matched the description; it does not mean 30 cases, all cases, or the remaining 28 cases. This item is set in a routine health-service context. The correct choice stays within the evidence presented.

questions.question: A health team is reviewing a case. At a care home, 1 in every 10 screened adults were referred for a second test, out of 150 cases reviewed. Question: How many cases is that?
questions.explanation: 1 in every 10 of 150 cases is 150 ÷ 10 = 15 cases. The scenario is drawn from ordinary team practice. Each option was judged against the stem alone.

questions.question: Study the case that follows. In one month, a physiotherapy service recorded 87 routine appointments and 41 urgent appointments. Question: Which statement correctly compares the two figures?

answers.text: There were 128 more routine appointments than urgent ones
The two figures are equal once urgent cases are weighted double
There were 46 more routine appointments than urgent ones (87 compared with 41)
Urgent appointments outnumbered routine ones by 46

questions.explanation: The difference is 87 − 41 = 46, in favour of the larger figure (87); the sum 128 is not a difference. The context is a common health-service situation. No outside clinical knowledge is needed to answer it.

questions.question: Read this case and decide. Scenario: A dental audit finds that patients who attend six-monthly check-ups have fewer fillings per year than patients who attend only when in pain. Which statement follows most reasonably from the information?

answers.text: Attending check-ups prevents all fillings
Patients who attend only in pain do not care about their teeth
Six-monthly check-ups should be compulsory by law
Regular attenders in this audit needed fewer fillings per year than patients who attended only when in pain

questions.explanation: The audit supports the comparison as stated; prevention claims, motives, and compulsion all go beyond what an audit of attendance can show. This item is set in a routine health-service context. Each option was judged against the stem alone.

questions.question: The following scenario is presented. Read this short case: A company selling a supplement claims it 'boosts immunity', citing a testimonial from a satisfied customer as its only evidence. Which of the following is the most defensible evaluation?

answers.text: The claim must be true because the customer is satisfied
Testimonials are stronger evidence than controlled comparisons
The claim is weak only because the customer was not named
A single customer's testimonial is weak evidence for a general health claim

questions.explanation: One person's experience cannot establish a general effect; controlled comparisons, not testimonials, are the relevant standard. This case reflects standard health-service working. The skill tested is reasoning, not recall.

questions.question: Work through this case carefully. Passage: A school health team noticed that pupils who ate breakfast scored better on morning concentration tasks. The team leader argues that schools should provide a breakfast club so that no pupil starts the day hungry. Question: What is the main conclusion of the passage?

answers.text: Breakfast is the only factor that affects concentration
Schools should provide a breakfast club so that no pupil starts the day hungry
Pupils who skip breakfast are lazy in class
Concentration tasks should only be set in the morning

questions.explanation: The passage builds toward one claim: schools should provide a breakfast club so that no pupil starts the day hungry. The other options either go beyond the passage, blame individuals, or rule out alternatives the author never rules out. This item uses a familiar service setting. Each option was judged against the stem alone.

questions.question: The passage below describes a situation. Scenario: A website advises patients to stop a prescribed medicine, giving as its reason that the medicine is 'chemical' whereas a herbal alternative is 'natural'. What is the most accurate judgement about the reasoning here?

answers.text: Herbal products are always unsafe for every patient
Prescribed medicines never have side effects
Patients should never read health advice on websites
Whether something is natural or chemical does not by itself show whether it is safe or effective

questions.explanation: The natural/chemical contrast is not evidence about safety or effect; the other options replace one sweeping claim with another. The context is a common health-service situation. Reasoning from the information given is what earns the mark.

questions.question: The scenario below is original. Read this short case: A poster claims a breakfast cereal 'supports heart health' because it contains an ingredient that, in much larger amounts, was associated with heart benefits in one study. Which of the following is the most defensible evaluation?

answers.text: Breakfast cereals can never be part of a healthy diet
The amount in the cereal may be far too small for the studied effect, so the claim overstates the evidence
The study must be wrong because it studied only one ingredient
Claims are only acceptable if they mention every ingredient

questions.explanation: Dose matters: evidence at a much larger amount does not transfer automatically to the small amount in the product. This case reflects standard health-service working. The skill tested is reasoning, not recall.

questions.question: This passage describes a real-type situation. Read this short case: A service claims its helpline is excellent because the average call is answered within two minutes. No data are given on whether callers' problems were resolved. Which of the following is the most defensible evaluation?

answers.text: Fast answering is a disadvantage for a helpline
Answer speed alone does not establish the quality of the help callers received
Two minutes is too slow for any helpline
Excellence can never be measured in any service

questions.explanation: The claim substitutes one convenient metric (speed) for the outcome that matters (problems resolved). This item uses a familiar service setting. The correct choice stays within the evidence presented.

questions.question: The passage below describes a situation. Rule at a vaccination centre: If a staff member finishes the data-protection module, then they may access patient records. Hana finishes the data-protection module. Question: Which statement follows from the rule and the fact given?

answers.text: Hana is the only staff member who may access patient records
Hana may access patient records
Nobody who has not completed it can ever work at a vaccination centre
Hana finishes the data-protection module because they may access patient records

questions.explanation: The rule is 'if finishes the data-protection module, then may access patient records', and Hana meets the condition, so the consequence follows; uniqueness and reversed causation do not. The setting is a typical health programme. The correct choice stays within the evidence presented.

questions.question: A practice team reviewed this example. Four tasks must be done in some order at an eye clinic. Clues: the briefing is done before the team huddle; the team huddle is done before the stock count; and the stock count is done before the clinic set-up. Question: Which statement must be true?

answers.text: the briefing is done before the clinic set-up
the clinic set-up is done before the briefing
the team huddle is the very first task of the four
the stock count is done before the briefing

questions.explanation: The clues chain the order as the briefing → the team huddle → the stock count → the clinic set-up, so the briefing necessarily precedes the clinic set-up; the team huddle is second, not first, and the stock count follows the briefing. The setting is a typical health programme. Reasoning from the information given is what earns the mark.

questions.question: Consider this situation. Scenario: A care home reports fewer falls after installing brighter corridor lighting, comparing the six months after installation with the six months before. Resident numbers changed during that year. Which missing information most weakens the conclusion as it stands?

answers.text: The wattage printed on the light bulbs
How the number and frailty of residents changed across the two periods
Whether visitors liked the brighter corridors
The month in which the lighting was installed

questions.explanation: If the resident population changed, the fall counts may not be comparable; the population change is the missing piece. The setting is a typical health programme. The correct choice stays within the evidence presented.

questions.question: This item presents a situation. Passage: A public-health team translated its leaflet about childhood vaccination into the three languages most spoken locally. Enquiries about vaccination times rose in the following term. The team concludes that language had been a barrier for some local families. Question: The argument depends on assuming which of the following?

answers.text: Translation was done by a local volunteer group
The leaflet was also redesigned with new colours
Enquiries rose only slightly in the following term
Some families who enquired after translation had previously been unable to use the English-only leaflet

questions.explanation: The conclusion only follows if this holds: some families who enquired after translation had previously been unable to use the English-only leaflet. The other options may be true, but the argument does not need them in order to work. This case reflects standard health-service working. No outside clinical knowledge is needed to answer it.

questions.question: A tutor presents the following case. Consider the evidence: A study of a new wound dressing follows 80 patients. Wounds dressed with the new dressing healed in a median of 12 days; wounds with the standard dressing healed in a median of 15 days. Both groups were similar in age and wound size. Which conclusion does the evidence support most strongly?

answers.text: The new dressing will heal every wound in exactly 12 days
The standard dressing should be withdrawn immediately
The age of the patients caused the difference in healing time
In this study, wounds treated with the new dressing typically healed sooner than wounds treated with the standard dressing

questions.explanation: The groups were similar and the medians differ, so the modest study-bound conclusion is supported; guarantees, withdrawals, and alternative causes are not. The scenario is drawn from ordinary team practice. Each option was judged against the stem alone.

questions.question: The information below concerns a service. Consider the pattern: In a rehabilitation unit, the last 40 patients given a structured walking programme all improved their walking distance over four weeks. The patients were all recovering from the same type of knee surgery. Which generalisation stays within what the evidence supports?

answers.text: The programme will improve walking for every patient in any rehabilitation unit
The programme's results in this unit support expecting benefit for similar knee-surgery patients, but not necessarily for all rehabilitation patients
Forty patients is too few to support any expectation at all
The improvement must have been caused by the surgery alone

questions.explanation: A consistent result in a defined group justifies a cautious expectation for similar patients; extending it to everyone, or dismissing it entirely, both misjudge the evidence. This case reflects standard health-service working. The correct choice stays within the evidence presented.

questions.question: Here is an example to evaluate. Read this passage: An eye clinic began checking patients' glasses prescriptions against a simple chart at booking. Fewer appointments were wasted on the wrong test. The clinic lead concludes that mismatches between booking and the test actually needed had caused most wasted appointments. The author's central claim is best stated as which of the following?

answers.text: Booking staff should be replaced by the chart system
Mismatches between booking and the test actually needed had caused most wasted appointments
Patients deliberately book the wrong test
The chart works for every eye condition

questions.explanation: The passage builds toward one claim: mismatches between booking and the test actually needed had caused most wasted appointments. The other options either go beyond the passage, blame individuals, or rule out alternatives the author never rules out. The scenario is drawn from ordinary team practice. The skill tested is reasoning, not recall.

questions.question: This item is set in a clinic. Passage: A ward switched to a new checklist for discharging patients. In the following month, the number of patients who returned with medication questions dropped sharply. The ward sister argues that the checklist is helping patients leave with a clearer understanding of their medicines. Which of the following is an unstated assumption behind the argument?

answers.text: The checklist takes longer to complete than the old paperwork
Some patients still prefer written leaflets to a checklist
The fall in return questions reflects better understanding rather than some unrelated change
The ward sister designed the checklist herself

questions.explanation: The conclusion only follows if this holds: the fall in return questions reflects better understanding rather than some unrelated change. The other options may be true, but the argument does not need them in order to work. The setting is a typical health programme. No outside clinical knowledge is needed to answer it.

questions.question: Consider the details given here. Consider this report: A study of a back-pain exercise programme reports good results at the end of the eight-week course. It does not report how many participants dropped out before the end. A careful reader would first ask for which additional information?

answers.text: How many participants dropped out, and whether their results differed
The colour of the exercise mats used
Whether the instructor had taught the course before
The size of the room where classes met

questions.explanation: If strugglers dropped out, end-of-course results flatter the programme; the dropout information is needed. The scenario is drawn from ordinary team practice. Each option was judged against the stem alone.

questions.question: This short passage raises a question. A programme at a respiratory clinic finds that roughly 25% of participants need a second appointment within a month. Question: If 200 new participants join, about how many should the programme expect to need a second appointment?

answers.text: About 25
About 50
About 150
Exactly 50 — the percentage guarantees the number

questions.explanation: 25% of 200 is 50; because 25% is approximate, the expectation is 'about 50', not an exact guarantee and not 25 itself. The setting is a typical health programme. The correct choice stays within the evidence presented.

questions.question: Below is a health-service scenario. Entry to the advanced wound-care course requires ALL of the following: an assessment score of at least 75, at least 5 years in role, and the prerequisite module completed. Candidates — Grace: score 79, 4 years in role, prerequisite completed; Xenia: score 85, 5 years in role, prerequisite not completed; Opal: score 78, 7 years in role, prerequisite completed; Umar: score 70, 6 years in role, prerequisite completed. Question: Which candidate meets all the entry requirements?

answers.text: Grace
Xenia
Umar
Opal

questions.explanation: Checking each candidate against all three requirements (score ≥ 75; ≥ 5 years; prerequisite completed), only Opal satisfies every one; each other candidate fails at least one stated requirement. The context here is an ordinary clinical service. The skill tested is reasoning, not recall.

toefl.quiz_title: TOEFL iBT — Test of English as a Foreign Language Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: The item below is set at a university. Complete the sentence with the word that fits best: "The experiment produced ___ results, so the researchers decided to repeat it before publishing." Question: Which word completes the sentence?

answers.text: useless
unexpected
predicted
ordinary

questions.explanation: Repeating an experiment before publishing fits results that were unexpected and need confirmation. The completed sentence reads: "The experiment produced unexpected results, so the researchers decided to repeat it before publishing."

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. A student must arrange the following words into a correct sentence: me her lecture notes / lent / the campus café. Question: Which option gives the correctly ordered sentence?

answers.text: The sentence reads: The campus café lent me her lecture notes
The sentence reads: Me her lecture notes lent the campus café
The sentence reads: Lent me her lecture notes the campus café
The sentence reads: Lent the campus café me her lecture notes

questions.explanation: English sentences in this pattern follow subject + verb + the rest of the sentence: "the campus café lent me her lecture notes". The other options place the phrase before the verb or start with the verb or the final phrase, which breaks the order of the original sentence.

questions.question: The item below is set at a university. You hear a speaker say a sentence once: "Please go to the examination office at two o'clock and register at the front desk." Question: Which option repeats the sentence exactly as it was spoken?

answers.text: Please go to the examination office at two o'clock and do not register at the front desk
Please go to the examination office at two o'clock and register at the front desk
Please go to the examination office at three fifteen and register at the front desk
Please go to the medical centre at two o'clock and register at the front desk

questions.explanation: The exact repetition is "Please go to the examination office at two o'clock and register at the front desk". On the real Listen and Repeat task, a single changed word — a different time, a different place, or an added 'not' — changes the meaning, and accurate repetition is what earns credit. The distractors each alter exactly one element of the spoken sentence.

questions.question: Consider the material that follows. A notice at the Brookside Study Centre says: "Course registration opens on May 1 and closes on May 10. Late registrations cannot be accepted." Question: How many days after registration opens does it close?

answers.text: 10 days
7 days
12 days
9 days

questions.explanation: Registration closes on May 10, which is 10 - 1 = 9 days after it opens on May 1.

questions.question: Work through the material below. You hear a speaker say a sentence once: "Please go to the language laboratory at nine o'clock and register at the front desk." Question: Which option repeats the sentence exactly as it was spoken?

answers.text: Please go to the main library at nine o'clock and register at the front desk
Please go to the language laboratory at two o'clock and register at the front desk
Please go to the language laboratory at nine o'clock and do not register at the front desk
Please go to the language laboratory at nine o'clock and register at the front desk

questions.explanation: The exact repetition is "Please go to the language laboratory at nine o'clock and register at the front desk". On the real Listen and Repeat task, a single changed word — a different time, a different place, or an added 'not' — changes the meaning, and accurate repetition is what earns credit. The distractors each alter exactly one element of the spoken sentence.

questions.question: The item that follows uses academic English. A notice at the Elm Park Swimming Pool says: "All swimmers under twelve must be accompanied by an adult. Lockers require a refundable deposit." Question: What should a child of ten who wants to swim do, according to the notice?

answers.text: may swim alone in the shallow end only
may swim alone if they can swim well
may swim only with an adult present
may swim alone after signing a form

questions.explanation: The notice sets an age rule: under-twelves must be accompanied by an adult, with no exception for strong swimmers.

questions.question: A lecture context follows here. Listen to an announcement about the student health centre. "Please note: offering free flu vaccinations to all registered students throughout November." Question: According to the announcement, what is being offered?

answers.text: Free flu vaccinations during November
Free eye tests for all students
A new walk-in clinic on weekends
Free membership of the sports centre

questions.explanation: Only the vaccination offer is announced, with its month. The other options change the arrangement, invent a charge or rule, or reverse the announcement. (Practice focus: Listen to an Announcement item 781 of the TOEFL bank.)

questions.question: This item presents a brief text. Listen to part of a lecture on photosynthesis in desert plants. "Most plants open tiny pores in their leaves during the day to take in carbon dioxide, but this also lets water escape. Desert plants such as cacti reverse the pattern: they open their pores at night, store the carbon dioxide chemically, and use it for photosynthesis during the day while the pores stay closed. This strategy greatly reduces water loss, though it also limits how fast the plant can grow." Question: What is the talk mainly about?

answers.text: How desert plants photosynthesise while saving water
Why deserts are expanding worldwide
How cacti produce flowers at night
Why desert plants grow faster than other plants

questions.explanation: The lecturer's statements settle this item. The correct point is: how desert plants photosynthesise while saving water. The other options misstate the lecture, focus on a side detail as if it were the main point, or add claims the lecturer never made. Lecture items reward separating the main point from the examples used to support it.

questions.question: Consider the following short text. In a spoken interview (round 2 of the practice set), the interviewer asks: "Tell me about a teacher who influenced you." Please explain your reasons. Question: Which response best answers the interviewer's question?

answers.text: I have had many teachers.
My high-school science teacher influenced me because she made difficult ideas clear and encouraged me to ask questions.
Influence is a long word.
Teachers exist in schools.

questions.explanation: The strongest interview answer responds directly, gives a reason, and adds a concrete detail: "My high-school science teacher influenced me because she made difficult ideas clear and encouraged me to ask questions." The other options are vague, off-topic, or refuse to answer — in a spoken interview, a developed answer of several sentences is what demonstrates fluency. (Practice focus: Take an Interview item 1366 of the TOEFL bank.)

questions.question: Read carefully and choose. A student is completing a sentence from an academic text: "The student's answer was ___ correct, so the teacher awarded full marks." Question: Which word best completes the sentence?

answers.text: completely
not
partly
barely

questions.explanation: Full marks require an answer that is completely correct. The completed sentence reads: "The student's answer was completely correct, so the teacher awarded full marks." (Practice focus: Complete the Words item 137 of the TOEFL bank.)

questions.question: Read this item carefully. Listen to an announcement. "Tickets for the graduation ball are now on sale at the student union. Tickets cost $10 each, and students may buy tickets for guests at the same price." Question: How much will a student pay for 5 tickets in total?
questions.explanation: Each ticket costs $10, so 5 tickets cost 10 x 5 = $50. Guest tickets are the same price, so no extra charge applies.

questions.question: Read the material and answer the question. In a spoken interview (round 11 of the practice set), the interviewer asks: "Why did you choose to study at this university?" Please give a specific example. Question: Which response best answers the interviewer's question?

answers.text: Because it is a university.
My friend told me universities are good.
I chose it because its engineering programme has strong links with local industry, and I hope to do an internship in my third year.
I did not choose anything.

questions.explanation: The strongest interview answer responds directly, gives a reason, and adds a concrete detail: "I chose it because its engineering programme has strong links with local industry, and I hope to do an internship in my third year." The other options are vague, off-topic, or refuse to answer — in a spoken interview, a developed answer of several sentences is what demonstrates fluency. (Practice focus: Take an Interview item 1451 of the TOEFL bank.)

questions.question: Work through the item presented here. Passage: Paper was invented in China, where Cai Lun is traditionally credited with improving its manufacture in 105 CE. Before paper, Chinese writers used bamboo strips and silk: bamboo was heavy and silk was expensive. Cai Lun's process used bark, old cloth, and fishing nets, beaten into pulp and spread thin to dry. The new material was light, cheap, and smooth enough for writing, and its use gradually spread along trade routes to Central Asia and eventually to Europe. Question: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

answers.text: Paper probably became popular partly because its raw materials were easy to obtain
Cai Lun invented writing in China
Paper reached Europe before it reached Central Asia
Silk remained the main writing material after paper appeared

questions.explanation: Although the passage does not state it in so many words, it follows from what is given: paper probably became popular partly because its raw materials were easy to obtain. The other options contradict the passage or add unsupported claims.

questions.question: The material below is original practice material. At the student services desk, you hear a conversation. You hear: "Could I speak to someone about my accommodation?" Question: Which is the most appropriate response?

answers.text: Accommodation near campus is expensive.
I live in a shared flat.
The ground floor has a café.
The housing office on the ground floor can help you.

questions.explanation: The speaker asks or reports something that calls for a direct reply. "The housing office on the ground floor can help you." answers the actual words spoken; the other responses change the subject or merely comment on a related topic. This item practises hearing a question as a request for the specific information or action it names. (Practice focus: Listen and Choose a Response item 552 of the TOEFL bank.)

questions.question: Read this passage extract carefully. Context: a student writing to a librarian needs to ask whether a book can be renewed for another two weeks. (Message draft 4-1.) Which is the most appropriate subject line for this email?

answers.text: Renewal request - Introduction to Economics (due Friday)
Book question
Renew pls
About Friday

questions.explanation: For an email written to ask whether a book can be renewed for another two weeks, the professional choice is "Renewal request - Introduction to Economics (due Friday)". The other options are too vague, too informal, or off-topic for a message of this kind: effective academic emails name their purpose in the subject line, open politely, state the request plainly, and close formally. (Draft 4-1.)

questions.question: Examine the following text. Passage: Cities are usually warmer than the countryside around them, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island. Roads and buildings absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night. Cities also have fewer trees, which would otherwise cool the air through shade and evaporation. As a result, a large city can be several degrees warmer than nearby rural areas, especially on calm, clear nights. Planting trees and using light-coloured roofs are two ways cities try to reduce the effect. Question: In the passage, the word "absorb" is closest in meaning to which option?

answers.text: move from place to place
take in and hold
reflect back completely
produce in large amounts

questions.explanation: In this context, "absorb" means "take in and hold". The surrounding sentences in the passage on why cities heat up fix this sense, and the other options give meanings the word does not have here.

questions.question: Read this passage extract carefully. At the student services desk, you hear a conversation. You hear: "Would you like to join our study group this evening?" Question: Which is the most appropriate response?

answers.text: I studied a lot last night.
The group has ten members.
Evenings are getting darker now.
That sounds great. What time are you meeting?

questions.explanation: The speaker asks or reports something that calls for a direct reply. "That sounds great. What time are you meeting?" answers the actual words spoken; the other responses change the subject or merely comment on a related topic. This item practises hearing a question as a request for the specific information or action it names. (Practice focus: Listen and Choose a Response item 460 of the TOEFL bank.)

questions.question: The following item is about university life. Listen to a conversation. Lucas, a student, is talking to the examinations officer: Lucas: I have two exams scheduled at the same time next month. Officer: That is a timetable clash. You will take one exam in the morning as normal, and the other in the afternoon in a supervised room. Lucas: Will I have to stay in the supervised room between them? Officer: Yes, you will stay there with an invigilator, and lunch will be brought to you. Lucas: That is a relief — I thought I would have to choose one. Question: Why does the student go to speak to the other person?

answers.text: To request a later exam date
To ask for his exam results early
To complain about exam conditions
To solve a clash between two of his exams

questions.explanation: Everything needed is stated in the conversation between the speakers. The key point here is: to solve a clash between two of his exams. The other options describe purposes, details, or arrangements the speakers do not state, or they reverse what was said. Listening items reward tracking who wants what, what is decided, and the exact conditions attached.

questions.question: Here is a short academic item. An online course discussion. The professor asks: "Do grades motivate students, or harm learning?" Student A writes: "Grades give students clear feedback and a reason to organise their work across the term." Student B writes: "Grades make students choose safe, easy tasks instead of interesting, difficult ones, because they fear lowering their average." (Discussion set, round 1.) Question: Which student argues that grades can push students toward safe tasks rather than challenging ones?

answers.text: Neither student makes this point
Both students argue this equally
Student B
Student A

questions.explanation: The point about grades can push students toward safe tasks rather than challenging ones appears in Student B's post. The other student takes the opposing side of the professor's question, and neither 'both' nor 'neither' fits what is written.

questions.question: Consider the following item. Listen to a conversation. Felix, a student, is talking to a bank clerk near campus (campus services): Felix: I would like to open a student account. Clerk: You will need your passport and a letter from the university confirming your course. Felix: I have my passport, but not the letter. Clerk: You can request the letter from the student services office; it is usually ready in two days. Felix: Can I start the application today? Clerk: Yes, we can begin it, and you can bring the letter when you collect your card. Question: Why does the student go to speak to the other person?

answers.text: To report a lost bank card
To change money into another currency
To ask for a student loan
To find out how to open a student account

questions.explanation: Everything needed is stated in the conversation between the speakers. The key point here is: to find out how to open a student account. The other options describe purposes, details, or arrangements the speakers do not state, or they reverse what was said. Listening items reward tracking who wants what, what is decided, and the exact conditions attached.

psbhoae.quiz_title: Psychological Services Bureau Health Occupations Aptitude Examination (PSB-HOAE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: The item that follows is original. Which word is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'generous'?

answers.text: similar
selfish
certain
obscure

questions.explanation: The opposite of 'generous' is 'selfish'; the other options do not reverse its meaning.

questions.question: Work through the material below. Which answer is correct? Two or more atoms joined together form what?

answers.text: An electron
A molecule
A nucleus
A mixture of gases only

questions.explanation: A molecule is a particle made of two or more atoms bonded together. (HOAE practice item 926.)

questions.question: Look at the material presented here. What allows the arm to bend at the elbow?

answers.text: A joint where bones meet, moved by muscles
Blood pressure
A single solid bone
The skin stretching

questions.explanation: Joints allow movement between bones; muscles crossing the joint produce the bend.

questions.question: Here is a brief aptitude item. A word list pairs opposites. Which word is the direct opposite of 'freedom' in such a list?

answers.text: noise
captivity
sorrow
victory

questions.explanation: The direct opposite of 'freedom' is 'captivity'; the other options do not reverse the meaning of 'freedom'.

questions.question: Look at the material presented here. Your team is given a task none of you has done before. What is the best action?

answers.text: Ask the supervisor for guidance and work through it together carefully
Let the newest member try it alone
Guess your way through quickly
Refuse the task entirely

questions.explanation: The best action is to do this: ask the supervisor for guidance and work through it together carefully. Seeking guidance together on an unfamiliar task is responsible teamwork

questions.question: Read the material and answer the question. A hall is arranged in 32 rows with 9 seats in each row. How many seats are there altogether?
questions.explanation: Multiply rows by seats per row: 32 × 9 = 288 seats altogether.

questions.question: Read the short item that follows. A student is reviewing basic science before an admissions test. The question is: what is the young form of a frog called?

answers.text: A fry
A tadpole
A larva of a moth
A cub

questions.explanation: A tadpole is the aquatic larval stage of a frog. (HOAE practice item 833.)

questions.question: This item is part of aptitude practice. A student is reviewing basic science before an admissions test. The question is: which of these is a renewable energy resource?

answers.text: Wind
Natural gas
Oil
Coal

questions.explanation: Wind is renewable; coal, oil and gas are fossil fuels that are used up. (HOAE practice item 975.)

questions.question: Look at the following practice material. You spot a simpler way of organising a storeroom that the whole team uses. Which of the following should the worker AVOID doing?

answers.text: Reorganise it alone overnight without telling anyone
Suggest it to the team or supervisor and help introduce it if agreed
Ask a supervisor for guidance before acting
Treat everyone involved with courtesy and respect

questions.explanation: The action to avoid is this: reorganise it alone overnight without telling anyone. Sharing improvements through the team makes change safe and lasting

questions.question: This practice item follows below. A patient's religious practice affects what they wish to eat during their stay. What is the best action?

answers.text: Respect the practice and make sure the right meals are ordered
Serve the standard meal anyway — it is simpler
Tell the patient the practice is unnecessary in hospital
Ask other patients to swap meals informally

questions.explanation: The best action is to do this: respect the practice and make sure the right meals are ordered. Respecting a patient's beliefs in everyday care is part of dignified treatment

questions.question: The following item is original practice material. 240 raffle tickets are shared equally among 20 classes. How many tickets does each class get?
questions.explanation: Share the tickets equally by dividing: 240 ÷ 20 = 12 tickets per class.

questions.question: Examine this short item. One of the four spellings below is correct. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'a person applying for a position'?

answers.text: candidite
candidate
caniddate
cindidate

questions.explanation: The word meaning 'a person applying for a position' is spelled 'candidate'. The other three spellings are incorrect.

questions.question: Consider the question that follows. A printed band shows the letters R, T, V, X, Z in order, following a steady letter pattern (the alphabet wraps from Z back to A when needed). Which letter comes next on the band?

answers.text: K
C
B
I

questions.explanation: Each letter advances 2 places in the alphabet, so after Z comes B.

questions.question: Study the material that follows. One of the four spellings below is correct. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'a very small version of something'?

answers.text: mminiature
miniature
miniatture
miniatrue

questions.explanation: The word meaning 'a very small version of something' is spelled 'miniature'. The other three spellings are incorrect.

questions.question: Work through the following item. A health-occupations student describes this situation: A confused patient keeps trying to get out of bed alone and may fall. Which response best shows sound professional adjustment?

answers.text: Move the patient to a chair by the door unsupervised
Stay with the patient and call for help from nursing staff
Tie the patient's hands to the bed rails
Tell the patient firmly to stay put and leave

questions.explanation: Sound professional adjustment here means this: stay with the patient and call for help from nursing staff. Staying with an at-risk patient and summoning help prevents a fall

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. One of the four spellings below is correct. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'suitable for a purpose'?

answers.text: ppropriate
apprupriate
appropreate
appropriate

questions.explanation: The word meaning 'suitable for a purpose' is spelled 'appropriate'. The other three spellings are incorrect.

questions.question: The item below tests a basic skill. A colleague jokes about a patient's appearance within the patient's hearing. Which action would be WRONG for the worker in this situation?

answers.text: Do not join in, and speak to the colleague privately about it afterwards
Treat everyone involved with courtesy and respect
Repeat the joke to the next shift
Ask a supervisor for guidance before acting

questions.explanation: The action to avoid is this: repeat the joke to the next shift. Mocking a patient is never acceptable; challenge it properly and privately

questions.question: The material below is followed by a question. Read the following passage. A secondary school introduced a recycling scheme after a student survey found that most lunch waste was thrown into general bins. Colour-coded bins were placed in the dining hall, and a short assembly explained what belonged in each. In the first month, contamination — items in the wrong bin — was high, mainly because crisp packets and juice cartons looked recyclable but were not accepted by the school's contractor. After picture labels were added above each bin, contamination fell by half, and the scheme's student leaders began weighing the recycling each week to report progress. Question: Which title best fits the whole passage?

answers.text: Labels make recycling work
The problem with crisp packets
A history of school assemblies
Weighing waste weekly

questions.explanation: 'Labels make recycling work' covers the whole passage; the other titles fit only a detail or a different subject.

questions.question: Look at the item presented here. Read the following notice. Notice at a sports centre: The sports centre is open from 7:00 to 21:00 every day except Thursday, when it is closed. A session ticket costs $12. Registration for courses opens on the 3rd of the month and closes on the 17th. Question: On which day would a visitor definitely find the sports centre closed?

answers.text: Thursday
Monday
Friday
Wednesday

questions.explanation: The notice says the sports centre is closed on Thursday. (HOAE practice item 755.)

questions.question: This practice item comes next. A health-occupations student describes this situation: A worker arrives for a shift and realises they are wearing the wrong uniform items. Which response best shows sound professional adjustment?

answers.text: Say nothing and hope nobody notices
Borrow items from a patient's room
Go home without telling anyone
Tell the supervisor straight away and follow the dress-code policy

questions.explanation: Sound professional adjustment here means this: tell the supervisor straight away and follow the dress-code policy. Being open about a mistake and following policy shows reliability

dat.quiz_title: Dental Admission Test (DAT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Study the following item. Introns are removed from pre-mRNA during which process?

answers.text: Capping alone
Replication
Polyadenylation alone
Translation
RNA splicing

questions.explanation: Splicing cuts out introns and joins exons to form mature mRNA before it leaves the nucleus.

questions.question: Read the item below and answer. A large cube is built from 8 by 8 by 8 small cubes. How many small cubes is it built from in total?
questions.explanation: The total is 8 x 8 x 8 = 512 small cubes.

questions.question: Examine this short item. What is the positive square root of 64?
questions.explanation: 8 x 8 = 64, so the positive square root of 64 is 8.

questions.question: This practice item comes next. An item priced at $70 is discounted by 20%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: The discount is 20% of $70 = $14, so the sale price is 70 - 14 = $56.

questions.question: Study the item presented here. Which term describes the variety of genes within a population or species?

answers.text: Ecosystem diversity
Habitat fragmentation
Species richness
Trophic diversity
Genetic diversity

questions.explanation: Genetic diversity is variation in genes within a population/species — distinct from species richness (number of species).

questions.question: The material below is followed by a question. Four angles are shown in a figure, described by their measures: angle A measures 70 degrees, angle B measures 30 degrees, angle C measures 110 degrees, angle D measures 45 degrees. Rank the angles from smallest to largest. Which ranking is correct?

answers.text: B < D < A < C
C < A < D < B
B < D < C < A
B < A < D < C
D < B < A < C

questions.explanation: Comparing the measures gives the order B < D < A < C from smallest (30 degrees) to largest (110 degrees).

questions.question: The next practice item is below. A sheet is folded in half horizontally, then folded in half vertically. A hole is punched through the folded stack near its outer corner, away from both folds. When unfolded, how are the holes arranged?

answers.text: Three holes in a row
Four holes, one toward each corner of the sheet, symmetrically placed
Two holes along one edge
One hole at the centre
Eight holes

questions.explanation: Two folds give four layers; one punch through all layers reappears in all four quadrants when unfolded — four symmetric holes.

questions.question:
This item practises a core skill. Notice: A physics class measured the period of a simple pendulum. With a string length of 100 cm, the pendulum completed one full swing in 2.0 seconds. Students found that changing the mass of the bob did not noticeably change the period, while changing the length did.

Which conclusion is best supported by the class's findings?

answers.text: Longer pendulums always swing faster
The period cannot be measured reliably
The period depends only on the bob's mass
The pendulum's period depends on its length rather than on the bob's mass
Mass and length affect the period equally

questions.explanation: Mass changes had no noticeable effect while length changes did — supporting length, not mass, as the controlling variable. (DAT practice item 1226.)

questions.question: This item practises a core skill. A bag contains 4 red marbles and 6 blue marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: Probability = favourable / total = 4 / 10 = 2/5.

questions.question: Read this item carefully. An infrared spectrum shows bands near 1600 cm-1 characteristic of a ring system. Which structural feature does this most strongly suggest?

answers.text: An O-H group (alcohol or phenol)
A C=O carbonyl group
An aromatic (benzene) ring
A C-Cl bond only
A C#N nitrile group (or a C#C alkyne)

questions.explanation: The stated absorption is the characteristic signature used in survey courses for: an aromatic (benzene) ring.

questions.question:
