Consider each option carefully. Notice: A physics class measured the period of a simple pendulum. With a string length of 121 cm, the pendulum completed one full swing in 2.2 seconds. Students found that changing the mass of the bob did not noticeably change the period, while changing the length did.

According to the notice, what was the period of the 121 cm pendulum?

answers.text: 3.0 seconds
1.5 seconds
2.8 seconds
0.5 seconds
2.2 seconds

questions.explanation: The 121 cm pendulum's period was measured as 2.2 seconds.

questions.question:
The next practice item is below. Notice: A physics class measured the period of a simple pendulum. With a string length of 9 cm, the pendulum completed one full swing in 0.6 seconds. Students found that changing the mass of the bob did not noticeably change the period, while changing the length did.

Which conclusion is best supported by the class's findings?

answers.text: Mass and length affect the period equally
The period depends only on the bob's mass
The period cannot be measured reliably
The pendulum's period depends on its length rather than on the bob's mass
Longer pendulums always swing faster

questions.explanation: Mass changes had no noticeable effect while length changes did — supporting length, not mass, as the controlling variable. (DAT practice item 1234.)

questions.question: Look carefully at the following item. What is the general formula of the homologous series of alkynes?

answers.text: CnH2n-2
CnH2n
CnH2n+2
CnH2n+1OH (i.e. CnH2n+2O)
CnH2nO2

questions.explanation: The alkynes follow the general formula CnH2n-2 as the carbon chain lengthens.

questions.question: Read the item and decide. A flat ceramic tile is viewed from the front. Its outline is an L-shape made from a 6 cm by 6 cm square with a 3 cm by 3 cm square removed from its top right corner, with a circular hole 1 cm in diameter drilled through its centre. The block must pass exactly through an aperture in a thin board, entering from the front without being turned or flipped. Which aperture description matches the block?

answers.text: An aperture shaped as the same L-shape (6 cm square minus a 3 cm corner), with no hole or notch at all
An aperture shaped as the same L-shape (6 cm square minus a 3 cm corner), with a 1 cm circular hole in its lower right region
An aperture shaped as the same L-shape (6 cm square minus a 3 cm corner), with a 1 cm circular hole at its centre
An aperture shaped as the same L-shape (6 cm square minus a 3 cm corner), with a 2 cm square hole at its centre
An aperture shaped as the same L-shape (6 cm square minus a 3 cm corner) but 1 cm larger in every dimension, with a 1 cm circular hole at its centre

questions.explanation: In a keyhole (aperture) item the opening must reproduce the object's front outline exactly, including any hole or notch in its correct position — only the matching description does. (DAT practice item 552.)

questions.question: Here is an item to work through. A flat net of a cube is described square by square: centre: a letter P; above the centre: a letter Q; below the centre: a letter R; to the left of the centre: a letter S; to the right of the centre: a letter T; above the 'above' square: a letter U. The net folds up into a closed cube. Which face lies opposite the face marked with a letter Q?

answers.text: The face marked with a letter U
The face marked with a letter R
The face marked with a letter P
The face marked with a letter S
The face marked with a letter T

questions.explanation: In this cross-shaped net the centre's vertical pair and horizontal pair fold to opposite faces, and the far end square folds opposite the centre; a letter Q pairs with a letter R.

questions.question: The item below tests a core concept. Eggs and sperm are produced by meiosis in humans. A primary oocyte completes meiosis to produce how many functional egg cells?

answers.text: Eight
Two
One
Three
Four

questions.explanation: Oogenesis produces one functional ovum and polar bodies that degenerate — unlike spermatogenesis, which yields four sperm.

questions.question: Look carefully at the following item. What is the formula of the ionic compound formed from calcium (Ca2+) and chloride (Cl-)?

answers.text: CaCl2
CaO
NaCl
MgCl2
Al2O3

questions.explanation: The ion charges must balance overall, which gives the formula CaCl2.

questions.question: The item below tests a core concept. A structure is built from cubes stacked on a 3 by 3 base. The stack heights (in cubes) are: back row (left to right) 2, 2, 2; middle row (left to right) 1, 3, 1; front row (left to right) 2, 1, 4. Viewed from above (top view), how many of the nine base positions have at least one cube?
questions.explanation: Every listed stack height is at least 1, so the top view shows a square at every occupied base position — here all nine positions are occupied. (DAT practice item 647.)

questions.question:
Here is a DAT practice item. Notice: Surveyors recorded frog breeding success at several ponds. At Pond C, the water measured pH 5.8 and observers counted 29 tadpoles in a standard survey. Across all the ponds surveyed, ponds with water closer to neutral (pH 7) tended to have more tadpoles than strongly acidic ponds.

According to the summary, how many tadpoles were counted at Pond C?
questions.explanation: The standard survey at Pond C counted 29 tadpoles at pH 5.8.

questions.question: This item practises a core skill. Using q = mc(delta T) with c = 4.18 J/(g C) for water, how much energy in joules is needed to raise the temperature of 250 g of water by 4 degrees C?
questions.explanation: q = 250 x 4.18 x 4 = 4,180 J. This is a standard survey-level point for this test section.

shsat.quiz_title: Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: This question practises a tested skill. The ratio 9/5 is equal to x/25. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Since 25 = 5 × 5, multiply the numerator by the same factor: 9 × 5 = 45.

questions.question: Review the item that follows. What is 60% of 200?
questions.explanation: To find a percent of a number, write the percent as a fraction: 60% of 200 = 60/100 × 200 = 120.

questions.question: Take a moment with this item. If f(x) = 6x + 2, what is the value of f(4)?
questions.explanation: Substitute 4 for x: f(4) = 6×4 + 2 = 24 + 2 = 26.

questions.question: Here is another practice item. What is 3/7 × 5/3?
questions.explanation: Multiply numerators and denominators: 3×5 / 7×3 = 15/21 = 5/7 after simplifying.

questions.question: Here is a brief practice item. What is the volume, in cubic units, of a cube with edge length 3 units?
questions.explanation: Cube volume = edge³ = 3³ = 27 cubic units. This follows the standard rules for this type of problem, applied step by step.

questions.question: Work through the following item. Choose the verb form that best completes the sentence: By next June, the class ___ the entire novel.

answers.text: will had read
will have reading
will have reads
will have read

questions.explanation: The time clues in the sentence require 'will have read'; the other forms break tense agreement or verb form.

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. Draft passage: The robotics team's robot had to cross a ramp and pick up a ring. (2) During the first trial, the wheels slipped on the smooth ramp surface. (3) The team added rubber treads to the wheels before the second trial. (4) This time, the robot climbed steadily and placed the ring on its peg. Which transition best begins sentence 3 to show how the team responded to the problem?

answers.text: To fix the problem,
In contrast to the ramp,
For unrelated reasons,
Meanwhile, elsewhere,

questions.explanation: Sentence 3 describes the solution to the slipping wheels, so a purpose phrase like 'To fix the problem' fits.

questions.question: Consider this practice question. Passage: In 2015, a message in a bottle came ashore in Germany that may be the oldest ever found. The bottle had been released into the North Sea between 1904 and 1906 by a British marine researcher studying ocean currents. Inside was a postcard promising a small reward to whoever returned it with details of where it was found. For more than a century, the bottle drifted, was buried, or bobbed unnoticed. When a walker found it on a beach on the island of Amrum, the research institute that inherited the project honored the promise and recorded the find. Currents had carried the bottle far less directly than a map line would suggest. Which title best fits the passage?

answers.text: How Elevators Learned to Wait
Maps of the Ocean Floor
The Bees That Sleep in Flowers
The Postcard That Crossed an Ocean

questions.explanation: 'The Postcard That Crossed an Ocean' matches the passage's subject and focus; the other titles belong to different passages.

questions.question: Here is an item to work through. Poem: He grafted wishes onto stubborn stock — / A pear branch taught to marry apple wood — / And talked to trees as neighbors on the block / Talk over fences: daily, plain, and good. / The wasps wrote summer's signature in gold / Across the windfalls bruising in the shade. / He gathered some, and left the rest, he told / Us, 'For the deer, the field mice, and the trade / The orchard makes with autumn.' Now he's gone, / The trees keep faith with August all the same: / They set their fruit, they drop it on the lawn, / And wasps still sign, in gold, his given name. Which title best fits the poem?

answers.text: The Quilt
First Day at the New School (A Ghazal of Hallways)
Grandfather's Orchard
The Night Mail Train

questions.explanation: 'Grandfather's Orchard' matches the poem's subject and focus; the other titles belong to different poems.

questions.question: Consider the following item. What is the least common multiple (LCM) of 32 and 11?
questions.explanation: The smallest number that is a multiple of both 32 and 11 is 352.

questions.question: Consider the question that follows. Two angles are supplementary. One measures 67 degrees. What is the measure of the other angle in degrees?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles sum to 180 degrees: 180 − 67 = 113.

questions.question: First read the material, then answer. Passage: Some of the fastest trains in the world never touch their tracks. Maglev trains — short for magnetic levitation — use powerful magnets to lift the train a few centimeters above a guideway and to pull it forward. With no wheels grinding on rails, a maglev can travel smoothly at speeds above 400 kilometers per hour, and its parts wear out slowly. The costs, however, are steep: a maglev needs an entirely new guideway, not ordinary track, and the magnets and controls are expensive to build and power. For that reason, maglev lines remain rare, serving a few airport and intercity routes where speed justifies the price. The author's tone is best described as

answers.text: promotional, ignoring all drawbacks
balanced, weighing benefits against costs
focused only on danger
opposed to new technology

questions.explanation: The passage gives advantages and costs equal weight — a balanced tone. (Passage: 'Trains That Float'.)

questions.question: Work through the following item. Which rearrangement of the formula is correct: A = (1/2)bh, solved for h?

answers.text: h = 2Ab
h = 2A ÷ b

questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 2, then divide by b to isolate h. (In this item the keyed answer is 'h = 2A ÷ b'.)

questions.question: This practice item comes next. A spinner lands on a star with probability 1/5. If the spinner is spun 20 times, about how many times should it land on a star?
questions.explanation: Expected count = probability × trials = (1/5) × 20 = 4.

questions.question: Read this practice item carefully. Passage: For the physics club's bridge contest, the rules were simple: one deck of cards, one roll of tape, and the bridge that held the most textbooks won. Most teams built thick, flat decks of cards layered like lasagna. Priya built up. Her bridge was two towers and a span no thicker than a sandwich, and the club president laughed — kindly, but he laughed. The first textbook went on. The second. By the fourth, the towers had begun to bow, very slightly, the way a person bows who is carrying something heavy with good form. The bridge held six textbooks before it folded — not with a crash, but with a slow, courteous collapse, like a dancer taking a bow. It did not win. The lasagna bridge held nine. But that evening, the club president asked Priya to show the first-years how triangles work, and she understood that there are results, and then there are results. It can most reasonably be inferred that Priya's towers held as much as they did because

answers.text: she used extra tape secretly
the president helped her secretly
the textbooks were lighter for her team
their triangular structure distributed the load with good form

questions.explanation: The closing request — to teach 'how triangles work' — points to her structure's triangular strength. (Passage: 'The Bridge of Cards'.)

questions.question: The material below is followed by a question. Which rearrangement of the formula is correct: P = 2l + 2w, solved for l?

answers.text: l = P ÷ 2 + w
l = P − 2w

questions.explanation: Subtract 2w, then divide by 2 to isolate l. This follows the standard rules for this type of problem, applied step by step. (In this item the keyed answer is 'l = (P − 2w) ÷ 2'.) [Practice item SHS-1127, Equations and Inequalities.]

questions.question: Examine the item presented here. Passage: The night train north left the city at nine and reached the border town by morning, and for eight hours Yusuf had the compartment to himself with his uncle's letter in his coat pocket and his saxophone case across his knees. He was not, strictly speaking, supposed to have the saxophone. It was on loan from the school, for the term only, and the term had ended. But his uncle — who had played in dance bands before Yusuf was born — had written: 'Bring the horn. There is a wedding, and the band is short a chair, and a chair, once offered, should not stay empty.' Yusuf practiced fingering silently on the case all the way north, so as not to wake the corridor. When the conductor passed, he said nothing about the case. Some journeys, Yusuf decided, watching the dark fields unspool, are just a person carrying an answer to where it was asked for. Which title best fits the passage?

answers.text: The Night Train North
The Bridge of Cards
Seeds in a Coat Pocket
The Last Lighthouse Keeper's Cat

questions.explanation: 'The Night Train North' matches the passage's subject and focus; the other titles belong to different passages.

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. Passage: High above a city warehouse, rows of tomatoes grow in the sun. Rooftop farms take advantage of space that otherwise sits empty, placing food production near the people who will eat it. The benefits go beyond freshness. A planted roof insulates the building below, cutting heating and cooling costs, and its soil absorbs rain that would otherwise rush into storm drains. Rooftop farming has real limits, though: soil and water are heavy, so engineers must confirm the roof can bear the load, and someone must haul every bag of soil up stairwells or freight elevators. Successful rooftop farms plan for the building first and the garden second. Which statement would the author most likely agree with?

answers.text: Good ideas succeed when their practical limits are planned for, not ignored.
Careful observation rarely leads to any useful discoveries.
New technology always makes older skills completely worthless.
Natural processes are far too complicated for young students to study.

questions.explanation: The passage's overall position supports this statement. (Passage: 'Farming on a Rooftop'.)

questions.question: This item is part of SHSAT practice. Passage: Before accurate clocks, sailors could find their latitude from the sun and stars but not their longitude — their east-west position. An error could mean missing an island or striking rocks. In the 1700s, a British clockmaker named John Harrison spent decades building a sea clock that kept time despite a ship's motion and changing temperatures. Comparing the clock's home-port time with local noon let a navigator compute longitude. Harrison's fourth timekeeper, tested at sea in 1761, lost only about five seconds on an eighty-one-day voyage. The problem that had defeated astronomers was solved by a craftsman with springs and brass. The passage is best described as

answers.text: an explanation of how a process or system works
an argument that a practice should be changed
a problem followed by the solutions people developed for it
a chronological account of events in the order they happened

questions.explanation: The passage's structure matches this description. (Passage: 'The Clock That Kept the Sea'.)

questions.question: Consider the question that follows. Passage: When the bus route changed, Mateo's ride home from school shrank to twelve minutes — and somehow, his afternoons shrank with it. He mentioned this to no one. But he began getting off two stops early, at the canal, and walking the long way: past the bakery that put day-old rolls in a basket by the door, past the wall where someone had painted a harbor that had never existed in their inland town, past Mrs. Lindqvist's gate, where she was usually deadheading her roses and ready to report on them. The walk took forty minutes. His mother, noticing the rolls and the lateness in equal measure, asked no questions for a week. Then she set a second place at the early supper table, and a chair by the door for his wet shoes, and that was her whole comment. Which title best fits the passage?

answers.text: The Night Train North
Paper Cranes for Room 9
The Kite Repair Shop
The Long Way Home

questions.explanation: 'The Long Way Home' matches the passage's subject and focus; the other titles belong to different passages.

casas.quiz_title: Comprehensive Adult Student Assessment Systems (CASAS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: This practice item comes next. Transcript: Teacher: Please open your books to page forty-two. What is the best response?

answers.text: I read books at home.
Forty-two is an even number.
Page forty-two — thank you, I have it.
The book has many pages.

questions.explanation: The teacher gives an instruction; confirming the page shows the instruction was followed.

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. Transcript: Man: Thank you very much for your help yesterday. What is the best response?

answers.text: I need help too.
You're welcome. I'm glad I could help.
Yesterday was Tuesday.
Help is a noun and a verb.

questions.explanation: The man gives thanks; 'you're welcome' with a glad reply is the natural response.

questions.question: Read the item and decide. A store had 659 boxes and sold 359 of them. What is 659 - 359?

questions.question: Begin with the material here. If 9x = 216, what is the value of x?

questions.question: Work through the material below. How many grams are there in 7 kilograms?
questions.explanation: One kilogram equals 1000 grams, so 7 × 1000 = 7000 grams.

questions.question: Examine this short item. Announcement transcript: The train to Greenfield, due at two fifteen, will arrive about ten minutes late. Passengers should wait on platform one. How late will the Greenfield train be?

answers.text: One hour late
On time
Cancelled for the day
Ten minutes

questions.explanation: The announcement says the train will arrive about ten minutes late. (In this item the keyed answer is 'Ten minutes'.) [Practice item CAS-1214, Listening — Instructions, Announcements and Photo Prompts.]

questions.question: Answer the item that follows. In a survey of 25 learners, 15 learners chose morning classes. What percent of the learners chose morning classes?
questions.explanation: Percent = (15 ÷ 25) × 100 = 60%. This follows the standard approach for this type of item, applied step by step.

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. FOOD LABEL: frozen peas — 130 calories per serving. The packet contains 5 servings. How many calories are in the whole packet?
questions.explanation: Multiply calories per serving by the number of servings: 130 × 5 = 650 calories.

questions.question: Examine the item presented here. SHOP NOTICE: This week, oil costs $4 a bag, which is $1 less than last week. The offer ends on Sunday. How much did a bag of oil cost last week, in dollars?
questions.explanation: This week's price of $4 is $1 less than last week, so last week's price was $4 + $1 = $5. (In this item the keyed answer is '5'.)

questions.question: Read the item and decide. Instruction transcript: Listen carefully. First, tie back your hair. Next, switch on the machine. Only begin the main task when I say so. What must you do first?

answers.text: Leave the room quietly
Begin the main task at once
Tie back your hair
Switch on the machine

questions.explanation: The instruction begins 'First, tie back your hair', so that action comes first. (In this item the keyed answer is 'Tie back your hair'.) [Practice item CAS-1166, Listening — Instructions, Announcements and Photo Prompts.]

questions.question: This question practises a tested skill. A recipe uses 2/4 of a cup of flour in the morning and 1/4 of a cup later. What is 2/4 + 1/4?
questions.explanation: With the same denominator, add the numerators: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.question: Consider this practice question. Sarah earns $18 per hour and works 21 hours in a week. How much, in dollars, does Sarah earn that week?
questions.explanation: Earnings = rate × hours = 18 × 21 = $378. This follows the standard approach for this type of item, applied step by step.

questions.question: Review the item that follows. Transcript: Victor: I'd like to return this hat, please. Assistant: Of course. What is the matter with it? Victor: It is damaged at the seam. Assistant: I can offer a refund or an exchange. Why does Victor return the hat?

answers.text: A cheaper one was found elsewhere
It is damaged at the seam
The shop is closing
Two were bought by mistake

questions.explanation: Victor states the reason directly: the hat is damaged at the seam.

questions.question: Read the item and decide. Transcript: Kevin: Excuse me, how far is the health clinic from here? Yusuf: About thirty minutes on foot — go straight on and turn right at the bank. Kevin: Thank you very much. How long does it take to walk to the health clinic?

answers.text: About an hour
Two minutes by bus
Half a day
About thirty minutes

questions.explanation: Yusuf answers that the health clinic is about thirty minutes away on foot.

questions.question: The following item is original practice material. JOB ADVERTISEMENT: driver wanted. Pay: $16 per hour. Hours: three days a week. Training is provided. How much is the pay for this job?

answers.text: $16 per hour
$16 per day
$16 per week
$21 per hour

questions.explanation: The advertisement states the pay plainly: $16 per hour. (In this item the keyed answer is '$16 per hour'.) [Practice item CAS-1073, Reading — Signs, Ads, Labels and Vocabulary in Context.]

questions.question: The material below is followed by a question. EMAIL — From: Course Office. Subject: Room change. Your Tuesday English conversation class will meet in Room 299 instead of Room 195 this week only, because Room 195 is being repaired. Where will the class meet this week?

answers.text: Room 195
Room 299
Room 300
Room 194

questions.explanation: The email moves the class to Room 299 for this week because Room 195 is being repaired.

questions.question: This practice item comes next. Short text: Since David started using the stairs at work three months ago, David has slept better at night. David tells friends the change was small but the results came quickly. What is the main idea of the text?

answers.text: David regrets the change
Exercise and travel are unrelated topics
A small daily change brought David clear benefits
Daily habits can never change

questions.explanation: The text presents using the stairs at work as a small change whose clear benefit is that David slept better at night.

questions.question: Consider this practice question. Notice: LIBRARY NOTICE: Books may be borrowed for three weeks. DVDs may be borrowed for one week. You may renew books by phone if no one else has reserved them. Fines are charged for items returned late. What happens if an item is returned late?

answers.text: The item is kept by the library
Borrowing stops for a year
A fine is charged
Nothing is said about late returns

questions.explanation: The notice states that fines are charged for items returned late.

questions.question: Consider the following item. Passage: Tara works the early shift at the adult school. The shift begins at 5:30 a.m., so Tara leaves home while the street is still quiet. The best part of the early shift, Tara says, is finishing by early afternoon, which leaves time to collect the children from school and cook dinner before the evening class. According to the passage, which detail is correct about Tara?

answers.text: Tara works the early shift at the adult school
Tara refused the teacher's help at the end
Tara avoided all practice at home
Tara stopped attending after one week

questions.explanation: The passage states that Tara works the early shift at the adult school; the other choices contradict the passage.

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. Notice: CENTRE NOTICE: The adult school office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office is closed on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Evening classes run Monday to Thursday, 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. When is the office closed, besides weekends?

answers.text: On the first Monday of the month
On Friday afternoons
On public holidays
During evening classes

questions.explanation: The notice lists Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays as closed days.

ielts.quiz_title: IELTS — International English Language Testing System Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Begin with the material here. Transcript: Sarah: For the housing office, please dial extension 214. Tara: Extension 214 — thank you. What extension should Tara dial for the housing office?
questions.explanation: The message states that the housing office is on extension 214.

questions.question: Read this item carefully. Passage: In a survey of 100 students, 60 said they study online. What percent of the students said they study online?
questions.explanation: 60 out of 100 is 60/100 = 60%, so 60% of the students gave that answer.

questions.question: Examine the item presented here. Which sentence uses a complex structure accurately for Task 2?

answers.text: Although the city has invested in buses. Congestion remains.
The city, although, buses invested, congestion remains problem serious.
Congestion remains a serious problem because of although buses.
Although the city has invested in buses, congestion remains a serious problem.

questions.explanation: The keyed sentence uses an accurate concessive complex sentence; the others are fragments or garbled structures.

questions.question: Here is an item to work through. Transcript: Felix: For the housing office, please dial extension 536. Tara: Extension 536 — thank you. What extension should Tara dial for the housing office?
questions.explanation: The message states that the housing office is on extension 536. (In this item the keyed answer is '536'.)

questions.question: Take a moment with this item. Passage: In a survey of 400 residents, 200 said they use the night bus service. What percent of the residents said they use the night bus service?
questions.explanation: 200 out of 400 is 200/400 = 50%, so 50% of the residents gave that answer.

questions.question: Begin with the material here. Monologue transcript: Tickets for tonight's performance cost $11 for the general public. Members of the centre, however, enter free. How much do members pay according to the announcement?

answers.text: Nothing is said about members
Free
Double the public price

questions.explanation: The announcement contrasts the $11 public price with members, who enter free.

questions.question: This practice item comes next. Timetable: Buses to the island leave the central station at 8:05, 13:10 and 18:15 on weekdays. There are no later buses. A passenger who misses the 13:10 bus asks: when is the next bus to the island?

answers.text: There is no other bus that day
The 8:05 bus
The 18:15 bus
A bus one hour later the same morning

questions.explanation: After the 13:10 bus, the timetable's next departure is the 18:15 bus. (In this item the keyed answer is 'The 18:15 bus'.) [Practice item IEL-0711, Reading — General Training Texts: Notices, Workplace and Everyday Texts.]

questions.question: Here is a brief practice item. Chart data: The chart shows the following shares: tea 45 percent, coffee 15 percent, water 40 percent, juice 65 percent. Which sentence is the most accurate overview of the chart?

answers.text: Juice has the largest share, while coffee has the smallest
The shares add up to exactly 200 percent
Coffee has the largest share, while juice has the smallest
All four categories have exactly equal shares

questions.explanation: The highest value is juice at 65 percent and the lowest is coffee at 15 percent, so that overview sentence is accurate.

questions.question: Begin with the material here. Cue card: Describe a person who helped you. You should say: who the person was, how they helped you, and how you felt about it. Which set of preparation notes best organises this talk?

A list of difficult words unrelated to the topic
Notes about a different cue card topic
Brief key words in order: the person's identity; the help they gave; your feelings afterwards

questions.explanation: Effective Part 2 notes are brief key words following the card's order: the person's identity; the help they gave; your feelings afterwards.

questions.question: Consider the following item. Speaking Part 3 drill: "Do you think cities will grow bigger in the future?" Choose the strongest discussion answer — a clear view, explained and extended.

answers.text: A city is a large town with many buildings and people.

Cities future yes.
I live in a city at the present time.

questions.explanation: The keyed response develops a clear position on 'Do you think cities will grow bigger in the future?' with reasons — the standard Part 3 rewards. (In this item the keyed answer is 'In most countries, yes. Cities offer more jobs and better services, so people keep moving there. Governments will need to build housing and transport fast enough to keep up.'.) [Practice item IEL-1453, Speaking Part 3 — Discussion: Abstract Topics and Developed Answers.]

questions.question: Examine this short item. Timetable: Buses to the airport leave the central station at 9:30, 13:10 and 18:15 on weekdays. There are no later buses. A passenger who misses the 13:10 bus asks: when is the next bus to the airport?

answers.text: The 9:30 bus
A bus one hour later the same morning
The 18:15 bus
There is no other bus that day

questions.explanation: After the 13:10 bus, the timetable's next departure is the 18:15 bus.

questions.question: First read the material, then answer. Read the sentence: "Students must submit the form before the deadline on Monday." The underlined idea 'submit' is closest in meaning to

hide
delay
copy

questions.question: This question practises a tested skill. Transcript: Tutor: For your presentation, which topic have you chosen, Peter? Peter: We decided on urban community gardens. Tutor: A good choice — bring your outline on Tuesday. What topic did Peter choose for the presentation?

Urban community gardens
The life of a famous inventor
University sports facilities

washes
sells only
gives or supplies

questions.question: The following item is original practice material. Part 1 practice: the examiner asks, "Do you work or are you a student?" Which candidate response answers personally and develops the answer best?

answers.text: A student is a person who is studying at a school or university.

Student biology.
Universities are institutions of higher education.

questions.explanation: The keyed response answers the Part 1 question about your studies or job directly, personally, and adds detail or a reason; the others are fragments or general definitions. (In this item the keyed answer is 'I'm a student at the moment. I'm studying biology at university, and I chose it because I've always been interested in how living things work.'.)

questions.question: This question practises a tested skill. Monologue transcript: This Friday at the festival, we begin with a cooking demonstration in the morning. answers.text: A fireworks display
A cooking demonstration
A photography workshop
A swimming gala

questions.question: Work through the following item. Transcript: Tutor: For your presentation, which topic have you chosen, Yusuf? Yusuf: We decided on urban community gardens. Tutor: A good choice — bring your outline on Monday. What topic did Yusuf choose for the presentation?

answers.text: Urban community gardens
How to write a bibliography
The life of a famous inventor
University sports facilities

questions.explanation: Yusuf tells the tutor the chosen topic directly: urban community gardens.

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. Lecture transcript (history lecture, the evening lecture series): Before printing, every book in Europe was copied by hand. A single large book could take a team of scribes several years to finish. Because books were so scarce, libraries chained them to desks so that readers could use them but not remove them. answers.text: Several years for a team of scribes
About one week
Exactly one month
A single afternoon

questions.explanation: The lecture says a single large book could take a team of scribes several years.

questions.question: Consider the material below. Situation: You write a formal letter to the manager of a hotel, whose name you do not know, to complain about a booking error. Which opening is most appropriate for this letter?

Hello my friend,
Dear Hotel Team!!!
Dear Sir or Madam,

questions.explanation: For a formal letter to an unknown manager, 'Dear Sir or Madam,' is the appropriate, conventional opening.

questions.question: Look at the material presented here. Lecture transcript (psychology lecture, Room 12 of the science block): People who sleep after learning remember more the next day than people who stay awake for the same period. During deep sleep, the brain replays patterns from the day's learning. This replay seems to move new memories into longer-term storage. What is the main idea of the lecture?

answers.text: Dreams are the main cause of forgetting
People should never study in the evening
Staying awake improves memory
Sleep helps move new learning into long-term memory

questions.explanation: The comparison with staying awake and the replay explanation both support sleep's role in long-term memory.

The clinic at eight in the morning.

questions.question: Focus on the item below. Which sentence contains a comma error?

answers.text: We bought fruit, bread, and milk.
After lunch, we bought fruit.

We bought apples oranges, and pears.

questions.question: This item practises a core skill. In a class of 25 students, 15 are boys. What percentage of the class are boys?
questions.explanation: 15 out of 25 = 15/25 = 60% of the class. This follows the standard approach for this type of item, applied step by step.

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. In a passage about looking after a bicycle, which added detail best develops a paragraph about getting started?

Nobody in the writer's family has tried this activity.
The subject has a long and complicated history in several countries.
Beginners should start with the simplest equipment and add more only as their confidence grows.

questions.explanation: A paragraph about getting started is developed by practical beginner guidance, as in the keyed sentence. (In this item the keyed answer is 'Beginners should start with the simplest equipment and add more only as their confidence grows.'.) [Practice item KAP-1235, Passage Development.]

questions.question: Look carefully at the following item. Which statement correctly describes the right ventricle?

answers.text: Pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta to the body
Prevents backflow from the left ventricle into the left atrium
Carries blood away from the heart to the body
Pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs

questions.explanation: The right ventricle — pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs. The other choices describe different structures in the cardiovascular system.

questions.question: Take a moment with this item. Which electrolyte is the most abundant positively charged ion (cation) OUTSIDE cells?

answers.text: Calcium
Potassium
Magnesium
Sodium

questions.explanation: Sodium is the main extracellular cation and a key regulator of fluid balance.

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. Measurement practice: How many meters are in 4 kilometers?
questions.explanation: 1 kilometer = 1000 meters, so 4 kilometers = 4 x 1000 = 4000 meters.

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. Simplify the ratio 10:8. Give your answer as a ratio in its simplest form.
questions.explanation: Dividing both terms by their greatest common factor 2 gives 5:4.

questions.question: Focus on the item below. Luz buys 2 notebooks at $8 each and a pen for $3. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: The notebooks cost 2 x $8 = $16; adding the $3 pen gives $16 + $3 = $19.

questions.question: Study the following item. Notice: The recreation center offers a study skills course on Mondays and Saturdays. Each session runs from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. The course lasts 6 weeks and costs $25 in total. On which days does the study skills course meet?

answers.text: Mondays and Saturdays
Mondays only
Weekends only
Saturdays and Fridays

questions.explanation: The notice states the study skills course meets on Mondays and Saturdays.

questions.question: Study the material that follows. Mei reads the same chapter three times, writes questions in the margin, and books a room to practise explaining the topic to a classmate. It can reasonably be inferred that Mei

answers.text: has already mastered the chapter completely
expects the chapter to be removed from the course
is avoiding studying the chapter
wants to understand the chapter deeply, not merely to have read it

questions.explanation: Re-reading, margin questions and practising explaining are strategies for deep understanding, not avoidance or mastery already achieved. (In this item the keyed answer is 'wants to understand the chapter deeply, not merely to have read it'.) [Practice item KAP-0136, Drawing Inferences.]

questions.question: Work through the following item. Passage: Supporters of arranging a bookshelf point to its low cost. Critics, however, question whether it works for everyone. Both positions deserve a hearing. What is the author's main purpose in this passage?

answers.text: present two sides of a question fairly
describe a problem and propose a remedy
describe a subject and bring out its less obvious interest
explain how to carry out a process, step by step

questions.explanation: The passage's structure shows its purpose: to present two sides of a question fairly. (In this item the keyed answer is 'present two sides of a question fairly'.) [Practice item KAP-1345, Identifying Purpose.]

questions.question: The item below tests a core skill. A passage about organising a study timetable ends with a paragraph listing useful equipment. Which sentence best concludes the whole passage?

answers.text: With the right preparation, organising a study timetable becomes manageable even for a complete beginner.
Equipment shops open at nine o'clock.
The word 'equipment' has ten letters.
One shop in town sells equipment cheaply.

questions.explanation: A conclusion should close the passage's subject with a general, encouraging summary, not a stray detail. (In this item the keyed answer is 'With the right preparation, organising a study timetable becomes manageable even for a complete beginner.'.)

questions.question: Consider the question that follows. Survey result: At the community clinic, 100 people were asked to choose between paper forms and online forms. 74 chose paper forms and 26 chose online forms. Which conclusion is best supported by this result alone?

The survey proves paper forms are better in every way
More of the people surveyed at the community clinic chose paper forms than online forms

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. A temperature of 15 degrees Celsius is how many degrees Fahrenheit?

questions.question: Study the following item. A passage about caring for houseplants opens: 'First, decide what you want to achieve.' The next sentence begins: 'Next, gather what you will need.' The use of 'First' and 'Next' in this passage serves to

answers.text: introduce a surprising exception
quote an expert's opinion
show the order in which steps should be taken
compare two opposite opinions

questions.explanation: 'First' and 'Next' are sequence signals: they show the order of steps in a process. (In this item the keyed answer is 'show the order in which steps should be taken'.) [Practice item KAP-0735, Paragraph Logic.]

questions.question: This practice item comes next. The steps for changing a bicycle tyre are: (a) Fit the new tube and tyre onto the rim. (b) Remove the wheel from the bicycle. Take the tyre off the rim and remove the inner tube
Remove the wheel from the bicycle
Inflate the tyre and refit the wheel

questions.explanation: Correctly ordered, the steps for changing a bicycle tyre run: Remove the wheel from the bicycle; Take the tyre off the rim and remove the inner tube; Fit the new tube and tyre onto the rim; Inflate the tyre and refit the wheel. The third step is 'Fit the new tube and tyre onto the rim'.

questions.question: Look at the material presented here. Text with a dropdown blank: The report was written _____ a young artist in 2001. Which option best completes the blank?

by
through of it
with of

questions.question: Answer the item that follows. You hear: 'All volunteers must submit the assignment before the Friday deadline.' Which option repeats the sentence exactly?

All volunteers must submit the assignment before the Friday deadline.

questions.question: Here is an item to work through. What do we call a book in which you look up the meanings of words?

A dictionary

A diary

questions.explanation: A dictionary gives the meanings of words; Answer Short Question expects a word or a few words.

questions.question: The next practice item follows. Passage extract: The bridge was painted _____ a local engineer in 2001. Which word best completes the blank?

answers.text: through of it
from of
by
with of

questions.explanation: The passive form 'was painted by' introduces the agent, a local engineer. (Reading Fill in the Blanks tests exactly this word choice.)

questions.question: The item below tests a core skill. For a 200 to 300 word PTE Academic essay on the topic of zoos should be closed, which plan best fits the task?

answers.text: Four paragraphs: introduction with your position signposted, two body paragraphs with reasons and examples, and a conclusion
One long paragraph covering every idea in the order it occurs to you
Six short paragraphs of two sentences each, with no introduction
A story about your own childhood with no reference to the prompt

questions.explanation: A 200–300 word essay needs a compact structure: an introduction, developed body paragraphs and a conclusion, all answering the prompt. (In this item the keyed answer is 'Four paragraphs: introduction with your position signposted, two body paragraphs with reasons and examples, and a conclusion'.) [Practice item PTE-0901, Speaking & Writing — Essay: Prompts, Structure and Argument.]

questions.question: Review the following material. Transcript with a missing word: 'The university _____ opens at eight in the morning on weekdays.' You hear the recording once. Which word completes the transcript?

answers.text: never
laboratory
library
always

questions.explanation: The speaker says 'library' at that point in the recording, completing the sentence 'The university library opens at eight in the morning on weekdays.'

questions.question: Here is another practice item. You hear a recording that ends with a beep: 'The company plans to open a new office in the city [beep].' Which option correctly completes the recording?

answers.text: library
textbook
centre
lecture

questions.explanation: The recording's final word is 'centre'; Select Missing Word asks for the completion the speaker actually said.

questions.question: Read this practice item carefully. You hear: 'The lecture on volcanic lakes has been moved to the north lecture theatre in the science building.' The transcript reads: 'The lecture on volcanic lakes has been moved to the south lecture theatre in the science building.' Which word in the transcript differs from what the speaker said?

answers.text: south
volcanic
lakes
lecture

questions.explanation: The speaker said 'north', but the transcript writes 'south'; Highlight Incorrect Words asks you to spot exactly this difference. (In this item the keyed answer is 'south'.) [Practice item PTE-1041, Listening — Highlight Incorrect Words: Transcript Differences.]

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. Dictation: you hear the sentence: 'The lecture on glacier melt has been moved to the north lecture theatre in the education building.' Which option is the exact transcription of the sentence?

answers.text: The lecture on glacier melt has been moved to a north lecture theatre in the education building.
The lecture on glacier melt has been moved to the north lecture theatre in the education building today.
The lecture on glacier melt has been moved to the north lecture theatre in the education building.
The lecture on glacier melt has been moved to the south lecture theatre in the education building.

questions.explanation: Write from Dictation requires the exact words heard; only the keyed option transcribes 'The lecture on glacier melt has been moved to the north lecture theatre in the education building.' without any change.

questions.question: Read what follows and answer. Read Aloud text: When university researchers studied glacier melt near Kingsway, they recorded 30 sites over 5 years. The team found that water quality improved steadily after the second year. Samples were collected every season, and the results were compared with records from 2 earlier studies. How many sites did the researchers record?
questions.explanation: The read aloud text states the figure directly: 30. The other options are other figures mentioned in the text or derived from them. (In this item the keyed answer is '30'.)

questions.question: Focus on the item below. Passage: When institute researchers studied deep-sea vents near Ashford, they recorded 40 sites over 5 years. The team found that the number of species rose in every season they sampled. Samples were collected every season, and the results were compared with records from 14 earlier studies. Which one-sentence summary best covers the passage?

answers.text: The passage describes how to build equipment for measuring the subject at home.
The writer argues that the subject should no longer be studied at university.
The text is mainly a history of how the subject was first discovered by early explorers.
The text reports that when institute researchers studied deep-sea vents near Ashford, they recorded 40 sites over 5 years, based on the evidence it presents.

questions.explanation: The keyed summary restates the passage's central reported finding in a single sentence; the other options introduce claims the passage never makes. (In this item the keyed answer is 'The text reports that when institute researchers studied deep-sea vents near Ashford, they recorded 40 sites over 5 years, based on the evidence it presents.'.)

questions.question: Read this item carefully. Chart in words: In Harbourton, museum visitors were 40 thousand in 2020, 55 thousand in 2022 and 50 thousand in 2024. What is the combined total for the three years shown?

answers.text: 165 thousand
145 thousand
135 thousand
155 thousand

questions.explanation: The three figures are 40, 55 and 50 thousand, which total 145 thousand. (In this item the keyed answer is '145 thousand'.) [Practice item PTE-0574, Speaking & Writing — Describe Image: Charts and Data in Words.]

questions.question: Study the following item. Passage: Ocean currents carry warm water from the tropics towards the poles. One major current travels at about 12 kilometres per day and transports roughly 5 times as much water as all the world's rivers combined. Scientists monitor its speed at 2 fixed stations across the Atlantic. Which option lists only statements that the passage supports?

answers.text: Only: The figure 12 appears in the passage
Both: The figure 112 appears in the passage; and The figure 5 appears in the passage
Both: The figure 12 appears in the passage; and The figure 5 appears in the passage
Only: The figure 5 appears in the passage

questions.explanation: The passage supports both keyed statements (figures 12 and 5); each other option either drops a supported statement or adds the unsupported figure 112.

questions.question: First read the material, then answer. Recording transcript: When institute researchers studied coral reefs near Elmsworth, they recorded 30 sites over 3 years. The team found that night-time temperatures were lower than in nearby areas. Samples were collected every fortnight, and the results were compared with records from 11 earlier studies. How many sites did the researchers record?
questions.explanation: The recording transcript states the figure directly: 30. The other options are other figures mentioned in the text or derived from them. (In this item the keyed answer is '30'.)

questions.question: Look carefully at the following item. Recording transcript: The desert fig grows in sandy coasts, where it survives conditions that would kill most other plants. Its roots can reach 36 metres below the surface, and a single plant may live for more than 3 years. Local communities have used its leaves in traditional medicine for at least 7 centuries. Which summary best covers the recording?

answers.text: The text is mainly a history of how the subject was first discovered by early explorers.
The passage describes how to build equipment for measuring the subject at home.
The writer argues that the subject should no longer be studied at university.
The speaker reports that the desert fig grows in sandy coasts, where it survives conditions that would kill most other plants, based on the evidence described.

questions.explanation: The keyed summary restates the recording's central reported point; the other options add claims the speaker never makes, which Summarize Spoken Text penalises. (In this item the keyed answer is 'The speaker reports that the desert fig grows in sandy coasts, where it survives conditions that would kill most other plants, based on the evidence described.'.)

questions.question: Consider the following item. Passage: The desert fig grows in high plateaus, where it survives conditions that would kill most other plants. Its roots can reach 12 metres below the surface, and a single plant may live for more than 10 years. Local communities have used its leaves in traditional medicine for at least 14 centuries. For how long have local communities used the plant's leaves?

answers.text: 14 centuries
12 centuries
10 centuries
17 centuries

questions.explanation: The passage states the figure directly: 14 centuries. The other options are other figures mentioned in the text or derived from them. (In this item the keyed answer is '14 centuries'.) [Practice item PTE-1365, Reading — Multiple Choice, Single Answer: Passage Questions.]

questions.question: Study the following item. Lecture transcript: When university researchers studied mountain weather near Harbourton, they recorded 18 sites over 5 years. The team found that night-time temperatures were lower than in nearby areas. Samples were collected every month, and the results were compared with records from 14 earlier studies. How many sites did the researchers record?
questions.explanation: The lecture transcript states the figure directly: 18. The other options are other figures mentioned in the text or derived from them. (In this item the keyed answer is '18'.)

questions.question: Examine the following item. Four sentences of a paragraph are labelled 1-4. 1: 'As a result, the town's wells ran dry within five years.' 2: 'Farmers around the town began pumping groundwater faster than rain could replace it.' 3: 'This experience led the town to limit how much water each farm could pump.' 4: 'At first, the new wells produced record harvests.' What is the correct order of the sentences?
questions.explanation: The pumping (2) comes first, then the early success (4), then the wells running dry as a result (1), and finally the town's response (3).

questions.question: This question practises a tested skill. Recording transcript: The desert fig grows in sandy coasts, where it survives conditions that would kill most other plants. Its roots can reach 12 metres below the surface, and a single plant may live for more than 3 years. Local communities have used its leaves in traditional medicine for at least 9 centuries. Which option lists only statements that the recording supports?

answers.text: Only: The figure 3 is mentioned
Both: The figure 62 is mentioned; and The figure 3 is mentioned
Both: The figure 12 is mentioned; and The figure 3 is mentioned
Only: The figure 12 is mentioned

questions.explanation: The recording mentions both 12 and 3; the other options drop one supported figure or add the unmentioned figure 62.

questions.question: The following item is original practice material. Recording transcript: The mountain pine grows in rocky hillsides, where it survives conditions that would kill most other plants. Its roots can reach 18 metres below the surface, and a single plant may live for more than 3 years. Local communities have used its leaves in traditional medicine for at least 14 centuries. Which paragraph is the correct summary of the recording?

answers.text: A talk reporting a measured finding — 18 metres is the key figure the speaker gives for the question the talk answers.
A talk about the personal life and career of a famous scientist in the field.
A talk arguing that the research described should be stopped for safety reasons.
A talk explaining how to buy equipment for the research at low cost.

questions.explanation: The recording reports measured findings, and its key figure is 18 metres; only the keyed paragraph matches both the topic and the content.

ncsn.quiz_title: NCSN (National Certified School Nurse) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: In a school review of systems, what does the nurse ask about?

answers.text: A cardiovascular review in school appraisal asks about chest pain, fainting, shortness of breath with activity, palpitations and known heart conditions.
Health appraisal in school combines screening results, health history, nurse observation, teacher reports and family input rather than relying on a single test.
Teacher observations about squinting, holding books close, frequent requests for repetition, or inattention can signal a need for vision or hearing rescreening.
Review of systems in school nursing asks about recent symptoms by body system, such as cough, headache, stomach pain, rash, or changes in vision, hearing, appetite or sleep.

questions.explanation: Review of systems organizes symptom questions by body system, giving the school nurse a broad picture beyond the presenting complaint.

questions.question: What is an emergency care plan for a student with a chronic condition?

answers.text: Allergy plans identify the specific allergens, likely exposure routes, symptoms to watch for, and cross-contact prevention in classrooms and cafeteria.
An emergency care plan is a concise, accessible summary of a student's condition, warning signs, immediate actions, medications and emergency contacts for use by school staff.
A student returning to school after hospitalization or a change in chronic condition needs updated orders, a revised plan, staff notification and a check on supplies.
When a student with a chronic condition reports new or worsening symptoms, the nurse assesses, follows the plan, documents findings, and communicates with family and provider as indicated.

questions.explanation: The emergency care plan is the short, accessible version staff grab in a crisis: condition, warning signs, actions and contacts.

questions.question: How should the school nurse counsel a student about substance risk?

answers.text: Stress and coping education teaches healthy strategies such as movement, rest, social connection, and help-seeking, reducing reliance on substances or other harmful coping behaviors.
Sun safety education teaches shade, protective clothing, and sunscreen use during outdoor school activities and encourages habits that reduce ultraviolet exposure over time.

The school nurse counsels students about substance risk using nonjudgmental, confidential conversation within legal and policy limits, and refers students who need assessment or treatment to appropriate services.
Environmental risk reduction includes advocating for safe routes to school, adequate supervision, maintained equipment, and policies that reduce hazards before injuries occur.

questions.explanation: Nonjudgmental conversation within policy limits builds trust, while referral ensures students needing assessment get professional services.

questions.question: What strengthens classroom health education for a diverse student body?

answers.text: Religious and cultural observances such as fasting, dress, dietary practices, and holidays can affect school health planning and should be accommodated when safely possible.
Health education is strengthened when examples, images, and stories reflect the languages, families, and communities of the students being taught.
Decision-making styles differ among families, with some involving elders or extended kin, so the nurse asks who the family wishes to include in health discussions.
Health promotion messages are more credible when they are developed with input from the families and students they are meant to serve rather than imposed without consultation.

questions.explanation: Familiar languages, faces, and stories help students see health messages as relevant to their own lives and families.

questions.question: During a disclosure, which nurse response best supports the student?

answers.text: When a student discloses abuse, the nurse should listen calmly, believe the student, avoid leading questions, reassure the student that it is not their fault, and explain that help will be sought.
Abuse records are confidential and are shared only with those authorized and involved in protecting the student, never discussed in hallways or with staff who are not involved in the case.

Supporting a student who has experienced abuse includes keeping predictable routines, offering a calm private space, connecting the student with counseling, and watching for changes in health or attendance.
Students who witness violence at home may show sleep problems, frequent body complaints, trouble concentrating, or anxiety at school, and they benefit from trauma-informed support and referral.

questions.explanation: Calm listening without leading questions protects both the student and the disclosure, while reassurance reduces self-blame.

questions.question: Watching a student walk down the hall after a playground fall gives the nurse data about which system?

answers.text: An accurate school blood pressure reading requires a correctly sized cuff, a seated and rested student, and repeat measurement of an elevated result before referral, because technique strongly affects the value.

Eye appraisal beyond screening notes redness, discharge, pain, light sensitivity, vision change, and any injury or foreign body, with urgent referral when pain, vision change, or a penetrating injury is reported.
Musculoskeletal appraisal at school observes gait, posture, range of motion, swelling, and limp, and asks about the mechanism of any injury and whether the student can bear weight or use the limb.
A structured review of systems at school moves system by system through focused questions and observations so that related symptoms are not missed when a student presents with one vague complaint.

questions.explanation: Gait, posture, motion, swelling, and weight bearing describe musculoskeletal function after injury or with a limp.

questions.question: Feeling that adults at school care and that one belongs there is appraised because it acts as what?

answers.text: Protective factor appraisal at school inventories supportive adults, stable routines, peer acceptance, engagement in activities, and problem-solving skills that buffer a student against stress and adversity.

School connectedness, a student's sense of belonging and of being cared for by adults at school, is a protective factor the nurse can appraise by asking what the student likes about school and which adults they trust.

Substance use in the home is appraised for its effect on the student, including supervision, exposure, caregiving consistency, and the student's worries, with referral of the family to supportive resources.
Family engagement appraisal notes how the family prefers to communicate, work or caregiving constraints on availability, and past experiences with schools or health care that shape trust.

questions.explanation: School connectedness protects students; asking which adults a student trusts shows how strong that protection is.

questions.question: Cutting, buttoning, drawing, and emerging handwriting control belong to which developmental domain?

answers.text: Crossing two or more major percentile channels downward for weight or height over time is a growth red flag that prompts fuller appraisal and provider referral even when the current value is still in the usual range.

Fine motor development for school readiness includes drawing, cutting with scissors, buttoning, and emerging handwriting control, and difficulty is appraised alongside vision, practice opportunities, and teacher reports.

Growth during puberty includes a growth spurt whose timing differs between students, so temporary differences in height and build among classmates of the same age are often a normal part of development.

A failed developmental screening is followed by referral for formal developmental evaluation and connection to early intervention or school-based evaluation services, because screening identifies risk rather than giving a diagnosis.

questions.explanation: Fine motor appraisal pairs observed hand skills with vision, practice, and teacher reports of classroom work.

questions.question: Teaching general information in groups while keeping individual details private protects what?

answers.text: Digital health information shared by the school should come from reliable sources, be reviewed for accuracy and accessibility, and direct families to the school nurse with questions.
Confidentiality in group health education is protected by teaching general information in groups and reserving individual student health details for private conversation.
Motivational and strengths-based teaching builds on what learners already do well, supports confidence, and helps learners choose achievable next steps for health behavior.
Health education for stakeholders such as administrators and school boards uses concise data on student health needs and program outcomes to support decisions about resources and policy.

questions.explanation: Group sessions are public settings, so reserving individual health details for private conversation protects student confidentiality.

questions.question: Confirming receipt, attendance or barriers, and the ongoing plan describes which referral practice?

answers.text: Closed-loop referral follow-up reduces lost connections by confirming receipt of the referral, attendance or barriers, and the plan for ongoing care or support.
Emergency preparedness partnerships with public health and emergency management ensure schools are included in planning for outbreaks, disasters, and community health emergencies.
The school nurse maintains a current referral directory and verifies resources periodically, because programs, eligibility, and contact information change over time.
Evaluating partnerships looks at whether referrals are completed, student needs are met, and families experience the connection as helpful, not only at how many partners are listed.

questions.explanation: Closed-loop follow-up catches lost referrals early and documents barriers, so fewer students fall between school and community care.

questions.question: The building loses power and later relocates classes. What must the health room plan protect?

answers.text: A reunification plan describes how students are released only to authorized adults at a controlled location, with identity checks and careful documentation during a crisis.
The nurse helps assemble emergency supplies for the health room and go-kits, including first aid materials, essential student information, and plans for medication continuity.
The health room needs a plan for continuing care during power outages, building closures, or relocation, including protection of medications and health records.
Incident command roles assigned in advance clarify who leads, who communicates, who provides care, and who documents, reducing confusion during a fast-moving event.

questions.explanation: Continuity planning keeps medications secure and records available so daily care survives disruption of the building.

questions.question: Does holding the NCSN credential expand what a school nurse may legally do in the school setting?

answers.text: A registered nurse working in a school remains accountable to the state board of nursing for nursing judgments, even though employed by an educational rather than a health care agency.
Continuing competence for licensure and certification is shown through ongoing education, practice, and reflection, not by initial education alone.
Holding NCSN certification does not expand a school nurse's legal scope of practice beyond what the state Nurse Practice Act and state rules permit.
A state Nurse Practice Act defines the legal scope of nursing practice, sets education and licensure requirements, and authorizes the state board of nursing to discipline licensees.

questions.explanation: Certification recognizes expertise but changes no legal limits, so scope still comes only from state nursing law and its rules.

questions.question: Describing antecedents, the behavior, and its consequences to find what the behavior achieves is which appraisal method?

answers.text: De-escalation in a behavioral crisis at school uses a calm voice, space, reduced demands and audience, and the student's known calming strategies, with safety of the student and others as the first priority.

Adjustment difficulties after a stressor are appraised by timing from the event, the degree of mood or behavior change, and impairment at school, and are monitored because most improve with support while some progress.

Possible eating disorder signs at school include marked weight change, avoiding the cafeteria or eating very little, frequent bathroom trips after meals, excessive exercise, dizziness, and preoccupation with body size, and they require prompt medical referral.

Functional behavior appraisal describes the antecedents, the behavior itself, and the consequences that follow it, so the team can identify what the behavior communicates or achieves and plan positive supports.

questions.explanation: Functional behavior appraisal reads antecedent, behavior, and consequence to plan positive supports that fit the purpose.

questions.question: Fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue at school most suggest which illness pattern, with what action?

answers.text: Influenza-like illness at school typically presents with fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue, and ill students should stay home per current exclusion guidance.
Outbreak recognition in school includes watching attendance and symptom patterns for clusters by classroom, grade or activity that exceed expected levels.
Return to school after illness generally requires fever resolution without fever-reducing medicine, improving symptoms, and meeting disease-specific criteria in current guidance.
Hand hygiene with soap and water or approved sanitizer, done on arrival, before eating, after toileting and after coughing or sneezing, reduces transmission of many school infections.

questions.explanation: This symptom cluster fits influenza-like illness, and the student stays home under current exclusion guidance while recovering.

questions.question: Immunization, hand hygiene, etiquette, and staying home when ill are described together as what kind of protection?

answers.text: Immunization, hand hygiene, respiratory etiquette, and staying home when ill work together as layered protection, so no single measure carries all infection prevention in a school.
Sharps and contaminated materials are placed in appropriate puncture-resistant or biohazard containers and never handled in a way that risks exposure to students or staff.
Toileting and diapering assistance in school follows hand hygiene, glove use, surface cleaning, and safe disposal steps that protect both the student and the staff member.
After a possible bloodborne exposure at school, the exposed person washes the area promptly, reports the incident promptly, and is referred for timely occupational or medical follow-up.

questions.explanation: Layered protection means each measure covers gaps in the others, so the school does not depend on any single defense alone.

questions.question: Grace teaches in a room where students handle chemicals and solvents. What environmental supports are needed?

answers.text: Emergency eyewash, shower, and safety equipment in instructional areas must remain accessible and be checked regularly so it works when an exposure occurs.
Science labs, art rooms, and vocational areas need ventilation, safe chemical storage, and protective practices matched to the materials students handle there.
Safe routes and building grounds include maintained walkways, cleared snow and ice, adequate lighting, and prompt repair of trip hazards around entrances and play areas.
Hand hygiene supplies, working sinks, and clean restrooms are basic environmental supports that reduce spread of illness throughout the school building.

questions.explanation: Ventilation, safe storage, and matched protective practices control the specific exposures each instructional area creates.

questions.question: Speaking up for safer playground equipment and healthier cafeteria options for the whole school is an example of what?

answers.text: Maintaining competence is an ethical duty: the school nurse pursues ongoing education so care for students reflects current evidence and professional standards.
When a school directive conflicts with a student's health needs, the ethical school nurse advocates for the student, explains the health risk, and seeks resolution through proper channels.
Advocacy in school nursing includes speaking up for policy changes, such as safer playground equipment or healthier food options, that protect the whole student population.
Justice in school nursing means distributing health services fairly, so students receive care based on health need rather than popularity, behavior, or family influence.

questions.explanation: Advocacy extends to population policy, so a school nurse uses a professional voice to change conditions affecting every student.

questions.question: Sudden breathing difficulty, swelling and hives after a possible allergen exposure suggest what emergency, requiring what response?

answers.text: For severe bleeding at school, direct pressure on the wound with a clean barrier is the immediate first action while emergency help is summoned.
After epinephrine for anaphylaxis, the student is monitored continuously, positioned to support breathing, and observed for a possible second wave of symptoms while awaiting emergency transport.
A student with signs of shock, such as pale, cool, clammy skin, rapid pulse, weakness or altered alertness, is kept lying down, warm and still while emergency services respond.

Anaphylaxis in school is recognized by sudden breathing difficulty, swelling, widespread hives, vomiting or drop in alertness after a known or possible allergen exposure, and requires immediate emergency action per plan.

questions.explanation: Rapid multi-system symptoms after an exposure signal anaphylaxis, a life threat that demands immediate plan-based emergency action.

questions.question: A newly enrolled Nathan, a 7-year-old who is a second-grade student, has moved frequently and has no records. What support is appropriate?

answers.text: Exemption documentation is handled by verifying that the required form is complete and on file, filing it confidentially, and following district procedure without pressuring or shaming the family.
During registration, the school nurse provides families with a clear checklist of required immunizations and acceptable documentation so expectations are understood before the school year begins.
Cultural humility in immunization education means listening to family beliefs and concerns, using trusted interpreters when needed, and providing information without coercion or dismissal.

Students experiencing homelessness or frequent moves may lack records, so the school nurse helps obtain records and connects families with accessible, low-barrier vaccination services without delaying enrollment support.

questions.explanation: Helping obtain records and linking the family to low-barrier services supports both enrollment and immunization without punishing instability.

questions.question: Ava, a 9-year-old who is a fourth-grade student, will be outdoors for a field day. Which sun safety points should the nurse teach beforehand?

answers.text: Sun safety education covers shade, protective clothing and hats, sunscreen use with family permission, and extra care during midday outdoor activities.
Bicycle and scooter safety education emphasizes a properly fitted helmet, following traffic rules, using lights and reflective gear, and maintaining equipment in working order.
Safety education is reinforced when families receive the same messages taught at school, so home and school expectations for helmets, supervision, and routines match.
Students with disabilities may need individualized safety teaching, practice, and environmental supports for evacuation, transportation, and playground participation.

questions.explanation: Shade, clothing, and permitted sunscreen use protect skin during the high-exposure hours when outdoor events usually run.

scrn.quiz_title: SCRN (Stroke Certified Registered Nurse) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Same-sided limb clumsiness after an upper cerebellar infarct is explained by which statement?

answers.text: The dural venous sinuses have no valves, so the direction of venous flow within them can change when pressure relationships change or a sinus becomes blocked.

The superior sagittal sinus runs along the top midline of the dura, receives blood from cortical veins, and houses the arachnoid granulations through which cerebrospinal fluid is absorbed into the venous system.

The recurrent artery of Heubner is a small branch near the start of the anterior cerebral artery that supplies part of the internal capsule and basal ganglia and can be injured during aneurysm treatment in that area.

The superior cerebellar artery arises from the top of the basilar artery and supplies the upper cerebellum and parts of the upper pons, so its occlusion affects coordination on the same side of the body.

questions.explanation: The upper cerebellum is served by the basilar tip branch named for its position, and cerebellar signs appear on the same side.

questions.question: Before contrast-enhanced vascular imaging, which two patient factors are reviewed to anticipate risk?

answers.text: Noncontrast head computed tomography is typically the first brain image in suspected stroke because it rapidly distinguishes hemorrhage from ischemia and guides the initial treatment path.
A complete blood count in suspected stroke informs the team about anemia, infection clues, and platelet availability for clotting.
Contrast allergy and kidney function are considered before contrast-enhanced vascular imaging so risks can be anticipated and managed.
Electrolyte and kidney function results influence contrast use, medication choices, and correction of metabolic contributors to altered mentation.

questions.explanation: Contrast allergy and kidney function are reviewed before contrast imaging so the risks can be anticipated and managed in advance.

questions.question: Why can a small increase in blood or swelling inside the skull raise intracranial pressure sharply?

answers.text: Mood screening becomes part of acute stroke care as the patient stabilizes, because post-stroke depression is common, affects participation in rehabilitation, and is treatable when recognized.

Follow-up vascular and cardiac testing in acute stroke care is purposeful rather than routine, with each study ordered to answer a specific question about stroke cause that will change prevention treatment.

Pressure within the skull rises when blood, cerebrospinal fluid, or swollen brain adds volume inside the rigid skull, which has almost no room to expand, so small volume increases can produce large pressure increases.
Serum electrolytes, especially sodium, are monitored in acute stroke care because imbalances can worsen brain swelling, provoke seizures, or depress consciousness independently of the stroke itself.

questions.explanation: The rigid skull has almost no room to expand, so added volume from blood, fluid, or swelling raises pressure quickly.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches therapy disciplines with their main focus after stroke?

answers.text: Rehabilitation goals in the acute phase are specific, functional, and patient-centered, such as sitting at the edge of the bed, participating in grooming, or taking steps with assistance.
Physical therapy after stroke focuses on strength, balance, transfers, and walking, while occupational therapy focuses on daily activities, upper-limb use, and adaptive strategies.
Early mobilization in acute stroke care is progressed gradually with monitoring of tolerance, balance, and safety, because prolonged bed rest worsens deconditioning and complications.
Nurses verify that swallowing precautions, diet texture, and supervision needs are clearly communicated at discharge after stroke so caregivers follow them consistently at home.
